phrases.he: מֵאֵימָתַי קוֹרִין אֶת שְׁמַע בְּעַרְבִית.
phrases.en: From when does one recite Shema in the evening?

phrases.he: מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁהַכֹּהֲנִים נִכְנָסִים לֶאֱכֹל בִּתְרוּמָתָן, עַד סוֹף הָאַשְׁמוּרָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.en: From the time when the priests enter to partake of their teruma. Until the end of the first watch. That is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, עַד חֲצוֹת.
phrases.en: The Rabbis say: until midnight.

phrases.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, עַד שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה עַמּוּד הַשָּׁחַר.
phrases.en: Rabban Gamliel says: until dawn.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבָּאוּ בָנָיו מִבֵּית הַמִּשְׁתֶּה, אָמְרוּ לוֹ, לֹא קָרִינוּ אֶת שְׁמַע.
phrases.en: There was an incident where his sons returned from a wedding hall. They said to him: We did not recite Shema.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, אִם לֹא עָלָה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר, חַיָּבִין אַתֶּם לִקְרוֹת.
phrases.en: He said to them: If the dawn has not arrived, you are obligated to recite Shema.

phrases.he: וְלֹא זוֹ בִּלְבַד, אֶלָּא כָּל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים עַד חֲצוֹת, מִצְוָתָן עַד שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה עַמּוּד הַשָּׁחַר.
phrases.en: and it is not only with regard to the recitation of Shema, but rather, wherever the Sages say until midnight, the mitzva may be performed until dawn.

phrases.he: הֶקְטֵר חֲלָבִים וְאֵבָרִים, מִצְוָתָן עַד שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה עַמּוּד הַשָּׁחַר.
phrases.en: the burning of fats and limbs may be performed until dawn.

phrases.he: וְכָל הַנֶּאֱכָלִים לְיוֹם אֶחָד, מִצְוָתָן עַד שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה עַמּוּד הַשָּׁחַר.
phrases.en: And all sacrifices that are eaten for one day may be eaten until dawn.

phrases.he: אִם כֵּן, לָמָּה אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים עַד חֲצוֹת, כְּדֵי לְהַרְחִיק אֶת הָאָדָם מִן הָעֲבֵרָה:
phrases.en: If so, why did the Sages say until midnight? In order to distance a person from transgression.

phrases.he: מֵאֵימָתַי קוֹרִין אֶת שְׁמַע בְּשַׁחֲרִית.
phrases.en: From when does one recite Shema in the morning?

phrases.he: מִשֶּׁיַּכִּיר בֵּין תְּכֵלֶת לְלָבָן.
phrases.en: From when a person can distinguish between sky-blue [tekhelet] and white.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, בֵּין תְּכֵלֶת לְכַרְתִּי.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: From when one can distinguish between sky-blue and leek-green.

phrases.he: וְגוֹמְרָהּ עַד הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה.
phrases.en: And one must finish reciting Shema until the end of the period when you rise, i.e., sunrise, when the sun begins to shine.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, עַד שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁעוֹת, שֶׁכֵּן דֶּרֶךְ בְּנֵי מְלָכִים לַעֲמֹד בְּשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁעוֹת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says: One may recite the morning Shema until three hours of the day, which this is still considered when you rise, as that is the habit of kings to rise from their sleep at three hours of the day.

phrases.he: הַקּוֹרֵא מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ לֹא הִפְסִיד, כְּאָדָם הַקּוֹרֵא בַתּוֹרָה:
phrases.en: One who recites Shema from that time onward loses nothing. Although he does not fulfill the mitzva of reciting of Shema at its appointed time, he is nevertheless considered like one who reads the Torah, and is rewarded accordingly.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים,
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say:

phrases.he: בָּעֶרֶב כָּל אָדָם יַטּוּ וְיִקְרְאוּ,
phrases.en: in the evening every person must recline and recite Shema,

phrases.he: וּבַבֹּקֶר יַעַמְדוּ,
phrases.en: and in the morning he must stand and recite Shema,

phrases.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים ו) וּבְשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ.
phrases.en: as it is stated: "When you lie down, and when you rise."

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים,
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say:

phrases.he: כָּל אָדָם קוֹרֵא כְדַרְכּוֹ,
phrases.en: Every person recites Shema as he is,

phrases.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שם) וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ.
phrases.en: as it is stated: "And when you walk along the way."

phrases.he: אִם כֵּן, לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר וּבְשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ,
phrases.en: If so, why was it stated: "When you lie down, and when you rise"?

phrases.he: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁבְּנֵי אָדָם שׁוֹכְבִים, וּבְשָׁעָה שֶׁבְּנֵי אָדָם עוֹמְדִים.
phrases.en: at the time when people lie down and the time when people rise.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן,
phrases.en: Rabbi Tarfon said:

phrases.he: אֲנִי הָיִיתִי בָא בַדֶּרֶךְ,
phrases.en: I was coming on the road

phrases.he: וְהִטֵּיתִי לִקְרוֹת,
phrases.en: and reclined to recite Shema,

phrases.he: כְּדִבְרֵי בֵית שַׁמַּאי,
phrases.en: in accordance with the statement of Beit Shammai.

phrases.he: וְסִכַּנְתִּי בְעַצְמִי מִפְּנֵי הַלִּסְטִים.
phrases.en: I endangered myself due to the highwaymen.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ,
phrases.en: The Sages said to him:

phrases.he: כְּדַי הָיִיתָ לָחוּב בְּעַצְמְךָ, שֶׁעָבַרְתָּ עַל דִּבְרֵי בֵית הִלֵּל:
phrases.en: You deserved to be liable with your life, as you transgressed the statement of Beit Hillel.

phrases.he: בַּשַּׁחַר מְבָרֵךְ שְׁתַּיִם לְפָנֶיהָ וְאַחַת לְאַחֲרֶיהָ,
phrases.en: In the morning one recites two blessings beforehand, and one thereafter,

phrases.he: וּבָעֶרֶב שְׁתַּיִם לְפָנֶיהָ וּשְׁתַּיִם לְאַחֲרֶיהָ.
phrases.en: And in the evening one recites two blessings beforehand, and two thereafter,

phrases.he: אַחַת אֲרֻכָּה וְאַחַת קְצָרָה.
phrases.en: whether one recites it in its long formula and whether one recites it in its short formula,

phrases.he: מָקוֹם שֶׁאָמְרוּ לְהַאֲרִיךְ, אֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי לְקַצֵּר.
phrases.en: Where the Sages said to recite a long blessing, one may not shorten it,

phrases.he: לְקַצֵּר, אֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי לְהַאֲרִיךְ.
phrases.en: wherever they said to recite a short blessing, one may not lengthen it.

phrases.he: לַחְתֹּם, אֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי שֶׁלֹּא לַחְתֹּם.
phrases.en: Where the Sages said that a blessing must conclude with a second blessing at the end, he may not fail to conclude with that blessing.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁלֹּא לַחְתֹּם, אֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי לַחְתֹּם:
phrases.en: Similarly, if the Sages said that a blessing must not conclude with a second blessing, one may not conclude with a blessing.

phrases.he: מַזְכִּירִין יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם בַּלֵּילוֹת.
phrases.en: The exodus from Egypt is mentioned at night

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה, הֲרֵי אֲנִי כְּבֶן שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה, וְלֹא זָכִיתִי שֶׁתֵּאָמֵר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם בַּלֵּילוֹת, עַד שֶׁדְּרָשָׁהּ בֶּן זוֹמָא,
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said: I am approximately seventy years old, and I was never privileged to have the exodus from Egypt mentioned at night, until Ben Zoma interpreted it homiletically

phrases.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים טז) לְמַעַן תִּזְכֹּר אֶת יוֹם צֵאתְךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם כֹּל יְמֵי חַיֶּיךָ.
phrases.en: as it is stated: "That you may remember the day you went out of the land of Egypt all the days of your life"

phrases.he: יְמֵי חַיֶּיךָ, הַיָּמִים.
phrases.en: The days of your life, refers to daytime alone

phrases.he: כֹּל יְמֵי חַיֶּיךָ, הַלֵּילוֹת.
phrases.en: All the days of your life, comes to add nights as well

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, יְמֵי חַיֶּיךָ, הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: The days of your life, refers to the days in this world

phrases.he: כֹּל יְמֵי חַיֶּיךָ, לְהָבִיא לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ:
phrases.en: all is added to include the days of the Messiah

phrases.he: הָיָה קוֹרֵא בַתּוֹרָה, וְהִגִּיעַ זְמַן הַמִּקְרָא, אִם כִּוֵּן לִבּוֹ, יָצָא.
phrases.en: One who was reading the sections of the Torah which comprise Shema, and the time for the recitation of the morning or evening Shema arrived, if he focused his heart, he fulfilled

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, לֹא יָצָא.
בַּפְּרָקִים שׁוֹאֵל מִפְּנֵי הַכָּבוֹד וּמֵשִׁיב, וּבָאֶמְצַע שׁוֹאֵל מִפְּנֵי הַיִּרְאָה וּמֵשִׁיב, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: At the breaks between paragraphs, one may greet due to the respect and one may respond to another's greeting due to respect. And in the middle one may greet due to the fear and one may respond. This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בָּאֶמְצַע שׁוֹאֵל מִפְּנֵי הַיִּרְאָה, וּמֵשִׁיב מִפְּנֵי הַכָּבוֹד, בַּפְּרָקִים שׁוֹאֵל מִפְּנֵי הַכָּבוֹד, וּמֵשִׁיב שָׁלוֹם לְכָל אָדָם:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: In the middle one may greet due to fear and respond due to respect. In the breaks between paragraphs, one may greet due to respect and respond with a greeting to any person

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ הֵן בֵּין הַפְּרָקִים, בֵּין בְּרָכָה רִאשׁוֹנָה לִשְׁנִיָּה, בֵּין שְׁנִיָּה לִשְׁמַע, וּבֵין שְׁמַע לִוְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ, בֵּין וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ לְוַיֹּאמֶר, בֵּין וַיֹּאמֶר לֶאֱמֶת וְיַצִּיב.
phrases.en: these are the breaks between the paragraphs: Between the first blessing and the second, between the second and Shema, between Shema and the second paragraph: If you indeed heed My commandments [VeHaya im Shamoa], between VeHaya im Shamoa and the third paragraph: And the Lord spoke [VaYomer] and between VaYomer and True and Firm [emet veyatziv]

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בֵּין וַיֹּאמֶר לֶאֱמֶת וְיַצִּיב לֹא יַפְסִיק.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda, says: Between VaYomer and emet veyatziv, one may not interrupt

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קָרְחָה, לָמָּה קָדְמָה שְׁמַע לִוְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ, אֶלָּא כְדֵי שֶׁיְּקַבֵּל עָלָיו עֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם תְּחִלָּה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ יְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עֹל מִצְוֹת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa said: Why, did the portion of Shema precede that of VeHaya im Shamoa? So that one will first accept upon himself the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven, and only then accept upon himself the yoke of the mitzvot

phrases.he: וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ לְוַיֹּאמֶר, שֶׁוְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ נוֹהֵג בַּיּוֹם וּבַלַּיְלָה, וַיֹּאמֶר אֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא בַּיּוֹם.
phrases.en: VeHaya im Shamoa precede VaYomer? Because the paragraph of VeHaya im Shamoa is practiced both by day and by night, while VaYomer, is only practiced during the day

phrases.he: הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת שְׁמַע וְלֹא הִשְׁמִיעַ לְאָזְנוֹ, יָצָא.
phrases.en: One who recites Shema and did not recite in a manner audible to his own ear, fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: He did not fulfill his obligation.

phrases.he: קָרָא וְלֹא דִקְדֵּק בְּאוֹתִיּוֹתֶיהָ, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר יָצָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.en: One who recited Shema and was not sufficiently precise in his enunciation of its letters, Rabbi Yosei says: He fulfilled his obligation. Rabbi Yehuda says: He did not fulfill his obligation.

phrases.he: הַקּוֹרֵא לְמַפְרֵעַ, לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.en: One who recited Shema out of order, he did not fulfill his obligation.

phrases.he: קָרָא וְטָעָה, יַחֲזֹר לְמָקוֹם שֶׁטָּעָה.
phrases.en: One who recited and erred, should return to the place that he erred.

phrases.he: הָאֻמָּנִין קוֹרִין בְּרֹאשׁ הָאִילָן אוֹ בְרֹאשׁ הַנִּדְבָּךְ,
phrases.en: Laborers recite Shema while standing atop the tree or atop the course of stones

phrases.he: מַה שֶּׁאֵינָן רַשָּׁאִין לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן בַּתְּפִלָּה:
phrases.en: which they are not permitted to do for the Amida prayer

phrases.he: חָתָן פָּטוּר מִקְּרִיאַת שְׁמַע בַּלַּיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן עַד מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת, אִם לֹא עָשָׂה מַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.en: A groom is exempt from the recitation of Shema on the first night until Saturday night, if he has not taken action

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל שֶׁקָּרָא בַלַּיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנָּשָׂא.
phrases.en: There was an incident where Rabban Gamliel married a woman and recited Shema even the first night.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו, לֹא לִמַּדְתָּנוּ, רַבֵּנוּ, שֶׁחָתָן פָּטוּר מִקְּרִיאַת שְׁמַע בַּלַּיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.en: His students said to him: Didn't our teacher teach us that a groom is exempt from the recitation of Shema?

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, אֵינִי שׁוֹמֵעַ לָכֶם לְבַטֵּל מִמֶּנִּי מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם אֲפִלּוּ שָׁעָה אֶחָת:
phrases.en: He answered them: I am not listening to you to preclude myself from the acceptance of the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven, for even one moment.

phrases.he: רָחַץ לַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁמֵּתָה אִשְׁתּוֹ.
phrases.en: He bathed on the first night after his wife died.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַלְמִידָיו, לֹא לִמַּדְתָּנוּ, רַבֵּנוּ, שֶׁאָבֵל אָסוּר לִרְחֹץ.
phrases.en: His students said to him: Have you not taught us, our teacher, that a mourner is prohibited to bathe?

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, אֵינִי כִשְׁאָר כָּל אָדָם, אִסְטְנִיס אָנִי:
phrases.en: He answered them: I am not like other people, I am delicate.

phrases.he: וּכְשֶׁמֵּת טָבִי עַבְדּוֹ, קִבֵּל עָלָיו תַּנְחוּמִין.
phrases.en: And when his slave, Tavi, died, accepted condolences for his

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו, לֹא לִמַּדְתָּנוּ רַבֵּנוּ, שֶׁאֵין מְקַבְּלִין תַּנְחוּמִין עַל הָעֲבָדִים.
phrases.en: His students said to him: Have you not taught us, our teacher, that one does not accept condolences for the death of slaves?

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, אֵין טָבִי עַבְדִּי כִּשְׁאָר כָּל הָעֲבָדִים, כָּשֵׁר הָיָה:
phrases.en: My slave, Tavi, is not like all the rest of the slaves, he was virtuous

phrases.he: חָתָן אִם רָצָה לִקְרוֹת קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע לַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן, קוֹרֵא.
phrases.en: if a groom wishes to recite Shema on the first night, he may do so

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, לֹא כָל הָרוֹצֶה לִטֹּל אֶת הַשֵּׁם יִטֹּל.
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: Not everyone who wishes to assume the reputation may assume it

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁמֵּתוֹ מוּטָל לְפָנָיו, פָּטוּר מִקְּרִיאַת שְׁמַע, מִן הַתְּפִלָּה וּמִן הַתְּפִלִּין.
phrases.en: One whose deceased relative is laid out before him is exempt from the recitation of Shema, from the Amida prayer, and from phylacteries,

phrases.he: נוֹשְׂאֵי הַמִּטָּה וְחִלּוּפֵיהֶן וְחִלּוּפֵי חִלּוּפֵיהֶן, אֶת שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַמִּטָּה וְאֶת שֶׁלְּאַחַר הַמִּטָּה, אֶת שֶׁלַּמִּטָּה צֹרֶךְ בָּהֶן פְּטוּרִים, וְאֶת שֶׁאֵין לַמִּטָּה צֹרֶךְ בָּהֶן חַיָּבִין.
phrases.en: With regard to the pallbearers and their replacements and the replacements of their replacements, those located before the bier who have not yet carried the deceased and those located after the bier. Those who are needed to carry the bier are exempt from reciting Shema; while those who are not needed to carry the bier, are obligated to recite Shema.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ פְּטוּרִים מִן הַתְּפִלָּה:
phrases.en: However, both these and those are exempt from reciting the Amida prayer,

phrases.he: קָבְרוּ אֶת הַמֵּת וְחָזְרוּ,
phrases.en: they buried the deceased and returned,

phrases.he: אִם יְכוֹלִין לְהַתְחִיל וְלִגְמֹר עַד שֶׁלֹּא יַגִּיעוּ לַשּׁוּרָה, יַתְחִילוּ.
phrases.en: if they have sufficient time to begin to recite Shema and conclude before they arrive at the row, they should begin.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, לֹא יַתְחִילוּ.
phrases.en: If they do not have sufficient time to conclude reciting the entire Shema, then they should not begin.

phrases.he: הָעוֹמְדִים בַּשּׁוּרָה, הַפְּנִימִים פְּטוּרִים, וְהַחִיצוֹנִים חַיָּבִין:
phrases.en: those standing in the row, those in the interior row are exempt from reciting Shema, while those in the exterior row are obligated to recite Shema.

phrases.he: נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים פְּטוּרִין מִקְּרִיאַת שְׁמַע וּמִן הַתְּפִלִּין,
phrases.en: Women, slaves and minors are exempt from the recitation of Shema and from phylacteries,

phrases.he: וְחַיָּבִין בִּתְפִלָּה וּבִמְזוּזָה, וּבְבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן:
phrases.en: but are obligated in prayer, mezuza and Grace after Meals.

phrases.he: בַּעַל קֶרִי מְהַרְהֵר בְּלִבּוֹ וְאֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ, לֹא לְפָנֶיהָ וְלֹא לְאַחֲרֶיהָ.
phrases.en: one is impure due to a seminal emission, he may contemplate in his heart, but neither recites the blessings preceding, nor the blessings following it.

phrases.he: וְעַל הַמָּזוֹן מְבָרֵךְ לְאַחֲרָיו, וְאֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ לְפָנָיו.
phrases.en: Over food one recites a blessing afterward, but one does not recite a blessing beforehand.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מְבָרֵךְ לִפְנֵיהֶם וּלְאַחֲרֵיהֶם:
phrases.en: And Rabbi Yehuda says: He recites a blessing beforehand and thereafter

phrases.he: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בַּתְּפִלָּה, וְנִזְכַּר שֶׁהוּא בַעַל קְרִי,
phrases.en: One who was standing in prayer and he recalled that he experienced a seminal emission,

phrases.he: לֹא יַפְסִיק,
phrases.en: not interrupt his prayer,

phrases.he: אֶלָּא יְקַצֵּר.
phrases.en: rather he should abridge each individual blessing.

phrases.he: יָרַד לִטְבֹּל, אִם יָכוֹל לַעֲלוֹת וּלְהִתְכַּסּוֹת וְלִקְרוֹת עַד שֶׁלֹּא תָנֵץ הַחַמָּה, יַעֲלֶה וְיִתְכַּסֶּה וְיִקְרָא.
phrases.en: One who descended to immerse himself, if he is able to ascend, cover himself with a garment, and recite the morning Shema before sunrise, he should ascend, cover himself, and recite Shema,

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, יִתְכַּסֶּה בַמַּיִם וְיִקְרָא.
phrases.en: and if not, he should cover himself in the water and recite Shema there.

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא יִתְכַּסֶּה, לֹא בַמַּיִם הָרָעִים וְלֹא בְמֵי הַמִּשְׁרָה, עַד שֶׁיַּטִּיל לְתוֹכָן מָיִם.
phrases.en: He may not, however, cover himself in either foul water, or water in which flax was soaked, until he pours other water into it.

phrases.he: וְכַמָּה יַרְחִיק מֵהֶם וּמִן הַצּוֹאָה, אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת:
phrases.en: And how far must one distance himself from urine and feces in order to recite Shema? At least four cubits.

phrases.he: זָב שֶׁרָאָה קְרִי,
phrases.en: a zav, whose impurity lasts at least seven days, who experienced a seminal emission,

phrases.he: וְנִדָּה שֶׁפָּלְטָה שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע,
phrases.en: a menstruating woman who discharged semen,

phrases.he: וְהַמְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת שֶׁרָאֲתָה נִדָּה,
phrases.en: and a woman who engaged in conjugal relations and later saw menstrual blood,

phrases.he: צְרִיכִין טְבִילָה,
phrases.en: require immersion.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה פּוֹטֵר:
phrases.en: And Rabbi Yehuda exempts them from immersion.

phrases.he: תְּפִלַּת הַשַּׁחַר, עַד חֲצוֹת.
phrases.en: the morning prayer may be recited until noon

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, עַד אַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: It may be recited only until four hours after sunrise

phrases.he: תְּפִלַּת הַמִּנְחָה עַד הָעֶרֶב.
phrases.en: the afternoon prayer may be recited until the evening

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, עַד פְּלַג הַמִּנְחָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: It may be recited only until the midpoint of the afternoon [pelag haminḥa]

phrases.he: תְּפִלַּת הָעֶרֶב אֵין לָהּ קֶבַע.
phrases.en: The evening prayer is not fixed to a specific hour

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל מוּסָפִין כָּל הַיּוֹם.
phrases.en: the additional prayer may be recited all day

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, עַד שֶׁבַע שָׁעוֹת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: It may be recited only until seven hours after sunrise

phrases.he: רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה הָיָה מִתְפַּלֵּל בִּכְנִיסָתוֹ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ וּבִיצִיאָתוֹ תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Neḥunya ben Hakana would recite a brief prayer upon his entrance into the study hall and upon his exit.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, מַה מָּקוֹם לִתְפִלָּה זוֹ.
phrases.en: What room is there for this prayer?

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, בִּכְנִיסָתִי אֲנִי מִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁלֹּא תֶאֱרַע תַּקָלָה עַל יָדִי, וּבִיצִיאָתִי אֲנִי נוֹתֵן הוֹדָיָה עַל חֶלְקִי.
phrases.en: He said to them: Upon my entrance, I pray that no mishap will transpire by me, and upon my exit, I give thanks for my portion.

phrases.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, בְּכָל יוֹם מִתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה.
phrases.en: Rabban Gamliel says: Each and every day a person recites the prayer of eighteen blessings.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, מֵעֵין שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says: an abridged version of the prayer of eighteen blessings.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אִם שְׁגוּרָה תְפִלָּתוֹ בְּפִיו, יִתְפַּלֵּל שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: If he is fluent in his prayer, he recites the prayer of eighteen blessings,

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, מֵעֵין שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה.
phrases.en: and if not, an abridged version of the prayer of eighteen blessings.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, הָעוֹשֶׂה תְפִלָּתוֹ קֶבַע, אֵין תְּפִלָּתוֹ תַּחֲנוּנִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: One whose prayer is fixed, his prayer is not supplication

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, הַמְהַלֵּךְ בִּמְקוֹם סַכָּנָה, מִתְפַּלֵּל תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says: One who is walking in a place of danger, recites a brief prayer

phrases.he: אוֹמֵר, הוֹשַׁע הַשֵּׁם אֶת עַמְּךָ אֶת שְׁאֵרִית יִשְׂרָאֵל, בְּכָל פָּרָשַׁת הָעִבּוּר יִהְיוּ צָרְכֵיהֶם לְפָנֶיךָ.
phrases.en: and says: Redeem, Lord, Your people, the remnant of Israel, at every transition [parashat ha'ibur], May their needs be before You.

phrases.he: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה' שׁוֹמֵעַ תְּפִלָּה:
phrases.en: Blessed are You, Lord, Who listens to prayer.

phrases.he: הָיָה רוֹכֵב עַל הַחֲמוֹר, יֵרֵד.
phrases.en: One who was riding on a donkey should dismount and pray

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לֵירֵד, יַחֲזִיר אֶת פָּנָיו,
phrases.en: If he is unable to dismount, he should turn his face

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהַחֲזִיר אֶת פָּנָיו, יְכַוֵּן אֶת לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית קֹדֶשׁ הַקָּדָשִׁים:
phrases.en: If he is unable to turn his face, he focus his heart opposite the Holy of Holies.

phrases.he: הָיָה יוֹשֵׁב בִּסְפִינָה אוֹ בְקָרוֹן אוֹ בְאַסְדָּה,
phrases.en: one who was traveling in a ship or on a wagon or on a raft

phrases.he: יְכַוֵּן אֶת לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית קֹדֶש הַקָּדָשִׁים.
phrases.en: should focus his heart opposite the Holy of Holies.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר, אֵין תְּפִלַּת הַמּוּסָפִין אֶלָּא בְּחֶבֶר עִיר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says: The additional prayer is only recited in a city where there is a quorum of ten [ḥever ir].

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בְּחֶבֶר עִיר וְשֶׁלֹּא בְחֶבֶר עִיר.
phrases.en: The Rabbis say: One may recite the additional prayer with a ḥever ir or without a ḥever ir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשְּׁמוֹ, כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ חֶבֶר עִיר, הַיָּחִיד פָּטוּר מִתְּפִלַּת הַמּוּסָפִין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says another opinion in his name, the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya: Any place where there is a ḥever ir, an individual is completely exempt from reciting the additional prayer.

phrases.he: אֵין עוֹמְדִים לְהִתְפַּלֵּל אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ כֹּבֶד רֹאשׁ.
phrases.en: One may only stand and begin to pray from an approach of gravity and submission.

phrases.he: חֲסִידִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים הָיוּ שׁוֹהִים שָׁעָה אַחַת וּמִתְפַּלְּלִים, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּכַוְּנוּ אֶת לִבָּם לַמָּקוֹם.
phrases.en: the early generations of pious men would wait one hour, and then pray, so that they would focus their hearts toward their Father in Heaven.

phrases.he: אֲפִלּוּ הַמֶּלֶךְ שׁוֹאֵל בִּשְׁלוֹמוֹ, לֹא יְשִׁיבֶנּוּ.
phrases.en: even if the king greets him, he should not respond to him;

phrases.he: וַאֲפִלּוּ נָחָשׁ כָּרוּךְ עַל עֲקֵבוֹ, לֹא יַפְסִיק:
phrases.en: and even if a snake is wrapped on his heel, he should not interrupt

phrases.he: מַזְכִּירִין גְּבוּרוֹת גְּשָׁמִים בִּתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים,
phrases.en: One mentions the might of the rains in the revival of the dead.

phrases.he: וְשׁוֹאֲלִין הַגְּשָׁמִים בְּבִרְכַּת הַשָּׁנִים,
phrases.en: And the request for rain in the blessing of the years.

phrases.he: וְהַבְדָּלָה בְּחוֹנֵן הַדָּעַת.
phrases.en: And the prayer of distinction in Who graciously grants knowledge.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אוֹמְרָהּ בְּרָכָה רְבִיעִית בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: it is recited as an independent fourth blessing.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, בְּהוֹדָאָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says in thanksgiving.

phrases.he: הָאוֹמֵר עַל קַן צִפּוֹר יַגִּיעוּ רַחֲמֶיךָ,
phrases.en: One who recites in his supplication: Just as Your mercy is extended to a bird's nest,

phrases.he: וְעַל טוֹב יִזָּכֵר שְׁמֶךָ,
phrases.en: and one who recites: May Your name be mentioned with the good

phrases.he: מוֹדִים מוֹדִים,
phrases.en: or one who recites: We give thanks, we give thanks twice,

phrases.he: מְשַׁתְּקִין אוֹתוֹ.
phrases.en: they silence him.

phrases.he: הָעוֹבֵר לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה וְטָעָה,
phrases.en: One who is passing before the ark, as prayer leader, and erred,

phrases.he: יַעֲבֹר אַחֵר תַּחְתָּיו,
phrases.en: another should immediately pass in his place,

phrases.he: וְלֹא יְהֵא סָרְבָן בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה.
phrases.en: and at that moment, this replacement should not refuse.

phrases.he: מִנַּיִן הוּא מַתְחִיל,
phrases.en: From where does the replacement commence?

phrases.he: מִתְּחִלַּת הַבְּרָכָה שֶׁטָּעָה בָהּ:
phrases.en: From the beginning of the blessing in which the former had erred.

phrases.he: הָעוֹבֵר לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה, לֹא יַעֲנֶה אַחַר הַכֹּהֲנִים אָמֵן, מִפְּנֵי הַטֵּרוּף.
phrases.en: one who passes before the ark should not respond amen after the priests, because of confusion.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵין שָׁם כֹּהֵן אֶלָּא הוּא, לֹא יִשָּׂא אֶת כַּפָּיו.
phrases.en: If there is no priest other than he, he does not lift his hands.

phrases.he: וְאִם הַבְטָחָתוֹ שֶׁהוּא נוֹשֵׂא אֶת כַּפָּיו וְחוֹזֵר לִתְפִלָּתוֹ, רַשַּׁאי:
phrases.en: And if he is certain that he can lift his hands and resume his prayer, he is permitted.

phrases.he: הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל וְטָעָה, סִימָן רַע לוֹ.
phrases.en: One who prays and erred in his prayer, it is a bad omen for him.

phrases.he: וְאִם שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר הוּא, סִימָן רַע לְשׁוֹלְחָיו, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁשְּׁלוּחוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם כְּמוֹתוֹ.
phrases.en: And if he is the communal prayer leader, it is a bad omen for those who sent him, because a person's agent has legal status equivalent to his own.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶן דּוֹסָא, כְּשֶׁהָיָה מִתְפַּלֵּל עַל הַחוֹלִים וְאוֹמֵר, זֶה חַי וְזֶה מֵת.
phrases.en: They said about Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa that he would pray on behalf of the sick and say: This one shall live and this one shall die.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, מִנַּיִן אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ.
phrases.en: They said to him: From where do you know?

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, אִם שְׁגוּרָה תְפִלָּתִי בְּפִי, יוֹדֵעַ אֲנִי שֶׁהוּא מְקֻבָּל.
phrases.en: He said to them: If my prayer is fluent in my mouth, I know that it is accepted.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, יוֹדֵעַ אֲנִי שֶׁהוּא מְטֹרָף:
phrases.en: And if not, I know that it is rejected.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד מְבָרְכִין עַל הַפֵּרוֹת.
phrases.en: How does one recite a blessing over fruits?

phrases.he: עַל פֵּרוֹת הָאִילָן אוֹמֵר, בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָעֵץ, חוּץ מִן הַיַּיִן, שֶׁעַל הַיַּיִן אוֹמֵר בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הַגָּפֶן.
phrases.en: Over fruits that grow on a tree one recites: Who creates fruit of the tree, with the exception of wine. Over wine one recites: Who creates fruit of the vine.

phrases.he: וְעַל פֵּרוֹת הָאָרֶץ אוֹמֵר בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה, חוּץ מִן הַפַּת, שֶׁעַל הַפַּת הוּא אוֹמֵר הַמּוֹצִיא לֶחֶם מִן הָאָרֶץ.
phrases.en: Over fruits that grow from the earth, one recites: Who creates fruit of the ground, with the exception of bread. As over bread one recites: Who brings forth bread from the earth.

phrases.he: וְעַל הַיְרָקוֹת אוֹמֵר בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה.
phrases.en: Over herbs and leafy vegetables one recites: Who creates fruit of the ground.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בּוֹרֵא מִינֵי דְשָׁאִים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: Who creates various kinds of herbs.

phrases.he: בֵּרַךְ עַל פֵּרוֹת הָאִילָן בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה, יָצָא.
phrases.en: One who recited: Who creates fruit of the ground, over fruit of the tree, fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.he: וְעַל פֵּרוֹת הָאָרֶץ בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָעֵץ, לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.en: One who recited: Who creates fruit of the tree, over fruits of the earth, did not fulfill his obligation.

phrases.he: עַל כֻּלָּם אִם אָמַר שֶׁהַכֹּל נִהְיָה, יָצָא:
phrases.en: And over all food items, one who recited: By whose word all things came to be, fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.he: עַל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין גִּדּוּלוֹ מִן הָאָרֶץ אוֹמֵר שֶׁהַכֹּל.
phrases.en: And over a food item whose growth is not from the ground, one recites: By whose word all things came to be.

phrases.he: עַל הַחֹמֶץ וְעַל הַנּוֹבְלוֹת וְעַל הַגּוֹבַאי אוֹמֵר שֶׁהַכֹּל.
phrases.en: And over vinegar, wine that fermented and spoiled, and over novelot, dates that spoiled, and over locusts, one recites: By whose word all things came to be.

phrases.he: עַל הֶחָלָב וְעַל הַגְּבִינָה וְעַל הַבֵּיצִים אוֹמֵר שֶׁהַכֹּל.
phrases.en: So too, over milk, and over cheese, and over eggs, one recites: By whose word all things came to be.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כָּל שֶׁהוּא מִין קְלָלָה אֵין מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: Over any food item that is a type resulting from a curse, one does not recite a blessing over it at all.

phrases.he: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו מִינִים הַרְבֵּה,
phrases.en: If there were many types of food before him,

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם יֵשׁ בֵּינֵיהֶם מִמִּין שִׁבְעָה, מְבָרֵךְ עָלָיו.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: If there is one of the seven species among them, he recites the first blessing over it.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, מְבָרֵךְ עַל אֵיזֶה מֵהֶם שֶׁיִּרְצֶה:
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: He recites a blessing over whichever of them he wants.

phrases.he: בֵּרַךְ עַל הַיַּיִן שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַמָּזוֹן, פָּטַר אֶת הַיַּיִן שֶׁלְּאַחַר הַמָּזוֹן.
phrases.en: One who recited a blessing over the wine that one drank before the meal, with that blessing he exempted the wine that he drinks after the meal.

phrases.he: בֵּרַךְ עַל הַפַּרְפֶּרֶת שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַמָּזוֹן, פָּטַר אֶת הַפַּרְפֶּרֶת שֶׁלְּאַחַר הַמָּזוֹן.
phrases.en: Similarly, one who recited a blessing over the appetizers that one ate before the meal, with that blessing he exempted the appetizers that he eats after the meal.

phrases.he: בֵּרַךְ עַל הַפַּת, פָּטַר אֶת הַפַּרְפֶּרֶת.
phrases.en: One who recited a blessing over the bread exempted the appetizers, as they are considered secondary to the bread.

phrases.he: עַל הַפַּרְפֶּרֶת, לֹא פָטַר אֶת הַפָּת.
phrases.en: However, one who recited a blessing over the appetizers did not exempt the bread.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אַף לֹא מַעֲשֵׂה קְדֵרָה:
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: The blessing recited over the appetizers did not exempt even a cooked dish that he eats during the meal.

phrases.he: הָיוּ יוֹשְׁבִין לֶאֱכֹל, כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מְבָרֵךְ לְעַצְמוֹ.
phrases.en: were sitting to eat not in the framework of a joint meal, each recites a blessing for himself.

phrases.he: הֵסֵבּוּ, אֶחָד מְבָרֵךְ לְכֻלָּן.
phrases.en: If they were reclined on divans to eat, which renders it a joint meal, one recites a blessing on behalf of them all.

phrases.he: בָּא לָהֶם יַיִן בְּתוֹךְ הַמָּזוֹן, כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מְבָרֵךְ לְעַצְמוֹ.
phrases.en: If wine came before them during the meal, each and every diner recites a blessing over the wine for himself.

phrases.he: לְאַחַר הַמָּזוֹן, אֶחָד מְבָרֵךְ לְכֻלָּם.
phrases.en: If the wine came after the meal, one recites a blessing on behalf of them all.

phrases.he: וְהוּא אוֹמֵר עַל הַמֻּגְמָר, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מְבִיאִין אֶת הַמֻּגְמָר אֶלָּא לְאַחַר הַסְּעֻדָּה.
phrases.en: And he, who recited the blessing over the wine, also says the blessing over the incense [mugmar], although they only bring the incense to the diners after the meal.

phrases.he: הֵבִיאוּ לְפָנָיו מָלִיחַ בַּתְּחִלָּה וּפַת עִמּוֹ, מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַמָּלִיחַ וּפוֹטֵר אֶת הַפַּת, שֶׁהַפַּת טְפֵלָה לוֹ.
phrases.en: they brought salted food before him to eat first and bread with it, he recites a blessing over the salted food and thereby exempts the bread, because the bread is secondary to it.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כֹּל שֶׁהוּא עִקָּר וְעִמּוֹ טְפֵלָה, מְבָרֵךְ עַל הָעִקָּר וּפוֹטֵר אֶת הַטְּפֵלָה:
phrases.en: This is the principle: Any food that is primary and a secondary food is with it, one recites a blessing over the primary and, in so doing, exempts the secondary from its own blessing.

phrases.he: אָכַל תְּאֵנִים עֲנָבִים וְרִמּוֹנִים, מְבָרֵךְ אַחֲרֵיהֶן שָׁלשׁ בְּרָכוֹת,
phrases.en: One who ate grapes and figs and pomegranates, recites the three blessings

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.en: the statement of Rabban Gamliel

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בְּרָכָה אַחַת מֵעֵין שָׁלשׁ.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: One need only recite one blessing abridged from the three blessings

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ אָכַל שֶׁלֶק וְהוּא מְזוֹנוֹ, מְבָרֵךְ אַחֲרָיו שָׁלשׁ בְּרָכוֹת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: even if one ate boiled vegetables, but it is his primary sustenance, he recites the three blessings

phrases.he: הַשּׁוֹתֶה מַיִם לִצְמָאוֹ, אוֹמֵר שֶׁהַכֹּל נִהְיֶה בִּדְבָרוֹ.
phrases.en: One who drinks water to quench his thirst recites: By whose word all things came to be

phrases.he: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר, בּוֹרֵא נְפָשׁוֹת רַבּוֹת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Tarfon says: Who creates the many forms of life and their needs

phrases.he: שְׁלשָׁה שֶׁאָכְלוּ כְאֶחָד, חַיָּבִין לְזַמֵּן.
phrases.en: Three people who ate as one are required to form a zimmun and recite Grace after Meals.

phrases.he: אָכַל דְּמַאי, וּמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּטְּלָה תְרוּמָתוֹ, וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁנִּפְדּוּ, וְהַשַּׁמָּשׁ שֶׁאָכַל כַּזַּיִת, וְהַכּוּתִי, מְזַמְּנִין עֲלֵיהֶם.
phrases.en: If, among the diners, one ate doubtfully tithed produce [demai], and first tithe from which its teruma was already taken, or second tithe, and consecrated food that were redeemed and therefore permitted to be eaten; and even the waiter who served the meal to the diners and who ate at least an olive-bulk from the meal, and the Samaritan [Kuti] who ate with two others at a meal; each of these people is included among the three to obligate those with whom they ate in a zimmun.

phrases.he: אֲבָל אָכַל טֶבֶל, וּמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלֹּא נִטְּלָה תְרוּמָתוֹ, וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא נִפְדּוּ, וְהַשַּׁמָּשׁ שֶׁאָכַל פָּחוֹת מִכַּזַּיִת, וְהַנָּכְרִי, אֵין מְזַמְּנִין עֲלֵיהֶם:
phrases.en: However, one who ate untithed produce [tevel], and first tithe from which its teruma was not separated, and second tithe, and consecrated food that were not redeemed, and the waiter who did not eat an olive-bulk, and the gentile who ate with two Jews, none of these people is included among the three to obligate those with whom they ate in a zimmun.

phrases.he: נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים, אֵין מְזַמְּנִין עֲלֵיהֶם.
phrases.en: Women, slaves, and minors do not obligate those with whom they ate in a zimmun.

phrases.he: עַד כַּמָּה מְזַמְּנִין, עַד כַּזָּיִת.
phrases.en: How much must one eat to obligate those with whom he ate in a zimmun? An olive-bulk of food suffices to obligate those with whom they ate in a zimmun.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, עַד כַּבֵּיצָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: An egg-bulk is the minimum measure to obligate those with whom they ate in a zimmun.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד מְזַמְּנִין, בִּשְׁלשָׁה אוֹמֵר נְבָרֵךְ.
phrases.en: How does one recite the zimmun? In a group of three people, the one reciting the zimmun says: Let us bless

phrases.he: בִּשְׁלשָׁה וְהוּא, אוֹמֵר בָּרְכוּ.
phrases.en: In a group of three people and him, the one reciting the zimmun says: Bless

phrases.he: בַּעֲשָׂרָה, אוֹמֵר נְבָרֵךְ לֵאלֹהֵינוּ.
phrases.en: In a group of ten people, the one reciting the zimmun says: Let us bless our God.

phrases.he: בַּעֲשָׂרָה וָהוּא, אוֹמֵר בָּרְכוּ.
phrases.en: In a group of ten people and him, the one reciting the zimmun says: Bless our God.

phrases.he: אֶחָד עֲשָׂרָה וְאֶחָד עֲשָׂרָה רִבּוֹא.
phrases.en: This formula is recited both in a group of ten and in a group of one hundred thousand.

phrases.he: בְּמֵאָה אוֹמֵר, נְבָרֵךְ לַייָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ.
phrases.en: In a group of one hundred people, the one reciting the zimmun says: Let us bless the Lord our God.

phrases.he: בְּמֵאָה וְהוּא, אוֹמֵר בָּרְכוּ.
phrases.en: In a group of one hundred people and him, the one reciting the zimmun says: Bless the Lord our God.

phrases.he: בְּאֶלֶף, אוֹמֵר נְבָרֵךְ לַייָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.en: In a group of one thousand people, the one reciting the zimmun says: Let us bless the Lord our God, the God of Israel.

phrases.he: בְּאֶלֶף וְהוּא, אוֹמֵר בָּרְכוּ.
phrases.en: In a group of one thousand people and him, he says: Bless the Lord our God, the God of Israel.

phrases.he: בְּרִבּוֹא, אוֹמֵר, נְבָרֵךְ לַייָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֱלֹהֵי הַצְּבָאוֹת יוֹשֵׁב הַכְּרוּבִים עַל הַמָּזוֹן שֶׁאָכָלְנוּ.
phrases.en: In a group of ten thousand people, the one reciting the zimmun says: Let us bless the Lord our God, the God of Israel, the God of Hosts, Who sits upon the cherubs, for the food that we have eaten.

phrases.he: בְּרִבּוֹא וְהוּא, אוֹמֵר בָּרְכוּ.
phrases.en: In a group of ten thousand people and him, the one reciting the zimmun says: Bless the Lord our God, the God of Israel, the God of Hosts, Who sits upon the cherubs, for the food that we have eaten.

phrases.he: כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁהוּא מְבָרֵךְ, כָּךְ עוֹנִין אַחֲרָיו, בָּרוּךְ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֱלֹהֵי הַצְּבָאוֹת יוֹשֵׁב הַכְּרוּבִים עַל הַמָּזוֹן שֶׁאָכָלְנוּ.
phrases.en: just as he recites the blessing, so too those present recite in response: Blessed be the Lord our God, the God of Israel, the God of Hosts, Who sits upon the cherubs, for the food that we have eaten.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר, לְפִי רֹב הַקָּהָל הֵן מְבָרְכִין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּמַקְהֵלוֹת בָּרְכוּ אֱלֹהִים, יְיָ מִמְּקוֹר יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says: According to the size of the crowd, they recite the blessing, as it is stated: "Bless you God in full assemblies, even the Lord, you who are from the fountain of Israel"

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, מַה מָּצִינוּ בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת, אֶחָד מְרֻבִּין וְאֶחָד מֻעָטִין אוֹמֵר, בָּרְכוּ אֶת יְיָ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva said that there are no distinctions based on the size of the crowd: What do we find in the synagogue? Both when there are many and when there are few, as long as there is a quorum of ten, the prayer leader says: Bless [barekhu] the Lord.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, בָּרְכוּ אֶת יְיָ הַמְבֹרָךְ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yishmael said that in the synagogue, one recites: Bless the Lord the blessed One.

phrases.he: שְׁלשָׁה שֶׁאָכְלוּ כְאֶחָד, אֵינָן רַשָּׁאִין לֵחָלֵק,
phrases.en: Three people who ate as one are not permitted to divide

phrases.he: וְכֵן אַרְבָּעָה, וְכֵן חֲמִשָּׁה.
phrases.en: And the same is true of four who ate together, and the same is true of five.

phrases.he: שִׁשָּׁה נֶחֱלָקִין, עַד עֲשָׂרָה.
phrases.en: However, a group of six, up to but not including ten people who ate as one, may divide into two groups, each reciting its own zimmun.

phrases.he: וַעֲשָׂרָה אֵינָן נֶחֱלָקִין, עַד שֶׁיִּהְיוּ עֶשְׂרִים:
phrases.en: And a group of ten may not divide into two groups until there are twenty people present.

phrases.he: שְׁתֵּי חֲבוּרוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹכְלוֹת בְּבַיִת אֶחָד, בִּזְמַן שֶׁמִּקְצָתָן רוֹאִין אֵלּוּ אֶת אֵלּוּ, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מִצְטָרְפִים לְזִמּוּן.
phrases.en: Two groups that were eating in one house, when some members of each group can see each other, they may combine to form a zimmun.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, אֵלּוּ מְזַמְּנִין לְעַצְמָן, וְאֵלּוּ מְזַמְּנִין לְעַצְמָן.
phrases.en: And if not, these recite a zimmun for themselves and those recite a zimmun for themselves.

phrases.he: אֵין מְבָרְכִין עַל הַיַּיִן עַד שֶׁיִּתֵּן לְתוֹכוֹ מַיִם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.en: One does not recite a blessing over wine until he adds water to it, that is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, מְבָרְכִין.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: recites a blessing over it.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ דְבָרִים שֶׁבֵּין בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל בַּסְּעֻדָּה.
phrases.en: These are the matters of dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel with regard to a meal:

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיּוֹם וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיַּיִן.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: one recites a blessing over the sanctification of the day and recites a blessing over the wine thereafter.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיַּיִן וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיּוֹם:
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: One recites a blessing over the wine and recites a blessing over the day thereafter.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, נוֹטְלִין לַיָּדַיִם, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מוֹזְגִין אֶת הַכּוֹס.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One washes his hands and mixes water with the wine in the cup thereafter,

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מוֹזְגִין אֶת הַכּוֹס וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹטְלִין לַיָּדָיִם:
phrases.en: and Beit Hillel say: One mixes water with the wine in the cup and only washes his hands thereafter.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים,
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say:

phrases.he: מְקַנֵּחַ יָדָיו בַּמַּפָּה וּמַנִּיחָהּ עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן.
phrases.en: one dries his hands with a cloth and places it on the table.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים,
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say:

phrases.he: עַל הַכֶּסֶת:
phrases.en: on the cushion

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מְכַבְּדִין אֶת הַבַּיִת וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹטְלִין לַיָּדַיִם.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One sweeps the area of the house where the meal took place and he washes his hands with the final waters before Grace after Meals thereafter.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, נוֹטְלִין לַיָּדַיִם וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְכַבְּדִין אֶת הַבָּיִת:
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: One washes his hands and sweeps the house thereafter.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, נֵר וּמָזוֹן וּבְשָׂמִים וְהַבְדָּלָה.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One recites the blessing over the candle, then the Grace after Meals blessing, then the blessing over the spices, and finally the blessing of havdala.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, נֵר וּבְשָׂמִים וּמָזוֹן וְהַבְדָּלָה.
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: The order is candle, spices, Grace after Meals, and havdala.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, שֶׁבָּרָא מְאוֹר הָאֵשׁ.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: Who created [bara] the light of fire.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, בּוֹרֵא מְאוֹרֵי הָאֵשׁ:
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: Who creates [boreh] the lights of fire.

phrases.he: אֵין מְבָרְכִין לֹא עַל הַנֵּר וְלֹא עַל הַבְּשָׂמִים שֶׁל עוֹבְדֵי כוֹכָבִים, וְלֹא עַל הַנֵּר וְלֹא עַל הַבְּשָׂמִים שֶׁל מֵתִים, וְלֹא עַל הַנֵּר וְלֹא עַל הַבְּשָׂמִים שֶׁלִּפְנֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.en: One may neither recite a blessing over the candle nor over the spices of gentiles, nor over the candle nor the spices designated to pay respects to the dead, nor over the candle nor the spices of idolatry.

phrases.he: אֵין מְבָרְכִין עַל הַנֵּר עַד שֶׁיֵּאוֹתוּ לְאוֹרוֹ:
phrases.en: And one does not recite the blessing over the candle until he derives benefit from its light.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁאָכַל וְשָׁכַח וְלֹא בֵרַךְ,
phrases.en: One who ate and forgot and did not recite a blessing;

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, יַחֲזֹר לִמְקוֹמוֹ וִיבָרֵךְ.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: He returns to the place where he ate and recites the blessing.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, יְבָרֵךְ בַּמָּקוֹם שֶׁנִּזְכָּר.
phrases.en: Beit Hillel say: He recites the blessing at the place where he remembered.

phrases.he: עַד אֵימָתַי הוּא מְבָרֵךְ.
phrases.en: And until when does he recite the blessing?

phrases.he: עַד כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְעַכֵּל הַמָּזוֹן שֶׁבְּמֵעָיו:
phrases.en: Until the food is digested in his intestines.

phrases.he: בָּא לָהֶם יַיִן לְאַחַר הַמָּזוֹן וְאֵין שָׁם אֶלָּא אוֹתוֹ הַכּוֹס,
phrases.en: Wine came before the diners after the meal; if only that cup of wine is there,

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיַּיִן וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַמָּזוֹן.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One recites a blessing over the wine and recites a blessing over the food, Grace after Meals, thereafter.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַמָּזוֹן וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיָּיִן.
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: One recites a blessing over the food and recites a blessing over the wine thereafter.

phrases.he: עוֹנִין אָמֵן אַחַר יִשְׂרָאֵל הַמְבָרֵךְ,
phrases.en: And one answers amen after a Jew who recites a blessing

phrases.he: וְאֵין עוֹנִין אָמֵן אַחַר הַכּוּתִי הַמְבָרֵךְ, עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע כָּל הַבְּרָכָה:
phrases.en: and one does not answer amen after a Samaritan who recites a blessing until he hears the whole blessing in its entirety,

phrases.he: הָרוֹאֶה מָקוֹם שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ בוֹ נִסִּים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, אוֹמֵר בָּרוּךְ שֶׁעָשָׂה נִסִּים לַאֲבוֹתֵינוּ בַּמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה.
phrases.en: One who sees a place where miracles occurred on Israel's behalf recites: Blessed…Who performed miracles for our forefathers in this place.

phrases.he: מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּעֶקְרָה מִמֶּנּוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, אוֹמֵר בָּרוּךְ שֶׁעָקַר עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מֵאַרְצֵנוּ:
phrases.en: One who sees a place from which idolatry was eradicated recites: Blessed…Who eradicated idolatry from our land.

phrases.he: עַל הַזִּיקִין, וְעַל הַזְּוָעוֹת, וְעַל הַבְּרָקִים, וְעַל הָרְעָמִים, וְעַל הָרוּחוֹת, אוֹמֵר בָּרוּךְ שֶׁכֹּחוֹ וּגְבוּרָתוֹ מָלֵא עוֹלָם.
phrases.en: For zikin and zeva'ot, for lightning, thunder, and winds, one recites: Blessed…Whose strength and power fill the world.

phrases.he: עַל הֶהָרִים, וְעַל הַגְּבָעוֹת, וְעַל הַיַּמִּים, וְעַל הַנְּהָרוֹת, וְעַל הַמִּדְבָּרוֹת, אוֹמֵר בָּרוּךְ עוֹשֵׂה מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית.
phrases.en: For mountains, hills, seas, rivers, and deserts, one recites: Blessed…Author of creation.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הָרוֹאֶה אֶת הַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל אוֹמֵר בָּרוּךְ שֶׁעָשָׂה אֶת הַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל, בִּזְמַן שֶׁרוֹאֶה אוֹתוֹ לִפְרָקִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: One who sees the great sea recites Blessed…Who made the great sea. When he sees it intermittently.

phrases.he: עַל הַגְּשָׁמִים וְעַל הַבְּשׂוֹרוֹת הַטּוֹבוֹת אוֹמֵר בָּרוּךְ הַטּוֹב וְהַמֵּטִיב, וְעַל שְׁמוּעוֹת רָעוֹת אוֹמֵר בָּרוּךְ דַּיַּן הָאֱמֶת:
phrases.en: For rain and good tidings, one recites Blessed…Who is good and Who does good. For bad tidings, one recites Blessed…the true Judge.

phrases.he: בָּנָה בַיִת חָדָשׁ, וְקָנָה כֵלִים חֲדָשִׁים, אוֹמֵר בָּרוּךְ שֶׁהֶחֱיָנוּ.
phrases.en: one built a new house or purchased new vessels, he recites: Blessed…Who has given us life, sustained us, and brought us to this time.

phrases.he: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הָרָעָה מֵעֵין הַטּוֹבָה, וְעַל הַטּוֹבָה מֵעֵין הָרָעָה.
phrases.en: One recites a blessing for the bad just as he does for the good. Similarly, one must recite a blessing for the good just as for the bad.

phrases.he: הַצּוֹעֵק לְשֶׁעָבַר, הֲרֵי זוֹ תְּפִלַּת שָׁוְא.
phrases.en: And one who cries out over the past it is a vain prayer.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד.
הָיְתָה אִשְׁתּוֹ מְעֻבֶּרֶת, וְאָמַר, יְהִי רָצוֹן שֶׁתֵּלֵד אִשְׁתִּי זָכָר, הֲרֵי זוֹ תְּפִלַּת שָׁוְא.
phrases.en: one whose wife was pregnant and he says: May it be God's will that my wife will give birth to a male child, it is a vain prayer.

phrases.he: הָיָה בָא בַדֶּרֶךְ וְשָׁמַע קוֹל צְוָחָה בָּעִיר, וְאָמַר יְהִי רָצוֹן שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ אֵלּוּ בְּנֵי בֵיתִי, הֲרֵי זוֹ תְּפִלַּת שָׁוְא.
phrases.en: one who was walking on the path home and he heard the sound of a scream in the city, and he says: May it be God's will that this scream will not be from my house, it is a vain prayer.

phrases.he: הַנִּכְנָס לִכְרַךְ מִתְפַּלֵּל שְׁתַּיִם, אַחַת בִּכְנִיסָתוֹ וְאַחַת בִּיצִיאָתוֹ.
phrases.en: One who enters a large city recites two prayers: One upon his entrance, and one upon his exit.

phrases.he: בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר, אַרְבַּע, שְׁתַּיִם בִּכְנִיסָתוֹ וּשְׁתַּיִם בִּיצִיאָתוֹ, וְנוֹתֵן הוֹדָאָה לְשֶׁעָבַר, וְצוֹעֵק לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא.
phrases.en: Ben Azzai says: He recites four prayers, two upon his entrance and two upon his exit. He gives thanks for the past and cries out in prayer for the future.

phrases.he: חַיָּב אָדָם לְבָרֵךְ עַל הָרָעָה כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהוּא מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַטּוֹבָה,
phrases.en: One is obligated to recite a blessing for the bad that befalls him just as he recites a blessing for the good that befalls him,

phrases.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים ו) וְאָהַבְתָּ אֵת יְיָ אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ וּבְכָל נַפְשְׁךָ וּבְכָל מְאֹדֶךָ.
phrases.en: as it is stated: "And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might" (Deuteronomy 6:5).

phrases.he: בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ, בִּשְׁנֵי יְצָרֶיךָ, בְּיֵצֶר טוֹב וּבְיֵצֶר רָע.
phrases.en: "With all your heart" means with your two inclinations, with your good inclination and your evil inclination,

phrases.he: וּבְכָל נַפְשְׁךָ, אֲפִלּוּ הוּא נוֹטֵל אֶת נַפְשֶׁךָ.
phrases.en: "With all your soul" means even if God takes your soul.

phrases.he: וּבְכָל מְאֹדֶךָ, בְּכָל מָמוֹנֶךָ.
phrases.en: "And with all your might" means with all your money,

phrases.he: דָּבָר אַחֵר בְּכָל מְאֹדֶךָ, בְּכָל מִדָּה וּמִדָּה שֶׁהוּא מוֹדֵד לְךָ הֱוֵי מוֹדֶה לוֹ בִּמְאֹד מְאֹד.
phrases.en: Alternatively, with all your might means with every measure that He metes out to you; thank Him.

phrases.he: לֹא יָקֵל אָדָם אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ כְּנֶגֶד שַׁעַר הַמִּזְרָח, שֶׁהוּא מְכֻוָּן כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית קָדְשֵׁי הַקָּדָשִׁים.
phrases.en: One may not act irreverently opposite the eastern gate of the Temple Mount, which is aligned opposite the Holy of Holies.

phrases.he: לֹא יִכָּנֵס לְהַר הַבַּיִת בְּמַקְלוֹ, וּבְמִנְעָלוֹ, וּבְפֻנְדָּתוֹ, וּבְאָבָק שֶׁעַל רַגְלָיו,
phrases.en: One may not enter the Temple Mount with his staff, his shoes, his money belt [punda], or the dust on his feet.

phrases.he: וְלֹא יַעֲשֶׂנּוּ קַפַּנְדַּרְיָא, וּרְקִיקָה מִקַּל וָחֹמֶר.
phrases.en: One may not make the Temple a shortcut to pass through it, and through an a fortiori inference, all the more so one may not spit on the Temple Mount.

phrases.he: כָּל חוֹתְמֵי בְרָכוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ בַמִּקְדָּשׁ, הָיוּ אוֹמְרִים מִן הָעוֹלָם.
phrases.en: At the conclusion of all blessings recited in the Temple, those reciting the blessing would say: Blessed are You Lord, God of Israel, until everlasting [haolam], the world.

phrases.he: מִשֶּׁקִּלְקְלוּ הַמִּינִין, וְאָמְרוּ, אֵין עוֹלָם אֶלָּא אֶחָד, הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהוּ אוֹמְרִים, מִן הָעוֹלָם וְעַד הָעוֹלָם.
phrases.en: But when the Sadducees strayed and declared that there is but one world and there is no World-to-Come, the Sages instituted that at the conclusion of the blessing one recites: From everlasting [haolam] to everlasting [haolam].

phrases.he: וְהִתְקִינוּ, שֶׁיְּהֵא אָדָם שׁוֹאֵל אֶת שְׁלוֹם חֲבֵרוֹ בַּשֵּׁם,
phrases.en: The Sages also instituted that one should greet another in the name of God, i.e., one should mention God's name in his greeting,

phrases.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (רות ב) וְהִנֵּה בֹעַז בָּא מִבֵּית לֶחֶם, וַיֹּאמֶר לַקּוֹצְרִים יְיָ עִמָּכֶם, וַיֹּאמְרוּ לוֹ, יְבָרֶכְךָ יְיָ.
phrases.en: as it is stated: "And presently Boaz came from Bethlehem and said to the harvesters, The Lord is with you, and they said to him, May the Lord bless you" (Ruth 2:4).

phrases.he: וְאוֹמֵר (שופטים ו) יְיָ עִמְּךָ גִּבּוֹר הֶחָיִל.
phrases.en: And it says: "and said to him, God is with you, mighty man of valor" (Judges 6:12).

phrases.he: וְאוֹמֵר (משלי כג) אַל תָּבוּז כִּי זָקְנָה אִמֶּךָ.
phrases.en: And it says: "And despise not your mother when she is old" (Proverbs 23:22),

phrases.he: וְאוֹמֵר (תהלים קיט) עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַייָ הֵפֵרוּ תוֹרָתֶךָ.
phrases.en: And lest you say that mentioning God's name is prohibited, it says: "It is time to work for the Lord; they have made void Your Torah" (Psalms 119:126),

phrases.he: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר, הֵפֵרוּ תוֹרָתֶךָ עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַייָ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Natan says another interpretation of the verse: "Make void Your Torah" because "it is the time to work for the Lord,"

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ דְבָרִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שִׁעוּר.
phrases.en: These are the things that have no definite quantity: The corners [of the field].

phrases.he: הַפֵּאָה, וְהַבִּכּוּרִים, וְהָרֵאָיוֹן, וּגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים, וְתַלְמוּד תּוֹרָה.
phrases.en: First-fruits; [The offerings brought] on appearing [at the Temple on the three pilgrimage festivals].

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ דְבָרִים שֶׁאָדָם אוֹכֵל פֵּרוֹתֵיהֶן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְהַקֶּרֶן קַיֶּמֶת לוֹ לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.en: The performance of righteous deeds; And the study of the torah.

phrases.he: כִּבּוּד אָב וָאֵם, וּגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים, וַהֲבָאַת שָׁלוֹם בֵּין אָדָם לַחֲבֵרוֹ, וְתַלְמוּד תּוֹרָה כְּנֶגֶד כֻּלָּם
phrases.en: The following are the things for which a man enjoys the fruits in this world while the principal remains for him in the world to come: Honoring one’s father and mother; The performance of righteous deeds; And the making of peace between a person and his friend; And the study of the torah is equal to them all.

phrases.he: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין לַפֵּאָה מִשִּׁשִּׁים, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ אֵין לַפֵּאָה שִׁעוּר.
phrases.en: They should not leave peah of less than one-sixtieth [of the field].

phrases.he: הַכֹּל לְפִי גֹדֶל הַשָּׂדֶה, וּלְפִי רֹב הָעֲנִיִּים, וּלְפִי רֹב הָעֲנָוָה
phrases.en: But even though they said, “there is no measure for peah,” everything depends upon the size of the field, the number of poor people, and the extent of the yield.

phrases.he: נוֹתְנִין פֵּאָה מִתְּחִלַּת הַשָּׂדֶה וּמֵאֶמְצָעָהּ.
phrases.en: They may give peah at either at the beginning of the [reaping of the] field or at the middle of it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיִּתֵּן בַּסּוֹף כַּשִּׁעוּר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: as long as he gives at the end according to the set amount.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם שִׁיֵּר קֶלַח אֶחָד, סוֹמֵךְ לוֹ מִשּׁוּם פֵּאָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: if he leaves one stalk, he can rely on this as [fulfilling the law of] peah; and if he did not, then he only gives as ownerless property.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, אֵינוֹ נוֹתֵן אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם הֶפְקֵר
כְּלָל אָמְרוּ בַּפֵּאָה. כָּל שֶׁהוּא אֹכֶל, וְנִשְׁמָר, וְגִדּוּלָיו מִן הָאָרֶץ, וּלְקִיטָתוֹ כְאַחַת, וּמַכְנִיסוֹ לְקִיּוּם, חַיָּב בַּפֵּאָה.
phrases.en: They said a general principle concerning peah: whatever is food, and is looked after, and grows from the land, and is harvested all at the same time, and is brought in for storage, is subject to the law of pe'ah.

phrases.he: וְהַתְּבוּאָה וְהַקִּטְנִיּוֹת בַּכְּלָל הַזֶּה
phrases.en: Grain and beans are in this category.

phrases.he: וּבָאִילָן, הָאוֹג וְהֶחָרוּבִין וְהָאֱגוֹזִים וְהַשְּׁקֵדִים וְהַגְּפָנִים וְהָרִמּוֹנִים וְהַזֵּיתִים וְהַתְּמָרִים, חַיָּבִין בַּפֵּאָה:
phrases.en: Among trees: the sumac, the carob, the nut, the almond, the grapevine, the pomegranate, the olive and the palm are subject to peah.

phrases.he: לְעוֹלָם הוּא נוֹתֵן מִשּׁוּם פֵּאָה וּפָטוּר מִן הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, עַד שֶׁיְּמָרֵחַ.
phrases.en: He may always give peah and be exempt from giving tithes until he makes a stack.

phrases.he: וְנוֹתֵן מִשּׁוּם הֶפְקֵר וּפָטוּר מִן הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, עַד שֶׁיְּמָרֵחַ.
phrases.en: One who gives [to the poor] as ownerless [produce] and be exempt from giving tithes until he makes a stack.

phrases.he: וּמַאֲכִיל לַבְּהֵמָה וְלַחַיָּה וְלָעוֹפוֹת וּפָטוּר מִן הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, עַד שֶׁיְּמָרֵחַ.
phrases.en: He may feed cattle, wild animals and birds and be exempt from giving tithes until he makes a stack.

phrases.he: וְנוֹטֵל מִן הַגֹּרֶן וְזוֹרֵעַ וּפָטוּר מִן הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, עַד שֶׁיְּמָרֵחַ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.en: He may take from the threshing floor and use it as seed and be exempt from giving tithes until he makes a stack, the words of Rabbi Akiva.

phrases.he: כֹּהֵן וְלֵוִי שֶׁלָּקְחוּ אֶת הַגֹּרֶן, הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם, עַד שֶׁיְּמָרֵחַ.
phrases.en: A priest or Levite who purchase [grain of] a threshing floor, the tithes are theirs unless [the owner] has already made a stack.

phrases.he: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ וּפוֹדֶה, חַיָּב בְּמַעַשְׂרוֹת, עַד שֶׁיְּמָרֵחַ הַגִּזְבָּר
phrases.en: One who dedicated [his crop] and redeems it [afterwards] is obligated to give tithes until the Temple treasurer has made a stack.

phrases.he: וְאֵלּוּ מַפְסִיקִין לַפֵּאָה. הַנַּחַל, וְהַשְּׁלוּלִית, וְדֶרֶךְ הַיָּחִיד, וְדֶרֶךְ הָרַבִּים, וּשְׁבִיל הָרַבִּים, וּשְׁבִיל הַיָּחִיד הַקָּבוּעַ בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה וּבִימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים, וְהַבּוּר, וְהַנִּיר, וְזֶרַע אַחֵר.
phrases.en: The following divide a field for peah: a stream, a pool, a private road, a public road, a public path, a private path in constant use in summer and the rainy season, fallow land, a plowed field and a different seed.

phrases.he: וְהַקּוֹצֵר לְשַׁחַת מַפְסִיק, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: One who harvested for animal fodder, [the plot] serves divides, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵינוֹ מַפְסִיק, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן חָרָשׁ:
phrases.en: But the sages say: it does not stop for peah unless it is plowed.

phrases.he: אַמַּת הַמַּיִם שֶׁאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לְהִקָּצֵר כְּאַחַת,
phrases.en: A water channel that makes harvesting [on one side] impossible [while standing on the other side], Rabbi Judah says: it divides.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מַפְסֶקֶת.
phrases.en: But all of the hills that can be tilled with a hoe, even though cattle cannot pass over it in with their equipment, [is regarded as part of the field] he gives one peah from it all.

phrases.he: וְכֹל הֶהָרִים אֲשֶׁר בַּמַּעְדֵּר יֵעָדֵרוּן, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין הַבָּקָר יָכוֹל לַעֲבֹר בְּכֵלָיו, הוּא נוֹתֵן פֵּאָה לַכֹּל
הַכֹּל מַפְסִיק לַזְּרָעִים, וְאֵינוֹ מַפְסִיק לָאִילָן אֶלָּא גָדֵר.
phrases.en: All of these divide in the case of a field [planted] with seeds, but in the case of trees nothing divides except a fence.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיָה שֵׂעָר כּוֹתֵשׁ, אֵינוֹ מַפְסִיק, אֶלָּא נוֹתֵן פֵּאָה לַכֹּל
phrases.en: Should the branches intertwine [on top of the fence], then it does not divide and he gives one peah for the whole field.

phrases.he: וְלֶחָרוּבִין, כָּל הָרוֹאִין זֶה אֶת זֶה.
phrases.en: As for carob trees, [they are not divided] as long as they see one another.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, נוֹהֲגִין הָיוּ בֵּית אַבָּא, נוֹתְנִין פֵּאָה אַחַת לַזֵּיתִים שֶׁהָיוּ לָהֶם בְּכָל רוּחַ, וְלֶחָרוּבִין, כָּל הָרוֹאִין זֶה אֶת זֶה.
phrases.en: Rabban Gamaliel said: we had this custom in the house of my father. We would give separate peah from the olive trees in each direction and [one peah] for all the carob trees that saw one another.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר מִשְּׁמוֹ, אַף לֶחָרוּבִין שֶׁהָיוּ לָהֶם בְּכָל הָעִיר
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar bar Zadok said in his name: also for the carob trees they had in the whole city [they only gave one peah].

phrases.he: הַזּוֹרֵעַ אֶת שָׂדֵהוּ מִין אֶחָד, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֵׂהוּ שְׁתֵּי גְרָנוֹת, נוֹתֵן פֵּאָה אַחַת.
phrases.en: He who plants his field with one kind of seed, even though he makes up of it two threshing-floors, he gives only one peah [for the lot].

phrases.he: זְרָעָהּ שְׁנֵי מִינִין, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעֲשָׂאָן גֹּרֶן אַחַת, נוֹתֵן שְׁתֵּי פֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: If he plants it of two kinds, even though he makes up of it one threshing-floor, he must give two peahs.

phrases.he: הַזּוֹרֵעַ אֶת שָׂדֵהוּ שְׁנֵי מִינֵי חִטִּין, עֲשָׂאָן גֹּרֶן אַחַת, נוֹתֵן פֵּאָה אַחַת.
phrases.en: One who plants his field with two species of wheat: If he makes up of it one threshing-floor, he gives only one peah; But if two threshing-floors, he gives two peahs.

phrases.he: שְׁתֵּי גְרָנוֹת, נוֹתֵן שְׁתֵּי פֵאוֹת
מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁזָּרַע רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אִישׁ הַמִּצְפָּה לִפְנֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, וְעָלוּ לְלִשְׁכַּת הַגָּזִית וְשָׁאָלוּ.
phrases.en: It happened that Rabbi Shimon of Mitzpah planted his field [with two different kinds] and came before Rabban Gamaliel. They both went up to the Chamber of Hewn Stone and asked [about the law].

phrases.he: אָמַר נַחוּם הַלַּבְלָר, מְקֻבָּל אֲנִי מֵרַבִּי מְיָאשָׁא, שֶׁקִּבֵּל מֵאַבָּא, שֶׁקִּבֵּל מִן הַזּוּגוֹת, שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ מִן הַנְּבִיאִים, הֲלָכָה לְמשֶׁה מִסִּינַי, בְּזוֹרֵעַ אֶת שָׂדֵהוּ שְׁנֵי מִינֵי חִטִּין, אִם עֲשָׂאָן גֹּרֶן אַחַת, נוֹתֵן פֵּאָה אַחַת.
phrases.en: Nahum the scribe said: I have a tradition from Rabbi Meyasha, who received it from Abba, who received it from the pairs [of sages], who received it from the prophets, a halakhah of Moses from Sinai, that one who plants his field with two species of wheat, if he makes up of it one threshing-floor, he gives only one peah, but if two threshing-floors, he gives two peahs.

phrases.he: שְׁתֵּי גְרָנוֹת, נוֹתֵן שְׁתֵּי פֵאוֹת
שָׂדֶה שֶׁקְּצָרוּהָ כּוּתִים, קְצָרוּהָ לִסְטִים, קִרְסְמוּהָ נְמָלִים, שְׁבָרַתָּהּ הָרוּחַ אוֹ בְהֵמָה, פְּטוּרָה.
phrases.en: A field harvested by gentiles, or harvested by robbers, or which ants have bitten [the stalks at the roots], or which wind and cattle have broken down, is exempt from peah.

phrases.he: קָצַר חֶצְיָהּ וְקָצְרוּ לִסְטִים חֶצְיָהּ, פְּטוּרָה, שֶׁחוֹבַת הַפֵּאָה בַּקָּמָה
phrases.en: If [the owner] harvested half of it and robbers harvested half, it is exempt from peah, for the obligation of peah is in the standing grain.

phrases.he: קְצָרוּהָ לִסְטִים חֶצְיָהּ וְקָצַר הוּא חֶצְיָהּ, נוֹתֵן פֵּאָה מִמַּה שֶּׁקָּצָר.
phrases.en: If robbers harvested half and the owner the other half, he gives peah from what he has harvested.

phrases.he: קָצַר חֶצְיָהּ וּמָכַר חֶצְיָהּ, הַלּוֹקֵחַ נוֹתֵן פֵּאָה לַכֹּל.
phrases.en: If he harvested half and sold the other half, then the purchaser must give peah for the whole.

phrases.he: קָצַר חֶצְיָהּ וְהִקְדִּישׁ חֶצְיָהּ, הַפּוֹדֶה מִיַּד הַגִּזְבָּר, הוּא נוֹתֵן פֵּאָה לַכֹּל
phrases.en: If he harvested half and dedicated the other half, then he who redeems it from the Temple treasurer must give peah for the whole.

phrases.he: מַלְבְּנוֹת הַתְּבוּאָה שֶׁבֵּין הַזֵּיתִים,
phrases.en: Plots of grain between olive trees: Bet Shammai say: peah from each and every plot.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, פֵּאָה מִכָּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel says: one peah for them all.

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מֵאֶחָד עַל הַכֹּל.
phrases.en: And they agree that if the ends of the rows enter one into the other, he gives one peah for them all.

phrases.he: וּמוֹדִים, שֶׁאִם הָיוּ רָאשֵׁי שׁוּרוֹת מְעֹרָבִין, שֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן פֵּאָה מֵאֶחָד עַל הַכֹּל
הַמְנַמֵּר אֶת שָׂדֵהוּ וְשִׁיֵּר קְלָחִים לַחִים,
phrases.en: One who gives his field a striped appearance and leaves behind moist stalks: Rabbi Akiva says: he gives peah from each and every stripe.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, נוֹתֵן פֵּאָה מִכָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
phrases.en: But the sages say: from one stripe for the whole field.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, מֵאֶחָד עַל הַכֹּל.
phrases.en: The sages agree with Rabbi Akiba that one who sows dill or mustard in three places must give peah from each place.

phrases.he: וּמוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּזוֹרֵעַ שֶׁבֶת אוֹ חַרְדָּל בִּשְׁלשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת, שֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן פֵּאָה מִכָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד
הַמַּחֲלִיק בְּצָלִים לַחִים לַשּׁוּק וּמְקַיֵּם יְבֵשִׁים לַגֹּרֶן, נוֹתֵן פֵּאָה לָאֵלּוּ לְעַצְמָן וְלָאֵלּוּ לְעַצְמָן.
phrases.en: One who clears [his field] of fresh onions for the market and leaves the dry ones [in the ground] for the [time of the] threshing floor, must give peah from these on their own and these on their own. The same applies to beans and to a vineyard.

phrases.he: וְכֵן בַּאֲפוּנִין, וְכֵן בַּכֶּרֶם.
phrases.en: If he, however, he only thins it out, then he gives [peah] from the remainder according to the quantity of that which he left.

phrases.he: הַמֵּדֵל, נוֹתֵן מִן הַמְשֹׁאָר עַל מַה שֶּׁשִּׁיֵּר.
phrases.en: But if he clears [three from one place] at one time, he gives from the remainder according to the entire quantity.

phrases.he: וְהַמַּחֲלִיק מֵאַחַת יָד, נוֹתֵן מִן הַמְשֹׁאָר עַל הַכֹּל
הָאִמָּהוֹת שֶׁל בְּצָלִים חַיָּבוֹת בְּפֵאָה, וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי פּוֹטֵר.
phrases.en: Onions grown for their seed are liable for peah.

phrases.he: מַלְבְּנוֹת הַבְּצָלִים שֶׁבֵּין הַיָּרָק,
phrases.en: But Rabbi Yose exempts them.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, פֵּאָה מִכָּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת.
phrases.en: Plots of onions [growing] between vegetables: Rabbi Yose says: peah must be given from each [plot].

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, מֵאַחַת עַל הַכֹּל:
phrases.en: But the sages say: from one [plot] for all.

phrases.he: הָאַחִין שֶׁחָלְקוּ, נוֹתְנִין שְׁתֵּי פֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: [Two] brothers who divided [an inheritance] must give [two] peahs.

phrases.he: חָזְרוּ וְנִשְׁתַּתְּפוּ, נוֹתְנִין פֵּאָה אַחַת.
phrases.en: If they afterwards again become partners they give one peah.

phrases.he: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁלָּקְחוּ אֶת הָאִילָן, נוֹתְנִין פֵּאָה אַחַת.
phrases.en: Two who purchase a tree, they give one peah.

phrases.he: לָקַח זֶה צְפוֹנוֹ וְזֶה דְרוֹמוֹ, זֶה נוֹתֵן פֵּאָה לְעַצְמוֹ, וְזֶה נוֹתֵן פֵּאָה לְעַצְמוֹ.
phrases.en: If one buys the northern section [of the tree] and the other the southern section, each must give peah separately.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹכֵר קִלְחֵי אִילָן בְּתוֹךְ שָׂדֵהוּ, נוֹתֵן פֵּאָה מִכָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
phrases.en: One who sells young saplings in his field, [the one who purchases] must give peah from each sapling.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁלֹּא שִׁיֵּר בַּעַל הַשָּׂדֶה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah said: When is this so? When the owner of the field left nothing [for himself].

phrases.he: אֲבָל אִם שִׁיֵּר בַּעַל הַשָּׂדֶה, הוּא נוֹתֵן פֵּאָה לַכֹּל
phrases.en: But if he did leave something [for himself], he gives one peah for the whole.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, קַרְקַע בֵּית רֹבַע, חַיֶּבֶת בַּפֵּאָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: a piece of ground [large enough to plant] one fourth of a kav is liable for peah.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, הָעוֹשָׂה סָאתַיִם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua says: it must [be large enough] to grow two seahs.

phrases.he: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר, שִׁשָּׁה עַל שִׁשָּׁה טְפָחִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Tarfon says: it must be six by six handbreadths. R.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶן בְּתֵירָה אוֹמֵר, כְּדֵי לִקְצֹר וְלִשְׁנוֹת. וַהֲלָכָה כִּדְבָרָיו.
phrases.en: Judah ben Batera says: [it must be large enough] for a sickle to cut at least two handfuls and the halakhah is according to his words.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, קַרְקַע כָּל שֶׁהוּא, חַיֶּבֶת בַּפֵּאָה, וּבַבִּכּוּרִים, וְלִכְתֹּב עָלָיו פְּרוֹזְבּוּל, וְלִקְנוֹת עִמּוֹ נְכָסִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אַחֲרָיוּת בְּכֶסֶף וּבִשְׁטָר וּבַחֲזָקָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: any size of land is liable for peah and for first-fruits, and [is sufficient] for the writing of the prozbul, and also to acquire through it movable property by money, by deed, or by a claim based on undisturbed possession.

phrases.he: הַכּוֹתֵב נְכָסָיו שְׁכִיב מְרַע, שִׁיֵּר קַרְקַע כָּל שֶׁהוּא, מַתְּנָתוֹ מַתָּנָה.
phrases.en: One who is about to die who assigns his property in writing [to another]: If he retains any land [for himself] however small, he renders his gift valid.

phrases.he: לֹא שִׁיֵּר קַרְקַע כָּל שֶׁהוּא, אֵין מַתְּנָתוֹ מַתָּנָה.
phrases.en: But if he retains no land whatsoever, his gift is not valid.

phrases.he: הַכּוֹתֵב נְכָסָיו לְבָנָיו, וְכָתַב לְאִשְׁתּוֹ קַרְקַע כָּל שֶׁהוּא, אִבְּדָה כְתֻבָּתָהּ.
phrases.en: One who assigns in writing his property to his children, and he assigns to his wife in writing any plot of land, however small, she lost her ketubah.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אִם קִבְּלָה עָלֶיהָ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא כָתַב לָהּ, אִבְּדָה כְתֻבָּתָהּ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: if she accepted [such an assignment] even though he did not assign it to her in writing she lost her ketubah.

phrases.he: הַכּוֹתֵב נְכָסָיו לְעַבְדּוֹ, יָצָא בֶן חוֹרִין.
phrases.en: One who assigns in writing his possessions to his slave, [the slave] thereby goes free.

phrases.he: שִׁיֵּר קַרְקַע כָּל שֶׁהוּא, לֹא יָצָא בֶן חוֹרִין.
phrases.en: If he reserved for himself any land, however small, he does not become free.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, לְעוֹלָם הוּא בֶן חוֹרִין, עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר הֲרֵי כָל נְכָסַי נְתוּנִין לְאִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי עַבְדִּי חוּץ מֵאֶחָד מֵרִבּוֹא שֶׁבָּהֶן:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: he always becomes free, unless [the master] says: “Behold, all my goods are given to so-and-so my slave, with the exception of one ten-thousandth part of them.”

phrases.he: הַפֵּאָה נִתֶּנֶת בִּמְחֻבָּר לַקַּרְקָע.
phrases.en: Peah is given from [the crop] while it is still connected with the soil.

phrases.he: בְּדָלִית וּבְדֶקֶל, בַּעַל הַבַּיִת מוֹרִיד וּמְחַלֵּק לָעֲנִיִּים.
phrases.en: But in the case of hanging vine-branches and the date-palm, the owner brings down [the fruit] and distributes it among the poor.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אַף בַּחֲלִיקֵי אֱגוֹזִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: the same applies to smooth nut trees.

phrases.he: אֲפִלּוּ תִשְׁעִים וְתִשְׁעָה אוֹמְרִים לְחַלֵּק וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר לָבוֹז, לָזֶה שׁוֹמְעִין, שֶׁאָמַר כַּהֲלָכָה
phrases.en: Even if ninety-nine [of the poor] say [to the owner] to distribute it and one says to leave it in the field, this latter is listened to, since he spoke in accordance with the halakhah.

phrases.he: בְּדָלִית וּבְדֶקֶל אֵינוֹ כֵן, אֲפִלּוּ תִשְׁעִים וְתִשְׁעָה אוֹמְרִים לָבוֹז וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר לְחַלֵּק, לָזֶה שׁוֹמְעִין, שֶׁאָמַר כַּהֲלָכָה:
phrases.en: With hanging vine-branches and date-palm trees it is not so; even if ninety-nine [of the poor] say [to the owner] to leave it in the field and one says to distribute it, this latter is listened to, since he spoke in accordance with the halakhah.

phrases.he: נָטַל מִקְצָת פֵּאָה וּזְרָקָהּ עַל הַשְּׁאָר, אֵין לוֹ בָהּ כְּלוּם.
phrases.en: If [a poor man] took some of the peah [already collected] and threw it onto the remainder [not yet collected], he gets none of it.

phrases.he: נָפַל לוֹ עָלֶיהָ, וּפֵרֵשׂ טַלִּיתוֹ עָלֶיהָ, מַעֲבִירִין אוֹתָהּ הֵימֶנּוּ.
phrases.en: If he fell down upon it, or spread his cloak over it, they take the peah away from him.

phrases.he: וְכֵן בְּלֶקֶט, וְכֵן בְּעֹמֶר הַשִּׁכְחָה
phrases.en: The same applies to gleanings and the forgotten sheaf.

phrases.he: פֵּאָה אֵין קוֹצְרִין אוֹתָהּ בְּמַגָּלוֹת, וְאֵין עוֹקְרִין אוֹתָהּ בְּקַרְדֻּמּוֹת, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יַכּוּ אִישׁ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ:
phrases.en: [The poor] may not harvest peah with scythes or tear it out [of the ground] with spades, so that they might not strike one another [with these implements].

phrases.he: שָׁלשׁ אַבְעָיוֹת בַּיּוֹם, בַּשַּׁחַר וּבַחֲצוֹת וּבַמִּנְחָה.
phrases.en: There are three times a day [the poor] make a search [in the field for peah]: morning, noon, and sunset.

phrases.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, לֹא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִפְחֲתוּ.
phrases.en: Rabban Gamaliel says: these [times] were only set lest they reduce them.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, לֹא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יוֹסִיפוּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: these were set lest they add to them.

phrases.he: שֶׁל בֵּית נָמֵר הָיוּ מְלַקְּטִין עַל הַחֶבֶל, וְנוֹתְנִים פֵּאָה מִכָּל אֻמָּן וְאֻמָּן
phrases.en: [The men] of Bet Namer used to have the poor harvest [the peah] with the aid of a rope, and they left peah at the end of each furrow.

phrases.he: עוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים שֶׁקָּצַר אֶת שָׂדֵהוּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְגַּיֵּר, פָּטוּר מִן הַלֶּקֶט וּמִן הַשִּׁכְחָה וּמִן הַפֵּאָה.
phrases.en: A non-Jew who harvested his field and then converted, he is exempt from [leaving] gleanings, the forgotten sheaf and peah.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְחַיֵּב בְּשִׁכְחָה, שֶׁאֵין הַשִּׁכְחָה אֶלָּא בִשְׁעַת הָעִמּוּר
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah makes him liable to leave the forgotten sheaf, since he becomes liable for the forgotten sheaf at the time of their binding.

phrases.he: הִקְדִּישׁ קָמָה וּפָדָה קָמָה, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: One who dedicated standing grain [to the Temple] and then redeemed it while it was still standing grain, he is liable [to give the agricultural gifts to the poor].

phrases.he: עֳמָרִין וּפָדָה עֳמָרִין, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: [If he dedicated] sheaves and redeemed them while they were still sheaves, he is liable.

phrases.he: קָמָה וּפָדָה עֳמָרִין, פְּטוּרָה, שֶׁבִּשְׁעַת חוֹבָתָהּ הָיְתָה פְטוּרָה
phrases.en: [If he dedicated] standing grain and redeemed it [when it was already in] sheaves, he is exempt, since at the time when it became liable it was exempt.

phrases.he: כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ, הַמַּקְדִּישׁ פֵּרוֹתָיו עַד שֶׁלֹּא בָאוּ לְעוֹנַת הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, וּפְדָאָן, חַיָּבִין.
phrases.en: Similarly one who dedicates his produce prior to the stage when they are subject to tithes and then redeemed them, they are liable [to be tithed].

phrases.he: מִשֶּׁבָּאוּ לְעוֹנַת הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, וּפְדָאָן, חַיָּבִין.
phrases.en: If [he dedicated them] when they had already become subject to tithes and then redeemed them, they are liable [to be tithed].

phrases.he: הִקְדִּישָׁן עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמְרוּ וּגְמָרָן הַגִּזְבָּר, וְאַחַר כָּךְ פְּדָאָן, פְּטוּרִים, שֶׁבִּשְׁעַת חוֹבָתָן הָיוּ פְטוּרִים
phrases.en: If he dedicated them before they had ripened, and they became ripe while in the possession of the [Temple] treasurer, and he then redeemed them, they are exempt, since at the time when they would have been liable, they were exempt.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁלָּקַט אֶת הַפֵּאָה וְאָמַר הֲרֵי זוֹ לְאִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי עָנִי,
phrases.en: One who collected peah and said, “This is for so-and-so a poor man:” Rabbi Eliezer says: he has thus acquired it for him.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, זָכָה לוֹ.
phrases.en: The sages say: he must give it to the first poor man he finds.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, יִתְּנֶנָּה לֶעָנִי שֶׁנִּמְצָא רִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.en: Gleanings, the forgotten sheaf and the peah of non-Jews are subject to tithes, unless he [the non-Jew] had declared them ownerless.

phrases.he: הַלֶּקֶט וְהַשִּׁכְחָה וְהַפֵּאָה שֶׁל עוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים חַיָּב בְּמַעַשְׂרוֹת, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִפְקִיר
אֵיזֶהוּ לֶקֶט, הַנּוֹשֵׁר בִּשְׁעַת הַקְּצִירָה.
phrases.en: What are gleanings? That which falls down at the time of harvesting.

phrases.he: הָיָה קוֹצֵר, קָצַר מְלֹא יָדוֹ, תָּלַשׁ מְלֹא קֻמְצוֹ, הִכָּהוּ קוֹץ וְנָפַל מִיָּדוֹ לָאָרֶץ, הֲרֵי הוּא שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבָּיִת.
phrases.en: If while he was harvesting, he harvested a handful, or plucked a fistful, and then a thorn pricked him, and what he had in his hand fell to the ground, it still belongs to the owner.

phrases.he: תּוֹךְ הַיָּד וְתוֹךְ הַמַּגָּל, לָעֲנִיִּים.
phrases.en: [That which drops from] inside the hand or the sickle [belongs] to the poor, but [that which falls from] the back of the hand or the sickle [belongs] to the owner.

phrases.he: אַחַר הַיָּד וְאַחַר הַמַּגָּל, לְבַעַל הַבָּיִת.
רֹאשׁ הַיָּד וְרֹאשׁ הַמַּגָּל,
רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, לָעֲנִיִּים.
phrases.en: [That which falls from] the top of the hand or sickle: Rabbi Ishmael says: to the poor; But Rabbi Akiva says: to the owner.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, לְבַעַל הַבָּיִת:
חוֹרֵי הַנְּמָלִים שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ הַקָּמָה, הֲרֵי הֵן שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבָּיִת.
phrases.en: [Grain found in] ant holes where the stalks are still standing, behold it still belongs to the owner.

phrases.he: שֶׁלְּאַחַר הַקּוֹצְרִים, הָעֶלְיוֹנִים לָעֲנִיִּים, וְהַתַּחְתּוֹנִים שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבָּיִת.
phrases.en: After the harvesters [had passed over them], those found in the top parts [of the ant holes belong] to the poor, but [those found] on the bottom parts [belong] to the owner.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, הַכֹּל לָעֲנִיִּים, שֶׁסְּפֵק לֶקֶט, לֶקֶט:
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: it all belongs to the poor, for gleanings about which there is any doubt are regarded as gleanings.

phrases.he: גָּדִישׁ שֶׁלֹּא לֻקַּט תַּחְתָּיו, כָּל הַנּוֹגֵעַ בָּאָרֶץ הֲרֵי הוּא שֶׁל עֲנִיִּים.
phrases.en: If a pile of grain was stacked [on part of a field] from which gleanings had not yet been collected, whatever touches the ground belongs to the poor.

phrases.he: הָרוּחַ שֶׁפִּזְּרָה אֶת הָעֳמָרִים, אוֹמְדִים אוֹתָהּ כַּמָּה לֶקֶט הִיא רְאוּיָה לַעֲשׂוֹת, וְנוֹתֵן לָעֲנִיִּים.
phrases.en: If the wind scattered the sheaves, they estimate the amount of gleanings the field would have yielded and they give that to the poor.

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, נוֹתֵן לָעֲנִיִּים בִּכְדֵי נְפִילָה
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel says: he must give to the poor the amount that would fall.

phrases.he: שִׁבֹּלֶת שֶׁבַּקָּצִיר וְרֹאשָׁהּ מַגִּיעַ לַקָּמָה, אִם נִקְצְרָה עִם הַקָּמָה, הֲרֵי הִיא שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת, וְאִם לָאו, הֲרֵי הִיא שֶׁל עֲנִיִּים.
phrases.en: The top of a single ear of grain [that remained] after the harvesting and its top touches the standing stalk: If it can be cut with the stalk, it belongs to the owner; But if not, it belongs to the poor.

phrases.he: שִׁבֹּלֶת שֶׁל לֶקֶט שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבָה בַגָּדִישׁ, מְעַשֵּׂר שִׁבֹּלֶת אַחַת וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ.
phrases.en: If an ear of grain of gleanings that became mixed up with a stack of grain, [the owner] must tithe one ear of grain and give it to him [the poor].

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וְכִי הֵיאַךְ הֶעָנִי הַזֶּה מַחֲלִיף דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָא בִרְשׁוּתוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: how can this poor man give in exchange something that had not yet become his? Rather, [the owner] must transfer to the poor man the ownership of the whole stack and then tithe one ear of grain and give it to him.

phrases.he: אֶלָּא מְזַכֶּה אֶת הֶעָנִי בְּכָל הַגָּדִישׁ, וּמְעַשֵּׂר שִׁבֹּלֶת אַחַת וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ
אֵין מְגַלְגְּלִין בְּטוֹפֵחַ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: They should not [irrigate a field] with a water wheel, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים מַתִּירִין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר
phrases.en: The sages permit it, because it is still possible [for the poor to get their gleanings].

phrases.he: בַּעַל הַבַּיִת שֶׁהָיָה עוֹבֵר מִמָּקוֹם לְמָקוֹם, וְצָרִיךְ לִטֹּל לֶקֶט שִׁכְחָה וּפֵאָה וּמַעְשַׂר עָנִי, יִטֹּל, וּכְשֶׁיַּחֲזֹר לְבֵיתוֹ יְשַׁלֵּם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.en: A property owner who was passing from place to place and need to take gleanings, the forgotten sheaf, peah or the poor man’s tithe, he may take them, and when he returns home, he must pay [for the amount gathered], the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, עָנִי הָיָה בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה:
phrases.en: The sages say: he was a poor man at that time [and so he need not make restitution].

phrases.he: הַמַּחֲלִיף עִם הָעֲנִיִּים, בְּשֶׁלּוֹ פָּטוּר, וּבְשֶׁל עֲנִיִּים חַיָּב.
phrases.en: One who exchanges with the poor, [what they give in exchange] for his is exempt [from tithes] but what [he gives in exchange] for that of the poor is subject [to tithes].

phrases.he: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה בַּאֲרִיסוּת, זֶה נוֹתֵן לָזֶה חֶלְקוֹ מַעְשַׂר עָנִי, וְזֶה נוֹתֵן לָזֶה חֶלְקוֹ מַעְשַׂר עָנִי.
phrases.en: Two who received a field as sharecroppers, this one may give to the other his share of the poor man’s tithe and this one may give to the other his share of the poor man’s tithe.

phrases.he: הַמְקַבֵּל שָׂדֶה לִקְצֹר, אָסוּר בְּלֶקֶט שִׁכְחָה וּפֵאָה וּמַעְשַׂר עָנִי.
phrases.en: One who receives a field in order to harvest it, he is forbidden to take gleanings, the forgotten sheaf, peah or the poor man’s tithe.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁקִּבֵּל מִמֶּנּוּ לְמֶחֱצָה, לִשְׁלִישׁ וְלִרְבִיעַ. אֲבָל אִם
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah said: When is this so? When he receives it [in order to pay the owner] a half, third or quarter [of the crop].

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ שְׁלִישׁ מַה שֶּׁאַתָּה קוֹצֵר שֶׁלָּךְ, מֻתָּר בְּלֶקֶט וּבְשִׁכְחָה וּבְפֵאָה, וְאָסוּר בְּמַעְשַׂר עָנִי:
phrases.en: But [if the owner] had said to him: “A third of that which you harvest belongs to you,” then he may take gleanings, the forgotten sheaf and peah, but not the poor man’s tithe.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת שָׂדֵהוּ, הַמּוֹכֵר מֻתָּר וְהַלּוֹקֵחַ אָסוּר.
phrases.en: One who sells, the seller is permitted [to take the agricultural gifts] and the purchaser is forbidden.

phrases.he: לֹא יִשְׂכֹּר אָדָם אֶת הַפּוֹעֲלִים עַל מְנָת שֶׁיְּלַקֵּט בְּנוֹ אַחֲרָיו.
phrases.en: One may not hire a worker on the condition that the son [of the worker] should gather the gleanings after him.
