phrases.he: מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַנִּיחַ אֶת הָעֲנִיִּים לִלְקֹט, אוֹ שֶׁהוּא מַנִּיחַ אֶת אֶחָד וְאֶחָד לֹא, אוֹ שֶׁהוּא מְסַיֵּעַ אֶת אֶחָד מֵהֶן, הֲרֵי זֶה גּוֹזֵל אֶת הָעֲנִיִּים.
phrases.en: One who does not allow the poor to gather, or one who allows one but not another, or one who helps one of them [to gather] behold he is a robber of the poor.

phrases.he: עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר (משלי כב) אַל תַּסֵּג גְּבוּל עוֹלִים
phrases.en: Concerning him it is said: “Do not remove the landmark of those that come up (olim)” (Proverbs 22:28).

phrases.he: הָעֹמֶר שֶׁשְּׁכָחוּהוּ פוֹעֲלִים וְלֹא שְׁכָחוֹ בַעַל הַבַּיִת, שְׁכָחוֹ בַעַל הַבַּיִת וְלֹא שְׁכָחוּהוּ פוֹעֲלִים, עָמְדוּ עֲנִיִּים בְּפָנָיו אוֹ שֶׁחִפּוּהוּ בְקַשׁ, הֲרֵי זֶה אֵינוֹ שִׁכְחָה:
phrases.en: A sheaf which the workers forgot but not the land owner, or which the land owner forgot but not the workers; or [a sheaf] which the poor stood in front of [and blocked its view], or they covered it up with stubble, it is not considered a forgotten sheaf.

phrases.he: הַמְעַמֵּר לְכֹבָעוֹת וּלְכֻמְסָאוֹת, לַחֲרָרָה וְלָעֳמָרִים, אֵין לוֹ שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: One who binds sheaves into stack covers, stack bases, round stacks or regular stacks, he is not subject to the law of the forgotten sheaf [while binding].

phrases.he: מִמֶּנּוּ וְלַגֹּרֶן, יֶשׁ לוֹ שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: [When bringing them afterwards] to the threshing-floor, he is subject to the law of the forgotten sheaf.

phrases.he: הַמְעַמֵּר לַגָּדִישׁ, יֶשׁ לוֹ שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: One who piles up the sheaves to make a stack, he is subject to the law of the forgotten sheaf.

phrases.he: מִמֶּנּוּ וְלַגֹּרֶן, אֵין לוֹ שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: [When bringing them afterwards] to the threshing-floor, he is not subject to the law of the forgotten sheaf.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל הַמְעַמֵּר לְמָקוֹם שֶׁהוּא גְמָר מְלָאכָה, יֶשׁ לוֹ שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: This is the general rule: whoever makes the sheaves at the place which is the end of the work is subject to the law of the forgotten sheaf, [and afterwards when he takes] them to the threshing-floor, he is not subject to the law of the forgotten sheaf.

phrases.he: מִמֶּנּוּ וְלַגֹּרֶן, אֵין לוֹ שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: However, [one who piles up the sheaves] at a place which is not the end of the work, is not subject to the law of the forgotten sheaf; [and afterwards when he takes] them to the threshing-floor, he is subject to the law of the forgotten sheaf.

phrases.he: לְמָקוֹם שֶׁאֵינוֹ גְמַר מְלָאכָה, אֵין לוֹ שִׁכְחָה.
מִמֶּנּוּ וְלַגֹּרֶן, יֶשׁ לוֹ שִׁכְחָה
בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, הֶבְקֵר לָעֲנִיִּים, הֶבְקֵר.
phrases.en: Bet Shammai says: [That which is] made ownerless only in regard to the poor is indeed ownerless.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, אֵינוֹ הֶפְקֵר, עַד שֶׁיֻּפְקַר אַף לָעֲשִׁירִים, כַּשְּׁמִטָּה.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel says: it is not ownerless unless ownership is renounced even for the rich, as in the case of the sabbatical year.

phrases.he: כָּל עָמְרֵי הַשָּׂדֶה שֶׁל קַב קַב וְאֶחָד שֶׁל אַרְבַּעַת קַבִּין וּשְׁכָחוֹ,
phrases.en: [If] all of the sheaves in a field are a kav each, and one is four kavs and that one is forgotten: Bet Shammai says: it is not considered forgotten.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אֵינוֹ שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel says: it is considered forgotten.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, שִׁכְחָה:
הָעֹמֶר שֶׁהוּא סָמוּךְ לַגָּפָה וְלַגָּדִישׁ, לַבָּקָר וְלַכֵּלִים, וּשְׁכָחוֹ,
phrases.en: A sheaf left near a stone fence, or near a stack [of grain] or near oxen, or near equipment: Bet Shammai says: it is not considered “forgotten”; Bet Hillel says: it is considered “forgotten.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אֵינוֹ שִׁכְחָה.
וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, שִׁכְחָה:
רָאשֵׁי שׁוּרוֹת, הָעֹמֶר שֶׁכְּנֶגְדּוֹ מוֹכִיחַ.
phrases.en: [With regard to sheaves forgotten] at the end of the row, the sheaf lying across from it proves [that the first sheaf has not been forgotten.

phrases.he: הָעֹמֶר שֶׁהֶחֱזִיק בּוֹ לְהוֹלִיכוֹ אֶל הָעִיר, וּשְׁכָחוֹ, מוֹדִים שֶׁאֵינוֹ שִׁכְחָה
phrases.en: [As for] a sheaf that [the owner] took to bring it to the city and forgot it, all agree that it is not considered a “forgotten sheaf.”

phrases.he: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן רָאשֵׁי שׁוּרוֹת.
phrases.en: These are to be considered ends of the rows:If two men begin [to gather] from the middle of the row, one facing north and the other south and they forget [some sheaves] in front of them and behind them, those left in front of them are “forgotten,” but those left behind them are not “forgotten.

phrases.he: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁהִתְחִילוּ מֵאֶמְצַע הַשּׁוּרָה, זֶה פָּנָיו לַצָּפוֹן וְזֶה פָּנָיו לַדָּרוֹם, וְשָׁכְחוּ לִפְנֵיהֶם וּלְאַחֲרֵיהֶם, אֶת שֶׁלִּפְנֵיהֶם שִׁכְחָה, וְאֶת שֶׁלְּאַחֲרֵיהֶם אֵינוֹ שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: If an individual begins from the end of the row and he forgets [some sheaves] in front of him and behind him, those in front of him are not “forgotten”, whereas those behind him are “forgotten,” for this comes under the category of “you shall not go back [to retrieve it].

phrases.he: יָחִיד שֶׁהִתְחִיל מֵרֹאשׁ הַשּׁוּרָה, וְשָׁכַח לְפָנָיו וּלְאַחֲרָיו, שֶׁלְּפָנָיו אֵינוֹ שִׁכְחָה, וְשֶׁלְּאַחֲרָיו שִׁכְחָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא בְּבַל תָּשׁוּב (דברים כד).
phrases.en: This is the general rule: anything that can be said to fall under the law “you shall not go back” is considered “forgotten,” but that to which the principle of “you shall not go back” cannot be applied is not considered “forgotten.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל שֶׁהוּא בְּבַל תָּשׁוּב, שִׁכְחָה.
וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּבַל תָּשׁוּב, אֵינוֹ שִׁכְחָה
שְׁנֵי עֳמָרִים, שִׁכְחָה, וּשְׁלשָׁה אֵינָן שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: Two sheaves [left lying together] are “forgotten,” but three are not “forgotten.

phrases.he: שְׁנֵי צִבּוּרֵי זֵיתִים וְחָרוּבִין, שִׁכְחָה, וּשְׁלשָׁה אֵינָן שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: Two bundles of olives or carobs are “forgotten” but three are not “forgotten.

phrases.he: שְׁנֵי הוּצְנֵי פִשְׁתָּן, שִׁכְחָה, וּשְׁלשָׁה אֵינָן שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: Two flax-stalks are “forgotten”, but three are not “forgotten”.

phrases.he: שְׁנֵי גַרְגְּרִים, פֶּרֶט, וּשְׁלשָׁה אֵינָן פֶּרֶט.
phrases.en: Two grapes are considered “grape gleanings,” but three are not “grape gleanings.

phrases.he: שְׁנֵי שִׁבֳּלִים, לֶקֶט, וּשְׁלֹשָׁה אֵינָן לֶקֶט.
phrases.en: Two ears of grain are deemed “gleanings,” but three are not gleanings.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ כְּדִבְרֵי בֵית הִלֵּל. וְעַל כֻּלָּן
phrases.en: All these [rulings] are according to Bet Hillel.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, שְׁלשָׁה, לָעֲנִיִּים, וְאַרְבָּעָה, לְבַעַל הַבָּיִת:
phrases.en: And concerning them all Bet Shammai says that three [that are left] belong to the poor, and four belong to the owner.

phrases.he: הָעֹמֶר שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ סָאתַיִם, וּשְׁכָחוֹ, אֵינוֹ שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: A sheaf that has two seahs and he forgot it it is not considered “forgotten.

phrases.he: שְׁנֵי עֳמָרִים וּבָהֶם סָאתַיִם, רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, לְבַעַל הַבָּיִת.
phrases.en: Two sheaves that together comprise two seahs: Rabban Gamaliel says: they belong to the owner; But the sages say: they belong to the poor.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, לָעֲנִיִּים. אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, וְכִי מֵרֹב הָעֳמָרִים יֻפֵּי כֹחַ שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אוֹ הוּרַע כֹּחוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabban Gamaliel said: “Are the rights of the owner strengthened or weakened according to the greater number of the sheaves?” They replied, “His rights are strengthened.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, יֻפֵּי כֹחוֹ.
phrases.en: He said to them: “If in a case of one sheaf of two seahs it is not deemed “forgotten,” then how much more should be the case of two sheaves that together contain two seahs?” They replied: “No.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, וּמָה אִם בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא עֹמֶר אֶחָד וּבוֹ סָאתַיִם וּשְׁכָחוֹ, אֵינוֹ שִׁכְחָה, שְׁנֵי עֳמָרִים וּבָהֶם סָאתַיִם, אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: If you argue in the case of one sheaf it is because it is large enough to be considered a stack.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ בְּעֹמֶר אֶחָד שֶׁהוּא כְגָדִישׁ, תֹּאמַר בִּשְׁנֵי עֳמָרִים שֶׁהֵן כִּכְרִיכוֹת:
phrases.en: Are you going to argue likewise in the case of two sheaves which are like bundles?”

phrases.he: קָמָה שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ סָאתַיִם, וּשְׁכָחָהּ, אֵינָהּ שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: A standing stalk of grain that contains two seahs and he forgot it, it is not considered “forgotten.

phrases.he: אֵין בָּהּ סָאתַיִם, אֲבָל הִיא רְאוּיָה לַעֲשׂוֹת סָאתַיִם, אֲפִלּוּ הִיא שֶׁל טוֹפֵחַ, רוֹאִין אוֹתָהּ כְּאִלּוּ הִיא עֲנָוָה שֶׁל שְׂעוֹרִים
phrases.en: If it does not contain two seahs now, but is fit to yield two seahs, even if it was of an inferior kind of barley, it is regarded as full barley [grains].

phrases.he: הַקָּמָה מַצֶּלֶת אֶת הָעֹמֶר וְאֶת הַקָּמָה.
phrases.en: A standing stalk of grain can save a sheaf and another standing stalk [from being regarded as “forgotten”].

phrases.he: הָעֹמֶר אֵינוֹ מַצִּיל לֹא אֶת הָעֹמֶר וְלֹא אֶת הַקָּמָה.
phrases.en: A sheaf cannot save either another sheaf or a standing stalk.

phrases.he: אֵיזוֹ הִיא קָמָה שֶׁהִיא מַצֶּלֶת אֶת הָעֹמֶר, כָּל שֶׁאֵינָהּ שִׁכְחָה אֲפִלּוּ קֶלַח אֶחָד
phrases.en: What is the standing stalk of grain that can save a sheaf? Anything which has not been forgotten, even though it is a single stalk.

phrases.he: סְאָה תְבוּאָה עֲקוּרָה וּסְאָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ עֲקוּרָה, וְכֵן בָּאִילָן, וְהַשּׁוּם וְהַבְּצָלִים, אֵינָן מִצְטָרְפִין לְסָאתַיִם, אֶלָּא שֶׁל עֲנִיִּים הֵם.
phrases.en: A seah of plucked grain and a seah of unplucked grain, and also trees; and garlic and to onions do not combine to count as two seahs, but rather they must be left to the poor.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אִם בָּאת רְשׁוּת הֶעָנִי בָּאֶמְצָע, אֵינָן מִצְטָרְפִין, וְאִם לָאו, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מִצְטָרְפִין:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: if anything that belongs to the poor comes in between them, the two are not combined together; otherwise, they do combine.

phrases.he: תְּבוּאָה שֶׁנִּתְּנָה לְשַׁחַת אוֹ לַאֲלֻמָּה, וְכֵן בַּאֲגֻדֵּי הַשּׁוּם, וַאֲגֻדּוֹת הַשּׁוּם וְהַבְּצָלִים, אֵין לָהֶן שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: Grain used for fodder or [stalks] used for binding sheaves, and also garlic-stalks used for tying other bunches, or tied bunches of garlic and onions they [all are not subject to the laws of] forgotten.

phrases.he: וְכָל הַטְּמוּנִים בָּאָרֶץ, כְּגוֹן הַלּוּף וְהַשּׁוּם וְהַבְּצָלִים,
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֵין לָהֶם שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: Anything stored in the ground like arum, garlic and onions: Rabbi Judah says: they do not subject to the laws of “forgotten”; But the sages say: they are subject to the laws of “forgotten.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, יֵשׁ לָהֶם שִׁכְחָה:
הַקּוֹצֵר בַּלַּיְלָה וְהַמְעַמֵּר וְהַסּוּמָא, יֵשׁ לָהֶם שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: One who harvests by night and binds sheaves [by night] or one who is blind [that which he leaves] is subject to the law of the “forgotten.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיָה מִתְכַּוֵּן לִטֹּל אֶת הַגַּס הַגַּס, אֵין לוֹ שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: If he intends to remove large leaves first, then the law of “forgotten” does not apply.

phrases.he: אִם אָמַר, הֲרֵי אֲנִי קוֹצֵר עַל מְנָת מַה שֶּׁאֲנִי שׁוֹכֵח אֲנִי אֶטֹּל, יֶשׁ לוֹ שִׁכְחָה
phrases.en: If he said: “Behold, I am reaping on the condition that I take afterwards that which I have forgotten,” the law of “forgotten” still applies.

phrases.he: כָּל זַיִת שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ שֵׁם בַּשָּׂדֶה, אֲפִלּוּ כְּזֵית הַנְּטוֹפָה בִּשְׁעָתוֹ, וּשְׁכָחוֹ, אֵינוֹ שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: An olive tree that has a name in the field, such as the olive tree of Netofah in its time, and he forgot it, it is not deemed “forgotten.

phrases.he: בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בִּשְׁמוֹ וּבְמַעֲשָׂיו וּבִמְקוֹמוֹ.
phrases.en: To what does this apply? [Only to a tree distinguished] by its name, produce, or position.

phrases.he: בִּשְׁמוֹ, שֶׁהָיָה שִׁפְכוֹנִי אוֹ בֵישָׁנִי.
phrases.en: “By its name:” if it were a shifkhoni or beshani.

phrases.he: בְּמַעֲשָׂיו, שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה הַרְבֵּה.
phrases.en: “By its produce:” if it yields large quantities.

phrases.he: בִּמְקוֹמוֹ, שֶׁהוּא עוֹמֵד בְּצַד הַגַּת אוֹ בְצַד הַפִּרְצָה.
phrases.en: “By its position:” if it stands at the side of the winepress or near the gap in the fence.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַזֵּיתִים, שְׁנַיִם שִׁכְחָה, וּשְׁלשָׁה אֵינָן שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: Other kinds of olive trees: two are deemed “forgotten”, but three are not deemed “forgotten.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אֵין שִׁכְחָה לַזֵּיתִים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: there is no law of “forgotten” for olive trees.

phrases.he: זַיִת שֶׁנִּמְצָא עוֹמֵד בֵּין שָׁלשׁ שׁוּרוֹת שֶׁל שְׁנֵי מַלְבְּנִים וּשְׁכָחוֹ, אֵינוֹ שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: An olive tree found standing between three rows [of olive trees] which have two plots separating them, and he forgot it, it is not deemed, “forgotten.

phrases.he: זַיִת שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ סָאתַיִם, וּשְׁכָחוֹ, אֵינוֹ שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: An olive tree containing two seahs and he forgot it, it is not deemed forgotten.

phrases.he: בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בִּזְמַן שֶׁלֹּא הִתְחִיל בּוֹ.
phrases.en: To what does this apply? Only when he [the owner] had not yet begun [to harvest the tree], but if he had begun, even if it were like the olive tree of Netofah in its time, and he forgot it, it is deemed forgotten.

phrases.he: אֲבָל אִם הִתְחִיל בּוֹ, אֲפִלּוּ כְּזֵית הַנְּטוֹפָה בִּשְׁעָתוֹ, וּשְׁכָחוֹ, יֶשׁ לוֹ שִׁכְחָה.
phrases.en: As long as the owner has some of the olives belonging to him at the foot of the tree, he has [possession] of those on top of the tree.

phrases.he: כָּל זְמַן שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ תַחְתָּיו, יֶשׁ לוֹ בְרֹאשׁוֹ.
רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁתֵּלֵךְ הַמַּחֲבֵא:
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: [forgotten applies only] after [those with] the beating-rod have gone.

phrases.he: אֵיזֶהוּ פֶרֶט, הַנּוֹשֵׁר בִּשְׁעַת הַבְּצִירָה.
phrases.en: What is peret? [Grapes] which fall down during the harvesting.

phrases.he: הָיָה בוֹצֵר, עָקַץ אֶת הָאֶשְׁכּוֹל, הֻסְבַּךְ בֶּעָלִים, נָפַל מִיָּדוֹ לָאָרֶץ וְנִפְרַט, הֲרֵי הוּא שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבָּיִת.
phrases.en: If while he was harvesting [the grapes], he cut off an entire cluster by its stalk, and it got tangled up in the [grape] leaves, and then it fell from his hand to the ground and the single berries were separated, it belongs to the owner.

phrases.he: הַמַּנִּיחַ אֶת הַכַּלְכָּלָה תַּחַת הַגֶּפֶן בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהוּא בוֹצֵר, הֲרֵי זֶה גּוֹזֵל אֶת הָעֲנִיִּים, עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר (משלי כב) אַל תַּסֵּג גְּבוּל עוֹלִים
phrases.en: One who places a basket under the vine when he is harvesting [the grapes], behold he is a robber of the poor. Concerning him it is said: “Do not remove the landmark of those that come up (olim)” (Proverbs 22:28).

phrases.he: אֵיזוֹהִי עוֹלֶלֶת. כָּל שֶׁאֵין לָהּ לֹא כָתֵף וְלֹא נָטֵף.
phrases.en: What constitutes a defective cluster (olelet) of grapes? Any [cluster] which has neither a shoulder [a wide upper part] nor a pendant [a cone-shaped lower part].

phrases.he: אִם יֶשׁ לָהּ כָּתֵף אוֹ נָטֵף, שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת, אִם סָפֵק, לָעֲנִיִּים.
phrases.en: If it has a shoulder or a pendant, it belongs to the owner.

phrases.he: עוֹלֶלֶת שֶׁבָּאַרְכֻּבָּה, אִם נִקְרֶצֶת עִם הָאֶשְׁכּוֹל, הֲרֵי הִיא שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת, וְאִם לָאו, הֲרֵי הִיא שֶׁל עֲנִיִּים. גַּרְגֵּר יְחִידִי,
phrases.en: If there is a doubt, it belongs to the poor. A defective cluster on the joint of a vine [where a normal cluster hangs from the vine], if it can be cut off with the cluster, it belongs to the owner; but if it can not, it belongs to the poor.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֶשְׁכּוֹל.
phrases.en: A single grape: Rabbi Judah says: It is deemed a whole cluster, But the sages say: It is deemed a defective cluster.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, עוֹלֶלֶת:
הַמֵּדֵל בַּגְּפָנִים, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהוּא מֵדֵל בְּתוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ, כֵּן הוּא מֵדֵל בְּשֶׁל עֲנִיִּים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: One who is thinning out vines, just as he may thin out in that which belongs to him, so too he may thin out in that which belongs to the poor, the words of Rabbi Judah.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, בְּשֶׁלּוֹ הוּא רַשַּׁאי, וְאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי בְּשֶׁל עֲנִיִּים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: in that which belongs to him, he is permitted, but he is not permitted in that which belongs to the poor.

phrases.he: כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי,
phrases.en: [The grapes of] a vineyard in its fourth year:Bet Shammai says: the laws of the added fifth and removal do not apply to them; But Bet Hillel says: they do.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אֵין לוֹ חֹמֶשׁ, וְאֵין לוֹ בִעוּר.
phrases.en: Bet Shammai says: the laws of peret and the defective clusters apply to them, and the poor can redeem the grapes for themselves.

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, יֶשׁ לוֹ.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel says: all [of them] go to the wine-press.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, יֶשׁ לוֹ פֶרֶט וְיֶשׁ לוֹ עוֹלְלוֹת, וְהָעֲנִיִּים פּוֹדִין לְעַצְמָן.
וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, כֻּלּוֹ לַגַּת:
כֶּרֶם שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ עוֹלְלוֹת,
phrases.en: A vineyard which consists entirely of defective clusters: Rabbi Eliezer says: it belongs to the owner.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, לְבַעַל הַבָּיִת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: to the poor.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, לָעֲנִיִּים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer: “When you harvest the grapes of your vineyard, do not take the defective clusters” (Deuteronomy 24:21).

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, כִּי תִבְצֹר לֹא תְעוֹלֵל (דברים כד), אִם אֵין בָּצִיר, מִנַּיִן עוֹלְלוֹת.
phrases.en: If there is no grape harvesting, how can there be “defective clusters”? Rabbi Akiva said to him: “And from your vineyard do not take the defective clusters” (Leviticus 19:10) even if it consists entirely of defective clusters.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, וְכַרְמְךָ לֹא תְעוֹלֵל (ויקרא יט), אֲפִלּוּ כֻלּוֹ עוֹלְלוֹת, אִם כֵּן לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר כִּי תִבְצֹר לֹא תְעוֹלֵל, אֵין לָעֲנִיִּים בָּעוֹלְלוֹת קֹדֶם הַבָּצִיר:
phrases.en: If that is so, why is it said: “When you harvest the grapes of your vineyard, do not take the defective clusters”? [This teaches that] the poor have no right to claim the defective clusters before the harvest.

phrases.he: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ כַּרְמוֹ עַד שֶׁלֹּא נוֹדְעוּ בוֹ הָעוֹלְלוֹת, אֵין הָעוֹלְלוֹת לָעֲנִיִּים.
phrases.en: One who dedicates his entire vineyard [to the Temple] before the “defective clusters” were recognizable, the “defective clusters” do not belong to the poor.

phrases.he: מִשֶּׁנּוֹדְעוּ בוֹ הָעוֹלְלוֹת, הָעוֹלְלוֹת לָעֲנִיִּים.
phrases.en: After the defective clusters were recognizable, then they do belong to the poor.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, יִתְּנוּ שְׂכַר גִּדּוּלָיו לַהֶקְדֵּשׁ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: [the poor] must give the value of their improved growth to the Temple.

phrases.he: אֵיזֶה הִיא שִׁכְחָה בֶּעָרִיס, כָּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִפְשֹׁט אֶת יָדוֹ וְלִטְּלָהּ, וּבְרֹגְלִיּוֹת, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲבֹר הֵימֶנָּה
phrases.en: What is deemed “forgotten” in the case of a trellis [a lattice for supporting plants]? Anything that one can no longer stretch his hand and take it. And in the case of ground-trained vines? From the time [the gatherers] pass by it.

phrases.he: מֵאֵימָתַי כָּל אָדָם מֻתָּרִין בְּלֶקֶט. מִשֶּׁיֵּלְכוּ הַנָּמוֹשׁוֹת.
phrases.en: From when are all people permitted to take gleanings, [forgotten sheaves and peah]? After the old ones of the poor have gone.

phrases.he: בְּפֶרֶט וְעוֹלְלוֹת, מִשֶּׁיֵּלְכוּ הָעֲנִיִּים בַּכֶּרֶם וְיָבֹאוּ.
phrases.en: And in the case of peret and defective clusters? After the poor have gone into the vineyard and come back again.

phrases.he: וּבְזֵיתִים, מִשֶּׁתֵּרֵד רְבִיעָה שְׁנִיָּה.
phrases.en: And in the case of the olive trees? After the descent of the second rainfall.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וַהֲלֹא יֵשׁ שֶׁאֵינָם מוֹסְקִין אֶת זֵיתֵיהֶם אֶלָּא לְאַחַר רְבִיעָה שְׁנִיָּה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah said: But aren’t there those who do not harvest their olives until after the second rainfall?” Rather, once the poor man has gone out [to gather the agricultural gifts taken from olive trees] and cannot bring back with him [more than the value of] four issars.

phrases.he: אֶלָּא כְדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא הֶעָנִי יוֹצֵא וְלֹא יְהֵא מֵבִיא בְּאַרְבָּעָה אִסָּרוֹת
נֶאֱמָנִים עַל הַלֶּקֶט וְעַל הַשִּׁכְחָה וְעַל הַפֵּאָה בִּשְׁעָתָן, וְעַל מַעְשַׂר עָנִי בְּכָל שְׁנָתוֹ.
phrases.en: They [amei haaretz] are to be believed concerning gleanings, the forgotten sheaf and peah during their [harvest] season, and concerning the poor man’s tithe during its whole year.

phrases.he: וּבֶן לֵוִי נֶאֱמָן לְעוֹלָם.
phrases.en: A Levite is always to be trusted.

phrases.he: וְאֵינָן נֶאֱמָנִין אֶלָּא עַל דָּבָר שֶׁבְּנֵי אָדָם נוֹהֲגִין כֵּן
phrases.en: They are only believed in those things which men are accustomed to give them.

phrases.he: נֶאֱמָנִין עַל הַחִטִּים, וְאֵין נֶאֱמָנִין עַל הַקֶּמַח וְלֹא עַל הַפָּת.
phrases.en: They are trusted concerning wheat, but they are not trusted when it is flour or bread.

phrases.he: נֶאֱמָנִין עַל הַשְּׂעוֹרָה שֶׁל אֹרֶז, וְאֵין נֶאֱמָנִין עָלָיו בֵּין חַי בֵּין מְבֻשָּׁל.
phrases.en: They are trusted concerning rice in its husk, but they are not trusted when it is either raw or cooked.

phrases.he: נֶאֱמָנִין עַל הַפּוֹל, וְאֵין נֶאֱמָנִין עַל הַגְּרִיסִין, לֹא חַיִּים וְלֹא מְבֻשָּׁלִין.
phrases.en: They are trusted concerning beans but they are not trusted when they have been pounded, neither raw nor cooked.

phrases.he: נֶאֱמָנִין עַל הַשֶּׁמֶן לוֹמַר שֶׁל מַעְשַׂר עָנִי הוּא, וְאֵין נֶאֱמָנִין עָלָיו לוֹמַר שֶׁל זֵיתֵי נִקּוּף הוּא
phrases.en: They are trusted when concerning oil, to declare that it is from the poor person’s tithe, but they are not trusted over [oil] when they claim that it is from the olives [left on the] top [of the tree.]

phrases.he: נֶאֱמָנִים עַל הַיָּרָק חַי, וְאֵין נֶאֱמָנִים עַל הַמְבֻשָּׁל, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיָה לוֹ דָּבָר מֻעָט, שֶׁכֵּן דֶּרֶךְ בַּעַל הַבַּיִת לִהְיוֹת מוֹצִיא מִלְּפָסוֹ:
phrases.en: They are trusted concerning raw vegetables, but they are not trusted concerning are cooked ones, unless he has only a little bit, for so it was the custom of a householder to take out of his stew-pot [and give a little to the poor].

phrases.he: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין לָעֲנִיִּים בַּגֹּרֶן מֵחֲצִי קַב חִטִּים וְקַב שְׂעוֹרִים.
phrases.en: They may not give to the poor from the threshing-floor less than a half-kav of wheat or a kav of barley.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, חֲצִי קַב.
phrases.en: R. Meir says: [only] half a kav [of barley].

phrases.he: קַב וָחֵצִי כֻסְּמִין, וְקַב גְּרוֹגָרוֹת, אוֹ מָנֶה דְּבֵלָה.
phrases.en: [They must give] a kav and a half of spelt, a kav of dried figs or a maneh of pressed figs.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, פְּרָס. חֲצִי לֹג יָיִן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: half a maneh.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, רְבִיעִית. רְבִיעִית שֶׁמֶן.
phrases.en: [They must give] half a log of wine. Rabbi Akiva says: a quarter.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, שְׁמִינִית.
phrases.en: [They must give] a quarter [log] of oil.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַפֵּרוֹת, אָמַר אַבָּא שָׁאוּל, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּמְכְּרֵם וְיִקַּח בָּהֶם מְזוֹן שְׁתֵּי סְעֻדּוֹת
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: an eighth. As for other kinds of produce: Abba Shaul says, [they must give enough] so that he can sell it and buy food enough for two meals.

phrases.he: מִדָּה זוֹ אֲמוּרָה בְּכֹהֲנִים וּבִלְוִיִּם וּבְיִשְׂרְאֵלִים.
phrases.en: This measure was stated for the priest, Levite and Israelite alike.

phrases.he: הָיָה מַצִּיל, נוֹטֵל מֶחֱצָה וְנוֹתֵן מֶחֱצָה.
phrases.en: If he was saving some [to give to his poor relatives], he can retain half and give the other half away.

phrases.he: הָיָה לוֹ דָבָר מֻעָט, נוֹתֵן לִפְנֵיהֶם, וְהֵן מְחַלְּקִין בֵּינֵיהֶם
phrases.en: If he has only a small amount, then he must place it before them and they then divide it among themselves.

phrases.he: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין לֶעָנִי הָעוֹבֵר מִמָּקוֹם לְמָקוֹם מִכִּכָּר בְּפוּנְדְיוֹן, מֵאַרְבַּע סְאִין בְּסֶלַע.
phrases.en: They may not give a poor person wandering from place to place less than a loaf worth a pundion at a time when four seahs [of wheat cost] one sela.

phrases.he: לָן, נוֹתְנִין לוֹ פַּרְנָסַת לִינָה.
phrases.en: If he spends the night [at a place], they must give him the cost of what he needs for the night.

phrases.he: שָׁבַת, נוֹתְנִין לוֹ מְזוֹן שָׁלשׁ סְעֻדּוֹת.
phrases.en: If he stays over Shabbat they must give him enough food for three meals.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ מְזוֹן שְׁתֵּי סְעֻדּוֹת, לֹא יִטֹּל מִן הַתַּמְחוּי.
phrases.en: He who has the money for two meals, he may not take anything from the charity dish.

phrases.he: מְזוֹן אַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה סְעֻדּוֹת, לֹא יִטֹּל מִן הַקֻּפָּה.
phrases.en: And if he has enough money for fourteen meals, he may not take any support from the communal fund.

phrases.he: וְהַקֻּפָּה נִגְבֵּית בִּשְׁנַיִם, וּמִתְחַלֶּקֶת בִּשְׁלשָׁה
phrases.en: The communal fund is collected by two and distributed by three people.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ מָאתַיִם זוּז, לֹא יִטֹּל לֶקֶט שִׁכְחָה וּפֵאָה וּמַעְשַׂר עָנִי.
phrases.en: One who possesses two hundred zuz, may not take gleanings” the forgotten sheaf, peah or the poor man’s tithe.

phrases.he: הָיוּ לוֹ מָאתַיִם חָסֵר דִּינָר, אֲפִלּוּ אֶלֶף נוֹתְנִין לוֹ כְאַחַת, הֲרֵי זֶה יִטֹּל.
phrases.en: If he possesses two hundred minus one denar, then even if a thousand [men] each give him at the same time, he may accept.

phrases.he: הָיוּ מְמֻשְׁכָּנִים לְבַעַל חוֹבוֹ אוֹ לִכְתֻבַּת אִשְׁתּוֹ, הֲרֵי זֶה יִטֹּל.
phrases.en: If he had [two hundred zuz] mortgaged to a creditor or to his wife’s ketubah, he may take.

phrases.he: אֵין מְחַיְּבִין אוֹתוֹ לִמְכֹּר אֶת בֵּיתוֹ וְאֶת כְּלֵי תַשְׁמִישׁוֹ
phrases.en: They do not force him to sell his house or his tools.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ חֲמִשִּׁים זוּז וְהוּא נוֹשֵׂא וְנוֹתֵן בָּהֶם, הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִטֹּל.
phrases.en: One who has fifty zuz and he is using them for his business, he must not take.

phrases.he: וְכָל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לִטֹּל וְנוֹטֵל, אֵינוֹ נִפְטָר מִן הָעוֹלָם עַד שֶׁיִּצְטָרֵךְ לַבְּרִיּוֹת.
phrases.en: And anyone who does not need to take [charity] and yet takes, will not depart from this world before he actually needs [charity] from others.

phrases.he: וְכָל מִי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִטֹּל וְאֵינוֹ נוֹטֵל, אֵינוֹ מֵת מִן הַזִּקְנָה עַד שֶׁיְּפַרְנֵס אֲחֵרִים מִשֶּׁלּוֹ, וְעָלָיו הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר בָּרוּךְ הַגֶּבֶר אֲשֶׁר יִבְטַח בַּה' וְהָיָה ה' מִבְטַחוֹ (ירמיה יז).
phrases.en: And anyone who needs to take and does not take, will not die of old age until he supports others with his own money. Concerning him the verse says: “Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord and whose hope is the Lord” (Jeremiah 17:7). And so too a judge who judges in truth according to its truth.

phrases.he: וְכֵן דַּיָּן שֶׁדָּן דִּין אֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ.
phrases.en: And anyone who is not lame or blind but pretends to be as one of these, he will not die of old age before he actually becomes one of these, as it is said, “He who searches for evil, it shall come upon him” (Proverbs 11:27) and it is also said: “Righteousness, righteousness shall you pursue" (Deuteronomy 16:20).

phrases.he: וְכָל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ לֹא חִגֵּר, וְלֹא סוּמָא, וְלֹא פִסֵּחַ, וְעוֹשֶׂה עַצְמוֹ כְּאַחַד מֵהֶם, אֵינוֹ מֵת מִן הַזִּקְנָה עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כְּאֶחָד מֵהֶם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים טז) צֶדֶק צֶדֶק תִּרְדֹּף.
phrases.en: And any judge who accepts a bribe or who perverts justice will not die in old age before his eyes have become dim, as it is said: “And you shall not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of those who have sight.

phrases.he: וְכָל דַּיָּן שֶׁלּוֹקֵחַ שֹׁחַד וּמַטֶּה אֶת הַדִּין, אֵינוֹ מֵת מִן הַזִּקְנָה עַד שֶׁעֵינָיו כֵּהוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמות כג) וְשֹׁחַד לֹא תִקָּח כִּי הַשֹּׁחַד יְעַוֵּר פִּקְחִים וְגוֹ':סְלִיק מַסֶּכֶת פֵּאָה
phrases.en: (Exodus 23:8)”

phrases.he: הַקַּלִּין שֶׁבַּדְּמַאי, הַשִּׁיתִין, וְהָרִימִין וְהָעֻזְרָדִין, וּבְנוֹת שׁוּחַ, וּבְנוֹת שִׁקְמָה, וְנוֹבְלוֹת הַתְּמָרָה, וְהַגֻּפְנִין, וְהַנִּצְפָּה.
phrases.en: The [following] are treated leniently in regard to [the rules of] demai: unripe figs, wild jujuba, azarolus, wild white figs, young sycamore figs, fallen dates, fennel and capers.

phrases.he: וּבִיהוּדָה, הָאוֹג, וְהַחֹמֶץ שֶׁבִּיהוּדָה, וְהַכֻּסְבָּר.
phrases.en: In Judea also sumac, Judean vinegar, and coriander.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כָּל הַשִּׁיתִין פְּטוּרִין, חוּץ מִשֶּׁל דּוּפְרָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: all unripe figs are exempt, except for those from a tree that bears fruit twice a year.

phrases.he: כָּל הָרִימִין פְּטוּרִין, חוּץ מֵרִימֵי שִׁקְמוֹנָה.
phrases.en: All wild jujuba are exempt, except the wild jujuba of Shikmonah.

phrases.he: כָּל בְּנוֹת שִׁקְמָה פְּטוּרוֹת, חוּץ מִן הַמֻּסְטָפוֹס
phrases.en: All young sycamore figs are exempt, except those that have been scarified.

phrases.he: הַדְּמַאי אֵין לוֹ חֹמֶשׁ, וְאֵין לוֹ בִעוּר, וְנֶאֱכָל לְאוֹנֵן, וְנִכְנָס לִירוּשָׁלַיִם וְיוֹצֵא, וּמְאַבְּדִין אֶת מִעוּטוֹ בַּדְּרָכִים, וְנוֹתְנוֹ לְעַם הָאָרֶץ, וְיֹאכַל כְּנֶגְדּוֹ.
phrases.en: The [second tithe of] demai is not subject to [the rules of adding a] fifth. It has no mandated time of removal. It may be eaten by an onen. It may be brought into Jerusalem and taken out again. They may allow a small amount to be lost on the road. One may give it to an am haaretz and consume its equivalent in Jerusalem.

phrases.he: וּמְחַלְּלִים אוֹתוֹ כֶּסֶף עַל כֶּסֶף, נְחֹשֶׁת עַל נְחשֶׁת, כֶּסֶף עַל נְחֹשֶׁת, וּנְחֹשֶׁת עַל הַפֵּרוֹת, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיַּחֲזֹר וְיִפְדֶּה אֶת הַפֵּרוֹת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: [Second tithe money of demai] may be redeemed silver [coins] for [other] silver [coins], copper [coins] for [other] copper [coins], silver for copper, and copper for produce, provided that the produce is again redeemed for money, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, יַעֲלֶה הַפֵּרוֹת וְיֵאָכְלוּ בִירוּשָׁלָיִם:
phrases.en: But the sages say: the produce itself must be brought up and eaten in Jerusalem.

phrases.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ לְזֶרַע וְלִבְהֵמָה, קֶמַח לְעוֹרוֹת, שֶׁמֶן לְנֵר, שֶׁמֶן לָסוּךְ בּוֹ אֶת הַכֵּלִים, פָּטוּר מִן הַדְּמַאי.
phrases.en: If a man bought [grain from an am haaretz] to be used for seed or for animal [feed], flour for hides, oil for a lamp, or oil for greasing utensils, it is exempt from [the rules of] demai.

phrases.he: מִכְּזִיב וּלְהַלָּן, פָּטוּר מִן הַדְּמַאי.
phrases.en: [Produce grown] beyond Cheziv and north is exempt from [the rules of] demai.

phrases.he: חַלַּת עַם הָאָרֶץ, וְהַמְדֻמָּע, וְהַלָּקוּחַ בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, וּשְׁיָרֵי הַמְּנָחוֹת, פְּטוּרִין מִן הַדְּמַאי.
phrases.en: The hallah of an am haaretz, produce mixed with terumah, produce bought with second tithe money, and the leftovers of minhah offerings are exempt from [the rules of] demai.

phrases.he: שֶׁמֶן עָרֵב, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מְחַיְּבִין, וּבֵית הִלֵּל פּוֹטְרִין
phrases.en: Oil spiced [with spices from an am haaretz]: Bet Shammai makes it liable [to the rules of demai]. But Bet Hillel exempts it.

phrases.he: הַדְּמַאי, מְעָרְבִין בּוֹ, וּמִשְׁתַּתְּפִין בּוֹ, וּמְבָרְכִין עָלָיו, וּמְזַמְּנִין עָלָיו, וּמַפְרִישִׁין אוֹתוֹ עָרוֹם, בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת.
phrases.en: Demai may be used to make an eruv, and to make an [alley] partnership, and they recite a blessing over it, and they make an invitation [to recite Birkat Hamazon] over it, and one may separate [tithes] from it even when one is naked, or when it is twilight [on the eve of Shabbat].

phrases.he: הָא אִם הִקְדִּים מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי לָרִאשׁוֹן, אֵין בְּכָךְ כְּלוּם.
phrases.en: And if he took out second tithe from it before the first tithe, it doesn’t matter.

phrases.he: שֶׁמֶן שֶׁהַגַּרְדִּי סָךְ בְּאֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו, חַיָּב בִּדְּמַאי.
phrases.en: The oil with which the weaver greases his fingers is liable to [the rules of] demai, but [the oil] which the wool-comber puts on the wool is exempt from [the rules of] demai.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁהַסּוֹרֵק נוֹתֵן בַּצֶּמֶר, פָּטוּר מִן הַדְּמָאי
וְאֵלּוּ דְבָרִים מִתְעַשְּׂרִין דְּמַאי בְּכָל מָקוֹם.
phrases.en: The following things must be tithed as demai in all places: pressed figs, dates, carobs, rice, and cumin.

phrases.he: הַדְּבֵלָה, וְהַתְּמָרִים, וְהֶחָרוּבִים, הָאֹרֶז, וְהַכַּמּוֹן.
phrases.en: As to rice from outside the land [of Israel], whoever uses it is exempt from tithing it.

phrases.he: הָאֹרֶז שֶׁבְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ, כָּל הַמִּשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ פָּטוּר
הַמְקַבֵּל עָלָיו לִהְיוֹת נֶאֱמָן, מְעַשֵּׂר אֶת שֶׁהוּא אוֹכֵל, וְאֶת שֶׁהוּא מוֹכֵר, וְאֶת שֶׁהוּא לוֹקֵחַ, וְאֵינוֹ מִתְאָרֵחַ אֵצֶל עַם הָאָרֶץ.
phrases.en: One who accepts upon himself to be trustworthy (ne’eman), must tithe whatever he eats and whatever he sells and whatever he buys, and he may not be the guest of an am haaretz.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף הַמִּתְאָרֵחַ אֵצֶל עַם הָאָרֶץ נֶאֱמָן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: even one who is the guest of an am haaretz can still be considered trustworthy.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, עַל עַצְמוֹ אֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן, כֵּיצַד יְהֵא נֶאֱמָן עַל שֶׁל אֲחֵרִים:
phrases.en: They said to him: He is not trustworthy in respect of himself! How can he be considered trustworthy in respect of others?

phrases.he: הַמְקַבֵּל עָלָיו לִהְיוֹת חָבֵר, אֵינוֹ מוֹכֵר לְעַם הָאָרֶץ לַח וְיָבֵשׁ, וְאֵינוֹ לוֹקֵחַ מִמֶּנּוּ לַח, וְאֵינוֹ מִתְאָרֵח אֵצֶל עַם הָאָרֶץ, וְלֹא מְאָרְחוֹ אֶצְלוֹ בִּכְסוּתוֹ.
phrases.en: One who takes upon himself to become a “chaver” may not sell to an am haaretz either moist or dry [produce], nor may he buy from him moist [produce], nor may he be the guest of an am haaretz, nor may he host an am haaretz as a guest while [the am haaretz] is wearing his own garment.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף לֹא יְגַדֵּל בְּהֵמָה דַקָּה, וְלֹא יְהֵא פָרוּץ בִּנְדָרִים וּבִשְׂחוֹק, וְלֹא יְהֵא מִטַּמֵּא לְמֵתִים, וּמְשַׁמֵּשׁ בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: he may not also raise small animals, nor may make a lot of vows or merriment, nor may he defile himself by contact with the dead. Rather he should be an attendant at the house of study.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, לֹא בָאוּ אֵלּוּ לַכְּלָל:
phrases.en: They said to him: these [requirements] do not come within the general rule [of being a chaver].

phrases.he: הַנַּחְתּוֹמִים, לֹא חִיְּבוּ אוֹתָם חֲכָמִים לְהַפְרִישׁ אֶלָּא כְדֵי תְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר וְחַלָּה.
phrases.en: Bakers the sages did not obligate them to separate [from demai produce] any more than suffices for terumat maaser and for hallah.

phrases.he: הַחֶנְוָנִים אֵינָן רַשָּׁאִין לִמְכֹּר אֶת הַדְּמַאי.
phrases.en: Grocers may not sell demai [produce].

phrases.he: כָּל הַמַּשְׁפִּיעִין בְּמִדָּה גַסָּה, רַשָּׁאִין לִמְכֹּר אֶת הַדְּמַאי.
phrases.en: All [merchants] who supply in large quantities may sell demai.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ הֵן הַמַּשְׁפִּיעִין בְּמִדָּה גַסָּה, כְּגוֹן הַסִּיטוֹנוֹת וּמוֹכְרֵי תְבוּאָה
phrases.en: Who are those who supply in large quantities? Those such as wholesalers and grain-sellers.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, אֶת שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לְהִמָּדֵד בְּגַסָּה וּמְדָדוֹ בְדַקָּה, טְפֵלָה דַקָּה לַגַּסָּה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: [if produce] which is usually measured out [for sale] in a large [quantity] was measured out in a small [quantity], the small quantity is treated as if it was a large [quantity].

phrases.he: אֶת שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לְהִמָּדֵד בְּדַקָּה וּמָדַד בַּגַסָּה, טְפֵלָה גַסָּה לַדַּקָּה.
phrases.en: If [produce] which is usually measured out for sale in a small [quantity] was measured out in a large [quantity], the large [quantity] is treated as if it was a small [quantity].

phrases.he: אֵיזוֹ הִיא מִדָּה גַסָּה, בְּיָבֵשׁ, שְׁלשֶׁת קַבִּין, וּבְלַח, דִּינָר.
phrases.en: What is considered a large quantity? For dry [produce] three kavs, and for liquids, the value of one dinar.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, סַלֵּי תְאֵנִים וְסַלֵּי עֲנָבִים וְקֻפּוֹת שֶׁל יָרָק, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהוּא מוֹכְרָן אַכְסָרָה, פָּטוּר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: baskets of figs, baskets of grapes, and bushels of vegetables when he sells them in lumps, they are exempt [from the rules of demai].

phrases.he: מַאֲכִילִין אֶת הָעֲנִיִּים דְּמַאי, וְאֶת הָאַכְסַנְיָא דְּמַאי.
phrases.en: They may feed demai to the poor and to guests (alt.

phrases.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָיָה מַאֲכִיל אֶת פּוֹעֲלָיו דְּמַאי. גַּבָּאֵי צְדָקָה,
phrases.en: passing troops). Rabban Gamaliel used to feed demai to his workmen.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, נוֹתְנִין אֶת הַמְעֻשָּׂר לְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מְעַשֵּׂר, וְאֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְעֻשָּׂר לִמְעַשֵּׂר.
phrases.en: [As for] charity collectors: Bet Shammai says: they should give tithed [produce] to one who doesn’t tithe, and untithed [produce] to one who does tithe.

phrases.he: נִמְצְאוּ כָל הָאָדָם אוֹכְלִין מְתֻקָּן.
phrases.en: In this way it will turn out that every one will eat [produce] that has been fixed (tithed).

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, גּוֹבִין סְתָם וּמְחַלְּקִין סְתָם, וְהָרוֹצֶה לְתַקֵּן יְתַקֵּן:
phrases.en: But the sages say: they may collect indiscriminately and distribute indiscriminately. And one who wishes to fix [his produce by tithing it], let him fix it.

phrases.he: הָרוֹצֶה לַחֲזֹם עֲלֵי יָרָק לְהָקֵל מִמַּשָּׂאוֹ, לֹא יַשְׁלִיךְ עַד שֶׁיְּעַשֵּׂר.
phrases.en: One who wants to cut off leaves of vegetables in order to lighten his burden, he may not throw them down until he has [first] tithed them.

phrases.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ יָרָק מִן הַשּׁוּק וְנִמְלַךְ לְהַחֲזִיר, לֹא יַחֲזִיר עַד שֶׁיְּעַשֵּׂר, שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְחֻסָּר אֶלָּא מִנְיָן.
phrases.en: One who takes vegetables from the market [with the intention of buying them], and then decides to put them back, he should not put them back until he has [first] tithed them, for nothing is missing [after they are tithed] except for their quantity.

phrases.he: הָיָה עוֹמֵד וְלוֹקֵחַ וְרָאָה טֹעַן אַחֵר יָפֶה מִמֶּנּוּ, מֻתָּר לְהַחֲזִיר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא מָשָׁךְ
phrases.en: But if he was standing [there and deciding what to] buy and then saw another load of better quality, he may put them back [untithed], since he had not yet drawn them into his possession.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹצֵא פֵרוֹת בַּדֶּרֶךְ וּנְטָלָן לְאָכְלָן, וְנִמְלַךְ לְהַצְנִיעַ, לֹא יַצְנִיעַ עַד שֶׁיְּעַשֵּׂר.
phrases.en: If one finds produce on the road and picks it up in order to eat it, and then decides to hide it, he may not hide it unless he has [first] tithed it.

phrases.he: וְאִם מִתְּחִלָּה נְטָלָן בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא יֹאבֵדוּ, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: But if from the outset he picked it up only in order to guard it against being destroyed, he is exempt [from tithing it].

phrases.he: כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין אָדָם רַשַּׁאי לְמָכְרוֹ דְּמַאי, לֹא יִשְׁלַח לַחֲבֵרוֹ דְּמַאי.
phrases.en: Any produce which one may not sell [in the condition of] demai, he may not send it [as a gift] to his friend [in the condition of] demai.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר בְּוַדַּאי, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיּוֹדִיעֶנּוּ
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose permits [one to send as a gift produce] that is certainly untithed, on condition that he makes the matter known to the recipient.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹלִיךְ חִטִּים לְטוֹחֵן כּוּתִי אוֹ לְטוֹחֵן עַם הָאָרֶץ, בְּחֶזְקָתָן לַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת וְלַשְּׁבִיעִית.
phrases.en: One who takes his wheat to a Samaritan miller or to an am haaretz miller, [the wheat when ground] retains its former status in respect of tithes and the law of seventh year produce.

phrases.he: לְטוֹחֵן עוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים, דְּמַאי.
phrases.en: [But if he carried it] to a Gentile miller, [the wheat when ground has the status of] demai.

phrases.he: הַמַּפְקִיד פֵּרוֹתָיו אֵצֶל הַכּוּתִי אוֹ אֵצֶל עַם הָאָרֶץ, בְּחֶזְקָתָן לַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת וְלַשְּׁבִיעִית.
phrases.en: One who deposited his produce with a Samaritan or am haaretz, [the produce] retains its former status in respect of tithes and the law of seventh year produce.

phrases.he: אֵצֶל הָעוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים, כְּפֵרוֹתָיו.
phrases.en: [But if he left it] with a Gentile, it is like the produce of the Gentile.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, דְּמָאי:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: [it becomes] demai.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹתֵן לְפֻנְדָּקִית, מְעַשֵּׂר אֶת שֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן לָהּ, וְאֶת שֶׁהוּא נוֹטֵל מִמֶּנָּה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁחֲשׁוּדָה לַחֲלֹף.
phrases.en: One who gives [produce] to an innkeeper [to prepare it for food], he must tithe what he gives to her and what he takes back from her, because she is suspected of exchanging it [with her own produce].

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, אֵין אָנוּ אַחֲרָאִין לָרַמָּאִין, אֵינוֹ מְעַשֵּׂר אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁהוּא נוֹטֵל מִמֶּנָּה בִּלְבָד:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose said: we are not responsible for deceivers. Rather, he must tithe only that which he takes from her.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹתֵן לַחֲמוֹתוֹ, מְעַשֵּׂר אֶת שֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן לָהּ, וְאֶת שֶׁהוּא נוֹטֵל מִמֶּנָּה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא חֲשׁוּדָה לַחֲלֹף אֶת הַמִּתְקַלְקֵל.
phrases.en: One who gives [produce] to his mother-in-law [to prepare it], he must tithe what he gives to her and what he takes back from her, because she is suspected of changing any [food] which has spoiled.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, רוֹצָה הִיא בְתַקָּנַת בִּתָּהּ וּבוֹשָׁה מֵחֲתָנָהּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah said: she desires the welfare of her daughter and is ashamed [of serving spoiled food] to her son-in-law.

phrases.he: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּנוֹתֵן לַחֲמוֹתוֹ שְׁבִיעִית, שֶׁאֵינָהּ חֲשׁוּדָה לְהַחֲלִיף לְהַאֲכִיל אֶת בִּתָּהּ שְׁבִיעִית
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah agrees [with the other sages] that if one gives his mother-in-law seventh year produce, she is not suspected of changing it and giving her daughter to eat of seventh year produce.

phrases.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ פֵּרוֹת מִמִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן עַל הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, וְשָׁכַח לְעַשְּׂרָן, וְשׁוֹאֲלוֹ בְשַׁבָּת, יֹאכַל עַל פִּיו.
phrases.en: One who buys produce from someone who is not trustworthy in respect of tithes, and he forgot to tithe it, and he asked [the seller] on Shabbat [if they were tithed], he may eat based on his word.

phrases.he: חָשְׁכָה מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת, לֹא יֹאכַל עַד שֶׁיְּעַשֵּׂר. לֹא מְצָאוֹ,
phrases.en: At nightfall of Shabbat, he may not eat of it unless he had first tithed it.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ אֶחָד שֶׁאֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן עַל הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, מְעֻשָּׂרִין הֵן, אוֹכֵל עַל פִּיו.
phrases.en: If he could not find the seller, and another person who was not trustworthy in respect of tithes said to him “they are tithed,” he may eat of it at his word.

phrases.he: חָשְׁכָה מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת, לֹא יֹאכַל עַד שֶׁיְּעַשֵּׂר.
phrases.en: At nightfall of Shabbat, he may not eat of it unless he had first tithed it.

phrases.he: תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר שֶׁל דְּמַאי שֶׁחָזְרָה לִמְקוֹמָהּ, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שְׁזוּרִי אוֹמֵר, אַף בְּחֹל שׁוֹאֲלוֹ וְאוֹכְלוֹ עַל פִּיו
phrases.en: Terumat maaser of demai which had become mixed up again [with the produce] from which it had been taken: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says: even on a week day he may ask the seller and eat based on his word.

phrases.he: הַמַּדִּיר אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ שֶׁיֹּאכַל אֶצְלוֹ, וְהוּא אֵינוֹ מַאֲמִינוֹ עַל הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, אוֹכֵל עִמּוֹ בַּשַּׁבָּת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַאֲמִינוֹ עַל הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר לוֹ מְעֻשָּׂרִין הֵן.
phrases.en: One who vowed [that his friend could not benefit from him] unless he eats with him, and the friend does not trust him in respect of tithes, he may eat with him on the first Shabbat even though he does not trust him in respect of tithes, provided that his friend said to him that the food had been tithed.

phrases.he: וּבְשַׁבָּת שְׁנִיָּה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנָּדַר מִמֶּנּוּ הֲנָיָה, לֹא יֹאכַל עַד שֶׁיְּעַשֵּׂר
phrases.en: But on the second week, even though he had vowed that he would not benefit from him, he may not eat with him unless he first tithed [the produce].

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אֵין אָדָם צָרִיךְ לִקְרוֹת שֵׁם לְמַעְשַׂר עָנִי שֶׁל דְּמַאי.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: a man need not designate the poor man’s tithe of demai.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, קוֹרֵא שֵׁם וְאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְהַפְרִישׁ:
phrases.en: But the sages say: he must designate it, but he need not separate.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁקָּרָא שֵׁם לִתְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר שֶׁל דְּמַאי וּלְמַעְשַׂר עָנִי שֶׁל וַדַּאי, לֹא יִטְּלֵם בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: One who had designated the terumat maaser of demai, or the poor man’s tithe of produce that had certainly not been tithed, he should not separate them on Shabbat.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיָה כֹהֵן אוֹ עָנִי לְמוּדִים לֶאֱכֹל אֶצְלוֹ, יָבֹאוּ וְיֹאכְלוּ, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיּוֹדִיעֵם
phrases.en: But if the priest or the poor man regularly ate with him, they may come and eat provided that he informs them.

phrases.he: הָאוֹמֵר לְמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן עַל הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, קַח לִי מִמִּי שֶׁהוּא נֶאֱמָן וּמִמִּי שֶׁהוּא מְעַשֵּׂר, אֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן.
phrases.en: One who says to another who is not trustworthy in respect of tithes: “Buy [produce] for me from one who is trustworthy or from one who gives tithes,” [the messenger] may not be trusted.

phrases.he: מֵאִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי, הֲרֵי זֶה נֶאֱמָן.
phrases.en: “Buy it for me from so-and-so,” he is to be trusted.

phrases.he: הָלַךְ לִקַּח מִמֶּנּוּ, וְאָמַר לוֹ לֹא מְצָאתִיו וְלָקַחְתִּי לְךָ מֵאַחֵר שֶׁהוּא נֶאֱמָן, אֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן
phrases.en: If he went to buy it from him [and then came back] and said: “I did not find him, so I bought for you from another man who is trustworthy,” he may not be trusted.

phrases.he: הַנִּכְנָס לְעִיר וְאֵינוֹ מַכִּיר אָדָם שָׁם, אָמַר, מִי כָּאן נֶאֱמָן. מִי כָּאן מְעַשֵּׂר.
phrases.en: One enters a city and doesn’t know anyone. He says: “Who here is trustworthy? Who gives tithes here?” One person one responds: “I am.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ אֶחָד, אֲנִי, אֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן.
phrases.en: He may not be trusted.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ, אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי נֶאֱמָן, הֲרֵי זֶה נֶאֱמָן. הָלַךְ לִקַּח מִמֶּנּוּ,
phrases.en: [But if] he replied: “So-and-so is trustworthy,” he may be trusted.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ, מִי כָּאן מוֹכֵר יָשָׁן.
phrases.en: He went to buy from so-and-so, and he asked him: “Who here sells aged produce?” and so-and-so replied: “He sent you to me,” though they appear to be repaying each other, they may be trusted.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ, מִי שֶׁשְּׁלָחֲךָ אֶצְלִי, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵן כְּגוֹמְלִין זֶה אֶת זֶה, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ נֶאֱמָנִין:
הַחַמָּרִים שֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ לְעִיר, אָמַר אֶחָד, שֶׁלִּי חָדָשׁ וְשֶׁל חֲבֵרִי יָשָׁן, שֶׁלִּי אֵינוֹ מְתֻקָּן וְשֶׁל חֲבֵרִי מְתֻקָּן, אֵינָן נֶאֱמָנִין.
phrases.en: If donkey-drivers entered a city and one of them declared: “My produce is new but my friend’s produce is old,” or, “My produce has not been tithed but my friend’s produce has been tithed,” they may not be trusted.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, נֶאֱמָנִין:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: they may be trusted.

phrases.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ מִן הַנַּחְתּוֹם, כֵּיצַד הוּא מְעַשֵּׂר.
phrases.en: One who buys bread from a baker how should he tithe? He should take sufficient for the terumat maaser and for hallah and say: “A hundredth part of what is here shall be tithe on this side, and what is nearest to it shall be the rest of the tithe.

phrases.he: נוֹטֵל כְּדֵי תְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר וְחַלָּה, וְאוֹמֵר, אֶחָד מִמֵּאָה מִמַּה שֶּׁיֶּשׁ כָּאן, הֲרֵי בְצַד זֶה מַעֲשֵׂר, וּשְׁאָר מַעֲשֵׂר סָמוּךְ לוֹ, זֶה שֶׁעָשִׂיתִי מַעֲשֵׂר עָשׂוּי תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר עָלָיו, וְהַשְּׁאָר חַלָּה, וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בִּצְפוֹנוֹ אוֹ בִדְרוֹמוֹ, וּמְחֻלָּל עַל הַמָּעוֹת
phrases.en: That which I made tithe will become terumat maaser for the rest, the remainder will be hallah, and the second tithe tithe is to the north or to the south of it and that will be exchanged for money.”

phrases.he: הָרוֹצֶה לְהַפְרִישׁ תְּרוּמָה וּתְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר כְּאַחַת, נוֹטֵל אֶחָד מִשְּׁלשִׁים וְשָׁלשׁ וּשְׁלִישׁ, וְאוֹמֵר, אֶחָד מִמֵּאָה מִמַּה שֶּׁיֶּשׁ כָּאן, הֲרֵי זֶה בְּצַד זֶה חֻלִּין, וְהַשְּׁאָר תְּרוּמָה עַל הַכֹּל.
phrases.en: One who wishes to separate terumah and the terumat maaser together:He should take one thirty third and say: One hundredth part of what is here, on this side is non-sacred produce (hullin), and the rest shall be terumah for the whole.

phrases.he: וּמֵאָה חֻלִּין שֶׁיֶּשׁ כָּאן, הֲרֵי זֶה בְּצַד זֶה מַעֲשֵׂר, וּשְׁאָר מַעֲשֵׂר סָמוּךְ לוֹ, זֶה שֶׁעָשִׂיתִי מַעֲשֵׂר עָשׂוּי תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר עָלָיו, וְהַשְּׁאָר חַלָּה, וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בִּצְפוֹנוֹ אוֹ בִדְרוֹמוֹ, וּמְחֻלָּל עַל הַמָּעוֹת
phrases.en: And the one hundred parts of non-sacred produce which is here on this side shall be tithe, and the rest that is next to it is tithe. That which I made tithe shall become the terumat maaser for it. The remainder will be hallah, and the second tithe tithe is to the north or to the south of it and that will be exchanged for money.”

phrases.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ מִן הַנַּחְתּוֹם, מְעַשֵּׂר מִן הַחַמָּה עַל הַצּוֹנֶנֶת, וּמִן הַצּוֹנֶנֶת עַל הַחַמָּה, אֲפִלּוּ מִטְּפוּסִין הַרְבֵּה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: One who bought [bread] from a baker, he may give tithe from hot bread for cold bread or from cold bread for hot bread, even when they are of various moulds, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹסֵר, שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר, חִטִּים שֶׁל אֶמֶשׁ הָיוּ מִשֶּׁל אֶחָד, וְשֶׁל הַיּוֹם הָיוּ מִשֶּׁל אַחֵר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah prohibits it, because I say that yesterday’s wheat was bought from one man and today’s wheat from another man.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹסֵר בִּתְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר, וּמַתִּיר בְּחַלָּה
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon prohibits it in the case of terumat maaser, but permits it in the case of hallah.

phrases.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ מִן הַפַּלְטֵר, מְעַשֵּׂר מִכָּל טְפוּס וּטְפוּס, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: If one bought from a bread seller he must tithe every mould [separately], the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מֵאַחַת עַל הַכֹּל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: he may give tithes from one mould for all the others.

phrases.he: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּלוֹקֵחַ מִן הַמַּנְפּוֹל, שֶׁהוּא מְעַשֵּׂר מִכָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד
phrases.en: But Rabbi Judah agrees that one who bought from a monopolist he must tithe every mould [separately].

phrases.he: הַלּוֹקֵח מִן הֶעָנִי, וְכֵן הֶעָנִי שֶׁנָּתְנוּ לוֹ פְרוּסוֹת פַּת אוֹ פִלְחֵי דְבֵלָה, מְעַשֵּׂר מִכָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
phrases.en: One who buys from a poor man, and similarly a poor man to whom they given slices of bread or pieces of fig-cake, he must tithe every piece.

phrases.he: וּבִתְמָרִים וּבִגְרוֹגָרוֹת, בּוֹלֵל וְנוֹטֵל.
phrases.en: But in the case of dates and dried figs he may mix them together and take [the tithes from the mixture].

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַמַּתָּנָה מְרֻבָּה, אֲבָל בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַמַּתָּנָה מֻעֶטֶת, מְעַשֵּׂר מִכָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah said: When is this so? When the amount [of dates or dried figs] given to the poor man was large; but when the amount was small, he must tithe each separately.

phrases.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ מִן הַסִּיטוֹן וְחָזַר וְלָקַח מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁנִיָּה, לֹא יְעַשֵּׂר מִזֶּה עַל זֶה, אֲפִלּוּ מֵאוֹתוֹ הַסּוּג, אֲפִלּוּ מֵאוֹתוֹ הַמִּין.
phrases.en: One who buys from a wholesaler, and then buys from him again, he may not give tithes from the one [purchase] for the other, even when both came from the same basket and even from the same kind.

phrases.he: נֶאֱמָן הַסִּיטוֹן לוֹמַר, מִשֶּׁל אֶחָד הֵם
phrases.en: But the wholesale merchant may be trusted if he says that both came from the same one.

phrases.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ מִבַּעַל הַבַּיִת וְחָזַר וְלָקַח מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁנִיָּה, מְעַשֵּׂר מִזֶּה עַל זֶה, אֲפִלּוּ מִשְּׁתֵּי קֻפּוֹת, אֲפִלּוּ מִשְּׁתֵּי עֲיָרוֹת.
phrases.en: One who buys from a field owner, and then buys from him again, he may give tithes from the one [purchase] for the other, even when [the purchases come] from two baskets and even from two towns.

phrases.he: בַּעַל הַבַּיִת שֶׁהָיָה מוֹכֵר יָרָק בַּשּׁוּק, בִּזְמַן שֶׁמְּבִיאִין לוֹ מִגַּנּוֹתָיו, מְעַשֵּׂר מֵאַחַת עַל הַכֹּל.
phrases.en: A field owner who was selling vegetables in the market: when he brings them from his garden, he may tithe from one for all; But [if he brings them] from other gardens, he must tithe each lot separately.

phrases.he: וּמִגַּנּוֹת אֲחֵרוֹת, מְעַשֵּׂר מִכָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד
הַלּוֹקֵחַ טֶבֶל מִשְּׁנֵי מְקוֹמוֹת, מְעַשֵּׂר מִזֶּה עַל זֶה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ, אֵין אָדָם רַשַּׁאי לִמְכֹּר טֶבֶל אֶלָּא לְצֹרֶךְ:
phrases.en: One who buys untithed produce from two places, he may tithe from one lot for the other. Although they have said one may not sell untithed produce except in the case of necessity.

phrases.he: מְעַשְּׂרִין מִשֶּׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל שֶׁל נָכְרִי, מִשֶּׁל נָכְרִי עַל שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, מִשֶּׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל שֶׁל כּוּתִים, מִשֶּׁל כּוּתִים עַל שֶׁל כּוּתִים.
phrases.en: They may give tithes from produce from a Jew for produce [bought] from a Gentile, from produce [bought] from a Gentile for produce from a Jew, from produce [bought] from a Jew for produce [bought] from Samaritans, and from produce [bought] from Samaritans for produce [bought] from [other] Samaritans.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹסֵר מִשֶּׁל כּוּתִים עַל שֶׁל כּוּתִים
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer prohibits [tithing] from produce [bought] from Samaritans for produce [bought] from [other] Samaritans.

phrases.he: עָצִיץ נָקוּב, הֲרֵי זֶה כָּאָרֶץ.
phrases.en: A perforated pot is considered like land.

phrases.he: תָּרַם מֵהָאָרֶץ עַל עָצִיץ נָקוּב, מֵעָצִיץ נָקוּב עַל הָאָרֶץ, תְּרוּמָתוֹ תְּרוּמָה.
phrases.en: If one gave terumah from [produce grown in] the soil for [produce grown in] a perforated pot, or from [produce grown in] a perforated pot for [produce grown in] the soil, his terumah is terumah.

phrases.he: מִשֶּׁאֵינוֹ נָקוּב עַל הַנָּקוּב, תְּרוּמָה, וְיַחֲזֹר וְיִתְרֹם.
phrases.en: [If he gave terumah] from [produce grown in] a pot that was not perforated for [produce grown in] a pot that was perforated, [it is] terumah, but he must go back and give terumah again.

phrases.he: מִן הַנָּקוּב עַל שֶׁאֵינוֹ נָקוּב, תְּרוּמָה, וְלֹא תֵאָכֵל עַד שֶׁיּוֹצִיא עָלֶיהָ תְּרוּמוֹת וּמַעַשְׂרוֹת
phrases.en: [If he gave terumah] from [produce grown in] a perforated pot for [produce grown in] a pot which was not perforated, [it is] terumah, but it may not be eaten until he first gives terumah and tithes for it.

phrases.he: תָּרַם מִן הַדְּמַאי עַל הַדְּמַאי, מִדְּמַאי עַל הַוַּדַּאי, תְּרוּמָה, וְיַחֲזֹר וְיִתְרֹם.
phrases.en: If one gave terumah from [produce of] demai for [other produce of] demai, or from [produce of] demai for [produce] which was certainly untithed, [this becomes] terumah, but he must give terumah over again.

phrases.he: מִן הַוַּדַּאי עַל הַדְּמַאי, תְּרוּמָה, וְלֹא תֵאָכֵל עַד שֶׁיּוֹצִיא עָלֶיהָ תְּרוּמוֹת וּמַעַשְׂרוֹת
phrases.en: [If he gave terumah] from [produce] which was certainly untithed for [produce of] demai, [this becomes] terumah, but it may not be eaten until he first gives terumah and tithes for it.

phrases.he: הַמְקַבֵּל שָׂדֶה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, מִן הַנָּכְרִי וּמִן הַכּוּתִי, יְחַלֵּק לִפְנֵיהֶם.
phrases.en: One who has received a field from a Jew, or from a Gentile, or from a Samaritan [for a share in the produce], he divvies up the produce in front of them [without first separating tithes].

phrases.he: הַחוֹכֵר שָׂדֶה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, תּוֹרֵם וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ.
phrases.en: One who has hired a field from a Jew [for a fixed amount from the produce], he first gives terumah [from the rental] and then gives it to him (the field owner).

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁנָּתַן לוֹ מֵאוֹתָהּ הַשָּׂדֶה וּמֵאוֹתוֹ הַמִּין, אֲבָל אִם נָתַן לוֹ מִשָּׂדֶה אַחֶרֶת אוֹ מִמִּין אַחֵר, מְעַשֵּׂר וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah said: When is this so? When he pays him [the rental with produce] of the same field and of the same kind; but when he pays him with the produce of another field or of another kind, he must [also] tithe [the rental first] and then give it to him.

phrases.he: הַחוֹכֵר שָׂדֶה מִן הַנָּכְרִי, מְעַשֵּׂר וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ.
phrases.en: One who has hired a field from a Gentile [for a fixed amount from the produce], he first gives tithes [from the rental] and then gives it to him (the field owner).

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף הַמְקַבֵּל שְׂדֵה אֲבוֹתָיו מִן הַנָּכְרִי, מְעַשֵּׂר וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: even if one rented from a Gentile a field which had formerly belonged to his fathers [for a share in the produce], he first gives tithes and then gives it to him.

phrases.he: כֹּהֵן וְלֵוִי שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ שָׂדֶה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁחוֹלְקִין בַּחֻלִּין כָּךְ חוֹלְקִין בַּתְּרוּמָה.
phrases.en: A priest or a Levite who rented a field from an Israelite [for a share in the produce], just as they divide the non-sacred produce, so they divide the terumah.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַף הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶן, שֶׁעַל מְנָת כֵּן בָּאוּ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: the tithes belong to them (the tenants), for they entered the field with this expectation.

phrases.he: יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁקִּבֵּל מִכֹּהֵן וּמִלֵּוִי, הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת לַבְּעָלִים.
phrases.en: If an Israelite rented a field from a priest or from a Levite [for a share in the produce] the tithes belong to the owners [of the field].

phrases.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, הַקַּרְתָּנִי שֶׁקִּבֵּל שָׂדֶה מִירוּשַׁלְמִי, מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁל יְרוּשַׁלְמִי.
phrases.en: Rabbi Ishmael says: if a city dweller [from outside of Jerusalem] rented a field from a Jerusalemite, the second tithe belongs to the inhabitant of Jerusalem.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, יָכוֹל הוּא הַקַּרְתָּנִי לַעֲלוֹת וּלְאָכְלוֹ בִירוּשָׁלָיִם:
phrases.en: But the sages say: the city dweller may go up and eat the second tithe in Jerusalem.

phrases.he: הַמְקַבֵּל זֵיתִים לְשֶׁמֶן, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁחוֹלְקִין בַּחֻלִּין כָּךְ חוֹלְקִין בַּתְּרוּמָה.
phrases.en: [An Israelite] who rents olive trees [from a priest or a Levite] for [a share in the] oil: just as they divide the non-sacred produce, so they divide the terumah.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁקִּבֵּל מִכֹּהֵן וּמִלֵּוִי זֵיתִים לְשֶׁמֶן לְמַחֲצִית שָׂכָר, הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת לַבְּעָלִים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: an Israelite who rented [olive trees] from a priest or a levite for the oil for a share of half the profit, the tithes belong to the owner.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, לֹא יִמְכֹּר אָדָם אֶת זֵיתָיו אֶלָּא לְחָבֵר.
phrases.en: Bet Shammai says: a man may sell his olives only to a “chaver (an ‘associate’).

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, אַף לִמְעַשֵּׂר.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel says: [one may sell them] even to one who only] tithes.

phrases.he: וּצְנוּעֵי בֵית הִלֵּל הָיוּ נוֹהֲגִין כְּדִבְרֵי בֵית שַׁמָּאי
phrases.en: And the pious among Bet Hillel used to act in accordance with the words of Bet Shammai.

phrases.he: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁבָּצְרוּ אֶת כַּרְמֵיהֶם לְתוֹךְ גַּת אַחַת, אֶחָד מְעַשֵּׂר וְאֶחָד שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְעַשֵּׂר, הַמְעַשֵּׂר מְעַשֵּׂר אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ, וְחֶלְקוֹ בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהוּא:
phrases.en: Two gathered [the fruit of] their vineyards into one winepress, one of whom tithes and the other does not tithe the one who tithes may tithe his own share and his share wherever it may be.

phrases.he: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ שָׂדֶה בַאֲרִיסוּת, אוֹ שֶׁיָּרְשׁוּ אוֹ שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּתְּפוּ, יָכוֹל הוּא לוֹמַר, טֹל אַתָּה חִטִּים שֶׁבְּמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי וַאֲנִי חִטִּים שֶׁבְּמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי, אַתָּה יַיִן שֶׁבְּמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי וַאֲנִי יַיִן שֶׁבְּמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי.
phrases.en: Two men who rented a field [for a share in the produce], or inherited [a field], or became partners in it: the one [who tithes] may say to the other [who does not tithe], “You take the wheat which is in this place and I will take the wheat which is in that place.” Or, “You take the wine which is in this place and I will take the wine which is in that place.

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא יֹאמַר לוֹ, טֹל אַתָּה חִטִּים וַאֲנִי שְׂעוֹרִים, טֹל אַתָּה יַיִן וַאֲנִי אֶטֹּל שָׁמֶן
phrases.en: But he may not say to him: “You take the wheat and I will take the barley,” or, “You take the wine and I will take the oil.”

phrases.he: חָבֵר וְעַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁיָּרְשׁוּ אֶת אֲבִיהֶם עַם הָאָרֶץ, יָכוֹל הוּא לוֹמַר לוֹ, טֹל אַתָּה חִטִּים שֶׁבְּמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי וַאֲנִי חִטִּים שֶׁבְּמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי, אַתָּה יַיִן שֶׁבְּמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי וַאֲנִי יַיִן שֶׁבְּמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי.
phrases.en: A chaver (rabbinic associate) and an am haaretz who inherited [the property of] their father who was an am haaretz, he (the chaver) may say to him (the am haaretz): “You take the wheat which is in this place and I will take the wheat which is in that place.” Or, “You take the wine which is in this place and I will take the wine which is in that place.

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא יֹאמַר לוֹ, טֹל אַתָּה חִטִּים וַאֲנִי שְׂעוֹרִים, טֹל אַתָּה הַלַּח וַאֲנִי אֶטֹּל אֶת הַיָּבֵשׁ
phrases.en: But he may not say to him: “You take the wheat and I will take the barley,” or, “You take the wine and I will take the oil,” or: “You take the moist produce and I will take the dry produce.”

phrases.he: גֵּר וְגוֹי שֶׁיָּרְשׁוּ אֶת אֲבִיהֶם גּוֹי, יָכוֹל הוּא לוֹמַר, טֹל אַתָּה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וַאֲנִי מָעוֹת, אַתָּה יַיִן וַאֲנִי פֵרוֹת.
phrases.en: A convert and a gentile who inherited [the property of] their father, a gentile: he (the convert) can say [to his brother the gentile]: “You take the idols and I will take the money,” or: “You take the wine and I will take the produce.

phrases.he: וְאִם מִשֶּׁבָּאוּ לִרְשׁוּת הַגֵּר, אָסוּר
phrases.en: But from the time [that any part of the inheritance] came into the possession of the convert, he is forbidden [to say so].

phrases.he: הַמּוֹכֵר פֵּרוֹת בְּסוּרְיָא, וְאָמַר מִשֶּׁל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵן, חַיָּב לְעַשֵּׂר.
phrases.en: One who sells produce in Syria and declared “It was grown in the land of Israel,” the purchaser must tithe it.

phrases.he: מְעֻשָּׂרִין הֵן, נֶאֱמָן, שֶׁהַפֶּה שֶׁאָסַר הוּא הַפֶּה שֶׁהִתִּיר.
phrases.en: [But if he also said], “It has been tithed,” he may be trusted, because the mouth that forbade is the same mouth that permitted.

phrases.he: מִשֶּׁלִּי הֵן, חַיָּב לְעַשֵּׂר, מְעֻשָּׂרִין הֵן, נֶאֱמָן, שֶׁהַפֶּה שֶׁאָסַר הוּא הַפֶּה שֶׁהִתִּיר.
phrases.en: [If he said: The produce is] from my own field,” the purchaser must tithe it. [But if he added:] “It has already been tithed,” he may be trusted, because the mouth that forbade is the same mouth that permitted.

phrases.he: וְאִם יָדוּעַ שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ שָׂדֶה אֶחָד בְּסוּרְיָא, חַיָּב לְעַשֵּׂר
phrases.en: If it was known that he had a field in Syria, the purchaser must tithe it.

phrases.he: עַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁאָמַר לְחָבֵר, קַח לִי אֲגֻדַּת יָרָק, קַח לִי גְלֻסְקָן אֶחָד, לוֹקֵחַ סְתָם וּפָטוּר.
phrases.en: If an am haaretz said to a chaver, “Buy me a bundle of vegetables,” or: “Buy me a loaf of bread,” the chaver may buy it without checking [whether it had been tithed], and he is exempt [from tithing it].

phrases.he: וְאִם אָמַר, שֶׁלִּי זֶה, וְזֶה שֶׁל חֲבֵרִי, וְנִתְעָרְבוּ, חַיָּב לְעַשֵּׂר, וַאֲפִלּוּ הֵן מֵאָה
phrases.en: But if the chaver said: “This one I am buying for myself and this one for my friend,” and they got mixed up, he must tithe [them both], even if there were one hundred [for the am haaretz.]

phrases.he: הַמַּזְמִין אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ שֶׁיֹּאכַל אֶצְלוֹ, וְהוּא אֵינוֹ מַאֲמִינוֹ עַל הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, אוֹמֵר מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת, מַה שֶּׁאֲנִי עָתִיד לְהַפְרִישׁ מָחָר, הֲרֵי הוּא מַעֲשֵׂר, וּשְׁאָר מַעֲשֵׂר סָמוּךְ לוֹ, זֶה שֶׁעָשִׂיתִי מַעֲשֵׂר עָשׂוּי תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר עָלָיו, וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בִּצְפוֹנוֹ אוֹ בִדְרוֹמוֹ, וּמְחֻלָּל עַל הַמָּעוֹת:
phrases.en: One who invites his friend [before Shabbat] to eat with him [on Shabbat], and [his friend] does not trust him in respect of tithes, [the friend] may say on the eve of Shabbat, “What I will set apart tomorrow, behold it shall be tithe, and what is nearest to it shall be the rest of the tithe. That which I made tithe will become the terumah of the tithe for the whole, and the second tithe is to the north or to the south and it shall be exchanged for money.”

phrases.he: מָזְגוּ לוֹ אֶת הַכּוֹס, אוֹמֵר, מַה שֶּׁאֲנִי עָתִיד לְשַׁיֵּר בְּשׁוּלֵי הַכּוֹס, הֲרֵי הוּא מַעֲשֵׂר, וּשְׁאָר מַעֲשֵׂר סָמוּךְ לוֹ, זֶה שֶׁעָשִׂיתִי מַעֲשֵׂר עָשׂוּי תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר עָלָיו, וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בְּפִיו, וּמְחֻלָּל עַל הַמָּעוֹת:
phrases.en: They pour him a cup [of wine on the sabbath], he says: “What I will leave at the bottom of the cup shall be tithe, and what is nearest to it shall be the rest of the tithe. That which I made tithe shall become terumat maaser for the whole, and second tithe is at the mouth of the cup, and it is exchanged for money.

phrases.he: פּוֹעֵל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַאֲמִין לְבַעַל הַבַּיִת, נוֹטֵל גְּרוֹגֶרֶת אַחַת וְאוֹמֵר, זוֹ וְתֵשַׁע הַבָּאוֹת אַחֲרֶיהָ, עֲשׂוּיוֹת מַעֲשֵׂר עַל תִּשְׁעִים שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹכֵל, זוֹ עֲשׂוּיָה תְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר עֲלֵיהֶן, וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בָּאַחֲרוֹנָה, וּמְחֻלָּל עַל הַמָּעוֹת, וְחוֹשֵׂךְ גְּרוֹגֶרֶת אֶחָת.
phrases.en: A worker who does not trust his employer [in respect of tithes], may take one dried fig and say: “This one and the nine which come after it shall become tithe for the ninety which I shall eat. This one shall become the terumat maaser for them, and the last ones shall be second tithe which shall be exchanged for money.

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, לֹא יַחְשׂךְ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מְמַעֵט מְלַאכְתּוֹ שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבָּיִת.
phrases.en: And he must put aside one dried fig. Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel says: he does not put one aside, because this reduce the work for his employer.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר לֹא יַחְשׂךְ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא תְנַאי בֵּית דִּין:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: he does not put one aside, because this is a court stipulation [imposed upon the employer].

phrases.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ יַיִן מִבֵּין הַכּוּתִים, אוֹמֵר, שְׁנֵי לֻגִּין שֶׁאֲנִי עָתִיד לְהַפְרִישׁ, הֲרֵי הֵן תְּרוּמָה, וַעֲשָׂרָה מַעֲשֵׂר, וְתִשְׁעָה מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי. מֵחֵל וְשׁוֹתֶה:
phrases.en: One who buys wine among Samaritans, he may say: “Two logs which I shall set apart shall be terumah, ten logs tithe, and nine logs second tithe.” He may then pour the wine and drink it.

phrases.he: הָיוּ לוֹ תְאֵנִים שֶׁל טֶבֶל בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ, וְהוּא בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ אוֹ בַשָּׂדֶה, אוֹמֵר, שְׁתֵּי תְאֵנִים שֶׁאֲנִי עָתִיד לְהַפְרִישׁ, הֲרֵי הֵן תְּרוּמָה, וְעֶשֶׂר מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן, וְתֵשַׁע מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי.
phrases.en: He had figs of tevel in his house, and he is in the house of study or in the field: he may say: “The two figs which I shall set apart shall be terumah, ten figs shall be first tithe, and nine figs second tithe.

phrases.he: הָיוּ דְמַאי, אוֹמֵר, מַה שֶּׁאֲנִי עָתִיד לְהַפְרִישׁ לְמָחָר, הֲרֵי הוּא מַעֲשֵׂר, וּשְׁאָר מַעֲשֵׂר סָמוּךְ לוֹ, זֶה שֶׁעָשִׂיתִי מַעֲשֵׂר עָשׂוּי תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר עָלָיו, וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בִּצְפוֹנוֹ אוֹ בִדְרוֹמוֹ, וּמְחֻלָּל עַל הַמָּעוֹת
phrases.en: If the figs were demai, he may say: “Whatever I shall separate tomorrow will be tithe, and the rest of the tithe is adjacent to it. That which I made tithe will become terumat maaser for the whole, and the second tithe is to the north or to the south and it shall be exchanged for money.”

phrases.he: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שְׁתֵּי כַלְכָּלוֹת שֶׁל טֶבֶל, וְאָמַר, מַעַשְׂרוֹת זוֹ בָזוֹ, הָרִאשׁוֹנָה מְעֻשָּׂרֶת.
phrases.en: There were before him two baskets full of tevel, and he said: “Let the tithes of this [basket] be in that [basket],” the first [basket] is tithed.

phrases.he: שֶׁל זוֹ בָזוֹ וְשֶׁל זוֹ בָזוֹ, הָרִאשׁוֹנָה מְעֻשֶּׂרֶת.
phrases.en: [If he said:] “Let the tithes of this [basket] be in that [basket], and the tithes of that [basket] in this [basket],” the first basket is tithed [whereas the second is not].

phrases.he: מַעַשְׂרוֹתֵיהֶן מַעַשְׂרוֹת כַּלְכָּלָה בַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ, קָרָא שֵׁם
phrases.en: [If he said:] “Let the tithes be so that the tithes of each basket be in the other,” he has designated [the tithes of either basket].

phrases.he: מֵאָה טֶבֶל מֵאָה חֻלִּין, נוֹטֵל מֵאָה וְאֶחָד.
phrases.en: One hundred [parts of] tevel which [were mixed with] a hundred [parts of] common produce, one must take out a hundred and one [parts].

phrases.he: מֵאָה טֶבֶל מֵאָה מַעֲשֵׂר, נוֹטֵל מֵאָה וְאֶחָד.
phrases.en: One hundred [parts of] tevel which [were mixed with] a hundred [parts of first] tithe, one must take out a hundred and one [parts].

phrases.he: מֵאָה חֻלִּין מְתֻקָּנִים מֵאָה מַעֲשֵׂר, נוֹטֵל מֵאָה וָעֶשֶׂר.
phrases.en: One hundred [parts of] common produce from which tithes had been separated [were mixed with] a hundred [parts of] tithe, one must take out a hundred and ten [parts].

phrases.he: מֵאָה טֶבֶל תִּשְׁעִים מַעֲשֵׂר, תִּשְׁעִים טֶבֶל וּשְׁמוֹנִים מַעֲשֵׂר, לֹא הִפְסִיד כְּלוּם.
phrases.en: One hundred [parts of] tevel [were mixed with] ninety [parts of] tithe, or ninety [parts of] tevel [were mixed with] eighty [parts of] tithe, he has not lost anything.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהַטֶּבֶל מְרֻבֶּה, לֹא הִפְסִיד כְּלוּם
phrases.en: This is the general rule: whenever the tevel is the greater [portion of the mixture] he has not lost anything.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ עֶשֶׂר שׁוּרוֹת שֶׁל עֶשֶׂר עֶשֶׂר כַּדֵּי יַיִן, וְאָמַר, שׁוּרָה הַחִיצוֹנָה אַחַת מַעֲשֵׂר, וְאֵין יָדוּעַ אֵיזוֹ הִיא, נוֹטֵל שְׁתֵּי חָבִיּוֹת לוֹכְסָן.
phrases.en: One who had ten rows each containing ten jugs of wine, and said: “One exterior row shall be tithe,” and it is not known which row [he meant], he must take two jugs [each from the ends of] a diagonal line.

phrases.he: חֲצִי שׁוּרָה הַחִיצוֹנָה אַחַת מַעֲשֵׂר, וְאֵין יָדוּעַ אֵיזוֹ הִיא, נוֹטֵל אַרְבַּע חָבִיּוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע זָוִיּוֹת.
phrases.en: [If he had said:] “One half of one exterior row shall be tithe” and it is not known which half row [he meant], he must take four jugs from the four corners.

phrases.he: שׁוּרָה אַחַת מַעֲשֵׂר, וְאֵין יָדוּעַ אֵיזוֹ הִיא, נוֹטֵל שׁוּרָה אַחַת לוֹכְסָן.
phrases.en: [If he had said:] “One row shall be tithe,” and it is not known which row [he meant], he must take one [whole] row in a diagonal line.

phrases.he: חֲצִי שׁוּרָה אַחַת מַעֲשֵׂר, וְאֵין יָדוּעַ אֵיזוֹ הִיא, נוֹטֵל שְׁתֵּי שׁוּרוֹת לוֹכְסָן.
phrases.en: [If he had said:] “Half of one row shall be tithe,” and it is not known which half row [he meant], he must take two rows in a diagonal line.

phrases.he: חָבִית אַחַת מַעֲשֵׂר, וְאֵין יָדוּעַ אֵיזוֹ הִיא, נוֹטֵל מִכָּל חָבִית וְחָבִית
phrases.en: [If he had said:] “One jug shall be tithe,” and it is not known which jug [he meant],he must take from every jug.

phrases.he: הַחִטִּים וְהַזּוּנִין אֵינָן כִּלְאַיִם זֶה בָזֶה.
phrases.en: Wheat and zunin do not constitute kilayim one with the other.

phrases.he: הַשְּׂעֹרִים וְשִׁבֹּלֶת שׁוּעָל, הַכֻּסְּמִין וְהַשִּׁיפוֹן, הַפּוֹל וְהַסַּפִּיר, הַפֻּרְקְדָן וְהַטֹּפֵחַ, וּפוֹל הַלָּבָן וְהַשְּׁעוּעִים, אֵינָם כִּלְאַיִם זֶה בָזֶה
phrases.en: Barley and oats, spelt and rye, or beans and sapir (a type of bean), or purkdan and tofah (two similar types of beans), or white beans and kidney beans, do not constitute kilayim one with the other.

phrases.he: הַקִּשּׁוּת וְהַמְּלָפְפוֹן, אֵינָם כִּלְאַיִם זֶה בָזֶה.
phrases.en: Cucumbers and melons do not constitute kilayim one with the other.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כִּלְאָיִם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah said they do constitute kilayim.

phrases.he: חֲזֶרֶת וַחֲזֶרֶת גַּלִּים, עֻלְשִׁין וְעֻלְשֵׁי שָׂדֶה, כְּרֵשִׁים וּכְרֵשֵׁי שָׂדֶה, כֻּסְבָּר וְכֻסְבַּר שָׂדֶה, חַרְדָּל וְחַרְדָּל מִצְרִי, וּדְלַעַת הַמִּצְרִי וְהָרְמוּצָה, וּפוֹל מִצְרִי וְהֶחָרוּב, אֵינָם כִּלְאַיִם זֶה בָזֶה
phrases.en: Lettuce and wild lettuce, endives and wild endives, leek and wild leek, coriander and wild coriander, or mustard and Egyptian mustard, Egyptian gourd and the bitter gourd, or Egyptian beans and carob shaped beans do not constitute kilayim one with the other.

phrases.he: הַלֶּפֶת וְהַנָּפוּץ, וְהַכְּרוּב וְהַתְּרוֹבְתוֹר, הַתְּרָדִים וְהַלְּעוּנִים, אֵינָם כִּלְאַיִם זֶה בָזֶה.
phrases.en: Turnips and the cabbage turnip, cabbage and cauliflower, beet and rumex do not constitute kilayim one with the other.

phrases.he: הוֹסִיף רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, הַשּׁוּם וְהַשּׁוּמָנִית, הַבָּצָל וְהַבְּצַלְצוּל, וְהַתֻּרְמוֹס וְהַפְּלַסְלוֹס, אֵינָן כִּלְאַיִם זֶה בָזֶה
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva added: garlic and small wild garlic, onion and small wild onion, lupine and wild lupine do not constitute kilayim one with the other.

phrases.he: וּבָאִילָן, הָאֲגָסִים וְהַקְּרֻסְתּוּמֵלִין, וְהַפְּרִישִׁים וְהָעֻזְרָדִים, אֵינָם כִּלְאַיִם זֶה בָזֶה.
phrases.en: As for trees: the pear and the crustumenian pear, the medlar and azarolus, do not constitute kilayim one with the other.

phrases.he: הַתַּפּוּחַ וְהַחַזְרָד, הַפַּרְסְקִים וְהַשְּׁקֵדִין, וְהַשִּׁזָּפִין וְהָרִימִין, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁדּוֹמִין זֶה לָזֶה, כִּלְאַיִם זֶה בָזֶה
phrases.en: The apple and the crab-apple, or the peach and almond, or the jujube and rimin, even though they are similar one to the other, they nevertheless constitute kilayim one with the other.

phrases.he: הַצְּנוֹן וְהַנָּפוּץ, הַחַרְדָּל וְהַלַּפְסָן, וּדְלַעַת יְוָנִית עִם הַמִּצְרִית וְהָרְמוּצָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁדּוֹמִין זֶה לָזֶה, כִּלְאַיִם זֶה בָזֶה:
phrases.en: The radish and the cabbage turnip, mustard and charlock mustard, Greek gourd with Egyptian gourd or [Greek gourd] with bitter gourd, even though they are similar one to the other, are nevertheless kilayim one with the other.

phrases.he: הַזְּאֵב וְהַכֶּלֶב, כֶּלֶב הַכֻּפְרִי וְהַשּׁוּעָל, הָעִזִּים וְהַצְּבָאִים, הַיְּעֵלִים וְהָרְחֵלִים, הַסּוּס וְהַפֶּרֶד, הַפֶּרֶד וְהַחֲמוֹר, הַחֲמוֹר וְהֶעָרוֹד, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁדּוֹמִין זֶה לָזֶה, כִּלְאַיִם זֶה בָזֶה:
phrases.en: A wolf and a dog, a wild dog and a fox, a goat and a deer, a gazelle and a ewe-lamb, a horse and a mule, or a mule and a donkey, a donkey and a wild donkey, even though they are similar one to the other, constitute nevertheless, kilayim one with the other.

phrases.he: אֵין מְבִיאִין אִילָן בְּאִילָן, יָרָק בְּיָרָק, וְלֹא אִילָן בְּיָרָק, וְלֹא יָרָק בְּאִילָן.
phrases.en: They may not graft from one tree to another, or from one vegetable to another, or from a tree to a vegetable, or from a vegetable to a tree.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר יָרָק בְּאִילָן
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah permits it from a vegetable to a tree.

phrases.he: אֵין נוֹטְעִין יְרָקוֹת בְּתוֹךְ סַדָּן שֶׁל שִׁקְמָה.
phrases.en: They may not plant vegetables in a trunk of a sycamore tree.

phrases.he: אֵין מַרְכִּיבִין פֵּיגָם עַל גַּבֵּי קִדָּה לְבָנָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא יָרָק בְּאִילָן.
phrases.en: They may not graft rue on white cassia, since that is [grafting] a vegetable on a tree.

phrases.he: אֵין נוֹטְעִין יִחוּר שֶׁל תְּאֵנָה לְתוֹךְ הַחֲצוּב, שֶׁיְּהֵא מְקֵרוֹ.
phrases.en: They may not plant a young fig-shoot in sea squill so that it might provide shade for it.

phrases.he: אֵין תּוֹחֲבִין זְמוֹרָה שֶׁל גֶּפֶן לְתוֹךְ הָאֲבַטִּיחַ, שֶׁתְּהֵא זוֹרֶקֶת מֵימֶיהָ לְתוֹכוֹ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא אִילָן בְּיָרָק.
phrases.en: They may not insert a vine branch into a melon, in order that the latter might shoot its moisture to the former, since that is [grafting] a tree on a vegetable.

phrases.he: אֵין נוֹתְנִין זֶרַע דְּלַעַת לְתוֹךְ הַחַלָּמִית, שֶׁתְּהֵא מְשַׁמַּרְתּוֹ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא יָרָק בְּיָרָק
phrases.en: They may not place gourd seed into anchusa for the purpose of preserving it (the gourd seed), since that is [grafting] a vegetable on another vegetable.

phrases.he: הַטּוֹמֵן לֶפֶת וּצְנוֹנוֹת תַּחַת הַגֶּפֶן, אִם הָיוּ מִקְצָת עָלָיו מְגֻלִּין, אֵינוֹ חוֹשֵׁשׁ לֹא מִשּׁוּם כִּלְאַיִם, וְלֹא מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִיעִית, וְלֹא מִשּׁוּם מַעַשְׂרוֹת, וְנִטָּלִים בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: One who buries turnips or radishes beneath a vine, if some of their leaves are uncovered, he need not have fear [of having transgressed] kilayim, or the sabbatical year, or tithes and they may also be pulled up on Shabbat.

phrases.he: הַזּוֹרֵעַ חִטָּה וּשְׂעוֹרָה כְּאַחַת, הֲרֵי זֶה כִלְאָיִם.
phrases.en: One who plants a [grain of] wheat and [a grain of] barley at one time, behold this is kilayim.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֵינוֹ כִּלְאַיִם, עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ שְׁנֵי חִטִּים וּשְׂעוֹרָה, אוֹ חִטָּה וּשְׁתֵּי שְׂעוֹרִים, אוֹ חִטָּה וּשְׂעוֹרָה וְכֻסָּמֶת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: it is not kilayim unless there are two grains of wheat and two grains of barley, or one grain of wheat and two grains of barley, or a grain of wheat, a grain of barley and a grain of spelt.

phrases.he: כָּל סְאָה שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ רֹבַע מִמִּין אַחֵר, יְמַעֵט.
phrases.en: Any seah which contains a quarter [of a kav] of a different species, one should reduce [its proportion of the latter] Rabbi Yose says: one should pick [it all out].

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, יָבֹר.
phrases.en: Whether it consists of one species or of two species.

phrases.he: בֵּין מִמִּין אֶחָד בֵּין מִשְּׁנֵי מִינִין.
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, לֹא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא מִמִּין אֶחָד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: they said this only if it consists of one species.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, כָּל שֶׁהוּא כִלְאַיִם בַּסְּאָה מִצְטָרֵף לְרֹבַע:
phrases.en: But the sages say: anything which is kilayim, in a seah [it adds up] in making up the quarter.

phrases.he: בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים. תְּבוּאָה בִתְבוּאָה וְקִטְנִית בְּקִטְנִית, תְּבוּאָה בְקִטְנִית וְקִטְנִית בִּתְבוּאָה.
phrases.en: To what does this refer? To [an mixture of] grain [occurring] with [different] grain, or pulse with [different] pulse, to grain with pulse, and to pulse with grain.

phrases.he: בֶּאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ, זֵרְעוֹנֵי גִנָּה שֶׁאֵינָן נֶאֱכָלִין, מִצְטָרְפִין אֶחָד מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע בְּנוֹפֵל לְבֵית סְאָה.
phrases.en: However they stated: Seeds from a garden which are not eaten, they add up [with other seeds to form an amount sufficient to prohibit the sowing of a seah] when there is 1/24 of the quantity [of such seed] that is necessary to sow a bet seah.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאָמְרוּ לְהַחְמִיר כָּךְ
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: just as they ruled to be stringent so too they ruled to be lenient flax [mixed in with] produce, combines when there is 1/24 of the quantity [of such seed] that is necessary to sow a bet seah.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לְהָקֵל, הַפִּשְׁתָּן בַּתְּבוּאָה מִצְטָרֶפֶת אֶחָד מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע בְּנוֹפֵל לְבֵית סְאָה:
הָיְתָה שָׂדֵהוּ זְרוּעָה חִטִּים וְנִמְלַךְ לְזָרְעָהּ שְׂעוֹרִים, יַמְתִּין לָהּ עַד שֶׁתַּתְלִיעַ, וְיוֹפַךְ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ יִזְרַע.
phrases.en: If one’s field was sown with wheat, and he changed his mind and decided to sow it with barley, he must wait until it [the wheat] rots. He turns [the soil] and then he may sow [the barley], if it [the wheat] had already grown.

phrases.he: אִם צִמְּחָה, לֹא יֹאמַר אֶזְרַע וְאַחַר כָּךְ אוֹפָךְ, אֶלָּא הוֹפֵךְ וְאַחַר כָּךְ זוֹרֵעַ.
phrases.en: He should not say: “I shall [first] sow [the barley] and, then turn [the soil]” rather he must first turn [the soil] and then sow.

phrases.he: כַּמָּה יְהֵא חוֹרֵשׁ, כְּתַלְמֵי הָרְבִיעָה.
phrases.en: How much must he plow [when overturning the soil]? Like the furrows [that are plowed after the [first] rainy season.

phrases.he: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְשַׁיֵּר רֹבַע לְבֵית סְאָה
phrases.en: Abba Shaul says: [one should plow] so that one does not leave [unplowed] as much [ground] as holds a quarter [kav] to a bet seah.

phrases.he: זְרוּעָה וְנִמְלַךְ לְנָטְעָהּ, לֹא יֹאמַר אֶטַּע וְאַחַר כָּךְ אוֹפָךְ, אֶלָּא הוֹפֵךְ וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹטֵעַ.
phrases.en: [His field was] sown [with grain, or pulse, or garden-seed], and he changed his mind and decided to plant it [with vines], he may not say: “First I shall plant [the vines] and then turn [the soil],” but he must [first] turn [the soil] and then he may plant [the vines].

phrases.he: נְטוּעָה וְנִמְלַךְ לְזָרְעָהּ, לֹא יֹאמַר אֶזְרַע וְאַחַר כָּךְ אֲשָׁרֵשׁ, אֶלָּא מְשָׁרֵשׁ וְאַחַר כָּךְ זוֹרֵעַ.
