phrases.en: A seah of unclean terumah which fell into a hundred of clean hullin:Rabbi Eliezer says: [a seah] must be taken out and burnt, for I say that the seah taken out is the one that fell in.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, תֵּרוֹם וְתִשָּׂרֵף, שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר, סְאָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה הִיא סְאָה שֶׁעָלְתָה.
phrases.en: But the sages say: it may be taken out and eaten in small quantities, or roasted, or kneaded with fruit juice, or divided into pieces of dough so that the size of one egg be not in any one place.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, תַּעֲלֶה וְתֵאָכֵל נִקּוּדִים אוֹ קְלָיוֹת, אוֹ תִלּוֹשׁ בְּמֵי פֵרוֹת, אוֹ תִתְחַלֵּק לְעִסּוֹת, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בְמָקוֹם אֶחָד כַּבֵּיצָה:

סְאָה תְרוּמָה טְהוֹרָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְמֵאָה חֻלִּין טְמֵאִין, תַּעֲלֶה וְתֵאָכֵל נִקּוּדִים אוֹ קְלָיוֹת, אוֹ תִלּוֹשׁ בְּמֵי פֵרוֹת, אוֹ תִתְחַלֵּק לְעִסּוֹת, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בְמָקוֹם אֶחָד כַּבֵּיצָה:
phrases.en: A seah of clean terumah fell into a hundred of unclean hullin, it may be eaten in small quantities, or roasted, or kneaded with fruit juice, or divided into pieces of dough so that the size of one egg be not in any one place.

phrases.he: סְאָה תְרוּמָה טְמֵאָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְמֵאָה סְאָה תְרוּמָה טְהוֹרָה, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹסְרִים, וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין.
phrases.en: A seah of unclean terumah that falls into one hundred seahs of clean terumah: Bet Shammai prohibits, But Bet Hillel permits.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ בֵית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי, הוֹאִיל וּטְהוֹרָה אֲסוּרָה לְזָרִים וּטְמֵאָה אֲסוּרָה לְכֹהֲנִים, מַה טְּהוֹרָה עוֹלָה, אַף טְמֵאָה תַּעֲלֶה.
phrases.en: Bet Hillel said to Bet Shammai: since clean [terumah] is forbidden to non-priests and unclean [terumah is forbidden] to priests, then just as clean [terumah] is brought up, so too unclean [terumah] can be brought up.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, לֹא, אִם הֶעֱלוּ הַחֻלִּין הַקַּלִּין הַמֻּתָּרִין לְזָרִים אֶת הַטְּהוֹרָה, תַּעֲלֶה תְרוּמָה הַחֲמוּרָה הָאֲסוּרָה לְזָרִים אֶת הַטְּמֵאָה. לְאַחַר שֶׁהוֹדוּ,
phrases.en: Bet Shammai answered them: No! If hullin which is treated more leniently [in that it is permitted to non-priests] allows us to bring up clean [terumah that falls into it], does terumah [which is more stringent in that it is forbidden to non-priests] also allow us to bring up that which is unclean? After [Bet Shammai] had agreed [with Bet Hillel], Rabbi Eliezer said: it should be taken out and burned.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, תֵּרוֹם וְתִשָּׂרֵף.
phrases.en: But the sages say: it is gone, on account of its being a tiny [portion of the whole mixture].

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אָבְדָה בְמִעוּטָהּ:
סְאָה תְרוּמָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְמֵאָה, הִגְבִּיהָהּ וְנָפְלָה לְמָקוֹם אַחֵר,
phrases.en: A seah of terumah that fell into a hundred [of hullin], and he lifted it out and fell into [hullin] elsewhere:Rabbi Eliezer says: it renders medumma as though it were certainly terumah.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, מְדַמַּעַת כִּתְרוּמָה וַדָּאי.
phrases.en: But the sages say: it is rendered medumma only according to proportion.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵינָה מְדַמַּעַת אֶלָּא לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן:
סְאָה תְרוּמָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְפָחוֹת מִמֵּאָה וְנִדַּמְּעוּ, וְנָפַל מִן הַמְדֻמָּע לְמָקוֹם אַחֵר,
phrases.en: A seah of terumah which fell into less than a hundred [of hullin], and rendered the whole medumma, and part of this mixture fell afterwards into another place: Rabbi Eliezer says: it renders again medumma as if certain terumah [had fallen in].

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, מְדַמַּעַת כִּתְרוּמָה וַדָּאי.
phrases.en: But the sages say: the [first] mixture renders medumma only according to the proportion.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵין הַמְדֻמָּע מְדַמֵּעַ אֶלָּא לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן, וְאֵין הַמְחֻמָּץ מַחְמִיץ אֶלָּא לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן, וְאֵין הַמַּיִם שְׁאוּבִים פּוֹסְלִים אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה אֶלָּא לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן:
phrases.en: [Similarly], that which is leavened [with terumah] renders other dough leavened [as with terumah] only according to the proportion. And drawn water disqualifies a ritual bath also only according to the proportion.

phrases.he: סְאָה תְרוּמָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְמֵאָה, הִגְבִּיהָהּ וְנָפְלָה אַחֶרֶת, הִגְבִּיהָהּ וְנָפְלָה אַחֶרֶת, הֲרֵי זוֹ מֻתֶּרֶת, עַד שֶׁתִּרְבֶּה תְרוּמָה עַל הַחֻלִּין:
phrases.en: If a seah of terumah fell into a hundred [of hullin] and he lifted [a seah] out, and then another fell in, and he lifted another out and another fell in, the pile is permissible as long as the amount of terumah does not exceed that of the hullin.

phrases.he: סְאָה תְרוּמָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְמֵאָה, וְלֹא הִסְפִּיק לְהַגְבִּיהָהּ עַד שֶׁנָּפְלָה אַחֶרֶת, הֲרֵי זוֹ אֲסוּרָה. וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר:
phrases.en: If a seah of terumah fell into a hundred [of hullin], and before he could take it out, another fell in, the whole becomes forbidden. Rabbi Shimon permits it.

phrases.he: סְאָה תְרוּמָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְמֵאָה, וּטְחָנָן וּפָחֲתוּ, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁפָּחֲתוּ הַחֻלִּין, כָּךְ פָּחֲתָה הַתְּרוּמָה, וּמֻתָּר.
phrases.en: If a seah of terumah fell into a hundred [of hullin], and they were ground together and reduced in bulk, just as the hullin was reduced so too the terumah was reduced, and it is permitted.

phrases.he: סְאָה תְרוּמָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְפָחוֹת מִמֵּאָה, וּטְחָנָן וְהוֹתִירוּ, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהוֹתִירוּ הַחֻלִּין, כָּךּ הוֹתִירָה הַתְּרוּמָה, וְאָסוּר.
phrases.en: If a seah of terumah fell into less than a hundred [of hullin] and they were ground together and increased in bulk, just as the hullin became more, so too the terumah became more, and it is forbidden.

phrases.he: אִם יָדוּעַ שֶׁהַחִטִּים שֶׁל חֻלִּין יָפוֹת מִשֶּׁל תְּרוּמָה, מֻתָּר.
phrases.en: If it is known that the kernels of hullin were better than the terumah, it is permitted.

phrases.he: סְאָה תְרוּמָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְפָחוֹת מִמֵּאָה, וְאַחַר כֵּן נָפְלוּ שָׁם חֻלִּין, אִם שׁוֹגֵג, מֻתָּר, וְאִם מֵזִיד, אָסוּר
phrases.en: If a seah of terumah fell into less than a hundred [of hullin], and more hullin fell in afterwards, if it was accidental it is permissible, but if intentional it is forbidden.

phrases.he: הָאוֹכֵל תְּרוּמָה שׁוֹגֵג, מְשַׁלֵּם קֶרֶן וְחֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.en: One who eats terumah unwittingly must repay its value plus a fifth, whether he eats it or drinks it, or anoints himself with it, or whether the terumah is clean or unclean.

phrases.he: אֶחָד הָאוֹכֵל וְאֶחָד הַשּׁוֹתֶה וְאֶחָד הַסָּךְ, אֶחָד תְּרוּמָה טְהוֹרָה וְאֶחָד תְּרוּמָה טְמֵאָה, מְשַׁלֵּם חֻמְשָׁהּ וְחֹמֶשׁ חֻמְשָׁהּ.
phrases.en: [If he eats the added fifth] he must pay its fifth, and a fifth of that fifth.

phrases.he: אֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם תְּרוּמָה, אֶלָּא חֻלִּין מְתֻקָּנִים, וְהֵם נַעֲשִׂין תְּרוּמָה, וְהַתַּשְׁלוּמִין תְּרוּמָה.
phrases.en: He may not repay with terumah, but rather with tithed hullin, which becomes terumah. And whatever may be repaid in its place also becomes terumah and if the priest wishes to forego [the fine], he cannot do so.

phrases.he: אִם רָצָה הַכֹּהֵן לִמְחֹל, אֵינוֹ מוֹחֵל
בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאָכְלָה תְרוּמָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִשֵּׂאת לְכֹהֵן, אִם תְּרוּמָה שֶׁלֹּא זָכָה בָהּ כֹּהֵן אָכְלָה, מְשַׁלֶּמֶת קֶרֶן וְחֹמֶשׁ לְעַצְמָהּ.
phrases.en: A daughter of an Israelite ate terumah and afterwards married a priest:If the terumah she ate had not yet been acquired by another priest she can repay to herself the value and the fifth.

phrases.he: וְאִם תְּרוּמָה שֶׁזָּכָה בָהּ כֹּהֵן אָכְלָה, מְשַׁלֶּמֶת קֶרֶן לַבְּעָלִים, וְחֹמֶשׁ לְעַצְמָהּ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָמְרוּ, הָאוֹכֵל תְּרוּמָה שׁוֹגֵג, מְשַׁלֵּם קֶרֶן לַבְּעָלִים, וְחֹמֶשׁ לְכָל מִי שֶׁיִּרְצֶה
phrases.en: But if a priest had already acquired the terumah she had eaten, she must repay the value to the owners, but [she can repay] the fifth to herself, because they said that he who eats terumah unwittingly, pays the value to the owners and the fifth to whoever he wants.

phrases.he: הַמַּאֲכִיל אֶת פּוֹעֲלָיו וְאֶת אוֹרְחָיו תְּרוּמָה, הוּא מְשַׁלֵּם אֶת הַקֶּרֶן, וְהֵם מְשַׁלְּמִין אֶת הַחֹמֶשׁ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: If one gives his workmen or his guests terumah to eat he must repay the principal and they must pay the fifth, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, הֵם מְשַׁלְּמִין קֶרֶן וְחֹמֶשׁ, וְהוּא מְשַׁלֵּם לָהֶם דְּמֵי סְעוּדָתָן:
phrases.en: But the sages say: they must pay both the value and the fifth, and he must pay them for the price of their meal.

phrases.he: הַגּוֹנֵב תְּרוּמָה וְלֹא אֲכָלָהּ, מְשַׁלֵּם תַּשְׁלוּמֵי כֵפֶל דְּמֵי תְרוּמָה.
phrases.en: If one stole terumah but did not eat it, he must return double-payment at the price of terumah.

phrases.he: אֲכָלָהּ, מְשַׁלֵּם שְׁנֵי קְרָנִים וְחֹמֶשׁ, קֶרֶן וְחֹמֶשׁ מִן הַחֻלִּין, וְקֶרֶן דְּמֵי תְרוּמָה.
phrases.en: If he ate it, he must pay twice the value plus a fifth, one principal value and a fifth at the price of hullin, and the other principal at the price of terumah.

phrases.he: גָּנַב תְּרוּמַת הֶקְדֵּשׁ וַאֲכָלָהּ, מְשַׁלֵּם שְׁנֵי חֳמָשִׁים וְקֶרֶן, שֶׁאֵין בַּהֶקְדֵּשׁ תַּשְׁלוּמֵי כָפֶל
phrases.en: If one stole terumah of dedicated property and ate it, he must repay two fifths and the principal value, for the laws of double-payment do not apply to dedicated property.

phrases.he: אֵין מְשַׁלְּמִין מִן הַלֶּקֶט וּמִן הַשִּׁכְחָה וּמִן הַפֵּאָה וּמִן הַהֶפְקֵר, וְלֹא מִמַּעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּטְּלָה תְּרוּמָתוֹ, וְלֹא מִמַּעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁנִּפְדּוּ, שֶׁאֵין הֶקְדֵּשׁ פּוֹדֶה אֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וַחֲכָמִים מַתִּירִין בָּאֵלּוּ:
phrases.en: They may not make repayment from gleanings, from forgotten sheaf, from peah or ownerless property. Nor from first tithe from which terumah has been taken, nor from second tithe or dedicated produce which have been redeemed, because one dedicated thing (kadosh) cannot be used to redeem another dedicated thing (kadosh), the words of Rabbi Meir. But the sages permit [payment] with these.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, מְשַׁלְּמִין מִמִּין עַל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ, בִּלְבַד שֶׁיְּשַׁלֵּם מִן הַיָּפֶה עַל הָרָע.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: they may make repayment from one kind for another, provided that it is from a superior kind for an inferior kind.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אֵין מְשַׁלְּמִין אֶלָּא מִמִּין עַל מִינוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: they may make repayment only from the same kind.

phrases.he: לְפִיכָךְ, אִם אָכַל קִשּׁוּאִין שֶׁל עֶרֶב שְׁבִיעִית, יַמְתִּין לְקִשּׁוּאִין שֶׁל מוֹצָאֵי שְׁבִיעִית, וִישַׁלֵּם מֵהֶם.
phrases.en: Hence if a man ate cucumbers grown a year before the seventh year, he must wait for those grown after the termination of the seventh year and repay with them.

phrases.he: מִמְּקוֹם שֶׁרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מֵקֵל, מִשָּׁם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַחְמִיר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ויקרא כב), וְנָתַן לַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ, כָּל שֶׁהוּא רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת קֹדֶשׁ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.en: The same source which causes Rabbi Eliezer to be lenient causes Rabbi Akiva to be stringent, for it says: “And he shall give the priest the holy thing (hakodesh)” (Leviticus 22:14), [implying,] whatever is liable to become “kodesh,” the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, וְנָתַן לַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ, קֹדֶשׁ שֶׁאָכָל:
phrases.en: But Rabbi Akiva says: “And he shall give the priest the holy thing (kodesh),” [implying] the same kind of holy thing which he ate.

phrases.he: הָאוֹכֵל תְּרוּמָה מֵזִיד, מְשַׁלֵּם אֶת הַקֶּרֶן וְאֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם אֶת הַחֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.en: One who eats terumah intentionally must repay its value, but not the fifth.

phrases.he: הַתַּשְׁלוּמִין חֻלִּין, אִם רָצָה הַכֹּהֵן לִמְחֹל, מוֹחֵל
phrases.en: And the repayment remains hullin, therefore, if the priest wishes to forgive the repayment, he may.

phrases.he: בַּת כֹּהֵן שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָכְלָה תְרוּמָה, מְשַׁלֶּמֶת אֶת הַקֶּרֶן וְאֵינָהּ מְשַׁלֶּמֶת אֶת הַחֹמֶשׁ, וּמִיתָתָהּ בִּשְׂרֵפָה.
phrases.en: If the daughter of a priest married an Israelite and afterwards ate terumah, she must repay the value but not the fifth, and her death-penalty [for adultery] is by burning.

phrases.he: נִשֵּׂאת לְאֶחָד מִכָּל הַפְּסוּלִין, מְשַׁלֶּמֶת קֶרֶן וְחֹמֶשׁ, וּמִיתָתָהּ בְּחֶנֶק, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: If she married any of those disqualified [from marrying her], she must pay back both the value and the fifth, and her death-penalty [for adultery] is by strangling, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, זוֹ וָזוֹ מְשַׁלְּמוֹת אֶת הַקֶּרֶן וְאֵינָן מְשַׁלְּמוֹת אֶת הַחֹמֶשׁ, וּמִיתָתָן בִּשְׂרֵפָה:
phrases.en: But the sages say: in either case, she repays the value but not the fifth, and the death penalty is by burning.

phrases.he: הַמַּאֲכִיל אֶת בָּנָיו קְטַנִּים, וְאֶת עֲבָדָיו בֵּין גְּדוֹלִים בֵּין קְטַנִּים, הָאוֹכֵל תְּרוּמַת חוּצָה לָאָרֶץ, וְהָאוֹכֵל פָּחוֹת מִכַּזַּיִת תְּרוּמָה, מְשַׁלֵּם אֶת הַקֶּרֶן, וְאֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם אֶת הַחֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.en: One who feeds [terumah] to his small children, or to his slaves whether they are of majority age or minors, or one who eats terumah from outside the land, or less than an olive’s bulk of terumah, must repay the value, but not the fifth; and the repayment remains hullin.

phrases.he: וְהַתַּשְׁלוּמִין חֻלִּין, אִם רָצָה הַכֹּהֵן לִמְחֹל, מוֹחֵל
phrases.en: Therefore, if the priest wishes to forgive the repayment, he may.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל הַמְשַׁלֵּם קֶרֶן וְחֹמֶשׁ, הַתַּשְׁלוּמִין תְּרוּמָה, אִם רָצָה הַכֹּהֵן לִמְחֹל, אֵינוֹ מוֹחֵל.
phrases.en: This is the general principle: whenever one has to repay both the value and the fifth, the repayment becomes terumah, and if the priest desires to forgive the repayment, he cannot forgive.

phrases.he: וְכָל הַמְשַׁלֵּם אֶת הַקֶּרֶן וְאֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם אֶת הַחֹמֶשׁ, הַתַּשְׁלוּמִין חֻלִּין, אִם רָצָה הַכֹּהֵן לִמְחֹל, מוֹחֵל
phrases.en: But whenever one has to repay the value only and not the fifth, the repayment remains hullin (non-sacred produce), and if the priest wishes to forgive the repayment, he can.

phrases.he: שְׁתֵּי קֻפּוֹת, אַחַת שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה וְאַחַת שֶׁל חֻלִּין, שֶׁנָּפְלָה סְאָה תְרוּמָה לְתוֹךְ אַחַת מֵהֶן וְאֵין יָדוּעַ לְאֵיזוֹ מֵהֶן נָפְלָה, הֲרֵי אֲנִי אוֹמֵר, לְתוֹךְ שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה נָפְלָה.
phrases.en: If there were two baskets, one of terumah and one of hullin, and a seah of terumah fell into one of them, but it is not known into which, behold I can assume that it had fallen into that of the terumah.

phrases.he: אֵין יָדוּעַ אֵיזוֹ הִיא שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא שֶׁל חֻלִּין, אָכַל אַחַת מֵהֶן, פָּטוּר, וְהַשְּׁנִיָּה, נוֹהֵג בָּהּ כִּתְרוּמָה, וְחַיֶּבֶת בְּחַלָּה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי פּוֹטְרָהּ.
phrases.en: [Two baskets] and it is not known which was of terumah and which of hullin, and he eats from one of them, he is exempt, and the second basket is treated as terumah and subject to the laws of hallah, the words of Rabbi Meir. But Rabbi Yose exempts it.

phrases.he: אָכַל אַחֵר אֶת הַשְּׁנִיָּה, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: If another person eats from the second basket he is exempt.

phrases.he: אָכַל אֶחָד אֶת שְׁתֵּיהֶן, מְשַׁלֵּם כַּקְּטַנָּה שֶׁבִּשְׁתֵּיהֶן
phrases.en: If one man ate of both, he must repay the value of the smaller of the two.

phrases.he: נָפְלָה אַחַת מֵהֶן לְתוֹךְ הַחֻלִּין, אֵינָהּ מְדַמַּעְתָּן, וְהַשְּׁנִיָּה, נוֹהֵג בָּהּ כִּתְרוּמָה, וְחַיֶּבֶת בְּחַלָּה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי פּוֹטֵר.
phrases.en: If one of these [baskets] fell into hullin, it does not render it medumma (doubtful terumah), but the second is treated as terumah and subject to the law of hallah, the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yose exempts it.

phrases.he: נָפְלָה שְׁנִיָּה לְמָקוֹם אַחֵר, אֵינָהּ מְדַמַּעְתָּן.
phrases.en: If the second falls elsewhere [into hullin] it does not render it medumma.

phrases.he: נָפְלוּ שְׁתֵּיהֶן לְמָקוֹם אֶחָד, מְדַמְּעוֹת כַּקְּטַנָּה שֶׁבִּשְׁתֵּיהֶן
phrases.en: If both of them fall into one place, they render it medumma according to [the proportion] of the smaller of the two.

phrases.he: זָרַע אֶת אַחַת מֵהֶן, פָּטוּר, וְהַשְּׁנִיָּה, נוֹהֵג בָּהּ כִּתְרוּמָה, וְחַיֶּבֶת בְּחַלָּה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי פּוֹטֵר.
phrases.en: If he used one of these [baskets] as seed, he is exempt, and the second is treated as if it were terumah and subject to the law of hallah, the words of Rabbi Meir. But Rabbi Yose exempts it. If another person uses the second as seed, then he is exempt.

phrases.he: זָרַע אַחֵר אֶת הַשְּׁנִיָּה, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: If one man uses both as seed, if it is of a kind whose seed disintegrates [in the ground] it is permissible, but if it is of the kind whose seed does not disintegrate it is prohibited.

phrases.he: זָרַע אֶחָד אֶת שְׁתֵּיהֶן, בְּדָבָר שֶׁזַּרְעוֹ כָלֶה, מֻתָּר, וּבְדָבָר שֶׁאֵין זַרְעוֹ כָלֶה. אָסוּר

הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָיְתָה אוֹכֶלֶת בִּתְרוּמָה, בָּאוּ וְאָמְרוּ לָהּ, מֵת בַּעְלִיךְ אוֹ גֵרְשֵׁךְ, וְכֵן הָעֶבֶד שֶׁהָיָה אוֹכֵל בִּתְרוּמָה, וּבָאוּ וְאָמְרוּ לוֹ, מֵת רַבָּךְ, אוֹ מְכָרָךְ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, אוֹ נְתָנָךְ בְּמַתָּנָה, אוֹ עֲשָׂאָךְ בֶּן חוֹרִין.
phrases.en: If a woman was eating terumah, and they came and said to her, “Your husband is dead”, or “He divorced you.” Or, if a slave was eating terumah, and they came and said to him: “Your master is dead”, or “He sold you to an Israelite”, or “He gave you away as a gift”, or “He emancipated you.

phrases.he: וְכֵן כֹּהֵן שֶׁהָיָה אוֹכֵל בִּתְרוּמָה, וְנוֹדַע שֶׁהוּא בֶן גְּרוּשָׁה אוֹ בֶן חֲלוּצָה, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְחַיֵּב קֶרֶן וְחֹמֶשׁ, וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ פּוֹטֵר.
phrases.en: So too, if a priest was eating terumah and it became known that he was the son of a divorced woman or a halutzah (a woman released from levirate marriage): Rabbi Eliezer says: they must repay both the value and the fifth. But Rabbi Joshua exempts them [from the added fifth].

phrases.he: הָיָה עוֹמֵד וּמַקְרִיב עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, וְנוֹדַע שֶׁהוּא בֶן גְּרוּשָׁה אוֹ בֶן חֲלוּצָה,
phrases.en: If [a priest] was standing and sacrificing on the altar and it became known that he was the son of a divorced woman or a halutzah: Rabbi Eliezer says: all the sacrifices he had offered on the altar are disqualified.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, כָּל הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת שֶׁהִקְרִיב עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, פְּסוּלִים. וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מַכְשִׁיר.
phrases.en: But Rabbi Joshua pronounces them valid. If it, however, it became known that he possessed a blemish, his service is disqualified.

phrases.he: נוֹדַע שֶׁהוּא בַעַל מוּם, עֲבוֹדָתוֹ פְּסוּלָה
וְכֻלָּם, שֶׁהָיְתָה תְרוּמָה בְתוֹךְ פִּיהֶם,
phrases.en: In all the above cases, if terumah was still in their mouth: Rabbi Eliezer says: they may swallow it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, יִבְלְעוּ.
phrases.en: But Rabbi Joshua says: they must spit it out.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, יִפְלֹטוּ.
phrases.en: [If it was said to him], “Your have become unclean”, or “the terumah has become unclean”, Rabbi Eliezer says: he may swallow it.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, נִטְמֵאתָ וְנִטְמֵאת תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.en: But Rabbi Joshua says: he must spit it out.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, יִבְלָע.
phrases.en: [If it was said to him], “You were unclean” or “the terumah was unclean”, or it became known that [the food he was eating] was untithed, or that it was first tithe from which terumah had not yet been taken, or second tithe or dedicated produce that had not been redeemed, or if he tasted the taste of a bug in his mouth, he must spit it out.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, יִפְלֹט.

טָמֵא הָיִיתָ וּטְמֵאָה הָיְתָה תְרוּמָה, אוֹ נוֹדַע שֶׁהוּא טֶבֶל, וּמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלֹּא נִטְּלָה תְרוּמָתוֹ, וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא נִפְדּוּ, אוֹ שֶׁטָּעַם טַעַם פִּשְׁפֵּשׁ לְתוֹךְ פִּיו, הֲרֵי זֶה יִפְלֹט
הָיָה אוֹכֵל בְּאֶשְׁכּוֹל וְנִכְנַס מִן הַגִּנָּה לֶחָצֵר,
phrases.en: If he was eating a bunch of grapes, and he entered from the garden into the courtyard: Rabbi Eliezer says: he may finish eating.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, יִגְמֹר.
phrases.en: But Rabbi Joshua says: he may not finish.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, לֹא יִגְמֹר. חֲשֵׁכָה לֵילֵי שַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: If dusk set in at the eve of Shabbat: Rabbi Joshua says: he may finish eating.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, יִגְמֹר.
phrases.en: But Rabbi Eliezer says: he may not finish.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, לֹא יִגְמֹר:
יַיִן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה, יִשָּׁפֵךְ, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר שֶׁל חֻלִּין.
phrases.en: If wine of terumah was left uncovered, it must be poured out, and there is no need to say this in the case of hullin.

phrases.he: שְׁלֹשָׁה מַשְׁקִין אֲסוּרִים מִשּׁוּם גִּלּוּי, הַמַּיִם וְהַיַּיִן וְהֶחָלָב.
phrases.en: Three kinds of liquids are forbidden if they were left uncovered: water, wine and milk, but all other drinks are permitted.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַמַּשְׁקִין מֻתָּרִים.
phrases.en: How long do they remain uncovered for them to become prohibited? The time it takes the snake to creep out from a place near by and drink.

phrases.he: כַּמָּה יִשְׁהוּ וְיִהְיוּ אֲסוּרִין, כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּצֵא הָרַחַשׁ מִמָּקוֹם קָרוֹב וְיִשְׁתֶּה
שִׁעוּר הַמַּיִם הַמְגֻלִּין, כְּדֵי שֶׁתֹּאבַד בָּהֶם הַמָּרָה.
phrases.en: The amount of water that is uncovered: enough to negate the poison.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, בְּכֵלִים, כָּל שֶׁהֵן, וּבַקַּרְקָעוֹת, אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: in vessels [it is forbidden] whatever the quantity, but for water on the ground, it must be forty se'ahs.

phrases.he: נִקּוּרֵי תְאֵנִים וַעֲנָבִים וְקִשּׁוּאִין וְהַדְּלוּעִין וְהָאֲבַטִּיחִים וְהַמְּלָפְפוֹנוֹת, אֲפִלּוּ הֵם כִּכָּר, אֶחָד גָּדוֹל וְאֶחָד קָטָן, אֶחָד תָּלוּשׁ וְאֶחָד מְחֻבָּר, כָּל שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ לֵחָה, אָסוּר.
phrases.en: Figs, grapes, cucumbers, pumpkins, melons or watermelons that have bite marks, even if they are in a jar, both large or small, both plucked or still attached to the soil, they are forbidden as long as there is juice in them.

phrases.he: וּנְשׁוּכַת הַנָּחָשׁ, אֲסוּרָה, מִפְּנֵי סַכָּנַת נְפָשׁוֹת
phrases.en: [An animal] bitten by a snake is forbidden on account of the danger to life.

phrases.he: הַמְשַׁמֶּרֶת שֶׁל יַיִן, אֲסוּרָה מִשּׁוּם גִּלּוּי. רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה מַתִּיר:
phrases.en: A wine-filter [used as a cover] does not prevent [the wine from becoming] forbidden by being uncovered. But Rabbi Nehemiah permits it.

phrases.he: חָבִית שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה שֶׁנּוֹלַד בָּהּ סְפֵק טֻמְאָה,
phrases.en: A jar of terumah which may have become impure:Rabbi Eliezer says: if it had been deposited in an exposed place, he must now place it in a hidden place; and if it had formerly been uncovered, it must now be covered.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אִם הָיְתָה מֻנַּחַת בִּמְקוֹם תֻּרְפָּה, יַנִּיחֶנָּה בְּמָקוֹם הַמֻּצְנָע, וְאִם הָיְתָה מְגֻלָּה, יְכַסֶּנָּה.
phrases.en: But Rabbi Joshua says: if it had been in a hidden place, he must now place it in an exposed place; and if it had formerly been covered up, he must now uncover it.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, אִם הָיְתָה מֻנַּחַת בְּמָקוֹם מֻצְנָע, יַנִּיחֶנָּה בִּמְקוֹם תֻּרְפָּה, וְאִם הָיְתָה מְכֻסָּה, יְגַלֶּנָּה.
phrases.en: Rabban Gamaliel says: let him not do anything new to it.

phrases.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, אַל יְחַדֵּשׁ בָּהּ דָּבָר
חָבִית שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה בַּגַּת הָעֶלְיוֹנָה, וְהַתַּחְתּוֹנָה טְמֵאָה, מוֹדֶה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, שֶׁאִם יְכוֹלִים לְהַצִּיל מִמֶּנָּה רְבִיעִית בְּטָהֳרָה, יַצִּיל. וְאִם לָאו,
phrases.en: A jar [of terumah] was broken in the upper part of the wine-press, and the lower part was unclean: Both Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Joshua agree that if one can save at least a reviit of it in cleanness he should save it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, תֵּרֵד וְתִטַּמֵּא, וְאַל יְטַמְּאֶנָּה בְיָדָיו:
phrases.en: But if not: Rabbi Eliezer says: let it flow down and become unclean of its own accord, and let him not make it unclean with his own hands.

phrases.he: וְכֵן חָבִית שֶׁל שֶׁמֶן שֶׁנִּשְׁפְּכָה, מוֹדֶה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, שֶׁאִם יָכוֹל לְהַצִּיל מִמֶּנָּה רְבִיעִית בְּטָהֳרָה, יַצִּיל. וְאִם לָאו,
phrases.en: Similarly a jar of [terumah] oil which spilled: Both Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Joshua agree that if he can save at least a reviit in purity he should save it; But if not: Rabbi Eliezer says: let it flow down and be swallowed up by the ground, and let him not make it unclean with his own hands.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, תֵּרֵד וְתִבָּלַע, וְאַל יְבַלְּעֶנָּה בְיָדָיו:
וְעַל זוֹ וְעַל זוֹ
phrases.en: Concerning both cases Rabbi Joshua said: This is not the kind of terumah over which I am cautioned lest I defile it, but rather to eat of it and not to defile it.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, לֹא זוֹ הִיא תְרוּמָה שֶׁאֲנִי מֻזְהָר עָלֶיהָ מִלְּטַמְּאָהּ, אֶלָּא מִלְּאָכְלָהּ.
phrases.en: If one was passing from place to place with loaves of terumah in his hand and a Gentile said to him: “Give me one of these and I will make it unclean; for if not, I will defile them all,” let him defile them all, and not give him deliberately one to defile, the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.he: וּבַל תְּטַמְּאָהּ כֵּיצַד, הָיָה עוֹבֵר מִמָּקוֹם לְמָקוֹם וְכִכָּרוֹת שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה בְיָדוֹ,
אָמַר לוֹ נָכְרִי, תֶּן לִי אַחַת מֵהֶן וַאֲטַמְּאָהּ, וְאִם לָאו, הֲרֵי אֲנִי מְטַמֵּא אֶת כֻּלָּהּ,
phrases.en: But Rabbi Joshua says: he should place one of them on a rock.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, יְטַמֵּא אֶת כֻּלָּהּ, וְאַל יִתֶּן לוֹ אַחַת מֵהֶן וִיטַמֵּא.
רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, יַנִּיחַ לְפָנָיו אַחַת מֵהֶן עַל הַסָּלַע:
וְכֵן נָשִׁים שֶׁאָמְרוּ לָהֶם נָכְרִים, תְּנוּ אַחַת מִכֶּם וּנְטַמֵּא, וְאִם לָאו, הֲרֵי אָנוּ מְטַמְּאִים אֶת כֻּלְּכֶם, יְטַמְּאוּ אֶת כֻּלָּן, וְאַל יִמְסְרוּ לָהֶם נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.en: Similarly, if gentiles say to women, “Give us one of you that we may defile her, and if not, we will defile you all”, then let them all be defiled rather than hand over to them one soul from Israel.

phrases.he: הַזּוֹרֵעַ תְּרוּמָה, שׁוֹגֵג, יוֹפַךְ. וּמֵזִיד, יְקַיֵּם.
phrases.en: He who plants terumah, if unwittingly, may overturn it, but if intentionally, he must allow it to remain.

phrases.he: אִם הֵבִיאָה שְׁלִישׁ, בֵּין שׁוֹגֵג בֵּין מֵזִיד, יְקַיֵּם. וּבְפִשְׁתָּן, מֵזִיד, יוֹפַךְ
phrases.en: If it had already grown a third of its full size, whether he had planted it unwittingly or intentionally, he must allow it to remain. But in the case of flax, even when planted intentionally he must overturn it.

phrases.he: וְחַיֶּבֶת בְּלֶקֶט וּבְשִׁכְחָה וּבְפֵאָה.
phrases.en: And it is subject to gleanings, the forgotten sheaf and peah.

phrases.he: וַעֲנִיֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַעֲנִיֵּי כֹהֲנִים, מְלַקְּטִים.
phrases.en: Poor Israelites and poor priests may glean them, but the poor Israelites must sell theirs to priests for the price of terumah and the money becomes theirs.

phrases.he: וַעֲנִיֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל, מוֹכְרִין אֶת שֶׁלָּהֶם לַכֹּהֲנִים בִּדְמֵי תְרוּמָה, וְהַדָּמִים שֶׁלָּהֶם.
רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר, לֹא יְלַקְּטוּ אֶלָּא עֲנִיֵּי כֹהֲנִים, שֶׁמָּא יִשְׁכְּחוּ וְיִתְּנוּ לְתוֹךְ פִּיהֶם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Tarfon says: only poor priests may glean them, lest [the others] forget and put it into their mouths.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, אִם כֵּן, לֹא יְלַקְּטוּ אֶלָּא טְהוֹרִים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva said to him: if that be so, then only those who are clean should be allowed to glean.

phrases.he: וְחַיֶּבֶת בְּמַעַשְׂרוֹת וּבְמַעֲשַׂר עָנִי, וַעֲנִיֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַעֲנִיֵּי כֹהֲנִים נוֹטְלִים, וַעֲנִיֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל מוֹכְרִין אֶת שֶׁלָּהֶם לְכֹהֲנִים בִּדְמֵי תְרוּמָה, וְהַדָּמִים שֶׁלָּהֶם. הַחוֹבֵט מְשֻׁבָּח.
phrases.en: And it is also subject to tithes and poor man’s tithe. Both Israelites and priests that are poor may accept them, but the poor Israelites must sell that which is theirs to the priest for the price of terumah and the money belongs to them. He who beats the grain with sticks [instead of threashing with an animal] is to be praised.

phrases.he: וְהַדָּשׁ כֵּיצַד יַעֲשֶׂה, תּוֹלֶה כְפִיפוֹת בְּצַוְּארֵי בְהֵמָה וְנוֹתֵן לְתוֹכָן מֵאוֹתוֹ הַמִּין, נִמְצָא לֹא זוֹמֵם אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה וְלֹא מַאֲכִיל אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה
phrases.en: But he who threshes it [by having an animal walk on it] what should he do? He must suspend baskets from the neck of the animal and place in them from the same kind, with the result that he will neither muzzle the animal nor feed it terumah.

phrases.he: גִּדּוּלֵי תְרוּמָה, תְּרוּמָה. וְגִּדּוּלֵי גִדּוּלִין, חֻלִּין.
phrases.en: What grows from terumah is terumah, but that which grows from growths [of terumah] is hullin.

phrases.he: אֲבָל הַטֶּבֶל וּמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן וּסְפִיחֵי שְׁבִיעִית וּתְרוּמַת חוּצָה לָאָרֶץ וְהַמְדֻמָּע וְהַבִּכּוּרִים, גִּדּוּלֵיהֶן, חֻלִּין.
phrases.en: As for untithed produce, first tithe, after-growths from the sabbatical year, terumah grown outside the land, mixtures of hullin with terumah (medumma) and first-fruits what grows from them is hullin.

phrases.he: גִּדּוּלֵי הֶקְדֵּשׁ וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, חֻלִּין, וּפוֹדֶה אוֹתָם בִּזְמַן זַרְעָם
phrases.en: What grows from dedicated produce and second tithe is hullin and it is to be redeemed [at its value] at the time when it was sown.

phrases.he: מֵאָה לִגְנָה שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה וְאַחַת שֶׁל חֻלִּין, כֻּלָּן מֻתָּרִין בְּדָבָר שֶׁזַּרְעוֹ כָלֶה.
phrases.en: If a hundred rows were planted with terumah seeds and one with hullin, they all are permitted, if they are of a kind whose seed disintegrates in the soil.

phrases.he: אֲבָל בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין זַרְעוֹ כָלֶה, אֲפִלּוּ מֵאָה שֶׁל חֻלִּין וְאַחַת שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, כֻּלָּן אֲסוּרִין
phrases.en: But if they are of a kind whose seed does not disintegrate in the soil, then even if there be a hundred [rows] of hullin and one of terumah, they all are prohibited.

phrases.he: הַטֶּבֶל, גִּדּוּלָיו מֻתָּרִין בְּדָבָר שֶׁזַּרְעוֹ כָלֶה.
phrases.en: As for untithed produce, what grows from it is permissible if of a kind whose seed disintegrates [in the soil].

phrases.he: אֲבָל בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין זַרְעוֹ כָלֶה, גִּדּוּלֵי גִדּוּלִין, אֲסוּרִין.
phrases.en: But if of a kind whose seed does not disintegrate, then even what grows from plants which grew out of it are forbidden.

phrases.he: אֵיזֶהוּ דָבָר שֶׁאֵין זַרְעוֹ כָלֶה, כְּגוֹן הַלּוּף וְהַשּׁוּם וְהַבְּצָלִים.
phrases.en: Which is the kind whose seed does not disintegrate? Like luf, garlic and onions.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הַשּׁוּם, כַּשְּׂעוֹרִים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: garlic is like barley.

phrases.he: הַמְנַכֵּשׁ עִם הַנָּכְרִי בַּחֲסִיּוֹת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁפֵּרוֹתָיו טֶבֶל, אוֹכֵל מֵהֶם עֲרַאי.
phrases.en: He who weeds allium plants (whose seeds do not disintegrate) for a Gentile, even though the produce is untithed he eat from them in a casual fashion.

phrases.he: שְׁתִילֵי תְרוּמָה שֶׁנִטְמְאוּ, שְׁתָלָן, טָהֲרוּ מִלְּטַמֵּא, וַאֲסוּרִין מִלֶּאֱכֹל עַד שֶׁיָּגֹם אֶת הָאֹכֶל.
phrases.en: Saplings of terumah which had become unclean and were re-planted, become clean from their uncleanness. But they must not be eaten until the edible part [of the stalk] has been lopped off.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר עַד שֶׁיָגֹם וְיִשְׁנֶה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: he must [before eating] lop off a second time that which grew on the edible part.

phrases.he: בָּצָל שֶׁנְּתָנוֹ בְתוֹךְ עֲדָשִׁים, אִם שָׁלֵם, מֻתָּר.
phrases.en: An onion [of terumah] was placed into lentils:If the onion was whole, it is permissible; But if [the onion] had been cut up, [it is forbidden if it] imparts a flavor.

phrases.he: וְאִם חִתְּכוֹ, בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם.
phrases.en: In the case of other dishes, whether the onion is whole or cut up [it is forbidden] if it imparts a flavor.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַתַּבְשִׁיל, בֵּין שָׁלֵם בֵּין מְחֻתָּךְ, בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah permits it in the case of mashed fish, because it is used only to remove the unpleasant flavor.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר בְּצַחֲנָה, שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לִטֹּל אֶת הַזֻּהֲמָא
תַּפּוּחַ שֶׁרִסְּקוֹ וּנְתָנוֹ לְתוֹךְ עִסָּה, וְחִמְּצָהּ, הֲרֵי זוֹ אֲסוּרָה.
phrases.en: If an apple [of terumah] was chopped and placed into dough [of hullin] so that it leavened it, [the dough] is forbidden.

phrases.he: שְׂעוֹרִים שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לְתוֹךְ הַבּוֹר שֶׁל מַיִם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִבְאִישׁוּ, מֵימָיו מֻתָּרִין
phrases.en: If barley [of terumah] fell into a cistern of water, though [the barley] stinks up the water, the water is permissible.

phrases.he: הָרוֹדֶה פַּת חַמָּה וּנְתָנָהּ עַל פִּי חָבִית שֶׁל יֵין תְּרוּמָה, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹסֵר, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר.
phrases.en: One who removes warm bread from an oven and places it over an open barrel of terumah wine:Rabbi Meir says: it is forbidden.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר בְּשֶׁל חִטִּים, וְאוֹסֵר בְּשֶׁל שְׂעוֹרִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַשְּׂעוֹרִים שׁוֹאֲבוֹת
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah permits it. Rabbi Yose permits the bread of wheat but not of barley, because barley absorbs.

phrases.he: תַּנּוּר שֶׁהִסִּיקוֹ בְכַמּוֹן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה וְאָפָה בוֹ, הַפַּת מֻתֶּרֶת, שֶׁאֵין טַעַם כַּמּוֹן, אֶלָּא רֵיחַ כַּמּוֹן:
phrases.en: If an oven was heated with cumin of terumah and bread was baked in it, the bread is permitted, for there is no taste of cumin, just the smell of cumin.

phrases.he: תִּלְתָּן שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְתוֹךְ הַבּוֹר שֶׁל יַיִן, בִּתְרוּמָה, בְּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, אִם יֵשׁ בַּזֶּרַע כְּדֵי לִתֵּן טַעַם, אֲבָל לֹא בָעֵץ.
phrases.en: Fenugreek which fell into a vat of wine:If it was terumah or second tithe and there is in the seed alone without the stalk sufficient to impart a flavor [it is forbidden].

phrases.he: בִּשְׁבִיעִית וּבְכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ, אִם יֵשׁ בַּזֶּרַע וּבָעֵץ כְּדֵי לִתֵּן טָעַם
phrases.en: But if it was seventh year produce or mixed seeds in vineyards, or dedicated produce, [it is forbidden] if in both seed and stalk there is sufficient to impart a flavor.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ חֲבִילֵי תִלְתָּן בְּכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, יִדָּלֵקוּ.
phrases.en: If one had bunches of fenugreek of mixed seeds of the vineyard, they must be burned.

phrases.he: הָיוּ לוֹ חֲבִילֵי תִלְתָּן שֶׁל טֶבֶל, כּוֹתֵשׁ, וּמְחַשֵּׁב כַּמָּה זֶרַע יֶשׁ בָּהֶם, וּמַפְרִישׁ אֶת הַזֶּרַע, וְאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְהַפְרִישׁ אֶת הָעֵץ.
phrases.en: If he had bunches of fenugreek of untithed produce, he must beat them and calculate the amount of seed within them and set aside [terumah] from the seed, but he need not separate terumah from the stalks.

phrases.he: אִם הִפְרִישׁ, לֹא יֹאמַר אֶכְתּוֹשׁ וְאֶטֹּל אֶת הָעֵץ וְאֶתֵּן אֶת הַזֶּרַע, אֶלָּא נוֹתֵן הָעֵץ עִם הַזָּרַע
phrases.en: But if he did set aside [the terumah from the stalks before he beat the bunches] he must not say: “I will beat out [the seed] and take the stalks and give only the seed” but he must give the stalks together with the seed.

phrases.he: זֵיתֵי חֻלִּין שֶׁכְּבָשָׁן עִם זֵיתֵי תְרוּמָה, פְּצוּעֵי חֻלִּין עִם פְּצוּעֵי תְרוּמָה, פְּצוּעֵי חֻלִּין עִם שְׁלֵמֵי תְרוּמָה, אוֹ בְמֵי תְרוּמָה, אָסוּר.
phrases.en: Olives of hullin which were pickled together with olives of terumah, whether it was a case where crushed [olives] of hullin [which were pickled together] with crushed [olives] of terumah, or crushed [olives] of hullin with whole [olives] of terumah, or with juice of terumah, they are forbidden.

phrases.he: אֲבָל שְׁלֵמֵי חֻלִּין עִם פְּצוּעֵי תְרוּמָה, מֻתָּר
phrases.en: But if whole [olives] of hullin were pickled with crushed [olives] of terumah, they are permitted.

phrases.he: דָּג טָמֵא שֶׁכְּבָשׁוֹ עִם דָּג טָהוֹר, כָּל גָּרָב שֶׁהוּא מַחֲזִיק סָאתַיִם, אִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ מִשְׁקַל עֲשָׂרָה זוּז בִּיהוּדָה שֶׁהֵן חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים בַּגָּלִיל דָּג טָמֵא, צִירוֹ אָסוּר.
phrases.en: Unclean fish which was pickled with clean fish:If the jug contains two seahs and the unclean fish weighs ten zuz in Judean measure, which is five selas in Galilean measure, the brine is forbidden.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, רְבִיעִית בְּסָאתָיִם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: it needs be a quarter [of a log] in two seahs.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אֶחָד מִשִּׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר בּוֹ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: one-sixteenth of it.

phrases.he: חֲגָבִים טְמֵאִים שֶׁנִּכְבְּשׁוּ עִם חֲגָבִים טְהוֹרִים, לֹא פָסְלוּ אֶת צִירָם.
phrases.en: If unclean locusts were pickled together with clean ones, they do not make the brine forbidden.

phrases.he: הֵעִיד רַבִּי צָדוֹק עַל צִיר חֲגָבִים טְמֵאִים, שֶׁהוּא טָהוֹר
phrases.en: Rabbi Zadok testified that the brine of unclean locusts is clean.

phrases.he: כָּל הַנִּכְבָּשִׁים זֶה עִם זֶה, מֻתָּרִים, אֶלָּא עִם הַחֲסִית.
phrases.en: [Vegetables] pickled together are permitted, except [when pickled] with allium (onions, garlic, leeks).

phrases.he: חֲסִית שֶׁל חֻלִּין עִם חֲסִית שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, יָרָק שֶׁל חֻלִּין עִם חֲסִית שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, אָסוּר.
phrases.en: Allim of hullin [pickled] with allium of terumah, or other vegetables of hullin with leeks of terumah are forbidden.

phrases.he: אֲבָל חֲסִית שֶׁל חֻלִּין עִם יָרָק שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, מֻתָּר
phrases.en: But allium of hullin with vegetables of terumah are permitted.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, כָּל הַנִּשְׁלָקִים עִם הַתְּרָדִים, אֲסוּרִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵם נוֹתְנִין אֶת הַטָּעַם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: Anything stewed with [terumah] beets becomes forbidden, because they impart a flavor.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, כְּרוּב שֶׁל שִׁקְיָא עִם כְּרוּב שֶׁל בַּעַל, אָסוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא בוֹלֵעַ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: cabbage from a field artificially irrigated [that is stewed] with [terumah] cabbage from a field watered by rain, is forbidden because it absorbs.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כָּל הַמִּתְבַּשְּׁלִין זֶה עִם זֶה, מֻתָּרִים, אֶלָּא עִם הַבָּשָׂר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiba says: all things cooked together are permitted, except those with meat.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר, הַכָּבֵד אוֹסֶרֶת וְאֵינָהּ נֶאֱסֶרֶת, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא פוֹלֶטֶת וְאֵינָהּ בּוֹלָעַת
phrases.en: Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri says: liver renders other things forbidden, but does not become forbidden, because it gives off [flavor] but does not absorb.

phrases.he: בֵּיצָה שֶׁנִּתְבַּשְּׁלָה בִּתְבָלִין אֲסוּרִין, אֲפִלּוּ חֶלְמוֹן שֶׁלָּהּ אָסוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא בוֹלֵעַ.
phrases.en: If an egg is boiled with forbidden spices even its yolk is forbidden, because it absorbs.

phrases.he: מֵי שְׁלָקוֹת וּמֵי כְבָשִׁים שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, אֲסוּרִים לְזָרִים
phrases.en: The water in which terumah has been stewed or pickled is forbidden to non-priests.

phrases.he: אֵין נוֹתְנִין דְּבֵלָה וּגְרוֹגָרוֹת לְתוֹךְ הַמּוּרְיָס, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מְאַבְּדָן, אֲבָל נוֹתְנִין אֶת הַיַּיִן לַמּוּרְיָס.
phrases.en: One must not put a cake of pressed [terumah] figs or dried [terumah] figs into fish-brine, since it spoils them.

phrases.he: וְאֵין מְפַטְּמִין אֶת הַשֶּׁמֶן, אֲבָל עוֹשִׂין אֶת הַיַּיִן יֵנוּמְלִין.
phrases.en: But one may place [terumah] wine into fish brine. One must not perfume the oil, But one may put honey and pepper into wine.

phrases.he: אֵין מְבַשְּׁלִין יַיִן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מַמְעִיטוֹ.
phrases.en: One may not boil terumah wine, because it decreases it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מַשְׁבִּיחוֹ
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah permits this, because it improves it.

phrases.he: דְּבַשׁ תְּמָרִים, וְיֵין תַּפּוּחִים, וְחֹמֶץ סִתְוָנִיּוֹת, וּשְׁאָר כָּל מֵי פֵרוֹת שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְחַיֵּב קֶרֶן וְחֹמֶשׁ, וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ פּוֹטֵר.
phrases.en: [A non-priest drank] honey of dates, wine of apples, vinegar from winter grapes, and all other kinds of fruit juice of terumah: Rabbi Eliezer makes him liable to repay their value and the fifth; But Rabbi Joshua exempts from the fifth.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְטַמֵּא מִשּׁוּם מַשְׁקֶה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer declares [these] susceptible to uncleanness as liquids.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, לֹא מָנוּ חֲכָמִים שִׁבְעָה מַשְׁקִים כְּמוֹנֵי פְטָמִים, אֶלָּא אָמְרוּ, שִׁבְעָה מַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִים, וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַמַּשְׁקִין טְהוֹרִין:
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua says: the sages have not enumerated seven liquids as those that count spices, but rather they stated: seven liquids make things susceptible to uncleaness, whereas all other liquids do not make susceptible.

phrases.he: אֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמָרִים דְּבַשׁ, וְלֹא תַפּוּחִים יַיִן, וְלֹא סִתְוָנִיּוֹת חֹמֶץ, וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַפֵּרוֹת אֵין מְשַׁנִּין אוֹתָם מִבְּרִיָּתָן בִּתְרוּמָה וּבְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, אֶלָּא זֵיתִים וַעֲנָבִים בִּלְבָד.
phrases.en: One must not make dates into honey, apples into wine, winter-grapes into vinegar, or change any other kind of fruit that is terumah or second tithe from their natural state, except olives and grapes.

phrases.he: אֵין סוֹפְגִין אַרְבָּעִים מִשּׁוּם עָרְלָה, אֶלָּא עַל הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַזֵּיתִים וּמִן הָעֲנָבִים.
phrases.en: One does not receive forty lashes on account of orlah except with that which comes from olives and grapes.

phrases.he: וְאֵין מְבִיאִין בִּכּוּרִים מַשְׁקִין, אֶלָּא הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַזֵּיתִים וּמִן הָעֲנָבִים.
phrases.en: Liquids cannot be brought as first fruits, except with that which comes from olives and grapes.

phrases.he: וְאֵינוֹ מִטַּמֵּא מִשּׁוּם מַשְׁקֶה, אֶלָּא הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַזֵּיתִים וּמִן הָעֲנָבִים.
phrases.en: And no fruit juice is susceptible to uncleanness as liquids except with that which comes from olives and grapes.

phrases.he: וְאֵין מַקְרִיבִין עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, אֶלָּא הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַזֵּיתִים וּמִן הָעֲנָבִים
phrases.en: And nothing [that is derived from fruit] can be offered on the altar except with that which comes from olives and grapes.

phrases.he: עֻקְצֵי תְאֵנִים וּגְרוֹגָרוֹת, וְהַכְּלִיסִים וְהֶחָרוּבִין שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, אֲסוּרִים לְזָרִים:
phrases.en: The stems of fresh figs and dried figs, klisim and carobs of terumah are forbidden to non-priests.

phrases.he: גַּרְעִינֵי תְרוּמָה, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא מְכַנְּסָן, אֲסוּרוֹת, וְאִם הִשְׁלִיכָן, מֻתָּרוֹת.
phrases.en: Seeds of terumah [fruit]: When he gathers them in, they are prohibited. But if he throws them away, they are permitted.

phrases.he: וְכֵן עַצְמוֹת הַקָּדָשִׁים, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא מְכַנְּסָן, אֲסוּרִין, וְאִם הִשְׁלִיכָן, מֻתָּרִין. הַמֻּרְסָן מֻתָּר.
phrases.en: Similarly, the bones of holy things: When he gathers them in, they are prohibited. But if he throws them away, they are permitted.

phrases.he: סֻבִּין שֶׁל חֲדָשׁוֹת אֲסוּרוֹת, וְשֶׁל יְשָׁנוֹת מֻתָּרוֹת.
phrases.en: Coarse bran is permitted. Fine bran of new wheat is forbidden, and old wheat permitted.

phrases.he: וְנוֹהֵג בַּתְּרוּמָה כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁהוּא נוֹהֵג בַּחֻלִּין.
phrases.en: One may act with regard to terumah as one does with hullin.

phrases.he: הַמְסַלֵּת קַב אוֹ קַבַּיִם לִסְאָה, לֹא יְאַבֵּד אֶת הַשְּׁאָר, אֶלָּא יַנִּיחֶנּוּ בְּמָקוֹם הַמֻּצְנָע
phrases.en: One who sifts a kav or two [of fine flour] from a seah of wheat, must not leave the rest to ruin, but rather he should put it in a hidden place.

phrases.he: מְגוּרָה שֶׁפִּנָּה מִמֶּנָּה חִטֵּי תְרוּמָה, אֵין מְחַיְּבִין אוֹתוֹ לִהְיוֹת יוֹשֵׁב וּמְלַקֵּט אַחַת אַחַת, אֶלָּא מְכַבֵּד כְּדַרְכּוֹ, וְנוֹתֵן לְתוֹכָהּ חֻלִּין:
phrases.en: If a store-chamber was cleared of terumah wheat, they do not need to force him to sit down and collect each grain, but rather he may sweep it all up in his usual manner and then deposit hullin in it.

phrases.he: וְכֵן חָבִית שֶׁל שֶׁמֶן שֶׁנִּשְׁפְּכָה, אֵין מְחַיְּבִין אוֹתוֹ לִהְיוֹת יוֹשֵׁב וּמְטַפֵּחַ, אֶלָּא נוֹהֵג בָּהּ כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁהוּא נוֹהֵג בְּחֻלִּין:
phrases.en: Similarly, if a jar of oil is upset, they do not need to force him to sit down and scoop it up [with his fingers], but he may deal with it as he would in a case of hullin.

phrases.he: הַמְעָרֶה מִכַּד לְכַד וְנוֹטֵף שָׁלֹשׁ טִפִּים, נוֹתֵן לְתוֹכָהּ חֻלִּין.
phrases.en: One who pours from jar to jar and three drops drip, he may place in it hullin.

phrases.he: הִרְכִּינָהּ וּמִצָּהּ, הֲרֵי זוֹ תְרוּמָה.
phrases.en: But if he inclined the jar [on its side] in order to drain it, it is terumah.

phrases.he: וְכַמָּה תְהֵא בִתְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר שֶׁל דְּמַאי וְיוֹלִיכֶנָּה לַכֹּהֵן, אֶחָד מִשְּׁמֹנָה לַשְּׁמִינִית
phrases.en: How much terumat maaser of demai must there be for him to take it to the priest? One eighth of an eighth [of a log].

phrases.he: כַּרְשִׁינֵי תְרוּמָה, מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתָם לַבְּהֵמָה וְלַחַיָּה וְלַתַּרְנְגוֹלִים.
phrases.en: Vetches of terumah may be given to cattle, to wild beasts or fowls.

phrases.he: יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁשָּׂכַר פָּרָה מִכֹּהֵן, מַאֲכִילָהּ כַּרְשִׁינֵי תְרוּמָה.
phrases.en: If an Israelite hired a cow from a priest, he may give it vetches of terumah to eat.

phrases.he: וְכֹהֵן שֶׁשָּׂכַר פָּרָה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּזוֹנוֹתֶיהָ עָלָיו, לֹא יַאֲכִילֶנָּה כַרְשִׁינֵי תְרוּמָה.
phrases.en: But if a priest hired a cow from an Israelite, even though the responsibility of feeding it is his, he must not feed it with vetches of terumah.

phrases.he: יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁשָּׁם פָּרָה מִכֹּהֵן, לֹא יַאֲכִילֶנָּה כַרְשִׁינֵי תְרוּמָה.
phrases.en: If an Israelite undertakes the care of a cow from a priest, he must not feed it with vetches of terumah.

phrases.he: וְכֹהֵן שֶׁשָּׁם פָּרָה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, מַאֲכִילָהּ כַּרְשִׁינֵי תְרוּמָה
phrases.en: But if a priest undertakes the care of a cow from an Israelite, he may feed it on vetches of terumah.

phrases.he: מַדְלִיקִין שֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵפָה בְּבָתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת, וּבְבָתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת, וּבַמְּבוֹאוֹת הָאֲפֵלִין, וְעַל גַּבֵּי הַחוֹלִין בִּרְשׁוּת כֹּהֵן.
phrases.en: One may burn terumah oil that has to be burnt in synagogues, houses of study, dark alleys, and for sick people with permission of the priest.

phrases.he: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְכֹהֵן, וְהִיא לְמוּדָה אֵצֶל אָבִיהָ, אָבִיהָ מַדְלִיק בִּרְשׁוּתָהּ.
phrases.en: If the daughter of an Israelite married to a priest regularly goes to her father's house, her father may burn [such oil] with her permission.

phrases.he: מַדְלִיקִין בְּבֵית הַמִּשְׁתֶּה, אֲבָל לֹא בְבֵית הָאֵבֶל, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: One may also burn [such oil] in a house of celebration but not in a house of mourning, the words of Rabbi Judah.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, בְּבֵית הָאֵבֶל, אֲבָל לֹא בְבֵית הַמִּשְׁתֶּה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: in the house of mourning, but not in a house of celebration.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹסֵר כָּאן וְכָאן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir forbids it in both places.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר כָּאן וְכָאן
phrases.en: But Rabbi Shimon permits it in both places.

phrases.he: כְּלָל אָמְרוּ בַּמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, כָּל שֶׁהוּא אֹכֶל, וְנִשְׁמָר, וְגִדּוּלָיו מִן הָאָרֶץ, חַיָּב בַּמַּעַשְׂרוֹת.
phrases.en: They said a general principle concerning tithes: whatever is food, and is looked after, and grows from the land, is liable for tithes.

phrases.he: וְעוֹד כְּלָל אַחֵר אָמְרוּ, כָּל שֶׁתְּחִלָּתוֹ אֹכֶל וְסוֹפוֹ אֹכֶל, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹמְרוֹ לְהוֹסִיף אֹכֶל, חַיָּב קָטָן וְגָדוֹל.
phrases.en: And they have further stated another general principle [concerning tithes]: whatever is considered food both at the beginning and at the conclusion [of its growth] even though he holds on to it in order to increase the quantity of food, is liable [to tithe] whether [it is harvested] in its earlier or later stages.

phrases.he: וְכָל שֶׁאֵין תְּחִלָּתוֹ אֹכֶל אֲבָל סוֹפוֹ אֹכֶל, אֵינוֹ חַיָּב עַד שֶׁיֵּעָשֶׂה אֹכֶל
phrases.en: But whatever is not considered food in the earlier stages [of its growth] but only in its later stages, is not liable [to tithe] until it can be considered food.

phrases.he: מֵאֵימָתַי הַפֵּרוֹת חַיָּבוֹת בַּמַּעַשְׂרוֹת. הַתְּאֵנִים, מִשֶּׁיַּבְחִילוּ. הָעֲנָבִים וְהָאֳבָשִׁים, מִשֶּׁהִבְאִישׁוּ. הָאוֹג וְהַתּוּתִים, מִשֶּׁיַּאְדִּימוּ. וְכָל הָאֲדֻמִּים, מִשֶּׁיַּאְדִּימוּ. הָרִמּוֹנִים, מִשֶּׁיִּמַּסּוּ. הַתְּמָרִים, מִשֶּׁיָּטִּילוּ שְׂאֹר. הָאֲפַרְסְקִים, מִשֶּׁיָּטִּילוּ גִידִים. הָאֱגוֹזִים, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשׂוּ מְגוּרָה.
phrases.en: When do fruits become liable for tithes?Figs from the time they begin to ripe. Grapes and wild grapes in the early stages of ripening. Sumac and mulberries after they become red; [similarly] all red fruits, after they become red. Pomegranates, when the insides become soft. Dates when they begin to swell. Peaches when [red] veins begin to show. Walnuts when the nuts are separate from the shell.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הָאֱגוֹזִים וְהַשְּׁקֵדִים, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשׂוּ קְלִפָּה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: walnuts and almonds, after their inner skins have been formed.

phrases.he: הֶחָרוּבִין, מִשֶּׁיִּנָּקֵדוּ. וְכָל הַשְּׁחוֹרִים, מִשֶּׁיִּנָּקְדוּ.
phrases.en: Carobs [are liable to] tithes after they form dark spots; similarly all black fruits after they form dark spots.

phrases.he: הָאֲגָסִים וְהַקְּרֻסְטוֹמֵלִין וְהַפָּרִישִׁין וְהָעֻזְרָדִים, מִשֶּׁיִּקָּרֵחוּ. וְכָל הַלְּבָנִים, מִשֶּׁיִּקָּרֵחוּ. הַתִּלְתָּן, מִשֶּׁתְּצַמֵּחַ.
phrases.en: Pears and crustumenian pears, quinces, and medlars [are liable to tithes] after their surface begins to grow smooth; similarly all white fruits, after their surface begins to grow smooth. Fenugreek [is liable to tithe] when the seeds [can be planted and] will grow.

phrases.he: הַתְּבוּאָה וְהַזֵּיתִים, מִשֶּׁיַּכְנִיסוּ שְׁלִישׁ
phrases.en: Grain and olives after they are one-third ripe.

phrases.he: וּבַיָּרָק, הַקִּשּׁוּאִין וְהַדְּלוּעִים וְהָאֲבַטִּיחִים וְהַמְּלָפְפוֹנוֹת, הַתַּפּוּחִים וְהָאֶתְרוֹגִין, חַיָּבִים גְּדוֹלִים וּקְטַנִּים.
phrases.en: With regard to when vegetables [are liable to tithes]:Cucumbers, gourds, water-melons, cucumber-melons, apples and etrogs are liable [for tithes], whether gathered in the earlier or later stages of ripening.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן פּוֹטֵר אֶת הָאֶתְרוֹגִים בְּקָטְנָן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon exempts the etrog in the earlier stages.

phrases.he: הַחַיָּב בַּשְּׁקֵדִים הַמָּרִים, פָּטוּר בַּמְּתוּקִים, הַחַיָּב בַּמְּתוּקִים, פָּטוּר בַּמָּרִים
phrases.en: The condition in which bitter almonds are liable [to tithes] is exempt in the case of sweet almonds, and the condition in which sweet almonds are liable [to tithe] is exempt in the case of bitter almonds.

phrases.he: אֵיזֶהוּ גָּרְנָן לַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת. הַקִּשּׁוּאִים וְהַדְּלוּעִים, מִשֶּׁיְּפַקְסוּ.
phrases.en: What is considered a “threshing floor” for tithes [i.e. when does produce become liable for tithes]?Cucumbers and gourds [are liable for tithes] once he removes their fuzz.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ מְפַקֵּס, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲמִיד עֲרֵמָה. אֲבַטִּיחַ, מִשֶּׁיְּשַׁלֵּק.
phrases.en: And if he doesn’t remove it, once he makes a pile. Melons once he removes the fuzz with hot water.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּק, עַד שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה מֻקְצֶה. יָרָק הַנֶּאֱגָד, מִשֶּׁיֹּאגַד.
phrases.en: And if they he does not remove the fuzz, once he stores them in the muktzeh.

phrases.he: אִם אֵינוֹ אוֹגֵד, עַד שֶׁיְּמַלֵּא אֶת הַכְּלִי.
phrases.en: Vegetables which are tied in bundles, from the time he ties them up in bundles.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ מְמַלֵּא אֶת הַכְּלִי, עַד שֶׁיְּלַקֵּט כָּל צָרְכּוֹ. כַּלְכָּלָה, עַד שֶׁיְּחַפֶּה.
phrases.en: If he does not tie them up in bundles, until he fills the vessel with them. And if he does not fill the vessel, after he has gathered all that he wishes to gather.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ מְחַפֶּה, עַד שֶׁיְמַלֵּא אֶת הַכְּלִי.
phrases.en: [Produce which is packed in] a basket [is liable for tithes] after he has covered it.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ מְמַלֵּא אֶת הַכְּלִי, עַד שֶׁיְּלַקֵּט כָּל צָרְכּוֹ.
phrases.en: If he is not going to cover it, until he fills the vessel with them. And if he does not fill the vessel, after he has gathered all that he wishes to gather.

phrases.he: בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בְּמוֹלִיךְ לַשּׁוּק.
phrases.en: When does this apply? When one brings [the produce] to the market.

phrases.he: אֲבָל בְּמוֹלִיךְ לְבֵיתוֹ, אוֹכֵל מֵהֶם עֲרַאי עַד שֶׁהוּא מַגִּיעַ לְבֵיתוֹ
phrases.en: But when he brings it to his own house, he may make a chance meal of it, until he reaches his house.

phrases.he: הַפֶּרֶד וְהַצִּמּוּקִין וְהֶחָרוּבִין, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲמִיד עֲרֵמָה. הַבְּצָלִים, מִשֶּׁיְּפַקֵּל.
phrases.en: Dried pomegranate seeds, raisins and carobs, [are liable for tithes] after he has made a pile. Onions, once he removes the onion seeds.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ מְפַקֵּל, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲמִיד עֲרֵמָה. הַתְּבוּאָה, מִשֶּׁיְּמָרֵחַ.
phrases.en: If he does not remove the onion seeds, after he makes a pile. Grain, once he smoothes out the pile.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ מְמָרֵחַ, עַד שֶׁיַּעֲמִיד עֲרֵמָה. הַקִּטְנִיּוֹת, מִשֶּׁיִּכְבֹּר.
phrases.en: If he does not smooth the pile, after he makes a pile. Pulse, after he has sifted it. If he does not sift, after he smoothes out a pile.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ כוֹבֵר, עַד שֶׁיְּמָרֵחַ.
phrases.en: Even after he has smoothed out the pile, he may [without tithing] take from the broken ears, from the sides of the piles, and from that which is mixed in with the chaff, and eat.

phrases.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמֵּרַח, נוֹטֵל מִן הַקֻּטָּעִים וּמִן הַצְּדָדִים וּמִמַּה שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ הַתֶּבֶן, וְאוֹכֵל
הַיַּיִן, מִשֶּׁיְּקַפֶּה. אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁקִּפָּה, קוֹלֵט מִן הַגַּת הָעֶלְיוֹנָה וּמִן הַצִּנּוֹר, וְשׁוֹתֶה. הַשֶּׁמֶן, מִשֶּׁיֵּרֵד לָעוּקָה.
phrases.en: Wine [is liable for tithes] after it has been skimmed [in the lower part of the winepress]. Even though it has been skimmed, he may take from the upper winepress, or from the duct, and drink [without taking out tithe].

phrases.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיָּרַד, נוֹטֵל מִן הֶעָקָל וּמִבֵּין הַמָּמָל וּמִבֵּין הַפַּצִּים, וְנוֹתֵן לַחֲמִטָּה וְלַתַּמְחוּי, אֲבָל לֹא יִתֵּן לַקְּדֵרָה וְלַלְּפָס כְּשֶׁהֵן רוֹתְחִין.
phrases.en: Oil [is liable for tithes] after it has gone down into the trough. But even after it has gone down into the trough he may still take oil from the pressing bale, or from the press beam, or from the boards between the press [without tithing,] And he may put such oil on a cake, or large plate.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, לַכֹּל הוּא נוֹתֵן, חוּץ מִדָּבָר שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ חֹמֶץ וְצִיר:
phrases.en: But he should not put the oil in a dish or stewpot, while they are boiling. Rabbi Judah says: he may put it into anything except that which contains vinegar or brine.

phrases.he: הָעִגּוּל, מִשֶּׁיַּחֲלִיקֶנּוּ. מַחֲלִיקִים בִּתְאֵנִים וּבַעֲנָבִים שֶׁל טֶבֶל. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹסֵר.
phrases.en: A cake of pressed figs [is liable for tithes] from the moment it has been smoothed out [with fruit juice]. They may smooth them out with [the juice of] untithed figs or grapes. Rabbi Judah forbids this.

phrases.he: הַמַּחֲלִיק בַּעֲנָבִים, לֹא הֻכְשָׁר.
phrases.en: If one smoothed with grapes, it is not susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הֻכְשָׁר. הַגְּרוֹגָרוֹת, מִשֶּׁיָּדוּשׁ. וּמְגוּרָה מִשֶּׁיְּעַגֵּל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says it is susceptible. Dried figs [are liable to tithe] after they have been pressed [into a jar]. And [figs] stored in a bin [are liable to tithe] after they have been pressed.

phrases.he: הָיָה דָשׁ בֶּחָבִית וּמְעַגֵּל בַּמְּגוּרָה, נִשְׁבְּרָה הֶחָבִית וְנִפְתְּחָה הַמְּגוּרָה, לֹא יֹאכַל מֵהֶם עֲרָאי. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר
phrases.en: If one was pressing [the figs] into a jar, or pressing them in a storage bin, and the jar was broken or the storage bin opened, he may not make a chance meal of them. Rabbi Yose permits this.

phrases.he: הָיָה עוֹבֵר בַּשּׁוּק וְאָמַר, טְלוּ לָכֶם תְּאֵנִים, אוֹכְלִין וּפְטוּרִין.
phrases.en: If one was passing through the street, and said “Take for yourself from my figs,” one may eat them and be exempt from tithes.

phrases.he: לְפִיכָךְ אִם הִכְנִיסוּ לְבָתֵּיהֶם, מְתַקְּנִים וַדָּאי.
phrases.en: Therefore if they brought them into their houses, they must separate [tithes and terumah] as if they were certainly untithed.

phrases.he: טְלוּ וְהַכְנִיסוּ לְבָתֵּיכֶם, לֹא יֹאכְלוּ מֵהֶם עֲרַאי.
phrases.en: [If he said], “Take and bring it into your houses,” they may not make a chance meal of them.

phrases.he: לְפִיכָךְ אִם הִכְנִיסוּ לְבָתֵּיהֶם, אֵינָם מְתַקְּנִים אֶלָּא דְמָאי
phrases.en: Therefore if they brought them into their houses, they need tithe them only as demai.

phrases.he: הָיוּ יוֹשְׁבִין בַּשַּׁעַר אוֹ בַחֲנוּת, וְאָמַר, טְלוּ לָכֶם תְּאֵנִים, אוֹכְלִין וּפְטוּרִין, וּבַעַל הַשַּׁעַר וּבַעַל הַחֲנוּת חַיָּבִין.
phrases.en: If they were sitting at the gate or a shop, and one said [to them], “Take for yourselves figs,” they may eat and be exempt from tithes, but the owner of the gate, or the owner of the shop, is liable [to give tithe].

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה פּוֹטֵר, עַד שֶׁיַּחֲזִיר אֶת פָּנָיו, אוֹ עַד שֶׁיְּשַׁנֶּה מְקוֹם יְשִׁיבָתוֹ
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah exempts him unless he turns his face or changes the place where he was sitting [and selling].

phrases.he: הַמַּעֲלֶה פֵרוֹת מִן הַגָּלִיל לִיהוּדָה, אוֹ עוֹלֶה לִירוּשָׁלַיִם, אוֹכֵל מֵהֶם עַד שֶׁהוּא מַגִּיעַ לְמָקוֹם שֶׁהוּא הוֹלֵךְ, וְכֵן בִּיהוּדָה.
phrases.en: One who brings produce from the Galilee to Judea, or if he goes up to Jerusalem, he may eat of them until he arrives at the place to which he intends to go, and the same is true when he returns.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, עַד שֶׁהוּא מַגִּיעַ לִמְקוֹם הַשְּׁבִיתָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: [he may eat] until he reaches the place where he intends to rest [on Shabbat].

phrases.he: וְהָרוֹכְלִין הַמְּחַזְּרִין בָּעֲיָרוֹת, אוֹכְלִים עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעִים לִמְקוֹם הַלִּינָה.
phrases.en: But peddlers who travel from town to town may eat until they reach the place where they intend to stay over night.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הַבַּיִת הָרִאשׁוֹן הוּא בֵיתוֹ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: the first house [he reaches] is his house.

phrases.he: פֵּרוֹת שֶׁתְּרָמָן עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתָּן, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹסֵר מִלֶּאֱכֹל מֵהֶם עֲרַאי.
phrases.en: Produce from which he separated terumah before its work was finished: Rabbi Eliezer says: it is forbidden to make a chance meal of it, But the sages permit it except when it is a basket of figs.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים מַתִּירִין, חוּץ מִכַּלְכָּלַת תְּאֵנִים.
phrases.en: A basket of figs from which one separated terumah: Rabbi Shimon permits it.

phrases.he: כַּלְכָּלַת תְּאֵנִים שֶׁתְּרָמָהּ, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִין
phrases.en: But the sages forbid it.

phrases.he: הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵרוֹ, הֵילָךְ אִסָּר זֶה וְתֶן לִי בוֹ חָמֵשׁ תְּאֵנִים, לֹא יֹאכַל עַד שֶׁיְּעַשֵּׂר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: One who says to his friend: “Here is this issar, give me five figs for it”, he may not eat of [them] until he has tithed them, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אוֹכֵל אַחַת אַחַת, פָּטוּר, וְאִם צֵרַף, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: if he ate them one by one, he is exempt, but if he gathered them [to eat them] together, he is liable [to tithe.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah said: it happened in a rose-garden in Jerusalem that there were figs being sold three or four for an issar, and neither terumah nor tithe was ever given from it.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בְגִנַּת וְרָדִים שֶׁהָיְתָה בִירוּשָׁלַיִם, וְהָיוּ תְאֵנִים נִמְכָּרוֹת מִשָּׁלֹשׁ וּמֵאַרְבַּע בְּאִסָּר, וְלֹא הֻפְרַשׁ מִמֶּנָּה תְרוּמָה וּמַעֲשֵׂר מֵעוֹלָם:
הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵרוֹ, הֵילָךְ אִסָּר זֶה בְּעֶשֶׂר תְּאֵנִים שֶׁאָבֹר לִי, בּוֹרֵר וְאוֹכֵל.
phrases.en: One who says to his friend: “Here is an issar for ten figs which I choose for myself,” he may choose them and eat [one at a time without tithing].

phrases.he: בְּאֶשְׁכּוֹל שֶׁאָבֹר לִי, מְגַרְגֵּר וְאוֹכֵל.
phrases.en: [If he said] “For a cluster of grapes which I choose for myself,” he may pick grapes from the cluster and eat.

phrases.he: בְּרִמּוֹן שֶׁאָבֹר לִי, פּוֹרֵט וְאוֹכֵל.
phrases.en: [If he said], “For a pomegranate which I choose for myself,” he may take apart [the pomegranate] and eat [it one piece at a time].

phrases.he: בַּאֲבַטִּיחַ שֶׁאָבֹר לִי, סוֹפֵת וְאוֹכֵל. אֲבָל אִם
אָמַר לוֹ בְּעֶשְׂרִים תְּאֵנִים אֵלוּ, בִּשְׁנֵי אֶשְׁכּוֹלוֹת אֵלוּ, בִּשְׁנֵי רִמּוֹנִים אֵלוּ, בִּשְׁנֵי אֲבַטִּיחִים אֵלוּ, אוֹכֵל כְּדַרְכּוֹ וּפָטוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁקָּנָה בִמְחֻבָּר לַקַּרְקָע:
phrases.en: [If he said] “For a watermelon, which I choose for myself,” he may slice and eat [it one piece at a time]. But if he said “For these twenty figs,” or “For these two clusters,” or “For these two water-melons,” he may eat them in his usual way and be exempt [from tithe], because he bought them while they were still attached to the ground.

phrases.he: הַשּׂוֹכֵר אֶת הַפּוֹעֵל לִקְצוֹת עִמּוֹ בִּתְאֵנִים,
phrases.en: One who has hired a worker to help him harvest figs, and he [the worker] said to him “On condition that I may eat the figs,” he may eat them and he is exempt [from tithing].

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ עַל מְנָת שֶׁאוֹכַל תְּאֵנִים, אוֹכֵל וּפָטוּר.
phrases.en: [If he said,] “On condition that I and my son may eat,” or “that my son may eat of them in lieu of my receiving a wage,” he may eat and he is exempt [from tithing], but his son may eat but he is liable [for tithes].

phrases.he: עַל מְנָת שֶׁאוֹכַל אֲנִי וּבְנֵי בֵיתִי, אוֹ שֶׁיֹּאכַל בְּנִי בִּשְׂכָרִי, הוּא אוֹכֵל וּפָטוּר, וּבְנוֹ אוֹכֵל וְחַיָּב.
phrases.en: [If he said,] “On condition that I may eat of them during the time of the fig harvest, and after the fig harvest,” during the time of the fig harvest he may eat and he is exempt [from tithing], but if he eats after the fig harvest he is liable, since he does not eat of them in the manner mandated by the Torah.

phrases.he: עַל מְנָת שֶׁאוֹכַל בִּשְׁעַת הַקְּצִיעָה וּלְאַחַר הַקְּצִיעָה, בִּשְׁעַת הַקְּצִיעָה אוֹכֵל וּפָטוּר, וּלְאַחַר הַקְּצִיעָה אוֹכֵל וְחַיָּב, שֶׁאֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
phrases.en: This is the general rule: one who eats in a manner mandated by the Torah is exempt [from tithes], and one who does not eat in the manner mandated by the Torah is liable.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, הָאוֹכֵל מִן הַתּוֹרָה, פָּטוּר, וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל מִן הַתּוֹרָה, חַיָּב
הָיָה עוֹשֶׂה בִלְבָסִים, לֹא יֹאכַל בִּבְנוֹת שֶׁבַע.
phrases.en: If a man is working [as a hired worker] among cooking figs, he may not eat of white figs, and if among white figs, he may not eat of cooking figs, but he may restrain himself until he reaches the place where there are the better figs, and then he may eat.

phrases.he: בִּבְנוֹת שֶׁבַע, לֹא יֹאכַל בִּלְבָסִים.
phrases.en: If a man exchanges with his friend either [figs] for eating for [figs] for eating, or [figs] to be dried for figs [to be dried], of figs [for eating] for figs [to be dried], then he is liable to give tithes.

phrases.he: אֲבָל מוֹנֵעַ הוּא אֶת עַצְמוֹ עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לִמְקוֹם הַיָּפוֹת וְאוֹכֵל.
הַמַּחֲלִיף עִם חֲבֵרוֹ, זֶה לֶאֱכֹל וְזֶה לֶאֱכֹל, זֶה לִקְצוֹת וְזֶה לִקְצוֹת, זֶה לֶאֱכֹל וְזֶה לִקְצוֹת, חַיָּב.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הַמַּחֲלִיף לֶאֱכֹל, חַיָּב, וְלִקְצוֹת, פָּטוּר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: one who exchanges [figs] for [other figs for eating] is liable, but [if for figs] for drying he is exempt.

phrases.he: הַמַּעֲבִיר תְּאֵנִים בַּחֲצֵרוֹ לִקְצוֹת, בָּנָיו וּבְנֵי בֵיתוֹ אוֹכְלִין וּפְטוּרִין.
phrases.en: One who was taking figs through his courtyard to be dried, his children and the other members of his household may eat [of them] and they are exempt [from tithes].

phrases.he: הַפּוֹעֲלִים שֶׁעִמּוֹ, בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם עָלָיו מְזוֹנוֹת, אוֹכְלִין וּפְטוּרִין.
phrases.en: The workers [who work] with him may eat and be exempt so long as he is not obliged to provide for them.

phrases.he: אֲבָל אִם יֶשׁ לָהֶם עָלָיו מְזוֹנוֹת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ לֹא יֹאכֵלוּ
phrases.en: If however, he is obligated to provide for them they may not eat.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹצִיא פּוֹעֲלָיו לַשָּׂדֶה, בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם עָלָיו מְזוֹנוֹת, אוֹכְלִין וּפְטוּרִין.
phrases.en: One who brought his workers into the field, when he is not obligated to provide for them, they may eat and be exempt from tithes.

phrases.he: וְאִם יֶשׁ לָהֶם עָלָיו מְזוֹנוֹת, אוֹכְלִין אַחַת אַחַת מִן הַתְּאֵנָה, אֲבָל לֹא מִן הַסַּל וְלֹא מִן הַקֻּפָּה וְלֹא מִן הַמֻּקְצֶה
phrases.en: If, however, he is obligated to provide for them they may eat of the figs one at a time, but not from the basket, nor from the large basket, nor from the storage yard.

phrases.he: הַשּׂוֹכֵר אֶת הַפּוֹעֵל לַעֲשׂוֹת בְּזֵיתִים,
phrases.en: One who hired a worker to work with olives and he said to him, “On condition that I may eat the olives,” he may eat of them one at a time and be exempt [from tithes].

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ עַל מְנָת לֶאֱכֹל זֵיתִים, אוֹכֵל אֶחָד אֶחָד וּפָטוּר. וְאִם צֵרַף, חַיָּב. לְנַכֵּשׁ בִּבְצָלִים,
phrases.en: If, however, he gathered several together he is liable [for tithes].

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ עַל מְנָת לֶאֱכֹל יָרָק, מְקַרְטֵם עָלֶה עָלֶה וְאוֹכֵל. וְאִם צֵרַף, חַיָּב:
phrases.en: [If he had been hired] to weed out onions, and he said to him, “On condition that I may eat the vegetables,” he may pluck leaf by leaf, and eat [without tithing]. If, however, he gathered several together, he is liable [for tithes].

phrases.he: מָצָא קְצִיצוֹת בַּדֶּרֶךְ, אֲפִלּוּ בְצַד שְׂדֵה קְצִיצוֹת, וְכֵן תְּאֵנָה שֶׁהִיא נוֹטָה עַל דֶּרֶךְ, וּמָצָא תַחְתֶּיהָ תְּאֵנִים, מֻתָּרוֹת מִשּׁוּם גָּזֵל וּפְטוּרוֹת מִן הַמַּעֲשְׂרוֹת. וּבְזֵיתִים וּבְחָרוּבִים, חַיָּבִים.
phrases.en: If one found cut figs on the road, or even beside a field [where cut figs] have been spread [to dry], and similarly, if a fig tree overhangs the road, and he found figs beneath it, they are allowed [with regard to the laws] of robbery, and they are exempt from tithe. But if they were olives and carobs, they are liable.

phrases.he: מָצָא גְרוֹגָרוֹת, אִם דָּרְסוּ רוֹב בְּנֵי אָדָם, חַיָּב, וְאִם לָאו, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: If one found dried figs, then if the majority of people had already trodden [their figs], he must tithe [them], but if not he is exempt.

phrases.he: מָצָא פִלְחֵי דְבֵלָה, חַיָּב, שֶׁיָּדוּעַ שֶׁהֵן מִדָּבָר גָּמוּר.
phrases.en: If one found slices of fig-cake he is liable [to tithe] since it is obvious they come from something whose processing had been fully completed.

phrases.he: וְהֶחָרוּבִין, עַד שֶׁלֹּא כְנָסָן לְרֹאשׁ הַגַּג, מוֹרִיד מֵהֶם לִבְהֵמָה, פָּטוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מַחֲזִיר אֶת הַמּוֹתָר
phrases.en: With carobs, if they had not yet been on the top of the roof, he may take some down for his animals and be exempt [from tithe] since he returns that which is left over.

phrases.he: אֵיזוֹ הִיא חָצֵר שֶׁהִיא חַיֶּבֶת בַּמַּעֲשְׂרוֹת,
phrases.en: Which courtyard is it which makes [the produce] liable to tithe? Rabbi Ishmael says: the Tyrian yard for the vessels are protected therein.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, חָצֵר הַצּוֹרִית, שֶׁהַכֵּלִים נִשְׁמָרִים בְּתוֹכָהּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: any courtyard which one person may open and another may shut is exempt.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, כָּל שֶׁאֶחָד פּוֹתֵחַ וְאֶחָד נוֹעֵל, פְּטוּרָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Nehemiah says: any courtyard in which a man is not ashamed to eat is liable.

phrases.he: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר, כָּל שֶׁאֵין אָדָם בּוֹשׁ מִלֶּאֱכֹל בְּתוֹכָהּ, חַיֶּבֶת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: any courtyard into which a person may enter and no one says to him, “what are you looking for” is exempt.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, כָּל שֶׁנִּכְנָס לָהּ וְאֵין אוֹמֵר מָה אַתָּה מְבַקֵּשׁ, פְּטוּרָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: if there are two courtyards one within the other, the inner one makes liable and the outer one is exempt.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, שְׁנֵי חֲצֵרוֹת זוֹ לִפְנִים מִזּוֹ, הַפְּנִימִית חַיֶּבֶת, וְהַחִיצוֹנָה פְּטוּרָה:
הַגַּגּוֹת פְּטוּרִין, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵם שֶׁל חָצֵר הַחַיָּבֶת.
phrases.en: Roofs do not render [produce] liable, even though they belong to a courtyard which renders it liable.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁעַר, אַכְסַדְרָה וּמִרְפֶּסֶת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ כֶּחָצֵר, אִם חַיֶּבֶת, חַיָּבִין, וְאִם פְּטוּרָה, פְּטוּרִים
phrases.en: A gate house, portico, or balcony, are like the courtyard [to which it belongs]; if [the courtyard] makes the [produce] liable [for tithes] so do they, and if it does not, they do not.

phrases.he: הַצְּרִיפִין וְהַבֻּרְגָּנִין וְהָאֶלְקָטִיּוֹת, פְּטוּרִין.
phrases.en: Cone-shaped huts, watchtowers, and sheds in the field do not render [produce] liable.

phrases.he: סֻכַּת גִּנּוֹסַר, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ רֵחַיִם וְתַרְנְגוֹלִים, פְּטוּרָה.
phrases.en: A sukkah-hut like those used in Ginnosar, even though it contains millstones and poultry, does not render [produce] liable.

phrases.he: סֻכַּת הַיּוֹצְרִים, הַפְּנִימִית חַיֶּבֶת, וְהַחִיצוֹנָה פְּטוּרָה.
phrases.en: As for the potter’s sukkah-hut, the inner part renders [produce] liable and the outer part does not.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, כָּל שֶׁאֵינָהּ דִּירַת הַחַמָּה וְדִירַת הַגְּשָׁמִים, פְּטוּרָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: anything which is not both a sunny season and rainy season dwelling does not render [produce] liable [to tithes].

phrases.he: סֻכַּת הֶחָג בֶּחָג, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְחַיֵּב, וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹטְרִין
phrases.en: A sukkah used on the Festival [of Sukkot]: Rabbi Judah says: this renders [produce] liable [for tithes] But the sages exempt.

phrases.he: תְּאֵנָה שֶׁהִיא עוֹמֶדֶת בֶּחָצֵר, אוֹכֵל אַחַת אַחַת וּפָטוּר. וְאִם צֵרַף, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: A fig tree which stands in a courtyard: one may eat the figs from it one at a time and be exempt [from tithes], but if he gathered some together he is liable.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אַחַת בִּימִינוֹ וְאַחַת בִּשְׂמֹאלוֹ וְאַחַת בְּפִיו.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: if he has [one in his right hand and one in his left hand and one in his mouth, he is exempt.

phrases.he: עָלָה לְרֹאשָׁהּ, מְמַלֵּא חֵיקוֹ וְאוֹכֵל
phrases.en: If he ascended to the top [of it], he may fill his bosom and eat.

phrases.he: גֶּפֶן שֶׁהִיא נְטוּעָה בֶחָצֵר, נוֹטֵל אֶת כָּל הָאֶשְׁכּוֹל.
phrases.en: A vine which was planted in a courtyard: one may take a whole cluster [and eat it without tithing].

phrases.he: וְכֵן בְּרִמּוֹן, וְכֵן בַּאֲבַטִּיחַ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן.
phrases.en: Similarly with a pomegranate, or a melon, the words of Rabbi Tarfon.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, מְגַרְגֵּר בָּאֶשְׁכּוֹלוֹת, וּפוֹרֵט בָּרִמּוֹן, וְסוֹפֵת בָּאֲבַטִּיחַ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: he can pick single berries from the cluster, or split the pomegranate into slices, or cut slices of melon [and eat without tithing].

phrases.he: כֻּסְבָּר שֶׁהִיא זְרוּעָה בֶחָצֵר, מְקַרְטֵם עָלֶה עָלֶה וְאוֹכֵל. וְאִם צֵרַף, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: Coriander which was sown in a courtyard: one may pluck leaf by leaf and eat [without tithing], but if he ate them together he is liable [for tithes].

phrases.he: הַסֵּאָה וְהָאֵזוֹב וְהַקּוֹרָנִית שֶׁבֶּחָצֵר, אִם הָיוּ נִשְׁמָרִים, חַיָּבִין
phrases.en: Savory and hyssop, and thyme which are in the courtyard, if they are kept watch over, they are liable for tithe.

phrases.he: תְּאֵנָה שֶׁהִיא עוֹמֶדֶת בֶּחָצֵר וְנוֹטָה לַגִּנָּה, אוֹכֵל כְּדַרְכּוֹ וּפָטוּר.
phrases.en: A fig tree which stands in a courtyard, and hangs over into a garden: one may eat in his customary fashion and be exempt [from tithes].

phrases.he: עוֹמֶדֶת בַּגִּנָּה וְנוֹטָה לֶחָצֵר, אוֹכֵל אַחַת אַחַת, פָּטוּר. וְאִם צֵרַף, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: If it stands in the garden and hangs over into the courtyard, one may eat [the figs] one at a time and be exempt, but if he gathers them together, he is liable [for tithes].

phrases.he: עוֹמֶדֶת בָּאָרֶץ וְנוֹטָה לְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ, בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ וְנוֹטָה לָאָרֶץ, הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הָעִקָּר.
phrases.en: If it stands in the land [of Israel] and hangs over [into the territory] outside the land, or if it stands outside the land, and hangs over into the land, [in all these cases the law is] decided according to the position of the root.

phrases.he: וּבְבָתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה, הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הָעִקָּר.
phrases.en: And as regards houses in walled cities, everything is decided according to the position of the root.

phrases.he: וּבְעָרֵי מִקְלָט, הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַנּוֹף.
phrases.en: But as regards cities of refuge, everything is decided [also] according to the location of the branches.

phrases.he: וּבִירוּשָׁלַיִם, הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַנּוֹף
phrases.en: And in what concerns Jerusalem, everything is decided by the location of the branches.

phrases.he: הַכּוֹבֵשׁ, הַשּׁוֹלֵק, הַמּוֹלֵחַ, חַיָּב. הַמְכַמֵּן בָּאֲדָמָה, פָּטוּר. הַמְטַבֵּל בַּשָּׂדֶה, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: If he pickled, stewed, or salted [produce], he is liable [to give tithes]. If he stored [produce] in the ground [in order to warm it up] he is exempt. If he dipped it [while yet] in the field, he is exempt.

phrases.he: הַפּוֹצֵעַ זֵיתִים שֶׁיֵּצֵא מֵהֶם הַשְּׂרָף, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: If he split olives so that the bitter taste may come out of them, he is exempt.

phrases.he: הַסּוֹחֵט זֵיתִים עַל בְּשָׂרוֹ, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: If he squeezed olives against his skin, he is exempt.

phrases.he: אִם סָחַט וְנָתַן לְתוֹךְ יָדוֹ, חַיָּב. הַמְקַפֵּא לְתַבְשִׁיל, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: If he squeezed them and put [the oil] into his hand, he is liable. One who makes a viscous liquid [from grapes or olives] in order to put it in a dish is exempt.

phrases.he: לִקְדֵרָה, חַיָּב, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא כְבוֹר קָטָן
phrases.en: But if to put it in an [empty] pot, he is liable for it is like a small vat.

phrases.he: תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁטָּמְנוּ תְאֵנִים לְשַׁבָּת, וְשָׁכְחוּ לְעַשְּׂרָן, לֹא יֹאכְלוּ לְמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת עַד שֶׁיְּעַשְּׂרוּ.
phrases.en: Children who have hidden figs [in the field] for Shabbat and they forgot to tithe them, they must not be eaten after Shabbat until they have been tithed.

phrases.he: כַּלְכָּלַת שַׁבָּת, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי פּוֹטְרִין וּבֵית הִלֵּל מְחַיְּבִין.
phrases.en: In the case of a basket of fruits for Shabbat: Bet Shammai exempt it from tithes; But Bet Hillel makes it liable.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף הַלּוֹקֵט אֶת הַכַּלְכָּלָה לִשְׁלֹחַ לַחֲבֵרוֹ, לֹא יֹאכַל עַד שֶׁיִּתְעַשֵּׂר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: even one who has gathered a basket of fruit to send as a present to his friend, must not eat of them, until they have been tithed.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹטֵל זֵיתִים מִן הַמַּעֲטָן, טוֹבֵל אֶחָד אֶחָד בְּמֶלַח וְאוֹכֵל.
phrases.en: One who took olives from a vat may dip them one at a time in salt, and eat them.

phrases.he: אִם מָלַח וְנָתַן לְפָנָיו, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: But if he salted them, and put them in front of him, he is liable [for tithes].

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, מִן הַמַּעֲטָן הַטָּהוֹר חַיָּב, וּמִן הַטָּמֵא פָּטוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מַחֲזִיר אֶת הַמּוֹתָר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer said: from a pure vat he is liable but from an impure [vat] he is exempt because can put back the leftovers.

phrases.he: שׁוֹתִים עַל הַגַּת, בֵּין עַל הַחַמִּין בֵּין עַל הַצּוֹנֵן פָּטוּר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: One may drink [wine] out of the winepress, whether [it is mixed] with hot or cold water, and be exempt [from tithes], the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק מְחַיֵּב.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer bar Zadok says he is liable.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, עַל הַחַמִּין חַיָּב, וְעַל הַצּוֹנֵן פָּטוּר:
phrases.en: But the sages say: with hot water he is liable [to tithe] but with cold water, he is exempt.

phrases.he: הַמְקַלֵּף שְׂעוֹרִים, מְקַלֵּף אַחַת אַחַת וְאוֹכֵל.
phrases.en: One who husks barley may husk one at a time and eat [without tithing], but if he husked and put them into his hand, he is liable [to tithe].

phrases.he: וְאִם קִלֵּף וְנָתַן לְתוֹךְ יָדוֹ, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: One who rubs [ears of] wheat may blow out [the chaff of the wheat] from hand to hand and eat, but if he blows and puts the grain in his lap he is liable.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹלֵל מְלִילוֹת שֶׁל חִטִּים, מְנַפֶּה מִיָּד לְיָד וְאוֹכֵל.
phrases.en: Coriander which was sown for the sake of the seed, the plant is exempt [from tithes].

phrases.he: וְאִם נִפָּה וְנָתַן לְתוֹךְ חֵיקוֹ, חַיָּב.
כֻּסְבָּר שֶׁזְּרָעָהּ לְזֶרַע, יַרְקָהּ פָּטוּר.
זְרָעָהּ לְיָרָק, מִתְעַשֶּׂרֶת זֶרַע וְיָרָק.
רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, הַשֶּׁבֶת מִתְעַשֶּׂרֶת זֶרַע וְיָרָק וְזֵירִין.
phrases.en: If he sowed it for the sake of the plant then both the seed and the plant must be tithed. Rabbi Eliezer said: as for dill, tithe must be given from the seed and the plant, and the pods.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵינוֹ מִתְעַשֵּׂר זֶרַע וְיָרָק אֶלָּא הַשַּׁחֲלַיִם וְהַגַּרְגִּיר בִּלְבָד:
phrases.en: But the sages say: only in the case of cress and eruca are both the seeds and plant tithed.

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, תְּמָרוֹת שֶׁל תִּלְתָּן וְשֶׁל חַרְדָּל וְשֶׁל פּוֹל הַלָּבָן, חַיָּבוֹת בַּמַּעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.en: Rabban Gamaliel says: shoots of fenugreek, of mustard, and of white beans are liable [to tithe].

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, הַצָּלָף מִתְעַשֵּׂר תְּמָרוֹת וַאֲבִיּוֹנוֹת וְקַפְרָס.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: as for the caper bush, tithes must be given from the shoots, the berries and the blossoms.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אֵין מִתְעַשֵּׂר אֶלָּא אֲבִיּוֹנוֹת, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן פֶּרִי:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiba says: only the berries are tithed since they [alone] count as fruit.

phrases.he: הָעוֹקֵר שְׁתָלִים מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ וְנָטַע לְתוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: One who uproots saplings from of his own [property] and plants them [elsewhere] within his own [property] is exempt [from tithes].

phrases.he: לָקַח בִּמְחֻבָּר לַקַּרְקַע, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: If he bought [saplings] attached to the ground, he is exempt.

phrases.he: לָקַט לִשְׁלֹחַ לַחֲבֵרוֹ, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: If he gathered them in order to send them to his fellow, he is exempt.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר, אִם יֵשׁ כַּיּוֹצֵא בָהֶם נִמְכָּרִים בַּשּׁוּק, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ חַיָּבִין
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah said: if similar ones were being sold in the market, behold they are liable [for tithes].

phrases.he: הָעוֹקֵר לֶפֶת וּצְנוֹנוֹת מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ וְנוֹטֵעַ לְתוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ לְזֶרַע, חַיָּב, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא גָּרְנָן.
phrases.en: One who uproots turnips and radishes from within his own [property] and plants [them elsewhere] within his own [property] for the purpose of seed, he is liable to tithe, since this is [equivalent to] their threshing floor.

phrases.he: בְּצָלִים, מִשֶּׁהִשְׁרִישׁוּ בָעֲלִיָּה, טָהֲרוּ מִלְּטַמֵּא.
phrases.en: If onions take root in an upper story they become clean from any impurity.

phrases.he: נָפְלָה עֲלֵיהֶם מַפֹּלֶת וְהֵם מְגֻלִּים, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ כִּנְטוּעִים בַּשָּׂדֶה
phrases.en: If some debris fell upon them and they are uncovered, they are regarded as though they were planted in the field.

phrases.he: לֹא יִמְכֹּר אָדָם אֶת פֵּרוֹתָיו מִשֶׁבָּאוּ לְעוֹנַת הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת לְמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן עַל הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, וְלֹא בַשְּׁבִיעִית לְמִי שֶׁהוּא חָשׁוּד עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית.
phrases.en: One may not sell produce after the season for tithing has arrived to one who is not trusted concerning tithes. Nor in the sabbatical year [may one sell sabbatical year produce] to one suspected of [transgressing] the sabbatical year.

phrases.he: וְאִם בִּכְּרוּ, נוֹטֵל אֶת הַבַּכּוּרוֹת וּמוֹכֵר אֶת הַשְּׁאָר
phrases.en: If only [some] produce ripened, he takes the ripe ones and may sell the remainder.

phrases.he: לֹא יִמְכֹּר אָדָם אֶת תִּבְנוֹ וְאֶת גִּפְתּוֹ וְאֶת זַגָּיו לְמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן עַל הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, לְהוֹצִיא מֵהֶן מַשְׁקִין.
phrases.en: One may not sell his straw, nor his olive peat, or his grape pulp to one who is not to be trusted in [with respect to] tithes, for him to extract the juice from them.

phrases.he: וְאִם הוֹצִיא, חַיָּב בַּמַּעַשְׂרוֹת וּפָטוּר מִן הַתְּרוּמָה, שֶׁהַתּוֹרֵם, בְּלִבּוֹ עַל הַקְּטוּעִים, עַל הַצְּדָדִים וְעַל מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹךְ הַתֶּבֶן
phrases.en: If he did extract the juice he is liable for tithes, but is exempt from terumah, because when one separates terumah he has in mind the fragments which [is] by the sides, and that which is inside the straw.
