phrases.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ שְׂדֵה יָרָק בְּסוּרְיָא, אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא בָא לְעוֹנַת הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: One who buys a field of vegetables in Syria: If before the season for tithing arrived, then he is liable to tithe.

phrases.he: וּמִשֶּׁבָּא לְעוֹנַת הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, פָּטוּר, וְלוֹקֵט כְּדַרְכּוֹ וְהוֹלֵךְ.
phrases.en: If after the season for tithing he is exempt, and he may go on gathering in his usual manner.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף יִשְׂכֹּר פּוֹעֲלִים וִילַקֵּט.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: he may even hire workers and gather.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בִּזְמַן שֶׁקָּנָה קַרְקַע, אֲבָל בִּזְמַן שֶׁלֹּא קָנָה קַרְקַע, אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא בָא לְעוֹנַת הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel says: When does this apply? If he has bought the land. But if, he has not bought the land, even before the season for tithing arrived he is exempt.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר, אַף לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן
phrases.en: Rabbi [Judah Hanasi] says: he must also tithe according to calculation.

phrases.he: הַמְתַמֵּד וְנָתַן מַיִם בַּמִּדָּה וּמָצָא כְדֵי מִדָּתוֹ, פָּטוּר. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְחַיֵּב.
phrases.en: One who makes grape-skin wine, and he put water on by measure, and he finds [afterwards] the same quantity, he is exempt from tithe.

phrases.he: מָצָא יוֹתֵר עַל כְּדֵי מִדָּתוֹ, מוֹצִיא עָלָיו מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah makes him liable. If he found more than the measure, he must give [tithe] for it from another place, in proportion.

phrases.he: חוֹרֵי הַנְּמָלִים שֶׁלָּנוּ בְצַד הָעֲרֵמָה הַחַיֶּבֶת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ חַיָּבִים, שֶׁיָּדוּעַ שֶׁמִּדָּבָר הַגָּמוּר הָיוּ גּוֹרְרִין כָּל הַלָּיְלָה:
phrases.en: Anthills which have remained the whole night near a pile of grain which was liable to tithe, [the grain found in them] is liable, since it is obvious that they [the ants] have been dragging away the whole night from something [of which the work] had been completed.

phrases.he: שׁוּם בַּעַל בֶּכִי, וּבָצָל שֶׁל רִכְפָּא, וּגְרִיסִין הַקִּילְקִין, וְהָעֲדָשִׁים הַמִּצְרִיּוֹת,
phrases.en: Garlic from Balbeck, onions from Rikpa, Cicilician beans and Egyptians lentils, and Rabbi Meir says qirqas, and Rabbi Yose says qotnym are exempt from tithes and may be brought from any man in the seventh year.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, אַף הַקַּרְקָס,
phrases.en: The seeds of upper arum pods, the seeds of leeks, the seeds of onions, the seeds of turnips and radishes, and other seeds of garden produce which are not eaten, are exempt from tithes, and may be bought from any man in the seventh year; and even though the plants from they grew were terumah, they may still be eaten [by non-priests].

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר אַף הַקּוּטְנִים, פְּטוּרִים מִן הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, וְנִלְקָחִין מִכָּל אָדָם בַּשְּׁבִיעִית.

זֶרַע לוּף הָעֶלְיוֹן, זֶרַע כְּרֵשִׁים, זֶרַע בְּצָלִים, זֶרַע לֶפֶת וּצְנוֹנוֹת, וּשְׁאָר זֵרְעוֹנֵי גִנָּה שֶׁאֵינָן נֶאֱכָלִים, פְּטוּרִים מִן הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, וְנִלְקָחִין מִכָּל אָדָם בַּשְּׁבִיעִית, שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֲבִיהֶן תְּרוּמָה, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ יֵאָכֵלוּ
מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, אֵין מוֹכְרִין אוֹתוֹ, וְאֵין מְמַשְׁכְּנִין אוֹתוֹ, וְאֵין מַחֲלִיפִין אוֹתוֹ, וְלֹא שׁוֹקְלִין כְּנֶּגְדּוֹ.
phrases.en: Second tithe: one may not sell it, use it as a pledge, exchange it, or use it as a weight.

phrases.he: וְלֹא יֹאמַר אָדָם לַחֲבֵרוֹ בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, הֵילָךְ יַיִן וְתֶן לִי שָׁמֶן.
phrases.en: One may not say to his friend [even] in Jerusalem: “Here is [second tithe] wine, give me [in exchange] oil, and the same with all other produce.

phrases.he: וְכֵן שְׁאָר כָּל הַפֵּרוֹת.
phrases.en: But people may give it to one another as a free gift.

phrases.he: אֲבָל נוֹתְנִין זֶה לָזֶה מַתְּנַת חִנָּם
מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה, אֵין מוֹכְרִין אוֹתוֹ תָּמִים חַי, וְלֹא בַעַל מוּם חַי וְשָׁחוּט, וְאֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין בּוֹ הָאִשָּׁה.
phrases.en: Tithe of cattle: one may not sell it when it is unblemished and alive, and when it is blemished [one may not sell it] neither alive nor slaughtered, nor may one betroth a woman with it.

phrases.he: הַבְּכוֹר מוֹכְרִין אוֹתוֹ תָּמִים חַי, וּבַעַל מוּם חַי וְשָׁחוּט, וּמְקַדְּשִׁין בּוֹ הָאִשָּׁה.
phrases.en: A first-born animal: one may sell it when it is unblemished and alive, and when blemished [one may sell it] both alive and slaughtered, and one may betroth a wife with it.

phrases.he: אֵין מְחַלְּלִין מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי עַל אֲסִימוֹן, וְלֹא עַל הַמַּטְבֵּעַ שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹצֵא, וְלֹא עַל הַמָּעוֹת שֶׁאֵינָן בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ
phrases.en: One may not redeem second tithe with unstamped coins, nor with coins which are not current, nor for money which is not in one's possession.

phrases.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ בְּהֵמָה לְזִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים, אוֹ חַיָּה לִבְשַׂר תַּאֲוָה, יָצָא הָעוֹר לְחֻלִּין, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָעוֹר מְרֻבֶּה עַל הַבָּשָׂר.
phrases.en: One who bought a domesticated animal for a shelamim offering or a wild animal for non-sacrificial eating, the hide becomes hullin [non-sacred], even though the value of the hide exceeds the value of the flesh.

phrases.he: כַּדֵּי יַיִן סְתוּמוֹת, מְקוֹם שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לִמְכֹּר סְתוּמוֹת, יָצָא קַנְקַן לְחֻלִּין.
phrases.en: Sealed jars of wine [which were bought] in a place where they were usually sold sealed, the jars are hullin.

phrases.he: הָאֱגוֹזִים וְהַשְּׁקֵדִים, יָצְאוּ קְלִפֵּיהֶם לְחֻלִּין.
phrases.en: Walnuts and almonds, their shells become hullin.

phrases.he: הַתֶּמֶד, עַד שֶׁלֹּא הֶחְמִיץ, אֵינוֹ נִלְקָח בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.en: Grape-skin wine: before it has fermented it cannot be bought with second tithe money, but after it has fermented it may be bought with second tithe money.

phrases.he: וּמִשֶּׁהֶחְמִיץ, נִלְקָח בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר
הַלּוֹקֵחַ חַיָּה לְזִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים, בְּהֵמָה לִבְשַׂר תַּאֲוָה, לֹא יָצָא הָעוֹר לְחֻלִּין.
phrases.en: One who bought a wild animal for a shelamim offering or a domesticated beast for non-sacrificial eating, the hide does not become hullin.

phrases.he: כַּדֵּי יַיִן פְּתוּחוֹת אוֹ סְתוּמוֹת, מְקוֹם שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לִמָּכֵר פְּתוּחוֹת, לֹא יָצָא קַנְקַן לְחֻלִּין.
phrases.en: Open or sealed jars of wine [which were bought] in a place where they are usually sold open, the jars do not become hullin.

phrases.he: סַלֵּי זֵיתִים וְסַלֵּי עֲנָבִים עִם הַכְּלִי, לֹא יָצְאוּ דְמֵי הַכְּלִי לְחֻלִּין
phrases.en: Baskets of olives or baskets of grapes [bought] together with the vessel, the value of the vessel does not become hullin.

phrases.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ מַיִם, וּמֶלַח, וּפֵרוֹת הַמְחֻבָּרִים לַקַּרְקַע, אוֹ פֵרוֹת שֶׁאֵינָן יְכוֹלִין לְהַגִּיעַ לִירוּשָׁלַיִם, לֹא קָנָה מַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.en: One who bought water or salt, or produce still joined to the soil, or produce which cannot reach Jerusalem, he has not purchased maaser [sheni]. One who bought produce unwittingly, the money must be restored to its former place.

phrases.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ פֵּרוֹת, שׁוֹגֵג, יַחְזְרוּ דָמִים לִמְקוֹמָן.
phrases.en: But if intentionally, the produce must be taken up and be consumed in the [holy] place, and when there is no Temple, it must be left to rot.

phrases.he: מֵזִיד, יָעֳלוּ וְיֵאָכְלוּ בַמָּקוֹם.
וְאִם אֵין מִקְדָּשׁ, יֵרַקְּבוּ
הַלּוֹקֵחַ בְּהֵמָה, שׁוֹגֵג, יַחְזְרוּ דָמֶיהָ לִמְקוֹמָן.
phrases.en: One who bought a domesticated animal unwittingly, the money must be restored to its former place.

phrases.he: מֵזִיד, תָּעֳלֶה וְתֵאָכֵל בַּמָּקוֹם.
phrases.en: Intentionally, it must be taken up and eaten in the [holy] place.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵין מִקְדָּשׁ, תִּקָּבֵר עַל יְדֵי עוֹרָהּ
phrases.en: And when there is no Temple, it must be buried together with its hide.

phrases.he: אֵין לוֹקְחִין עֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת וְקַרְקָעוֹת וּבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה מִדְּמֵי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי.
phrases.en: One may not buy male slaves or female slaves, land, or unclean animals with maaser sheni money. And if he did buy [one of these], its value must be consumed [as maaser sheni in Jerusalem].

phrases.he: וְאִם לָקַח, יֹאכַל כְּנֶגְדָּן.
phrases.en: One may not bring bird-offerings of a zav or zavah, or bird-offerings of women after child-birth, or sin-offerings, or guilt-offerings, from maaser sheni money.

phrases.he: אֵין מְבִיאִין קִנֵּי זָבִים, וְקִנֵּי זָבוֹת, וְקִנֵּי יוֹלְדוֹת, חַטָּאוֹת, וַאֲשָׁמוֹת, מִדְּמֵי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי.
phrases.en: And if he did buy [one of these], their value must be consumed [as maaser sheni in Jerusalem].

phrases.he: וְאִם הֵבִיא, יֹאכַל כְּנֶגְדָּם.
phrases.en: This is the general rule: whatever [is bought] out of maaser sheni money which cannot be used for eating or drinking or anointing, its value must be consumed [as maaser sheni in Jerusalem].

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל שֶׁהוּא חוּץ לַאֲכִילָה וְלִשְׁתִיָּה וּלְסִיכָה מִדְּמֵי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, יֹאכַל כְּנֶגְדּוֹ
מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, נִתָּן לַאֲכִילָה וְלִשְׁתִיָּה וּלְסִיכָה, לֶאֱכֹל דָּבָר שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לֶאֱכֹל, לָסוּךְ דָּבָר שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לָסוּךְ.
phrases.en: Second tithe is set apart for eating, for drinking and for anointing; for eating what is usually eaten, for drinking what is usually drunk, and for anointing what is usually used for anointing.

phrases.he: לֹא יָסוּךְ יַיִן וְחֹמֶץ, אֲבָל סָךְ הוּא אֶת הַשֶּׁמֶן.
phrases.en: One may not anoint oneself with wine or with vinegar, but one may anoint oneself with oil.

phrases.he: אֵין מְפַטְּמִין שֶׁמֶן שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, וְאֵין לוֹקְחִין בִּדְמֵי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁמֶן מְפֻטָּם, אֲבָל מְפַטֵּם הוּא אֶת הַיַּיִן.
phrases.en: One may not spice oil of second tithe, nor may one buy spiced oil with second tithe money. But one may spice wine.

phrases.he: נָפַל לְתוֹכוֹ דְבַשׁ וּתְבָלִין וְהִשְׁבִּיחוֹ, הַשֶּׁבַח לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן.
phrases.en: If honey or spices fell into wine and improved its value, the improved value [is divided] according to the proportion.

phrases.he: דָּגִים שֶׁנִּתְבַּשְּׁלוּ עִם הַקַּפְלוֹטוֹת שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהִשְׁבִּיחוּ, הַשֶּׁבַח לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן.
phrases.en: If fish was cooked with leek of second tithe and it improved in value, the improved value [is divided] according to the proportion. If dough of second tithe was baked and it improved in value, the whole improved value is second [tithe].

phrases.he: עִסָּה שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁאֲפָאָהּ וְהִשְׁבִּיחַ, הַשֶּׁבַח לַשֵּׁנִי.
phrases.en: This is the general rule: whenever the improvement is recognizable the improved value [is divided] according to the proportion, but whenever the improved value is not recognizable the improved value belongs to the second [tithe].

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל שֶׁשִּׁבְחוֹ נִכָּר, הַשֶּׁבַח לְפִי הַחֶשְׁבּוֹן.
וְכָל שֶׁאֵין שִׁבְחוֹ נִכָּר, הַשֶּׁבַח לַשֵּׁנִי
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אֵין סָכִין שֶׁמֶן שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם. וַחֲכָמִים מַתִּירִין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: one may not anoint oneself with oil of second tithe in Jerusalem. But the sages allow it.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, אִם הֵקֵל בִּתְרוּמָה חֲמוּרָה, לֹא נָקֵל בְּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי הַקַּל.
phrases.en: They said to Rabbi Shimon: if a lenient ruling has been adopted in the case of terumah which is a grave matter, should we not also adopt a lenient ruling in the case of second tithe which is a light matter? He said to them: No; a lenient ruling has been adopted in the

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, מַה, לֹא, אִם הֵקֵל בִּתְרוּמָה הַחֲמוּרָה מְקוֹם שֶׁהֵקֵל בְּכַרְשִׁינִים וּבְתִלְתָּן, נָקֵל בְּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי הַקַּל מְקוֹם שֶׁלֹּא הֵקֵל בְּכַרְשִׁינִים וּבְתִלְתָּן:
phrases.en: case of terumah though it is a grave matter, because in terumah we have adopted a lenient ruling also with regard to vetches and fenugreek, but how can we adopt a lenient ruling in the case of second tithe though it is a light matter, when we have not adopted a lenient ruling in second tithe with regard to vetches and fenugreek?

phrases.he: תִּלְתָּן שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, תֵּאָכֵל צִמְחוֹנִים. וְשֶׁל תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.en: Fenugreek of second tithe may be eaten when it is still tender.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, כָּל מַעֲשֶׂיהָ בְּטָהֳרָה, חוּץ מֵחֲפִיפָתָהּ.
phrases.en: Fenugreek of terumah: Bet Shammai says: whatever is done with it must be done in a state of purity, except when it is used for cleansing the head.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, כָּל מַעֲשֶׂיהָ בְטֻמְאָה, חוּץ מִשְּׁרִיָּתָהּ:
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel says: whatever is done with it may be done in a state of impurity, except soaking it in water.

phrases.he: כַּרְשִׁינֵי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, יֵאָכְלוּ צִמְחוֹנִים, וְנִכְנָסִין לִירוּשָׁלַיִם וְיוֹצְאִין. נִטְמְאוּ,
phrases.en: Vetches of second tithe may be eaten when still tender. And they may be brought into Jerusalem and taken out again.

phrases.he: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר, יִתְחַלְּקוּ לְעִסּוֹת,
phrases.en: If they became unclean: Rabbi Tarfon says: they must be divided among pieces of dough. But the sages say: they may be redeemed.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, יִפָּדוּ. וְשֶׁל תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.en: [Vetches] of terumah: Bet Shammai says: they must be soaked and rubbed in a state of purity, but may be given as food [to an animal] in a state of impurity.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, שׁוֹרִין וְשָׁפִין בְּטָהֳרָה, וּמַאֲכִילִין בְּטֻמְאָה.
phrases.en: Bet Hillel says: they must be soaked [only] in a state of purity, but they may be rubbed and given as food [to an animal] in a state of impurity.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, שׁוֹרִין בְּטָהֳרָה, וְשָׁפִין וּמַאֲכִילִין בְּטֻמְאָה.
phrases.en: Shammai says: they must be eaten dry [only].

phrases.he: שַׁמַּאי אוֹמֵר, יֵאָכְלוּ צָרִיד.
רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, כָּל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶן בְּטֻמְאָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiba says: whatever is done with them may be done in a state of impurity.

phrases.he: מְעוֹת חֻלִּין וּמְעוֹת מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁנִּתְפַּזְּרוּ, מַה שֶּׁלִּקֵּט, לִקֵּט לְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, עַד שֶׁיַּשְׁלִים, וְהַשְּׁאָר חֻלִּין.
phrases.en: Hullin coins and second tithe coins which were scattered together: whatever is picked up [one at a time] belongs to second tithe until the sum is completed, and the remainder is hullin. If they were so mixed up as to be taken up by the handful, [they are divided] according to the proportion.

phrases.he: אִם בָּלַל וְחָפַן, לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן.
phrases.en: This is the general rule: what is picked up [one at a time] must be first given to second tithe, but [what is picked up] mixed [quantity is divided] according to the proportion.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, הַמִּתְלַקְּטִים, לְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי. וְהַנִּבְלָלִים, לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן

סֶלַע שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְשֶׁל חֻלִּין שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ, מֵבִיא בְסֶלַע מָעוֹת וְאוֹמֵר, סֶלַע שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהִיא, מְחֻלֶּלֶת עַל הַמָּעוֹת הָאֵלּוּ, וּבוֹרֵר אֶת הַיָּפָה שֶׁבָּהּ, וּמְחַלְּלָן עָלֶיהָ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָמְרוּ, מְחַלְּלִין כֶּסֶף עַל נְחֹשֶׁת מִדֹּחַק, וְלֹא שֶׁיִּתְקַיֵּם כֵּן, אֶלָּא חוֹזֵר וּמְחַלְּלָם עַל הַכָּסֶף:
phrases.en: A sela of maaser sheni which was mixed up with a sela of hullin, one may bring copper coins for the sela and say: “Let the sela of maaser sheni wherever it may be, be exchanged for these coins.” Then he must select the better of the two selas, and change [again] the copper coins for it. For they have said: one may change silver for copper [only] in case of necessity, and not to leave it so but to change it again for silver.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם אֶת סְלָעָיו דִּינְרֵי זָהָב, וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין.
phrases.en: Bet Shammai says: one may not turn his selas into gold dinars. But Bet Hillel permits it.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, אֲנִי עָשִׂיתִי לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וּלְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֶת כַּסְפָּן דִּינְרֵי זָהָב:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva said: For Rabban Gamaliel and Rabbi Joshua I turned silver into gold dinars.

phrases.he: הַפּוֹרֵט סֶלַע מִמְּעוֹת מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי,
phrases.en: One who changes copper coins of second tithe for a sela: Bet Shammai says: he may change copper coins for a whole sela.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, כָּל הַסֶּלַע מָעוֹת.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel says: a shekel of silver and a shekel’s worth of copper coins [can be exchanged for the sela].

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף וְשֶׁקֶל מָעוֹת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: one may not exchange silver and produce for silver.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, אֵין מְחַלְּלִין כֶּסֶף וּפֵרוֹת עַל הַכֶּסֶף, וַחֲכָמִים מַתִּירִים:
phrases.en: But the sages allow it.

phrases.he: הַפּוֹרֵט סֶלַע שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם,
phrases.en: One who exchanges a sela of second tithe in Jerusalem:Bet Shammai says: he may exchange the whole sela for copper coins.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, כָּל הַסֶּלַע מָעוֹת.
phrases.en: Bet Hillel says: a shekel of silver and a shekel’s worth of copper coins [can be exchanged for the sela].

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף וְשֶׁקֶל מָעוֹת. הַדָּנִין לִפְנֵי
phrases.en: Those discussing before the sages say: silver for three dinars and copper coins for one denar.

phrases.he: חֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דִינָרֵי כֶּסֶף וְדִינָר מָעוֹת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: silver for three denars and copper coins for a fourth [of the fourth denar].

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, שְׁלֹשָׁה דִינָרִין כֶּסֶף, וּרְבִיעִית מָעוֹת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Tarfon says: four aspers in silver.

phrases.he: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר, אַרְבָּעָה אַסְפְּרֵי כֶסֶף.
phrases.en: Shammai says: he must leave it in a shop and eat as much as it is worth.

phrases.he: שַׁמַּאי אוֹמֵר, יַנִּיחֶנָּה בַחֲנוּת וְיֹאכַל כְּנֶגְדָּהּ
מִי שֶׁהָיוּ מִקְצָת בָּנָיו טְמֵאִין וּמִקְצָתָן טְהוֹרִים, מַנִּיחַ אֶת הַסֶּלַע וְאוֹמֵר, מַה שֶּׁהַטְּהוֹרִים שׁוֹתִים, סֶלַע זוֹ מְחֻלֶּלֶת עָלָיו.
phrases.en: If one had some of his sons pure and some impure, he may put down a sela and say: “What the pure drink, this sela will be redeemed for it.

phrases.he: נִמְצְאוּ טְהוֹרִים וּטְמֵאִים שׁוֹתִין מִכַּד אֶחָד
phrases.en: In this way the pure and the impure may drink from one jar.

phrases.he: לֹא יֹאמַר אָדָם לַחֲבֵרוֹ, הַעַל אֶת הַפֵּרוֹת הָאֵלּוּ לִירוּשָׁלַיִם לְחַלֵּק, אֶלָּא אוֹמֵר לוֹ, הַעֲלֵם שֶׁנֹּאכְלֵם וְנִשְׁתֵּם בִּירוּשָׁלָיִם.
phrases.en: One should not say to his friend: “Carry up this [second tithe] produce to Jerusalem that in order to divide it.” Rather he should say to him, “Carry it up that so that we may eat and drink of it in Jerusalem.

phrases.he: אֲבָל נוֹתְנִים זֶה לָזֶה מַתְּנַת חִנָּם
phrases.en: But people may give it to one another as a free gift.

phrases.he: אֵין לוֹקְחִין תְּרוּמָה בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מְמַעֵט בַּאֲכִילָתוֹ, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר.
phrases.en: One may not buy terumah with maaser sheni money, because this reduces the number of those who can eat it. But Rabbi Shimon permits it.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, מָה אִם הֵקֵל בְּזִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים, שֶׁהוּא מְבִיאָן לִידֵי פִגּוּל וְנוֹתָר וְטָמֵא, לֹא נָקֵל בַּתְּרוּמָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon said to them: If the law is lenient in the case of wellbeing offerings, though they may become unfit or a remnant or unclean, why should it not also be lenient with regard to terumah? But they said to him: The law was lenient

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, מָה אִם הֵקֵל בְּזִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים, שֶׁהֵן מֻתָּרִים לְזָרִים, נָקֵל בַּתְּרוּמָה, שֶׁהִיא אֲסוּרָה לְזָרִים:
phrases.en: in the case of wellbeing offerings, because they are permitted to non-priests, but should we therefore be lenient with regard to terumah, which is forbidden to non-priests?

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ מָעוֹת בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם וְצָרִיךְ לוֹ, וְלַחֲבֵרוֹ פֵרוֹת, אוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵרוֹ, הֲרֵי הַמָּעוֹת הָאֵלּוּ מְחֻלָּלִין עַל פֵּרוֹתֶיךָ.
phrases.en: One who has [second tithe] money in Jerusalem and he needs [to spend] it, and his friend had [non-sacred] produce, he may say to his friend: “Let this money be exchanged for your produce.

phrases.he: נִמְצָא זֶה אוֹכֵל פֵּרוֹתָיו בְּטָהֳרָה, וְהַלָּה עוֹשֶׂה צָרְכּוֹ בִּמְעוֹתָיו.
phrases.en: It turns out that the one [must] eat his produce in purity and the other may do what he needs with his money.

phrases.he: וְלֹא יֹאמַר כֵּן לְעַם הָאָרֶץ, אֶלָּא בִדְמָאי
phrases.en: But he may not say thus to an am haaretz except when [the money was] from [second tithe of] demai.

phrases.he: פֵּרוֹת בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם וּמָעוֹת בַּמְּדִינָה, אוֹמֵר, הֲרֵי הַמָּעוֹת הָהֵם מְחֻלָּלִין עַל פֵּרוֹת הָאֵלּוּ.
phrases.en: If [one had hullin] produce in Jerusalem and [second tithe money] in the provinces, he may say: “Let that money be exchanged for this produce.

phrases.he: מָעוֹת בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם וּפֵרוֹת בַּמְּדִינָה, אוֹמֵר הֲרֵי הַמָּעוֹת הָאֵלּוּ מְחֻלָּלִין עַל פֵּרוֹת הָהֵם, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיָּעֳלוּ הַפֵּרוֹת וְיֵאָכְלוּ בִירוּשָׁלָיִם
phrases.en: If [he had second tithe] money in Jerusalem and [hullin] produce in the provinces, he may say: “Let this money be exchanged for that produce,” as long as he will carry that produce and eat it in Jerusalem.

phrases.he: מָעוֹת נִכְנָסוֹת לִירוּשָׁלַיִם וְיוֹצְאוֹת, וּפֵרוֹת נִכְנָסִין וְאֵינָן יוֹצְאִין.
phrases.en: [Second tithe] money may be brought into Jerusalem and taken out again, but [second tithe] produce may only be brought in, but not taken out again.

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, אַף הַפֵּרוֹת נִכְנָסִין וְיוֹצְאִין
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel says: produce also may be brought in and be taken out again.

phrases.he: פֵּרוֹת שֶׁנִּגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתָּן וְעָבְרוּ בְתוֹךְ יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, יַחֲזֹר מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁלָּהֶן וְיֵאָכֵל בִּירוּשָׁלָיִם.
phrases.en: Produce whose processing was completed and it passed through Jerusalem, its second tithe must be brought back and eaten in Jerusalem.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁלֹּא נִגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתָּן, סַלֵּי עֲנָבִים לַגַּת וְסַלֵּי תְאֵנִים לַמֻּקְצֶה,
phrases.en: If its processing had not been completed, [such as] baskets of grapes [that were going] to the wine-press or baskets of figs [that were going] to the drying-place: Bet Shammai says: its second tithe must be brought back and be eaten in Jerusalem.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, יַחֲזֹר מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁלָּהֶם וְיֵאָכֵל בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel says: it may be redeemed and eaten anywhere.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, יִפָּדֶה וְיֵאָכֵל בְּכָל מָקוֹם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Judah says in the name of Rabbi Yose: Bet Shammai and Bet Hillel did not disagree concerning produce whose processing had not been completed that its second tithe may be redeemed and be eaten anywhere.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל עַל פֵּרוֹת שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתָּן, שֶׁיִּפָּדֶה מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁלָּהֶם וְיֵאָכֵל בְּכָל מָקוֹם.
phrases.en: What did they disagree about? About produce whose processing was completed.

phrases.he: וְעַל מַה נֶחְלְקוּ, עַל פֵּרוֹת שֶׁנִּגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתָּן, שֶׁבֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, יַחֲזֹר מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁלָּהֶם וְיֵאָכֵל בִּירוּשָׁלָיִם.
phrases.en: Bet Shammai says that its second tithe must be brought back and be eaten in Jerusalem. And Bet Hillel says that it may be redeemed and be eaten anywhere.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, יִפָּדֶה וְיֵאָכֵל בְּכָל מָקוֹם.
phrases.en: [The second tithe of] demai may [always] be brought in and taken out again and be redeemed.

phrases.he: וְהַדְּמַאי, נִכְנָס וְיוֹצֵא וְנִפְדֶּה
אִילָן שֶׁהוּא עוֹמֵד בִּפְנִים וְנוֹטֶה לַחוּץ, אוֹ עוֹמֵד בַּחוּץ וְנוֹטֶה לִפְנִים, מִכְּנֶגֶד הַחוֹמָה וְלִפְנִים, כְּלִפְנִים.
phrases.en: A tree which stood within [Jerusalem] and was bending outwards, or if it stood outside [Jerusalem] and was bending inwards, what is opposite the wall and inwards is deemed as being within, and what is opposite the wall and outwards is deemed as being outside.

phrases.he: מִכְּנֶגֶד הַחוֹמָה וְלַחוּץ, כְּלַחוּץ.
phrases.en: Olive-presses which have their entrance within and their inner space outside, or which have their entrance outside and their inner space within: Bet Shammai says: the whole is deemed as being within.

phrases.he: בָּתֵּי הַבַּדִּים שֶׁפִּתְחֵיהֶן לִפְנִים וַחֲלָלָן לַחוּץ, אוֹ שֶׁפִּתְחֵיהֶן לַחוּץ וַחֲלָלָן לִפְנִים,
בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, הַכֹּל כְּלִפְנִים.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel says: what is opposite the wall and inwards is deemed as being within, and what is opposite the wall and outwards is deemed as being outside.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מִכְּנֶגֶד הַחוֹמָה וְלִפְנִים, כְּלִפְנִים.
מִכְּנֶגֶד הַחוֹמָה וְלַחוּץ, כְּלַחוּץ
הַלְּשָׁכוֹת, בְּנוּיוֹת בַּקֹּדֶשׁ וּפְתוּחוֹת לַחֹל, תּוֹכָן חֹל וְגַגּוֹתֵיהֶן קֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.en: The chambers [of the Temple] which were built on holy ground but were open towards common ground: their interior was deemed common and their roofs were deemed holy.

phrases.he: בְּנוּיוֹת בַּחֹל וּפְתוּחוֹת לַקֹּדֶשׁ, תּוֹכָן קֹדֶשׁ וְגַגּוֹתֵיהֶן חֹל.
phrases.en: Those which were built on common ground but were open towards holy ground: their interior was deemed holy and their roofs were deemed common.

phrases.he: בְּנוּיוֹת בַּקֹּדֶשׁ וּבַחֹל וּפְתוּחוֹת לַקֹּדֶשׁ וְלַחֹל, תּוֹכָן וְגַגּוֹתֵיהֶן מִכְּנֶגֶד הַקֹּדֶשׁ וְלַקֹּדֶשׁ, קֹדֶשׁ, מִכְּנֶגֶד הַחֹל וְלַחֹל, חֹל
phrases.en: Those which were built both on holy and on common ground and were open both towards holy and common ground: the interior and the roofs that were on holy ground and inwards were deemed holy, but [the interior and roofs] on common ground and outwards were deemed common.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁנִּכְנַס לִירוּשָׁלַיִם וְנִטְמָא, בֵּין שֶׁנִּטְמָא בְאַב הַטֻּמְאָה, בֵּין שֶׁנִּטְמָא בִּוְלַד הַטֻּמְאָה, בֵּין בִּפְנִים בֵּין בַּחוּץ,
phrases.en: Second tithe which was brought into Jerusalem and became unclean, whether it became unclean by a principal defilement or by a secondary defilement, whether it became unclean within [Jerusalem] or outside:Bet Shammai says: it must all be redeemed and be eaten within except that which became unclean by a principal defilement outside.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, יִפָּדֶה וְיֵאָכֵל הַכֹּל בִּפְנִים, חוּץ מִשֶּׁנִּטְמָא בְּאַב הַטֻּמְאָה בַּחוּץ.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel says: it must all be redeemed and may be eaten outside except that which became unclean by a secondary defilement within.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, הַכֹּל יִפָּדֶה וְיֵאָכֵל בַּחוּץ, חוּץ מִשֶּׁנִּטְמָא בִּוְלַד הַטֻּמְאָה בִּפְנִים:
הַלָּקוּחַ בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁנִּטְמָא, יִפָּדֶה.
phrases.en: If that which was bought with maaser sheni money became unclean, it should be redeemed.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, יִקָּבֵר.
phrases.en: R. Judah says: it must be buried.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וּמָה אִם מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי עַצְמוֹ שֶׁנִּטְמָא, הֲרֵי הוּא נִפְדֶּה, הַלָּקוּחַ בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁנִּטְמָא, אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁיִּפָּדֶה.
phrases.en: They said to Rabbi Judah: if maaser sheni itself when it became unclean may be redeemed, should not also that which is bought with maaser sheni money be redeemed when it became unclean? He said to them: No! If you say this of maaser sheni itself, it is because it may be redeemed also when pure at a distance from the [holy] place.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם בְּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי עַצְמוֹ, שֶׁכֵּן הוּא נִפְדֶּה בְטָהוֹר בְּרִחוּק מָקוֹם, תֹּאמְרוּ בְלָקוּחַ בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר, שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִפְדֶּה בְטָהוֹר בְּרִחוּק מָקוֹם:
phrases.en: But how can you say this of that which is bought with maaser sheni money, seeing that it cannot be redeemed when clean at a distance from the [holy] place.

phrases.he: צְבִי שֶׁלְּקָחוֹ בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר, וָמֵת, יִקָּבֵר עַל יְדֵי עוֹרוֹ.
phrases.en: If a deer which had been bought with maaser sheni money died, it must be buried together with its hide.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, יִפָּדֶה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: it may be redeemed.

phrases.he: לְקָחוֹ חַי וּשְׁחָטוֹ וְנִטְמָא, יִפָּדֶה.
phrases.en: If it was bought alive and slaughtered and it then became unclean, it may be redeemed.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, יִקָּבֵר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: it must be buried.

phrases.he: לְקָחוֹ שָׁחוּט וְנִטְמָא, הֲרֵי הוּא כְפֵרוֹת
phrases.en: If it was bought slaughtered and it became unclean, behold it is like produce.

phrases.he: הַמַּשְׁאִיל קַנְקַנִּין לְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁגָּפָן, לֹא קָנָה מַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.en: One who lends jars for maaser sheni [wine], even if they were corked, they do not acquire [the sanctity of] maaser sheni.

phrases.he: זָלַף לְתוֹכָן סְתָם, עַד שֶׁלֹּא גָפָן, לֹא קָנָה מַעֲשֵׂר. מִשֶּׁגָּפָן, קָנָה מַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.en: If wine was poured into them without specifying [that it was for sale] they do not acquire [the sanctity of] maaser sheni before they are corked, but after they are corked they acquire [the sanctity of] maaser sheni.

phrases.he: עַד שֶׁלֹּא גָפָן, עוֹלוֹת בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה, וּמִשֶּׁגָּפָן, מְקַדְּשׁוֹת בְּכָל שֶׁהֵן.
phrases.en: Before they are corked they are neutralized in a hundred and one, but after they are corked they sanctify any quantity.

phrases.he: עַד שֶׁלֹּא גָפָן, תּוֹרֵם מֵאַחַת עַל הַכֹּל, וּמִשֶּׁגָּפָן, תּוֹרֵם מִכָּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת
phrases.en: Before they are corked terumah may be taken from one jar for all the others, but after they are corked terumah must be taken from each jar separately.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מְפַתֵּחַ וּמְעָרֶה לַגַּת.
phrases.en: Bet Shammai says: the jars must be opened and emptied into the wine-press.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מְפַתֵּחַ וְאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְעָרוֹת.
phrases.en: Bet Hillel says: they must be opened but need not be emptied.

phrases.he: בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לִמְכֹּר סְתוּמוֹת.
phrases.en: When does this apply? In a place where they are usually sold closed, but in a place where they are usually sold open, the jar does not revert to hullin.

phrases.he: אֲבָל בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לִמְכֹּר פְּתוּחוֹת, לֹא יָצָא קַנְקַן לְחֻלִּין.
phrases.en: If, however, he wishes to be stringent upon himself and to sell [only] by measure, the jar reverts hullin.

phrases.he: אֲבָל אִם רָצָה לְהַחְמִיר עַל עַצְמוֹ לִמְכֹּר בְּמִדָּה, יָצָא קַנְקַן לְחֻלִּין.
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אַף הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵרוֹ, חָבִית זוֹ אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לְךָ חוּץ מִקַּנְקַנִּים, יָצָא קַנְקַן לְחֻלִּין:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: also when one says to his friend, “This jar [of wine] I am selling to you from its jar, the jar reverts to hullin.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹלִיךְ פֵּרוֹת מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי מִמְּקוֹם הַיֹּקֶר לִמְקוֹם הַזּוֹל, אוֹ מִמְּקוֹם הַזּוֹל לִמְקוֹם הַיֹּקֶר, פּוֹדֵהוּ כְשַׁעַר מְקוֹמוֹ.
phrases.en: One who carries produce of maaser sheni from a place where it is expensive to a place where it is cheap, or from a place where it is cheap to a place where it is expensive, he redeems it according to the market price of the place [where he redeems it].

phrases.he: הַמֵּבִיא פֵרוֹת מִן הַגֹּרֶן לָעִיר, וְכַדֵּי יַיִן מִן הַגַּת לָעִיר, הַשֶּׁבַח לַשֵּׁנִי וִיצִיאוֹת מִבֵּיתוֹ
phrases.en: One who brings produce from the threshing-floor into the city, or jars of wine from the wine-press into the city, the increase in the price belongs to maaser sheni and the expenses [must be covered] from his household.

phrases.he: פּוֹדִין מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בְּשַׁעַר הַזּוֹל, כְּמוֹת שֶׁהַחֶנְוָנִי לוֹקֵחַ, לֹא כְמוֹת שֶׁהוּא מוֹכֵר.
phrases.en: Maaser sheni may be redeemed at the lower market price: At the price at which the shopkeeper buys and not at which he sells.

phrases.he: כְּמוֹת שֶׁהַשֻּׁלְחָנִי פוֹרֵט, וְלֹא כְמוֹת שֶׁהוּא מְצָרֵף.
phrases.en: At the price at which the money-changer takes small change and not at the price at which he gives small change.

phrases.he: וְאֵין פּוֹדִין מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי אַכְסָרָה.
phrases.en: Maaser sheni may not be redeemed in an estimated lump.

phrases.he: אֶת שֶׁדָּמָיו יְדוּעִים, יִפָּדֶה עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד.
phrases.en: If its value is known, it may be redeemed according to the evaluation of one.

phrases.he: וְאֶת שֶׁאֵין דָּמָיו יְדוּעִים, יִפָּדֶה עַל פִּי שְׁלֹשָׁה, כְּגוֹן הַיַּיִן שֶׁקָּרַם וּפֵרוֹת שֶׁהִרְקִיבוּ וּמָעוֹת שֶׁהֶחֱלִיאוּ
phrases.en: But if its value is not known, it must be redeemed according to the evaluation of three, as for instance in the case of wine which has formed a film, or produce which has begun to rot, or coins which have become rusty.

phrases.he: בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אוֹמֵר בְּסֶלַע וְאַחֵר אוֹמֵר בְּסֶלַע, בַּעַל הַבַּיִת קוֹדֵם, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מוֹסִיף חֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.en: If the owner says, “With a sela [I will redeem this maaser sheni] and another person says “With a sela,” the owner has the first right, because he must add a fifth.

phrases.he: בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אוֹמֵר בְּסֶלַע וְאַחֵר אוֹמֵר בְּסֶלַע וְאִסָּר, אֶת שֶׁל סֶלַע וְאִסָּר קוֹדֵם, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מוֹסִיף עַל הַקֶּרֶן.
phrases.en: If the owner says “With a sela” and another person says “With a sela and an issar,” the one who offered a sela and an issar has the first right, because he added to the principal.

phrases.he: הַפּוֹדֶה מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁלּוֹ, מוֹסִיף עָלָיו חֲמִשִּׁית, בֵּין שֶׁהוּא שֶׁלּוֹ וּבֵין שֶׁנִּתַּן לוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה
phrases.en: When one redeems his maaser sheni he must add a fifth, whether it is his own or it was given him as a gift.

phrases.he: מַעֲרִימִין עַל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי.
phrases.en: One may act in a deceptive manner when it comes to maaser sheni.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד, אוֹמֵר אָדָם לִבְנוֹ וּלְבִתּוֹ הַגְּדוֹלִים, לְעַבְדּוֹ וּלְשִׁפְחָתוֹ הָעִבְרִים, הֵילָךְ מָעוֹת אֵלּוּ וּפְדֵה לָךְ מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי זֶה.
phrases.en: How so? A man may say to his grown-up son or daughter, or to his Hebrew slave or female slave, “Take this money and redeem this maaser sheni for yourself.

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא יֹאמַר כֵּן לִבְנוֹ וּלְבִתּוֹ הַקְּטַנִּים, לְעַבְדּוֹ וּלְשִׁפְחָתוֹ הַכְּנַעֲנִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיָּדָן כְּיָדוֹ
phrases.en: But he may not say so to his son or daughter who are minors or to his Canaanite slave or female slave, because their hand is as his own hand.

phrases.he: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בַּגֹּרֶן וְאֵין בְּיָדוֹ מָעוֹת, אוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵרוֹ, הֲרֵי הַפֵּרוֹת הָאֵלּוּ נְתוּנִים לָךְ בְּמַתָּנָה.
phrases.en: One who was standing at the threshing-floor and didn’t have any coins may say to his friend: “Behold, this produce is given to you as a gift,” and then he may say again, “Behold, let this produce be exchanged for money which I have in the house.

phrases.he: חוֹזֵר וְאוֹמֵר, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מְחֻלָּלִין עַל מָעוֹת שֶׁבַּבָּיִת
מָשַׁךְ מִמֶּנּוּ מַעֲשֵׂר בְּסֶלַע, וְלֹא הִסְפִּיק לִפְדּוֹתוֹ עַד שֶׁעָמַד בִּשְׁתַּיִם, נוֹתֵן לוֹ סֶלַע, וּמִשְׂתַּכֵּר בְּסֶלַע, וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁלּוֹ.
phrases.en: If one took possession from the owner of maaser sheni for a sela, but before he had time to redeem it, it stood at the price of two selas, he may give him one sela and make a profit of one sela and the maaser sheni remains his.

phrases.he: מָשַׁךְ מִמֶּנּוּ מַעֲשֵׂר בִּשְׁתַּיִם, וְלֹא הִסְפִּיק לִפְדּוֹתוֹ עַד שֶׁעָמַד בְּסֶלַע, נוֹתֵן לוֹ סֶלַע מֵחֻלִּין וְסֶלַע שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁלּוֹ.
phrases.en: If he took possession from the owner of maaser sheni for two selas, but before he had time to redeem it, it stood at the price of one sela, he may give him one sela out of hullin [money] and one sela of his maaser sheni money.

phrases.he: אִם הָיָה עַם הָאָרֶץ, נוֹתֵן לוֹ מִדְּמָאי
phrases.en: If the owner was an am haaretz, he should give him out of [maaser sheni of] demai.

phrases.he: הַפּוֹדֶה מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְלֹא קָרָא שֵׁם,
phrases.en: If one redeemed maaser sheni but did not call it by its name: Rabbi Yose says: it is sufficient.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, דַּיּוֹ.
phrases.en: But Rabbi Judah says: he must name it explicitly.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, צָרִיךְ לְפָרֵשׁ.
phrases.en: If a man was speaking to a woman concerning her divorce or her betrothal, and gave her a get or betrothal money but did not state explicitly [what he was doing]: Rabbi Yose says: it is sufficient.

phrases.he: הָיָה מְדַבֵּר עִם הָאִשָּׁה עַל עִסְקֵי גִטָּהּ וְקִדּוּשֶׁיהָ, וְנָתַן לָהּ גִּטָּהּ וְקִדּוּשֶׁיהָ וְלֹא פֵרֵשׁ,
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, דַּיּוֹ.
phrases.en: But Rabbi Judah says: he must say it explicitly.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, צָרִיךְ לְפָרֵשׁ:
הַמַּנִּיחַ אִסָּר וְאָכַל עָלָיו חֶצְיוֹ, וְהָלַךְ לְמָקוֹם אַחֵר וַהֲרֵי הוּא יֹצֵא בְּפֻנְדְּיוֹן, אוֹכֵל עָלָיו עוֹד אִסָּר.
phrases.en: One who sets aside an issar [for the redemption of maaser sheni] and on its account he ate [the value of] half [an issar of maaser sheni] and then went to another place where [the issar] was worth a pondion, he may eat of [maaser sheni the value of] another issar.

phrases.he: הַמַּנִּיחַ פֻּנְדְּיוֹן וְאָכַל עָלָיו חֶצְיוֹ, וְהָלַךְ לְמָקוֹם אַחֵר וַהֲרֵי הוּא יוֹצֵא בְּאִסָּר, אֹכֵל עָלָיו עוֹד פְּלָג.
phrases.en: One who sets aside a pundion [for the redemption of maaser sheni] and on its account he ate [the value of] half [a pundion of maaser sheni] and then went to another place where [the pundion] was worth an issar, he may eat [maaser sheni the value of] another half [an issar].

phrases.he: הַמַּנִּיחַ אִסָּר שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, אוֹכֵל עָלָיו אַחַד עָשָׂר בְּאִסָּר וְאֶחָד מִמֵּאָה בְּאִסָּר.
phrases.en: One who sets aside an issar of maaser sheni [money] he should eat on its account eleven parts of the value of an issar, or [he should eat an additional] one hundredth of an issar.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, הַכֹּל עֲשָׂרָה.
phrases.en: Bet Shammai say: in both cases one tenth part [of an issar].

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, בַּוַּדַּאי אַחַד עָשָׂר, וּבַדְּמַאי עֲשָׂרָה:
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel says: in the case of certain [maaser sheni] an eleventh part, in the case of demai a tenth part.

phrases.he: כָּל הַמָּעוֹת הַנִּמְצָאִים, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ חֻלִּין, אֲפִלּוּ דִּינַר זָהָב עִם הַכֶּסֶף וְעִם הַמָּעוֹת.
phrases.en: Any money found is considered hullin, even gold dinars with silver and with copper coins.

phrases.he: מָצָא בְתוֹכָן חֶרֶשׂ וְכָתוּב עָלָיו מַעֲשֵׂר, הֲרֵי זֶה מַעֲשֵׂר
phrases.en: If a potsherd was found with the money on which was written “tithe” this is considered maaser sheni [money].

phrases.he: הַמּוֹצֵא כְלִי וְכָתוּב עָלָיו קָרְבָּן,
phrases.en: One who finds a vessel one which was written “korban:” Rabbi Judah says: if it was of clay, it is itself hullin and what is in it is a korban (holy).

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם הָיָה שֶׁל חֶרֶס, הוּא חֻלִּין וּמַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ קָרְבָּן.
phrases.en: But if it was of metal it is itself korban and what is in it is hullin.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיָה שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת, הוּא קָרְבָּן וּמַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ חֻלִּין.
אָמְרוּ לוֹ, אֵין דֶּרֶךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם לִהְיוֹת כּוֹנְסִין חֻלִּין לְקָרְבָּן:
phrases.en: They said to him: it is not the custom of people to put what is common into what is korban.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹצֵא כְלִי וְכָתוּב עָלָיו קוּ"ף, קָרְבָּן. מ', מַעֲשֵׂר. ד', דְּמַאי. ט', טֶבֶל.
phrases.en: One who finds a vessel on which was written a kof, it is korban. If a mem, it is maaser.

phrases.he: ת', תְּרוּמָה, שֶׁבִּשְׁעַת סַכָּנָה הָיוּ כוֹתְבִין ת' תַּחַת תְּרוּמָה.
phrases.en: If a dalet, it is demai. If a tet, it is tevel (untithed produced). If a tav, it is terumah.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, כֻּלָּם שְׁמוֹת בְּנֵי אָדָם הֵם.
phrases.en: For in the time of danger people would write a tav for terumah. Rabbi Yose says: they may all stand for the names of people.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, אֲפִלּוּ מָצָא חָבִית וְהִיא מְלֵאָה פֵרוֹת וְכָתוּב עָלֶיהָ תְּרוּמָה, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ חֻלִּין, שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר אֶשְׁתָּקַד הָיְתָה מְלֵאָה פֵרוֹת תְּרוּמָה, וּפִנָּהּ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose said: even if he finds a jar which was full of produce and on it was written ‘terumah’ it may yet be considered hullin, because I can say that last year it was full of produce of terumah and was afterwards emptied.

phrases.he: הָאוֹמֵר לִבְנוֹ, מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בְּזָוִית זוֹ, וּמָצָא בְזָוִית אַחֶרֶת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ חֻלִּין.
phrases.en: One who says to his son, “There is maaser sheni [produce] in this corner,” but the son found [produce] in another corner, this may be considered hullin.

phrases.he: הָיָה שָׁם מָנֶה וּמָצָא מָאתַיִם, הַשְּׁאָר חֻלִּין.
phrases.en: [If the father said] there was there a hundred [of maaser sheni] and the son found two hundred, the remainder is hullin.

phrases.he: מָאתַיִם וּמָצָא מָנֶה, הַכֹּל מַעֲשֵׂר
phrases.en: [If the father said there were there] two hundred and the son found one hundred, it is all maaser sheni.

phrases.he: כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי, מְצַיְּנִין אוֹתוֹ בְּקוֹזְזוֹת אֲדָמָה, וְשֶׁל עָרְלָה בְּחַרְסִית, וְשֶׁל קְבָרוֹת בְּסִיד, וּמְמַחֶה וְשׁוֹפֵךְ.
phrases.en: A vineyard in its fourth year, they mark it with clods of earth, and of orlah with potter's clay, and graves with lime which is dissolved and poured on.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בַּשְּׁבִיעִית.
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel said: When does this apply? In the seventh year.

phrases.he: וְהַצְּנוּעִים מַנִּיחִין אֶת הַמָּעוֹת וְאוֹמְרִים, כָּל הַנִּלְקָט מִזֶּה, יְהֵא מְחֻלָּל עַל הַמָּעוֹת הָאֵלּוּ
phrases.en: The conscientious used to put down money and say: any fruit gathered from this vineyard may be exchanged for this money.

phrases.he: כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי הָיָה עוֹלֶה לִירוּשָׁלַיִם מַהֲלַךְ יוֹם אֶחָד לְכָל צָד.
phrases.en: [The produce of] a vineyard in its fourth year was brought up to Jerusalem within a distance of one day’s journey on each side.

phrases.he: וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא תְחוּמָהּ, אֵילַת מִן הַדָּרוֹם וְעַקְרַבַּת מִן הַצָּפוֹן, לוֹד מִן הַמַּעֲרָב וְהַיַּרְדֵּן מִן הַמִּזְרָח.
phrases.en: And what is the border [of a day’s journey on each side]? Eilat to the south, Akrabat on the north, Lod to the west, and the Jordan [river] to the east.

phrases.he: וּמִשֶּׁרַבּוּ הַפֵּרוֹת, הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהֵא נִפְדֶּה סָמוּךְ לַחוֹמָה.
phrases.en: When produce increased, it was decreed that it can be redeemed even if the vineyard was close to the wall.

phrases.he: וּתְנַאי הָיָה הַדָּבָר, שֶׁאֵימָתַי שֶׁיִּרְצוּ, יַחֲזֹר הַדָּבָר לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהָיָה.
phrases.en: And there was a stipulation on this matter, that whenever it was so desired, the arrangement would be restored as it had been before.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, הָיָה הַתְּנַאי הַזֶּה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: this was the stipulation after the Temple was destroyed, and the stipulation was that when the Temple should be rebuilt the arrangement would be restored as it had been before.

phrases.he: וּתְנַאי הָיָה, אֵימָתַי שֶׁיִּבָּנֶה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, יַחֲזֹר הַדָּבָר לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהָיָה
כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי,
phrases.en: [The grapes of] a vineyard in its fourth year:Bet Shammai says: the laws of the added fifth and removal do not apply to them; But Bet Hillel says: they do.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אֵין לוֹ חֹמֶשׁ וְאֵין לוֹ בִעוּר.
phrases.en: Bet Shammai says: the laws of peret and the defective clusters apply to them, and the poor can redeem the grapes for themselves.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, יֶשׁ לוֹ.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel says: all [of them] go to the wine-press.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, יֶשׁ לוֹ פֶרֶט וְיֶשׁ לוֹ עוֹלְלוֹת, וְהָעֲנִיִּים פּוֹדִין לְעַצְמָן.
וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, כֻּלּוֹ לַגָּת:
כֵּיצַד פּוֹדִין נֶטַע רְבָעִי, מַנִּיחַ אֶת הַסַּל עַל פִּי שְׁלֹשָׁה, וְאוֹמֵר, כַּמָּה אָדָם רוֹצֶה לִפְדּוֹת לוֹ בְסֶלַע עַל מְנָת לְהוֹצִיא יְצִיאוֹת מִבֵּיתוֹ.
phrases.en: How does one redeem the fruit of a plant in its fourth year? The owner puts down a basket in the presence of three [people] and says: “How many such baskets would a man wish to redeem for himself for a sela on condition that the costs [to produce the fruit] shall be on his house? And then he puts down the money and says: “Whatever shall be picked from this plant may it be exchanged for this money at the price of so many baskets for a sela.

phrases.he: וּמַנִּיחַ אֶת הַמָּעוֹת, וְאוֹמֵר, כָּל הַנִּלְקָט מִזֶּה, מְחֻלָּל עַל הַמָּעוֹת הָאֵלּוּ בְּכָךְ וְכָךְ סַלִּים בְּסָלַע
וּבַשְּׁבִיעִית, פּוֹדֵהוּ בְשָׁוְיוֹ. וְאִם הָיָה הַכֹּל מֻפְקָר, אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא שְׂכַר לְקִיטָה.
phrases.en: But in the seventh year he must redeem it for its full value. If [in other years] it had all been made ownerless property, the person [who redeems it] can only claim the cost of picking it.

phrases.he: הַפּוֹדֶה נֶטַע רְבָעִי שֶׁלּוֹ, מוֹסִיף עָלָיו חֲמִשִּׁיתוֹ, בֵּין שֶׁהוּא שֶׁלּוֹ וּבֵין שֶׁנִּתַּן לוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה
phrases.en: One who redeems his own plant in its fourth year, he must add a fifth of its value, whether the fruit was his own or was given him as a gift.

phrases.he: עֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח שֶׁל רְבִיעִית וְשֶׁל שְׁבִיעִית, הָיָה בִעוּר.
phrases.en: On the eve of the first [others read “last”] festival-day of Pesah in the fourth and in the seventh [years of the sabbatical cycle] the removal was performed.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד הָיָה בִעוּר, נוֹתְנִין תְּרוּמָה וּתְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר לַבְּעָלִים, וּמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן לִבְעָלָיו, וּמַעֲשַׂר עָנִי לִבְעָלָיו.
phrases.en: Terumah and the terumah of tithe were given to their owners, the first tithe was given to its owner, the tithe of the poor to its owner, and maaser sheni and first-fruits were removed in every place.

phrases.he: וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהַבִּכּוּרִים מִתְבַּעֲרִים בְּכָל מָקוֹם.
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, הַבִּכּוּרִים נִתָּנִין לַכֹּהֲנִים כַּתְּרוּמָה. הַתַּבְשִׁיל,
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: first-fruits were given to the priests like terumah.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, צָרִיךְ לְבַעֵר.
phrases.en: As for a cooked dish [with maaser sheni in it]: Bet Shammai says: it must be removed.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, הֲרֵי הוּא כִּמְבֹעָר:
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel say: lo, it may be considered as already removed.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ פֵרוֹת בַּזְּמָן הַזֶּה וְהִגִּיעָה שְׁעַת הַבִּעוּר,
phrases.en: One who had produce at this time and the time of removal arrived:Bet Shammai says: he must exchange it for money.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, צָרִיךְ לְחַלְּלָן עַל הַכֶּסֶף.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel says: it is all the same whether it becomes money or it remains fruit.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, אֶחָד שֶׁהֵן כֶּסֶף וְאֶחָד שֶׁהֵן פֵּרוֹת:
אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ שׁוֹלְחִין אֵצֶל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים שֶׁבַּמְּדִינוֹת, מַהֲרוּ וְהַתְקִינוּ אֶת פֵּרוֹתֵיכֶם עַד שֶׁלֹּא תַגִּיעַ שְׁעַת הַבִּעוּר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah said: in early times they used to send to householders in the provinces [saying:] “Hasten to set right your produce before the time of removal arrives,” until Rabbi Akiva came and taught that all produce which has not reached the time of tithing is exempt from the removal.

phrases.he: עַד שֶׁבָּא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְלִמֵּד, שֶׁכָּל הַפֵּרוֹת שֶׁלֹּא בָאוּ לְעוֹנַת הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, פְּטוּרִים מִן הַבִּעוּר
מִי שֶׁהָיוּ פֵרוֹתָיו רְחוֹקִים מִמֶּנּוּ, צָרִיךְ לִקְרוֹא לָהֶם שֵׁם.
phrases.en: One whose produce was far away from him, he must call it by name.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְהַזְּקֵנִים שֶׁהָיוּ בָאִין בִּסְפִינָה, אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, עִשּׂוּר שֶׁאֲנִי עָתִיד לָמוֹד, נָתוּן לִיהוֹשֻׁעַ, וּמְקוֹמוֹ מֻשְׂכָּר לוֹ.
phrases.en: Once it happened that Rabban Gamaliel and the elders were traveling by ship, and Rabban Gamaliel said: “The tithe which I shall measure out in the future is given to Joshua, and the place which it is in is leased to him.

phrases.he: עִשּׂוּר אַחֵר שֶׁאֲנִי עָתִיד לָמֹד, נָתוּן לַעֲקִיבָא בֶן יוֹסֵף שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה בוֹ לָעֲנִיִּים, וּמְקוֹמוֹ מֻשְׂכָּר לוֹ.
phrases.en: The other tithe which I shall measure out in the future is given to Akiva ben Joseph that he may hold it for the poor, and the place which it is in is leased to him.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, עִשּׂוּר שֶׁאֲנִי עָתִיד לָמוֹד נָתוּן לְאֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה, וּמְקוֹמוֹ מֻשְׂכָּר לוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua said: “The tithe [taken from terumah] which I shall measure out is given to Elazar ben Azariah, and the place which it is in is leased to him,” and they each received rent one from another.

phrases.he: וְנִתְקַבְּלוּ זֶה מִזֶּה שָׂכָר
בַּמִּנְחָה בְיוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן הָיוּ מִתְוַדִּין.
phrases.en: At minhah on the last festival day they would make the confession.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד הָיָה הַוִּדּוּי, בִּעַרְתִּי הַקֹּדֶשׁ מִן הַבַּיִת (דברים כו), זֶה מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְנֶטַע רְבָעִי.
phrases.en: How was the confession made? “I have cleared out the holy portion from the house” this refers to maaser sheni and the fruit of plants in their fourth year.

phrases.he: נְתַתִּיו לַלֵּוִי, זֶה מַעְשַׂר לֵוִי.
phrases.en: “I have given them to the Levite” this refers to the tithe of the levites.

phrases.he: וְגַם נְתַתִּיו, זוֹ תְּרוּמָה וּתְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.en: “And also I have given them” this refers to terumah and the terumah of tithe.

phrases.he: לַגֵּר לַיָּתוֹם וְלָאַלְמָנָה, זֶה מַעֲשַׂר עָנִי, הַלֶּקֶט וְהַשִּׁכְחָה וְהַפֵּאָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָן מְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַוִּדּוּי.
phrases.en: “To the stranger, to the orphans, and to the widow” this refers to the tithe of the poor, gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corners of the field, even though these do not prevent [one from making] the confession.

phrases.he: מִן הַבַּיִת, זוֹ חַלָּה
phrases.en: “Out of the house” this refers to hallah.

phrases.he: כְּכָל מִצְוָתְךָ אֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתָנִי (שם), הָא אִם הִקְדִּים מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי לָרִאשׁוֹן, אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהִתְוַדּוֹת.
phrases.en: “According to all Your commandments which You have commanded me,” thus, if he took out maaser sheni before the first tithe he cannot make the confession.

phrases.he: לֹא עָבַרְתִּי מִמִּצְוֹתֶיךָ, לֹא הִפְרַשְׁתִּי מִמִּין עַל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ, וְלֹא מִן הַתָּלוּשׁ עַל הַמְחֻבָּר, וְלֹא מִן הַמְחֻבָּר עַל הַתָּלוּשׁ, וְלֹא מִן הֶחָדָשׁ עַל הַיָּשָׁן, וְלֹא מִן הַיָּשָׁן עַל הֶחָדָשׁ.
phrases.en: “I have not transgressed any of Your commandments” I have not set apart [tithes] from one kind for a different kind, nor from plucked [produce] for [produce still] joined [to the soil], nor from new [produce] for old [produce], nor from old [produce] for new.

phrases.he: וְלֹא שָׁכָחְתִּי, לֹא שָׁכַחְתִּי מִלְּבָרֶכְךָ וּמִלְּהַזְכִּיר שִׁמְךָ עָלָיו
phrases.en: “Neither have I forgotten” I have not forgotten to bless You, nor to make mention of Your name over it.

phrases.he: לֹא אָכַלְתִּי בְאֹנִי מִמֶּנּוּ (שם), הָא אִם אֲכָלוֹ בַאֲנִינָה אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהִתְוַדּוֹת.
phrases.en: “I have not eaten from it in my mourning” thus, if he had eaten it in his mourning (aninut), he cannot make the confession.

phrases.he: וְלֹא בִעַרְתִּי מִמֶּנּוּ בְּטָמֵא, הָא אִם הִפְרִישׁוֹ בְטֻמְאָה אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהִתְוַדּוֹת.
phrases.en: “Neither have I removed any of it when unclean” thus, if he had removed it in uncleanness he cannot make the confession.

phrases.he: וְלֹא נָתַתִּי מִמֶּנּוּ לְמֵת, לֹא לָקַחְתִּי מִמֶּנּוּ אָרוֹן וְתַכְרִיכִים לְמֵת, וְלֹא נְתַתִּיו לְאוֹנְנִים אֲחֵרִים.
phrases.en: “And I have not given any of it to the dead” I have not used any of it for a coffin or shrouds for the dead, and I have not given any of it to other mourners.

phrases.he: שָׁמַעְתִּי בְקוֹל ה' אֱלֹהָי, הֲבֵאתִיו לְבֵית הַבְּחִירָה.
phrases.en: “I have listened to the voice of the Lord my God” I have brought it to the chosen house.

phrases.he: עָשִׂיתִי כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתָנִי, שָׂמַחְתִּי וְשִׂמַּחְתִּי בוֹ
phrases.en: “I have done just as you commanded me I have rejoiced and made others rejoice.

phrases.he: הַשְׁקִיפָה מִמְּעוֹן קָדְשְׁךָ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם (דברים כו, טו), עָשִׂינוּ מַה שֶׁגָּזַרְתָּ עָלֵינוּ, אַף אַתָּה עֲשֵׂה מַה שֶׁהִבְטַחְתָּנוּ, הַשְׁקִיפָה מִמְּעוֹן קָדְשְׁךָ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם וּבָרֵךְ אֶת עַמְּךָ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּבָנִים וּבְבָנוֹת.
phrases.en: “Look down from Your holy abode, from heaven” We have done what You decreed upon us, You too do what You have promised us. “Look down from Your holy abode, from heaven, and bless Your people Israel” with sons and daughters.

phrases.he: וְאֵת הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר נָתַתָּה לָנוּ, בְּטַל וּבְמָטָר וּבְוַלְדוֹת בְּהֵמָה.
phrases.en: “And the land which You have given us” with dew and rain and with offspring of cattle.

phrases.he: כַּאֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּעְתָּ לַאֲבוֹתֵינוּ אֶרֶץ זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבָשׁ, כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּתֵּן טַעַם בַּפֵּרוֹת
phrases.en: “As You swore to our fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey” that You may give a good taste to the produce.

phrases.he: מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ, יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמַמְזֵרִים מִתְוַדִּים, אֲבָל לֹא גֵרִים וְלֹא עֲבָדִים מְשֻׁחְרָרִים, שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק בָּאָרֶץ.
phrases.en: From here they said that Israelites and mamzerim may make the confession, but not converts, nor freed slaves, since they have no inheritance in the land.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, אַף לֹא כֹהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם, שֶׁלֹּא נָטְלוּ חֵלֶק בָּאָרֶץ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: neither do priests and Levites since they did not take a share of the land.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, יֵשׁ לָהֶם עָרֵי מִגְרָשׁ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: they have the Levitical cities.

phrases.he: יוֹחָנָן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל הֶעֱבִיר הוֹדָיוֹת הַמַּעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.en: Yohanan the high priest stopped [the recitation] of the confession of the tithes.

phrases.he: אַף הוּא בִּטֵּל אֶת הַמְעוֹרְרִים, וְאֶת הַנּוֹקְפִים.
phrases.en: He also abolished the “wakers” and the “strikers.

phrases.he: וְעַד יָמָיו הָיָה פַטִּישׁ מַכֶּה בִירוּשָׁלָיִם, וּבְיָמָיו אֵין אָדָם צָרִיךְ לִשְׁאוֹל עַל הַדְּמָאי
phrases.en: Until his days the hammer used to beat in Jerusalem. And in his days one did not have to ask about demai.

phrases.he: חֲמִשָּׁה דְבָרִים חַיָּבִים בַּחַלָּה, הַחִטִּים וְהַשְּׂעוֹרִים וְהַכֻּסְּמִין וְשִׁבֹּלֶת שׁוּעָל וְשִׁיפוֹן.
phrases.en: Five species [of grains] are subject to [the law of] hallah: wheat, barley, spelt, oats and rye.

phrases.he: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ חַיָּבִין בַּחַלָּה, וּמִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה, וַאֲסוּרִין בֶּחָדָשׁ מִלִּפְנֵי הַפֶּסַח, וּמִלִּקְצֹר מִלִּפְנֵי הָעֹמֶר.
phrases.en: These are subject to hallah, and [dough made from different types of these grains] are accounted together one with another [as one quantity]. And their “new” [harvest] is prohibited prior to Pesah, and [they are subject] to [the prohibition of] reaping prior to the Omer.

phrases.he: וְאִם הִשְׁרִישׁוּ קֹדֶם לָעֹמֶר, הָעֹמֶר מַתִּירָן.
phrases.en: If they took root prior to the Omer, the omer permits them.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, אֲסוּרִין עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא הָעֹמֶר הַבָּא
phrases.en: If not, they are prohibited until the next Omer has come.

phrases.he: הָאוֹכֵל מֵהֶם כַּזַּיִת מַצָּה בְּפֶסַח, יָצָא יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ.
phrases.en: If one has eaten of [these five] on Pesah an olive-size piece of matzah, he has fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.he: כַּזַּיִת חָמֵץ, חַיָּב בְּהִכָּרֵת.
phrases.en: [If he ate on Pesah] an olive-size of piece of hametz [made of these grains], he is liable for karet.

phrases.he: נִתְעָרֵב אֶחָד מֵהֶם בְּכָל הַמִּינִים, הֲרֵי זֶה עוֹבֵר בְּפֶסַח.
phrases.en: If one of these [grains, having become leavened,] became mixed with any other species, one must remove it on Pesah.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹדֵר מִן הַפַּת וּמִן הַתְּבוּאָה, אָסוּר בָּהֶם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: If one has vowed [to abstain] from [consuming] bread and tevuah (produce), he is prohibited from consuming these [five species] the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, הַנּוֹדֵר מִן הַדָּגָן אֵינוֹ אָסוּר אֶלָּא מֵהֶן. וְחַיָּבִין בַּחַלָּה וּבַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת:
phrases.en: The sages say: if one has vowed [to abstain] from [consuming] dagan, is prohibited only from [consuming] these [species] only. They are subject to hallah and tithes.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ חַיָּבִין בַּחַלָּה וּפְטוּרִים מִן הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת.
phrases.en: The following are subject to hallah, but exempt from tithes: gleanings, from the forgotten sheaf, from peah or from ownerless produce and the first tithe from which terumah has been removed, second tithe and consecrated [produce] which has been redeemed, and that which remains over from the omer, and grain which has not grown one-third [ripe].

phrases.he: הַלֶּקֶט, וְהַשִּׁכְחָה, וְהַפֵּאָה, וְהַהֶפְקֵר, וּמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּטְּלָה תְרוּמָתוֹ, וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁנִּפְדּוּ, וּמוֹתַר הָעֹמֶר, וּתְבוּאָה שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיאָה שְׁלִישׁ.
רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, תְּבוּאָה שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיאָה שְׁלִישׁ, פְּטוּרָה מִן הַחַלָּה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: grain which has not grown one-third [ripe] is exempt [also] from hallah.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ חַיָּבִין בַּמַּעַשְׂרוֹת וּפְטוּרִים מִן הַחַלָּה, הָאֹרֶז, וְהַדֹּחַן, וְהַפְּרָגִים, וְהַשֻּׁמְשְׁמִין, וְהַקִּטְנִיּוֹת, וּפָחוֹת מֵחֲמֵשֶׁת רְבָעִים בַּתְּבוּאָה.
phrases.en: The following are liable for tithes, but exempt from hallah: rice, millet, poppy-seed, sesame seeds, pulse, and less than five-fourths [of a kab] of [the five kinds of] grain, sponge-cakes, honey-cakes, dumplings, a cake [cooked] in a pan and medumma are exempt from hallah.

phrases.he: הַסֻּפְגָּנִין, וְהַדֻּבְשָׁנִין, וְהָאִסְקְרִיטִין, וְחַלַּת הַמַּשְׂרֵת, וְהַמְדֻמָּע, פְּטוּרִין מִן הַחַלָּה
עִסָּה שֶׁתְּחִלָּתָהּ סֻפְגָּנִין וְסוֹפָהּ סֻפְגָּנִין, פְּטוּרָה מִן הַחַלָּה.
phrases.en: Dough which was originally [intended for] sponge-cakes, and in the end is [cooked as] sponge-cake, is exempt from hallah.

phrases.he: תְּחִלָּתָהּ עִסָּה וְסוֹפָהּ סֻפְגָּנִין, תְּחִלָּתָהּ סֻפְגָּנִין וְסוֹפָהּ עִסָּה, חַיָּבִין בַּחַלָּה. וְכֵן הַקְּנוּבְקָאוֹת חַיָּבוֹת
phrases.en: [If it was] originally [ordinary] dough, but in the end [cooked as] sponge-cakes, [or if it was] originally [intended for] sponge-cakes, but finally [cooked as ordinary] dough, it is subject to hallah. Similarly, bread crumbs (kenuvkaot) are subject [to hallah].

phrases.he: הַמְּעִסָּה, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי פּוֹטְרִין, וּבֵית הִלֵּל מְחַיְּבִין.
phrases.en: Meisah: Bet Shammai exempts [from hallah], And Bet Hillel makes liable [for hallah].

phrases.he: הַחֲלִיטָה, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מְחַיְּבִין, וּבֵית הִלֵּל פּוֹטְרִין.
phrases.en: Halita: Bet Shammai makes liable, And Bet Hillel exempts.

phrases.he: חַלּוֹת תּוֹדָה וּרְקִיקֵי נָזִיר, עֲשָׂאָן לְעַצְמוֹ, פָּטוּר. לִמְכֹּר בַּשּׁוּק, חַיָּב
phrases.en: The loaves of the thanksgiving sacrifice and the wafers of a nazirite: if one made them for oneself, they are exempt [from hallah]. [If one made them] to sell in the market, they are subject [to hallah].

phrases.he: נַחְתּוֹם שֶׁעָשָׂה שְׂאֹר לְחַלֵּק, חַיָּב בַּחַלָּה.
phrases.en: A baker who made dough to divide it up into pieces, it is subject to hallah.

phrases.he: נָשִׁים שֶׁנָּתְנוּ לְנַחְתּוֹם לַעֲשׂוֹת לָהֶן שְׂאֹר, אִם אֵין בְּשֶׁל אַחַת מֵהֶן כַּשִּׁעוּר, פְּטוּרָה מִן הַחַלָּה
phrases.en: Women who gave [flour] to a baker to make for them dough, if there is not in any one of them a [minimum] measure, it is exempt from hallah.

phrases.he: עִסַּת הַכְּלָבִים, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָרוֹעִים אוֹכְלִין מִמֶּנָּה, חַיֶּבֶת בַּחַלָּה, וּמְעָרְבִין בָּהּ, וּמִשְׁתַּתְּפִין בָּהּ, וּמְבָרְכִין עָלֶיהָ, וּמְזַמְּנִין עָלֶיהָ, וְנַעֲשֵׂית בְּיוֹם טוֹב, וְיוֹצֵא בָהּ אָדָם יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בְּפֶסַח.
phrases.en: Dough for dogs:If shepherds eat it: it is subject to hallah, and one may use it to make an eruv or a shittuf; and one should say the blessings over it, and one should make an invitation for birkat hamazon over it; and it may be made on a festival; and one fulfills his obligation with it on Pesah.

phrases.he: אִם אֵין הָרוֹעִים אוֹכְלִין מִמֶּנָּה, אֵינָהּ חַיֶּבֶת בַּחַלָּה, וְאֵין מְעָרְבִין בָּהּ, וְאֵין מִשְׁתַּתְּפִין בָּהּ, וְאֵין מְבָרְכִין עָלֶיהָ, וְאֵין מְזַמְּנִין עָלֶיהָ, וְאֵינָהּ נַעֲשֵׂית בְּיוֹם טוֹב, וְאֵין אָדָם יוֹצֵא בָהּ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בְּפֶסַח.
phrases.en: But if shepherds do not eat it: it is not subject to hallah; and one may not use it to make an eruv, or a shittuf; and one does not say the blessings over it, and one does not make an invitation for birkat hamazon over it; and it may not be made on a festival; and one does not fulfill his obligation with it on Pesah.

phrases.he: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ, מִטַּמְּאָה טֻמְאַת אֳכָלִין
phrases.en: In either case it is susceptible to ritual defilement affecting food.

phrases.he: הַחַלָּה וְהַתְּרוּמָה, חַיָּבִין עָלֶיהָ מִיתָה וְחֹמֶשׁ, וַאֲסוּרִים לְזָרִים, וְהֵם נִכְסֵי כֹהֵן, וְעוֹלִין בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה, וּטְעוּנִין רְחִיצַת יָדַיִם וְהַעֲרֵב שֶׁמֶשׁ, וְאֵין נִטָּלִין מִן הַטָּהוֹר עַל הַטָּמֵא, אֶלָּא מִן הַמֻּקָּף וּמִן הַדָּבָר הַגָּמוּר.
phrases.en: In the case of hallah and terumah:One is liable for death on account of [having eaten] them death [intentionally], or to [repay] an added fifth [if unwittingly]; They are forbidden to non-priests; They are the property of the priest; They are nullified [in a mixture of] one-hundred-and-one [parts, the rest being non-sacred dough or produce]; They require washing of one’s hands; And [waiting until] the setting of the sun [prior to eating them]; They may not be separated from pure [stuff] for impure; But rather from that which is close, And from that [in a] finished [state].

phrases.he: הָאוֹמֵר, כָּל גָּרְנִי תְרוּמָה וְכָל עִסָּתִי חַלָּה, לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם, עַד שֶׁיְּשַׁיֵּר מִקְצָת
phrases.en: If one said: “All my threshing-floor is terumah, or all my dough is hallah,” he has not said anything, unless he has left some over.

phrases.he: פֵּרוֹת חוּצָה לָאָרֶץ שֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ לָאָרֶץ, חַיָּבִים בַּחַלָּה.
phrases.en: Produce [grown] outside the land [of Israel] that came into the land is subject to Hallah.

phrases.he: יָצְאוּ מִכָּאן לְשָׁם, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְחַיֵּב, וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא פּוֹטֵר
phrases.en: [If it] went out from here to there: Rabbi Eliezer makes it liable, But Rabbi Akiva makes it exempt.

phrases.he: עֲפַר חוּצָה לָאָרֶץ שֶׁבָּא בִסְפִינָה לָאָרֶץ, חַיֶּבֶת בַּמַּעַשְׂרוֹת וּבַשְּׁבִיעִית.
phrases.en: Earth from outside the land has come to the land [of Israel] in a boat, [the produce grown in it] is subject to tithes and to the [law relating to] the seventh year.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַסְּפִינָה גוֹשֶׁשֶׁת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah: when does this apply? When the boat touches [the ground].

phrases.he: עִסָּה שֶׁנִּלּוֹשָׁה בְמֵי פֵרוֹת, חַיֶּבֶת בַּחַלָּה, וְנֶאֱכֶלֶת בְּיָדַיִם מְסוֹאָבוֹת
phrases.en: Dough which has been kneaded with fruit-juice is subject to hallah, and may be eaten with unclean hands.

phrases.he: הָאִשָּׁה יוֹשֶׁבֶת וְקוֹצָה חַלָּתָהּ עֲרֻמָּה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא יְכוֹלָה לְכַסּוֹת עַצְמָהּ, אֲבָל לֹא הָאִישׁ.
phrases.en: A woman may sit and separate hallah while she is naked, since she can cover herself but a man may not.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לַעֲשׂוֹת עִסָּתוֹ בְטָהֳרָה, יַעֲשֶׂנָּה קַבִּין, וְאַל יַעֲשֶׂנָּה בְטֻמְאָה.
phrases.en: If one is not able to make one's dough in cleanness he should make it [in separate] kavs, rather than make it in uncleanness.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, יַעֲשֶׂנָּה בְטֻמְאָה וְאַל יַעֲשֶׂנָּה קַבִּים, שֶׁכְּשֵׁם שֶׁהוּא קוֹרֵא לַטְּהוֹרָה, כָּךְ הוּא קוֹרֵא לַטְּמֵאָה, לְזוֹ קוֹרֵא חַלָּה בַשֵּׁם וּלְזוֹ קוֹרֵא חַלָּה בַשֵּׁם, אֲבָל קַבִּים אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק בַּשֵּׁם:
phrases.en: But Rabbi Akiva says: let him make it in uncleanness rather than make it [in separate] kavs, just as he calls the clean, so too he calls the unclean; this one he cals hallah with the Name, and the other he also calls hallah with the Name, but [separate] kavs have no portion [devoted] to the Name.

phrases.he: הָעוֹשֶׂה עִסָּתוֹ קַבִּים וְנָגְעוּ זֶה בָזֶה, פְּטוּרִים מִן הַחַלָּה עַד שֶׁיִּשּׁוֹכוּ.
phrases.en: One who makes his dough [in separate] kavs, and they touch one another, they are exempt from hallah unless they stick together.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַף הָרוֹדֶה וְנוֹתֵן לַסַּל, הַסַּל מְצָרְפָן לַחַלָּה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: also if one takes out [loaves from an oven] and puts [them] into a basket, the basket joins them together for [the purposes of] hallah.

phrases.he: הַמַּפְרִישׁ חַלָּתוֹ קֶמַח, אֵינָהּ חַלָּה, וְגָזֵל בְּיַד כֹּהֵן.
phrases.en: If one separates his hallah [while it is still] flour, it is not hallah, and in the hand of a priest it is considered stolen property.

phrases.he: הָעִסָּה עַצְמָהּ, חַיֶּבֶת בַּחַלָּה.
phrases.en: The dough is still subject to hallah; And the flour, if there is the minimum quantity, it [also is] subject to hallah.

phrases.he: וְהַקֶּמַח, אִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ כַשִּׁעוּר, חַיֶּבֶת בַּחַלָּה, וַאֲסוּרָה לְזָרִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
phrases.en: And it is prohibited to non-priests, the words of Rabbi Joshua.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ,
phrases.en: They said to him: It happened that a non-priest sage seized it [for himself].

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה וּקְפָשָׁהּ זָקֵן זָר.
phrases.en: He said to them: He did something damaging to himself, but he benefited others.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, אַף הוּא קִלְקֵל לְעַצְמוֹ וְתִקֵּן לַאֲחֵרִים
חֲמֵשֶׁת רְבָעִים קֶמַח, חַיָּבִים בַּחַלָּה.
phrases.en: Five-fourths [of a kav] of flour are subject to hallah.

phrases.he: הֵם וּשְׂאֹרָן וְסֻבָּן וּמֻרְסָנָן חֲמֵשֶׁת רְבָעִים, חַיָּבִין.
phrases.en: If their leaven, their light bran and their coarse bran [make up the] five-fourths, they are subject.

phrases.he: נִטַּל מֻרְסָנָן מִתּוֹכָן וְחָזַר לְתוֹכָן, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ פְטוּרִין
phrases.en: If their coarse bran had been removed from them and returned to them, they are exempt.

phrases.he: שִׁעוּר הַחַלָּה, אֶחָד מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה.
phrases.en: The [minimum] measure of hallah is one twenty-fourth [part of the dough].

phrases.he: הָעוֹשֶׂה עִסָּה לְעַצְמוֹ, וְהָעוֹשֶׂה לְמִשְׁתֵּה בְנוֹ, אֶחָד מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה.
phrases.en: If he makes dough for himself, or if he makes it for his son’s [wedding] banquet, it is one twenty-fourth.

phrases.he: נַחְתּוֹם שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה לִמְכֹּר בַּשּׁוּק, וְכֵן הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהִיא עוֹשָׂה לִמְכֹּר בַּשּׁוּק, אֶחָד מֵאַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמֹנָה.
phrases.en: If a baker makes to sell in the market, and so [also] if a woman makes to sell in the market, it is one forty-eighth.

phrases.he: נִטְמֵאת עִסָּתָהּ שׁוֹגֶגֶת אוֹ אֲנוּסָה, אֶחָד מֵאַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמֹנָה.
phrases.en: If dough is made unclean either unwittingly or by an unforeseeable circumstance, it is one forty-eighth.

phrases.he: נִטְמֵאת מְזִידָה, אֶחָד מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא חוֹטֵא נִשְׂכָּר
phrases.en: If it was made unclean intentionally, it is one twenty-fourth, in order that a sinner should not profit.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, נִטֶּלֶת מִן הַטָּהוֹר עַל הַטָּמֵא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: Hallah may be taken from [dough] that is clean, [in order to exempt] that which is unclean.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד, עִסָּה טְהוֹרָה וְעִסָּה טְמֵאָה, נוֹטֵל כְּדֵי חַלָּה מֵעִסָּה שֶׁלֹּא הוּרָם חַלָּתָהּ, וְנוֹתֵן פָּחוֹת מִכַּבֵּיצָה בָּאֶמְצַע, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּטֹּל מִן הַמֻּקָּף. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִין
phrases.en: How [may this be done]? [If one has] clean dough and unclean dough, he takes sufficient hallah out of the [clean] dough whose hallah has not yet been taken, and puts [dough] less than the size of an egg in the middle, in order that he may take off [the hallah] from what is close together. But the sages prohibit.

phrases.he: אוֹכְלִין עֲרַאי מִן הָעִסָּה, עַד שֶׁתִּתְגַּלְגֵּל בַּחִטִּים וְתִטַּמְטֵם בַּשְּׂעוֹרִים.
phrases.en: One may snack from dough, until it is rolled, in [the case of] wheat [flour], or before it is made into a solid mass, in [the case of] barley [flour].

phrases.he: גִּלְגְּלָהּ בַּחִטִּים וְטִמְטְמָהּ בַּשְּׂעוֹרִים, הָאוֹכֵל מִמֶּנָּה חַיָּב מִיתָה.
phrases.en: [Once] one has rolled it [in the case of] wheat [flour], or made it into a solid mass, in [the case of] barley [flour], one who eats it is liable for death [at the hands of heaven].

phrases.he: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִיא נוֹתֶנֶת אֶת הַמַּיִם, מַגְבַּהַת חַלָּתָהּ, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא שָׁם חֲמִשָּׁה רִבְעֵי קֶמַח
phrases.en: As soon as she puts in the water she should lift out the hallah, provided that there are not five-fourths [of a kav] of flour left there.

phrases.he: נִדְמְעָה עִסָּתָהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא גִלְגְּלָה, פְּטוּרָה, שֶׁהַמְּדֻמָּע פָּטוּר. וּמִשֶּׁגִּלְגְּלָה, חַיֶּבֶת.
phrases.en: Dough which became medumma before she had rolled it, it is exempt [from hallah]. If after she had rolled it, it is subject [to hallah].

phrases.he: נוֹלַד לָהּ סְפֵק טֻמְאָה עַד שֶׁלֹּא גִלְגְּלָה, תֵּעָשֶׂה בְטֻמְאָה, וּמִשֶּׁגִּלְגְּלָה, תֵּעָשֶׂה בְטָהֳרָה
phrases.en: If there occurred to her some doubtful uncleanness before she had rolled it, it may be completed in uncleanness. If after she had rolled it, it should be completed in cleanness.

phrases.he: הִקְדִּישָׁה עִסָּתָהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא גִלְגְּלָה, וּפְדָאַתָּהּ, חַיֶּבֶת. מִשֶּׁגִּלְגְּלָה, וּפְדָאַתָּה, חַיֶּבֶת.
phrases.en: [If] she dedicated her dough [to the Temple] before rolling it, and then redeemed it, it is subject [to hallah]. [If she dedicated it] after rolling it, and redeemed it, it is subject [to hallah].

phrases.he: הִקְדִּישַׁתָּהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא גִלְגְּלָה, וְגִלְגְּלָהּ הַגִּזְבָּר, וְאַחַר כָּךְ פְּדָאַתָּהּ, פְּטוּרָה, שֶׁבִּשְׁעַת חוֹבָתָהּ הָיְתָה פְטוּרָה
phrases.en: [But if] she dedicated it before rolling it, and the Temple treasurer rolled it, and after that she redeemed it, it is exempt, since at the time of its obligation it was exempt.

phrases.he: כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ, הַמַּקְדִּישׁ פֵּרוֹתָיו עַד שֶׁלֹּא בָאוּ לְעוֹנַת הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, וּפְדָאָן, חַיָּבִין.
phrases.en: Similarly one who dedicates his produce prior to the stage when they are subject to tithes and then redeemed them, they are liable [to be tithed].

phrases.he: וּמִשֶּׁבָּאוּ לְעוֹנַת הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, וּפְדָאָן, חַיָּבִין.
phrases.en: If [he dedicated them] when they had already become subject to tithes and then redeemed them, they are liable [to be tithed].

phrases.he: הִקְדִּישָׁן עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמְרוּ, וּגְמָרָן הַגִּזְבָּר, וְאַחַר כָּךְ פְּדָאָן, פְּטוּרִין, שֶׁבִּשְׁעַת חוֹבָתָן הָיוּ פְטוּרִין
phrases.en: If he dedicated them before they had ripened, and they became ripe while in the possession of the [Temple] treasurer, and he then redeemed them, they are exempt, since at the time when they would have been liable, they were exempt.

phrases.he: נָכְרִי שֶׁנָּתַן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ עִסָּה, פְּטוּרָה מִן הַחַלָּה.
phrases.en: If a Gentile gave [flour] to an Israelite to make for him dough, it is exempt from hallah.

phrases.he: נְתָנָהּ לוֹ מַתָּנָה, עַד שֶׁלֹּא גִלְגֵּל, חַיָּב, וּמִשֶּׁגִּלְגֵּל, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: If the Gentile gave it to him as a gift, before rolling it, he is liable. If after rolling it, he is exempt.

phrases.he: הָעוֹשֶׂה עִסָּה עִם הַנָּכְרִי, אִם אֵין בְּשֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּשִׁעוּר חַלָּה, פְּטוּרָה מִן הַחַלָּה
phrases.en: If one makes dough together with a Gentile, then if there is not in [the portion] of the Israelite the minimum measure subject to hallah, it is exempt from hallah.

phrases.he: גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּר וְהָיְתָה לוֹ עִסָּה, נַעֲשֵׂית עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְגַּיֵּר, פָּטוּר, וּמִשֶּׁנִּתְגַיֵּר, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: A convert who converted and had dough: if it was made before he became a convert, he is exempt [from hallah]. After he converted, he is liable.

phrases.he: וְאִם סָפֵק, חַיָּב, וְאֵין חַיָּבִין עָלֶיהָ חֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.en: And if there is doubt, he is liable, but [a non-priest who has unwittingly eaten of such hallah] is not liable for the additional one-fifth.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַקְּרִימָה בַתַּנּוּר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva said: it all depends on the [time of the] formation of the light crust in the oven.

phrases.he: הָעוֹשֶׂה עִסָּה מִן הַחִטִּים וּמִן הָאֹרֶז, אִם יֶשׁ בָּהּ טַעַם דָּגָן, חַיֶּבֶת בַּחַלָּה, וְיוֹצֵא בָהּ אָדָם יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בְּפֶסַח.
phrases.en: One who makes dough from wheat [flour] and from rice [flour] if it has a taste of grain, it is subject to hallah, and one can fulfill one’s obligation with it on Pesah.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵין בָּהּ טַעַם דָּגָן, אֵינָהּ חַיֶּבֶת בַּחַלָּה, וְאֵין אָדָם יוֹצֵא בָהּ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בְּפֶסַח
phrases.en: But if it does not have the taste of grain, it is not subject to hallah, and one cannot fulfill with it one’s obligation on Pesah.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹטֵל שְׂאֹר מֵעִסָּה שֶׁלֹּא הוּרְמָה חַלָּתָהּ וְנוֹתֵן לְתוֹךְ עִסָּה שֶׁהוּרְמָה חַלָּתָהּ, אִם יֶשׁ לוֹ פַרְנָסָה מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר, מוֹצִיא לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן.
phrases.en: One who takes leaven out of dough from which hallah had not been taken and puts it into dough from which hallah had been taken:If he has a supply from another place, he can take out [hallah] in accordance with the precise amount.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, מוֹצִיא חַלָּה אַחַת עַל הַכֹּל
phrases.en: But if does not, he takes out one [portion of] hallah for the whole [dough].

phrases.he: כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ, זֵיתֵי מָסִיק שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ עִם זֵיתֵי נִקּוּף, עִנְּבֵי בָצִיר עִם עִנְּבֵי עוֹלְלוֹת, אִם יֶשׁ לוֹ פַרְנָסָה מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר, מוֹצִיא לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן.
phrases.en: Similarly, if olives of [regular] picking became mixed with olives [left over] for striking-off [by the poor], or grapes of [regular] picking, with grapes [left over] for gleaning [by the poor]:If he has a supply from another place, he can take out [terumah and tithes] in accordance with the precise amount.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, מוֹצִיא תְרוּמָה וּתְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר לַכֹּל, וְהַשְּׁאָר מַעֲשֵׂר וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן
phrases.en: But if does not, he takes out one terumah and terumat maaser for all of the grapes. And as for the rest, [he takes out] tithe and the second tithe in accordance with the precise amount.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹטֵל שְׂאֹר מֵעִסַּת חִטִּים וְנוֹתֵן לְתוֹךְ עִסַּת אֹרֶז, אִם יֶשׁ בָּהּ טַעַם דָּגָן חַיֶּבֶת בַּחַלָּה. וְאִם לָאו, פְּטוּרָה.
phrases.en: One who takes leaven from a dough of wheat [flour] and puts [it] into dough of rice [flour], [then] if it has the taste of grain, it is subject to hallah, [but] if not, it is exempt.

phrases.he: אִם כֵּן, לָמָּה אָמְרוּ הַטֶּבֶל אוֹסֵר כָּל שֶׁהוּא, מִין בְּמִינוֹ.
phrases.en: If so, why did they say: “Untithed produce of any amount renders food prohibited”? That is [with regard to a mixture of] a species with its own species, but [with regard to a mixture of a species] not with its own species, only when it imparts taste.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁלֹּא בְמִינוֹ, בְּנוֹתֵן טָעַם
שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים שֶׁעָשׂוּ שְׁנֵי קַבִּין, וְנָגְעוּ זֶה בָזֶה, אֲפִלּוּ הֵם מִמִּין אֶחָד, פְּטוּרִים.
phrases.en: Two women who made [separate doughs] from two [separate] kavs, and these [doughs] touched one another, even if they are of the same species, they are exempt [from hallah].

phrases.he: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁהֵם שֶׁל אִשָּׁה אַחַת, מִין בְּמִינוֹ, חַיָּב. וְשֶׁלֹּא בְמִינוֹ, פָּטוּר
phrases.en: When they belong to one woman: If one species [comes into contact] with the same species, they are subject [to hallah]. If different species, they are exempt.

phrases.he: אֵיזֶה הוּא מִין בְּמִינוֹ, הַחִטִּים אֵינָן מִצְטָרְפוֹת עִם הַכֹּל, אֶלָּא עִם הַכֻּסְּמִין.
phrases.en: What counts as a species with its same species?Wheat is not reckoned together with any [species] other than with spelt; Barley is reckoned together with all [species] except wheat.

phrases.he: הַשְּׂעוֹרִים מִצְטָרְפוֹת עִם הַכֹּל, חוּץ מִן הַחִטִּים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri says: the rest of the species are reckoned together one with another.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר, שְׁאָר הַמִּינִים מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה
שְׁנֵי קַבִּים, וְקַב אֹרֶז אוֹ קַב תְּרוּמָה בָּאֶמְצַע, אֵינָן מִצְטָרְפִין.
phrases.en: [If there are two doughs from] two [separate] kavs, and a kav of rice [dough] or a kav of terumah dough [lying] between, they are not reckoned together.

phrases.he: דָּבָר שֶׁנִּטְּלָה חַלָּתוֹ בָּאֶמְצַע, מִצְטָרְפִין, שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְחַיֵּב בַּחַלָּה
phrases.en: [If there was] dough from which hallah had already been taken [lying] between, they are reckoned together, since it had once been subject to hallah.

phrases.he: קַב חָדָשׁ וְקַב יָשָׁן שֶׁנָּשְׁכוּ זֶה בָזֶה,
phrases.en: A kav of [dough made from] new grain and a kav of [dough from] old grain which are stuck together: Rabbi Ishmael says: let him take [hallah] from the middle; But the sages prohibit.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, יִטֹּל מִן הָאֶמְצַע, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִים.
phrases.en: One who has taken hallah from [dough made out of] one kav: Rabbi Akiva says: it is hallah; But the sages say: it is not hallah.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹטֵל חַלָּה מִן הַקַּב,
רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, חַלָּה.
וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵינָהּ חַלָּה:
שְׁנֵי קַבִּין שֶׁנִּטְּלָה חַלָּתוֹ שֶׁל זֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וְשֶׁל זֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, חָזַר וַעֲשָׂאוֹ עִסָּה אַחַת, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא פוֹטֵר, וַחֲכָמִים מְחַיְּבִין. נִמְצָא חֻמְרוֹ קֻלּוֹ:
phrases.en: Two [separate] kavs [of dough], this one had its hallah removed on its own, and this one had its hallah removed on its own, and then he went back and made of them one dough: Rabbi Akiva exempts; But the sages make it liable. It turns out that the stringency of his [first] ruling leads to the leniency of his other ruling.

phrases.he: נוֹטֵל אָדָם כְּדֵי חַלָּה מֵעִסָּה שֶׁלֹּא הוּרְמָה חַלָּתָהּ, לַעֲשׂוֹתָה בְּטָהֳרָה, לִהְיוֹת מַפְרִישׁ עָלֶיהָ וְהוֹלֵךְ חַלַּת דְּמַאי עַד שֶׁתִּסָּרֵחַ.
phrases.en: A man may take the requisite amount for hallah out of [clean] dough from which hallah has not [previously] been removed in order to remove it in a state of cleanness in order to go on separating [hallah] from it for [unclean] demai, until it becomes putrid, since hallah for demai may be taken from clean [dough] for unclean [dough], and from [one dough for another dough] which is not in close proximity.

phrases.he: שֶׁחַלַּת דְּמַאי נִטֶּלֶת מִן הַטָּהוֹר עַל הַטָּמֵא, וְשֶׁלֹּא מִן הַמֻּקָּף
יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהָיוּ אֲרִיסִין לְנָכְרִים בְּסוּרְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְחַיֵּב פֵּרוֹתֵיהֶם בַּמַּעַשְׂרוֹת וּבַשְּׁבִיעִית, וְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל פּוֹטֵר.
phrases.en: An Israelite who was a tenant of a non-Jew in Syria: Rabbi Eliezer makes their produce liable to tithes and to [the law of] the sabbatical year; But Rabban Gamaliel makes [it] exempt.

phrases.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, שְׁתֵּי חַלּוֹת בְּסוּרְיָא.
phrases.en: Rabban Gamaliel says: [one is to give] two hallah-portions in Syria; But Rabbi Eliezer says: [only] one hallah-portion.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, חַלָּה אֶחָת.
phrases.en: They adopted the lenient ruling of Rabban Gamaliel and the lenient ruling of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.he: אָחֲזוּ קֻלּוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְקֻלּוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.en: Eventually they went back and acted in accordance with Rabban Gamaliel in both respects.

phrases.he: חָזְרוּ לִנְהוֹג כְּדִבְרֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בִּשְׁתֵּי דְרָכִים
רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, שָׁלֹשׁ אֲרָצוֹת לַחַלָּה.
phrases.en: Rabban Gamaliel says: there are three territories with regard to [liability to] hallah:From the land of Israel to Chezib: one hallah-portion.

phrases.he: מֵאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַד כְּזִיב, חַלָּה אֶחָת.
phrases.en: From Chezib to the river and to Amanah: two hallah-portions.

phrases.he: מִכְּזִיב וְעַד הַנָּהָר וְעַד אֲמָנָה, שְׁתֵּי חַלּוֹת, אַחַת לָאוּר וְאַחַת לַכֹּהֵן.
phrases.en: One for the fire and one for the priest. The one for the fire has a minimum measure, and the one for the priest does not have a minimum measure.

phrases.he: שֶׁל אוּר יֶשׁ לָהּ שִׁעוּר, וְשֶׁל כֹּהֵן אֵין לָהּ שִׁעוּר.
phrases.en: From the river and from Amanah and inward: two hallah-portions.

phrases.he: מִן הַנָּהָר וְעַד אֲמָנָה וְלִפְנִים, שְׁתֵּי חַלּוֹת, אַחַת לָאוּר וְאַחַת לַכֹּהֵן.
phrases.en: One for the fire and one for the priest. The one for the fire has no minimum measure, and the one for the priest has a minimum measure.

phrases.he: שֶׁל אוּר אֵין לָהּ שִׁעוּר, וְשֶׁל כֹּהֵן יֶשׁ לָהּ שִׁעוּר. וּטְבוּל יוֹם אוֹכְלָהּ.
phrases.en: And [a priest] who has immersed himself during the day [and has not waited till sunset for his purification to be complete] may eat it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ טְבִילָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: he does not require immersion.
