phrases.he: וַאֲסוּרָה לַזָּבִים וְלַזָּבוֹת לַנִּדָּה וְלַיּוֹלְדוֹת, וְנֶאֱכֶלֶת עִם הַזָּר עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן, וְנִתֶּנֶת לְכָל כֹּהֵן
phrases.en: But it is forbidden to zavim and zavot, to menstruants, and to women after childbirth; It may be eaten with a non-priest at the [same] table; And it may be given to any priest.

phrases.he: וְאֵלּוּ נִתָּנִין לְכָל כֹּהֵן, הַחֲרָמִים, וְהַבְּכוֹרוֹת, וּפִדְיוֹן הַבֵּן, וּפִדְיוֹן פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר, וְהַזְּרוֹעַ, וְהַלְּחָיַיִם, וְהַקֵּבָה, וְרֵאשִׁית הַגֵּז, וְשֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵפָה, וְקָדְשֵׁי הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, וְהַבִּכּוּרִים.
phrases.en: These may be given to any priest:Devoted things (haramim); Firstlings; The redemption of the first born; The [lamb substituted as] ransom for the firstling of a donkey; The shoulder, the two cheeks and the maw; The first of the fleece; Oil [fit only] for burning; Consecrated food [which must be eaten] within the Temple; And bikkurim.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹסֵר בַּבִּכּוּרִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah prohibits bikkurim.

phrases.he: כַּרְשִׁינֵי תְרוּמָה, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַתִּיר וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִים
phrases.en: Vetches of terumah: Rabbi Akiva permits, But the sages prohibit.

phrases.he: נִתַּאי אִישׁ תְּקוֹעַ הֵבִיא חַלּוֹת מִבֵּיתָר, וְלֹא קִבְּלוּ מִמֶּנּוּ.
phrases.en: Nittai of Tekoa brought hallah-portions from Be-Yitur, but they did not accept from him.

phrases.he: אַנְשֵׁי אֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִיָּא הֵבִיאוּ חַלּוֹתֵיהֶן מֵאֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִיָּא, וְלֹא קִבְּלוּ מֵהֶם.
phrases.en: The people of Alexandria brought hallah, but they did not accept from them. The people from Mt.

phrases.he: אַנְשֵׁי הַר צְבוֹעִים הֵבִיאוּ בִכּוּרֵיהֶם קֹדֶם עֲצֶרֶת, וְלֹא קִבְּלוּ מֵהֶם, מִפְּנֵי הַכָּתוּב שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה (שמות כג), וְחַג הַקָּצִיר בִּכּוּרֵי מַעֲשֶׂיךָ אֲשֶׁר תִּזְרַע בַּשָּׂדֶה
phrases.en: Zevoim brought bikkurim prior to Atzeret (Shavuot), but they did not accept from them, on for it is written in the Torah: “And the festival of the harvest, the first-fruits of your labors, which you have sown in the field” (Exodus 23:16).

phrases.he: בֶּן אַנְטִינוֹס הֶעֱלָה בְכוֹרוֹת מִבָּבֶל, וְלֹא קִבְּלוּ מִמֶּנּוּ.
phrases.en: Ben Antigonus brought up firstlings from Babylon, but they did not accept from him.

phrases.he: יוֹסֵף הַכֹּהֵן הֵבִיא בִכּוּרֵי יַיִן וְשֶׁמֶן, וְלֹא קִבְּלוּ מִמֶּנּוּ.
phrases.en: Joseph the priest brought first fruits of wine and oil, but they did not accept from him.

phrases.he: אַף הוּא הֶעֱלָה אֶת בָּנָיו וּבְנֵי בֵיתוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת פֶּסַח קָטָן בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, וְהֶחֱזִירוּהוּ, שֶׁלֹּא יִקָּבַע הַדָּבָר חוֹבָה.
phrases.en: He also brought up his sons and members of his household to celebrate Pesah katan in Jerusalem, but they turned him back, so that the thing should not become firmly fixed as an obligation.

phrases.he: אֲרִיסְטוֹן הֵבִיא בִכּוּרָיו מֵאַפַּמְיָא, וְקִבְּלוּ מִמֶּנּוּ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָמְרוּ, הַקּוֹנֶה בְסוּרְיָא, כְּקוֹנֶה בְּפַרְוָר שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלָיִם
phrases.en: Ariston brought his first fruits from Apamea and they accepted from him, because they said, one who buys [a field] in Syria is as one who buys [a field] in the outskirts of Jerusalem.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹטֵעַ לִסְיָג וּלְקוֹרוֹת, פָּטוּר מִן הָעָרְלָה.
phrases.en: One who plants [a fruit tree] as a fence or to provide wood beams, it is exempt from [the law of] orlah.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ אָמַר הַפְּנִימִי לְמַאֲכָל וְהַחִיצוֹן לִסְיָג, הַפְּנִימִי חַיָּב, וְהַחִיצוֹן פָּטוּר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: even if he said “The inward [facing part of the tree] is for food, and the outward [facing part] is for a fence,” the inward [facing part] is subject [to orlah], and the outward [facing part] is exempt.

phrases.he: עֵת שֶׁבָּאוּ אֲבוֹתֵינוּ לָאָרֶץ, מָצְאוּ נָטוּעַ, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: If at the time when our ancestors came into the land and they found [a tree already] planted it was exempt [from the laws of orlah].

phrases.he: נָטְעוּ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא כִבְּשׁוּ, חַיָּב. הַנּוֹטֵעַ לָרַבִּים, חַיָּב. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה פּוֹטֵר.
phrases.en: If they planted [a tree], even though they had not yet conquered [the land], it was subject [to orlah]. If one planted a tree for [the use of] the many, it is subject.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹטֵעַ בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, וְהַנָּכְרִי שֶׁנָּטַע, וְהַגַּזְלָן שֶׁנָּטַע, וְהַנּוֹטֵעַ בִּסְפִינָה, וְהָעוֹלֶה מֵאֵלָיו, חַיָּב בָּעָרְלָה
phrases.en: But Rabbi Judah makes it exempt. If one has planted [a tree] in the public domain, or if a non-Jew has planted, or if a robber has planted, or one who plants on a boat, or [a tree] that has grown of itself, it is subject to orlah.

phrases.he: אִילָן שֶׁנֶּעֱקַר וְהַסֶּלַע עִמּוֹ, שְׁטָפוֹ נָהָר וְהַסֶּלַע עִמּוֹ, אִם יָכוֹל לִחְיוֹת, פָּטוּר, וְאִם לָאו, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: If a tree was uprooted and the hard soil together with it, or if a stream swept it away and the hard soil together with it, [then] if it could have lived it is exempt, But if [it could] not, it is subject.

phrases.he: נֶעֱקַר הַסֶּלַע מִצִּדּוֹ, אוֹ שֶׁזִּעְזְעַתּוּ הַמַּחֲרֵשָׁה, אוֹ שֶׁזִּעְזְעוֹ וַעֲשָׂאוֹ כְעָפָר, אִם יָכוֹל לִחְיוֹת, פָּטוּר, וְאִם לָאו, חַיָּב
phrases.en: If the hard soil has been detached from its side, or if a ploughshare shook it, or if someone shook it, and one reset it with earth, [then] if it could have lived, it is exempt, But if not, it is subject.

phrases.he: אִילָן שֶׁנֶּעֱקַר וְנִשְׁתַּיֵּר בּוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: If a tree was uprooted and one root was left [in the ground], it is exempt.

phrases.he: וְכַמָּה יְהֵא הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ, רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן יְהוּדָה אִישׁ בַּרְתּוֹתָא, כְּמַחַט שֶׁל מִתּוּן
phrases.en: How much must the [thickness of the] root be? Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel said in the name of Rabb Eliezer ben Judah a man of Bartota: as [thick as] a pin [used for] stretching.

phrases.he: אִילָן שֶׁנֶּעֱקַר וּבוֹ בְרֵכָה, וְהוּא חָיֶּה מִמֶּנָּה, חָזְרָה הַזְּקֵנָה לִהְיוֹת כַּבְּרֵכָה.
phrases.en: A tree which was uprooted and it has a bent-down [and rooted] shoot, and it [the tree] derives sustenance from it [the shoot], the old [tree] is [considered] like the shoot.

phrases.he: הִבְרִיכָהּ שָׁנָה אַחַר שָׁנָה, וְנִפְסְקָה, מוֹנֶה מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁנִּפְסְקָה.
phrases.en: If one bends [and roots] from it year after year, and it became detached, one counts from the time it became detached.

phrases.he: סִפּוּק הַגְּפָנִים, וְסִפּוּק עַל גַּבֵּי סִפּוּק, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִבְרִיכָן בָּאָרֶץ, מֻתָּר.
phrases.en: A grafted shoot of vines, and a grafted shoot [growing] on another grafted shoot, even if he rooted them in the soil, they are permitted.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, מָקוֹם שֶׁכֹּחָהּ יָפֶה, מֻתָּר, וְמָקוֹם שֶׁכֹּחָהּ רָע, אָסוּר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir said: in an instance where it is strongly [grafted], it is permitted, but in an instance where it is poorly [grafted], it is prohibited.

phrases.he: וְכֵן בְּרֵכָה שֶׁנִּפְסְקָה וְהִיא מְלֵאָה פֵרוֹת, אִם הוֹסִיף בְּמָאתַיִם, אָסוּר
phrases.en: A bent-down [and rooted] shoot that has become detached and is full of fruit, [then] if it increased one two hundredth, it is prohibited.

phrases.he: נְטִיעָה שֶׁל עָרְלָה וְשֶׁל כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ בִנְטִיעוֹת, הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִלְקֹט.
phrases.en: If a shoot of orlah or a vineyard in which seeds had been planted (kilayim), became mixed up with [other] shoots, behold one may not gather [the fruit].

phrases.he: וְאִם לָקַט, יַעֲלֶה בְאֶחָד וּמָאתַיִם, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִתְכַּוֵּן לִלְקֹט.
phrases.en: But if one has gathered [it], it is neutralized in two hundred-and-one, provided that he did not act deliberately.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַף יִתְכַּוֵּן לִלְקֹט וְיַעֲלֶה בְאֶחָד וּמָאתָיִם:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: even if he acted deliberately, it becomes neutralized in two hundred-and-one.

phrases.he: הֶעָלִים, וְהַלּוּלָבִים, וּמֵי גְּפָנִים, וּסְמָדַר, מֻתָּרִים בָּעָרְלָה וּבָרְבָעִי וּבַנָּזִיר, וַאֲסוּרִים בָּאֲשֵׁרָה.
phrases.en: Leaves, sprouts, sap of vines, and vine-buds are permitted in respect of orlah and the laws of the fourth year, and to a nazirite, but are prohibited if they come from an Asherah [tree].

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, הַסְּמָדַר אָסוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא פְּרִי.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: vine-buds are prohibited because they are fruit.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, הַמַּעֲמִיד בִּשְׂרָף הָעָרְלָה, אָסוּר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer said: if one curdles [milk] with the resinous substances of [a tree liable to] orlah, it is prohibited.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּפֵרוּשׁ, שֶׁהַמַּעֲמִיד בִּשְׂרָף הֶעָלִים וּבִשְׂרָף הָעִקָּרִים, מֻתָּר, בִּשְׂרָף הַפַּגִּים, אָסוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵם פְּרִי:
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua said: I have received an explicit tradition that if one curdles [milk] with the resinous substance of the leaves, or with the resinous substance of the roots, it is permitted, but with the resinous substance of the unripe berries, it is prohibited, because these are fruit.

phrases.he: עַנְקוֹקְלוֹת, וְהַחַרְצַנִּים, וְהַזַּגִּים, וְהַתֶּמֶד שֶׁלָּהֶם, קְלִפֵּי רִמּוֹן וְהַנֵּץ שֶׁלּוֹ, קְלִפֵּי אֱגוֹזִים, וְהַגַּרְעִינִים, אֲסוּרִים בָּעָרְלָה, וּבָאֲשֵׁרָה, וּבַנָּזִיר, וּמֻתָּרִין בָּרְבָעִי. וְהַנּוֹבְלוֹת, כֻּלָּן אֲסוּרוֹת:
phrases.en: Defective grapes, grape kernels, grape husks, and the temed drink made from them, the peel of a pomegranate and its sprout, nutshells, and fruit-seeds, are all subject to the laws of orlah, asherah and a nazirite, but permitted in respect of a fourth year vineyard. Fallen unripe fruit is subject to all of them.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, נוֹטְעִין יִחוּר שֶׁל עָרְלָה, וְאֵין נוֹטְעִין אֱגוֹז שֶׁל עָרְלָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא פְּרִי.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: one may plant a shoot of orlah; But one may not plant a nut of orlah, because it is fruit.

phrases.he: וְאֵין מַרְכִּיבִין בְּכַפְנִיּוֹת שֶׁל עָרְלָה
phrases.en: And one may not graft early date berries of orlah.

phrases.he: הַתְּרוּמָה, וּתְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר שֶׁל דְּמַאי, הַחַלָּה וְהַבִּכּוּרִים, עוֹלִים בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה, וּמִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה, וְצָרִיךְ לְהָרִים.
phrases.en: Terumah, terumat maaser of demai, hallah and bikkurim, are neutralized in a hundred-and-one mixture. And they are reckoned together [to form the statutory minimum]. And it is necessary to remove [from the mixture an amount equal to that of the consecrated produce contained in it].

phrases.he: הָעָרְלָה וְכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, עוֹלִים בְּאֶחָד וּמָאתַיִם, וּמִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לְהָרִים.
phrases.en: Orlah and kilayim of the vineyard are neutralized in a two-hundred-and-one mixture. And they are reckoned together [to form the statutory minimum].

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אֵינָן מִצְטָרְפִין.
phrases.en: But it is not necessary to remove [from the mixture an amount equal to that of the consecrated produce contained in it].

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, מִצְטָרְפִין בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם, אֲבָל לֹא לֶאֱסֹר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: they are not reckoned together. Rabbi Eliezer says: they are reckoned together when they impart flavor, but not to prohibit.

phrases.he: הַתְּרוּמָה מַעֲלָה אֶת הָעָרְלָה, וְהָעָרְלָה אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה.
phrases.en: Terumah can void orlah, and orlah can void terumah.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד, סְאָה תְרוּמָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְמֵאָה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָפְלוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה קַבִּין עָרְלָה, אוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה קַבִּין כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, זוֹ הִיא שֶׁהַתְּרוּמָה מַעֲלָה אֶת הָעָרְלָה וְהָעָרְלָה אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה
phrases.en: How so? [For instance] a seah of terumah fell into one hundred, and afterwards three kavs of orlah or three kavs of mixed-seeds of the vineyard [fell in]. This is [an instance] where terumah goes towards neutralizing orlah, and orlah terumah.

phrases.he: הָעָרְלָה מַעֲלָה אֶת הַכִּלְאַיִם, וְהַכִּלְאַיִם אֶת הָעָרְלָה, וְהָעָרְלָה אֶת הָעָרְלָה.
phrases.en: Orlah can void kilayim, and kilayim [can void] orlah, and orlah [can void] orlah.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד, סְאָה עָרְלָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְמָאתַיִם, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָפְלָה סְאָה וְעוֹד עָרְלָה, אוֹ סְאָה וְעוֹד שֶׁל כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, זוֹ הִיא שֶׁהָעָרְלָה מַעֲלָה אֶת הַכִּלְאַיִם, וְהַכִּלְאַיִם אֶת הָעָרְלָה, וְהָעָרְלָה אֶת הָעָרְלָה
phrases.en: How so? A seah of orlah falls into two hundred [seahs] and afterwards there falls in a seah and a little bit more of orlah, or a seah and a little bit more of kilayim of the vineyard--this is [a case] where orlah can void kilayim, and kilayim [can void] orlah, and orlah [can void] orlah.

phrases.he: כָּל הַמְחַמֵּץ וְהַמְתַבֵּל וְהַמְדַמֵּעַ בַּתְּרוּמָה וּבָעָרְלָה וּבְכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, אָסוּר.
phrases.en: Whatever causes something to ferment, or seasons, or makes medumma with terumah, with orlah or with ‘mixed-seeds’ of the vineyard, is prohibited.

phrases.he: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אַף מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.en: Bet Shammai says: it also renders unclean.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ כַּבֵּיצָה:
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel says: it never renders unclean unless it has the volume of an egg.

phrases.he: דּוֹסְתַּאי אִישׁ כְּפַר יִתְמָה, הָיָה מִתַּלְמִידֵי בֵית שַׁמַּאי, וְאָמַר, שָׁמַעְתִּי מִשַּׁמַּאי הַזָּקֵן שֶׁאָמַר, לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ כַּבֵּיצָה:
phrases.en: Dostai of Kefar Yitmah was one of the disciples of Bet Shammai, and he said, “I received a tradition from Shammai the elder who said: “It never renders unclean unless it contains the volume of an egg.”

phrases.he: וּלְמָה אָמְרוּ כָּל הַמְחַמֵּץ וְהַמְתַבֵּל וְהַמְדַמֵּעַ לְהַחֲמִיר, מִין בְּמִינוֹ.
phrases.en: Concerning what did they say: “Anything that causes fermentation or seasons or which renders medumma we rule stringently”? [In the case of] a species [mixed] with its [like] species.

phrases.he: לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחֲמִיר, מִין בְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ.
phrases.en: [When did they say] “we rule [sometimes] leniently and [sometimes] stringently”? [In the case of] a species [mixed] with a different kind of species.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד, שְׂאֹר שֶׁל חִטִּים שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹךְ עִסַּת חִטִּים, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ, בֵּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ לַעֲלוֹת בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה וּבֵין שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ לַעֲלוֹת בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה, אָסוּר.
phrases.en: How so? If leaven of wheat fell into dough of wheat and there is enough to cause fermentation, [then] whether there is enough to become neutralized in one-hundred-and-one, or there is not enough to become neutralized in one-hundred-and-one, it is prohibited.

phrases.he: אֵין בּוֹ לַעֲלוֹת בְּמֵאָה וְאֶחָד, בֵּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ, בֵּין שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ, אָסוּר
phrases.en: If there is not enough to become neutralized in one-hundred-and-one, [then] whether there is enough to cause fermentation, or there is not enough to cause fermentation, it is prohibited.

phrases.he: לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחֲמִיר מִין בְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ, כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: [We rule sometimes] leniently and [sometimes] stringently, [in the case of] a species [mixed] with a different kind of species.

phrases.he: כְּגוֹן גְּרִיסִין שֶׁנִּתְבַּשְּׁלוּ עִם עֲדָשִׁים, וְיֵשׁ בָּהֶם בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם, בֵּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם לַעֲלוֹת בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה, וּבֵין שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם לַעֲלוֹת בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה, אָסוּר.
phrases.en: How so? If crushed beans were boiled together with lentils, and there is enough of them [the crushed beans] to impart flavor, [then] whether there is enough to become neutralized in one-hundred-and-one, or there is not enough to become neutralized in one-hundred-and-one, it is prohibited.

phrases.he: אֵין בָּהֶם בְּנוֹתֵן טַעַם, בֵּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם לַעֲלוֹת בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה, וּבֵין שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם לַעֲלוֹת בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה, מֻתָּר
phrases.en: [But] if there is not enough to impart flavor, [then] whether there is enough to become neutralized in one-hundred-and-one, or there is not enough to become neutralized in one-hundred-and-one, [the mixture] is permitted.

phrases.he: שְׂאֹר שֶׁל חֻלִּין שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹךְ עִסָּה, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ כְּדֵי לְחַמֵּץ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָפַל שְׂאֹר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, אוֹ שְׂאֹר שֶׁל כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ, אָסוּר:
phrases.en: If leaven of hullin has fallen into dough, and there was enough of it to cause fermentation, and after that leaven of terumah fell in or leaven of kilayim of the vineyard, and there is enough to cause fermentation, [the dough] is prohibited.

phrases.he: שְׂאֹר שֶׁל חֻלִּין שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹךְ עִסָּה וְחִמְּצָהּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָפַל שְׂאֹר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה אוֹ שְׂאֹר שֶׁל כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ, אָסוּר. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר:
phrases.en: If leaven of hullin has fallen into dough and caused it to ferment, and after that there fell in leaven of terumah or of kilayim of the vineyard, and there was enough to cause fermentation, [the dough] is prohibited. But Rabbi Shimon permits it.

phrases.he: תְּבָלִין, שְׁנַיִם וּשְׁלֹשָׁה שֵׁמוֹת מִמִּין אֶחָד, אוֹ מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה, אָסוּר, וּמִצְטָרְפִין.
phrases.en: Seasonings [consisting] of two or three categories of one species, or [consisting] of three species [of one category], are forbidden and combine.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, שְׁנַיִם וּשְׁלֹשָׁה שֵׁמוֹת מִמִּין אֶחָד, אוֹ שְׁנֵי מִינִין מִשֵּׁם אֶחָד, אֵינָן מִצְטָרְפִין:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon said: Two or three categories of one species, or two species of one category, do not combine.

phrases.he: שְׂאֹר שֶׁל חֻלִּין וְשֶׁל תְּרוּמָה שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לְתוֹךְ עִסָּה, לֹא בָּזֶה כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ וְלֹא בָּזֶה כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ, נִצְטָרְפוּ וְחִמְּצוּ,
phrases.en: Leaven of hullin and of terumah fell into dough, and neither this was sufficient to cause fermentation nor was that sufficient to cause fermentation, but together they caused [the dough] to ferment:Rabbi Eliezer says: I go after the last.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַחַר הָאַחֲרוֹן אֲנִי בָא.
phrases.en: But the sages say: whether the prohibited fell in first or last, it never causes the dough to become prohibited unless there is enough to cause fermentation.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בֵּין שֶׁנָּפַל אִסּוּר בַּתְּחִלָּה, בֵּין בַּסּוֹף, לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ:

יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ הַבִּירָה הָיָה מִתַּלְמִידֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, וְאָמַר, שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַזָּקֵן עוֹמֵד בְּשַׁעַר הַמִּזְרָח, וְאָמַר, לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר, עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ:
phrases.en: Yoezer, master of the temple (Ish Habirah), was one of the disciples of Bet Shammai and he said: I asked Rabban Gamaliel the elder as he was standing at the eastern gate [of the Temple], and he said: it never causes the dough to become prohibited unless there is enough to cause fermentation.

phrases.he: כֵּלִים שֶׁסָּכָן בְּשֶׁמֶן טָמֵא, וְחָזַר וְסָכָן בְּשֶׁמֶן טָהוֹר, אוֹ שֶׁסָּכָן בְּשֶׁמֶן טָהוֹר, וְחָזַר וְסָכָן בְּשֶׁמֶן טָמֵא,
phrases.en: Vessels which were oiled with unclean oil, and [later] he returned and oiled them with clean oil; Or he [first] oiled them with clean oil, and [later] he returned [to them] and oiled them with unclean oil: Rabbi Eliezer says: “I go after the first.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַחַר הָרִאשׁוֹן אֲנִי בָּא.
phrases.en: And the sages say: after the last.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אַחַר הָאַחֲרוֹן:
שְׂאֹר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה וְשֶׁל כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לְתוֹךְ עִסָּה, לֹא בָזֶה כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ וְלֹא בָזֶה כְדֵי לְחַמֵּץ, וְנִצְטָרְפוּ וְחִמְּצוּ, אָסוּר לְזָרִים וּמֻתָּר לַכֹּהֲנִים.
phrases.en: Leaven of terumah and of kilayim of the vineyard which fell into dough, this one is not sufficient to cause fermentation, nor is that one sufficient to cause fermentation, but together they cause fermentation:It [the dough] is prohibited to non-priests and permitted to priests.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר לְזָרִים וְלַכֹּהֲנִים
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon permits it to both to non-priests and to priests.

phrases.he: תְּבָלִין שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה וְשֶׁל כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם שֶׁנָּפְלוּ בַּקְּדֵרָה, לֹא בָאֵלוּ כְדֵי לְתַבֵּל וְלֹא בָאֵלּוּ כְדֵי לְתַבֵּל, וְנִצְטָרְפוּ וְתִבְּלוּ, אָסוּר לְזָרִים וּמֻתָּר לַכֹּהֲנִים.
phrases.en: Seasonings of terumah and of kilayim of the vineyard that fell into a dish, and there is not enough of one to season, nor is there of the other to season, but together they seasoned:It [the dish] is prohibited to non-priests but permitted to priests.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר לְזָרִים וְלַכֹּהֲנִים
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon declares it permitted to non-priests and to priests.

phrases.he: חֲתִיכָה שֶׁל קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים, שֶׁל פִּגּוּל, וְשֶׁל נוֹתָר, שֶׁנִּתְבַּשְּׁלוּ עִם הַחֲתִיכוֹת, אָסוּר לְזָרִים וּמֻתָּר לַכֹּהֲנִים.
phrases.en: A piece of [meat from] one of the most holy [sacrifices] and [a piece] of [meat which is] piggul, or remnant, which were cooked with other pieces, it [the non-sacred meat] is prohibited to non-priests but permitted to priests.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר לְזָרִים וְלַכֹּהֲנִים
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon declares it permitted to non-priests and to priests.

phrases.he: בְּשַׂר קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים וּבְשַׂר קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים שֶׁנִּתְבַּשְּׁלוּ עִם בְּשַׂר הַתַּאֲוָה, אָסוּר לִטְמֵאִים וּמֻתָּר לִטְהוֹרִים:
phrases.en: Meat of most holy [sacrifices] and meat of less holy [sacrifices] were cooked together with ordinary meat: [the dish] is prohibited to the unclean, but permitted to the clean.

phrases.he: בֶּגֶד שֶׁצְּבָעוֹ בִקְלִפֵּי עָרְלָה, יִדָּלֵק.
phrases.en: A garment dyed with peels of orlah [fruit] must be burned.

phrases.he: נִתְעָרֵב בַּאֲחֵרִים, כֻּלָּם יִדָּלֵקוּ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: If it became mixed up with other [garments], all of them shall be burned, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, יַעֲלֶה בְּאֶחָד וּמָאתָיִם:
phrases.en: But the sages say: it becomes neutralized in two-hundred-and-one.

phrases.he: הַצּוֹבֵעַ מְלֹא הַסִּיט בִּקְלִפֵּי עָרְלָה, וַאֲרָגוֹ בְבֶגֶד, וְאֵין יָדוּעַ אֵיזֶה הוּא,
phrases.en: If one dyed a thread the whole [length] of a sit with orlah peels, and wove it into a garment, and it is not known which [thread] it is:Rabbi Meir says: the garment must be burned; But the sages say: it becomes neutralized in two-hundred-and-one.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, יִדָּלֵק הַבֶּגֶד.
וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, יַעֲלֶה בְאֶחָד וּמָאתָיִם:
הָאוֹרֵג מְלֹא הַסִּיט מִצֶּמֶר הַבְּכוֹר בְּבֶגֶד, יִדָּלֵק הַבֶּגֶד.
phrases.en: If one wove thread the whole [length] of a sit from [the wool of a] first-born animal into a garment, the garment must be burned.

phrases.he: וּמִשְּׂעַר הַנָּזִיר וּמִפֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר בְּשַׂק, יִדָּלֵק הַשָּׂק.
phrases.en: [If from] the hair of a nazirite or of the first-born of a donkey into sack-cloth, the sack-cloth must be burned.

phrases.he: וּבְמֻקְדָּשִׁין, מְקַדְּשִׁין כָּל שֶׁהֵן
phrases.en: And if even the smallest amount [from wool or hair of] consecrated [animals], that which it is woven into] is consecrated.

phrases.he: תַּבְשִׁיל שֶׁבִּשְּׁלוֹ בִקְלִפֵּי עָרְלָה, יִדָּלֵק.
phrases.en: A dish which one cooked with shells of orlah must be burned.

phrases.he: נִתְעָרֵב בַּאֲחֵרִים, יַעֲלֶה בְּאֶחָד וּמָאתָיִם
phrases.en: If [the dish] became mixed up with other [dishes], it becomes neutralized in two-hundred-and-one.

phrases.he: תַּנּוּר שֶׁהִסִּיקוּהוּ בִקְלִפֵּי עָרְלָה וְאָפָה בוֹ אֶת הַפַּת, תִּדָּלֵק הַפָּת.
phrases.en: An oven that was lit with shells of orlah, and then one baked bread in it, the bread must be burned.

phrases.he: נִתְעָרְבָה בַאֲחֵרוֹת, תַּעֲלֶה בְּאֶחָד וּמָאתָיִם
phrases.en: If it became mixed up with other [loaves] it becomes neutralized in two-hundred-and-one.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ חֲבִילֵי תִלְתָּן שֶׁל כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, יִדָּלֵקוּ.
phrases.en: If one has bundles of fenugreek of kilayim of the vineyard, they must be burned.

phrases.he: נִתְעָרְבוּ בַאֲחֵרִים, כֻּלָּם יִדָּלֵקוּ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: If they became mixed up with others, all of them must be burned, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, יַעֲלוּ בְּאֶחָד וּמָאתָיִם:
phrases.en: But the sages say they become neutralized in two-hundred-and-one.

phrases.he: שֶׁהָיָה
phrases.en: For Rabbi Meir used to say: anything that is normally [sold] by counting causes [a mixture] to become consecrated [in even the smallest amount].

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, אֶת שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לִמָּנוֹת, מְקַדֵּשׁ.
phrases.en: But the sages say only six things consecrate [a mixture in even the smallest amount], and Rabbi Akiba says seven [things].

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵינוֹ מְקַדֵּשׁ אֶלָּא שִׁשָּׁה דְבָרִים בִּלְבָד.
phrases.en: And these are they: Nuts with soft shells; badan pomegranates; stopped-up casks; beet shoots; cabbage-heads; Greek pumpkins.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiba says: also loaves [baked by] a householder.

phrases.he: וְאֵלּוּ הֵם, אֱגוֹזֵי פֶרֶךְ, רִמּוֹנֵי בָדָן, וְחָבִיּוֹת סְתוּמוֹת, וְחֻלְפוֹת תְּרָדִין, וְקֻלְסֵי כְרוּב, וּדְלַעַת יְוָנִית.
רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אַף כִּכָּרוֹת שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבָּיִת. הָרָאוּי לְעָרְלָה, עָרְלָה.
phrases.en: To those to which orlah applies [they prohibit the mixture] as orlah, [to those of which] kilayim of the vineyard apply [they prohibit the mixture as] kilayim of the vineyard.

phrases.he: לְכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, כִּלְאֵי הַכָּרֶם
כֵּיצַד. נִתְפַּצְּעוּ הָאֱגוֹזִים, נִתְפָּרְדוּ הָרִמּוֹנִים, נִתְפַּתְּחוּ הֶחָבִיּוֹת, נִתְחַתְּכוּ הַדְּלוּעִים, נִתְפָּרְסוּ הַכִּכָּרוֹת, יַעֲלוּ בְּאֶחָד וּמָאתָיִם:
phrases.en: How so? If the nuts cracked, or if the pomegranates burst open, or the casks became unstopped, or the pumpkins were cut, or the loaves were broken up, they become neutralized in two-hundred-and-one.

phrases.he: סְפֵק עָרְלָה, בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל אָסוּר, וּבְסוּרְיָא מֻתָּר, וּבְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ יוֹרֵד וְלוֹקֵחַ, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִרְאֶנּוּ לוֹקֵט.
phrases.en: Doubtful orlah: in the land of Israel is prohibited, in Syria is permitted, and outside the land one may go down and purchase [from a non-Israelite] as long as he has not seen him gathering it.

phrases.he: כֶּרֶם נָטוּעַ יָרָק, וְיָרָק נִמְכָּר חוּצָה לוֹ, בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל אָסוּר, וּבְסוּרְיָא מֻתָּר, וּבְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ יוֹרֵד וְלוֹקֵט, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִלְקֹט בַּיָּד.
phrases.en: A vineyard planted with vegetables [which are kilayim], and they [the vegetables] are sold outside of it: in the land of Israel these are prohibited, and in Syria they are permitted; outside the land one may go down and purchase them as long as he does not gather [them] with [one’s own] hand.

phrases.he: הֶחָדָשׁ, אָסוּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה בְּכָל מָקוֹם. וְהָעָרְלָה, הֲלָכָה. וְהַכִּלְאַיִם, מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים
phrases.en: New [produce] is prohibited by the Torah in all places. And orlah is a halachah. And kilayim are an enactment of the scribes.

phrases.he: יֵשׁ מְבִיאִין בִּכּוּרִים וְקוֹרִין, מְבִיאִין וְלֹא קוֹרִין, וְיֵשׁ שֶׁאֵינָן מְבִיאִין.
phrases.en: There are some who bring bikkurim and recite [the declaration]; others who only bring, but do not recite; and there are some who neither bring nor recite.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵינָן מְבִיאִין, הַנּוֹטֵעַ לְתוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ וְהִבְרִיךְ לְתוֹךְ שֶׁל יָחִיד אוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּים, וְכֵן הַמַּבְרִיךְ מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁל יָחִיד אוֹ מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁל רַבִּים לְתוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ.
phrases.en: he following are those that do not bring: one who plants [a vine] on his own property, but buries [a shoot in the ground] so that [it] grows on property belonging to [another] individual or to the public.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹטֵעַ לְתוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ וְהִבְרִיךְ לְתוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ, וְדֶרֶךְ הַיָּחִיד וְדֶרֶךְ הָרַבִּים בָּאֶמְצַע, הֲרֵי זֶה אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא.
phrases.en: And similarly if one buries [a shoot in the ground] of another person’s private property or in public property, so that it grows on his own property; Or, if one plants [a vine] on his own [property] and [buries it in the ground] so that it still grows on his own property, but there is a private or public road between, such a one does not bring [bikkurim.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כָּזֶה מֵבִיא:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: such a one has to bring bikkurim.

phrases.he: מֵאֵיזֶה טַעַם אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא, מִשּׁוּם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר, רֵאשִׁית בִּכּוּרֵי אַדְמָתְךָ (שמות כג), עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ כָל הַגִּדּוּלִין מֵאַדְמָתְךָ.
phrases.en: For what reason may he not bring them? Because it is said, “The first-fruits of your land” (Exodus 23:19) until all of their growth is on your land.

phrases.he: הָאֲרִיסִין וְהֶחָכוֹרוֹת וְהַסִּקָּרִיקוֹן וְהַגַּזְלָן, אֵין מְבִיאִין מֵאוֹתוֹ הַטַּעַם, מִשּׁוּם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר, רֵאשִׁית בִּכּוּרֵי אַדְמָתְךָ
phrases.en: Sharecroppers, leasers, or occupiers of confiscated property (sikarikon), or a robber does not bring them for the same reason, because it says, “The first-fruits of your land.”

phrases.he: אֵין מְבִיאִין בִּכּוּרִים חוּץ מִשִּׁבְעַת הַמִּינִים.
phrases.en: Bikkurim are brought only from the seven species.

phrases.he: לֹא מִתְּמָרִים שֶׁבֶּהָרִים, וְלֹא מִפֵּרוֹת שֶׁבָּעֲמָקִים, וְלֹא מִזֵּיתֵי שֶׁמֶן שֶׁאֵינָם מִן הַמֻּבְחָר.
phrases.en: Not from dates grown on hills, nor from [the other species] grown in the valley, nor from olives that are not choice. Bikkurim are not to be brought before Shavuot.

phrases.he: אֵין מְבִיאִין בִּכּוּרִים קֹדֶם לָעֲצֶרֶת.
phrases.en: The people from Mt.

phrases.he: אַנְשֵׁי הַר צְבוֹעִים הֵבִיאוּ בִכּוּרֵיהֶם קֹדֶם לָעֲצֶרֶת, וְלֹא קִבְּלוּ מֵהֶם, מִפְּנֵי הַכָּתוּב שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה (שמות כג) וְחַג הַקָּצִיר בִּכּוּרֵי מַעֲשֶׂיךָ אֲשֶׁר תִּזְרַע בַּשָּׂדֶה
phrases.en: Zevoim brought bikkurim prior to Atzeret (Shavuot), but they did not accept from them, on for it is written in the Torah: “And the festival of the harvest, the first-fruits of your labors, which you have sown in the field” (Exodus 23:16).

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ מְבִיאִין וְלֹא קוֹרִין, הַגֵּר מֵבִיא וְאֵינוֹ קוֹרֵא, שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לוֹמַר אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע ה' לַאֲבוֹתֵינוּ לָתֵת לָנוּ (דברים כ״ו:ג׳).
phrases.en: These bring [bikkurim] but do not read the declaration:The convert, since he cannot say: “Which the Lord has sworn to our fathers, to give to us” (Deuteronomy 26:3).

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיְתָה אִמּוֹ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, מֵבִיא וְקוֹרֵא.
phrases.en: If his mother was an Israelite, then he brings bikkurim and recites.

phrases.he: וּכְשֶׁהוּא מִתְפַּלֵּל בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין עַצְמוֹ, אוֹמֵר, אֱלֹהֵי אֲבוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.en: When he prays privately, he says: “God of the fathers of Israel,” but when he is in the synagogue, he should say: “The God of your fathers.

phrases.he: וּכְשֶׁהוּא בְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת, אוֹמֵר, אֱלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵיכֶם.
phrases.en: But if his mother was an Israelite, he says: “The God of our fathers’.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיְתָה אִמּוֹ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, אוֹמֵר, אֱלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ
רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר, אִשָּׁה בַת גֵּרִים לֹא תִנָּשֵׂא לַכְּהֻנָּה, עַד שֶׁתְּהֵא אִמָּהּ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says: a woman who is a daughter of a convert may not marry a priest unless her mother was herself an Israelite.

phrases.he: אֶחָד גֵּרִים וְאֶחָד עֲבָדִים מְשֻׁחְרָרִים, וַאֲפִלּוּ עַד עֲשָׂרָה דוֹרוֹת, עַד שֶׁתְּהֵא אִמָּן מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.en: [This law applies equally to the offspring] whether of proselytes or freed slaves, even to ten generations, unless their mother is an Israelite.

phrases.he: הָאַפּוֹטְרוֹפּוֹס וְהַשָּׁלִיחַ וְהָעֶבֶד וְהָאִשָּׁה וְטֻמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס, מְבִיאִין וְלֹא קוֹרִין, שֶׁאֵינָן יְכוֹלִין לוֹמַר (דברים כ״ו:י׳) אֲשֶׁר נָתַתָּה לִּי ה'
phrases.en: A guardian, an agent, a slave, a woman, one of doubtful sex, or a hermaphrodite bring the bikkurim, but do not recite, since they cannot say: “Which you, O Lord, have given to me” (Deuteronomy 26:10).

phrases.he: הַקּוֹנֶה שְׁתֵּי אִילָנוֹת בְּתוֹךְ שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ, מֵבִיא וְאֵינוֹ קוֹרֵא.
phrases.en: One who buys two trees [that had grown] in property belonging to his fellow brings bikkurim but does not recite the declaration.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, מֵבִיא וְקוֹרֵא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: he brings and recites.

phrases.he: יָבַשׁ הַמַּעְיָן, נִקְצַץ הָאִילָן, מֵבִיא וְאֵינוֹ קוֹרֵא.
phrases.en: If the well dried up, or the tree was cut down, he brings but does not recite.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מֵבִיא וְקוֹרֵא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: he brings and recites.

phrases.he: מֵעֲצֶרֶת וְעַד הֶחָג, מֵבִיא וְקוֹרֵא.
phrases.en: From Atzeret (Shavuot) until the Festival (of Sukkot) he brings and recites.

phrases.he: מִן הֶחָג וְעַד חֲנֻכָּה, מֵבִיא וְאֵינוֹ קוֹרֵא.
phrases.en: From the Festival (of Sukkot) and until Hannukah he brings, but does not recite.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר, מֵבִיא וְקוֹרֵא
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah ben Batera says: he brings and recites.

phrases.he: הִפְרִישׁ בִּכּוּרָיו וּמָכַר שָׂדֵהוּ, מֵבִיא וְאֵינוֹ קוֹרֵא.
phrases.en: If one set aside his bikkurim and [afterwards] sold his field, he brings but does not recite.

phrases.he: וְהַשֵּׁנִי, מֵאוֹתוֹ הַמִּין אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא, מִמִּין אַחֵר, מֵבִיא וְקוֹרֵא.
phrases.en: The second one [who bought the field] does not bring [bikkurim] of the same species, but of another species he brings and recites.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף מֵאוֹתוֹ הַמִּין מֵבִיא וְקוֹרֵא:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: he may also bring of the same kind and recite.

phrases.he: הִפְרִישׁ בִּכּוּרָיו, נִבְזְזוּ, נָמַקּוּ, נִגְנְבוּ, אָבְדוּ, אוֹ שֶׁנִּטְמְאוּ, מֵבִיא אֲחֵרִים תַּחְתֵּיהֶם וְאֵינוֹ קוֹרֵא.
phrases.en: If one set aside his bikkurim and they were robbed, or rotted, were stolen or lost, or became unclean, he must bring others in their place, but does not recite [the declaration].

phrases.he: וְהַשְּׁנִיִּים אֵינָם חַיָּבִים עֲלֵיהֶם חֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.en: These others are not subject to the law of the [added] fifth.

phrases.he: נִטְמְאוּ בָעֲזָרָה, נוֹפֵץ וְאֵינוֹ קוֹרֵא
phrases.en: If they become unclean while in the Temple court, he must scatter them and he does not recite.

phrases.he: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁהוּא חַיָּב בְּאַחֲרָיוּתָן עַד שֶׁיָּבִיא לְהַר הַבַּיִת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמות כג) רֵאשִׁית בִּכּוּרֵי אַדְמָתְךָ תָּבִיא בֵּית ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁחַיָּב בְּאַחֲרָיוּתָם עַד שֶׁיָּבִיא לְהַר הַבָּיִת.
phrases.en: From where do we know that one is responsible [for his bikkurim] until he brings them to the temple Mount? Because it says: “The first of the first-fruits of your land you shall bring into the house of the Lord your God” (Exodus 23:19) this teaches that he is responsible until he brings them to the Temple Mount.

phrases.he: הֲרֵי שֶׁהֵבִיא מִמִּין אֶחָד וְקָרָא, וְחָזַר וְהֵבִיא מִמִּין אַחֵר, אֵינוֹ קוֹרֵא
phrases.en: If he brought [bikkurim] of one kind and made the recital and then brought of another kind, he does not make a [second] recital.

phrases.he: וְאֵלּוּ מְבִיאִין וְקוֹרִין, מִן הָעֲצֶרֶת וְעַד הֶחָג, מִשִּׁבְעַת הַמִּינִים, מִפֵּרוֹת שֶׁבֶּהָרִים, מִתְּמָרוֹת שֶׁבָּעֲמָקִים, וּמִזֵּיתֵי שֶׁמֶן, מֵעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן.
phrases.en: These bring and recite:[One who brings bikkurim] from Atzeret until the Festival [of Sukkot], from the seven species, from fruit grown on the mountains, or dates grown in the valleys, from oil-olives, and from [produce] from the other side of the Jordan.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר, אֵין מְבִיאִין בִּכּוּרִים מֵעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן, שֶׁאֵינָהּ אֶרֶץ זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבָשׁ
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose the Galilean says: one does not bring [bikkurim] from transjordania, since that is not a land flowing with milk and honey.

phrases.he: הַקּוֹנֶה שְׁלֹשָׁה אִילָנוֹת בְּתוֹךְ שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ, מֵבִיא וְקוֹרֵא.
phrases.en: One who bought three trees in another’s field, he brings [bikkurim] and recites.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ שְׁנָיִם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: even [if he bought] only two.

phrases.he: קָנָה אִילָן וְקַרְקָעוֹ, מֵבִיא וְקוֹרֵא.
phrases.en: If he bought one tree with its land, he brings [bikkurim] and recites.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף בַּעֲלֵי אֲרִיסוּת וְחָכוֹרוֹת, מְבִיאִין וְקוֹרִין:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: even sharecroppers and leasers bring and recite.

phrases.he: הַתְּרוּמָה וְהַבִּכּוּרִים, חַיָּבִים עֲלֵיהֶן מִיתָה וְחֹמֶשׁ, וַאֲסוּרִים לְזָרִים, וְהֵם נִכְסֵי כֹהֵן, וְעוֹלִין בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה, וּטְעוּנִין רְחִיצַת יָדַיִם וְהַעֲרֵב שֶׁמֶשׁ.
phrases.en: Regarding terumah and bikkurim:One is liable to death And the [additional] fifth; And they are forbidden to non-priests; And they are the property of the priest; And they are neutralized in a hundred and one parts; And they require the washing of hands; And the setting of the sun.

phrases.he: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ בִתְרוּמָה וּבִכּוּרִים, מַה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן בַּמַּעֲשֵׂר
phrases.en: These [laws] apply only to terumah and bikkurim, but not to tithe.

phrases.he: יֵשׁ בְּמַעֲשֵׂר וּבִכּוּרִים מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּתְּרוּמָה, שֶׁהַמַּעֲשֵׂר וְהַבִּכּוּרִים טְעוּנִים הֲבָאַת מָקוֹם, וּטְעוּנִים וִדּוּי, וַאֲסוּרִין לָאוֹנֵן. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר. וְחַיָּבִין בַּבִּעוּר. וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן פּוֹטֵר.
phrases.en: There are [laws] which apply to [second tithe] and bikkurim but not to terumah:That [second] tithe and bikkurim must to be brought to [the appointed] place; They require confession; They are forbidden to an onen. But Rabbi Shimon permits [bikkurim to an onen]; They are subject to [the law of] removal. But Rabbi Shimon exempts [bikkurim from removal].

phrases.he: וַאֲסוּרִין כָּל שֶׁהֵן מִלֶּאֱכֹל בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם.
phrases.en: And in Jerusalem the slightest mixture of them [with hullin of the same species] renders it forbidden to be consumed [as common food outside of Jerusalem.

phrases.he: וְגִדּוּלֵיהֶן אֲסוּרִים מִלֶּאֱכֹל בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם אַף לְזָרִים וְלַבְּהֵמָה. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר.
phrases.en: And what grows from them in Jerusalem is forbidden to be consumed [outside of Jerusalem], Even by non-priests or by cattle; But Rabbi Shimon permits.

phrases.he: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ בַּמַּעֲשֵׂר וּבַבִּכּוּרִים, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּתְּרוּמָה
phrases.en: These are [the laws] which apply to [second] tithe and bikkurim, but not to terumah.

phrases.he: יֵשׁ בַּתְּרוּמָה וְבַמַּעֲשֵׂר מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּבִּכּוּרִים, שֶׁהַתְּרוּמָה וְהַמַּעֲשֵׂר אוֹסְרִין אֶת הַגֹּרֶן, וְיֵשׁ לָהֶם שִׁעוּר, וְנוֹהֲגִים בְּכָל הַפֵּרוֹת, בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת וְשֶׁלֹּא בִפְנֵי הַבַּיִת, וּבָאֲרִיסִין וּבֶחָכוֹרוֹת וּבַסִּקָּרִיקוֹן וּבַגַּזְלָן.
phrases.en: There are [laws] which apply to terumah and maaser [sheni] but not to bikkurim:Terumah and the [second] tithe render forbidden [the contents of] the threshing-floor; They have a set amount. They apply to all produce; Both during and after Temple times; [And they apply to to produce grown] by sharecroppers, leasers, or occupiers of confiscated property (sikarikon), or a robber.

phrases.he: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ בַתְּרוּמָה וּבַמַּעֲשֵׂר, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּבִּכּוּרִים
phrases.en: These are [the laws] which apply to terumah and maaser [sheni], but not to bikkurim.

phrases.he: וְיֵשׁ בַּבִּכּוּרִים מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּתְּרוּמָה וּבַמַּעֲשֵׂר, שֶׁהַבִּכּוּרִים נִקְנִין בִּמְחֻבָּר לַקַּרְקַע, וְעוֹשֶׂה אָדָם כָּל שָׂדֵהוּ בִּכּוּרִים, וְחַיָּב בְּאַחֲרָיוּתָם, וּטְעוּנִים קָרְבָּן וְשִׁיר וּתְנוּפָה וְלִינָה:
phrases.en: And there are [laws] which apply to bikkurim which do not [apply] to terumah or maaser sheni:For bikkurim can become acquired while still attached [to the soil]. And a man may make his entire field bikkurim; He is responsible for them; And they require a sacrifice, a song, waving and spending the night in Jerusalem.

phrases.he: תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר שָׁוָה לַבִּכּוּרִים בִּשְׁתֵּי דְרָכִים, וְלַתְּרוּמָה בִּשְׁתֵּי דְרָכִים.
phrases.en: The terumah of tithe is like bikkurim in two ways, and like terumah in two other ways:It may be taken from pure produce for impure produce; And from such produce that is not in close proximity, like bikkurim.

phrases.he: נִטֶּלֶת מִן הַטָּהוֹר עַל הַטָּמֵא, וְשֶׁלֹּא מִן הַמֻּקָּף, כַּבִּכּוּרִים.
phrases.en: And it renders the contents of the threshing-floor forbidden, And it has a prescribed amount like terumah.

phrases.he: וְאוֹסֶרֶת אֶת הַגֹּרֶן, וְיֶשׁ לָהּ שִׁעוּר, כַּתְּרוּמָה
אֶתְרוֹג שָׁוֶה לָאִילָן בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְרָכִים, וְלַיָּרָק בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶחָד.
phrases.en: An etrog is similar in three ways to [the fruit of an ordinary] tree, and in one way to a vegetable.

phrases.he: שָׁוֶה לָאִילָן, בָּעָרְלָה וּבָרְבָעִי וּבַשְּׁבִיעִית.
phrases.en: It is similar to a tree in respect of orlah, fourth year plantings, and [the law of] the seventh year; And it is similar to a vegetable in one thing: that its tithing goes according to the time it is harvested, the words of Rabban Gamaliel.

phrases.he: וְלַיָּרָק בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶחָד, שֶׁבִּשְׁעַת לְקִיטָתוֹ עִשּׂוּרוֹ, דִּבְרֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, שָׁוֶה לָאִילָן בְּכָל דָּבָר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: it is similar to a tree in all ways.

phrases.he: דַּם מְהַלְּכֵי שְׁתַּיִם, שָׁוֶה לְדַם בְּהֵמָה, לְהַכְשִׁיר אֶת הַזְּרָעִים.
phrases.en: The blood of those who walk on two [legs] is like the blood of beasts in that it renders seeds susceptible [to impurity].

phrases.he: וְדַם הַשֶּׁרֶץ, אֵין חַיָּבִין עָלָיו
phrases.en: And it is like the blood of a sheretz, in that one is not liable for eating it.

phrases.he: כּוֹי, יֶשׁ בּוֹ דְרָכִים שָׁוֶה לַחַיָּה, וְיֶשׁ בּוֹ דְרָכִים שָׁוֶה לַבְּהֵמָה, וְיֶשׁ בּוֹ דְרָכִים שָׁוֶה לַבְּהֵמָה וְלַחַיָּה, וְיֶשׁ בּוֹ דְרָכִים שֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה לֹא לַבְּהֵמָה וְלֹא לַחַיָּה:
phrases.en: A koy is in some ways like a wild animal (hayyah); in some ways it is like a domesticated animal (behemah); in some ways it is like both a behemah and a hayyah, and in some ways it is like neither a behemah nor a hayyah.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד שָׁוֶה לַחַיָּה, דָּמוֹ טָעוּן כִּסּוּי כְּדַם חַיָּה, וְאֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אוֹתוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב, וְאִם שְׁחָטוֹ, אֵין מְכַסִּין אֶת דָּמוֹ, וְחֶלְבּוֹ מְטַמֵּא בְטֻמְאַת נְבֵלָה כַּחַיָּה, וְטֻמְאָתוֹ בְסָפֵק, וְאֵין פּוֹדִין בּוֹ פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר:
phrases.en: How is it like a wild animal?Its blood must be covered like the blood of a wild animal. It may not be slaughtered on a festival. If he slaughtered it, he should not cover its blood. Its fat is impure like that of a wild animal, but its impurity is of doubtful status. One does not redeem with it the first-born of a donkey.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד שָׁוֶה לַבְּהֵמָה, חֶלְבּוֹ אָסוּר כְּחֵלֶב בְּהֵמָה, וְאֵין חַיָּבִין עָלָיו כָּרֵת, וְאֵינוֹ נִלְקָח בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר לֶאֱכֹל בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, וְחַיָּב בִּזְרוֹעַ וּלְחָיַיִם וְקֵבָה.
phrases.en: And how is [the koy] similar to a behemah (a domesticated beast)?Its fat (helev) is prohibited like the fat of a behemah, but one [who eats it] is not liable for karet. It may not be bought with the money from second tithe to be eaten in Jerusalem. It is subject to [the priest’s share of] the shoulder, the two cheeks and the maw.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פּוֹטֵר, שֶׁהַמּוֹצִיא מֵחֲבֵרוֹ עָלָיו הָרְאָיָה
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer exempts it because the burden of proof is upon the one who extracts from his neighbor.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד אֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה לֹא לַחַיָּה וְלֹא לַבְּהֵמָה, אָסוּר מִשּׁוּם כִּלְאַיִם עִם הַחַיָּה וְעִם הַבְּהֵמָה, הַכּוֹתֵב חַיָּתוֹ וּבְהֶמְתּוֹ לִבְנוֹ, לֹא כָתַב לוֹ אֶת הַכּוֹי, אִם אָמַר הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר שֶׁזֶּה חַיָּה אוֹ בְהֵמָה, הֲרֵי הוּא נָזִיר.
phrases.en: And how is [a koy] neither like a behemah nor like a hayyah?It is forbidden because of kilayim [to yoke it] with either a behemah or a hayyah. One who deeds his son his behemah and his hayyah he has not [thereby] given him the koy. If one says, “I will become a nazirite if this is [not] a hayyah or a behemah”, he is a nazirite.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל דְּרָכָיו, שָׁוִים לַחַיָּה וְלַבְּהֵמָה, וְטָעוּן שְׁחִיטָה כָּזֶה וְכָזֶה, וּמְטַמֵּא מִשּׁוּם נְבֵלָה וּמִשּׁוּם אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי כָּזֶה וְכָזֶה
phrases.en: In all other ways it is like a behemah and a hayyah: It requires slaughtering (shehitah) like them both; It carries carrion impurity; And to it applies the law relating to a limb of a living being like them both.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד מַפְרִישִׁין הַבִּכּוּרִים. יוֹרֵד אָדָם בְּתוֹךְ שָׂדֵהוּ וְרוֹאֶה תְּאֵנָה שֶׁבִּכְּרָה, אֶשְׁכּוֹל שֶׁבִּכֵּר, רִמּוֹן שֶׁבִּכֵּר, קוֹשְׁרוֹ בְגֶמִי, וְאוֹמֵר, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ בִּכּוּרִים.
phrases.en: How does one set aside bikkurim? A man goes down into his field, he sees a fig that ripened, or a cluster of grapes that ripened, or a pomegranate that ripened, he ties a reed-rope around it and says: “Let these be bikkurim.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן חוֹזֵר וְקוֹרֵא אוֹתָם בִּכּוּרִים מֵאַחַר שֶׁיִּתָּלְשׁוּ מִן הַקַּרְקָע:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: even so, he must again designate them as bikkurim after they have been plucked from the soil.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד מַעֲלִין אֶת הַבִּכּוּרִים.
phrases.en: How were the bikkurim taken up [to Jerusalem]? All [the inhabitants of] the cities of the maamad would assemble in the city of the maamad, and they would spend the night in the open street and they would not entering any of the houses.

phrases.he: כָּל הָעֲיָרוֹת שֶׁבַּמַּעֲמָד מִתְכַּנְּסוֹת לָעִיר שֶׁל מַעֲמָד, וְלָנִין בִּרְחוֹבָהּ שֶׁל עִיר, וְלֹא הָיוּ נִכְנָסִין לַבָּתִּים.
phrases.en: Early in the morning the officer would say: “Let us arise and go up to Zion, into the house of the Lord our God” (Jeremiah 31:5).

phrases.he: וְלַמַּשְׁכִּים, הָיָה הַמְמֻנֶּה אוֹמֵר (ירמיה לא), קוּמוּ וְנַעֲלֶה צִיּוֹן אֶל בֵּית ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ
הַקְּרוֹבִים מְבִיאִים הַתְּאֵנִים וְהָעֲנָבִים, וְהָרְחוֹקִים מְבִיאִים גְּרוֹגָרוֹת וְצִמּוּקִים.
phrases.en: Those who lived near [Jerusalem] would bring fresh figs and grapes, while those who lived far away would bring dried figs and raisins.

phrases.he: וְהַשּׁוֹר הוֹלֵךְ לִפְנֵיהֶם, וְקַרְנָיו מְצֻפּוֹת זָהָב, וַעֲטֶרֶת שֶׁל זַיִת בְּרֹאשׁוֹ.
phrases.en: An ox would go in front of them, his horns bedecked with gold and with an olive-crown on its head.

phrases.he: הֶחָלִיל מַכֶּה לִפְנֵיהֶם, עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעִים קָרוֹב לִירוּשָׁלָיִם.
phrases.en: The flute would play before them until they would draw close to Jerusalem.

phrases.he: הִגִּיעוּ קָרוֹב לִירוּשָׁלַיִם, שָׁלְחוּ לִפְנֵיהֶם, וְעִטְּרוּ אֶת בִּכּוּרֵיהֶם.
phrases.en: When they drew close to Jerusalem they would send messengers in advance, and they would adorn their bikkurim.

phrases.he: הַפַּחוֹת, הַסְּגָנִים וְהַגִּזְבָּרִים יוֹצְאִים לִקְרָאתָם.
phrases.en: The governors and chiefs and treasurers [of the Temple] would go out to greet them, and according to the rank of the entrants they would go forth.

phrases.he: לְפִי כְבוֹד הַנִּכְנָסִים הָיוּ יוֹצְאִים.
phrases.en: All the skilled artisans of Jerusalem would stand up before them and greet them saying, “Our brothers, men of such and such a place, we welcome you in peace.

phrases.he: וְכָל בַּעֲלֵי אֻמָּנִיּוֹת שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם עוֹמְדִים לִפְנֵיהֶם וְשׁוֹאֲלִין בִּשְׁלוֹמָם, אַחֵינוּ אַנְשֵׁי הַמָּקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי, בָּאתֶם לְשָׁלוֹם
הֶחָלִיל מַכֶּה לִפְנֵיהֶם עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעִין לְהַר הַבָּיִת.
phrases.en: The flute would play before them, until they reached the Temple Mount.

phrases.he: הִגִּיעוּ לְהַר הַבַּיִת, אֲפִלּוּ אַגְרִיפַּס הַמֶּלֶךְ נוֹטֵל הַסַּל עַל כְּתֵפוֹ וְנִכְנָס, עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לָעֲזָרָה.
phrases.en: When they reached the Temple Mount even King Agrippas would take the basket and place it on his shoulder and walk as far as the Temple Court.

phrases.he: הִגִּיעַ לָעֲזָרָה וְדִבְּרוּ הַלְוִיִּם בַּשִּׁיר, אֲרוֹמִמְךָ ה' כִּי דִלִּיתָנִי וְלֹא שִׂמַּחְתָּ אֹיְבַי לִי (תהלים ל)
phrases.en: When he got to the Temple Court, the Levites would sing the song: “I will extol You, O Lord, for You have raised me up, and You have not let my enemies rejoice over me” (Psalms 30:2).

phrases.he: הַגּוֹזָלוֹת שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי הַסַּלִּים, הָיוּ עוֹלוֹת.
phrases.en: The birds [tied to] the basket were [offered] as whole burnt-offerings, and those which they held in their hands they gave to the priests.

phrases.he: וּמַה שֶּׁבְּיָדָם, נוֹתְנִים לַכֹּהֲנִים
עוֹדֵהוּ הַסַּל עַל כְּתֵפוֹ, קוֹרֵא מֵהִגַּדְתִּי הַיּוֹם לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ (דברים כו), עַד שֶׁגּוֹמֵר כָּל הַפָּרָשָׁה.
phrases.en: While the basket was still on his shoulder he recites from: "I acknowledge this day before the LORD your God that I have entered the land that the LORD swore to our fathers to assign us” (Deuteronomy 26:3) until he completes the passage.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר עַד אֲרַמִּי אֹבֵד אָבִי.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah said: until [he reaches] “My father was a fugitive Aramean” (v.

phrases.he: הִגִּיעַ לַאֲרַמִּי אֹבֵד אָבִי, מוֹרִיד הַסַּל מֵעַל כְּתֵפוֹ וְאוֹחֲזוֹ בְשִׂפְתוֹתָיו, וְכֹהֵן מַנִּיחַ יָדוֹ תַחְתָּיו וּמְנִיפוֹ, וְקוֹרֵא מֵאֲרַמִּי אֹבֵד אָבִי עַד שֶׁהוּא גוֹמֵר כָּל הַפָּרָשָׁה, וּמַנִּיחוֹ בְּצַד הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוָה וְיָצָא
phrases.en: When he reaches, “My father was a fugitive Aramean”, he takes the basket off his shoulder and holds it by its edges, and the priest places his hand beneath it and waves it. He then recites from “My father was a fugitive Aramean” until he completes the entire passage. He then deposits the basket by the side of the altar, bow and depart.

phrases.he: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה, כָּל מִי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ לִקְרוֹת, קוֹרֵא.
phrases.en: Originally all who knew how to recite would recite while those who did not know how to recite, others would read it for them [and they would repeat the words].

phrases.he: וְכָל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ לִקְרוֹת, מַקְרִין אוֹתוֹ.
phrases.en: But when they refrained from bringing, they decreed that they should read the words to both those who could and those who could not [recite so that they could repeat after them].

phrases.he: נִמְנְעוּ מִלְּהָבִיא, הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהוּ מַקְרִין אֶת מִי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ וְאֶת מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ
הָעֲשִׁירִים מְבִיאִים בִּכּוּרֵיהֶם בִּקְלָתוֹת שֶׁל כֶּסֶף וְשֶׁל זָהָב, וְהָעֲנִיִּים מְבִיאִין אוֹתָם בְּסַלֵּי נְצָרִים שֶׁל עֲרָבָה קְלוּפָה, וְהַסַּלִּים וְהַבִּכּוּרִים נִתָּנִין לַכֹּהֲנִים:
phrases.en: The rich would bring their bikkurim in baskets overlaid with silver or gold, while the poor used wicker-baskets of peeled willow-branches, and the baskets and the bikkurim were given to the priest.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן נַנָּס אוֹמֵר, מְעַטְּרִין אֶת הַבִּכּוּרִים חוּץ מִשִּׁבְעַת הַמִּינִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Nanas says: they would decorate the bikkurim [with produce] other than the seven species.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אֵין מְעַטְּרִין אֶת הַבִּכּוּרִים אֶלָּא מִשִּׁבְעַת הַמִּינִים:
phrases.en: But Rabbi Akiva says: they may decorate only with produce of the seven kinds.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, שָׁלֹשׁ מִדּוֹת בַּבִּכּוּרִים, הַבִּכּוּרִים, וְתוֹסֶפֶת הַבִּכּוּרִים, וְעִטּוּר הַבִּכּוּרִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: there are three elements in bikkurim: the bikkurim, the additions to the bikkurim, and the ornamentations of the bikkurim.

phrases.he: תּוֹסֶפֶת הַבִּכּוּרִים, מִין בְּמִינוֹ.
phrases.en: The additions to the bikkurim must be of a like kind; But the ornamentations can be of a different kind.

phrases.he: וְעִטּוּר הַבִּכּוּרִים, מִין בְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ.
phrases.en: The additions to the bikkurim can only be eaten in purity, and are exempt from demai.

phrases.he: תּוֹסֶפֶת הַבִּכּוּרִים נֶאֱכֶלֶת בְּטָהֳרָה, וּפְטוּרָה מִן הַדְּמַאי.
phrases.en: But the ornamentations of the bikkurim are subject to demai.

phrases.he: וְעִטּוּר הַבִּכּוּרִים חַיָּב בַּדְּמַאי
אֵימָתַי אָמְרוּ תּוֹסֶפֶת הַבִּכּוּרִים כַּבִּכּוּרִים, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִיא בָאָה מִן הָאָרֶץ.
phrases.en: When did they say that the additions to the bikkurim are like bikkurim [themselves]? When they come from the land [of Israel]; but if they do not come from the land, they were not regarded as bikkurim [themselves].

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינָהּ בָּאָה מִן הָאָרֶץ, אֵינָהּ כַּבִּכּוּרִים
לְמָה אָמְרוּ הַבִּכּוּרִים כְּנִכְסֵי כֹהֵן, שֶׁהוּא קוֹנֶה מֵהֶם עֲבָדִים וְקַרְקָעוֹת וּבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה, וּבַעַל חוֹב נוֹטְלָן בְּחוֹבוֹ, וְהָאִשָּׁה בִכְתֻבָּתָהּ, כְּסֵפֶר תּוֹרָה.
phrases.en: In what respect did they say that bikkurim are the property of the priest? In that he can purchase with bikkurim slaves and land and unclean beasts, and a creditor [of his] may take them for his debt, and his wife for her ketubah. As may be done with a Torah scroll.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֵין נוֹתְנִים אוֹתָם אֶלָּא לְחָבֵר בְּטוֹבָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: bikkurim may be given only to [a priest that is] a haver (an associate) and as a favor.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, נוֹתְנִין אוֹתָם לְאַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר, וְהֵם מְחַלְּקִין בֵּינֵיהֶם, כְּקָדְשֵׁי הַמִּקְדָּשׁ:
phrases.en: But the sages say: they are given to the men of the mishmar, and they divide them among themselves as [they do] with all other consecrated objects.

phrases.he: אַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס יֵשׁ בּוֹ דְּרָכִים שָׁוֶה לַאֲנָשִׁים, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ דְּרָכִים שָׁוֶה לַנָּשִׁים, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ דְּרָכִים שָׁוֶה לַאֲנָשִׁים וְנָשִׁים, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ דְּרָכִים אֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה לֹא לַאֲנָשִׁים וְלֹא לַנָּשִׁים:
phrases.en: The hermaphrodite is in some ways like men, and in other ways like women. In other ways he is like men and women, and in others he is like neither men nor women.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד שָׁוֶה לַאֲנָשִׁים: מְטַמֵּא בְּלֹבֶן כַּאֲנָשִׁים, וְזוֹקֵק לְיִבּוּם כַּאֲנָשִׁים, וּמִתְעַטֵּף וּמִסְתַּפֵּר כַּאֲנָשִׁים, וְנוֹשֵׂא אֲבָל לֹא נִשָּׂא כַּאֲנָשִׁים, וְחַיָּב בְּכָל מִצְוֹת הָאֲמוּרוֹת בַּתּוֹרָה כַּאֲנָשִׁים:
phrases.en: In what ways is he like men? He causes impurity with white discharge, like men; He dresses like men; He can take a wife but not be taken as a wife, like men. [When he is born] his mother counts the blood of purification, like men; He may not be secluded with women, like men. He is not maintained with the daughters, like men; He transgresses the law of: “You shall not round” (Leviticus 19:2 and “You shall not defile for the dead,” (Leviticus 21:1) like men; And he must perform all the commandments of the Torah, like men.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד שָׁוֶה לַנָּשִׁים: מְטַמֵּא בְּאֹדֶם כַּנָּשִׁים, וְאֵינוֹ מִתְיַחֵד עִם הָאֲנָשִׁים כַּנָּשִׁים, וְאֵינוֹ עוֹבֵר עַל "בַּל תַּקִּיף" וְלֹא עַל "בַּל תַּשְׁחִית" וְלֹא עַל "בַּל תְּטַמֵּא לַמֵּתִים" כַּנָּשִׁים, וּפָסוּל מִן הָעֵדוּת כַּנָּשִׁים, וְאֵינוֹ נִבְעַל בַּעֲבֵירָה כַּנָּשִׁים, וְנִפְסַל מִן הַכְּהֻנָּה כַּנָּשִׁים:
phrases.en: And in what ways is he like women? He causes impurity with red discharge, like women; And he must not be secluded with men, like women; And he doesn’t make his brother’s wife liable for yibbum (levirate marriage); And he does not share [in the inheritance] with the sons, like women; And he cannot eat most holy sacrifices, like women. At his birth his mother counts the blood of her impurity like [they do when they give birth to a] girl; And he is disqualified from being a witness, like women. If he had illicit intercourse, he is disqualified from eating terumah, like women.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד שָׁוֶה לַאֲנָשִׁים וְלַנָּשִׁים: חַיָּבִים עַל מַכָּתוֹ וְעַל קִלְלָתוֹ כַּאֲנָשִׁים וְכַנָּשִׁים, וְהַהוֹרְגוֹ שׁוֹגֵג גּוֹלֶה וּמֵזִיד נֶהֱרַג כַּאֲנָשִׁים וְנָשִׁים, וְיוֹשֶׁבֶת עָלָיו דָּם טָמֵא וְדָם טָהוֹר כַּאֲנָשִׁים וְכַנָּשִׁים, וְחוֹלֵק בְּקָדְשֵׁי קֳדָשִׁים כַּאֲנָשִׁים וְכַנָּשִׁים, וְנוֹחֵל לְכָל הַנְּחָלוֹת כַּאֲנָשִׁים וְכַנָּשִׁים, וְאִם אָמַר "הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר שֶׁזֶּה אִישׁ וְאִשָּׁה" הֲרֵי זֶה נָזִיר:
phrases.en: In what ways is he like both men and women? One who strikes him or curses him is liable, as in the case of men and women; One who unwittingly kills him must go into exile, and if on purpose, then [the slayer] receives the death penalty, as in the case of men and women. His mother must [at his birth] bring an offering, as in the case of men and women. He may eat holy things that are eaten outside of the Temple; And he may inherit any inheritance, as in the case of men and women.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד אֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה לֹא לַאֲנָשִׁים וְלֹא לַנָּשִׁים: אֵין חַיָּבִים לֹא עַל מַכָּתוֹ וְלֹא עַל קִלְלָתוֹ לֹא כַּאֲנָשִׁים וְלֹא כַּנָּשִׁים, וְאֵינוֹ נֶעֱרָךְ לֹא כַּאֲנָשִׁים וְלֹא כַּנָּשִׁים, וְאִם אָמַר "הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר שֶׁזֶּה לֹא אִישׁ וְלֹא אִשָּׁה" אֵינוֹ נָזִיר.
phrases.en: And in what is he different from both men and women? One does not burn terumah if it came into contact with his discharge, Neither is he liable for entering the temple while impure, unlike men or women. He must not be sold as a Hebrew slave, unlike men or women. He cannot be evaluated, unlike men or women.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס בְּרִיָּה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ הוּא וְלֹא יָכְלוּ חֲכָמִים לְהַכְרִיעַ עָלָיו אִם הוּא אִישׁ אוֹ אִשָּׁה.
phrases.en: If one says: “I will be a nazirite, if he is neither a man nor a woman,” then he becomes a nazirite. Rabbi Yose says: the hermaphrodite is a unique creature, and the sages could not decide about him.

phrases.he: אֲבָל טֻמְטוּם אֵינוֹ כֵּן, פְּעָמִים שֶׁהוּא אִישׁ פְּעָמִים שֶׁהוּא אִשָּׁה
phrases.en: But this is not so with a tumtum (one of doubtful), for sometimes he is a man and sometimes he is a woman.

phrases.he: יְצִיאוֹת הַשַּׁבָּת שְׁתַּיִם שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע בִּפְנִים, וּשְׁתַּיִם שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע בַּחוּץ.
phrases.en: The acts of carrying out from a public domain into a private domain or vice versa, which are prohibited on Shabbat, are primarily two basic actions that comprise four cases from the perspective of a person inside a private domain, and two basic actions that comprise four cases from the perspective of a person outside, in a public domain.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: How do these eight cases take place?

phrases.he: הֶעָנִי עוֹמֵד בַּחוּץ וּבַעַל הַבַּיִת בִּפְנִים, פָּשַׁט הֶעָנִי אֶת יָדוֹ לִפְנִים וְנָתַן לְתוֹךְ יָדוֹ שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת, אוֹ שֶׁנָּטַל מִתּוֹכָהּ וְהוֹצִיא, הֶעָנִי חַיָּב וּבַעַל הַבַּיִת פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: The poor person stands outside, in the public domain, and the homeowner stands inside, in the private domain. The poor person lifted an object in the public domain, extended his hand into the private domain, and placed the object into the hand of the homeowner. Or, the poor person reached his hand into the private domain, took an item from the hand of the homeowner, and carried it out into the public domain. In both of these cases, because the poor person performed the prohibited labor in its entirety, he is liable and the homeowner is exempt.

phrases.he: פָּשַׁט בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אֶת יָדוֹ לַחוּץ וְנָתַן לְתוֹךְ יָדוֹ שֶׁל עָנִי, אוֹ שֶׁנָּטַל מִתּוֹכָהּ וְהִכְנִיס, בַּעַל הַבַּיִת חַיָּב וְהֶעָנִי פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: The homeowner lifted an item in the private domain, extended his hand into the public domain, and placed the object into the hand of the poor person. Or, the homeowner reached his hand into the public domain, took an object from the hand of the poor person, and carried it into the private domain. In both of those cases, because the homeowner performed the prohibited labor in its entirety, he is liable and the poor person is exempt.

phrases.he: פָּשַׁט הֶעָנִי אֶת יָדוֹ לִפְנִים וְנָטַל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת מִתּוֹכָהּ, אוֹ שֶׁנָּתַן לְתוֹכָהּ וְהוֹצִיא, שְׁנֵיהֶם פְּטוּרִין.
phrases.en: The poor person extended his hand into the private domain and either the homeowner took an object from his hand and placed it in the private domain or the homeowner placed an object into the hand of the poor person, and the poor person carried the object out into the public domain. In those cases and the two that follow, the act of transferring the object from one domain to another was performed jointly by two people, the poor person and the homeowner. Because each performed only part of the prohibited labor, both of them are exempt.

phrases.he: פָּשַׁט בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אֶת יָדוֹ לַחוּץ וְנָטַל הֶעָנִי מִתּוֹכָהּ, אוֹ שֶׁנָּתַן לְתוֹכָהּ וְהִכְנִיס, שְׁנֵיהֶם פְּטוּרִין.
phrases.en: So too, in a case where the homeowner extended his hand into the public domain and, either the poor person took an object from the homeowner's hand and placed it in the public domain or the poor person placed an object into the homeowner's hand and the homeowner carried the object into the private domain. Because each performed only part of the prohibited labor, both of them are exempt.

phrases.he: לֹא יֵשֵׁב אָדָם לִפְנֵי הַסַּפָּר סָמוּךְ לַמִּנְחָה, עַד שֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל.
phrases.en: A person may not sit before the barber adjacent to the time of minḥa until he recites the afternoon prayer.

phrases.he: לֹא יִכָּנֵס אָדָם לַמֶּרְחָץ וְלֹא לַבֻּרְסְקִי וְלֹא לֶאֱכֹל וְלֹא לָדִין.
phrases.en: And a person may not enter the bathhouse and may not to work in a tannery [burseki]. And he may neither begin to eat a meal nor to sit in judgment until he prays.

phrases.he: וְאִם הִתְחִילוּ, אֵין מַפְסִיקִין.
phrases.en: And however, if they already began engaging in those activities, they need not stop and recite the Amida prayer.

phrases.he: מַפְסִיקִים לִקְרוֹת קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, וְאֵין מַפְסִיקִים לַתְּפִלָּה.
phrases.en: One stops engaging in all of these activities to recite Shema and one does not stop to recite the Amida prayer.

phrases.he: לֹא יֵצֵא הַחַיָּט בְּמַחְטוֹ סָמוּךְ לַחֲשֵׁכָה, שֶׁמָּא יִשְׁכַּח וְיֵצֵא.
phrases.en: The tailor may not go out with his needle adjacent to nightfall on Shabbat eve, lest he forget that he is carrying the needle and go out with it to the public domain even after Shabbat begins.

phrases.he: וְלֹא הַלַּבְלָר בְּקֻלְמוֹסוֹ.
phrases.en: And, similarly, the scribe [lavlar] may not go out with his quill [kulmos] for the same reason.

phrases.he: וְלֹא יְפַלֶּה אֶת כֵּלָיו, וְלֹא יִקְרָא לְאוֹר הַנֵּר.
phrases.en: And one may not shake his clothes on Shabbat to rid them of lice; and one may not read a book by candlelight, so that he will not come to adjust the wick of the lamp.

phrases.he: בֶּאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ, הַחַזָּן רוֹאֶה הֵיכָן תִּינוֹקוֹת קוֹרְאִים, אֲבָל הוּא לֹא יִקְרָא.
phrases.en: However, in truth they said an established halakha: The attendant sees where in the book the children under his supervision are reading in the Torah, even by candlelight on Shabbat. However, he himself may not read.

phrases.he: כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ, לֹא יֹאכַל הַזָּב עִם הַזָּבָה, מִפְּנֵי הֶרְגֵּל עֲבֵרָה:
phrases.en: Similarly, the zav may not eat even with his wife the zava, despite the fact that they are both ritually impure, because, by eating together, they will come to excessive intimacy and become accustomed to sin.

phrases.he: וְאֵלּוּ מִן הַהֲלָכוֹת שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַעֲלִיַּת חֲנַנְיָה בֶן חִזְקִיָּה בֶן גֻּרְיוֹן כְּשֶׁעָלוּ לְבַקְּרוֹ.
phrases.en: And these are among the halakhot that the Sages, who went up to visit him, said in the upper story of Ḥananya ben Ḥizkiya ben Garon.

phrases.he: נִמְנוּ וְרַבּוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי עַל בֵּית הִלֵּל, וּשְׁמֹנָה עָשָׂר דְּבָרִים גָּזְרוּ בוֹ בַיּוֹם:
phrases.en: When the people expressing opinions were counted, Beit Shammai outnumbered Beit Hillel, and they issued decrees with regard to eighteen matters on that day.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אֵין שׁוֹרִין דְּיוֹ וְסַמְמָנִים וְכַרְשִׁינִים, אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּשּׁוֹרוּ מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One may only soak dry ink in water and dry plants, which produce dyes, in water and vetch for animal food to soften them in water on Shabbat eve, adjacent to Shabbat, if there is clearly sufficient time for them to soak for their designated purpose while it is still day, before Shabbat begins, and their continued soaking on Shabbat will have no effect.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין:
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel permit doing so.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אֵין נוֹתְנִין אוּנִין שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן לְתוֹךְ הַתַּנּוּר, אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּהְבִּילוּ מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One may only place bundles of combed flax inside the oven on Shabbat eve if there is sufficient time so that they will be heated while it is still day.

phrases.he: וְלֹא אֶת הַצֶּמֶר לַיּוֹרָה, אֶלָּא כְדֵי שֶׁיִּקְלֹط הָעַיִן.
phrases.en: And one may only place wool into the dyer's kettle if there is sufficient time for the wool to absorb the dye while it is still day.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין.
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel permit doing so.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אֵין פּוֹרְשִׂין מְצוּדוֹת חַיָּה וְעוֹפוֹת וְדָגִים, אֶלָּא כְדֵי שֶׁיִּצּוֹדוּ מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One may spread traps for an animal and birds and fish only if there is sufficient time remaining in the day for them to be trapped in them while it is still day,

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין.
phrases.en: and Beit Hillel permit doing so even if there is not sufficient time remaining in the day.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אֵין מוֹכְרִים לַנָּכְרִי
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One may only sell to a gentile

phrases.he: וְאֵין טוֹעֲנִים עִמּוֹ
phrases.en: and one may only load a burden on his donkey with him

phrases.he: וְאֵין מַגְבִּיהִים עָלָיו, אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ לְמָקוֹם קָרוֹב.
phrases.en: and one may only lift a burden on him if there remains sufficient time for the gentile to arrive to a near place

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין:
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel permit doing so

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אֵין נוֹתְנִין עוֹרוֹת לְעַבְּדָן וְלֹא כֵלִים לְכוֹבֵס נָכְרִי,
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One may not give skins to a gentile tanner, nor clothes to a gentile launderer,

phrases.he: אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּעָשׂוּ מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם.
phrases.en: unless there is sufficient time for work on them to be completed while it is still day,

phrases.he: וּבְכֻלָּן בֵּית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין עִם הַשָּׁמֶשׁ:
phrases.en: And in all of them Beit Hillel permit doing so with the sun,

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:

phrases.he: נוֹהֲגִין הָיוּ בֵּית אַבָּא שֶׁהָיוּ נוֹתְנִין כְּלֵי לָבָן לְכוֹבֵס נָכְרִי שְׁלשָׁה יָמִים קֹדֶם לַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.en: The ancestral house of my father was accustomed to give its white clothes to a gentile launderer three days before Shabbat.

phrases.he: וְשָׁוִין אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ, שֶׁטּוֹעֲנִין קוֹרוֹת בֵּית הַבַּד וְעִגּוּלֵי הַגָּת:
phrases.en: And these and those agree that one may load the beam of the olive press and the circular wine press.

phrases.he: אֵין צוֹלִין בָּשָׂר, בָּצָל, וּבֵיצָה, אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּצּוֹלוּ מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם.
phrases.en: One may only roast meat, an onion, or an egg if there remains sufficient time so that they could be roasted while it is still day.

phrases.he: אֵין נוֹתְנִין פַּת לַתַּנּוּר עִם חֲשֵׁכָה, וְלֹא חֲרָרָה עַל גַּבֵּי גֶחָלִים, אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּקְרְמוּ פָנֶיהָ מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם.
phrases.en: One may only place dough to bake into bread in the oven at nightfall, and may only place a cake on the coals, if there is time enough that the surface of this cake or bread will form a crust while it is still day.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּקְרֹם הַתַּחְתּוֹן שֶׁלָּהּ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: Enough time so that its bottom crust should harden,

phrases.he: מְשַׁלְשְׁלִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח בַּתַּנּוּר עִם חֲשֵׁכָה.
phrases.en: one may, ab initio, lower the Paschal lamb into the oven on Shabbat eve at nightfall

phrases.he: וּמַאֲחִיזִין אֶת הָאוּר בִּמְדוּרַת בֵּית הַמּוֹקֵד.
phrases.en: And one may, ab initio, kindle the fire in the bonfire of the Chamber of the Hearth in the Temple on Shabbat eve

phrases.he: וּבַגְּבוּלִין, כְּדֵי שֶׁיֶּאֱחֹז הָאוּר בְּרֻבָּן.
phrases.en: And, however, in the outlying areas, it is prohibited to light a bonfire on Shabbat eve, unless there is sufficient time for the fire to take hold in most of the bonfire, while it is still day

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בְּפֶחָמִין, כָּל שֶׁהוּא:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: With a bonfire of coals, even in the outlying areas one is permitted to light the fire on Shabbat eve at nightfall, even if the fire only spread to any amount of the bonfire

phrases.he: בַּמֶּה מַדְלִיקִין וּבַמָּה אֵין מַדְלִיקִין.
phrases.en: With what may one light the Shabbat lamp, and with what may one not light it?

phrases.he: אֵין מַדְלִיקִין לֹא בְלֶכֶשׁ, וְלֹא בְחֹסֶן, וְלֹא בְכָלָךְ, וְלֹא בִפְתִילַת הָאִידָן, וְלֹא בִפְתִילַת הַמִּדְבָּר, וְלֹא בִירוֹקָה שֶׁעַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם.
phrases.en: With regard to types of prohibited wicks, one may light neither with cedar bast [lekhesh], nor with uncombed flax [ḥosen], nor with raw silk [kalakh], nor with willow bast [petilat ha'idan], nor with desert weed [petilat hamidbar], nor with green moss that is on the surface of the water.

phrases.he: וְלֹא בְזֶפֶת, וְלֹא בְשַׁעֲוָה, וְלֹא בְשֶׁמֶן קִיק, וְלֹא בְשֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵפָה, וְלֹא בְאַלְיָה, וְלֹא בְחֵלֶב.
phrases.en: With regard to types of prohibited oils, one may light neither with pitch [zefet], nor with wax [sha'ava], nor with castor oil [shemen kik], nor with burnt oil [shemen sereifa], nor with fat from a sheep's tail [alya], nor with tallow [ḥelev].

phrases.he: נַחוּם הַמָּדִי אוֹמֵר, מַדְלִיקִין בְּחֵלֶב מְבֻשָּׁל.
phrases.en: Naḥum the Mede says: One may light with boiled tallow.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֶחָד מְבֻשָּׁל וְאֶחָד שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְבֻשָּׁל, אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בּוֹ.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: Both tallow that was boiled and tallow that was not boiled, one may not light with them.

phrases.he: אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בְּשֶׁמֶן שְׂרֵפָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.en: one may not light with burnt oil on a Festival

phrases.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בְּעִטְרָן, מִפְּנֵי כְבוֹד הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yishmael says that one may not light with tar [itran] in deference to Shabbat

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים מַתִּירִין בְּכָל הַשְּׁמָנִים, בְּשֶׁמֶן שֻׁמְשְׁמִין, בְּשֶׁמֶן אֱגוֹזִים, בְּשֶׁמֶן צְנוֹנוֹת, בְּשֶׁמֶן דָּגִים, בְּשֶׁמֶן פַּקּוּעוֹת, בְּעִטְרָן וּבְנֵפְט.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis permit lighting with all oils for lamps; with sesame oil, with nut oil, with turnip oil, with fish oil, with gourd oil, with tar, and even with naphtha [neft]

phrases.he: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר, אֵין מַדְלִיקִין אֶלָּא בְשֶׁמֶן זַיִת בִּלְבָד:
phrases.en: Rabbi Tarfon says: One may light only with olive oil

phrases.he: כָּל הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הָעֵץ אֵין מַדְלִיקִין בּוֹ אֶלָּא פִשְׁתָּן.
phrases.en: All substances that emerge from the tree, one may light only with flax

phrases.he: וְכָל הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הָעֵץ אֵינוֹ מִטַּמֵּא טֻמְאַת אֹהָלִים אֶלָּא פִשְׁתָּן.
phrases.en: And all substances that emerge from the tree, the only substance that becomes ritually impure with impurity transmitted by tents over a corpse is flax.

phrases.he: פְּתִילַת הַבֶּגֶד שֶׁקִּפְּלָהּ וְלֹא הִבְהֲבָהּ, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, טְמֵאָה, וְאֵין מַדְלִיקִין בָּהּ.
phrases.en: The wick of a garment that one folded it but did not singe it, Rabbi Eliezer says: This wick is ritually impure and one may not light with it

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, טְהוֹרָה, וּמַדְלִיקִין בָּהּ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: It is ritually pure and one may light with it

phrases.he: לֹא יִקֹּב אָדָם שְׁפוֹפֶרֶת שֶׁל בֵּיצָה וִימַלְאֶנָּה שֶׁמֶן וְיִתְּנֶנָּה עַל פִּי הַנֵּר בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁתְּהֵא מְנַטֶּפֶת.
phrases.en: A person may not pierce a hole in an eggshell and fill it with oil, and place it over the mouth of a lamp so that the egg will drip additional oil into the lamp and thereby extend the time that it burns.

phrases.he: אֲפִלּוּ הִיא שֶׁל חֶרֶס.
phrases.en: And this is the ruling even if it is not an actual egg but an earthenware vessel.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר.
phrases.en: And Rabbi Yehuda permits doing so.

phrases.he: אֲבָל אִם חִבְּרָהּ הַיּוֹצֵר מִתְּחִלָּה, מֻתָּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא כְלִי אֶחָד.
phrases.en: However, if the craftsman, who crafts ceramic vessels, attached the egg to the lamp from the outset, one is permitted to fill it with oil because it constitutes a single, large vessel.

phrases.he: לֹא יְמַלֵּא אָדָם אֶת הַקְּעָרָה שֶׁמֶן וְיִתְּנֶנָּה בְצַד הַנֵּר וְיִתֵּן רֹאשׁ הַפְּתִילָה בְתוֹכָהּ, בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁתְּהֵא שׁוֹאֶבֶת.
phrases.en: The Rabbis decreed that a person may not fill a bowl with oil, and place it beside the lamp, and place the unlit head of the wick into the bowl so that it draws additional oil from the bowl and thereby extend the time that the lamp burns.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר.
phrases.en: And Rabbi Yehuda permits doing so.

phrases.he: הַמְכַבֶּה אֶת הַנֵּר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מִתְיָרֵא מִפְּנֵי גוֹיִם, מִפְּנֵי לִסְטִים, מִפְּנֵי רוּחַ רָעָה,
phrases.en: One who extinguishes the lamp because he is afraid due to gentiles, and due to thieves, or due to an evil spirit,

phrases.he: וְאִם בִּשְׁבִיל הַחוֹלֶה שֶׁיִּישַׁן, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: or if he extinguished the flame due to the sick person so that he will sleep, he is exempt.

phrases.he: כְּחָס עַל הַנֵּר, כְּחָס עַל הַשֶּׁמֶן, כְּחָס עַל הַפְּתִילָה, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: However, in a case where he extinguishes the flame in order to spare the lamp, spare the oil, or spare the wick, he is liable.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי פּוֹטֵר בְּכֻלָּן חוּץ מִן הַפְּתִילָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא עוֹשָׂהּ פֶּחָם:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei exempts him in all of those cases, except for the case where he seeks to spare the wick. Only in that case is extinguishing a creative action because he makes the wick into charcoal by extinguishing the flame.

phrases.he: עַל שָׁלשׁ עֲבֵרוֹת נָשִׁים מֵתוֹת בִּשְׁעַת לֵדָתָן,
phrases.en: For three transgressions women die during childbirth:

phrases.he: עַל שֶׁאֵינָן זְהִירוֹת בַּנִּדָּה וּבַחַלָּה וּבְהַדְלָקַת הַנֵּר:
phrases.en: For that they are not careful in a menstruating woman, and in ḥalla and in lighting the lamp.

phrases.he: שְׁלשָׁה דְבָרִים צָרִיךְ אָדָם לוֹמַר בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת עִם חֲשֵׁכָה.
phrases.en: three things a person must say in his home on Shabbat eve at nightfall
have you tithed

phrases.he: עֵרַבְתֶּם.
phrases.en: Have you placed the eiruv

phrases.he: הַדְלִיקוּ אֶת הַנֵּר.
phrases.en: light the lamp

phrases.he: סָפֵק חֲשֵׁכָה סָפֵק אֵין חֲשֵׁכָה, אֵין מְעַשְּׂרִין אֶת הַוַּדַּאי, וְאֵין מַטְבִּילִין אֶת הַכֵּלִים, וְאֵין מַדְלִיקִין אֶת הַנֵּרוֹת,
phrases.en: If the time arrives on Friday when there is uncertainty whether it is nightfall and uncertainty whether it is not yet nightfall, one may not tithe the crop that has definitely not been tithed, and one may not immerse ritually impure vessels in a ritual bath to render them ritually pure, and one may not light the Shabbat lights.

phrases.he: אֲבָל מְעַשְּׂרִין אֶת הַדְּמַאי, וּמְעָרְבִין, וְטוֹמְנִין אֶת הַחַמִּין:
phrases.en: However, one may tithe demai, doubtfully tithed produce, which must be tithed due to mere suspicion. And one may place an eiruv and insulate the hot water

phrases.he: כִּירָה שֶׁהִסִּיקוּהָ בְקַשׁ וּבִגְבָבָא, נוֹתְנִים עָלֶיהָ תַּבְשִׁיל.
phrases.en: a stove that was lit with straw or with rakings, one may place a pot of cooked food atop it

phrases.he: בְּגֶפֶת וּבְעֵצִים, לֹא יִתֵּן עַד שֶׁיִּגְרֹף, אוֹ עַד שֶׁיִּתֵּן אֶת הָאֵפֶר.
phrases.en: with pomace, and if it was lit with wood, one may not place a pot atop it until he sweeps the coals from the stove while it is still day or until he places ashes on the coals

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, חַמִּין אֲבָל לֹא תַבְשִׁיל.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: hot water but not cooked food

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, חַמִּין וְתַבְשִׁיל.
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: hot water and cooked food

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, נוֹטְלִין אֲבָל לֹא מַחֲזִירִין.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One may remove but may not return it

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, אַף מַחֲזִירִין:
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: One may even return it

phrases.he: תַּנּוּר שֶׁהִסִּיקוּהוּ בְקַשׁ וּבַגְּבָבָא, לֹא יִתֵּן בֵּין מִתּוֹכוֹ בֵּין מֵעַל גַּבָּיו.
phrases.en: An oven that they lit even with straw or rakings, one may neither place a pot inside it nor atop it

phrases.he: כֻּפָּח שֶׁהִסִּיקוּהוּ בְקַשׁ וּבִגְבָבָא, הֲרֵי זֶה כְכִירַיִם, בְּגֶפֶת וּבְעֵצִים, הֲרֵי הוּא כְתַנּוּר:
phrases.en: A kupaḥ that was lit with straw or rakings, its legal status is like that of a stove. If it were lit with pomace or with wood, its legal status is like that of an oven

phrases.he: אֵין נוֹתְנִין בֵּיצָה בְצַד הַמֵּחַם בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁתִּתְגַּלְגֵּל.
phrases.en: One may not place a raw egg next to an urn full of hot water so that it will roast slightly.

phrases.he: וְלֹא יַפְקִיעֶנָּה בְסוּדָרִין.
phrases.en: And one may not even wrap it in cloths.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר.
phrases.en: And Rabbi Yosei permits doing so in that case.

phrases.he: וְלֹא יַטְמִינֶנָּה בְחֹל וּבַאֲבַק דְּרָכִים בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁתִּצָּלֶה:
phrases.en: And, similarly, one may not insulate it in sand or in road dust so that it will roast.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָשׂוּ אַנְשֵׁי טְבֶרְיָא וְהֵבִיאוּ סִלּוֹן שֶׁל צוֹנֵן לְתוֹךְ אַמָּה שֶׁל חַמִּין.
phrases.en: a story about the people of Tiberias, and they ran a cold-water pipe through a canal of hot water

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לָהֶן חֲכָמִים, אִם בְּשַׁבָּת, כְּחַמִּין שֶׁהוּחַמּוּ בְשַׁבָּת, אֲסוּרִין בִּרְחִיצָה וּבִשְׁתִיָּה;
phrases.en: The Rabbis said to them: If the water passed through on Shabbat, its legal status is like that of hot water that was heated on Shabbat, and the water is prohibited both for bathing and for drinking.

phrases.he: בְּיוֹם טוֹב, כְּחַמִּין שֶׁהוּחַמּוּ בְיוֹם טוֹב, אֲסוּרִין בִּרְחִיצָה וּמֻתָּרִין בִּשְׁתִיָּה.
phrases.en: And if the water passed through on a Festival, then it is prohibited for bathing but permitted for drinking.

phrases.he: מוּלְיָאר הַגָּרוּף, שׁוֹתִין הֵימֶנּוּ בְשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: a mulyar, whose coals were swept, one may drink from it on Shabbat.

phrases.he: אַנְטִיכִי, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁגְּרוּפָה, אֵין שׁוֹתִין מִמֶּנָּה:
phrases.en: an antikhi, even if its coals were swept, one may not drink from it

phrases.he: הַמֵּחַם שֶׁפִּנָּהוּ, לֹא יִתֵּן לְתוֹכוֹ צוֹנֵן בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁיֵּחַמּוּ,
phrases.en: An urn that was emptied of its hot water on Shabbat, one may not place cold water into it so that the cold water will be heated.

phrases.he: אֲבָל נוֹתֵן הוּא לְתוֹכוֹ אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַכּוֹס כְּדֵי לְהַפְשִׁירָן.
phrases.en: However, one may place into an urn or into a cup in order to warm it but not in order to heat it.

phrases.he: הָאִלְפָּס וְהַקְּדֵרָה שֶׁהֶעֱבִירָן מְרֻתָּחִין, לֹא יִתֵּן לְתוֹכָן תְּבָלִין,
phrases.en: A stew pot [ilpas] and a pot that were removed from the fire while they were still boiling, one may not place spices into them.

phrases.he: אֲבָל נוֹתֵן הוּא לְתוֹךְ הַקְּעָרָה אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַתַּמְחוּי.
phrases.en: However, one may place the spices into a bowl or into a tureen [tamḥui].

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, לַכֹּל הוּא נוֹתֵן, חוּץ מִדָּבָר שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ חֹמֶץ וְצִיר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: One may place spices into anything on Shabbat except for a vessel that has in it something containing vinegar or brine of salted fish.

phrases.he: אֵין נוֹתְנִין כְּלִי תַּחַת הַנֵּר לְקַבֵּל בּוֹ אֶת הַשֶּׁמֶן.
phrases.en: One may not place a vessel beneath the lamp to receive the oil

phrases.he: וְאִם נוֹתְנוֹ מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם, מֻתָּר.
phrases.en: And if one placed the vessel on Friday while it was still day, it is permitted.

phrases.he: וְאֵין נֵאוֹתִין מִמֶּנּוּ, לְפִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִן הַמּוּכָן.
phrases.en: However, one may not make use of the oil because it is not from the prepared

phrases.he: מְטַלְטְלִין נֵר חָדָשׁ, אֲבָל לֹא יָשָׁן.
phrases.en: One may move a new lamp but not an old one

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, כָּל הַנֵּרוֹת מְטַלְטְלִין, חוּץ מִן הַנֵּר הַדּוֹלֵק בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: All lamps may be moved except for an lamp that is burning on Shabbat

phrases.he: נוֹתְנִין כְּלִי תַחַת הַנֵּר לְקַבֵּל נִיצוֹצוֹת.
phrases.en: One may place a vessel beneath the lamp in order to receive burning sparks

phrases.he: וְלֹא יִתֵּן לְתוֹכוֹ מַיִם, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מְכַבֶּה:
phrases.en: And he may not place water into the vessel because he thereby extinguishes

phrases.he: בַּמֶּה טוֹמְנִין וּבַמָּה אֵין טוֹמְנִין.
phrases.en: In what may one insulate a pot of cooked food on Shabbat eve, and in what may one not insulate it?
