phrases.he: אֵין טוֹמְנִין לֹא בְגֶפֶת וְלֹא בְזֶבֶל, לֹא בְמֶלַח וְלֹא בְסִיד וְלֹא בְחֹל, בֵּין לַחִים בֵּין יְבֵשִׁים.
phrases.en: One may neither insulate it in the solid residue of produce that has been pressed free of its oil, nor in manure, nor in salt, nor in lime, nor in sand, whether those materials are moist or whether they are dry.

phrases.he: לֹא בְתֶבֶן וְלֹא בְזָגִים וְלֹא בְמוֹכִים וְלֹא בַעֲשָׂבִים בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן לַחִים, אֲבָל טוֹמְנִין בָּהֶן כְּשֶׁהֵן יְבֵשִׁין.
phrases.en: And one may neither insulate a pot in straw, nor in the residue of grapes that have been pressed for their juice, nor in soft material, e.g., from tattered clothing, nor in grass, when these materials are moist. However, one may insulate a pot in them when they are dry.

phrases.he: טוֹמְנִין בִּכְסוּת וּבְפֵרוֹת, בְּכַנְפֵי יוֹנָה וּבִנְסֹרֶת שֶׁל חָרָשִׁים וּבִנְעֹרֶת שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן דַּקָּה.
phrases.en: One may insulate a pot of hot food on Shabbat eve in clothing, in produce, in doves' wings, in a carpenter's wood-shavings, and in the chaff of fine flax.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹסֵר בְּדַקָּה וּמַתִּיר בְּגַסָּה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda prohibits doing so when it is fine, and permits doing so when it is coarse.

phrases.he: טוֹמְנִין בִּשְׁלָחִין, וּמְטַלְטְלִין אוֹתָן, בְּגִזֵּי צֶמֶר, וְאֵין מְטַלְטְלִין אוֹתָן.
phrases.en: One may insulate cooked food on Shabbat eve in animal hides and may move those hides on Shabbat. So too, one may insulate food in wool fleece and, in contrast to hides, one may not move the fleece.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד הוּא עוֹשֶׂה, נוֹטֵל אֶת הַכִּסּוּי וְהֵן נוֹפְלוֹת.
phrases.en: How, then, does one act if he insulated food in fleece, and now wishes to remove the pot? He lifts the cover, which he is permitted to move, and the fleece falls by itself.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר, קֻפָּה, מַטָּהּ עַל צִדָּהּ וְנוֹטֵל, שֶׁמָּא יִטֹּל וְאֵינוֹ יָכֹל לְהַחֲזִיר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says: If he placed the pot in a basket filled with fleece, he leans the basket on its side so that the fleece will fall to the side and takes the pot. Otherwise, there is concern lest the wool collapse when he lifts the pot from the basket. And then, he will be unable to replace the pot, as it is prohibited to move the wool to make room for the pot, since the wool is set-aside.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, נוֹטֵל וּמַחֲזִיר.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis disagree and say: He may take the pot and afterward replace it.

phrases.he: לֹא כִסָּהוּ מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם, לֹא יְכַסֶּנּוּ מִשֶּׁתֶּחְשָׁךְ.
phrases.en: If one did not cover a pot of cooked food on Shabbat eve while it was still day, he may not cover it after dark.

phrases.he: כִּסָּהוּ וְנִתְגַּלָּה, מֻתָּר לְכַסּוֹתוֹ.
phrases.en: However, if one covered it while it was still day and it was uncovered on Shabbat, he is permitted to cover it even on Shabbat.

phrases.he: מְמַלֵּא אֶת הַקִּיתוֹן וְנוֹתֵן לְתַחַת הַכַּר, אוֹ תַחַת הַכָּסֶת:
phrases.en: One may fill a jug with cold water on Shabbat and place it beneath a pillow or a cushion to prevent it from getting warm.

phrases.he: בַּמֶּה בְּהֵמָה יוֹצְאָה וּבַמָּה אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה.
phrases.en: With what may an animal go out into the public domain on Shabbat and with what may it not go out?

phrases.he: יוֹצֵא הַגָּמָל בְּאַפְסָר, וְנָאקָה בַחֲטָם, וְלֻבְדְּקִיס בִּפְרֻמְבְּיָא, וְסוּס בְּשֵׁיר,
phrases.en: A camel may go out on Shabbat with an afsar, and a naka may go out with a ḥatam, and a luvdekim may go out with a perumbiya. And a horse may go out with a chain around its neck.

phrases.he: וְכָל בַּעֲלֵי הַשֵּׁיר יוֹצְאִים בַּשֵּׁיר וְנִמְשָׁכִים בַּשֵּׁיר,
phrases.en: And, in general, all animals that typically have a chain around their necks when they go out to the public domain may go out with a chain on Shabbat and may be pulled by the chain.

phrases.he: וּמַזִּין עֲלֵיהֶן וְטוֹבְלִין בִּמְקוֹמָן.
phrases.en: one may sprinkle waters of purification on them and immerse them in their place on the animal, and they need not first be removed.

phrases.he: חֲמוֹר יוֹצֵא בְמַרְדַּעַת, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִיא קְשׁוּרָה לוֹ.
phrases.en: A donkey may go out with a saddlecloth when it is tied to the animal.

phrases.he: זְכָרִים יוֹצְאִין לְבוּבִין.
phrases.en: Rams may go out levuvin.

phrases.he: רְחֵלוֹת יוֹצְאוֹת שְׁחוּזוֹת, כְּבוּלוֹת וּכְבוּנוֹת.
phrases.en: Ewes may go out sheḥuzot, kevulot, and kevunot.

phrases.he: הָעִזִּים יוֹצְאוֹת צְרוּרוֹת.
phrases.en: She-goats may go out with their udders bound.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹסֵר בְּכֻלָּן, חוּץ מִן הָרְחֵלִין הַכְּבוּנוֹת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei prohibits with all of these except for the ewes that are kevunot.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, עִזִּים יוֹצְאוֹת צְרוּרוֹת לְיַבֵּשׁ, אֲבָל לֹא לְחָלָב:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: Goats may go out bound to dry, however, not to milk.

phrases.he: וּבַמָּה אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה.
phrases.en: And with what may an animal not go out into the public domain on Shabbat?

phrases.he: לֹא יֵצֵא גָמָל בִּמְטוּטֶלֶת, לֹא עָקוּד וְלֹא רָגוּל, וְכֵן שְׁאָר כָּל הַבְּהֵמוֹת.
phrases.en: A camel may not go out with a saddlecloth, nor may it go out akud or ragul, which are different ways of tying its legs together, as will be explained in the Gemara. And likewise, all other animals in those manners is prohibited.

phrases.he: לֹא יִקְשֹׁר גְּמַלִּים זֶה בָזֶה וְיִמְשֹׁךְ.
phrases.en: one may not tie camels one to the other and pull the lead camel, thereby pulling the others after it.

phrases.he: אֲבָל מַכְנִיס חֲבָלִים לְתוֹךְ יָדוֹ וְיִמְשֹׁךְ, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִכְרֹךְ:
phrases.en: However, he may place the ropes tied to each of the camels in his hand and pull them all, provided that he does not intertwine the ropes.

phrases.he: אֵין חֲמוֹר יוֹצֵא בְמַרְדַּעַת בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵינָהּ קְשׁוּרָה לוֹ.
phrases.en: A donkey may neither go out with the saddlecloth when it is not tied to its back

phrases.he: וְלֹא בְזוֹג, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא פָקוּק.
phrases.en: nor with a bell even if it is plugged to prevent it from ringing

phrases.he: וְלֹא בְסֻלָּם שֶׁבְּצַוָּארוֹ, וְלֹא בִרְצוּעָה שֶׁבְּרַגְלוֹ.
phrases.en: nor with a ladder that is around its neck, nor with a strap that is around its leg

phrases.he: וְאֵין הַתַּרְנְגוֹלִין יוֹצְאִין בְּחוּטִין, וְלֹא בִרְצוּעוֹת שֶׁבְּרַגְלֵיהֶם.
phrases.en: And the roosters may not go out with strings and not with a strap on their feet

phrases.he: וְאֵין הַזְּכָרִים יוֹצְאִין בַּעֲגָלָה שֶׁתַּחַת הָאַלְיָה שֶׁלָּהֶן.
phrases.en: And the rams may not go out with a small wagon under their tails

phrases.he: וְאֵין הָרְחֵלִים יוֹצְאוֹת חֲנוּנוֹת.
phrases.en: And ewes may not go out ḥanunot

phrases.he: וְאֵין הָעֵגֶל יוֹצֵא בְגִימוֹן.
phrases.en: nor may a calf go out with a gimon

phrases.he: וְלֹא פָרָה בְּעוֹר הַקֻּפָּר, וְלֹא בִרְצוּעָה שֶׁבֵּין קַרְנֶיהָ.
phrases.en: nor may a cow go out with the skin of a hedgehog [kupar], nor with a strap between its horns

phrases.he: פָּרָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה הָיְתָה יוֹצְאָה בִרְצוּעָה שֶׁבֵּין קַרְנֶיהָ, שֶׁלֹּא בִרְצוֹן חֲכָמִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya's cow would go out on Shabbat with a strap between its horns, contrary to the will of the Sages

phrases.he: בַּמֶּה אִשָּׁה יוֹצְאָה וּבַמָּה אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה.
phrases.en: With what items may a woman go out into the public domain on Shabbat and with what items may she not go out?

phrases.he: לֹא תֵצֵא אִשָּׁה לֹא בְחוּטֵי צֶמֶר וְלֹא בְחוּטֵי פִשְׁתָּן וְלֹא בִרְצוּעוֹת שֶׁבְּרֹאשָׁהּ.
phrases.en: A woman may neither go out with strings of wool, nor with strings of flax, nor with strips in the hair of her head.

phrases.he: וְלֹא תִטְבֹּל בָּהֶן עַד שֶׁתְּרַפֵּם.
phrases.en: And a woman may not immerse in a ritual bath with them in her hair until she loosens them.

phrases.he: וְלֹא בְטֹטֶפֶת וְלֹא בְסַנְבּוּטִין בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵינָן תְּפוּרִין.
phrases.en: And, likewise, a woman may neither go out with the ornament called totefet, nor with sarvitin that are not sewn into her head covering,

phrases.he: וְלֹא בְכָבוּל לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים.
phrases.en: nor with a kavul into the public domain.

phrases.he: וְלֹא בְעִיר שֶׁל זָהָב, וְלֹא בְקַטְלָא, וְלֹא בִנְזָמִים, וְלֹא בְטַבַּעַת שֶׁאֵין עָלֶיהָ חוֹתָם, וְלֹא בְמַחַט שֶׁאֵינָהּ נְקוּבָה.
phrases.en: And, likewise, a woman may neither go out with a city of gold ornament, nor with a katla ornament, nor with nose rings, nor with a ring that has no seal on it, nor with a needle that is not perforated,

phrases.he: וְאִם יָצָאת, אֵינָהּ חַיֶּבֶת חַטָּאת:
phrases.en: And if she unwittingly went out wearing any of these, she is not liable to bring a sin-offering.

phrases.he: לֹא יֵצֵא הָאִישׁ בְּסַנְדָּל הַמְסֻמָּר,
phrases.en: A man may not go out with a spiked sandal,

phrases.he: וְלֹא בְיָחִיד בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בְּרַגְלוֹ מַכָּה,
phrases.en: And he may not go out with a single sandal when there is no wound on his foot.

phrases.he: וְלֹא בִתְפִלִּין,
phrases.en: And he may neither go out with phylacteries,

phrases.he: וְלֹא בְקָמֵעַ בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִן הַמֻּמְחֶה,
phrases.en: nor with an amulet when it is not from an expert,

phrases.he: וְלֹא בְשִׁרְיוֹן,
phrases.en: And he may neither go out with shiryon,

phrases.he: וְלֹא בְקַסְדָּא,
phrases.en: nor with a kasda,

phrases.he: וְלֹא בְמַגָּפַיִם.
phrases.en: nor with maggafayim.

phrases.he: וְאִם יָצָא,
phrases.en: And if he went out

phrases.he: אֵינוֹ חַיָּב חַטָּאת:
phrases.en: he is not liable to bring a sin-offering.

phrases.he: לֹא תֵצֵא אִשָּׁה בְמַחַט הַנְּקוּבָה,
phrases.en: A woman may neither go out with a perforated needle,

phrases.he: וְלֹא בְטַבַּעַת שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלֶיהָ חוֹתָם,
phrases.en: nor with a ring that has a seal on it,

phrases.he: וְלֹא בְכוֹלְיָאר,
phrases.en: nor with a kulyar,

phrases.he: וְלֹא בְכוֹבֶלֶת,
phrases.en: nor with a kovelet,

phrases.he: וְלֹא בִצְלוֹחִית שֶׁל פַּלְיָטוֹן.
phrases.en: nor with a flask of balsam oil.

phrases.he: וְאִם יָצְתָה, חַיֶּבֶת חַטָּאת,
phrases.en: And if she did go out, she is liable to bring a sin-offering;

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir,

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹטְרִין בְּכוֹבֶלֶת וּבִצְלוֹחִית שֶׁל פַּלְיָטוֹן:
phrases.en: And the Rabbis exempt one who goes out on Shabbat with a kovelet and with a flask of balsam oil.

phrases.he: לֹא יֵצֵא הָאִישׁ לֹא בְסַיִף, וְלֹא בְקֶשֶׁת, וְלֹא בִתְרִיס, וְלֹא בְאַלָּה, וְלֹא בְרֹמַח.
phrases.en: a man may neither go out with a sword, nor with a bow, nor with a shield [teris], nor with an alla, nor with a spear.

phrases.he: וְאִם יָצָא, חַיָּב חַטָּאת.
phrases.en: And if he went out he is liable to bring a sin-offering.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, תַּכְשִׁיטִין הֵן לוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: These are ornaments for him;

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵינָן אֶלָּא לִגְנַאי, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ישעיה ב) וְכִתְּתוּ חַרְבוֹתָם לְאִתִּים וַחֲנִיתוֹתֵיהֶם לְמַזְמֵרוֹת, לֹא יִשָּׂא גּוֹי אֶל גּוֹי חֶרֶב וְלֹא יִלְמְדוּ עוֹד מִלְחָמָה.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: They are nothing other than reprehensible as it is written: "And they shall beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks; nation will not raise sword against nation, neither will they learn war anymore"

phrases.he: בִּירִית, טְהוֹרָה, וְיוֹצְאִין בָּהּ בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: a garter is pure and she may go out with it on Shabbat.

phrases.he: כְּבָלִים, טְמֵאִין, וְאֵין יוֹצְאִין בָּהֶם בְּשַׁבָּת:
phrases.en: ankle chains, can become ritually impure, and she may not go out with them on Shabbat.

phrases.he: יוֹצְאָה אִשָּׁה בְחוּטֵי שֵׂעָר, בֵּין מִשֶּׁלָּהּ בֵּין מִשֶּׁל חֲבֶרְתָּהּ בֵּין מִשֶּׁל בְּהֵמָה,
phrases.en: A woman may go out with strands of hair whether they are from her own hair that she made into a wig, or whether they are from the hair of another, or whether they are from the hair of an animal.

phrases.he: וּבְטֹטֶפֶת וּבְסַנְבּוּטִין בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן תְּפוּרִין.
phrases.en: And with a totefet, and with sarvitin when they are sewn

phrases.he: בְּכָבוּל וּבְפֵאָה נָכְרִית לֶחָצֵר.
phrases.en: with a woolen cap or with a wig to the courtyard,

phrases.he: בְּמוֹךְ שֶׁבְּאָזְנָהּ וּבְמוֹךְ שֶׁבְּסַנְדָּלָהּ וּבְמוֹךְ שֶׁהִתְקִינָה לְנִדָּתָהּ.
phrases.en: And with a cloth that is in her ear, and with a cloth in her sandal, and with a cloth that she placed due to her menstrual status.

phrases.he: בְּפִלְפֵּל וּבְגַרְגִּיר מֶלַח וּבְכָל דָּבָר שֶׁתִּתֵּן לְתוֹךְ פִּיהָ, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא תִתֵּן לְכַתְּחִלָּה בְשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: with pepper, or with a grain of salt, or anything placed in her mouth as long as she does not put these objects in her mouth for the first time on Shabbat.

phrases.he: וְאִם נָפַל, לֹא תַחֲזִיר.
phrases.en: And if it fell out she may not replace it.

phrases.he: שֵׁן תּוֹתֶבֶת וְשֵׁן שֶׁל זָהָב, רַבִּי מַתִּיר, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִים:
phrases.en: A false tooth as well as a gold tooth, Rabbi permits, and the Rabbis prohibit.

phrases.he: יוֹצְאָה בְסֶלַע שֶׁעַל הַצִּינִית.
phrases.en: may go out with a sela coin that she ties on a wound on her foot.

phrases.he: הַבָּנוֹת קְטַנּוֹת יוֹצְאוֹת בְּחוּטִין וַאֲפִלּוּ בְקִסְמִין שֶׁבְּאָזְנֵיהֶם.
phrases.en: The young girls may go out with strings, and even with wood chips that are in the holes in their ears

phrases.he: עַרְבִיּוֹת יוֹצְאוֹת רְעוּלוֹת, וּמָדִיּוֹת פְּרוּפוֹת,
phrases.en: Jewish women in Arab countries may go out veiled, and Jewish women in Media may go out with cloaks fastened

phrases.he: וְכָל אָדָם,
phrases.en: And, any person

phrases.he: אֶלָּא שֶׁדִּבְּרוּ חֲכָמִים בַּהֹוֶה:
phrases.en: however, the Sages spoke in the present,

phrases.he: פּוֹרֶפֶת עַל הָאֶבֶן וְעַל הָאֱגוֹז וְעַל הַמַּטְבֵּעַ,
phrases.en: may fasten her cloak on a stone and likewise, she may do so on a nut or on a coin,

phrases.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא תִפְרֹף לְכַתְּחִלָּה בְשַׁבָּת:
phrases.en: as long as she does not fasten her cloak with them on Shabbat ab initio.

phrases.he: הַקִּטֵּעַ יוֹצֵא בְקַב שֶׁלּוֹ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: One with an amputated leg may go out with his wooden leg, as it has the legal status of a shoe; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹסֵר.
phrases.en: And Rabbi Yosei prohibits going out into the public domain with the wooden leg, since he does not consider it to have the legal status of a shoe.

phrases.he: וְאִם יֶשׁ לוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל כְּתוּתִים, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: And if the wooden leg has a receptacle for pads, a concave space at the top of the leg into which pads are placed to cushion the amputated leg, it assumes the status of a wooden vessel and can become ritually impure.

phrases.he: סָמוֹכוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ, טְמֵאִין מִדְרָס, וְיוֹצְאִין בָּהֶן בְּשַׁבָּת, וְנִכְנָסִין בָּהֶן בָּעֲזָרָה.
phrases.en: And his supports, which are shoes that one who had both of his feet amputated places on his knees in order to walk on his knees, if a zav wears them, they are subject to ritual impurity imparted by treading. And one may go out with them into the public domain on Shabbat since they have the legal status of shoes. And one may enter the Temple courtyard with them.

phrases.he: כִּסֵּא וְסָמוֹכוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ, טְמֵאִין מִדְרָס, וְאֵין יוֹצְאִין בָּהֶן בְּשַׁבָּת, וְאֵין נִכְנָסִין בָּהֶן בָּעֲזָרָה.
phrases.en: However, if one who is crippled to the extent that he cannot walk at all sits on a chair that is attached to him, places supports on his hands, and propels himself along with his hands, his chair and supports are subject to ritual impurity imparted by treading. And one may not go out with them on Shabbat, and one may not enter the Temple courtyard with them.

phrases.he: אַנְקַטְמִין טְהוֹרִין, וְאֵין יוֹצְאִין בָּהֶן:
phrases.en: Loketamin, which will be explained in the Gemara, are ritually pure in the sense that they cannot become ritually impure because they are not vessels, and one may not go out with them on Shabbat.

phrases.he: הַבָּנִים יוֹצְאִין בִּקְשָׁרִים,
phrases.en: boys may go out on Shabbat with knots

phrases.he: וּבְנֵי מְלָכִים בְּזוֹגִין.
phrases.en: and princes with bells

phrases.he: וְכָל אָדָם,
phrases.en: And any person

phrases.he: אֶלָּא שֶׁדִּבְּרוּ חֲכָמִים בַּהֹוֶה:
phrases.en: however, the Sages spoke in the present

phrases.he: יוֹצְאִין בְּבֵיצַת הַחַרְגּוֹל, וּבְשֵׁן שׁוּעָל, וּבְמַסְמֵר מִן הַצָּלוּב, מִשּׁוּם רְפוּאָה,
phrases.en: One may go out on Shabbat with a locust egg, and with a fox tooth, and with a nail from the crucified, for the purpose of healing;

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אַף בְּחֹל אָסוּר, מִשּׁוּם דַּרְכֵי הָאֱמוֹרִי:
phrases.en: The Rabbis prohibit using these remedies even during the week, due to the prohibition of following the ways of the Amorite.

phrases.he: כְּלָל גָּדוֹל אָמְרוּ בַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.en: stated a significant principle with regard to Shabbat:

phrases.he: כָּל הַשּׁוֹכֵחַ עִקַּר שַׁבָּת וְעָשָׂה מְלָאכוֹת הַרְבֵּה בְשַׁבָּתוֹת הַרְבֵּה, אֵינוֹ חַיָּב אֶלָּא חַטָּאת אֶחָת.
phrases.en: One who forgets the essence of Shabbat and performed numerous prohibited labors on multiple Shabbatot, is liable only one sin-offering

phrases.he: הַיּוֹדֵעַ עִקַּר שַׁבָּת וְעָשָׂה מְלָאכוֹת הַרְבֵּה בְּשַׁבָּתוֹת הַרְבֵּה, חַיָּב עַל כָּל שַׁבָּת וְשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: One who knows the essence of Shabbat and performs numerous prohibited labors on multiple Shabbatot is liable to bring a sin-offering for each Shabbat

phrases.he: הַיּוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהוּא שַׁבָּת וְעָשָׂה מְלָאכוֹת הַרְבֵּה בְּשַׁבָּתוֹת הַרְבֵּה, חַיָּב עַל כָּל אַב מְלָאכָה וּמְלָאכָה.
phrases.en: One who is aware that the day is Shabbat and performed numerous prohibited labors on multiple Shabbatot is liable to bring a sin-offering for each and every primary category of labor

phrases.he: הָעוֹשֶׂה מְלָאכוֹת הַרְבֵּה מֵעֵין מְלָאכָה אַחַת, אֵינוֹ חַיָּב אֶלָּא חַטָּאת אֶחָת:
phrases.en: One who performs numerous prohibited labors subsumed under a single category of labor is liable only one sin-offering.

phrases.he: אֲבוֹת מְלָאכוֹת אַרְבָּעִים חָסֵר אֶחָת.
phrases.en: primary categories of labor prohibited on Shabbat, which number forty-less-one.

phrases.he: הַזּוֹרֵעַ.
phrases.en: One who sows

phrases.he: וְהַחוֹרֵשׁ.
phrases.en: and one who plows

phrases.he: וְהַקּוֹצֵר.
phrases.en: and one who reaps

phrases.he: וְהַמְעַמֵּר.
phrases.en: and one who gathers sheaves into a pile
and one who threshes, removing the kernel from the husk

phrases.he: וְהַזּוֹרֶה.
phrases.en: and one who winnows threshed grain in the wind

phrases.he: הַבּוֹרֵר.
phrases.en: and one who selects the inedible waste from the edible

phrases.he: הַטּוֹחֵן.
phrases.en: and one who grinds

phrases.he: וְהַמְרַקֵּד.
phrases.en: and one who sifts the flour in a sieve

phrases.he: וְהַלָּשׁ.
phrases.en: and one who kneads dough

phrases.he: וְהָאוֹפֶה.
phrases.en: and one who bakes.

phrases.he: הַגּוֹזֵז אֶת הַצֶּמֶר.
phrases.en: One who shears wool

phrases.he: הַמְלַבְּנוֹ.
phrases.en: and one who whitens it

phrases.he: וְהַמְנַפְּצוֹ.
phrases.en: and one who combs the fleece and straightens it

phrases.he: וְהַצּוֹבְעוֹ.
phrases.en: and one who dyes it

phrases.he: וְהַטּוֹוֶה.
phrases.en: and one who spins the wool

phrases.he: וְהַמֵּסֵךְ.
phrases.en: and one who stretches the threads of the warp in the loom

phrases.he: וְהָעוֹשֶׂה שְׁנֵי בָתֵּי נִירִין.
phrases.en: and one who constructs two meshes, tying the threads of the warp to the base of the loom

phrases.he: וְהָאוֹרֵג שְׁנֵי חוּטִין.
phrases.en: and one who weaves two threads

phrases.he: וְהַפּוֹצֵעַ שְׁנֵי חוּטִין.
phrases.en: and one who severs two threads for constructive purposes

phrases.he: הַקּוֹשֵׁר.
phrases.en: and one who ties a knot

phrases.he: וְהַמַּתִּיר.
phrases.en: and one who unties a knot

phrases.he: וְהַתּוֹפֵר שְׁתֵּי תְפִירוֹת.
phrases.en: and one who sews two stitches with a needle

phrases.he: הַקּוֹרֵעַ עַל מְנָת לִתְפֹּר שְׁתֵּי תְפִירוֹת.
phrases.en: as well as one who tears a fabric in order to sew two stitches.

phrases.he: הַצָּד צְבִי.
phrases.en: One who traps a deer, or any living creature

phrases.he: הַשּׁוֹחֲטוֹ.
phrases.en: and one who slaughters it

phrases.he: וְהַמַּפְשִׁיטוֹ.
phrases.en: and one who flays it

phrases.he: הַמּוֹלְחוֹ,
phrases.en: and one who salts its hide, a step in the tanning process

phrases.he: וְהַמְעַבֵּד אֶת עוֹרוֹ.
phrases.en: and one who tans its hide

phrases.he: וְהַמּוֹחֲקוֹ.
phrases.en: and one who smooths it, removing hairs and veins

phrases.he: וְהַמְחַתְּכוֹ.
phrases.en: and one who cuts it into measured parts.

phrases.he: הַכּוֹתֵב שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת.
phrases.en: One who writes two letters

phrases.he: וְהַמּוֹחֵק עַל מְנָת לִכְתֹּב שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת.
phrases.en: and one who erases in order to write two letters.

phrases.he: הַבּוֹנֶה.
phrases.en: One who builds a structure

phrases.he: וְהַסּוֹתֵר.
phrases.en: and one who dismantles it

phrases.he: הַמְכַבֶּה.
phrases.en: one who extinguishes a fire

phrases.he: וְהַמַּבְעִיר.
phrases.en: and one who kindles a fire.

phrases.he: הַמַּכֶּה בַפַּטִּישׁ.
phrases.en: One who strikes a blow with a hammer to complete the production process of a vessel

phrases.he: הַמּוֹצִיא מֵרְשׁוּת לִרְשׁוּת.
phrases.en: and one who carries out an object from domain to domain.

phrases.he: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ אֲבוֹת מְלָאכוֹת אַרְבָּעִים חָסֵר אֶחָת:
phrases.en: All these are primary categories of labor, and they number forty-less-one.

phrases.he: וְעוֹד כְּלָל אַחֵר אָמְרוּ.
phrases.en: And they stated an additional principle

phrases.he: כָּל הַכָּשֵׁר לְהַצְנִיעַ וּמַצְנִיעִין כָּמוֹהוּ וְהוֹצִיאוֹ בְשַׁבָּת, חַיָּב עָלָיו חַטָּאת,
phrases.en: Anything fit to store, and people typically store items like it, and one carried it out into a prohibited domain on Shabbat, he is liable to bring a sin-offering for that action.

phrases.he: וְכָל שֶׁאֵינוֹ כָשֵׁר לְהַצְנִיעַ וְאֵין מַצְנִיעִין כָּמוֹהוּ וְהוֹצִיאוֹ בְשַׁבָּת, אֵינוֹ חַיָּב אֶלָּא הַמַּצְנִיעוֹ.
phrases.en: And anything not fit to store and people typically do not store items like it, and one carried it out on Shabbat, only the one who stores it is liable.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹצִיא תֶבֶן, כִּמְלֹא פִי פָרָה.
phrases.en: One who carries out straw in a measure equivalent to a cow's mouthful is liable.

phrases.he: עָצָה, כִּמְלֹא פִי גָמָל.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for etza is equivalent to a camel's mouthful.

phrases.he: עָמִיר, כִּמְלֹא פִי טָלֶה.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for ears of grain is equivalent to a lamb's mouthful.

phrases.he: עֲשָׂבִים, כִּמְלֹא פִי גְדִי.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for grass is equivalent to a goat's mouthful.

phrases.he: עֲלֵי שׁוּם וַעֲלֵי בְצָלִים, לַחִים, כִּגְרוֹגֶרֶת, יְבֵשִׁים, כִּמְלֹא פִי גְדִי.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for garlic leaves and onion leaves, if they are moist and fit for human consumption, is equivalent to a dried fig-bulk. If the garlic leaves and onion leaves are dry, the measure for liability is equivalent to a goat's mouthful.

phrases.he: וְאֵין מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁווּ בְשִׁעוּרֵיהֶן.
phrases.en: And none of these substances join together with one another to constitute a measure for liability because they are not equal in their measures.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹצִיא אֳכָלִים כִּגְרוֹגֶרֶת, חַיָּב, וּמִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁשָּׁווּ בְשִׁעוּרֵיהֶן, חוּץ מִקְּלִפֵּיהֶן וְגַרְעִינֵיהֶן וְעֻקְצֵיהֶן וְסֻבָּן וּמֻרְסָנָן.
phrases.en: One who carries out a measure of foods fit for human consumption equivalent to a dried fig-bulk into a domain where carrying is prohibited on Shabbat is liable. And all those foods join together with one another to constitute that amount because they are equal in their measures. This amount is calculated without their shells, and their seeds, and their stems, and their bran, and their coarse bran.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, חוּץ מִקְּלִפֵּי עֲדָשִׁים שֶׁמִּתְבַּשְּׁלוֹת עִמָּהֶן:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: None of the shells are calculated, except for the shells of lentils, which join together with the lentils to comprise the measure for liability because they are cooked and eaten with them.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹצִיא יַיִן, כְּדֵי מְזִיגַת הַכּוֹס.
phrases.en: One who carries out wine from a private domain to a public domain or vice versa is liable only for a measure equivalent to the wine typically diluted in a cup.

phrases.he: חָלָב, כְּדֵי גְמִיעָה.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out milk is equivalent to that which is swallowed in one gulp.

phrases.he: דְּבַשׁ, כְּדֵי לִתֵּן עַל הַכָּתִית.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out honey is equivalent to that which is used to place on a sore caused by chafing.

phrases.he: שֶׁמֶן, כְּדֵי לָסוּךְ אֵבֶר קָטָן.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out oil is equivalent to that which is used to spread on a small limb.

phrases.he: מַיִם, כְּדֵי לָשׁוּף בָּהֶם אֶת הַקִּילוֹר.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out water is equivalent to that which is used to rub and spread on an eye bandage.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַמַּשְׁקִין, בִּרְבִיעִית.
phrases.en: And the measure that determines liability for carrying out all other liquids is a quarter of a log.

phrases.he: וְכָל הַשּׁוֹפָכִין, בִּרְבִיעִית.
phrases.en: And the measure that determines liability for carrying out all waste water is a quarter of a log.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, כֻּלָּן בִּרְבִיעִית, וְלֹא אָמְרוּ כָל הַשִּׁעוּרִין הַלָּלוּ אֶלָּא לְמַצְנִיעֵיהֶן:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: The measure that determines liability for all liquids is a quarter of a log. And all these measures were only stated with regard to those who store them.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹצִיא חֶבֶל, כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת אֹזֶן לְקֻפָּה.
phrases.en: One who carries out a rope is liable in a measure equivalent to that which is used to form an ear-shaped handle for a basket.

phrases.he: גֶּמִי, כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת תְּלַאי לְנָפָה וְלִכְבָרָה.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out reed grass is equivalent to that which is used to make a loop for hanging a sifter or a sieve.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כְּדֵי לִטֹּל מִמֶּנּוּ מִדַּת מִנְעָל לְקָטָן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: The measure for liability is equivalent to that which is used to take the measure of a shoe for a child, as the reed is used to measure the size of the foot.

phrases.he: נְיָר, כְּדֵי לִכְתֹּב עָלָיו קֶשֶׁר מוֹכְסִין.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out paper is equivalent to that which is used to write a tax receipt.

phrases.he: וְהַמּוֹצִיא קֶשֶׁר מוֹכְסִין, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: And one who carries out a tax receipt itself on Shabbat is liable.

phrases.he: נְיָר מָחוּק, כְּדֵי לִכְרֹךְ עַל פִּי צְלוֹחִית קְטַנָּה שֶׁל פַּלְיָטוֹן:
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out paper from which the writing has been erased and which can no longer be used for writing, is equivalent to that which is used to wrap around a small jar of perfume.

phrases.he: עוֹר, כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת קָמֵעַ.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out animal hide is equivalent to that which is used to make an amulet.

phrases.he: קְלָף, כְּדֵי לִכְתֹּב עָלָיו פָּרָשָׁה קְטַנָּה שֶׁבַּתְּפִלִּין, שֶׁהִיא שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out parchment is equivalent to that which is used to write the shortest portion in the phylacteries, which is the portion of Shema Yisrael.

phrases.he: דְּיוֹ, כְּדֵי לִכְתֹּב שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out ink is equivalent to that which is used to write two letters.

phrases.he: כְּחֹל, כְּדֵי לִכְחֹל עַיִן אֶחָת:
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out blue eye shadow is equivalent to that which is used to paint one eye blue.

phrases.he: דֶּבֶק, כְּדֵי לִתֵּן בְּרֹאשׁ הַשַּׁבְשֶׁבֶת.
phrases.en: glue is equivalent to that which is used to place on the top of a board to catch birds.

phrases.he: זֶפֶת וְגָפְרִית, כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת נֶקֶב.
phrases.en: tar and sulfur is equivalent to that which is used to seal a hole in a vessel and to make a small hole in that seal.

phrases.he: שַׁעֲוָה, כְּדֵי לִתֵּן עַל פִּי נֶקֶב קָטָן.
phrases.en: wax is equivalent to that which is used to place on the opening of a small hole to seal it.

phrases.he: חַרְסִית, כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת פִּי כוּר שֶׁל צוֹרְפֵי זָהָב.
phrases.en: crushed earthenware is equivalent to that which is used to knead and make from it an opening for the bellows to be placed in a gold refiners' crucible.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת פִּטְפּוּט.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: Equivalent to that which is used to make a small tripod [pitput] for the crucible.

phrases.he: סֻבִּין, כְּדֵי לִתֵּן עַל פִּי כוּר שֶׁל צוֹרְפֵי זָהָב.
phrases.en: bran is equivalent to that which is used to place on the hole of a gold refiners' crucible.

phrases.he: סִיד, כְּדֵי לָסוּד קְטַנָּה שֶׁבַּבָּנוֹת.
phrases.en: lime is equivalent to that which is used to spread as a depilatory on the smallest of girls.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת כִּלְכּוּל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: Equivalent to that which is used to spread on the hair that grows over the temple so that it will lie flat.

phrases.he: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר, כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת אַנְדִּיפֵי:
phrases.en: Rabbi Neḥemya says: Equivalent to that which is used to spread on the temple to remove fine hairs.

phrases.he: אֲדָמָה, כְּחוֹתַם הַמַּרְצוּפִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out earth on Shabbat is equivalent to the seal of large sacks; this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, כְּחוֹתַם הָאִגְּרוֹת.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: The measure for liability is much smaller, equivalent to the seal of letters.

phrases.he: זֶבֶל וְחֹל הַדַּק, כְּדֵי לְזַבֵּל קֶלַח שֶׁל כְּרוּב, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out manure and fine sand is equivalent to that which is used to fertilize one stalk of cabbage; this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, כְּדֵי לְזַבֵּל כְּרֵשָׁא.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: The measure that determines liability for carrying it out is equivalent to that which is used to fertilize a leek, which is less than that used for cabbage.

phrases.he: חֹל הַגַּס, כְּדֵי לִתֵּן עַל מְלֹא כַף סִיד.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out coarse sand is equivalent to that which is used to place on a full spoon of plaster.

phrases.he: קָנֶה, כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת קֻלְמוֹס.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out a reed is equivalent to that which is used to make a quill.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיָה עָב אוֹ מְרֻסָּס, כְּדֵי לְבַשֵּׁל בוֹ בֵיצָה קַלָּה שֶׁבַּבֵּיצִים, טְרוּפָה וּנְתוּנָה בָאִלְפָּס:
phrases.en: And if the reed was thick and unfit for writing, or if it was fragmented, its measure for liability is equivalent to that which is used to cook an egg most easily cooked, one that is already beaten and placed in a stew pot.

phrases.he: עֶצֶם, כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת תַּרְוָד.
phrases.en: a bone is equivalent to that which is used to make a spoon.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת מִמֶּנּוּ חָף.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: In a measure equivalent to that which is used to make from it a key.

phrases.he: זְכוּכִית, כְּדֵי לִגְרֹר בּוֹ רֹאשׁ הַכַּרְכָּר.
phrases.en: glass is equivalent to that which is used to scrape and smooth the top of a bobbin,

phrases.he: צְרוֹר אוֹ אֶבֶן, כְּדֵי לִזְרֹק בְּעוֹף.
phrases.en: a pebble or a stone is equivalent to that which is used to throw at a bird to chase it away.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּר יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר, כְּדֵי לִזְרֹק בִּבְהֵמָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar bar Ya'akov says: Equivalent to that which is used to throw at an animal,

phrases.he: חֶרֶס, כְּדֵי לִתֵּן בֵּין פַּצִּים לַחֲבֵרוֹ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: One who carries out a shard of earthenware on Shabbat is liable if it is in a measure equivalent to that which is used to place between one pillar and another when piled on the ground to separate them; this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, כְּדֵי לַחְתּוֹת בּוֹ אֶת הָאוּר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: In a measure equivalent to that which is used to stoke a fire with it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, כְּדֵי לְקַבֵּל בּוֹ רְבִיעִית.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: In a measure equivalent to that which is used to hold a quarter of a log in it.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר, זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר (ישעיה ל), וְלֹא יִמָּצֵא בִמְכִתָּתוֹ חֶרֶשׂ לַחְתּוֹת אֵשׁ מִיָּקוּד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir said: Although there is no proof for the matter, there is a biblical allusion to my opinion, as it is stated: "And He shall break it as a potter's vessel is broken, smashing it without sparing; and there shall not be found among its pieces a shard to rake fire on the hearth" (Isaiah 30:14).

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, מִשָּׁם רְאָיָה, וְלַחְשֹׂף מַיִם מִגֶּבֶא (שם):
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei said to him: Is there proof from there? The verse concludes: "And to extract water from the cistern," indicating that earthenware is significant if it is large enough to hold water.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, מִנַּיִן לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁהִיא מְּטַמְּאָה בְמַשָּׂא כַּנִּדָּה,
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva said: From where is it derived that idolatry, e.g., a statue of a deity, transmits impurity imparted by carrying even when the person who carries it does not come into contact with it, just as a menstruating woman does?

phrases.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ישעיה ל) תִּזְרֵם כְּמוֹ דָוָה, צֵא תֹּאמַר לוֹ,
phrases.en: As it is stated: "And you will defile the silver overlays of your statues, and the golden plating of your idols, you will cast them away as you would a menstruating woman [dava], you will tell it, get out" (Isaiah 30:22).

phrases.he: מַה נִּדָּה מְטַמְּאָה בְמַשָּׂא, אַף עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מְטַמְּאָה בְמַשָּׂא:
phrases.en: Just as a menstruating woman transmits impurity imparted by carrying, so too, idolatry transmits impurity imparted by carrying.

phrases.he: מִנַּיִן לִסְפִינָה שֶׁהִיא טְהוֹרָה,
phrases.en: From where is it derived that the ship is ritually pure,

phrases.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (משלי ל) דֶּרֶךְ אֳנִיָּה בְלֶב יָם.
phrases.en: as it is stated: "The way of a ship in the midst of the sea"

phrases.he: מִנַּיִן לַעֲרוּגָה שֶׁהִיא שִׁשָּׁה עַל שִׁשָּׁה טְפָחִים שֶׁזּוֹרְעִין בְּתוֹכָהּ חֲמִשָּׁה זֵרְעוֹנִין,
phrases.en: From where is it derived that in a garden bed that is six by six handbreadths, that one may plant five different types of seeds in it?

phrases.he: אַרְבָּעָה בְאַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת הָעֲרוּגָה וְאֶחָד בָּאֶמְצַע,
phrases.en: Four on each of the four sides of the garden bed and one in the middle.

phrases.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ישעיה סא) כִּי כָאָרֶץ תּוֹצִיא צִמְחָהּ וּכְגַנָּה זֵרוּעֶיהָ תַצְמִיחַ,
phrases.en: As it is stated: "For as the earth brings forth its growth, and as a garden causes its seeds to grow,

phrases.he: זַרְעָהּ לֹא נֶאֱמַר, אֶלָּא זֵרוּעֶיהָ:
phrases.en: Its seed, in the singular, is not stated; rather, its seeds, written in the plural.

phrases.he: מִנַּיִן לְפוֹלֶטֶת שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי שֶׁהִיא טְמֵאָה,
phrases.en: From where is it derived that a woman who discharges semen even on the third day after relations is ritually impure,

phrases.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמות יט) הֱיוּ נְכוֹנִים לִשְׁלשֶׁת יָמִים.
phrases.en: as it is stated prior to the revelation at Sinai: "And he said to the people, prepare yourselves for three days, do not approach a woman"

phrases.he: מִנַּיִן שֶׁמַּרְחִיצִין אֶת הַמִּילָה בַיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: From where is it derived that one may wash the circumcision on the third day, meaning the third day after the circumcision, even if it occurs on Shabbat?

phrases.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (בראשית לד) וַיְהִי בַיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי בִּהְיוֹתָם כֹּאֲבִים.
phrases.en: As it is stated: "And it came to pass on the third day when they were in pain"

phrases.he: מִנַּיִן שֶׁקּוֹשְׁרִין לָשׁוֹן שֶׁל זְהוֹרִית בְּרֹאשׁ שָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ,
phrases.en: From where is it derived that one ties a scarlet strip of wool to the head of the scapegoat that is dispatched to Azazel?

phrases.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ישעיה א) אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ:
phrases.en: As it is stated: "If your sins be like scarlet, they will become white like snow"

phrases.he: מִנַּיִן לְסִיכָה שֶׁהִיא כַשְּׁתִיָּה בְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
phrases.en: From where is it derived that smearing oil on one's body is like drinking and is similarly prohibited on Yom Kippur?

phrases.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר, זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר,
phrases.en: Although there is no proof for this, there is an allusion to it,

phrases.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (תהלים קט) וַתָּבֹא כַמַּיִם בְּקִרְבּוֹ וְכַשֶּׁמֶן בְּעַצְמוֹתָיו:
phrases.en: as it is stated: "And it comes into his inward parts like water and like oil into his bones"

phrases.he: הַמּוֹצִיא עֵצִים, כְּדֵי לְבַשֵּׁל בֵּיצָה קַלָּה.
phrases.en: One who carries out wood is liable for a measure equivalent to the amount of wood necessary to cook an easily cooked egg.

phrases.he: תְּבָלִין, כְּדֵי לְתַבֵּל בֵּיצָה קַלָּה, וּמִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out spices is equivalent to that which is used to season an easily cooked egg. And all types of spices join together with one another to constitute the measure for liability.

phrases.he: קְלִפֵּי אֱגוֹזִים, קְלִפֵּי רִמּוֹנִים, אִסְטִיס וּפוּאָה, כְּדֵי לִצְבֹּעַ בָּהֶן בֶּגֶד קָטָן בַּסְּבָכָה.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out nutshells, pomegranate peels, safflower, and madder, which are used to produce dyes, is equivalent to the amount that is used to dye a small garment placed atop a woman's hairnet.

phrases.he: מֵי רַגְלַיִם, נֶתֶר וּבֹרִית, קִמּוֹנְיָא וְאַשְׁלָג, כְּדֵי לְכַבֵּס בָּהֶן בֶּגֶד קָטָן בַּסְּבָכָה.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out urine, natron, and borit, cimolian earth, and potash, all of which are abrasive materials used for laundry, is equivalent to the amount that is used to launder a small garment placed atop a woman's hairnet.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כְּדֵי לְהַעֲבִיר עַל הַכָּתֶם:
phrases.en: And Rabbi Yehuda says: The measure that determines liability for these materials is equivalent to that which is used to remove a stain.

phrases.he: פִּלְפֶּלֶת, כָּל שֶׁהוּא.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out pepper on Shabbat is any amount.

phrases.he: וְעִטְרָן, כָּל שֶׁהוּא.
phrases.en: Similarly, the measure that determines liability for carrying out tar is any amount.

phrases.he: מִינֵי בְשָׂמִים וּמִינֵי מַתָּכוֹת, כָּל שֶׁהֵן.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out various kinds of perfumes and various kinds of metals is any amount.

phrases.he: מֵאַבְנֵי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וּמֵעֲפַר הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, מֶקֶק סְפָרִים וּמֶקֶק מִטְפְּחוֹתֵיהֶם, כָּל שֶׁהוּא, שֶׁמַּצְנִיעִין אוֹתָן לְגָנְזָן.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out stones of the altar or earth of the altar, sacred scrolls or their coverings that became tattered due to an insect called mekek that destroys scrolls, and mekek that destroys their coverings, is any amount. That is because people store them in order to bury them, due to their sanctity, and accord significance to even a small measure of those items.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף הַמּוֹצִיא מִמְּשַׁמְּשֵׁי עֲבוֹדַת כּוֹכָבִים, כָּל שֶׁהוּא, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים יג) וְלֹא יִדְבַּק בְּיָדְךָ מְאוּמָה מִן הַחֵרֶם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: Even one who carries out accessories of idolatry on Shabbat is liable for carrying out any amount, as it is stated: "And there shall cleave nothing of the proscribed items to your hand"

phrases.he: הַמּוֹצִיא קֻפַּת הָרוֹכְלִים, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ מִינִים הַרְבֵּה, אֵינוֹ חַיָּב אֶלָּא חַטָּאת אֶחָת.
phrases.en: One who carries out a merchant's basket, even if there are many types in it, is obligated to bring only one sin-offering.

phrases.he: זֵרְעוֹנֵי גִנָּה, פָּחוֹת מִכַּגְּרוֹגֶרֶת.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out garden seeds on Shabbat is less than a fig-bulk.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר, חֲמִשָּׁה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says: The measure for liability is five seeds.

phrases.he: זֶרַע קִשּׁוּאִין, שְׁנַיִם.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out cucumber seeds is two seeds.

phrases.he: זֶרַע דְּלוּעִין, שְׁנַיִם.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out squash seeds is two seeds.

phrases.he: זֶרַע פּוֹל הַמִּצְרִי, שְׁנַיִם.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out seeds of Egyptian beans is two.

phrases.he: חָגָב חַי טָהוֹר, כָּל שֶׁהוּא.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out a live kosher locust is any amount.

phrases.he: מֵת, כַּגְּרוֹגֶרֶת.
phrases.en: For carrying out a dead kosher locust, which is edible, it is the same as any other food, a fig-bulk.

phrases.he: צִפֹּרֶת כְּרָמִים, בֵּין חַיָּה בֵּין מֵתָה, כָּל שֶׁהוּא, שֶׁמַּצְנִיעִין אוֹתָהּ לִרְפוּאָה.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for carrying out the locust called tzipporet keramim, whether dead or alive, is any amount; this is because one stores them for medicinal purposes.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף הַמּוֹצִיא חָגָב חַי טָמֵא, כָּל שֶׁהוּא, שֶׁמַּצְנִיעִין אוֹתוֹ לְקָטָן לִשְׂחֹק בּוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: Even one who carries out a live non-kosher locust is liable for carrying out any amount, because people store locusts for a child who wants to play with it.

phrases.he: הַמַּצְנִיעַ לְזֶרַע וּלְדֻגְמָא וְלִרְפוּאָה, וְהוֹצִיאוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת, חַיָּב בְּכָל שֶׁהוּא.
phrases.en: One who stores a seed for sowing, or as a sample, or for medicinal purposes and carried it out on Shabbat is liable for carrying out any amount.

phrases.he: וְכָל אָדָם אֵין חַיָּב עָלָיו אֶלָּא כְשִׁעוּרוֹ.
phrases.en: And any other person is only liable for carrying it out on Shabbat if he carries out its measure for liability.

phrases.he: חָזַר וְהִכְנִיסוֹ, אֵינוֹ חַיָּב עָלָיו אֶלָּא כְשִׁעוּרוֹ:
phrases.en: If one stored the seed, carried it out, and then brought it back in, he is only liable if he brought in its measure for liability.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹצִיא אֳכָלִין וּנְתָנָן עַל הָאַסְקֻפָּה,
phrases.en: One who carries out food and placed it on the threshold of the door,

phrases.he: בֵּין שֶׁחָזַר וְהוֹצִיאָן בֵּין שֶׁהוֹצִיאָן אַחֵר, פָּטוּר,
phrases.en: whether he then carried it out or another person carried it out, he is exempt

phrases.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא עָשָׂה מְלַאכְתּוֹ בְּבַת אֶחָת.
phrases.en: because he did not perform his prohibited labor of carrying from domain to domain all at once.

phrases.he: קֻפָּה שֶׁהִיא מְלֵאָה פֵרוֹת וּנְתָנָהּ עַל הָאַסְקֻפָּה הַחִיצוֹנָה,
phrases.en: Similarly, if one placed a basket that is full of fruit on the outer threshold, which is in the public domain, and part of the basket remained inside,

phrases.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרֹב הַפֵּרוֹת מִבַּחוּץ, פָּטוּר,
phrases.en: even though most of the fruit is outside in the public domain, he is exempt

phrases.he: עַד שֶׁיּוֹצִיא אֶת כָּל הַקֻּפָּה:
phrases.en: until he carries out the entire basket.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹצִיא בֵּין בִּימִינוֹ בֵּין בִּשְׂמֹאלוֹ, בְּתוֹךְ חֵיקוֹ אוֹ עַל כְּתֵפוֹ, חַיָּב,
phrases.en: One who carries out whether he carried it out in his right hand or in his left hand, whether he carried it in his lap or on his shoulders, he is liable.

phrases.he: שֶׁכֵּן מַשָּׂא בְנֵי קְהָת.
phrases.en: as this was the method of carrying the sacred vessels of the Tabernacle employed by the sons of Kehat in the desert.

phrases.he: כִּלְאַחַר יָדוֹ, בְּרַגְלוֹ, בְּפִיו וּבְמַרְפְּקוֹ, בְּאָזְנוֹ וּבִשְׂעָרוֹ, וּבְפֻנְדָּתוֹ וּפִיהָ לְמַטָּה, בֵּין פֻּנְדָּתוֹ לַחֲלוּקוֹ, וּבִשְׂפַת חֲלוּקוֹ, בְּמִנְעָלוֹ, בְּסַנְדָּלוֹ, פָּטוּר,
phrases.en: But one who carries an object out in an unusual, backhanded manner, or with his foot, or with his mouth, or with his elbow, with his ear, or with his hair, or with his belt whose opening faced downward, or between his belt and his cloak, or with the hem of his cloak, or with his shoe, or with his sandal, he is exempt

phrases.he: שֶׁלֹּא הוֹצִיא כְּדֶרֶךְ הַמּוֹצִיאִין.
phrases.en: because he did not carry it out in a manner typical of those who carry.

phrases.he: הַמִּתְכַּוֵּן לְהוֹצִיא לְפָנָיו וּבָא לוֹ לְאַחֲרָיו, פָּטוּר,
phrases.en: One who intends to carry out an object with the object before him, and as he was walking the object came to be carried behind him, is exempt.

phrases.he: לְאַחֲרָיו וּבָא לוֹ לְפָנָיו, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: However, if he intended to carry it out behind him and it came to be carried before him, he is liable.

phrases.he: בֶּאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ, הָאִשָּׁה הַחוֹגֶרֶת בְּסִינָר בֵּין מִלְּפָנֶיהָ וּבֵין מִלְּאַחֲרֶיהָ חַיֶּבֶת, שֶׁכֵּן רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת חוֹזֵר.
phrases.en: In truth they said: A woman who girded herself in a pants-like sinar worn beneath the outer garments, whether she placed an object before her or behind her, and it came to be carried on the other side, she is liable, as it is common for the sinar to be reversed.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף מְקַבְּלֵי פִתְקִין:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: Even those royal couriers, who receive notes, are liable.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹצִיא כִכָּר לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: One who carries a large mass out to the public domain on Shabbat is liable.

phrases.he: הוֹצִיאוּהוּ שְׁנַיִם, פְּטוּרִין.
phrases.en: If two carried it out together, they are exempt because neither performed a complete prohibited labor.

phrases.he: לֹא יָכֹל אֶחָד לְהוֹצִיאוֹ וְהוֹצִיאוּהוּ שְׁנַיִם, חַיָּבִים.
phrases.en: However, if one person is unable to carry it out alone, and therefore two people carried it out, they are liable.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן פּוֹטֵר.
phrases.en: And Rabbi Shimon deems them exempt even in that case.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹצִיא אֳכָלִין פָּחוֹת מִכַּשִּׁעוּר בִּכְלִי, פָּטוּר אַף עַל הַכְּלִי, שֶׁהַכְּלִי טְפֵלָה לוֹ.
phrases.en: One who carries out foods less than the measure that determines liability for carrying out food in a vessel on Shabbat is exempt, even for carrying out the vessel, because the vessel is secondary to the food inside it.

phrases.he: אֶת הַחַי בַּמִּטָּה, פָּטוּר אַף עַל הַמִּטָּה, שֶׁהַמִּטָּה טְפֵלָה לוֹ.
phrases.en: Similarly, one who carries out a living person on a bed is exempt, even for carrying out the bed, because the bed is secondary to the person.

phrases.he: אֶת הַמֵּת בַּמִּטָּה, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: One who carries out a corpse on a bed is liable.

phrases.he: וְכֵן כַּזַּיִת מִן הַמֵּת וְכַזַּיִת מִן הַנְּבֵלָה וְכָעֲדָשָׁה מִן הַשֶּׁרֶץ, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: And similarly, one who carries out an olive-bulk of a corpse, or an olive-bulk of an animal carcass, or a lentil-bulk of a creeping animal, which are the minimal measures of these items that transmit ritual impurity, is liable.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן פּוֹטֵר:
phrases.en: And Rabbi Shimon deems him exempt.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹטֵל צִפָּרְנָיו זוֹ בָזוֹ, אוֹ בְשִׁנָּיו,
phrases.en: one who removes his fingernails with one another or with his teeth

phrases.he: וְכֵן שְׂעָרוֹ,
phrases.en: and the same is true with regard to his hair

phrases.he: וְכֵן שְׂפָמוֹ,
phrases.en: and the same is true with regard to his mustache

phrases.he: וְכֵן זְקָנוֹ,
phrases.en: and the same is true with regard to his beard

phrases.he: וְכֵן הַגּוֹדֶלֶת,
phrases.en: and the same is true with regard to a woman who braids her hair

phrases.he: וְכֵן הַכּוֹחֶלֶת,
phrases.en: and the same is true with regard to one who applies blue eye shadow

phrases.he: וְכֵן הַפּוֹקֶסֶת,
phrases.en: and the same is true with regard to one who applies blush

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְחַיֵּב,
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer deems them all liable

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִין מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis prohibited performing all of these actions due to rabbinic decree

phrases.he: הַתּוֹלֵשׁ מֵעָצִיץ נָקוּב, חַיָּב,
phrases.en: One who severs a leaf or a fruit from a plant growing in a perforated flowerpot is liable

phrases.he: וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ נָקוּב, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: And one who picks from an imperforated pot is exempt

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן פּוֹטֵר בָּזֶה וּבָזֶה:
phrases.en: And Rabbi Shimon deems one who does so exempt in this and that

phrases.he: הַזּוֹרֵק מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, מֵרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים לִרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: One who throws from the private domain to the public domain or from the public domain to the private domain is liable.

phrases.he: מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לִרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים בָּאֶמְצַע, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְחַיֵּב, וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹטְרִין.
phrases.en: However, one who throws an object from the private domain to the other private domain, and the object passes through the public domain between the two, Rabbi Akiva deems him liable for carrying into the public domain, and the Rabbis deem him exempt.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: How so?

phrases.he: שְׁתֵּי גְזוּזְטְרָאוֹת זוֹ כְנֶגֶד זוֹ בִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, הַמּוֹשִׁיט וְהַזּוֹרֵק מִזּוֹ לָזוֹ, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: If there are two balconies [gezuztra'ot] that are private domains opposite each other on either side of the public domain, one who passes or throws an object from the one on this side to the one on that side is exempt.

phrases.he: הָיוּ שְׁתֵּיהֶן בִּדְיוֹטָא אַחַת, הַמּוֹשִׁיט חַיָּב, וְהַזּוֹרֵק פָּטוּר, שֶׁכָּךְ הָיְתָה עֲבוֹדַת הַלְוִיִּם, שְׁתֵּי עֲגָלוֹת זוֹ אַחַר זוֹ בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, מוֹשִׁיטִין הַקְּרָשִׁים מִזּוֹ לָזוֹ, אֲבָל לֹא זוֹרְקִין.
phrases.en: However, if the balconies were on the same level on the same side of the public thoroughfare, and the public domain separated the two, one who passes from one to the other is liable, and one who throws is exempt, as that method, passing, was the service of the Levites who carried the beams of the Tabernacle. In the Tabernacle, two wagons along the same level stood behind one another in the public domain, and the Levites passed the beams from one wagon to the other through the public domain on the same side of a thoroughfare. But they did not throw from one wagon to another because the beams were heavy.

phrases.he: חֻלְיַת הַבּוֹר וְהַסֶּלַע שֶׁהֵן גְּבוֹהִין עֲשָׂרָה וְרָחְבָּן אַרְבָּעָה, הַנּוֹטֵל מֵהֶן וְהַנּוֹתֵן עַל גַּבָּן, חַיָּב, פָּחוֹת מִכֵּן, פָּטוּר:
phrases.en: With regard to the bank surrounding a pit and the boulder that are ten handbreadths high and four handbreadths wide, one who takes an object from them to the public domain and similarly one who places an object from the public domain atop them is liable for carrying from one domain to another. If the height or width of the pit or the boulder is less than that height, ten handbreadths, one is exempt because the legal status of those protrusions is not distinct from that of the surrounding public domain.

phrases.he: הַזּוֹרֵק אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת בַּכֹּתֶל, לְמַעְלָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
phrases.en: one who throws an object four cubits in the public domain, if the object hits the wall above ten handbreadths from the ground, which is an exempt domain,

phrases.he: כְּזוֹרֵק בָּאֲוִיר,
phrases.en: it is as if one threw it in the air,

phrases.he: לְמַטָּה מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, כְּזוֹרֵק בָּאָרֶץ.
phrases.en: If it hits the wall below ten handbreadths from the ground, it is as if he threw it and it landed on the ground,

phrases.he: הַזּוֹרֵק בָּאָרֶץ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: and one who throws an object four cubits and it lands on the ground is liable.

phrases.he: זָרַק לְתוֹךְ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וְנִתְגַּלְגֵּל חוּץ לְאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: If one threw an object in the public domain, intending for it to land within four cubits, meaning that he had no intention of violating the Torah prohibition of carrying, and the object rolled and went beyond four cubits, he is exempt.

phrases.he: חוּץ לְאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, וְנִתְגַּלְגֵּל לְתוֹךְ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, חַיָּב:
phrases.en: However, if one threw an object with the intention of it landing beyond four cubits, and the object rolled back within four cubits, he is liable from when he originally threw the object.

phrases.he: הַזּוֹרֵק בַּיָּם אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: One who throws an object four cubits into the sea is exempt.

phrases.he: אִם הָיָה רְקָק מַיִם וּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים מְהַלֶּכֶת בּוֹ, הַזּוֹרֵק לְתוֹכוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: If there was a swamp and the public domain passes through it, one who throws an object four cubits into it is liable.

phrases.he: וְכַמָּה הוּא רְקָק מַיִם, פָּחוֹת מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים.
phrases.en: And how is this swamp? It is less than ten handbreadths deep.

phrases.he: רְקָק מַיִם וּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים מְהַלֶּכֶת בּוֹ, הַזּוֹרֵק בְּתוֹכוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, חַיָּב:
phrases.en: In the case of a swamp that the public domain passes through, one who throws an object four cubits into the swamp is liable.

phrases.he: הַזּוֹרֵק מִן הַיָּם לַיַּבָּשָׁה וּמִן הַיַּבָּשָׁה לַיָּם, וּמִן הַיָּם לַסְּפִינָה וּמִן הַסְּפִינָה לַיָּם, וּמִן הַסְּפִינָה לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: One who throws an object from the sea to dry land, or from dry land to the sea, or from the sea onto a boat, or from a boat into the sea, or from one boat to another is exempt

phrases.he: סְפִינוֹת קְשׁוּרוֹת זוֹ בָזוֹ, מְטַלְטְלִין מִזּוֹ לָזוֹ.
phrases.en: If boats are tied together, one may carry an object from one to the other on Shabbat

phrases.he: אִם אֵינָן קְשׁוּרוֹת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמֻּקָּפוֹת, אֵין מְטַלְטְלִין מִזּוֹ לָזוֹ:
phrases.en: However, if they are not tied, even though they are adjacent, one may not carry from one to the other

phrases.he: הַזּוֹרֵק וְנִזְכַּר לְאַחַר שֶׁיָּצְתָה מִיָּדוֹ, קְלָטָהּ אַחֵר, קְלָטָהּ כֶּלֶב, אוֹ שֶׁנִּשְׂרְפָה, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: One who unwittingly throws an object from one domain to another or one who throws an object four cubits within the public domain, and after the object left his hand he remembered that he is in violation of a prohibition, if another caught it, or if a dog caught it, or if it was burned, he is exempt.

phrases.he: זָרַק לַעֲשׂוֹת חַבּוּרָה, בֵּין בְּאָדָם בֵּין בִּבְהֵמָה, וְנִזְכַּר עַד שֶׁלֹּא נַעֲשָׂה חַבּוּרָה, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: Similarly, if one threw a rock on Shabbat to inflict a wound on a person or on an animal, for which one is liable to bring a sin-offering, and he remembered that he was in violation of a prohibition before the wound was inflicted, he is exempt.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל חַיָּבֵי חַטָּאוֹת אֵינָן חַיָּבִין עַד שֶׁתְּהֵא תְחִלָּתָן וְסוֹפָן שְׁגָגָה.
phrases.en: This is the principle: All who are liable to bring sin-offerings are only liable if the beginning of their action and the conclusion of their action are unwitting.

phrases.he: תְּחִלָּתָן שְׁגָגָה וְסוֹפָן זָדוֹן, תְּחִלָּתָן זָדוֹן וְסוֹפָן שְׁגָגָה, פְּטוּרִין, עַד שֶׁתְּהֵא תְחִלָּתָן וְסוֹפָן שְׁגָגָה:
phrases.en: However, if the beginning of one's action was unwitting and the conclusion was intentional, as he became aware that he was in violation of a prohibition, or if the beginning of one's action was intentional and the conclusion was unwitting, the individuals in both of these cases are exempt until both the beginning and the conclusion are unwitting.

phrases.he: הַבּוֹנֶה, כַּמָּה יִבְנֶה וִיהֵא חַיָּב
phrases.en: one who builds on Shabbat, thereby violating a prohibition in a primary category of prohibited labor, how much must he build to be liable to bring a sin-offering?

phrases.he: הַבּוֹנֶה כָּל שֶׁהוּא, וְהַמְסַתֵּת, וְהַמַּכֶּה בַפַּטִּישׁ וּבְמַעֲצָד, הַקּוֹדֵחַ כָּל שֶׁהוּא, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: One who builds is liable for building any amount. And one who chisels, or strikes with a hammer or with an adze, or one who drills a hole of any size on Shabbat, is liable.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל הָעוֹשֶׂה מְלָאכָה וּמְלַאכְתּוֹ מִתְקַיֶּמֶת בְּשַׁבָּת, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: This is the principle: Anyone who performs a prohibited labor and his labor endures on Shabbat is liable.

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, אַף הַמַּכֶּה בְקֻרְנָס עַל הַסַּדָּן בִּשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה, חַיָּב, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא כִמְתַקֵּן מְלָאכָה:
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: Even one who strikes an anvil with a sledgehammer during his labor has performed a constructive act and is liable, because he is as one who improves the labor that he is performing.

phrases.he: הַחוֹרֵשׁ כָּל שֶׁהוּא, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: One who plows is liable for plowing any amount of land on Shabbat.

phrases.he: הַמְנַכֵּשׁ וְהַמְקַרְסֵם וְהַמְזָרֵד כָּל שֶׁהוּא, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: One who weeds and removes grass on Shabbat, and one who removes dry branches and who prunes any amount is liable.

phrases.he: הַמְלַקֵּט עֵצִים, אִם לְתַקֵּן, כָּל שֶׁהֵן, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: With regard to one who gathers wood, if he did so to enhance the tree or the land, he is liable for any amount.

phrases.he: אִם לְהֶסֵּק, כְּדֵי לְבַשֵּׁל בֵּיצָה קַלָּה, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: If he did so for fuel, he is liable for collecting a measure equivalent to that which is used to cook an easily cooked egg.

phrases.he: הַמְלַקֵּט עֲשָׂבִים, אִם לְתַקֵּן, כָּל שֶׁהוּא, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: With regard to one who gathers grass, if he did so to enhance the plants or the land, he is liable for any amount.

phrases.he: אִם לִבְהֵמָה, כִּמְלֹא פִי הַגְּדִי, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: If he did so to feed an animal, he is liable for collecting a measure equivalent to a goat's mouthful.

phrases.he: הַכּוֹתֵב שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת, בֵּין בִּימִינוֹ בֵּין בִּשְׂמֹאלוֹ, בֵּין מִשֵּׁם אֶחָד בֵּין מִשְּׁנֵי שֵׁמוֹת, בֵּין מִשְּׁנֵי סַמְמָנִיּוֹת, בְּכָל לָשׁוֹן, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: One who writes two letters whether he did so with his right hand or his left, whether they were the same letter or two different letters, whether he did so using two different types of ink, in any language, he is liable.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, לֹא חִיְּבוּ שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם רֹשֶׁם, שֶׁכָּךְ הָיוּ כוֹתְבִין עַל קַרְשֵׁי הַמִּשְׁכָּן, לֵידַע אֵיזוֹ בֶן זוּגוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei said: One is deemed liable for writing two letters only due to marking, as they would write symbols on adjacent beams of the Tabernacle to know which beam was another beam's counterpart.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי, מָצִינוּ שֵׁם קָטָן מִשֵּׁם גָּדוֹל, שֵׁם מִשִּׁמְעוֹן וּשְׁמוּאֵל, נֹחַ מִנָּחוֹר, דָּן מִדָּנִיֵּאל, גָּד מִגַּדִּיאֵל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda said: We found that one is liable for writing even if he did not complete what he was writing, so that he wrote a small name that constituted part of a longer name, e.g., Shem from the name Shimon or from Shmuel; Noaḥ from Naḥor; Dan from Daniel; Gad from Gaddiel.

phrases.he: הַכּוֹתֵב שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת בְּהֶעְלֵם אֶחָד, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: One who writes two letters during one lapse of awareness is liable.

phrases.he: כָּתַב בִּדְיוֹ, בְּסַם, בְּסִקְרָא, בְּקוֹמוֹס וּבְקַנְקַנְתּוֹם, וּבְכָל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא רוֹשֵׁם,
phrases.en: he wrote with deyo, with sam, with sikra, with gum [komos], or with copper sulfate [kankantom] or with any substance that makes a mark.

phrases.he: עַל שְׁנֵי כָתְלֵי זָוִיּוֹת וְעַל שְׁנֵי לוּחֵי פִנְקָס, וְהֵן נֶהְגִּין זֶה עִם זֶה, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: on two walls of a house that form a corner, or on two parts of a writing tablet, and the two items are read together, he is liable.

phrases.he: הַכּוֹתֵב עַל בְּשָׂרוֹ, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: One who writes on his flesh is liable.

phrases.he: הַמְסָרֵט עַל בְּשָׂרוֹ, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְחַיֵּב חַטָּאת, וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ פּוֹטֵר:
phrases.en: If one unwittingly scratches letters on his flesh on Shabbat, Rabbi Eliezer deems him liable to bring a sin-offering and Rabbi Yehoshua deems him exempt.

phrases.he: כָּתַב בְּמַשְׁקִין, בְּמֵי פֵרוֹת, בַּאֲבַק דְּרָכִים, בַּאֲבַק הַסּוֹפְְרִים, וּבְכָל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְקַיֵּם, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: If one wrote with liquids or with fruit juice, or if one drew letters with road dust, with scribes' dust that they use to dry the ink, or with any substance with which the writing does not endure, he is exempt.

phrases.he: לְאַחַר יָדוֹ, בְּרַגְלוֹ, בְּפִיו וּבְמַרְפְּקוֹ, כָּתַב אוֹת אַחַת סָמוּךְ לִכְתָב, וּכְתָב עַל גַּבֵּי כְתָב, נִתְכַּוֵּן לִכְתֹּב חֵי״ת וְכָתַב שְׁנֵי זַיְ״נִין, אֶחָד בָּאָרֶץ וְאֶחָד בַּקּוֹרָה, כָּתַב עַל שְׁנֵי כָתְלֵי הַבַּיִת, עַל שְׁנֵי דַפֵּי פִנְקָס וְאֵין נֶהְגִּין זֶה עִם זֶה, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: Similarly, if one wrote by holding the pen on the back of his hand, with his foot, with his mouth, or with his elbow; if one wrote only a single letter, even if it was adjacent to other preexisting writing; or if one wrote over other writing; if one meant to write the letter ḥet and instead wrote the two halves of the ḥet as two instances of the letter zayin; if one wrote one letter on the ground and one on a rafter; if one wrote one letter on two walls of a house, or on two parts of a writing tablet that are not read together, he is exempt.

phrases.he: כָּתַב אוֹת אַחַת נוֹטָרִיקוֹן, רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן בְּתֵירָא מְחַיֵּב, וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹטְרִין.
phrases.en: If one wrote one letter as an abbreviation representing an entire word, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Beteira deems him liable to bring a sin-offering, and the Rabbis deem him exempt.

phrases.he: הַכּוֹתֵב שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת בִּשְׁנֵי הֶעְלֵמוֹת, אַחַת שַׁחֲרִית וְאַחַת בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם,
phrases.en: one who writes two letters in two separate lapses of awareness separated by a period of awareness that the day was Shabbat, writing one letter in the morning and one letter in the afternoon

phrases.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מְחַיֵּב,
phrases.en: Rabban Gamliel deems him liable

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹטְרִין:
phrases.en: and the Rabbis deem him exempt

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, הָאוֹרֵג שְׁלשָׁה חוּטִין בַּתְּחִלָּה וְאַחַת עַל הָאָרִיג, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: One who weaves on Shabbat is liable to bring a sin-offering if he wove three threads at the beginning of something new, or if he adds one thread to a preexisting woven fabric.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בֵּין בַּתְּחִלָּה בֵּין בַּסּוֹף, שִׁעוּרוֹ שְׁנֵי חוּטִין.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: Both at the beginning and at the end, its measure for liability is two threads.

phrases.he: הָעוֹשֶׂה שְׁנֵי בָתֵּי נִירִין בַּנִּירִין, בַּקֵּרוֹס, בַּנָּפָה, בַּכְּבָרָה וּבַסַּל, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: to the nirin or the keiros, in a winnow, sieve, or basket, is liable

phrases.he: וְהַתּוֹפֵר שְׁתֵּי תְפִירוֹת,
phrases.en: And one who sews two stitches

phrases.he: וְהַקּוֹרֵעַ עַל מְנָת לִתְפֹּר שְׁתֵּי תְפִירוֹת:
phrases.en: And one who tears in order to sew two stitches

phrases.he: הַקּוֹרֵעַ בַּחֲמָתוֹ וְעַל מֵתוֹ,
phrases.en: One who rends his garment in his anger or in anguish over his dead relative

phrases.he: וְכָל הַמְקַלְקְלִין, פְּטוּרִין.
phrases.en: And anyone else who performs labors destructively on Shabbat is exempt.

phrases.he: וְהַמְקַלְקֵל עַל מְנָת לְתַקֵּן, שִׁעוּרוֹ כַמְתַקֵּן:
phrases.en: And one who performs a labor destructively in order to repair is liable, and his measure for liability is equivalent to the measure for one who performs that labor constructively.

phrases.he: שִׁעוּר הַמְלַבֵּן וְהַמְנַפֵּץ וְהַצּוֹבֵעַ וְהַטּוֹוֶה, כִּמְלֹא רֹחַב הַסִּיט כָּפוּל.
phrases.en: The measure that determines liability for one who whitens, or one who combs, or one who dyes, or one who spins wool is the full width of a double sit, which is the distance between the forefinger and the middle finger.

phrases.he: וְהָאוֹרֵג שְׁנֵי חוּטִין, שִׁעוּרוֹ כִּמְלֹא הַסִּיט:
phrases.en: And for one who weaves two threads, the measure that determines liability is one sit.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הַצָּד צִפּוֹר לַמִּגְדָּל וּצְבִי לַבַּיִת, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: One who traps a bird into a closet and one who traps a deer into a house is liable.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, צִפּוֹר לַמִּגְדָּל, וּצְבִי לַבַּיִת וְלֶחָצֵר וְלַבֵּיבָרִין.
phrases.en: The Rabbis say: One is liable for trapping a bird into a closet and for trapping a deer into a garden, or into a courtyard, or into an enclosure.

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, לֹא כָל הַבֵּיבָרִין שָׁוִין.
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: Not all enclosures are identical.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, מְחֻסַּר צִידָה, פָּטוּר, וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מְחֻסַּר צִידָה, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: This is the principle: If the trapping of the animal is inadequate and it is still necessary to pursue and apprehend it, one is not liable. However, if one trapped a deer into an enclosure in which the trapping is not inadequate, he is liable.

phrases.he: צְבִי שֶׁנִּכְנַס לַבַּיִת וְנָעַל אֶחָד בְּפָנָיו, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: a deer entered a house on its own and one locked the door before it, he is liable for trapping.

phrases.he: נָעֲלוּ שְׁנַיִם, פְּטוּרִין.
phrases.en: two people locked the door, they are exempt, because neither performed a complete labor.

phrases.he: לֹא יָכֹל אֶחָד לִנְעֹל וְנָעֲלוּ שְׁנַיִם, חַיָּבִין.
phrases.en: one person is incapable of locking the door and two people locked it, they are liable because that is the typical manner of performing that labor.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן פּוֹטֵר:
phrases.en: And Rabbi Shimon deems them exempt as he holds that two people who perform a single labor are never liable by Torah law.

phrases.he: יָשַׁב הָאֶחָד עַל הַפֶּתַח וְלֹא מִלְּאָהוּ, יָשַׁב הַשֵּׁנִי וּמִלְּאָהוּ, הַשֵּׁנִי חַיָּב.
phrases.en: one person sat in the entrance but did not fill the entire doorway, and a second person sat and filled it, the second person is liable

phrases.he: יָשַׁב הָרִאשׁוֹן עַל הַפֶּתַח וּמִלְּאָהוּ, וּבָא הַשֵּׁנִי וְיָשַׁב בְּצִדּוֹ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעָמַד הָרִאשׁוֹן וְהָלַךְ לוֹ, הָרִאשׁוֹן חַיָּב וְהַשֵּׁנִי פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: the first person sat in the doorway and filled it, and a second person came and sat next to him, the first person is liable and the second is exempt even if the first person stood and went away

phrases.he: הָא לְמַה זֶּה דוֹמֶה, לְנוֹעֵל אֶת בֵּיתוֹ לְשָׁמְרוֹ וְנִמְצָא צְבִי שָׁמוּר בְּתוֹכוֹ:
phrases.en: To what is this similar? To one who locks his house to secure it, and it turns out a deer is also secured inside it

phrases.he: שְׁמֹנָה שְׁרָצִים הָאֲמוּרִים בַּתּוֹרָה, הַצָּדָן וְהַחוֹבֵל בָּהֶן, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: the eight creeping animals mentioned in the Torah, one who traps them or wounds them is liable.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר שְׁקָצִים וּרְמָשִׂים, הַחוֹבֵל בָּהֶן פָּטוּר, הַצָּדָן לְצֹרֶךְ, חַיָּב, שֶׁלֹּא לְצֹרֶךְ, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: other abominations and crawling things, one who wounds them is exempt. One who traps them for a specific need is liable; one who traps them for no specific need is exempt.

phrases.he: חַיָּה וְעוֹף שֶׁבִּרְשׁוּתוֹ, הַצָּדָן פָּטוּר, וְהַחוֹבֵל בָּהֶן חַיָּב:
phrases.en: animals or birds that are in his possession, one who traps them is exempt; and, one who wounds them is liable.

phrases.he: אֵין עוֹשִׂין הִילְמִי בְשַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: One may not make brine on Shabbat,

phrases.he: אֲבָל עוֹשֶׂה הוּא אֶת מֵי הַמֶּלַח וְטוֹבֵל בָּהֶן פִּתּוֹ וְנוֹתֵן לְתוֹךְ הַתַּבְשִׁיל.
phrases.en: but one may make salt water and dip one's bread in it, and place it in cooked food.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, וַהֲלֹא הוּא הִילְמִי, בֵּין מְרֻבֶּה וּבֵין מֻעָט.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei said: But isn't it still brine, whether it is a large quantity or whether it is a small quantity?

phrases.he: וְאֵלוּ הֵן מֵי מֶלַח הַמֻּתָּרִין, נוֹתֵן שֶׁמֶן בַּתְּחִלָּה לְתוֹךְ הַמַּיִם אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַמֶּלַח:
phrases.en: And this is the type of salt water that is permitted: Salt water in which one places oil initially into the water or into the salt.

phrases.he: אֵין אוֹכְלִין אֵזוֹב יוֹן בְּשַׁבָּת, לְפִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַאֲכַל בְּרִיאִים,
phrases.en: One may not eat eizoveyon on Shabbat because healthy people do not eat it,

phrases.he: אֲבָל אוֹכֵל הוּא אֶת יוֹעֶזֶר וְשׁוֹתֶה אַבּוּב רוֹעֶה.
phrases.en: However, one may eat a plant called yo'ezer and may drink abuvro'e.

phrases.he: כָּל הָאֳכָלִין אוֹכֵל אָדָם לִרְפוּאָה,
phrases.en: All types of food that healthy people eat may be eaten by a person even for medicinal purposes.

phrases.he: וְכָל הַמַּשְׁקִין שׁוֹתֶה, חוּץ מִמֵּי דְקָלִים וְכוֹס עִקָּרִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן לַיְרוֹקָה.
phrases.en: And one may drink all drinks except for water from palm trees and a kos ikarin because they are known as a remedy for jaundice.

phrases.he: אֲבָל שׁוֹתֶה הוּא מֵי דְקָלִים לִצְמָאוֹ,
phrases.en: However, one may drink palm tree water in order to quench his thirst,

phrases.he: וְסָךְ שֶׁמֶן עִקָּרִין שֶׁלֹּא לִרְפוּאָה:
phrases.en: and one may smear ikarin oil for non-medical purposes.

phrases.he: הַחוֹשֵׁשׁ בְּשִׁנָּיו, לֹא יִגְמַע בָּהֶן אֶת הַחֹמֶץ,
phrases.en: One who is concerned about pain in his teeth may not sip vinegar through them

phrases.he: אֲבָל מְטַבֵּל הוּא כְדַרְכּוֹ,
phrases.en: however, he may dip his food in vinegar in his usual manner

phrases.he: וְאִם נִתְרַפֵּא נִתְרַפֵּא.
phrases.en: and if he is healed by the vinegar, he is healed

phrases.he: הַחוֹשֵׁשׁ בְּמָתְנָיו, לֹא יָסוּךְ יַיִן וְחֹמֶץ,
phrases.en: One who is concerned about pain in his loins may not smear wine and vinegar on them

phrases.he: אֲבָל סָךְ הוּא אֶת הַשֶּׁמֶן,
phrases.en: However, one may smear oil on them

phrases.he: וְלֹא שֶׁמֶן וֶרֶד.
phrases.en: However, one may not use rose oil,

phrases.he: בְּנֵי מְלָכִים סָכִין שֶׁמֶן וֶרֶד עַל מַכּוֹתֵיהֶן,
phrases.en: princes may smear with rose oil on their wounds

phrases.he: שֶׁכֵּן דַּרְכָּם לָסוּךְ בַּחֹל.
phrases.en: because it is their usual manner to smear rose oil on themselves during the week

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּנֵי מְלָכִים הֵם:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: All of the Jewish people are princes,

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ קְשָׁרִים שֶׁחַיָּבִין עֲלֵיהֶן, קֶשֶׁר הַגַּמָּלִין וְקֶשֶׁר הַסַּפָּנִין.
phrases.en: And these are knots for which one is liable to bring a sin-offering if one tied them on Shabbat: A camel driver's knot and a sailor's knot, both of which are meant to be permanent.

phrases.he: וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁהוּא חַיָּב עַל קִשּׁוּרָן כָּךְ הוּא חַיָּב עַל הֶתֵּרָן.
phrases.en: And just as one is liable to bring a sin-offering for tying these knots, so too, he is liable to bring a sin-offering for untying them.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, כָּל קֶשֶׁר שֶׁהוּא יָכוֹל לְהַתִּירוֹ בְאַחַת מִיָּדָיו, אֵין חַיָּבִין עָלָיו:
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says a principle: For any knot that one can untie with one of his hands, one is not liable to bring a sin-offering, because a loose knot of that sort is not considered permanent even if that was his intention.

phrases.he: יֵשׁ לְךָ קְשָׁרִים שֶׁאֵין חַיָּבִין עֲלֵיהֶן כְּקֶשֶׁר הַגַּמָּלִין וּכְקֶשֶׁר הַסַּפָּנִין.
phrases.en: You have knots for which one is not liable as one is liable for tying a camel driver's knot and a sailor's knot

phrases.he: קוֹשֶׁרֶת אִשָּׁה מִפְתַּח חֲלוּקָהּ, וְחוּטֵי סְבָכָה וְשֶׁל פְּסִיקְיָא, וּרְצוּעוֹת מִנְעָל וְסַנְדָּל, וְנוֹדוֹת יַיִן וָשֶׁמֶן, וּקְדֵרָה שֶׁל בָּשָׂר.
phrases.en: A woman may tie closed the opening of her robe with straps, as well as the strings of her hairnet and the laces of her girdle, i.e., a wide belt tied with laces. One may also tie the straps of a shoe or a sandal, as well as the spouts of wine or oil jugs. One may also tie a garment over a pot of meat.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר, קוֹשְׁרִין לִפְנֵי הַבְּהֵמָה בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא תֵצֵא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says: One may tie a rope across an entrance before an animal so that it will not go out.

phrases.he: קוֹשְׁרִין דְּלִי בִּפְסִיקְיָא, אֲבָל לֹא בְחֶבֶל.
phrases.en: One may tie a bucket with a belt on Shabbat, as he will certainly not leave it tied to the bucket, and therefore it is not a permanent knot. But one may not tie a bucket with a rope.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda permits doing so.

phrases.he: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, כָּל קֶשֶׁר שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁל קְיָמָא, אֵין חַיָּבִין עָלָיו:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda stated a principle: With regard to any knot that is not permanent, one is not liable for tying it.

phrases.he: מְקַפְּלִין אֶת הַכֵּלִים אֲפִלּוּ אַרְבָּעָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה פְעָמִים,
phrases.en: One may fold the garments even four or five times,

phrases.he: וּמַצִּיעִין אֶת הַמִּטּוֹת מִלֵּילֵי שַׁבָּת לְשַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: and one may make the beds from Shabbat evening for Shabbat day,

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא מִשַּׁבָּת לְמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: but not from Shabbat for the conclusion of Shabbat,

phrases.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, מְקַפְּלִין אֶת הַכֵּלִים וּמַצִּיעִין אֶת הַמִּטּוֹת מִיּוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים לְשַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yishmael says: One may fold the garments and make the beds from Yom Kippur for Shabbat

phrases.he: וְחֶלְבֵי שַׁבָּת קְרֵבִין בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
phrases.en: And the fats of Shabbat are offered on Yom Kippur,

phrases.he: (אֲבָל לֹא שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים בְּשַׁבָּת).
phrases.en: but not those of Yom Kippur on Shabbat,

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר לֹא שֶׁל שַׁבָּת קְרֵבִין בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: Neither are the fats of Shabbat offered on Yom Kippur,

phrases.he: וְלֹא שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים קְרֵבִין בְּשַׁבָּת:
phrases.en: nor are those of Yom Kippur offered on Shabbat.

phrases.he: כָּל כִּתְבֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ מַצִּילִין אוֹתָן מִפְּנֵי הַדְּלֵקָה, בֵּין שֶׁקּוֹרִין בָּהֶן וּבֵין שֶׁאֵין קוֹרִין בָּהֶן.
phrases.en: all sacred writings, one may rescue them from the fire, whether they are read in public, or whether they are not read in public

phrases.he: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכְּתוּבִים בְּכָל לָשׁוֹן, טְעוּנִים גְּנִיזָה.
phrases.en: even though they were written in any foreign language, they require burial

phrases.he: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין קוֹרִין בָּהֶן, מִפְּנֵי בִטּוּל בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ.
phrases.en: And why does one not read the Writings on Shabbat? Due to suspension of Torah study in the study hall

phrases.he: מַצִּילִין תִּיק הַסֵּפֶר עִם הַסֵּפֶר, וְתִיק הַתְּפִלִּין עִם הַתְּפִלִּין, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּתוֹכָן מָעוֹת.
phrases.en: One may rescue the casing of a Torah scroll from a fire on Shabbat together with the Torah scroll, and the casing of phylacteries along with the phylacteries, even if they have money inside them

phrases.he: וּלְהֵיכָן מַצִּילִין אוֹתָן, לְמָבוֹי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְפֻלָּשׁ.
phrases.en: And to where may one rescue them? Into an alley that is closed

phrases.he: בֶּן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר, אַף לִמְפֻלָּשׁ:
phrases.en: Ben Beteira says: Even into an open alley

phrases.he: מַצִּילִין מְזוֹן שָׁלשׁ סְעֻדּוֹת,
phrases.en: One may rescue food for three meals

phrases.he: הָרָאוּי לְאָדָם לְאָדָם,
phrases.en: that is suitable for a person for a person;

phrases.he: הָרָאוּי לִבְהֵמָה לִבְהֵמָה.
phrases.en: that is suitable for an animal for an animal.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: How so?

phrases.he: נָפְלָה דְלֵקָה בְלֵילֵי שַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: If a fire ignited on Friday night

phrases.he: מַצִּילִין מְזוֹן שָׁלשׁ סְעֻדּוֹת,
phrases.en: one may rescue food for three meals.

phrases.he: בְּשַׁחֲרִית,
phrases.en: If a fire ignited in the morning,

phrases.he: מַצִּילִין מְזוֹן שְׁתֵּי סְעֻדּוֹת,
phrases.en: one may only rescue food for two meals.

phrases.he: בְּמִנְחָה,
phrases.en: If a fire ignited in the afternoon,

phrases.he: מְזוֹן סְעֻדָּה אֶחָת.
phrases.en: one may rescue food for one meal.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, לְעוֹלָם מַצִּילִין מְזוֹן שָׁלשׁ סְעֻדּוֹת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: One may always rescue food for three meals,

phrases.he: מַצִּילִין סַל מָלֵא כִכָּרוֹת,
phrases.en: One may rescue a basket full of loaves

phrases.he: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ מֵאָה סְעֻדּוֹת,
phrases.en: even if there is food for one hundred meals in it.

phrases.he: וְעִגּוּל שֶׁל דְּבֵלָה,
phrases.en: And one may rescue a round cake of dried figs,

phrases.he: וְחָבִית שֶׁל יַיִן.
phrases.en: and one may rescue a barrel full of wine.

phrases.he: וְאוֹמֵר לַאֲחֵרִים, בֹּאוּ וְהַצִּילוּ לָכֶם.
phrases.en: And one may even say to others: Come and rescue for yourselves.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיוּ פִקְחִין, עוֹשִׂין עִמּוֹ חֶשְׁבּוֹן אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.en: And if the people who rescue with him were clever, they make a calculation with him after Shabbat in order to receive payment for the items that they rescued.

phrases.he: לְהֵיכָן מַצִּילִין אוֹתָן, לְחָצֵר הַמְעֹרֶבֶת.
phrases.en: To where may one rescue items moved from the fire? One may do so to a courtyard where an eiruv was established, and it is permitted to carry.

phrases.he: בֶּן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר, אַף לְשֶׁאֵינָהּ מְעֹרָבֶת:
phrases.en: Ben Beteira says: One may do so even to a courtyard where an eiruv was not established.

phrases.he: וּלְשָׁם מוֹצִיא כָל כְּלֵי תַשְׁמִישׁוֹ, וְלוֹבֵשׁ כָּל מַה שֶּׁיָּכוֹל לִלְבּשׁ, וְעוֹטֵף כָּל מַה שֶּׁיָּכוֹל לַעֲטֹף.
phrases.en: And one may carry there all the utensils, and put on all the garments that he can wear, and one may wrap all the cloths that he can wrap around himself in order to rescue his property.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, שְׁמֹנָה עָשָׂר כֵּלִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: One may put on only eighteen garments at once, as people sometimes wear that number of garments, but not more.

phrases.he: וְחוֹזֵר וְלוֹבֵשׁ וּמוֹצִיא, וְאוֹמֵר לַאֲחֵרִים, בֹּאוּ וְהַצִּילוּ עִמִּי:
phrases.en: However, one may again put on that number of garments and carry it out. And he may say to others: Come and rescue with me.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן נַנָּס אוֹמֵר, פּוֹרְסִין עוֹר שֶׁל גְּדִי עַל גַּבֵּי שִׁדָּה תֵּבָה וּמִגְדָּל שֶׁאָחַז בָּהֶן אֶת הָאוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מְחָרֵךְ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Nannas says: One may spread out a moist goat's hide over a box, a chest, or a closet that caught fire, because the fire singes and does not burn it.

phrases.he: וְעוֹשִׂין מְחִצָּה בְּכָל הַכֵּלִים, בֵּין מְלֵאִים בֵּין רֵיקָנִים, בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא תַעֲבֹר הַדְּלֵקָה.
phrases.en: And one may establish a barrier against the fire with all vessels, both full and empty, so that the fire will not pass.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹסֵר בִּכְלֵי חֶרֶס חֲדָשִׁים מְלֵאִין מַיִם, לְפִי שֶׁאֵין יְכוֹלִין לְקַבֵּל אֶת הָאוּר וְהֵן מִתְבַּקְּעִין וּמְכַבִּין אֶת הַדְּלֵקָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei prohibits using new earthenware vessels full of water, because they cannot withstand the heat of the fire and they will burst and extinguish the fire.

phrases.he: נָכְרִי שֶׁבָּא לְכַבּוֹת, אֵין אוֹמְרִים לוֹ כַּבֵּה וְאַל תְּכַבֶּה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין שְׁבִיתָתוֹ עֲלֵיהֶן,
phrases.en: a gentile comes to extinguish a Jew's fire on Shabbat, one may not say to him: Extinguish, and: Do not extinguish, because responsibility for his rest is not incumbent upon the Jew.

phrases.he: אֲבָל קָטָן שֶׁבָּא לְכַבּוֹת, אֵין שׁוֹמְעִין לוֹ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁשְּׁבִיתָתוֹ עֲלֵיהֶן:
