phrases.en: However, if a Jewish child comes to extinguish a fire on Shabbat, they do not listen to him and allow him to extinguish it, even though he is not yet obligated in mitzva observance, because responsibility for his rest is incumbent upon the Jew.

phrases.he: כּוֹפִין קְעָרָה עַל גַּבֵּי הַנֵּר בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא תֶאֱחֹז בַּקּוֹרָה,
phrases.en: One may overturn a bowl on top of a lamp so that fire will not take hold in the ceiling beam on Shabbat.

phrases.he: וְעַל צוֹאָה שֶׁל קָטָן,
phrases.en: And similarly, one may overturn a bowl on top of a child's feces inside the house so he will not touch it and dirty himself,

phrases.he: וְעַל עַקְרָב שֶׁלֹּא תִשֹּׁךְ.
phrases.en: and on top of a scorpion so that it will not bite.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, מַעֲשֶׂה בָא לִפְנֵי רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי בַּעֲרָב,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda said: An incident came before Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai in his village of Arav,

phrases.he: וְאָמַר, חוֹשְׁשָׁנִי לוֹ מֵחַטָּאת:
phrases.en: and Rabban Yoḥanan said: I am concerned that he is liable to bring a sin-offering because he might have violated a Torah prohibition.

phrases.he: נָכְרִי שֶׁהִדְלִיק אֶת הַנֵּר, מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ לְאוֹרוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאִם בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל, אָסוּר.
phrases.en: If a gentile kindled a lamp on Shabbat for his own purposes, a Jew also uses its light; and if the gentile kindled it for a Jew, the Sages prohibited to utilize its light.

phrases.he: מִלֵּא מַיִם לְהַשְׁקוֹת בְּהֶמְתּוֹ, מַשְׁקֶה אַחֲרָיו יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאִם בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל, אָסוּר.
phrases.en: Similarly, if a gentile drew water from a well in the public domain to give his animal to drink, a Jew gives his own animal to drink after him from the same water; and if he drew the water initially for the benefit of a Jew, it is prohibited for a Jew to give his animal to drink from that water.

phrases.he: עָשָׂה גוֹי כֶּבֶשׁ לֵירֵד בּוֹ, יוֹרֵד אַחֲרָיו יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאִם בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל, אָסוּר.
phrases.en: Similarly, if a gentile made a ramp on Shabbat to disembark from a ship, a Jew disembarks after him; and if he made the ramp for a Jew, it is prohibited.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וּזְקֵנִים שֶׁהָיוּ בָאִין בִּסְפִינָה, וְעָשָׂה גוֹי כֶּבֶשׁ לֵירֵד בּוֹ, וְיָרְדוּ בוֹ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וּזְקֵנִים:
phrases.en: There was an incident in which Rabban Gamliel and the Elders were traveling on a ship and a gentile made a ramp on Shabbat in order to disembark from the ship on it; and Rabban Gamliel and the Elders disembarked on it as well.

phrases.he: כָּל הַכֵּלִים נִטָּלִין בְּשַׁבָּת וְדַלְתוֹתֵיהֶם עִמָּהֶן, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּתְפָּרְקוּ בְשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: All vessels may be moved on Shabbat, and their doors, which are part of these vessels, along with them, even if they were dismantled on Shabbat, as

phrases.he: שֶׁאֵינָן דּוֹמִין לְדַלְתוֹת הַבַּיִת, לְפִי שֶׁאֵינָן מִן הַמּוּכָן:
phrases.en: the doors of these vessels are unlike the doors of the house. because they are not prepared

phrases.he: נוֹטֵל אָדָם קֻרְנָס לְפַצֵּעַ בּוֹ אֶת הָאֱגוֹזִים,
phrases.en: a person may move a mallet to crack nuts with it.

phrases.he: וְקֻרְדֹּם לַחְתֹּךְ אֶת הַדְּבֵלָה.
phrases.en: an axe to cut a cake of figs with it.

phrases.he: מְגֵרָה, לִגְרֹר בָּהּ אֶת הַגְּבִינָה.
phrases.en: a saw to cut cheese with it.

phrases.he: מַגְרֵפָה, לִגְרֹף בָּהּ אֶת הַגְּרוֹגָרוֹת.
phrases.en: a spade to scoop dried figs with it.

phrases.he: אֶת הָרַחַת וְאֶת הַמַּזְלֵג, לָתֵת עָלָיו לְקָטָן.
phrases.en: a winnowing shovel and a pitchfork to place food on it for a child.

phrases.he: אֶת הַכּוּשׁ וְאֶת הַכַּרְכָּר, לִתְחֹב בּוֹ.
phrases.en: a reed or a shuttle to insert it into food like a fork.

phrases.he: מַחַט שֶׁל יָד, לִטֹּל בּוֹ אֶת הַקּוֹץ,
phrases.en: a hand needle to extract a thorn with it,

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל סַקָּאִים, לִפְתֹּחַ בּוֹ אֶת הַדָּלֶת:
phrases.en: a sack maker's needle to open the door with it.

phrases.he: קָנֶה שֶׁל זֵיתִים, אִם יֵשׁ קֶשֶׁר בְּרֹאשׁוֹ, מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה,
phrases.en: A reed for olives, if there is a knot at the top of it, it can become ritually impure as a vessel,

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, אֵין מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה.
phrases.en: and if not, it cannot become ritually impure,

phrases.he: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ, נִטָּל בְּשַׁבָּת:
phrases.en: In either case, it may be moved on Shabbat

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, כָּל הַכֵּלִים נִטָּלִין, חוּץ מִן הַמַּסָּר הַגָּדוֹל וְיָתֵד שֶׁל מַחֲרֵשָׁה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: All utensils may be moved except for a large saw and the blade of a plow.

phrases.he: כָּל הַכֵּלִים נִטָּלִין לְצֹרֶךְ וְשֶׁלֹּא לְצֹרֶךְ.
phrases.en: All vessels may be moved for a specific purpose and not for a specific purpose.

phrases.he: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר, אֵין נִטָּלִין אֶלָּא לְצֹרֶךְ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Neḥemya says: Vessels may only be moved for a specific purpose.

phrases.he: כָּל הַכֵּלִים הַנִּטָּלִין בְּשַׁבָּת, שִׁבְרֵיהֶן נִטָּלִין עִמָּהֶן, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיִּהְיוּ עוֹשִׂין מֵעֵין מְלָאכָה.
phrases.en: All vessels that may be moved on Shabbat, their shards may be moved along with them, as long as they are suited for some purpose.

phrases.he: שִׁבְרֵי עֲרֵבָה, לְכַסּוֹת בָּהֶן אֶת פִּי הֶחָבִית.
phrases.en: Shards of a large bowl may be used to cover the mouth of a barrel.

phrases.he: שִׁבְרֵי זְכוּכִית, לְכַסּוֹת בָּהֶן אֶת פִּי הַפָּךְ.
phrases.en: Shards of a glass vessel may be used to cover the mouth of a cruse.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיִּהְיוּ עוֹשִׂין מֵעֵין מְלַאכְתָּן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: As long as they are suited for a purpose similar to their original use.

phrases.he: שִׁבְרֵי עֲרֵבָה, לִצּוֹק לְתוֹכָן מִקְפָּה.
phrases.en: Shards of a large bowl must be suited to pour soup into them,

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל זְכוּכִית לִצּוֹק לְתוֹכָן שָׁמֶן:
phrases.en: and shards of a glass vessel must be suited to pour oil into them.

phrases.he: הָאֶבֶן שֶׁבְּקֵרוּיָה, אִם מְמַלְּאִין בָּהּ וְאֵינָהּ נוֹפֶלֶת, מְמַלְּאִין בָּהּ.
phrases.en: A stone that is in a gourd used to draw water [kiruya], if they fill it with water and the stone does not fall, one may fill with it on Shabbat

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, אֵין מְמַלְּאִין בָּהּ.
phrases.en: and if not, and the stone does fall, one may not fill with it

phrases.he: זְמוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא קְשׁוּרָה בְטָפִיחַ, מְמַלְּאִין בָּהּ בְּשַׁבָּת:
phrases.en: a vine branch that is tied to a pitcher, one may fill water with it on Shabbat

phrases.he: פְּקַק הַחַלּוֹן, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא קָשׁוּר וְתָלוּי, פּוֹקְקִין בּוֹ,
phrases.en: a window shutter, Rabbi Eliezer says: When it is tied and hanging from the window, one may shutter the window with it,

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, אֵין פּוֹקְקִין בּוֹ.
phrases.en: and if not, one may not shutter the window with it.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ פּוֹקְקִין בּוֹ:
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: Both in this case and in that case one may shutter with it.

phrases.he: כָּל כִּסּוּיֵי הַכֵּלִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם בֵּית אֲחִיזָה נִטָּלִים בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: All covers of vessels that have a handle may be moved on Shabbat.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei said: In what case is this statement said?

phrases.he: בְּכִסּוּי קַרְקַע, אֲבָל בְּכִסּוּי הַכֵּלִים, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ נִטָּלִים בְּשַׁבָּת:
phrases.en: In the case of a cover for the ground, however, with regard to covers of vessels, both in this case and in that case, they may be moved on Shabbat.

phrases.he: מְפַנִּין אֲפִלּוּ אַרְבַּע וְחָמֵשׁ קֻפּוֹת שֶׁל תֶּבֶן וְשֶׁל תְּבוּאָה מִפְּנֵי הָאוֹרְחִים וּמִפְּנֵי בִטּוּל בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ, אֲבָל לֹא אֶת הָאוֹצָר.
phrases.en: one may move even four or five baskets of straw and baskets of produce, due to the guests, and due to suspension of Torah study in the study hall. However, one may not move these items to create space in the storeroom.

phrases.he: מְפַנִּין תְּרוּמָה טְהוֹרָה, וּדְמַאי, וּמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּטְּלָה תְרוּמָתוֹ, וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁנִּפְדּוּ, וְהַתֻּרְמוֹס הַיָּבֵשׁ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מַאֲכָל לַעֲנִיִּים.
phrases.en: One may move ritually pure teruma, and doubtfully tithed produce, and first tithe whose teruma has been taken and given to priests; and second tithe and consecrated items that were redeemed; and even dry lupine, because it is goat food.

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא אֶת הַטֶּבֶל, וְלֹא מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלֹּא נִטְּלָה תְרוּמָתוֹ, וְלֹא אֶת מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא נִפְדּוּ, וְלֹא אֶת הַלּוּף, וְלֹא הַחַרְדָּל.
phrases.en: However, one may neither move untithed produce, nor first tithe whose teruma has not been taken, nor second tithe and consecrated items that were not redeemed, nor arum and mustard.

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מַתִּיר בְּלוּף, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מַאֲכַל עוֹרְבִין:
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel permits moving in the case of arum because it is food for ravens.

phrases.he: חֲבִילֵי קַשׁ וַחֲבִילֵי עֵצִים וַחֲבִילֵי זְרָדִים, אִם הִתְקִינָן לְמַאֲכַל בְּהֵמָה, מְטַלְטְלִין אוֹתָן.
phrases.en: bundles of straw, and bundles of wood, and bundles of twigs, if one prepared them for animal food, one may move them.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, אֵין מְטַלְטְלִין אוֹתָן.
phrases.en: And if not, one may not move them.

phrases.he: כּוֹפִין אֶת הַסַּל לִפְנֵי הָאֶפְרוֹחִים, כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּעֲלוּ וְיֵרְדוּ.
phrases.en: One may overturn a basket in front of the chicks so that they can climb on and climb off of it.

phrases.he: תַּרְנְגֹלֶת שֶׁבָּרְחָה, דּוֹחִין אוֹתָהּ עַד שֶׁתִּכָּנֵס.
phrases.en: a hen that fled one may push it until it reenters the house.

phrases.he: מְדַדִּין עֲגָלִין וּסְיָחִין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים.
phrases.en: One may help calves and foals to walk, and likewise

phrases.he: אִשָּׁה מְדַדָּה אֶת בְּנָהּ.
phrases.en: a woman may help her son to walk.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא נוֹטֵל אַחַת וּמְנִיחַ אַחַת,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda said: When is it permitted? When her son picks one foot up and puts one foot down by himself.

phrases.he: אֲבָל אִם הָיָה גוֹרֵר, אָסוּר.
phrases.en: However, if her son were dragging both his feet, it would be prohibited because it would be like carrying him in the public domain.

phrases.he: אֵין מְיַלְּדִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בְיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.en: One may not birth an animal on a Festival,

phrases.he: אֲבָל מְסַעֲדִין.
phrases.en: However, one may assist it to give birth.

phrases.he: וּמְיַלְּדִין אֶת הָאִשָּׁה בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: And one may birth a woman even on Shabbat, and call a midwife for her

phrases.he: וְקוֹרִין לָהּ חֲכָמָה מִמָּקוֹם לְמָקוֹם,
phrases.en: to travel from place to place,

phrases.he: וּמְחַלְּלִין עָלֶיהָ אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.en: And one may desecrate Shabbat for a woman giving birth.

phrases.he: וְקוֹשְׁרִין אֶת הַטַּבּוּר.
phrases.en: And one may tie the umbilical cord

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַף חוֹתְכִין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: One may even cut the umbilical cord.

phrases.he: וְכָל צָרְכֵי מִילָה עוֹשִׂין בְּשַׁבָּת:
phrases.en: And all the requirements of circumcision may be performed on Shabbat.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אִם לֹא הֵבִיא כְלִי מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת, מְבִיאוֹ בְשַׁבָּת מְגֻלֶּה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: If he did not bring an implement on Shabbat eve, he brings it on Shabbat itself uncovered.

phrases.he: וּבַסַּכָּנָה, מְכַסֵּהוּ עַל פִּי עֵדִים.
phrases.en: And in times of danger, one covers it in the presence of witnesses.

phrases.he: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, כּוֹרְתִין עֵצִים לַעֲשׂוֹת פֶּחָמִין וְלַעֲשׂוֹת כְּלִי בַרְזֶל.
phrases.en: And furthermore, Rabbi Eliezer said: One may even cut down trees to prepare charcoal in order to fashion iron tools.

phrases.he: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, כָּל מְלָאכָה שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת אֵינָהּ דּוֹחָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת, וְשֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת דּוֹחָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת:
phrases.en: A principle was stated by Rabbi Akiva: Any prohibited labor that can be performed on Shabbat eve does not override Shabbat, and any prohibited labor that cannot be performed on Shabbat eve overrides Shabbat.

phrases.he: עוֹשִׂין כָּל צָרְכֵי מִילָה בְשַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: one performs all the necessities of the circumcision, even on Shabbat:

phrases.he: מוֹהֲלִין,
phrases.en: One circumcises

phrases.he: וּפוֹרְעִין,
phrases.en: and uncovers

phrases.he: וּמוֹצְצִין,
phrases.en: and sucks

phrases.he: וְנוֹתְנִין עָלֶיהָ אִסְפְּלָנִית וְכַמּוֹן.
phrases.en: and places on it both a bandage [ispelanit] and cumin

phrases.he: אִם לֹא שָׁחַק מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: If one did not grind the cumin from Shabbat eve,

phrases.he: לוֹעֵס בְּשִׁנָּיו וְנוֹתֵן.
phrases.en: he chews it with his teeth and places

phrases.he: אִם לֹא טָרַף יַיִן וְשֶׁמֶן מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: If he did not mix wine and oil on Shabbat eve,

phrases.he: יִנָּתֵן זֶה בְעַצְמוֹ וְזֶה בְעַצְמוֹ.
phrases.en: this, the wine, is placed by itself and that, the oil, is placed by itself.

phrases.he: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין לָהּ חָלוּק לְכַתְּחִלָּה,
phrases.en: And one may not make a pouch ab initio,

phrases.he: אֲבָל כּוֹרֵךְ עָלֶיהָ סְמַרְטוּט.
phrases.en: but he may wrap a rag over it

phrases.he: אִם לֹא הִתְקִין מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: If he did not prepare the bandage on Shabbat eve

phrases.he: כּוֹרֵךְ עַל אֶצְבָּעוֹ וּמֵבִיא,
phrases.en: he wraps the bandage on his finger and brings

phrases.he: וַאֲפִלּוּ מֵחָצֵר אַחֶרֶת:
phrases.en: even from a different courtyard.

phrases.he: מַרְחִיצִין אֶת הַקָּטָן, בֵּין לִפְנֵי הַמִּילָה וּבֵין לְאַחַר הַמִּילָה, וּמְזַלְּפִין עָלָיו בַּיָּד, אֲבָל לֹא בִכְלִי.
phrases.en: One may wash the baby both before the circumcision and after the circumcision. And one may sprinkle on him by hand but not with a vessel.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר, מַרְחִיצִין אֶת הַקָּטָן בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (בראשית לד) וַיְהִי בַיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי בִּהְיוֹתָם כֹּאֲבִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says: One may wash the baby on the third day that occurs on Shabbat, as it is stated: "And it came to pass on the third day, when they were in pain"

phrases.he: סָפֵק וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס אֵין מְחַלְּלִין עָלָיו אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר בְּאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס:
phrases.en: If there is uncertainty and a hermaphrodite one does not desecrate Shabbat, and Rabbi Yehuda permits for a hermaphrodite.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי תִינוֹקוֹת, אֶחָד לָמוּל אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת וְאֶחָד לָמוּל בְּשַׁבָּת, וְשָׁכַח וּמָל אֶת שֶׁל אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת בְּשַׁבָּת, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: One who had two babies to circumcise, one of whom he needed to circumcise on the day after Shabbat, and one of whom he needed to circumcise on Shabbat, and he forgot and circumcised the one that should have been circumcised after Shabbat on Shabbat, he is liable to bring a sin-offering.

phrases.he: אֶחָד לָמוּל בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת וְאֶחָד לָמוּל בְּשַׁבָּת, וְשָׁכַח וּמָל אֶת שֶׁל עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בְּשַׁבָּת, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְחַיֵּב חַטָּאת, וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ פּוֹטֵר.
phrases.en: If there were two babies, one to circumcise on Shabbat eve, and one to circumcise on Shabbat, and he forgot and circumcised the one that he should have circumcised on Shabbat eve on Shabbat, Rabbi Eliezer deems him liable to bring a sin-offering, and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts him.

phrases.he: קָטָן נִמּוֹל לִשְׁמֹנָה, לְתִשְׁעָה, וְלַעֲשָׂרָה, וּלְאַחַד עָשָׂר, וְלִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר, לֹא פָחוֹת וְלֹא יוֹתֵר.
phrases.en: a child is circumcised at eight days, at times at nine days, at times at ten days, at eleven days, and at twelve days, no earlier and no later.

phrases.he: הָא כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: How so?

phrases.he: כְּדַרְכּוֹ, לִשְׁמֹנָה.
phrases.en: In his usual manner, a child is circumcised at eight days.

phrases.he: נוֹלַד לְבֵין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת, נִמּוֹל לְתִשְׁעָה.
phrases.en: If he was born at twilight he is circumcised at nine days.

phrases.he: בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת שֶׁל עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת, נִמּוֹל לַעֲשָׂרָה.
phrases.en: If he was born at twilight on Shabbat eve, he is circumcised at ten days.

phrases.he: יוֹם טוֹב לְאַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת, נִמּוֹל לְאַחַד עָשָׂר.
phrases.en: If there was a Festival after that Shabbat, he is circumcised at eleven days.

phrases.he: שְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, נִמּוֹל לִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר.
phrases.en: And if that Shabbat was followed by two days of Rosh HaShana, he is circumcised at twelve days.

phrases.he: קָטָן הַחוֹלֶה, אֵין מוֹהֲלִין אוֹתוֹ עַד שֶׁיַּבְרִיא.
phrases.en: With regard to a sick child, one does not circumcise him until he becomes healthy.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ הֵן צִיצִין הַמְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַמִּילָה, בָּשָׂר הַחוֹפֶה אֶת רֹב הָעֲטָרָה.
phrases.en: These are the shreds that invalidate the circumcision if they are not cut. The essential element of circumcision is the removal of the flesh that covers most of the corona,

phrases.he: וְאֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל בַּתְּרוּמָה.
phrases.en: and he does not eat teruma.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיָה בַעַל בָּשָׂר, מְתַקְּנוֹ מִפְּנֵי מַרְאִית הָעָיִן.
phrases.en: And if he was fleshy, correct it by circumcising more than necessary, to avoid the appearance of transgression.

phrases.he: מָל וְלֹא פָרַע אֶת הַמִּילָה, כְּאִלּוּ לֹא מָל.
phrases.en: If one circumcised but did not uncover the flesh at the area of the circumcision, it is as if he had not circumcised.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, תּוֹלִין אֶת הַמְשַׁמֶּרֶת בְּיוֹם טוֹב, וְנוֹתְנִין לַתְּלוּיָה בְשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: One may suspend the strainer on a Festival. And one may place wine through a suspended strainer the day before; however, one may not suspend the strainer on Shabbat.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵין תּוֹלִין אֶת הַמְשַׁמֶּרֶת בְּיוֹם טוֹב, וְאֵין נוֹתְנִין לַתְּלוּיָה בְשַׁבָּת, אֲבָל נוֹתְנִין לַתְּלוּיָה בְיוֹם טוֹב:
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: One may not suspend the strainer on a Festival, and one may not place wine for filtering through a suspended strainer on Shabbat; however, one may place wine through a suspended strainer on a Festival.

phrases.he: נוֹתְנִין מַיִם עַל גַּבֵּי הַשְּׁמָרִים בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁיִּצַּלּוּ,
phrases.en: One may pour water over sediment that is in a strainer on Shabbat so that it will become clear

phrases.he: וּמְסַנְּנִין אֶת הַיַּיִן בְּסוּדָרִין וּבִכְפִיפָה מִצְרִית,
phrases.en: And one may filter wine through cloths and through an Egyptian basket

phrases.he: וְנוֹתְנִין בֵּיצָה בִמְסַנֶּנֶת שֶׁל חַרְדָּל,
phrases.en: And one may place an egg in a mustard strainer

phrases.he: וְעוֹשִׂין אֵנוּמְלִין בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: and one may prepare anumlin, a wine-based drink, on Shabbat.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בְּשַׁבָּת, בְּכוֹס, בְּיוֹם טוֹב, בְּלָגִין, וּבַמּוֹעֵד, בְּחָבִית.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: On Shabbat one may only make anumlin in a small cup; on a Festival, in a larger vessel; and on the intermediate days of a Festival, one may even prepare it in a barrel.

phrases.he: רַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר, הַכֹּל לְפִי הָאוֹרְחִין:
phrases.en: Rabbi Tzadok says: it is all according to the guests;

phrases.he: אֵין שׁוֹרִין אֶת הַחִלְתִּית בְּפוֹשְׁרִין, אֲבָל נוֹתֵן לְתוֹךְ הַחֹמֶץ.
phrases.en: One may not soak asafoetida in lukewarm water to prepare a medicinal drink from it; however, one may place it into vinegar like a standard spice.

phrases.he: וְאֵין שׁוֹרִין אֶת הַכַּרְשִׁינִין וְלֹא שָׁפִין אוֹתָן, אֲבָל נוֹתֵן לְתוֹךְ הַכְּבָרָה אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַכַּלְכַּלָּה.
phrases.en: And one may not soak vetches in water in order to separate them from their chaff, nor rub them by hand so as to remove their chaff. However, one may place them into a sieve or into a basket, and if the chaff gets removed, so be it.

phrases.he: אֵין כּוֹבְרִין אֶת הַתֶּבֶן בִּכְבָרָה, וְלֹא יִתְּנֶנּוּ עַל גַּבֵּי מָקוֹם גָּבוֹהַּ בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁיֵּרֵד הַמֹּץ, אֲבָל נוֹטֵל הוּא בִכְבָרָה וְנוֹתֵן לְתוֹךְ הָאֵבוּס:
phrases.en: One may not sift straw in a sieve, and similarly, one may not place it on a high place so that that the chaff blows away in the wind; however, one may take the straw in a sieve and place it into the trough of an animal, and one need not be concerned if the chaff is removed in the process.

phrases.he: גּוֹרְפִין מִלִּפְנֵי הַפְּטָם, וּמְסַלְּקִין לִצְדָדִין מִפְּנֵי הָרְעִי, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי דוֹסָא.
phrases.en: One may sweep hay from before an animal that is being fattened, and one may move hay to the sides for an animal that grazes; this is the statement of Rabbi Dosa.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִין.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis prohibit.

phrases.he: נוֹטְלִין מִלִּפְנֵי בְהֵמָה זוֹ וְנוֹתְנִין לִפְנֵי בְהֵמָה זוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת:
phrases.en: One may take from before this animal and place it before that animal on Shabbat.

phrases.he: הַקַּשׁ שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּטָּה, לֹא יְנַעְנְעוֹ בְיָדוֹ, אֶלָּא מְנַעְנְעוֹ בְגוּפוֹ.
phrases.en: straw that is on top of a bed, he may not move it with his hand rather, he may move it with his body.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיָה מַאֲכַל בְּהֵמָה, אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה עָלָיו כַּר אוֹ סָדִין, מְנַעְנְעוֹ בְיָדוֹ.
phrases.en: And if the straw was designated as animal food, or a pillow or sheet was on it, one may move it even with his hand.

phrases.he: מַכְבֵּשׁ שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים, מַתִּירִין, אֲבָל לֹא כוֹבְשִׁין.
phrases.en: A press which belongs to a homeowner, one may loosen it However, one may not press

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל כּוֹבְסִין, לֹא יִגַּע בּוֹ.
phrases.en: And belongs to a launderer, one may not touch it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם הָיָה מֻתָּר מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת, מַתִּיר אֶת כֻּלּוֹ וְשׁוֹמְטוֹ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: If the launderer's press was loosened somewhat on Shabbat eve, he may loosen it completely on Shabbat and remove the garment.

phrases.he: נוֹטֵל אָדָם אֶת בְּנוֹ וְהָאֶבֶן בְּיָדוֹ,
phrases.en: A person may take his son and even though there is a stone, which is a set-aside item, in the child's hand,

phrases.he: וְכַלְכַּלָּה וְהָאֶבֶן בְּתוֹכָהּ.
phrases.en: And it is permissible to take a basket with a stone inside it on Shabbat.

phrases.he: וּמְטַלְטְלִין תְּרוּמָה טְמֵאָה עִם הַטְּהוֹרָה וְעִם הַחֻלִּין.
phrases.en: And one may move ritually impure teruma, which may not be eaten and is set-aside, with ritually pure teruma, as well as with non-sacred produce.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף מַעֲלִין אֶת הַמְדֻמָּע בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: One may even lift a measure of teruma that was nullified from a mixture of one hundred measures of non-sacred produce and one measure of teruma.

phrases.he: הָאֶבֶן שֶׁעַל פִּי הֶחָבִית, מַטָּהּ עַל צִדָּהּ וְהִיא נוֹפֶלֶת.
phrases.en: a stone which is set-aside on Shabbat and may not be moved, that was placed on the mouth of a barrel, one tilts the barrel on its side, and the stone falls.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה בֵין הֶחָבִיּוֹת, מַגְבִּיהַּ וּמַטָּהּ עַל צִדָּהּ וְהִיא נוֹפֶלֶת.
phrases.en: If the barrel was among other barrels, and the other barrels might break if the stone falls on them, he lifts the barrel to distance it from the other barrels, and then tilts it on its side, and the stone falls.

phrases.he: מָעוֹת שֶׁעַל הַכַּר, נוֹעֵר אֶת הַכַּר וְהֵן נוֹפְלוֹת.
phrases.en: coins that are on a cushion, he shakes the cushion and the coins fall.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה עָלָיו לַשְׁלֶשֶׁת, מְקַנְּחָהּ בִּסְמַרְטוּט.
phrases.en: If there was bird dung on the cushion, he wipes it with a rag,

phrases.he: הָיְתָה שֶׁל עוֹר, נוֹתְנִין עָלֶיהָ מַיִם עַד שֶׁתִּכְלֶה:
phrases.en: If the cushion was made of leather, and laundering is not a concern, he places water on it until the bird dung ceases.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מַגְבִּיהִין מִן הַשֻּׁלְחָן עֲצָמוֹת וּקְלִפִּין.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One may clear bones and shells from the table

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, נוֹטֵל אֶת הַטַּבְלָה כֻלָּהּ וּמְנַעֲרָהּ.
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: One may remove the entire board and shake it

phrases.he: מַעֲבִירִין מִלִּפְנֵי הַשֻּׁלְחָן פֵּרוּרִין פָּחוֹת מִכַּזַּיִת וְשֵׂעָר שֶׁל אֲפוּנִים וְשֵׂעָר שֶׁל עֲדָשִׁים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מַאֲכַל בְּהֵמָה.
phrases.en: One may clear crumbs from the table, even if they are less than an olive-bulk, and pea and lentil pods because it is animal fodder.

phrases.he: סְפוֹג, אִם יֶשׁ לוֹ עוֹר בֵּית אֲחִיזָה, מְקַנְּחִין בּוֹ, וְאִם לָאו, אֵין מְקַנְּחִין בּוֹ.
phrases.en: With regard to a sponge, if it has leather as a handle, one may wipe with it, and if not, one may not wipe with it

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ, נִטָּל בְּשַׁבָּת, וְאֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: Both this and that may be moved on Shabbat and it does not become ritually impure.

phrases.he: חָבִית שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה, מַצִּילִין הֵימֶנָּה מְזוֹן שָׁלֹשׁ סְעֻדּוֹת,
phrases.en: a barrel that broke on Shabbat, one may rescue from it food sufficient for three meals,

phrases.he: וְאוֹמֵר לַאֲחֵרִים, בֹּאוּ וְהַצִּילוּ לָכֶם,
phrases.en: and one may also say to others: Come and rescue food for yourselves.

phrases.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִסְפֹּג.
phrases.en: provided that one does not soak up the wine or oil with a sponge or rag

phrases.he: אֵין סוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַפֵּרוֹת לְהוֹצִיא מֵהֶן מַשְׁקִין,
phrases.en: One may not squeeze fruits on Shabbat in order to extract liquids from them.

phrases.he: וְאִם יָצְאוּ מֵעַצְמָן, אֲסוּרִין.
phrases.en: And if liquids seeped out on their own, it is prohibited to use them on Shabbat.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם לְאֳכָלִין, הַיּוֹצֵא מֵהֶן מֻתָּר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: If the fruits were designated for eating, the liquid that seeps from them on Shabbat is permitted.

phrases.he: וְאִם לְמַשְׁקִין, הַיּוֹצֵא מֵהֶן אָסוּר.
phrases.en: And if the fruits were originally designated for liquids, the liquids that seep from them on Shabbat are prohibited.

phrases.he: חַלּוֹת דְּבַשׁ שֶׁרִסְּקָן מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת וְיָצְאוּ מֵעַצְמָן, אֲסוּרִין.
phrases.en: In the case of honeycombs that one crushed on Shabbat eve, and honey and wax seeped from them on their own on Shabbat, they are prohibited,

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מַתִּיר.
phrases.en: and Rabbi Eliezer permits using them.

phrases.he: כֹּל שֶׁבָּא בְחַמִּין מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת, שׁוֹרִין אוֹתוֹ בְחַמִּין בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: Any salted food item that was already placed in hot water before Shabbat, one may soak it in hot water even on Shabbat.

phrases.he: וְכֹל שֶׁלֹּא בָא בְחַמִּין מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת, מְדִיחִין אוֹתוֹ בְחַמִּין בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: And anything that was not placed in hot water before Shabbat, one may rinse it in hot water on Shabbat

phrases.he: חוּץ מִן הַמָּלִיחַ הַיָּשָׁן, וְדָגִים מְלוּחִים קְטַנִּים וְקוּלְיָס הָאִסְפָּנִין,
phrases.en: with the exception of old salted fish and small salted fish and the kolyas ha'ispanin fish,

phrases.he: שֶׁהֲדָחָתָן זוֹ הִיא גְמַר מְלַאכְתָּן:
phrases.en: for which rinsing with hot water itself is completion of the prohibited labor of cooking.

phrases.he: שׁוֹבֵר אָדָם אֶת הֶחָבִית לֶאֱכֹל הֵימֶנָּה גְרוֹגָרוֹת, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִתְכַּוֵּן לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּלִי.
phrases.en: A person may break a barrel to eat dried figs from it, provided he does not intend to make a vessel.

phrases.he: וְאֵין נוֹקְבִים מְגוּפָה שֶׁל חָבִית, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: And one may not perforate the plug of a barrel. This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים מַתִּירִין.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis permit.

phrases.he: וְלֹא יִקְּבֶנָּה מִצִּדָּהּ.
phrases.en: One may not perforate on its side.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיְתָה נְקוּבָה, לֹא יִתֵּן עָלֶיהָ שַׁעֲוָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מְמָרֵחַ.
phrases.en: And if it was already perforated, one may not apply wax to it because he spreads the wax evenly on the barrel.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, מַעֲשֶׂה בָא לִפְנֵי רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי בַּעֲרָב, וְאָמַר, חוֹשְׁשָׁנִי לוֹ מֵחַטָּאת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda said: An incident came before Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai in Arav, and he said: I am concerned for him, because he may be liable to bring a sin-offering.

phrases.he: נוֹתְנִין תַּבְשִׁיל לְתוֹךְ הַבּוֹר בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁיְּהֵא שָׁמוּר,
phrases.en: One may place a cooked dish into an empty pit on Shabbat so that it will be protected from the heat,

phrases.he: וְאֶת הַמַּיִם הַיָּפִים בָּרָעִים בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁיִּצַּנּוּ,
phrases.en: and similarly, one may place good potable water into a vessel and place the vessel into bad, non-potable water so that the potable water will cool off.

phrases.he: וְאֶת הַצּוֹנֵן בַּחַמָּה בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁיֵּחַמּוּ.
phrases.en: And one may also place cold water out in the sun so that it will be heated.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁנָּשְׁרוּ כֵלָיו בַּדֶּרֶךְ בְּמַיִם, מְהַלֵּךְ בָּהֶן וְאֵינוֹ חוֹשֵׁשׁ.
phrases.en: Someone whose garments fell into water while walking on the road may replace them and continue to walk wearing them and need not be concerned about violating the prohibitions against wringing or laundering.

phrases.he: הִגִּיעַ לֶחָצֵר הַחִיצוֹנָה, שׁוֹטְחָן בַּחַמָּה,
phrases.en: When he reaches the outer courtyard of a place where he can leave his clothes, he spreads them in the sun to dry,

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא כְנֶגֶד הָעָם:
phrases.en: but not opposite the masses, as they will suspect him of laundering on Shabbat.

phrases.he: הָרוֹחֵץ בְּמֵי מְעָרָה וּבְמֵי טְבֶרְיָא וְנִסְתַּפֵּג, אֲפִלּוּ בְעֶשֶׂר אֲלוּנְטִיאוֹת, לֹא יְבִיאֵם בְּיָדוֹ.
phrases.en: One who bathes in cave water or in the water of Tiberias and dried himself even with ten towels may not carry them in his hand.

phrases.he: אֲבָל עֲשָׂרָה בְנֵי אָדָם מִסְתַּפְּגִין בַּאֲלוּנְטִית אַחַת פְּנֵיהֶם יְדֵיהֶם וְרַגְלֵיהֶם, וּמְבִיאִין אוֹתָהּ בְּיָדָן.
phrases.en: However, ten people may use one towel to dry their faces, hands, and feet, and may carry them in their hands.

phrases.he: סָכִין וּמְמַשְׁמְשִׁין בִּבְנֵי מֵעַיִם
phrases.en: One may smear oil on his body and gently rub his body with his hand

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא מִתְעַמְּלִין וְלֹא מִתְגָּרְדִין
phrases.en: however, one may not exert himself with vigorous massage or by means of exercise in order to benefit from the therapeutic effects of sweating; and one may not scrape the oil off with a scraper

phrases.he: אֵין יוֹרְדִין לְקוֹרְדִּימָה
phrases.en: one may not go into a swampy river [kurdima], on Shabbat

phrases.he: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין אַפִּקְטְוִזִין
phrases.en: And one may not make a drug to induce vomiting

phrases.he: וְאֵין מְעַצְּבִין אֶת הַקָּטָן
phrases.en: nor may one align a young infant's bones to straighten them

phrases.he: וְאֵין מַחֲזִירִין אֶת הַשֶּׁבֶר
phrases.en: nor may one reset a break in a bone

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁנִּפְרְקָה יָדוֹ וְרַגְלוֹ, לֹא יִטְרְפֵם בְּצוֹנֵן
phrases.en: One whose hand or foot was dislocated may not move them about vigorously in cold water, which is the standard method of treatment

phrases.he: אֲבָל רוֹחֵץ הוּא כְדַרְכּוֹ
phrases.en: however, one may wash the limb in the typical manner

phrases.he: וְאִם נִתְרַפָּא נִתְרַפָּא
phrases.en: and if one is cured through this washing, he is cured

phrases.he: שׁוֹאֵל אָדָם מֵחֲבֵרוֹ כַּדֵּי יַיִן וְכַדֵּי שֶׁמֶן,
phrases.en: One may borrow jugs of wine and jugs of oil from another

phrases.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמַר לוֹ הַלְוֵנִי,
phrases.en: as long as one does not say to him: Loan me.

phrases.he: וְכֵן הָאִשָּׁה מֵחֲבֶרְתָּהּ כִּכָּרוֹת.
phrases.en: And similarly, a woman may borrow from another loaves of bread

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ מַאֲמִינוֹ,
phrases.en: And if the lender does not trust him that he will return them,

phrases.he: מַנִּיחַ טַלִּיתוֹ אֶצְלוֹ וְעוֹשֶׂה עִמּוֹ חֶשְׁבּוֹן לְאַחַר שַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: the borrower may leave his cloak with him as collateral and make the proper calculation with him after Shabbat.

phrases.he: וְכֵן עֶרֶב פֶּסַח בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: And similarly, on the eve of Passover in Jerusalem, when it occurs on Shabbat,

phrases.he: מַנִּיחַ טַלִּיתוֹ אֶצְלוֹ וְנוֹטֵל אֶת פִּסְחוֹ, וְעוֹשֶׂה עִמּוֹ חֶשְׁבּוֹן לְאַחַר יוֹם טוֹב:
phrases.en: one who is procuring a Paschal lamb may leave his cloak with him, i.e., the person from whom he is purchasing it, and take the lamb to bring as his Paschal lamb, and then make the proper calculation with him after the Festival.

phrases.he: מוֹנֶה אָדָם אֶת אוֹרְחָיו וְאֶת פַּרְפְּרוֹתָיו מִפִּיו, אֲבָל לֹא מִן הַכְּתָב.
phrases.en: One may count his guests and his appetizers, as long as he does so from memory; but one may not read them from a written list

phrases.he: וּמֵפִיס עִם בָּנָיו וְעִם בְּנֵי בֵיתוֹ עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִתְכַּוֵּן לַעֲשׂוֹת מָנָה גְדוֹלָה כְּנֶגֶד קְטַנָּה, מִשּׁוּם קֻבְיָא.
phrases.en: A person may draw lots with his children and family members at the table, as long as he does not intend to set a large portion against a small portion in such a lottery

phrases.he: וּמַטִּילִין חֲלָשִׁים עַל הַקָּדָשִׁים בְּיוֹם טוֹב, אֲבָל לֹא עַל הַמָּנוֹת:
phrases.en: And one may cast lots among the priests for sanctified foods on a Festival, but not for the specific portions

phrases.he: לֹא יִשְׂכֹּר אָדָם פּוֹעֲלִים בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: A person may not hire workers on Shabbat

phrases.he: וְלֹא יֹאמַר אָדָם לַחֲבֵרוֹ לִשְׂכֹּר לוֹ פוֹעֲלִים.
phrases.en: a person may not tell another to hire workers for him

phrases.he: אֵין מַחְשִׁיכִין עַל הַתְּחוּם לִשְׂכֹּר פּוֹעֲלִים וּלְהָבִיא פֵרוֹת,
phrases.en: One may not wait for nightfall at the edge of the Shabbat boundary to hire workers for himself or to bring produce

phrases.he: אֲבָל מַחְשִׁיךְ הוּא לִשְׁמֹר, וּמֵבִיא פֵרוֹת בְּיָדוֹ.
phrases.en: But he may wait for nightfall to guard his produce, and he may then bring produce in his hand

phrases.he: כְּלָל אָמַר אַבָּא שָׁאוּל, כֹּל שֶׁאֲנִי זַכַּאי בַּאֲמִירָתוֹ, רַשַּׁאי אֲנִי לְהַחְשִׁיךְ עָלָיו:
phrases.en: Abba Shaul stated a general principle: With regard to anything that I am permitted to discuss on Shabbat, I am permitted to wait for nightfall at the edge of the Shabbat boundary for its sake

phrases.he: מַחְשִׁיכִין עַל הַתְּחוּם לְפַקֵּחַ עַל עִסְקֵי כַלָּה, וְעַל עִסְקֵי הַמֵּת לְהָבִיא לוֹ אָרוֹן וְתַכְרִיכִין.
phrases.en: One may wait for nightfall at the Shabbat boundary to attend to the needs of a bride and the needs of a corpse, such as to bring him a coffin and shrouds.

phrases.he: גּוֹי שֶׁהֵבִיא חֲלִילִין בְּשַׁבָּת, לֹא יִסְפֹּד בָּהֶן יִשְׂרָאֵל, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן בָּאוּ מִמָּקוֹם קָרוֹב.
phrases.en: If a gentile brought flutes on Shabbat, a Jew may not eulogize with them, unless they were brought from a nearby location.

phrases.he: עָשׂוּ לוֹ אָרוֹן וְחָפְרוּ לוֹ קֶבֶר, יִקָּבֵר בּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאִם בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל, לֹא יִקָּבֵר בּוֹ עוֹלָמִית.
phrases.en: If gentiles made someone a coffin and dug him a grave, a Jew may be buried in it. However, if it was for a Jew, a Jew may never be buried in it.

phrases.he: עוֹשִׂין כָּל צָרְכֵי הַמֵּת,
phrases.en: One may perform all of the needs of the dead

phrases.he: סָכִין וּמְדִיחִין אוֹתוֹ,
phrases.en: One may smear oil on the body and rinse it

phrases.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יָזִיזוּ בוֹ אֵבֶר.
phrases.en: provided that one does not move any of its limbs

phrases.he: שׁוֹמְטִין אֶת הַכַּר מִתַּחְתָּיו וּמַטִּילִין אוֹתוֹ עַל הַחֹל בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁיַּמְתִּין.
phrases.en: one may remove a pillow from beneath it and place it on cold sand in order to delay

phrases.he: קוֹשְׁרִים אֶת הַלֶּחִי, לֹא שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא יוֹסִיף.
phrases.en: one may tie the jaw not that it will rise but so that it will not continue

phrases.he: וְכֵן קוֹרָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה, סוֹמְכִין אוֹתָהּ בְּסַפְסָל אוֹ בַּאֲרֻכּוֹת הַמִּטָּה, לֹא שֶׁתַּעֲלֶה, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא תוֹסִיף.
phrases.en: And similarly, a roof beam that has broken, one may support it with a bench or with long poles from a bed. One may not move it so that the beam will rise but so that it will not continue to fall

phrases.he: אֵין מְעַמְּצִין אֶת הַמֵּת בְּשַׁבָּת, וְלֹא בְחֹל עִם יְצִיאַת נֶפֶשׁ.
phrases.en: One may not shut the eyes of the dead on Shabbat. And one may not shut the eyes even on a weekday while the soul departs

phrases.he: וְהַמְעַמֵּץ עִם יְצִיאַת נֶפֶשׁ, הֲרֵי זֶה שׁוֹפֵךְ דָּמִים:
phrases.en: And one who shuts the eyes while the soul departs is a murderer

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁהֶחְשִׁיךְ בַּדֶּרֶךְ, נוֹתֵן כִּיסוֹ לְנָכְרִי, וְאִם אֵין עִמּוֹ נָכְרִי, מְנִיחוֹ עַל הַחֲמוֹר.
phrases.en: One who was traveling on Shabbat eve and night fell, and Shabbat began while he was still en route, gives his money pouch to a gentile traveling with him. And if there is no gentile with him he places it on the donkey.

phrases.he: הִגִּיעַ לֶחָצֵר הַחִיצוֹנָה, נוֹטֵל אֶת הַכֵּלִים הַנִּטָּלִין בְּשַׁבָּת, וְשֶׁאֵינָן נִטָּלִין בְּשַׁבָּת, מַתִּיר אֶת הַחֲבָלִים, וְהַשַּׂקִּין נוֹפְלִין מֵאֲלֵיהֶם.
phrases.en: Once he reached the outer courtyard of the city, where belongings can be securely placed, he takes the vessels that may be moved on Shabbat off the donkey. With regard to the vessels that may not be moved on Shabbat, he unties the ropes that attach his bags to the donkey, and the bags of vessels fall on their own.

phrases.he: מַתִּירִין פְּקִיעֵי עָמִיר לִפְנֵי בְהֵמָה, וּמְפַסְפְּסִים אֶת הַכֵּפִין, אֲבָל לֹא אֶת הַזֵּרִין.
phrases.en: One may untie peki'in of grain before an animal and one may spread the kifin but not the zirin.

phrases.he: אֵין מְרַסְּקִין לֹא אֶת הַשַּׁחַת וְלֹא אֶת הֶחָרוּבִין לִפְנֵי בְהֵמָה, בֵּין דַּקָּה בֵּין גַּסָּה.
phrases.en: One may not crush hay or carobs before an animal neither for a small animal nor for a large one.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר בֶּחָרוּבִים לַדַּקָּה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda permits to do so with carobs for a small animal.

phrases.he: אֵין אוֹבְסִין אֶת הַגָּמָל, וְלֹא דוֹרְסִין, אֲבָל מַלְעִיטִין.
phrases.en: One may not forcibly overfeed a camel and one may not force-feed it. However, one may place food into its mouth.

phrases.he: וְאֵין מַמְרִים אֶת הָעֲגָלִים, אֲבָל מַלְעִיטִין.
phrases.en: One may not place food in the mouths of calves in the manner of hamra'a, but one may do so in the manner of halata.

phrases.he: וּמְהַלְקְטִין לַתַּרְנְגוֹלִין.
phrases.en: And one may force-feed chickens.

phrases.he: וְנוֹתְנִין מַיִם לַמֻּרְסָן, אֲבָל לֹא גוֹבְלִים.
phrases.en: And one may add water to bran, but one may not knead the mixture.

phrases.he: וְאֵין נוֹתְנִין מַיִם לִפְנֵי דְבוֹרִים וְלִפְנֵי יוֹנִים שֶׁבַּשֹּׁבָךְ, אֲבָל נוֹתְנִין לִפְנֵי אֲוָזִים וְתַרְנְגוֹלִים וְלִפְנֵי יוֹנֵי הָרְדְּסִיּוֹת:
phrases.en: And one may not place water before bees or before doves in a dove-cote, however, one may place water before geese and chickens and before hardisian doves.

phrases.he: מְחַתְּכִין אֶת הַדְּלוּעִין לִפְנֵי הַבְּהֵמָה.
phrases.en: One may cut the pumpkins before an animal

phrases.he: וְאֶת הַנְּבֵלָה לִפְנֵי הַכְּלָבִים.
phrases.en: And likewise one may cut an animal carcass before the dogs

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם לֹא הָיְתָה נְבֵלָה מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת, אֲסוּרָה, לְפִי שֶׁאֵינָהּ מִן הַמּוּכָן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: If it was not already a carcass, prior to Shabbat, it is prohibited because it is not prepared for use on Shabbat.

phrases.he: מְפִירִין נְדָרִים בְּשַׁבָּת
phrases.en: may nullify vows on Shabbat

phrases.he: וְנִשְׁאָלִין לִדְבָרִים שֶׁהֵן לְצֹרֶךְ הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.en: and one may request to dissolve vows that are for the purpose of Shabbat

phrases.he: פּוֹקְקִין אֶת הַמָּאוֹר
phrases.en: And one may seal a window

phrases.he: וּמוֹדְדִין אֶת הַמַּטְלִית וְאֶת הַמִּקְוֶה.
phrases.en: and one may measure a rag and one may measure a ritual bath

phrases.he: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בִימֵי אָבִיו שֶׁל רַבִּי צָדוֹק וּבִימֵי אַבָּא שָׁאוּל בֶּן בָּטְנִית
phrases.en: The mishna relates that there was an incident in the time of Rabbi Tzadok's father and the time of Abba Shaul ben Botnit

phrases.he: שֶׁפָּקְקוּ אֶת הַמָּאוֹר בְּטָפִיחַ
phrases.en: in which they sealed a window using an earthenware vessel

phrases.he: וְקָשְׁרוּ אֶת הַמְּקֵדָה בְגֶמִי
phrases.en: and tied an earthenware shard with a reed-grass

phrases.he: לֵידַע אִם יֵשׁ בַּגִּיגִית פּוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח אִם לָאו.
phrases.en: to ascertain whether or not the roofing had an opening the size of a handbreadth

phrases.he: וּמִדִּבְרֵיהֶן לָמַדְנוּ
phrases.en: And from their statements we derived

phrases.he: שֶׁפּוֹקְקִין וּמוֹדְדִין וְקוֹשְׁרִין בְּשַׁבָּת:
phrases.en: that one may seal and measure and tie a knot on Shabbat

phrases.he: מָבוֹי שֶׁהוּא גָבוֹהַּ לְמַעְלָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה, יְמַעֵט.
phrases.en: an alleyway at a height above twenty cubits, one must diminish

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: He need not

phrases.he: וְהָרָחָב מֵעֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת, יְמַעֵט.
phrases.en: wider than ten cubits, one must diminish

phrases.he: וְאִם יֶשׁ לוֹ צוּרַת הַפֶּתַח, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא רָחָב מֵעֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת, אֵין צָרִיךְ לְמַעֵט:
phrases.en: However, if the entrance to the alleyway has the form of a doorway, even if it is wider than ten cubits, he need not diminish

phrases.he: הֶכְשֵׁר מָבוֹי, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, לֶחִי וְקוֹרָה, וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, לֶחִי אוֹ קוֹרָה.
phrases.en: There is a basic dispute with regard to the method of rendering an alleyway fit for one to carry within it on Shabbat. Beit Shammai say: Both a side post and a cross beam are required. Beit Hillel say: Either a side post or a cross beam.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, לְחָיַיִם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: Two side posts are required, one on each side of the alleyway.

phrases.he: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמַר תַּלְמִיד אֶחָד לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל עַל מָבוֹי שֶׁהוּא פָחוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, שֶׁהוּא אוֹ בְלֶחִי אוֹ בְקוֹרָה.
phrases.en: In the name of Rabbi Yishmael, one student said before Rabbi Akiva: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree about an alleyway that is less than four cubits wide, as they both agree that carrying is rendered permitted by either a side post or a cross beam.

phrases.he: עַל מַה נֶּחְלְקוּ, עַל רָחָב מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וְעַד עֶשֶׂר, שֶׁבֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, לֶחִי וְקוֹרָה, וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, אוֹ לֶחִי אוֹ קוֹרָה.
phrases.en: With regard to what did they disagree? It is with regard to an alleyway that is wider than four cubits, and up to ten cubits wide; as Beit Shammai say: It requires both a side post and a cross beam. And Beit Hillel say: It requires either a side post or a cross beam.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, עַל זֶה וְעַל זֶה נֶחֱלָקוּ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva said to the disciple: It is not so, as they disagree both about this case, i.e., an alleyway that is less than four cubits wide, and about that case, i.e., an alleyway that is between four and ten cubits wide.

phrases.he: הַקּוֹרָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ, רְחָבָה כְּדֵי לְקַבֵּל אָרִיחַ.
phrases.en: The cross beam, which the Sages stated may be used to render an alleyway fit for one to carry within it, must be wide enough to receive and hold a small brick.

phrases.he: וְאָרִיחַ, חֲצִי לְבֵנָה שֶׁל שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים.
phrases.en: And this small brick is half a large brick, which measures three handbreadths, i.e., a handbreadth and a half.

phrases.he: דַּיָּה לַקּוֹרָה שֶׁתְּהֵא רְחָבָה טֶפַח, כְּדֵי לְקַבֵּל אָרִיחַ לְאָרְכּוֹ:
phrases.en: It is sufficient that the cross beam will be a handbreadth in width, not a handbreadth and a half, enough to hold a small brick across its width.

phrases.he: רְחָבָה, כְּדֵי לְקַבֵּל אָרִיחַ,
phrases.en: wide enough to hold a small brick

phrases.he: וּבְרִיאָה, כְּדֵי לְקַבֵּל אָרִיחַ.
phrases.en: sturdy enough to hold a small brick

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.he: רְחָבָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בְּרִיאָה:
phrases.en: If it is wide enough to hold the brick, even though it is not sturdy enough to actually support it, it is sufficient.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה שֶׁל קַשׁ אוֹ שֶׁל קָנִים, רוֹאִין אוֹתָהּ כְּאִלּוּ הִיא שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת.
phrases.en: is made of straw or reeds, one considers it as though it were made of metal.

phrases.he: עֲקֻמָּה, רוֹאִין אוֹתָהּ כְּאִלּוּ הִיא פְשׁוּטָה.
phrases.en: If the cross beam is curved, one considers it as though it were straight;

phrases.he: עֲגֻלָּה, רוֹאִין אוֹתָהּ כְּאִלּוּ הִיא מְרֻבַּעַת.
phrases.en: if it is round, one considers it as though it were square.

phrases.he: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּהֶקֵּפוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים, יֶשׁ בּוֹ רֹחַב טָפַח:
phrases.en: Any beam with a circumference of three handbreadths is a handbreadth in width,

phrases.he: לְחָיַיִן שֶׁאָמְרוּ
phrases.en: The side posts the Sages spoke of

phrases.he: גָּבְהָן עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים
phrases.en: their height must be at least ten handbreadths

phrases.he: וְרָחְבָּן וְעָבְיָן כָּל שֶׁהוּא
phrases.en: and their width and thickness may be any amount

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, רָחְבָּן שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: Their width must be at least three handbreadths

phrases.he: בַּכֹּל עוֹשִׂין לְחָיַיִן, אֲפִלּוּ בְדָבָר שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ רוּחַ חַיִּים.
phrases.en: One may construct side posts from anything, even a living creature

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹסֵר.
phrases.en: and Rabbi Yosei prohibits

phrases.he: וּמְטַמֵּא מִשּׁוּם גּוֹלֵל, וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר מְטַהֵר.
phrases.en: imparts ritual impurity if it used as the covering of a grave. But Rabbi Meir deems it pure.

phrases.he: וְכוֹתְבִין עָלָיו גִּטֵּי נָשִׁים, וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי פוֹסֵל:
phrases.en: one may write women's bills of divorce on anything, even a living creature. But Rabbi Yosei HaGelili invalidates a bill of divorce written on a living creature.

phrases.he: שַׁיָּרָא שֶׁחָנְתָה בְּבִקְעָה וְהִקִּיפוּהָ בִכְלֵי בְהֵמָה, מְטַלְטְלִין בְּתוֹכָהּ,
phrases.en: a caravan camped in a valley, and the travelers enclosed their camp with partitions made of the animals' equipment, one may carry inside the enclosed area,

phrases.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיְּהֵא גָדֵר גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, וְלֹא יִהְיוּ פְרָצוֹת יְתֵרוֹת עַל הַבִּנְיָן.
phrases.en: provided that the resultant partition will be a fence ten handbreadths high, and that there will not be breaches greater than the built segment.

phrases.he: כָּל פִּרְצָה שֶׁהִיא כְעֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת, מֻתֶּרֶת, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא כְפֶתַח.
phrases.en: Any breach that is approximately ten cubits wide is permitted and does not invalidate the partition because it is considered like an entrance.

phrases.he: יָתֵר מִכָּאן, אָסוּר:
phrases.en: However, if one of the breaches is greater than ten cubits, it is prohibited to carry anywhere in the enclosed area.

phrases.he: מַקִּיפִין שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲבָלִים, זֶה לְמַעְלָה מִזֶּה וְזֶה לְמַעְלָה מִזֶּה,
phrases.en: one surrounds the area with three ropes, one above another, and one above the other two.

phrases.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בֵּין חֶבֶל לַחֲבֵרוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים.
phrases.en: provided that there will not be a gap of three handbreadths between one rope and the next.

phrases.he: שִׁעוּר חֲבָלִים וְעָבְיָן, יָתֵר עַל טֶפַח, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא הַכֹּל עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים:
phrases.en: The measure of the ropes and their thickness must be greater than a handbreadth, so that the entire partition, consisting of three ropes and the empty spaces between them, will be ten handbreadths high.

phrases.he: מַקִּיפִין בְּקָנִים, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בֵין קָנֶה לַחֲבֵרוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים.
phrases.en: one may surround the area with boards that stand upright, provided that there will not be a gap of three handbreadths between one board and the next.

phrases.he: בְּשַׁיָּרָא דִבְּרוּ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: they spoke exclusively of a caravan; this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, לֹא דִבְּרוּ בְשַׁיָּרָא אֶלָּא בַהֹוֶה.
phrases.en: However, the Rabbis say: They spoke of a caravan only because they spoke in the present,

phrases.he: כָּל מְחִצָּה שֶׁאֵינָהּ שֶׁל שְׁתִי וְשֶׁל עֵרֶב, אֵינָהּ מְחִצָּה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: Any partition that is not constructed of both warp and woof, is not a partition; this is the statement of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֶחָד מִשְּׁנֵי דְבָרִים.
phrases.en: However, the Rabbis say: One of the two elements,

phrases.he: אַרְבָּעָה דְבָרִים פָּטְרוּ בַמַּחֲנֶה, מְבִיאִין עֵצִים מִכָּל מָקוֹם, וּפְטוּרִים מֵרְחִיצַת יָדַיִם, וּמִדְּמַאי, וּמִלְּעָרֵב:
phrases.en: The Sages exempted a soldier in a military camp in four matters: One may bring wood from any place with no concern that he is stealing wood from its owners; and one is exempt from ritual washing of the hands before eating; and one is exempt from the separation of tithes from doubtfully tithed produce [demai], and one is exempt from establishing an eiruv.

phrases.he: עוֹשִׂין פַּסִּין לַבֵּירָאוֹת אַרְבָּעָה דְיוּמְדִין, נִרְאִין כִּשְׁמֹנָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: One may arrange upright boards [passin] around a well. Four double posts [deyomadin] that look like eight single posts, i.e., four corner pieces, each comprised of two posts joined together at right angles; this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, שְׁמֹנָה, נִרְאִין כִּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר, אַרְבָּעָה דְיוּמְדִין וְאַרְבָּעָה פְשׁוּטִין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: There must be eight posts that look like twelve. How so? There must be four double posts, one in each corner, with four plain posts, one between each pair of double posts.

phrases.he: גָּבְהָן עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, וְרָחְבָּן שִׁשָּׁה, וְעָבְיָן כָּל שֶׁהוּא, וּבֵינֵיהֶן כִּמְלֹא שְׁתֵּי רְבָקוֹת שֶׁל שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁלֹשׁ בָּקָר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: The height of the double posts must be at least ten handbreadths, their width must be six handbreadths, and their thickness may be even a minimal amount. And between them, i.e., between the posts, there may be a gap the size of two teams [revakot] of three oxen each; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, שֶׁל אַרְבַּע אַרְבַּע, קְשׁוּרוֹת וְלֹא מֻתָּרוֹת, אַחַת נִכְנֶסֶת וְאַחַת יוֹצֵאת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda disagrees and says: There may be a slightly larger gap, the size of two teams of four oxen each, and this gap is measured with the cows being tied together and not untied, and with the minimal space necessary for one team to be entering while the other one is leaving.

phrases.he: מֻתָּר לְהַקְרִיב לַבְּאֵר,
phrases.en: It is permitted to bring the posts closer to the well,

phrases.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁתְּהֵא פָרָה רֹאשָׁהּ וְרֻבָּהּ בִּפְנִים וְשׁוֹתָה.
phrases.en: provided that the enclosed area is large enough for a cow to stand with its head and the majority of its body inside the partitioned space while it drinks.

phrases.he: מֻתָּר לְהַרְחִיק כָּל שֶׁהוּא,
phrases.en: It is permitted to distance the boards from the well and expand the enclosed area by any amount, i.e., as much as one wishes,

phrases.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיַּרְבֶּה בְּפַסִּין:
phrases.en: provided that he increases the number of upright boards between the double posts.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, עַד בֵּית סָאתָיִם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: The partitioned area may be expanded up to an area of two beit se'a,

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, לֹא אָמְרוּ בֵית סָאתַיִם אֶלָּא לְגִנָּה וּלְקַרְפֵּף,
phrases.en: The Rabbis said to him: They only spoke of an area of two beit se'a with regard to a garden or an enclosure [karpef].

phrases.he: אֲבָל אִם הָיָה דִּיר אוֹ סַחַר, אוֹ מֻקְצֶה אוֹ חָצֵר,
phrases.en: But if it was a pen [dir], or a stable [sahar], or a backyard, or a courtyard

phrases.he: אֲפִלּוּ בֵית חֲמֵשֶׁת כּוֹרִין, אֲפִלּוּ בֵית עֲשָׂרָה כּוֹרִין, מֻתָּר.
phrases.en: even if it had an area of five beit kor or even ten beit kor, it is permitted.

phrases.he: וּמֻתָּר לְהַרְחִיק כָּל שֶׁהוּא, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיַּרְבֶּה בְּפַסִּין:
phrases.en: And it is permitted to distance the boards and expand the enclosed area by any amount, provided that one increases the upright boards

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם הָיְתָה דֶרֶךְ הָרַבִּים מַפְסַקְתָּן, יְסַלְּקֶנָּה לַצְּדָדִין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: If the path of the public domain passes through and obstructs it, one must divert the path to the sides,

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: One need not

phrases.he: אֶחָד בּוֹר הָרַבִּים, וּבְאֵר הָרַבִּים, וּבְאֵר הַיָּחִיד, עוֹשִׂין לָהֶן פַּסִּין,
phrases.en: a public cistern as well as a public well and even a private well, one may arrange upright boards around them

phrases.he: אֲבָל לְבוֹר הַיָּחִיד עוֹשִׂין לוֹ מְחִצָּה גָבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.en: But in the case of a private cistern, one must construct for it a partition ten handbreadths high; this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶן בָּבָא אוֹמֵר, אֵין עוֹשִׂין פַּסִּין אֶלָּא לִבְאֵר הָרַבִּים בִּלְבַד, וְלַשְּׁאָר עוֹשִׂין חֲגוֹרָה גָבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava says: One may arrange upright boards only for a public well. But for the others, one must set up a belt, ten handbreadths high.

phrases.he: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶן בָּבָא,
phrases.en: And furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava said:

phrases.he: הַגִּנָּה וְהַקַּרְפֵּף שֶׁהֵן שִׁבְעִים אַמָּה וְשִׁירַיִם עַל שִׁבְעִים אַמָּה וְשִׁירַיִם,
phrases.en: With regard to a garden or a karpef, that is not more than seventy cubits and a remainder, a little more, as will be explained below, by seventy cubits and a remainder,

phrases.he: מֻקֶּפֶת גָּדֵר גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
phrases.en: and is surrounded by a wall ten handbreadths high,

phrases.he: מְטַלְטְלִין בְּתוֹכָהּ,
phrases.en: one may carry inside it,

phrases.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בָהּ שׁוֹמֵירָה אוֹ בֵית דִּירָה, אוֹ שֶׁתְּהֵא סְמוּכָה לָעִיר.
phrases.en: provided that it contains a watchman's booth or a dwelling place, or it is near the town

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.he: אֲפִלּוּ אֵין בָּהּ אֶלָּא בוֹר וְשִׁיחַ וּמְעָרָה,
phrases.en: even if it contains only a cistern, an elongated water ditch, or a cave,

phrases.he: מְטַלְטְלִין בְּתוֹכָהּ.
phrases.en: one may carry inside it,

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.he: אֲפִלּוּ אֵין בָּהּ אַחַת מִכָּל אֵלּוּ,
phrases.en: Even if it has none of these

phrases.he: מְטַלְטְלִין בְּתוֹכָהּ,
phrases.en: one may carry inside it,

phrases.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בָהּ שִׁבְעִים אַמָּה וְשִׁירַיִם עַל שִׁבְעִים אַמָּה וְשִׁירָיִם.
phrases.en: provided that it measures not more than seventy cubits and a remainder by seventy cubits and a remainder.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.he: אִם הָיָה אָרְכָּהּ יָתֵר עַל רָחְבָּהּ אֲפִלּוּ אַמָּה אַחַת,
phrases.en: If its length is greater than its breadth, even by one cubit,

phrases.he: אֵין מְטַלְטְלִין בְּתוֹכָהּ.
phrases.en: one may not carry inside it,

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.he: אֲפִלּוּ אָרְכָּהּ פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּרָחְבָּהּ,
phrases.en: Even if its length is double its breadth,

phrases.he: מְטַלְטְלִין בְּתוֹכָהּ:
phrases.en: one may carry inside it,

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אִלָּעִאי, שָׁמַעְתִּי מֵרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וַאֲפִלּוּ הִיא כְּבֵית כּוֹר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Elai said: I heard from Rabbi Eliezer that one is permitted to carry in a garden or karpef, even if the garden is an area of a beit kor

phrases.he: וְכֵן שָׁמַעְתִּי מִמֶּנּוּ, אַנְשֵׁי חָצֵר שֶׁשָּׁכַח אַחַד מֵהֶן וְלֹא עֵרֵב, בֵּיתוֹ אָסוּר מִלְּהַכְנִיס וּלְהוֹצִיא, לוֹ, אֲבָל לָהֶם מֻתָּר.
phrases.en: And I also heard from him another halakha: If one of the residents of a courtyard forgot and did not join in an eiruv with the other residents when they established an eiruv, then it is prohibited for him, the one who forgot to establish an eiruv, to bring in objects or take them out from his house to the courtyard; however, it is permitted to them

phrases.he: וְכֵן שָׁמַעְתִּי מִמֶּנּוּ, שֶׁיּוֹצְאִין בְּעַקְרַבְנִים בְּפֶסַח.
phrases.en: And I also heard from him another halakha, that one may fulfill his obligation to eat bitter herbs on Passover with arkablin

phrases.he: וְחִזַּרְתִּי עַל כָּל תַּלְמִידָיו וּבִקַּשְׁתִּי לִי חָבֵר, וְלֹא מָצָאתִי:
phrases.en: I circulated among all of Rabbi Eliezer's disciples, seeking a colleague who had also heard these matters from him, but I could not find one

phrases.he: בַּכֹּל מְעָרְבִין וּמִשְׁתַּתְּפִים, חוּץ מִן הַמַּיִם וּמִן הַמֶּלַח.
phrases.en: One may establish a joining with all kinds of food except for water and salt.

phrases.he: וְהַכֹּל נִקָּח בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר, חוּץ מִן הַמַּיִם וּמִן הַמֶּלַח.
phrases.en: All types of food may be bought with second-tithe money, except for water and salt.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹדֵר מִן הַמָּזוֹן, מֻתָּר בְּמַיִם וּבְמֶלַח.
phrases.en: One who vows that nourishment is prohibited to him is permitted to eat water and salt.

phrases.he: מְעָרְבִין לְנָזִיר בְּיַיִן וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵל בִּתְרוּמָה.
phrases.en: One may establish an eiruv for a nazirite with wine, and similarly, for an Israelite with teruma.

phrases.he: סוּמְכוֹס אוֹמֵר, בְּחֻלִּין.
phrases.en: Summakhos says: with unconsecrated food.

phrases.he: וּלְכֹהֵן בְּבֵית הַפְּרָס.
phrases.en: For a priest in a beit haperas.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיָּכוֹל לֵילֵךְ לָחוּץ וְלֶאֱכֹל:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: even between the graves in a graveyard, since he can interpose between himself and the graves and go and eat.

phrases.he: מְעָרְבִין בִּדְמַאי, וּבְמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִטְּלָה תְרוּמָתוֹ, וּבְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁנִּפְדּוּ.
phrases.en: One may establish an eiruv with demai, and similarly, one may establish an eiruv with the first tithe whose teruma has been taken in order to be given to a priest, and with the second tithe and consecrated articles that have been redeemed

phrases.he: וְהַכֹּהֲנִים, בְּחַלָּה וּבִתְרוּמָה.
phrases.en: and priests may establish an eiruv with ḥalla, the portion of dough that must be given to a priest

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא בְטֶבֶל, וְלֹא בְמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלֹּא נִטְּלָה תְרוּמָתוֹ, וְלֹא בְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא נִפְדּוּ.
phrases.en: However, one may not establish an eiruv with tevel, produce from which the priestly dues and other tithes have not been separated, nor with first tithe whose teruma, which must be given to a priest, has not been taken, nor with the second tithe or consecrated articles that have not been redeemed

phrases.he: הַשּׁוֹלֵחַ עֵרוּבוֹ בְּיַד חֵרֵשׁ, שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן, אוֹ בְיַד מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹדֶה בָעֵרוּב, אֵינוֹ עֵרוּב.
phrases.en: If one sends his eiruv in the hands of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor, all of whom are regarded as legally incompetent, or in the hands of one who does not accept the principle of eiruv, it is not a valid eiruv

phrases.he: וְאִם אָמַר לְאַחֵר לְקַבְּלוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ, הֲרֵי זֶה עֵרוּב:
phrases.en: But if one told another person to receive it from him at a specific location and set it down in that spot, it is a valid eiruv

phrases.he: נְתָנוֹ בְאִילָן, לְמַעְלָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, אֵין עֵרוּבוֹ עֵרוּב.
phrases.en: If one placed his eiruv in a tree above ten handbreadths from the ground, his eiruv is not a valid eiruv;

phrases.he: לְמַטָּה מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, עֵרוּבוֹ עֵרוּב.
phrases.en: if it is below ten handbreadths, his eiruv is a valid eiruv.

phrases.he: נְתָנוֹ בְּבוֹר, אֲפִלּוּ עָמוֹק מֵאָה אַמָּה, עֵרוּבוֹ עֵרוּב.
phrases.en: If he placed the eiruv in a pit, even if it was a hundred cubits deep, his eiruv is a valid eiruv.

phrases.he: נְתָנוֹ בְרֹאשׁ הַקָּנֶה אוֹ בְרֹאשׁ הַקֻּנְדָּס בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא תָלוּשׁ וְנָעוּץ, אֲפִלּוּ גָבוֹהַּ מֵאָה אַמָּה, הֲרֵי זֶה עֵרוּב.
phrases.en: If one placed his eiruv on top of a reed or on top of a pole [kundas], when the reed or pole is detached from its original place and stuck into the ground, even if it is a hundred cubits high, it is a valid eiruv,

phrases.he: נְתָנוֹ בְמִגְדָּל וְאָבַד הַמַּפְתֵּחַ, הֲרֵי זֶה עֵרוּב.
phrases.en: If one put the eiruv in a cupboard and locked it, and the key was lost, it is nonetheless a valid eiruv.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אִם אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהַמַּפְתֵּחַ בִּמְקוֹמוֹ, אֵינוֹ עֵרוּב:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: If he does not know that the key is in its place, it is not a valid eiruv.

phrases.he: נִתְגַּלְגֵּל חוּץ לַתְּחוּם,
phrases.en: rolled beyond the Shabbat limit,

phrases.he: וְנָפַל עָלָיו גַּל,
phrases.en: a pile of stones fell on it, or

phrases.he: אוֹ נִשְׂרַף,
phrases.en: it was burnt,

phrases.he: אוֹ תְרוּמָה וְנִטְמֵאת,
phrases.en: teruma and it became ritually impure;

phrases.he: מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם,
phrases.en: while it was still day,

phrases.he: אֵינוֹ עֵרוּב,
phrases.en: it is not a valid eiruv,

phrases.he: מִשֶּׁחֲשֵׁכָה, הֲרֵי זֶה עֵרוּב.
phrases.en: after dark, it is a valid eiruv.

phrases.he: אִם סָפֵק,
phrases.en: If the matter is in doubt,

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמְרִים, הֲרֵי זֶה חַמָּר גַּמָּל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda say: This is the position of both a donkey driver and a camel driver,

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים, סְפֵק עֵרוּב, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say: An eiruv whose validity is in doubt is valid.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, אַבְטוֹלְמוֹס הֵעִיד מִשּׁוּם חֲמִשָּׁה זְקֵנִים עַל סְפֵק עֵרוּב שֶׁכָּשֵׁר:
phrases.en: Rav Yosei said: The Sage Avtolemos testified in the name of five Elders that an eiruv whose validity is in doubt is valid.

phrases.he: מַתְנֶה אָדָם עַל עֵרוּבוֹ וְאוֹמֵר, אִם בָּאוּ גוֹיִים מִן הַמִּזְרָח, עֵרוּבִי לַמַּעֲרָב.
phrases.en: A person may make a condition with regard to his eiruv and say: If gentiles come from the east, my eiruv is in the west,

phrases.he: מִן הַמַּעֲרָב, עֵרוּבִי לַמִּזְרָח.
phrases.en: from the west, my eiruv is in the east.

phrases.he: אִם בָּאוּ מִכָּאן וּמִכָּאן, לִמְקוֹם שֶׁאֶרְצֶה אֵלֵךְ.
phrases.en: If they come from here and from there, I will go wherever I wish,

phrases.he: לֹא בָאוּ לֹא מִכָּאן וְלֹא מִכָּאן, הֲרֵינִי כִבְנֵי עִירִי.
phrases.en: if they do not come neither from here nor from there, I will be like the inhabitants of my town.

phrases.he: אִם בָּא חָכָם מִן הַמִּזְרָח, עֵרוּבִי לַמִּזְרָח.
phrases.en: If a Sage comes from the east my eiruv is in the east,

phrases.he: מִן הַמַּעֲרָב, עֵרוּבִי לַמַּעֲרָב.
phrases.en: from the west, my eiruv is in the west.

phrases.he: בָּא לְכָאן וּלְכָאן, לִמְקוֹם שֶׁאֶרְצֶה אֵלֵךְ.
phrases.en: comes from here, and from there, I will go wherever I wish;

phrases.he: לֹא לְכָאן וְלֹא לְכָאן, הֲרֵינִי כִבְנֵי עִירִי.
phrases.en: and if no Sage comes, neither from here nor from there, I will be like the inhabitants of my town.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם הָיָה אֶחָד מֵהֶן רַבּוֹ, הוֹלֵךְ אֵצֶל רַבּוֹ,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: If one of them was his teacher, he may go to his teacher,

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם רַבּוֹתָיו, לִמְקוֹם שֶׁיִּרְצֶה יֵלֵךְ:
phrases.en: And if they were both his teachers, he may go wherever he wishes.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.he: יוֹם טוֹב הַסָּמוּךְ לְשַׁבָּת, בֵּין מִלְּפָנֶיהָ וּבֵין מִלְּאַחֲרֶיהָ,
phrases.en: With regard to a Festival adjacent to Shabbat, whether before it, on a Friday, or after it, on a Sunday,

phrases.he: מְעָרֵב אָדָם שְׁנֵי עֵרוּבִין וְאוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: a person may establish two eiruvin of Shabbat borders [teḥumin] and say as follows:

phrases.he: עֵרוּבִי הָרִאשׁוֹן לַמִּזְרָח, וְהַשֵּׁנִי לַמַּעֲרָב.
phrases.en: My eiruv on the first day shall be to the east, and on the second day to the west.

phrases.he: הָרִאשׁוֹן לַמַּעֲרָב, וְהַשֵּׁנִי לַמִּזְרָח.
phrases.en: On the first day it shall be to the west and on the second day to the east.

phrases.he: עֵרוּבִי הָרִאשׁוֹן, וְהַשֵּׁנִי כִּבְנֵי עִירִי.
phrases.en: My eiruv shall apply on the first day, but on the second day I shall be like the rest of the inhabitants of my town,

phrases.he: עֵרוּבִי הַשֵּׁנִי, וְהָרִאשׁוֹן כִּבְנֵי עִירִי.
phrases.en: My eiruv shall apply on the second day, but on the first day I shall be like the rest of the inhabitants of my town.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים,
phrases.en: And the Rabbis disagree and say that such a split is impossible.

phrases.he: מְעָרֵב לְרוּחַ אַחַת, אוֹ אֵינוֹ מְעָרֵב כָּל עִקָּר.
phrases.en: Rather, he either establishes an eiruv in one direction for both days, or he establishes no eiruv at all;

phrases.he: אוֹ מְעָרֵב לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים, אוֹ אֵינוֹ מְעָרֵב כָּל עִקָּר.
phrases.en: either he establishes an eiruv for the two days, or he establishes no eiruv at all.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד יַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.en: What does one do to establish an eiruv that will be valid for both the Festival and Shabbat?

phrases.he: מוֹלִיכוֹ בָרִאשׁוֹן, וּמַחְשִׁיךְ עָלָיו וְנוֹטְלוֹ וּבָא לוֹ.
phrases.en: He or his agent brings the eiruv to the location that he wishes to establish as his residence on the eve of the first day, and he stays there with it until nightfall, the time when the eiruv establishes that location as his residence for the Festival, and then he takes it with him and goes away, so that it will not become lost before the following evening, in which case he would not have an eiruv for the second day.

phrases.he: בַּשֵּׁנִי מַחְשִׁיךְ עָלָיו וְאוֹכְלוֹ.
phrases.en: On the eve of the second day, he takes it back to the same place as the day before, and he stays there with it until nightfall, thereby establishing his residence for Shabbat, and then he may eat the eiruv and go away, if he so desires.

phrases.he: וְנִמְצָא מִשְׂתַּכֵּר בַּהֲלִיכָתוֹ וּמִשְׂתַּכֵּר בְּעֵרוּבוֹ.
phrases.en: Consequently, he benefits in that he is permitted to walk in the direction that he desires, and he benefits in that he is permitted to eat his eiruv.

phrases.he: נֶאֱכַל בָּרִאשׁוֹן, עֵרוּבוֹ לָרִאשׁוֹן וְאֵינוֹ עֵרוּב לַשֵּׁנִי.
phrases.en: However, if the eiruv was eaten on the first day, his eiruv is effective for the first day, and his eiruv is not effective for the second day.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, מוֹדִים אַתֶּם לִי שֶׁהֵן שְׁתֵּי קְדֻשּׁוֹת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer said to them: If so, you agree with me that Shabbat and a Festival constitute two distinct sanctities, as if not, the eiruv that went into effect during the twilight period on the eve of the first day should have remained in effect for both days, even if it was eaten during the first day. This being the case, you should also agree with me that one can make two separate eiruvin for the two days in two different directions.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.he: רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, שֶׁהָיָה יָרֵא שֶׁמָּא תִּתְעַבֵּר,
phrases.en: With regard to Rosh HaShana, if one feared that the month of Elul might be extended,

phrases.he: מְעָרֵב אָדָם שְׁנֵי עֵרוּבִין וְאוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: person may establish two eiruvin and say:

phrases.he: עֵרוּבִי בָרִאשׁוֹן לַמִּזְרָח וּבַשֵּׁנִי לַמַּעֲרָב,
phrases.en: My eiruv on the first day shall be to the east and on the second day to the west,

phrases.he: בָּרִאשׁוֹן לַמַּעֲרָב וּבַשֵּׁנִי לַמִּזְרָח.
phrases.en: On the first day it shall be to the west, and on the second day to the east.

phrases.he: עֵרוּבִי בָּרִאשׁוֹן, וּבַשֵּׁנִי כִּבְנֵי עִירִי.
phrases.en: My eiruv shall apply on the first day, but on the second day I shall be like the rest of the inhabitants of my town,

phrases.he: עֵרוּבִי בַּשֵּׁנִי, וּבָרִאשׁוֹן כִּבְנֵי עִירִי.
phrases.en: My eiruv shall apply on the second day, but on the first day I shall be like the rest of the inhabitants of my town.

phrases.he: וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים:
phrases.en: And the Rabbis did not agree with him

phrases.he: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.en: And Rabbi Yehuda said further,

phrases.he: מַתְנֶה אָדָם עַל הַכַּלְכָּלָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן וְאוֹכְלָהּ בַּשֵּׁנִי.
phrases.en: A person may make a condition with regard to a basket on the first day of the Festival and he may then eat it on the second day of the Festival,

phrases.he: וְכֵן בֵּיצָה שֶׁנּוֹלְדָה בָרִאשׁוֹן, תֵּאָכֵל בַּשֵּׁנִי.
phrases.en: And similarly, an egg that was laid on the first day of the Festival may be eaten on the second day,

phrases.he: וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים:
phrases.en: And the Rabbis did not agree with him

phrases.he: רַבִּי דוֹסָא בֶן הַרְכִּינָס אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Dosa ben Harekinas says:

phrases.he: הָעוֹבֵר לִפְנֵי הַתֵּבָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: One who passes before the ark on the first day of the festival of Rosh HaShana says:

phrases.he: הַחֲלִיצֵנוּ ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ אֶת יוֹם רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה, אִם הַיּוֹם, אִם לְמָחָר.
phrases.en: Strengthen us, O Lord our God, on this day of the New Moon, whether it is today or tomorrow.

phrases.he: וּלְמָחָר הוּא אוֹמֵר, אִם הַיּוֹם, אִם אֶמֶשׁ.
phrases.en: And on the following day he says: Whether Rosh HaShana is today or yesterday.

phrases.he: וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים:
phrases.en: And the Rabbis did not agree with him.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּהוּ גוֹיִם אוֹ רוּחַ רָעָה, אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.en: one whom gentiles took him out or if an evil spirit took him out, i.e., he was temporarily insane, and found himself outside the Shabbat limit, he has only four cubits that he may walk from where he is standing.

phrases.he: הֶחֱזִירוּהוּ, כְּאִלּוּ לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.en: If the gentiles returned him, or if he came back while still under the influence of the evil spirit, it is as though he had never left his Shabbat limit, and he may move about within his original limit as before.

phrases.he: הוֹלִיכוּהוּ לְעִיר אַחֶרֶת.
phrases.en: If the gentiles brought him to a different city that was surrounded by walls,

phrases.he: נְתָנוּהוּ בְדִיר אוֹ בְסַהַר, רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמְרִים, מְהַלֵּךְ אֶת כֻּלָּהּ.
phrases.en: or if they put him into a pen or a stable, i.e., animal enclosures, the Sages disagree. Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya say: He may walk about the entire city, as the whole city is considered like four cubits.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמְרִים, אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva say: He has only four cubits from where he was placed.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבָּאוּ מִפְּרַנְדִּיסִין וְהִפְלִיגָה סְפִינָתָם בַּיָּם.
phrases.en: There was an incident where all of these Sages were coming from Pelandarsin, an overseas location, and their boat set sail on the sea on Shabbat, taking them beyond their Shabbat limit.

phrases.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה הִלְּכוּ אֶת כֻּלָּהּ.
phrases.en: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya walked about the entire boat, as they hold that the entire boat is considered like four cubits,

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לֹא זָזוּ מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, שֶׁרָצוּ לְהַחֲמִיר עַל עַצְמָן.
phrases.en: while Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva did not move beyond four cubits, as they sought to be stringent with themselves.

phrases.he: פַּעַם אַחַת לֹא נִכְנְסוּ לַנָּמָל עַד שֶׁחֲשֵׁכָה.
phrases.en: one occasion, they did not enter the port until after nightfall

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, מָה אָנוּ לֵירֵד.
phrases.en: said to Rabban Gamliel: What alighting

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶן, מֻתָּר אַתֶּם, שֶׁכְּבָר הָיִיתִי מִסְתַּכֵּל, וְהָיִינוּ בְתוֹךְ הַתְּחוּם עַד שֶׁלֹּא חֲשֵׁכָה.
phrases.en: He said to them: You are permitted as I was watching, and we were within the limit before nightfall.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁיָּצָא בִרְשׁוּת וְאָמְרוּ לוֹ, כְּבָר נַעֲשָׂה מַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.en: one who was permitted to leave his Shabbat limit, i.e., he went out to testify that he had seen the new moon or for some life-saving purpose, and they said to him along the way: The action has already been performed, and there is no need for you to travel for that purpose,

phrases.he: יֶשׁ לוֹ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכָל רוּחַ.
phrases.en: he has two thousand cubits in each direction from the location where he was standing when this was told to him.

phrases.he: אִם הָיָה בְתוֹךְ הַתְּחוּם, כְּאִלּוּ לֹא יָצָא,
phrases.en: If he was within his original limit, it is considered as if he had not left his limit, and he may return to his original location.

phrases.he: שֶׁכָּל הַיּוֹצְאִים לְהַצִּיל, חוֹזְרִין לִמְקוֹמָן:
phrases.en: All who go out to battle and save lives may return to their original locations on Shabbat.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁיָּשַׁב בַּדֶּרֶךְ, וְעָמַד, וְרָאָה וַהֲרֵי הוּא סָמוּךְ לָעִיר,
phrases.en: a person who was sitting along the road and he stood up he saw that he was near the town

phrases.he: הוֹאִיל וְלֹא הָיְתָה כַוָּנָתוֹ לְכָךְ, לֹא יִכָּנֵס, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: since he had not intended to acquire his place of residence in the town, he may not enter it; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, יִכָּנֵס.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: He may enter the town.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, מַעֲשֶׂה הָיָה, וְנִכְנַס רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן בְּלֹא מִתְכַּוֵּן:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda said: It once happened that Rabbi Tarfon entered a town on Shabbat without intention from the beginning of Shabbat to establish residence in the city.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁיָּשֵׁן בַּדֶּרֶךְ וְלֹא יָדַע שֶׁחֲשֵׁכָה, יֵשׁ לוֹ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכָל רוּחַ,
phrases.en: one who was sleeping along the road and did not know that night had fallen, he has two thousand cubits in each direction;

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי.
phrases.en: this is the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri,

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.en: But the Rabbis say: He has only four cubits,

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, וְהוּא בְאֶמְצָעָן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: and he is in the middle of them,

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, לְאֵיזֶה רוּחַ שֶׁיִּרְצֶה יֵלֵךְ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: He may walk in any direction he wishes.

phrases.he: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה שֶׁאִם בֵּרֵר לוֹ, שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לַחֲזֹר בּוֹ:
phrases.en: But Rabbi Yehuda agrees that if he selected for himself he cannot retract

phrases.he: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם, מִקְצָת אַמּוֹתָיו שֶׁל זֶה בְּתוֹךְ אַמּוֹתָיו שֶׁל זֶה, מְבִיאִין וְאוֹכְלִין בָּאֶמְצַע, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יוֹצִיא זֶה מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ לְתוֹךְ שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ.
phrases.en: there were two people in this situation, positioned in such a way that part of the four cubits of one were subsumed within the four cubits of the other, they may each bring food and eat together in the shared area in the middle, provided that the one does not carry anything from his four-cubit limit into that of his fellow.

phrases.he: הָיוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה, וְהָאֶמְצָעִי מֻבְלָע בֵּינֵיהֶן, הוּא מֻתָּר עִמָּהֶן וְהֵן מֻתָּרִין עִמּוֹ, וּשְׁנַיִם הַחִיצוֹנִים אֲסוּרִים זֶה עִם זֶה.
phrases.en: there were three people in this situation, and certain parts of the four cubits of the middle one were subsumed within the respective limits of each of the others, so that he shared a certain area with each of them, he is permitted to eat with either of them, and they are both permitted to eat with him; but the two outer ones are forbidden to eat with each other, since they share no common area.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה, לְשָׁלֹשׁ חֲצֵרוֹת הַפְּתוּחוֹת זוֹ לָזוֹ וּפְתוּחוֹת לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, עֵרְבוּ שְׁתֵּיהֶן עִם הָאֶמְצָעִית, הִיא מֻתֶּרֶת עִמָּהֶם וְהֵן מֻתָּרוֹת עִמָּהּ, וּשְׁתַּיִם הַחִיצוֹנוֹת אֲסוּרוֹת זוֹ עִם זוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon said: To what is this comparable? It is like three courtyards that open into one another, and also open into a public domain. If the two outer courtyards established an eiruv with the middle one, the middle one is permitted to carry to the two outer ones, and they are permitted to carry to it, but the two outer courtyards are prohibited to carry from one to the other, as they did not establish an eiruv with one another.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁבָּא בַדֶּרֶךְ וְחָשְׁכָה לוֹ
phrases.en: one who was coming along the way and it grew dark while he was traveling

phrases.he: וְהָיָה מַכִּיר אִילָן אוֹ גָדֵר
phrases.en: and he was familiar with a tree or a fence

phrases.he: וְאָמַר, שְׁבִיתָתִי תַחְתָּיו, לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם.
phrases.en: and he said: My residence is beneath that tree, he has not said anything

phrases.he: שְׁבִיתָתִי בְעִקָּרוֹ, מְהַלֵּךְ מִמְּקוֹם רַגְלָיו וְעַד עִקָּרוֹ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה
phrases.en: My residence is at the trunk, he may walk from the place he is standing to the trunk two thousand cubits

phrases.he: וּמֵעִקָּרוֹ וְעַד בֵּיתוֹ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה.
phrases.en: and from the trunk to his house, two thousand cubits

phrases.he: נִמְצָא מְהַלֵּךְ מִשֶּׁחֲשֵׁכָה אַרְבַּעַת אֲלָפִים אַמָּה.
phrases.en: Consequently, he walks after nightfall four thousand cubits

phrases.he: אִם אֵינוֹ מַכִּיר, אוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָקִי בַהֲלָכָה,
phrases.en: If one is not familiar or if he is not an expert in the halakha,

phrases.he: וְאָמַר, שְׁבִיתָתִי בִמְקוֹמִי,
phrases.en: and he said: My residence is at my current location,

phrases.he: זָכָה לוֹ מְקוֹמוֹ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכָל רוּחַ.
phrases.en: then his presence at his current location acquires for him the right to walk two thousand cubits in each direction.

phrases.he: עֲגֻלּוֹת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס.
phrases.en: circularly, this is the statement of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigenos.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, מְרֻבָּעוֹת, כְּטַבְלָא מְרֻבַּעַת, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא נִשְׂכָּר לַזָּוִיּוֹת:
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: These are measured squarely, as a square tablet, so that he gains the corners.

phrases.he: וְזוֹ הִיא שֶׁאָמְרוּ, הֶעָנִי מְעָרֵב בְּרַגְלָיו.
phrases.en: And this is which the Sages said: The pauper establishes an eiruv with his feet,

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר, אָנוּ אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא עָנִי.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir said: We have this leniency in effect only for a pauper,

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֶחָד עָנִי וְאֶחָד עָשִׁיר, לֹא אָמְרוּ מְעָרְבִין בְּפַת אֶלָּא לְהָקֵל עַל הֶעָשִׁיר, שֶׁלֹּא יֵצֵא וִיעָרֵב בְּרַגְלָיו:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: Both a pauper and a wealthy person. The Sages said that one establishes an eiruv with bread only in order to be lenient with the wealthy person, so that he need not exert himself and go out and establish an eiruv with his feet.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁיָּצָא לֵילֵךְ בְּעִיר שֶׁמְּעָרְבִין בָּהּ
phrases.en: If a person set out to go to a town for which an eiruv is established

phrases.he: וְהֶחֱזִירוֹ חֲבֵרוֹ,
phrases.en: and another person caused him to return

phrases.he: הוּא מֻתָּר לֵילֵךְ
phrases.en: he himself is permitted to go

phrases.he: וְכָל בְּנֵי הָעִיר אֲסוּרִין,
phrases.en: and all the residents of the town it is prohibited

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, כֹּל שֶׁהוּא יָכוֹל לְעָרֵב וְלֹא עֵרֵב,
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: Anyone who can establish an eiruv, and did not establish an eiruv,

phrases.he: הֲרֵי זֶה חַמָּר גַּמָּל:
phrases.en: is a donkey driver, and a camel driver,

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁיָּצָא חוּץ לַתְּחוּם, אֲפִלּוּ אַמָּה אַחַת, לֹא יִכָּנֵס.
phrases.en: One who went out beyond his Shabbat limit, even if only one cubit, may not reenter.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, שְׁתַּיִם, יִכָּנֵס, שָׁלֹשׁ, לֹא יִכָּנֵס.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: If he went out two cubits he may reenter; however, if he went out three cubits he may not reenter.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁהֶחְשִׁיךְ חוּץ לַתְּחוּם, אֲפִלּוּ אַמָּה אַחַת, לֹא יִכָּנֵס.
