phrases.en: With regard to one for whom it grew dark while he was traveling outside the Shabbat limit of the town where he was heading, even if he was only one cubit outside the limit he may not enter the town.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמּוֹת, יִכָּנֵס, שֶׁאֵין הַמָּשׁוֹחוֹת מְמַצִּין אֶת הַמִּדּוֹת, מִפְּנֵי הַטּוֹעִין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: Even if he was fifteen cubits beyond the limit he may enter the town, because the surveyors do not precisely demarcate the measures; rather, they mark the Shabbat limit within the two thousand cubits, due to those who err.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הֶעָרִים
phrases.en: How does one extend the boundaries of cities

phrases.he: בַּיִת נִכְנָס בַּיִת יוֹצֵא
phrases.en: a house is recessed and another house protrudes

phrases.he: פָּגוּם נִכְנָס פָּגוּם יוֹצֵא
phrases.en: a turret is recessed and another turret protrudes

phrases.he: הָיוּ שָׁם גְּדוּדִיּוֹת גְּבוֹהוֹת עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים
phrases.en: there were remnants of walls ten handbreadths high

phrases.he: וּגְשָׁרִים וּנְפָשׁוֹת
phrases.en: and bridges and monuments

phrases.he: שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן בֵּית דִּירָה
phrases.en: over graves in which there is a residence

phrases.he: מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הַמִּדָּה כְנֶגְדָּן
phrases.en: one extends the measure opposite them

phrases.he: וְעוֹשִׂין אוֹתָהּ כְּמִין טַבְלָא מְרֻבַּעַת
phrases.en: And one renders it like a square tablet

phrases.he: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא נִשְׂכָּר אֶת הַזָּוִיּוֹת
phrases.en: so that it gains the corners

phrases.he: נוֹתְנִין קַרְפֵּף לָעִיר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: One allocates a karpef to every city, this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, לֹא אָמְרוּ קַרְפֵּף אֶלָּא בֵין שְׁתֵּי עֲיָרוֹת,
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: They spoke of a karpef only between two cities.

phrases.he: אִם יֵשׁ לָזוֹ שִׁבְעִים אַמָּה וְשִׁירַיִם, וְלָזוֹ שִׁבְעִים אַמָּה וְשִׁירַיִם,
phrases.en: If this city has seventy cubits and a remainder and that city has seventy cubits and a remainder,

phrases.he: עוֹשֶׂה קַרְפֵּף לִשְׁתֵּיהֶן לִהְיוֹתָן כְּאֶחָת:
phrases.en: the karpef combines the two cities into one.

phrases.he: וְכֵן שְׁלֹשָׁה כְפָרִים הַמְּשֻׁלָּשִׁין,
phrases.en: And likewise, in the case of three villages that are arranged as a triangle,

phrases.he: אִם יֵשׁ בֵּין שְׁנַיִם הַחִיצוֹנִים מֵאָה וְאַרְבָּעִים וְאֶחָד וּשְׁלִישׁ,
phrases.en: if there are only 141⅓ cubits separating between the two outer villages,

phrases.he: עָשָׂה אֶמְצָעִי אֶת שְׁלָשְׁתָּן לִהְיוֹתָן כְּאֶחָד:
phrases.en: the middle village combines the three villages into one.

phrases.he: אֵין מוֹדְדִין אֶלָּא בְחֶבֶל שֶׁל חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה, לֹא פָחוֹת וְלֹא יוֹתֵר.
phrases.en: One may measure a Shabbat limit only with a rope fifty cubits long, no less and no more.

phrases.he: וְלֹא יִמְדּוֹד אֶלָּא כְנֶגֶד לִבּוֹ.
phrases.en: And one may measure the limit only at the level of one's heart.

phrases.he: הָיָה מוֹדֵד וְהִגִּיעַ לְגַיְא אוֹ לְגָדֵר, מַבְלִיעוֹ וְחוֹזֵר לְמִדָּתוֹ.
phrases.en: If one was measuring the limit and he reached a canyon or a fence, he spans it and then resumes his measurement.

phrases.he: הִגִּיעַ לְהָר, מַבְלִיעוֹ וְחוֹזֵר לְמִדָּתוֹ, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יֵצֵא חוּץ לַתְּחוּם.
phrases.en: If one reached a hill, he spans the hill as if it were not there and then resumes his measurement, provided he does not thereby go out beyond the city's Shabbat limit.

phrases.he: אִם אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהַבְלִיעוֹ, בָּזוֹ אָמַר רַבִּי דוֹסְתַּאי בַּר רַבִּי יַנַּאי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר, שָׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁמְּקַדְּרִין בֶּהָרִים.
phrases.en: If, due to the width of the canyon or hill, he cannot span it, with regard to this situation Rabbi Dostai bar Yannai said in the name of Rabbi Meir: I heard that one may pierce hills.

phrases.he: אֵין מוֹדְדִין אֶלָּא מִן הַמֻּמְחֶה.
phrases.en: may measure the Shabbat limit only with an expert surveyor

phrases.he: רִבָּה לְמָקוֹם אֶחָד וּמִעֵט לְמָקוֹם אַחֵר, שׁוֹמְעִין לִמְקוֹם שֶׁרִבָּה.
phrases.en: If it is discovered that the surveyor extended the limit in one place and reduced it in another place, one accepts the measurement of the place where he extended the limit and straightens the limit accordingly

phrases.he: רִבָּה לְאֶחָד וּמִעֵט לְאַחֵר, שׁוֹמְעִין לַמְרֻבֶּה.
phrases.en: Similarly, if the surveyor extended the limit for one and reduced it for another, one accepts the extended measurement

phrases.he: אֲפִלּוּ עֶבֶד, אֲפִלּוּ שִׁפְחָה, נֶאֱמָנִין לוֹמַר, עַד כָּאן תְּחוּם שַׁבָּת, שֶׁלֹּא אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים אֶת הַדָּבָר לְהַחֲמִיר אֶלָּא לְהָקֵל:
phrases.en: And furthermore, even a gentile slave and even a gentile maidservant, whose testimonies are generally considered unreliable, are trustworthy to say: The Shabbat limit extended until here; as the Sages did not state the matter, the laws of Shabbat limits, to be stringent, but rather to be lenient

phrases.he: עִיר שֶׁל יָחִיד וְנַעֲשֵׂית שֶׁל רַבִּים, מְעָרְבִין אֶת כֻּלָּהּ.
phrases.en: a private city, which does not have many residents, grows and becomes a heavily populated public city, one may establish a joining of the courtyards for all of it,

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל רַבִּים וְנַעֲשֵׂית שֶׁל יָחִיד, אֵין מְעָרְבִין אֶת כֻּלָּהּ, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשָׂה חוּצָה לָהּ כְּעִיר חֲדָשָׁה שֶׁבִּיהוּדָה, שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ חֲמִשִּׁים דִּיוּרִים,
phrases.en: And if a public city loses residents over time and becomes a private city, one may not establish an eiruv for all of it unless one maintains an area outside the eiruv that is like the size of the city of Ḥadasha in Judea, which has fifty residents.

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, שָׁלֹשׁ חֲצֵרוֹת שֶׁל שְׁנֵי בָתִּים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: three courtyards with two houses each.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁהָיָה בַמִּזְרָח וְאָמַר לִבְנוֹ, עָרֵב לִי בַמַּעֲרָב,
phrases.en: One who was to the east of his home when Shabbat began, and he had said to his son: Establish an eiruv for me to the west;

phrases.he: בַּמַּעֲרָב וְאָמַר לִבְנוֹ, עָרֵב לִי בַמִּזְרָח,
phrases.en: or, if he was to the west of his home and he had said to his son: Establish an eiruv for me to the east,

phrases.he: אִם יֵשׁ הֵימֶנּוּ וּלְבֵיתוֹ אַלְפַּיִם אַמּוֹת, וּלְעֵרוּבוֹ יוֹתֵר מִכָּאן, מֻתָּר לְבֵיתוֹ וְאָסוּר לְעֵרוּבוֹ.
phrases.en: If there is a distance of two thousand cubits from his current location to his house, and the distance to his eiruv is greater than this, he is permitted to walk to his house, but it is prohibited for him to his eiruv.

phrases.he: לְעֵרוּבוֹ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה, וּלְבֵיתוֹ יוֹתֵר מִכָּאן, אָסוּר לְבֵיתוֹ וּמֻתָּר לְעֵרוּבוֹ.
phrases.en: If the distance from one's current location to his eiruv is two thousand cubits, and the distance to his house is greater than this, he is prohibited from walking to his house, and he is permitted to his eiruv,

phrases.he: הַנּוֹתֵן אֶת עֵרוּבוֹ בְעִבּוּרָהּ שֶׁל עִיר, לֹא עָשָׂה וְלֹא כְלוּם.
phrases.en: One who places his eiruv in the outskirts of the city, he has not done anything.

phrases.he: נְתָנוֹ חוּץ לַתְּחוּם, אֲפִלּוּ אַמָּה אַחַת, מַה שֶׁנִּשְׂכָּר הוּא מַפְסִיד:
phrases.en: If he placed his eiruv outside the city's boundary, even one cubit, what he gains he loses

phrases.he: אַנְשֵׁי עִיר גְּדוֹלָה מְהַלְּכִין אֶת כָּל עִיר קְטַנָּה, וְאֵין אַנְשֵׁי עִיר קְטַנָּה מְהַלְּכִין אֶת כָּל עִיר גְּדוֹלָה.
phrases.en: The residents of a large city may walk through an entire small city, and the residents of a small city may not walk through an entire large city,

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד.
מִי שֶׁהָיָה בְעִיר גְּדוֹלָה וְנָתַן אֶת עֵרוּבוֹ בְעִיר קְטַנָּה, בְּעִיר קְטַנָּה וְנָתַן אֶת עֵרוּבוֹ בְעִיר גְּדוֹלָה, מְהַלֵּךְ אֶת כֻּלָּהּ וְחוּצָה לָהּ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה.
phrases.en: One who was in a large city and placed his eiruv in a small city, or one who was in a small city and placed his eiruv in a large city, may walk through the entire city in which he placed his eiruv and another two thousand cubits beyond it,

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא מִמְּקוֹם עֵרוּבוֹ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: He has only two thousand cubits from the place of his eiruv,

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva said to the Rabbis:

phrases.he: אִי אַתֶּם מוֹדִים לִי בְנוֹתֵן עֵרוּבוֹ בִמְעָרָה, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מִמְּקוֹם עֵרוּבוֹ אֶלָּא אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה.
phrases.en: Do you not concede to me that one who places his eiruv in a cave has only two thousand cubits from the place of his eiruv,

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, אֵימָתַי,
phrases.en: The Rabbis said to him: When

phrases.he: בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ דִּיוּרִין,
phrases.en: When the cave has no residents.

phrases.he: אֲבָל יֶשׁ בָּהּ דִּיוּרִין, מְהַלֵּךְ אֶת כֻּלָּהּ וְחוּצָה לָהּ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה.
phrases.en: But if it has residents, one may walk through all of it and another two thousand cubits beyond it.

phrases.he: נִמְצָא, קַל תּוֹכָהּ מֵעַל גַּבָּהּ.
phrases.en: Consequently, the halakha with regard to an eiruv placed inside a cave is sometimes more lenient than the halakha governing an eiruv placed in the area above the cave.

phrases.he: וְלַמּוֹדֵד שֶׁאָמְרוּ נוֹתְנִין לוֹ אַלְפַּיִם, שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ סוֹף מִדָּתוֹ כָּלֶה בִמְעָרָה:
phrases.en: And as for one who is measuring with regard to whom the Sages said that one gives him two thousand cubits, that measurement applies even if the end of his measurement terminates in the middle of a cave.

phrases.he: הַדָּר עִם הַנָּכְרִי בֶחָצֵר, אוֹ עִם מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹדֶה בָעֵרוּב, הֲרֵי זֶה אוֹסֵר עָלָיו, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: One who resides with a gentile in the same courtyard, or with one who does not accept the principle of eiruv, this person renders it prohibited for him.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר, לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ שְׁנֵי יִשְׂרְאֵלִים אוֹסְרִין זֶה עַל זֶה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says: Actually, the gentile does not render it prohibited unless there are two Jews living in the same courtyard who themselves would prohibit one another.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.en: Rabban Gamliel said:

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בִצְדוֹקִי אֶחָד, שֶׁהָיָה דָר עִמָּנוּ בְּמָבוֹי בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם,
phrases.en: There was an incident involving a certain Sadducee who lived with us in the same alleyway in Jerusalem,

phrases.he: וְאָמַר לָנוּ אַבָּא, מַהֲרוּ וְהוֹצִיאוּ אֶת כָּל הַכֵּלִים לַמָּבוֹי,
phrases.en: And Father said to us: Hurry and take out your utensils to the alleyway

phrases.he: עַד שֶׁלֹּא יוֹצִיא וְיֶאֱסֹר עֲלֵיכֶם.
phrases.en: before he takes out and renders it prohibited for you to

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר בְּלָשׁוֹן אַחֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: with a different formulation,

phrases.he: מַהֲרוּ וַעֲשׂוּ צָרְכֵיכֶם בַּמָּבוֹי
phrases.en: Hurry and do whatever you must do in the alleyway

phrases.he: עַד שֶׁלֹּא יוֹצִיא וְיֶאֱסֹר עֲלֵיכֶם:
phrases.en: before he takes out and renders it prohibited for you to

phrases.he: אַנְשֵׁי חָצֵר שֶׁשָּׁכַח אַחַד מֵהֶן וְלֹא עֵרֵב.
phrases.en: If one of the residents of a courtyard forgot and did not participate in an eiruv

phrases.he: בֵּיתוֹ אָסוּר מִלְּהַכְנִיס וּמִלְּהוֹצִיא, לוֹ וְלָהֶם.
phrases.en: his house is prohibited to him and to them to bring in objects from the courtyard to his house or to take them out from his house into the courtyard

phrases.he: וְשֶׁלָּהֶם מֻתָּרִין, לוֹ וְלָהֶם.
phrases.en: But their houses are permitted to him and to them

phrases.he: נָתְנוּ לוֹ רְשׁוּתָן, הוּא מֻתָּר וְהֵן אֲסוּרִין.
phrases.en: If they gave away their rights to him, he is permitted but they are prohibited

phrases.he: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם, אוֹסְרִין זֶה עַל זֶה.
phrases.en: If two residents of the courtyard forgot to establish an eiruv, they prohibit one another

phrases.he: שֶׁאֶחָד נוֹתֵן רְשׁוּת וְנוֹטֵל רְשׁוּת, שְׁנַיִם נוֹתְנִים רְשׁוּת וְאֵין נוֹטְלִין רְשׁוּת.
phrases.en: For one may give away and receive rights, whereas two may only give away rights but they may not receive rights

phrases.he: מֵאֵימָתַי נוֹתְנִין רְשׁוּת.
phrases.en: When may one give away rights in a domain?

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם,
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: While it is still day,

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מִשֶּׁחֲשֵׁכָה.
phrases.en: and Beit Hillel say: Even after nightfall,

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁנָּתַן רְשׁוּתוֹ וְהוֹצִיא, בֵּין בְּשׁוֹגֵג בֵּין בְּמֵזִיד, הֲרֵי זֶה אוֹסֵר,
phrases.en: If one gave away his rights in his courtyard to the other residents of the courtyard, renouncing them after having forgotten to establish an eiruv with them the previous day, and then he carried something out from his house into the courtyard – whether unwittingly, forgetting that he had renounced his rights, or intentionally, he renders carrying prohibited for all the residents of the courtyard, for his action cancels his renunciation;

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בְּמֵזִיד אוֹסֵר, בְּשׁוֹגֵג אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: If he acted intentionally, he renders carrying prohibited; but if he acted unwittingly, he does not render carrying prohibited.

phrases.he: בַּעַל הַבַּיִת שֶׁהָיָה שֻׁתָּף לִשְׁכֵנִים, לָזֶה בְיַיִן וְלָזֶה בְיַיִן, אֵינָם צְרִיכִים לְעָרֵב.
phrases.en: a homeowner was in partnership with his neighbors, with this one in wine and with that one in wine, they need not establish an eiruv

phrases.he: לָזֶה בְיַיִן וְלָזֶה בְשֶׁמֶן, צְרִיכִים לְעָרֵב.
phrases.en: with this one in wine and with that one in oil, they must establish an eiruv

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה, אֵינָם צְרִיכִים לְעָרֵב.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: In both this case and that case, they need not establish an eiruv

phrases.he: חָמֵשׁ חֲבוּרוֹת שֶׁשָּׁבְתוּ בִטְרַקְלִין אֶחָד,
phrases.en: five groups of people who spent Shabbat in one hall [teraklin]

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, עֵרוּב לְכָל חֲבוּרָה וַחֲבוּרָה.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: An eiruv is required for each and every group

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, עֵרוּב אֶחָד לְכֻלָּן.
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: One eiruv suffices for all of them

phrases.he: וּמוֹדִים, בִּזְמַן שֶׁמִּקְצָתָן שְׁרוּיִן בַּחֲדָרִים אוֹ בַעֲלִיּוֹת, שֶׁהֵן צְרִיכִין עֵרוּב לְכָל חֲבוּרָה וַחֲבוּרָה:
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel concede that when some of them occupy separate rooms or upper stories, they require a separate eiruv for each and every group

phrases.he: הָאַחִין הַשֻּׁתָּפִין שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹכְלִין עַל שֻׁלְחַן אֲבִיהֶם וִישֵׁנִים בְּבָתֵּיהֶם, צְרִיכִין עֵרוּב לְכָל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
phrases.en: brothers who were eating at their father's table and sleeping in their own houses in the same courtyard, a separate contribution to the eiruv is required for each and every one of them

phrases.he: לְפִיכָךְ, אִם שָׁכַח אֶחָד מֵהֶם וְלֹא עֵרֵב, מְבַטֵּל אֶת רְשׁוּתוֹ.
phrases.en: Therefore, if one of them forgot and did not contribute to the eiruv, he must renounce his rights in the courtyard in order to render carrying in the courtyard permitted to the rest of the courtyard's residents

phrases.he: אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁמּוֹלִיכִין עֵרוּבָן בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר,
phrases.en: When do they state this halakha? They state it when they take their eiruv elsewhere in the courtyard, i.e., to the house of one of the other residents

phrases.he: אֲבָל אִם הָיָה עֵרוּב בָּא אֶצְלָן, אוֹ שֶׁאֵין עִמָּהֶן דִּיוּרִין בֶּחָצֵר, אֵינָן צְרִיכִין לְעָרֵב:
phrases.en: But if the eiruv was coming to them, or if there are no other residents with the brothers and their father in the courtyard, they are not required to establish an eiruv

phrases.he: חָמֵשׁ חֲצֵרוֹת פְּתוּחוֹת זוֹ לָזוֹ וּפְתוּחוֹת לְמָבוֹי,
phrases.en: five courtyards open into one another and also open into an alleyway,

phrases.he: עֵרְבוּ בַחֲצֵרוֹת וְלֹא נִשְׁתַּתְּפוּ בַמָּבוֹי,
phrases.en: the residents of the courtyard established an eiruv in the courtyards and did not merge the courtyards that open into the alleyway,

phrases.he: מֻתָּרִין בַּחֲצֵרוֹת וַאֲסוּרִין בַּמָּבוֹי.
phrases.en: they are permitted to carry in the courtyards and they are prohibited to carry in the alleyway.

phrases.he: וְאִם נִשְׁתַּתְּפוּ בַמָּבוֹי,
phrases.en: And if they merged the courtyards of the alleyway,

phrases.he: מֻתָּרִין כָּאן וָכָאן.
phrases.en: they are permitted to carry both here, in the alleyway, and there, in the courtyards.

phrases.he: עֵרְבוּ בַחֲצֵרוֹת וְנִשְׁתַּתְּפוּ בַמָּבוֹי,
phrases.en: If they established an eiruv in the courtyards and also merged the courtyards of the alleyway,

phrases.he: וְשָׁכַח אֶחָד מִבְּנֵי חָצֵר וְלֹא עֵרֵב,
phrases.en: and one of the residents of the courtyard forgot and did not contribute to the eiruv in his courtyard, but did participate in the merging of the courtyards in the alleyway,

phrases.he: מֻתָּרִין כָּאן וָכָאן.
phrases.en: they are permitted both here and there,

phrases.he: מִבְּנֵי מָבוֹי וְלֹא נִשְׁתַּתֵּף,
phrases.en: However, if one of the residents of the alleyway forgot and did not participate in the merging of courtyards that open into the alleyway,

phrases.he: מֻתָּרִין בַּחֲצֵרוֹת וַאֲסוּרִין בַּמָּבוֹי,
phrases.en: they are permitted to carry in the courtyards and prohibited from carrying in the alleyway,

phrases.he: שֶׁהַמָּבוֹי לַחֲצֵרוֹת כֶּחָצֵר לַבָּתִּים:
phrases.en: as the principle is: An alleyway is to its courtyards as a courtyard is to its houses.

phrases.he: שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵרוֹת, זוֹ לִפְנִים מִזּוֹ,
phrases.en: two courtyards, one of which was within the other,

phrases.he: עֵרְבָה הַפְּנִימִית וְלֹא עֵרְבָה הַחִיצוֹנָה,
phrases.en: the inner courtyard established an eiruv for itself and the outer one did not establish an eiruv,

phrases.he: הַפְּנִימִית מֻתֶּרֶת וְהַחִיצוֹנָה אֲסוּרָה.
phrases.en: carrying in the inner one is permitted and carrying in the outer one is prohibited.

phrases.he: הַחִיצוֹנָה, וְלֹא הַפְּנִימִית,
phrases.en: the outer courtyard established an eiruv and the inner one did not,

phrases.he: שְׁתֵּיהֶן אֲסוּרוֹת.
phrases.en: carrying in both is prohibited,

phrases.he: עֵרְבָה זוֹ לְעַצְמָהּ וְזוֹ לְעַצְמָהּ,
phrases.en: this courtyard established an eiruv for itself, and that courtyard also established an eiruv for itself,

phrases.he: זוֹ מֻתֶּרֶת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ וְזוֹ מֻתֶּרֶת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ.
phrases.en: this one is permitted by itself, and that one is permitted by itself,

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹסֵר הַחִיצוֹנָה,
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva prohibits carrying in the outer one

phrases.he: שֶׁדְּרִיסַת הָרֶגֶל אוֹסַרְתָּהּ.
phrases.en: as the right of entry to the outer courtyard enjoyed by the residents of the inner courtyard renders it prohibited.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים,
phrases.en: And the Rabbis disagree and say:

phrases.he: אֵין דְּרִיסַת הָרֶגֶל אוֹסַרְתָּהּ:
phrases.en: The right of entry enjoyed by the residents of the inner courtyard does not render it prohibited.

phrases.he: שָׁכַח אַחַד מִן הַחִיצוֹנָה וְלֹא עֵרֵב, הַפְּנִימִית מֻתֶּרֶת וְהַחִיצוֹנָה אֲסוּרָה.
phrases.en: If one resident of the outer courtyard forgot and did not contribute to the eiruv, carrying in the inner courtyard is permitted and in the outer one is prohibited.

phrases.he: מִן הַפְּנִימִית וְלֹא עֵרֵב, שְׁתֵּיהֶן אֲסוּרוֹת.
phrases.en: If one resident of the inner courtyard forgot and did not contribute to the eiruv, they are both prohibited,

phrases.he: נָתְנוּ עֵרוּבָן בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד, וְשָׁכַח אֶחָד, בֵּין מִן הַפְּנִימִית בֵּין מִן הַחִיצוֹנָה, וְלֹא עֵרֵב, שְׁתֵּיהֶן אֲסוּרוֹת.
phrases.en: If the residents of both courtyards put their eiruv in one place, and one person, whether he was from the inner courtyard or from the outer one, forgot and did not contribute to the eiruv, they are both prohibited

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיוּ שֶׁל יְחִידִים, אֵינָן צְרִיכִין לְעָרֵב:
phrases.en: And if the courtyards belonged to individuals, they are not required to establish an eiruv,

phrases.he: חַלּוֹן שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵרוֹת, אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה, בְּתוֹךְ עֲשָׂרָה, מְעָרְבִין שְׁנַיִם, וְאִם רָצוּ, מְעָרְבִין אֶחָד.
phrases.en: a window in a wall that separates between two courtyards, and the window measures four by four handbreadths and is within ten handbreadths of the ground, the inhabitants of the courtyards establish two eiruvin, one for each courtyard. And if they desire, they may establish one eiruv, thereby merging the two courtyards, as they may be considered as one due to the window.

phrases.he: פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה, אוֹ לְמַעְלָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה, מְעָרְבִין שְׁנַיִם וְאֵין מְעָרְבִין אֶחָד:
phrases.en: less than four by four handbreadths, or if it is above ten handbreadths from the ground, it is no longer considered a valid opening, and the two courtyards cannot be considered a single courtyard. Therefore, the residents establish two eiruvin, but they may not establish one eiruv.

phrases.he: כֹּתֶל שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵרוֹת גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה וְרָחָב אַרְבָּעָה,
phrases.en: a wall between two courtyards is ten handbreadths high and four handbreadths wide,

phrases.he: מְעָרְבִין שְׁנַיִם וְאֵין מְעָרְבִין אֶחָד.
phrases.en: the residents of the courtyard establish two eiruvin, a separate one for each courtyard, but they may not establish one eiruv.

phrases.he: הָיוּ בְרֹאשׁוֹ פֵרוֹת, אֵלּוּ עוֹלִין מִכָּאן וְאוֹכְלִין, וְאֵלּוּ עוֹלִין מִכָּאן וְאוֹכְלִין, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יוֹרִידוּ לְמַטָּה.
phrases.en: If there was produce on top of the wall, these residents of one courtyard may ascend from this side and eat from it, and those residents of the other courtyard may ascend from that side and eat from it, provided that they do not lower the produce down from on top of the wall to one of the courtyards.

phrases.he: נִפְרְצָה הַכֹּתֶל עַד עֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת, מְעָרְבִין שְׁנַיִם, וְאִם רָצוּ מְעָרְבִין אֶחָד, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא כְפֶתַח.
phrases.en: If the wall was breached, the following distinction applies: If the breach was up to ten cubits wide, they establish two eiruvin, and if they desire, they may establish one eiruv, as it is similar to an entrance, like any opening less than ten cubits wide.

phrases.he: יוֹתֵר מִכָּאן, מְעָרְבִין אֶחָד וְאֵין מְעָרְבִין שְׁנָיִם:
phrases.en: If the breach was more than this, they establish one eiruv, and they may not establish two,

phrases.he: חָרִיץ שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵרוֹת עָמוֹק עֲשָׂרָה וְרָחָב אַרְבַּע,
phrases.en: a ditch between two courtyards that is ten handbreadths deep and four handbreadths wide,

phrases.he: מְעָרְבִין שְׁנַיִם וְאֵין מְעָרְבִין אֶחָד,
phrases.en: establish two eiruvin, but they may not establish one eiruv.

phrases.he: אֲפִלּוּ מָלֵא קַשׁ אוֹ תֶבֶן.
phrases.en: Even if the ditch is filled with straw or hay,

phrases.he: מָלֵא עָפָר, אוֹ צְרוֹרוֹת, מְעָרְבִין אֶחָד, וְאֵין מְעָרְבִין שְׁנָיִם:
phrases.en: if the ditch is filled with dirt or pebbles, the residents establish one eiruv, but they may not establish two eiruvin,

phrases.he: נָתַן עָלָיו נֶסֶר שֶׁהוּא רָחָב אַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים,
phrases.en: one placed a board four handbreadths wide across

phrases.he: וְכֵן שְׁתֵּי גְזֻזְטְרָאוֹת זוֹ כְנֶגֶד זוֹ,
phrases.en: and similarly, two balconies in two different courtyards are opposite one another,

phrases.he: מְעָרְבִין שְׁנַיִם,
phrases.en: establish two eiruvin,

phrases.he: וְאִם רָצוּ, מְעָרְבִין אֶחָד.
phrases.en: and if they desire, they establish one,

phrases.he: פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן, מְעָרְבִין שְׁנַיִם וְאֵין מְעָרְבִין אֶחָד:
phrases.en: If the width of the plank is less than four handbreadths, the residents establish two eiruvin, but they may not establish one eiruv.

phrases.he: מַתְבֵּן שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵרוֹת, גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
phrases.en: a haystack that is positioned between two courtyards and is ten handbreadths high,

phrases.he: מְעָרְבִין שְׁנַיִם וְאֵין מְעָרְבִין אֶחָד.
phrases.en: they establish two eiruvin, and they do not establish one eiruv.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ מַאֲכִילִין מִכָּאן וְאֵלּוּ מַאֲכִילִין מִכָּאן.
phrases.en: These may feed from here, and those may feed from there,

phrases.he: נִתְמַעֵט הַתֶּבֶן מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
phrases.en: If the hay was reduced to less than ten handbreadths

phrases.he: מְעָרְבִין אֶחָד וְאֵין מְעָרְבִין שְׁנָיִם.
phrases.en: they establish one eiruv, and they do not establish two eiruvin.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד מִשְׁתַּתְּפִין בַּמָּבוֹי.
phrases.en: How does one merge the courtyards that open into the alleyway,

phrases.he: מֵנִיחַ אֶת הֶחָבִית וְאוֹמֵר, הֲרֵי זוֹ לְכָל בְּנֵי מָבוֹי,
phrases.en: He places a barrel and says: This is for all the residents of the alleyway.

phrases.he: וּמְזַכֶּה לָהֶן עַל יְדֵי בְנוֹ וּבִתּוֹ הַגְּדוֹלִים וְעַל יְדֵי עַבְדּוֹ וְשִׁפְחָתוֹ הָעִבְרִים וְעַל יְדֵי אִשְׁתּוֹ,
phrases.en: and he may confer possession to them even by means of his adult son or daughter, and likewise by means of his Hebrew slave or maidservant, and by means of his wife.

phrases.he: אֲבָל אֵינוֹ מְזַכֶּה לֹא עַל יְדֵי בְנוֹ וּבִתּוֹ הַקְּטַנִּים וְלֹא עַל יְדֵי עַבְדּוֹ וְשִׁפְחָתוֹ הַכְּנַעֲנִים,
phrases.en: However, he may not confer possession by means of his minor son or daughter, nor by means of his Canaanite slave or maidservant,

phrases.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיָּדָן כְּיָדוֹ:
phrases.en: because their possession is as his possession.

phrases.he: נִתְמַעֵט הָאֹכֶל, מוֹסִיף וּמְזַכֶּה, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לְהוֹדִיעַ.
phrases.en: If the food diminished and was less than the requisite measure, one may add a little of his own and confer possession to the others, and he need not inform them of his addition.

phrases.he: נִתּוֹסְפוּ עֲלֵיהֶם, מוֹסִיף וּמְזַכֶּה, וְצָרִיךְ לְהוֹדִיעַ:
phrases.en: However, if new residents were added to the residents of the alleyway, he may add food on behalf of those residents and confer possession to them, and he must inform the new residents of their inclusion in the merging of alleyways.

phrases.he: כַּמָּה הוּא שִׁעוּרוֹ.
phrases.en: What is the measure

phrases.he: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן מְרֻבִּין, מְזוֹן שְׁתֵּי סְעוּדוֹת לְכֻלָּם.
phrases.en: When the residents of the alley are numerous, food for two meals is sufficient for all of them;

phrases.he: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן מֻעָטִין, כִּגְרוֹגֶרֶת לְהוֹצָאַת שַׁבָּת לְכָל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד:
phrases.en: when they are few, a dried fig-bulk for each and every one of them is enough.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בִּתְחִלַּת עֵרוּב.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei said: In what case is this statement said? It is said with regard to the beginning of an eiruv, when it is initially established.

phrases.he: אֲבָל בִּשְׁיָרֵי עֵרוּב, כָּל שֶׁהוּא.
phrases.en: However, with regard to the remnants of an eiruv, any amount remains.

phrases.he: וְלֹא אָמְרוּ לְעָרֵב בַּחֲצֵרוֹת אֶלָּא כְדֵי שֶׁלֹּא לְשַׁכֵּחַ אֶת הַתִּינוֹקוֹת:
phrases.en: And they said that it is necessary to join the courtyards, only so that the halakhic category of eiruv will not be forgotten by the children.

phrases.he: בַּכֹּל מְעָרְבִין וּמִשְׁתַּתְּפִין, חוּץ מִן הַמַּיִם וּמִן הַמֶּלַח,
phrases.en: One may join courtyards and merge alleyways with all types of food, except for water and salt,

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.en: the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, כִּכָּר הוּא עֵרוּב.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says that a different limitation applies: A whole loaf may be used for an eiruv.

phrases.he: אֲפִלּוּ מַאֲפֵה סְאָה וְהִיא פְרוּסָה, אֵין מְעָרְבִין בָּהּ.
phrases.en: With regard to a baked product even the size of a se'a, if it consists of pieces, one may not join courtyards with it.

phrases.he: כִּכָּר בְּאִסָּר וְהוּא שָׁלֵם, מְעָרְבִין בּוֹ:
phrases.en: However, with regard to a loaf, even one the size of an issar, if it is whole, one may join courtyards with it.

phrases.he: נוֹתֵן אָדָם מָעָה לְחֶנְוָנִי וּלְנַחְתּוֹם כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה לוֹ עֵרוּב, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.en: A person may give a ma'a coin to a grocer or a baker, so that the grocer or baker will confer upon him possession of an eiruv. This is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, לֹא זָכוּ לוֹ מְעוֹתָיו.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: His money did not confer possession on him,

phrases.he: וּמוֹדִים בִּשְׁאָר כָּל אָדָם שֶׁזָּכוּ לוֹ מְעוֹתָיו, שֶׁאֵין מְעָרְבִין לְאָדָם אֶלָּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis concede with regard to all other people, that his money confers possession upon him, as one may establish an eiruv for a person only with his knowledge.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בְּעֵרוּבֵי תְחוּמִין, אֲבָל בְּעֵרוּבֵי חֲצֵרוֹת, מְעָרְבִין לְדַעְתּוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא לְדַעְתּוֹ, לְפִי שֶׁזָּכִין לְאָדָם שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו, וְאֵין חָבִין לְאָדָם שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda said: In what case is this statement said? It is said with regard to a joining of Shabbat boundaries, but with regard to a joining of courtyards, one may establish an eiruv for a person either with his knowledge or without his knowledge. The reason is because one may act for a person's benefit in his absence, but one may not act to a person's disadvantage in his absence.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד מִשְׁתַּתְּפִין בַּתְּחוּמִין.
phrases.en: How does one participate in the joining of Shabbat boundaries?

phrases.he: מֵנִיחַ אֶת הֶחָבִית וְאוֹמֵר, הֲרֵי זֶה לְכָל בְּנֵי עִירִי, לְכָל מִי שֶׁיֵּלֵךְ לְבֵית הָאֵבֶל אוֹ לְבֵית הַמִּשְׁתֶּה.
phrases.en: One places a barrel and says: This is for all the residents of my town, for anyone who goes to a house of mourning or to a house of a wedding feast.

phrases.he: וְכֹל שֶׁקִּבֵּל עָלָיו מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם, מֻתָּר.
phrases.en: Anyone who accepted upon himself while it was still day, is permitted.

phrases.he: מִשֶּׁתֶּחְשַׁךְ, אָסוּר, שֶׁאֵין מְעָרְבִין מִשֶּׁתֶּחְשָׁךְ.
phrases.en: After nightfall, he is prohibited, as one may not establish an eiruv after nightfall.

phrases.he: כַּמָּה הוּא שִׁעוּרוֹ, מְזוֹן שְׁתֵּי סְעוּדוֹת לְכָל אֶחָד.
phrases.en: What is the measure for food sufficient for two meals for each and every one

phrases.he: מְזוֹנוֹ לְחֹל וְלֹא לְשַׁבָּת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: one's food that he eats on a weekday and not on Shabbat; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, לְשַׁבָּת וְלֹא לְחֹל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: on Shabbat and not on a weekday.

phrases.he: וְזֶה וָזֶה מִתְכַּוְּנִין לְהָקֵל.
phrases.en: And both this and that intended to be lenient,

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר, מִכִּכָּר בְּפֻנְדְּיוֹן, מֵאַרְבַּע סְאִין בְּסֶלַע.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says: of a loaf bought with a pundeyon, when four se'a of wheat are sold for a sela.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, שְׁתֵּי יָדוֹת לְכִכָּר מִשָּׁלֹשׁ לְקָב.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: two parts of a loaf, when three from a kav.

phrases.he: חֶצְיָהּ לְבַיִת הַמְנֻגָּע, וַחֲצִי חֶצְיָהּ לִפְסֹל אֶת הַגְּוִיָּה:
phrases.en: half for a leprous house, and half of its half disqualifies the body.

phrases.he: אַנְשֵׁי חָצֵר וְאַנְשֵׁי מִרְפֶּסֶת שֶׁשָּׁכְחוּ וְלֹא עֵרְבוּ,
phrases.en: the residents of houses that open directly into a courtyard and the residents of apartments that open onto a balcony from which stairs lead down to that courtyard forgot and did not establish an eiruv between them,

phrases.he: כֹּל שֶׁגָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, לַמִּרְפֶּסֶת.
phrases.en: anything in the courtyard that is ten handbreadths high, is part of the balcony.

phrases.he: פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן, לֶחָצֵר.
phrases.en: lower than this height is part of the courtyard.

phrases.he: חֻלְיַת הַבּוֹר וְהַסֶּלַע, גְּבוֹהִים עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, לַמִּרְפֶּסֶת.
phrases.en: an embankment that surrounds a cistern or a rock: If the embankments that surround a cistern or rock are ten handbreadths high, they belong to the balcony;

phrases.he: פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן, לֶחָצֵר.
phrases.en: if they are lower than this, they may be used only by the inhabitants of the courtyard.

phrases.he: בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בִּסְמוּכָה.
phrases.en: In what case are these matters, the halakha that anything higher than ten handbreadths belongs to the balcony, stated? When the mound or embankment is near the balcony.

phrases.he: אֲבָל בְּמֻפְלֶגֶת, אֲפִלּוּ גָבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, לֶחָצֵר.
phrases.en: But in a case where the embankment or mound is distant from it, even if it is ten handbreadths high, the right to use the embankment or mound goes to the members of the courtyard.

phrases.he: וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא סְמוּכָה, כֹּל שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְחוֹקָה אַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים:
phrases.en: And what is considered near? Anything that is not four handbreadths removed from the balcony.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹתֵן אֶת עֵרוּבוֹ בְּבֵית שַׁעַר, אַכְסַדְרָה וּמִרְפֶּסֶת, אֵינוֹ עֵרוּב.
phrases.en: One who placed his eiruv in a gatehouse or in a portico or a balcony, this is not a valid eiruv.

phrases.he: וְהַדָּר שָׁם, אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר עָלָיו.
phrases.en: And one who resides there, does not render it prohibited.

phrases.he: בְּבֵית הַתֶּבֶן וּבְבֵית הַבָּקָר וּבְבֵית הָעֵצִים וּבְבֵית הָאוֹצָרוֹת, הֲרֵי זֶה עֵרוּב.
phrases.en: In a hay shed or in a cowshed or in a woodshed or in a storehouse, this is a valid eiruv.

phrases.he: וְהַדָּר שָׁם, אוֹסֵר עָלָיו.
phrases.en: And one who resides there, renders it prohibited.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם יֶשׁ שָׁם תְּפִיסַת יָד שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת, אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר עָלָיו:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: If the homeowner has there a right of usage, he does not render it prohibited.

phrases.he: הַמַּנִּיחַ בֵּיתוֹ וְהָלַךְ לִשְׁבּוֹת בְּעִיר אַחֶרֶת, אֶחָד נָכְרִי וְאֶחָד יִשְׂרָאֵל, הֲרֵי זֶה אוֹסֵר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: One who leaves his house and goes to spend Shabbat in a different town, whether he is a gentile or a Jew, he renders it prohibited; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: He does not render it prohibited.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, נָכְרִי אוֹסֵר, יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר, שֶׁאֵין דֶּרֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָבֹא בְשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: A gentile renders it prohibited but a Jew does not render it prohibited, as it is not the manner of a Jew to come on Shabbat.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ הִנִּיחַ בֵּיתוֹ וְהָלַךְ לִשְׁבּוֹת אֵצֶל בִּתּוֹ בְאוֹתָהּ הָעִיר, אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר, שֶׁכְּבָר הִסִּיעַ מִלִּבּוֹ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: Even if the Jew left his house and went to spend Shabbat with his daughter who lived in the same town, he does not render it prohibited, that he has already removed from his mind.

phrases.he: בּוֹר שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵרוֹת
phrases.en: a cistern that is located between two courtyards

phrases.he: אֵין מְמַלְּאִין מִמֶּנּוּ בְשַׁבָּת
phrases.en: one may not draw water from it on Shabbat

phrases.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשׂוּ לוֹ מְחִצָּה גָבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים
phrases.en: unless a partition ten handbreadths high was erected for it

phrases.he: בֵּין מִלְמַעְלָה, בֵּין מִלְּמַטָּה, בֵּין מִתּוֹךְ אֹגְנוֹ
phrases.en: whether it is below, or whether it is within the airspace of the cistern below the rim

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מִלְּמַטָּה
phrases.en: Beit Shammai said below

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מִלְמָעְלָה
phrases.en: and Beit Hillel said above

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, לֹא תְהֵא מְחִצָּה גְדוֹלָה מִן הַכֹּתֶל שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶם
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda said: A partition is no better than the wall between them

phrases.he: אַמַּת הַמַּיִם שֶׁהִיא עוֹבֶרֶת בֶּחָצֵר, אֵין מְמַלְּאִין הֵימֶנָּה בְשַׁבָּת, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשׂוּ לָהּ מְחִצָּה גָבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים בַּכְּנִיסָה וּבַיְצִיאָה.
phrases.en: a water channel that passes through a courtyard, the residents may not draw water from it on Shabbat, unless they erected for it a partition ten handbreadths high at the entrance and at the exit

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כֹּתֶל שֶׁעַל גַּבָּהּ תִּדּוֹן מִשּׁוּם מְחִצָּה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: There is no need for a special partition, as the wall that runs on top of it, i.e., the courtyard wall, is considered as a partition.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, מַעֲשֶׂה בָאַמָּה שֶׁל אָבֵל שֶׁהָיוּ מְמַלְּאִין מִמֶּנָּה עַל פִּי זְקֵנִים בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda said: There was an incident involving a water channel that passed through the courtyards of the town of Avel, from which the residents would draw water from it on Shabbat by the authority of the Elders, relying on the courtyard wall suspended above it.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בָהּ כַּשִּׁעוּר:
phrases.en: They said to him: It is due to the fact that channel was not of the size that requires a partition, i.e., it was less than ten handbreadths deep or less than ten handbreadths wide, it was permitted to draw water from it even without a partition.

phrases.he: גְּזוּזְטְרָא שֶׁהִיא לְמַעְלָה מִן הַמַּיִם,
phrases.en: a balcony that extends over a body of water,

phrases.he: אֵין מְמַלְּאִין הֵימֶנָּה בְשַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: if a hole was opened in the floor, its residents may not draw water from it through the hole on Shabbat,

phrases.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשׂוּ לָהּ מְחִצָּה גָבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
phrases.en: unless they erected for it a partition ten handbreadths high

phrases.he: בֵּין מִלְמַעְלָה בֵּין מִלְּמַטָּה.
phrases.en: whether it is positioned above the balcony, in which case the partition is seen as descending downward, or whether it is placed below the balcony.

phrases.he: וְכֵן שְׁתֵּי גְזוּזְטְרָאוֹת זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ.
phrases.en: And likewise, with regard to two such balconies, one above the other,

phrases.he: עָשׂוּ לָעֶלְיוֹנָה וְלֹא עָשׂוּ לַתַּחְתּוֹנָה,
phrases.en: if they erected a partition for the upper balcony but they did not erect one for the lower one,

phrases.he: שְׁתֵּיהֶן אֲסוּרוֹת עַד שֶׁיְּעָרֵבוּ:
phrases.en: the residents are both prohibited from drawing water through the upper one, unless they establish an eiruv between them.

phrases.he: חָצֵר שֶׁהִיא פְחוּתָה מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.en: a courtyard that is less than four cubits

phrases.he: אֵין שׁוֹפְכִין בְּתוֹכָהּ מַיִם בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: one may not pour water into it on Shabbat

phrases.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשׂוּ לָהּ עוּקָה מַחֲזֶקֶת סָאתַיִם מִן הַנֶּקֶב וּלְמַטָּה,
phrases.en: unless a pit was fashioned to receive the water, and the pit holds two se'a in volume from its edge below

phrases.he: בֵּין מִבַּחוּץ בֵּין מִבִּפְנִים,
phrases.en: whether outside the courtyard or whether it was dug inside the courtyard itself

phrases.he: אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּבַּחוּץ צָרִיךְ לִקְמוֹר,
phrases.en: If the pit was dug outside in the adjoining public domain, it is necessary to arch over it

phrases.he: מִבִּפְנִים אֵין צָרִיךְ לִקְמוֹר:
phrases.en: If it was dug inside the courtyard, it is not necessary to arch over it

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:

phrases.he: בִּיב שֶׁהוּא קָמוּר אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, שׁוֹפְכִין לְתוֹכוֹ מַיִם בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: In the case of a drainage ditch whose first four cubits are arched over in the public domain, one may pour waste water into it on Shabbat.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֲפִלּוּ גַג אוֹ חָצֵר מֵאָה אַמָּה, לֹא יִשְׁפֹּךְ עַל פִּי הַבִּיב,
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: Even if a roof or a courtyard is a hundred cubits in area, one may not pour water directly onto the mouth of the drainage ditch.

phrases.he: אֲבָל שׁוֹפֵךְ מִגַּג לְגַג, וְהַמַּיִם יוֹרְדִין לַבִּיב.
phrases.en: However, he may pour it upon the roof, from which the water spills into the drain of its own accord.

phrases.he: הֶחָצֵר וְהָאַכְסַדְרָה מִצְטָרְפִין לְאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת:
phrases.en: A courtyard and a portico, a roofed but unwalled structure in front of a house, combine for the four cubits by virtue of which it is permitted to pour water even into a courtyard that lacks a pit.

phrases.he: וְכֵן שְׁתֵּי דְיוֹטָאוֹת זוֹ כְנֶגֶד זוֹ,
phrases.en: And likewise, with regard to two upper stories [deyotaot], one opposite the other

phrases.he: מִקְצָתָן עָשׂוּ עוּקָה וּמִקְצָתָן לֹא עָשׂוּ עוּקָה,
phrases.en: if the residents of one of them fashioned a pit in the courtyard, and the residents of the other did not fashion a pit,

phrases.he: אֶת שֶׁעָשׂוּ עוּקָה, מֻתָּרִין,
phrases.en: those who fashioned a pit are permitted to pour their waste water into the courtyard,

phrases.he: וְאֶת שֶׁלֹּא עָשׂוּ עוּקָה, אֲסוּרִין:
phrases.en: whereas those who did not fashion a pit are prohibited to do so.

phrases.he: כָּל גַּגּוֹת הָעִיר, רְשׁוּת אַחַת,
phrases.en: All the roofs of the city are considered one domain.

phrases.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא גַג גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה אוֹ נָמוֹךְ עֲשָׂרָה,
phrases.en: provided that one roof is neither ten handbreadths higher nor ten handbreadths lower than the adjacent roof.

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד רְשׁוּת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: Each and every one of the roofs is a domain in and of itself.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אֶחָד גַּגּוֹת וְאֶחָד חֲצֵרוֹת וְאֶחָד קַרְפֵּיפוֹת, רְשׁוּת אֶחָד לַכֵּלִים שֶׁשָּׁבְתוּ לְתוֹכָן,
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: Roofs, courtyards, and enclosures are all one domain with regard to vessels that were inside them when Shabbat began.

phrases.he: וְלֹא לַכֵּלִים שֶׁשָּׁבְתוּ בְתוֹךְ הַבָּיִת:
phrases.en: However, they are not one domain with regard to vessels that were inside the house when Shabbat began.

phrases.he: גַּג גָּדוֹל סָמוּךְ לְקָטָן, הַגָּדוֹל מֻתָּר וְהַקָּטָן אָסוּר.
phrases.en: a large roof was adjacent to a small roof, and the large one is permitted, and the small one is prohibited.

phrases.he: חָצֵר גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁנִּפְרְצָה לִקְטַנָּה, גְּדוֹלָה מֻתֶּרֶת, וּקְטַנָּה אֲסוּרָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא כְפִתְחָהּ שֶׁל גְּדוֹלָה.
phrases.en: a large courtyard that was breached into a small one, permitted for the large courtyard, but prohibited for the small one, because its legal status is like that of the entrance of the large courtyard.

phrases.he: חָצֵר שֶׁנִּפְרְצָה לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, הַמַּכְנִיס מִתּוֹכָהּ לִרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד, אוֹ מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לְתוֹכָהּ, חַיָּב, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.en: a courtyard that was breached into the public domain, one who carries from inside the courtyard into the private domain, or from the private domain into it, is liable, the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, מִתּוֹכָהּ לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, אוֹ מֵרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים לְתוֹכָהּ, פָּטוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא כְּכַרְמְלִית:
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say, from inside the courtyard into the public domain, or from the public domain into it, is exempt, because its legal status is like that of a karmelit.

phrases.he: חָצֵר שֶׁנִּפְרְצָה לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים מִשְּׁתֵּי רוּחוֹתֶיהָ
phrases.en: a courtyard that was breached into a public domain from two of its sides

phrases.he: וְכֵן בַּיִת שֶׁנִּפְרַץ מִשְּׁתֵּי רוּחוֹתָיו
phrases.en: and likewise a house that was breached from two of its sides

phrases.he: וְכֵן מָבוֹי שֶׁנִּטְּלוּ קוֹרוֹתָיו אוֹ לְחָיָיו
phrases.en: and likewise an alleyway whose cross beams or side posts were removed

phrases.he: מֻתָּרִין בְּאוֹתוֹ שַׁבָּת
phrases.en: are permitted on that Shabbat

phrases.he: וַאֲסוּרִין לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא
phrases.en: but are prohibited in the future

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.en: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says

phrases.he: אִם מֻתָּרִין לְאוֹתוֹ שַׁבָּת, מֻתָּרִין לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא
phrases.en: if they are permitted on that Shabbat, they are likewise permitted in the future

phrases.he: וְאִם אֲסוּרִין לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא, אֲסוּרִין לְאוֹתוֹ שַׁבָּת
phrases.en: and if they are prohibited in the future, they are also prohibited on that Shabbat

phrases.he: הַבּוֹנֶה עֲלִיָּה עַל גַּבֵּי שְׁנֵי בָתִּים, וְכֵן גְּשָׁרִים הַמְפֻלָּשִׁים, מְטַלְטְלִין תַּחְתֵּיהֶן בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: one who builds an upper story atop two houses and likewise bridges with a thoroughfare beneath them one may carry beneath the upper story and beneath the bridge on Shabbat.

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִין.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis prohibit

phrases.he: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, מְעָרְבִין לְמָבוֹי הַמְפֻלָּשׁ.
phrases.en: And furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda said: One may establish an eiruv even for an alleyway that is open

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִין:
phrases.en: and the Rabbis prohibit

phrases.he: הַמּוֹצֵא תְפִלִּין, מַכְנִיסָן זוּג זוּג.
phrases.en: One who finds phylacteries brings them in pair by pair

phrases.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, שְׁנַיִם שְׁנָיִם.
phrases.en: Rabban Gamliel says: two pairs by two pairs

phrases.he: בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בִּישָׁנוֹת, אֲבָל בַּחֲדָשׁוֹת, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: In what case is this statement said? It is with regard to old phylacteries. However, with regard to new ones, he is exempt

phrases.he: מְצָאָן צְבָתִים אוֹ כְרִיכוֹת, מַחְשִׁיךְ עֲלֵיהֶן וּמְבִיאָן.
phrases.en: If one finds phylacteries tied in bundles or in wrapped piles, he waits with them until dark, and brings them in

phrases.he: וּבַסַּכָּנָה, מְכַסָּן וְהוֹלֵךְ לוֹ:
phrases.en: And in a time of danger, he covers them and proceeds on his way

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says

phrases.he: נוֹתְנָן לַחֲבֵרוֹ, וַחֲבֵרוֹ לַחֲבֵרוֹ, עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לֶחָצֵר הַחִיצוֹנָה.
phrases.en: One gives them to another who is less than four cubits from him, and the other passes them to another, until the phylacteries reach the outermost courtyard of the city.

phrases.he: וְכֵן בְּנוֹ, נוֹתְנוֹ לַחֲבֵרוֹ, וַחֲבֵרוֹ לַחֲבֵרוֹ, אֲפִלּוּ מֵאָה.
phrases.en: And similarly, with regard to one's son who was born in a field and may not be carried on Shabbat, since that is akin to carrying a burden in the public domain: One gives him to another, and the other passes him to another, even if it requires a hundred people.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, נוֹתֵן אָדָם חָבִית לַחֲבֵרוֹ, וַחֲבֵרוֹ לַחֲבֵרוֹ, אֲפִלּוּ חוּץ לַתְּחוּם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: A person may even give a barrel to another, and the other may pass it to another, and in that way even take it beyond the Shabbat limit, provided that no one person carries it more than four cubits.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, לֹא תְהַלֵּךְ זוֹ יוֹתֵר מֵרַגְלֵי בְעָלֶיהָ:
phrases.en: They said to him: This barrel may not go a greater distance than the feet of its owner, i.e., it may not be carried any farther than its owner may walk.

phrases.he: הָיָה קוֹרֵא בַסֵּפֶר עַל הָאַסְקֻפָּה, נִתְגַּלְגֵּל הַסֵּפֶר מִיָּדוֹ, גּוֹלְלוֹ אֶצְלוֹ.
phrases.en: was reading a sacred book in scroll form on an elevated, wide threshold, and the book rolled from his hand into the public domain, he may roll it back to himself,

phrases.he: הָיָה קוֹרֵא בְרֹאשׁ הַגַּג וְנִתְגַּלְגֵּל הַסֵּפֶר מִיָּדוֹ, עַד שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ לַעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, גּוֹלְלוֹ אֶצְלוֹ.
phrases.en: he was reading on top the roof, and the book rolled from his hand, as long as the edge of the book did not reach within ten handbreadths above the public domain, he may roll it back to himself.

phrases.he: מִשֶּׁהִגִּיעַ לַעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, הוֹפְכוֹ עַל הַכְּתָב.
phrases.en: once the book has reached within ten handbreadths above the public domain, he may only turn it over onto the side with writing,

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ אֵין מְסֻלָּק מִן הָאָרֶץ אֶלָּא כִמְלֹא מַחַט, גּוֹלְלוֹ אֶצְלוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: Even if the scroll is removed only a needle breadth from the ground, he rolls it back to himself.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ בָאָרֶץ עַצְמוֹ גּוֹלְלוֹ אֶצְלוֹ, שֶׁאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת עוֹמֵד בִּפְנֵי כִתְבֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: Even if the scroll is on the ground itself, he rolls it back to himself, as you have nothing that was instituted as a rabbinic decree to enhance the character of Shabbat as a day of rest that stands as an impediment before the rescue of sacred writings.

phrases.he: זִיז שֶׁלִּפְנֵי חַלּוֹן, נוֹתְנִין עָלָיו וְנוֹטְלִין מִמֶּנּוּ בְשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: a ledge in front of a window, one may place objects upon it or remove them from it on Shabbat

phrases.he: עוֹמֵד אָדָם בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וּמְטַלְטֵל בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים וּמְטַלְטֵל בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יוֹצִיא חוּץ מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת:
phrases.en: A person may stand in a private domain and move objects that are in a public domain, as there is no concern that he might mistakenly bring them into the private domain. Similarly, one may stand in a public domain and move objects in a private domain, provided that he does not carry them beyond four cubits in the public domain, which is prohibited on Shabbat.

phrases.he: לֹא יַעֲמֹד אָדָם בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וְיַשְׁתִּין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים וְיַשְׁתִּין בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד.
phrases.en: a person may not stand in a private domain and urinate into a public domain, nor may one stand in a public domain and urinate into a private domain.

phrases.he: וְכֵן לֹא יָרֹק.
phrases.en: And likewise, one may not spit in such a manner that the spittle passes from a private domain to a public domain or vice versa.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף מִשֶּׁנִּתְלַשׁ רֻקּוֹ בְּפִיו, לֹא יְהַלֵּךְ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת עַד שֶׁיָרֹק.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: Even once a person's spittle is gathered in his mouth, he may not walk four cubits in the public domain until he spits it out.

phrases.he: לֹא יַעֲמֹד אָדָם בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָחִיד וְיִשְׁתֶּה בִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
phrases.en: A person may stand in a private domain and extend his head and drink in a public domain,

phrases.he: בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים וְיִשְׁתֶּה בִרְשׁוּת הַיָחִיד,
phrases.en: and he may stand in a public domain and drink in a private domain,

phrases.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִכְנִיס רֹאשׁוֹ וְרֻבּוֹ לִמְקוֹם שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹתֶה.
phrases.en: only if he brings his head and most of his body into the domain in which he drinks.

phrases.he: וְכֵן בְּגַת.
phrases.en: And the same applies in a winepress,

phrases.he: קוֹלֵט אָדָם מִן הַמַּזְחֵלָה לְמַטָּה מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים.
phrases.en: A person standing in a public domain on Shabbat may catch water in a vessel from a gutter running along the side of a roof, if it is less than ten handbreadths off the ground, which is part of the public domain.

phrases.he: וּמִן הַצִּנּוֹר, מִכָּל מָקוֹם שׁוֹתֶה:
phrases.en: And from a pipe that protrudes from the roof, one may drink in any manner,

phrases.he: בּוֹר בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, וְחֻלְיָתוֹ גְבוֹהָה עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
phrases.en: a cistern in a public domain, with an embankment ten handbreadths high,

phrases.he: חַלּוֹן שֶׁעַל גַּבָּיו מְמַלְּאִין הֵימֶנּוּ בְשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: a window above one may draw water from the cistern on Shabbat

phrases.he: אַשְׁפָּה בִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים גְּבוֹהָה עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
phrases.en: a garbage dump in a public domain that is ten handbreadths high,

phrases.he: חַלּוֹן שֶׁעַל גַּבָּהּ שׁוֹפְכִין לְתוֹכָהּ מַיִם בְּשַׁבָּת:
phrases.en: a window above one may throw water onto the dump on Shabbat

phrases.he: אִילָן שֶׁהוּא מֵסֵךְ עַל הָאָרֶץ, אִם אֵין נוֹפוֹ גָבוֹהַּ מִן הָאָרֶץ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים, מְטַלְטְלִין תַּחְתָּיו.
phrases.en: a tree that was hanging over the ground, if the tips of its branches are no higher than three handbreadths from the ground, one may carry under it.

phrases.he: שָׁרָשָׁיו גְּבוֹהִים מִן הָאָרֶץ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים, לֹא יֵשֵׁב עֲלֵיהֶן.
phrases.en: If its roots were three handbreadths higher than the ground, one may not sit on them.

phrases.he: הַדֶּלֶת שֶׁבַּמֻּקְצֶה וַחֲדָקִים שֶׁבַּפִּרְצָה וּמַחֲצָלוֹת, אֵין נוֹעֲלִין בָּהֶן, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן גְּבוֹהִים מִן הָאָרֶץ:
phrases.en: the door to a rear court, and bundles of thorns that seal a breach; and reed mats, one may not close an opening with them on Shabbat, unless they remain above the ground even when they are open.

phrases.he: לֹא יַעֲמֹד אָדָם בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וְיִפְתַּח בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
phrases.en: A person may not stand in the private domain and open a door located in the public domain with a key

phrases.he: בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים וְיִפְתַּח בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד
phrases.en: Likewise, one may not stand in the public domain and open a door in the private domain with a key

phrases.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשָׂה מְחִצָּה גְבוֹהָה עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים
phrases.en: unless in the latter case he erected a partition ten handbreadths high around the door and stands inside it

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
phrases.en: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ
phrases.en: The Rabbis said to him:

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בְשׁוּק שֶׁל פַּטָּמִין שֶׁהָיָה בִירוּשָׁלַיִם
phrases.en: There was an incident at the poultry dealers' market in Jerusalem

phrases.he: שֶׁהָיוּ נוֹעֲלִין וּמַנִּיחִין אֶת הַמַּפְתֵּחַ בַּחַלּוֹן שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי הַפֶּתַח
phrases.en: where they would lock the doors to their shops and place the key in the window that was over the door

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.he: שׁוּק שֶׁל צַמָּרִים הָיָה
phrases.en: That place was a market of wool dealers

phrases.he: נֶגֶר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ גְלֻסְטְרָא
phrases.en: a bolt that has a thick knob [gelustera] at its end

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹסֵר
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer prohibits

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר
phrases.en: and Rabbi Yosei permits it

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer said

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בַכְּנֶסֶת שֶׁבִּטְבֶרְיָא שֶׁהָיוּ נוֹהֲגִין בּוֹ הֶתֵּר
phrases.en: An incident occurred in a synagogue in Tiberias, where they were accustomed to treat use of this bolt as permitted

phrases.he: עַד שֶׁבָּא רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְהַזְּקֵנִים וְאָסְרוּ לָהֶן
phrases.en: until Rabban Gamliel and the Elders came and prohibited it to them

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says

phrases.he: אִסּוּר נָהֲגוּ בָהּ
phrases.en: they were accustomed to treat use of this bolt as prohibited

phrases.he: בָּא רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְהַזְּקֵנִים וְהִתִּירוּ לָהֶן
phrases.en: Rabban Gamliel and the Elders came and permitted it to them

phrases.he: נֶגֶר הַנִּגְרָר, נוֹעֲלִים בּוֹ בַמִּקְדָּשׁ, אֲבָל לֹא בַמְּדִינָה.
phrases.en: a bolt that drags along the ground, one may lock a door with it in the Temple on Shabbat, however, one may not lock a door with this bolt in the country outside the Temple.

phrases.he: וְהַמֻּנָּח, כָּאן וָכָאן אָסוּר.
phrases.en: And with regard to one that rests entirely on the ground, it is prohibited in both places, in and outside the Temple.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הַמֻּנָּח מֻתָּר בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ, וְהַנִּגְרָר בַּמְּדִינָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: One that rests entirely on the ground is permitted in the Temple, and one that drags along the ground is permitted even in the rest of the country.

phrases.he: מַחֲזִירִין צִיר הַתַּחְתּוֹן בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ, אֲבָל לֹא בַמְּדִינָה.
phrases.en: One may restore the lower hinge pin of the door of a carriage, box, or cupboard that becomes dislocated to its place on Shabbat in the Temple, as this action is prohibited by rabbinic decree, which is not in effect in the Temple; but it may not be restored to its place in the rest of the country.

phrases.he: וְהָעֶלְיוֹן, כָּאן וְכָאן אָסוּר.
phrases.en: And restoring the upper hinge pin is prohibited in both places, as this is considered building, a labor prohibited by Torah law, which applies everywhere.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הָעֶלְיוֹן בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ, וְהַתַּחְתּוֹן בַּמְּדִינָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: Restoring the upper hinge pin to its place is permitted in the Temple, while one may restore the lower one to its place even in the rest of the country.

phrases.he: מַחֲזִירִין רְטִיָּה בַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.en: One may return to its place a bandage in the Temple.

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא בַמְּדִינָה.
phrases.en: However, one may not return a bandage to its place in the rest of the country.

phrases.he: אִם בַּתְּחִלָּה, כָּאן וְכָאן אָסוּר.
phrases.en: If one sought to apply the bandage for the first time to an untreated wound on Shabbat, it is prohibited in both places.

phrases.he: קוֹשְׁרִין נִימָא בַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.en: One may tie up a string [nima] that came loose from a harp used in the Temple,

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא בַמְּדִינָה.
phrases.en: but not in the rest of the country.

phrases.he: אִם בַּתְּחִלָּה, כָּאן וְכָאן אָסוּר.
phrases.en: And tying the string to the harp for the first time is prohibited both here and there.

phrases.he: חוֹתְכִין יַבֶּלֶת בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.en: One may cut off a wart by hand in the Temple,

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא בַמְּדִינָה.
phrases.en: However, he may not cut off a wart in the rest of the country.

phrases.he: וְאִם בִּכְלִי, כָּאן וְכָאן אָסוּר:
phrases.en: And if he seeks to cut off the wart with an instrument, it is prohibited in both places.

phrases.he: כֹּהֵן שֶׁלָּקָה בְאֶצְבָּעוֹ, כּוֹרֵךְ עָלֶיהָ גֶמִי בַמִּקְדָּשׁ, אֲבָל לֹא בַמְּדִינָה.
phrases.en: a priest who was injured on his finger, he may temporarily wrap it with a reed in the Temple, but not in the country

phrases.he: אִם לְהוֹצִיא דָם, כָּאן וְכָאן אָסוּר.
phrases.en: If is to draw blood, it is prohibited in both places

phrases.he: בּוֹזְקִין מֶלַח עַל גַּבֵּי כֶבֶשׁ בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא יַחֲלִיקוּ, וּמְמַלְּאִים מִבּוֹר הַגּוֹלָה וּמִבּוֹר הַגָּדוֹל בַּגַּלְגַּל בְּשַׁבָּת, וּמִבְּאֵר הַקַּר בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.en: One may scatter salt on the ramp so that the priests will not slip on their way up. And likewise, one may draw water from the Cistern of the Exiles and from the Great Cistern, by means of the wheel designed for drawing water, even on Shabbat. And one may draw water from the Heker Well only on a Festival

phrases.he: שֶׁרֶץ שֶׁנִּמְצָא בַמִּקְדָּשׁ, כֹּהֵן מוֹצִיאוֹ בְהֶמְיָנוֹ, שֶׁלֹּא לְשַׁהוֹת אֶת הַטֻּמְאָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה.
phrases.en: a creeping animal that is found in the Temple, a priest should carry it out in his girdle, so as not to delay the impurity. This is the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בִּצְבָת שֶׁל עֵץ, שֶׁלֹּא לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַטֻּמְאָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: with wooden prongs, so as not to increase the impurity,

phrases.he: מֵהֵיכָן מוֹצִיאִין אוֹתוֹ, מִן הַהֵיכָל וּמִן הָאוּלָם וּמִבֵּין הָאוּלָם וְלַמִּזְבֵּחַ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן נַנָּס.
phrases.en: from where does one remove it from the Sanctuary, from the Entrance Hall, and from between the Entrance Hall and the altar, the statement of Rabbi Shimon ben Nannas.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, מְקוֹם שֶׁחַיָּבִין עַל זְדוֹנוֹ כָּרֵת וְעַל שִׁגְגָתוֹ חַטָּאת, מִשָּׁם מוֹצִיאִין אוֹתוֹ, וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַמְּקוֹמוֹת כּוֹפִין עָלָיו פְּסַכְתֵּר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: Any place where one is liable to be punished with karet if he intentionally and is liable to bring a sin-offering if he does so unwittingly, from there one must remove it. And the rest of the places one covers with a bowl [pesakhter]

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, מְקוֹם שֶׁהִתִּירוּ לְךָ חֲכָמִים, מִשֶּׁלְּךָ נָתְנוּ לְךָ, שֶׁלֹּא הִתִּירוּ לְךָ אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says Wherever the Sages permitted to you, they granted you only from your own, as they permitted to you only due to rabbinic decree,

phrases.he: אוֹר לְאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר, בּוֹדְקִין אֶת הֶחָמֵץ לְאוֹר הַנֵּר.
phrases.en: On the evening of the fourteenth one searches for leavened bread by candlelight.

phrases.he: כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין מַכְנִיסִין בּוֹ חָמֵץ אֵין צָרִיךְ בְּדִיקָה.
phrases.en: Any place into which one does not take leavened bread does not require a search.

phrases.he: וְלָמָה אָמְרוּ שְׁתֵּי שׁוּרוֹת בַּמַּרְתֵּף, מָקוֹם שֶׁמַּכְנִיסִין בּוֹ חָמֵץ.
phrases.en: And with regard to what said two rows in a cellar, a place into which one takes leavened bread.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, שְׁתֵּי שׁוּרוֹת עַל פְּנֵי כָל הַמַּרְתֵּף.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say two rows across the entire cellar.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, שְׁתֵּי שׁוּרוֹת הַחִיצוֹנוֹת שֶׁהֵן הָעֶלְיוֹנוֹת:
phrases.en: and Beit Hillel say the two external rows which are the upper ones.

phrases.he: אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין שֶׁמָּא גָרְרָה חֻלְדָּה מִבַּיִת לְבַיִת וּמִמָּקוֹם לְמָקוֹם,
phrases.en: one need not be concerned that perhaps a marten dragged leaven from house to house, or from place to place,

phrases.he: דְּאִם כֵּן, מֵחָצֵר לְחָצֵר וּמֵעִיר לְעִיר,
phrases.en: As if so, one need also be concerned that perhaps leaven might have been dragged from courtyard to courtyard and from city to city.

phrases.he: אֵין לַדָּבָר סוֹף:
phrases.en: there is no end to the matter

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בּוֹדְקִין אוֹר אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר וּבְאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר שַׁחֲרִית וּבִשְׁעַת הַבִּעוּר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: One searches for leaven on the evening of the fourteenth of Nisan, and on the fourteenth in the morning, and at the time of the removal of leaven.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, לֹא בָדַק אוֹר אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר, יִבְדֹּק בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: if one did not search on the evening of the fourteenth he should search on the fourteenth during the day.

phrases.he: לֹא בָדַק בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר, יִבְדֹּק בְּתוֹךְ הַמּוֹעֵד.
phrases.en: If he did not search on the fourteenth, he should search during the festival of Passover.

phrases.he: לֹא בָדַק בְּתוֹךְ הַמּוֹעֵד, יִבְדֹּק לְאַחַר הַמּוֹעֵד.
phrases.en: If he did not search during the Festival, he should search after the Festival,

phrases.he: וּמַה שֶּׁמְּשַׁיֵּר, יַנִּיחֶנּוּ בְצִנְעָא, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא צָרִיךְ בְּדִיקָה אַחֲרָיו:
phrases.en: And the principle is: With regard to the leaven that one leaves after the search, he should place it in a concealed location so that it will not require searching after it

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, אוֹכְלִין כָּל חָמֵשׁ, וְשׂוֹרְפִין בִּתְחִלַּת שֵׁשׁ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: One may eat leaven the entire fifth hour of the fourteenth of Nisan, and one must burn it immediately afterward at the beginning of the sixth hour.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אוֹכְלִין כָּל אַרְבַּע, וְתוֹלִין כָּל חָמֵשׁ, וְשׂוֹרְפִין בִּתְחִלַּת שֵׁשׁ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: One may eat the entire fourth hour and one places it in abeyance for the entire fifth hour, and one burns it at the beginning of the sixth hour.

phrases.he: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, שְׁתֵּי חַלּוֹת שֶׁל תּוֹדָה פְסוּלוֹת מֻנָּחוֹת עַל גַּג הָאִצְטַבָּא.
phrases.en: And furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda said: Two disqualified loaves of a thanks-offering are placed on the bench in the colonnade in the Temple as an indicator.

phrases.he: כָּל זְמַן שֶׁמֻּנָּחוֹת, כָּל הָעָם אוֹכְלִים.
phrases.en: As long as the loaves are placed there, the entire nation continues to eat leaven.

phrases.he: נִטְּלָה אַחַת, תּוֹלִין, לֹא אוֹכְלִין וְלֹא שׂוֹרְפִין.
phrases.en: When one of the loaves was taken away, the people know that the time had come to place the leaven in abeyance, meaning that they neither eat nor burn their leaven.

phrases.he: נִטְּלוּ שְׁתֵּיהֶן, הִתְחִילוּ כָל הָעָם שׂוֹרְפִין.
phrases.en: When they were both taken away, the entire nation began burning their leaven.

phrases.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, חֻלִּין נֶאֱכָלִין כָּל אַרְבַּע, וּתְרוּמָה כָּל חָמֵשׁ, וְשׂוֹרְפִין בִּתְחִלַּת שֵׁשׁ:
phrases.en: Rabban Gamliel says that the times are divided differently: Non-sacred foods are eaten the entire fourth hour, and teruma may be eaten during the entire fifth hour. And one burns all leaven including teruma at the beginning of the sixth hour.

phrases.he: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Ḥanina the deputy High Priest says:

phrases.he: מִימֵיהֶם שֶׁל כֹּהֲנִים לֹא נִמְנְעוּ מִלִּשְׂרֹף אֶת הַבָּשָׂר שֶׁנִּטְמָא בִוְלַד הַטֻּמְאָה עִם הַבָּשָׂר שֶׁנִּטְמָא בְאַב הַטֻּמְאָה,
phrases.en: In all the days of the priests, they did not refrain from burning meat that became ritually impure by coming into contact with a secondary source of ritual impurity, together with meat that became ritually impure by contact with a primary source of impurity.

phrases.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמּוֹסִיפִין טֻמְאָה עַל טֻמְאָתוֹ.
phrases.en: even though they would thereby add a degree of impurity to the impurity of the first piece of meat, which was previously impure to a lesser degree.

phrases.he: הוֹסִיף רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְאָמַר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva added and said:

phrases.he: מִימֵיהֶם שֶׁל כֹּהֲנִים לֹא נִמְנְעוּ מִלְּהַדְלִיק אֶת הַשֶּׁמֶן שֶׁנִּפְסַל בִּטְבוּל יוֹם בְּנֵר שֶׁנִּטְמָא בִטְמֵא מֵת,
phrases.en: In all the days of the priests, they did not refrain from lighting teruma oil that was disqualified by coming into contact with one who immersed himself during that day in a lamp that became ritually impure through contact with one who became ritually impure with impurity imparted by a corpse.

phrases.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמּוֹסִיפִין טֻמְאָה עַל טֻמְאָתוֹ:
phrases.en: even though they would thereby add impurity to the impurity of the oil.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר, מִדִּבְרֵיהֶם לָמַדְנוּ, שֶׁשּׂוֹרְפִין תְּרוּמָה טְהוֹרָה עִם הַטְּמֵאָה בְּפֶסַח.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir said: From their statements we learned that one may burn ritually pure teruma with impure teruma when removing leaven on Passover eve.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, אֵינָהּ הִיא הַמִּדָּה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei said: That is not the inference from which the halakha in the case of ritually pure and ritually impure teruma can be learned.

phrases.he: וּמוֹדִים רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, שֶׁשּׂוֹרְפִין זוֹ לְעַצְמָהּ וְזוֹ לְעַצְמָהּ.
phrases.en: And Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, who disagree with regard to the burning of leavened teruma, nevertheless concede that one burns this by itself and that by itself.

phrases.he: עַל מַה נֶּחֱלְקוּ, עַל הַתְּלוּיָה וְעַל הַטְּמֵאָה, שֶׁרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, תִּשָּׂרֵף זוֹ לְעַצְמָהּ וְזוֹ לְעַצְמָהּ, וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, שְׁתֵּיהֶן כְּאֶחָת:
phrases.en: With regard to what did they disagree? They disagreed with regard to whether one may burn teruma in abeyance and definitely impure teruma together, as Rabbi Eliezer says: This should be burned by itself, and that should be burned by itself; and Rabbi Yehoshua says: Both of them may be burned as one.

phrases.he: כָּל שָׁעָה שֶׁמֻּתָּר לֶאֱכֹל, מַאֲכִיל לַבְּהֵמָה לַחַיָּה וְלָעוֹפוֹת, וּמוֹכְרוֹ לַנָּכְרִי, וּמֻתָּר בַּהֲנָאָתוֹ.
phrases.en: For the entire time that it is permitted to eat leavened bread, one may also feed it to his domesticated animals, to non-domesticated animals, and to birds; and one may sell it to a gentile; and it is permitted to derive benefit from it.

phrases.he: עָבַר זְמַנּוֹ, אָסוּר בַּהֲנָאָתוֹ, וְלֹא יַסִּיק בּוֹ תַּנּוּר וְכִירָיִם.
phrases.en: After its time passes, it is prohibited to derive benefit from it, and one may not even light an oven or a stove with leavened bread.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֵין בִּעוּר חָמֵץ אֶלָּא שְׂרֵפָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: The removal of leavened bread is to be accomplished only through burning.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אַף מְפָרֵר וְזוֹרֶה לָרוּחַ אוֹ מַטִּיל לַיָּם:
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: one may even crumble it and throw it into the wind or cast it into the sea.

phrases.he: חָמֵץ שֶׁל נָכְרִי שֶׁעָבַר עָלָיו הַפֶּסַח, מֻתָּר בַּהֲנָאָה.
phrases.en: It is permitted for a Jew to derive benefit from leavened bread of a gentile over which Passover has elapsed.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, אָסוּר בַּהֲנָאָה.
phrases.en: However, it is prohibited to derive benefit from leaven of a Jew over which Passover has elapsed.

phrases.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמות יג) לֹא יֵרָאֶה לְךָ שְׂאֹר:
phrases.en: as it is stated: And no leavened bread shall be seen with you, neither shall there be leaven seen with you, in all your borders

phrases.he: נָכְרִי שֶׁהִלְוָה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל חֲמֵצוֹ, אַחַר הַפֶּסַח מֻתָּר בַּהֲנָאָה.
phrases.en: a gentile lent money to a Jew, and the Jew gave him leavened bread as collateral until after Passover, and after Passover one is permitted to derive benefit from

phrases.he: וְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהִלְוָה אֶת הַנָּכְרִי עַל חֲמֵצוֹ, אַחַר הַפֶּסַח אָסוּר בַּהֲנָאָה.
phrases.en: a Jew lent money to a gentile, and leavened bread was given as collateral during Passover in the same manner as in the previous case, then after Passover it is forbidden to derive benefit

phrases.he: חָמֵץ שֶׁנָּפְלָה עָלָיו מַפֹּלֶת, הֲרֵי הוּא כִמְבֹעָר.
phrases.en: Leavened bread upon which a rockslide has fallen is considered as though it has been eliminated,

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, כָּל שֶׁאֵין הַכֶּלֶב יָכוֹל לְחַפֵּשׂ אַחֲרָיו:
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: Any leavened bread that has been covered to such an extent that a dog cannot search after it

phrases.he: הָאוֹכֵל תְּרוּמַת חָמֵץ בְּפֶסַח בְּשׁוֹגֵג, מְשַׁלֵּם קֶרֶן וְחֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.en: If one unwittingly eats teruma of leavened bread on Passover, he must pay the principal and an additional fifth.

phrases.he: בְּמֵזִיד, פָּטוּר מִתַּשְׁלוּמִים וּמִדְּמֵי עֵצִים:
phrases.en: If he intentionally ate the teruma then he is exempt from payment; its monetary value in wood,

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ דְבָרִים שֶׁאָדָם יוֹצֵא בָהֶן יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בְּפֶסַח, בְּחִטִּים, בִּשְׂעוֹרִים, בְּכֻסְּמִין וּבְשִׁיפוֹן וּבְשִׁבֹּלֶת שׁוּעָל.
phrases.en: These are the types of grain with which a person fulfills his obligation to eat matza on the first night of Passover: With wheat, with barley, with spelt [kusmin], with rye [shifon], and with oats [shibbolet shu'al].

phrases.he: וְיוֹצְאִין בִּדְמַאי וּבְמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּטְּלָה תְרוּמָתוֹ, וּבְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁנִּפְדּוּ, וְהַכֹּהֲנִים בְּחַלָּה וּבִתְרוּמָה.
phrases.en: And one fulfills his obligation by eating not only matza made from properly tithed grains, but even with matza made from doubtfully tithed produce, and matza made with first tithe from which its teruma was already taken, or second tithe and consecrated food that were redeemed. And priests may eat matza prepared from ḥalla, the portion of dough that is given to priests, or with teruma, as priests are permitted to eat these portions.

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא בְטֶבֶל, וְלֹא בְמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלֹּא נִטְּלָה תְרוּמָתוֹ, וְלֹא בְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא נִפְדּוּ.
phrases.en: However, one may not fulfill one's obligation to eat matza made with untithed produce, nor with matza made from the first tithe from which its teruma was not separated, nor with matza made either from the second tithe, nor from consecrated grain that was not redeemed.

phrases.he: חַלּוֹת תּוֹדָה וּרְקִיקֵי נָזִיר, עֲשָׂאָן לְעַצְמוֹ, אֵין יוֹצְאִין בָּהֶן.
phrases.en: With regard to one who prepared loaves of matza that are brought with a thanks-offering, or to the wafers brought by a nazirite, the Sages drew the following distinction: If he prepared them for himself, then he does not fulfill his obligation to eat matza with them.

phrases.he: עֲשָׂאָן לִמְכֹּר בַּשּׁוּק, יוֹצְאִין בָּהֶן:
phrases.en: However, if he prepared them to sell them in the market to those who require these loaves or wafers, one fulfills the obligation to eat matza with them.

phrases.he: וְאֵלּוּ יְרָקוֹת שֶׁאָדָם יוֹצֵא בָהֶן יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בְּפֶסַח,
phrases.en: And these are the vegetables with which a person can fulfill his obligation to eat bitter herbs on Passover:

phrases.he: בַּחֲזֶרֶת וּבְעֻלָשִׁין וּבְתַמְכָא וּבְחַרְחֲבִינָה וּבְמָרוֹר.
phrases.en: One can fulfill his obligation with ḥazeret, with chervil [tamkha], and with field eryngo [ḥarḥavina], and with endives [olashin], and with maror.

phrases.he: יוֹצְאִין בָּהֶן בֵּין לַחִין בֵּין יְבֵשִׁין,
phrases.en: One fulfills his obligation with them whether they are fresh or whether they are dry.

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא כְבוּשִׁין וְלֹא שְׁלוּקִין וְלֹא מְבֻשָּׁלִין.
phrases.en: However, one does not fulfill his obligation if they are pickled in water or vinegar, nor if they are over-boiled [shaluk] in hot water, nor if they are boiled [mevushal].

phrases.he: וּמִצְטָרְפִין לְכַזָּיִת.
phrases.en: And all these different types of vegetables join together to the measure of an olive-bulk,

phrases.he: וְיוֹצְאִין בַּקֶּלַח שֶׁלָּהֶן,
phrases.en: And one fulfills his obligation by eating their stalk,

phrases.he: וּבִדְמַאי,
phrases.en: And one fulfills the obligation with doubtfully tithed produce,

phrases.he: וּבְמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּטְּלָה תְרוּמָתוֹ,
phrases.en: with first-tithe produce whose teruma has been taken and given to a priest,

phrases.he: וּבְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁנִּפְדּוּ:
phrases.en: and with second-tithe produce and consecrated property that were redeemed.

phrases.he: אֵין שׁוֹרִין אֶת הַמֻּרְסָן לַתַּרְנְגוֹלִים, אֲבָל חוֹלְטִין.
phrases.en: One may not soak coarse bran for feeding chickens, however, one may pour boiling water onto the bran before feeding it to the chickens, as it will not become leavened from this brief exposure to water.

phrases.he: הָאִשָּׁה לֹא תִשְׁרֶה אֶת הַמֻּרְסָן שֶׁתּוֹלִיךְ בְּיָדָהּ לַמֶּרְחָץ, אֲבָל שָׁפָה הִיא בִּבְשָׂרָהּ יָבֵשׁ.
phrases.en: A woman may not soak coarse bran to bring by hand to the bathhouse for use as a cleanser; however, she may rub coarse bran on her dry skin.

phrases.he: לֹא יִלְעֹס אָדָם חִטִּין וְיַנִּיחַ עַל מַכָּתוֹ בְּפֶסַח, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מַחֲמִיצוֹת:
phrases.en: A person may not chew wheat and place it on his wound, due to the fact that the wheat will be leavened from the saliva and his chewing.

phrases.he: אֵין נוֹתְנִין קֶמַח לְתוֹךְ הַחֲרֹסֶת אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַחַרְדָּל,
phrases.en: One may not add flour to ḥaroset, or to mustard,

phrases.he: וְאִם נָתַן, יֹאכַל מִיָּד,
phrases.en: And if one added flour to either of these, the mixture may be eaten immediately

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹסֵר.
phrases.en: and Rabbi Meir prohibits this, lest the food be leavened immediately.

phrases.he: אֵין מְבַשְּׁלִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח לֹא בְמַשְׁקִין וְלֹא בְמֵי פֵרוֹת,
phrases.en: One may not boil the Paschal lamb in ordinary liquids or in fruit juices,

phrases.he: אֲבָל סָכִין וּמַטְבִּילִין אוֹתוֹ בָהֶן.
phrases.en: However, one may baste it while it is roasting and dip it into liquid while eating it.

phrases.he: מֵי תַשְׁמִישׁוֹ שֶׁל נַחְתּוֹם, יִשָּׁפְכוּ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מַחֲמִיצִין:
phrases.en: Water that has been used by a baker for cooling his hands or washing dishes should be poured out, because this water leavens the dough,

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ עוֹבְרִין בְּפֶסַח, כֻּתָּח הַבַּבְלִי, וְשֵׁכָר הַמָּדִי, וְחֹמֶץ הָאֲדוֹמִי, וְזֵתוֹם הַמִּצְרִי, וְזוֹמָן שֶׁל צַבָּעִים, וַעֲמִילָן שֶׁל טַבָּחִים, וְקוֹלָן שֶׁל סוֹפְרִים.
phrases.en: these one transgresses on Passover, Babylonian kutaḥ, Median beer, Edomite vinegar, Egyptian zitom, dyers' broth, bakers' well-worked dough, and kolan of soferim.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַף תַּכְשִׁיטֵי נָשִׁים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: also women's adornments.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל שֶׁהוּא מִמִּין דָּגָן, הֲרֵי זֶה עוֹבֵר בְּפֶסַח.
phrases.en: This is the principle: any that is from a type of grain, one transgresses on Passover.

phrases.he: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ בְאַזְהָרָה, וְאֵין בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם כָּרֵת:
phrases.en: These are included in the warning, but there is no element of karet

phrases.he: בָּצֵק שֶׁבְּסִדְקֵי עֲרֵבָה, אִם יֵשׁ כַּזַּיִת בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד, חַיָּב לְבַעֵר.
phrases.en: dough that is in the cracks of a kneading bowl, if there is an olive-bulk of dough in one place, one is obligated to remove it.

phrases.he: וְאִם לֹא, בָּטֵל בְּמִעוּטוֹ.
phrases.en: And if the dough does not add up to this amount, it is nullified due to its insignificance.

phrases.he: וְכֵן לְעִנְיַן הַטֻּמְאָה, אִם מַקְפִּיד עָלָיו, חוֹצֵץ.
phrases.en: And similarly, with regard to ritual impurity, if one is particular about it, it interposes.

phrases.he: וְאִם רוֹצֶה בְקִיּוּמוֹ, הֲרֵי הוּא כָעֲרֵבָה.
phrases.en: And if he wants to remain, its status is like of the kneading bowl.

phrases.he: בָּצֵק הַחֵרֵשׁ, אִם יֵשׁ כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ שֶׁהֶחֱמִיץ, הֲרֵי זֶה אָסוּר.
phrases.en: Deaf dough is dough for which it is difficult to determine if it has been leavened. If there is dough similar to it which became leavened, the deaf dough is prohibited.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד מַפְרִישִׁין חַלָּה בְטֻמְאָה בְיוֹם טוֹב
phrases.en: How does one separate ḥalla in ritual impurity during the Festival day of Passover

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, לֹא תִקְרָא לָהּ שֵׁם עַד שֶׁתֵּאָפֶה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: A woman should not designate it as ḥalla prior to baking; rather, she should refrain from doing so until it is baked.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר, תַּטִּיל בְּצוֹנֵן.
phrases.en: Ben Beteira says: She should separate the ḥalla before it is baked, and place the dough in cold water so that it will not become leavened.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, לֹא זֶה הוּא חָמֵץ שֶׁמֻּזְהָרִים עָלָיו בְּבַל יֵרָאֶה וּבְבַל יִמָּצֵא,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said: This is not the leavened bread about which we are warned with the prohibitions: It shall not be seen, and: It shall not be found.

phrases.he: אֶלָּא מַפְרַשְׁתָּהּ וּמַנַּחְתָּה עַד הָעֶרֶב, וְאִם הֶחֱמִיצָה, הֶחֱמִיצָה:
phrases.en: Rather, she should separate the ḥalla and leave it until the evening; and if it becomes leavened, then it will become leavened.

phrases.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, שָׁלֹשׁ נָשִׁים לָשׁוֹת כְּאַחַת וְאוֹפוֹת בְּתַנּוּר אֶחָד, זוֹ אַחַר זוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabban Gamliel says: Three women may knead their dough as one, and bake in one oven, one after the other

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, שָׁלֹשׁ נָשִׁים עוֹסְקוֹת בַּבָּצֵק, אַחַת לָשָׁה וְאַחַת עוֹרֶכֶת וְאַחַת אוֹפָה.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: Three women may be engaged in preparing dough as one, in the following manner: One kneads her dough as another one arranges her own dough so it takes the form of matza, while another one bakes her dough

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, לֹא כָל הַנָּשִׁים וְלֹא כָל הָעֵצִים וְלֹא כָל הַתַּנּוּרִים שָׁוִין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: Not all women, not all wood, and not all ovens are the same

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, תָּפַח, תִּלְטֹשׁ בְּצוֹנֵן:
phrases.en: this is the principle: If the dough begins to rise, she should spread cold water in which she immersed her hands, onto the dough

phrases.he: שִׂאוּר, יִשָּׂרֵף, וְהָאוֹכְלוֹ פָטוּר.
phrases.en: Dough at the beginning of the leavening process [siur], must be burned, but one who eats it is exempt from the punishment of karet because the dough had not become fully leavened.

phrases.he: סָדוּק, יִשָּׂרֵף, וְהָאוֹכְלוֹ חַיָּב כָּרֵת.
phrases.en: Dough that has reached the stage of cracking must be burned, and one who eats it intentionally is liable to receive karet, as he has intentionally eaten leavened bread during Passover.

phrases.he: אֵיזֶהוּ שִׂאוּר, כְּקַרְנֵי חֲגָבִים.
phrases.en: What is considered siur? Dough that has been leavened to the point that it has cracks that look like the antennae of locusts.

phrases.he: סָדוּק, שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ סְדָקָיו זֶה בָזֶה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: The stage of cracking occurs later in the leavening process, when the cracks intermingle. This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, זֶה וָזֶה, הָאוֹכְלוֹ חַיָּב כָּרֵת.
