phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: One who intentionally eats either this or that, dough with cracks like locust antennae or with cracks that have become intermingled, is liable to receive karet, as once dough begins to crack it has certainly become leavened.

phrases.he: וְאֵיזֶהוּ שִׂאוּר, כָּל שֶׁהִכְסִיפוּ פָנָיו כְּאָדָם שֶׁעָמְדוּ שַׂעֲרוֹתָיו:
phrases.en: And what is siur? It is any dough whose surface has becomes pale like the face of a person whose hair stands on end due to fear.

phrases.he: אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת, מְבַעֲרִים אֶת הַכֹּל מִלִּפְנֵי הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.en: the fourteenth of Nisan that occurs on Shabbat, one removes all leaven from his possession before Shabbat,

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בִּזְמַנָּן.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: One may remove the leaven at its usual time

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר, תְּרוּמָה מִלִּפְנֵי הַשַּׁבָּת, וְחֻלִּין בִּזְמַנָּן:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer bar Tzadok says: Teruma should be removed before Shabbat, as non-sacred foods should be removed at their usual time,

phrases.he: הַהוֹלֵךְ לִשְׁחֹט אֶת פִּסְחוֹ, וְלָמוּל אֶת בְּנוֹ, וְלֶאֱכֹל סְעֻדַּת אֵרוּסִין בְּבֵית חָמִיו, וְנִזְכַּר שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ חָמֵץ בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ.
phrases.en: One who is traveling on the eve of Passover to slaughter his Paschal lamb, to circumcise his son, or to eat a betrothal feast in his father-in-law's house, and he remembers that he has leavened bread in his house.

phrases.he: אִם יָכוֹל לַחֲזֹר וּלְבַעֵר וְלַחֲזֹר לְמִצְוָתוֹ, יַחֲזֹר וִיבַעֵר.
phrases.en: If he is able to return to his house and remove the leaven and afterward return to the mitzva toward which he was traveling, he should return home and remove his leaven.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, מְבַטְּלוֹ בְלִבּוֹ.
phrases.en: But if there is not enough time for him to go home and remove the leaven, and still complete the mitzva that he already began, he should nullify it in his heart, as by Torah law this is sufficient.

phrases.he: לְהַצִּיל מִן הַנָּכְרִים, וּמִן הַנָּהָר, וּמִן הַלִּסְטִים, וּמִן הַדְּלֵקָה, וּמִן הַמַּפֹּלֶת, יְבַטֵּל בְּלִבּוֹ.
phrases.en: If one was traveling to save Jews from an attack by gentiles, from a flooding river, from bandits, from a fire, or from a collapsed building, he should not even attempt to return, and instead he should nullify the leaven in his heart.

phrases.he: וְלִשְׁבֹּת שְׁבִיתַת הָרְשׁוּת, יַחֲזֹר מִיָּד:
phrases.en: If he went to establish his Shabbat residence in order to adjust his Shabbat limit for an optional purpose, rather than in order to fulfill a commandment, he should return immediately to remove his leaven.

phrases.he: וְכֵן מִי שֶׁיָּצָא מִירוּשָׁלַיִם וְנִזְכַּר שֶׁיֶּשׁ בְּיָדוֹ בְּשַׂר קֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.en: And so too, one who left Jerusalem and remembered that there was consecrated meat in his hand.

phrases.he: אִם עָבַר צוֹפִים, שׂוֹרְפוֹ בִמְקוֹמוֹ.
phrases.en: If he passed Scopus, he burns it at the site where he is located;

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, חוֹזֵר וְשׂוֹרְפוֹ לִפְנֵי הַבִּירָה מֵעֲצֵי הַמַּעֲרָכָה.
phrases.en: and if he has not traveled that far, he must return and burn it before the Temple with wood from the arrangement.

phrases.he: וְעַד כַּמָּה הֵן חוֹזְרִין,
phrases.en: For how much is one required to return?

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, זֶה וָזֶה בְכַבֵּיצָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: In both this case and that case, one must return for an egg-bulk.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, זֶה וָזֶה בְכַזָּיִת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: In both this case and that case, one must return for an olive-bulk.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בְּשַׂר קֹדֶשׁ בְּכַזַּיִת, וְחָמֵץ בְּכַבֵּיצָה:
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say that with regard to consecrated meat, he is required to return if he has an olive-bulk, but in a case where he remembers that he has leavened bread, he is required to return only for an egg-bulk.

phrases.he: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה בְּעַרְבֵי פְסָחִים עַד חֲצוֹת, עוֹשִׂין.
phrases.en: In a place where the people were accustomed to perform labor on Passover eve until midday, one may do so on that day.

phrases.he: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲשׂוֹת, אֵין עוֹשִׂין.
phrases.en: In a place where the people were accustomed not to perform labor, one may not do so.

phrases.he: הַהוֹלֵךְ מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁעוֹשִׂין לְמָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין, אוֹ מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין לְמָקוֹם שֶׁעוֹשִׂין, נוֹתְנִין עָלָיו חֻמְרֵי מָקוֹם שֶׁיָּצָא מִשָּׁם וְחֻמְרֵי מָקוֹם שֶׁהָלַךְ לְשָׁם.
phrases.en: If one travels from a place where people perform labor on Passover eve to a place where people do not perform labor, or from a place where people do not perform labor on Passover eve to a place where people perform labor, the Sages impose upon him the stringencies of both the place from which he left and the stringencies of the place to which he went.

phrases.he: וְאַל יְשַׁנֶּה אָדָם, מִפְּנֵי הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת:
phrases.en: And a person may not deviate from the local custom, due to potential dispute.

phrases.he: כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ, הַמּוֹלִיךְ פֵּרוֹת שְׁבִיעִית מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁכָּלוּ לְמָקוֹם שֶׁלֹּא כָלוּ, אוֹ מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁלֹּא כָלוּ לְמָקוֹם שֶׁכָּלוּ, חַיָּב לְבַעֵר.
phrases.en: Similarly, one who transports Sabbatical Year produce from a place where a crop has ceased in the fields to a place where it has not yet ceased or from a place where it has not yet ceased to a place where it has already ceased is obligated to remove the produce from his possession.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אוֹמְרִים לוֹ, צֵא וְהָבֵא לְךָ אַף אָתָּה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says that he need not remove the produce, as he can say to a local resident: You, too, go out and bring this produce from a place where it remains in the field.

phrases.he: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לִמְכֹּר בְּהֵמָה דַקָּה לַגּוֹיִם, מוֹכְרִין.
phrases.en: In a place where the people were accustomed to sell small livestock to gentiles, one may sell them.

phrases.he: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לִמְכֹּר, אֵין מוֹכְרִין.
phrases.en: In a place where the people were not accustomed to sell them due to certain concerns and decrees, one may not sell them.

phrases.he: וּבְכָל מָקוֹם אֵין מוֹכְרִין לָהֶם בְּהֵמָה גַסָּה, עֲגָלִים וּסְיָחִים שְׁלֵמִין וּשְׁבוּרִין.
phrases.en: However, in every place, one may sell to gentiles neither large livestock, e.g., cows and camels, nor calves or foals, whether these animals are whole or damaged.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר בִּשְׁבוּרָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda permits the sale of a damaged animal because it is incapable of performing labor.

phrases.he: בֶּן בְּתֵירָה מַתִּיר בְּסוּס:
phrases.en: Ben Beteira permits the sale of a horse for riding, because riding a horse on Shabbat is not prohibited by Torah law.

phrases.he: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לֶאֱכֹל צָלִי בְלֵילֵי פְסָחִים, אוֹכְלִין.
phrases.en: In a place where people were accustomed to eat roasted meat on Passover evenings, one may eat it.

phrases.he: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לֶאֱכֹל, אֵין אוֹכְלִין.
phrases.en: In a place where people were accustomed not to eat, one may not eat it.

phrases.he: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לְהַדְלִיק אֶת הַנֵּר בְּלֵילֵי יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, מַדְלִיקִין.
phrases.en: In a place where people were accustomed to kindle a lamp on Yom Kippur evenings, one kindles it.

phrases.he: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לְהַדְלִיק, אֵין מַדְלִיקִין.
phrases.en: In a place where people were accustomed not to kindle, one does not kindle it.

phrases.he: וּמַדְלִיקִין בְּבָתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת וּבְבָתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת, וּבַמְּבוֹאוֹת הָאֲפֵלִים, וְעַל גַּבֵּי הַחוֹלִים:
phrases.en: However, one kindles in synagogues and study halls, in dark alleyways, and next to the sick.

phrases.he: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה בְתִשְׁעָה בְאָב, עוֹשִׂין.
phrases.en: a place where people were accustomed to perform labor on the Ninth of Av, one performs labor.

phrases.he: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה, אֵין עוֹשִׂין.
phrases.en: a place where people were accustomed not to perform labor, one does not perform labor.

phrases.he: וּבְכָל מָקוֹם תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים בְּטֵלִים.
phrases.en: And in all places Torah scholars are idle and do not perform labor on the Ninth of Av, due to the mourning over the Temple's destruction.

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, לְעוֹלָם יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם עַצְמוֹ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם.
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: a person should always conduct himself as a Torah scholar and refrain from performing labor.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בִּיהוּדָה הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין מְלָאכָה בְעַרְבֵי פְסָחִים עַד חֲצוֹת, וּבַגָּלִיל לֹא הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין כָּל עִקָּר.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: In Judea, people would perform labor on Passover eves until midday, and in the Galilee people would not perform labor on Passover eve at all.

phrases.he: וְהַלַּיְלָה, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹסְרִין, וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין עַד הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה:
phrases.en: the night Beit Shammai prohibit, and Beit Hillel permit doing so until sunrise.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, כָּל מְלָאכָה שֶׁהִתְחִיל בָּהּ קֹדֶם לְאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר, גּוֹמְרָהּ בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: With regard to any labor that one began before the fourteenth of Nisan, he may complete it on the fourteenth before midday.

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא יַתְחִיל בָּהּ בַּתְּחִלָּה בְאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְגָמְרָהּ.
phrases.en: However, one may not begin to perform that labor from the outset on the fourteenth, even if he is able to complete it before midday.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, שָׁלֹשׁ אֻמָּנֻיּוֹת עוֹשִׂין מְלָאכָה בְעַרְבֵי פְסָחִים עַד חֲצוֹת, וְאֵלּוּ הֵן, הַחַיָּטִים, הַסַּפָּרִים וְהַכּוֹבְסִין.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: The practitioners of only three crafts are permitted to perform labor until midday on Passover eve, and they are: Tailors, barbers, and launderers, whose work is needed for the Festival.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף הָרַצְעָנִים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says: Even shoemakers are permitted to work on the fourteenth.

phrases.he: מוֹשִׁיבִין שׁוֹבָכִין לַתַּרְנְגוֹלִים בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר.
phrases.en: One may place eggs under hens on the fourteenth of Nisan so that the birds will brood until the eggs hatch.

phrases.he: וְתַרְנְגֹלֶת שֶׁבָּרְחָה, מַחֲזִירִין אוֹתָהּ לִמְקוֹמָהּ.
phrases.en: And if a hen fled from brooding, one may restore it to its place.

phrases.he: וְאִם מֵתָה, מוֹשִׁיבִין אַחֶרֶת תַּחְתֶּיהָ.
phrases.en: And if a brooding hen died, one may place another in its stead.

phrases.he: גּוֹרְפִין מִתַּחַת רַגְלֵי בְהֵמָה בְאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר, וּבַמּוֹעֵד מְסַלְּקִין לַצְּדָדִין.
phrases.en: Similarly, one may sweep dung from beneath the legs of an animal on the fourteenth of Nisan. And during the intermediate days of the Festival one may clear it to the sides.

phrases.he: מוֹלִיכִין וּמְבִיאִין כֵּלִים מִבֵּית הָאֻמָּן, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָם לְצֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹעֵד:
phrases.en: Similarly, one may take vessels to the craftsman's house for repair and bring others from there even though they are not for the purpose of the Festival.

phrases.he: שִׁשָּׁה דְבָרִים עָשׂוּ אַנְשֵׁי יְרִיחוֹ,
phrases.en: Six actions were performed by the residents of Jericho,

phrases.he: עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה מִחוּ בְיָדָם,
phrases.en: to three, the Sages reprimanded them,

phrases.he: וְעַל שְׁלֹשָׁה לֹא מִחוּ בְיָדָם.
phrases.en: and to three, the Sages did not reprimand them.

phrases.he: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן שֶׁלֹּא מִחוּ בְיָדָם,
phrases.en: And these are the ones which they did not reprimand them:

phrases.he: מַרְכִּיבִין דְּקָלִים כָּל הַיּוֹם,
phrases.en: graft palm trees the entire day

phrases.he: וְכוֹרְכִין אֶת שְׁמַע,
phrases.en: and bundle Shema,

phrases.he: וְקוֹצְרִין וְגוֹדְשִׁין לִפְנֵי הָעֹמֶר,
phrases.en: and harvest and pile before the omer

phrases.he: וְלֹא מִחוּ בְיָדָם.
וְאֵלּוּ שֶׁמִּחוּ בְיָדָם,
phrases.en: And these are the ones reprimanded them:

phrases.he: מַתִּירִין גִּמְזִיּוֹת שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ,
phrases.en: permit the use of consecrated branches

phrases.he: וְאוֹכְלִין מִתַּחַת הַנְּשָׁרִים בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: and eat from beneath trees that shed fruit on Shabbat;

phrases.he: וְנוֹתְנִים פֵּאָה לַיָּרָק,
phrases.en: and they designate the corner for the poor in a field of vegetables,

phrases.he: וּמִחוּ בְיָדָם חֲכָמִים:
phrases.en: And the Sages reprimanded

phrases.he: שִׁשָּׁה דְבָרִים עָשָׂה חִזְקִיָּה הַמֶּלֶךְ, עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה הוֹדוּ לוֹ, וְעַל שְׁלֹשָׁה לֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ.
phrases.en: The Sages taught: King Hezekiah performed six actions. With regard to three of them, the Sages of his generation conceded to him; and with regard to three of them, the Sages did not concede to him.

phrases.he: גֵּרַר עַצְמוֹת אָבִיו עַל מִטָּה שֶׁל חֲבָלִים, וְהוֹדוּ לוֹ.
phrases.en: he dragged the bones of his father on a bier of ropes and did not afford him the respect due to a king, and the Sages conceded to him.

phrases.he: כִּתֵּת נְחַשׁ הַנְּחֹשֶׁת, וְהוֹדוּ לוֹ.
phrases.en: He ground the copper snake and the Sages conceded to him.

phrases.he: גָּנַז סֵפֶר רְפוּאוֹת, וְהוֹדוּ לוֹ.
phrases.en: He suppressed the Book of Cures, and they conceded to him.

phrases.he: עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה לֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ, קִצֵּץ דְּלָתוֹת שֶׁל הֵיכָל וְשִׁגְּרָן לְמֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר, וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ.
phrases.en: And with regard to three actions, the Sages did not concede to him. He cut off the doors of the Sanctuary and sent them to the King of Assyria, and they did not concede to him.

phrases.he: סָתַם מֵי גִיחוֹן הָעֶלְיוֹן, וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ.
phrases.en: He sealed the waters of the upper Gihon stream, and they did not concede to him.

phrases.he: עִבֵּר נִיסָן בְּנִיסָן, וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ:
phrases.en: He intercalated the year, delaying the advent of the month of Nisan during Nisan, and they did not concede to him.

phrases.he: תָּמִיד נִשְׁחָט בִּשְׁמֹנֶה וּמֶחֱצָה
phrases.en: The daily offering is slaughtered at eight and a half hours of the day

phrases.he: וְקָרֵב בְּתֵשַׁע וּמֶחֱצָה.
phrases.en: and is sacrificed at nine and a half hours of the day

phrases.he: בְּעַרְבֵי פְסָחִים נִשְׁחָט בְּשֶׁבַע וּמֶחֱצָה וְקָרֵב בִּשְׁמֹנֶה וּמֶחֱצָה, בֵּין בְּחֹל בֵּין בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: On the eves of Passover, it is slaughtered at seven and a half hours and sacrificed at eight and a half hours, whether during the week or on Shabbat

phrases.he: חָל עֶרֶב פֶּסַח לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת, נִשְׁחָט בְּשֵׁשׁ וּמֶחֱצָה וְקָרֵב בְּשֶׁבַע וּמֶחֱצָה, וְהַפֶּסַח אַחֲרָיו:
phrases.en: If Passover eve occurs on Shabbat eve, the daily offering is slaughtered at six and a half hours and sacrificed at seven and a half hours, and the Paschal lamb is offered thereafter

phrases.he: הַפֶּסַח שֶׁשְּׁחָטוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ,
phrases.en: The Paschal lamb that the priest slaughtered not for its own purpose,

phrases.he: וְקִבֵּל וְהִלֵּךְ וְזָרַק שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ,
phrases.en: or if the priest received the blood, or carried the blood to the altar, or sprinkled the blood on the altar while saying that it was not for the purpose of the Paschal lamb;

phrases.he: אוֹ לִשְׁמוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ,
phrases.en: or if the priest performed the rites both for its own purpose and not for its own purpose;

phrases.he: אוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ וְלִשְׁמוֹ,
phrases.en: or not for its own purpose and for its own purpose;

phrases.he: פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: in all these cases, the Paschal lamb is disqualified.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד לִשְׁמוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ,
phrases.en: How does one perform the rites for its own purpose and not for its own purpose?

phrases.he: לְשֵׁם פֶּסַח וּלְשֵׁם שְׁלָמִים.
phrases.en: It is in a case where the priest said that his intent is for the purpose of the Paschal lamb and for the purpose of a peace-offering.

phrases.he: שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ וְלִשְׁמוֹ,
phrases.en: And how does one perform rites not for its own purpose and for its own purpose?

phrases.he: לְשֵׁם שְׁלָמִים וּלְשֵׁם פָּסַח:
phrases.en: It is in a case where the priest says that the offering is for the purpose of a peace-offering and for the purpose of a Paschal lamb.

phrases.he: שְׁחָטוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לְאוֹכְלָיו וְשֶׁלֹּא לִמְנוּיָיו, לַעֲרֵלִים וְלִטְמֵאִים, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: If one slaughtered the Paschal lamb for people who cannot eat it or for those who did not register in advance to eat it, or if one slaughtered it for people who are uncircumcised or for those who are ritually impure, whom the Torah prohibits from eating the Paschal lamb, it is disqualified.

phrases.he: לְאוֹכְלָיו וְשֶׁלֹּא לְאוֹכְלָיו, לִמְנוּיָיו וְשֶׁלֹּא לִמְנוּיָיו, לְמוּלִים וְלַעֲרֵלִים, לִטְמֵאִים וְלִטְהוֹרִים, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: However, if one slaughtered it for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it; for those who have registered for it and for those who have not registered for it; for the circumcised and for the uncircumcised; for the ritually impure and for the ritually pure, it is valid, for a partially invalid intent does not disqualify the offering.

phrases.he: שְׁחָטוֹ קֹדֶם חֲצוֹת, פָּסוּל, מִשּׁוּם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמות יב) בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם.
phrases.en: If one slaughtered the Paschal lamb before midday it is disqualified, as it is stated: And the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall slaughter it in the afternoon (Exodus 12:6).

phrases.he: שְׁחָטוֹ קֹדֶם לַתָּמִיד, כָּשֵׁר, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיְּהֵא אֶחָד מְמָרֵס בְּדָמוֹ עַד שֶׁיִּזָּרֵק דַּם הַתָּמִיד.
phrases.en: If he slaughtered it before the daily afternoon offering it is valid, as long as another person stirs its blood in order to prevent it from congealing until the blood of the daily offering is sprinkled.

phrases.he: וְאִם נִזְרַק, כָּשֵׁר:
phrases.en: And if the blood of the Paschal lamb is sprinkled before the blood of the daily offering, it is nonetheless valid, as this change does not disqualify the offering.

phrases.he: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל הֶחָמֵץ, עוֹבֵר בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.en: One who slaughters the Paschal lamb with leavened bread still in his possession violates a negative commandment

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף הַתָּמִיד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: Even the daily afternoon offering

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, הַפֶּסַח בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר, לִשְׁמוֹ חַיָּב, וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: One who slaughters the Paschal lamb on the fourteenth of Nisan for its own purpose with leaven in his possession is liable; but if he slaughtered it for a different purpose he is exempt.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַזְּבָחִים, בֵּין לִשְׁמָן וּבֵין שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: And for all other offerings that one slaughters on Passover eve, when owning leaven is prohibited, whether he slaughtered them for their own purpose or he slaughtered them for a different purpose, he is exempt.

phrases.he: וּבַמּוֹעֵד, לִשְׁמוֹ פָּטוּר, וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ חַיָּב,
phrases.en: And during the festival of Passover, if one slaughtered the Paschal lamb for its own purpose he is exempt. However, if he slaughtered it for a different purpose and thereby validated the sacrifice as a peace-offering, he is liable

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַזְּבָחִים, בֵּין לִשְׁמָן וּבֵין שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן, חַיָּב,
phrases.en: And for all other offerings that one slaughters on Passover, when it is prohibited to slaughter with leaven in one's possession, whether he slaughtered them for their own purpose or he slaughtered them for a different purpose, he is liable.

phrases.he: חוּץ מִן הַחַטָּאת שֶׁשְּׁחָטָהּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ.
phrases.en: with the exception of a sin-offering that he slaughtered for a different purpose with leaven in his possession

phrases.he: הַפֶּסַח נִשְׁחָט בְּשָׁלֹשׁ כִּתּוֹת,
phrases.en: The Paschal lamb was slaughtered in three groups,

phrases.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְשָׁחֲטוּ אֹתוֹ כֹּל קְהַל עֲדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.en: as it is stated: "And the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall slaughter it

phrases.he: קָהָל וְעֵדָה וְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.en: Assembly, congregation, and Israel.

phrases.he: נִכְנְסָה כַת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה,
phrases.en: The first group entered,

phrases.he: נִתְמַלֵּאת הָעֲזָרָה,
phrases.en: the Temple courtyard became filled

phrases.he: נָעֲלוּ דַלְתוֹת הָעֲזָרָה.
phrases.en: they closed the doors of the Temple courtyard.

phrases.he: תָּקְעוּ, הֵרִיעוּ וְתָקָעוּ.
phrases.en: They sounded uninterrupted, broken, and uninterrupted blasts,

phrases.he: הַכֹּהֲנִים עוֹמְדִים שׁוּרוֹת שׁוּרוֹת,
phrases.en: The priests stood in rows

phrases.he: וּבִידֵיהֶם בָּזִיכֵי כֶסֶף וּבָזִיכֵי זָהָב.
phrases.en: and in their hands they held bowls of silver and bowls of gold

phrases.he: שׁוּרָה שֶׁכֻּלָּהּ כֶּסֶף כֶּסֶף,
phrases.en: a row entirely composed of priests holding silver bowls,

phrases.he: וְשׁוּרָה שֶׁכֻּלָּהּ זָהָב זָהָב.
phrases.en: and a row entirely composed of priests holding gold bowls,

phrases.he: לֹא הָיוּ מְעֹרָבִין.
phrases.en: were not mixed

phrases.he: וְלֹא הָיוּ לַבָּזִיכִין שׁוּלַיִם,
phrases.en: The bowls did not have flat bases

phrases.he: שֶׁמָּא יַנִּיחוּם וְיִקְרַשׁ הַדָּם:
phrases.en: out of concern that perhaps the priests would set them down and the blood would congeal

phrases.he: שָׁחַט יִשְׂרָאֵל וְקִבֵּל הַכֹּהֵן,
phrases.en: An Israelite would slaughter the sacrifice, and a priest would receive the blood and immediately

phrases.he: נוֹתְנוֹ לַחֲבֵרוֹ וַחֲבֵרוֹ לַחֲבֵרוֹ,
phrases.en: hand it to another priest standing next to him, and the other priest would pass it to another.

phrases.he: וּמְקַבֵּל אֶת הַמָּלֵא וּמַחֲזִיר אֶת הָרֵיקָן.
phrases.en: Each priest would receive a full bowl of blood from the priest next to him and return to him an empty bowl being passed in the opposite direction, the contents of which had already been sprinkled on the altar.

phrases.he: כֹּהֵן הַקָּרוֹב אֵצֶל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ זוֹרְקוֹ זְרִיקָה אַחַת כְּנֶגֶד הַיְסוֹד:
phrases.en: The priest who was closest to the altar would sprinkle a single sprinkling of blood against the base of the altar, i.e., against the north and west sides of the altar, where there was a base.

phrases.he: יָצְתָה כַת רִאשׁוֹנָה וְנִכְנְסָה כַת שְׁנִיָּה.
phrases.en: The first group exited and the second group entered

phrases.he: יָצְתָה שְׁנִיָּה, נִכְנְסָה שְׁלִישִׁית.
phrases.en: the second group left and the third group entered

phrases.he: כְּמַעֲשֵׂה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה כָּךְ מַעֲשֵׂה הַשְּׁנִיָּה וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁית.
phrases.en: As it was done by the first group, so was it done by the second and third groups

phrases.he: קָרְאוּ אֶת הַהַלֵּל.
phrases.en: recite hallel

phrases.he: אִם גָּמְרוּ שָׁנוּ, וְאִם שָׁנוּ שִׁלְּשׁוּ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא שִׁלְּשׁוּ מִימֵיהֶם.
phrases.en: If they finished they recited it a second time, and if they finished reciting it a second time, they recited it a third time, although they never recited it a third time

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מִימֵיהֶם שֶׁל כַּת שְׁלִישִׁית לֹא הִגִּיעַ לְאָהַבְתִּי כִּי יִשְׁמַע ה', מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעַמָּהּ מֻעָטִין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: The third group never reached I love that the Lord hears, because its people were few

phrases.he: כְּמַעֲשֵׂהוּ בְחֹל כָּךְ מַעֲשֵׂהוּ בְשַׁבָּת, אֶלָּא שֶׁהַכֹּהֲנִים מְדִיחִים אֶת הָעֲזָרָה שֶׁלֹּא בִרְצוֹן חֲכָמִים.
phrases.en: As it was done during the week, so was it done on Shabbat; only that the priests would rinse the Temple courtyard, contrary to the wishes of the Sages.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כּוֹס הָיָה מְמַלֵּא מִדַּם הַתַּעֲרֹבוֹת, זְרָקוֹ זְרִיקָה אַחַת עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: a priest would fill a cup with the blood of the many offerings brought that day that was now mixed together on the floor and then sprinkle it with a single sprinkling upon the altar. But the Rabbis did not agree with him.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד תּוֹלִין וּמַפְשִׁיטִין,
phrases.en: How would one suspend and flay

phrases.he: אֻנְקְלָיוֹת שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל הָיוּ קְבוּעִים בַּכְּתָלִים וּבָעַמּוּדִים,
phrases.en: Iron hooks were secured into the walls and pillars

phrases.he: שֶׁבָּהֶן תּוֹלִין וּמַפְשִׁיטִין.
phrases.en: and upon them one would suspend the offering and flay it

phrases.he: וְכָל מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מָקוֹם לִתְלוֹת וּלְהַפְשִׁיט,
phrases.en: If anyone lacked a place to suspend and flay the offering

phrases.he: מַקְלוֹת דַּקִּים חֲלָקִים הָיוּ שָׁם,
phrases.en: there were thin, smooth rods there

phrases.he: וּמֵנִיחַ עַל כְּתֵפוֹ וְעַל כֶּתֶף חֲבֵרוֹ,
phrases.en: he would place on his own shoulder and on another's shoulder

phrases.he: וְתוֹלֶה וּמַפְשִׁיט.
phrases.en: and from it he would suspend the offering and flay it

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says

phrases.he: אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: When the fourteenth of Nisan occurred on Shabbat

phrases.he: מֵנִיחַ יָדוֹ עַל כֶּתֶף חֲבֵרוֹ,
phrases.en: he would rest his hand on another's shoulder

phrases.he: וְיַד חֲבֵרוֹ עַל כְּתֵפוֹ,
phrases.en: and the other's hand on his own shoulder

phrases.he: וְתוֹלֶה וּמַפְשִׁיט:
phrases.en: and suspend the offering and flay it

phrases.he: קְרָעוֹ וְהוֹצִיא אֵמוּרָיו,
phrases.en: He would tear open the flesh of the offering and remove its sacrificial parts

phrases.he: נְתָנוֹ בְמָגִיס וְהִקְטִירָן עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
phrases.en: He would place the sacrificial parts in a large basin [mageis] and burn them on the altar.

phrases.he: יָצְתָה כַת רִאשׁוֹנָה וְיָשְׁבָה לָהּ בְּהַר הַבַּיִת,
phrases.en: The first group would exit and remain on the Temple Mount

phrases.he: שְׁנִיָּה בַּחֵיל,
phrases.en: the second group would remain within the rampart

phrases.he: וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁית בִּמְקוֹמָהּ עוֹמֶדֶת.
phrases.en: and the third group would stand in its place in the Temple

phrases.he: חֲשֵׁכָה, יָצְאוּ וְצָלוּ אֶת פִּסְחֵיהֶן:
phrases.en: it became dark, they would go out and roast their Paschal lambs

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ דְבָרִים בַּפֶּסַח דּוֹחִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.en: These are the matters related to the Paschal lamb that override Shabbat,

phrases.he: שְׁחִיטָתוֹ וּזְרִיקַת דָּמוֹ וּמִחוּי קְרָבָיו וְהֶקְטֵר חֲלָבָיו.
phrases.en: Its slaughter, the sprinkling of its blood, the cleaning of its intestines and the burning of its fats

phrases.he: אֲבָל צְלִיָּתוֹ וַהֲדָחַת קְרָבָיו אֵינָן דּוֹחִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.en: However, its roasting and the washing of its intestines, do not override Shabbat;

phrases.he: הַרְכָּבָתוֹ וַהֲבָאָתוֹ מִחוּץ לַתְּחוּם, וַחֲתִיכַת יַבַּלְתּוֹ, אֵין דּוֹחִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.en: Carrying bringing it from outside the Shabbat limit and cutting off its wart do not override Shabbat,

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, דּוֹחִין:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: override

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וַהֲלֹא דִין הוּא,
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer said: Could this not be derived through an a fortiori inference?

phrases.he: מָה אִם שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁהִיא מִשּׁוּם מְלָאכָה דּוֹחָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.en: If slaughter, which is ordinarily forbidden on Shabbat as a biblically prohibited labor, nonetheless overrides Shabbat when performed for the sake of the Paschal lamb,

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ שֶׁהֵן מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת לֹא יִדְחוּ אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.en: then these activities, namely carrying the animal, bringing it from outside the Shabbat limit, and the like, which are prohibited due to rabbinic decree, should they not override Shabbat?

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, יוֹם טוֹב יוֹכִיחַ,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: The law governing a Festival proves otherwise,

phrases.he: שֶׁהִתִּירוּ בוֹ מִשּׁוּם מְלָאכָה, וְאָסוּר בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת.
phrases.en: for the Torah permitted on it acts that are normally prohibited as labor, such as slaughtering, cooking, and baking, and yet it is forbidden to do on it acts that are prohibited due to rabbinic decree.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, מַה זֶּה, יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, מָה רְאָיָה רְשׁוּת לְמִצְוָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer said to him: What is this, Yehoshua? What proof can be deduced from optional activities that would apply to a mitzva?

phrases.he: הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְאָמַר, הַזָּאָה תוֹכִיחַ,
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva responded and said in defense of Rabbi Yehoshua's opinion: Sprinkling the purifying water of a red heifer upon someone who had contracted ritual impurity through contact with a corpse proves the matter,

phrases.he: שֶׁהִיא מִצְוָה וְהִיא מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת וְאֵינָהּ דּוֹחָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.en: for it is done for the sake of a mitzva, in order to allow the person to offer the Paschal lamb, and it is prohibited only due to rabbinic decree, and nonetheless it does not override Shabbat, for the purification rite is not performed on the eve of Passover that falls on Shabbat.

phrases.he: אַף אַתָּה אַל תִּתְמַהּ עַל אֵלּוּ, שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵן מִצְוָה וְהֵן מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת, לֹא יִדְחוּ אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.en: So, too, you should not be surprised about these activities, namely carrying the animal, bringing it from outside the Shabbat limit, and cutting off its wart, that although they are performed for the sake of a mitzva and they are prohibited only due to rabbinic decree, they do not override Shabbat.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וְעָלֶיהָ אֲנִי דָן,
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer said to him: With regard to this sprinkling itself, I infer that it, too, is permitted for the same reason:

phrases.he: וּמָה אִם שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁהִיא מִשּׁוּם מְלָאכָה, דּוֹחָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.en: If slaughter, which is a biblically prohibited labor, overrides Shabbat,

phrases.he: הַזָּאָה שֶׁהִיא מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת, אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁדּוֹחָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.en: is it not right that sprinkling the purifying water of a red heifer, which is prohibited only due to rabbinic decree, should override Shabbat?

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, אוֹ חִלּוּף,
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva said to Rabbi Eliezer: Or perhaps we can reverse the order of your argument and say the opposite:

phrases.he: מָה אִם הַזָּאָה שֶׁהִיא מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת, אֵינָהּ דּוֹחָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.en: If, as we know by accepted tradition, sprinkling the purifying water on Shabbat, which is prohibited only due to rabbinic decree, does not override Shabbat,

phrases.he: שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁהִיא מִשּׁוּם מְלָאכָה, אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא תִדְחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.en: then with regard to slaughter, which is prohibited as a biblically prohibited labor, is it not right that it should not override Shabbat?

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, עֲקִיבָא, עָקַרְתָּ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה,
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer said to him: Akiva, how can you say this? You have thus uprooted what is written in the Torah:

phrases.he: בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם בְּמֹעֲדוֹ (במדבר ט),
phrases.en: Let the children of Israel offer the Paschal lamb in its appointed time (Numbers 9:2);

phrases.he: בֵּין בְּחֹל בֵּין בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: the phrase at its appointed time indicates that the offering must be brought on that day, whether it is a weekday or Shabbat.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ, רַבִּי, הָבֵא לִי מוֹעֵד לָאֵלּוּ כַּמּוֹעֵד לַשְּׁחִיטָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva said to Rabbi Eliezer: My teacher, bring me an appointed time stated in the Torah for these tasks, namely, carrying the animal or bringing it from outside the Shabbat limits, like the appointed time stated with respect to slaughter.

phrases.he: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, כָּל מְלָאכָה שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת, אֵינָהּ דּוֹחָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva stated a principle: Any prohibited labor required for the offering of the sacrifice that can be performed on the eve of Shabbat does not override Shabbat;

phrases.he: שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת, דּוֹחָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת:
phrases.en: slaughter, which cannot be performed on the eve of Shabbat, overrides Shabbat.

phrases.he: אֵימָתַי מֵבִיא חֲגִיגָה עִמּוֹ,
phrases.en: When does one bring a Festival peace-offering with

phrases.he: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא בָא בְּחֹל, בְּטָהֳרָה וּבְמֻעָט.
phrases.en: when the Paschal lamb comes on a weekday in a state of ritual purity and when many people are registered for the Paschal lamb so that each person will receive only a small portion from it

phrases.he: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁהוּא בָא בְּשַׁבָּת, בִּמְרֻבֶּה וּבְטֻמְאָה, אֵין מְבִיאִין עִמּוֹ חֲגִיגָה:
phrases.en: When, however, the Paschal lamb comes on Shabbat, or when few people are registered for it so that each person will receive a large portion, or when it is brought in a state of ritual impurity, one does not bring a Festival peace-offering with it.

phrases.he: חֲגִיגָה הָיְתָה בָאָה מִן הַצֹּאן, מִן הַבָּקָר, מִן הַכְּבָשִׂים וּמִן הָעִזִּים, מִן הַזְּכָרִים וּמִן הַנְּקֵבוֹת.
phrases.en: Festival peace-offering would come from the flock, from the herd, from sheep or from goats, from males or from females,

phrases.he: וְנֶאֱכֶלֶת לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד:
phrases.en: And is eaten for two days and one night

phrases.he: הַפֶּסַח שֶׁשְּׁחָטוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ בְשַׁבָּת, חַיָּב עָלָיו חַטָּאת.
phrases.en: A Paschal lamb that one slaughtered for a different purpose on Shabbat, he is liable to bring a sin-offering for it

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַזְּבָחִים שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן לְשׁוּם פֶּסַח, אִם אֵינָן רְאוּיִין, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: As for all other offerings, that one unwittingly slaughtered on Shabbat for the purpose of a Paschal offering, if they were not fit for the Paschal offering, he is liable

phrases.he: וְאִם רְאוּיִין הֵן, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְחַיֵּב חַטָּאת, וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ פּוֹטֵר.
phrases.en: And if they were fit, Rabbi Eliezer deems him liable to bring a sin-offering. But Rabbi Yehoshua exempts him

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, מָה אִם הַפֶּסַח שֶׁהוּא מֻתָּר לִשְׁמוֹ, כְּשֶׁשִּׁנָּה אֶת שְׁמוֹ, חַיָּב, זְבָחִים שֶׁהֵן אֲסוּרִין לִשְׁמָן, כְּשֶׁשִּׁנָּה אֶת שְׁמָן, אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁיְּהֵא חַיָּב.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer said to Rabbi Yehoshua: If, with regard to the Paschal lamb, which is permitted to be slaughtered on Shabbat for its own purpose, when one changed its purpose he is nevertheless liable, then, with regard to other offerings that are forbidden to be slaughtered on Shabbat even for their own purpose, when one changed their purpose, is it not right that he should be liable?

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ בַּפֶּסַח, שֶׁשִּׁנָּהוּ לְדָבָר אָסוּר, תֹּאמַר בַּזְּבָחִים, שֶׁשִּׁנָּן לְדָבָר הַמֻּתָּר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: No, if you say that one is liable to bring a sin-offering if he slaughtered a Paschal lamb for a different purpose, it is because he changed its purpose for something forbidden, but can you necessarily say the same thing about offerings that he slaughtered for the purpose of a Paschal offering and thus changed their purpose for something that is permitted to be sacrificed on Shabbat?

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, אֵמוּרֵי צִבּוּר יוֹכִיחוּ, שֶׁהֵן מֻתָּרִין לִשְׁמָן, וְהַשּׁוֹחֵט לִשְׁמָן, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer said to Rabbi Yehoshua: Let the communal offerings, prove the matter, for they are permitted to be slaughtered on Shabbat for their own purpose, and nevertheless, one who unnecessarily slaughters a different offering for their purpose is liable

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ בְאֵמוּרֵי צִבּוּר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן קִצְבָּה, תֹּאמַר בַּפֶּסַח שֶׁאֵין לוֹ קִצְבָּה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: No, if you say this halakha with regard to communal offerings, it is because they have a limit, but can you necessarily say the same thing about the Paschal lamb, which does not have a limit

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, אַף הַשּׁוֹחֵט לְשֵׁם אֵמוּרֵי צִבּוּר, פָּטוּר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: Even one who unwittingly slaughters other offerings for the purpose of communal offerings beyond their daily limit is exempt

phrases.he: שְׁחָטוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לְאוֹכְלָיו וְשֶׁלֹּא לִמְנוּיָיו, לַעֲרֵלִין וְלִטְמֵאִין, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: If one slaughtered a Paschal lamb on Shabbat and mistakenly intended it for those who cannot eat it, such as sick or elderly people who are unable to eat the meat, or for those who did not register for it, or for the sake of the uncircumcised or for those ritually impure, the offering is disqualified and he is liable to bring a sin-offering for his unnecessary act of slaughter.

phrases.he: לְאוֹכְלָיו וְשֶׁלֹּא לְאוֹכְלָיו, לִמְנוּיָיו וְשֶׁלֹּא לִמְנוּיָיו, לְמוּלִין וְלַעֲרֵלִין, לִטְהוֹרִים וְלִטְמֵאִים, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: If, however, he slaughtered it for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it, or for those who registered for it and for those who did not register for it, or for the circumcised and for those who are uncircumcised, or for those who are ritually impure and those who are ritually pure, he is exempt.

phrases.he: שְׁחָטוֹ וְנִמְצָא בַעַל מוּם, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: If he slaughtered it and it was found to have a blemish, the offering is disqualified, and he is liable to bring a sin-offering for having unwittingly performed a prohibited labor on Shabbat, as he should have examined the animal before it was slaughtered.

phrases.he: שְׁחָטוֹ וְנִמְצָא טְרֵפָה בַסֵּתֶר, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: If he slaughtered it and it was found to have a hidden condition that would cause it to die within twelve months [tereifa] and that could not have been discovered before the slaughter even if it were examined properly, the offering is disqualified, but he is exempt from bringing a sin-offering.

phrases.he: שְׁחָטוֹ וְנוֹדַע שֶׁמָּשְׁכוּ הַבְּעָלִים אֶת יָדָם, אוֹ שֶׁמֵּתוּ אוֹ שֶׁנִּטְמְאוּ, פָּטוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁשָּׁחַט בִּרְשׁוּת.
phrases.en: If he slaughtered it and afterward it became known that the owners had withdrawn from it and registered for a different Paschal lamb, in which case this one was slaughtered unnecessarily, as no one was registered for it, or it became known that they had died or became ritually impure, in all these cases he is exempt from bringing a sin-offering, because he slaughtered with permission.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד צוֹלִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח, מְבִיאִין שַׁפּוּד שֶׁל רִמּוֹן, תּוֹחֲבוֹ מִתּוֹךְ פִּיו עַד בֵּית נְקוּבָתוֹ, וְנוֹתֵן אֶת כְּרָעָיו וְאֶת בְּנֵי מֵעָיו לְתוֹכוֹ.
phrases.en: How does one roast the Paschal lamb? One brings a spit of pomegranate wood and thrusts it into the mouth until it reaches its anus, and one then puts its legs and entrails inside it and roasts it all together;

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי.
phrases.en: this is the statement of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, כְּמִין בִּשּׁוּל הוּא זֶה, אֶלָּא תוֹלִין חוּצָה לוֹ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: this is a type of cooking. Rather, one suspends the legs and entrails from the spit above the animal's head outside it.

phrases.he: אֵין צוֹלִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח לֹא עַל הַשַּׁפּוּד וְלֹא עַל הָאַסְכְּלָא.
phrases.en: One may not roast the Paschal lamb on the metal spit nor on a metal grill [askela].

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי צָדוֹק, מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל שֶׁאָמַר לְטָבִי עַבְדּוֹ, צֵא וּצְלֵה לָנוּ אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל הָאַסְכְּלָא.
phrases.en: However, Rabbi Tzadok said: There was an incident with Rabban Gamliel, who said to his slave Tavi: Go and roast the Paschal lamb for us on the grill.

phrases.he: נָגַע בְּחַרְסוֹ שֶׁל תַּנּוּר, יִקְלֹף אֶת מְקוֹמוֹ.
phrases.en: If the Paschal lamb touched the earthenware surface of an oven, one must peel off its place on the Paschal lamb, as it was roasted by the heat of the oven and not by the fire itself.

phrases.he: נָטַף מֵרָטְבּוֹ עַל הַחֶרֶס וְחָזַר עָלָיו, יִטֹּל אֶת מְקוֹמוֹ.
phrases.en: If some of the gravy of the Paschal lamb dripped on the earthenware and then returned to it, i.e., the gravy splattered back onto the meat, one must remove its place.

phrases.he: נָטַף מֵרָטְבּוֹ עַל הַסֹּלֶת, יִקְמֹץ אֶת מְקוֹמוֹ.
phrases.en: If some of the Paschal lamb's gravy dripped onto hot flour, one must remove a handful of flour from its place, i.e., the place where the gravy landed in the flour, and destroy it.

phrases.he: סָכוֹ בְשֶׁמֶן תְּרוּמָה, אִם חֲבוּרַת כֹּהֲנִים, יֹאכֵלוּ.
phrases.en: smears the Paschal lamb with teruma oil, if the Paschal lamb belongs to a group of priests they may eat it,

phrases.he: אִם יִשְׂרָאֵל, אִם חַי הוּא, יְדִיחֶנּוּ.
phrases.en: If the Paschal lamb belongs to a group of Israelites, then if it is still raw, one must rinse it

phrases.he: וְאִם צָלִי הוּא, יִקְלֹף אֶת הַחִיצוֹן.
phrases.en: and if it is roasted, one must peel off the outer layer

phrases.he: סָכוֹ בְשֶׁמֶן שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, לֹא יַעֲשֶׂנּוּ דָמִים עַל בְּנֵי חֲבוּרָה, שֶׁאֵין פּוֹדִין מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בִירוּשָׁלָיִם:
phrases.en: one smears the Paschal lamb with oil of the second tithe, he may not demand money for it from the members of the group, as one may not redeem second tithe in Jerusalem.

phrases.he: חֲמִשָּׁה דְבָרִים בָּאִין בְּטֻמְאָה וְאֵינָן נֶאֱכָלִין בְּטֻמְאָה.
phrases.en: Five items may be brought in a state of ritual impurity, but they may not be eaten in a state of ritual impurity.

phrases.he: הָעֹמֶר, וּשְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם, וְלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים, וְזִבְחֵי שַׁלְמֵי צִבּוּר, וּשְׂעִירֵי רָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים.
phrases.en: The omer, the two loaves, the shewbread, the communal peace-offerings, and the goats sacrificed on the New Moons.

phrases.he: הַפֶּסַח שֶׁבָּא בְטֻמְאָה, נֶאֱכָל בְּטֻמְאָה, שֶׁלֹּא בָא מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ אֶלָּא לַאֲכִילָה:
phrases.en: The Paschal lamb that is sacrificed in impurity is eaten even in impurity, as it is brought to begin with only for eating.

phrases.he: נִטְמָא הַבָּשָׂר וְהַחֵלֶב קַיָּם, אֵינוֹ זוֹרֵק אֶת הַדָּם.
phrases.en: If the meat became ritually impure, and the fat remains pure and may be burned on the altar, one may not sprinkle the blood.

phrases.he: נִטְמָא הַחֵלֶב וְהַבָּשָׂר קַיָּם, זוֹרֵק אֶת הַדָּם.
phrases.en: On the other hand, if the fat became impure and the meat remains pure, one may sprinkle the blood.

phrases.he: וּבַמֻּקְדָּשִׁין אֵינוֹ כֵן, אֶלָּא אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּטְמָא הַבָּשָׂר וְהַחֵלֶב קַיָּם, זוֹרֵק אֶת הַדָּם:
phrases.en: With regard to other offerings it is not so. Rather, although the meat has become impure and the fat remains pure, one may sprinkle the blood.

phrases.he: נִטְמָא קָהָל אוֹ רֻבּוֹ, אוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים טְמֵאִים וְהַקָּהָל טְהוֹרִים, יֵעָשֶׂה בְטֻמְאָה.
phrases.en: If the entire community or most of it became ritually impure, or the priests were all impure and the community was pure, they should perform the ritual of the Paschal lamb in ritual impurity.

phrases.he: נִטְמָא מִעוּט הַקָּהָל, הַטְּהוֹרִין עוֹשִׂין אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹן, וְהַטְּמֵאִין עוֹשִׂין אֶת הַשֵּׁנִי:
phrases.en: If a minority of the community became impure, those who are pure perform the ritual of the Paschal lamb on the first Pesaḥ, and those who are impure perform the ritual on the second Pesaḥ.

phrases.he: הַפֶּסַח שֶׁנִּזְרַק דָּמוֹ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹדַע שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא, הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה.
phrases.en: a Paschal lamb whose blood was sprinkled and subsequently it became known that the meat or blood was ritually impure, the frontplate appeases

phrases.he: נִטְמָא הַגּוּף, אֵין הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָמְרוּ, הַנָּזִיר וְעוֹשֶׂה פֶסַח, הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה עַל טֻמְאַת הַדָּם, וְאֵין הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה עַל טֻמְאַת הַגּוּף.
phrases.en: the body had become ritually impure, the frontplate does not appease because the Sages said that with regard to the nazirite and one who performs the ritual of the Paschal lamb, the frontplate appeases for impurity of the blood and meat of the offering, but the frontplate does not appease for impurity of the body

phrases.he: נִטְמָא טֻמְאַת הַתְּהוֹם, הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה:
phrases.en: become impure due to ritual impurity of the deep, the frontplate appeases

phrases.he: נִטְמָא שָׁלֵם אוֹ רֻבּוֹ, שׂוֹרְפִין אוֹתוֹ לִפְנֵי הַבִּירָה מֵעֲצֵי הַמַּעֲרָכָה.
phrases.en: If the whole Paschal lamb or most of it became ritually impure, one burns it before the Temple with wood from the arrangement of wood on the altar that was given to the owners of the Paschal lamb for this purpose.

phrases.he: נִטְמָא מִעוּטוֹ, וְהַנּוֹתָר, שׂוֹרְפִין אוֹתוֹ בְחַצְרוֹתֵיהֶן אוֹ עַל גַּגּוֹתֵיהֶן מֵעֲצֵי עַצְמָן.
phrases.en: If a minority of it became impure, and similarly, with regard to the parts of the Paschal lamb that are leftover, which must be burned, the owners of the Paschal lamb burn it in their courtyards or on their roofs, with their own wood.

phrases.he: הַצַּיְקָנִין שׂוֹרְפִין אוֹתוֹ לִפְנֵי הַבִּירָה, בִּשְׁבִיל לֵהָנוֹת מֵעֲצֵי הַמַּעֲרָכָה:
phrases.en: Only the miserly, who want to save the expenditure of wood, burn it before the Temple in order to benefit from the wood of the arrangement.

phrases.he: הַפֶּסַח שֶׁיָּצָא אוֹ שֶׁנִּטְמָא, יִשָּׂרֵף מִיָּד.
phrases.en: A Paschal lamb that was taken out or that became ritually impure should be burned immediately.

phrases.he: נִטְמְאוּ הַבְּעָלִים אוֹ שֶׁמֵּתוּ, תְּעֻבַּר צוּרָתוֹ וְיִשָּׂרֵף בְּשִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר.
phrases.en: If the owners became ritually impure or died, its form must be allowed to decay and it should be burned on the sixteenth.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא אוֹמֵר, אַף זֶה יִשָּׂרֵף מִיָּד, לְפִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אוֹכְלִין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says: This, too, should be burned immediately, because it has no one to eat it.

phrases.he: הָעֲצָמוֹת, וְהַגִּידִין, וְהַנּוֹתָר, יִשָּׂרְפוּ בְשִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר.
phrases.en: The bones and the sinews; and the leftover should all be burned on the sixteenth

phrases.he: חָל שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת, יִשָּׂרְפוּ בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר,
phrases.en: If the sixteenth occurs on Shabbat, they should be burned on the seventeenth,

phrases.he: לְפִי שֶׁאֵינָן דּוֹחִין לֹא אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְלֹא אֶת יוֹם טוֹב:
phrases.en: because them does not override Shabbat or the Festival.

phrases.he: כָּל הַנֶּאֱכָל בְּשׁוֹר הַגָּדוֹל, יֵאָכֵל בִּגְדִי הָרַךְ,
phrases.en: Anything that is fit to be eaten in an adult ox, may be eaten in a young kid.

phrases.he: וְרָאשֵׁי כְנָפַיִם וְהַסְּחוּסִים.
phrases.en: And the soft ends of the ribs and the cartilage

phrases.he: הַשּׁוֹבֵר אֶת הָעֶצֶם בַּפֶּסַח הַטָּהוֹר, הֲרֵי זֶה לוֹקֶה אַרְבָּעִים.
phrases.en: One who breaks the bone of a Paschal lamb that is ritually pure receives forty lashes

phrases.he: אֲבָל הַמּוֹתִיר בַּטָּהוֹר וְהַשּׁוֹבֵר בַּטָּמֵא, אֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה אֶת הָאַרְבָּעִים:
phrases.en: But one who leaves over of a ritually pure and one who breaks the bone of a ritually impure do not receive forty lashes.

phrases.he: אֵבָר שֶׁיָּצָא מִקְצָתוֹ, חוֹתֵךְ עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לָעֶצֶם,
phrases.en: If a portion of a limb has gone out of its permissible boundary, one must cut the meat until one reaches the bone

phrases.he: וְקוֹלֵף עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לַפֶּרֶק, וְחוֹתֵךְ.
phrases.en: and peel the meat away from the bone until one reaches the joint, and cut

phrases.he: וּבַמֻּקְדָּשִׁין קוֹצֵץ בַּקּוֹפִיץ, שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם.
phrases.en: And with regard to other offerings, one may chop off the part that exited with a hatchet, as it is not subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone.

phrases.he: מִן הָאֲגַף וְלִפְנִים כְּלִפְנִים,
phrases.en: Anything that is located from the inside of the doorway inward is considered as though it is inside,

phrases.he: מִן הָאֲגַף וְלַחוּץ כְּלַחוּץ.
phrases.en: and anything that is located from the doorway outward is considered as though it is outside.

phrases.he: הַחַלּוֹנוֹת וְעֹבִי הַחוֹמָה, כְּלִפְנִים:
phrases.en: And the windows in the wall and the thickness of the wall are considered as though they are inside,

phrases.he: שְׁתֵּי חֲבוּרוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹכְלוֹת בְּבַיִת אֶחָד,
phrases.en: Two groups that were eating in one house

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ הוֹפְכִין אֶת פְּנֵיהֶם הֵילָךְ וְאוֹכְלִין, וְאֵלּוּ הוֹפְכִין אֶת פְּנֵיהֶם הֵילָךְ וְאוֹכְלִין,
phrases.en: these turn their faces this way and eat, and these turn their faces that way and eat.

phrases.he: וְהַמֵּחַם בָּאֶמְצַע.
phrases.en: And the boiler in the middle,

phrases.he: וּכְשֶׁהַשַּׁמָּשׁ עוֹמֵד לִמְזֹג,
phrases.en: When the attendant gets up to pour

phrases.he: קוֹפֵץ אֶת פִּיו וּמַחֲזִיר אֶת פָּנָיו עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ אֵצֶל חֲבוּרָתוֹ וְאוֹכֵל.
phrases.en: he must close his mouth and turn his face until he reaches his group and eats.

phrases.he: וְהַכַּלָּה, הוֹפֶכֶת פָּנֶיהָ וְאוֹכֶלֶת:
phrases.en: And the bride, turns her face and eats,

phrases.he: הָאִשָּׁה בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִיא בְּבֵית בַּעְלָהּ, שָׁחַט עָלֶיהָ בַּעְלָהּ וְשָׁחַט עָלֶיהָ אָבִיהָ, תֹּאכַל מִשֶּׁל בַּעְלָהּ.
phrases.en: A woman, when she is living in her husband's house, if her husband slaughtered the Paschal lamb on her behalf and her father also slaughtered the Paschal lamb on her behalf, she should eat from her husband's lamb because it is assumed that the wife intended to be included in her husband's group.

phrases.he: הָלְכָה רֶגֶל רִאשׁוֹן לַעֲשׂוֹת בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ, שָׁחַט עָלֶיהָ אָבִיהָ וְשָׁחַט עָלֶיהָ בַּעְלָהּ, תֹּאכַל בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁהִיא רוֹצָה.
phrases.en: However, if, as was often customary, she went on the first Festival following her marriage to observe the Festival in her father's house, then, if both her husband slaughtered the Paschal lamb on her behalf and her father also slaughtered the Paschal lamb on her behalf, she may eat in whichever place she wishes, since it is not obvious with whose group she intended to be included.

phrases.he: יָתוֹם שֶׁשָּׁחֲטוּ עָלָיו אַפֹּטְרוֹפְּסִין, יֹאכַל בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁהוּא רוֹצֶה.
phrases.en: In the case of an orphan with multiple guardians, if each of his guardians [apotropsin] slaughtered a Paschal lamb on his behalf, intending that he be included in their group, he may eat in whichever place he wishes.

phrases.he: עֶבֶד שֶׁל שְׁנֵי שֻׁתָּפִין, לֹא יֹאכַל מִשֶּׁל שְׁנֵיהֶן.
phrases.en: A slave jointly owned by two partners may not eat from the lamb of either of them, unless it was stipulated beforehand from whose lamb he will partake.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶן חוֹרִין, לֹא יֹאכַל מִשֶּׁל רַבּוֹ:
phrases.en: One who is half slave and half free man may not eat from his master's lamb. It is assumed that the master did not intend to allow this person's free half to partake of the lamb, and therefore the master did not slaughter the lamb with him in mind. Consequently, the half slave is not included among those registered for his master's offering unless he was explicitly included.

phrases.he: הָאוֹמֵר לְעַבְדּוֹ, צֵא וּשְׁחֹט עָלַי אֶת הַפֶּסַח, שָׁחַט גְּדִי, יֹאכַל.
phrases.en: one who says to his slave: Go and slaughter the Paschal offering on my behalf, if the slave slaughtered a kid, his master may eat it

phrases.he: שָׁחַט טָלֶה, יֹאכַל.
phrases.en: if he slaughtered a lamb, his master may eat it

phrases.he: שָׁחַט גְּדִי וְטָלֶה, יֹאכַל מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.en: If the slave slaughtered both a kid and a lamb, his master should eat from the first one

phrases.he: שָׁכַח מָה אָמַר לוֹ רַבּוֹ, כֵּיצַד יַעֲשֶׂה, יִשְׁחַט טָלֶה וּגְדִי וְיֹאמַר, אִם גְּדִי אָמַר לִי רַבִּי, גְּדִי שֶׁלּוֹ וְטָלֶה שֶׁלִּי.
phrases.en: If the master had stated explicitly which type of animal to slaughter, but the slave forgot what his master said to him, what should he do? He should slaughter both a lamb and a kid and say the following stipulation: If my master said to me that I should slaughter a kid, the kid is for his Paschal offering and the lamb is for mine

phrases.he: וְאִם טָלֶה אָמַר לִי רַבִּי, הַטָּלֶה שֶׁלּוֹ וּגְדִי שֶׁלִּי.
phrases.en: and if my master said to me that I should slaughter a lamb, the lamb is for his Paschal offering and the kid is for mine

phrases.he: שָׁכַח רַבּוֹ מָה אָמַר לוֹ, שְׁנֵיהֶם יֵצְאוּ לְבֵית הַשְּׂרֵפָה, וּפְטוּרִין מִלַּעֲשׂוֹת פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי:
phrases.en: If his master also forgot what he said to him, both of them, go out to the place designated for burning, and are exempt from observing the second Pesaḥ

phrases.he: הָאוֹמֵר לְבָנָיו, הֲרֵינִי שׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל מִי שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה מִכֶּם רִאשׁוֹן לִירוּשָׁלַיִם,
phrases.en: one who says to his children: I am slaughtering the Paschal lamb on behalf of whomever of you goes up first to Jerusalem

phrases.he: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִכְנִיס הָרִאשׁוֹן רֹאשׁוֹ וְרֻבּוֹ,
phrases.en: as soon as the first of the children has entered his head and the majority of his body into Jerusalem

phrases.he: זָכָה בְחֶלְקוֹ וּמְזַכֶּה אֶת אֶחָיו עִמּוֹ.
phrases.en: he has acquired his portion and acquires on behalf of his brothers their portions together with him

phrases.he: לְעוֹלָם נִמְנִין עָלָיו עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בוֹ כַזַּיִת לְכָל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
phrases.en: Additional people can always be registered for a Paschal lamb, as long as there will be at least an olive-bulk of the lamb's meat for each and every person registered

phrases.he: נִמְנִין וּמוֹשְׁכִין אֶת יְדֵיהֶן מִמֶּנּוּ עַד שֶׁיִּשָּׁחֵט.
phrases.en: People can be registered and withdraw themselves from being registered for a Paschal lamb until it is slaughtered

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, עַד שֶׁיִּזְרֹק עָלָיו אֶת הַדָּם:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: Even until the priest sprinkles the blood

phrases.he: הַמַּמְנֶה עִמּוֹ אֲחֵרִים בְּחֶלְקוֹ,
phrases.en: If one who is registered for a Paschal lamb unilaterally registers another person with him in his portion of the Paschal lamb,

phrases.he: רַשָּׁאִין בְּנֵי חֲבוּרָה לִתֵּן לוֹ אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ,
phrases.en: the other members of his group are permitted to give him, i.e., the one who included the additional person, only his portion, which was originally allotted to him.

phrases.he: וְהוּא אוֹכֵל מִשֶּׁלּוֹ,
phrases.en: And he, the additional person, eats from his portion, i.e., the portion of he who added him;

phrases.he: וְהֵן אוֹכְלִין מִשֶּׁלָּהֶן:
phrases.en: and they, the other members of the group, eat from theirs.

phrases.he: זָב שֶׁרָאָה שְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת, שׁוֹחֲטִין עָלָיו בַּשְּׁבִיעִי.
phrases.en: A zav who saw two sightings, one slaughters on his behalf on his seventh.

phrases.he: רָאָה שָׁלֹשׁ, שׁוֹחֲטִין עָלָיו בַּשְּׁמִינִי שֶׁלּוֹ.
phrases.en: If he saw three, one slaughters on his behalf on his eighth.

phrases.he: שׁוֹמֶרֶת יוֹם כְּנֶגֶד יוֹם, שׁוֹחֲטִין עָלֶיהָ בַשֵּׁנִי שֶׁלָּהּ.
phrases.en: A woman who keeps watch a day for a day, one slaughters on her behalf on her second day.

phrases.he: רָאֲתָה שְׁנֵי יָמִים, שׁוֹחֲטִין עָלֶיהָ בַשְּׁלִישִׁי.
phrases.en: If she saw two days, one slaughters on her behalf on the third.

phrases.he: וְהַזָּבָה, שׁוֹחֲטִין עָלֶיהָ בַשְּׁמִינִי:
phrases.en: And a zava, one slaughters on her behalf on the eighth.

phrases.he: הָאוֹנֵן, וְהַמְפַקֵּחַ אֶת הַגַּל, וְכֵן מִי שֶׁהִבְטִיחוּהוּ לְהוֹצִיאוֹ מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִים, וְהַחוֹלֶה וְהַזָּקֵן שֶׁהֵן יְכוֹלִין לֶאֱכֹל כַּזַּיִת, שׁוֹחֲטִין עֲלֵיהֶן.
phrases.en: An acute mourner, and one clearing a pile of stones that collapsed on top of a person, in which case there is a possibility that the person buried underneath is dead and his corpse will impart ritual impurity to the person clearing the pile; and similarly, one whom the governing body promised to release from prison on the night of Passover; and an ill person and an elderly person who are still capable of eating an olive-bulk of meat, one slaughters the Paschal lamb on their behalf, since they are currently fit to eat the Paschal lamb.

phrases.he: עַל כֻּלָּן אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין עֲלֵיהֶן בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן, שֶׁמָּא יָבִיאוּ אֶת הַפֶּסַח לִידֵי פְסוּל.
phrases.en: However, with regard to all of them, this is only true when they are included in a group with other people who will definitely be able to partake of the lamb; but we do not slaughter the Paschal lamb on their behalf if they are by themselves, either as individuals or in a group composed entirely of such people, because perhaps they will cause the Paschal lamb to become disqualified, since there is a possibility that by the night of Passover they will be unable to partake of the Paschal lamb.

phrases.he: לְפִיכָךְ אִם אֵרַע בָּהֶן פְּסוּל, פְּטוּרִין מִלַּעֲשׂוֹת פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי, חוּץ מִן הַמְפַקֵּחַ בַּגַּל, שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ:
phrases.en: Therefore, since they were registered for a Paschal lamb and it was slaughtered when they were still fit to partake of it, even if a disqualification occurred to them later, preventing them from partaking of the Paschal lamb, they are nevertheless exempt from observing the second Pesaḥ. The exemption from the second Pesaḥ is dependent not on whether they partook of a Paschal lamb, but on whether it was validly slaughtered on their behalf. This holds true except for one who was clearing a pile of stones where the person buried underneath was eventually found dead, because in such a case the person searching for him certainly stood over the corpse at some point. He had therefore become ritually impure from the outset, even before the Paschal lamb was slaughtered.

phrases.he: אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל הַיָּחִיד, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: We do not slaughter the Paschal lamb on behalf of an individual, this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר.
phrases.en: And Rabbi Yosei permits it.

phrases.he: אֲפִלּוּ חֲבוּרָה שֶׁל מֵאָה שֶׁאֵין יְכוֹלִין לֶאֱכֹל כַּזַּיִת, אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין עֲלֵיהֶן.
phrases.en: And even if there is a group of one hundred who together are unable to eat an olive-bulk of it, we do not slaughter on their behalf.

phrases.he: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין חֲבוּרַת נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים:
phrases.en: And we do not make a group of women, slaves, and minors.

phrases.he: אוֹנֵן טוֹבֵל וְאוֹכֵל אֶת פִּסְחוֹ לָעֶרֶב, אֲבָל לֹא בַקָּדָשִׁים.
phrases.en: An acute mourner immerses and eats his Paschal lamb in the evening. But he may still not eat other sacrificial food.

phrases.he: הַשּׁוֹמֵעַ עַל מֵתוֹ, וְהַמְלַקֵּט לוֹ עֲצָמוֹת, טוֹבֵל וְאוֹכֵל בַּקָּדָשִׁים.
phrases.en: One who hears about the death of his dead, and one who gathers the bones of his parents, these mourners immerse and eat all types of sacrificial food at night.

phrases.he: גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּר בְּעֶרֶב פֶּסַח, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, טוֹבֵל וְאוֹכֵל אֶת פִּסְחוֹ לָעֶרֶב.
phrases.en: A convert who converted on Passover eve, Beit Shammai say: He immerses and eats his Paschal lamb in the evening.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִן הָעָרְלָה כְּפוֹרֵשׁ מִן הַקָּבֶר:
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: One who separates from the foreskin is ritually impure, like one who separates from the grave.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁהָיָה טָמֵא אוֹ בְדֶרֶךְ רְחוֹקָה וְלֹא עָשָׂה אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹן, יַעֲשֶׂה אֶת הַשֵּׁנִי.
phrases.en: One who was ritually impure or on a distant journey and did not observe the first should observe the second.

phrases.he: שָׁגַג אוֹ נֶאֱנַס וְלֹא עָשָׂה אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹן, יַעֲשֶׂה אֶת הַשֵּׁנִי.
phrases.en: If one unwittingly forgot or was prevented due to circumstances beyond his control and did not observe the first, he too should observe the second.

phrases.he: אִם כֵּן, לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר טָמֵא אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בְדֶרֶךְ רְחוֹקָה, שֶׁאֵלּוּ פְּטוּרִין מֵהִכָּרֵת, וְאֵלּוּ חַיָּבִין בְּהִכָּרֵת:
phrases.en: If so, why is it stated that one was ritually impure or on a distant journey? That these are exempt from karet, but those are liable to karet.

phrases.he: אֵיזוֹ הִיא דֶרֶךְ רְחוֹקָה.
phrases.en: What is the definition of a distant journey

phrases.he: מִן הַמּוֹדִיעִים וְלַחוּץ, וּכְמִדָּתָהּ לְכָל רוּחַ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.en: from the city of Modi'im and beyond, and from anywhere located an equal distance from Jerusalem and beyond in every direction; this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, מֵאַסְקֻפַּת הָעֲזָרָה וְלַחוּץ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: From the threshold of the Temple courtyard and beyond

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, לְפִיכָךְ נָקוּד עַל ה'.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei said to him: Therefore, the word is dotted over the letter heh

phrases.he: לוֹמַר, לֹא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁרְחוֹקָה וַדַּאי, אֶלָּא מֵאִסְקֻפַּת הָעֲזָרָה וְלַחוּץ.
phrases.en: to say that the meaning of the word should be qualified: It should be understood that it is not because he is really distant; rather, it includes anyone located from the threshold of the Temple courtyard and beyond.

phrases.he: מַה בֵּין פֶּסַח רִאשׁוֹן לַשֵּׁנִי,
phrases.en: What is the difference between the Paschal lamb offered on the first Pesaḥ and the second Pesaḥ?

phrases.he: הָרִאשׁוֹן אָסוּר בְּבַל יֵרָאֶה וּבַל יִמָּצֵא,
phrases.en: On the first Pesaḥ, at the time of slaughtering the Paschal lamb, it is prohibited to own leavened bread due to the prohibitions: It shall not be seen, and: It shall not be found.

phrases.he: וְהַשֵּׁנִי, מַצָּה וְחָמֵץ עִמּוֹ בַּבָּיִת.
phrases.en: And on the second Pesaḥ it is permissible for one to have both leavened bread and matza with him in the house.

phrases.he: הָרִאשׁוֹן טָעוּן הַלֵּל בַּאֲכִילָתוֹ,
phrases.en: the Paschal lamb offered on the first Pesaḥ requires the recitation of hallel as it is eaten

phrases.he: וְהַשֵּׁנִי אֵינוֹ טָעוּן הַלֵּל בַּאֲכִילָתוֹ.
phrases.en: and the second does not require the recitation of hallel as it is eaten.

phrases.he: זֶה וָזֶה טָעוּן הַלֵּל בַּעֲשִׂיָּתָן,
phrases.en: the Paschal lambs sacrificed on both the first and second Pesaḥ require the recitation of hallel as they are prepared,

phrases.he: וְנֶאֱכָלִין צָלִי עַל מַצּוֹת וּמְרוֹרִים,
phrases.en: and they are both eaten roasted with matza and bitter herbs,

phrases.he: וְדוֹחִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת:
phrases.en: and they override Shabbat in that they may be slaughtered and their blood sprinkled even on Shabbat.

phrases.he: הַפֶּסַח שֶׁבָּא בְטֻמְאָה, לֹא יֹאכְלוּ מִמֶּנּוּ זָבִין וְזָבוֹת נִדּוֹת וְיוֹלְדוֹת.
phrases.en: the Paschal lamb is sacrificed in ritual impurity zavim, and zavot, menstruating women, and women after childbirth may not eat it

phrases.he: וְאִם אָכְלוּ, פְּטוּרִים מִכָּרֵת.
phrases.en: if they ate they are exempt from karet

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פּוֹטֵר אַף עַל בִּיאַת מִקְדָּשׁ:
phrases.en: And Rabbi Eliezer exempts even for entering the Temple

phrases.he: מַה בֵּין פֶּסַח מִצְרַיִם לְפֶסַח דּוֹרוֹת
phrases.en: What are the differences between the Paschal lamb that the Jewish people offered in Egypt and the Paschal lamb offered in all later generations?

phrases.he: פֶּסַח מִצְרַיִם מִקָּחוֹ מִבֶּעָשׂוֹר
phrases.en: The Paschal lamb the Jewish people offered in Egypt had to be taken from the tenth of the month of Nisan

phrases.he: וְטָעוּן הַזָּאָה בַאֲגֻדַּת אֵזוֹב עַל הַמַּשְׁקוֹף וְעַל שְׁתֵּי מְזוּזוֹת
phrases.en: and required the people to sprinkle its blood with a bundle of hyssop, unlike the Paschal lamb in all later years, and its blood was also sprinkled upon the lintel and the two doorposts

phrases.he: וְנֶאֱכָל בְּחִפָּזוֹן בְּלַיְלָה אֶחָד
phrases.en: and it was eaten with haste; in addition, the Paschal lamb in Egypt was only on one night

phrases.he: וּפֶסַח דּוֹרוֹת נוֹהֵג כָּל שִׁבְעָה
phrases.en: whereas the Paschal lamb throughout the generations is observed for seven days

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, שָׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁתְּמוּרַת הַפֶּסַח קְרֵבָה, וּתְמוּרַת הַפֶּסַח אֵינָהּ קְרֵבָה, וְאֵין לִי לְפָרֵשׁ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said: I heard that the substitute of a Paschal lamb is sacrificed and the substitute of a Paschal lamb is not sacrificed; and I cannot explain these two rulings.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, אֲנִי אֲפָרֵשׁ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva said: I will explain:

phrases.he: הַפֶּסַח שֶׁנִּמְצָא קֹדֶם שְׁחִיטַת הַפֶּסַח, יִרְעֶה עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֵב, וְיִמָּכֵר, וְיִקַּח בְּדָמָיו שְׁלָמִים, וְכֵן תְּמוּרָתוֹ.
phrases.en: With regard to a Paschal lamb that is found before the slaughter of the Paschal lamb, it is left to graze until it becomes unfit and disqualified for use as a sacrifice. It is then sold and the owner must bring a peace-offering with its proceeds. And so too, its substitute:

phrases.he: אַחַר שְׁחִיטַת הַפֶּסַח, קָרֵב שְׁלָמִים, וְכֵן תְּמוּרָתוֹ:
phrases.en: After the slaughter of the Paschal lamb, it is sacrificed as a peace-offering, and so too, its substitute

phrases.he: הַמַּפְרִישׁ נְקֵבָה לְפִסְחוֹ אוֹ זָכָר בֶּן שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים,
phrases.en: one who separates a female animal for his Paschal lamb although the Torah requires a male, or a male that is in its second year although a Paschal lamb must be an animal that is in its first year,

phrases.he: יִרְעֶה עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֵב, וְיִמָּכֵר, וְיִפְּלוּ דָמָיו לִנְדָבָה.
phrases.en: is left to graze until it develops a blemish and becomes unfit, and it is then sold and its money is used for free-will offerings or peace-offerings.

phrases.he: הַמַּפְרִישׁ פִּסְחוֹ וָמֵת,
phrases.en: one who separates his Paschal lamb and then dies,

phrases.he: לֹא יְבִיאֶנּוּ בְנוֹ אַחֲרָיו לְשֵׁם פֶּסַח,
phrases.en: his son may not bring it after him for the purpose of a Paschal lamb

phrases.he: אֶלָּא לְשֵׁם שְׁלָמִים:
phrases.en: Rather, it is brought for the purpose of a peace-offering.

phrases.he: הַפֶּסַח שֶׁנִּתְעָרֵב בִּזְבָחִים,
phrases.en: a Paschal lamb that was intermingled with offerings,

phrases.he: כֻּלָּן יִרְעוּ עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֲבוּ,
phrases.en: all of them are left to graze until they develop a blemish and become unfit;

phrases.he: וְיִמָּכְרוּ,
phrases.en: and they are then sold,

phrases.he: וְיָבִיא בִדְמֵי הַיָּפֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן מִמִּין זֶה,
phrases.en: and with the proceeds of the choicest of them he must bring this type of sacrifice,

phrases.he: וּבִדְמֵי הַיָּפֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן מִמִּין זֶה,
phrases.en: and with the proceeds of the choicest of them he must bring this other type of sacrifice,

phrases.he: וְיַפְסִיד הַמּוֹתָר מִבֵּיתוֹ.
phrases.en: And he loses the difference from his own pocket.

phrases.he: נִתְעָרֵב בִּבְכוֹרוֹת,
phrases.en: If a Paschal lamb was intermingled with firstborn animals,

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אִם חֲבוּרַת כֹּהֲנִים, יֹאכְלוּ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: If those whose offerings became mixed together were groups of priests, they may eat all of the animals on Passover night.

phrases.he: חֲבוּרָה שֶׁאָבַד פִּסְחָהּ, וְאָמְרָה לְאֶחָד, צֵא וּבַקֵּשׁ וּשְׁחֹט עָלֵינוּ, וְהָלַךְ וּמָצָא וְשָׁחַט, וְהֵם לָקְחוּ וְשָׁחֲטוּ,
phrases.en: a group whose Paschal lamb was lost, and they said to one member of the group: Go and search for our Paschal lamb, and when you find it, slaughter it on our behalf; and he went and found the missing offering and slaughtered it on behalf of the entire group, but in the meantime they took a different animal and slaughtered it as a Paschal lamb,

phrases.he: אִם שֶׁלּוֹ נִשְׁחַט רִאשׁוֹן, הוּא אוֹכֵל מִשֶּׁלּוֹ, וְהֵם אוֹכְלִים עִמּוֹ מִשֶּׁלּוֹ,
phrases.en: If his Paschal lamb was slaughtered first, he eats from his offering, as he is considered to be registered specifically for that offering, and they eat with him from his offering, because he included them in his offering and it belongs to the entire group.

phrases.he: וְאִם שֶׁלָּהֶן נִשְׁחַט רִאשׁוֹן, הֵם אוֹכְלִין מִשֶּׁלָּהֶן, וְהוּא אוֹכֵל מִשֶּׁלּוֹ.
phrases.en: And if theirs was slaughtered first, they eat from theirs because they withdrew from the original offering through the act of slaughtering a replacement, and he eats from his because he was not registered for the replacement offering sacrificed by the remainder of his group.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ יָדוּעַ אֵיזֶה מֵהֶן נִשְׁחַט רִאשׁוֹן, אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁחֲטוּ שְׁנֵיהֶן כְּאֶחָד, הוּא אוֹכֵל מִשֶּׁלּוֹ, וְהֵם אֵינָם אוֹכְלִים עִמּוֹ, וְשֶׁלָּהֶן יֵצֵא לְבֵית הַשְּׂרֵפָה, וּפְטוּרִין מִלַּעֲשׂוֹת פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי.
phrases.en: And if it is not known which of the offerings was slaughtered first, or if both the group and the individual slaughtered them together, he eats from his and they do not eat with him in case theirs was slaughtered first, and theirs must be taken out to the place designated for burning. They are exempt from performing the offering of the Paschal lamb on the second Pesaḥ, because they were included in the slaughter of whichever animal was slaughtered first.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶן, אִם אֵחַרְתִּי, צְאוּ וְשַׁחֲטוּ עָלָי. הָלַךְ וּמְצָאוֹ, וְשָׁחַט, וְהֵן לָקְחוּ וְשָׁחֲטוּ,
phrases.en: said to the other members of the group before he left: If I am late, go and slaughter a Paschal lamb for me. He then went and found the lost Paschal lamb and slaughtered it, and they took another animal and slaughtered it as a Paschal lamb.

phrases.he: אִם שֶׁלָּהֶן נִשְׁחַט רִאשׁוֹן, הֵן אוֹכְלִין מִשֶּׁלָּהֶן, וְהוּא אוֹכֵל עִמָּהֶן.
phrases.en: if theirs was slaughtered first, they eat from theirs and he eats with them, because he requested to be included in their offering and they registered him for their Paschal lamb.

phrases.he: וְאִם שֶׁלּוֹ נִשְׁחַט רִאשׁוֹן, הוּא אוֹכֵל מִשֶּׁלּוֹ, וְהֵן אוֹכְלִין מִשֶּׁלָּהֶן.
phrases.en: And if his was slaughtered first, he eats from his and they eat from theirs, because the fact that they slaughtered a different animal indicates that they have withdrawn from the original offering.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ יָדוּעַ אֵיזֶה מֵהֶם נִשְׁחַט רִאשׁוֹן, אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁחֲטוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם כְּאֶחָד, הֵן אוֹכְלִין מִשֶּׁלָּהֶן, וְהוּא אֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל עִמָּהֶן, וְשֶׁלּוֹ יֵצֵא לְבֵית הַשְּׂרֵפָה, וּפָטוּר מִלַּעֲשׂוֹת פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי.
phrases.en: And if it is not known which of the animals was slaughtered first, or if both the group and the individual slaughtered them together, they eat from theirs because they definitely withdrew from the original offering by slaughtering a different one, and he does not eat with them because he also intended to be included in the animal he slaughtered and it is not clear which was slaughtered first. Therefore, his must be taken out to the place designated for burning; and he is exempt from performing the sacrifice of the Paschal lamb on the second Pesaḥ.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶן וְאָמְרוּ לוֹ, אוֹכְלִין כֻּלָּם מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.en: If he said to them and they said to him, all of them eat from the first sacrifice that was slaughtered.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵין יָדוּעַ אֵיזֶה מֵהֶן נִשְׁחַט רִאשׁוֹן, שְׁנֵיהֶם יוֹצְאִין לְבֵית הַשְּׂרֵפָה.
phrases.en: And if it is not known which of them was slaughtered first, both of them must be taken out to the place designated for burning,

phrases.he: לֹא אָמַר לָהֶן וְלֹא אָמְרוּ לוֹ, אֵינָן אַחֲרָאִין זֶה לָזֶה:
phrases.en: If he did not say anything to them and they did not say anything to him, they are not responsible for each other,

phrases.he: שְׁתֵּי חֲבוּרוֹת שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ פִסְחֵיהֶן,
phrases.en: Two groups whose Paschal lambs have become intermingled

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ מוֹשְׁכִין לָהֶן אֶחָד וְאֵלּוּ מוֹשְׁכִין לָהֶן אֶחָד,
phrases.en: These draw one for themselves, and those draw one for themselves.

phrases.he: אֶחָד מֵאֵלּוּ בָא לוֹ אֵצֶל אֵלּוּ, וְאֶחָד מֵאֵלּוּ בָא לוֹ אֵצֶל אֵלּוּ,
phrases.en: One of these comes to those, and one of those comes to these.

phrases.he: וְכָךְ הֵם אוֹמְרִים, אִם שֶׁלָּנוּ הוּא הַפֶּסַח הַזֶּה, יָדֶיךָ מְשׁוּכוֹת מִשֶּׁלְּךָ וְנִמְנֵיתָ עַל שֶׁלָּנוּ,
phrases.en: And this is what they says: If this Paschal lamb is ours, you are withdrawn from yours, and you are registered for ours,

phrases.he: וְאִם שֶׁלְּךָ הוּא הַפֶּסַח הַזֶּה, יָדֵינוּ מְשׁוּכוֹת מִשֶּׁלָּנוּ וְנִמְנֵינוּ עַל שֶׁלָּךְ.
phrases.en: And if this Paschal lamb is yours, we are withdrawn from ours and we are registered for yours.

phrases.he: וְכֵן חָמֵשׁ חֲבוּרוֹת שֶׁל חֲמִשָּׁה חֲמִשָּׁה, וְשֶׁל עֲשָׂרָה עֲשָׂרָה,
phrases.en: And similarly, five groups of five each or of ten each,

phrases.he: מוֹשְׁכִין לָהֶן אֶחָד מִכָּל חֲבוּרָה וַחֲבוּרָה, וְכֵן הֵם אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.en: they draw one from each and every group, and they say this

phrases.he: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ פִסְחֵיהֶם,
phrases.en: two individuals whose Paschal lambs became intermingled

phrases.he: זֶה מוֹשֵׁךְ לוֹ אֶחָד,
phrases.en: This person draws one of the Paschal lambs for himself

phrases.he: וְזֶה מוֹשֵׁךְ לוֹ אֶחָד,
phrases.en: and that person draws one for himself

phrases.he: זֶה מַמְנֶה עִמּוֹ אֶחָד מִן הַשּׁוּק,
phrases.en: this person registers someone from the marketplace with him on his Paschal lamb

phrases.he: וְזֶה מַמְנֶה עִמּוֹ אֶחָד מִן הַשּׁוּק,
phrases.en: and that person registers someone from the marketplace with him on his Paschal lamb

phrases.he: זֶה בָא אֵצֶל זֶה,
phrases.en: this one comes to that person from the marketplace

phrases.he: וְזֶה בָא אֵצֶל זֶה,
phrases.en: and that one comes to this person from the marketplace

phrases.he: וְכָךְ הֵם אוֹמְרִים, אִם שֶׁלִּי הוּא פֶסַח זֶה, יָדֶיךָ מְשׁוּכוֹת מִשֶּׁלְּךָ וְנִמְנֵיתָ עַל שֶׁלִּי.
phrases.en: and this is what they say: If this Paschal lamb is mine, you are withdrawn from yours and you are registered for mine

phrases.he: וְאִם שֶׁלְּךָ הוּא פֶסַח זֶה, יָדַי מְשׁוּכוֹת מִשֶּׁלִּי וְנִמְנֵיתִי עַל שֶׁלָּךָ:
phrases.en: and if this is your Paschal lamb, I am withdrawn from mine and I am hereby registered for yours

phrases.he: עַרְבֵי פְסָחִים סָמוּךְ לַמִּנְחָה
phrases.en: On the eve of Passover, adjacent to minḥa time

phrases.he: לֹא יֹאכַל אָדָם עַד שֶׁתֶּחְשָׁךְ.
phrases.en: a person may not eat until dark

phrases.he: וַאֲפִלּוּ עָנִי שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יֹאכַל עַד שֶׁיָּסֵב.
phrases.en: Even the poorest of Jews should not eat the meal on Passover night until he reclines on his left side, as free and wealthy people recline when they eat

phrases.he: וְלֹא יִפְחֲתוּ לוֹ מֵאַרְבַּע כּוֹסוֹת שֶׁל יַיִן
phrases.en: And the distributors of charity should not give a poor person less than four cups of wine for the Festival meal of Passover night

phrases.he: וַאֲפִלּוּ מִן הַתַּמְחוּי:
phrases.en: And even if the poor person is one of the poorest members of society and receives his food from the charity plate

phrases.he: מָזְגוּ לוֹ כוֹס רִאשׁוֹן,
phrases.en: poured the wine of the first cup

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיּוֹם, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיָּיִן.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One recites the blessing over the day, and thereafter he recites the blessing over the wine:

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיַּיִן, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיּוֹם:
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: One recites the blessing over the wine and thereafter recites the blessing over the day.

phrases.he: הֵבִיאוּ לְפָנָיו, מְטַבֵּל בַּחֲזֶרֶת, עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְפַרְפֶּרֶת הַפַּת.
phrases.en: They brought before him matza. He dips the ḥazeret into water or vinegar, to taste some food before he reaches the dessert of the bread.

phrases.he: הֵבִיאוּ לְפָנָיו מַצָּה וַחֲזֶרֶת וַחֲרֹסֶת וּשְׁנֵי תַבְשִׁילִין, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין חֲרֹסֶת מִצְוָה.
phrases.en: They brought before him matza and ḥazeret and ḥaroset, and two cooked dishes although ḥaroset is not a mitzva.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר, מִצְוָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Tzadok says: a mitzva.

phrases.he: וּבַמִּקְדָּשׁ הָיוּ מְבִיאִים לְפָנָיו גּוּפוֹ שֶׁל פָּסַח:
phrases.en: And in the Temple they brought before him the body of the Paschal lamb.

phrases.he: מָזְגוּ לוֹ כוֹס שֵׁנִי,
phrases.en: poured the second cup for

phrases.he: וְכָאן הַבֵּן שׁוֹאֵל אָבִיו,
phrases.en: and here the son asks his father

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵין דַּעַת בַּבֵּן, אָבִיו מְלַמְּדוֹ,
phrases.en: And if the son does not have the intelligence to ask questions on his own, his father teaches him

phrases.he: מַה נִּשְׁתַּנָּה הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה מִכָּל הַלֵּילוֹת,
phrases.en: Why is this night different from all other nights?

phrases.he: שֶׁבְּכָל הַלֵּילוֹת אָנוּ אוֹכְלִין חָמֵץ וּמַצָּה, הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה כֻלּוֹ מַצָּה.
phrases.en: As on all other nights we eat leavened bread and matza as preferred; on this night all our bread is matza.

phrases.he: שֶׁבְּכָל הַלֵּילוֹת אָנוּ אוֹכְלִין שְׁאָר יְרָקוֹת, הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה מָרוֹר.
phrases.en: As on all other nights we eat other vegetables; on this night we eat bitter herbs.

phrases.he: שֶׁבְּכָל הַלֵּילוֹת אָנוּ אוֹכְלִין בָּשָׂר צָלִי, שָׁלוּק, וּמְבֻשָּׁל, הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה כֻלּוֹ צָלִי.
phrases.en: As on all other nights we eat either roasted, stewed, or cooked meat, but on this night all the meat is the roasted meat of the Paschal lamb.

phrases.he: שֶׁבְּכָל הַלֵּילוֹת אָנוּ מַטְבִּילִין פַּעַם אַחַת, הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה שְׁתֵּי פְעָמִים.
phrases.en: As on all other nights we dip the vegetables in a liquid during the meal only once; however, on this night we dip twice.

phrases.he: וּלְפִי דַעְתּוֹ שֶׁל בֵּן, אָבִיו מְלַמְּדוֹ.
phrases.en: And according to the intelligence and the ability of the son, his father teaches him

phrases.he: מַתְחִיל בִּגְנוּת וּמְסַיֵּם בְּשֶׁבַח,
phrases.en: He begins with the Jewish people's disgrace and concludes with their glory.

phrases.he: וְדוֹרֵשׁ מֵאֲרַמִּי אוֹבֵד אָבִי,
phrases.en: And he expounds from the passage: "An Aramean tried to destroy my father"

phrases.he: עַד שֶׁיִּגְמֹר כֹּל הַפָּרָשָׁה כֻלָּהּ:
phrases.en: until he concludes explaining the entire section.

phrases.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָיָה אוֹמֵר, כָּל שֶׁלֹּא אָמַר שְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים אֵלּוּ בְּפֶסַח, לֹא יָצָא יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ,
phrases.en: Rabban Gamliel would say: Anyone who did not say these three matters on Passover has not fulfilled his obligation:

phrases.he: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן, פֶּסַח, מַצָּה, וּמָרוֹר.
phrases.en: The Paschal lamb, matza, and bitter herbs.

phrases.he: פֶּסַח, עַל שׁוּם שֶׁפָּסַח הַמָּקוֹם עַל בָּתֵּי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ בְמִצְרַיִם.
phrases.en: The Paschal lamb is brought because the Omnipresent passed over the houses of our forefathers in Egypt

phrases.he: מַצָּה, עַל שׁוּם שֶׁנִּגְאֲלוּ אֲבוֹתֵינוּ בְמִצְרַיִם.
phrases.en: The reason for matza is because our forefathers were redeemed from Egypt

phrases.he: מָרוֹר, עַל שׁוּם שֶׁמֵּרְרוּ הַמִּצְרִים אֶת חַיֵּי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ בְמִצְרָיִם.
phrases.en: The reason for bitter herbs is because the Egyptians embittered our forefathers' lives in Egypt

phrases.he: בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר חַיָּב אָדָם לִרְאוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ כְאִלּוּ הוּא יָצָא מִמִּצְרַיִם,
phrases.en: In each and every generation a person must view himself as though he personally left Egypt

phrases.he: לְפִיכָךְ אֲנַחְנוּ חַיָּבִין לְהוֹדוֹת, לְהַלֵּל, לְשַׁבֵּחַ, לְפָאֵר, לְרוֹמֵם, לְהַדֵּר, לְבָרֵךְ, לְעַלֵּה, וּלְקַלֵּס, לְמִי שֶׁעָשָׂה לַאֲבוֹתֵינוּ וְלָנוּ אֶת כָּל הַנִּסִּים הָאֵלּוּ, הוֹצִיאָנוּ מֵעַבְדוּת לְחֵרוּת, מִיָּגוֹן לְשִׂמְחָה, וּמֵאֵבֶל לְיוֹם טוֹב, וּמֵאֲפֵלָה לְאוֹר גָּדוֹל, וּמִשִּׁעְבּוּד לִגְאֻלָּה.
phrases.en: Therefore we are obligated to thank, praise, glorify, extol, exalt, honor, bless, revere, and laud the One who performed for our forefathers and for us all these miracles: He took us out from slavery to freedom, from sorrow to joy, from mourning to a Festival, from darkness to a great light, and from enslavement to redemption.

phrases.he: וְנֹאמַר לְפָנָיו, הַלְלוּיָהּ:
phrases.en: And we will say before Him: Halleluya.

phrases.he: עַד הֵיכָן הוּא אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Until where does one recite

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, עַד אֵם הַבָּנִים שְׂמֵחָה.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: Until a joyful mother of children,

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, עַד חַלָּמִישׁ לְמַעְיְנוֹ מָיִם.
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: Until the flint into a fountain of waters

phrases.he: וְחוֹתֵם בִּגְאֻלָּה.
phrases.en: And one concludes with a blessing that refers to redemption.

phrases.he: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר, אֲשֶׁר גְּאָלָנוּ וְגָאַל אֶת אֲבוֹתֵינוּ מִמִּצְרָיִם, וְלֹא הָיָה חוֹתֵם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Tarfon says that although one should recite: Who redeemed us and redeemed our forefathers from Egypt, one who did so would not conclude with the formula: Blessed are You, Lord.
