phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, כֵּן ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ יַגִּיעֵנוּ לְמוֹעֲדִים וְלִרְגָלִים אֲחֵרִים הַבָּאִים לִקְרָאתֵנוּ לְשָׁלוֹם, שְׂמֵחִים בְּבִנְיַן עִירֶךָ וְשָׂשִׂים בַּעֲבוֹדָתֶךָ, וְנֹאכַל שָׁם מִן הַזְּבָחִים וּמִן הַפְּסָחִים כוּ', עַד בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה' גָּאַל יִשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says that one recites a different version of this blessing: So too, the Lord our God and the God of our forefathers will bring us to future holidays and Festivals in peace, happy over the building of Your city and joyous in Your service. And there we will eat from the Paschal lamb and other offerings, etc., until: Blessed are You, Lord, Who redeemed Israel.

phrases.he: מָזְגוּ לוֹ כוֹס שְׁלִישִׁי, מְבָרֵךְ עַל מְזוֹנוֹ.
phrases.en: They poured for him the third cup, and he recites the blessing over his food.

phrases.he: רְבִיעִי, גּוֹמֵר עָלָיו אֶת הַהַלֵּל, וְאוֹמֵר עָלָיו בִּרְכַּת הַשִּׁיר.
phrases.en: Fourth, he completes hallel over it, and he recites the blessing of the song over it.

phrases.he: בֵּין הַכּוֹסוֹת הַלָּלוּ, אִם רוֹצֶה לִשְׁתּוֹת, יִשְׁתֶּה.
phrases.en: Between these cups, if one wishes to drink he may drink.

phrases.he: בֵּין שְׁלִישִׁי לָרְבִיעִי, לֹא יִשְׁתֶּה:
phrases.en: Between the third and the fourth one should not drink.

phrases.he: וְאֵין מַפְטִירִין אַחַר הַפֶּסַח אֲפִיקוֹמָן.
phrases.en: One does not conclude after the Paschal lamb with an afikoman.

phrases.he: יָשְׁנוּ מִקְצָתָן, יֹאכְלוּ.
phrases.en: If some of the participants at the seder fell asleep, they may eat from the Paschal lamb when they awake.

phrases.he: כֻּלָּן, לֹא יֹאכֵלוּ.
phrases.en: If the entire company fell asleep, they may not eat any more.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, נִתְנַמְנְמוּ, יֹאכְלוּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: If they dozed they may eat from the Paschal lamb when they awake,

phrases.he: נִרְדְּמוּ, לֹא יֹאכְלוּ:
phrases.en: but if they fell fast asleep they may not eat from it.

phrases.he: הַפֶּסַח אַחַר חֲצוֹת, מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדָיִם.
phrases.en: The Paschal lamb after midnight renders one's hands ritually impure,

phrases.he: הַפִּגּוּל וְהַנּוֹתָר, מְטַמְּאִין אֶת הַיָּדָיִם.
phrases.en: piggul, and notar render one's hands ritually impure.

phrases.he: בֵּרַךְ בִּרְכַּת הַפֶּסַח פָּטַר אֶת שֶׁל זֶבַח.
phrases.en: one recited the blessing over the Paschal lamb, he has also exempted himself from reciting a blessing over the Festival offering.

phrases.he: בֵּרַךְ אֶת שֶׁל זֶבַח, לֹא פָטַר אֶת שֶׁל פֶּסַח, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל.
phrases.en: he recited the blessing over the Festival offering, he has not exempted himself from reciting a blessing over the Paschal lamb. This is the statement of Rabbi Yishmael.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, לֹא זוֹ פוֹטֶרֶת זוֹ, וְלֹא זוֹ פוֹטֶרֶת זוֹ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: This does not exempt one from reciting a blessing over this one, and that does not exempt that one,

phrases.he: בְּאֶחָד בַּאֲדָר מַשְׁמִיעִין עַל הַשְּׁקָלִים וְעַל הַכִּלְאַיִם.
phrases.en: On the first of Adar the court proclaims concerning the collection of shekels, and with regard to the obligation to uproot forbidden mixtures of diverse kinds of food crops in gardens and fields.

phrases.he: בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בּוֹ קוֹרִין אֶת הַמְּגִלָּה בַּכְּרַכִּין,
phrases.en: And on the fifteenth day of the month of Adar, the Scroll [Megilla] of Esther is read in the cities [kerakim] surrounded by walls from the time of Joshua.

phrases.he: וּמְתַקְּנִין אֶת הַדְּרָכִים וְאֶת הָרְחוֹבוֹת וְאֶת מִקְוְאוֹת הַמַּיִם,
phrases.en: And they repair the roads that were damaged in the winter, and the streets, and the cisterns.

phrases.he: וְעוֹשִׂין כָּל צָרְכֵי הָרַבִּים,
phrases.en: And they perform all that is necessary for public welfare.

phrases.he: וּמְצַיְּנִין אֶת הַקְּבָרוֹת,
phrases.en: And they mark the gravesites anew, so that people would know their location and avoid ritual impurity, as the previous markers may have eroded during the rainy season.

phrases.he: וְיוֹצְאִין אַף עַל הַכִּלְאָיִם:
phrases.en: And agents of the court also go out to inspect the fields for diverse kinds of food crops, to determine whether or not the farmers had in fact uprooted these seeds after the proclamation on the first of the month.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ עוֹקְרִין וּמַשְׁלִיכִין לִפְנֵיהֶם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda said: At first those agents would uproot the diverse kinds of crops and cast them in front of the owners of the fields.

phrases.he: מִשֶּׁרַבּוּ עוֹבְרֵי עֲבֵרָה, הָיוּ עוֹקְרִין וּמַשְׁלִיכִין עַל הַדְּרָכִים, הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהוּ מַפְקִירִין כָּל הַשָּׂדֶה כֻּלָּהּ.
phrases.en: When the number of transgressors who would not uproot diverse kinds in their fields increased, they would cast the uprooted crops onto the roads. Ultimately, they instituted that the entire field should be declared ownerless.

phrases.he: בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בּוֹ, שֻׁלְחָנוֹת הָיוּ יוֹשְׁבִין בַּמְּדִינָה.
phrases.en: On the fifteenth of Adar, money changers would sit at tables set up in the rest of the country, outside the Temple, to handle the collection of shekels.

phrases.he: בְּעֶשְׂרִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה, יָשְׁבוּ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ.
phrases.en: On the twenty-fifth of Adar, the money changers sat in the Temple.

phrases.he: מִשֶּׁיָּשְׁבוּ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ, הִתְחִילוּ לְמַשְׁכֵּן.
phrases.en: From the time when the money changers sat in the Temple, the court began to seize collateral from those who had yet to donate the half-shekel.

phrases.he: אֶת מִי מְמַשְׁכְּנִין, לְוִיִּם וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִים, גֵּרִים וַעֲבָדִים מְשֻׁחְרָרִים, אֲבָל לֹא נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים.
phrases.en: From whom did they seize collateral? From Levites, Israelites, converts, and emancipated slaves. However, they did not seize collateral from women, slaves, or minors.

phrases.he: כָּל קָטָן שֶׁהִתְחִיל אָבִיו לִשְׁקוֹל עַל יָדוֹ, שׁוּב אֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵק.
phrases.en: And any minor whose father began one year to contribute a half-shekel on his behalf, he may not cease to do so in subsequent years.

phrases.he: וְאֵין מְמַשְׁכְּנִין אֶת הַכֹּהֲנִים מִפְּנֵי דַּרְכֵּי שָׁלוֹם.
phrases.en: The court does not seize collateral from priests, because of the ways of peace.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda said

phrases.he: הֵעִיד בֶּן בּוּכְרִי בְּיַבְנֶה, כָּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁשּׁוֹקֵל אֵינוֹ חוֹטֵא.
phrases.en: ben Bukhri testified in Yavne: Any priest who contributes the half-shekel is not considered a sinner, despite the fact that he is not obligated to do so.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי,
phrases.en: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai said to

phrases.he: לֹא כִּי, אֶלָּא כָּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁאֵינוֹ שׁוֹקֵל חוֹטֵא,
phrases.en: Not so; rather, any priest who does not contribute the half-shekel is considered a sinner, as they are obligated like all other Jews.

phrases.he: אֶלָּא שֶׁהַכֹּהֲנִים דּוֹרְשִׁים מִקְרָא זֶה לְעַצְמָן,
phrases.en: However, the priests who do not contribute interpret this verse to their own advantage:

phrases.he: (ויקרא ו) וְכָל מִנְחַת כֹּהֵן כָּלִיל תִּהְיֶה לֹא תֵאָכֵל,
phrases.en: "And every meal-offering of the priest shall be wholly made to smoke; it shall not be eaten" (Leviticus 6:16).

phrases.he: הוֹאִיל וְעֹמֶר וּשְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם וְלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים שֶׁלָּנוּ, הֵיאָךְ נֶאֱכָלִים:
phrases.en: Since the omer offering and the two loaves, i.e., the public offering of two loaves from the new wheat brought on the festival of Shavuot, and the shewbread placed on the sacred table in the Sanctuary each Shabbat, which are all meal-offerings, are ours, then if we contribute shekels we will have partial ownership of these communal offerings, as they are purchased with the shekels. How, then, can they be eaten?

phrases.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ, אֵין מְמַשְׁכְּנִין נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים,
phrases.en: Although the Sages said, as stated in the previous mishna, that the court does not seize collateral from women, slaves, and minors, as they are not obligated to contribute,

phrases.he: אִם שָׁקְלוּ מְקַבְּלִין מִיָּדָן.
phrases.en: however, if they contributed a shekel of their own accord, the Temple treasurers accept from them.

phrases.he: הַנָּכְרִי וְהַכּוּתִי שֶׁשָּׁקְלוּ, אֵין מְקַבְּלִין מִיָּדָן.
phrases.en: Conversely, in the case of a gentile or a Samaritan [Kuti] who contributed a shekel to participate in the communal offerings, they do not accept it from them.

phrases.he: וְאֵין מְקַבְּלִין מִיָּדָן קִנֵּי זָבִים וְקִנֵּי זָבוֹת וְקִנֵּי יוֹלְדוֹת, וְחַטָאוֹת וַאֲשָׁמוֹת.
phrases.en: And likewise, they do not accept from a gentile or a Samaritan pairs of birds sacrificed in the purification ritual of a zav, pairs of birds of a zava, or pairs of birds of a woman who gave birth, all of which are brought for ritual purification, or sin-offerings or guilt-offerings.

phrases.he: נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת, מְקַבְּלִין מִיָּדָן.
phrases.en: With regard to anything that can be brought to the altar as a vow or as a free-will offering, the priests accept it from gentiles and Samaritans,

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל שֶׁנִּדָּר וְנִדָּב, מְקַבְּלִין מִיָּדָן.
phrases.en: This is the principle: With regard to anything that can be brought to the altar as a vow or as a free-will offering, the priests accept it from them.

phrases.he: כָּל שֶׁאֵין נִדָּר וְנִדָּב אֵין מְקַבְּלִין מִיָּדָן.
phrases.en: with regard to anything that cannot be brought as a vow or as a free-will offering, they may not accept it from them.

phrases.he: וְכֵן הוּא מְפֹרָשׁ עַל יְדֵי עֶזְרָא, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (עזרא ד) לֹא לָכֶם וְלָנוּ לִבְנוֹת בַּיִת לֵאלֹהֵינוּ:
phrases.en: And this principle was similarly articulated by Ezra, when he recorded the Jewish leadership's rejection of the Samaritans' request to assist the Jews in the construction of the Second Temple, as it is stated: You have nothing to do with us to build a house unto our God;

phrases.he: וְאֵלּוּ שֶׁחַיָּבִין בַּקָּלְבּוֹן, לְוִיִּם וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִים וְגֵרִים וַעֲבָדִים מְשֻׁחְרָרִים, אֲבָל לֹא כֹּהֲנִים וְנָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים.
phrases.en: And these are the people who are obligated in the premium [kalbon], a small sum added to the half-shekel collected: Levites, Israelites, converts, and emancipated Canaanite slaves, but not priests, women, Canaanite slaves, or minors.

phrases.he: הַשּׁוֹקֵל עַל יְדֵי כֹּהֵן, עַל יְדֵי אִשָּׁה, עַל יְדֵי עֶבֶד, עַל יְדֵי קָטָן, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: One who contributes a half-shekel on behalf of a priest, on behalf of a woman, on behalf of a slave, or on behalf of a child, is exempt from the premium, as they are exempt.

phrases.he: וְאִם שָׁקַל עַל יָדוֹ וְעַל יַד חֲבֵרוֹ, חַיָּב בְּקָלְבּוֹן אֶחָד.
phrases.en: But if he contributed on his own behalf and on behalf of another, i.e., he contributed one whole shekel to discharge both his own obligation and that of someone else, he is obligated in one premium.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, שְׁנֵי קָלְבּוֹנוֹת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: He must pay two premiums.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹתֵן סֶלַע וְנוֹטֵל שֶׁקֶל, חַיָּב שְׁנֵי קָלְבּוֹנוֹת:
phrases.en: One who gives the collection agent a sela, i.e., a whole shekel, and takes a shekel, i.e., a half-shekel, as change is obligated in two premiums.

phrases.he: הַשּׁוֹקֵל עַל יְדֵי עָנִי, וְעַל יְדֵי שְׁכֵנוֹ, וְעַל יְדֵי בֶּן עִירוֹ, פָטוּר.
phrases.en: One who contributes on behalf of a poor person, on behalf of his neighbor, or on behalf of a resident of his city is exempt from the premium.

phrases.he: וְאִם הִלְוָם חַיָּב.
phrases.en: But if one loaned them a half-shekel, rather than paying it on their behalf, he is obligated to pay the premium.

phrases.he: הָאַחִין וְהַשֻּׁתָּפִין שֶׁחַיָּבִין בַּקָּלְבּוֹן, פְּטוּרִין מִמַּעֲשֵׂר בְּהֵמָה.
phrases.en: Partnered brothers, who have fully divided among themselves their late father's assets, and who, if they jointly pay a whole shekel from those assets to discharge both of their obligations, are obligated in the premium like any other two private individuals, are exempt from the animal tithe.

phrases.he: וּכְשֶׁחַיָּבִין בְּמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה, פְּטוּרִין מִן הַקָּלְבּוֹן.
phrases.en: But when they have not completely divided the assets, and they are therefore obligated in the animal tithe, as the livestock is considered in their father's possession, they are exempt from the premium for their joint payment, as in the case of one who pays on behalf of another.

phrases.he: וְכַמָּה הוּא קָלְבּוֹן, מָעָה כֶּסֶף, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: And how much is a premium? A silver ma'a. This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, חֵצִי:
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: It is only half a ma'a.

phrases.he: מְצָרְפִין שְׁקָלִים לְדַרְכּוֹנוֹת מִפְּנֵי מַשּׂוֹי הַדֶּרֶךְ.
phrases.en: they may combine their shekels and exchange them for darics [darkonot], which are large gold coins, due to the burden of the way.

phrases.he: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהָיוּ שׁוֹפָרוֹת בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ, כָּךְ הָיוּ שׁוֹפָרוֹת בַּמְּדִינָה.
phrases.en: Just as there were collection horns in the Temple to receive the half-shekel contributions, so too there were collection horns in the rest of the country, i.e., areas outside of Jerusalem.

phrases.he: בְּנֵי הָעִיר שֶׁשָּׁלְחוּ אֶת שִׁקְלֵיהֶן וְנִגְנְבוּ אוֹ שֶׁאָבָדוּ, אִם נִתְרְמָה הַתְּרוּמָה, נִשְׁבָּעִין לַגִּזְבָּרִים.
phrases.en: the residents of a town who sent their shekels to the Temple and they were stolen from the agent on the way or were lost, if the collection of the chamber had already been collected before these shekels arrived, the agents must take the oath of a bailee to the treasurers [gizbarin].

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו נִשְׁבָּעִין לִבְנֵי הָעִיר, וּבְנֵי הָעִיר שׁוֹקְלִין תַּחְתֵּיהֶן.
phrases.en: If the ceremony has not yet been performed and the contributions have not yet been collected into the baskets, the shekels are considered the property of the residents of the town, and therefore the agents must take an oath to absolve themselves to the residents of the town. Since those shekels are still considered the property of the residents of the town because the shekels never reached the Temple, they have not fulfilled their obligation. Therefore, the residents of the town must contribute other shekels in their place.

phrases.he: נִמְצָאוּ, אוֹ שֶׁהֶחֱזִירוּם הַגַּנָּבִים, אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ שְׁקָלִים, וְאֵין עוֹלִין לָהֶן לְשָׁנָה הַבָּאָה:
phrases.en: If, after the residents of the town contributed other shekels, the original shekels were found or the thieves returned them, both these original shekels and those newly contributed ones have the status of consecrated shekels and belong to the Temple. However, they do not count for the following year.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹתֵן שִׁקְלוֹ לַחֲבֵרוֹ לִשְׁקֹל עַל יָדוֹ, וּשְׁקָלוֹ עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ, אִם נִתְרְמָה תְּרוּמָה מָעַל.
phrases.en: one who gives his shekel to his fellow to contribute on his behalf and the fellow instead contributed it for himself, if at the time that he placed the shekel in the collection horn the collection of the chamber had been collected, the fellow is guilty of misuse of consecrated property.

phrases.he: הַשּׁוֹקֵל שִׁקְלוֹ מִמְּעוֹת הֶקְדֵּשׁ, אִם נִתְרְמָה תְרוּמָה וְקָרְבָה הַבְּהֵמָה מָעַל.
phrases.en: one who contributes his shekel from consecrated money, and the collection of the chamber was collected and an animal purchased with those funds was sacrificed, he is guilty of misuse of consecrated property.

phrases.he: מִדְּמֵי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, מִדְּמֵי שְׁבִיעִית, יֹאכַל כְּנֶגְדָּן:
phrases.en: from money used to redeem the fruits of the second tithe or from money from the permitted sale of produce grown during the Sabbatical Year, he must eat corresponding to the value of the shekel.

phrases.he: הַמְכַנֵּס מָעוֹת וְאָמַר, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ לְשִׁקְלִי,
phrases.en: one who gathers together small coins and said: These are for my shekel,

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מוֹתָרָן נְדָבָה.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: The leftover coins are placed in the collection horn designated for a free-will offering,

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מוֹתָרָן חֻלִּין.
phrases.en: Beit Hillel say: The leftover money is non-sacred property

phrases.he: שֶׁאָבִיא מֵהֶן לְשִׁקְלִי, שָׁוִין שֶׁמּוֹתָרָן חֻלִּין.
phrases.en: that I will bring my shekel from these, they agree that the leftover money is non-sacred property.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ לְחַטָאת, שָׁוִין שֶׁהַמּוֹתָר נְדָבָה.
phrases.en: These are for my sin-offering, then if he had accumulated more than was needed, they agree that the leftover money must be designated as a free-will offering.

phrases.he: שֶׁאָבִיא מֵהֶן לְחַטָאת, שָׁוִין שֶׁהַמּוֹתָר חֻלִּין:
phrases.en: That I will bring my sin-offering from these, they agree that the leftover money is non-sacred property.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, מַה בֵּין שְׁקָלִים לְחַטָאת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon said: What is the difference between shekels and a sin-offering?

phrases.he: שְׁקָלִים יֵשׁ לָהֶם קִצְבָה, וְחַטָאת אֵין לָהּ קִצְבָה.
phrases.en: Shekels have a fixed value, a half-shekel and no more. However, a sin-offering has no fixed value.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף לִשְׁקָלִים אֵין לָהֶן קִצְבָה, שֶׁכְּשֶׁעָלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִן הַגּוֹלָה הָיוּ שׁוֹקְלִים דַּרְכּוֹנוֹת, חָזְרוּ לִשְׁקוֹל סְלָעִים, חָזְרוּ לִשְׁקוֹל טְבָעִין, וּבִקְּשׁוּ לִשְׁקֹל דִּינָרִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: Even for shekels there is no fixed value. For when the Jewish people ascended from the exile, they would contribute darics, they reverted to contributing a sela, they reverted to contributing a tiva, and wished to contribute dinars.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן, יַד כֻּלָּן שָׁוָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon said: Even so, everyone has equal standing.

phrases.he: אֲבָל חַטָאת, זֶה מֵבִיא בְּסֶלַע וְזֶה מֵבִיא בִּשְׁתַּיִם וְזֶה מֵבִיא בְּשָׁלשׁ:
phrases.en: However, a sin-offering this person may bring an animal worth a sela, and that one may bring one worth two, and this one may bring one worth three.

phrases.he: מוֹתַר שְׁקָלִים, חֻלִּין.
phrases.en: The leftover money from what was set aside for shekels is non-sacred property.

phrases.he: מוֹתַר עֲשִׂירִית הָאֵפָה, מוֹתַר קִנֵּי זָבִין, קִנֵּי זָבוֹת, קִנֵּי יוֹלְדוֹת, וְחַטָאוֹת וַאֲשָׁמוֹת, מוֹתְרֵיהֶן נְדָבָה.
phrases.en: The leftover money from what one set aside to purchase the tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a meal-offering and the leftover money from what one set aside to purchase offerings that he is liable to sacrifice due to ritual impurity or a sin, such as the pairs of birds of a zav, the pairs of birds of a zava, and the pairs of birds of a woman after childbirth, sin-offerings, or guilt-offerings, in these cases, its leftover money must be used for free-will offerings that are offered as repletion of the altar, i.e., burnt-offerings sacrificed at times when the altar was idle.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל שֶׁהוּא בָּא לְשֵׁם חַטָאת וּלְשֵׁם אַשְׁמָה, מוֹתָרָן נְדָבָה.
phrases.en: This is the principle: Whatever money is designated for a sin-offering or for a guilt-offering, its leftover money must be used for a free-will offering.

phrases.he: מוֹתַר עוֹלָה, לָעוֹלָה.
phrases.en: The leftover money from what one set aside to purchase a burnt-offering that he owes, due to a vow or to volunteering, must be used for another burnt-offering that he will bring in the future.

phrases.he: מוֹתַר מִנְחָה, לַמִּנְחָה.
phrases.en: The leftover money from what one set aside to purchase fine flour for a meal-offering must be used for another meal-offering.

phrases.he: מוֹתַר שְׁלָמִים, לַשְּׁלָמִים.
phrases.en: The leftover money from what one set aside to purchase a peace-offering must be used for another peace-offering.

phrases.he: מוֹתַר פֶּסַח, לַשְּׁלָמִים.
phrases.en: The leftover money from what one set aside to purchase a lamb for his Paschal lamb is not used for another Paschal lamb, such as for the following year. Rather, it is used for purchasing a peace-offering.

phrases.he: מוֹתַר נְזִירִים, לַנְּזִירִים.
phrases.en: The leftover money from what one set aside to purchase sacrifices for a number of nazirites must be used to purchase sacrifices for other nazirites.

phrases.he: מוֹתַר נָזִיר, לַנְּדָבָה.
phrases.en: The leftover money from what a single nazirite set aside for his own offering must be used for a free-will offering.

phrases.he: מוֹתַר עֲנִיִּים, לָעֲנִיִּים.
phrases.en: The leftover money collected for freeing unspecified captives must be allocated to freeing captives.

phrases.he: מוֹתַר עָנִי, לְאוֹתוֹ עָנִי.
phrases.en: The leftover money collected for a specific poor person is given as a gift to that poor person.

phrases.he: מוֹתַר שְׁבוּיִים, לַשְּׁבוּיִים.
phrases.en: The leftover money collected for freeing captives must be allocated to freeing captives.

phrases.he: מוֹתַר שָׁבוּי, לְאוֹתוֹ שָׁבוּי.
phrases.en: The leftover money collected for freeing a specific captive is given as a gift to that captive.

phrases.he: מוֹתַר הַמֵּתִים, לַמֵּתִים.
phrases.en: The leftover money collected as charity for the poor must be allocated to the poor.

phrases.he: מוֹתַר הַמֵּת, לְיוֹרְשָׁיו.
phrases.en: The leftover money collected to bury or provide burial shrouds for a particular deceased person is given to his heirs.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, מוֹתַר הַמֵּת, יְהֵא מֻנָּח עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: It is uncertain what should be done, and therefore the leftover money for the deceased should be placed in a safe place until Elijah comes and teaches what should be done.

phrases.he: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר, מוֹתַר הַמֵּת בּוֹנִין לוֹ נֶפֶשׁ עַל קִבְרוֹ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Natan says: With the leftover money collected for a deceased person they build a monument [nefesh] on his grave for him.

phrases.he: בִּשְׁלשָׁה פְּרָקִים בַּשָּׁנָה, תּוֹרְמִין אֶת הַלִּשְׁכָּה, בִּפְרוֹס הַפֶּסַח, בִּפְרוֹס עֲצֶרֶת, בִּפְרוֹס הֶחָג,
phrases.en: On three occasions during the year the ceremony of the collection of the Temple treasury chamber is performed. Half a month before Passover, half a month before Shavuot, half a month before the festival

phrases.he: וְהֵן גְּרָנוֹת לְמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.en: These are the due dates for animal tithes. This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

phrases.he: בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר, בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בַּאֲדָר, וּבְאֶחָד בְּסִיוָן, וּבְעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב.
phrases.en: Ben Azzai says the twenty-ninth of Adar, the first of Sivan, and the twenty-ninth of Av.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים, בְּאֶחָד בְּנִיסָן, בְּאֶחָד בְּסִיוָן, בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בֶּאֱלוּל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say the first of Nisan, the first of Sivan, and the twenty-ninth of Elul.

phrases.he: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בֶּאֱלוּל, וְלֹא אָמְרוּ בְּאֶחָד בְּתִשְׁרֵי,
phrases.en: And why did they say the twenty-ninth of Elul and not the first of Tishrei,

phrases.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא יוֹם טוֹב, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְעַשֵּׂר בְּיוֹם טוֹב, לְפִיכָךְ הִקְדִּימוּהוּ לְעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בֶּאֱלוּל:
phrases.en: Because it is the festival and it is not permitted to tithe on a Festival. Therefore, they advanced it to the twenty-ninth of Elul.

phrases.he: בְּשָׁלשׁ קֻפּוֹת שֶׁל שָׁלשׁ שָׁלשׁ סְאִין תּוֹרְמִין אֶת הַלִּשְׁכָּה,
phrases.en: are collected from the Temple treasury chamber with three baskets, each measuring three se'a.

phrases.he: וְכָתוּב בָּהֶן אָל״ף בֵי״ת גִימ״ל.
phrases.en: On the baskets is written, respectively, alef, beit, gimmel,

phrases.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, יְוָנִית כָּתוּב בָּהֶן אָלפ״א בֵית״א גָמל״א.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yishmael says: The letters written on them were in Greek, alfa, beta, gamma.

phrases.he: אֵין הַתּוֹרֵם נִכְנָס לֹא בְּפַרְגּוֹד חָפוּת, וְלֹא בְּמִנְעָל, וְלֹא בְּסַנְדָּל, וְלֹא בִּתְפִלִּין, וְלֹא בְּקָמִיעַ,
phrases.en: The one who collects the funds from the chamber must not enter while wearing a cuffed garment [ḥafut], and not with a shoe, and not with a sandal, and not with phylacteries, and not with an amulet,

phrases.he: שֶׁמָּא יַעֲנִי, וְיֹאמְרוּ מֵעֲוֹן הַלִּשְׁכָּה הֶעֱנִי,
phrases.en: perhaps the one collecting the funds will one day become poor, and people will say that it is because of the sin of stealing the shekels of the chamber that he became poor,

phrases.he: אוֹ שֶׁמָּא יַעֲשִׁיר, וְיֹאמְרוּ מִתְּרוּמַת הַלִּשְׁכָּה הֶעֱשִׁיר.
phrases.en: Or perhaps he will become rich and people will say that he became rich from stealing the funds of the chamber,

phrases.he: לְפִי שֶׁאָדָם צָרִיךְ לָצֵאת יְדֵי הַבְּרִיּוֹת כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לָצֵאת יְדֵי הַמָּקוֹם,
phrases.en: as a person must appear justified before people just as he must appear justified before the Omnipresent [HaMakom],

phrases.he: שְׁנֶּאֱמַר (במדבר לב) וִהְיִיתֶם נְקִיִים מֵיְיָ וּמִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.en: and it is stated: "And you shall be guiltless before the Lord and before Israel"

phrases.he: וְאוֹמֵר (משלי ג) וּמְצָא חֵן וְשֵׂכֶל טוֹב בְּעֵינֵי אֱלֹהִים וְאָדָם:
phrases.en: And the verse states: "So shall you find grace and good understanding in the sight of God and man"

phrases.he: שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.en: of the house of Rabban Gamliel

phrases.he: (הָיָה) נִכְנָס וְשִׁקְלוֹ בֵּין אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו, וְזוֹרְקוֹ לִפְנֵי הַתּוֹרֵם,
phrases.en: would enter the chamber with his shekel between his fingers, and toss it in front of the one collecting

phrases.he: וְהַתּוֹרֵם מִתְכַּוֵּן וְדוֹחֲקוֹ לַקֻּפָּה.
phrases.en: the one collecting the money from the chamber would purposely push this shekel into the basket,

phrases.he: אֵין הַתּוֹרֵם תּוֹרֵם עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר לָהֶם, אֶתְרֹם.
phrases.en: The one collecting the funds from the chamber may not begin to collect the money until he asks Shall I collect the funds,

phrases.he: וְהֵן אוֹמְרִים לוֹ, תְּרֹם, תְּרֹם, תְּרֹם, שָׁלשׁ פְּעָמִים:
phrases.en: and they say to him: Collect them, collect them, collect them, three times.

phrases.he: תָּרַם אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה וּמְחַפֶּה בִּקְטַבְלָאוֹת,
phrases.en: he collected the funds from the first large basket and put them into one of the smaller baskets labeled with the letter alef, he immediately covered with a leather cover the large basket from which he had removed the money.

phrases.he: שְׁנִיָּה וּמְחַפֶּה בִּקְטַבְלָאוֹת.
phrases.en: from the second large basket, he covered it with a leather cover as well.

phrases.he: שְׁלִישִׁית לֹא הָיָה מְחַפֶּה, שֶׁמָּא יִשְׁכַּח וְיִתְרֹם מִן הַדָּבָר הַתָּרוּם.
phrases.en: the third large basket, he did not cover it. Why did he cover the first two baskets? In order to mark them as already having had funds collected from them. In this way, there was no concern that perhaps he would forget and once again collect funds from a basket from which funds had already been collected.

phrases.he: תָּרַם אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה לְשֵׁם אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, וּשְׁנִיָּה לְשׁוּם כְּרַכִין הַמֻּקָּפִין לָהּ, וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁית לְשׁוּם בָּבֶל וּלְשׁוּם מָדַי וּלְשׁוּם מְדִינוֹת הָרְחוֹקוֹת:
phrases.en: He collected funds from the first basket on behalf of the people living in Eretz Yisrael; from the second basket on behalf of the people living in the cities near Eretz Yisrael; and from the third basket on behalf of the people living in Babylonia, and on behalf of the people living in Media, and on behalf of the people living in the distant countries.

phrases.he: הַתְּרוּמָה מֶה הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין בָּהּ,
phrases.en: The collection of half-shekels, what would they do with it?

phrases.he: לוֹקְחִין בָּהּ תְּמִידִין וּמוּסָפִין וְנִסְכֵּיהֶם,
phrases.en: They would purchase animals for the daily offerings, and for the additional offerings, and wine for their libations;

phrases.he: הָעֹמֶר וּשְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם וְלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים,
phrases.en: barley for the omer meal-offering; and wheat for both the two loaves offered on Shavuot and the shewbread;

phrases.he: וְכָל קָרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּבּוּר.
phrases.en: and animals for all the communal offerings.

phrases.he: שׁוֹמְרֵי סְפִיחִים בַּשְּׁבִיעִית, נוֹטְלִין שְׂכָרָן מִתְּרוּמַת הַלִּשְׁכָּה.
phrases.en: The guards of the sefiḥin, grain that grew without being purposely planted, during the Sabbatical Year, collect their wages from the collection of the Temple treasury chamber.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַף הָרוֹצֶה מִתְנַדֵּב שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: One who so desires may even volunteer his services and guard the grain as an unpaid bailee.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, אַף אַתָּה אוֹמֵר, שֶׁאֵינָן בָּאִין אֶלָּא מִשֶּׁל צִבּוּר:
phrases.en: The Rabbis said to him: Even you must say that the omer and the two loaves come only from communal funds and not from any one individual.

phrases.he: פָּרָה וְשָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ וְלָשׁוֹן שֶׁל זְהוֹרִית, בָּאִין מִתְּרוּמַת הַלִשְׁכָּה.
phrases.en: The red heifer, the scapegoat, and the strip of crimson wool used in the process of burning the red heifer all come from the collection of the Temple treasury chamber,

phrases.he: כֶּבֶשׁ פָּרָה, וְכֶבֶשׁ שָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ וְלָשׁוֹן שֶׁבֵּין קַרְנָיו, וְאַמַּת הַמַּיִם, וְחוֹמַת הָעִיר וּמִגְדְּלוֹתֶיהָ, וְכָל צָרְכֵי הָעִיר, בָּאִין מִשְּׁיָרֵי הַלִּשְׁכָּה.
phrases.en: the ramp built from the Temple Mount to the location on the Mount of Olives, where they would slaughter the red heifer; the ramp built to lead the scapegoat out of the city; the strip of crimson wool that was tied between its horns; any repairs required for the aqueduct that ran through the Temple courtyard and the walls of the city and its towers; and for all the needs of the city, come from the remains of the chamber,

phrases.he: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר, כֶּבֶשׁ פָּרָה כֹּהֲנִים גְּדוֹלִים עוֹשִׂין אוֹתוֹ מִשֶּׁל עַצְמָן:
phrases.en: Abba Shaul says: The High Priests construct the ramp for the red heifer from their own funds.

phrases.he: מוֹתַר שְׁיָרֵי הַלִּשְׁכָּה מֶה הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין בָּהֶן,
phrases.en: What would they do with the leftover remains of the chamber

phrases.he: לוֹקְחִין בָּהֶן יֵינוֹת, שְׁמָנִים וּסְלָתוֹת,
phrases.en: They would purchase wine, oil, and fine flour

phrases.he: וְהַשָּׂכָר לַהֶקְדֵּשׁ,
phrases.en: And the profit to consecrated property

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל.
phrases.en: this is the statement of Rabbi Yishmael

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.he: אֵין מִשְׂתַּכְּרִין מִשֶּׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ
phrases.en: One may not generate profit by selling consecrated property

phrases.he: וְלֹא מִשֶּׁל עֲנִיִּים:
phrases.en: neither may one profit from funds set aside for the poor

phrases.he: מוֹתַר תְּרוּמָה מֶה הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין בָּהּ, רִקּוּעֵי זָהָב צִפּוּי לְבֵית קָדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים.
phrases.en: What would they do with the leftover funds of the collection that had not been spent on communal offerings? They would purchase golden plates as a coating for the walls and floor of the Holy of Holies.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, מוֹתַר הַפֵּרוֹת לְקַיִץ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, וּמוֹתַר הַתְּרוּמָה לִכְלֵי שָׁרֵת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yishmael says: The leftover produce was used to purchase the repletion of the altar, i.e., burnt-offerings sacrificed at times when the altar was idle. The leftover funds of the collection were used to purchase sacred vessels.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, מוֹתַר הַתְּרוּמָה לְקַיִץ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, וּמוֹתַר נְסָכִים לִכְלֵי שָׁרֵת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: The leftover funds of the collection were used to purchase the animals used for the repletion of the altar, since they had originally been collected for offerings. The leftover libations were used to purchase sacred vessels.

phrases.he: רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים אוֹמֵר, מוֹתַר נְסָכִים לְקַיִץ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, וּמוֹתַר הַתְּרוּמָה לִכְלֵי שָׁרֵת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Ḥananya, the deputy High Priest, says: The leftover libations were used to purchase animals for the repletion of the altar, while the leftover funds of the collection were used to purchase sacred vessels.

phrases.he: זֶה וָזֶה לֹא הָיוּ מוֹדִים בַּפֵּרוֹת:
phrases.en: Both this Sage, Rabbi Akiva, and that Sage, Rabbi Ḥananya, did not agree with Rabbi Yishmael's opinion with regard to the leftover produce.

phrases.he: מוֹתַר הַקְּטֹרֶת
phrases.en: The leftover incense

phrases.he: מֶה הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין בָּהּ,
phrases.en: What would be done with it

phrases.he: מַפְרִישִׁין (מִמֶּנָּה) שְׂכַר הָאֻמָּנִין,
phrases.en: would set aside an amount of it equal to the value of the wages of the artisans

phrases.he: וּמְחַלְּלִין אוֹתָהּ עַל שְׂכַר הָאֻמָּנִין,
phrases.en: They would then desacralize that incense by transferring its sanctity to the money owed to the artisans.

phrases.he: וְנוֹתְנִין אוֹתָהּ לָאֻמָּנִין בִּשְׂכָרָן,
phrases.en: They would then give the incense to the artisans as their wages.

phrases.he: וְחוֹזְרִין וְלוֹקְחִין אוֹתָהּ מִתְּרוּמָה חֲדָשָׁה.
phrases.en: they would return and buy back the incense from the artisans with funds from the new collection of shekels.

phrases.he: אִם בָּא הֶחָדָשׁ בִּזְמַנּוֹ, לוֹקְחִין אוֹתָהּ מִתְּרוּמָה חֲדָשָׁה.
phrases.en: If the new funds come on time, they purchase the incense with funds from the new collection of shekels.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו מִן הַיְּשָׁנָה:
phrases.en: And if not, they may still purchase it from the old collection

phrases.he: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ נְכָסָיו
phrases.en: One who consecrates all his possessions

phrases.he: וְהָיוּ בָּהֶן דְּבָרִים רְאוּיִין לְקָרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּבּוּר,
phrases.en: and if among them there are items that are suitable for use as communal offerings,

phrases.he: יִנָּתְנוּ לָאֻמָּנִין בִּשְׂכָרָן,
phrases.en: They are given to Temple artisans as their wages,

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.en: this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ בֶּן עֲזַאי, אֵינָהּ הִיא הַמִּדָּה,
phrases.en: Ben Azzai said to him: This is not the method to be used.

phrases.he: אֶלָּא מַפְרִישִׁין מֵהֶן שְׂכַר הָאֻמָּנִין,
phrases.en: Rather, they set aside from the consecrated items the equivalent of the value owed to the artisans for their wages,

phrases.he: וּמְחַלְּלִין אוֹתָן עַל מָעוֹת הָאֻמָּנִין,
phrases.en: and they desacralize them by transferring their sanctity onto the money allocated for the artisans' wages,

phrases.he: וְנוֹתְנִין אוֹתָן לָאֻמָּנִין בִּשְׂכָרָן,
phrases.en: and they give those items, which are no longer consecrated, to the artisans as their wages.

phrases.he: וְחוֹזְרִין וְלוֹקְחִין אוֹתָן מִתְּרוּמָה חֲדָשָׁה:
phrases.en: should repurchase those items using money from that year's new collection of half-shekels,

phrases.he: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ נְכָסָיו וְהָיְתָה בָּהֶן בְּהֵמָה רְאוּיָה לְגַבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, זְכָרִים וּנְקֵבוֹת,
phrases.en: one who consecrates all his possessions without specifying for what purpose, and among them there is an animal that is suitable to be sacrificed on the altar, male or female,

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, זְכָרִים יִמָּכְרוּ לְצָרְכֵי עוֹלוֹת, וּנְקֵבוֹת יִמָּכְרוּ לְצָרְכֵי זִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים, וּדְמֵיהֶן יִפְּלוּ עִם שְׁאָר נְכָסִים לְבֶדֶק הַבָּיִת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: males should be sold for the needs of burnt-offerings, and females, since they cannot be brought as burnt-offerings, should be sold for the needs of peace-offerings, i.e., to individuals who will sacrifice them as such. And their monetary value that is received from their sale is allocated with the rest of his property for Temple maintenance.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, זְכָרִים עַצְמָן יִקָּרְבוּ עוֹלוֹת, וּנְקֵבוֹת יִמָּכְרוּ לְצָרְכֵי זִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים, וְיָבִיא בִּדְמֵיהֶן עוֹלוֹת, וּשְׁאָר נְכָסִים יִפְּלוּ לְבֶדֶק הַבָּיִת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says: males should themselves be sacrificed as burnt-offerings, and females, since they cannot be brought as burnt-offerings, should be sold for the needs of peace-offerings, i.e., to individuals who will sacrifice them as such, and their monetary value that is received from their sale should be used to purchase and bring burnt-offerings. According to both opinions, the rest of the possessions, which are not suitable for sacrificial use, are allocated for Temple maintenance.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, רוֹאֶה אֲנִי אֶת דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מִדִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, שֶׁרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִשְׁוָה אֶת מִדָּתוֹ, וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ חָלַק.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva said: I see the statement of Rabbi Eliezer as more correct than the statement of Rabbi Yehoshua, since Rabbi Eliezer applied his method equally to both animals and other possessions in treating both as consecrated for Temple maintenance, whereas Rabbi Yehoshua made a distinction between them.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי פַּפְּיַס, שָׁמַעְתִּי כְּדִבְרֵי שְׁנֵיהֶן, שֶׁהַמַּקְדִּישׁ בְּפֵרוּשׁ, כְּדִבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Papeyyas said: I heard the statements of both of them applied to different situations: One who consecrates all his possessions and explicitly states that his animals are to be included, clearly intends to equate his animals with the rest of his possessions, that both should be consecrated for the same purpose, i.e., for Temple maintenance. Therefore, he should act in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.he: וְהַמַּקְדִּישׁ סְתָם, כְּדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.en: However, with regard to one who consecrates all his possessions without explicitly specifying that this includes his animals, since there is no reason to presume that he wishes them all to be consecrated for the same purpose, it is presumed that each item is consecrated for the purpose most suited to it. Therefore, he should act in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Yehoshua.

phrases.he: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ נְכָסִים וְהָיוּ בָּהֶן דְּבָרִים רְאוּיִים עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, יֵינוֹת, שְׁמָנִים וְעוֹפוֹת,
phrases.en: one who consecrates all his possessions, and among them there were items that are suitable to be sacrificed on the altar, such as wines for libations, and oils for meal-offerings, and birds

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר, יִמָּכְרוּ לְצָרְכֵי אוֹתוֹ הַמִּין וְיָבִיא בִּדְמֵיהֶן עוֹלוֹת,
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: They are sold for the needs of that kind of item, i.e., to individuals who will use them as such. And he should bring with their monetary value that is received from their sale burnt-offerings.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר נְכָסִים יִפְּלוּ לְבֶדֶק הַבָּיִת.
phrases.en: And the rest of the possessions are allocated for Temple maintenance.

phrases.he: אַחַת לִשְׁלשִׁים יוֹם, מְשַׁעֲרִין אֶת הַלִּשְׁכָּה.
phrases.en: Once every thirty days, the prices are set for the Temple chamber.

phrases.he: כָּל הַמְקַבֵּל עָלָיו לְסַפֵּק סְלָתוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע, עָמְדוּ מִשָּׁלשׁ, יְסַפֵּק מֵאַרְבַּע.
phrases.en: Any merchant who undertakes to provide fine flour after the chamber set a price of four se'a per sela, even if the general market price rose and stood at three se'a per sela, he must provide fine flour based on the set price of four se'a per sela.

phrases.he: מִשָּׁלשׁ וְעָמְדוּ מֵאַרְבַּע, יְסַפֵּק מֵאַרְבַּע, שֶׁיַּד הֶקְדֵּשׁ עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנָה.
phrases.en: However, if the chamber's set price was three se'a per sela, and the general market price fell to four se'a per sela, he must now provide fine flour based on the new market price of four se'a per sela. This is in order that the Temple treasury of consecrated property always has the upper hand.

phrases.he: וְאִם הִתְלִיעָה סֹלֶת, הִתְלִיעָה לוֹ.
phrases.en: If the fine flour became wormy, it became wormy for the merchant.

phrases.he: וְאִם הֶחְמִיץ יַיִן, הֶחְמִיץ לוֹ.
phrases.en: If the wine turned to vinegar, it turned to vinegar for the merchant.

phrases.he: וְאֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל אֶת מְעוֹתָיו, עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הַמִּזְבֵּחַ מְרַצֶּה:
phrases.en: He only receives his money once the altar is satisfied.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ הֵן הַמְמֻנִּין שֶׁהָיוּ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.en: These are the officials who served in the Temple:

phrases.he: יוֹחָנָן בֶּן פִּנְחָס עַל הַחוֹתָמוֹת,
phrases.en: Yoḥanan ben Pineḥas was responsible for the seals.

phrases.he: אֲחִיָּה עַל הַנְּסָכִים,
phrases.en: Aḥiyya was responsible for the libations,

phrases.he: מַתִּתְיָה בֶּן שְׁמוּאֵל עַל הַפְּיָסוֹת,
phrases.en: Matya ben Shmuel was responsible for the lotteries,

phrases.he: פְּתַחְיָה עַל הַקִּנִּין.
phrases.en: Petaḥya was responsible for the pairs of birds,

phrases.he: פְּתַחְיָה, זֶה מָרְדְּכָי.
phrases.en: Petaḥya is Mordecai

phrases.he: לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ פְּתַחְיָה.
phrases.en: And why was he called Petaḥya,

phrases.he: שֶׁהָיָה פּוֹתֵחַ בִּדְבָרִים וְדוֹרְשָׁן, וְיוֹדֵעַ שִׁבְעִים לָשׁוֹן.
phrases.en: that he would open difficult topics and interpret them and he knew all seventy languages

phrases.he: בֶּן אֲחִיָּה עַל חוֹלֵי מֵעַיִם,
phrases.en: Ben Aḥiyya was responsible for the care of the priests who suffered from intestinal disease.

phrases.he: נְחוּנְיָא חוֹפֵר שִׁיחִין,
phrases.en: Neḥunya was the well digger

phrases.he: גְּבִינֵי כָרוֹז,
phrases.en: Gevini was the Temple crier

phrases.he: בֶּן גֶּבֶר עַל נְעִילַת שְׁעָרִים,
phrases.en: Ben Gever was responsible for locking the Temple gates

phrases.he: בֶּן בֵּבָי עַל הַפָּקִיעַ,
phrases.en: Ben Bevai was appointed over the shreds

phrases.he: בֶּן אַרְזָה עַל הַצִּלְצָל,
phrases.en: Ben Arza was responsible for the cymbal,

phrases.he: הֻגְרַס בֶּן לֵוִי עַל הַשִּׁיר,
phrases.en: Hugras ben Levi was responsible for the song.

phrases.he: בֵּית גַּרְמוּ עַל מַעֲשֵׂה לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים,
phrases.en: The house of Garmu was responsible for the preparation of the shewbread;

phrases.he: בֵּית אַבְטִינָס עַל מַעֲשֵׂה הַקְּטֹרֶת,
phrases.en: the house of Avtinas was responsible for the preparation of the incense;

phrases.he: אֶלְעָזָר עַל הַפָּרוֹכוֹת,
phrases.en: Elazar was responsible for weaving the Temple curtains;

phrases.he: וּפִנְחָס עַל הַמַּלְבּוּשׁ:
phrases.en: and Pineḥas was the valet,

phrases.he: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִשְּׁלֹשָה גִּזְבָּרִין וּמִשִּׁבְעָה אֲמַרְכָּלִין,
phrases.en: There must be no fewer than seven trustees [amarkolin] and three treasurers

phrases.he: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין שְׂרָרָה עַל הַצִּבּוּר בְּמָמוֹן פָּחוּת מִשְּׁנַיִם,
phrases.en: And we do not appoint an authority over the public comprised of fewer than two people,

phrases.he: חוּץ מִבֶּן אֲחִיָּה שֶׁעַל חוֹלֵי מֵעַיִם וְאֶלְעָזָר שֶׁעַל הַפָּרוֹכוֹת,
phrases.en: except for ben Aḥiyya, who was responsible for healing priests who suffered from intestinal disease, and Elazar, who was responsible for the weaving of the Temple curtains.

phrases.he: שֶׁאוֹתָן קִבְּלוּ רוֹב הַצִּבּוּר עֲלֵיהֶן:
phrases.en: that the majority of the public accepted these men upon themselves

phrases.he: אַרְבָּעָה חוֹתָמוֹת הָיוּ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.en: There were four seals in the Temple

phrases.he: וְכָתוּב עֲלֵיהֶן, עֵגֶל, זָכָר, גְּדִי, חוֹטֵא.
phrases.en: And one of the following inscriptions was written on them: Calf; male, i.e., a ram; kid; and sinner, i.e., a leper, as leprosy is a punishment for one of seven sins

phrases.he: בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר, חֲמִשָּׁה הָיוּ,
phrases.en: ben Azzai says: There were five seals,

phrases.he: וַאֲרָמִית כָּתוּב עֲלֵיהֶן, עֵגֶל, זָכָר, גְּדִי, חוֹטֵא דַּל, וְחוֹטֵא עָשִׁיר.
phrases.en: and the following was written upon them in Aramaic, not Hebrew: Calf, male, kid, poor sinner, and rich sinner.

phrases.he: עֵגֶל מְשַׁמֵּשׁ עִם נִסְכֵּי בָּקָר גְּדוֹלִים וּקְטַנִּים, זְכָרִים וּנְקֵבוֹת.
phrases.en: The calf seal serves as a payment receipt for libations of cattle offerings, whether they are large or small, male or female, as all offerings from the cow family are accompanied by the same libation.

phrases.he: גְּדִי מְשַׁמֵּשׁ עִם נִסְכֵּי צֹאן גְּדוֹלִים וּקְטַנִּים, זְכָרִים וּנְקֵבוֹת, חוּץ מִשֶּׁל אֵילִים.
phrases.en: The kid seal serves for libations of sheep or goat offerings, whether large or small, male or female, except for those of rams aged thirteen months and older.

phrases.he: זָכָר מְשַׁמֵּשׁ עִם נִסְכֵּי אֵילִים בִּלְבָד.
phrases.en: The ram seal, which was earlier called the male seal, serves exclusively for ram libations.

phrases.he: חוֹטֵא מְשַׁמֵּשׁ עִם נִסְכֵּי שָׁלשׁ בְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁל מְצוֹרָעִין:
phrases.en: The sinner seal serves for libations of the three animal offerings of a leper, for the completion of his purification.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁהוּא מְבַקֵּשׁ נְסָכִים הוֹלֵךְ לוֹ אֵצֶל יוֹחָנָן שֶׁהוּא מְמֻנֶּה עַל הַחוֹתָמוֹת.
phrases.en: One who seeks libations for his offering goes to Yoḥanan, the official who was responsible for the seals.

phrases.he: נוֹתֵן לוֹ מָעוֹת וּמְקַבֵּל מִמֶּנּוּ חוֹתָם.
phrases.en: and gives him the appropriate sum of money and receives a seal from him.

phrases.he: בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל אֲחִיָּה שֶׁהוּא מְמֻנֶּה עַל הַנְּסָכִים.
phrases.en: he subsequently comes to Aḥiyya, who was responsible for the libations.

phrases.he: וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ חוֹתָם וּמְקַבֵּל מִמֶּנּוּ נְסָכִים.
phrases.en: and gives him Yoḥanan's seal and receives his libations from him.

phrases.he: וְלָעֶרֶב בָּאִין זֶה אֵצֶל זֶה.
phrases.en: In the evening, Yoḥanan and Aḥiyya would get together

phrases.he: וַאֲחִיָּה מוֹצִיא אֶת הַחוֹתָמוֹת וּמְקַבֵּל כְּנֶגְדָּן מָעוֹת.
phrases.en: and Aḥiyya would take out the seals he had received and accept the money Yoḥanan had received in exchange for them.

phrases.he: וְאִם הוֹתִירוּ הוֹתִירוּ לַהֶקְדֵּשׁ.
phrases.en: And if there was some money left over, i.e., the total money was greater than the value of the seals, they were left over to the benefit of the Temple treasury of consecrated property.

phrases.he: וְאִם פָּחָתוּ, הָיָה מְשַׁלֵּם יוֹחָנָן מִבֵּיתוֹ, שֶׁיַּד הֶקְדֵּשׁ עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנָה:
phrases.en: If the money was less than the value of the seals, they were less to him, i.e., Yoḥanan would bear the loss, and Yoḥanan would have to pay the difference to the Temple treasury from his own property, as the Temple treasury always has the upper hand.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁאָבַד מִמֶּנּוּ חוֹתָמוֹ,
phrases.en: one who lost his seal

phrases.he: מַמְתִּינִין לוֹ עַד הָעֶרֶב.
phrases.en: would wait until the evening

phrases.he: אִם מוֹצְאִין לוֹ כְּדֵי חוֹתָמוֹ, נוֹתְנִין לוֹ.
phrases.en: if they found for him equivalent to his seal, they would give him

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו לֹא הָיָה לוֹ.
phrases.en: And if not, they would not give him

phrases.he: וְשֵׁם הַיּוֹם כָּתוּב עֲלֵיהֶן מִפְּנֵי הָרַמָּאִין:
phrases.en: And the name of the day was written upon them because of the cheats

phrases.he: שְׁתֵּי לְשָׁכוֹת הָיוּ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ, אַחַת לִשְׁכַּת חֲשָׁאִים, וְאַחַת לִשְׁכַּת הַכֵּלִים,
phrases.en: There were two special chambers in the Temple, one called the chamber of secret gifts and the other one called the chamber of vessels.

phrases.he: לִשְׁכַּת חֲשָׁאִים יִרְאֵי חֵטְא נוֹתְנִים לְתוֹכָה בַּחֲשַׁאי, וַעֲנִיִּים בְּנֵי טוֹבִים מִתְפַּרְנְסִים מִתוֹכָהּ בַּחֲשַׁאי.
phrases.en: In the chamber of secret gifts, sin-fearing people put money secretly and poor people of noble descent support themselves from it secretly.

phrases.he: לִשְׁכַּת הַכֵּלִים, כָּל מִי שֶׁהוּא מִתְנַדֵּב כֶּלִי, זוֹרְקוֹ לְתוֹכָהּ.
phrases.en: With regard to the chamber of vessels, anyone who donates a vessel to the Temple drops it inside that chamber,

phrases.he: וְאַחַת לִשְׁלשִׁים יוֹם, גִּזְבָּרִין פּוֹתְחִין אוֹתָהּ.
phrases.en: and once every thirty days the treasurers open it.

phrases.he: וְכָל כְּלִי שֶׁמּוֹצְאִין בּוֹ צֹרֶךְ לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת, מַנִּיחִין אוֹתוֹ.
phrases.en: And any vessel that they found for it a use for Temple maintenance, they leave it for that purpose,

phrases.he: וְהַשְּׁאָר נִמְכָּרִין בִּדְמֵיהֶן וְנוֹפְלִין לְלִשְׁכַּת בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת:
phrases.en: and the rest are sold, and their monetary value is allocated to Temple maintenance.

phrases.he: שְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר שׁוֹפָרוֹת, שְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר שׁוּלְחָנוֹת, שְׁלשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה הִשְׁתַּחֲוָיוֹת, הָיוּ בַּמִקְדָּשׁ.
phrases.en: There were thirteen horns, were also thirteen tables for various purposes, and thirteen prostrations in the Temple.

phrases.he: שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְשֶׁל בֵּית רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים הָיוּ מִשְׁתַּחֲוִין אַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה.
phrases.en: The members of the household of Rabban Gamliel and the members of the household of Rabbi Ḥananya, the deputy High Priest, would prostrate themselves in fourteen places.

phrases.he: וְהֵיכָן הָיְתָה יְתֵרָה, כְּנֶגֶד דִּיר הָעֵצִים, שֶׁכֵּן מָסֹרֶת בְּיָדָם מֵאֲבוֹתֵיהֶם שֶׁשָּׁם הָאָרוֹן נִגְנַז:
phrases.en: And where was this extra location? It was facing the wood depository, as there was a tradition handed down to them from their fathers that the Ark was sequestered there.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּכֹהֵן אֶחָד שֶׁהָיָה מִתְעַסֵּק, וְרָאָה הָרִצְפָּה שֶׁהִיא מְשֻׁנָּה מֵחֲבֵרוֹתֶיהָ.
phrases.en: an incident involving a certain priest who was going about and saw a flagstone that was different from the others.

phrases.he: בָּא וְאָמַר לַחֲבֵרוֹ.
phrases.en: He came and said to his fellow

phrases.he: לֹא הִסְפִּיק לִגְמֹר אֶת הַדָּבָר עַד שֶׁיָּצְתָה נִשְׁמָתוֹ,
phrases.en: He did not manage to conclude the incident before his soul left him,

phrases.he: וְיָדְעוּ בְיִחוּד שֶׁשָּׁם הָאָרוֹן נִגְנַז:
phrases.en: they knew with certainty that the Ark was sequestered there

phrases.he: וְהֵיכָן הָיוּ מִשְׁתַּחֲוִים,
phrases.en: Where were these prostrations?

phrases.he: אַרְבַּע בַּצָּפוֹן, וְאַרְבַּע בַּדָּרוֹם, שָׁלשׁ בַּמִּזְרָח, וּשְׁתַּיִם בַּמַּעֲרָב,
phrases.en: There were four in the north of the courtyard, four in the south, three in the east and two in the west,

phrases.he: כְּנֶגֶד שְׁלשָׁה עָשָׂר שְׁעָרִים.
phrases.en: as the thirteen prostrations were facing the thirteen gates of the Temple courtyard.

phrases.he: שְׁעָרִים דְּרוֹמִיִּים סְמוּכִין לַמַּעֲרָב, שַׁעַר הָעֶלְיוֹן,
phrases.en: The southern ones, listed in order, beginning with the one adjacent to the western side, were the Upper Gate,

phrases.he: שַׁעַר הַדֶּלֶק,
phrases.en: the Gate of Kindling,

phrases.he: שַׁעַר הַבְּכוֹרוֹת,
phrases.en: the Gate of the Firstborn,

phrases.he: שַׁעַר הַמָּיִם.
phrases.en: and the Gate of Water.

phrases.he: וְלָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ שַׁעַר הַמַּיִם, שֶׁבּוֹ מַכְנִיסִין צְלוֹחִית שֶׁל מַיִם שֶׁל נִסּוּךְ בֶּחָג.
phrases.en: And why was it named the Gate of Water? Since through it they would bring in the vial of water for the water libation on the festival of Sukkot,

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר, בּוֹ הַמַּיִם מְפַכִּים וַעֲתִידִין לִהְיוֹת יוֹצְאִין מִתַּחַת מִפְתַּן הַבַּיִת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says: There was a different reason for this name. It was called the Gate of Water because through it the water would trickle [mefakim], and in the future this water will increase and go out from under the threshold of the House.

phrases.he: לְעֻמָּתָן בַּצָּפוֹן סְמוּכִין לַמַּעֲרָב, שַׁעַר יְכָנְיָה,
phrases.en: Facing these gates were the ones in the north, listed in order from the one closest to the west: The Gate of Jeconiah;

phrases.he: שַׁעַר קָרְבָּן,
phrases.en: the Gate of the Offering,

phrases.he: שַׁעַר נָשִׁים,
phrases.en: the Gate of Women,

phrases.he: שַׁעַר הַשִּׁיר.
phrases.en: and the Gate of Song,

phrases.he: וְלָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ שַׁעַר יְכָנְיָה, שֶׁבּוֹ יָצָא יְכָנְיָה בְּגָלוּתוֹ.
phrases.en: And why was it called the Gate of Jeconiah? The reason is that through it Jeconiah went out to his exile.

phrases.he: בַּמִּזְרָח, שַׁעַר נִיקָנוֹר,
phrases.en: The mishna resumes the list with the gates that are in the east: the Gate of Nicanor,

phrases.he: וּשְׁנֵי פִשְׁפְּשִׁין הָיוּ לוֹ, אֶחָד בִּימִינוֹ וְאֶחָד בִּשְׂמֹאלוֹ.
phrases.en: And the Gate of Nicanor had two wickets [pishpeshin], one on its right and one on its left.

phrases.he: וּשְׁנַיִם בַּמַּעֲרָב שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהֶם שֵׁם:
phrases.en: And there were two gates in the west that did not have a name,

phrases.he: שְׁלשָׁה עָשָׂר שֻׁלְחָנוֹת הָיוּ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ, שְׁמוֹנֶה שֶׁל שַׁיִשׁ בְּבֵית הַמִּטְבְּחַיִם, שֶׁעֲלֵיהֶן מְדִיחִין אֶת הַקְּרָבַיִם.
phrases.en: were thirteen tables in the Temple. Eight of them were made of marble and were located in the slaughtering area, Upon these tables they would wash the innards of the offerings

phrases.he: וּשְׁנַיִם בְּמַעֲרַב הַכֶּבֶשׁ, אֶחָד שֶׁל שַׁיִשׁ וְאֶחָד שֶׁל כֶּסֶף עַל שֶׁל שַׁיִשׁ הָיוּ נוֹתְנִים אֶת הָאֵבָרִים, עַל שֶׁל כֶּסֶף כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת.
phrases.en: And there were two more tables on the western side of the ramp, one of marble and one of silver. On the table of marble they would place the limbs On the table made of silver they would place the sacred vessels

phrases.he: וּשְׁנַיִם בָּאוּלָם מִבִּפְנִים עַל פֶּתַח הַבַּיִת, אֶחָד שֶׁל שַׁיִשׁ וְאֶחָד שֶׁל זָהָב, עַל שֶׁל שַׁיִשׁ נוֹתְנִין לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים בִּכְנִיסָתוֹ, וְעַל שֶׁל זָהָב בִּיצִיאָתוֹ, שֶׁמַּעֲלִין בַּקֹּדֶשׁ וְלֹא מוֹרִידִין.
phrases.en: And there were two tables in the Entrance Hall on the inside of the Entrance Hall, near the opening to the Temple, one of marble and one of gold. On the table of marble they would put the shewbread before its entrance And on the table of gold upon its exit that one elevates in matters of sanctity and one does not downgrade.

phrases.he: וְאֶחָד שֶׁל זָהָב מִבִּפְנִים, שֶׁעָלָיו לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים תָּמִיד:
phrases.en: And one table of gold inside upon which the shewbread was placed always.

phrases.he: שְׁלשָׁה עָשָׂר שׁוֹפָרוֹת הָיוּ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ, וְכָתוּב עֲלֵיהֶם,
phrases.en: There were thirteen collection horns in the Temple, and the intended use of the funds was written upon

phrases.he: תִּקְלִין חַדְתִין וְתִקְלִין עַתִּיקִין, קִנִּין וְגוֹזְלֵי עוֹלָה, עֵצִים, וּלְבוֹנָה, זָהָב לַכַּפֹּרֶת.
phrases.en: New shekels, old shekels, pairs of birds, fledglings designated for burnt-offerings, wood for the arrangement on the altar, frankincense that accompanied meal-offerings, and gold donated for the Ark cover.

phrases.he: שִׁשָּׁה, לִנְדָבָה.
phrases.en: The remaining six horns were designated for communal free-will offerings.

phrases.he: תִּקְלִין חַדְתִּין, שֶׁבְּכָל שָׁנָה וְשָׁנָה.
phrases.en: The horn labeled new shekels was designated for the half-shekel donation that was brought every year for the needs of that year.

phrases.he: עַתִּיקִין, מִי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁקַל אֶשְׁתָּקַד, שׁוֹקֵל לְשָׁנָה הַבָּאָה.
phrases.en: The horn labeled old shekels was for one who did not bring his half-shekel the previous year, who would contribute his shekel for the following year.

phrases.he: קִנִּין, הֵם תּוֹרִים.
phrases.en: The funds in the horn labeled pairs of birds are designated for the turtledoves used for bird-offerings,

phrases.he: וְגוֹזְלֵי עוֹלָה, הֵן בְּנֵי יוֹנָה.
phrases.en: and the one labeled fledglings for burnt-offerings are used to purchase young pigeons as burnt-offerings.

phrases.he: וְכֻלָּן עוֹלוֹת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: All of these, i.e., the funds in both horns, were used exclusively for voluntary burnt-offerings. This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, קִנִּין, אֶחָד חַטָאת וְאֶחָד עוֹלָה.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: The funds in the horn labeled pairs of birds were designated for obligatory offerings. These offerings included a pair of birds, one brought for a sin-offering, and the other one brought for a burnt-offering.

phrases.he: וְגוֹזְלֵי עוֹלָה, כֻּלָּן עוֹלוֹת:
phrases.en: Conversely, the funds in the horn labeled fledglings for burnt-offerings were all used exclusively for voluntary burnt-offerings.

phrases.he: הָאוֹמֵר, הֲרֵי עָלַי עֵצִים, לֹא יִפְחוֹת מִשְּׁנֵי גִּזְרִין.
phrases.en: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate wood to the Temple, must donate no fewer than two logs for the arrangement on the altar.

phrases.he: לְבוֹנָה, לֹא יִפְחוֹת מִקֹּמֶץ.
phrases.en: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate frankincense, must donate no less than a handful of frankincense, the amount brought with a meal-offering.

phrases.he: זָהָב, לֹא יִפְחוֹת מִדִּינַר זָהָב.
phrases.en: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate gold, must donate no less than a dinar of gold.

phrases.he: שִׁשָּׁה לִנְדָבָה.
phrases.en: It was stated that six horns were designated for communal free-will offerings.

phrases.he: נְדָבָה מֶה הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין בָּהּ.
phrases.en: The Mishna asks: With regard to the money designated for communal free-will offerings, what would they do with this money?

phrases.he: לוֹקְחִין בָּהּ עוֹלוֹת, הַבָּשָׂר לַשֵּׁם, וְהָעוֹרוֹת לַכֹּהֲנִים.
phrases.en: The Mishna answers that they used it to purchase animals for burnt-offerings, as the meat from these offerings was offered on the altar to God and the hides were given to the priests.

phrases.he: זֶה מִדְרָשׁ דָּרַשׁ יְהוֹיָדָע כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל.
phrases.en: This midrash was taught by Jehoiada the High Priest:

phrases.he: (ויקרא ה) אָשָׁם הוּא אָשֹׁם אָשַׁם לַיְיָ.
phrases.en: "It is a guilt-offering; he is certainly guilty before the Lord"

phrases.he: (זֶה הַכְּלָל), כֹּל שֶׁהוּא בָּא מִשּׁוּם חֵטְא וּמִשּׁוּם אַשְׁמָה, יִלָּקַח בּוֹ עוֹלוֹת, הַבָּשָׂר לַשֵּׁם, וְהָעוֹרוֹת לַכֹּהֲנִים.
phrases.en: This is the principle: Any funds that come due to a sin-offering or due to a guilt-offering, i.e., leftover coins designated for one of these offerings, they should be used for the purchase of animals for a voluntary burnt-offering, as the meat will be offered on the altar to God, and the hides will go to the priests.

phrases.he: נִמְצְאוּ שְׁנֵי כְּתוּבִים קַיָּמִים, אָשָׁם לַה', וְאָשָׁם לַכֹּהֲנִים.
phrases.en: In this manner the two verses are found to be fulfilled, as it is both a guilt-offering to God as well as a guilt-offering to the priest.

phrases.he: וְאוֹמֵר, (מלכים ב יב), כֶּסֶף אָשָׁם וְכֶסֶף חַטָאוֹת לֹא יוּבָא בֵּית ה' לַכֹּהֲנִים יִהְיוּ.
phrases.en: And this halakha also explains the verse that says: "The guilt-offering money and the sin-offering money was not brought into the House of the Lord; it was for the priests"

phrases.he: מָעוֹת שֶׁנִּמְצְאוּ בֵּין הַשְּׁקָלִים לִנְדָבָה,
phrases.en: If money was found on the floor of the Temple between one of the collection horns marked shekels and the collection horn marked free-will offerings,

phrases.he: קָרוֹב לַשְּׁקָלִים יִפְּלוּ לַשְּׁקָלִים,
phrases.en: If the money was found closer to the horn marked shekels, it is allocated to the shekels;

phrases.he: לַנְּדָבָה יִפְּלוּ לַנְּדָבָה,
phrases.en: if it was found closer to the horn marked free-will offerings, it is allocated to free-will offerings;

phrases.he: מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה יִפְּלוּ לַנְּדָבָה.
phrases.en: and if it was equidistant from the horn marked shekels and the horn marked free-will offerings, it is allocated to free-will offerings.

phrases.he: בֵּין עֵצִים לִלְבוֹנָה,
phrases.en: If the money was found between the horn marked wood and the horn marked frankincense,

phrases.he: קָרוֹב לָעֵצִים יִפְּלוּ לָעֵצִים,
phrases.en: if it was closer to the horn marked wood, it is allocated to wood;

phrases.he: לַלְּבוֹנָה יִפְּלוּ לַלְּבוֹנָה,
phrases.en: if it was closer to the horn marked frankincense, it is allocated to frankincense;

phrases.he: מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה יִפְּלוּ לַלְּבוֹנָה.
phrases.en: and if it was found equidistant from both, it is allocated to frankincense.

phrases.he: בֵּין קִנִּין לְגוֹזְלֵי עוֹלָה,
phrases.en: If the money was found between the horn marked pairs of bird-offerings and the horn marked doves for burnt-offerings,

phrases.he: קָרוֹב לַקִּנִּין יִפְּלוּ לַקִּנִּין.
phrases.en: if it is closer to the horn marked pairs of bird-offerings, it is allocated to pairs of bird-offerings;

phrases.he: לְגוֹזְלֵי עוֹלָה יִפְּלוּ לְגוֹזְלֵי עוֹלָה,
phrases.en: if it was found closer to the horn marked doves for burnt-offerings, it is allocated to doves for burnt-offerings;

phrases.he: מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה יִפְּלוּ לְגוֹזְלֵי עוֹלָה.
phrases.en: and if it was found equidistant from both, it is allocated to doves for burnt-offerings.

phrases.he: בֵּין חֻלִּין לְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי,
phrases.en: If money was found anywhere else between a container for ordinary, non-sacred money and one containing second-tithe money,

phrases.he: קָרוֹב לַחֻלִּין יִפְּלוּ לַחֻלִּין,
phrases.en: If the money was found closer to the non-sacred money, it is allocated to the non-sacred money;

phrases.he: לְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי יִפְּלוּ לְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי,
phrases.en: if it was found closer to second-tithe money, it is allocated to second-tithe money;

phrases.he: מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה יִפְּלוּ לְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי.
phrases.en: and if it was found equidistant from both, it is allocated to second-tithe money.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, הוֹלְכִים אַחַר הַקָּרוֹב (לְהָקֵל).
phrases.en: This is the principle: In cases of doubt, the ruling follows whichever is closer, even if this involves being lenient,

phrases.he: מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה לְהַחְמִיר:
phrases.en: but if the money was found equidistant from both, the ruling follows whichever allocation involves being stringent.

phrases.he: מָעוֹת שֶׁנִּמְצְאוּ לִפְנֵי סוֹחֲרֵי בְּהֵמָה, לְעוֹלָם מַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.en: Money found before animal merchants is always presumed to be second-tithe money.

phrases.he: בְּהַר הַבַּיִת, חֻלִּין.
phrases.en: And money found on the Temple Mount is presumed to be non-sacred money.

phrases.he: בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם בִּשְׁעַת הָרֶגֶל, מַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.en: If it was found during the time of a pilgrim Festival, it is all presumed to be second-tithe money.

phrases.he: וּבִשְׁאָר כָּל יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה, חֻלִּין:
phrases.en: If it was found during the rest of the days of the year, it is presumed to be non-sacred money.

phrases.he: בָּשָׂר שֶׁנִּמְצָא בָּעֲזָרָה,
phrases.en: meat that was found in the Temple courtyard,

phrases.he: אֵבָרִים, עוֹלוֹת.
phrases.en: limbs are burnt-offerings.

phrases.he: וַחֲתִיכוֹת, חַטָאוֹת.
phrases.en: And pieces are sin-offerings.

phrases.he: בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, זִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים.
phrases.en: In Jerusalem, peace-offerings,

phrases.he: זֶה וָזֶה תְּעֻבַּר צוּרָתוֹ וְיֵצֵא לְבֵית הַשְּׂרֵפָה.
phrases.en: this and that its form to decay, and it must be taken out to the place of burning,

phrases.he: נִמְצָא בַּגְּבוּלִין, אֵבָרִים, נְבֵלוֹת.
phrases.en: found in the outlying areas, limbs, carcasses.

phrases.he: חֲתִיכוֹת, מֻתָּרוֹת.
phrases.en: But pieces, permitted.

phrases.he: וּבִשְׁעַת הָרֶגֶל שֶׁהַבָּשָׂר מְרֻבֶּה, אַף אֵבָרִים מֻתָּרִין:
phrases.en: And if meat is found at the time of a Festival, when meat is plentiful, then even limbs are permitted

phrases.he: בְּהֵמָה שֶׁנִּמְצֵאת מִירוּשָׁלַיִם וְעַד מִגְדַּל עֵדֶר, וּכְמִדָּתָהּ לְכָל רוּחַ,
phrases.en: an animal that is fit for the altar was found from Jerusalem and as far as Migdal Eder, and similarly if it was found within that distance from Jerusalem in any other direction,

phrases.he: זְכָרִים, עוֹלוֹת.
phrases.en: Males are presumed to be burnt-offerings,

phrases.he: נְקֵבוֹת, זִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים.
phrases.en: Females are presumed to be peace-offerings,

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הָרָאוּי לִפְסָחִים, פְּסָחִים קֹדֶם לָרֶגֶל שְׁלשִׁים יוֹם:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: An animal that is fit for the Paschal offering, is presumed to be a Paschal offering, provided that it was found within thirty days before the Festival of Passover.

phrases.he: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מְמַשְׁכְּנִין אֶת מוֹצְאֶיהָ, עַד שֶׁהוּא מֵבִיא נְסָכֶיהָ.
phrases.en: Originally, the court would seize collateral from one who found such an animal, as security until he would bring with it the libations associated with this offering

phrases.he: חָזְרוּ לִהְיוֹת מַנִּיחִין אוֹתָהּ וּבוֹרְחִין.
phrases.en: began leaving them where they found them, and absconding

phrases.he: הִתְקִינוּ בֵּית דִּין שֶׁיְּהוּ נְסָכֶיהָ בָּאִין מִשֶּׁל צִבּוּר:
phrases.en: The court therefore instituted that the libations accompanying these offerings would come from public funds

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, שִׁבְעָה דְּבָרִים הִתְקִינוּ בֵּית דִּין, וְזֶה אֶחָד מֵהֶן,
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon said: The court instituted seven ordinances. And this is one of them.

phrases.he: נָכְרִי שֶׁשִּׁלַּח עוֹלָתוֹ מִמְּדִינַת הַיָּם וְשִׁלַּח עִמָּהּ נְסָכִים, קְרֵבִין מִשֶׁלּוֹ.
phrases.en: If a gentile sent his burnt-offering from abroad and he sent with it libations, the libations are offered at his expense.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, קְרֵבִין מִשֶּׁל צִבּוּר.
phrases.en: And if he did not, the libations are sacrificed at the public's expense.

phrases.he: וְכֵן גֵּר שֶׁמֵּת וְהִנִּיחַ זְבָחִים, אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ נְסָכִים, קְרֵבִין מִשֶּׁלּוֹ.
phrases.en: And likewise, a convert who died and left offerings. If he has the libations, the libations are sacrificed from his estate.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, קְרֵבִין מִשֶּׁל צִבּוּר.
phrases.en: And if he did not, the libations are sacrificed from public funds.

phrases.he: וּתְנַאי בֵּית דִּין הוּא עַל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל שֶׁמֵּת, שֶׁתְּהֵא מִנְחָתוֹ קְרֵבָה מִשֶּׁל צִבּוּר.
phrases.en: And it is a condition of the court with regard to a High Priest who died, that his meal-offering would be sacrificed from public funds.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁל יוֹרְשִׁין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: from the property of the heirs.

phrases.he: וּשְׁלֵמָה הָיְתָה קְרֵבָה:
phrases.en: It was sacrificed from a whole one-tenth of an ephah.

phrases.he: עַל הַמֶּלַח וְעַל הָעֵצִים שֶׁיִּהְיוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים נֵאוֹתִים בָּהֶן,
phrases.en: about the salt and the wood that the priests may use them

phrases.he: וְעַל הַפָּרָה שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ מוֹעֲלִין בְּאֶפְרָהּ,
phrases.en: And concerned the red heifer: that deriving benefit from its ashes is not considered misusing consecrated property.

phrases.he: וְעַל הַקִּנִּין הַפְּסוּלוֹת שֶׁיְּהוּ בָאוֹת מִשֶּׁל צִבּוּר.
phrases.en: And about disqualified pairs of bird-offerings: It ruled that their replacements should come from public funds.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.he: הַמְסַפֵּק אֶת הַקִּנִּין, מְסַפֵּק אֶת הַפְּסוּלוֹת:
phrases.en: whoever supplies the pairs of bird-offerings to the Temple; he must also supply, at no additional charge, the replacements for the disqualified birds.

phrases.he: כָּל הָרֻקִּין הַנִּמְצָאִים בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם טְהוֹרִין,
phrases.en: All the spittle that is found in Jerusalem is ritually pure.

phrases.he: חוּץ מִשֶּׁל שׁוּק הָעֶלְיוֹן,
phrases.en: except for spittle found in the upper marketplace,

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.he: בִּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה, שֶׁבָּאֶמְצַע טְמֵאִין וְשֶׁבַּצְּדָדִין טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: On all the other days of the year, spittle that is found in the middle of the street is ritually impure, and spittle that is found on the sides of the street is ritually pure.

phrases.he: וּבִשְׁעַת הָרֶגֶל, שֶׁבָּאֶמְצַע טְהוֹרִין וְשֶׁבַּצְּדָדִין טְמֵאִין,
phrases.en: But during the time of the Festival, the spittle found in the middle of the street was ritually pure, and that found on the sides of the street was ritually impure.

phrases.he: שֶׁמִּפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מֻעָטִין מִסְתַּלְּקִין לַצְּדָדִין:
phrases.en: due to the fact that the ritually impure minority moves to the sides of the streets.

phrases.he: כָּל הַכֵּלִים הַנִּמְצָאִין בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם דֶּרֶךְ יְרִידָה לְבֵית הַטְבִילָה טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: All the vessels that are found in Jerusalem on the way down into the bathhouse, wherein one purifies vessels in a ritual bath, are ritually impure,

phrases.he: דֶּרֶךְ עֲלִיָּה, טְהוֹרִין,
phrases.en: and those that are found on the way up are ritually pure.

phrases.he: שֶׁלֹּא כְּדֶרֶךְ יְרִידָתָן עֲלִיָּתָן,
phrases.en: Their descent into the bathhouse is not by the same route as their ascent out of it,

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, כֻּלָּן טְהוֹרִין, חוּץ מִן הַסַּל וְהַמַּגְרֵפָה וְהַמְּרִצָּה הַמְיֻחָדִין לַקְּבָרוֹת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: They are all ritually pure, except for the basket, and the shovel, and the meritza, which are specifically used for graves,

phrases.he: סַכִּין שֶׁנִּמְצֵאת בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר, שׁוֹחֵט בָּהּ מִיָּד.
phrases.en: slaughter immediately with a knife that was found on the fourteenth

phrases.he: בִּשְׁלשָׁה עָשָׂר, שׁוֹנֶה וּמַטְבִּיל.
phrases.en: on the thirteenth he immerses it again

phrases.he: וְקוֹפִיץ, בֵּין בָּזֶה וּבֵין בָּזֶה שׁוֹנֶה וּמַטְבִּיל.
phrases.en: cleaver [kofitz], whether it was on this day or on that day, he immerses it again

phrases.he: חָל אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת, שׁוֹחֵט בָּהּ מִיָּד.
phrases.en: if the fourteenth occurs on Shabbat, he may slaughter with it immediately

phrases.he: בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר, שׁוֹחֵט בָּהּ מִיָּד.
phrases.en: on the fifteenth he may slaughter with it immediately

phrases.he: נִמְצֵאת קְשׁוּרָה לְסַכִּין, הֲרֵי זוֹ כַּסַּכִּין:
phrases.en: was found attached to a knife, it is like a knife

phrases.he: פָּרֹכֶת שֶׁנִּטְמֵאת בִּוְלַד הַטֻמְאָה, מַטְבִּילִין אוֹתָהּ בִּפְנִים וּמַכְנִיסִין אוֹתָהּ מִיָּד.
phrases.en: a curtain that became ritually impure from a secondary source of impurity, it is immersed inside and it can be brought back into the courtyard immediately.

phrases.he: וְאֶת שֶׁנִּטְמֵאת בְּאַב הַטֻמְאָה, מַטְבִּילִין אוֹתָהּ בַּחוּץ וְשׁוֹטְחִין אוֹתָהּ בַּחֵיל.
phrases.en: if it became impure from a primary source of impurity, it is immersed outside and is spread out on the rampart.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיְתָה חֲדָשָׁה, שׁוֹטְחִין אוֹתָהּ עַל גַּג הָאִצְטַבָּא, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּרְאוּ הָעָם אֶת מְלַאכְתָּהּ שֶׁהִיא נָאָה:
phrases.en: if it were new, it is spread out on top of the bench [itztabba], so that the people will see its craftsmanship and perceive its beauty.

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן הַסְּגַן,
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says in the name of Rabbi Shimon the son of the deputy High Priest:

phrases.he: פָּרֹכֶת עָבְיָהּ טֶפַח,
phrases.en: The curtain has the thickness of a handbreadth,

phrases.he: וְעַל שִׁבְעִים וּשְׁתַּיִם נִימִין נֶאֱרֶגֶת,
phrases.en: and it is woven from seventy-two strands of yarn.

phrases.he: וְעַל כָּל נִימָא וְנִימָא עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה חוּטִין.
phrases.en: And each and every strand from those seventy-two is made from twenty-four threads.

phrases.he: אָרְכָּהּ אַרְבָּעִים אַמָּה וְרָחְבָּהּ עֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה,
phrases.en: its length was forty cubits, and its width was twenty cubits,

phrases.he: וּמִשְּׁמוֹנִים וּשְׁתֵּי רִבּוֹא נַעֲשֵׂית.
phrases.en: and it was made from eighty-two ten-thousands.

phrases.he: וּשְׁתַּיִם עוֹשִׂין בְּכָל שָׁנָה,
phrases.en: And they used to make two new curtains every year.

phrases.he: וּשְׁלשׁ מֵאוֹת כֹּהֲנִים מַטְבִּילִין אוֹתָהּ:
phrases.en: And three hundred priests to carry it when they would immerse it.

phrases.he: בְּשַׂר קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים שֶׁנִּטְמָא, בֵּין בְּאַב הַטֻמְאָה, בֵּין בִּוְלַד הַטֻמְאָה, בֵּין בִּפְנִים, בֵּין בַּחוּץ,
phrases.en: the flesh of offerings of the most sacred order that became impure, whether it became impure from a primary source of impurity or from a secondary source of impurity, whether it became impure inside the courtyard or outside,

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, הַכֹּל יִשָּׂרֵף בִּפְנִים, חוּץ מִשֶּׁנִּטְמָא בְּאַב הַטֻמְאָה בַּחוּץ.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: It all should be burned inside except for that which became impure from a primary source of ritual impurity outside,

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, הַכֹּל יִשָּׂרֵף בַּחוּץ, חוּץ מִשֶּׁנִּטְמָא בִּוְלַד הַטֻמְאָה בִּפְנִים:
phrases.en: Beit Hillel say: It all should be burned outside except for that which became ritually impure by a secondary source of impurity inside.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar says:

phrases.he: אֶת שֶׁנִּטְמָא בְּאַב הַטֻמְאָה, בֵּין בִּפְנִים בֵּין בַּחוּץ, יִשָּׂרֵף בַּחוּץ.
phrases.en: Flesh from offerings of the most sacred order that became ritually impure from a primary source of ritual impurity, whether it became so inside the courtyard or outside, is burned outside.

phrases.he: וְאֶת שֶׁנִּטְמָא בִּוְלַד הַטֻמְאָה, בֵּין בִּפְנִים בֵּין בַּחוּץ, יִשָּׂרֵף בִּפְנִים.
phrases.en: an item that became ritually impure from a secondary source of ritual impurity, whether it became ritually impure outside or inside, is burned inside.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.he: מְקוֹם טֻמְאָתוֹ שָׁם שְׂרֵפָתוֹ:
phrases.en: The place of its impurity is where its burning should occur.

phrases.he: אֵבָרֵי הַתָּמִיד, נִתָּנִין מֵחֲצִי כֶּבֶשׁ וּלְמַטָה בַּמִּזְרָח,
phrases.en: The limbs of the daily offering were placed from the halfway point and below, on the western side.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל מוּסָפִין נִתָּנִין מֵחֲצִי כֶּבֶשׁ וּלְמַטָה בַּמַּעֲרָב,
phrases.en: Limbs of the additional offerings were placed on the ramp from the halfway point and below on its eastern side.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל רָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים נִתָּנִין מִתַּחַת כַּרְכֹּב הַמִּזְבֵּחַ מִלְּמָטָה,
phrases.en: Additional New Moon offerings were placed on top of the upper part of the edge of the altar.

phrases.he: הַשְּׁקָלִים וְהַבִּכּוּרִים אֵין נוֹהֲגִין אֶלָּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת,
phrases.en: The obligation to give half-shekels and to offer the first fruits is practiced only in the presence of the Temple.

phrases.he: אֲבָל מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן וּמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה וְהַבְּכוֹרוֹת נוֹהֲגִין בֵּין בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת.
phrases.en: But the mitzvot of produce tithes and grain tithes and of animal tithes and of the sanctified firstborn animals are practiced whether one is in the presence of the Temple, or one is not in the presence of the Temple.

phrases.he: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ שְׁקָלִים וּבִכּוּרִים, הֲרֵי זֶה קֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.en: If one consecrates shekels or first fruits, they are consecrated.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, הָאוֹמֵר בִּכּוּרִים קֹדֶשׁ, אֵינָן קֹדֶשׁ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: One who declared first fruits to be consecrated, they are not consecrated.

phrases.he: שִׁבְעַת יָמִים קֹדֶם יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מַפְרִישִׁין כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מִבֵּיתוֹ לְלִשְׁכַּת פַּלְהֶדְרִין.
phrases.en: Seven days prior to Yom Kippur the Sages would remove the High Priest from his house to the Chamber of Parhedrin

phrases.he: וּמַתְקִינִין לוֹ כֹהֵן אַחֵר תַּחְתָּיו, שֶׁמָּא יֶאֱרַע בּוֹ פְסוּל.
phrases.en: And they would designate another priest in his stead lest a disqualification prevent him from entering the Temple on Yom Kippur

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף אִשָּׁה אַחֶרֶת מַתְקִינִין לוֹ, שֶׁמָּא תָמוּת אִשְׁתּוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְכִפֶּר בַּעֲדוֹ וּבְעַד בֵּיתוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: The Sages would even designate another wife for him lest his wife die, as it is stated: And it will atone for him and for his house

phrases.he: בֵּיתוֹ, זוֹ אִשְׁתּוֹ.
phrases.en: His house, that is his wife

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, אִם כֵּן, אֵין לַדָּבָר סוֹף.
phrases.en: The Rabbis said to Rabbi Yehuda: If so, there is no end to the matter

phrases.he: כָּל שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים הוּא זוֹרֵק אֶת הַדָּם וּמַקְטִיר אֶת הַקְּטֹרֶת וּמֵטִיב אֶת הַנֵּרוֹת וּמַקְרִיב אֶת הָרֹאשׁ וְאֶת הָרֶגֶל.
phrases.en: During all seven days he sprinkles the blood and he burns the incense, and he removes the lamps and he sacrifices the head and the leg.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַיָּמִים, אִם רָצָה לְהַקְרִיב, מַקְרִיב, שֶׁכֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מַקְרִיב חֵלֶק בָּרֹאשׁ וְנוֹטֵל חֵלֶק בָּרֹאשׁ:
phrases.en: On all the other days, if the High Priest wishes to sacrifice any of the offerings, he sacrifices them, as the High Priest sacrifices any portion that he chooses first and takes any portion that he chooses first.

phrases.he: מָסְרוּ לוֹ זְקֵנִים מִזִּקְנֵי בֵית דִּין, וְקוֹרִין לְפָנָיו בְּסֵדֶר הַיּוֹם,
phrases.en: provided the High Priest with Elders selected from the Elders of the court, and they would read before him the order of the service of the day

phrases.he: וְאוֹמְרִים לוֹ, אִישִׁי כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, קְרָא אַתָּה בְּפִיךָ,
phrases.en: And they would say to him: My Master, High Priest. Read the order of the service with your own mouth,

phrases.he: שֶׁמָּא שָׁכַחְתָּ אוֹ שֶׁמָּא לֹא לָמָדְתָּ.
phrases.en: perhaps you forgot this reading or perhaps you did not learn to read.

phrases.he: עֶרֶב יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שַׁחֲרִית, מַעֲמִידִין אוֹתוֹ בְּשַׁעַר מִזְרָח,
phrases.en: On Yom Kippur eve in the morning, the Elders stand him at the eastern gate of the courtyard

phrases.he: וּמַעֲבִירִין לְפָנָיו פָּרִים וְאֵילִים וּכְבָשִׂים, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא מַכִּיר וְרָגִיל בָּעֲבוֹדָה:
phrases.en: and pass before him bulls and rams and sheep so that he will be familiar with the animals and grow accustomed to the service,

phrases.he: כָּל שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים לֹא הָיוּ מוֹנְעִין מִמֶּנּוּ מַאֲכָל וּמִשְׁתֶּה,
phrases.en: Throughout all the seven days they would not withhold from him any food or drink

phrases.he: עֶרֶב יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים עִם חֲשֵׁכָה, לֹא הָיוּ מַנִּיחִים אוֹתוֹ לֶאֱכֹל הַרְבֵּה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַמַּאֲכָל מֵבִיא אֶת הַשֵּׁנָה:
phrases.en: on Yom Kippur eve at nightfall, they would not allow him to eat a great deal because food induces sleep

phrases.he: מְסָרוּהוּ זִקְנֵי בֵית דִּין לְזִקְנֵי כְהֻנָּה,
phrases.en: The Elders of the court passed him to the Elders of the priesthood,

phrases.he: וְהֶעֱלוּהוּ לַעֲלִיַּת בֵּית אַבְטִינָס,
phrases.en: and they took him up to the House of Avtinas.

phrases.he: וְהִשְׁבִּיעוּהוּ וְנִפְטְרוּ וְהָלְכוּ לָהֶם.
phrases.en: And they administered him an oath and took leave of him and went on their way.

phrases.he: וְאָמְרוּ לוֹ, אִישִׁי כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, אָנוּ שְׁלוּחֵי בֵית דִּין, וְאַתָּה שְׁלוּחֵנוּ וּשְׁלִיחַ בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.en: they said to him: My Master, High Priest. We are agents of the court, and you are our agent and the agent of the court.

phrases.he: מַשְׁבִּיעִין אָנוּ עָלֶיךָ בְּמִי שֶׁשִּׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ בַבַּיִת הַזֶּה,
phrases.en: We administer an oath to you in the name of Him who housed His name in this House,

phrases.he: שֶׁלֹּא תְשַׁנֶּה דָבָר מִכָּל מַה שֶּׁאָמַרְנוּ לָךְ.
phrases.en: that you will not change even one matter from all that we have said to you

phrases.he: הוּא פוֹרֵשׁ וּבוֹכֶה, וְהֵן פּוֹרְשִׁין וּבוֹכִין:
phrases.en: he would leave them and cry, and they would leave him and cry

phrases.he: אִם הָיָה חָכָם, דּוֹרֵשׁ.
phrases.en: If he was a scholar, he would teach Torah.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים דּוֹרְשִׁין לְפָנָיו.
phrases.en: If he was not a scholar, Torah scholars would teach Torah before him.

phrases.he: וְאִם רָגִיל לִקְרוֹת, קוֹרֵא.
phrases.en: And if he was accustomed to read the Bible, he would read;

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, קוֹרִין לְפָנָיו.
phrases.en: and if he was not, they would read the Bible before him.

phrases.he: וּבַמֶּה קוֹרִין לְפָנָיו, בְּאִיּוֹב וּבְעֶזְרָא וּבְדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים.
phrases.en: And what books would they read before him to pique his interest so that he would not fall asleep? They would read from Job, and from Ezra, and from Chronicles.

phrases.he: זְכַרְיָה בֶּן קְבוּטָל אוֹמֵר, פְּעָמִים הַרְבֵּה קָרִיתִי לְפָנָיו בְּדָנִיֵּאל:
phrases.en: Zekharya, son of Kevutal, says: Many times I read before him from the book of Daniel.

phrases.he: בִּקֵּשׁ לְהִתְנַמְנֵם,
phrases.en: sought to sleep

phrases.he: פִּרְחֵי כְהֻנָּה מַכִּין לְפָנָיו בְּאֶצְבַּע צְרֵדָה,
phrases.en: the young priests would snap the middle [tzerada] finger against the thumb before him,

phrases.he: וְאוֹמְרִים לוֹ,
phrases.en: and they would say to him

phrases.he: אִישִׁי כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, עֲמֹד וְהָפֵג אַחַת עַל הָרִצְפָּה.
phrases.en: My Master, High Priest. Stand from your bed and chill yourself once on the floor

phrases.he: וּמַעֲסִיקִין אוֹתוֹ עַד שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ זְמַן הַשְּׁחִיטָה:
phrases.en: And they would engage him in various ways until the time would arrive to slaughter the daily offering.

phrases.he: בְּכָל יוֹם תּוֹרְמִין אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ בִּקְרִיאַת הַגֶּבֶר אוֹ סָמוּךְ לוֹ, בֵּין לְפָנָיו בֵּין לְאַחֲרָיו.
