phrases.en: one who establishes his sukka between the trees, and the trees serve as walls for it, the sukka is fit.

phrases.he: שְׁלוּחֵי מִצְוָה פְּטוּרִין מִן הַסֻּכָּה.
phrases.en: Those on the path to perform a mitzva are exempt from the mitzva of sukka.

phrases.he: חוֹלִין וּמְשַׁמְּשֵׁיהֶן פְּטוּרִין מִן הַסֻּכָּה.
phrases.en: The ill and their caretakers are exempt from the mitzva of sukka.

phrases.he: אוֹכְלִין וְשׁוֹתִין עֲרַאי חוּץ לַסֻּכָּה:
phrases.en: One may eat and drink in the framework of a casual meal outside the sukka.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה
phrases.en: An incident

phrases.he: וְהֵבִיאוּ לוֹ לְרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי לִטְעוֹם אֶת הַתַּבְשִׁיל,
phrases.en: occurred where they brought a cooked dish to Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai for him to taste

phrases.he: וּלְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל שְׁתֵּי כוֹתָבוֹת וּדְלִי שֶׁל מַיִם,
phrases.en: and to Rabban Gamliel they brought two dates and a bucket of water

phrases.he: וְאָמְרוּ, הַעֲלוּם לַסֻּכָּה.
phrases.en: And they each said: Take them up to the sukka and we will eat them there

phrases.he: וּכְשֶׁנָּתְנוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי צָדוֹק אֹכֶל פָּחוֹת מִכַּבֵּיצָה,
phrases.en: And when they gave Rabbi Tzadok less than an egg-bulk of food

phrases.he: נְטָלוֹ בַמַּפָּה וַאֲכָלוֹ חוּץ לַסֻּכָּה,
phrases.en: he took the food in a cloth and he ate it outside the sukka

phrases.he: וְלֹא בֵרַךְ אַחֲרָיו:
phrases.en: and did not recite a blessing after it

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה סְעוּדוֹת חַיָּב אָדָם לֶאֱכֹל בַּסֻּכָּה,
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: A person is obligated to eat fourteen meals in the sukka

phrases.he: אַחַת בַּיּוֹם וְאַחַת בַּלָּיְלָה.
phrases.en: one during the day and one at night

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵין לַדָּבָר קִצְבָה, חוּץ מִלֵּילֵי יוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חָג בִּלְבָד.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: There is no quota except for the evening of the first Festival day of Sukkot,

phrases.he: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, מִי שֶׁלֹּא אָכַל לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן, יַשְׁלִים בְּלֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן.
phrases.en: And furthermore, Rabbi Eliezer said: One who did not eat evening of the first day of the Festival should compensate with a meal on the evening of the last day of the Festival,

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵין לַדָּבָר תַּשְׁלוּמִין,
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: There is no compensation for this matter,

phrases.he: עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר (קהלת א) מְעֻוָּת לֹא יוּכַל לִתְקֹן, וְחֶסְרוֹן לֹא יוּכַל לְהִמָּנוֹת:
phrases.en: and with regard to similar cases it is stated: "That which is crooked cannot be made straight; and that which is wanting cannot be numbered"

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁהָיָה רֹאשׁוֹ וְרֻבּוֹ בַסֻּכָּה, וְשׁוּלְחָנוֹ בְתוֹךְ הַבַּיִת,
phrases.en: one whose head and most of his body were in the sukka and his table was in the house,

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי פּוֹסְלִין, וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַכְשִׁירִין.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai deem it unfit, and Beit Hillel deem it fit.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי,
phrases.en: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:

phrases.he: לֹא כָךְ הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה, שֶׁהָלְכוּ זִקְנֵי בֵית שַׁמַּאי וְזִקְנֵי בֵית הִלֵּל לְבַקֵּר אֶת רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן הַחוֹרָנִי,
phrases.en: wasn't there an incident where the Elders of Beit Shammai and the Elders of Beit Hillel went to visit Rabbi Yoḥanan ben HaḤoranit

phrases.he: וּמְצָאוּהוּ שֶׁהָיָה יוֹשֵׁב רֹאשׁוֹ וְרֻבּוֹ בַסֻּכָּה, וְשׁוּלְחָנוֹ בְתוֹךְ הַבַּיִת,
phrases.en: and they found him such that he was sitting with his head and most of his body in the sukka and his table in the house,

phrases.he: וְלֹא אָמְרוּ לוֹ דָבָר.
phrases.en: and they said nothing to him?

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית שַׁמַּאי,
phrases.en: Beit Shammai said to them:

phrases.he: מִשָּׁם רְאָיָה,
phrases.en: Is there proof from there?

phrases.he: אַף הֵם אָמְרוּ לוֹ, אִם כֵּן הָיִיתָ נוֹהֵג, לֹא קִיַּמְתָּ מִצְוַת סֻכָּה מִיָּמֶיךָ:
phrases.en: they said to him: If you were accustomed to act in this manner, you have never fulfilled the mitzva of sukka in your life.

phrases.he: נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים, פְּטוּרִים מִן הַסֻּכָּה.
phrases.en: Women, slaves, and minors are exempt from the sukka.

phrases.he: קָטָן שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְאִמּוֹ, חַיָּב בַּסֻּכָּה.
phrases.en: A minor who does not need his mother any longer is obligated in the sukka.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה וְיָלְדָה כַלָּתוֹ שֶׁל שַׁמַּאי הַזָּקֵן וּפִחֵת אֶת הַמַּעֲזִיבָה וְסִכֵּךְ עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּטָּה בִּשְׁבִיל הַקָּטָן.
phrases.en: There was an incident where the daughter-in-law of Shammai the Elder gave birth, and Shammai removed the coat of plaster from the roof and roofed with the beams over the bed for the newborn minor.

phrases.he: כָּל שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים אָדָם עוֹשֶׂה סֻכָּתוֹ קֶבַע וּבֵיתוֹ עֲרַאי.
phrases.en: All seven days a person renders his sukka his permanent residence and his house his temporary residence.

phrases.he: יָרְדוּ גְשָׁמִים, מֵאֵימָתַי מֻתָּר לְפַנּוֹת, מִשֶּׁתִּסְרַח הַמִּקְפָּה.
phrases.en: If rain fell, from when is it permitted to vacate the sukka? From the point that it is raining so hard that the congealed dish will spoil.

phrases.he: מָשְׁלוּ מָשָׁל, לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה, לְעֶבֶד שֶׁבָּא לִמְזוֹג כּוֹס לְרַבּוֹ, וְשָׁפַךְ לוֹ קִיתוֹן עַל פָּנָיו.
phrases.en: The Sages told a parable: To what is this matter comparable? It is comparable to a servant who comes to pour wine for his master, and he pours a jug of water in his face.

phrases.he: לוּלָב הַגָּזוּל וְהַיָּבֵשׁ, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: A lulav that was stolen or that is completely dry is unfit for use in fulfilling the mitzva of the four species.

phrases.he: שֶׁל אֲשֵׁרָה וְשֶׁל עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: The lulav of a tree worshipped as idolatry [asheira] and a lulav from a city whose residents were incited to idolatry, which must be burned along with all the city's property, are unfit.

phrases.he: נִקְטַם רֹאשׁוֹ, נִפְרְצוּ עָלָיו, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: If the top of the lulav was severed or if the palm leaves were severed from the spine of the lulav, it is unfit.

phrases.he: נִפְרְדוּ עָלָיו, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: If its leaves, although still attached, were spread and are no longer completely joined to the spine, it is fit.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, יֶאֶגְדֶנּוּ מִלְמָעְלָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: One should bind the lulav from the top, to join the leaves that spread to the spine.

phrases.he: צִנֵּי הַר הַבַּרְזֶל, כְּשֵׁרוֹת.
phrases.en: A lulav from the palms of the Iron Mountain are fit for use, although it differs from one taken from a standard palm tree, in that its leaves are shorter and do not cover the entire spine.

phrases.he: לוּלָב שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ שְׁלשָׁה טְפָחִים כְּדֵי לְנַעְנֵעַ בּוֹ, כָּשֵׁר:
phrases.en: A lulav that has three handbreadths in length, sufficient to enable one to wave with it, is fit for use in fulfilling the mitzva.

phrases.he: הֲדַס הַגָּזוּל וְהַיָּבֵשׁ, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: A myrtle branch that was stolen or that is completely dry is unfit.

phrases.he: שֶׁל אֲשֵׁרָה וְשֶׁל עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: A myrtle branch of a tree worshipped as idolatry [asheira] or a myrtle branch from a city whose residents were incited to idolatry is unfit.

phrases.he: נִקְטַם רֹאשׁוֹ, נִפְרְצוּ עָלָיו אוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ עֲנָבָיו מְרֻבּוֹת מֵעָלָיו, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: If the top of the myrtle branch was severed, if the leaves were severed completely, or if its berries were more numerous than its leaves, it is unfit.

phrases.he: וְאִם מִעֲטָן, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: If one diminished their number by plucking berries so that they no longer outnumbered the leaves, the myrtle branch is fit.

phrases.he: וְאֵין מְמַעֲטִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב:
phrases.en: But one may not diminish the number on the Festival itself.

phrases.he: עֲרָבָה גְזוּלָה וִיבֵשָׁה, פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.en: A willow branch that was stolen or is completely dry is unfit.

phrases.he: שֶׁל אֲשֵׁרָה וְשֶׁל עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת, פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.en: One from a tree worshipped as idolatry [asheira] or from a city whose residents were incited to idolatry is unfit.

phrases.he: נִקְטַם רֹאשָׁהּ, נִפְרְצוּ עָלֶיהָ, וְהַצַּפְצָפָה, פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.en: If the top was severed, or its leaves were severed, or if it is the tzaftzafa, a species similar to, but not actually a willow, it is unfit.

phrases.he: כְּמוּשָׁה, וְשֶׁנָּשְׁרוּ מִקְצָת עָלֶיהָ, וְשֶׁל בַּעַל, כְּשֵׁרָה:
phrases.en: However, a willow branch that is slightly dried, and one that a minority of its leaves fell, and a branch from a willow that does not grow by the river, but instead is from a non-irrigated field, is fit.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yishmael says:

phrases.he: שְׁלשָׁה הֲדַסִּים וּשְׁתֵּי עֲרָבוֹת, לוּלָב אֶחָד וְאֶתְרוֹג אֶחָד,
phrases.en: three myrtle branches, and two willow branches, one lulav, and one etrog.

phrases.he: אֲפִלּוּ שְׁנַיִם קְטוּמִים וְאֶחָד אֵינוֹ קָטוּם.
phrases.en: even if the tops of two are severed and the top of one is not severed,

phrases.he: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Tarfon says:

phrases.he: אֲפִלּוּ שְׁלָשְׁתָּן קְטוּמִים.
phrases.en: Even if the tops of all three are severed,

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says

phrases.he: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁלּוּלָב אֶחָד וְאֶתְרוֹג אֶחָד, כָּךְ הֲדַס אֶחָד וַעֲרָבָה אֶחָת:
phrases.en: Just as there is one lulav and one etrog, so too there is one myrtle branch and one willow branch.

phrases.he: אֶתְרוֹג הַגָּזוּל וְהַיָּבֵשׁ, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: An etrog that was stolen or is completely dry is unfit.

phrases.he: שֶׁל אֲשֵׁרָה וְשֶׁל עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: One from a tree worshipped as idolatry [asheira] or from a city whose residents were incited to idolatry is unfit.

phrases.he: שֶׁל עָרְלָה, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: An etrog that is fruit that grew on a tree during the three years after it was planted [orla] is unfit,

phrases.he: שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה טְמֵאָה, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: An etrog of impure teruma is unfit.

phrases.he: שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה טְהוֹרָה, לֹא יִטֹּל, וְאִם נָטַל, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: With regard to an etrog of pure teruma, one may not take it ab initio, and if one took it, it is fit,

phrases.he: שֶׁל דְּמַאי, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי פּוֹסְלִין, וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַכְשִׁירִין.
phrases.en: With regard to an etrog of demai, which is produce acquired from an am ha'aretz, who does not reliably tithe his produce, Beit Shammai deem it unfit, and Beit Hillel deem it fit.

phrases.he: שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, לֹא יִטֹּל, וְאִם נָטַל, כָּשֵׁר:
phrases.en: With regard to an etrog of second tithe in Jerusalem, one may not take it ab initio; and if he took it, it is fit.

phrases.he: עָלְתָה חֲזָזִית עַל רֻבּוֹ, נִטְּלָה פִטְמָתוֹ, נִקְלַף, נִסְדַּק, נִקַּב וְחָסַר כָּל שֶׁהוּא, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: If boil-like blemishes arose on the majority of the etrog; if its pestle-like protuberance on the upper, blossom end was removed; if the etrog was peeled, split, or pierced and is missing any amount, it is unfit.

phrases.he: עָלְתָה חֲזָזִית עַל מִעוּטוֹ, נִטַּל עֻקְצוֹ, נִקַּב וְלֹא חָסַר כָּל שֶׁהוּא, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: However, if boil-like blemishes arose only on its minority; if its stem, which connects it to the tree, was removed; or it was pierced but is not missing any amount, it is fit.

phrases.he: אֶתְרוֹג הַכּוּשִׁי, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: A Cushite etrog, which is black like a Cushite, is unfit.

phrases.he: וְהַיָרוֹק כְּכַרְתִי, רַבִּי מֵאִיר מַכְשִׁיר, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה פּוֹסֵל:
phrases.en: And with regard to an etrog that is leek green, Rabbi Meir deems it fit and Rabbi Yehuda deems it unfit.

phrases.he: שִׁעוּר אֶתְרוֹג הַקָּטָן, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, כָּאֱגוֹז.
phrases.en: the minimum measure of a small etrog? Rabbi Meir says: It may be no smaller than a walnut-bulk.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כַּבֵּיצָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: It may be no smaller than an egg-bulk.

phrases.he: וּבְגָדוֹל, כְּדֵי שֶׁיֹּאחַז שְׁנַיִם בְּיָדוֹ אַחַת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: And in a large etrog, the maximum measure is so that one could hold two in his one hand; this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ אֶחָד בִּשְׁתֵּי יָדָיו:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: It is fit even if it is so large that he can hold only one in his two hands.

phrases.he: אֵין אוֹגְדִין אֶת הַלּוּלָב אֶלָּא בְמִינוֹ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: One may bind the lulav only with its own species; the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ בִמְשִׁיחָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: One may do so even with a string or with a cord.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר, מַעֲשֶׂה בְאַנְשֵׁי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹגְדִין אֶת לוּלְבֵיהֶן בְּגִימוֹנִיּוֹת שֶׁל זָהָב.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir said: There was an incident involving the men of Jerusalem who would bind their lulavim with gold rings.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, בְּמִינוֹ הָיוּ אוֹגְדִין אוֹתוֹ מִלְּמָטָּה:
phrases.en: The Sages said to him: They would bind it with its own species beneath the rings, which serve a merely decorative purpose and not a halakhic one.

phrases.he: וְהֵיכָן הָיוּ מְנַעְנְעִין
phrases.en: And where would they wave

phrases.he: בְּהוֹדוּ לַה' תְּחִלָּה וָסוֹף
phrases.en: at "Thank the Lord, for He is good" that appears at both the beginning and the end

phrases.he: וּבְאָנָּא ה' הוֹשִׁיעָה נָּא
phrases.en: and at "Lord, please save us"

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי בֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.en: this is the statement of Beit Hillel

phrases.he: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אַף בְּאָנָּא ה' הַצְלִיחָה נָא
phrases.en: And Beit Shammai say: They would wave the lulav even at "Lord, please grant us success"

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, צוֹפֶה הָיִיתִי בְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וּבְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva said: I was observing Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua

phrases.he: שֶׁכָּל הָעָם הָיוּ מְנַעְנְעִים אֶת לוּלְבֵיהֶן
phrases.en: that all the people were waving their lulavim

phrases.he: וְהֵן לֹא נִעְנְעוּ אֶלָּא בְאָנָּא ה' הוֹשִׁיעָה נָּא
phrases.en: and them waved their lulav only at: "Lord, please save us"

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁבָּא בַדֶּרֶךְ וְלֹא הָיָה בְיָדוֹ לוּלָב לִטֹּל
phrases.en: one who was coming along the way and did not have a lulav in his hand to take

phrases.he: לִכְשֶׁיִּכָּנֵס לְבֵיתוֹ יִטֹּל עַל שֻׁלְחָנוֹ
phrases.en: when he enters his house he should take at his table

phrases.he: לֹא נָטַל שַׁחֲרִית, יִטֹּל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם
phrases.en: If he did not take the lulav in the morning, he should take it in the afternoon

phrases.he: שֶׁכָּל הַיּוֹם כָּשֵׁר לַלּוּלָב
phrases.en: as the entire day is suited for lulav

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁהָיָה עֶבֶד אוֹ אִשָּׁה אוֹ קָטָן מַקְרִין אוֹתוֹ, עוֹנֶה אַחֲרֵיהֶן מַה שֶּׁהֵן אוֹמְרִין,
phrases.en: one for whom a Canaanite slave, a woman, or a minor was reciting hallel, he repeats after them what they are saying

phrases.he: וּתְהִי לוֹ מְאֵרָה.
phrases.en: And may a curse come to him

phrases.he: אִם הָיָה גָדוֹל מַקְרֵא אוֹתוֹ, עוֹנֶה אַחֲרָיו הַלְלוּיָהּ:
phrases.en: If an adult male was reciting hallel on his behalf, he answers: Halleluya,

phrases.he: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לִכְפֹּל, יִכְפֹּל.
phrases.en: In a place where they were accustomed to repeat, he, too, should repeat them.

phrases.he: לִפְשֹׁט, יִפְשֹׁט.
phrases.en: If the custom is to recite them plainly, without repetition, he should recite them plainly.

phrases.he: לְבָרֵךְ אַחֲרָיו, יְבָרֵךְ אַחֲרָיו.
phrases.en: In a place where the custom is to recite a blessing after hallel, he should recite a blessing.

phrases.he: הַכֹּל כְּמִנְהַג הַמְּדִינָה.
phrases.en: Everything is in accordance with the local custom.

phrases.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ לוּלָב מֵחֲבֵרוֹ בַשְּׁבִיעִית, נוֹתֵן לוֹ אֶתְרוֹג בְּמַתָּנָה, לְפִי שֶׁאֵין רַשַּׁאי לְלָקְחוֹ בַשְּׁבִיעִית:
phrases.en: One who purchases a lulav from another during the Sabbatical Year, the seller gives him an etrog as a gift, as he is not permitted to purchase the etrog during the Sabbatical Year.

phrases.he: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיָה לוּלָב נִטָּל בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ שִׁבְעָה, וּבַמְּדִינָה יוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.en: Originally, during the Temple era, the lulav was taken in the Temple for seven days, and in the rest of the country outside the Temple it was taken for one day.

phrases.he: מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי שֶׁיְּהֵא לוּלָב נִטָּל בַּמְּדִינָה שִׁבְעָה, זֵכֶר לַמִּקְדָשׁ.
phrases.en: Once the Temple was destroyed, Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted an ordinance that the lulav should be taken even in the rest of the country for seven days, in commemoration of the Temple.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁיְּהֵא יוֹם הָנֵף כֻּלּוֹ אָסוּר:
phrases.en: And for similar reasons, he instituted an ordinance that for the entire day of waving the omer offering, it should be prohibited to eat the grain of the new crop.

phrases.he: יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חָג שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת, כָּל הָעָם מוֹלִיכִין אֶת לוּלְבֵיהֶן לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת.
phrases.en: the first day of the festival of Sukkot occurs on Shabbat, all of the people bring their lulavim to the synagogue

phrases.he: לַמָּחֳרָת מַשְׁכִּימִין וּבָאִין, כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מַכִּיר אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ, וְנוֹטְלוֹ.
phrases.en: The next day, on Shabbat, everyone rises early and comes to the synagogue. Each and every one recognizes his lulav and takes it.

phrases.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים, אֵין אָדָם יוֹצֵא יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חָג בְּלוּלָבוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ.
phrases.en: because the Sages said: A person does not fulfill his obligation to take the lulav on the first day of the Festival with the lulav of another,

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הֶחָג, אָדָם יוֹצֵא יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בְּלוּלָבוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ:
phrases.en: and on the rest of the days of the Festival a person fulfills his obligation even with the lulav of another.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.he: יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חָג שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת, וְשָׁכַח וְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַלּוּלָב לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, פָּטוּר,
phrases.en: the first day of the Festival occurs on Shabbat, and he forgot and carried the lulav out into the public domain, he is exempt

phrases.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוֹצִיאוֹ בִרְשׁוּת:
phrases.en: because he carried it out with permission

phrases.he: מְקַבֶּלֶת אִשָּׁה מִיַּד בְּנָהּ וּמִיַּד בַּעְלָהּ וּמַחֲזִירָתוֹ לַמַּיִם בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: A woman may receive a lulav from her son or from her husband and return it on Shabbat to the water

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בְּשַׁבָּת מַחֲזִירִין, בְּיוֹם טוֹב מוֹסִיפִין, וּבַמּוֹעֵד מַחֲלִיפִין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: On Shabbat one may return the lulav to the water; and on the Festival one may even add fresh water to the vessel so the lulav will not wilt; and during the intermediate days of the Festival, one may even change the water

phrases.he: קָטָן הַיּוֹדֵעַ לְנַעְנֵעַ, חַיָּב בַּלּוּלָב:
phrases.en: A minor who knows how to wave the lulav is obligated in the mitzva of lulav

phrases.he: לוּלָב וַעֲרָבָה, שִׁשָּׁה וְשִׁבְעָה.
phrases.en: The lulav is taken and the altar is encircled together with the willow branch either six or seven days, depending on which day of the Festival occurs on Shabbat.

phrases.he: הַהַלֵּל וְהַשִּׂמְחָה, שְׁמֹנָה.
phrases.en: The obligation to recite the full hallel and the mitzva of rejoicing, i.e., eating the meat of the peace-offering, is in effect for eight days, seven days of Sukkot and the Eighth Day of Assembly.

phrases.he: סֻכָּה וְנִסּוּךְ הַמַּיִם, שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.en: The mitzva of sukka and the ritual of the water libation on the altar are in effect for seven days.

phrases.he: וְהֶחָלִיל, חֲמִשָּׁה וְשִׁשָּׁה:
phrases.en: The flute is played in the Temple for five or six days, depending on which day of the Festival occurs on Shabbat, to enhance the rejoicing on the Festival.

phrases.he: לוּלָב שִׁבְעָה כֵּיצַד,
phrases.en: The lulav is taken for seven days. How so?

phrases.he: יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חָג שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת, לוּלָב שִׁבְעָה,
phrases.en: If the first day of the Festival occurs on Shabbat, the lulav is then taken for seven days.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַיָּמִים, שִׁשָּׁה:
phrases.en: And if the rest of the days of the week, six days.

phrases.he: עֲרָבָה שִׁבְעָה כֵּיצַד,
phrases.en: The willow branch for seven days. How so?

phrases.he: יוֹם שְׁבִיעִי שֶׁל עֲרָבָה שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: If the seventh day of the willow branch occurs on Shabbat,

phrases.he: עֲרָבָה שִׁבְעָה,
phrases.en: the mitzva of the willow branch is then performed for seven days.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַיָּמִים שִׁשָּׁה:
phrases.en: And if the seventh day occurs on one of the rest of the days of the week, and one of the other days of the Festival coincides with Shabbat, since the mitzva of the willow branch is then by rabbinic law and consequently does not override Shabbat, it is performed for only six days.

phrases.he: מִצְוַת לוּלָב כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: How is the mitzva of lulav fulfilled in the Temple when the first day of the Festival occurs on Shabbat?

phrases.he: יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חָג שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת, מוֹלִיכִין אֶת לוּלְבֵיהֶן לְהַר הַבַּיִת,
phrases.en: If the first day of the Festival occurs on Shabbat, all the people bring their lulavim to the Temple Mount on Friday.

phrases.he: וְהַחַזָּנִים מְקַבְּלִין מֵהֶן וְסוֹדְרִין אוֹתָן עַל גַּב הָאִצְטַבָּא, וְהַזְּקֵנִים מַנִּיחִין אֶת שֶׁלָּהֶן בַּלִּשְׁכָּה.
phrases.en: The attendants receive the lulavim from them and arrange them on a bench [itztaba], while the Elders place their lulavim in the chamber.

phrases.he: וּמְלַמְּדִים אוֹתָם לוֹמַר, כָּל מִי שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לוּלָבִי בְיָדוֹ, הֲרֵי הוּא לוֹ בְמַתָּנָה.
phrases.en: And the court teaches the people to say: With regard to anyone whom my lulav reaches his possession, it is his as a gift.

phrases.he: לְמָחָר מַשְׁכִּימִין וּבָאִין, וְהַחַזָּנִים זוֹרְקִין אוֹתָם לִפְנֵיהֶם.
phrases.en: The next day everyone rises early and comes to the Temple, and the attendants throw the lulavim before them.

phrases.he: וְהֵן מְחַטְּפִין וּמַכִּין אִישׁ אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ.
phrases.en: And in the confusion, the people snatch the lulavim and in the process strike one another.

phrases.he: וּכְשֶׁרָאוּ בֵית דִּין שֶׁבָּאוּ לִידֵי סַכָּנָה, הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהֵא כָל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד נוֹטֵל בְּבֵיתוֹ.
phrases.en: And when the court saw that they came to potential danger, they instituted that each and every person will take his lulav in his house and fulfill the mitzva there.

phrases.he: מִצְוַת עֲרָבָה כֵּיצַד,
phrases.en: How is the mitzva of the willow branch fulfilled?

phrases.he: מָקוֹם הָיָה לְמַטָּה מִירוּשָׁלַיִם, וְנִקְרָא מוֹצָא.
phrases.en: There was a place below Jerusalem, and it was called Motza.

phrases.he: יוֹרְדִין לְשָׁם וּמְלַקְּטִין מִשָּׁם מֻרְבִּיּוֹת שֶׁל עֲרָבָה,
phrases.en: They would descend there and gather willow branches [murbiyyot] from there.

phrases.he: וּבָאִין וְזוֹקְפִין אוֹתָן בְּצִדֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.en: And they would then come and stand them upright at the sides of the altar,

phrases.he: וְרָאשֵׁיהֶן כְּפוּפִין עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
phrases.en: and the tops of the branches would be inclined over the top of the altar.

phrases.he: תָּקְעוּ וְהֵרִיעוּ וְתָקָעוּ.
phrases.en: They then sounded a tekia, a simple uninterrupted blast, sounded a terua, a broken sound and/or a series of short staccato blasts, and sounded another tekia.

phrases.he: בְּכָל יוֹם מַקִּיפִין אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ פַּעַם אַחַת, וְאוֹמְרִים, אָנָּא ה' הוֹשִׁיעָה נָּא, אָנָּא ה' הַצְלִיחָה נָּא.
phrases.en: Each day they would circle the altar one time and say: "Lord, please save us. Lord, please grant us success".

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֲנִי וָהוֹ הוֹשִׁיעָה נָּא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says that they would say: Ani vaho, please save us.

phrases.he: וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם מַקִּיפִין אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים.
phrases.en: And on that day, they would circle the altar seven times.

phrases.he: בִּשְׁעַת פְּטִירָתָן, מָה הֵן אוֹמְרִים, יֹפִי לְךָ מִזְבֵּחַ, יֹפִי לְךָ מִזְבֵּחַ.
phrases.en: At the time of their departure at the end of the Festival, what would they say? It is beautiful for you, altar; it is beautiful for you, altar.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, לְיָהּ וּלְךָ, מִזְבֵּחַ. לְיָהּ וּלְךָ, מִזְבֵּחַ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar said that they would say: To the Lord and to you, altar; to the Lord and to you, altar.

phrases.he: כְּמַעֲשֵׂהוּ בְחֹל כָּךְ מַעֲשֵׂהוּ בְשַׁבָּת, אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיוּ מְלַקְּטִין אוֹתָן מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת וּמַנִּיחִים אוֹתָן בְּגִיגִיּוֹת שֶׁל זָהָב, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִכְמֹשׁוּ.
phrases.en: As its performance during the week, so is its performance on Shabbat; except that they would gather the branches from Shabbat eve and place them in basins of gold so that they would not dry.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר, חֲרִיּוֹת שֶׁל דֶּקֶל הָיוּ מְבִיאִין, וְחוֹבְטִין אוֹתָן בַּקַּרְקַע בְּצִדֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם נִקְרָא יוֹם חִבּוּט חֲרִיּוֹת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says: They would bring palm branches to the Temple and place them on the ground at the sides of the altar, and that seventh day of Sukkot was called: The day of the placing of palm branches.

phrases.he: מִיַּד הַתִּינוֹקוֹת שׁוֹמְטִין אֶת לוּלְבֵיהֶן וְאוֹכְלִין אֶתְרוֹגֵיהֶן:
phrases.en: Immediately children remove their lulavim and eat their etrogim

phrases.he: הַהַלֵּל וְהַשִּׂמְחָה שְׁמֹנָה כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: The obligation to recite hallel and the mitzva of rejoicing on the Festival by sacrificing and eating the meat of peace-offerings are always for eight days. How so?

phrases.he: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁחַיָּב אָדָם בַּהַלֵּל וּבַשִּׂמְחָה וּבִכְבוֹד יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חָג, כִּשְׁאָר כָּל יְמוֹת הֶחָג.
phrases.en: This teaches that a person is obligated in hallel, and in the mitzva of rejoicing, and in reverence for the last day of the Festival like he is for all the other days of the Festival.

phrases.he: סֻכָּה שִׁבְעָה כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: The mitzva of sukka is seven days. How does one fulfill this obligation for seven full days?

phrases.he: גָּמַר מִלֶּאֱכֹל, לֹא יַתִּיר סֻכָּתוֹ, אֲבָל מוֹרִיד אֶת הַכֵּלִים מִן הַמִּנְחָה וּלְמַעְלָה, מִפְּנֵי כְבוֹד יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חָג:
phrases.en: When one finished eating on the seventh day, he should not dismantle his sukka immediately, because the obligation continues until the end of the day. However, he takes the vessels down from the sukka into the house from minḥa time and onward in deference to the last day of the Festival, when he will require the vessels in the house.

phrases.he: נִסּוּךְ הַמַּיִם כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: How was the rite of water libation performed?

phrases.he: צְלוֹחִית שֶׁל זָהָב מַחֲזֶקֶת שְׁלשֶׁת לֻגִּים הָיָה מְמַלֵּא מִן הַשִּׁלּוֹחַ.
phrases.en: One would fill a golden jug with a capacity of three log with water from the Siloam pool.

phrases.he: הִגִּיעוּ לְשַׁעַר הַמַּיִם, תָּקְעוּ וְהֵרִיעוּ וְתָקָעוּ.
phrases.en: When those who went to bring the water reached the Gate of the Water, they sounded a tekia, sounded a terua, and sounded another tekia.

phrases.he: עָלָה בַכֶּבֶשׁ וּפָנָה לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ, שְׁנֵי סְפָלִים שֶׁל כֶּסֶף הָיוּ שָׁם.
phrases.en: The priest ascended the ramp of the altar and turned to his left. There were two silver basins there into which he poured the water.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, שֶׁל סִיד הָיוּ, אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיוּ מֻשְׁחָרִין פְּנֵיהֶם מִפְּנֵי הַיָּיִן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda said: They were limestone basins, but they would blacken due to the wine.

phrases.he: וּמְנֻקָּבִין כְּמִין שְׁנֵי חֳטָמִין דַּקִּים, אֶחָד מְעֻבֶּה וְאֶחָד דַּק, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם כָּלִין בְּבַת אַחַת.
phrases.en: The two basins were perforated at the bottom with two thin perforated nose-like protrusions. One of the basins, used for the wine libation, had a perforation that was broad, and one, used for the water libation, had a perforation that was thin, so that the flow of both the water and the wine, which do not have the same viscosity, would conclude simultaneously.

phrases.he: מַעֲרָבִי שֶׁל מַיִם, מִזְרָחִי שֶׁל יָיִן.
phrases.en: The basin to the west of the altar was for water, and the basin to the east of the altar was for wine.

phrases.he: עֵרָה שֶׁל מַיִם לְתוֹךְ שֶׁל יַיִן, וְשֶׁל יַיִן לְתוֹךְ שֶׁל מַיִם, יָצָא.
phrases.en: If one poured the contents of the basin of water into the basin of wine, or the contents of the basin of wine into the basin of water, he fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בְּלֹג הָיָה מְנַסֵּךְ כָּל שְׁמֹנָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: One would pour the water with a vessel that had a capacity of one log on all eight days of the Festival.

phrases.he: וְלַמְנַסֵּךְ אוֹמְרִים לוֹ, הַגְבַּהּ יָדֶךָ, שֶׁפַּעַם אַחַת נִסֵּךְ אֶחָד עַל גַּבֵּי רַגְלָיו, וּרְגָמוּהוּ כָל הָעָם בְּאֶתְרוֹגֵיהֶן.
phrases.en: And the appointee says to the one pouring the water into the silver basin: Raise your hand, as one time a Sadducee priest intentionally poured the water on his feet, and in their rage all the people pelted him with their etrogim.

phrases.he: כְּמַעֲשֵׂהוּ בְחֹל כָּךְ מַעֲשֵׂהוּ בְשַׁבָּת, אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיָה מְמַלֵּא מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת חָבִית שֶׁל זָהָב שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְקֻדֶּשֶׁת, מִן הַשִּׁלּוֹחַ, וּמַנִּיחָהּ בַּלִּשְׁכָּה.
phrases.en: As its performance during the week, so is its performance on Shabbat, except that on Shabbat eve, one would fill a golden barrel that was not consecrated for exclusive use in the Temple from the Siloam pool, and he would place it in the Temple chamber

phrases.he: נִשְׁפְּכָה אוֹ נִתְגַּלְּתָה, הָיָה מְמַלֵּא מִן הַכִּיּוֹר, שֶׁהַיַּיִן וְהַמַּיִם הַמְּגֻלִּין, פְּסוּלִים לְגַבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ:
phrases.en: If the water in the barrel spilled, or if it was exposed overnight, one would fill the jug with water from the basin in the Temple courtyard, as exposed wine or water is unfit for the altar.

phrases.he: הֶחָלִיל חֲמִשָּׁה וְשִׁשָּׁה.
phrases.en: The flute is played on the festival of Sukkot for five or six days.

phrases.he: זֶהוּ הֶחָלִיל שֶׁל בֵּית הַשּׁוֹאֵבָה, שֶׁאֵינָה דּוֹחָה לֹא אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְלֹא אֶת יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.en: This is the flute of the Place of the Drawing of the Water, whose playing overrides neither Shabbat nor the Festival.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ, כָּל מִי שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה שִׂמְחַת בֵּית הַשּׁוֹאֵבָה, לֹא רָאָה שִׂמְחָה מִיָּמָיו:
phrases.en: One who did not see the Celebration of the Place of the Drawing of the Water never saw celebration in his days.

phrases.he: בְּמוֹצָאֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חָג,
phrases.en: At the conclusion of the first Festival day

phrases.he: יָרְדוּ לְעֶזְרַת נָשִׁים,
phrases.en: descended to the Women's Courtyard

phrases.he: וּמְתַקְּנִין שָׁם תִּקּוּן גָּדוֹל.
phrases.en: where they would introduce a significant repair

phrases.he: וּמְנוֹרוֹת שֶׁל זָהָב הָיוּ שָׁם,
phrases.en: There were golden candelabra there

phrases.he: וְאַרְבָּעָה סְפָלִים שֶׁל זָהָב בְּרָאשֵׁיהֶן,
phrases.en: And there were four basins made of gold at the top of each candelabrum

phrases.he: וְאַרְבָּעָה סֻלָּמוֹת לְכָל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד,
phrases.en: And there were four ladders for each and every pole and

phrases.he: וְאַרְבָּעָה יְלָדִים מִפִּרְחֵי כְהֻנָּה וּבִידֵיהֶם כַּדִּים שֶׁל שֶׁמֶן שֶׁל מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים לֹג,
phrases.en: there were four children from the priesthood trainees, and in their hands were pitchers with a capacity of 120 log of oil

phrases.he: שֶׁהֵן מַטִּילִין לְכָל סֵפֶל וָסֵפֶל:
phrases.en: that they would pour into each and every basin

phrases.he: מִבְּלָאֵי מִכְנְסֵי כֹהֲנִים וּמֵהֶמְיָנֵיהֶן מֵהֶן הָיוּ מַפְקִיעִין
phrases.en: From the worn trousers of the priests and their belts they would loosen

phrases.he: וּבָהֶן הָיוּ מַדְלִיקִין
phrases.en: and with them they would light

phrases.he: וְלֹא הָיְתָה חָצֵר בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְאִירָה מֵאוֹר בֵּית הַשּׁוֹאֵבָה
phrases.en: And there was not a courtyard in Jerusalem that was not illuminated from the light of the Place of the Drawing of the Water

phrases.he: חֲסִידִים וְאַנְשֵׁי מַעֲשֶׂה הָיוּ מְרַקְּדִים לִפְנֵיהֶם בַּאֲבוּקוֹת שֶׁל אוֹר שֶׁבִּידֵיהֶן, וְאוֹמְרִים לִפְנֵיהֶן דִּבְרֵי שִׁירוֹת וְתִשְׁבָּחוֹת.
phrases.en: The pious and the men of action would dance before the people who attended the celebration, with flaming torches that they would juggle in their hands, and they would say before them passages of song and praise to God.

phrases.he: וְהַלְוִיִּם בְּכִנּוֹרוֹת וּבִנְבָלִים וּבִמְצִלְתַּיִם וּבַחֲצוֹצְרוֹת וּבִכְלֵי שִׁיר בְּלֹא מִסְפָּר, עַל חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה מַעֲלוֹת הַיּוֹרְדוֹת מֵעֶזְרַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעֶזְרַת נָשִׁים, כְּנֶגֶד חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר שִׁיר הַמַּעֲלוֹת שֶׁבַּתְּהִלִּים, שֶׁעֲלֵיהֶן לְוִיִּים עוֹמְדִין בִּכְלֵי שִׁיר וְאוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה.
phrases.en: And the Levites would play on lyres, harps, cymbals, and trumpets, and countless other musical instruments. The musicians would stand on the fifteen stairs that descend from the Israelites' courtyard to the Women's Courtyard, corresponding to the fifteen Songs of the Ascents in Psalms, i.e., chapters 120–134, and upon which the Levites stand with musical instruments and recite their song.

phrases.he: וְעָמְדוּ שְׁנֵי כֹהֲנִים בַּשַּׁעַר הָעֶלְיוֹן שֶׁיּוֹרֵד מֵעֶזְרַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעֶזְרַת נָשִׁים, וּשְׁתֵּי חֲצוֹצְרוֹת בִּידֵיהֶן.
phrases.en: And Two priests stood at the Upper Gate that descends from the Israelites' courtyard to the Women's Courtyard, with two trumpets in their hands.

phrases.he: קָרָא הַגֶּבֶר, תָּקְעוּ וְהֵרִיעוּ וְתָקָעוּ.
phrases.en: When the rooster crowed at dawn, they sounded a tekia, and sounded a terua, and sounded a tekia.

phrases.he: הִגִּיעוּ לְמַעְלָה עֲשִׂירִית, תָּקְעוּ וְהֵרִיעוּ וְתָקָעוּ.
phrases.en: When they who would draw the water reached the tenth stair the trumpeters sounded a tekia, and sounded a terua, and sounded a tekia, to indicate that the time to draw water from the Siloam pool had arrived.

phrases.he: הִגִּיעוּ לָעֲזָרָה, תָּקְעוּ וְהֵרִיעוּ וְתָקָעוּ.
phrases.en: When they reached the Women's Courtyard with the basins of water in their hands, the trumpeters sounded a tekia, and sounded a terua, and sounded a tekia.

phrases.he: הָיוּ תוֹקְעִין וְהוֹלְכִין, עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעִין לַשַּׁעַר הַיּוֹצֵא מִזְרָח.
phrases.en: They continued sounding the trumpets until they reached the gate through which one exits to the east, from the Women's Courtyard to the eastern slope of the Temple Mount.

phrases.he: הִגִּיעוּ לַשַּׁעַר הַיּוֹצֵא מִמִּזְרָח, הָפְכוּ פְנֵיהֶן לַמַּעֲרָב, וְאָמְרוּ, אֲבוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁהָיוּ בַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה אֲחוֹרֵיהֶם אֶל הֵיכַל ה' וּפְנֵיהֶם קֵדְמָה, וְהֵמָּה מִשְׁתַּחֲוִים קֵדְמָה לַשָּׁמֶשׁ, וְאָנוּ לְיָהּ עֵינֵינוּ.
phrases.en: When they reached the gate through which one exits to the east, they turned from facing east to facing west, toward the Holy of Holies, and said: Our ancestors who were in this place during the First Temple period who did not conduct themselves appropriately, stood "with their backs toward the Sanctuary of the Lord, and their faces toward the east; and they worshipped the sun toward the east" (Ezekiel 8:16), and we, our eyes are to God.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הָיוּ שׁוֹנִין וְאוֹמְרִין, אָנוּ לְיָהּ, וּלְיָהּ עֵינֵינוּ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says that they would repeat and say: We are to God, and our eyes are to God.

phrases.he: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַחַת תְּקִיעוֹת בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ, וְאֵין מוֹסִיפִין עַל אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמֹנֶה.
phrases.en: One sounds no fewer than twenty-one trumpet blasts in the Temple, and one sounds no more than forty-eight.

phrases.he: בְּכָל יוֹם הָיוּ שָׁם עֶשְׂרִים וְאַחַת תְּקִיעוֹת בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ, שָׁלשׁ לִפְתִיחַת שְׁעָרִים, וְתֵשַׁע לְתָמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר, וְתֵשַׁע לְתָמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם.
phrases.en: Each day there were twenty-one trumpet blasts in the Temple: Three blasts were sounded for the opening of the gates in the morning, nine for the daily morning offering, and nine for the daily afternoon offering,

phrases.he: וּבַמּוּסָפִין הָיוּ מוֹסִיפִין עוֹד תֵּשַׁע.
phrases.en: And with the additional offerings they would add nine additional blasts.

phrases.he: וּבְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת הָיוּ מוֹסִיפִין עוֹד שֵׁשׁ, שָׁלשׁ לְהַבְטִיל הָעָם מִמְּלָאכָה, וְשָׁלשׁ לְהַבְדִּיל בֵּין קֹדֶשׁ לְחֹל.
phrases.en: And on Shabbat eve they would add six blasts sounded adjacent to the onset of Shabbat: Three to stop the people from their labor, and three at the onset of Shabbat to demarcate between sacred and profane.

phrases.he: עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ הֶחָג הָיוּ שָׁם אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמֹנֶה, שָׁלשׁ לִפְתִיחַת שְׁעָרִים, שָׁלשׁ לַשַּׁעַר הָעֶלְיוֹן, וְשָׁלשׁ לַשַּׁעַר הַתַּחְתּוֹן, וְשָׁלשׁ לְמִלּוּי הַמַּיִם, וְשָׁלשׁ עַל גַּבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, תֵּשַׁע לְתָמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר, וְתֵשַׁע לְתָמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם, וְתֵשַׁע לַמּוּסָפִין, שָׁלשׁ לְהַבְטִיל אֶת הָעָם מִן הַמְּלָאכָה, וְשָׁלשׁ לְהַבְדִּיל בֵּין קֹדֶשׁ לְחֹל:
phrases.en: On Shabbat eve during the festival there were forty-eight blasts. How so? Three in the morning for the opening of the gates; three for the upper gate; and three for the lower gate; and three for the filling of the vessel with water, and three when pouring the water libation upon the altar; nine for the daily morning offering; and nine for the daily afternoon offering; and nine for the additional offerings; three to stop the people from work; and three more to demarcate between sacred and profane, totaling forty-eight blasts.

phrases.he: יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חָג הָיוּ שָׁם שְׁלשָׁה עָשָׂר פָּרִים, וְאֵילִים שְׁנַיִם, וְשָׂעִיר אֶחָד.
phrases.en: the first Festival day of Sukkot there were thirteen bulls, two rams, and one goat there.

phrases.he: נִשְׁתַּיְּרוּ שָׁם אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר כְּבָשִׂים לִשְׁמֹנֶה מִשְׁמָרוֹת.
phrases.en: Fourteen sheep remained to be divided among the eight remaining watches.

phrases.he: בַּיּוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן, שִׁשָּׁה מַקְרִיבִין שְׁנַיִם שְׁנַיִם, וְהַשְּׁאָר אֶחָד אֶחָד.
phrases.en: On the first day of the Festival, six of the eight remaining watches sacrifice two sheep each for a total of twelve, and the remaining two watches sacrifice one sheep each.

phrases.he: בַּיּוֹם הָשֵּׁנִי, חֲמִשָּׁה מַקְרִיבִין שְׁנַיִם שְׁנַיִם, וְהַשְׁאָר אֶחָד אֶחָד.
phrases.en: On the second day of the Festival, i.e., the first day of the intermediate days, when twelve bulls were sacrificed, fifteen of the priestly watches sacrifice the bulls, rams, and goat, five of the remaining watches sacrifice two sheep each, and the remaining four watches sacrifice one sheep each.

phrases.he: בַּשְּׁלִישִׁי, אַרְבָּעָה מַקְרִיבִין שְׁנַיִם שְׁנַיִם, וְהַשְׁאָר אֶחָד אֶחָד.
phrases.en: On the third day of the Festival, when eleven bulls were sacrificed, fourteen of the priestly watches sacrifice the bulls, rams, and goat, four of the remaining watches sacrifice two sheep each, and the remaining six watches sacrifice one sheep each.

phrases.he: בָּרְבִיעִי, שְׁלשָׁה מַקְרִיבִין שְׁנַיִם שְׁנַיִם, וְהַשְּׁאָר אֶחָד אֶחָד.
phrases.en: On the fourth day of the Festival, when ten bulls were sacrificed, thirteen of the priestly watches sacrifice the bulls, rams, and goat, three of the remaining watches sacrifice two sheep each, and the remaining eight watches sacrifice one sheep each.

phrases.he: בַּחֲמִשִּׁי, שְׁנַיִם מַקְרִיבִין שְׁנַיִם שְׁנַיִם, וְהַשְּׁאָר אֶחָד אֶחָד.
phrases.en: On the fifth day, when nine bulls were sacrificed, twelve watches sacrifice the bulls, rams, and goat, two of the twelve remaining watches sacrifice two sheep each, and the remaining ten watches sacrifice one sheep each.

phrases.he: בַּשִּׁשִּׁי, אֶחָד מַקְרִיב שְׁנַיִם, וְהַשְּׁאָר אֶחָד אֶחָד.
phrases.en: On the sixth day, when eight bulls were sacrificed, eleven watches sacrifice the bulls, rams, and goat, one of the remaining watches sacrifices two sheep, and the remaining twelve watches sacrifice one sheep each.

phrases.he: בַּשְּׁבִיעִי, כֻּלָּן שָׁוִין.
phrases.en: On the seventh day they are all equal and bring one offering each.

phrases.he: בַּשְּׁמִינִי, חָזְרוּ לַפַּיִס כְּבָרְגָלִים.
phrases.en: On the eighth day, when there was a completely different configuration of offerings, they returned to the standard lottery system used to determine which of the priestly watches would sacrifice the offerings, as they did on the other pilgrimage Festivals, which do not have as many offerings as does Sukkot.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ, מִי שֶׁהִקְרִיב פָּרִים הַיּוֹם, לֹא יַקְרִיב לְמָחָר, אֶלָּא חוֹזְרִין חֲלִילָה:
phrases.en: They said about the ordering of the priestly watches: One who sacrificed bulls today will not sacrifice bulls tomorrow; rather, they will sacrifice one of the other types of offerings. They rotate, so that each of the watches will have the opportunity to sacrifice bulls as well as other animals.

phrases.he: בִּשְׁלשָׁה פְרָקִים בַּשָּׁנָה הָיוּ כָּל מִשְׁמָרוֹת שָׁווֹת בְּאֵמוּרֵי הָרְגָלִים וּבְחִלּוּק לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים.
phrases.en: At three times during the year, all twenty-four priestly watches have equal status, in that all receive a share in the Temple service independent of the standard order of the watches and all receive a share in the accompanying gifts of the priesthood: In the portions of the offerings of the Festivals sacrificed on the altar and in the distribution of the shewbread on Shabbat during the Festivals.

phrases.he: בַּעֲצֶרֶת אוֹמְרִים לוֹ, הֵילָךְ מַצָּה הֵילָךְ חָמֵץ.
phrases.en: On Shavuot that coincides with Shabbat, when the two loaves offered on Shavuot would be distributed together with the distribution of the shewbread, the priest charged with the distribution says to each priest: Here is matza from the shewbread for you, and here is leavened bread from the two loaves for you.

phrases.he: מִשְׁמָר שֶׁזְּמַנּוֹ קָבוּעַ, הוּא מַקְרִיב תְּמִידִין, נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת וּשְׁאָר קָרְבְּנוֹת צִבּוּר, וּמַקְרִיב אֶת הַכֹּל.
phrases.en: The principle is that the priestly watch whose time is fixed during the Festival sacrifices the daily offerings during the Festival, as well as vow-offerings, free-will offerings, and all other communal offerings. And that watch sacrifices all of them even during the Festival, when other aspects of the service are shared by all the watches.

phrases.he: יוֹם טוֹב הַסָּמוּךְ לְשַׁבָּת, בֵּין מִלְּפָנֶיהָ בֵּין מִלְּאַחֲרֶיהָ, הָיוּ כָל הַמִּשְׁמָרוֹת שָׁווֹת בְּחִלּוּק לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים:
phrases.en: In the case of a Festival that occurs adjacent to Shabbat, both when it occurs preceding it and when it occurs following it, all the watches that arrived early or remained late to serve in the Temple were of equal status in the distribution of the shewbread on that Shabbat.

phrases.he: חָל לִהְיוֹת יוֹם אֶחָד לְהַפְסִיק בֵּינְתַיִם, מִשְׁמָר שֶׁזְּמַנּוֹ קָבוּעַ, הָיָה נוֹטֵל עֶשֶׂר חַלּוֹת, וְהַמִּתְעַכֵּב נוֹטֵל שְׁתָּיִם.
phrases.en: If one day happened to separate between the Festival and Shabbat, the watch whose time was scheduled would take ten of the twelve loaves of shewbread, and the watch that was detained after the Festival because there was insufficient time to get home before Shabbat takes two loaves.

phrases.he: וּבִשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה, הַנִּכְנָס נוֹטֵל שֵׁשׁ, וְהַיּוֹצֵא נוֹטֵל שֵׁשׁ.
phrases.en: And during the rest of the days of the year, the incoming watch takes six loaves and the outgoing watch takes six loaves.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הַנִּכְנָס נוֹטֵל שֶׁבַע, וְהַיּוֹצֵא נוֹטֵל חָמֵשׁ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: The incoming watch takes seven loaves and the outgoing takes five.

phrases.he: הַנִּכְנָסִין חוֹלְקִין בַּצָּפוֹן, וְהַיּוֹצְאִין בַּדָּרוֹם.
phrases.en: The incoming watch divide the shewbread in the north section of the courtyard, and the outgoing watch in the south.

phrases.he: בִּלְגָּה לְעוֹלָם חוֹלֶקֶת בַּדָּרוֹם, וְטַבַּעְתָּהּ קְבוּעָה, וְחַלּוֹנָהּ סְתוּמָה.
phrases.en: The watch of Bilga always divides the shewbread to its members in the south. And its ring was fixed in place, rendering it useless, and its niche was sealed.

phrases.he: בֵּיצָה שֶׁנּוֹלְדָה בְיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.en: an egg that was laid on a Festival

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, תֵּאָכֵל.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: It may be eaten

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, לֹא תֵאָכֵל.
phrases.en: and Beit Hillel say: It may not be eaten

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, שְׂאֹר בְּכַזַּיִת וְחָמֵץ בְּכַכּוֹתֶבֶת.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: Leaven, i.e., dough that has leavened to such an extent that it is no longer used as food but as a leavening agent for other dough, is prohibited on Passover in the measure of an olive-bulk. However, the measure for edible leavened bread is greater, that of a large date-bulk.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, זֶה וָזֶה בְּכַזָּיִת:
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: For both this and that, the measure is that of an olive-bulk.

phrases.he: הַשּׁוֹחֵט חַיָּה וָעוֹף בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.en: one who slaughters an undomesticated animal or a bird on a Festival

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, יַחְפֹּר בְּדֶקֶר וִיכַסֶּה,
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: He digs with a shovel and covers

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, לֹא יִשְׁחֹט, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיָה לוֹ עָפָר מוּכָן מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם.
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: He may not slaughter unless he had earth prepared while it was still day.

phrases.he: וּמוֹדִים, שֶׁאִם שָׁחַט, שֶׁיַּחְפֹּר בְּדֶקֶר וִיכַסֶּה,
phrases.en: But concede that if one slaughtered, then he should dig with a shovel and cover

phrases.he: שֶׁאֵפֶר כִּירָה מוּכָן הוּא:
phrases.en: that the ashes of a stove are prepared

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אֵין מוֹלִיכִין אֶת הַסֻּלָּם מִשּׁוֹבָךְ לְשׁוֹבָךְ, אֲבָל מַטֵּהוּ מֵחַלּוֹן לְחַלּוֹן.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One may not carry a ladder from one dovecote to another. However, he tilts it from one window to another

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין.
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel permit

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, לֹא יִטֹּל, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִעֲנֵעַ מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One may not take unless he shook while it was still day

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, עוֹמֵד וְאוֹמֵר זֶה וָזֶה אֲנִי נוֹטֵל:
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: stands and says: I take this and that

phrases.he: זִמֵּן שְׁחוֹרִים וּמָצָא לְבָנִים, לְבָנִים וּמָצָא שְׁחוֹרִים, שְׁנַיִם וּמָצָא שְׁלֹשָׁה, אֲסוּרִים.
phrases.en: If one designated black fledglings to be slaughtered and found white ones in the dovecote, rather than the birds he had designated, or if one designated white ones to be slaughtered and found black ones, or if one designated two fledglings to be slaughtered and found three, they are prohibited.

phrases.he: שְׁלֹשָׁה וּמָצָא שְׁנַיִם, מֻתָּרִים.
phrases.en: If one designated three to be slaughtered and found only two, they are permitted.

phrases.he: בְּתוֹךְ הַקֵּן וּמָצָא לִפְנֵי הַקֵּן, אֲסוּרִים.
phrases.en: If one designated them inside the nest and the next day he cannot find them there, and he found fledglings before the nest, they are prohibited.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵין שָׁם אֶלָּא הֵם, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מֻתָּרִים:
phrases.en: But if there are only those fledglings in the immediate vicinity, they are permitted.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אֵין מְסַלְּקִין אֶת הַתְּרִיסִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One may not remove the shutters [terisin] of a store on a Festival

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין אַף לְהַחֲזִיר.
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel permit one not only to open the shutters, but even to replace them.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אֵין נוֹטְלִין אֶת הָעֱלִי לְקַצֵּב עָלָיו בָּשָׂר.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One may not take a large pestle to cut meat on it

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין.
phrases.en: and Beit Hillel permit it.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אֵין נוֹתְנִין אֶת הָעוֹר לִפְנֵי הַדּוֹרְסָן וְלֹא יַגְבִּיהֶנּוּ, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ עִמּוֹ כַזַּיִת בָּשָׂר.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One may not place an unprocessed hide before those who will tread on it, and one may not lift it from its place, unless there is an olive-bulk of meat on it

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין.
phrases.en: and Beit Hillel permit it in both cases.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אֵין מוֹצִיאִין לֹא אֶת הַקָּטָן וְלֹא אֶת הַלּוּלָב וְלֹא אֶת סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One may carry out neither a minor child, nor a lulav, nor a Torah Scroll into the public domain

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין.
phrases.en: and Beit Hillel permit it.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אֵין מוֹלִיכִין חַלָּה וּמַתָּנוֹת לַכֹּהֵן בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One may not bring ḥalla or gifts, to a priest on a Festival,

phrases.he: בֵּין שֶׁהוּרְמוּ מֵאֶמֶשׁ, בֵּין שֶׁהוּרְמוּ מֵהַיּוֹם.
phrases.en: whether they were separated last evening, or whether they were separated today.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין.
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel permit it.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה, חַלָּה וּמַתָּנוֹת מַתָּנָה לַכֹּהֵן, וּתְרוּמָה מַתָּנָה לַכֹּהֵן,
phrases.en: Beit Shammai said to them: This halakha can be derived by an analogy: Ḥalla and gifts are both considered a gift to the priest, and likewise teruma separated from produce is also a gift to the priest.

phrases.he: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין מוֹלִיכִין אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה, כָּךְ אֵין מוֹלִיכִין אֶת הַמַּתָּנוֹת.
phrases.en: Just as you agree that one may not bring teruma to a priest on a Festival, so too, one may not bring the gifts.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל, לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם בַּתְּרוּמָה, שֶׁאֵינוֹ זַכַּאי בַּהֲרָמָתָהּ, תֹּאמְרוּ בַמַּתָּנוֹת, שֶׁזַּכַּאי בַּהֲרָמָתָן:
phrases.en: Beit Hillel said to them: No, if you said that you derive the halakha from teruma, where its separation is not allowed on the Festival, how will you say the same with regard to the gifts from an animal or ḥalla, concerning which their separation is allowed on the Festival?

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, תְּבָלִים נִדּוֹכִין בְּמָדוֹךְ שֶׁל עֵץ.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: Spices may be pounded with a wooden pestle.

phrases.he: וְהַמֶּלַח בְּפַךְ, וּבְעֵץ הַפָּרוּר.
phrases.en: and salt with an earthenware flask or with a wooden pot ladle.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, תְּבָלִים נִדּוֹכִין כְּדַרְכָּן בְּמָדוֹךְ שֶׁל אֶבֶן.
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: Spices may be pounded in their usual manner with a stone pestle.

phrases.he: וְהַמֶּלַח בְּמָדוֹךְ שֶׁל עֵץ.
phrases.en: and salt with a wooden pestle.

phrases.he: הַבּוֹרֵר קִטְנִית בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.en: one who selects legumes on a Festival

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, בּוֹרֵר אֹכֶל וְאוֹכֵל.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: He may select food and eat it immediately

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, בּוֹרֵר כְּדַרְכּוֹ בְּחֵיקוֹ, בְּקָנוֹן וּבְתַמְחוּי,
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: He may select in his usual manner, in his lap, with a tray, or with a large vessel

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא בְטַבְלָא וְלֹא בְנָפָה וְלֹא בִכְבָרָה.
phrases.en: but he may not do so with a tablet, nor with a winnow, nor with a sieve

phrases.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, אַף מֵדִיחַ וְשׁוֹלֶה:
phrases.en: Rabban Gamliel says: One may even wash the legumes in water and skim off the refuse floating on top

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אֵין מְשַׁלְּחִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב אֶלָּא מָנוֹת.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One may send only portions on a Festival,

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מְשַׁלְּחִין בְּהֵמָה חַיָּה וָעוֹף, בֵּין חַיִּין בֵּין שְׁחוּטִין.
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: One may send gifts of domesticated animals, undomesticated animals, and fowl, whether alive or slaughtered.

phrases.he: מְשַׁלְּחִין יֵינוֹת שְׁמָנִים וּסְלָתוֹת וְקִטְנִיּוֹת, אֲבָל לֹא תְבוּאָה,
phrases.en: Similarly, one may send wines, oils, and vessels of flour, and even legumes, but not grain,

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר בִּתְבוּאָה:
phrases.en: And Rabbi Shimon permits sending gifts even in the case of grain,

phrases.he: מְשַׁלְּחִין כֵּלִים, בֵּין תְּפוּרִין בֵּין שֶׁאֵינָן תְּפוּרִין, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן כִּלְאַיִם, וְהֵן לְצֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹעֵד,
phrases.en: One may send clothes, whether they are sewn or whether they are unsewn, and even if they contain diverse kinds, and they serve the purposes of the Festival.

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא סַנְדָּל הַמְסֻמָּר וְלֹא מִנְעָל שֶׁאֵינוֹ תָפוּר.
phrases.en: However, one may not send a spiked sandal, nor an unsewn shoe.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף לֹא מִנְעָל לָבָן, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ אֻמָּן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: One may not even send a white shoe, because it requires an artisan.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כֹּל שֶׁנֵּאוֹתִין בּוֹ, בְּיוֹם טוֹב מְשַׁלְּחִין אוֹתוֹ:
phrases.en: This is the general principle: Anything that one may use on a Festival, one may send it.

phrases.he: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת, לֹא יְבַשֵּׁל אָדָם בַּתְּחִלָּה מִיּוֹם טוֹב לַשַּׁבָּת, אֲבָל מְבַשֵּׁל הוּא לְיוֹם טוֹב, וְאִם הוֹתִיר, הוֹתִיר לַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.en: a Festival that occurs on Shabbat eve, one may not cook on the Festival with the initial intent to cook for Shabbat. However, he may cook for the Festival itself, and if he left over any food, he left it over for Shabbat.

phrases.he: וְעוֹשֶׂה תַבְשִׁיל מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב וְסוֹמֵךְ עָלָיו לַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.en: One may prepare a cooked dish on a Festival eve and rely on it to cook for Shabbat.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, שְׁנֵי תַבְשִׁילִין.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: two cooked dishes,

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, תַּבְשִׁיל אֶחָד.
phrases.en: and Beit Hillel say: One dish is sufficient.

phrases.he: וְשָׁוִין בְּדָג וּבֵיצָה שֶׁעָלָיו שֶׁהֵן שְׁנֵי תַבְשִׁילִין.
phrases.en: And they both agree with regard to a fish and the egg that is fried on it that these are considered two dishes.

phrases.he: אֲכָלוֹ אוֹ שֶׁאָבַד, לֹא יְבַשֵּׁל עָלָיו בַּתְּחִלָּה.
phrases.en: If one ate the food or if it was lost, he may not rely on it and cook with the initial intent to cook for Shabbat.

phrases.he: וְאִם שִׁיֵּר מִמֶּנּוּ כָל שֶׁהוּא, סוֹמֵךְ עָלָיו לַשַּׁבָּת:
phrases.en: If he left any part of the eiruv, he may rely on it for Shabbat.

phrases.he: חָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.en: occurs directly after Shabbat,

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מַטְבִּילִין אֶת הַכֹּל מִלִּפְנֵי הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One must immerse everything before Shabbat,

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, כֵּלִים מִלִּפְנֵי הַשַּׁבָּת, וְאָדָם בַּשַּׁבָּת:
phrases.en: and Beit Hillel say: Vessels must be immersed before Shabbat, but a person may immerse himself even on Shabbat.

phrases.he: וְשָׁוִין שֶׁמַּשִּׁיקִין אֶת הַמַּיִם בִּכְלִי אֶבֶן לְטַהֲרָן,
phrases.en: And Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel both agree that one may bring ritually impure water into contact with ritually pure water in stone vessels in order to purify the water.

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא מַטְבִּילִין.
phrases.en: However, one may not immerse the impure water in a ritually impure vessel in order to purify the vessel at the same time.

phrases.he: וּמַטְבִּילִין מִגַּב לְגַב וּמֵחֲבוּרָה לַחֲבוּרָה:
phrases.en: Likewise, one may immerse on a Festival from one principle to another, and from one group to another,

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מְבִיאִין שְׁלָמִים וְאֵין סוֹמְכִין עֲלֵיהֶן, אֲבָל לֹא עוֹלוֹת.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One may bring peace-offerings but one may not place his hands on them. However, one may not bring burnt-offerings.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מְבִיאִין שְׁלָמִים וְעוֹלוֹת וְסוֹמְכִין עֲלֵיהֶם:
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: One may bring peace-offerings and burnt-offerings, and one may place his hands on them.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, לֹא יָחֵם אָדָם חַמִּין לְרַגְלָיו, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן רְאוּיִים לִשְׁתִיָּה.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: A person may not heat water to wash his feet unless it is fit for drinking,

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין.
phrases.en: But Beit Hillel permit

phrases.he: עוֹשֶׂה אָדָם מְדוּרָה וּמִתְחַמֵּם כְּנֶגְדָּהּ.
phrases.en: A person may kindle a fire and warm himself at it.

phrases.he: שְׁלשָׁה דְבָרִים רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מַחֲמִיר כְּדִבְרֵי בֵית שַׁמַּאי,
phrases.en: Rabban Gamliel was stringent about three things in accordance with the statement of Beit Shammai:

phrases.he: אֵין טוֹמְנִין אֶת הַחַמִּין מִיּוֹם טוֹב לַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.en: One may not insulate hot food on a Festival for Shabbat ab initio,

phrases.he: וְאֵין זוֹקְפִין אֶת הַמְּנוֹרָה בְיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.en: and one may not set up a metal candelabrum that fell on a Festival;

phrases.he: וְאֵין אוֹפִין פִּתִּין גְּרִיצִין אֶלָּא רְקִיקִין.
phrases.en: and one may not bake thick loaves but only thin ones,

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, מִימֵיהֶן שֶׁל בֵּית אַבָּא לֹא הָיוּ אוֹפִין פִּתִּין גְּרִיצִין, אֶלָּא רְקִיקִין.
phrases.en: Rabban Gamliel said: From the days of my father's household they would never bake thick loaves but only thin ones.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, מַה נַּעֲשֶׂה לְבֵית אָבִיךָ, שֶׁהָיוּ מַחֲמִירִין עַל עַצְמָן וּמְקִלִּין לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל, לִהְיוֹת אוֹפִין פִּתִּין גְּרִיצִין וְחֹרִי:
phrases.en: The Sages said to him: What shall we do for your father's household, who were stringent with themselves but lenient with all of the Jewish people, to allow them to bake thick loaves and cakes baked on coals.

phrases.he: אַף הוּא אָמַר שְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים לְהָקֵל,
phrases.en: also said three things as leniencies,

phrases.he: מְכַבְּדִין בֵּין הַמִּטּוֹת,
phrases.en: One may sweep the room of the couches

phrases.he: וּמַנִּיחִין אֶת הַמֻּגְמָר בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.en: And one may place incense on a Festival.

phrases.he: וְעוֹשִׂין גְּדִי מְקֻלָּס בְּלֵילֵי פְסָחִים.
phrases.en: And one may prepare a whole kid on the night of Passover,

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִין:
phrases.en: the Rabbis prohibit

phrases.he: שְׁלשָׁה דְבָרִים רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה מַתִּיר, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִין.
phrases.en: three things that Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya permits and the Rabbis prohibit

phrases.he: פָּרָתוֹ יוֹצְאָה בִרְצוּעָה שֶׁבֵּין קַרְנֶיהָ,
phrases.en: His cow would go out with a decorative strap between its horns

phrases.he: וּמְקָרְדִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בְיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.en: And one may comb an animal on a Festival

phrases.he: וְשׁוֹחֲקִין אֶת הַפִּלְפְּלִין בָּרֵחַיִם שֶׁלָּהֶם.
phrases.en: And one may grind pepper in its own mill

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֵין מְקָרְדִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בְיוֹם טוֹב, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה חַבּוּרָה, אֲבָל מְקַרְצְפִין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: One may not comb an animal on a Festival because this creates a wound, but one may brush it

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵין מְקָרְדִין, אַף לֹא מְקַרְצְפִין:
phrases.en: But the Rabbis say: One may not comb, nor may one even brush

phrases.he: הָרֵחַיִם שֶׁל פִּלְפְּלִין טְמֵאָה,
phrases.en: The pepper mill is susceptible to ritual impurity

phrases.he: מִשּׁוּם שְׁלשָׁה כֵלִים,
phrases.en: because of three vessels

phrases.he: מִשּׁוּם כְּלִי קִבּוּל,
phrases.en: because it is a receptacle

phrases.he: וּמִשּׁוּם כְּלִי מַתָּכוֹת,
phrases.en: and because it is a metal vessel

phrases.he: וּמִשּׁוּם כְּלִי כְבָרָה:
phrases.en: and because it is a sieve

phrases.he: עֲגָלָה שֶׁל קָטָן טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס
phrases.en: A child's wagon is susceptible to ritual impurity imparted by treading.

phrases.he: וְנִטֶּלֶת בְּשַׁבָּת
phrases.en: And may be handled on Shabbat

phrases.he: וְאֵינָהּ נִגְרֶרֶת אֶלָּא עַל גַּבֵּי כֵלִים
phrases.en: And it may be dragged only upon cloth

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.he: כָּל הַכֵּלִים אֵין נִגְרָרִין חוּץ מִן הָעֲגָלָה
phrases.en: no vessels may be dragged except for a wagon

phrases.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא כוֹבֶשֶׁת
phrases.en: because it presses the earth down

phrases.he: אֵין צָדִין דָּגִים מִן הַבֵּיבָרִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.en: One may not trap fish from their ponds on a Festival

phrases.he: וְאֵין נוֹתְנִין לִפְנֵיהֶם מְזוֹנוֹת.
phrases.en: Nor may one place food before them

phrases.he: אֲבָל צָדִין חַיָּה וָעוֹף מִן הַבֵּיבָרִין.
phrases.en: However, one may trap an animal or a bird from their enclosures [beivarim]

phrases.he: וְנוֹתְנִין לִפְנֵיהֶם מְזוֹנוֹת.
phrases.en: And one may also place food before them

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, לֹא כָל הַבֵּיבָרִין שָׁוִין.
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: Not all enclosures are identical

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל הַמְחֻסָּר צִידָה אָסוּר.
phrases.en: This is the principle: With regard to any animal inside such an enclosure whose trapping is inadequate, it is prohibited

phrases.he: וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מְחֻסָּר צִידָה מֻתָּר.
phrases.en: and with regard to any animal whose trapping is not inadequate, it is permitted

phrases.he: מְצוּדוֹת חַיָּה וָעוֹף וְדָגִים שֶׁעֲשָׂאָן מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב, לֹא יִטֹּל מֵהֶן בְּיוֹם טוֹב, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁנִּצּוֹדוּ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.en: Traps for animals, birds, and fish were set on the eve of a Festival, one may not take anything from them on the Festival, unless he knows that the animals found in the traps had already been caught on the eve of the Festival.

phrases.he: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְנָכְרִי אֶחָד, שֶׁהֵבִיא דָגִים לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, וְאָמַר, מֻתָּרִין הֵן, אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין רְצוֹנִי לְקַבֵּל הֵימֶנּוּ.
phrases.en: And an incident is related where a certain gentile brought fish to Rabban Gamliel, and the latter said: The fish are permitted, but I do not wish to accept them from him.

phrases.he: בְּהֵמָה מְסֻכֶּנֶת לֹא יִשְׁחֹט, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ שָׁהוּת בַּיּוֹם לֶאֱכֹל מִמֶּנָּה כַּזַּיִת צָלִי.
phrases.en: an animal is in danger of dying, he may not slaughter it on a Festival unless there is still time in the day for him to eat an olive-bulk of roasted meat from the animal

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ כַזַּיִת חַי מִבֵּית טְבִיחָתָהּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: even if there is only time to eat an olive-bulk of raw meat from the place where the animal is slaughtered

phrases.he: שְׁחָטָהּ בַּשָּׂדֶה, לֹא יְבִיאֶנָּה בְמוֹט וּבְמוֹטָה.
phrases.en: If one slaughtered an animal on a Festival in the field, he may not bring it on a pole or on a set of poles

phrases.he: אֲבָל מֵבִיא בְיָדוֹ אֵבָרִים אֵבָרִים:
phrases.en: Rather, he must alter his usual weekday manner of performing this action and bring it in by hand, limb by limb

phrases.he: בְּכוֹר שֶׁנָּפַל לְבוֹר,
phrases.en: a firstborn animal fell into a cistern

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.he: יֵרֵד מֻמְחֶה וְיִרְאֶה,
phrases.en: An expert goes down and examines

phrases.he: אִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ מוּם, יַעֲלֶה וְיִשְׁחֹט.
phrases.en: If it has a permanent blemish, he may raise it and slaughter it

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, לֹא יִשְׁחֹט.
phrases.en: but if it does not have a blemish, he may not slaughter it

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.he: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין מוּמוֹ נִכָּר מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם, אֵין זֶה מִן הַמּוּכָן:
phrases.en: any firstborn animal whose blemish is not perceptible while it is still day, is not considered to be among the animals prepared

phrases.he: בְּהֵמָה שֶׁמֵּתָה, לֹא יְזִיזֶנָּה מִמְּקוֹמָהּ.
phrases.en: an animal that died, one may not move it from its place

phrases.he: וּמַעֲשֶׂה וְשָׁאֲלוּ אֶת רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן עָלֶיהָ וְעַל הַחַלָּה שֶׁנִּטְמְאָה,
phrases.en: And such an incident once occurred and they asked Rabbi Tarfon about it. And about halla that had been separated from dough and then became ritually impure

phrases.he: וְנִכְנַס לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ וְשָׁאַל,
phrases.en: Rabbi Tarfon entered the study hall and inquired

phrases.he: וְאָמְרוּ לוֹ, לֹא יְזִיזֵם מִמְּקוֹמָם:
phrases.en: and the Sages said to him: One may not move them from their place.

phrases.he: אֵין נִמְנִין עַל הַבְּהֵמָה לְכַתְּחִלָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.en: One may not register to have a portion of an animal on a Festival ab initio,

phrases.he: אֲבָל נִמְנִין עָלֶיהָ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב וְשׁוֹחֲטִין וּמְחַלְּקִין בֵּינֵיהֶן.
phrases.en: But one may register for the animal on the eve of the Festival, and then those who registered for the animal may slaughter and divide it between them on the Festival itself in accordance with the agreement reached the day before.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, שׁוֹקֵל אָדָם בָּשָׂר כְּנֶגֶד הַכְּלִי אוֹ כְנֶגֶד הַקּוֹפִיץ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: A person may weigh the meat against a vessel or against a cleaver [kofitz]

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵין מַשְׁגִּיחִין בְּכַף מֹאזְנַיִם כָּל עִקָּר:
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: One may not look at the pans of a balance scale at all,

phrases.he: אֵין מַשְׁחִיזִין אֶת הַסַּכִּין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.en: One may not sharpen a knife on a Festival in the ordinary weekday manner.

phrases.he: אֲבָל מַשִּׂיאָהּ עַל גַּבֵּי חֲבֶרְתָּהּ.
phrases.en: However, one may do so in an unusual fashion, e.g., to run one knife over another, thereby sharpening the blade.

phrases.he: לֹא יֹאמַר אָדָם לַטַּבָּח, שְׁקוֹל לִי בְדִינָר בָּשָׂר.
phrases.en: A person may not say to a butcher on a Festival: Weigh for me a dinar's worth of meat, since if he mentions a sum of money, it looks like a commercial transaction.

phrases.he: אֲבָל שׁוֹחֵט וּמְחַלְּקִים בֵּינֵיהֶן:
phrases.en: But the butcher may slaughter an animal and apportion it among his customers without stipulating a price.

phrases.he: אוֹמֵר אָדָם לַחֲבֵרוֹ, מַלֵּא לִי כְלִי זֶה, אֲבָל לֹא בַמִּדָּה.
phrases.en: One person may say to another on a Festival: Fill this vessel for me, but he may not ask him to fill the vessel in a particular measure.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם הָיָה כְלִי שֶׁל מִדָּה, לֹא יְמַלְאֶנּוּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: If it was a measuring utensil, he may not fill it.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בְאַבָּא שָׁאוּל בֶּן בָּטְנִית, שֶׁהָיָה מְמַלֵּא מִדּוֹתָיו מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב וְנוֹתְנָן לַלָּקוֹחוֹת בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.en: There was an incident involving Abba Shaul ben Botnit, a Sage who was also a grocer, who would fill his measures on the eve of a Festival and give them to his customers on the Festival.

phrases.he: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר, אַף בַּמּוֹעֵד עוֹשֶׂה כֵן, מִפְּנֵי בֵרוּרֵי הַמִּדּוֹת.
phrases.en: Abba Shaul, a Sage distinct from Abba Shaul ben Botnit, says: He would do this even on the intermediate days of a Festival because of the clarity of the measures.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אַף בְּחֹל עוֹשֶׂה כֵן, מִפְּנֵי מִצּוּי הַמִּדּוֹת.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: Even on a weekday it is proper to do so, because of the draining of the measures.

phrases.he: הוֹלֵךְ אָדָם אֵצֶל חֶנְוָנִי הָרָגִיל אֶצְלוֹ, וְאוֹמֵר לוֹ, תֵּן לִי בֵּיצִים וֶאֱגוֹזִים בְּמִנְיָן, שֶׁכֵּן דֶּרֶךְ בַּעַל הַבַּיִת לִהְיוֹת מוֹנֶה בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ:
phrases.en: A person may go on a Festival to a grocer from whom he is accustomed to buy and say to him: Give me eggs and nuts of such-and-such a number, as it is the manner of a homeowner to count this way in his own house.

phrases.he: הַמֵּבִיא כַדֵּי יַיִן מִמָּקוֹם לְמָקוֹם, לֹא יְבִיאֵם בְּסַל וּבְקֻפָּה,
phrases.en: One who brings wine jugs from one place to another place may not bring them in a basket or in a tub

phrases.he: אֲבָל מֵבִיא הוּא עַל כְּתֵפוֹ אוֹ לְפָנָיו.
phrases.en: but he may bring on his shoulder or in front of himself

phrases.he: וְכֵן הַמּוֹלִיךְ אֶת הַתֶּבֶן, לֹא יַפְשִׁיל אֶת הַקֻּפָּה לַאֲחוֹרָיו,
phrases.en: Similarly, one who brings straw may not place the tub behind him

phrases.he: אֲבָל מְבִיאָהּ הוּא בְיָדוֹ.
phrases.en: but he may transport it in his hand

phrases.he: וּמַתְחִילִין בַּעֲרֵמַת הַתֶּבֶן,
phrases.en: And one may begin from the pile of straw

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא בָעֵצִים שֶׁבַּמֻּקְצֶה:
phrases.en: but one may not begin to take from the wood in the storage

phrases.he: אֵין נוֹטְלִין עֵצִים מִן הַסֻּכָּה, אֶלָּא מִן הַסָּמוּךְ לָהּ.
phrases.en: One may not take wood from a sukka but one may take from near it.

phrases.he: מְבִיאִין עֵצִים מִן הַשָּׂדֶה מִן הַמְכֻנָּס, וּמִן הַקַּרְפֵּף אֲפִלּוּ מִן הַמְפֻזָּר.
phrases.en: One may bring wood from a field from that which has been gathered and from a karpef even from the scattered.

phrases.he: אֵיזֶהוּ קַרְפֵּף, כֹּל שֶׁסָּמוּךְ לָעִיר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: What is a karpef? Any that is near a city, the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, כֹּל שֶׁנִּכְנָסִין לוֹ בְפוֹתַחַת, וַאֲפִלּוּ בְתוֹךְ תְּחוּם שַׁבָּת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: Any into which one can enter with a key, even if it is within the Shabbat limit.

phrases.he: אֵין מְבַקְּעִין עֵצִים, לֹא מִן הַקּוֹרוֹת, וְלֹא מִן הַקּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה בְיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.en: One may not chop wood neither from beams nor from a beam that broke on a Festival

phrases.he: וְאֵין מְבַקְּעִין לֹא בְקַרְדֹּם וְלֹא בִמְגֵרָה וְלֹא בְמַגָּל, אֶלָּא בְקוֹפִיץ.
phrases.en: And one may not chop neither with an ax, nor with a saw, nor with a sickle, rather, one may chop only with a cleaver

phrases.he: בַּיִת שֶׁהוּא מָלֵא פֵרוֹת, סָתוּם וְנִפְחַת, נוֹטֵל מִמְּקוֹם הַפְּחָת.
phrases.en: a house that is filled with produce and locked and a hole formed one may remove produce through the place of the hole

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, אַף פּוֹחֵת לְכַתְּחִלָּה וְנוֹטֵל:
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: One may even make a hole ab initio and take

phrases.he: אֵין פּוֹתְחִין אֶת הַנֵּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה כְלִי.
phrases.en: one may not hollow out a piece of clay to form a lamp into which he will place oil and a wick because he thereby creates a vessel.

phrases.he: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין פֶּחָמִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.en: And similarly, one may not produce charcoal on a Festival

phrases.he: וְאֵין חוֹתְכִין אֶת הַפְּתִילָה לִשְׁנַיִם.
phrases.en: And similarly, one may not cut the wick

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, חוֹתְכָהּ בָּאוּר לִשְׁתֵּי נֵרוֹת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: he may cut it by burning it in a fire

phrases.he: אֵין שׁוֹבְרִין אֶת הַחֶרֶס,
phrases.en: One may not break earthenware on a Festival.

phrases.he: וְאֵין חוֹתְכִין אֶת הַנְּיָר לִצְלוֹת בּוֹ מָלִיחַ,
phrases.en: And one may not cut paper in order to roast salted fish on it.

phrases.he: וְאֵין גּוֹרְפִין תַּנּוּר וְכִירַיִם,
phrases.en: And one may not sweep out anything that has fallen into an oven or stove

phrases.he: אֲבָל מְכַבְּשִׁין,
phrases.en: But one may press down

phrases.he: וְאֵין מַקִּיפִין שְׁתֵּי חָבִיּוֹת לִשְׁפֹּת עֲלֵיהֶן אֶת הַקְּדֵרָה,
phrases.en: And one may not draw two barrels together in order to place a pot on them,

phrases.he: וְאֵין סוֹמְכִין אֶת הַקְּדֵרָה בְבַקַּעַת,
phrases.en: And one may not prop a pot with a piece of wood,

phrases.he: וְכֵן בְּדֶלֶת,
phrases.en: And similarly, with a door.

phrases.he: וְאֵין מַנְהִיגִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בְמַקֵּל בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.en: And one may not lead an animal with a stick on a Festival;

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר:
phrases.en: and Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, permits it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.he: נוֹטֵל אָדָם קֵיסָם מִשֶּׁלְּפָנָיו לַחֲצֹץ בּוֹ שִׁנָּיו.
phrases.en: a person may remove a sliver from a pile of straw or from similar material that is before him, in order to clean with it between his teeth.

phrases.he: וּמְגַבֵּב מִן הֶחָצֵר וּמַדְלִיק,
phrases.en: And he may collect straw from a courtyard and kindle it,

phrases.he: שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁבֶּחָצֵר מוּכָן הוּא.
phrases.en: for anything in a courtyard is considered prepared for all purposes.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים,
phrases.en: The Rabbis say:

phrases.he: מְגַבֵּב מִשֶּׁלְּפָנָיו וּמַדְלִיק:
phrases.en: He may collect these materials only from things placed before him in his house, as they are certainly prepared for all uses, and kindle them.

phrases.he: אֵין מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הָאוּר לֹא מִן הָעֵצִים,
phrases.en: One may not produce fire, neither from wood,

phrases.he: וְלֹא מִן הָאֲבָנִים,
phrases.en: nor from stones

phrases.he: וְלֹא מִן הֶעָפָר,
phrases.en: nor from hot dirt; nor from tiles

phrases.he: וְלֹא מִן הַמַּיִם,
phrases.en: nor from water

phrases.he: וְאֵין מְלַבְּנִין אֶת הָרְעָפִים לִצְלוֹת בָּהֶן.
phrases.en: And similarly, one may not whiten tiles with a burning-hot heat in order to roast upon them afterward.

phrases.he: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר,
phrases.en: And Rabbi Eliezer further stated the following leniency:

phrases.he: עוֹמֵד אָדָם עַל הַמֻּקְצֶה עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בַּשְּׁבִיעִית,
phrases.en: A person may stand over objects in storage, such as produce that he has for some reason previously set aside from use, on Shabbat eve during the Sabbatical Year, during which no tithes are separated, which means one may take fruit on the following day without the need for any corrective measure,

phrases.he: וְאוֹמֵר, מִכָּאן אֲנִי אוֹכֵל לְמָחָר.
phrases.en: and say: From here, from these fruits, I will eat tomorrow.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, עַד שֶׁיִּרְשֹׁם וְיֹאמַר, מִכָּאן וְעַד כָּאן:
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: He may not eat unless he marks the pile of fruit the day before and explicitly says: From here to there I will take.

phrases.he: מַשִּׁילִין פֵּרוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֲרֻבָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב, אֲבָל לֹא בְשַׁבָּת,
phrases.en: One may lower produce through a skylight on a Festival, however, not on Shabbat.

phrases.he: וּמְכַסִּים פֵּרוֹת בְּכֵלִים מִפְּנֵי הַדֶּלֶף,
phrases.en: And one may cover produce with cloths due to a leak

phrases.he: וְכֵן כַּדֵּי יַיִן וְכַדֵּי שֶׁמֶן.
phrases.en: and similarly jugs of wine and jugs of oil

phrases.he: וְנוֹתְנִין כְּלִי תַּחַת הַדֶּלֶף בְּשַׁבָּת:
phrases.en: And one may place a vessel beneath a leak on Shabbat,

phrases.he: כֹּל שֶׁחַיָּבִין עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת, מִשּׁוּם רְשׁוּת, מִשּׁוּם מִצְוָה, בְּשַׁבָּת, חַיָּבִין עָלָיו בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.en: Any act for which one is liable due to a rabbinic decree made to enhance the character of Shabbat as a day of rest [shevut]; or if it is notable because it is optional, i.e., it involves an aspect of a mitzva but is not a complete mitzva; or if it is notable because it is a full-fledged mitzva, if it is prohibited on Shabbat, one is liable for it on a Festival as well.

phrases.he: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת, לֹא עוֹלִין בָּאִילָן, וְלֹא רוֹכְבִין עַל גַּבֵּי בְהֵמָה, וְלֹא שָׁטִין עַל פְּנֵי הַמַּיִם, וְלֹא מְטַפְּחִין, וְלֹא מְסַפְּקִין, וְלֹא מְרַקְּדִין.
phrases.en: And these are the acts prohibited by the Sages as shevut: One may not climb a tree on Shabbat, nor ride on an animal, nor swim in the water, nor clap his hands together, nor clap his hand on the thigh, nor dance.

phrases.he: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן מִשּׁוּם רְשׁוּת, לֹא דָנִין, וְלֹא מְקַדְּשִׁין, וְלֹא חוֹלְצִין, וְלֹא מְיַבְּמִין.
phrases.en: And the following are acts that are prohibited on Shabbat and are notable because they are optional, i.e., which involve an aspect of a mitzva but are not complete mitzvot: One may not judge, nor betroth a woman, nor perform ḥalitza, which is done in lieu of levirate marriage, nor perform levirate marriage.

phrases.he: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן מִשּׁוּם מִצְוָה, לֹא מַקְדִּישִׁין, וְלֹא מַעֲרִיכִין, וְלֹא מַחֲרִימִין, וְלֹא מַגְבִּיהִין תְּרוּמָה וּמַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.en: And the following are prohibited on Shabbat despite the fact that they are notable because of the full-fledged mitzva involved in them: One may not consecrate, nor take a valuation vow, nor consecrate objects for use by the priests or the Temple, nor separate teruma and tithes from produce.

phrases.he: כָּל אֵלּוּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב אָמְרוּ, קַל וָחֹמֶר בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: The Sages spoke of all these acts being prohibited even with regard to a Festival; all the more so are they prohibited on Shabbat.

phrases.he: אֵין בֵּין יוֹם טוֹב לְשַׁבָּת אֶלָּא אֹכֶל נֶפֶשׁ בִּלְבָד:
phrases.en: There is no difference between a Festival and Shabbat, except for work involving preparation of food alone, which is permitted on a Festival but prohibited on Shabbat.

phrases.he: הַבְּהֵמָה וְהַכֵּלִים כְּרַגְלֵי הַבְּעָלִים.
phrases.en: The status of animals and vessels on Festivals is as the feet of their owner, meaning that one's animals and vessels are governed by his own travel limitations on Shabbat and Festivals.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹסֵר בְּהֶמְתּוֹ לִבְנוֹ אוֹ לְרוֹעֶה, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ כְרַגְלֵי הַבְּעָלִים.
phrases.en: In the case of one who delivers his animal to his son or to a shepherd before the Festival to care for it, these are as the feet of the owner, rather than those of the son or the shepherd.

phrases.he: כֵּלִים הַמְיֻחָדִין לְאַחַד מִן הָאַחִין שֶׁבַּבַּיִת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ כְרַגְלָיו.
phrases.en: Vessels that have been inherited by several brothers and have not been divided among them but are still owned jointly, if they are designated for the use of one of the brothers in the house and the other brothers have no part in them, these are as his feet, and they are subject to his travel limitations.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁאֵין מְיֻחָדִין, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ כִמְקוֹם שֶׁהוֹלְכִין:
phrases.en: And as for those that are not designated for any particular brother, these are as a place where they may all go.

phrases.he: הַשּׁוֹאֵל כְּלִי מֵחֲבֵרוֹ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב, כְּרַגְלֵי הַשּׁוֹאֵל.
phrases.en: One who borrows a vessel from another on the eve of a Festival, it is as the feet of the borrower

phrases.he: בְּיוֹם טוֹב, כְּרַגְלֵי הַמַּשְׁאִיל.
phrases.en: on the Festival itself, it is as the feet of the lender

phrases.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁשָּׁאֲלָה מֵחֲבֶרְתָּהּ תְּבָלִין וּמַיִם וּמֶלַח לְעִסָּתָהּ, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ כְרַגְלֵי שְׁתֵּיהֶן.
phrases.en: a woman who borrowed spices from another to put in a dish, or water and salt to put in her dough, these are as the feet of both of them

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה פוֹטֵר בְּמַיִם, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן מַמָּשׁ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda exempts in the case of water, because it has no substance

phrases.he: הַגַּחֶלֶת כְּרַגְלֵי הַבְּעָלִים, וְשַׁלְהֶבֶת בְּכָל מָקוֹם.
phrases.en: A coal that one borrowed from another on the Festival is as the feet of the owner, and it may be carried on the Festival to any place where its owner may walk. Since it has substance, it is associated with its owner. But a flame that one lit from another's flame may be taken anywhere, as it has no substance.

phrases.he: גַּחֶלֶת שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ מוֹעֲלִין בָּהּ, וְשַׁלְהֶבֶת לֹא נֶהֱנִין וְלֹא מוֹעֲלִין.
phrases.en: If one uses a coal of consecrated property for a non-consecrated purpose, he is liable for misuse of consecrated property, since it has substance. But if one uses a consecrated flame, although according to rabbinic law one may not derive benefit from it ab initio, if one did benefit from it, he is not liable for misuse, since it does not have substance.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹצִיא גַחֶלֶת לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: One who takes out a coal from a private domain to the public domain on Shabbat is liable for the prohibited labor of carrying,

phrases.he: וְשַׁלְהֶבֶת, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: but one who takes out a flame is exempt.

phrases.he: בּוֹר שֶׁל יָחִיד, כְּרַגְלֵי הַיָּחִיד.
phrases.en: With regard to a cistern of an individual, water drawn from it is as the feet of the individual who owns the cistern, and the water may be carried only to those places where its owner is permitted to walk.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל אַנְשֵׁי אוֹתָהּ הָעִיר, כְּרַגְלֵי אַנְשֵׁי אוֹתָהּ הָעִיר.
phrases.en: And water drawn from a cistern belonging jointly to all the people dwelling in a particular town is as the feet of the people of that town.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל עוֹלֵי בָבֶל, כְּרַגְלֵי הַמְמַלֵּא:
