phrases.en: On the seventeenth of Tammuz the tablets were broken by Moses when he saw that the Jews had made the golden calf; the daily offering was nullified by the Roman authorities and was never sacrificed again; the city walls of Jerusalem were breached; the general Apostemos publicly burned a Torah scroll; and Manasseh placed an idol in the Sanctuary.

phrases.he: בְּתִשְׁעָה בְאָב נִגְזַר עַל אֲבוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּנְסוּ לָאָרֶץ, וְחָרַב הַבַּיִת בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה וּבַשְּׁנִיָּה, וְנִלְכְּדָה בֵיתָר, וְנֶחְרְשָׁה הָעִיר.
phrases.en: On the Ninth of Av it was decreed upon our ancestors that they would all die in the wilderness and not enter Eretz Yisrael; and the Temple was destroyed the first time, in the days of Nebuchadnezzar, and the second time, by the Romans; and Beitar was captured; and the city of Jerusalem was plowed, as a sign that it would never be rebuilt.

phrases.he: מִשֶּׁנִּכְנַס אָב, מְמַעֲטִין בְּשִׂמְחָה:
phrases.en: from when the month of Av begins, one decreases acts of rejoicing.

phrases.he: שַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל תִּשְׁעָה בְאָב לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹכָהּ, אָסוּר מִלְּסַפֵּר וּמִלְּכַבֵּס,
phrases.en: the week in which the Ninth of Av occurs, it is prohibited to cut one's hair and to launder clothes

phrases.he: וּבַחֲמִישִׁי מֻתָּרִין מִפְּנֵי כְבוֹד הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.en: but if the Ninth of Av occurs on a Friday, on Thursday these actions are permitted in deference to Shabbat.

phrases.he: עֶרֶב תִּשְׁעָה בְאָב לֹא יֹאכַל אָדָם שְׁנֵי תַבְשִׁילִין,
phrases.en: the eve of the Ninth of Av a person may not eat two cooked dishes

phrases.he: לֹא יֹאכַל בָּשָׂר וְלֹא יִשְׁתֶּה יָיִן.
phrases.en: neither eat meat nor drink wine

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, יְשַׁנֶּה.
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: One must adjust

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְחַיֵּב בִּכְפִיַּת הַמִּטָּה,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda obligates one to overturn the bed

phrases.he: וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים:
phrases.en: but the Rabbis did not agree with him.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, לֹא הָיוּ יָמִים טוֹבִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב וּכְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, שֶׁבָּהֶן בְּנוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם יוֹצְאוֹת בִּכְלֵי לָבָן שְׁאוּלִין, שֶׁלֹּא לְבַיֵּשׁ אֶת מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: There were no days as joyous for the Jewish people as the fifteenth of Av and as Yom Kippur, as on them the daughters of Jerusalem would go out in white clothes, which each woman borrowed from another. Why were they borrowed? They did this so as not to embarrass one who did not have her own white garments.

phrases.he: כָּל הַכֵּלִים טְעוּנִין טְבִילָה.
phrases.en: All the garments that the women borrowed require immersion, as those who previously wore them might have been ritually impure.

phrases.he: וּבְנוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם יוֹצְאוֹת וְחוֹלוֹת בַּכְּרָמִים.
phrases.en: And the daughters of Jerusalem would go out and dance in the vineyards.

phrases.he: וּמֶה הָיוּ אוֹמְרוֹת, בָּחוּר, שָׂא נָא עֵינֶיךָ וּרְאֵה, מָה אַתָּה בוֹרֵר לָךְ.
phrases.en: And what would they say? Young man, please lift up your eyes and see what you choose for yourself for a wife.

phrases.he: אַל תִּתֵּן עֵינֶיךָ בַנּוֹי, תֵּן עֵינֶיךָ בַמִּשְׁפָּחָה.
phrases.en: Do not set your eyes toward beauty, but set your eyes toward a good family, as the verse states:

phrases.he: שֶׁקֶר הַחֵן וְהֶבֶל הַיֹּפִי, אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה' הִיא תִתְהַלָּל.
phrases.en: "Grace is deceitful and beauty is vain, but a woman who fears the Lord, she shall be praised"

phrases.he: וְאוֹמֵר, תְּנוּ לָהּ מִפְּרִי יָדֶיהָ, וִיהַלְלוּהָ בַשְּׁעָרִים מַעֲשֶׂיהָ.
phrases.en: and it further says: "Give her the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her in the gates"

phrases.he: וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר, צְאֶינָה וּרְאֶינָה בְּנוֹת צִיּוֹן בַּמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה בָּעֲטָרָה שֶׁעִטְּרָה לּוֹ אִמּוֹ בְּיוֹם חֲתֻנָּתוֹ וּבְיוֹם שִׂמְחַת לִבּוֹ.
phrases.en: And similarly, it says in another verse: "Go forth, daughters of Zion, and gaze upon King Solomon, upon the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding, and on the day of the gladness of his heart"

phrases.he: בְּיוֹם חֲתֻנָּתוֹ, זֶה מַתַּן תּוֹרָה.
phrases.en: "On the day of his wedding"; this is the giving of the Torah through the second set of tablets on Yom Kippur. The name King Solomon in this context, which also means king of peace, is interpreted as a reference to God.

phrases.he: וּבְיוֹם שִׂמְחַת לִבּוֹ, זֶה בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, שֶׁיִּבָּנֶה בִמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ.
phrases.en: "And on the day of the gladness of his heart"; this is the building of the Temple, may it be rebuilt speedily in our days.

phrases.he: אָמֵן:
מְגִלָּה נִקְרֵאת בְּאַחַד עָשָׂר, בִּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר, בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר, בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר, בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר, לֹא פָחוֹת וְלֹא יוֹתֵר.
phrases.en: The Megilla is read on the eleventh, on the twelfth, on the thirteenth, on the fourteenth, or on the fifteenth of the month of Adar, not earlier and not later.

phrases.he: כְּרַכִּין הַמֻּקָּפִין חוֹמָה מִימוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן, קוֹרִין בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר.
phrases.en: Cities that have been surrounded by a wall since the days of Joshua, son of Nun, read the Megilla on the fifteenth of Adar,

phrases.he: כְּפָרִים וַעֲיָרוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת, קוֹרִין בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר, אֶלָּא שֶׁהַכְּפָרִים מַקְדִּימִין לְיוֹם הַכְּנִיסָה:
phrases.en: whereas villages and large towns read it on the fourteenth. However, that the villages may advance their reading to the day of assembly,

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: How so?

phrases.he: חָל לִהְיוֹת יוֹם אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר בַּשֵּׁנִי, כְּפָרִים וַעֲיָרוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת קוֹרִין בּוֹ בַיּוֹם, וּמֻקָּפוֹת חוֹמָה לְמָחָר.
phrases.en: If the fourteenth of Adar occurs on Monday, the villages and large towns read it on that day, and the walled cities read it on the next day, the fifteenth.

phrases.he: חָל לִהְיוֹת בַּשְּׁלִישִׁי אוֹ בָּרְבִיעִי, כְּפָרִים מַקְדִּימִין לְיוֹם הַכְּנִיסָה וַעֲיָרוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת קוֹרִין בּוֹ בַיּוֹם, וּמֻקָּפוֹת חוֹמָה לְמָחָר.
phrases.en: If the fourteenth occurs on Tuesday or Wednesday, the villages advance their reading to the day of assembly, i.e., Monday, the twelfth or thirteenth of Adar; the large towns read it on that day, i.e., the fourteenth of Adar, and the walled cities read it on the next day, the fifteenth.

phrases.he: חָל לִהְיוֹת בָּחֲמִישִׁי, כְּפָרִים וַעֲיָרוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת קוֹרִין בּוֹ בַיּוֹם, וּמֻקָּפוֹת חוֹמָה לְמָחָר.
phrases.en: If the fourteenth occurs on Thursday, the villages and large towns read it on that day, the fourteenth, and the walled cities read it on the next day, the fifteenth.

phrases.he: חָל לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת, כְּפָרִים מַקְדִּימִין לְיוֹם הַכְּנִיסָה, וַעֲיָרוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת וּמֻקָּפוֹת חוֹמָה קוֹרִין בּוֹ בַיּוֹם.
phrases.en: If the fourteenth occurs on Shabbat eve, the villages advance their reading to the day of assembly, i.e., Thursday, the thirteenth of Adar; and the large towns and the walled cities read it on that day, i.e., the fourteenth of Adar.

phrases.he: חָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת, כְּפָרִים וַעֲיָרוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת מַקְדִּימִין וְקוֹרִין לְיוֹם הַכְּנִיסָה, וּמֻקָּפוֹת חוֹמָה לְמָחָר.
phrases.en: If the fourteenth occurs on Shabbat, both the villages and large towns advance their reading to the day of assembly, i.e., Thursday, the twelfth of Adar; and the walled cities read it on the day after Purim, the fifteenth.

phrases.he: חָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת, כְּפָרִים מַקְדִּימִין לְיוֹם הַכְּנִיסָה, וַעֲיָרוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת קוֹרִין בּוֹ בַיּוֹם, וּמֻקָּפוֹת חוֹמָה לְמָחָר:
phrases.en: If the fourteenth occurs on Sunday, the villages advance their reading to the day of assembly, i.e., Thursday, the eleventh of Adar; and the large towns read it on that day, i.e., the fourteenth of Adar; and the walled cities read it on the next day, the fifteenth.

phrases.he: אֵיזוֹ הִיא עִיר גְּדוֹלָה, כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ עֲשָׂרָה בַטְלָנִים.
phrases.en: What is considered a large city, where the Megilla is read on the fourteenth of Adar? Any city in which there are ten idlers.

phrases.he: פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן, הֲרֵי זֶה כְפָר.
phrases.en: However, if there are fewer than that, it is considered a village, even if it has many inhabitants.

phrases.he: בָּאֵלּוּ אָמְרוּ מַקְדִּימִין וְלֹא מְאַחֲרִין.
phrases.en: It was with regard to these times for reading the Megilla that the Sages said that one advances the reading of the Megilla before the fourteenth of Adar and one does not postpone the reading to after its proper time.

phrases.he: אֲבָל זְמַן עֲצֵי כֹהֲנִים וְתִשְׁעָה בְאָב, חֲגִיגָה וְהַקְהֵל, מְאַחֲרִין וְלֹא מַקְדִּימִין.
phrases.en: However, with regard to the time when families of priests donate wood for the fire on the altar, which were times those families would treat as Festivals; as well as the fast of the Ninth of Av; the Festival peace-offering that was brought on the Festivals; and the commandment of assembly [hakhel] of the entire Jewish people in the Temple courtyard on Sukkot in the year following the Sabbatical year to hear the king read the book of Deuteronomy; one postpones their observance until after Shabbat and does not advance their observance to before Shabbat.

phrases.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ מַקְדִּימִין וְלֹא מְאַחֲרִין, מֻתָּרִין בְּהֶסְפֵּד וּבְתַעֲנִיּוֹת וּמַתָּנוֹת לָאֶבְיוֹנִים.
phrases.en: Even though the Sages said that one advances the time for reading the Megilla and one does not postpone the reading, one is permitted to eulogize and fast on these days, as they are not actually Purim; nevertheless, gifts for the poor are distributed on this day.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אֵימָתַי, מְקוֹם שֶׁנִּכְנָסִין בְּשֵׁנִי וּבַחֲמִישִׁי.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda said: When is the Megilla read on the day of assembly, before the fourteenth of Adar? In a place where the villagers generally enter town on Monday and Thursday.

phrases.he: אֲבָל מְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין נִכְנָסִין לֹא בְּשֵׁנִי וְלֹא בַחֲמִישִׁי, אֵין קוֹרִין אוֹתָהּ אֶלָּא בִזְמַנָּהּ:
phrases.en: However, in a place where they do not generally enter town on Monday and Thursday, one may read the Megilla only in its designated time, the fourteenth of Adar.

phrases.he: קָרְאוּ אֶת הַמְּגִלָּה בַּאֲדָר הָרִאשׁוֹן וְנִתְעַבְּרָה הַשָּׁנָה,
phrases.en: read the Megilla during the first Adar and the year was then intercalated

phrases.he: קוֹרִין אוֹתָהּ בַּאֲדָר הַשֵּׁנִי,
phrases.en: one reads the Megilla again during the second Adar.

phrases.he: אֵין בֵּין אֲדָר הָרִאשׁוֹן לַאֲדָר הַשֵּׁנִי אֶלָּא קְרִיאַת הַמְּגִלָּה וּמַתָּנוֹת לָאֶבְיוֹנִים:
phrases.en: The difference between the first Adar and the second Adar is only that the reading of the Megilla and gifts to the poor

phrases.he: אֵין בֵּין יוֹם טוֹב לְשַׁבָּת אֶלָּא אֹכֶל נֶפֶשׁ בִּלְבָד.
phrases.en: The difference between Festivals and Shabbat is only in preparing food alone.

phrases.he: אֵין בֵּין שַׁבָּת לְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים אֶלָּא שֶׁזֶּה זְדוֹנוֹ בִּידֵי אָדָם וְזֶה זְדוֹנוֹ בְּכָרֵת:
phrases.en: The difference between Shabbat and Yom Kippur is only that in this case, its intentional desecration is punishable at the hand of Man, and in that case, its intentional desecration is punishable with karet.

phrases.he: אֵין בֵּין הַמֻּדָּר הֲנָאָה מֵחֲבֵרוֹ לַמֻּדָּר מִמֶּנּוּ מַאֲכָל אֶלָּא דְּרִיסַת הָרֶגֶל וְכֵלִים שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין בָּהֶן אֹכֶל נֶפֶשׁ.
phrases.en: The difference between one for whom benefit from another is forbidden by vow and one for whom benefit from another's food is forbidden by vow is only with regard to stepping foot on his property, and with regard to borrowing utensils from him that one does not use in the preparation of food.

phrases.he: אֵין בֵּין נְדָרִים לִנְדָבוֹת אֶלָּא שֶׁהַנְּדָרִים חַיָּב בְּאַחֲרָיוּתָן, וּנְדָבוֹת אֵינוֹ חַיָּב בְּאַחֲרָיוּתָן:
phrases.en: The difference between vow offerings and gift offerings is only that in the case of vow offerings, one is obligated in the responsibility to replace them, and in the case of gift offerings, one is not obligated in the responsibility to replace them.

phrases.he: אֵין בֵּין זָב הָרוֹאֶה שְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת לְרוֹאֶה שָׁלֹשׁ אֶלָּא קָרְבָּן.
phrases.en: The difference between a zav who experiences two emissions and one who experiences three is only an offering.

phrases.he: אֵין בֵּין מְצֹרָע מֻסְגָּר לִמְצֹרָע מֻחְלָט אֶלָּא פְרִיעָה וּפְרִימָה.
phrases.en: The difference between a quarantined leper and a confirmed leper is only letting the hair on one's head grow wild and rending one's garments.

phrases.he: אֵין בֵּין טָהוֹר מִתּוֹךְ הֶסְגֵּר לְטָהוֹר מִתּוֹךְ הֶחְלֵט אֶלָּא תִגְלַחַת וְצִפֳּרִים:
phrases.en: The difference between a leper purified from quarantine and a leper purified from confirmed leprosy is only shaving and bringing birds.

phrases.he: אֵין בֵּין סְפָרִים לִתְפִלִּין וּמְזוּזוֹת אֶלָּא שֶׁהַסְּפָרִים נִכְתָּבִין בְּכָל לָשׁוֹן, וּתְפִלִּין וּמְזוּזוֹת אֵינָן נִכְתָּבוֹת אֶלָּא אַשּׁוּרִית.
phrases.en: The difference between Torah scrolls, and phylacteries and mezuzot, is only that Torah scrolls are written in any language, whereas phylacteries and mezuzot are written only in Ashurit.

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, אַף בַּסְּפָרִים לֹא הִתִּירוּ שֶׁיִּכָּתְבוּ אֶלָּא יְוָנִית:
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: Even with regard to Torah scrolls, the Sages permitted them to be written only in Greek.

phrases.he: אֵין בֵּין כֹּהֵן מָשׁוּחַ בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה לִמְרֻבֶּה בְגָדִים אֶלָּא פַּר הַבָּא עַל כָּל הַמִּצְוֹת.
phrases.en: The difference between a High Priest anointed with the oil of anointing, and one consecrated by donning multiple garments is only that the latter does not bring the bull that comes for transgression of any of the mitzvot.

phrases.he: אֵין בֵּין כֹּהֵן מְשַׁמֵּשׁ לְכֹהֵן שֶׁעָבַר אֶלָּא פַּר יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וַעֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה:
phrases.en: The difference between a High Priest currently serving in that capacity and a former High Priest, is only with regard to the bull brought by the High Priest on Yom Kippur, and the tenth of an ephah meal-offering.

phrases.he: אֵין בֵּין בָּמָה גְדוֹלָה לְבָמָה קְטַנָּה אֶלָּא פְסָחִים.
phrases.en: The difference between a great, public altar, and a small, personal altar is only with regard to Paschal lambs.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל שֶׁהוּא נִדָּר וְנִדָּב, קָרֵב בַּבָּמָה.
phrases.en: This is the principle: Any offering that is vowed or contributed voluntarily is sacrificed on a small altar.

phrases.he: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ לֹא נִדָּר וְלֹא נִדָּב, אֵינוֹ קָרֵב בַּבָּמָה:
phrases.en: And any offering that is neither vowed nor contributed voluntarily is not sacrificed on a small altar.

phrases.he: אֵין בֵּין שִׁילֹה לִירוּשָׁלַיִם אֶלָּא שֶׁבְּשִׁילֹה אוֹכְלִים קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בְּכָל הָרוֹאֶה, וּבִירוּשָׁלַיִם לִפְנִים מִן הַחוֹמָה.
phrases.en: The difference between Shilo and Jerusalem is only that in Shiloh one eats offerings of lesser sanctity, and the second tithe, in any place that overlooks it. And in Jerusalem within the walls.

phrases.he: וְכָאן וְכָאן קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים נֶאֱכָלִים לִפְנִים מִן הַקְּלָעִים.
phrases.en: And here, and there, offerings of the most sacred order are eaten within the hangings.

phrases.he: קְדֻשַּׁת שִׁילֹה יֵשׁ אַחֲרֶיהָ הֶתֵּר, וּקְדֻשַּׁת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם אֵין אַחֲרֶיהָ הֶתֵּר.
phrases.en: The sanctity of Shiloh, after there is permission. But the sanctity of Jerusalem, after there is no permission.

phrases.he: הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת הַמְּגִלָּה לְמַפְרֵעַ, לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.en: One who reads the Megilla out of order, he has not fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.he: קְרָאָהּ עַל פֶּה, קְרָאָהּ תַּרְגּוּם, בְּכָל לָשׁוֹן, לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.en: If he read it by heart, or if he read it in Aramaic translation or in any other language, he has not fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.he: אֲבָל קוֹרִין אוֹתָהּ לַלּוֹעֲזוֹת בְּלַעַז.
phrases.en: However, for those who speak a foreign language, one may read the Megilla in that foreign language.

phrases.he: וְהַלּוֹעֵז שֶׁשָּׁמַע אַשּׁוּרִית, יָצָא:
phrases.en: And one who speaks a foreign language who heard in Ashurit, has fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.he: קְרָאָהּ סֵרוּגִין, וּמִתְנַמְנֵם, יָצָא.
phrases.en: If one read the Megilla at intervals, pausing and resuming, or while he is dozing off, he has fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.he: הָיָה כוֹתְבָהּ, דּוֹרְשָׁהּ, וּמַגִּיהָהּ, אִם כִּוֵּן לִבּוֹ, יָצָא.
phrases.en: If one was writing a Megilla, or expounding upon it, or correcting it, and he had intent to fulfill his obligation with that reading he has fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.en: but if not, he has not fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה כְּתוּבָה בְּסַם, וּבְסִקְרָא, וּבְקוֹמוֹס וּבְקַנְקַנְתּוֹם, עַל הַנְּיָר וְעַל הַדִּפְתְּרָא, לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.en: If one reads from a Megilla that was written with sam or with sikra or with komos or with kankantom, or from a Megilla that was written on neyar or on diftera, he has not fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.he: עַד שֶׁתְּהֵא כְּתוּבָה אַשּׁוּרִית, עַל הַסֵּפֶר וּבִדְיוֹ:
phrases.en: unless he reads from a Megilla that is written in Ashurit, upon parchment and with ink.

phrases.he: בֶּן עִיר שֶׁהָלַךְ לִכְרַךְ וּבֶן כְּרַךְ שֶׁהָלַךְ לְעִיר,
phrases.en: a resident of an unwalled town who went to a walled city, and a resident of a walled city who went to an unwalled town

phrases.he: אִם עָתִיד לַחֲזֹר לִמְקוֹמוֹ, קוֹרֵא כִמְקוֹמוֹ.
phrases.en: If he is destined to return to his place, he reads according to his place.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, קוֹרֵא עִמָּהֶן.
phrases.en: and if not, he reads with them.

phrases.he: וּמֵהֵיכָן קוֹרֵא אָדָם אֶת הַמְּגִלָּה וְיוֹצֵא בָּהּ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ,
phrases.en: Beginning from where must a person read the Megilla in order to fulfill his obligation,

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, כֻּלָּהּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: all of it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מֵאִישׁ יְהוּדִי (אסתר ב ה).
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: from a certain Jew (Esther 2:5).

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, מֵאַחַר הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה (אסתר ג׳:א׳):
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: From After these things (Esther 3:1).

phrases.he: הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִין לִקְרוֹת אֶת הַמְּגִלָּה, חוּץ מֵחֵרֵשׁ, שׁוֹטֶה, וְקָטָן.
phrases.en: Everyone is fit to read the Megilla, except for a deaf person, an imbecile, and a minor.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַכְשִׁיר בְּקָטָן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says that a minor is fit to read the Megilla.

phrases.he: אֵין קוֹרִין אֶת הַמְּגִלָּה, וְלֹא מָלִין, וְלֹא טוֹבְלִין, וְלֹא מַזִּין,
phrases.en: One may not read the Megilla, nor perform a circumcision, nor immerse himself in a ritual bath, nor sprinkle water of purification to purify people and objects that had contracted ritual impurity through contact with a corpse

phrases.he: וְכֵן שׁוֹמֶרֶת יוֹם כְּנֶגֶד יוֹם לֹא תִטְבֹּל, עַד שֶׁתָּנֵץ הַחַמָּה.
phrases.en: And also a woman who observes a clean day for each day she experiences a discharge may not immerse herself until the sun has risen.

phrases.he: וְכֻלָּן שֶׁעָשׂוּ מִשֶּׁעָלָה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר, כָּשֵׁר:
phrases.en: And with regard to all these activities that are supposed to be performed during the day, if one did them after daybreak, they are valid.

phrases.he: כָּל הַיּוֹם כָּשֵׁר לִקְרִיאַת הַמְּגִלָּה, וְלִקְרִיאַת הַהַלֵּל, וְלִתְקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר,
phrases.en: the entire day is a valid time for reading the Megilla; for reciting hallel; for sounding the shofar

phrases.he: וְלִנְטִילַת לוּלָב,
phrases.en: for taking the lulav

phrases.he: וְלִתְפִלַּת הַמּוּסָפִין, וְלַמּוּסָפִין,
phrases.en: for the additional prayer and for the additional offerings

phrases.he: וּלְוִדּוּי הַפָּרִים,
phrases.en: And for the confession over the bulls

phrases.he: וּלְוִדּוּי הַמַּעֲשֵׂר,
phrases.en: for the declaration with regard to tithes

phrases.he: וּלְוִדּוּי יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
phrases.en: and for the confession on Yom Kippur

phrases.he: לַסְּמִיכָה,
phrases.en: for placing hands

phrases.he: לַשְּׁחִיטָה,
phrases.en: for slaughtering

phrases.he: לַתְּנוּפָה,
phrases.en: for waving

phrases.he: לַהַגָּשָׁה,
phrases.en: for bringing near

phrases.he: לַקְּמִיצָה וְלַהַקְטָרָה,
phrases.en: for scooping out a fistful and for burning

phrases.he: לַמְּלִיקָה,
phrases.en: for pinching

phrases.he: וְלַקַּבָּלָה,
phrases.en: and for receiving

phrases.he: וְלַהַזָּיָה,
phrases.en: and for sprinkling

phrases.he: וּלְהַשְׁקָיַת סוֹטָה,
phrases.en: And for giving a woman suspected by her husband of having been unfaithful [sota] to drink

phrases.he: וְלַעֲרִיפַת הָעֶגְלָה,
phrases.en: for breaking the neck of the heifer

phrases.he: וּלְטַהֲרַת הַמְּצֹרָע:
phrases.en: and for the purification process of the leper

phrases.he: כָּל הַלַּיְלָה כָּשֵׁר לִקְצִירַת הָעֹמֶר וּלְהֶקְטֵר חֲלָבִים וְאֵבָרִים.
phrases.en: The entire night is a valid time for reaping the omer and for burning the fats and the limbs.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, דָּבָר שֶׁמִּצְוָתוֹ בַיּוֹם, כָּשֵׁר כָּל הַיּוֹם.
phrases.en: This is the principle: Something that it is a mitzva to perform during the day is valid if performed anytime during the entire day;

phrases.he: דָּבָר שֶׁמִּצְוָתוֹ בַלַּיְלָה, כָּשֵׁר כָּל הַלָּיְלָה:
phrases.en: something that it is a mitzva to perform at night is valid if performed anytime during the entire night.

phrases.he: בְּנֵי הָעִיר שֶׁמָּכְרוּ רְחוֹבָהּ שֶׁל עִיר, לוֹקְחִין בְּדָמָיו בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת.
phrases.en: Residents of a town who sold the town square, may purchase a synagogue with the proceeds.

phrases.he: בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת, לוֹקְחִין תֵּבָה.
phrases.en: If they sold a synagogue, they may purchase an ark.

phrases.he: תֵּבָה, לוֹקְחִין מִטְפָּחוֹת.
phrases.en: If they sold an ark, they may purchase wrapping cloths.

phrases.he: מִטְפָּחוֹת, לוֹקְחִין סְפָרִים.
phrases.en: If they sold wrapping cloths, they may purchase scrolls.

phrases.he: סְפָרִים, לוֹקְחִין תּוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If they sold scrolls of the Prophets and Writings, they may purchase a Torah scroll.

phrases.he: אֲבָל אִם מָכְרוּ תוֹרָה, לֹא יִקְחוּ סְפָרִים.
phrases.en: However, if they sold a Torah scroll, they may not purchase scrolls.

phrases.he: סְפָרִים, לֹא יִקְחוּ מִטְפָּחוֹת.
phrases.en: If they sold scrolls of the Prophets and Writings, they may not purchase wrapping cloths.

phrases.he: מִטְפָּחוֹת, לֹא יִקְחוּ תֵבָה.
phrases.en: If they sold wrapping cloths, they may not purchase an ark.

phrases.he: תֵּבָה, לֹא יִקְחוּ בֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת.
phrases.en: If they sold an ark, they may not purchase a synagogue.

phrases.he: בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת, לֹא יִקְחוּ אֶת הָרְחוֹב.
phrases.en: If they sold a synagogue, they may not purchase a town square.

phrases.he: וְכֵן בְּמוֹתְרֵיהֶן.
phrases.en: And similarly, to any surplus funds.

phrases.he: אֵין מוֹכְרִין אֶת שֶׁל רַבִּים לְיָחִיד, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמּוֹרִידִין אוֹתוֹ מִקְּדֻשָּׁתוֹ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: They may not sell a sacred object belonging to the community to an individual, due to the fact that they downgrade its degree of sanctity; this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, אִם כֵּן, אַף לֹא מֵעִיר גְּדוֹלָה לְעִיר קְטַנָּה:
phrases.en: The Rabbis said to him: If so, it should also not be permitted to sell a sacred object from a large town to a small town.

phrases.he: אֵין מוֹכְרִין בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת, אֶלָּא עַל תְּנַאי שֶׁאִם יִרְצוּ יַחֲזִירוּהוּ,
phrases.en: They may sell a synagogue only with a stipulation that if the sellers so desire it, the buyers will return it to them;

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, מוֹכְרִים אוֹתוֹ מִמְכַּר עוֹלָם, חוּץ מֵאַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים,
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: They may sell a synagogue with a permanent sale for any usage, except the following four things,

phrases.he: לְמֶרְחָץ
phrases.en: For a bathhouse,

phrases.he: וּלְבֻרְסְקִי
phrases.en: or for a tannery [burseki],

phrases.he: וְלִטְבִילָה
phrases.en: for immersion,

phrases.he: וּלְבֵית הַמָּיִם.
phrases.en: or for a lavatory.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מוֹכְרִים אוֹתוֹ לְשֵׁם חָצֵר, וְהַלּוֹקֵחַ מַה שֶּׁיִּרְצֶה יַעֲשֶׂה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: They may sell a synagogue for the generic purpose of serving as a courtyard, and then the buyer may then do with it as he wishes,

phrases.he: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת שֶׁחָרַב, אֵין מַסְפִּידִין בְּתוֹכוֹ
phrases.en: And Rabbi Yehuda said further: A synagogue that fell into ruin still may not be used for a mundane purpose. Therefore, one may not eulogize in it.

phrases.he: וְאֵין מַפְשִׁילִין בְּתוֹכוֹ חֲבָלִים
phrases.en: And nor may one stretch out and repair ropes in it.

phrases.he: וְאֵין פּוֹרְשִׂין לְתוֹכוֹ מְצוּדוֹת
phrases.en: And nor may one spread animal traps within it.

phrases.he: וְאֵין שׁוֹטְחִין עַל גַּגּוֹ פֵרוֹת
phrases.en: And nor may one spread out produce upon its roof

phrases.he: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין אוֹתוֹ קַפַּנְדַּרְיָא
phrases.en: And nor may one make it into a shortcut.

phrases.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ויקרא כו), וַהֲשִׁמּוֹתִי אֶת מִקְדְּשֵׁיכֶם
phrases.en: as it is stated: "And I will bring desolation to your sanctuaries"

phrases.he: קְדֻשָּׁתָן אַף כְּשֶׁהֵן שׁוֹמֵמִין
phrases.en: their sanctity remains upon them even when they are desolate.

phrases.he: עָלוּ בוֹ עֲשָׂבִים, לֹא יִתְלֹשׁ
phrases.en: If grass sprang up of its own accord in the ruined synagogue, although it is not befitting its sanctity, one should not pick it

phrases.he: מִפְּנֵי עָגְמַת נָפֶשׁ
phrases.en: due to the anguish that it will bring to those who see it.

phrases.he: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת, קוֹרִין בְּפָרָשַׁת שְׁקָלִים (שמות ל).
phrases.en: When the New Moon of Adar occurs on Shabbat, the congregation reads the portion of Shekalim on that Shabbat.

phrases.he: חָל לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹךְ הַשַּׁבָּת, מַקְדִּימִין לְשֶׁעָבַר וּמַפְסִיקִין לְשַׁבָּת אַחֶרֶת.
phrases.en: If the New Moon occurs during the middle of the week, they advance the reading of that portion to the previous Shabbat, and, in such a case, they interrupt the reading of the four portions on the following Shabbat.

phrases.he: בַּשְּׁנִיָּה, זָכוֹר (דברים כה).
phrases.en: On the second Shabbat, the Shabbat prior to Purim, they read the portion: Remember what Amalek did.

phrases.he: בַּשְּׁלִישִׁית, פָּרָה אֲדֻמָּה (במדבר י״ט:ב׳).
phrases.en: On the third Shabbat, they read the portion of the Red Heifer.

phrases.he: בָּרְבִיעִית, הַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה לָכֶם (שמות יב).
phrases.en: On the fourth Shabbat, they read the portion: This month shall be for you.

phrases.he: בָּחֲמִישִׁית, חוֹזְרִין לִכְסִדְרָן.
phrases.en: On the fifth Shabbat, they resume the regular weekly order of readings and no special portion is read.

phrases.he: לַכֹּל מַפְסִיקִין, בְּרָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים, בַּחֲנֻכָּה וּבְפוּרִים, בַּתַּעֲנִיּוֹת וּבַמַּעֲמָדוֹת וּבְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים:
phrases.en: For all special days, the congregation interrupts the regular weekly order of readings on the New Moons, on Hanukkah, and on Purim, on fast days, and on the non-priestly watches, and on Yom Kippur.

phrases.he: בְּפֶסַח קוֹרִין בְּפָרָשַׁת מוֹעֲדוֹת שֶׁל תּוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים (ויקרא כב).
phrases.en: On the first day of Passover, the congregation reads from the portion of the Festivals of Leviticus (Leviticus 22:26–23:44).

phrases.he: בַּעֲצֶרֶת, שִׁבְעָה שָׁבֻעוֹת (דברים טז).
phrases.en: On Shavuot they read the portion of "Seven weeks" (Deuteronomy 16:9–12).

phrases.he: בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִי בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ (ויקרא כג).
phrases.en: On Rosh HaShana they read the portion of "And on the seventh month on the first of the month" (Leviticus 23:23–25).

phrases.he: בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, אַחֲרֵי מוֹת (שם טז).
phrases.en: On Yom Kippur they read the portion of "After the death" (Leviticus 16).

phrases.he: בְּיוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חָג קוֹרִין בְּפָרָשַׁת מוֹעֲדוֹת שֶׁבְּתוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים (ויקרא כג), וּבִשְׁאָר כָּל יְמוֹת הֶחָג בְּקָרְבְּנוֹת הֶחָג (במדבר כט).
phrases.en: On the first Festival day of Sukkot they read from the portion of the Festivals of Leviticus (Leviticus 22:26–23:44), and on the other days of Sukkot they read selections from the portion of the offerings of Sukkot (Numbers 29:12–39).

phrases.he: בַּחֲנֻכָּה, בַּנְּשִׂיאִים (שם ז).
phrases.en: On each day of Hanukkah they read selections from the portion of the dedication of the altar by the tribal princes (Numbers 7).

phrases.he: בְּפוּרִים, וַיָּבֹא עֲמָלֵק (שמות יז).
phrases.en: On Purim they read the portion of "And Amalek came" (Exodus 17:8–16).

phrases.he: בְּרָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים, וּבְרָאשֵׁי חָדְשֵׁיכֶם (במדבר כח).
phrases.en: On the New Moon they read the portion of "And in the beginnings of your months" (Numbers 28:11–15).

phrases.he: בַּמַּעֲמָדוֹת, בְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְּרֵאשִׁית (בראשית א).
phrases.en: And in the non-priestly watches they read the act of Creation (Genesis 1:1–2:3).

phrases.he: בַּתַּעֲנִיּוֹת, בְּרָכוֹת וּקְלָלוֹת (ויקרא כו).
phrases.en: On fast days, they read the portion of blessings and curses (Leviticus, chapter 26).

phrases.he: אֵין מַפְסִיקִין בַּקְּלָלוֹת, אֶלָּא אֶחָד קוֹרֵא אֶת כֻּלָּן.
phrases.en: One should not interrupt the reading of the curses by having two different people read them. Rather, one person reads all of them.

phrases.he: בַּשֵּׁנִי וּבַחֲמִישִׁי וּבְשַׁבָּת בַּמִּנְחָה, קוֹרִין כְּסִדְרָן, וְאֵין עוֹלִין לָהֶם מִן הַחֶשְׁבּוֹן.
phrases.en: On Mondays, and on Thursdays, and on Shabbat during the afternoon service, they read in accordance with the regular weekly order. However, these readings are not counted as a progression in the reckoning.

phrases.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ויקרא כג), וַיְדַבֵּר מֹשֶׁה אֶת מֹעֲדֵי יְיָ אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, מִצְוָתָן שֶׁיְּהוּ קוֹרִין כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד בִּזְמַנּוֹ:
phrases.en: as it is stated: "And Moses declared to the children of Israel the appointed seasons of the Lord" (Leviticus 23:44), which indicates that part of the mitzva of the Festivals is that the people should read the portion relating to them, each one in its appointed time.

phrases.he: הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת הַמְּגִלָּה עוֹמֵד וְיוֹשֵׁב.
phrases.en: One who reads the Megilla may position himself as he wishes, either standing or sitting.

phrases.he: קְרָאָהּ אֶחָד, קְרָאוּהָ שְׁנַיִם, יָצְאוּ.
phrases.en: Whether one person reads the Megilla or two people read it together, they have fulfilled their obligation.

phrases.he: מְקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לְבָרֵךְ, יְבָרֵךְ.
phrases.en: In a place where the people are accustomed to recite a blessing over the reading, one should recite a blessing.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁלֹּא לְבָרֵךְ, לֹא יְבָרֵךְ.
phrases.en: And in a place where it is customary not to recite a blessing, one should not recite a blessing.

phrases.he: בְּשֵׁנִי וּבַחֲמִישִׁי וּבְשַׁבָּת בַּמִּנְחָה, קוֹרִין שְׁלֹשָׁה, אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין וְאֵין מוֹסִיפִין עֲלֵיהֶן, וְאֵין מַפְטִירִין בַּנָּבִיא.
phrases.en: On Mondays and Thursdays during the morning service and on Shabbat during the afternoon service, three people read from the Torah; one may neither decrease the number of readers nor add to them. And one does not conclude with a reading from the Prophets on these occasions.

phrases.he: הַפּוֹתֵחַ וְהַחוֹתֵם בַּתּוֹרָה, מְבָרֵךְ לְפָנֶיהָ וּלְאַחֲרֶיהָ:
phrases.en: Both the one who begins the reading and the one who concludes the reading from the Torah recite a blessing; one recites before the beginning of the reading and one recites after its conclusion.

phrases.he: בְּרָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים וּבְחֻלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד, קוֹרִין אַרְבָּעָה,
phrases.en: On the days of the New Moon and on the intermediate days of a Festival, four people read from the Torah;

phrases.he: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵהֶן וְאֵין מוֹסִיפִין עֲלֵיהֶן,
phrases.en: one may neither decrease the number of readers nor add to them.

phrases.he: וְאֵין מַפְטִירִין בַּנָּבִיא.
phrases.en: And one does not conclude with a reading from the Prophets.

phrases.he: הַפּוֹתֵחַ וְהַחוֹתֵם בַּתּוֹרָה, מְבָרֵךְ לְפָנֶיהָ וּלְאַחֲרֶיהָ.
phrases.en: Both the one who begins the reading and the one who concludes the reading from the Torah recite a blessing.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מוּסָף וְאֵינוֹ יוֹם טוֹב, קוֹרִין אַרְבָּעָה.
phrases.en: This is the principle: Any day on which there is an additional offering sacrificed in the Temple and that is not a Festival, i.e., the New Moon and the intermediate days of a Festival, four people read from the Torah;

phrases.he: בְּיוֹם טוֹב, חֲמִשָּׁה.
phrases.en: on a Festival, five people read;

phrases.he: בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, שִׁשָּׁה.
phrases.en: on Yom Kippur, six people read;

phrases.he: בְּשַׁבָּת, שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.en: and on Shabbat, seven people read.

phrases.he: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵהֶן, אֲבָל מוֹסִיפִין עֲלֵיהֶן,
phrases.en: One may not decrease the number of readers, but one may add to them.

phrases.he: וּמַפְטִירִין בַּנָּבִיא.
phrases.en: And one concludes with a reading from the Prophets.

phrases.he: הַפּוֹתֵחַ וְהַחוֹתֵם בַּתּוֹרָה, מְבָרֵךְ לְפָנֶיהָ וּלְאַחֲרֶיהָ:
phrases.en: Both the one who begins the reading and the one who concludes the reading from the Torah recite a blessing;

phrases.he: אֵין פּוֹרְסִין אֶת שְׁמַע,
phrases.en: One does not recite the introductory prayers and blessing before Shema;

phrases.he: וְאֵין עוֹבְרִין לִפְנֵי הַתֵּבָה,
phrases.en: nor does one pass before the ark to repeat the Amida prayer;

phrases.he: וְאֵין נוֹשְׂאִין אֶת כַּפֵּיהֶם,
phrases.en: nor do the priests lift their hands to recite the Priestly Benediction;

phrases.he: וְאֵין קוֹרִין בַּתּוֹרָה,
phrases.en: nor is the Torah read in public;

phrases.he: וְאֵין מַפְטִירִין בַּנָּבִיא,
phrases.en: nor does one conclude with a reading from the Prophets in the presence of fewer than ten men.

phrases.he: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין מַעֲמָד וּמוֹשָׁב,
phrases.en: And one does not observe the practice of standing up and sitting down for the delivery of eulogies at a funeral service;

phrases.he: וְאֵין אוֹמְרִים בִּרְכַּת אֲבֵלִים וְתַנְחוּמֵי אֲבֵלִים וּבִרְכַּת חֲתָנִים,
phrases.en: nor does one recite the mourners' blessing or comfort mourners in two lines after the funeral; or recite the bridegrooms' blessing;

phrases.he: וְאֵין מְזַמְּנִין בַּשֵּׁם, פָּחוֹת מֵעֲשָׂרָה.
phrases.en: and one does not invite others to recite Grace after Meals with the name of God, with fewer than ten men present.

phrases.he: וּבַקַּרְקָעוֹת, תִּשְׁעָה וְכֹהֵן.
phrases.en: If one consecrated land and now wishes to redeem it, the land must be assessed by nine men and one priest,

phrases.he: וְאָדָם, כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶן:
phrases.en: And similarly, assessing the value of a person who has pledged his own value to the Temple must be undertaken by ten people, one of whom must be a priest.

phrases.he: הַקּוֹרֵא בַּתּוֹרָה לֹא יִפְחֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה פְסוּקִים.
phrases.en: One who reads from the Torah in the synagogue should not read fewer than three verses.

phrases.he: לֹא יִקְרָא לַמְּתֻרְגְּמָן יוֹתֵר מִפָּסוּק אֶחָד, וּבַנָּבִיא שְׁלֹשָׁה.
phrases.en: And when it is being translated, he should not read to the translator more than one verse at a time, so that the translator will not become confused. And with regard to the Prophets, one may read to the translator three verses at a time.

phrases.he: הָיוּ שְׁלָשְׁתָּן שָׁלֹשׁ פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת, קוֹרִין אֶחָד אֶחָד.
phrases.en: If the three verses constitute three separate paragraphs, that is to say, if each verse is a paragraph in itself, one must read them to the translator one by one.

phrases.he: מְדַלְּגִין בַּנָּבִיא וְאֵין מְדַלְּגִין בַּתּוֹרָה.
phrases.en: One may skip from one place to another while reading the Prophets, but one may not skip from one place to another while reading the Torah.

phrases.he: וְעַד כַּמָּה הוּא מְדַלֵּג, עַד כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִפְסֹק הַמְּתֻרְגְּמָן:
phrases.en: How far may he skip? As far as he can, provided that the translator will not conclude his translation while the reader is still rolling the scroll to the new location.

phrases.he: הַמַּפְטִיר בַּנָּבִיא, הוּא פּוֹרֵס עַל שְׁמַע,
phrases.en: The one who concludes with a reading from the Prophets is also the one who is honored to recite the introductory prayers and blessing before Shema,

phrases.he: וְהוּא עוֹבֵר לִפְנֵי הַתֵּבָה,
phrases.en: and he passes before the ark

phrases.he: וְהוּא נוֹשֵׂא אֶת כַּפָּיו.
phrases.en: and if he is a priest he lifts his hands

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיָה קָטָן, אָבִיו אוֹ רַבּוֹ עוֹבְרִין עַל יָדוֹ:
phrases.en: And if the one who reads the haftara is a minor, his father or teacher is honored to pass before the ark in his place.

phrases.he: קָטָן קוֹרֵא בַּתּוֹרָה וּמְתַרְגֵּם,
phrases.en: A minor may read the Torah in public and also translate the text for the congregation into Aramaic,

phrases.he: אֲבָל אֵינוֹ פּוֹרֵס עַל שְׁמַע,
phrases.en: but he may not recite the introductory prayers and blessing before Shema,

phrases.he: וְאֵינוֹ עוֹבֵר לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה,
phrases.en: and he may not pass before the ark to lead the congregation in prayer,

phrases.he: וְאֵינוֹ נוֹשֵׂא אֶת כַּפָּיו.
phrases.en: and he may not lift his hands to recite the Priestly Benediction.

phrases.he: פּוֹחֵחַ פּוֹרֵס אֶת שְׁמַע וּמְתַרְגֵּם,
phrases.en: One whose limbs are exposed may recite the introductory prayers and blessing before Shema and translate the Torah reading into Aramaic,

phrases.he: אֲבָל אֵינוֹ קוֹרֵא בַתּוֹרָה
phrases.en: but he may not read from the Torah out of respect for the Torah;

phrases.he: וְאֵינוֹ עוֹבֵר לִפְנֵי הַתֵּבָה
phrases.en: he may not pass before the ark to lead the congregation in prayer;

phrases.he: וְאֵינוֹ נוֹשֵׂא אֶת כַּפָּיו.
phrases.en: and he may not lift his hands to recite the Priestly Benediction out of respect for the congregation.

phrases.he: סוּמָא פּוֹרֵס אֶת שְׁמַע וּמְתַרְגֵּם.
phrases.en: One who is blind may recite the introductory prayers and blessing before Shema, and he may also translate the Torah reading into Aramaic.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.he: כֹּל שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה מְאוֹרוֹת מִיָּמָיו,
phrases.en: Anyone who has not seen the luminaries, the sun, moon, and stars, in his life, i.e., he was blind from birth,

phrases.he: אֵינוֹ פּוֹרֵס עַל שְׁמַע:
phrases.en: may not recite the introductory prayers and blessing before Shema.

phrases.he: כֹּהֵן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיָדָיו מוּמִין, לֹא יִשָּׂא אֶת כַּפָּיו.
phrases.en: A priest who has blemishes on his hands may not lift his hands

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף מִי שֶׁהָיוּ יָדָיו צְבוּעוֹת אִסְטִיס וּפוּאָה, לֹא יִשָּׂא אֶת כַּפָּיו, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָעָם מִסְתַּכְּלִין בּוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: Even one whose hands were colored with satis, a blue dye, may not lift his hands because the congregation will look at him.

phrases.he: הָאוֹמֵר אֵינִי עוֹבֵר לִפְנֵי הַתֵּבָה בִצְבוּעִין, אַף בִּלְבָנִים לֹא יַעֲבֹר.
phrases.en: One who says: I will not pass before the ark in colored garments, may not pass before the ark even in white garments.

phrases.he: בְּסַנְדָּל אֵינִי עוֹבֵר, אַף יָחֵף לֹא יַעֲבֹר.
phrases.en: I will not pass before the ark wearing sandals, he may not pass before it even barefoot.

phrases.he: הָעוֹשֶׂה תְפִלָּתוֹ עֲגֻלָּה, סַכָּנָה וְאֵין בָּהּ מִצְוָה.
phrases.en: One who constructs his phylacteries in a round shape exposes himself to danger and yet he does not fulfill the mitzva.

phrases.he: נְתָנָהּ עַל מִצְחוֹ אוֹ עַל פַּס יָדוֹ, הֲרֵי זוֹ דֶּרֶךְ הַמִּינוּת.
phrases.en: If one placed the phylacteries worn on the head on his forehead, or if he placed the phylacteries worn on the arm on his palm, this is the way of the heretics.

phrases.he: צִפָּן זָהָב, וּנְתָנָהּ עַל בֵּית אֻנְקְלִי שֶׁלּוֹ, הֲרֵי זוֹ דֶּרֶךְ הַחִיצוֹנִים:
phrases.en: If one plated his phylacteries with gold or placed the phylacteries worn on the arm on the outside of his sleeve, this is the way of the outsiders.

phrases.he: הָאוֹמֵר יְבָרְכוּךָ טוֹבִים, הֲרֵי זוֹ דֶּרֶךְ הַמִּינוּת.
phrases.en: one says: May the good bless You, this is a path of heresy,

phrases.he: עַל קַן צִפּוֹר יַגִּיעוּ רַחֲמֶיךָ, וְעַל טוֹב יִזָּכֵר שְׁמֶךָ,
phrases.en: Your mercy is extended to a bird's nest, or: May Your name be mentioned with the good;

phrases.he: מוֹדִים מוֹדִים, מְשַׁתְּקִין אוֹתוֹ.
phrases.en: We give thanks, we give thanks, twice, he is suspected of heretical beliefs and they silence him.

phrases.he: הַמְכַנֶּה בָעֲרָיוֹת, מְשַׁתְּקִין אוֹתוֹ.
phrases.en: one modifies the text while reading the laws of forbidden sexual relations, they silence him.

phrases.he: הָאוֹמֵר, וּמִזַּרְעֲךָ לֹא תִתֵּן לְהַעֲבִיר לַמֹּלֶךְ (ויקרא יח), וּמִזַרְעָךְ לֹא תִתֵּן לְאַעְבָּרָא בְּאַרְמָיוּתָא, מְשַׁתְּקִין אוֹתוֹ בִנְזִיפָה:
phrases.en: one says while translating the verse: "And you shall not give any of your seed to set them apart to Molekh" (Leviticus 18:21): And you shall not give any of your seed to impregnate an Aramean woman, he is silenced with rebuke.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֵׂה רְאוּבֵן (בראשית לה), נִקְרָא וְלֹא מִתַּרְגֵּם.
phrases.en: The incident of Reuben, about which it says: "And Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine" (Genesis 35:22), is read from the Torah in public but not translated, so that the uneducated not come to denigrate Reuben.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֵׂה תָמָר (בראשית לח), נִקְרָא וּמִתַּרְגֵּם.
phrases.en: The incident of Tamar (Genesis, chapter 38) is read in public and also translated.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֵׂה עֵגֶל הָרִאשׁוֹן (שמות לב), נִקְרָא וּמִתַּרְגֵּם.
phrases.en: The first report of the incident of the Golden Calf, i.e., the Torah's account of the incident itself (Exodus 32:1–20), is read and translated,

phrases.he: וְהַשֵּׁנִי (שם), נִקְרָא וְלֹא מִתַּרְגֵּם.
phrases.en: but the second narrative, i.e., Aaron's report to Moses of what had taken place (Exodus 32:21–24) is read but not translated.

phrases.he: בִּרְכַּת כֹּהֲנִים (במדבר ו), מַעֲשֵׂה דָּוִד (שמואל ב י״א:כ״ז) וְאַמְנוֹן (שמואל ב יג), לֹא נִקְרָאִין וְלֹא מִתַּרְגְּמִין.
phrases.en: The verses constituting the Priestly Benediction (Numbers 6:24–26) and the incident of David and Amnon (II Samuel, chapter 13) are neither read nor translated.

phrases.he: אֵין מַפְטִירִין בַּמֶּרְכָּבָה (יחזקאל א), וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר.
phrases.en: One may not conclude the Torah reading with by reading from the Prophets the account of the Divine Chariot (Ezekiel, chapter 1), so as not to publicize that which was meant to remain hidden. And Rabbi Yehuda permits it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אֵין מַפְטִירִין בְּהוֹדַע אֶת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם (יחזקאל ט״ז:ב׳):
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: One may not conclude with section from the Prophets beginning with: "Make known to Jerusalem her abominations" (Ezekiel 16:2), because it speaks derogatively of the Jewish people.

phrases.he: מַשְׁקִין בֵּית הַשְּׁלָחִין בַּמּוֹעֵד וּבַשְּׁבִיעִית, בֵּין מִמַּעְיָן שֶׁיָּצָא בַתְּחִלָּה, בֵּין מִמַּעְיָן שֶׁלֹּא יָצָא בַתְּחִלָּה.
phrases.en: One may irrigate a field that requires irrigation on the intermediate days of a Festival as well as during the Sabbatical Year, both from a newly emerged spring that began to flow only during the Festival, and from a spring that did not just emerge and that has been flowing for some time.

phrases.he: אֲבָל אֵין מַשְׁקִין לֹא מִמֵּי הַגְּשָׁמִים וְלֹא מִמֵּי הַקִּילוֹן.
phrases.en: However, one may not irrigate a field with rainwater collected in a cistern, a procedure that requires excessive exertion, or with water drawn with a shadoof [kilon], a lever used to raise water with a bucket from deep down in a well.

phrases.he: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין עוּגִיּוֹת לַגְּפָנִים:
phrases.en: And one may not construct circular ditches around the bases of grapevines on the intermediate days of a Festival.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר, אֵין עוֹשִׂין אֶת הָאַמָּה בַתְּחִלָּה בַּמּוֹעֵד וּבַשְּׁבִיעִית,
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says: One may not construct a new water channel during the intermediate days of a Festival or during the Sabbatical Year.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, עוֹשִׂין אֶת הָאַמָּה בַּתְּחִלָּה בַּשְּׁבִיעִית, וּמְתַקְּנִין אֶת הַמְּקֻלְקָלוֹת בַּמּוֹעֵד.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: One may construct a new water channel during the Sabbatical Year and one may repair damaged water channels during the intermediate days of a Festival.

phrases.he: וּמְתַקְּנִין אֶת קִלְקוּלֵי הַמַּיִם שֶׁבִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים וְחוֹטְטִין אוֹתָן.
phrases.en: One may repair damaged water cisterns that are in the public domain, and clean them out.

phrases.he: וּמְתַקְּנִין אֶת הַדְּרָכִים וְאֶת הָרְחוֹבוֹת וְאֶת מִקְווֹת הַמַּיִם, וְעוֹשִׂין כָּל צָרְכֵי הָרַבִּים,
phrases.en: one may repair roads, streets, and ritual baths; and one may tend to all other public needs.

phrases.he: וּמְצַיְּנִין אֶת הַקְּבָרוֹת,
phrases.en: one may mark graves

phrases.he: וְיוֹצְאִין אַף עַל הַכִּלְאָיִם:
phrases.en: and inspectors may even go out to uproot the shoots of prohibited diverse kinds.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:

phrases.he: מוֹשְׁכִים אֶת הַמַּיִם מֵאִילָן לְאִילָן,
phrases.en: one may draw water via channels from one tree to another tree

phrases.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַשְׁקֶה אֶת כָּל הַשָּׂדֶה.
phrases.en: And this is permitted provided that in doing so he does not water the entire field.

phrases.he: זְרָעִים שֶׁלֹּא שָׁתוּ לִפְנֵי הַמּוֹעֵד, לֹא יַשְׁקֵם בַּמּוֹעֵד.
phrases.en: With regard to plants that were not watered prior to the Festival, one may not water them on the intermediate days of the Festival

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים מַתִּירִין בָּזֶה וּבָזֶה:
phrases.en: But the Rabbis permit watering in this case, i.e., trees, and that case, i.e., plants.

phrases.he: צָדִין אֶת הָאִישׁוּת וְאֶת הָעַכְבָּרִים מִשְּׂדֵה הָאִילָן וּמִשְּׂדֵה הַלָּבָן, שֶׁלֹּא כְדַרְכּוֹ, בַּמּוֹעֵד וּבַשְּׁבִיעִית.
phrases.en: One may trap moles and mice in an orchard and in a field of grain in a way that is not his usual manner, both on the intermediate days of a Festival and during the Sabbatical Year.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, מִשְּׂדֵה הָאִילָן כְּדַרְכּוֹ, וּמִשְּׂדֵה הַלָּבָן שֶׁלֹּא כְדַרְכּוֹ.
phrases.en: But the Rabbis say: In an orchard he may trap them in his usual manner, but in a field of grain, he may only trap them in a way that is not his usual manner.

phrases.he: וּמְקָרִין אֶת הַפִּרְצָה בַּמּוֹעֵד, וּבַשְּׁבִיעִית בּוֹנֶה כְדַרְכּוֹ:
phrases.en: And one may seal a breach on the intermediate days of a Festival, and during the Sabbatical Year one may even build in his usual manner.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.he: רוֹאִין אֶת הַנְּגָעִים בַּתְּחִלָּה לְהָקֵל, אֲבָל לֹא לְהַחְמִיר.
phrases.en: A priest may initially examine an individual showing symptoms of leprosy on the intermediate days of a Festival in order to be lenient, but not in order to be stringent;

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, לֹא לְהָקֵל וְלֹא לְהַחְמִיר.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: The priest may not examine the symptoms in order to be lenient or in order to be stringent.

phrases.he: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir also stated

phrases.he: מְלַקֵּט אָדָם עַצְמוֹת אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁשִּׂמְחָה הִיא לוֹ.
phrases.en: A person may gather the bones of his father and mother because the fact that one merited to bring the bones of his deceased parents to the graves of their ancestors is a source of joy for him.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אֵבֶל הוּא לוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: it is a source of mourning for him.

phrases.he: לֹא יְעוֹרֵר אָדָם עַל מֵתוֹ וְלֹא יַסְפִּידֶנּוּ קֹדֶם לָרֶגֶל שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם:
phrases.en: a person may not arouse lamentation for his deceased relative, and he may not eulogize him during the thirty days before a pilgrimage Festival.

phrases.he: אֵין חוֹפְרִין כּוּכִין וּקְבָרוֹת בַּמּוֹעֵד,
phrases.en: One may not dig crypts or graves on the intermediate days of a Festival

phrases.he: אֲבָל מְחַנְּכִים אֶת הַכּוּכִין בַּמּוֹעֵד.
phrases.en: but one may adjust previously dug crypts on the intermediate days of a Festival

phrases.he: וְעוֹשִׂין נִבְרֶכֶת בַּמּוֹעֵד,
phrases.en: And one may also construct a laundry pond on the intermediate days of a Festival

phrases.he: וְאָרוֹן עִם הַמֵּת בֶּחָצֵר.
phrases.en: And one may also prepare a coffin if he is together with the corpse in the same courtyard,

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹסֵר, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ עִמּוֹ נְסָרִים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda prohibits making the coffin unless one has wooden boards with him

phrases.he: אֵין נוֹשְׂאִין נָשִׁים בַּמּוֹעֵד, לֹא בְתוּלוֹת, וְלֹא אַלְמָנוֹת, וְלֹא מְיַבְּמִין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁשִּׂמְחָה הִיא לוֹ.
phrases.en: One may not marry a woman on the intermediate days of a Festival, not virgins and not widows, and one may not perform levirate marriage with his sister-in-law, if his brother died childless, because it is a joyous occasion for him.

phrases.he: אֲבָל מַחֲזִיר הוּא אֶת גְּרוּשָׁתוֹ.
phrases.en: However, one may remarry his divorced wife on the intermediate days of a Festival.

phrases.he: וְעוֹשָׂה אִשָּׁה תַּכְשִׁיטֶיהָ בַמּוֹעֵד.
phrases.en: And a woman may engage in all her usual cosmetic treatments to enhance her physical appearance on the intermediate days of a Festival.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, לֹא תָּסוּד מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּוּוּל הוּא לָהּ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: She may not apply lime to her skin because it is temporarily a disgrace to her.

phrases.he: הַהֶדְיוֹט תּוֹפֵר כְּדַרְכּוֹ, וְהָאֻמָּן מַכְלִיב.
phrases.en: A layman may sew in his usual manner if necessary for the Festival, whereas a craftsman may form only temporary stitches.

phrases.he: וּמְסָרְגִין אֶת הַמִּטּוֹת.
phrases.en: And one may interweave the cords attached to the frames of beds upon which a mattress is placed.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַף מְמַתְּחִין:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: One may only tighten the cords but not interweave them.

phrases.he: מַעֲמִידִין תַּנּוּר וְכִירַיִם וְרֵחַיִם בַּמּוֹעֵד.
phrases.en: One may set up an oven, a stove, and a mill on the intermediate days of a Festival.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֵין מְכַבְּשִׁין אֶת הָרֵחַיִם בַּתְּחִלָּה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: One may not chisel millstones for the first time on the intermediate days of a Festival.

phrases.he: עוֹשִׂין מַעֲקֶה לְגַג וּלְמִרְפֶּסֶת מַעֲשֵׂה הֶדְיוֹט, אֲבָל לֹא מַעֲשֵׂה אֻמָּן.
phrases.en: One may construct a railing for a roof or a balcony if it is done in a nonprofessional manner, as the work of a layman, but not if it is done skillfully, as the work of a craftsman.

phrases.he: שָׁפִין אֶת הַסְּדָקִין וּמַעְגִּילִין אוֹתָן בַּמַּעְגִּילָה בַּיָּד וּבָרֶגֶל, אֲבָל לֹא בַמַּחֲלָצָיִם.
phrases.en: One may plaster the cracks in an oven and roll over them with a roller, a wooden tool used to smooth out clay, with a hand or a foot, but not with a presser, a tool that is specially designed for this task.

phrases.he: הַצִּיר וְהַצִּנּוֹר וְהַקּוֹרָה וְהַמַּנְעוּל וְהַמַּפְתֵּחַ שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרוּ, מְתַקְּנָן בַּמּוֹעֵד, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְכַוֵּן מְלַאכְתּוֹ בַּמּוֹעֵד.
phrases.en: The hinge and the cylinder of the hinge, and the cross beam that holds the door, and a lock and a key that broke, one may fix them on a Festival provided that he does not intend ahead of time to do his labor on the Festival and delay it until that time.

phrases.he: וְכָל כְּבָשִׁין שֶׁהוּא יָכוֹל לֶאֱכֹל מֵהֶן בַּמּוֹעֵד, כּוֹבְשָׁן:
phrases.en: And with regard to all preserved food from which one can eat on the Festival, he may preserve them on the intermediate days of a Festival.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁהָפַךְ אֶת זֵיתָיו וְאֵרְעוֹ אֵבֶל אוֹ אֹנֶס, אוֹ שֶׁהִטְעוּהוּ פוֹעֲלִים, טוֹעֵן קוֹרָה רִאשׁוֹנָה וּמַנִּיחָהּ לְאַחַר הַמּוֹעֵד.
phrases.en: One who had turned over his olives and mourning befell him or some other unavoidable accident occurred, or his workers misled him, he may place the olives in the press and load the beam with weights for the initial pressing of the olives and leave it until after the Festival.

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, זוֹלֵף וְגוֹמֵר וְגָף כְּדַרְכּוֹ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: He may press the olives and complete the process and plug each barrel of oil in its usual manner.

phrases.he: וְכֵן מִי שֶׁהָיָה יֵינוֹ בְּתוֹךְ הַבּוֹר וְאֵרְעוֹ אֵבֶל אוֹ אֹנֶס, אוֹ שֶׁהִטְעוּהוּ פוֹעֲלִים,
phrases.en: And similarly, with regard to one whose wine was already in the collection pit beside the wine press and needed to be removed lest it sour, and mourning for some close relative or some other unavoidable accident befell him, or his workers misled him, promising to come but failing to do so,

phrases.he: זוֹלֵף וְגוֹמֵר וְגָף כְּדַרְכּוֹ,
phrases.en: during the intermediate days of the Festival he may draw off the wine and complete the process, and then plug each barrel of wine in its usual manner;

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.en: this is the statement of Rabbi Yosei.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, עוֹשֶׂה לוֹ לִמּוּדִים, בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא יַחְמִיץ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: He should construct a wooden panel to cover the collection pit so that the wine will not sour.

phrases.he: מַכְנִיס אָדָם פֵּרוֹתָיו מִפְּנֵי הַגַּנָּבִים,
phrases.en: A person may bring his fruit in because he is concerned about thieves,

phrases.he: וְשׁוֹלֶה פִשְׁתָּנוֹ מִן הַמִּשְׁרָה בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא תֹאבַד,
phrases.en: and he may draw his flax out of the soaking pool so that it is not ruined

phrases.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְכַוֵּן אֶת מְלַאכְתּוֹ בַּמּוֹעֵד.
phrases.en: provided that he does not plan his work on the intermediate days of the Festival.

phrases.he: וְכֻלָּן אִם כִּוְּנוּ מְלַאכְתָּן בַּמּוֹעֵד, יֹאבֵדוּ:
phrases.en: And all of these cases, if one planned his labor on the intermediate days of the Festival, the fruit of that labor must be lost

phrases.he: אֵין לוֹקְחִין בָּתִּים, עֲבָדִים וּבְהֵמָה, אֶלָּא לְצֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹעֵד, אוֹ לְצֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹכֵר, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מַה יֹּאכָל.
phrases.en: One may not purchase houses, slaves, and cattle unless it is for the sake of the Festival, or to provide for the needs of the seller who does not have anything to eat.

phrases.he: אֵין מְפַנִּין מִבַּיִת לְבַיִת, אֲבָל מְפַנֶּה הוּא לַחֲצֵרוֹ.
phrases.en: One may not move his possessions from house to house during the intermediate days of a Festival, but he may move them to his courtyard if that is necessary.

phrases.he: אֵין מְבִיאִין כֵּלִים מִבֵּית הָאֻמָּן.
phrases.en: One may not bring home utensils from the house of a craftsman after he has completed his work,

phrases.he: וְאִם חוֹשֵׁשׁ לָהֶם, מְפַנָּן לְחָצֵר אַחֶרֶת:
phrases.en: but if one is concerned about them that if he leaves them in the craftsman's house they are likely to be stolen, he may move them to another courtyard.

phrases.he: מְחַפִּין אֶת הַקְּצִיעוֹת בְּקַשׁ.
phrases.en: figs that were spread out to dry may be covered with straw to protect them from rain and dew.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף מְעַבִּין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: One may even condense the figs.

phrases.he: מוֹכְרֵי פֵרוֹת, כְּסוּת וְכֵלִים, מוֹכְרִים בְּצִנְעָה לְצֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹעֵד.
phrases.en: Those who sell produce, clothing, and utensils may sell them in private, for the sake of the Festival.

phrases.he: הַצַּיָּדִין וְהַדָּשׁוֹשׁוֹת וְהַגָּרוֹסוֹת, עוֹשִׂין בְּצִנְעָה לְצֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹעֵד.
phrases.en: Fishermen, and groats makers, and bean pounders, who pulverize the beans, may ply their trades in private for the sake of the Festival.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, הֵם הֶחְמִירוּ עַל עַצְמָן:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: They were stringent with themselves to refrain from this work even with respect to what was needed for the Festival.

phrases.he: וְאֵלּוּ מְגַלְּחִין בַּמּוֹעֵד,
phrases.en: And these may shave and cut their hair on the intermediate days of a Festival:

phrases.he: הַבָּא מִמְּדִינַת הַיָּם,
phrases.en: One who comes from a country overseas;

phrases.he: וּמִבֵּית הַשִּׁבְיָה,
phrases.en: and one who is released from a house of captivity;

phrases.he: וְהַיּוֹצֵא מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִין,
phrases.en: and one who comes out of prison on the intermediate days of a Festival;

phrases.he: וְהַמְנֻדֶּה שֶׁהִתִּירוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים,
phrases.en: and one who had been ostracized and therefore prohibited from cutting his hair, and the Sages released him from his decree of ostracism on the intermediate days of the Festival;

phrases.he: וְכֵן מִי שֶׁנִּשְׁאַל לְחָכָם וְהֻתַּר,
phrases.en: and similarly, one who had vowed not to cut his hair and then requested of a Sage to dissolve his vow and was released from it on the intermediate days of the Festival;

phrases.he: וְהַנָּזִיר,
phrases.en: and the nazirite whose term of naziriteship ended on the intermediate days of a Festival;

phrases.he: וְהַמְּצֹרָע הָעוֹלֶה מִטֻּמְאָתוֹ לְטָהֳרָתוֹ:
phrases.en: and the leper who needs to purify himself on the intermediate days and must shave his entire body in order to leave his state of ritual impurity and regain his ritual purity.

phrases.he: וְאֵלּוּ מְכַבְּסִין בַּמּוֹעֵד,
phrases.en: And these may launder their clothes on the intermediate days of a Festival:

phrases.he: הַבָּא מִמְּדִינַת הַיָּם,
phrases.en: One who comes from a country overseas;

phrases.he: וּמִבֵּית הַשִּׁבְיָה,
phrases.en: and one who is released from a house of captivity;

phrases.he: וְהַיּוֹצֵא מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִים,
phrases.en: and one who comes out of prison on the intermediate days of a Festival;

phrases.he: וְהַמְנֻדֶּה שֶׁהִתִּירוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים,
phrases.en: and one who had been ostracized and the Sages released him from his decree of ostracism;

phrases.he: וְכֵן מִי שֶׁנִּשְׁאַל לְחָכָם וְהֻתַּר,
phrases.en: and similarly, one who had vowed not to launder his clothes and he requested from a Sage to dissolve his vow and was released from it on the intermediate days of a Festival.

phrases.he: מִטְפְּחוֹת הַיָּדַיִם וּמִטְפְּחוֹת הַסַּפָּרִים וּמִטְפְּחוֹת הַסְּפָג,
phrases.en: Hand towels; and barbers' towels, which are used to cover a person having a haircut; and body-drying towels, all of which get quickly soiled, may be laundered on the intermediate days of a Festival.

phrases.he: הַזָּבִין וְהַזָּבוֹת וְהַנִּדּוֹת וְהַיּוֹלְדוֹת,
phrases.en: Zavim, men suffering from an impure venereal emission; zavot, women who experience a flow of menstrual-type blood on three consecutive days during a time of the month when they do not expect to experience menstrual bleeding; menstruating women; women who have just given birth;

phrases.he: וְכָל הָעוֹלִין מִטֻּמְאָה לְטָהֳרָה,
phrases.en: and all others who leave a state of ritual impurity for a state of ritual purity on the intermediate days of the Festival,

phrases.he: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מֻתָּרִין.
phrases.en: these people are all permitted to launder their clothes in order to purify themselves.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל אָדָם, אֲסוּרִין:
phrases.en: But all other people are prohibited from laundering during the intermediate days of the Festival.

phrases.he: וְאֵלּוּ כּוֹתְבִין בַּמּוֹעֵד,
phrases.en: And these are the documents that may be written on the intermediate days of a Festival:

phrases.he: קִדּוּשֵׁי נָשִׁים,
phrases.en: Documents of betrothal of wives,

phrases.he: גִּטִּין וְשׁוֹבָרִין,
phrases.en: bills of divorce; receipts

phrases.he: דְּיָתֵיקֵי,
phrases.en: wills [deyateiki];

phrases.he: מַתָּנָה וּפְרוֹזְבּוּלִין,
phrases.en: deeds of gift; perozbolin,

phrases.he: אִגְּרוֹת שׁוּם וְאִגְּרוֹת מָזוֹן,
phrases.en: letters of valuation, and letters of sustenance,

phrases.he: שִׁטְרֵי חֲלִיצָה וּמֵאוּנִים,
phrases.en: Documents of the ritual through which the brother-in-law frees the yevama of her levirate bonds [ḥalitza], documents in which the court records the refusal

phrases.he: וְשִׁטְרֵי בֵרוּרִין,
phrases.en: documents of arbitration,

phrases.he: וּגְזֵרוֹת בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.en: court rulings; and

phrases.he: וְאִגְּרוֹת שֶׁל רָשׁוּת:
phrases.en: the official correspondence of the ruling authorities.

phrases.he: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין שִׁטְרֵי חוֹב בַּמּוֹעֵד.
phrases.en: One may not write bills of debt on the intermediate days of a Festival.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ מַאֲמִינוֹ אוֹ שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מַה יֹּאכַל, הֲרֵי זֶה יִכְתֹּב.
phrases.en: But if the lender does not trust the borrower, and he is concerned that the borrower will later deny the loan, or if the scribe has nothing to eat, then he may write a bill of debt during the Festival week.

phrases.he: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין סְפָרִים, תְּפִלִּין וּמְזוּזוֹת, בַּמּוֹעֵד, וְאֵין מַגִּיהִין אוֹת אַחַת, אֲפִלּוּ בְּסֵפֶר (הָעֲזָרָה) עֶזְרָא.
phrases.en: One may not write Torah scrolls, phylacteries, or mezuzot on the intermediate days of a Festival, nor may one correct a single letter, even in the Torah scroll of Ezra, which was kept in the Temple and upon which all the Jewish communities relied.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כּוֹתֵב אָדָם תְּפִלִּין וּמְזוּזוֹת לְעַצְמוֹ, וְטוֹוֶה עַל יְרֵכוֹ תְּכֵלֶת לְצִיצִיתוֹ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: One may write phylacteries and mezuzot for himself on the intermediate days of a Festival if he needs them. And one may spin sky-blue wool for his ritual fringes on his thigh, but not in the ordinary manner with a spindle, as this procedure must be performed in an altered manner on the intermediate days of a Festival.

phrases.he: הַקּוֹבֵר אֶת מֵתוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים קֹדֶם לָרֶגֶל, בָּטְלָה הֵימֶנּוּ גְּזֵרַת שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.en: One who buries his deceased relative three days before a pilgrimage Festival has the decree of the seven-day period of mourning nullified for him by the Festival.

phrases.he: שְׁמֹנָה, בָּטְלָה הֵימֶנּוּ גְּזֵרַת שְׁלֹשִׁים,
phrases.en: If one buries his deceased relative eight days before a pilgrimage Festival, then the decree of thirty days is nullified for him.

phrases.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָמְרוּ, שַׁבָּת עוֹלָה וְאֵינָהּ מַפְסֶקֶת, רְגָלִים מַפְסִיקִין וְאֵינָן עוֹלִין:
phrases.en: This is because the Sages said a principle with regard to this issue: Shabbat counts as one of the days of mourning, although one may not mourn on it and it does not interrupt the mourning period, which continues after Shabbat. The pilgrimage Festivals, on the other hand, interrupt the mourning period, so that if one began mourning before such a Festival, then the mourning period is canceled by the Festival. They do not, however, count.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, עֲצֶרֶת כְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: From the time that the Temple was destroyed, Shavuot is like Shabbat,

phrases.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, כָּרְגָלִים.
phrases.en: Rabban Gamliel says: Even Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur are considered like the pilgrimage Festivals,

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, לֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה, אֶלָּא עֲצֶרֶת כָּרְגָלִים, רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים כְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: The halakha is neither in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Eliezer nor in accordance with the statement of Rabban Gamliel. Rather, with regard to mourning, Shavuot is treated like the other pilgrimage Festivals, whereas Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur are treated like Shabbat.

phrases.he: אֵין קוֹרְעִין, וְלֹא חוֹלְצִין,
phrases.en: do not rend their garments during the intermediate days of a Festival and do not remove their garments from their shoulders.

phrases.he: וְאֵין מַבְרִין, אֶלָּא קְרוֹבָיו שֶׁל מֵת,
phrases.en: And others do not provide them with a meal [mavrin] after the burial, except for close relatives of the deceased. And the consolers provide the first meal after the burial

phrases.he: וְאֵין מַבְרִין אֶלָּא עַל מִטָּה זְקוּפָה.
phrases.en: only while the mourner is sitting on an upright bed, and not on one that is overturned.

phrases.he: אֵין מוֹלִיכִין לְבֵית הָאֵבֶל לֹא בְּטַבְלָא וְלֹא בְאִסְקוּטְלָא וְלֹא בְקָנוֹן, אֶלָּא בְסַלִּים.
phrases.en: One does not bring the first meal after the burial to the house of mourning on a small tray [tavla], in a bowl [iskutla], or in a narrow-mouthed basket [kanon], but rather in ordinary baskets.

phrases.he: וְאֵין אוֹמְרִים בִּרְכַּת אֲבֵלִים בַּמּוֹעֵד, אֲבָל עוֹמְדִין בְּשׁוּרָה וּמְנַחֲמִין וּפוֹטְרִין אֶת הָרַבִּים:
phrases.en: And the mourners' blessing is not recited on the intermediate days of a Festival, but the consolers may stand in a row when the mourners leave the cemetery and console them. And the mourners dismiss the many consolers, by telling them that they may return home after they have fulfilled the mitzva of consoling the mourners.

phrases.he: אֵין מַנִּיחִין אֶת הַמִּטָּה בָּרְחוֹב, שֶׁלֹּא לְהַרְגִּיל אֶת הַהֶסְפֵּד,
phrases.en: The bier is not set down in the street so as not to encourage eulogies.

phrases.he: וְלֹא שֶׁל נָשִׁים לְעוֹלָם, מִפְּנֵי הַכָּבוֹד.
phrases.en: And the biers of women are never set down, due to their honor.

phrases.he: נָשִׁים בַּמּוֹעֵד מְעַנּוֹת, אֲבָל לֹא מְטַפְּחוֹת.
phrases.en: On a Festival women may wail, but they may not clap.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, הַסְּמוּכוֹת לַמִּטָּה, מְטַפְּחוֹת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yishmael says: Those who are close to the bier may clap.

phrases.he: בְּרָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים, בַּחֲנֻכָּה וּבְפוּרִים, מְעַנּוֹת, וּמְטַפְּחוֹת בָּזֶה וּבָזֶה, אֲבָל לֹא מְקוֹנְנוֹת.
phrases.en: On New Moons, Hanukkah and Purim, which are not Festivals by Torah law, the women may both wail and clap their hands in mourning. On both the intermediate days of a Festival and on New Moons, Hanukkah and Purim they may not lament.

phrases.he: נִקְבַּר הַמֵּת, לֹא מְעַנּוֹת וְלֹ מְטַפְּחוֹת.
phrases.en: After the deceased has been buried they may neither wail nor clap.

phrases.he: אֵיזֶהוּ עִנּוּי, שֶׁכֻּלָּן עוֹנוֹת כְּאֶחָת.
phrases.en: What is considered wailing? This is when they all wail together simultaneously.

phrases.he: קִינָה, שֶׁאַחַת מְדַבֶּרֶת וְכֻלָּן עוֹנוֹת אַחֲרֶיהָ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ירמיה ט), וְלַמֵּדְנָה בְנֹתֵיכֶם נֶהִי, וְאִשָּׁה רְעוּתָהּ קִינָה.
phrases.en: And what is considered a lament? This is when one speaks and they all answer after her with a repeated refrain, as it is stated: "And teach your daughters wailing and everyone her neighbor lamentation" (Jeremiah 9:19).

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא הוּא אוֹמֵר (ישעיה כה), בִּלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח, וּמָחָה ה' אֱלֹהִים דִּמְעָה מֵעַל כָּל פָּנִים וְגוֹ'.
phrases.en: But with regard to the future, the verse states: "He will destroy death forever; and the Lord, God, will wipe away tears from off all faces and the reproach of His people He will take away from off all the earth" (Isaiah 25:8).

phrases.he: הַכֹּל חַיָּבִין בָּרְאִיָּה,
phrases.en: All are obligated in the mitzva of appearance,

phrases.he: חוּץ מֵחֵרֵשׁ, שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן, וְטֻמְטוּם, וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס, וְנָשִׁים, וַעֲבָדִים שֶׁאֵינָם מְשֻׁחְרָרִים, הַחִגֵּר, וְהַסּוּמָא, וְהַחוֹלֶה, וְהַזָּקֵן, וּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לַעֲלוֹת בְּרַגְלָיו.
phrases.en: except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor; and a tumtum, and a hermaphrodite, and women, and slaves who are not emancipated; and the lame, and the blind, and the sick, and the old, and one who is unable to ascend on his own legs.

phrases.he: אֵיזֶהוּ קָטָן,
phrases.en: Who has the status of a minor with regard to this halakha?

phrases.he: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִרְכּוֹב עַל כְּתֵפָיו שֶׁל אָבִיו וְלַעֲלוֹת מִירוּשָׁלַיִם לְהַר הַבַּיִת,
phrases.en: Any child who is unable to ride on his father's shoulders and ascend from Jerusalem to the Temple Mount;

phrases.he: דִּבְרֵי בֵית שַׁמַּאי.
phrases.en: this is the statement of Beit Shammai.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים,
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say:

phrases.he: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לֶאֱחֹז בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו וְלַעֲלוֹת מִירוּשָׁלַיִם לְהַר הַבַּיִת,
phrases.en: Any child who is unable to hold his father's hand and ascend on foot from Jerusalem to the Temple Mount,

phrases.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמות כג) שָׁלֹשׁ רְגָלִים:
phrases.en: as it is stated: "Three times" (Exodus 23:14).

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, הָרְאִיָּה שְׁתֵּי כֶסֶף, וַחֲגִיגָה מָעָה כֶסֶף.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: The burnt-offering of appearance brought on a pilgrim Festival must be worth at least two silver coins, and the Festival peace-offering must be worth at least one silver ma'a coin.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, הָרְאִיָּה מָעָה כֶסֶף, וַחֲגִיגָה שְׁתֵּי כָסֶף:
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: The burnt-offering of appearance must be worth at least one silver ma'a and the Festival peace-offering at least two silver coins.

phrases.he: עוֹלוֹת בַּמּוֹעֵד בָּאוֹת מִן הַחֻלִּין,
phrases.en: Burnt-offerings that one sacrifices on the intermediate days of the Festival must come from non-sacred property

phrases.he: וְהַשְּׁלָמִים מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.en: But the peace-offerings may be brought from the second tithe

phrases.he: יוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מִן הַחֻלִּין,
phrases.en: With regard to the Festival peace-offering sacrificed on the first day of the festival of Passover, Beit Shammai say: It must come from non-sacred property

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר:
phrases.en: and Beit Hillel say: It may be brought even from the second tithe

phrases.he: יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹצְאִין יְדֵי חוֹבָתָן בִּנְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת וּבְמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה,
phrases.en: Israelites fulfill their obligation with vows and gift offerings and animal tithes.

phrases.he: וְהַכֹּהֲנִים בַּחַטָּאוֹת וּבָאֲשָׁמוֹת וּבַבְּכוֹר וּבֶחָזֶה וָשׁוֹק,
phrases.en: And the priests with sin-offerings and guilt-offerings and with firstborn and with the breast and thigh.

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא בָעוֹפוֹת וְלֹא בַמְּנָחוֹת:
phrases.en: However, they do not with birds, nor with meal-offerings.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אוֹכְלִים מְרֻבִּים וּנְכָסִים מֻעָטִים, מֵבִיא שְׁלָמִים מְרֻבִּים וְעוֹלוֹת מֻעָטוֹת.
phrases.en: One who has many eaters and a small amount of property, may bring many peace-offerings and few burnt-offerings

phrases.he: נְכָסִים מְרֻבִּים וְאוֹכְלִין מֻעָטִין, מֵבִיא עוֹלוֹת מְרֻבּוֹת וּשְׁלָמִים מֻעָטִין.
phrases.en: If one has much property and few eaters, he should bring many burnt-offerings and few peace-offerings

phrases.he: זֶה וָזֶה מֻעָט, עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר, מָעָה כֶסֶף וּשְׁתֵּי כָסֶף.
phrases.en: If both these and those are few, with regard to this individual it is stated that the Sages established the smallest amount of one silver ma'a for the burnt-offering of appearance in the Temple and two silver coins for the Festival peace-offerings

phrases.he: זֶה וָזֶה מְרֻבִּים, עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר (דברים טז) אִישׁ כְּמַתְּנַת יָדוֹ כְּבִרְכַּת יְיָ אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר נָתַן לָךְ.
phrases.en: If both his eaters and his property are many, with regard to this individual it is stated: "Every man shall give as he is able, according to the blessing of the Lord your God, which He has given you"

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁלֹּא חַג בְּיוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חָג, חוֹגֵג אֶת כָּל הָרֶגֶל וְיוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חָג.
phrases.en: one who did not celebrate by bringing the Festival peace-offering on the first day of the festival of Sukkot, he may celebrate and bring it during the entire remaining days of the pilgrimage Festival, and even on the final day of the Festival

phrases.he: עָבַר הָרֶגֶל וְלֹא חַג, אֵינוֹ חַיָּב בְּאַחֲרָיוּתוֹ.
phrases.en: the pilgrimage Festival passed and one did not celebrate by bringing the Festival peace-offering, he is not obligated to pay restitution for it

phrases.he: עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר (קהלת א) מְעֻוָּת לֹא יוּכַל לִתְקֹן, וְחֶסְרוֹן לֹא יוּכַל לְהִמָּנוֹת:
phrases.en: about this it is stated: "That which is crooked cannot be made straight; and that which is wanting cannot be numbered"

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא אוֹמֵר, אֵיזֶהוּ מְעֻוָּת שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִתְקֹן,
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says: Who is the crooked that cannot be made straight?

phrases.he: זֶה הַבָּא עַל הָעֶרְוָה וְהוֹלִיד מִמֶּנָּה מַמְזֵר.
phrases.en: This verse is referring to one who engaged in intercourse with a woman forbidden to him and fathered a mamzer with her.

phrases.he: אִם תֹּאמַר בְּגוֹנֵב וְגוֹזֵל, יָכוֹל הוּא לְהַחֲזִירוֹ וִיתַקֵּן.
phrases.en: If you say that it is referring to one who steals or robs, although he is crooked he can return what he stole and in this manner his sin will be rectified.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אוֹמֵר, אֵין קוֹרִין מְעֻוָּת אֶלָּא לְמִי שֶׁהָיָה מְתֻקָּן בַּתְּחִלָּה וְנִתְעַוֵּת,
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says: One calls crooked only someone who was initially straight and subsequently became crooked.

phrases.he: וְאֵיזֶה, זֶה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
phrases.en: And who is this? This is a Torah scholar who leaves his Torah study.

phrases.he: הֶתֵּר נְדָרִים פּוֹרְחִין בָּאֲוִיר, וְאֵין לָהֶם עַל מַה שֶּׁיִּסְמֹכוּ.
phrases.en: dissolution of vows, fly in the air and have nothing to support them,

phrases.he: הִלְכוֹת שַׁבָּת, חֲגִיגוֹת וְהַמְּעִילוֹת, הֲרֵי הֵם כַּהֲרָרִים הַתְּלוּיִין בְּשַׂעֲרָה, שֶׁהֵן מִקְרָא מֻעָט וַהֲלָכוֹת מְרֻבּוֹת.
phrases.en: The halakhot of Shabbat, Festival peace-offerings, and misuse of consecrated property are like mountains suspended by a hair, as they have little written about them in the Torah, and yet the details of their halakhot are numerous.

phrases.he: הַדִּינִין וְהָעֲבוֹדוֹת, הַטָּהֳרוֹת וְהַטֻּמְאוֹת וַעֲרָיוֹת, יֵשׁ לָהֶן עַל מַה שֶּׁיִּסְמֹכוּ.
phrases.en: The details of monetary law, sacrificial rites, ritual purity and impurity, and those with whom relations are forbidden all have something to support them,

phrases.he: הֵן הֵן גּוּפֵי תּוֹרָה:
phrases.en: and these are the essential parts of Torah.

phrases.he: אֵין דּוֹרְשִׁין בַּעֲרָיוֹת בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה.
phrases.en: One may not expound the topic of forbidden sexual relations before three or more individuals

phrases.he: וְלֹא בְמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית בִּשְׁנַיִם.
phrases.en: nor may one expound the act of Creation and the secrets of the beginning of the world before two or more individuals

phrases.he: וְלֹא בַמֶּרְכָּבָה בְּיָחִיד, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיָה חָכָם וּמֵבִין מִדַּעְתּוֹ.
phrases.en: nor may one expound by oneself the Design of the Divine Chariot, a mystical teaching with regard to the ways God conducts the world, unless he is wise and understands most matters on his own

phrases.he: כָּל הַמִּסְתַּכֵּל בְּאַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים, רָאוּי לוֹ כְּאִלּוּ לֹא בָּא לָעוֹלָם, מַה לְּמַעְלָה, מַה לְּמַטָּה, מַה לְּפָנִים, וּמַה לְּאָחוֹר.
phrases.en: Whoever looks at four matters, it would have been better for him had he never entered the world: Anyone who reflects upon what is above the firmament and what is below the earth, what was before Creation, and what will be after the end of the world

phrases.he: וְכָל שֶׁלֹּא חָס עַל כְּבוֹד קוֹנוֹ, רָאוּי לוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם:
phrases.en: And anyone who has no concern for the honor of his Maker, who inquires into and deals with matters not permitted to him, deserves to have never come to the world

phrases.he: יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא לִסְמוֹךְ,
phrases.en: Yosei ben Yo'ezer says not to place

phrases.he: יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹחָנָן אוֹמֵר לִסְמוֹךְ.
phrases.en: Yosef ben Yoḥanan, says to place them

phrases.he: יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן פְּרַחְיָה אוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא לִסְמוֹךְ,
phrases.en: Yehoshua ben Peraḥya says not to place them

phrases.he: נִתַּאי הָאַרְבֵּלִי אוֹמֵר לִסְמוֹךְ.
phrases.en: Nitai HaArbeli says to place them

phrases.he: יְהוּדָה בֶּן טַבַּאי אוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא לִסְמוֹךְ,
phrases.en: Yehuda ben Tabbai says not to place them

phrases.he: שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטָח אוֹמֵר לִסְמוֹךְ.
phrases.en: Shimon ben Shataḥ says to place them

phrases.he: שְׁמַעְיָה אוֹמֵר לִסְמוֹךְ.
phrases.en: Shemaya says to place them

phrases.he: אַבְטַלְיוֹן אוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא לִסְמוֹךְ.
phrases.en: Avtalyon says not to place them

phrases.he: הִלֵּל וּמְנַחֵם לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ.
phrases.en: Hillel and Menaḥem did not disagree

phrases.he: יָצָא מְנַחֵם,
phrases.en: Menaḥem departed

phrases.he: נִכְנַס שַׁמַּאי.
phrases.en: Shammai entered

phrases.he: שַׁמַּאי אוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא לִסְמוֹךְ,
phrases.en: Shammai says not to place them

phrases.he: הִלֵּל אוֹמֵר לִסְמוֹךְ.
phrases.en: Hillel says to place them

phrases.he: הָרִאשׁוֹנִים הָיוּ נְשִׂיאִים, וּשְׁנִיִּים לָהֶם אַב בֵּית דִּין:
phrases.en: The first served as Nasi, and their counterparts served as deputy Nasi.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מְבִיאִין שְׁלָמִים
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: One may bring peace-offerings

phrases.he: וְאֵין סוֹמְכִין עֲלֵיהֶם,
phrases.en: but one may not place his hands on them

phrases.he: אֲבָל לֹא עוֹלוֹת.
phrases.en: However, one may not bring burnt-offerings

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מְבִיאִין שְׁלָמִים וְעוֹלוֹת וְסוֹמְכִין עֲלֵיהֶם:
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: One may bring peace-offerings and also burnt-offerings, and one places his hands on both of them.

phrases.he: עֲצֶרֶת שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, יוֹם טְבוֹחַ אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.en: the festival of Shavuot occurs on the eve of Shabbat, Beit Shammai say: The day of slaughter is after Shabbat,

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, אֵין יוֹם טְבוֹחַ אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: The day of slaughter is not after Shabbat.

phrases.he: וּמוֹדִים שֶׁאִם חָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת, שֶׁיּוֹם טְבוֹחַ אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.en: But they concede that if Shavuot occurs on Shabbat, the day of slaughter is after Shabbat.

phrases.he: וְאֵין כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מִתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּכֵלָיו,
phrases.en: the High Priest would not dress in his garments

phrases.he: וּמֻתָּרִין בְּהֶסְפֵּד וּבְתַעֲנִית,
phrases.en: And all were permitted to eulogize and fast

phrases.he: שֶׁלֹּא לְקַיֵּם דִּבְרֵי הָאוֹמְרִין עֲצֶרֶת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת:
phrases.en: not to uphold the opinion of who would say: Shavuot must always occur after Shabbat.

phrases.he: נוֹטְלִין לַיָּדַיִם לְחֻלִּין וּלְמַעֲשֵׂר וְלִתְרוּמָה.
phrases.en: One must wash his hands by pouring a quarter-log of water over them before eating non-sacred food, and for tithes and for teruma;

phrases.he: וּלְקֹדֶשׁ, מַטְבִּילִין.
phrases.en: but for eating sacrificial food one must immerse one's hands in purification waters, such as those of a ritual bath.

phrases.he: וּלְחַטָּאת, אִם נִטְמְאוּ יָדָיו, נִטְמָא גוּפוֹ:
phrases.en: And with regard to one who wishes to touch the purification waters of the red heifer used for sprinkling, if one's hands were rendered impure even by rabbinical ritual impurity, which usually only renders the hands impure, his entire body is rendered impure, and he must immerse himself in a ritual bath.

phrases.he: הַטּוֹבֵל לְחֻלִּין וְהֻחְזַק לְחֻלִּין, אָסוּר לְמַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.en: If one immersed for the purpose of eating non-sacred food, he assumes a presumptive status of ritual purity for non-sacred food, and it is prohibited for him to eat tithes.

phrases.he: טָבַל לְמַעֲשֵׂר וְהֻחְזַק לְמַעֲשֵׂר, אָסוּר לִתְרוּמָה.
phrases.en: If one immersed to eat tithes, he assumes a presumptive status for tithes, but he is prohibited from eating teruma.

phrases.he: טָבַל לִתְרוּמָה, וְהֻחְזַק לִתְרוּמָה, אָסוּר לְקֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.en: If one immersed for teruma, he assumes a presumptive status for teruma, but he is prohibited from eating sacrificial food.

phrases.he: טָבַל לְקֹדֶשׁ וְהֻחְזַק לְקֹדֶשׁ, אָסוּר לְחַטָּאת.
phrases.en: If he immersed for sacrificial food, he assumes a presumptive status for sacrificial food, but he is prohibited from coming in contact with the purification waters.

phrases.he: טָבַל לְחָמוּר, מֻתָּר לְקַל.
phrases.en: One who immersed to eat a food in a stringent category is permitted to eat a food in a lenient one.

phrases.he: טָבַל וְלֹא הֻחְזַק, כְּאִלּוּ לֹא טָבָל:
