phrases.he: הַקַּלָתוּת שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִים שֶׁנִּפְחֲתָה פָחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים, טְמֵאָה, שֶׁהוּא מַסִּיק מִלְּמַטָּן וּקְדֵרָה בְשֵׁלָה מִלְמַעְלָן. יָתֵר מִכָּאן, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: The fire-basket of a householder which was lessened by less than three handbreadths is susceptible to impurity because when it is heated from below a pot above would still boil. If [it was lessened] to a lower depth it is not susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: נָתַן אֶבֶן אוֹ צְרוֹר, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If subsequently a stone or gravel was put into it, it is still not susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: מֵרְחָהּ בְּטִיט, מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא.
phrases.en: If it was plastered over with clay, it may contract impurity from that point and onwards.

phrases.he: זוֹ הָיְתָה תְשׁוּבַת רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְתַנּוּר שֶׁנְּתָנוֹ עַל פִּי הַבּוֹר אוֹ עַל פִּי הַדּוּת
phrases.en: This was Rabbi Judah's reply in connection with the oven that was placed over the mouth of a cistern or over that of a cellar.

phrases.he: דָּכוֹן שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל קְדֵרוֹת, טָהוֹר מִשּׁוּם כִּירָה, וְטָמֵא מִשּׁוּם כְּלִי קִבּוּל.
phrases.en: A hob that has a receptacle for pots is clean as a stove but unclean as a receptacle.

phrases.he: הַצְּדָדִין שֶׁלּוֹ, הַנּוֹגֵעַ בָּהֶם אֵינוֹ טָמֵא מִשּׁוּם כִּירָה.
phrases.en: As to its sides, whatever touches them does not become unclean as if the hob had been a stove, But as regards its wide side: Rabbi Meir holds it to be clean But Rabbi Judah holds it to be unclean.

phrases.he: הָרַחַב שֶׁלּוֹ, רַבִּי מֵאִיר מְטַהֵר, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.en: The same law applies also where a basket was inverted and a stove was put upon it.

phrases.he: וְכֵן הַכּוֹפֶה אֶת הַסַּל וְעוֹשֶׂה עַל גַּבָּיו כִּירָה
כִּירָה שֶׁנֶּחְלְקָה לְאָרְכָּהּ, טְהוֹרָה. וּלְרָחְבָּהּ, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: A double stove which was split into two parts along its length is clean. Through its breadth is unclean.

phrases.he: כֻּפָּח שֶׁנֶּחְלַק בֵּין לְאָרְכּוֹ בֵּין לְרָחְבּוֹ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A single stove which was split into two parts, by its length or by its width, it is not susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: חֲצַר הַכִּירָה, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִיא גְבוֹהָה שָׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת, מִטַּמְּאָה בְמַגָּע וּבַאֲוִיר.
phrases.en: As to the extension around a stove, whenever it is three fingerbreadths high it contracts impurity by contact and also through its air-space, but if it is less it contracts impurity through contact and not through its air- space.

phrases.he: פְּחוּתָה מִכָּאן, מִטַּמְּאָה בְמַגָּע וְאֵינָהּ מִטַּמְּאָה בַאֲוִיר. כֵּיצַד מְשַׁעֲרִין אוֹתָהּ.
רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, נוֹתֵן אֶת הַשַּׁפּוּד מִלְמַעְלָן לְמַטָּן וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ מִטַּמְּאָה בַאֲוִיר.
phrases.en: How is the air-space determined? Rabbi Ishmael says: He puts a spit from above to below and opposite it contracts impurity through the air-space.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר, נִטְמְאָה הַכִּירָה, נִטְמֵאת הֶחָצֵר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Jacob says: if the stove contracted impurity the extension is also unclean, but if the fender contracts impurity the stove does not become unclean.

phrases.he: נִטְמְאָה הֶחָצֵר, לֹא נִטְמֵאת הַכִּירָה
הָיְתָה מֻפְרֶשֶׁת מִן הַכִּירָה, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִיא גְבוֹהָה שָׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת, מִטַּמָּא בְמַגָּע וּבַאֲוִיר.
phrases.en: If it [the extension] was detached from the stove, whenever it was three fingerbreadths high it contracts impurity by contact and through its air-space, If it was lower or if it was smooth it is clean.

phrases.he: פְּחוּתָה מִכָּאן אוֹ שֶׁהָיְתָה חֲלָקָה, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If three props on a stove were three fingerbreadths high, they contract impurity by contact and through their air-space.

phrases.he: פִּטְפּוּטֵי כִירָה, שְׁלֹשָׁה, שֶׁל שָׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת, מִטַּמְּאִים בְּמַגָּע וּבַאֲוִיר.
phrases.en: If they were lower, all the more so they contract impurity, even where they were four in number.

phrases.he: פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן, כָּל שֶׁכֵּן הֵן טְמֵאִים, וַאֲפִלּוּ הֵן אַרְבָּעָה
נִטַּל אַחַד מֵהֶן, מִטַּמְּאִין בְּמַגָּע וְאֵינָם מִטַּמְּאִים בַּאֲוִיר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַהֵר.
phrases.en: If one of them [i.e. the props] was removed, the remaining ones contract impurity by contact but not through air-space, the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Shimon says that they are clean.

phrases.he: עָשָׂה שְׁנַיִם, זֶה כְנֶגֶד זֶה, מִטַּמְּאִין בְּמַגָּע וּבַאֲוִיר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַהֵר.
phrases.en: If originally he made two props, one opposite the other, they contract impurity by contact and through air-space; the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Shimon says that they are clean.

phrases.he: הָיוּ גְבוֹהִין מִשָּׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת, מִשָּׁלֹשׁ וּלְמַטָּן מִטַּמְּאִים בְּמַגָּע וּבַאֲוִיר, מִשָּׁלֹשׁ וּלְמַעְלָן מִטַּמְּאִין בְּמַגָּע וְאֵינָן מִטַּמְּאִין בַּאֲוִיר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַהֵר.
phrases.en: If they were more than three fingerbreadths high, the parts that are three fingerbreadths high and below contract impurity by contact and through air-space but the parts that are more than three fingerbreadths high contract impurity by contact and not through air-space; the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Shimon says that they are clean.

phrases.he: הָיוּ מְשׁוּכִים מִן הַשָּׂפָה, בְּתוֹךְ שָׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת, מִטַּמְּאִים בְּמַגָּע וּבַאֲוִיר, חוּץ מִשָּׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת מִטַּמְּאִים בְּמַגָּע וְאֵינָם מִטַּמְּאִים בַּאֲוִיר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַהֵר
phrases.en: If they were withdrawn from the rim [of the stove], the parts which are within three fingerbreadths contract impurity by contact and through air-space, and those parts that are removed more than three fingerbreadths contract impurity by contact but not through air-space, the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Shimon says that they are clean.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד מְשַׁעֲרִין אוֹתָן. רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, נוֹתֵן אֶת הַכַּנָּה בֵּינֵיהֶן, מִן הַכַּנָּה וְלַחוּץ טָהוֹר, מִן הַכַּנָּה וְלִפְנִים, וּמְקוֹם הַכַּנָּה טָמֵא:
phrases.en: How do we measure them? Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel says: he puts the measuring-rod between them, and any part that is outside the measuring-rod is clean while any part inside the measuring-rod, including the place of the measuring-rod itself, is unclean.

phrases.he: הַתַּנּוּר שֶׁחֲצָצוֹ בִנְסָרִים אוֹ בִירִיעוֹת, נִמְצָא שֶׁרֶץ בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד, הַכֹּל טָמֵא.
phrases.en: An oven which they partitioned with boards or hangings, and in it was found a sheretz in one compartment, the entire oven is unclean.

phrases.he: כַּוֶּרֶת פְּחוּתָה וּפְקוּקָה בְקַשׁ וּמְשֻׁלְשֶׁלֶת לַאֲוִיר הַתַּנּוּר, הַשֶּׁרֶץ בְּתוֹכָהּ, הַתַּנּוּר טָמֵא.
phrases.en: A hive which was broken and its gap was stopped up with straw and was suspended within the air-space of an oven while a sheretz was within it, the oven becomes unclean.

phrases.he: הַשֶּׁרֶץ בַּתַּנּוּר, אֳכָלִין שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ טְמֵאִין. וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְטַהֵר.
phrases.en: If a sheretz was within the oven, any food within the hive becomes unclean. But Rabbi Eliezer says that it is clean.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, אִם הִצִּילָה בְמֵת הֶחָמוּר, לֹא תַצִּיל בִּכְלִי חֶרֶס הַקַּל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer said: if it affords protection in the case of a corpse which is more consequential, should it not afford protection in the case of an earthenware vessel which is less consequential?

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, אִם הִצִּילָה בְמֵת הֶחָמוּר, שֶׁכֵּן חוֹלְקִים אֹהָלִים, תַּצִּיל בִּכְלִי חֶרֶס הַקַּל, שֶׁאֵין חוֹלְקִים כְּלִי חָרֶס:
phrases.en: They said to him: if it affords protection in the case of corpse impurity, this is because tents are divided, should it also afford protection in the case of an earthenware vessel which is not divided?

phrases.he: הָיְתָה שְׁלֵמָה, וְכֵן הַקֻּפָּה, וְכֵן הַחֵמֶת, הַשֶּׁרֶץ בְּתוֹכָהּ, הַתַּנּוּר טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If the hive was complete, and so too in the case of a basket or a skin-bottle, and a sheretz was within it the oven remains clean.

phrases.he: הַשֶּׁרֶץ בַּתַּנּוּר, אֳכָלִין שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: If the sheretz was in the oven, any food in the hive remain clean.

phrases.he: נִקְּבוּ, הֶעָשׂוּי לְאֳכָלִין, שִׁעוּרָן בְּזֵיתִים.
phrases.en: If a hole was made in it: A vessel that is used for food must have a hole large enough for olives to fall through, If it is used for liquids the hole must be large enough for liquids to pass into it, And if it is used for either it is subjected to the greater restriction: the hole need only be large enough for liquids to pass into it.

phrases.he: הֶעָשׂוּי לְמַשְׁקִין, שִׁעוּרָן בְּמַשְׁקִים.
הֶעָשׂוּי לְכָךְ וּלְכָךְ, מַטִּילִים אוֹתוֹ לְחֻמְרוֹ, בְּכוֹנֵס מַשְׁקֶה
סְרֵידָה שֶׁהִיא נְתוּנָה עַל פִּי הַתַּנּוּר וְשׁוֹקַעַת לְתוֹכוֹ וְאֵין לָהּ גַּפַּיִם, הַשֶּׁרֶץ בְּתוֹכָהּ, הַתַּנּוּר טָמֵא.
phrases.en: Netting placed over the mouth of an oven and slightly sinking into it, and having no frame: If a sheretz was in it, the oven becomes unclean; If the sheretz was in the oven, the food in the netting becomes unclean, since only vessels afford protection against an impurity in an earthen vessel.

phrases.he: הַשֶּׁרֶץ בַּתַּנּוּר, אֳכָלִים שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ, טְמֵאִין, שֶׁאֵין מַצִּילִין מִיַּד כְּלִי חֶרֶס אֶלָּא כֵלִים.
phrases.en: A jar full of pure liquids placed beneath the bottom of an oven, and a sheretz in the oven – the jar and the liquids remain clean.

phrases.he: חָבִית שֶׁהִיא מְלֵאָה מַשְׁקִין טְהוֹרִין, וּנְתוּנָה לְמַטָּה מִנְּחֻשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל תַּנּוּר, הַשֶּׁרֶץ בַּתַּנּוּר, הֶחָבִית וְהַמַּשְׁקִין טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: If it was inverted, with its mouth projecting into the air-space of the oven, and a sheretz was in the oven, the liquid that clings to the sides of the jar remains clean.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה כְפוּיָה וּפִיהָ לַאֲוִיר הַתַּנּוּר, הַשֶּׁרֶץ בַּתַּנּוּר, מַשְׁקֶה טוֹפֵחַ שֶׁבְּשׁוּלֵי הֶחָבִית טָהוֹר
קְדֵרָה שֶׁהִיא נְתוּנָה בַתַּנּוּר, הַשֶּׁרֶץ בַּתַּנּוּר, הַקְּדֵרָה טְהוֹרָה, שֶׁאֵין כְּלִי חֶרֶס מְטַמֵּא כֵלִים.
phrases.en: A pot which was placed in an oven if a sheretz was in the oven, the pot remains clean since an earthen vessel does not impart impurity to vessels.

phrases.he: הָיָה בָהּ מַשְׁקֶה טוֹפֵחַ, נִטְמָא וְטִמְּאָהּ.
phrases.en: If it contained dripping liquid, the latter contracts impurity and the pot also becomes unclean.

phrases.he: הֲרֵי זֶה אוֹמֵר, מְטַמְּאֶיךָ לֹא טִמְּאוּנִי וְאַתָּה טִמֵּאתָנִי
phrases.en: It is as if this one says, "That which made you unclean did not make me unclean, but you have made me unclean."

phrases.he: תַּרְנְגוֹל שֶׁבָּלַע אֶת הַשֶּׁרֶץ וְנָפַל לַאֲוִיר הַתַּנּוּר, טָהוֹר. וְאִם מֵת, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If a rooster that swallowed a sheretz fell within the air-space of an oven, the oven remains clean; If the rooster died, the oven becomes unclean.

phrases.he: הַשֶּׁרֶץ שֶׁנִּמְצָא בַתַּנּוּר, הַפַּת שֶׁבְּתוֹכוֹ, שְׁנִיָּה, שֶׁהַתַּנּוּר תְּחִלָּה
phrases.en: If a sheretz was found in an oven, any bread in it contracts second degree impurity since the oven is of the first degree.

phrases.he: בֵּית שְׂאֹר מֻקָּף צָמִיד פָּתִיל וְנָתוּן לְתוֹךְ הַתַּנּוּר, הַשְּׂאֹר וְהַשֶּׁרֶץ בְּתוֹכוֹ וְהַקֶּרֶץ בֵּינְתַיִם, הַתַּנּוּר טָמֵא וְהַשְּׂאֹר טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A leavening pot with a tightly fitting lid which was put in an oven, and there was some leaven and a sheretz within the pot, but there was a partition (of inedible bread) between them, the oven is unclean but the leaven is clean.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיָה כַזַּיִת מִן הַמֵּת, הַתַּנּוּר וְהַבַּיִת טָמֵא, וְהַשְּׂאֹר טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: But if it was an olive's bulk of corpse, both the oven and the house are unclean, and the leaven remains clean.

phrases.he: אִם יֶשׁ שָׁם פּוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח, הַכֹּל טָמֵא
phrases.en: If in the partition there was an opening of one handbreadth, all become unclean.

phrases.he: הַשֶּׁרֶץ שֶׁנִּמְצָא בָעַיִן שֶׁל תַּנּוּר, בָּעַיִן שֶׁל כִּירָה, בָּעַיִן שֶׁל כֻּפָּח, מִן הַשָּׂפָה הַפְּנִימִית וְלַחוּץ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A sheretz which was found in the eye-hole of an oven or of a double stove or of a single stove: If it was outside the inner edge, it is clean.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיָה בָאֲוִיר, אֲפִלּוּ כַזַּיִת מִן הַמֵּת, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If it [the oven] was in the open air, even if it was an olive's bulk of corpse it is clean.

phrases.he: וְאִם יֶשׁ שָׁם פּוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח, הַכֹּל טָמֵא
phrases.en: If there was [in the eye-hole] an opening of one handbreadth, it is all unclean.

phrases.he: נִמְצָא מְקוֹם הַנָּחַת הָעֵצִים,
phrases.en: If a sheretz was found in the [place in a stove] where wood is put: Rabbi Judah says: if it was within the outer edge, [the stove] becomes unclean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מִן הַשָּׂפָה הַחִיצוֹנָה וְלִפְנִים, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: But the sages say: if it was outside the inner edge [the stove] remains clean.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, מִשָּׂפָה הַפְּנִימִית וְלַחוּץ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: if it was found beneath the spot where the pot is placed and inwards, the stove becomes unclean, but if beneath the spot where the pot is set and outwards, it remains clean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, מִכְּנֶגֶד שְׁפִיתַת הַקְּדֵרָה וְלִפְנִים, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If it was found on the place where the bath-keeper sits, or where the dyer sits, or where the olive-boilers sit, the stove remains clean.

phrases.he: מִכְּנֶגֶד שְׁפִיתַת הַקְּדֵרָה וְלַחוּץ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: It only becomes unclean only [when the sheretz] is found in the enclosed part and inwards.

phrases.he: נִמְצָא מְקוֹם יְשִׁיבַת הַבַּלָּן, מְקוֹם יְשִׁיבַת הַצַּבָּע, מְקוֹם יְשִׁיבַת שֶׁל שׁוֹלְקֵי זֵיתִים, טָהוֹר.
אֵין טָמֵא אֶלָּא מִן הַסְּתִימָה וְלִפְנִים
בּוֹר שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ בֵית שְׁפִיתָה, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: A pit which has a place on which a pot may be set is unclean.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל עוֹשֵׂי זְכוּכִית, אִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ בֵית שְׁפִיתָה, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: And so also an oven of glass-blowers, if it has a place on which a pot may be set, it is unclean.

phrases.he: כִּבְשָׁן שֶׁל סַיָּדִין וְשֶׁל זַגָּגִין וְשֶׁל יוֹצְרִים, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: The furnace of lime-burners, or of glaziers, or of potters is clean.

phrases.he: פוּרְנָה, אִם יֶשׁ לָהּ לִזְבֵּז, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: A purna: If it has a frame is unclean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם יֶשׁ לָהּ אִסְטְגִיּוֹת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: if it has coverings [for compartments.

phrases.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, אִם יֶשׁ לָהּ שְׂפָיוֹת
phrases.en: Rabban Gamaliel says: if it has edges.

phrases.he: מַגַּע טְמֵא מֵת, שֶׁהָיוּ אֳכָלִין וּמַשְׁקִין לְתוֹךְ פִּיו, הִכְנִיס רֹאשׁוֹ לַאֲוִיר הַתַּנּוּר טָהוֹר, טִמְּאוּהוּ.
phrases.en: If a person who came in contact with one who has contracted corpse impurity had (food liquids in his mouth and he put his head into the air-space of an oven that was clean, they cause the oven to be unclean.

phrases.he: וְטָהוֹר שֶׁהָיוּ אֳכָלִין וּמַשְׁקִין לְתוֹךְ פִּיו וְהִכְנִיס רֹאשׁוֹ לַאֲוִיר הַתַּנּוּר טָמֵא, נִטְמָאוּ.
phrases.en: If a person who was clean had food or liquids in his mouth and he put his head into the air-space of an oven that was unclean, they become unclean.

phrases.he: הָיָה אוֹכֵל דְּבֵלָה בְיָדַיִם מְסֹאָבוֹת, הִכְנִיס יָדוֹ לְתוֹךְ פִּיו לִטֹּל אֶת הַצְּרוֹר, רַבִּי מֵאִיר מְטַמֵּא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַהֵר.
phrases.en: If a person was eating a pressed fig with impure hands and he put his hand into his mouth to remove a small stone: Rabbi Meir considers the fig to be unclean But Rabbi Judah says it as clean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אִם הָפַךְ, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: if he turned it over [in his mouth] the fig is unclean but if he did not turn it over the fig is clean.

phrases.he: אִם לֹא הָפַךְ, טָהוֹר.
הָיָה פֻנְדְּיוֹן לְתוֹךְ פִּיו,
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אִם לִצְמָאוֹ, טָמֵא:
phrases.en: If the person had a pondion in his mouth, Rabbi Yose says: if he kept it there to relieve his thirst it becomes unclean.

phrases.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁנָּטַף חָלָב מִדַּדֶּיהָ וְנָפַל לַאֲוִיר הַתַּנּוּר, טָמֵא, שֶׁהַמַּשְׁקֶה מְטַמֵּא לְרָצוֹן וְשֶׁלֹּא לְרָצוֹן.
phrases.en: If milk [of an impure woman] dripped from a woman's breasts and fell into the air-space of an oven, the oven becomes unclean, since a liquid conveys impurity regardless of whether one wanted it there or not.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה גוֹרַפְתּוֹ וְהִכַּתָּהּ הַקּוֹץ וְיָצָא מִמֶּנָּה דָם, אוֹ שֶׁנִּכְוָת וְנָתְנָה אֶצְבָּעָהּ לְתוֹךְ פִּיהָ, נִטְמָא
phrases.en: If she was sweeping it out and a thorn pricked her and she bled, or if she burnt herself and put her finger into her mouth, the oven becomes unclean.

phrases.he: מַחַט אוֹ טַבַּעַת שֶׁנִּמְצְאוּ בִנְחֻשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל תַּנּוּר, נִרְאִין אֲבָל לֹא יוֹצְאִים, אִם אוֹפֶה אֶת הַבָּצֵק וְהוּא נוֹגֵעַ בָּהֶן, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If a needle or a ring was found in the ground of an oven, and they can be seen but they don't stick out into the oven, if one bakes dough and it touches them, the [oven] is unclean.

phrases.he: בְּאֵיזֶה בָצֵק אָמְרוּ, בְּבָצֵק הַבֵּינוֹנִי.
phrases.en: Regarding which dough did they speak? Medium dough.

phrases.he: נִמְצְאוּ בִטְפֵלַת הַתַּנּוּר מֻקָּף צָמִיד פָּתִיל, אִם בְּטָמֵא, טְמֵאִין. וְאִם בְּטָהוֹר, טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: If they are found in the plaster of an oven with a tightly fitting lid: If the oven is unclean, they are unclean, If the oven is clean, they are clean.

phrases.he: נִמְצְאוּ בִמְגוּפַת הֶחָבִית, מִצִּדֶּיהָ, טְמֵאִים, מִכְּנֶגֶד פִּיהָ, טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: If they are found in the stopper of a jar: If on the sides, they are unclean. If opposite the mouth, they are clean.

phrases.he: נִרְאִין בְּתוֹכָהּ אֲבָל לֹא לַאֲוִירָהּ, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: If they can be seen in it, but they do not enter its airspace, they are clean.

phrases.he: שׁוֹקְעִים בְּתוֹכָהּ וְתַחְתֵּיהֶם כִּקְלִפַּת הַשּׁוּם, טְהוֹרִין
phrases.en: If they sink into it, and there is [plaster] underneath them as thick as garlic peel, they are clean.

phrases.he: חָבִית שֶׁהִיא מְלֵאָה מַשְׁקִין טְהוֹרִין וּמְנִיקָת בְּתוֹכָהּ, מֻקֶּפֶת צָמִיד פָּתִיל וּנְתוּנָה בְאֹהֶל הַמֵּת,
phrases.en: A jar that was full of clean liquids, with a siphon in it, and it had a tightly fitting cover and was in a tent in which there was a corpse: Bet Shammai says: both the jar and the liquids are clean but the siphon is unclean.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, הֶחָבִית וְהַמַּשְׁקִין טְהוֹרִין, וּמְנִיקָת טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: And Bet Hillel says: the siphon also is clean.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִין, אַף מְנִיקָת טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: Bet Hillel changed their mind and ruled in agreement with Bet Shammai.

phrases.he: חָזְרוּ בֵית הִלֵּל לְהוֹרוֹת כְּדִבְרֵי בֵית שַׁמָּאי
הַשֶּׁרֶץ שֶׁנִּמְצָא לְמַטָּה מִנְּחֻשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל תַּנּוּר, טָהוֹר, שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר, חַי נָפַל וְעַכְשָׁיו מֵת.
phrases.en: If a sheretz was found beneath the bottom of an oven, the oven remains clean, for I can assume that it fell there while it was still alive and that it died only now.

phrases.he: מַחַט אוֹ טַבַּעַת שֶׁנִּמְצְאוּ לְמַטָּה מִנְּחֻשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל תַּנּוּר, טָהוֹר, שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר, שָׁם הָיוּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא בָא הַתַּנּוּר.
phrases.en: If a needle or a ring was found beneath the bottom of an oven, the oven remains clean, for I can assume that they were there before the oven arrived.

phrases.he: נִמְצְאוּ בְאֵפֶר מִקְלֶה, טָמֵא, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בַמֶּה יִתְלֶה
phrases.en: If it was found in the wood ashes, the oven is unclean since one has no ground on which to base an assumption of cleanness.

phrases.he: סְפוֹג שֶׁבָּלַע מַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִין וְנָגוּב מִבַּחוּץ וְנָפַל לַאֲוִיר הַתַּנּוּר, טָמֵא, שֶׁסּוֹף מַשְׁקֶה לָצֵאת.
phrases.en: A sponge which had absorbed unclean liquids and its outer surface became dry and it fell into the air-space of an oven, the oven is unclean, for the liquid would eventually come out.

phrases.he: וְכֵן חֲתִיכָה שֶׁל לֶפֶת וְשֶׁל גֶּמִי.
phrases.en: And the same with regard to a piece of turnip or reed grass.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַהֵר בִּשְׁנֵי אֵלּוּ
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: the oven is clean in both these cases.

phrases.he: חֲרָסִין שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן מַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִין וְנָפְלוּ לַאֲוִיר הַתַּנּוּר, הֻסַּק הַתַּנּוּר, טָמֵא, שֶׁסּוֹף מַשְׁקֶה לָצֵאת.
phrases.en: Potsherds that had been used for unclean liquids which fell into the air-space of an oven, if the oven was heated, it becomes unclean, for the liquid would eventually come out.

phrases.he: וְכֵן בְּגֶפֶת חֲדָשָׁה, אֲבָל בִּישָׁנָה, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: And the same with regard to fresh olive peat, but if it was old, the oven remains clean.

phrases.he: וְאִם יָדוּעַ שֶׁיּוֹצֵא מֵהֶן מַשְׁקִין, אֲפִלּוּ לְאַחַר שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים, נִטְמָא
phrases.en: If it was known that liquid emerges, even after the lapse of three years, the oven becomes unclean.

phrases.he: הַגֶּפֶת וְהַזַּגִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ בְטָהֳרָה וְהָלְכוּ עֲלֵיהֶם טְמֵאִים, וְאַחַר כָּךְ יָצְאוּ מֵהֶן מַשְׁקִין, טְהוֹרִין, שֶׁמִּתְּחִלָּתָן נַעֲשׂוּ בְטָהֳרָה.
phrases.en: If olive peat or grape skins had been prepared in conditions of cleanness, and unclean persons trod upon them and afterwards liquids emerged from them, they remain clean, since they had originally been prepared in conditions of cleanness.

phrases.he: כּוּשׁ שֶׁבָּלַע אֶת הַצִּנּוֹרָא, מַלְמָד שֶׁבָּלַע אֶת הַדָּרְבָן, לְבֵנָה שֶׁבָּלְעָה אֶת הַטַּבַּעַת, וְהֵן טְהוֹרִים, נִכְנְסוּ לְאֹהֶל הַמֵּת, נִטְמָאוּ. הֱסִיטָן הַזָּב, נִטְמָאוּ.
phrases.en: If a spindle hook was sunk into the spindle, or the iron point into the ox goad, or a ring into a brick, and all these were clean, and then they were brought into a tent in which was a corpse, they become unclean. If a zav caused them to move they become unclean.

phrases.he: נָפְלוּ לַאֲוִיר הַתַּנּוּר טָהוֹר, טִמְּאוּהוּ.
phrases.en: If they then fell into the air-space of a clean oven, they cause it to be unclean.

phrases.he: נָגַע בָּהֶן כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, טָהוֹר
phrases.en: If a loaf of terumah came in contact with them, it remains clean.

phrases.he: סְרֵידָה שֶׁהִיא נְתוּנָה עַל פִּי הַתַּנּוּר מֻקָּף צָמִיד פָּתִיל, נִסְדַּק מִן הַתַּנּוּר לַסְּרֵידָה, שִׁעוּרוֹ מְלֹא פִי מַרְדֵּעַ שֶׁלֹּא נִכְנָס.
phrases.en: If there was netting placed over the mouth of an oven, forming a tightly fitting lid, and a split appeared between the oven and the colander, the minimum size [to allow impurity to enter] is that of the circumference of the tip of an ox goad that cannot actually enter it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, נִכְנָס.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: it must be one into which the tip can actually enter.

phrases.he: נִסְדְּקָה סְרֵידָה, שִׁעוּרוֹ כִמְלֹא פִי מַרְדֵּע נִכְנָס.
phrases.en: If a split appeared in the netting, the minimum size is the circumference of the tip of an ox goad that can enter it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, שֶׁלֹּא נִכְנָס.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: even if it cannot enter.

phrases.he: הָיָה עָגֹל, אֵין רוֹאִין אוֹתוֹ אָרֹךְ, אֶלָּא שִׁעוּרוֹ כִמְלֹא פִי מַרְדֵּעַ נִכְנָס
phrases.en: If the split was curved it must not be regarded as straight, and still the minimum size must be the circumference of the tip of an ox goad that can actually enter.

phrases.he: תַּנּוּר שֶׁנִּקַּב מֵעֵינוֹ, שִׁעוּרוֹ מְלֹא כוּשׁ נִכְנָס וְיוֹצֵא דּוֹלֵק.
phrases.en: If there was a hole in the "eye" of an oven, the minimum size [for it to leave the category of being tightly closed] is the circumference of a burning spindle staff that can enter and come out [without being extinguished].

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, שֶׁלֹּא דוֹלֵק.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: one that is not burning.

phrases.he: נִקַּב מִצִּדּוֹ, שִׁעוּרוֹ כִמְלֹא כוּשׁ נִכְנָס וְיוֹצֵא שֶׁלֹּא דוֹלֵק.
phrases.en: If the hole appeared at its side, the minimum size must be that of the circumference of a spindle staff that can enter and come out while it is not burning.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, דּוֹלֵק.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: while burning.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, מִן הָאֶמְצָע, נִכְנָס.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: if the hole is in the middle its size must be such that a spindle staff can enter it, but if it was at the side it need only be such as the spindle staff cannot actually enter.

phrases.he: מִן הַצַּד, אֵינוֹ נִכְנָס.
phrases.en: And similarly he used to rule concerning the stopper of a jar in which a hole appeared: the minimum size is the circumference of the second knot in an oat stalk.

phrases.he: וְכֵן הָיָה אוֹמֵר בִּמְגוּפַת הֶחָבִית שֶׁנִּקְּבָה, שִׁעוּרָהּ מְלֹא מִיצָה שְׁנִיָּה שֶׁל שִׁיפוֹן. מִן הָאֶמְצָע, נִכְנָס.
phrases.en: If the hole was in the middle the stalk should be able to enter, and if at the side it need not be able to enter.

phrases.he: מִן הַצַּד, אֵינוֹ נִכְנָס.
phrases.en: And similarly he used to rule concerning large stone jars in the stoppers of which appeared a hole.

phrases.he: וְכֵן הָיָה אוֹמֵר בַּחֲצָבִים גְּדוֹלִים שֶׁנִּקְּבוּ, שִׁעוּרָם מְלֹא מִיצָה שְׁנִיָּה שֶׁל קָנֶה. מִן הָאֶמְצָע, נִכְנָס.
phrases.en: The minimum size is the circumference of the second knot in a reed.

phrases.he: מִן הַצַּד, אֵינוֹ נִכְנָס.
phrases.en: If the hole was in the middle the reed must be able to enter it, and if it was at the side the reed need not be able to enter it.

phrases.he: בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בִּזְמַן שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ לְיַיִן, אֲבָל אִם נַעֲשׂוּ לִשְׁאָר מַשְׁקִין, אֲפִלּוּ כָל שֶׁהוּא, טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: When is this so? When the jars were made for wine, but if they were made for other liquids, if they have even the smallest hole, they are unclean.

phrases.he: בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בִּזְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נַעֲשׂוּ בִידֵי אָדָם.
phrases.en: When is this so? When the holes were not made by a person, but if they were made by a person, if they have even the smallest hole, they are unclean.

phrases.he: אֲבָל אִם נַעֲשׂוּ בִידֵי אָדָם, אֲפִלּוּ כָל שֶׁהוּא, טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: If a hole appeared [in other vessels its prescribed size ] is as follows: if the vessel was used for food, [the hole must be one] through which olives can fall out; if for liquids, one that lets out liquids; If for either, the greater restriction is imposed [even with regard to the issue of] a tightly fitting cover [the size of the hole need only be] one that admits a liquid.

phrases.he: נִקְּבוּ, הֶעָשׂוּי לָאֳכָלִים, שִׁעוּרָן בְּזֵיתִים.
הֶעָשׂוּי לְמַשְׁקִים, שִׁעוּרָן בְּמַשְׁקִים.
הֶעָשׂוּי לְכָךְ וּלְכָךְ, מַטִּילִים אוֹתוֹ לְחֻמְרוֹ, בְּצָמִיד פָּתִיל וּבְכוֹנֵס מַשְׁקֶה

אֵלּוּ כֵלִים מַצִּילִין בְּצָמִיד פָּתִיל, כְּלֵי גְלָלִים, כְּלֵי אֲבָנִים, כְּלֵי אֲדָמָה, כְּלֵי חֶרֶס, וּכְלֵי נֶתֶר, עַצְמוֹת הַדָּג וְעוֹרוֹ, עַצְמוֹת חַיָּה שֶׁבַּיָּם וְעוֹרָהּ, וּכְלֵי עֵץ הַטְּהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: The following vessels protect their contents when they have a tightly fitting cover: those made of cattle dung, of stone, of clay, of earthenware, of sodium carbonate, of the bones of a fish or of its skin, or of the bones of any animal of the sea or of its skin, and wooden vessels that are always clean.

phrases.he: מַצִּילִים בֵּין מִפִּיהֶם בֵּין מִצִּדֵּיהֶן, בֵּין יוֹשְׁבִין עַל שׁוּלֵיהֶן בֵּין מֻטִּין עַל צִדֵּיהֶן.
phrases.en: They protect whether the covers close their mouths or their sides, whether they stand on their bottoms or lean on their sides.

phrases.he: הָיוּ כְפוּיִים עַל פִּיהֶן, מַצִּילִים כֹּל שֶׁתַּחְתֵּיהֶן עַד הַתְּהוֹם. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.en: If they were turned over with their mouths downwards they afford protection to all that is beneath them to the nethermost deep.

phrases.he: עַל הַכֹּל מַצִּילִין, חוּץ מִכְּלֵי חֶרֶס, שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַצִּיל אֶלָּא עַל הָאֳכָלִים וְעַל הַמַּשְׁקִין וְעַל כְּלֵי חָרֶס
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer declares this unclean. These protect everything, except that an earthen vessel protects only foods, liquids and earthen vessels.

phrases.he: בַּמֶּה מַקִּיפִים. בְּסִיד וּבְגִפְּסִיס, בְּזֶפֶת וּבְשַׁעֲוָה, בְּטִיט וּבְצוֹאָה, בְּחֹמֶר וּבְחַרְסִית, וּבְכָל דָּבָר הַמִּתְמָרֵחַ.
phrases.en: How may it be tightly covered? With lime or gypsum, pitch or wax, mud or excrement, crude clay or potter's clay, or any substance that is used for plastering.

phrases.he: אֵין מַקִּיפִים לֹא בְּבַעַץ וְלֹא בְעוֹפֶרֶת, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא פָתִיל וְאֵינוֹ צָמִיד.
phrases.en: One may not make a tightly fitting cover with tin or with lead because though it is a covering, it is not tightly fitting.

phrases.he: אֵין מַקִּיפִין לֹא בִדְבֵלָה שְׁמֵנָה, וְלֹא בְּבָצֵק שֶׁנִּלּוֹשׁ בְּמֵי פֵרוֹת, שֶׁלֹּא יְבִיאֶנּוּ לִידֵי פְסוּל. וְאִם הִקִּיף, הִצִּיל
phrases.en: One may not make a tightly fitting cover with swollen fig-cakes or with dough that was kneaded with fruit juice, since it might cause it to become unfit. If he did make a tightly fitting cover [from such material] it protects.

phrases.he: מְגוּפַת הֶחָבִית הַמְחֻלְחֶלֶת וְאֵינָהּ נִשְׁמֶטֶת,
phrases.en: A stopper of a jar that is loose but does not fall out: Rabbi Judah says: it protects.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מַצֶּלֶת.
phrases.en: But the sages say: it does not protect.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵינָהּ מַצֶּלֶת.
phrases.en: If its finger-hold was sunk within the jar and a sheretz was in it, the jar becomes unclean.

phrases.he: הָיָה בֵית אֶצְבַּע שֶׁלָּהּ שׁוֹקֵעַ בְּתוֹכָהּ, הַשֶּׁרֶץ בְּתוֹכָהּ, הֶחָבִית טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: If the sheretz was in the jar, any food in it, become unclean.

phrases.he: הַשֶּׁרֶץ בֶּחָבִית, אֳכָלִין שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ טְמֵאִים
הַכַּדּוּר וְהַפְּקַעַת שֶׁל גֶּמִי שֶׁנְּתָנָן עַל פִּי הֶחָבִית, אִם מֵרַח מִן הַצְּדָדִין, לֹא הִצִּיל, עַד שֶׁיְּמָרַח מִלְמַעְלָן וּמִלְּמַטָּן.
phrases.en: If a ball or coil of reed grass was placed over the mouth of a jar, and only its sides were plastered, it does not protect unless it was also plastered above or below.

phrases.he: וְכֵן בְּמַטְלִית שֶׁל בֶּגֶד.
phrases.en: The same is true with regard to a patch of cloth.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה שֶׁל נְיָר אוֹ שֶׁל עוֹר, וּקְשָׁרָהּ בִּמְשִׁיחָה, אִם מֵרַח מִן הַצְּדָדִין, הִצִּיל
phrases.en: If it was of paper or leather and bound with a cord, if he plastered it from the sides, it protects.

phrases.he: חָבִית שֶׁנִּתְקַלְּפָה וְהַזֶּפֶת שֶׁלָּהּ עוֹמֶדֶת, וְכֵן קְבוֹסִים שֶׁל מֻרְיָס שֶׁגְּפָתָן עִם הַשָּׂפָה,
phrases.en: If [the outer layer] a jar had been peeled off but its pitch [lining] remained intact, And similarly if pots of fish brine were sealed up with gypsum at a level with the brim: Rabbi Judah says: they do not protect.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֵינָם מַצִּילִין.
phrases.en: But the sages say: they do protect.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, מַצִּילִין:
חָבִית שֶׁנִּקְּבָה וּסְתָמוּהָ שְׁמָרִים, הִצִּילוּהָ.
phrases.en: If a jar had a hole in it and wine lees stopped it up, they protect it.

phrases.he: פְּקָקָהּ בִּזְמוֹרָה, עַד שֶׁיְּמָרַח מִן הַצְּדָדִים.
phrases.en: If one stopped it up with a vine shoot [it does not protect] until he plasters it at the sides.

phrases.he: הָיוּ שְׁתַּיִם, עַד שֶׁיְּמָרַח מִן הַצְּדָדִין וּבֵין זְמוֹרָה לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ.
phrases.en: If there were two vine shoots, [it does not protect] unless he plastered it at the sides and also between the one shoot and the other.

phrases.he: נֶסֶר שֶׁהוּא נָתוּן עַל פִּי הַתַּנּוּר, אִם מֵרַח מִן הַצְּדָדִין, הִצִּיל.
phrases.en: If a board was placed over the mouth of an oven, it protects if he plastered it at the sides.

phrases.he: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם, עַד שֶׁיְּמָרַח מִן הַצְּדָדִין וּבֵין נֶסֶר לַחֲבֵרוֹ.
phrases.en: If there were two boards [it does not protect] unless he plastered at the sides and also between the one board and the other.

phrases.he: עֲשָׂאָן בְּסִינִין אוֹ בְשֹׁגְמִין, אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְמָרֵחַ מִן הָאֶמְצָע
phrases.en: If they were fastened together with pegs or with bamboo joints there is no need for them to be plastered in the middle.

phrases.he: תַּנּוּר יָשָׁן בְּתוֹךְ הֶחָדָשׁ וּסְרֵידָה עַל פִּי הַיָּשָׁן, נִטַּל הַיָּשָׁן וּסְרֵידָה נוֹפֶלֶת, הַכֹּל טָמֵא.
phrases.en: An old oven was within a new one and netting was over the mouth of the old [new] one: If [it was placed such that if] the old one were to be removed the netting would drop, all [the contents of both ovens] are unclean; But if it would not drop, all are clean.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, הַכֹּל טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A new oven was within an old one and netting was over the mouth of the old one if there was not a handbreadth of space between the new oven and the netting, all the contents of the new one are clean.

phrases.he: חָדָשׁ בְּתוֹךְ הַיָּשָׁן וּסְרֵידָה עַל פִּי הַיָּשָׁן, אִם אֵין בֵּין חָדָשׁ לַסְּרֵידָה פוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח, כֹּל שֶׁבֶּחָדָשׁ טָהוֹר
לְפָסִין זוֹ בְתוֹךְ זוֹ וְשִׂפְתוֹתֵיהֶן שָׁווֹת, הַשֶּׁרֶץ בָּעֶלְיוֹנָה אוֹ בַתַּחְתּוֹנָה, הִיא טְמֵאָה וְכֻלָּן טְהוֹרוֹת.
phrases.en: If [earthenware] pans were placed one within the other and their rims were on the same level, and there was a sheretz in the upper one or in the lower one, that pan alone becomes unclean but all the others remain clean.

phrases.he: הָיוּ בְכוֹנֵס מַשְׁקֶה, הַשֶּׁרֶץ בָּעֶלְיוֹנָה, כֻּלָּן טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: If [they were perforated] to the extent of admitting a liquid, and the sheretz was in the uppermost one, all become unclean.

phrases.he: בַּתַּחְתּוֹנָה, הִיא טְמֵאָה וְכֻלָּן טְהוֹרוֹת.
phrases.en: If in the lowest one, that one is unclean while the others remain clean.

phrases.he: הַשֶּׁרֶץ בָּעֶלְיוֹנָה, וְהַתַּחְתּוֹנָה עוֹדֶפֶת, הִיא וְהַתַּחְתּוֹנָה טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: If the sheretz was in the uppermost one and the lowest projected above it, both are unclean.

phrases.he: בָּעֶלְיוֹנָה, וְהַתַּחְתּוֹנָה עוֹדֶפֶת, כֹּל שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ מַשְׁקֶה טוֹפֵחַ, טְמֵאָה
phrases.en: If the sheretz was in the uppermost one and the lowest projected above it, any one that contained dripping liquid becomes unclean.

phrases.he: כְּלֵי מַתָּכוֹת, פְּשׁוּטֵיהֶן וּמְקַבְּלֵיהֶן טְמֵאִין. נִשְׁבְּרוּ, טָהָרוּ.
phrases.en: Metal vessels, whether they are flat or form a receptacle, are susceptible to impurity. On being broken they become clean.

phrases.he: חָזַר וְעָשָׂה מֵהֶן כְּלִי, חָזְרוּ לְטֻמְאָתָן הַיְשָׁנָה.
phrases.en: If they were re-made into vessels they revert to their former impurity.

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, לֹא לְכָל טֻמְאָה, אֶלָּא לְטֻמְאַת הַנָּפֶשׁ
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel says: this does not apply to every form of impurity but only to that contracted from a corpse.

phrases.he: כָּל כְּלִי מַתָּכוֹת שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ שֵׁם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, טָמֵא, חוּץ מִן הַדֶּלֶת, וּמִן הַנֶּגֶר, וּמִן הַמַּנְעוּל, וְהַפּוֹתָה שֶׁתַּחַת הַצִּיר, וְהַצִּיר, וְהַקּוֹרָה, וְהַצִּנּוֹר, שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ לַקַּרְקָע:
phrases.en: Every metal vessel that has a name of its own [is susceptible to impurity,] Except for a door, a bolt, a lock, a socket under a hinge, a hinge, a clapper, and the [threshold] groove under a door post, since these are intended to be attached to the ground.

phrases.he: הָעוֹשֶׂה כֵלִים מִן הָעֶשֶׁת, וּמִן הַחֲרָרָה, וּמִן הַסּוֹבֵב שֶׁל גַּלְגַּל, וּמִן הַטַּסִּין, וּמִן הַצִּפּוּיִין, מִכַּנֵּי כֵלִים, וּמֵאֹגְנֵי כֵלִים, מֵאָזְנֵי כֵלִים, מִן הַשְּׁחוֹלֶת, וּמִן הַגְּרוּדוֹת, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: If vessels are made from iron ore, from smelted iron, from the hoop of a wheel, from sheets, from plating, from the bases, rims or handles of vessels, from chippings or filings, they are clean. Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri says: even those made of pieces of vessels.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר, אַף מִן הַקְּצוּצוֹת.
phrases.en: From [vessels that are made] of fragments of vessels, from pieces of old vessels, or from nails that were known to have been made from vessels, are unclean.

phrases.he: מִשִּׁבְרֵי כֵלִים, מִן הַגְּרוּטִים, וּמִן הַמַּסְמְרוֹת, שֶׁיָּדוּעַ שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ מִכְּלִי, טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: [If they were made] from ordinary nails: Bet Shammai says: they are unclean, And Bet Hillel says that they are clean.

phrases.he: מִן הַמַּסְמְרוֹת, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מְטַמְּאִין, וּבֵית הִלֵּל מְטַהֲרִין
בַּרְזֶל טָמֵא שֶׁבְּלָלוֹ עִם בַּרְזֶל טָהוֹר, אִם רֹב מִן הַטָּמֵא, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If unclean iron was smelted together with clean iron and the greater part was from the unclean iron, [the vessel made of the mixture] is unclean; If the greater part was from the clean iron, the vessel is clean.

phrases.he: וְאִם רֹב מִן הַטָּהוֹר, טָהוֹר. מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If each was half, it is unclean.

phrases.he: וְכֵן מִן הַחֲלָמָא וּמִן הַגְּלָלִים. קְלוֹסְטְרָא, טְמֵאָה. וּמְצֻפָּה, טְהוֹרָה. הַפִּין, וְהַפּוּרְנָה, טְמֵאִין. וְהַקְּלוֹסְטְרָא,
phrases.en: The same law also applies to a mixture of cement and cattle dung. A door bolt is susceptible to impurity, but [one of wood] that is only plated with metal is not susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, שׁוֹמְטָהּ מִפֶּתַח זֶה וְתוֹלָהּ בַּחֲבֵרוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.en: The clutch and the crosspiece [of a lock] are susceptible to impurity. A door-bolt: Rabbi Joshua says: he may remove it from one door and hang it on another on Shabbat.

phrases.he: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר, הֲרֵי הִיא לוֹ כְּכָל הַכֵּלִים, וּמִטַּלְטֶלֶת בֶּחָצֵר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Tarfon says: it is like all other vessels and may be carried about in a courtyard.

phrases.he: עַקְרָב שֶׁל פְּרֻמְבְּיָא, טְמֵאָה. וּלְחָיַיִם, טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: The scorpion [-shaped] bit of a bridle is susceptible to impurity, but the cheek-pieces are clean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְטַמֵּא בַלְּחָיָיִם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says that the cheek-pieces are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵין טָמֵא אֶלָּא עַקְרָב.
phrases.en: But the sages says that the scorpion-bit alone is susceptible to impurity, When they are joined together it is all susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: וּבִשְׁעַת חִבּוּרָן, הַכֹּל טָמֵא
פִּיקָה שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַמֵּא, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין. וּמְצֻפָּה, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A metal spindle-knob:Rabbi Akiva says it is susceptible to impurity But the sages say it is not susceptible. If it was only plated [with metal] it is clean.

phrases.he: הַכּוּשׁ, וְהָאִימָּה, וְהַמַּקֵּל, וְסִמְפּוֹנְיָה, וְחָלִיל שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת, טְמֵאִין. וּמְצֻפִּין, טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: A spindle, a distaff, a rod, a double flute and a pipe are susceptible to impurity if they are of metal, but if they are only plated [with metal] they are clean.

phrases.he: סִמְפּוֹנְיָה, אִם יֶשׁ בָּהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל כְּנָפַיִם, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ טְמֵאָה
phrases.en: If a double flute has a receptacle for the wings it is susceptible to impurity in either case.

phrases.he: קֶרֶן עֲגֻלָּה, טְמֵאָה. וּפְשׁוּטָה, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A curved horn is susceptible to impurity but a straight one is clean.

phrases.he: אִם הָיְתָה מְצֻפִּית שֶׁלָּהּ שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: If its mouthpiece was covered with metal it is unclean.

phrases.he: הַקַּב שֶׁלָּהּ, רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן מְטַמֵּא, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין.
phrases.en: If its broad side [is covered with metal]: Rabbi Tarfon says it is susceptible to impurity But the sages say it is clean.

phrases.he: וּבִשְׁעַת חִבּוּרָן, הַכֹּל טָמֵא.
phrases.en: While they are joined together the whole is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ, קְנֵי מְנוֹרָה, טְהוֹרִין. הַפֶּרַח וְהַבָּסִיס, טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: Similarly: the branches of a candlestick are clean. And the cups and the base are susceptible to impurity, But while they are joined together the whole is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: וּבִשְׁעַת חִבּוּרָן, הַכֹּל טָמֵא
קַסְדָּא, טְמֵאָה. וּלְחָיַיִם, טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: A helmet is susceptible to impurity but the cheek-pieces are clean, But if they have a receptacle for water they are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: אִם יֵשׁ בָּהֶן בֵּית קִבּוּל מַיִם, טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: All weapons of war are susceptible to impurity: a javelin, a spear-head, metal boots, and a breastplate are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: כָּל כְּלֵי הַמִּלְחָמָה, טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: All women's ornaments are susceptible to impurity: a golden city (a tiara), a necklace, ear-rings, finger-rings, a ring whether it has a seal or does not have a seal, and nose-rings.

phrases.he: הַכִּידוֹן, הַנִּיקוֹן, וְהַמַּגָּפַיִן, וְהַשִּׁרְיוֹן, טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: If a necklace has metal beads on a thread of flax or wool and the thread broke, the beads are still susceptible to impurity, since each one is a vessel in itself.

phrases.he: כָּל תַּכְשִׁיטֵי נָשִׁים, טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: If the thread was of metal and the beads were of precious stones or pearls or glass, and the beads were broken while the thread alone remained, it is still susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: עִיר שֶׁל זָהָב, קַטְלָיוֹת, נְזָמִים וְטַבָּעוֹת, וְטַבַּעַת, בֵּין שֶׁיֶּשׁ לָהּ חוֹתָם וּבֵין שֶׁאֵין לָהּ חוֹתָם, נִזְמֵי הָאָף.
phrases.en: The remnant of a necklace [is susceptible] as long as there is enough for the neck of a little girl.

phrases.he: קַטְלָה שֶׁחֻלְיוֹת שֶׁלָּהּ שֶׁל מַתָּכוֹת בְּחוּט שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן אוֹ שֶׁל צֶמֶר, נִפְסַק הַחוּט, הַחֻלְיוֹת טְמֵאוֹת, שֶׁכָּל אַחַת וְאַחַת כְּלִי בִפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ.
חוּט שֶׁל מַתָּכוֹת, וְחֻלְיוֹת שֶׁל אֲבָנִים טוֹבוֹת וּמַרְגָּלִיּוֹת, וְשֶׁל זְכוּכִית, נִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ הַחֻלְיוֹת, הַחוּט בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ קַיָּם, טָמֵא.
שְׁיָרֵי קַטְלָא, כִּמְלֹא צַוַּאר קְטַנָּה.
רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ טַבַּעַת אַחַת, טְמֵאָה, שֶׁכֵּן תּוֹלִין בַּצַּוָּאר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: even if only one ring remained it is unclean, since it also is hung around the neck.

phrases.he: נֶזֶם שֶׁהוּא עָשׂוּי כִּקְדֵרָה מִלְּמַטָּן וְכָעֲדָשָׁה מִלְמַעְלָן, וְנִפְרַק, כִּקְדֵרָה טָמֵא מִשּׁוּם כְּלִי בֵית קִבּוּל, וְכָעֲדָשָׁה טָמֵא בִפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ. צִנּוֹרָא, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If an earring was shaped like a pot at its bottom and like a lentil at the top and the sections fell apart, the pot-shaped section is susceptible to impurity because it is a receptacle, while the lentil shaped section is susceptible to impurity in itself. The hooklet is clean.

phrases.he: הֶעָשׂוּי כְּמִין אֶשְׁכּוֹל, וְנִפְרַק, טָהוֹר
phrases.en: If the sections of an ear-ring that was in the shape of a cluster of grapes fell apart, they are clean.

phrases.he: טַבַּעַת אָדָם, טְמֵאָה. טַבַּעַת בְּהֵמָה וְכֵלִים וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַטַּבָּעוֹת, טְהוֹרוֹת. קוֹרַת הַחִצִּים, טְמֵאָה. וְשֶׁל אֲסִירִין, טְהוֹרָה. הַקּוֹלָר, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: A man's ring is susceptible to impurity. A ring for cattle or for vessels and all other rings are clean. A beam for arrows is susceptible to impurity, but one for prisoners is clean. A prisoner's collar is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: שַׁלְשֶׁלֶת שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ בֵּית נְעִילָה, טְמֵאָה. הָעֲשׂוּיָה לִכְפִיתָה, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A chain that has a lock-piece is susceptible to impurity. But that used for tying up cattle is clean.

phrases.he: שַׁלְשֶׁלֶת שֶׁל סִיטוֹנוֹת, טְמֵאָה, שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: The chain used by wholesalers is susceptible to impurity. That used by householders is clean.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא מַפְתֵּחַ אֶחָד, אֲבָל אִם הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם, אוֹ שֶׁקָּשַׁר חִלָּזוֹן בְּרֹאשָׁהּ, טְמֵאָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose said: When is this so? When it attaches to one door, but if it attaches to two doors or if it had a snail[-shaped] piece at its end it is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: קְנֵה מֹאזְנַיִם שֶׁל סָרוֹקוֹת, טָמֵא, מִפְּנֵי אֻנְקְלָיוֹת.
phrases.en: The beam of a wool-combers’ balance is susceptible to impurity on account of the hooks.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים, אִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ אֻנְקְלָיוֹת, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: And that of a householder, if it has hooks is also susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: אֻנְקְלִין שֶׁל כַּתָּפִין, טְהוֹרָה. וְשֶׁל רוֹכְלִים, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: The hooks of porters are clean but those of peddlers are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, שֶׁל רוֹכְלִים, שֶׁלְּפָנָיו טְמֵאָה, וְשֶׁלְּאַחֲרָיו טְהוֹרָה. אֻנְקְלִי דַרְגָּשׁ, טְמֵאָה. וְשֶׁל נַקְלִיטִין, טְהוֹרָה. שֶׁל שִׁדָּה, טְמֵאָה. וְשֶׁל אָקוֹן, טְהוֹרָה. שֶׁל שֻׁלְחָן, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: in the case of the peddlers' [hooks], [the hook] that is in front is susceptible to impurity but that which is behind is clean. The hook of a couch is susceptible to impurity but that of bed poles is clean. [The hook of] a chest is susceptible to impurity but that of a fish trap is clean. That of a table is susceptible to impurity but that of a wooden candlestick is clean.

phrases.he: שֶׁל מְנוֹרַת הָעֵץ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: This is the general rule: any hook that is attached to a susceptible vessel is susceptible to impurity, but one that is attached to a vessel that is not susceptible to impurity is clean.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל הַמְחֻבָּר לַטָּמֵא, טָמֵא. וְהַמְחֻבָּר לַטָּהוֹר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: All these, however, are by themselves clean.

phrases.he: וְכֻלָּן, אַחַת אַחַת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן, טְהוֹרוֹת
כִּסּוּי טֶנִי שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת, שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים, רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מְטַמֵּא, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין. וְשֶׁל רוֹפְאִים, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: The metal cover of a basket of householders: Rabban Gamaliel says: it is susceptible to impurity, The sages say that it is clean. But that of physicians is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: הַדֶּלֶת שֶׁבַּמִּגְדָּל, שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים, טְהוֹרָה. וְשֶׁל רוֹפְאִים, טְמֵאָה. הַיַּתּוּכִין, טְמֵאִים. וְהַפְּרָכִין, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: The door of a cupboard of householders is clean but that of physicians is susceptible to impurity. Tongs are susceptible to impurity but stove-tongs are clean.

phrases.he: עַקְרַב בֵּית הַבַּד, טְמֵאָה. וְאֻנְקְלִי שֶׁבַּכְּתָלִים, טְהוֹרָה
phrases.en: The scorpion [-shaped] hook in an olive-press is susceptible to impurity but the hooks for the walls are clean.

phrases.he: מַסְמֵר הַגָּרָע, טָמֵא. וְשֶׁל אֶבֶן הַשָּׁעוֹת, טָהוֹר. רַבִּי צָדוֹק מְטַמֵּא. מַסְמֵר הַגַּרְדִּי, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: A blood-letters’ nail is susceptible to impurity. But [the nail] of a sundial is clean. Rabbi Zadok says that it is susceptible to impurity. A weaver's nail is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: וְאָרוֹן שֶׁל גָּרוֹסוֹת, רַבִּי צָדוֹק מְטַמֵּא, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין.
phrases.en: The chest of a grist-dealer: Rabbi Zadok says: it is susceptible to impurity, But the sages say that it is clean.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה עֲגָלָה שֶׁלָּהּ שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת, טְמֵאָה
phrases.en: If its wagon was made of metal it is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: מַסְמֵר שֶׁהִתְקִינוֹ לִהְיוֹת פּוֹתֵחַ וְנוֹעֵל בּוֹ, טָמֵא. הֶעָשׂוּי לִשְׁמִירָה, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A nail which he adapted to be able to open or to shut a lock is susceptible to impurity. But one used for guarding is clean.

phrases.he: מַסְמֵר שֶׁהִתְקִינוֹ לִהְיוֹת פּוֹתֵחַ בּוֹ אֶת הֶחָבִית, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.en: A nail which he adapted to open a jar: Rabbi Akiva says that it is susceptible to impurity, But the sages say that it is clean unless he forges it.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין, עַד שֶׁיִּצְרְפֶנּוּ.
phrases.en: A money-changer's nail is clean, But Rabbi Zadok says: it is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: מַסְמֵר שֶׁל שֻׁלְחָנִי, טָהוֹר. וְרַבִּי צָדוֹק מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.en: There are three things which Rabbi Zadok holds to be susceptible to impurity and the sages hold clean: The nail of a money-changer, The chest of a grist-dealer And the nail of a sundial.

phrases.he: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים רַבִּי צָדוֹק מְטַמֵּא, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Zadok rules that these are susceptible to impurity and the sages rule that they are clean.

phrases.he: מַסְמֵר שֶׁל שֻׁלְחָנִי, וְאָרוֹן שֶׁל גָּרוֹסוֹת, וּמַסְמֵר שֶׁל אֶבֶן הַשָּׁעוֹת, רַבִּי צָדוֹק מְטַמֵּא, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין
אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מְטַמֵּא, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין.
phrases.en: There are four things which Rabban Gamaliel says are susceptible to impurity, and the sages say are not susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: כִּסּוּי טֶנִי שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים, וּתְלוֹי הַמַּגְרֵדוֹת, וְגֹלְמֵי כְלֵי מַתָּכוֹת, וְטַבְלָה שֶׁנֶּחְלְקָה לִשְׁנָיִם.
phrases.en: he covering of a metal basket, if it belongs to householders; And the hanger of a strigil; And metal vessels which are still unshaped; And a plate that is divided into two [equal] parts.

phrases.he: וּמוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בְּטַבְלָה שֶׁנֶּחְלְקָה לִשְׁנַיִם, אֶחָד גָּדוֹל וְאֶחָד קָטָן, שֶׁהַגָּדוֹל טָמֵא וְהַקָּטָן טָהוֹר
phrases.en: And the sages agree with Rabban Gamaliel in the case of a plate that was divided into two parts, one large and one small, that the large one is susceptible to impurity and the small one is not susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: דִּינָר שֶׁנִּפְסַל וְהִתְקִינוֹ לִתְלוֹתוֹ בְצַוַּאר קְטַנָּה, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If a dinar had been invalidated and then was adapted for hanging around a young girl's neck it is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: וְכֵן סֶלַע שֶׁנִּפְסְלָה וְהִתְקִינָהּ לִהְיוֹת שׁוֹקֵל בָּהּ, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: So, too, if a sela had been invalidated was adapted for use as a weight, it is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: עַד כַּמָּה תִפָּסֵל וִיהֵא רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּמָהּ, עַד שְׁנֵי דִינָרִין. פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן, יָקֹץ
phrases.en: How much may it depreciate while one is still permitted to keep it? As much as two denars. Less and he must be cut it up.

phrases.he: הָאוֹלָר, וְהַקֻּלְמוֹס, וְהַמְּטוּטֶלֶת, וְהַמִּשְׁקָלוֹת, וְהַכּוּרִים, וְהַכַּן, וְהַכַּנָּא, טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: A pen-knife, a writing pen, a plummet, a weight, pressing plates, a measuring-rod, and a measuring-table are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: וְכָל גֹּלְמֵי כְלֵי עֵץ, טְמֵאִים, חוּץ מִשֶּׁל אֶשְׁכְּרוֹעַ.
phrases.en: All unfinished wooden vessels also are susceptible to impurity, excepting those made of boxwood.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף גְּרוֹפִית שֶׁל זַיִת, טְהוֹרָה, עַד שֶׁתִּשָּׁלֵק:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: one made of an olive-tree branch is also clean unless it was first heated.

phrases.he: הַסַּיִף, וְהַסַּכִּין, וְהַפִּגְיוֹן, וְהָרֹמַח, מַגַּל יָד וּמַגַּל קָצִיר, וְהַשְּׁחוֹר וְזוּג שֶׁל סַפָּרִים, שֶׁנֶּחֱלְקוּ, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: The sword, knife, dagger, spear, hand-sickle, harvest-sickle, clipper, and barbers’ whose component parts were separated, are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, הַסָּמוּךְ לַיָּד, טָמֵא. וְהַסָּמוּךְ לָרֹאשׁ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: the part that is near the hand is susceptible to impurity, but that which is near the top is clean.

phrases.he: מִסְפֶּרֶת שֶׁנֶּחְלְקָה לִשְׁנַיִם, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַמֵּא, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין
phrases.en: The two parts of shears which were separated: Rabbi Judah says: they are still susceptible to impurity; But the sages say that they are clean.

phrases.he: קֹלִגְרִיפוֹן שֶׁנִּטְּלָה כַפָּהּ, טְמֵאָה מִפְּנֵי שִׁנָּהּ.
phrases.en: A koligrophon whose spoon has been removed is still susceptible to impurity on account of its teeth.

phrases.he: נִטְּלָה שִׁנָּהּ, טְמֵאָה מִפְּנֵי כַפָּהּ.
phrases.en: If its teeth have been removed it is still susceptible on account of its spoon.

phrases.he: מִכְחוֹל שֶׁנִּטַּל הַכַּף, טָמֵא מִפְּנֵי הַזָּכָר.
phrases.en: A makhol whose spoon is missing is still susceptible to impurity on account of its point; If its point was missing it is still susceptible on account of its spoon.

phrases.he: נִטַּל הַזָּכָר, טָמֵא מִפְּנֵי הַכָּף.
phrases.en: A stylus whose writing point is missing is still susceptible to impurity on account of its eraser; If its eraser is missing it is susceptible on account of its writing point.

phrases.he: מַכְתֵּב שֶׁנִּטַּל הַכּוֹתֵב, טָמֵא מִפְּנֵי הַמּוֹחֵק.
phrases.en: A zomalister whose spoon is lost is still susceptible to impurity on account of its fork; If its fork is missing, it is still susceptible on account of its spoon.

phrases.he: נִטַּל הַמּוֹחֵק, טָמֵא מִפְּנֵי הַכּוֹתֵב.
phrases.en: So too with regard to the prong of a mattock.

phrases.he: זוֹמָא לִסְטְרָא שֶׁנִּטְּלָה כַפָּהּ, טְמֵאָה מִפְּנֵי הַמַּזְלֵג.
phrases.en: The minimum size for all these instruments: so that they can perform their usual work.

phrases.he: נִטַּל הַמַּזְלֵג, טְמֵאָה מִפְּנֵי כַפָּהּ.
וְכֵן הַשֵּׁן שֶׁל מַעְדֵּר.
שִׁעוּר כֻּלָּן, כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלַאכְתָּן
חַרְחוּר שֶׁנִּפְגַּם, טָמֵא, עַד שֶׁיִּנָּטֵל רֻבּוֹ. נִשְׁבַּר מְקוֹפוֹ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A harhur that is damaged is still susceptible to impurity until its greater part is removed. But if its shaft-socket is broken it is clean.

phrases.he: קֻרְדֹּם שֶׁנִּטַּל עֻשְׁפּוֹ, טָמֵא מִפְּנֵי בֵית בִּקּוּעוֹ.
phrases.en: A hatchet whose cutting edge is lost remains susceptible to impurity on account of its splitting edge.

phrases.he: נִטַּל בֵּית בִּקּוּעוֹ, טָמֵא מִפְּנֵי עֻשְׁפּוֹ. נִשְׁבַּר מְקוֹפוֹ, טָהוֹר
phrases.en: If its splitting edge is lost it remains susceptible on account of its cutting edge. If its shaft-socket is broken it is clean.

phrases.he: מַגְרֵפָה שֶׁנִּטְּלָה כַפָּהּ, טְמֵאָה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא כְקֻרְנָס, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין.
phrases.en: An ash-shovel whose spoon was missing is still susceptible to impurity, since it is still like a hammer, the words of Rabbi Meir. But the sages rule that it is clean.

phrases.he: מְגֵרָה שֶׁנִּטְּלוּ שִׁנֶּיהָ אַחַת מִבֵּינְתַיִם, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A saw whose teeth are missing one in every two is clean.

phrases.he: נִשְׁתַּיֵּר בָּהּ מְלֹא הַסִּיט בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: But if a hasit length of consecutive teeth remained it is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: הַמַּעֲצָד וְהָאִזְמֵל וְהַמַּפְסֶלֶת וְהַמַּקְדֵּחַ, שֶׁנִּפְגְּמוּ, טְמֵאִים. נִטַּל חִסּוּמָן, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: An adze, scalpel, plane, or drill that was damaged remains susceptible to impurity, but if its steel edge was missing it is clean.

phrases.he: וְכֻלָּן שֶׁנֶּחְלְקוּ לִשְׁנַיִם, טְמֵאִים, חוּץ מִן הַמַּקְדֵּחַ.
phrases.en: In all these cases if it was split into two parts both remain susceptible to impurity, except for the drill.

phrases.he: וְהָרוּקְנִי בִפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ, טְהוֹרָה
phrases.en: The block of a plane by itself is clean.

phrases.he: מַחַט שֶׁנִּטַּל חֲרִירָהּ אוֹ עֻקְצָהּ, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A needle whose eye or point is missing is clean.

phrases.he: אִם הִתְקִינָהּ לְמִתּוּחַ, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: If he adapted it to be a stretching-pin it is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: שֶׁל סַקָּיִין שֶׁנִּטַּל חֲרִירָהּ, טְמֵאָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא כוֹתֵב בָּהּ. נִטַּל עֻקְצָהּ, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A pack-needle whose eye was missing is still susceptible to impurity since one writes with it. If its point was missing it is clean.

phrases.he: שֶׁל מִתּוּחַ, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: A stretching-pin is in either case susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: מַחַט שֶׁהֶעֶלְתָה חֲלֻדָּה, אִם מְעַכֶּבֶת אֶת הַתְּפִירָה, טְהוֹרָה. וְאִם לָאו, טְמֵאָה. צִנּוֹרָא שֶׁפְּשָׁטָהּ, טְהוֹרָה. כְּפָפָהּ, חָזְרָה לְטֻמְאָתָהּ
phrases.en: A needle that has become rusty: If this hinders it from sewing it is clean, But if not it remains susceptible to impurity. A hook that was straightened out is clean. If it is bent back it resumes its susceptibility to impurity.

phrases.he: עֵץ הַמְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת הַמַּתֶּכֶת, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: Wood that serves a metal vessel is susceptible to impurity, but metal that serves a wooden vessel is clean.

phrases.he: וְהַמַּתֶּכֶת הַמְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת הָעֵץ, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: How so? If a lock is of wood and its clutches are of metal, even if only one of them is so, it is susceptible to impurity, but if the lock is of metal and its clutches are of wood, it is clean.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד, פּוֹתַחַת שֶׁל עֵץ וְהַפִּין שֶׁלָּהּ שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת, אֲפִלּוּ אַחַת, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: If a ring was of metal and its seal of coral, it is susceptible to impurity, but if the ring was of coral and its seal of metal, it is clean.

phrases.he: פּוֹתַחַת שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת וְהַפִּין שֶׁלָּהּ שֶׁל עֵץ, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: The tooth in the plate of a lock or in a key is susceptible to impurity by itself.

phrases.he: טַבַּעַת שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת וְחוֹתָם שֶׁלָּהּ שֶׁל אַלְמוֹג, טְמֵאָה.
טַבַּעַת שֶׁל אַלְמוֹג וְחוֹתָם שֶׁלָּהּ שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת, טְהוֹרָה.
הַשֵּׁן שֶׁבַּטַּס, שֶׁבַּפּוֹתַחַת, וְשֶׁבַּמַּפְתֵּחַ, טְמֵאָה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ
הַכַּדּוּמִין הָאַשְׁקְלוֹנִין שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרוּ וְהָאֻנְקְלִי שֶׁלָּהֶן קַיֶּמֶת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: If Ashkelon grappling-irons were broken but their hooks remained, they remain susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: הַמַּעְבֵּר, וְהַמַּזְרֶה, וְהַמַּגּוֹב, וְכֵן מַסְרֵק שֶׁל רֹאשׁ שֶׁנִּטְּלָה אַחַת מִשִּׁנֵּיהֶן, וַעֲשָׂאָן שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְמֵאִין. וְעַל כֻּלָּן
phrases.en: If a pitch-fork, winnowing-fan, or rake, and the same applies to a hair-comb, lost one of its teeth and it was replaced by one of metal, it is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, דְּבַר חִדּוּשׁ חִדְּשׁוּ סוֹפְרִים, וְאֵין לִי מָה אָשִׁיב:
phrases.en: And concerning all these Rabbi Joshua said: the scribes have here introduced a new principle of law, and I have no explanation to offer.

phrases.he: מַסְרֵק שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן שֶׁנִּטְּלוּ שִׁנָּיו וְנִשְׁתַּיֵּר בּוֹ שְׁתַּיִם, טָמֵא. וְאַחַת, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A flax-comb: if the teeth were missing but two remained, it is still susceptible to impurity. If only one remained it is clean.

phrases.he: וְכֻלָּן, אַחַת אַחַת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן, טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: As regards all the teeth, each one individually is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל צֶמֶר שֶׁנִּטְּלוּ שִׁנָּיו אַחַת מִבֵּינְתַיִם, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A wool-comb: if one tooth out of every two is missing it is clean. If three consecutive teeth remained, it is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: נִשְׁתַּיֵּר בּוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If the outermost tooth was one of them, the comb is clean.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה הַחִיצוֹנָה אַחַת מֵהֶן, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If two teeth were removed from the comb and made into a pair of tweezers, they are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: נִטְּלוּ מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁתַּיִם וַעֲשָׂאָן לְמַלְקֶטֶת, טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: Even if only one was removed but it was adapted to be used for a lamp or as a stretching-pin, it is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: אַחַת וְהִתְקִינָהּ לְנֵר אוֹ לְמִתּוּחַ, טְמֵאָה
כְּלֵי מַתָּכוֹת, כַּמָּה הוּא שִׁעוּרָן.
phrases.en: What is the minimum size of [broken] metal vessels [for them to be susceptible to impurity]? A bucket must be of such a size as to draw water with it.

phrases.he: הַדְּלִי, כְּדֵי לְמַלֹּאת בּוֹ.
phrases.en: A kettle must be such as water can be heated in it.

phrases.he: קֻמְקוּם, כְּדֵי לֵיחֵם בּוֹ.
phrases.en: A boiler, such as can hold selas.

phrases.he: מֵחַם, כְּדֵי לְקַבֵּל סְלָעִים.
phrases.en: A cauldron, such as can hold jugs.

phrases.he: הַלֶּפֶס, כְּדֵי לְקַבֵּל קִיתוֹנוֹת.
phrases.en: Jugs, such as can hold perutahs.

phrases.he: קִיתוֹנוֹת, כְּדֵי לְקַבֵּל פְּרוּטוֹת. מִדּוֹת יַיִן, בְּיַיִן. וּמִדּוֹת שֶׁמֶן, בְּשָׁמֶן.
phrases.en: Wine-measures, such as can measure wine; and oil-measures, such as can measure oil.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, כֻּלָּן בִּפְרוּטוֹת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: the size for all these is such as can hold perutahs.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, הַמְחֻסָּר חֲטִיפָה, טָמֵא. וְהַמְחֻסָּר לְטִישָׁה, טָהוֹר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: a vessel that lacks trimming is susceptible to impurity, but one that lacks polishing is clean.

phrases.he: מַקֵּל שֶׁעָשָׂה בְרֹאשׁוֹ מַסְמֵר כְּמִין חַזְיָנָא, טָמֵא. סִמְּרוֹ, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: A staff to the end of which he attached a nail like an axe is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, עַד שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה בוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה סְדָרִים.
phrases.en: If the staff was studded with nails it is susceptible to impurity. Rabbi Shimon ruled: only if he put in three rows.

phrases.he: וְכֻלָּן שֶׁעֲשָׂאָן לְנוֹי, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: In all cases where he put them in as ornamentation the staff is clean.

phrases.he: עָשָׂה בְרֹאשׁוֹ מְנִיקָת, וְכֵן בַּדֶּלֶת, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If he attached a tube to its end, and so also in the case of a door, it is clean.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה כְלִי וְחִבְּרָהּ לוֹ, טְמֵאָה. מֵאֵימָתַי הִיא טָהֳרָתָהּ,
phrases.en: If it was once an independent vessel and then it was fixed to the staff, it remains susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מִשֶּׁיְּחַבֵּל.
phrases.en: When does it become pure? Bet Shammai says: when it is damaged; And Bet Hillel says: when it is joined on.

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מִשֶּׁיְּחַבֵּר:
הַקַּנְטָר שֶׁל בַּנַּאי, וְהַדָּקוֹר שֶׁל חָרָשׁ, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: A builder's staff and a carpenter's axes are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: יִתְדוֹת אֹהָלִים וְיִתְדוֹת הַמָּשׁוֹחוֹת, טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: Tent-pegs and surveyors’ pegs are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: שַׁלְשֶׁלֶת שֶׁל מָשׁוֹחוֹת, טְמֵאָה. הָעֲשׂוּיָה לָעֵצִים, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A surveyor's chain is susceptible to impurity, but one used for wood is clean.

phrases.he: שַׁלְשֶׁלֶת דְּלִי גָדוֹל, אַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים. וְשֶׁל קָטָן, עֲשָׂרָה.
phrases.en: The chain of a big bucket [is susceptible to impurity to a length of] four handbreadths, and that of a small one [to a length of] ten handbreadths.

phrases.he: חֲמוֹר שֶׁל נַפָּחִין, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: A blacksmith's jack is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: מְגֵרָה שֶׁעָשָׂה שִׁנֶּיהָ בְתוֹךְ הַחוֹר, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: A saw whose teeth were made in a hole susceptible to impurity, but if they were turned from below upwards it is clean.

phrases.he: עֲשָׂאָהּ מִלְּמַטָּן לְמַעְלָן, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: All covers are clean except that of a boiler.

phrases.he: וְכָל הַכְּסוּיִן טְהוֹרִים, חוּץ מִשֶּׁל מֵחָם

הַטְּמֵאִין שֶׁבָּעֲגָלָה, הָעֹל שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת, וְהַקַּטְרָב, וְהַכְּנָפַיִם הַמְקַבְּלוֹת אֶת הָרְצוּעוֹת, וְהַבַּרְזֶל שֶׁתַּחַת צַוְּארֵי בְהֵמָה, הַסּוֹמֵךְ, וְהַמַּחְגֵּר, וְהַתַּמְחוּיוֹת, הָעִנְבָּל, וְהַצִּנּוֹרָה, וּמַסְמֵר הַמְחַבֵּר אֶת כֻּלָּן:
phrases.en: The parts of a wagon that are susceptible to impurity: the metal yoke, the cross-bar, the side-pieces that hold the straps, the iron bar under the necks of the cattle, the pole-pin, the metal girth, the trays, the clapper, the hook, and any nail that holds any of its parts together.

phrases.he: הַטְּהוֹרִין שֶׁבָּעֲגָלָה, הָעֹל הַמְצֻפֶּה, כְּנָפַיִם הָעֲשׂוּיוֹת לְנוֹי, וּשְׁפוֹפָרוֹת הַמַּשְׁמִיעוֹת אֶת הַקּוֹל, וְהָאֲבָר שֶׁבְּצַד צַוְּארֵי בְהֵמָה, הַסּוֹבֵב שֶׁל גַּלְגַּל, הַטַּסִּים, וְהַצִּפּוּיִים, וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַמַּסְמְרוֹת, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: The clean parts of a wagon are the following: the yoke that is only plated [with metal], side-pieces made for ornamentation, tubes that give out a noise, the lead at the side of the necks of the cattle, the rim of the wheel, the plates and mountings, and all other nails, all of these are clean.

phrases.he: סַנְדְּלֵי בְהֵמָה שֶׁל מַתָּכוֹת, טְמֵאִין. שֶׁל שַׁעַם, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: Metal shoes of cattle are susceptible to impurity but those made of cork are clean.

phrases.he: הַסַּיִף מֵאֵימָתַי מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה, מִשֶּׁיְּשׁוּפֶנּוּ. וְהַסַּכִּין, מִשֶּׁיַשְׁחִיזֶנָּה
phrases.en: When does a sword become susceptible to impurity? When it has been polished. And a knife? When it has been sharpened.

phrases.he: כְּסוּי טֶנִי שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת שֶׁעָשָׂה בוֹ מַרְאָה, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַהֵר, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַמְּאִין.
phrases.en: A metal basket-cover which was turned into a mirror: Rabbi Judah rules that it is clean. And the sages rule that it is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: מַרְאָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה, אִם אֵינָהּ מַרְאָה אֶת רֹב הַפָּנִים, טְהוֹרָה
phrases.en: A broken mirror, if it does not reflect the greater part of the face, is clean.

phrases.he: כְּלֵי מַתָּכוֹת מִטַּמְּאִין וּמִטַּהֲרִין שְׁבוּרִין, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.en: Metal vessels remain unclean and become clean even when broken, the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, אֵינָן מִטַּהֲרִין אֶלָּא שְׁלֵמִין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua says: they can be made clean only when they are whole.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד, הִזָּה עֲלֵיהֶן, נִשְׁבְּרוּ בוֹ בַיּוֹם, הִתִּיכָן וְחָזַר וְהִזָּה עֲלֵיהֶן שֵׁנִית בּוֹ בַיּוֹם, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְהוֹרִין, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.en: How so? If they were sprinkled upon and on the same day they were broken and then they were recast and sprinkled upon on the same day, they are clean, the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, אֵין הַזָּיָה פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלִישִׁי וּשְׁבִיעִי:
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua says: there can be no effective sprinkling earlier than on the third and the seventh day.

phrases.he: מַפְתֵּחַ שֶׁל אַרְכֻּבָּה שֶׁנִּשְׁבַּר מִתּוֹךְ אַרְכֻּבָּתוֹ, טָהוֹר, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַמֵּא, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא פוֹתֵחַ בּוֹ מִבִּפְנִים.
phrases.en: A knee-shaped key that was broken off at the knee is clean. Rabbi Judah says that it is unclean because one can open with it from within.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל גַּם שֶׁנִּשְׁבַּר מִתּוֹךְ גֻּמּוֹ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A gamma-shaped key that was broken off at its shorter arm is clean.

phrases.he: הָיוּ בוֹ חָפִין וּנְקָבִין, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If it retained the teeth and the gaps it remains unclean.

phrases.he: נִטְּלוּ חָפִין, טָמֵא מִפְּנֵי נְקָבִין.
phrases.en: If the teeth were missing it is still unclean on account of the gaps; if the gaps were blocked up it is unclean on account of the teeth.

phrases.he: נִסְתַּתְּמוּ נְקָבִין, טָמֵא מִפְּנֵי חָפִין.
phrases.en: If the teeth were missing and the gaps were blocked up, or if they were merged into one another, it is clean.

phrases.he: נִטְּלוּ חָפִין וְנִסְתַּתְּמוּ נְקָבִין, אוֹ שֶׁפָּרְצוּ זֶה לְתוֹךְ זֶה, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If in a mustard-strainer three holes in its bottom were merged into one another the strainer is clean.

phrases.he: מְסַנֶּנֶת שֶׁל חַרְדָּל שֶׁנִּפְרְצוּ בָהּ שְׁלֹשָׁה נְקָבִים מִלְּמַטָּן זֶה לְתוֹךְ זֶה, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A metal mill-funnel is unclean.

phrases.he: וְהָאֲפַרְכֵּס שֶׁל מַתָּכוֹת, טְמֵאָה
כְּלֵי עֵץ, כְּלֵי עוֹר, כְּלֵי עֶצֶם, כְּלֵי זְכוּכִית, פְּשׁוּטֵיהֶן טְהוֹרִין, וּמְקַבְּלֵיהֶן טְמֵאִים. נִשְׁבְּרוּ, טָהָרוּ.
phrases.en: Vessels of wood, leather, bone or glass: those that are flat are clean and those that form a receptacle are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: חָזַר וְעָשָׂה מֵהֶן כֵּלִים, מְקַבְּלִין טֻמְאָה מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא.
phrases.en: If they are broken they become clean again. If one remade them into vessels they are susceptible to impurity henceforth.

phrases.he: הַשִּׁדָּה, וְהַתֵּבָה, וְהַמִּגְדָּל, כַּוֶּרֶת הַקַּשׁ, וְכַוֶּרֶת הַקָּנִים, וּבוֹר סְפִינָה אֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִית, שֶׁיֶּשׁ לָהֶם שׁוּלַיִם, וְהֵן מַחֲזִיקִין אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה בְלַח, שֶׁהֵם כּוֹרַיִם בְּיָבֵשׁ, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: A chest, a box, a cupboard, a straw basket, a reed basket, or the tank of an Alexandrian ship, that have flat bottoms and can hold a minimum of forty se'ah in liquid measure which represent two kor in dry measure, are clean.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַכֵּלִים, בֵּין מְקַבְּלִין, בֵּין אֵינָם מְקַבְּלִין, טְמֵאִין, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: All other vessels whether they can contain the minimum or cannot contain it, are susceptible to impurity, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, דַּרְדּוּר עֲגָלָה, וְקֻסְטוֹת הַמְּלָכִים, וַעֲרֵבַת הָעַבְּדָנִין, וּבוֹר סְפִינָה קְטַנָּה, וְהָאָרוֹן, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּקַבְּלִין, טְמֵאִין, שֶׁאֵינָן עֲשׂוּיִן לִטַּלְטֵל אֶלָּא בְמַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכָן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: the tub of a wagon, the food chests of kings, the tanners trough, the tank of a small ship, and an ark, even though they are able to contain the minimum, are susceptible to impurity, since they are intended to be moved about with their contents.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַכֵּלִים, הַמְּקַבְּלִים, טְהוֹרִין, וְשֶׁאֵינָן מְקַבְּלִין, טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: As to all other vessels, those that can contain the minimum are clean and those that cannot contain it are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: אֵין בֵּין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֶלָּא עֲרֵבַת בַּעַל הַבָּיִת
phrases.en: There is no difference between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Judah except a baking trough which belongs to a householder.

phrases.he: אֲרוּבוֹת שֶׁל נַחְתּוֹמִים, טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: Bakers’ baking-boards are susceptible to impurity, but those used by householders are clean.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים, טְהוֹרוֹת.
phrases.en: But if he dyed them red or saffron they are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: סֵרְקָן אוֹ כִרְכְּמָן, טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: If a bakers’ shelf was fixed to a wall: Rabbi Eliezer rules that it is clean And the sages rule that it is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: דַּף שֶׁל נַחְתּוֹמִין שֶׁקְּבָעוֹ בַכֹּתֶל, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְטַהֵר, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַמְּאִים.
phrases.en: The bakers' frame is susceptible to impurity but one used by householders is clean.

phrases.he: סְרוֹד שֶׁל נַחְתּוֹמִין, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If he made a rim on its four sides it is susceptible to impurity, but if one side was open it is clean.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים, טָהוֹר.
גִּפְּפוֹ מֵאַרְבַּע רוּחוֹתָיו, טָמֵא.
נִפְרַץ מֵרוּחַ אַחַת, טָהוֹר.
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אִם הִתְקִינוֹ לִהְיוֹת קוֹרֵץ עָלָיו, טָמֵא. וְכֵן הַמַּעֲרוֹךְ, טָמֵא:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: if he fixed it so that one can cut the dough upon it, it is susceptible to impurity. Similarly, a rolling-pin is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: יַם נָפָה שֶׁל סִלָּתִין, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: The container of the flour-dealers’ sifter is susceptible to impurity, but the one of a householder is clean.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים, טָהוֹר.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף שֶׁל גּוֹדֶלֶת טָמֵא מוֹשָׁב, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַבָּנוֹת יוֹשְׁבוֹת בְּתוֹכוֹ וְגוֹדְלוֹת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: also one that is used by a hairdresser is susceptible to impurity as a seat, since girls sit in it when their hair is dressed.

phrases.he: כָּל הַתְּלוֹיִים, טְמֵאִין, חוּץ מִתְּלוֹי נָפָה וּכְבָרָה שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: All hangers are susceptible to impurity, except for those of a sifter and a sieve that are used by householders, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, כֻּלָּן טְהוֹרִין, חוּץ מִתְּלוֹי נָפָה שֶׁל סִלָּתִין, וּתְלוֹי כִּבְרַת גְּרָנוֹת, וּתְלוֹי מַגַּל יָד, וּתְלוֹי מַקֵּל הַבַּלָּשִׁין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מְסַיְּעִין בִּשְׁעַת הַמְּלָאכָה.
phrases.en: But the sages say: all hangers are clean, excepting those of a sifter of flour-dealers, of a sieve used in threshing-floors, of a hand-sickle and of a detective's staff, since they aid when the instrument is in use.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, הֶעָשׂוּי לְסַיֵּעַ בִּשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה, טָמֵא. הֶעָשׂוּי לִתְלוֹי, טָהוֹר
phrases.en: This is the general rule: [a hanger] that is intended to aid when the instrument is in use is susceptible to impurity and one intended to serve only as a hanger is clean.

phrases.he: רַחַת שֶׁל גָּרוֹסוֹת, טְמֵאָה. שֶׁל אוֹצָרוֹת, טְהוֹרָה. שֶׁל גִּתּוֹת, טְמֵאָה. שֶׁל גְּרָנוֹת, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: The grist-dealers’ shovel is susceptible to impurity but the one used in grain stores is clean. The one used in wine- presses is susceptible to impurity but that used in threshing- floors is clean.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, הֶעָשׂוּי לְקַבָּלָה, טָמֵא. לְכִנּוּס, טָהוֹר
phrases.en: This is the general rule: [a shovel] that is intended to hold anything is susceptible to impurity but one intended only to heap stuff together is clean.

phrases.he: נִבְלֵי הַשָּׁרָה, טְמֵאִין. וְנִבְלֵי בְנֵי לֵוִי, טְהוֹרִין. כָּל הַמַּשְׁקִין, טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: Ordinary harps are susceptible to impurity, but the harps of Levites are clean.

phrases.he: וּמַשְׁקֵה בֵית מַטְבְּחַיָּא, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: All liquids are susceptible to impurity, but the liquids in the Temple slaughtering house are clean.

phrases.he: כָּל הַסְּפָרִים מְטַמְּאִין אֶת הַיָּדַיִם, חוּץ מִסֵּפֶר הָעֲזָרָה. הַמַּרְכּוֹף, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: All scrolls convey impurity to the hands, excepting the scroll of the Temple courtyard. A wooden toy horse is clean.

phrases.he: הַבַּטְנוֹן, וְהַנִּקְטְמוֹן, וְהָאֵרוּס, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: The belly-lute, the donkey-shaped musical instrument and the erus are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הָאֵרוּס טָמֵא מוֹשָׁב, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָאַלָּיִת יוֹשֶׁבֶת עָלָיו. מְצֻדַּת הַחֻלְדָּה, טְמֵאָה. וְשֶׁל הָעַכְבָּרִין, טְהוֹרָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: the erus is susceptible to sitting impurity since the wailing woman sits on it. A weasel-trap is susceptible to impurity, but a mouse- trap is clean.

phrases.he: כָּל כְּלִי עֵץ שֶׁנֶּחֱלַק לִשְׁנַיִם, טָהוֹר, חוּץ מִשֻּׁלְחָן הַכָּפוּל, וְתַמְחוּי הַמִּזְנוֹן, וְהָאֱפִיפוֹרִין שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי הַבָּיִת.
phrases.en: A wooden vessel that was broken into two parts becomes clean, except for a folding table, a dish with compartments for [different kinds of] food, and a householder's footstool.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף הַמָּגֵס, וְקוֹד הַבַּבְלִי כַּיּוֹצֵא בָהֶן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: a double dish and a Babylonian drinking vessel are subject to the same law.

phrases.he: כְּלֵי עֵץ, מֵאֵימָתַי מְקַבְּלִין טֻמְאָה.
phrases.en: When do wooden vessels begin to be susceptible to impurity? A bed and a cot, after they are sanded with fishskin.

phrases.he: הַמִּטָּה וְהָעֲרִיסָה, מִשֶּׁיְּשׁוּפֵם בְּעוֹר הַדָּג.
phrases.en: If the owner determined not to sand them over they are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: גָּמַר שֶׁלֹּא לָשׁוּף, טְמֵאָה.
רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, הַמִּטָּה, מִשֶּׁיְּסָרֵג בָּהּ שְׁלֹשָׁה בָתִּים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: a bed becomes susceptible to impurity as soon as three rows of meshes have been knitted in it.

phrases.he: הַסַּלִּים שֶׁל עֵץ, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב.
phrases.en: Wooden baskets [become susceptible to impurity] as soon as their rims are rounded off and their rough ends are smoothed off.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל תְּמָרָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא קִנֵּב מִבִּפְנִים, טָמֵא, שֶׁכֵּן מְקַיְּמִין.
phrases.en: But those that are made of palm-branches [become susceptible to impurity] even though their ends were not smoothed off on the inside, since they are allowed to remain in this condition.

phrases.he: כַּלְכָּלָה, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב וְיִגְמֹר אֶת הַתְּלוֹיָה.
phrases.en: A basket [of reed-grass becomes susceptible to impurity] as soon as its rim is rounded off, its rough ends are smoothed off, and its hanger is finished.

phrases.he: בֵּית הַלְּגִינִין, וּבֵית הַכּוֹסוֹת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא קִנֵּב מִבִּפְנִים, טָמֵא, שֶׁכֵּן מְקַיְּמִין
phrases.en: A wicker basket flasks or for cups [is susceptible to impurity] even if the rough ends were not smoothed off on the inside, since these are allowed to remain in this condition.

phrases.he: הַקְּנוֹנִין הַקְּטַנִּים, וְהַקְּלָתוֹת, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב.
phrases.en: Small reed baskets and baskets [become susceptible to impurity] as soon as their rims are rounded off and their rough ends are smoothed off.

phrases.he: הַקְּנוֹנִים הַגְּדוֹלִים, וְהַסּוּגִין הַגְּדוֹלִים, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה שְׁנֵי דוּרִים לָרֹחַב שֶׁלָּהֶם.
phrases.en: Large reed baskets and large hampers, as soon as two rows have been made round their sides.

phrases.he: יָם נָפָה, וּכְבָרָה, וְכַף שֶׁל מֹאזְנַיִם, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה דוּר אֶחָד לָרֹחַב שֶׁלָּהֶן.
phrases.en: The container of a sifter or a sieve and a cup of the balances, as soon as one circling band has been made round their sides.

phrases.he: הַקֻּפָּה, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה שְׁתֵּי צְפִירוֹת לָרֹחַב שֶׁלָּהּ.
phrases.en: A willow basket, as soon as two twists have been made around its wide sides.

phrases.he: וְהֶעָרָק, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה בוֹ צְפִירָה אֶחָת
phrases.en: And a rush basket, as soon as one twist has been made round it.

phrases.he: כְּלֵי עוֹר, מֵאֵימָתַי מְקַבְּלִין טֻמְאָה.
phrases.en: When do leather vessels become susceptible to impurity?A leather pouch, as soon as its hem has been stitched, its rough ends trimmed and its straps sewn on.

phrases.he: הַתּוּרְמֵל, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב וְיַעֲשֶׂה קִיחוֹתָיו.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה אֶת אָזְנָיו.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: so soon as its ears have been sewn on.

phrases.he: סְקֹרְטְיָא, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב וְיַעֲשֶׂה אֶת צִיצָתָהּ.
phrases.en: A leather apron [becomes susceptible to impurity] as soon as its hem has been stitched, its rough end trimmed and its strings sewn on.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה אֶת טַבְּעוֹתֶיהָ. קָטָבוֹלְיָא, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: as soon as its loops have been sewn on. A leather bed cover [becomes susceptible] as soon as its hem has been stitched and its rough ends trimmed.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה אֶת קִיחוֹתֶיהָ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: as soon as its straps have been sewn on.

phrases.he: הַכַּר וְהַכֶּסֶת שֶׁל עוֹר, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב.
phrases.en: A leather cushion or mattress [becomes susceptible] as soon as its hem has been stitched and its rough ends trimmed.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁיִּתְפְּרֵם וִישַׁיֵּר בָּהֶם פָּחוֹת מֵחֲמִשָּׁה טְפָחִים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: as it has been sew up and less than five handbreadths remained open.

phrases.he: פָּטִילְיָה, טְמֵאָה. וַחֲסִינָה, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A basket [for figs] is susceptible to uncleanness but a basket for wheat is clean.

phrases.he: סִגְנִיּוֹת שֶׁל עָלִין, טְהוֹרוֹת. שֶׁל נְצָרִין, טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: Small baskets made of leaves are clean, but those made of branches are susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: חוֹתָל שֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן לְתוֹכוֹ וְנוֹטֵל מִתּוֹכוֹ, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: The palm wrapping [in which dates are left] and into which they can be easily put and from which they can easily be taken out is susceptible to uncleanness, but if this cannot be done without tearing it or undoing it, it is clean.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל עַד שֶׁיִּקְרָעֶנּוּ אוֹ עַד שֶׁיַּתִּירֶנּוּ, טָהוֹר
קְסָיָה שֶׁל זוֹרֵי גְרָנוֹת, שֶׁל הוֹלְכֵי דְרָכִים, שֶׁל עוֹשֵׂי פִשְׁתָּן, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: The leather glove of winnowers, travelers, or flax workers is susceptible to uncleanness. But the one for dyers or blacksmiths is clean.

phrases.he: אֲבָל שֶׁל צַבָּעִין וְשֶׁל נַפָּחִין, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: the same law applies to the glove of grist dealers.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַף שֶׁל גָּרוֹסוֹת כַּיּוֹצֵא בָהֶן.
phrases.en: This is the general rule: that which is made for holding anything is susceptible to uncleanness, but that which only affords protection against perspiration is clean.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, הֶעָשׂוּי לְקַבָּלָה, טָמֵא. מִפְּנֵי הַזֵּעָה, טָהוֹר
הַמַּלְקוֹט שֶׁל בָּקָר, וְהֶחָסִים שֶׁלּוֹ, וְהַמַּדָּף שֶׁל דְּבוֹרִים, וְהַמְּנָפָה, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: The dung bag of a bull and its muzzle, a bee shelf, and a fan are clean.

phrases.he: כְּסוּי שֶׁל קֻפְסָא, טָמֵא. כְּסוּי קַמְטְרָא, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: The cover of a small box is susceptible to uncleanness; The cover of a clothes chest is clean.

phrases.he: כְּסוּי תֵּבָה, כְּסוּי טֶנִי, וְהַמַּכְבֵּשׁ שֶׁל חָרָשׁ, וְהַכֶּסֶת שֶׁתַּחַת הַתֵּבָה, וְהַקִּמְרוֹן שֶׁלָּהּ, וְאַנְגְּלִין שֶׁל סֵפֶר, בֵּית הַנֶּגֶר, בֵּית הַמַּנְעוּל, וּבֵית הַמְּזוּזָה, וְתִיק נְבָלִין, וְתִיק כִּנּוֹרֶת, וְהָאֵמוּם שֶׁל גּוֹדְלֵי מִצְנָפוֹת, וְהַמַּרְכּוֹף שֶׁל זַמָּר, וּרְבִיעִית שֶׁל אַלָּיִת, וּגְנוֹגְנִית הֶעָנִי, וְסָמוֹכוֹת הַמִּטָּה, וּטְפוּס שֶׁל תְּפִלָּה, וְאֵמוּם שֶׁל עוֹשֵׂה סוּתוֹת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְהוֹרִים. זֶה הַכְּלָל,
