phrases.en: The hides of a householder become susceptible to uncleanness by intention, but those that belong to a tanner do not become susceptible by mere intention.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל עַבְּדָן, אֵין מַחֲשָׁבָה מְטַמֵּאתָן.
phrases.en: Those taken by a thief become susceptible by intention, but those taken by a robber do not become susceptible by mere intention.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל גַּנָּב, מַחֲשָׁבָה מְטַמֵּאתָן.
וְשֶׁל גַּזְלָן, אֵין מַחֲשָׁבָה מְטַמֵּאתָן.
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, חִלּוּף הַדְּבָרִים, שֶׁל גַּזְלָן, מַחֲשָׁבָה מְטַמֵּאתָן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: the rule is to be reversed; those taken by a robber become susceptible by mere intention, but those taken by a thief do not become susceptible by intention, since in the latter case the owner does not abandon hope for recovery.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל גַּנָּב, אֵין מַחֲשָׁבָה מְטַמֵּאתָן, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְיָאֲשׁוּ הַבְּעָלִים
עוֹר שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא מִדְרָס, וְחִשַּׁב עָלָיו לִרְצוּעוֹת וּלְסַנְדָּלִין, כֵּיוָן שֶׁנָּתַן בּוֹ אֶת הָאִזְמֵל, טָהוֹר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: If a hide had contracted midras uncleanness and its owner then intended it to be used for straps or sandals, it becomes clean as soon as he put the knife to it, the words of Rabbi Judah.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, עַד שֶׁיְּמַעֲטֶנּוּ פָחוֹת מֵחֲמִשָּׁה טְפָחִים. רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר
phrases.en: But the sages say: it does not become clean until he has reduced its size to less than five handbreadths.

phrases.he: רַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר, אַף הָעוֹשֶׂה מִטְפַּחַת מִן הָעוֹר, טְמֵאָה. וּמִן הַכֶּסֶת, טְהוֹרָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar bar Zadok says: even if one made a napkin from a hide it remains unclean, But if [he made one from] a covering it becomes clean.

phrases.he: הַבֶּגֶד מִטַּמֵּא מִשּׁוּם חֲמִשָּׁה שֵׁמוֹת. הַשַּׂק, מִשּׁוּם אַרְבָּעָה. הָעוֹר, מִשּׁוּם שְׁלֹשָׁה. הָעֵץ, מִשּׁוּם שְׁנַיִם.
phrases.en: Cloth is susceptible to five categories of uncleanness; Sack-cloth is susceptible to four; Leather to three; Wood to two; And an earthenware vessel to one.

phrases.he: וּכְלִי חֶרֶס, מִשּׁוּם אֶחָד.
phrases.en: An earthenware vessel is susceptible to uncleanness [only] as a receptacle; any earthen vessel that has no inner part is not susceptible to uncleanness from its outer part.

phrases.he: כְּלִי חֶרֶס מִטַּמֵּא מִשּׁוּם כְּלִי קִבּוּל.
phrases.en: Wood is subject to an additional form of uncleanness in that it is also susceptible to uncleanness as a seat.

phrases.he: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תוֹךְ בִּכְלֵי חֶרֶס, אֵין לוֹ אֲחוֹרָיִם.
phrases.en: Similarly a tablet which has no rim is susceptible to uncleanness if it is a wooden object and insusceptible if it is an earthenware one.

phrases.he: מוּסָף עָלָיו הָעֵץ, שֶׁהוּא מִטַּמֵּא מִשּׁוּם מוֹשָׁב.
phrases.en: Leather is susceptible to an additional form of uncleanness in that it is also susceptible to the uncleanness of a tent.

phrases.he: וְכֵן טַבְלָא שֶׁאֵין לָהּ לִזְבֵּז, בִּכְלֵי עֵץ, טְמֵאָה, וּבִכְלֵי חֶרֶס, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: Sack-cloth has an additional form of uncleanness in that it is susceptible to uncleanness as woven work.

phrases.he: מוּסָף עָלָיו הָעוֹר, שֶׁהוּא מִטַּמֵּא מִשּׁוּם אֹהָלִים.
phrases.en: Cloth has an additional form of uncleanness in that it is susceptible to uncleanness when it is only three by three fingerbreadths.

phrases.he: מוּסָף עָלָיו הַשַּׂק, שֶׁהוּא מִטַּמֵּא מִשּׁוּם אָרִיג.
מוּסָף עָלָיו הַבֶּגֶד, שֶׁהוּא מִטַּמֵּא מִשּׁוּם שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ
הַבֶּגֶד מִטַּמֵּא מִשּׁוּם שְׁלֹשָׁה עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה, לְמִדְרָס, וּמִשּׁוּם שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ לִטְמֵא מֵת.
phrases.en: Cloth is susceptible to midras uncleanness when it is three handbreadths by three handbreadths, and to corpse uncleanness when it is three fingerbreadths by three fingerbreadths.

phrases.he: הַשַּׂק אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה, הָעוֹר חֲמִשָּׁה עַל חֲמִשָּׁה, מַפָּץ שִׁשָּׁה עַל שִׁשָּׁה, שָׁוִין לְמִדְרָס וְלִטְמֵא מֵת.
phrases.en: Sack-cloth when it is four handbreadths by four handbreadths. Leather, five handbreadths by five handbreadths. And matting, six handbreadths by six handbreadths. [All of these] are equally susceptible to both midras and corpse uncleanness.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, הַשַּׂק שְׁיָרָיו אַרְבָּעָה, וּתְחִלָּתוֹ מִשֶּׁיִּגָּמֵר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: what remains of sack-cloth is susceptible to uncleanness if it is four handbreadths, but when in its first condition [it becomes susceptible only after its manufacture] is completed.

phrases.he: הָעוֹשֶׂה שְׁנַיִם מִן הַבֶּגֶד וְאֶחָד מִן הַשַּׂק, שְׁלָשְׁתָּן מִן הַשַּׂק וְאֶחָד מִן הָעוֹר, אַרְבָּעָה מִן הָעוֹר וְאֶחָד מִן הַמַּפָּץ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If one made up a piece of material from two handbreadths of cloth and one of sack-cloth, or of three of sack-cloth and one of leather or four of leather and one of matting, it is not susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: חֲמִשָּׁה מִן הַמַּפָּץ וְאֶחָד מִן הָעוֹר, אַרְבָּעָה מִן הָעוֹר וְאֶחָד מִן הַשַּׂק, שְׁלֹשָׁה מִן הַשַּׂק וְאֶחָד מִן הַבֶּגֶד, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If the piece of material was made up of five handbreadths of matting and one of leather or four of leather and one of sack-cloth, or three of sack-cloth and one of cloth it is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כֹּל שֶׁחִבֵּר לוֹ מִן הֶחָמוּר מִמֶּנּוּ, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: This is the general rule: if the material added is subject to greater restrictions it is susceptible to uncleanness, but if the material added was subject to lesser restrictions it is not susceptible.

phrases.he: מִן הַקַּל מִמֶּנּוּ, טָהוֹר
הַמְקַצֵּעַ מִכֻּלָּם טֶפַח עַל טֶפַח, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If one cut off from any of these a piece one by one handbreadth it is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: מִשּׁוּלֵי הַקֻּפָּה טֶפַח עַל טֶפַח, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: [If one cut off a one by one handbreadth piece] from the bottom of a basket it is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: מִצְּדָדֵי הַקֻּפָּה, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַהֵר.
וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, הַמְקַצֵּעַ טֶפַח עַל טֶפַח בְּכָל מָקוֹם, טָמֵא:
phrases.en: If one cut off from the sides of the basket: Rabbi Shimon says that it is not susceptible to uncleanness, But the sages say one who cuts off a square handbreadth from anywhere, it is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: בְּלוֹיֵי נָפָה וּכְבָרָה שֶׁהִתְקִינָן לִישִׁיבָה, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַמֵּא, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין עַד שֶׁיְּקַצֵּעַ.
phrases.en: Worn-out pieces of a sifter or a sieve that were adapted for use as a seat: Rabbi Akiva rules that they are susceptible to uncleanness, But the sages rule that they are not susceptible unless their rough ends were cut off.

phrases.he: כִּסֵּא שֶׁל קָטָן שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ רַגְלַיִם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ גָבֹהַּ טֶפַח, טָמֵא. חָלוּק שֶׁל קָטָן,
phrases.en: A child's stool that has legs, even though it is less than a handbreadth high, is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, כָּל שֶׁהוּא.
phrases.en: A child's shirt: Rabbi Eliezer rules it is susceptible to uncleanness at any size.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בוֹ כַשִּׁעוּר, וְנִמְדָּד כָּפוּל:
phrases.en: But the sages rule: it is susceptible only if it is of the prescribed size, and it is measured when doubled over.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ נִמְדָּדִין כְּפוּלִין. אַמְפַּלְיָא, וּפְמוֹלִינְיָא, וּמִכְנָסַיִם, וְכוֹבַע, וְכִיס שֶׁל פֻּנְדִּיָּא.
phrases.en: The following are measured when doubled: Felt socks, long stockings, pants, a cap and a money-belt.

phrases.he: וּמַטְלִית שֶׁטְּלָיָהּ עַל הַשָּׂפָה, אִם פְּשׁוּטָה, נִמְדֶּדֶת פְּשׁוּטָה, וְאִם כְּפוּלָה, נִמְדֶּדֶת כְּפוּלָה
phrases.en: As regards a patch sewn on the hem, if it was simple it is measured simple, but if it was doubled it is measured when doubled.

phrases.he: הַבֶּגֶד שֶׁאָרַג בּוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה, וְנִטְמָא מִדְרָס, וְהִשְׁלִים עָלָיו אֶת כָּל הַבֶּגֶד, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָטַל חוּט אֶחָד מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ, טָהוֹר מִן הַמִּדְרָס, אֲבָל טָמֵא מַגַּע מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: If a piece of cloth was woven to the size of three by three handbreadths, and then it contracted midras uncleanness, and then he completed the rest of the piece, and then one removed a single thread from the original part, it is free from midras uncleanness but is still unclean from contact with midras uncleanness.

phrases.he: נָטַל חוּט אֶחָד מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִשְׁלִים עָלָיו אֶת כָּל הַבֶּגֶד, טָמֵא מַגַּע מִדְרָס
phrases.en: If he removed a thread from the original part and then he finished the whole cloth, it is still unclean from contact with midras uncleanness.

phrases.he: וְכֵן בֶּגֶד שֶׁאָרַג בּוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ, וְנִטְמָא טְמֵא מֵת, וְהִשְׁלִים עָלָיו אֶת כָּל הַבֶּגֶד, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָטַל חוּט אֶחָד מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ, טָהוֹר מִטְּמֵא מֵת, אֲבָל טָמֵא מַגַּע טְמֵא מֵת.
phrases.en: Similarly, if a piece of cloth was woven to the size of three [fingerbreadths] square, and it contracted corpse uncleanness, and afterwards he finished the entire piece, and then he removed a single thread from its original part, it is free from corpse uncleanness but is still unclean from contact with corpse uncleanness.

phrases.he: נָטַל חוּט אֶחָד מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִשְׁלִים עָלָיו אֶת כָּל הַבֶּגֶד, טָהוֹר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָמְרוּ, שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ שֶׁנִּתְמַעֵט, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If a thread was removed from the original part and then all the cloth was finished it remains clean, for the sages have ruled: if a piece of three [fingerbreadths] square is lessened it becomes clean.

phrases.he: אֲבָל שְׁלֹשָׁה עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁנִּתְמַעֵט, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁטָּהוֹר מִמִּדְרָס, טָמֵא בְכָל הַטֻּמְאוֹת
phrases.en: But if one of three handbreadths square is lessened, even though it is released from midras, it is still susceptible to all other forms of uncleanness.

phrases.he: סָדִין שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא מִדְרָס, וַעֲשָׂאוֹ וִילוֹן, טָהוֹר מִן הַמִּדְרָס, אֲבָל טָמֵא מַגַּע מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: If a sheet that had contracted midras uncleanness was made into a curtain, it is pure from midras uncleanness but is still unclean from contact with midras uncleanness.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, וְכִי בְאֵיזֶה מִדְרָס נָגַע זֶה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose said: but what midras uncleanness has this touched! Only if a zav had touched it is it unclean from contact with a zav.

phrases.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נָגַע בּוֹ הַזָּב, טָמֵא בְמַגַּע הַזָּב
שְׁלֹשָׁה עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁנֶּחֱלַק, טָהוֹר מִן הַמִּדְרָס, אֲבָל טָמֵא מַגַּע מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: If a piece of cloth three [handbreadths] square was divided, it is pure from midras uncleanness but is still unclean from contact with midras uncleanness.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, וְכִי בְאֵיזֶה מִדְרָס נָגַע זֶה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose said: but what midras uncleanness has this touched! Only if a zav had touched it is it unclean from contact with a zav.

phrases.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נָגַע בּוֹ הַזָּב, טָמֵא מַגַּע הַזָּב
שְׁלֹשָׁה עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה, בָּאַשְׁפּוֹת, בָּרִיא וְצוֹרֵר מֶלַח.
phrases.en: If a piece of cloth three [handbreadths] square [was found] in a rubbish heap it must be both sound and capable of wrapping up salt; But [if it was found] in the house it need only be either sound or capable of wrapping up salt.

phrases.he: בַּבַּיִת, אוֹ בָרִיא אוֹ צוֹרֵר מֶלַח.
כַּמָּה מֶלַח יְהֵא צוֹרֵר, רֹבַע.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בְּדַקָּה.
phrases.en: How much salt must it be capable of wrapping up? A quarter of a kav.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בְּגַסָּה. אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ מִתְכַּוְּנִים לְהָקֵל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: this refers to fine salt, But the sages stated: it refers to coarse salt. Both intended to be lenient.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, שָׁוִים שְׁלֹשָׁה עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה בָאַשְׁפּוֹת לְשָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ בַּבָּיִת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: the law concerning a piece of cloth three [handbreadths] square found in a rubbish heap is the same as that for a piece of cloth that was three [fingerbreadths] square in a house.

phrases.he: שְׁלֹשָׁה עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁנִּקְרַע, אִם נְתָנוֹ עַל הַכִּסֵּא וּבְשָׂרוֹ נוֹגֵעַ בַּכִּסֵּא, טָהוֹר, וְאִם לָאו, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: [A piece of cloth] three [handbreadths] square that was torn: if he put it on a chair, and his skin touches the chair, it is pure; And if not, it remains impure.

phrases.he: שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ שֶׁנִּמְהָה מִמֶּנָּה חוּט אֶחָד, אוֹ שֶׁנִּמְצָא בוֹ קֶשֶׁר, אוֹ שְׁנֵי חוּטִין מַתְאִימִין, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: [A piece of cloth] three [fingerbreadths] square one thread of which was worn away, or in which a knot was found, or in which two threads ran alongside each other, is pure.

phrases.he: שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ שֶׁהִשְׁלִיכָהּ בָּאַשְׁפּוֹת, טְהוֹרָה. הֶחֱזִירָהּ, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: [A piece of cloth] three [fingerbreadths] square that was thrown on the rubbish heap becomes pure. If he brought it back, it it becomes susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: לְעוֹלָם הַשְׁלָכָתָהּ מְטַהֲרַתָּה, וַחֲזָרָתָהּ מְטַמֵּאתָהּ, חוּץ מִשֶּׁל אַרְגָּמָן וְשֶׁל זְהוֹרִית טוֹבָה.
phrases.en: Throwing it away always renders it pure and taking it back renders it susceptible to uncleanness, except when it is of purple or fine crimson.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַף מַטְלִית חֲדָשָׁה כַּיּוֹצֵא בָהֶן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: a patch of new cloth is also subject to the same law.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, כֻּלָּן טְהוֹרִין, לֹא הֻזְכְּרוּ אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי הֲשָׁבַת אֲבֵדָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: all these materials become pure; they were mentioned only in connection with the return of lost property.

phrases.he: שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ שֶׁנְּתָנָהּ בְּכַדּוּר, אוֹ שֶׁעֲשָׂאָהּ כַּדּוּר בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: [A piece of cloth] three [fingerbreadths] square that was stuffed into a ball or was itself made into a ball is clean.

phrases.he: אֲבָל שְׁלֹשָׁה עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁנְּתָנוֹ בְכַדּוּר, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: But [a piece of cloth] three [handbreadths] square that was stuffed into a ball remains unclean.

phrases.he: עֲשָׂאוֹ כַדּוּר בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, טָהוֹר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַתֶּפֶר מְמַעֲטוֹ
phrases.en: If he made it into a ball itself, it is clean because the sewing reduces its size.

phrases.he: פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁהִתְקִינוֹ לָפוֹק בּוֹ אֶת הַמֶּרְחָץ, לְנַעֵר בּוֹ אֶת הַקְּדֵרָה, לְקַנֵּחַ בּוֹ אֶת הָרֵחַיִם, בֵּין מוּכָן בֵּין שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּכָן, טָמֵא, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.en: [A piece of cloth] less than three [handbreadths] square that was adapted for the purpose of stopping up a hole in a bath house, of emptying a cooking-pot or of wiping with it the mill stones, whether it was or was not kept in readiness for any such use, is susceptible to uncleanness, the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, בֵּין מִן הַמּוּכָן, בֵּין שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִן הַמּוּכָן, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua says: whether it was or was not kept in readiness it is pure.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, מִן הַמּוּכָן, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiba ruled: if it was kept in readiness it is susceptible, and if it was not kept in readiness it is pure.

phrases.he: שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִן הַמּוּכָן, טָהוֹר
הָעוֹשֶׂה אִסְפְּלָנִית, בֵּין בְּבֶגֶד בֵּין בְּעוֹר, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If a bandage is made of cloth or leather it is pure. (Rabbi Yose says: with leather it is pure.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, עַל הָעוֹר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A poultice is pure if it is on cloth, but if on leather it is susceptible.

phrases.he: מְלוּגְמָא, בְּבֶגֶד, טְהוֹרָה, וּבְעוֹר, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel says: even if it was on cloth it remains susceptible to uncleanness because it can be shaken off.

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, אַף בְּבֶגֶד, טְמֵאָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא נִנְעָרֶת
מִטְפְּחוֹת סְפָרִים, בֵּין מְצֻיָּרוֹת בֵּין שֶׁאֵינָן מְצֻיָּרוֹת, טְמֵאוֹת, כְּדִבְרֵי בֵית שַׁמַּאי.
phrases.en: Covers of scrolls, whether they are decorated or not, are susceptible to uncleanness according to the view of Bet Shammai.

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מְצֻיָּרוֹת, טְהוֹרוֹת, וְשֶׁאֵינָם מְצֻיָּרוֹת, טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: Bet Hillel says: those that are decorated are pure, but those that are not decorated are susceptible.

phrases.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ טְהוֹרוֹת
phrases.en: Rabban Gamaliel says: both the former and the latter are pure.

phrases.he: כִּפָּה שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא מִדְרָס, וּנְתָנוֹ עַל הַסֵּפֶר, טָהוֹר מִן הַמִּדְרָס, אֲבָל טָמֵא טְמֵא מֵת.
phrases.en: If a head-wrap that had contracted midras uncleanness was wrapped around a scroll, it is released from midras uncleanness but it remains susceptible to corpse uncleanness.

phrases.he: חֵמֶת שֶׁעֲשָׂאָהּ שָׁטִיחַ, וְשָׁטִיחַ שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ חֵמֶת, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A skin that was made into a rug or a rug that was made into a skin becomes clean.

phrases.he: חֵמֶת שֶׁעֲשָׂאָהּ תּוּרְמֵל וְתוּרְמֵל שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ חֵמֶת, כַּר שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ סָדִין וְסָדִין שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ כַּר, כֶּסֶת שֶׁעֲשָׂאָהּ מִטְפַּחַת וּמִטְפַּחַת שֶׁעֲשָׂאָהּ כֶּסֶת, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: A skin that was made into a [shepherd's] wallet or a [shepherd's] wallet that was made into a skin; Or a cushion cover that was made into a sheet or a sheet that was made into a cushion cover; Or a sheet cover that was made into a plain sheet or a plain sheet that was made into a sheet cover, remains unclean.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כֹּל שֶׁשִּׁנָּהוּ לִשְׁמוֹ, טָמֵא. לְשֵׁם אַחֵר, טָהוֹר
phrases.en: This is the general rule: any object that has been changed into one of the same class remains unclean, but if into one of another class it becomes clean.

phrases.he: מַטְלִית שֶׁטְּלָיָהּ עַל הַקֻּפָּה, מְטַמְּאָה אֶחָד וּפוֹסֶלֶת אֶחָד.
phrases.en: If a patch was sewn on to a basket, it conveys one grade of uncleanness and one of unfitness.

phrases.he: הִפְרִישָׁהּ מִן הַקֻּפָּה, הַקֻּפָּה מְטַמָּא אֶחָד וּפוֹסֶלֶת אֶחָד, וְהַמַּטְלִית טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If it was separated from the basket, it conveys one grade of uncleanness and one of unfitness, but the patch becomes clean.

phrases.he: טְלָיָהּ עַל הַבֶּגֶד, מְטַמָּא שְׁנַיִם וּפוֹסֶלֶת אֶחָד.
phrases.en: If it was sewn on to cloth it conveys two grades of uncleanness and one of unfitness.

phrases.he: הִפְרִישָׁהּ מִן הַבֶּגֶד, הַבֶּגֶד מְטַמֵּא אֶחָד וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד, וְהַמַּטְלִית מְטַמְּאָה שְׁנַיִם וּפוֹסֶלֶת אֶחָד.
phrases.en: If it was separated from the cloth, it conveys one grade of uncleanness and one of unfitness, while the patch conveys two grades of uncleanness and one of unfitness.

phrases.he: וְכֵן הַטּוֹלֶה עַל הַשַּׂק אוֹ עַל הָעוֹר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַהֵר.
phrases.en: The same law applies to a patch was sewn on to sacking or leather, the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Shimon says that it is clean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, עַל הָעוֹר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: if [it was sewn] on leather it becomes clean; but if on sacking it remains unclean, since the latter is a woven material.

phrases.he: עַל הַשַּׂק, טָמֵא, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא אָרִיג
שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ שֶׁאָמְרוּ, חוּץ מִן הַמְּלָל, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.en: The three (fingerbreadths) square of which they have spoken do not include the hem, the words of Rabbi Shimon.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ מְכֻוָּנֶת.
phrases.en: But the sages say: exactly three [fingerbreadths] square.

phrases.he: טְלָיָהּ עַל הַבֶּגֶד, מֵרוּחַ אַחַת, אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: If a patch was sewn on to a cloth by one side only, it is not considered as connected.

phrases.he: מִשְּׁתֵּי רוּחוֹת זוֹ כְנֶגֶד זוֹ, חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: If it was sewn on by two opposite sides, it is considered connected.

phrases.he: עֲשָׂאוֹ כְמִין גַּאם, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַמֵּא, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין.
phrases.en: If it was sewn on the shape of a gamma: Rabbi Akiva says that the cloth is unclean, But the sages say that it is clean.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בְּטַלִּית.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah stated: When does this apply? To a cloak, but in the case of an undershirt the patch is regarded as connected if it was sewn by its upper side, but if by its lower side it is not connected.

phrases.he: אֲבָל בְּחָלוּק, מִלְמַעְלָן, חִבּוּר. וּמִלְּמַטָּן, אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר
בִּגְדֵי עֲנִיִּים, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְמֵאִין מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: Poor men's clothes, though made up of pieces none of which is three [fingerbreadths] square are susceptible to midras uncleanness.

phrases.he: טַלִּית שֶׁהִתְחִיל בָּהּ לְקָרְעָהּ, כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּקְרַע רֻבָּהּ, אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: If a cloak began to be torn, as soon as its greater part is torn [the pieces] are not regarded as connected.

phrases.he: הֶעָבִים וְהָרַכִּים, אֵין בָּהֶם מִשּׁוּם שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ
phrases.en: Exceptionally thick or thin materials are not governed by the prescribed minimum of three [fingerbreadths] square.

phrases.he: כֶּסֶת הַסַּבָּלִין, טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: A porter's pad is susceptible to midras uncleanness.

phrases.he: מְשַׁמֶּרֶת שֶׁל יַיִן, אֵין בָּהּ מִשּׁוּם מוֹשָׁב.
phrases.en: A wine filter is not susceptible to uncleanness as a seat.

phrases.he: סְבָכָה שֶׁל זְקֵנָה, טְמֵאָה מִשּׁוּם מוֹשָׁב.
phrases.en: An old woman's hair-net is susceptible to uncleanness as a seat.

phrases.he: חָלוּק שֶׁל יוֹצֵאת הַחוּץ הֶעָשׂוּי כִּסְבָכָה, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A prostitute's shirt which is woven like a net is not susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: הָעוֹשֶׂה בֶגֶד מִן הַחֵרֶם, טָהוֹר. וּמִזּוּטוֹ, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: A garment made of fishing net is not susceptible to uncleanness, but one made of its bag is susceptible.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר, אַף הָעוֹשֶׂה בֶגֶד מִן הַחֵרֶם וּכְפָלוֹ, טָמֵא
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Jacob says: if a garment is made out of a fishing net but is made double it is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: סְבָכָה שֶׁהִתְחִיל בָּהּ מִפִּיהָ, טְהוֹרָה, עַד שֶׁיִּגְמֹר אֶת קוּרְקוּרְתָּהּ.
phrases.en: A hair-net that one began to make from its upper hem remains pure until its bottom section is finished.

phrases.he: הִתְחִיל בָּהּ מִקּוּרְקוּרְתָּהּ, טְהוֹרָה, עַד שֶׁיִּגְמֹר אֶת פִּיהָ.
phrases.en: If one began from its bottom section, it remains pure until its hem is finished.

phrases.he: שָׁבִיס שֶׁלָּהּ, טָמֵא בִפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.en: Its head band is susceptible to uncleanness in itself.

phrases.he: הַחוּטִין שֶׁלָּהּ, טְמֵאִין מִשּׁוּם חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: Its strings are susceptible to uncleanness because they are connected.

phrases.he: סְבָכָה שֶׁנִּקְרְעָה, אִם אֵינָהּ מְקַבֶּלֶת אֶת רֹב הַשֵּׂעָר, טְהוֹרָה
phrases.en: A hair-net that is torn becomes pure if it cannot contain the greater part of the hair.

phrases.he: נוֹמֵי הַסָּדִין וְהַסּוּדָרִין וְהַטַּרְטִין וְהַפִּלְיוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ, שֵׁשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת. שֶׁל אַפְקַרְסִין, עֶשֶׂר.
phrases.en: The fringe strings of a sheet, a scarf, a head-wrap and a felt cap [are regarded as connected] up to a length of six fingerbreadths; Those of an undergarment up to ten [fingerbreadths].

phrases.he: נִימֵי סָגוֹס, וְהָרְדִיד, וְהֶחָלוּק, וְהַטַּלִּית, שָׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת.
phrases.en: The fringes of a thick wool cloak, a veil, a shirt, or a light cloak [are regarded as connected] up to a length of three fingerbreadths.

phrases.he: נִימֵי כִפָּה שֶׁל זְקֵנָה, וְהַגּוּמְדִין שֶׁל עַרְבִיִּין, וְהַקֻּלְקִין, וְהַפֻּנְדָּא, וְהַמַּעֲפֹרֶת, וְהַפַּרְגּוֹד, נִימֵיהֶן כָּל שֶׁהֵן
phrases.en: The fringes of an old woman's head-wrap, of Arabian face wraps, of Cilician goat's-hair clothing, of a money-belt, of a turban or of a curtain are regarded as connected whatever their length may be.

phrases.he: שָׁלֹשׁ כְּסָתוֹת שֶׁל צֶמֶר, שֵׁשׁ שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן, שְׁלֹשָׁה סְדִינִין, שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה מִטְפָּחוֹת, שְׁנֵי סוּבְרִיקִין, חָלוּק אֶחָד, טַלִּית אֶחָד, קְלֻבְקָרִין אֶחָד, חִבּוּר לַטֻּמְאָה וְלַהֲזָּיָה.
phrases.en: Three woolen pillow-covers, six linen ones, three sheets, twelve handkerchiefs, two pant-sleeves, one shirt, one cloak, or one winter-cloak, can be regarded as connected in respect of both uncleanness and sprinkling.

phrases.he: יָתֵר מִכָּאן, חִבּוּר לַטֻּמְאָה, וְאֵין חִבּוּר לַהַזָּיָה.
phrases.en: If they exceed this number they are regarded as connected in respect of uncleanness but not in respect of sprinkling.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַף לֹא לַטֻּמְאָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: not even in respect of uncleanness.

phrases.he: חוּט הַמִּשְׁקֹלֶת, שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר.
phrases.en: The string of a [common] plumb-line is regarded as connected up to a length of twelve [cubits]; That of the carpenters’ plumb-line, up to eighteen [cubits]; And that of the builders’ plumb-line up to fifty cubits.

phrases.he: שֶׁל חָרָשִׁין, שְׁמֹנָה עָשָׂר.
phrases.en: The parts that exceed these lengths, even if it was desired to retain them, are pure.

phrases.he: שֶׁל בַּנָּיִן, חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה.
phrases.en: The plumb-line of plasterers or moulders is regarded as connected whatsoever its length.

phrases.he: יָתֵר מִכָּאן, אִם רָצָה לְקַיֵּם, טָהוֹר.
שֶׁל סַיָּדִין וְשֶׁל צַיָּרִין, כָּל שֶׁהֵן
חוּט מֹאזְנַיִם שֶׁל זֶהָבִים וְשֶׁל שׁוֹקְלֵי אַרְגָּמָן טוֹב, שָׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת.
phrases.en: The cord of the balances of goldsmiths or the weighers of fine purple cloth is regarded as a connective up to a length of three fingerbreadths, The handle of an axe behind the grip, up to a length of three fingerbreadths.

phrases.he: יַד הַקֻּרְדֹּם מֵאַחֲרָיו, שָׁלשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת.
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, טֶפַח, טָהוֹר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: if the length behind the grip is no less than one handbreadth the entire handle is unsusceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: חוּט מֹאזְנַיִם שֶׁל חֶנְוָנִים, שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים טֶפַח.
phrases.en: The cord of the balances of shopkeepers or householders is regarded as connected up to a length of one handbreadth.

phrases.he: יַד הַקֻּרְדֹּם מִלְּפָנָיו, טֶפַח.
phrases.en: The shaft of an axe in front of the grip, up to one handbreadth.

phrases.he: שְׁיָרֵי יַד הַפַּרְגּוֹל, טֶפַח.
phrases.en: The projection of the shaft of a compass, up to one handbreadth.

phrases.he: יַד מַקֶּבֶת שֶׁל יָד שֶׁל מְפַתְּחֵי אֲבָנִים, טָפַח
phrases.en: That of the shaft of the stone-masons’ chisel, one handbreadth.

phrases.he: חוּט מֹאזְנַיִם שֶׁל צַמָּרִים, וְשֶׁל שׁוֹקְלֵי זְכוּכִית, טְפָחַיִם. יַד הַמַּקּוֹר, טְפָחַיִם.
phrases.en: The cord of the balances of wool dealers or of glass-weighers is regarded as connected up to a length of two handbreadths. The shaft of a millstone chisel, up to a length of two handbreadths.

phrases.he: יַד הַמַּעֲצָד שֶׁל לִגְיוֹנוֹת, טְפָחַיִם.
phrases.en: The shaft of the battle-axe of the legions, up to a length of two handbreadths.

phrases.he: יַד הַקֻּרְנָס שֶׁל זֶהָבִים, טְפָחַיִם.
phrases.en: The shaft of the goldsmiths’ hammer, up to a length of two handbreadths.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל חָרָשִׁין, שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים
phrases.en: And that of the blacksmiths' hammer, up to three handbreadths.

phrases.he: שְׁיָרֵי הַדָּרְבָן מִלְמַעְלָן, אַרְבָּעָה. יַד הַבָּדִיד, אַרְבָּעָה.
phrases.en: The remnant of the shaft of an ox-goad at its upper end is regarded as connected up to a length of four [handbreadths].

phrases.he: יַד הַקֻּרְדֹּם שֶׁל נִכּוּשׁ, חֲמִשָּׁה.
phrases.en: The shaft of a spade, to a length of four [handbreadths].

phrases.he: יַד בֶּן הַפַּטִּישׁ, חֲמִשָּׁה. וְשֶׁל הַפַּטִּישׁ, שִׁשָּׁה.
phrases.en: The shaft of a weeding-spade, to five handbreadths. The shaft of a small hammer, to five handbreadths. That of a common hammer, to six handbreadths.

phrases.he: יַד הַקֻּרְדֹּם שֶׁל בִּקּוּעַ וְשֶׁל עָדִיר, שִׁשָּׁה.
phrases.en: The shaft of an axe used for splitting wood or of one used for digging, to six [handbreadths].

phrases.he: וְיַד מַקֶּבֶת שֶׁל סַתָּתִין, שִׁשָּׁה
phrases.en: The shaft of the stone-trimmers’ axe, up to six handbreadths.

phrases.he: שְׁיָרֵי חַרְחוּר מִלְּמַטָּן, שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.en: The remnant of the shaft of an ox-goad at its lower end is regarded as connected up to a length of seven handbreadths.

phrases.he: יַד מַגְרֵפָה שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים,
בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.en: The shaft of a householders' shovel Bet Shammai says: to a length of seven handbreadths, And Bet Hillel says: eight handbreadths.

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, שְׁמֹנָה. שֶׁל סַיָּדִין,
phrases.en: That of the plasterers: Bet Shammai says: nine handbreadths And Bet Hillel says: ten handbreadths.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, תִּשְׁעָה.
phrases.en: Any parts exceeding these lengths, if he wanted to retain it, is also susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, עֲשָׂרָה.
phrases.en: The shafts of fire instruments are susceptible to uncleanness whatsoever their length.

phrases.he: יָתֵר מִכָּאן, אִם רָצָה לְקַיֵּם, טָמֵא.
וְיַד מְשַׁמְּשֵׁי הָאוּר, כָּל שֶׁהוּא
כְּלֵי זְכוּכִית, פְּשׁוּטֵיהֶן טְהוֹרִין, וּמְקַבְּלֵיהֶן טְמֵאִים. נִשְׁבְּרוּ, טָהָרוּ.
phrases.en: Glass vessels--those that are flat are pure and those that have receptacles are susceptible.

phrases.he: חָזַר וְעָשָׂה מֵהֶן כֵּלִים, מְקַבְּלִין טֻמְאָה מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא.
phrases.en: After they are broken they become clean. If he again made vessels of them they become susceptible to uncleanness from that point and onward.

phrases.he: הַטַּבְלָא וְהָאִסְקוּטְלָא שֶׁל זְכוּכִית, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: A glass tray or a flat dish is pure.

phrases.he: אִם יֶשׁ לָהֶן לִזְבֵּז, טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: If it has a rim it is susceptible.

phrases.he: שׁוּלֵי קְעָרָה וְשׁוּלֵי אִסְקוּטְלָא שֶׁל זְכוּכִית שֶׁהִתְקִינָן לְתַשְׁמִישׁ, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: The concave bottom of a glass bowl or plate which was adapted for use is pure.

phrases.he: קִרְטְסָן אוֹ שָׁפָן בְּשׁוּפִין, טְמֵאִין
phrases.en: If it was polished or scraped with a file it becomes susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: אַסְפַּקְלַרְיָא, טְהוֹרָה. וְתַמְחוּי שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ אַסְפַּקְלַרְיָא, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: A mirror is pure. A tray that was made into a mirror remains susceptible, but if it was originally made to serve as a mirror it is pure.

phrases.he: וְאִם מִתְּחִלָּה עֲשָׂאוֹ לְשֵׁם אַסְפַּקְלַרְיָא, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A large [glass] spoon that has been placed on a table is susceptible to uncleanness if it can hold anything whatsoever.

phrases.he: תַּרְוָד שֶׁהוּא נוֹתְנוֹ עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן, אִם מְקַבֵּל כָּל שֶׁהוּא, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: But if it cannot do so: Rabbi Akiva says that it is susceptible, And Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri says that it is pure.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַמֵּא, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי מְטַהֵר
כּוֹס שֶׁנִּפְגַּם רֻבּוֹ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A cup the greater part of which is broken off is pure.

phrases.he: נִפְגַּם בּוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ בְּרֻבּוֹ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If it was broken in three places extending over its greater part it is pure.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אִם מְפַזֵּר הוּא אֶת רֹב הַמַּיִם, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: if it lets the greater part of the water leak out it is pure.

phrases.he: נִקַּב, וַעֲשָׂאוֹ בֵּין בְּבַעַץ בֵּין בְּזֶפֶת, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If a hole appeared in it and it was mended with tin or pitch it is pure.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, בְּבַעַץ, טָמֵא, וּבְזֶפֶת, טָהוֹר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: if with tin it is susceptible to uncleanness, but if with pitch it is pure.

phrases.he: צְלוֹחִית קְטַנָּה שֶׁנִּטַּל פִּיהָ, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: A small flask whose neck was removed remains susceptible to uncleanness, But a large one whose neck was removed becomes pure.

phrases.he: וּגְדוֹלָה שֶׁנִּטַּל פִּיהָ, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: [A small flask] of spikenard oil whose neck was removed becomes pure, since it scratches the hand.

phrases.he: שֶׁל פַּלְיָטוֹן שֶׁנִּטַּל פִּיהָ, טְהוֹרָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא סוֹרַחַת אֶת הַיָּד.
phrases.en: Large flagons whose necks were removed remain susceptible to uncleanness, since they are adapted for the use of holding pickled foods.

phrases.he: לְגִינִין גְּדוֹלִים שֶׁנִּטַּל פִּיהֶן, טְמֵאִין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מְתַקְּנָן לִכְבָשִׁין.
phrases.en: A glass funnel is clean.

phrases.he: וְהָאֲפַרְכֵּס שֶׁל זְכוּכִית, טְהוֹרָה.
אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, אַשְׁרַיִךְ כֵּלִים, שֶׁנִּכְנַסְתְּ בְּטֻמְאָה, וְיָצָאת בְּטָהֳרָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose said: Happy are you Kelim; for you began with uncleanness, but you ended with cleanness.

phrases.he: שְׁנַיִם טְמֵאִים בְּמֵת, אֶחָד טָמֵא טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה וְאֶחָד טָמֵא טֻמְאַת עָרֶב.
phrases.en: Two are defiled through a corpse, one being defiled with seven days' defilement and one being defiled with a defilement lasting until the evening.

phrases.he: שְׁלשָׁה טְמֵאִין בְּמֵת, שְׁנַיִם טְמֵאִין טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה וְאֶחָד טָמֵא טֻמְאַת עָרֶב.
phrases.en: Three are defiled through a corpse, two being defiled with seven days’ defilement and one with a defilement lasting until the evening.

phrases.he: אַרְבָּעָה טְמֵאִין בְּמֵת, שְׁלשָׁה טְמֵאִין טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה וְאֶחָד טָמֵא טֻמְאַת עָרֶב. כֵּיצַד שְׁנַיִם.
phrases.en: Four are defiled through a corpse, three being defiled with seven days’ defilement and one with a defilement lasting until the evening.

phrases.he: אָדָם הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּמֵת, טָמֵא טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.en: What [is the case of] two? A person who touches a corpse is defiled with seven days’ defilement and a person who touches him is defiled with a defilement lasting until the evening.

phrases.he: וְאָדָם הַנּוֹגֵע בּוֹ, טָמֵא טֻמְאַת עָרֶב
כֵּיצַד שְׁלשָׁה. כֵּלִים הַנּוֹגְעִים בְּמֵת, וְכֵלִים בַּכֵּלִים, טְמֵאִין טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.en: What [is the case of] three? Vessels touching a corpse and [other] vessels [touching these] vessels are defiled with seven days’ defilement.

phrases.he: הַשְּׁלִישִׁי, בֵּין אָדָם וּבֵין כֵּלִים, טְמֵאִין טֻמְאַת עָרֶב
phrases.en: The third: whether a person or vessels, is defiled with a defilement lasting until the evening.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד אַרְבָּעָה. כֵּלִים נוֹגְעִין בְּמֵת, וְאָדָם בַּכֵּלִים, וְכֵלִים בָּאָדָם, טְמֵאִין טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.en: What is the case of four? Vessels touching a corpse, a person [touching these] vessels, and [other] vessels [touching this] person, are defiled with seven days' defilement.

phrases.he: הָרְבִיעִי, בֵּין אָדָם בֵּין כֵּלִים, טָמֵא טֻמְאַת עָרֶב.
phrases.en: The fourth, whether a person or vessels, is defiled with a defilement [lasting until the] evening.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, יֶשׁ לִי חֲמִישִׁי, הַשַּׁפּוּד הַתָּחוּב בָּאֹהֶל, הָאֹהֶל וְהַשַּׁפּוּד וְאָדָם הַנּוֹגֵעַ בַּשַּׁפּוּד וְכֵלִים בָּאָדָם, טְמֵאִין טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva said: I have a fifth, [if] a peg was fixed in a tent, the tent, the peg, a person touching the peg and vessels [touching] the person are defiled with seven days' defilement.

phrases.he: הַחֲמִישִׁי, בֵּין אָדָם בֵּין כֵּלִים, טָמֵא טֻמְאַת עָרֶב.
phrases.en: The fifth, whether a person or vessels, is defiled with a defilement [lasting until the] evening.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, אֵין הָאֹהֶל מִתְחַשֵּׁב:
phrases.en: They said to him: the tent does not count.

phrases.he: אָדָם וְכֵלִים מִטַּמְּאִין בְּמֵת.
phrases.en: [Both] persons and vessels can be defiled through a corpse.

phrases.he: חֹמֶר בָּאָדָם מִבַּכֵּלִים וְכֵלִים מִבָּאָדָם.
phrases.en: A greater stringency applies to persons than to vessels and to vessels than to persons.

phrases.he: שֶׁהַכֵּלִים שְׁלשָׁה וְהָאָדָם שְׁנָיִם.
phrases.en: For with vessels [there can be] three [series of defilements], whereas with persons [there can be only] two.

phrases.he: חֹמֶר בָּאָדָם, שֶׁכָּל זְמַן שֶׁהוּא בָאֶמְצַע, הֵן אַרְבָּעָה.
phrases.en: A greater stringency applies to persons, for whenever they are in the middle of a [series] there can be four [in the series], whereas when they are not in the middle of a [series] there can be [only] three.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ בָאֶמְצַע, הֵן שְׁלשָׁה
אָדָם וּבְגָדִים מִטַּמְּאִים בְּזָב.
phrases.en: Persons and garments can be defiled by a zav.

phrases.he: חֹמֶר בָּאָדָם מִבַּבְּגָדִים, וּבַבְּגָדִים מִבָּאָדָם.
phrases.en: A greater stringency applies to persons than to garments and a greater stringency applies to garments than to persons.

phrases.he: שֶׁהָאָדָם הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּזָב מְטַמֵּא בְגָדִים, וְאֵין בְּגָדִים הַנּוֹגְעִין בְּזָב מְטַמְּאִין בְּגָדִים.
phrases.en: For a person who touches a zav can defile garments, whereas garments that touch a zav cannot defile [other] garments.

phrases.he: חֹמֶר בַּבְּגָדִים, שֶׁהַבְּגָדִים הַנּוֹשְׂאִין אֶת הַזָּב מְטַמְּאִין אָדָם, וְאֵין אָדָם הַנּוֹשֵׂא אֶת הַזָּב מְטַמֵּא אָדָם
phrases.en: A greater stringency applies to garments, for garments which form the support of a zav can defile persons, whereas a person who forms the support of a zav cannot defile [other] persons.

phrases.he: אָדָם אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא, עַד שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשׁוֹ.
phrases.en: A person does not defile [as a corpse] until he dies.

phrases.he: וַאֲפִלּוּ מְגֻיָּד, וַאֲפִלּוּ גוֹסֵס.
phrases.en: Even he is cut up or even if he is about to die, he [still] makes levirate marriage obligatory and exempts from levirate marriage, he feeds [his mother] terumah and disqualifies [his mother] from eating terumah.

phrases.he: זוֹקֵק לַיִּבּוּם וּפוֹטֵר מִן הַיִּבּוּם, מַאֲכִיל בַּתְּרוּמָה וּפוֹסֵל בַּתְּרוּמָה.
phrases.en: Similarly in the case of cattle or wild animals, they do not defile until they die.

phrases.he: וְכֵן בְּהֵמָה וְחַיָּה אֵינָן מְטַמְּאִין, עַד שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשָׁם.
phrases.en: If their heads have been cut off, even though they are moving convulsively, they are unclean, like a lizard's tail, which moves convulsively.

phrases.he: הֻתְּזוּ רָאשֵׁיהֶם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּפַרְכְּסִים, טְמֵאִים, כְּגוֹן זָנָב שֶׁל לְטָאָה שֶׁהִיא מְפַרְכָּסֶת
הָאֵבָרִין אֵין לָהֶן שִׁעוּר, אֲפִלּוּ פָּחוֹת מִכַּזַּיִת מִן הַמֵּת, וּפָחוֹת מִכַּזַּיִת מִן הַנְּבֵלָה, וּפָחוֹת מִכָּעֲדָשָׁה מִן הַשֶּׁרֶץ, מְטַמְּאִין טֻמְאָתָן:
phrases.en: Whole limbs [of the body] have no [restriction as to] size: even less than an olive-sized portion of a corpse or less than an olive-sized portion of nevelah (carrion), or less than a lentil-sized portion of a sheretz can defile, [each in the manner of] their respective defilements.

phrases.he: מָאתַיִם וְאַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמֹנָה אֵבָרִים בָּאָדָם, שְׁלשִׁים בְּפִסַּת הָרֶגֶל, שִׁשָּׁה בְכָל אֶצְבַּע, עֲשָׂרָה בַקֻּרְסָל, שְׁנַיִם בַּשּׁוֹק, חֲמִשָּׁה בָאַרְכֻּבָּה, אֶחָד בַּיָּרֵךְ, שְׁלשָׁה בַקַּטְלִית, אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה צְלָעוֹת, שְׁלשִׁים בְּפִסַּת הַיָּד, שִׁשָּׁה בְכָל אֶצְבַּע, שְׁנַיִם בַּקָּנֶה, וּשְׁנַיִם בַּמַּרְפֵּק, אֶחָד בַּזְּרוֹעַ, וְאַרְבָּעָה בַכָּתֵף.
phrases.en: There are two hundred and forty-eight limbs in a human body: Thirty in the foot, six for every toe, Ten in the ankle, Two in the shin, Five in the knee, One in the thigh, Three in the hip, Eleven ribs, Thirty in the hand, [that is] six to every finger, Two in the fore-arm, Two in the elbow, One in the upper arm and Four in the shoulder, [For a total of] one hundred and one on the one side [of the body] and one hundred and one on the other.

phrases.he: מֵאָה וְאֶחָד מִזֶּה וּמֵאָה וְאֶחָד מִזֶּה.
phrases.en: Eighteen vertebrae in the spine, Nine in the head, Eight in the neck, Six in the key of the heart, And five around the genitals.

phrases.he: וּשְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה חֻלְיוֹת בַּשִּׁדְרָה, תִּשְׁעָה בָרֹאשׁ, שְׁמֹנָה בַצַּוָּאר, שִׁשָּׁה בַמַּפְתֵּחַ שֶׁל לֵב, וַחֲמִשָּׁה בִנְקָבָיו.
phrases.en: Each one [of these] can defile by contact, carriage or overshadowing.

phrases.he: כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מְטַמֵּא בְמַגָּע וּבְמַשָּׂא וּבְאֹהֶל.
phrases.en: When is this so? When they have upon them the appropriate amount of flesh, But if they do not have the appropriate amount flesh upon them, they can defile by contact and carriage but cannot defile by overshadowing.

phrases.he: אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁיֵּשׁ עֲלֵיהֶן בָּשָׂר כָּרָאוּי.
אֲבָל אִם אֵין עֲלֵיהֶן בָּשָׂר כָּרָאוּי, מְטַמְּאִין בְּמַגָּע וּבְמַשָּׂא, וְאֵין מְטַמְּאִין בְּאֹהֶל

אֵלּוּ מְטַמְּאִין בְּאֹהֶל. הַמֵּת, וְכַזַּיִת מִן הַמֵּת, וְכַזַּיִת נֶצֶל, וּמְלֹא תַרְוָד רָקָב, הַשִּׁדְרָה, וְהַגֻּלְגֹּלֶת, אֵבָר מִן הַמֵּת וְאֵבָר מִן הַחַי שֶׁיֵּשׁ עֲלֵיהֶן בָּשָׂר כָּרָאוּי, רֹבַע עֲצָמוֹת מֵרֹב הַבִּנְיָן אוֹ מֵרֹב הַמִּנְיָן.
phrases.en: These things defile by overshadowing: a corpse, an olive-sized [portion of flesh] of a corpse, an olive-sized [portion] of nezel, a ladleful of corpse-mold, the spine or the skull, [a] full limb of a corpse, or [a full] limb [severed] from a living person with the appropriate amount of flesh, a quarter [of a kav] of bones from the structural majority or numerical majority, and the structural majority or numerical majority [of the bones] of a corpse even though they do not amount to a quarter [of a kab]; [all these] are unclean.

phrases.he: וְרֹב בִּנְיָנוֹ וְרֹב מִנְיָנוֹ שֶׁל מֵת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם רֹבַע, טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: How many [bones] form the numerical majority? One hundred and twenty-five.

phrases.he: כַּמָּה הוּא רֹב מִנְיָנוֹ, מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה
רְבִיעִית דָּם, וּרְבִיעִית דַּם תְּבוּסָה מִמֵּת אֶחָד.
phrases.en: [The following likewise defile:]A quarter [of a log] of blood, A quarter [of a log] of mixed blood from one corpse.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, מִשְּׁנֵי מֵתִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: [even] from two corpses.

phrases.he: דַּם קָטָן שֶׁיָּצָא כֻלּוֹ,
רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, כָּל שֶׁהוּא.
phrases.en: [With regard to] the blood of a child that has completely flowed forth: Rabbi Akiva says: [it defiles] in even the smallest quantity, But the sages say: [there must be] a quarter [of a log].

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, רְבִיעִית. כַּזַּיִת רִמָּה, בֵּין חַיָּה בֵּין מֵתָה, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְטַמֵּא כִבְשָׂרוֹ, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִים. אֵפֶר שְׂרוּפִים,
phrases.en: [With regard to] an olive-sized [portion] of [corpse] worms whether alive or dead: Rabbi Eliezer declares [it] unclean, like the flesh, But the sages declare [it] clean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, שִׁעוּרוֹ בְרֹבַע, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין.
phrases.en: [With regard to] the ashes of burnt persons: Rabbi Eliezer says: the [minimum] quantity [for defilement is] a quarter [of a kav].

phrases.he: מְלֹא תַרְוָד וְעוֹד עֲפַר קְבָרוֹת, טָמֵא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַהֵר.
phrases.en: But the sages declare [them to be] clean. A ladleful and [a little] more of grave-dust is unclean. Rabbi Shimon declares [it to be] clean.

phrases.he: מְלֹא תַרְוָד רָקָב שֶׁגְּבָלוֹ בְמַיִם, אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר לְטֻמְאָה
phrases.en: A ladleful of corpse-mold mixed with water is not [regarded as] joined [into one mass] for [the purposes of] defilement.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ מְטַמְּאִין בְּמַגָּע וּבְמַשָּׂא וְאֵינָן מְטַמְּאִין בְּאֹהֶל.
phrases.en: The following defile by contact and carriage but not by overshadowing: A bone of barleycorn size, Earth from a foreign country, A bet peras, A limb of a corpse, or a limb [severed] from a living person which has no longer its appropriate flesh, A spine or a skull which is deficient.

phrases.he: עֶצֶם כַּשְּׂעֹרָה, וְאֶרֶץ הָעַמִּים, וּבֵית הַפְּרָס, אֵבָר מִן הַמֵּת וְאֵבָר מִן הַחַי שֶׁאֵין עֲלֵיהֶן בָּשָׂר כָּרָאוּי, הַשִּׁדְרָה וְהַגֻּלְגֹּלֶת שֶׁחָסָרוּ.
כַּמָּה הוּא חֶסְרוֹן בַּשִּׁדְרָה,
בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, שְׁתֵּי חֻלְיוֹת.
phrases.en: How much is [considered] a deficiency in the spine? Bet Shammai say: two vertebrae, But Bet Hillel say: even one vertebra.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, אֲפִלּוּ חֻלְיָה אֶחָת. וּבַגֻּלְגֹּלֶת,
phrases.en: And in the skull? Bet Shammai say: [the size of a] hole [made] by a drill, But Bet Hillel say: as much as would be taken from a living person and he would die.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, כִּמְלֹא מַקְדֵּחַ.
phrases.en: Of what drill did they speak? Of the small one [used] by physicians, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּנָּטֵל מִן הַחַי וְיָמוּת.
phrases.en: But the sages say: of the large one in the Temple-chamber.

phrases.he: בְּאֵיזֶה מַקְדֵּחַ אָמְרוּ, בַּקָּטָן שֶׁל רוֹפְאִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בַּגָּדוֹל שֶׁל לִשְׁכָּה:
הַגּוֹלֵל וְהַדּוֹפֵק מְטַמְּאִין בְּמַגָּע וּבְאֹהֶל, וְאֵינָן מְטַמְּאִין בְּמַשָּׂא.
phrases.en: The covering stone and the buttressing stone [of a grave] defile by contact and overshadowing but not by carriage.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, מְטַמְּאִין בְּמַשָּׂא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: they do defile by carriage.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, אִם יֵשׁ תַּחְתֵּיהֶן עֲפַר קְבָרוֹת, מְטַמְּאִין בְּמַשָּׂא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua says: if there is grave dust beneath them, they defile by carriage, but if not they do not defile by carriage.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, אֵינָן מְטַמְּאִין בְּמַשָּׂא.
phrases.en: What is the buttressing stone? That upon which the covering stone is supported.

phrases.he: אֵיזֶהוּ הַדּוֹפֵק, אֶת שֶׁהַגּוֹלֵל נִשְׁעָן עָלָיו.
phrases.en: But the stone that serves as buttress to the buttressing stone is clean.

phrases.he: אֲבָל דּוֹפֵק דּוֹפְקִין, טָהוֹר
אֵלּוּ שֶׁאִם חָסְרוּ טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: These are clean if they are deficient:An olive-sized [portion] of a corpse; An olive-sized [portion] of nezel, A ladleful of corpse-mold, A quarter [of a log] of blood, A bone of the size of a barley-corn, And a limb [severed] from a living person, the bone of which [limb] is deficient.

phrases.he: כַּזַּיִת מִן הַמֵּת, וְכַזַּיִת נֶצֶל, וּמְלֹא תַרְוָד רָקָב, וּרְבִיעִית דָּם, וְעֶצֶם כַּשְּׂעֹרָה, וְאֵבָר מִן הַחַי שֶׁחָסַר עַצְמוֹ

הַשִּׁדְרָה וְהַגֻּלְגֹּלֶת מִשְּׁנֵי מֵתִים, וּרְבִיעִית דָּם מִשְּׁנֵי מֵתִים, וְרֹבַע עֲצָמוֹת מִשְּׁנֵי מֵתִים, וְאֵבָר מִן הַמֵּת מִשְּׁנֵי מֵתִים, וְאֵבָר מִן הַחַי מִשְּׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַמֵּא, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין:
phrases.en: A backbone or a skull [made up from the bones] of two corpses, A quarter [of a log] of blood from two corpses, A quarter [of a kav] of bones from two corpses, A limb of a corpse from two corpses, And a limb [severed] from a living person, [such a limb being made up] from two persons, Rabbi Akiva declares [the all] unclean But the sages declare them clean.

phrases.he: עֶצֶם כַּשְּׂעֹרָה שֶׁנֶּחֱלַק לִשְׁנַיִם, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַמֵּא, וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי מְטַהֵר.
phrases.en: A bone the size of a barley-corn that is divided into two: Rabbi Akiva declares it unclean But Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri declares it clean.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי, לֹא אָמְרוּ עֲצָמוֹת כַּשְּׂעֹרָה, אֶלָּא עֶצֶם כַּשְּׂעֹרָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri says: they did not say 'bones’ the size of a barley-corn, but ‘bone’ the size of a barley-corn.

phrases.he: רֹבַע עֲצָמוֹת שֶׁנִּדַּקְדְּקוּ וְאֵין בְּכָל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד עֶצֶם כַּשְּׂעֹרָה, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַהֵר, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַמְּאִין.
phrases.en: A quarter [of a kav] of bones crushed fine, and there is not a single [bone] the size of a barley-corn: Rabbi Shimon declares it clean But the sages unclean.

phrases.he: אֵבָר מִן הַחַי שֶׁנֶּחֱלַק לִשְׁנַיִם, טָהוֹר. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.en: A limb [severed] from a living person which has been divided into two is clean.

phrases.he: וּמוֹדֶה שֶׁאִם נִטַּל חֲצָאִים שֶׁהוּא טָהוֹר
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose declares [it] unclean; But he agrees that if it is taken from a living person by halves it is clean.

phrases.he: כָּל הַמְטַמְּאִין בְּאֹהֶל שֶׁנֶּחְלְקוּ וְהִכְנִיסָן לְתוֹךְ הַבַּיִת, רַבִּי דוֹסָא בֶן הַרְכִּינַס מְטַהֵר, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַמְּאִים. כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: All objects that defile by overshadowing which were divided and then brought into a house: Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas declares clean. But the sages declare [it] unclean.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּכִשְׁנֵי חֲצָיֵי זֵיתִים מִן הַנְּבֵלָה אוֹ נוֹשְׂאָן.
phrases.en: What is the case? One who touches two pieces of nevelah, each the size of half an olive, or carries them, Or, in the case of a corpse, if he touches a piece the size of half an olive and overshadows [another piece] the size of half an olive, Or if he touches [a piece] the size of half an olive and [another piece] the size of half an olive overshadows him, Or if he overshadows two [pieces, each] the size of half an olive, Or if he overshadows [a piece] the size of half an olive and [another piece] the size of half an olive overshadows him: Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas declares him clean, And the sages declare him unclean.

phrases.he: וּבַמֵּת, הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּכַחֲצִי זַיִת וּמַאֲהִיל עַל כַּחֲצִי זַיִת, אוֹ נוֹגֵע בְּכַחֲצִי זַיִת וְכַחֲצִי זַיִת מַאֲהִיל עָלָיו, מַאֲהִיל עַל כִּשְׁנֵי חֲצָיֵי זֵיתִים, מַאֲהִיל עַל כַּחֲצִי זַיִת וְכַחֲצִי זַיִת מַאֲהִיל עָלָיו, רַבִּי דוֹסָא בֶן הַרְכִּינַס מְטַהֵר, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַמְּאִין.
phrases.en: But if he touches [a piece] the size of half an olive and another object overshadows him and [another piece] the size of half an olive, Or if he overshadows [a piece] the size of half an olive and another object overshadows him and [another piece] the size of half an olive, he is clean.

phrases.he: אֲבָל הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּכַחֲצִי זַיִת וְדָבָר אַחֵר מַאֲהִיל עָלָיו וְעַל כַּחֲצִי זַיִת, אוֹ מַאֲהִיל עַל כַּחֲצִי זַיִת וְדָבָר אַחֵר מַאֲהִיל עָלָיו וְעַל כַּחֲצִי זַיִת, טָהוֹר.
אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר, אַף בָּזֶה רַבִּי דוֹסָא בֶן הַרְכִּינַס מְטַהֵר, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַמְּאִין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: Even here Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas declares him clean and the sages declare him unclean.

phrases.he: הַכֹּל טָמֵא, חוּץ מִן הַמַּגָּע עִם הַמַּשָּׂא, וְהַמַּשָּׂא עִם הָאֹהֶל.
phrases.en: Every [case] is unclean except [a case of] contact [combined] with carriage or of carriage [combined] with overshadowing.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כֹּל שֶׁהוּא מִשֵּׁם אֶחָד, טָמֵא. מִשְּׁנֵי שֵׁמוֹת, טָהוֹר
phrases.en: This is the general principle: every object [whose defilement] proceeds from one cause is unclean, from two causes is clean.

phrases.he: מְלֹא תַרְוָד רָקָב שֶׁנִּתְפַּזֵּר בְּתוֹךְ הַבַּיִת, הַבַּיִת טָמֵא. וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַהֵר.
phrases.en: If a ladleful of corpse-mold was scattered about in a house, the house is unclean But Rabbi Shimon declares it clean.

phrases.he: רְבִיעִית דָּם שֶׁנִּבְלְעָה בְתוֹךְ הַבַּיִת, הַבַּיִת טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If a quarter [of a log] of blood was absorbed in [the ground] of a house, the house is clean.

phrases.he: נִבְלְעָה בִכְסוּת, אִם מִתְכַּבֶּסֶת וְיוֹצֵא מִמֶּנָּה רְבִיעִית דָּם, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: If it was absorbed by a garment: if the garment is washed and a quarter [of a log] of blood emerges from it, it is unclean, if not, it is clean, since anything absorbed that cannot emerge is clean.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, טְהוֹרָה, שֶׁכֹּל הַבָּלוּעַ שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לָצֵאת, טָהוֹר
נִשְׁפַּךְ בָּאֲוִיר, אִם הָיָה מְקוֹמוֹ קְטַפְרֵס וְהֶאֱהִיל עַל מִקְצָתוֹ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: [Blood] which was poured out in the air: If the place [where it fell] was an incline and [a person or vessel] overshadowed part of it, he [remains] clean.

phrases.he: הָיָה אַשְׁבֹּרֶן, אוֹ שֶׁקָּרַשׁ, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If it was a cavity, or if the blood congealed, he [becomes] unclean.

phrases.he: נִשְׁפַּךְ עַל הָאַסְקֻפָּה וְהִיא קְטַפְרֵס, בֵּין מִבִּפְנִים בֵּין מִבַּחוּץ, וְהַבַּיִת מַאֲהִיל עָלָיו, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If it was poured out on a threshold: If it inclined either inwards or outwards and the house overshadowed it [that which is in the house] is clean.

phrases.he: הָיָה אַשְׁבֹּרֶן אוֹ שֶׁקָּרַשׁ, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If there was a cavity, or if it congealed, [that which is in the house becomes] unclean.

phrases.he: כֹּל שֶׁבַּמֵּת, טָמֵא, חוּץ מִן הַשִּׁנַּיִם וְהַשֵּׂעָר וְהַצִּפֹּרֶן.
phrases.en: Every part of a corpse is unclean except the teeth, hair and nails; But when they are joined [to the corpse], they are all unclean.

phrases.he: וּבִשְׁעַת חִבּוּרוֹ, הַכֹּל טָמֵא
כֵּיצַד. הַמֵּת מִבַּחוּץ וּשְׂעָרוֹ בִפְנִים, הַבַּיִת טָמֵא.
phrases.en: How so? If the corpse was outside and its hair inside, the house is unclean.

phrases.he: עֶצֶם שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו כַּזַּיִת בָּשָׂר, הִכְנִיס מִקְצָתוֹ מִבִּפְנִים וְהַבַּיִת מַאֲהִיל עָלָיו, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: [With regard to] a bone which had upon it an olive-sized portion of flesh, if one brought part of it within so that the house was overshadowing it, [the house] is unclean.

phrases.he: שְׁנֵי עֲצָמוֹת וַעֲלֵיהֶן כִּשְׁנֵי חֲצָאֵי זֵיתִים בָּשָׂר, הִכְנִיס מִקְצָתָם מִבִּפְנִים וְהַבַּיִת מַאֲהִיל עֲלֵיהֶם, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: [With regard to] two bones which had upon them two pieces of flesh, [each] the size of half an olive, if one brought part of them within so that the house was overshadowing them, [the house] is unclean.

phrases.he: הָיוּ תְחוּבִים בִּידֵי אָדָם, טָהוֹר, שֶׁאֵין חִבּוּרֵי אָדָם חִבּוּר
phrases.en: But if [the pieces of flesh] were set into [the bone] by a person, the house is clean since connections created by human agency are not [regarded as] connections.

phrases.he: אֵיזֶהוּ דַם תְּבוּסָה. הַמֵּת שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁמִינִית בְּחַיָּיו וּשְׁמִינִית בְּמוֹתוֹ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.en: What is ‘mixed blood? The blood of a corpse of which an eighth [of a log] came out during his lifetime and an eighth after death, the words of Rabbi Akiva.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, רְבִיעִית בְּחַיָּיו וּרְבִיעִית בְּמוֹתוֹ, נִטַּל מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה רְבִיעִית.
phrases.en: Rabbi Ishmael says: a quarter [of a log] during his lifetime and a quarter after death. [If] a quarter [of a log] is taken from both of these: Rabbi Elazar bar Judah says: both of these are as water.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, זֶה וָזֶה כַמָּיִם. אֵיזֶהוּ דַם תְּבוּסָה.
phrases.en: What then is ‘mixed blood’? It is that of a crucified person whose blood is streaming forth and under whom is found a quarter [of a log] of blood it is unclean.

phrases.he: צָלוּב שֶׁדָּמוֹ שׁוֹתֵת וְנִמְצָא תַחְתָּיו רְבִיעִית דָּם, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: However a corpse whose blood drips forth and under whom is found a quarter [of a log] of blood, [the blood] is clean.

phrases.he: אֲבָל הַמֵּת שֶׁדָּמוֹ מְנַטֵּף וְנִמְצָא תַחְתָּיו רְבִיעִית דָּם, טָהוֹר.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, לֹא כִי, אֶלָּא הַשּׁוֹתֵת, טָהוֹר. וְהַמְנַטֵּף, טָמֵא:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: not so, but that which streams forth is clean and that which drips forth is unclean.

phrases.he: כַּזַּיִת מִן הַמֵּת, פִּתְחוֹ בְטֶפַח, וְהַמֵּת, פִּתְחוֹ בְאַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים, לְהַצִּיל הַטֻּמְאָה עַל הַפְּתָחִים.
phrases.en: For an olive-sized portion of a corpse, an opening [in the room in which it is found] of one handbreadth [square], and for a [whole] corpse, an opening of four handbreadths [square, is enough] to prevent the uncleanness from [spreading to the other] openings; But for allowing the uncleanness to go out, an opening of one handbreadth [square is enough].

phrases.he: אֲבָל לְהוֹצִיא הַטֻּמְאָה, בְּפוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח. גָּדוֹל מִכַּזַּיִת, כַּמֵּת.
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, הַשִּׁדְרָה וְהַגֻּלְגֹּלֶת, כַּמֵּת:
phrases.en: [A portion] greater than the size of an olive is as a [whole] corpse. Rabbi Yose says: [only] the spine and the skull are as a [whole] corpse.

phrases.he: טֶפַח עַל טֶפַח עַל רוּם טֶפַח, מְרֻבָּע, מֵבִיא אֶת הַטֻּמְאָה, וְחוֹצֵץ בִּפְנֵי הַטֻּמְאָה. כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: [An object] one handbreadth square and one handbreadth high conveys uncleanness and blocks uncleanness.

phrases.he: בִּיב שֶׁהוּא קָמוּר תַּחַת הַבַּיִת, יֶשׁ בּוֹ פוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח וְיֵשׁ בִּיצִיאָתוֹ פּוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח, טֻמְאָה בְתוֹכוֹ, הַבַּיִת טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: How does it [block uncleanness]? In the case of a covered drain beneath a house, if it has a space a handbreadth wide and its outlet was a handbreadth wide, and there is uncleanness inside it, the house remains clean; And when there is uncleanness in the house, that which is within [the drain] remains clean, for the manner of the uncleanness is to go out and not to go in.

phrases.he: טֻמְאָה בַבַּיִת, מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ טָהוֹר, שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ הַטֻּמְאָה לָצֵאת וְאֵין דַּרְכָּהּ לְהִכָּנֵס.
phrases.en: If it had a space one handbreadth wide but its outlet was not one handbreadth wide, when there is uncleanness in it, the house becomes unclean; But when there is uncleanness in the house, that which is within it remains clean, for the manner of the uncleanness is to go out and not to go in.

phrases.he: יֶשׁ בּוֹ פוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח וְאֵין בִּיצִיאָתוֹ פוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח, הַטֻּמְאָה בְתוֹכוֹ, הַבַּיִת טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If it did not have a space one handbreadth wide and its outlet was not one handbreadth wide, when there is uncleanness within it, the house becomes unclean; And when there is uncleanness in the house, it [also] becomes unclean.

phrases.he: טֻמְאָה בַבַּיִת, מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ טָהוֹר, שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ הַטֻּמְאָה לָצֵאת וְאֵין דַּרְכָּהּ לְהִכָּנֵס.
phrases.en: It makes no difference if the cavity was carved out by water or by a sheretz or if it had been eaten out by salt.

phrases.he: אֵין בּוֹ פוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח וְאֵין בִּיצִיאָתוֹ פוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח, טֻמְאָה בְתוֹכוֹ, הַבַּיִת טָמֵא.
phrases.en: And similarly [if it is in] a row of stones or a pile of beams.

phrases.he: טֻמְאָה בַבַּיִת, מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ טָמֵא.
אֶחָד חוֹר שֶׁחֲרָרוּהוּ מַיִם אוֹ שְׁרָצִים, אוֹ שֶׁאֲכָלַתּוּ מַלַּחַת, וְכֵן מִרְבָּךְ שֶׁל אֲבָנִים, וְכֵן סְוָאר שֶׁל קוֹרוֹת.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כָּל אֹהֶל שֶׁאֵינוֹ עָשׂוּי בִּידֵי אָדָם, אֵינוֹ אֹהֶל. וּמוֹדֶה בִשְׁקִיפִים וּבִסְלָעִים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: any "tent" not made by a person is not considered a tent’. But he agrees that crevices and crags [can be considered as ‘tents’].

phrases.he: מִגְדָּל שֶׁהוּא עוֹמֵד בָּאֲוִיר, טֻמְאָה בְתוֹכוֹ, כֵּלִים שֶׁבְּעָבְיוֹ טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: A cupboard standing in the open air: If there is uncleanness within it, vessels in the [niches in the] thickness [of its walls] remain clean.

phrases.he: טֻמְאָה בְעָבְיוֹ, כֵּלִים שֶׁבְּתוֹכוֹ טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: If there is uncleanness in [the niches in] its thickness, vessels inside [the cupboard] remain clean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: half and half.

phrases.he: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בְּתוֹךְ הַבַּיִת, טֻמְאָה בְתוֹכוֹ, הַבַּיִת טָמֵא.
phrases.en: When it is standing inside a house: If there is uncleanness inside [the cupboard], the house is unclean; If there is uncleanness in the house that which is within [the cupboard] remains clean, for the manner of uncleanness is to go out and not to go in.

phrases.he: טֻמְאָה בַבַּיִת, מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ טָהוֹר, שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ הַטֻּמְאָה לָצֵאת וְאֵין דַּרְכָּהּ לְהִכָּנֵס.
phrases.en: Vessels which are between [the cupboard] and the ground, or between it and the wall, or between it and the roof-beams: If there is a space of one cubic handbreadth there, they become unclean.

phrases.he: כֵּלִים שֶׁבֵּינוֹ לְבֵין הָאָרֶץ, שֶׁבֵּינוֹ לְבֵין הַכֹּתֶל, שֶׁבֵּינוֹ לְבֵין הַקּוֹרוֹת, אִם יֶשׁ שָׁם פּוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח, טְמֵאִין. וְאִם לָאו, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: If not they remain clean.

phrases.he: טֻמְאָה שָׁם, הַבַּיִת טָמֵא
phrases.en: If there is uncleanness there, the house becomes unclean.

phrases.he: תֵּבַת הַמִּגְדָּל, יֶשׁ בָּהּ פּוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח וְאֵין בִּיצִיאָתָהּ פּוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח, טֻמְאָה בְתוֹכָהּ, הַבַּיִת טָמֵא.
phrases.en: [With regard to] a drawer of the cupboard, which is one cubic handbreadth, but whose outlet is not a square handbreadth, if there is uncleanness inside it, the house becomes unclean; But if there is uncleanness in the house, that which is within [the drawer] remains clean, for the manner of uncleanness is to go out and not to go in.

phrases.he: טֻמְאָה בַבַּיִת, מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכָהּ טָהוֹר, שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ הַטֻּמְאָה לָצֵאת וְאֵין דַּרְכָּהּ לְהִכָּנֵס.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose declares [the house] clean, since he can remove [the uncleanness] by halves or burn it where it stands.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְטַהֵר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא יָכוֹל לְהוֹצִיאָהּ לַחֲצָאִים אוֹ לְשָׂרְפָהּ בִּמְקוֹמָהּ
הָיָה עוֹמֵד בְּתוֹךְ הַפֶּתַח וְנִפְתַּח לַחוּץ, טֻמְאָה בְתוֹכוֹ, הַבַּיִת טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: [In the case where] the cupboard is standing in the doorway and is opened outward, if there is uncleanness inside it, the house remains clean.

phrases.he: טֻמְאָה בַבַּיִת, מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ טָמֵא, שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ הַטֻּמְאָה לָצֵאת וְאֵין דַּרְכָּהּ לְהִכָּנֵס.
phrases.en: If there is uncleanness in the house, that which is within [the cupboard] becomes unclean, for the manner of uncleanness is to go out and not to go in.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה מוּכְנִי שֶׁלּוֹ מְשׁוּכָה לַאֲחוֹרָיו שָׁלשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת, טֻמְאָה שָׁם כְּנֶגֶד הַקּוֹרוֹת, הַבַּיִת טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If its wheeled base protruded three fingerbreadths behind it and there was uncleanness inside it under the roof-beams, the house remains clean.

phrases.he: בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בִּזְמַן שֶׁיֶּשׁ שָׁם פּוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח, וְאֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה, וְהַמִּגְדָּל בָּא בְמִדָּה
phrases.en: When does this ruling apply? When there is a space of one cubic handbreadth, when it is not easily detachable, and when the cupboard is of the stipulated size.

phrases.he: תַּנּוּר שֶׁהוּא עוֹמֵד בְּתוֹךְ הַבַּיִת וְעֵינוֹ קְמוּרָה לַחוּץ, וְהֶאֱהִילוּ עָלָיו קוֹבְרֵי הַמֵּת,
phrases.en: [With regard to] an oven which stood in a house, with its outlet curved to the outside [of the house], and those burying a corpse overshadowed it: Bet Shammai says: all becomes unclean.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, הַכֹּל טָמֵא.
phrases.en: Bet Hillel says: the oven becomes unclean, but the house remains clean.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, הַתַּנּוּר טָמֵא וְהַבַּיִת טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: even the oven remains clean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אַף הַתַּנּוּר טָהוֹר:
אֲרֻבָּה שֶׁבֵּין הַבַּיִת לָעֲלִיָּה, וּקְדֵרָה נְתוּנָה עָלֶיהָ וּנְקוּבָה בְכוֹנֵס מַשְׁקֶה,
phrases.en: [With regard to] a hatch between the house and the upper story, if there was a pot placed over it and it was perforated [by a hole of sufficient size] to admit liquid: Bet Shammai says: all becomes unclean.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, הַכֹּל טָמֵא.
phrases.en: Bet Hillel says: the pot becomes unclean but the upper story remains clean.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, הַקְּדֵרָה טְמֵאָה, וַעֲלִיָּה טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: all remains clean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אַף הַקְּדֵרָה טְהוֹרָה:
הָיְתָה שְׁלֵמָה,
phrases.en: If [the pot] was whole:Bet Hillel says: it protects all [from uncleanness].

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מַצֶּלֶת עַל הַכֹּל.
phrases.en: vessel of earthenware can protect everything [in it from contracting impurity], according to Beth Hillel. Bet Shammai says: it protects only food, drink and earthenware vessels.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אֵינָהּ מַצֶּלֶת אֶלָּא עַל הָאֳכָלִים וְעַל הַמַּשְׁקִים וְעַל כְּלֵי חָרֶס.
phrases.en: ut Beth Shammai says: “It protects only food and liquids and [other] vessels of earthenware.” Bet Hillel changed their opinion and taught as Bet Shammai.Beth Hillel said to them: “Why?” Beth Shammai said to them: “Because it is [itself] impure with respect to an ignoramus, and no impure vessel can screen [against impurity].

phrases.he: חָזְרוּ בֵית הִלֵּל לְהוֹרוֹת כְּדִבְרֵי בֵית שַׁמָּאי
phrases.en: Beth Hillel said to them: “And did you not pronounce pure the food and liquids inside it?” Beth Shammai said to them: “When we pronounced pure the food and liquids inside it, we pronounced them pure for him [the ignoramus] only, but when you pronounced the vessel pure you pronounced it pure for yourself and for him.” Then Beth Hillel changed their mind and taught according to the opinion of Beth Shammai.

phrases.he: לָגִין שֶׁהוּא מָלֵא מַשְׁקִין טְהוֹרִין, הַלָּגִין טָמֵא טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה, וְהַמַּשְׁקִין טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: [With regard to] a flagon that is full of pure liquid, the flagon is defiled with seven days' impurity but the liquid remains clean.

phrases.he: וְאִם פִּנָּן בִּכְלִי אַחֵר, טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: But if one poured it out into another vessel, it becomes unclean.

phrases.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהִיא לָשָׁה בָעֲרֵבָה, הָאִשָּׁה וְהָעֲרֵבָה טְמֵאִים טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה, וְהַבָּצֵק טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If a woman was kneading [in the upper story] at a trough, the woman and the trough become unclean with seven days impurity, but the dough remains clean But if one turned it out into another vessel, it becomes unclean.

phrases.he: וְאִם פִּנַּתּוּ לִכְלִי אַחֵר, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: Bet Hillel changed their opinion and taught as Bet Shammai.

phrases.he: חָזְרוּ בֵית הִלֵּל לְהוֹרוֹת כְּדִבְרֵי בֵית שַׁמָּאי
הָיוּ כְלֵי גְלָלִים, כְּלֵי אֲבָנִים, כְּלֵי אֲדָמָה, הַכֹּל טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If [lying over the hatch] there were vessels made of dung, vessels of stone, or vessels of [unbaked] earth, everything [in the upper story] remains clean.

phrases.he: הָיָה כְלִי טָהוֹר לַקֹּדֶשׁ וְלַחַטָּאת, הַכֹּל טָהוֹר, שֶׁהַכֹּל נֶאֱמָנִין עַל הַחַטָּאת, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַכֵּלִים טְהוֹרִין וּכְלֵי חֶרֶס טְהוֹרִין וּמַצִּילִין עִם דָּפְנוֹת אֹהָלִים
phrases.en: If it was a vessel known to be clean for holy things or for [the water of] purification, everything remains clean, since everyone is trusted with [regard to matters of] purification. For clean vessels and earthenware vessels that are [known to be] clean protect with the walls of ‘tents'.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד. הַבּוֹר וְהַדּוּת שֶׁבַּבַּיִת, וּכְפִישָׁה נְתוּנָה עָלָיו, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: How so? If there was a cistern or a cellar in a house and a large basket was placed over it, [the contents of the cistern or cellar] remain clean.

phrases.he: אִם הָיְתָה בְאֵר חֲלָקָה, אוֹ כַוֶּרֶת פְּחוּתָה, וּכְפִישָׁה נְתוּנָה עָלֶיהָ, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: But if it was a well [with its upper edge] level [with the ground] or a deficient beehive upon which the basket was placed, [the contents] become unclean.

phrases.he: אִם הָיָה נֶסֶר חָלָק, אוֹ סְרִידָה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ גַּפַּיִם, טָהוֹר, שֶׁאֵין הַכֵּלִים מַצִּילִים עִם דָּפְנוֹת אֹהָלִים עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא לָהֶן דְּפָנוֹת.
phrases.en: If it was a smooth board or netting without rims, [the contents] remain clean. For vessels cannot protect along with walls of an ohel unless they themselves have walls.

phrases.he: וְכַמָּה תְהֵא הַדֹּפֶן, טֶפַח.
phrases.en: How much must the wall be? A handbreadth.

phrases.he: הָיָה לָהּ חֲצִי טֶפַח מִכָּאן וַחֲצִי טֶפַח מִכָּאן, אֵינָהּ דֹּפֶן, עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא לָהּ טֶפַח מִמָּקוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.en: If there was half a handbreadth on one side and half a handbreadth on the other, it is not [considered] a wall, as there must be a whole handbreadth on one object.

phrases.he: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמַּצִּילִין מִבִּפְנִים, כָּךְ מַצִּילִין מִבַּחוּץ.
phrases.en: Just as they protect inside so they protect outside.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד, כְּפִישָׁה שֶׁהִיא נְתוּנָה עַל הַיְתֵדוֹת מִבַּחוּץ, טֻמְאָה תַחְתֶּיהָ, כֵּלִים שֶׁבַּכְּפִישָׁה טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: How so? In the case of a large basket supported on pegs on the outside [of an ohel], If there was uncleanness beneath it, vessels in the basket remain clean.

phrases.he: אִם הָיָה כֹתֶל חָצֵר אוֹ כֹתֶל גִּנָּה, אֵינוֹ מַצִּיל.
phrases.en: But if it was [next to] the wall of a courtyard or of a garden, it does not protect.

phrases.he: קוֹרָה שֶׁהָיְתָה נְתוּנָה מִכֹּתֶל לְכֹתֶל וּקְדֵרָה תְלוּיָה בָהּ, טֻמְאָה תַחְתֶּיהָ, כֵּלִים שֶׁבַּקְּדֵרָה, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַהֵר, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַמְּאִין
phrases.en: [In the case of] a beam placed across from one wall to an other, with a pot hanging from it, if there was uncleanness beneath it, Rabbi Akiva declares the vessels inside it to be clean, But the sages declare them unclean.

phrases.he: אָדָם וְכֵלִים נַעֲשִׂין אֹהָלִין לְטַמֵּא, אֲבָל לֹא לְטַהֵר. כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: Both persons and vessels can form ‘tents’ to bring uncleanness, but not to [protect objects so that they] remain clean.

phrases.he: אַרְבָּעָה נוֹשְׂאִין אֶת הַנִּדְבָּךְ, טֻמְאָה תַחְתָּיו, כֵּלִים שֶׁעַל גַּבָּיו טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: How so? There are four people carrying a chest: If there is uncleanness beneath it, vessels upon it become unclean.

phrases.he: טֻמְאָה עַל גַּבָּיו, כֵּלִים שֶׁתַּחְתָּיו טְמֵאִים. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְטַהֵר.
phrases.en: If there is uncleanness upon it, vessels beneath it become unclean. Rabbi Eliezer declares them clean.

phrases.he: נָתוּן עַל אַרְבָּעָה כֵלִים, אֲפִלּוּ כְלֵי גְלָלִים, כְּלֵי אֲבָנִים, כְּלֵי אֲדָמָה, טֻמְאָה תַחְתָּיו, כֵּלִים שֶׁעַל גַּבָּיו טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: [If the chest] is placed upon four vessels, even if they are vessels made of dung, vessels of stone, or vessels of [unbaked] earth, If there is uncleanness beneath [the chest], vessels upon it become unclean.

phrases.he: טֻמְאָה עַל גַּבָּיו, כֵּלִים שֶׁתַּחְתָּיו טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: If there is uncleanness beneath it, vessels upon it become unclean.

phrases.he: נָתוּן עַל אַרְבָּעָה אֲבָנִים, אוֹ עַל דָּבָר שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ רוּחַ חַיִּים, טֻמְאָה תַחְתָּיו, כֵּלִים שֶׁעַל גַּבָּיו טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: [If the chest] is placed on four stones or on any living creature, If there is uncleanness beneath it, vessels upon it remain clean.

phrases.he: טֻמְאָה עַל גַּבָּיו, כֵּלִים שֶׁתַּחְתָּיו טְהוֹרִין
phrases.en: If there is uncleanness upon it vessels beneath it remain clean.

phrases.he: קוֹבְרֵי הַמֵּת שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹבְרִים בְּאַכְסַדְרָה, וְהֵגִיף אַחַד מֵהֶן אֶת הַדֶּלֶת וּסְמָכוֹ בַמַּפְתֵּחַ, אִם יָכוֹל הַדֶּלֶת לַעֲמֹד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, טָהוֹר. וְאִם לָאו, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If corpse-bearers were passing along a portico and one of them shut a door and locked it with a key, If the door can remain in its position on its own,[the contents of the house] remain clean, But if not, they become unclean.

phrases.he: וְכֵן חָבִית שֶׁל גְּרוֹגָרוֹת אוֹ קֻפָּה שֶׁל תֶּבֶן שֶׁהֵן נְתוּנוֹת בְּחַלּוֹן, אִם יְכוֹלִין הַגְּרוֹגָרוֹת וְהַתֶּבֶן לַעֲמֹד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן, טְהוֹרִין. וְאִם לָאו, טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: Similarly [in the case of] a barrel of dried figs or a basket of straw placed in a window, If the dried figs or the straw can remain in their position on their own, [the contents of the room] remain clean, But if not they become unclean.

phrases.he: בַּיִת שֶׁחֲצָצוֹ בְקַנְקַנִּים וְטָח בְּטִיחַ, אִם יָכוֹל הַטִּיחַ לַעֲמֹד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, טָהוֹר. וְאִם לָאו, טָמֵא
phrases.en: [In the case of] a house partitioned off by wine-jars, which had been plastered with clay, If the clay can remain in its position on its own, [the space partitioned off] remains clean, But if not, it becomes unclean.

phrases.he: כֹּתֶל הַמְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת הַבַּיִת, יִדּוֹן מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה. כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: A wall serving a house is treated as if it was separate halves.

phrases.he: כֹּתֶל שֶׁהוּא לָאֲוִיר וְהַטֻּמְאָה בְתוֹכוֹ, מֵחֶצְיוֹ וְלִפְנִים, הַבַּיִת טָמֵא, וְהָעוֹמֵד מִלְמַעְלָן טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: How so? A wall serving an open space, that has uncleanness within it: If it is in the inward half, the house is unclean, But what is above [the wall] remains clean.

phrases.he: מֵחֶצְיוֹ וְלַחוּץ, הַבַּיִת טָהוֹר, וְהָעוֹמֵד מִלְמַעְלָן טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If it is in the outward half, the house remains clean, But what is above [the wall] becomes unclean.

phrases.he: מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, הַבַּיִת טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If it is exactly in the middle, the house becomes unclean, And as for what is above, Rabbi Meir declares it unclean, But the sages declare it clean.

phrases.he: וְהָעוֹמֵד מִלְמַעְלָן, רַבִּי מֵאִיר מְטַמֵּא, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כָּל הַכֹּתֶל לַבָּיִת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: the whole of the wall belongs to the house.

phrases.he: כֹּתֶל שֶׁבֵּין שְׁנֵי בָתִּים וְהַטֻּמְאָה בְתוֹכוֹ, בַּיִת הַקָּרוֹב לַטֻּמְאָה, טָמֵא. וְהַקָּרוֹב לַטָּהֳרָה, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: [In the case of] a wall between two houses and there is uncleanness within it, The house nearer to the uncleanness is unclean, And the house nearer to the clean part is clean.

phrases.he: מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, שְׁנֵיהֶם טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: If [the uncleanness] is in the middle, both are unclean.

phrases.he: טֻמְאָה בְאַחַד מֵהֶן וְכֵלִים בַּכֹּתֶל, מֵחֶצְיוֹ וּכְלַפֵּי טֻמְאָה, טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: If there is uncleanness in one of the [houses] and there are vessels in [the thickness of] the wall: Those in the half nearer the uncleanness are unclean, Those in the half nearer the clean [house] are clean, And those in the middle are unclean.

phrases.he: מֵחֶצְיוֹ וּכְלַפֵּי טָהֳרָה, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: [With regard to the] plaster-work between the house and the upper story, and there is uncleanness in it: If it is in the lower half, the house [below] is unclean and the upper story is clean If it is in the upper half, the upper story is unclean and the house is clean: If it is in the middle, both are unclean.

phrases.he: מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, הֲרֵי הֵן טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: If there is uncleanness in either [the house or the upper story] and there are vessels inside the plaster-work, Those in the half nearer the uncleanness are unclean, And those in the half nearer the clean [space] are clean.

phrases.he: מַעֲזִיבָה שֶׁבֵּין הַבַּיִת לָעֲלִיָּה, טֻמְאָה בְתוֹכָהּ, מֵחֶצְיָהּ וּלְמַטָּן, הַבַּיִת טָמֵא וַעֲלִיָּה טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If they are in the middle, they are unclean.

phrases.he: מֵחֶצְיָהּ וּלְמַעְלָן, הָעֲלִיָּה טְמֵאָה וְהַבַּיִת טָהוֹר.
מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, שְׁנֵיהֶן טְמֵאִין.
טֻמְאָה בְאַחַד מֵהֶן וְכֵלִים בַּמַּעֲזִיבָה, מֵחֶצְיָהּ וּכְלַפֵּי טֻמְאָה, טְמֵאִין.
מֵחֶצְיָהּ וּכְלַפֵּי טָהֳרָה, טְהוֹרִין.
מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, הֲרֵי הֵן טְמֵאִין.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כָּל הַמַּעֲזִיבָה לָעֲלִיָּה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: all the plaster-work is considered as part of the upper story.

phrases.he: טֻמְאָה בֵין הַקּוֹרוֹת וְתַחְתֶּיהָ כִקְלִפַּת הַשּׁוּם, אִם יֶשׁ שָׁם פּוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח, הַכֹּל טָמֵא.
phrases.en: [In the case of] uncleanness among the roof-beams, [with a covering] beneath it thin as thin as garlic-skin, If there is a space within of a cubic handbreadth, everything becomes unclean.

phrases.he: אִם אֵין שָׁם פּוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח, רוֹאִין אֶת הַטֻּמְאָה כְּאִלּוּ הִיא אֹטֶם.
phrases.en: If there is not a space of a cubic handbreadth, the uncleanness is considered plugged up.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה נִרְאֵית בְּתוֹךְ הַבַּיִת, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ, הַבַּיִת טָמֵא
phrases.en: If the uncleanness was visible within the house, in either case the house becomes unclean.

phrases.he: בַּיִת הַמְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת הַכֹּתֶל, יִדּוֹן כִּקְלִפַּת הַשּׁוּם. כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: A house serving a wall is subject to the principle of garlic-skin.

phrases.he: כֹּתֶל שֶׁבֵּין שְׁנֵי כוּכִין, אוֹ בֵין שְׁתֵּי מְעָרוֹת, טֻמְאָה בַבָּתִּים וְכֵלִים בַּכֹּתֶל וַעֲלֵיהֶם כִּקְלִפַּת הַשּׁוּם, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: How so? [In the case of] a wall between two tomb-niches or two caverns, If there is uncleanness in them and vessels in the walls, and there is a covering thin as garlic-skin over them, they remain clean.

phrases.he: טֻמְאָה בַכֹּתֶל וְכֵלִים בַּבָּתִּים וְעָלֶיהָ כִקְלִפַּת הַשּׁוּם, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: If the uncleanness is in the wall and the vessels are in them, and there is a covering thin as garlic-skin over the uncleanness, they remain clean.

phrases.he: טֻמְאָה תַחַת הָעַמּוּד, טֻמְאָה בוֹקַעַת וְעוֹלָה, בּוֹקַעַת וְיוֹרָדֶת
phrases.en: If there is uncleanness beneath a pillar, the uncleanness cleaves upwards and downwards.

phrases.he: כֵּלִים שֶׁתַּחַת הַפֶּרַח, טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: Vessels beneath the flowerlike top [of a pillar] remain clean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri declares them unclean.

phrases.he: הַטֻּמְאָה וְהַכֵּלִים שֶׁתַּחַת הַפֶּרַח, אִם יֶשׁ שָׁם פּוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח, טְמֵאִין. וְאִם לָאו, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: [In the case of] the uncleanness and the vessels being [together] beneath the flowerlike top [of a pillar]: If there is a space of one cubic handbreadth there, [the vessels] become unclean; If not, they remain clean.

phrases.he: שְׁנֵי פַרְדַּסְקִים זֶה בְצַד זֶה, אוֹ זֶה עַל גַּב זֶה, נִפְתַּח אַחַד מֵהֶן, הוּא וְהַבַּיִת טָמֵא, וַחֲבֵרוֹ טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: [In the case of] two wall-cupboards, one beside the other, or one above the other, if one of them was opened, both it and the house become unclean, but its companion remains clean.

phrases.he: וְרוֹאִין אֶת הַפַּרְדַּסְקִין כְּאִלּוּ הוּא אֹטֶם, יִדּוֹן מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה לְהָבִיא אֶת הַטֻּמְאָה לַבָּיִת
phrases.en: The wall-cupboard is considered as if it is plugged up, and it is subject to the principle of halves for conveying uncleanness into the house.

phrases.he: הַטֻּמְאָה בַכֹּתֶל, וּמְקוֹמָהּ טֶפַח עַל טֶפַח עַל רוּם טֶפַח, כָּל הָעֲלִיּוֹת שֶׁעַל גַּבָּהּ, אֲפִלּוּ הֵן עֶשֶׂר, טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: If there is uncleanness in a wall, in a space of one cubic handbreadth, all upper stories above it, even if there are ten of them, are unclean.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה עֲלִיָּה אַחַת עַל גַּבֵּי שְׁנֵי בָתִּים, הִיא טְמֵאָה, וְכָל הָעֲלִיּוֹת שֶׁעַל גַּבָּהּ, טְהוֹרוֹת.
phrases.en: If there was a single upper story [built] over two houses, that one becomes unclean but all upper stories above it remain clean.

phrases.he: כֹּתֶל שָׁנִית, טֻמְאָה בוֹקַעַת וְעוֹלָה, בּוֹקַעַת וְיוֹרָדֶת.
phrases.en: [In a] beach- wall, uncleanness cleaves upwards and downward.

phrases.he: נֶפֶשׁ אֲטוּמָה, הַנּוֹגֵעַ בָּהּ מִן הַצְּדָדִין, טָהוֹר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁטֻּמְאָה בוֹקַעַת וְעוֹלָה, בּוֹקַעַת וְיוֹרָדֶת.
phrases.en: [With regard to] a solid tomb monument, a person who touches it from the side remains clean, since [its] uncleanness cleaves upwards and downwards.

phrases.he: אִם הָיָה מְקוֹם הַטֻּמְאָה טֶפַח עַל טֶפַח עַל רוּם טֶפַח, הַנּוֹגֵעַ בָּהּ מִכָּל מָקוֹם, טָמֵא, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא כְקֶבֶר סָתוּם.
phrases.en: But if there was a [free] space of a cubic handbreadth in the place where the uncleanness was, a person touching it anywhere becomes unclean, because it is like a closed grave.

phrases.he: סָמַךְ לָהּ סֻכּוֹת, טְמֵאוֹת. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַהֵר
phrases.en: If he supported sukkot on [the monument] they become unclean. Rabbi Judah declares them clean.

phrases.he: כָּל שִׁפּוּעֵי אֹהָלִין, כָּאֹהָלִין.
phrases.en: All sloping [parts] of ‘tents’ are reckoned like ‘tents.

phrases.he: אֹהֶל שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹפֵעַ וְיוֹרֵד, וְכָלֶה עַד כְּאֶצְבַּע, טֻמְאָה בָאֹהֶל, כֵּלִים שֶׁתַּחַת הַשִּׁפּוּעַ, טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: A ‘tent’ [whose sides] sloped downwards and finished off one fingerbreadth [from the ground]: If there is uncleanness in the ‘tent’, vessels beneath the slope become unclean.

phrases.he: טֻמְאָה תַחַת הַשִּׁפּוּעַ, כֵּלִים שֶׁבָּאֹהֶל, טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: If there is uncleanness beneath the slope, vessels in the ‘tent’ become unclean.

phrases.he: טֻמְאָה מִתּוֹכוֹ, הַנּוֹגֵעַ בּוֹ מִתּוֹכוֹ, טָמֵא טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.en: If there is uncleanness within, a person who touches [the tent] from the inside acquires a seven [days’] defilement, but from the outside, a defilement [lasting till] evening.

phrases.he: וּמֵאֲחוֹרָיו, טָמֵא טֻמְאַת עָרֶב.
phrases.en: If there had been uncleanness outside, a person who touches the ‘tent’ from the outside acquires a seven [days’] defilement, but from the inside, a defilement [lasting till] evening.

phrases.he: טֻמְאָה מֵאֲחוֹרָיו, הַנּוֹגֵעַ בּוֹ מֵאֲחוֹרָיו, טָמֵא טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.en: If there was [a portion of uncleanness] the size of half an olive [touching it] from inside and half an olive from the outside, a person who touches [the ‘tent’] either from within or without acquires a defilement [lasting till] evening.

phrases.he: מִתּוֹכוֹ, טָמֵא טֻמְאַת עָרֶב.
phrases.en: If a part [of the ‘tent’ side] trailed along the ground, when there is uncleanness beneath or above [this part], the uncleanness cleaves upwards and downwards.

phrases.he: כַּחֲצִי זַיִת מִתּוֹכוֹ וְכַחֲצִי זַיִת מֵאֲחוֹרָיו, הַנּוֹגֵעַ בּוֹ, בֵּין מִתּוֹכוֹ בֵּין מֵאֲחוֹרָיו, טָמֵא טֻמְאַת עָרֶב.
phrases.en: [In the case of] a ‘tent’ erected in an upper story, with a portion [of its side] trailing over the hatch between the house and the upper story: Rabbi Yose says it does protect.

phrases.he: מִקְצָתוֹ מְרֻדָּד עַל הָאָרֶץ, טֻמְאָה תַחְתָּיו אוֹ עַל גַּבָּיו, טֻמְאָה בוֹקַעַת וְעוֹלָה, בּוֹקַעַת וְיוֹרָדֶת.
אֹהֶל שֶׁהוּא נָטוּי בָּעֲלִיָּה, מִקְצָתוֹ מְרֻדָּד עַל הָאֲרֻבָּה שֶׁבֵּין בַּיִת לָעֲלִיָּה,
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, מַצִּיל.
