phrases.en: And that which is left [over from before the scall] affords protection against yellow hair and against a spreading, whether it is clustered together or dispersed, and also when encompassed, but it affords no protection where it is at the side unless it is distant from the standing hair by the place of two hairs.

phrases.he: וְאֵינוֹ מַצִּיל מִן הַצַּד, עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא רָחוֹק מִן הַקָּמָה מְקוֹם שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת.
phrases.en: If one hair was yellow and the other black, or if one was yellow and the other white, they afford no protection.

phrases.he: אַחַת צְהֻבָּה וְאַחַת שְׁחֹרָה, אַחַת צְהֻבָּה וְאַחַת לְבָנָה, אֵינָן מַצִּילוֹת
שֵׂעָר צָהֹב שֶׁקָּדַם אֶת הַנֶּתֶק, טָהוֹר. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.en: Yellow hair that preceded a scall is clean. Rabbi Judah says that it is unclean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר, לֹא מְטַמֵּא וְלֹא מַצִּיל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Jacob says: it neither causes uncleanness nor does it afford protection.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ סִימַן טֻמְאָה בַנֶּתֶק, הֲרֵי הוּא סִימַן טָהֳרָה בַנָּתֶק:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: anything in a scall that is not a sign of uncleanness is a sign of cleanness.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד מְגַלְּחִין אֶת הַנֶּתֶק.
phrases.en: How does one shave who has a scall? He shaves outside it and leaves next to it two hairs in order to determine whether it spreads.

phrases.he: מְגַלֵּחַ חוּצָה לוֹ וּמַנִּיחַ שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת סָמוּךְ לוֹ, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא נִכָּר אִם פָּשָׂה.
phrases.en: If he was certified unclean on account of yellow hair, and then the yellow hair disappeared and other yellow hair appeared, and so also if there was a spreading, irrespective of whether the certification took place at the beginning, at the end of the first week, at the end of the second week or after his release from uncleanness, behold he remains as he was before.

phrases.he: הֶחְלִיטוֹ בְשֵׂעָר צָהֹב, הָלַךְ שֵׂעָר צָהֹב וְחָזַר שֵׂעָר צָהֹב, וְכֵן בְּפִשְׂיוֹן, בַּתְּחִלָּה, בְּסוֹף שָׁבוּעַ רִאשׁוֹן, בְּסוֹף שָׁבוּעַ שֵׁנִי, לְאַחַר הַפְּטוּר, הֲרֵי הוּא כְמוֹת שֶׁהָיָה.
phrases.en: If he was certified unclean on account of a spreading, and the spreading disappeared and then reappeared, and so also if there was yellow hair, irrespective of whether the certification took place at the end of the first week, at the end of the second week or after his release from uncleanness, he remains as he was before.

phrases.he: הֶחְלִיטוֹ בְּפִשְׂיוֹן, וְהָלַךְ הַפִּשְׂיוֹן וְחָזַר הַפִּשְׂיוֹן.
וְכֵן בְּשֵׂעָר צָהֹב, בְּסוֹף שָׁבוּעַ רִאשׁוֹן, בְּסוֹף שָׁבוּעַ שֵׁנִי, לְאַחַר הַפְּטוּר, הֲרֵי הוּא כְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה
שְׁנֵי נְתָקִים, זֶה בְצַד זֶה, וְשִׁיטָה שֶׁל שֵׂעָר מַפְסֶקֶת בֵּינֵיהֶם, נִפְרַץ מִמָּקוֹם אֶחָד, טָמֵא. מִשְּׁנֵי מְקוֹמוֹת, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Two scalls side by side and a line of hair separating between them: If a gap opened up in one place he is unclean, But if it opened up in two places he is clean.

phrases.he: כַּמָּה תְהֵא הַפִּרְצָה, מְקוֹם שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת.
phrases.en: How big should the gap be? The space of two hairs.

phrases.he: נִפְרַץ מִמָּקוֹם אֶחָד כַּגְּרִיס, טָמֵא
phrases.en: If there was a gap in one place, even though it is as big as a split bean, he is unclean.

phrases.he: שְׁנֵי נְתָקִין, זֶה לִפְנִים מִזֶּה, וְשִׁיטָה שֶׁל שֵׂעָר מַפְסֶקֶת בֵּינֵיהֶן, נִפְרַץ מִמָּקוֹם אֶחָד, טָמֵא. מִשְּׁנֵי מְקוֹמוֹת, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Two scalls one within the other and a line of hair separating between them: If there appeared a gap in one place the inner one is unclean, But if in two places it is clean.

phrases.he: כַּמָּה תְהֵא הַפִּרְצָה, מְקוֹם שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת.
phrases.en: How big must the gap be? The space of two hairs.

phrases.he: נִפְרַץ מִמָּקוֹם אֶחָד כַּגְּרִיס, טָהוֹר
phrases.en: If there was a gap in one place of the size of a split bean he is clean.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁהָיָה בוֹ נֶתֶק וּבוֹ שֵׂעָר צָהֹב, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: One who has a scall with yellow hair within it is unclean.

phrases.he: נוֹלַד לוֹ שֵׂעָר שָׁחֹר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If subsequently black hair grew in it, he is clean; even if the black hair disappeared again he remains clean.

phrases.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָלַךְ לוֹ שֵׂעָר שָׁחֹר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Judah says in the name of Rabbi Shimon: any scall that has once been pronounced clean can never again be unclean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, כָּל נֶתֶק שֶׁטָּהַר שָׁעָה אַחַת, אֵין לוֹ טֻמְאָה לְעוֹלָם.
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, כָּל שֵׂעָר צָהֹב שֶׁטָּהַר שָׁעָה אַחַת, אֵין לוֹ טֻמְאָה לְעוֹלָם:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: any yellow hair that has once been pronounced clean can never again be unclean.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁהָיָה בוֹ נֶתֶק כַּגְּרִיס, וְנִתַּק כָּל רֹאשׁוֹ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If one had a scall the size of a split bean and it spread over all his head he becomes clean.

phrases.he: הָרֹאשׁ וְהַזָּקָן אֵין מְעַכְּבִין זֶה אֶת זֶה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: The head and the beard do not prevent [one another], the words of Rabbi Judah.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, מְעַכְּבִין זֶה אֶת זֶה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: they do prevent.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, וְדִין הוּא, מָה אִם עוֹר הַפָּנִים וְעוֹר הַבָּשָׂר, שֶׁיֵּשׁ דָּבָר אַחֵר מַפְסִיק בֵּינֵיהֶם, מְעַכְּבִין זֶה אֶת זֶה, הָרֹאשׁ וְהַזָּקָן שֶׁאֵין דָּבָר אַחֵר מַפְסִיק בֵּינֵיהֶם, אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁיְּעַכְּבוּ זֶה אֶת זֶה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon said: Is there not a logical inference: if the skin of the face and the skin of the body, between which something intervenes, do prevent [one another], the head and the beard, between which nothing intervenes, should they not also prevent [one another]? The head and the beard do not combine, nor is a spreading from one to the other effective.

phrases.he: הָרֹאשׁ וְהַזָּקָן אֵין מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה, וְאֵין פּוֹשִׂין מִזֶּה לָזֶה.
phrases.en: What exactly counts as the beard? From the joint of the jaw to the thyroid cartilage.

phrases.he: אֵיזֶה הוּא זָקָן, מִן הַפֶּרֶק שֶׁל לֶחִי עַד פִּקָּה שֶׁל גַּרְגָּרֶת
הַקָּרַחַת וְהַגַּבַּחַת מִטַּמְּאוֹת בִּשְׁנֵי שָׁבוּעוֹת, בִּשְׁנֵי סִימָנִים, בְּמִחְיָה וּבְפִסְיוֹן.
phrases.en: Scalp baldness (karahat) or forehead baldness (gabahat) may become unclean in two weeks and by two signs: by quick flesh or by spreading.

phrases.he: אֵיזוֹ הִיא קָרַחַת, אָכַל נֶשֶׁם, סָךְ נֶשֶׁם, מַכָּה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לְגַדֵּל שֵׂעָר.
phrases.en: What constitutes baldness? If one ate neshem or smeared himself with neshem or had a wound from which hair can no longer grow.

phrases.he: אֵיזוֹ הִיא קָרַחַת, מִן הַקָּדְקֹד הַשּׁוֹפֵעַ לַאֲחוֹרָיו עַד פִּקָּה שֶׁל צַוָּאר.
phrases.en: What is the extent of scalp baldness? From the crown sloping backwards to the protruding cartilage of the neck.

phrases.he: אֵיזוֹ הִיא גַּבַּחַת, מִן הַקָּדְקֹד הַשּׁוֹפֵעַ לְפָנָיו עַד כְּנֶגֶד שֵׂעָר מִלְמַעְלָן.
phrases.en: What is the extent of forehead baldness? From the crown sloping forwards to the region facing the hair above.

phrases.he: הַקָּרַחַת וְהַגַּבַּחַת אֵינָן מִצְטָרְפוֹת זוֹ עִם זוֹ, וְאֵינָן פּוֹשׂוֹת מִזּוֹ לָזוֹ.
phrases.en: Scalp baldness and forehead baldness cannot be combined, nor is spreading from one to the other effective.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם יֵשׁ שֵׂעָר בֵּינֵיהֶן, אֵינָן מִצְטָרְפוֹת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: if there is hair between them they cannot be combined, but if there is none they must be combined.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מִצְטָרְפוֹת
כָּל הַבְּגָדִים מִטַּמְּאִין בַּנְּגָעִים, חוּץ מִשֶּׁל נָכְרִים.
phrases.en: All garments can contract the uncleanness of negaim except those of non-Jews.

phrases.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ בְּגָדִים מִן הַנָּכְרִים, יֵרָאוּ בַתְּחִלָּה.
phrases.en: One who buys garments [with signs of negaim] from non-Jews they must be inspected as if the signs had then first appeared.

phrases.he: וְעוֹרוֹת הַיָּם אֵינָן מִטַּמְּאִין בַּנְּגָעִים.
phrases.en: The hides [of animals] of the sea do not contract the uncleanness of negaim.

phrases.he: חִבֵּר לָהֶם מִן הַגָּדֵל בָּאָרֶץ, אֲפִלּוּ חוּט, אֲפִלּוּ מְשִׁיחָה, דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה, טָמֵא
phrases.en: If one joined to them anything which grows on land, even if it is only a thread or a cord, as long as it is something that is susceptible to uncleanness, they also become susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: צֶמֶר גְּמַלִּים וְצֶמֶר רְחֵלִים שֶׁטְּרָפָן זֶה בָזֶה, אִם רֹב מִן הַגְּמַלִּים, אֵינָם מִטַּמְּאִין בַּנְּגָעִים.
phrases.en: Camel's wool and sheep's wool that have been hackled together: If the majority is camel's hair, they are not susceptible to negaim; But if the majority is sheep's wool they are susceptible to negaim.

phrases.he: אִם רֹב מִן הָרְחֵלִים, מִטַּמְּאִים בַּנְּגָעִים.
phrases.en: If it is half and half they are susceptible to negaim.

phrases.he: מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, מִטַּמְּאִין בַּנְּגָעִים.
phrases.en: And the same law applies also to linen and hemp that have been hackled together.

phrases.he: וְכֵן הַפִּשְׁתָּן וְהַקַּנְבּוֹס שֶׁטְּרָפָן זֶה בָזֶה
הָעוֹרוֹת וְהַבְּגָדִים הַצְּבוּעִים, אֵין מִטַּמְּאִין בַּנְּגָעִים.
phrases.en: Colored hides and garments are not susceptible to negaim.

phrases.he: הַבָּתִּים, בֵּין צְבוּעִים בֵּין שֶׁאֵינָן צְבוּעִים, מִטַּמְּאִין בַּנְּגָעִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: Houses whether they are colored or not colored, are susceptible to negaim, the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Judah says: hides are like houses.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הָעוֹרוֹת כַּבָּתִּים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: those that are naturally [colored] are susceptible to uncleanness but those that are artificially [dyed] are not susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, הַצְּבוּעִים בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם, מִטַּמְּאִין.
וּבִידֵי אָדָם, אֵינָן מִטַּמְּאִין
בֶּגֶד שֶׁשִּׁתְיוֹ צָבוּעַ וְעֶרְבּוֹ לָבָן, עֶרְבּוֹ צָבוּעַ וְשִׁתְיוֹ לָבָן, הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַנִּרְאֶה.
phrases.en: A garment whose warp was colored and whose woof was white, or whose woof was colored and whose warp was white, all depends on what is most visible.

phrases.he: הַבְּגָדִים מִטַּמְּאִין בִּירַקְרַק שֶׁבַּיְרֻקִּים, וּבַאֲדַמְדַּם שֶׁבָּאֲדֻמִּים.
phrases.en: Garments contract uncleanness if they are an intense green or an intense red.

phrases.he: הָיָה יְרַקְרַק וּפָשָׂה אֲדַמְדַּם, אֲדַמְדַּם וּפָשָׂה יְרַקְרַק, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If [the nega] was green and it spread out red, or if it was red and it spread out green, it is unclean.

phrases.he: נִשְׁתַּנָּה וּפָשָׂה, נִשְׁתַּנָּה וְלֹא פָשָׂה, כְּאִלּוּ לֹא נִשְׁתַּנָּה.
phrases.en: If its color changed and then it spread, or if it changed and it did not spread, it is regarded as if it had not changed.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, יֵרָאֶה בַתְּחִלָּה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: let it be inspected as if it then appeared for the first time.

phrases.he: הָעוֹמֵד בָּרִאשׁוֹן, יְכַבֵּס וְיַסְגִּיר. הָעוֹמֵד בַּשֵּׁנִי, יִשָּׂרֵף.
phrases.en: [A nega] that remained unchanged during the first week must be washed and isolated. One that remains unchanged during the second week must be burned.

phrases.he: הַפּוֹשֶׂה בָזֶה וּבָזֶה, יִשָּׂרֵף. הִכְהָה בַתְּחִלָּה,
phrases.en: One that spread during the first or the second week must be burned.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, יְכַבֵּס וְיַסְגִּיר.
phrases.en: If it becomes dimmer in the beginning: Rabbi Ishmael says: it should be washed and isolated.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵינוֹ זָקוּק לוֹ.
phrases.en: But the sages say: he is not required [to do so].

phrases.he: הִכְהָה בָרִאשׁוֹן, יְכַבֵּס וְיַסְגִּיר.
phrases.en: If the nega became dimmer during the first week it must be washed and isolated.

phrases.he: הִכְהָה בַשֵּׁנִי, קוֹרְעוֹ וְשׂוֹרֵף מַה שֶּׁקָּרַע. וְצָרִיךְ מַטְלִית.
phrases.en: If it became dimmer during the second week it must be torn out, and that which is torn out must be burnt, and it is necessary for a patch to be put on.

phrases.he: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר, אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ מַטְלִית:
phrases.en: Rabbi Nehemiah says: a patch is not necessary.

phrases.he: חָזַר נֶגַע לַבֶּגֶד, מַצִּיל אֶת הַמַּטְלִית.
phrases.en: If the nega reappears on the garment, the patch is protected.

phrases.he: חָזַר לַמַּטְלִית, שׂוֹרֵף אֶת הַבֶּגֶד.
phrases.en: If it reappears on the patch the garment must be burned.

phrases.he: הַטּוֹלֶה מִן הַמֻּסְגָּר בַּטָּהוֹר, חָזַר נֶגַע לַבֶּגֶד, שׂוֹרֵף אֶת הַמַּטְלִית.
phrases.en: One who makes a patch from a garment that was isolated and then pronounced pure, and then the nega reappeared on the garment, the patch must be burned.

phrases.he: חָזַר לַמַּטְלִית, הַבֶּגֶד הָרִאשׁוֹן יִשָּׂרֵף, וְהַמַּטְלִית תְּשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת הַבֶּגֶד הַשֵּׁנִי בְּסִימָנִין
phrases.en: If it reappeared on the patch, the first garment must be burned, and the patch serves the second garment while the two signs are under observation.

phrases.he: קַיְטָא שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ פִּסְפָּסִים צְבוּעִים וּלְבָנִים, פּוֹשִׂין מִזֶּה לָזֶה.
phrases.en: A screen that had colored and white stripes, a nega may effectively spread from one to the other.

phrases.he: שָׁאֲלוּ אֶת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וַהֲרֵי הוּא פִסְפָּס יָחִיד.
phrases.en: They asked Rabbi Eliezer: But the white stripe is separate? He replied: I have heard no ruling on this question.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶן, לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah ben Batera said to him: Shall I derive the answer? He replied: If this would confirm the words of the sages, then yes! He said back: It is possible that it would remain on it in an unchanged condition for two weeks, and that which remains unchanged on garments for two weeks is unclean.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶן בְּתֵירָא, אֲלַמֵּד בּוֹ.
phrases.en: He said to him: You are a great sage, for you have confirmed the words of the sages.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ, אִם לְקַיֵּם דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים, הֵן.
phrases.en: A spreading that is close [to the original nega is effective] however small it may be.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ, שֶׁמָּא יַעֲמֹד בּוֹ שְׁנֵי שָׁבוּעוֹת, וְהָעוֹמֵד בַּבְּגָדִים שְׁנֵי שָׁבוּעוֹת טָמֵא.
phrases.en: One that is distant [is effective only] if it is of the size of a split bean.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ, חָכָם גָּדוֹל אַתָּה, שֶׁקִּיַּמְתָּ דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים.
phrases.en: And one that reappears [is effective only if it is] of the size of a split bean.

phrases.he: הַפִּשְׂיוֹן הַסָּמוּךְ, כָּל שֶׁהוּא. הָרָחוֹק, כַּגְּרִיס. וְהַחוֹזֵר, כַּגְּרִיס
הַשְּׁתִי וְהָעֵרֶב מִטַּמְּאִים בַּנְּגָעִים מִיָּד.
phrases.en: The warp and the woof can contract the uncleanness of negaim immediately.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הַשְּׁתִי, מִשֶּׁיִּשָּׁלֵק, וְהָעֵרֶב, מִיָּד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: the warp, only after it has been boiled, but the woof immediately.

phrases.he: וְהָאוּנִין שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן, מִשֶּׁיִּתְלַבֵּנוּ.
phrases.en: And bundles of flax after they have been bleached.

phrases.he: כַּמָּה יְהֵא בַפְּקַעַת וּתְהֵא מִטַּמְּאָה בַנְּגָעִים, כְּדֵי לֶאֱרֹג מִמֶּנָּה שָׁלשׁ עַל שָׁלשׁ שְׁתִי וָעֵרֶב, אֲפִלּוּ כֻלָּהּ שְׁתִי, אֲפִלּוּ כֻלָּהּ עֵרֶב.
phrases.en: How much must there be in a coil for it to be capable of contracting the uncleanness of negaim? Enough to weave from it a piece of three fingerbreadths square, either warp or woof, even if it is all warp or all woof.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה פְסִיקוֹת, אֵינָהּ מִטַּמְּאָה בַנְּגָעִים.
phrases.en: If it consisted of broken threads it does not contract the uncleanness of negaim.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ פְסִיקָה אַחַת וּקְשָׁרָהּ, אֵינָהּ מִטַּמְּאָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: even if the thread was broken only in one place, and he knotted together, it does not contract the uncleanness of negaim.

phrases.he: הַמַּעֲלֶה מִן הַפְּקַעַת לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ, מִן הַסְּלִיל לַחֲבֵרוֹ, מִן הַכֹּבֶד הָעֶלְיוֹנָה לַכֹּבֶד הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה, וְכֵן שְׁנֵי דַפֵּי חָלוּק שֶׁנִּרְאָה נֶגַע בְּאַחַד מֵהֶן, הֲרֵי הַשֵּׁנִי טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: One who winds [a thread] from one coil to another, or from one spool to another, or from the upper beam to the lower beam, and so also in the case of the two sides of a shirt, if a nega appears on the one, the other remains clean.

phrases.he: בְּנֶפֶשׁ הַמַּסֶּכֶת וּבַשְּׁתִי הָעוֹמֵד, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מִטַּמְּאִין בַּנְּגָעִים מִיָּד.
phrases.en: If it appears on the shedded woof or on the standing warp, they become susceptible to the uncleanness of negaim immediately.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, הַשְּׁתִי, אִם הָיָה רָצוּף, מִטַּמֵּא:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: the warp may contract uncleanness only if it is closely ordered.

phrases.he: נִרְאָה בַּשְּׁתִי הָעוֹמֵד, הָאָרִיג טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: [If a nega] appeared on the standing warp, the already woven cloth remains clean.

phrases.he: נִרְאָה בָאָרִיג, הַשְּׁתִי הָעוֹמֵד טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If it appeared on the already woven cloth, the standing warp remains clean.

phrases.he: נִרְאָה בַסָּדִין, שׂוֹרֵף אֶת הַנִּימִין.
phrases.en: If it appeared on a sheet, he must also burn the fringes.

phrases.he: נִרְאָה בַנִּימִין, הַסָּדִין טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If it appeared on the fringes the sheet remains clean.

phrases.he: חָלוּק שֶׁנִּרְאָה בוֹ נֶגַע, מַצִּיל אֶת הָאֻמְרִיּוֹת שֶׁבּוֹ, אֲפִלּוּ הֵן אַרְגָּמָן
phrases.en: A shirt on which a nega appeared affords protection to its hems, even though they are of purple wool.

phrases.he: כֹּל הָרָאוּי לִטַּמֵּא טְמֵא מֵת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי לִטַּמֵּא מִדְרָס, מִטַּמֵּא בַנְּגָעִים.
phrases.en: Any object that is susceptible to corpse uncleanness, though not susceptible to midras uncleanness, is still susceptible to negaim uncleanness.

phrases.he: כְּגוֹן קֶלַע שֶׁל סְפִינָה, וּוִילוֹן, וְשָׁבִיס שֶׁל סְבָכָה, וּמִטְפָּחוֹת שֶׁל סְפָרִים, וְגַלְגִּלּוֹן, וּרְצוּעוֹת מִנְעָל וְסַנְדָּל שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהֶן רֹחַב כַּגְּרִיס, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מִטַּמְּאִין בַּנְּגָעִים.
phrases.en: For instance: the sail of a ship, a curtain, the forehead band of a hair-net, the wrappings of scrolls, a coiled belt, the straps of a shoe or sandal that are at least as wide as a split bean, Behold these are susceptible to the uncleanness of negaim.

phrases.he: סָגוֹס שֶׁנִּרְאָה בוֹ נֶגַע, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר, עַד שֶׁיֵּרָאֶה בָאָרִיג וּבַמּוֹכִין.
phrases.en: A thick cloak on which a nega appeared: Rabbi Eliezer ben Jacob says: unless it appears on the texture and on the stuffing.

phrases.he: הַחֵמֶת וְהַתּוּרְמָל נִרְאִין כְּדַרְכָּן, וּפוֹשֶׂה מִתּוֹכוֹ לַאֲחוֹרָיו וּמֵאֲחוֹרָיו לְתוֹכוֹ
phrases.en: A skin bottle or a shepherd's leather wallet are inspected in the position in which they are used, and a nega may effectively spread from its inner side to its outer side and from its outer side to its inner side.

phrases.he: בֶּגֶד הַמֻּסְגָּר שֶׁנִּתְעָרֵב בַּאֲחֵרִים, כֻּלָּן טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: If a garment that had been isolated was mixed up with others, all are clean.

phrases.he: קְצָצוֹ וַעֲשָׂאוֹ מוֹכִין, טָהוֹר, וּמֻתָּר בַּהֲנָיָתוֹ.
phrases.en: If it was cut up and made into shreds, it is clean, and benefit may be derived from it.

phrases.he: וְהַמֻּחְלָט שֶׁנִּתְעָרֵב בַּאֲחֵרִים, כֻּלָּם טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: But if a garment that had been certified unclean was mixed up with others, all are unclean.

phrases.he: קְצָצוֹ וַעֲשָׂאוֹ מוֹכִין, טָמֵא, וְאָסוּר בַּהֲנָיָתוֹ
phrases.en: If it was cut up and made into shreds it also remains unclean and it is forbidden to have any benefit from it.

phrases.he: כָּל הַבָּתִּים מִטַּמְּאִין בַּנְּגָעִים, חוּץ מִשֶּׁל נָכְרִים.
phrases.en: All houses may contract negaim uncleanness, except those of non-Jews.

phrases.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ בָּתִּים מִן הַנָּכְרִים, יֵרָאוּ בַתְּחִלָּה.
phrases.en: If one bought houses from non-Jews, any it must be inspected as if they had then first appeared.

phrases.he: בַּיִת עָגֹל, בַּיִת טְרִיגוֹן, בַּיִת הַבָּנוּי בִּסְפִינָה אוֹ בְאַסְקַרְיָא, עַל אַרְבַּע קוֹרוֹת, אֵינוֹ מִטַּמֵּא בַנְּגָעִים.
phrases.en: A round house, a triangular house, or a house built on a ship, on a raft or on four beams, is not susceptible to negaim uncleanness.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיָה מְרֻבָּע, אֲפִלּוּ עַל אַרְבָּעָה עַמּוּדִים, מִטַּמֵּא
phrases.en: But if it was four-sided, even if it was built on four pillars, it is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: בַּיִת שֶׁאַחַד מִצְּדָדָיו מְחֻפֶּה בְשַׁיִשׁ, אֶחָד בְּסֶלַע, וְאֶחָד בִּלְבֵנִים, וְאֶחָד בְּעָפָר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A house, one of whose walls was covered with marble, with rock, with bricks or with earth, is pure.

phrases.he: בַּיִת שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ בוֹ אֲבָנִים וְעֵצִים וְעָפָר וְנִרְאָה בוֹ נֶגַע וְאַחַר כָּךְ הֵבִיאוּ בוֹ אֲבָנִים וְעֵצִים וְעָפָר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A house that did not have in it stones, wood or earth, and a nega appeared in it and afterwards stones, wood and earth were brought into it, it remains clean.

phrases.he: וְכֵן בֶּגֶד שֶׁלֹּא אָרַג בּוֹ שָׁלשׁ עַל שָׁלשׁ וְנִרְאָה בוֹ נֶגַע וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָרַג בּוֹ שָׁלשׁ עַל שָׁלשׁ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: So also a garment in which there was no woven part that was three fingerbreadths square and a nega appeared in it and afterwards there was woven into it a piece of cloth three fingerbreadths square, it remains clean.

phrases.he: אֵין הַבַּיִת מִטַּמֵּא בַנְּגָעִים עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בוֹ אֲבָנִים וְעֵצִים וְעָפָר
phrases.en: A house does is not susceptible to negaim uncleanness unless there are in it stones, wood and earth.

phrases.he: וְכַמָּה אֲבָנִים יְהוּ בוֹ.
phrases.en: And how many stones must there be in it [for it to be susceptible to negaim]? Rabbi Ishmael says: four.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, אַרְבַּע.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: eight.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, שְׁמֹנֶה. שֶׁהָיָה
phrases.en: For Rabbi Ishmael used to say: a nega is not a cause of uncleanness unless it appeared in the size of two split beans on two stones or on one stone.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, עַד שֶׁיֵּרָאֶה כִשְׁנֵי גְרִיסִין עַל שְׁתֵּי אֲבָנִים אוֹ עַל אֶבֶן אֶחָת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva say: unless it appears in the size of two split beans on two stones, and not on one stone.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, עַד שֶׁיֵּרָאֶה כִשְׁנֵי גְרִיסִין עַל שְׁתֵּי אֲבָנִים, לֹא עַל אֶבֶן אֶחָת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Shimon says: unless it appears in the size of two split beans, on two stones, on two walls in a corner, Its length being that of two split beans and its breadth that of one split bean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, עַד שֶׁיֵּרָאֶה כִשְׁנֵי גְרִיסִין עַל שְׁתֵּי אֲבָנִים בִּשְׁנֵי כְתָלִים בַּזָּוִית, אָרְכּוֹ כִּשְׁנֵי גְרִיסִין וְרָחְבּוֹ כַּגְּרִיס
עֵצִים, כְּדֵי לִתֵּן תַּחַת הַשְּׁקוֹף.
phrases.en: [And how much] wood [must be in the wall for it to susceptible]? Enough to be set under the lintel.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת סַנְדָּל לַאֲחוֹרֵי הַשְּׁקוֹף.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: it must suffice to make the support at the back of the lintel.

phrases.he: עָפָר, כְּדֵי לִתֵּן בֵּין פַּצִּים לַחֲבֵרוֹ.
phrases.en: [And how much] earth [must be in the wall for it to susceptible]? Such as would suffice to fill up the space between one row of stones and another.

phrases.he: קִירוֹת הָאֵבוּס, וְקִירוֹת הַמְּחִצָּה, אֵינָן מִטַּמְּאִין בַּנְּגָעִים.
phrases.en: The walls of a cattle-trough or the walls of a partition are not susceptible to the uncleanness of negaim.

phrases.he: יְרוּשָׁלַיִם וְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ, אֵינָן מִטַּמְּאִין בַּנְּגָעִים
phrases.en: A house in Jerusalem or in any place outside the land of Israel is not susceptible to the uncleanness of negaim.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד רְאִיַּת הַבָּיִת. וּבָא אֲשֶׁר לוֹ הַבַּיִת וְהִגִּיד לַכֹּהֵן לֵאמֹר כְּנֶגַע נִרְאָה לִי בַּבָּיִת (ויקרא יד).
phrases.en: What is the procedure for the inspection of a house? "The owner of the house shall come and tell the priest, saying, "Something like a plague has appeared upon my house" (Leviticus 14:35).

phrases.he: אֲפִלּוּ תַלְמִיד חָכָם וְיוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהוּא נֶגַע וַדַּאי, לֹא יִגְזֹר וְיֹאמַר נֶגַע נִרְאָה לִי בַּבָּיִת, אֶלָּא כְּנֶגַע נִרְאָה לִי בַּבָּיִת.
phrases.en: Even if he is a learned sage and knows that it is definitely a nega, he may not speak with certainty saying, "A plague has appeared upon my house," but rather, "Something like a plague has appeared upon my house.

phrases.he: וְצִוָּה הַכֹּהֵן וּפִנּוּ אֶת הַבַּיִת (בְּטֶרֶם יָבֹא הַכֹּהֵן לִרְאוֹת אֶת הַנֶּגַע וְלֹא יִטְמָא כָּל אֲשֶׁר בַּבָּיִת וְאַחַר כֵּן יָבֹא הַכֹּהֵן לִרְאוֹת אֶת הַבָּיִת) (שם), וַאֲפִלּוּ חֲבִילֵי עֵצִים, וַאֲפִלּוּ חֲבִילֵי קָנִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: "The priest shall order the house cleared before the priest enters to examine the plague, so that nothing in the house may become unclean; after that the priest shall enter to examine the house." Even bundles of wood and even bundles of reeds [must be removed], the words of Rabbi Judah.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, עֵסֶק הוּא לַפִּנּוּי.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon said: clearing keeps him occupied.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְכִי מָה מִטַּמֵּא לוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir said: But which [of his goods] could become unclean? If you were to say, his articles of wood, of cloth or of metal, he could immerse them and they will become clean.

phrases.he: אִם תֹּאמַר, כְּלֵי עֵצָיו וּבְגָדָיו וּמַתְּכוֹתָיו, מַטְבִּילָן וְהֵן טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: What is it that the Torah has spared? His earthenware, even his cruse and his bucket.

phrases.he: עַל מֶה חָסָה הַתּוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If

phrases.he: עַל כְּלֵי חַרְסוֹ וְעַל פַּכּוֹ וְעַל טִפְיוֹ.
phrases.en: the Torah

phrases.he: אִם כָּךְ חָסָה הַתּוֹרָה עַל מָמוֹנוֹ הַבָּזוּי, קַל וָחֹמֶר עַל מָמוֹנוֹ הֶחָבִיב.
phrases.en: thus spared a man's humble possessions, how much more so would it spare his cherished possessions! If for his material

phrases.he: אִם כָּךְ עַל מָמוֹנוֹ, קַל וָחֹמֶר עַל נֶפֶשׁ בָּנָיו וּבְנוֹתָיו.
phrases.en: possessions, how much more so for the life of his sons and daughters! If for the possessions

phrases.he: אִם כָּךְ עַל שֶׁל רָשָׁע, קַל וָחֹמֶר עַל שֶׁל צַדִּיק
phrases.en: of a wicked man, how much more so for the possessions of a righteous one!

phrases.he: אֵינוֹ הוֹלֵךְ לְתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ וּמַסְגִּיר, וְלֹא בְתוֹךְ הַבַּיִת שֶׁהַנֶּגַע בְּתוֹכוֹ וּמַסְגִּיר, אֶלָּא עוֹמֵד עַל פֶּתַח הַבַּיִת שֶׁהַנֶּגַע בְּתוֹכוֹ וּמַסְגִּיר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ויקרא יד), וְיָצָא הַכֹּהֵן מִן הַבַּיִת אֶל פֶּתַח הַבָּיִת וְהִסְגִּיר אֶת הַבַּיִת שִׁבְעַת יָמִים.
phrases.en: [The priest] must not go into his own house to isolate it, nor may he stand within the house in which there is a nega. Rather, he must stand at the door of the house in which is there is a nega, and isolate it from there, as it is said, "The priest shall come out of the house to the entrance of the house, and close up the house for seven days" (Leviticus 14:38).

phrases.he: וּבָא בְסוֹף הַשָּׁבוּעַ וְרָאָה אִם פָּשָׂה, וְצִוָּה הַכֹּהֵן וְחִלְּצוּ אֶת הָאֲבָנִים אֲשֶׁר בָּהֵן הַנָּגַע וְהִשְׁלִיכוּ אֶתְהֶן אֶל מִחוּץ לָעִיר אֶל מָקוֹם טָמֵא.
phrases.en: He comes again at the end of the week and inspects the sign to see if it spread. "The priest shall order the stones with the plague in them to be pulled out and cast outside the city into an unclean place" (v.

phrases.he: וְלָקְחוּ אֲבָנִים אֲחֵרוֹת וְהֵבִיאוּ אֶל תַּחַת הָאֲבָנִים וְעָפָר אַחֵר יִקַּח וְטָח אֶת הַבָּיִת (שם).
phrases.en: "They shall take other stones and replace those stones with them, and take other dirt and plaster the house" (v.

phrases.he: אֵינוֹ נוֹטֵל אֲבָנִים מִצַּד זֶה וּמֵבִיא לְצַד זֶה, וְלֹא עָפָר מִצַּד זֶה וּמֵבִיא לְצַד זֶה, וְלֹא סִיד מִכָּל מָקוֹם.
phrases.en: He must not take stones from the one side and bring them to the other; nor earth from the one side and bring it to the other; nor lime from anywhere.

phrases.he: אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא לֹא אַחַת תַּחַת שְׁתַּיִם וְלֹא שְׁתַּיִם תַּחַת אַחַת, אֶלָּא מֵבִיא שְׁתַּיִם תַּחַת שְׁתַּיִם, תַּחַת שָׁלשׁ, תַּחַת אַרְבַּע.
phrases.en: He must not bring one stone to replace two, nor two to replace one. But he can bring two to replace two or to replace three or to replace four.

phrases.he: מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ, אוֹי לָרָשָׁע אוֹי לִשְׁכֵנוֹ, שְׁנֵיהֶן חוֹלְצִין, שְׁנֵיהֶן קוֹצְעִין, שְׁנֵיהֶן מְבִיאִין אֶת הָאֲבָנִים.
phrases.en: From here they have said: Woe to the wicked, woe to his neighbor. Both must take out the stones, both must scrape the walls, and both must bring the new stones.

phrases.he: אֲבָל הוּא לְבַדּוֹ מֵבִיא אֶת הֶעָפָר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שם), וְעָפָר אַחֵר יִקַּח וְטָח אֶת הַבָּיִת, אֵין חֲבֵרוֹ מִטַּפֵּל עִמּוֹ בַּטִּיחָה
phrases.en: He alone, however, brings the earth, as it is said, "And he shall take other coating and plaster the house." His neighbor need not join with him in the plastering.

phrases.he: בָּא בְסוֹף שָׁבוּעַ וְרָאָה, אִם חָזַר, וְנָתַץ אֶת הַבַּיִת אֶת אֲבָנָיו וְאֶת עֵצָיו וְאֵת כָּל עֲפַר הַבָּיִת וְהוֹצִיא אֶל מִחוּץ לָעִיר אֶל מָקוֹם טָמֵא (שם).
phrases.en: He comes again at the end of the week and inspects the nega. If it has returned, "He shall break down the house, its stones, and its timber, and all the mortar of the house; and he shall carry them out of the city into an unclean place" (Leviticus 14:45).

phrases.he: הַפִּסְיוֹן הַסָּמוּךְ, כָּל שֶׁהוּא. וְהָרָחוֹק, כַּגְּרִיס.
phrases.en: A spreading that adjoins [the original nega] is effective however small it may be; One that is distant must be no less than the size of a split bean.

phrases.he: וְהַחוֹזֵר בַּבָּתִּים, כִּשְׁנֵי גְרִיסִין
phrases.en: And a nega that returns in houses must be no less than the size of two split beans.

phrases.he: עֲשָׂרָה בָתִּים הֵן, הַכֵּהֶה בָרִאשׁוֹן, וְהַהוֹלֵךְ לוֹ, קוֹלְפוֹ וְהוּא טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: There are ten [laws concerning the negaim in] houses:(1 + If during the first week a nega became faint or disappeared, it must be scraped and is then clean.

phrases.he: הַכֵּהֶה בַשֵּׁנִי, וְהַהוֹלֵךְ לוֹ, קוֹלְפוֹ וְהוּא טָעוּן צִפֳּרִים.
phrases.en: (3 + If during the second week it became faint or disappeared, it must be scraped and the owner must bring the birds.

phrases.he: הַפּוֹשֶׂה בָרִאשׁוֹן, חוֹלֵץ וְקוֹצֶה וְטָח וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ שָׁבוּעַ. חָזַר, יִנָּתֵץ.
phrases.en: If it spread during the first week, the stones must be taken out and the wall scraped and plastered, and another week must be allowed. If it then returned the entire house must be pulled down; If it did not return, the birds must be brought.

phrases.he: לֹא חָזַר, טָעוּן צִפֳּרִים.
phrases.en: If it remained unchanged during the first week but spread during the second week, the stones must be taken out and the wall scraped and plastered, and another week must be allowed.

phrases.he: עָמַד בָּרִאשׁוֹן וּפָשָׂה בַשֵּׁנִי, חוֹלֵץ וְקוֹצֶה וְטָח וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ שָׁבוּעַ. חָזַר, יִנָּתֵץ.
phrases.en: If it then returned, the house must be pulled down; If it did not return the birds must be brought.

phrases.he: לֹא חָזַר, טָעוּן צִפֳּרִים.
phrases.en: If it remained unchanged in both weeks, the stones must be taken out, and the wall scraped and plastered, and a week must be allowed.

phrases.he: עָמַד בָּזֶה וּבָזֶה, חוֹלֵץ וְקוֹצֶה וְטָח וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ שָׁבוּעַ. חָזַר, יִנָּתֵץ.
phrases.en: If it then returned the house must be pulled down; If it did not return, the birds must be brought.

phrases.he: לֹא חָזַר, טָעוּן צִפֳּרִים.
phrases.en: If before cleanness was attained through the birds a new nega appeared, the house must be pulled down; But if it appeared after cleanness through the birds had been attained, it must be inspected as if it had appeared for the first time.

phrases.he: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא טִהֲרוֹ בַצִּפֳּרִים נִרְאָה בוֹ נֶגַע, הֲרֵי זֶה יִנָּתֵץ.
וְאִם מִשֶּׁטִּהֲרוֹ בַצִּפֳּרִים נִרְאָה בוֹ נֶגַע, יֵרָאֶה בַּתְּחִלָּה
הָאֶבֶן שֶׁבַּזָּוִית, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא חוֹלֵץ, חוֹלֵץ אֶת כֻּלּוֹ.
phrases.en: In the case of a stone in a corner, when the stone is taken out it, he must take it all out; But when [the house is] torn down he tears down his own [part] and leaves that which belongs to his neighbor.

phrases.he: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵץ, נוֹתֵץ אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ וּמַנִּיחַ אֶת שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ.
phrases.en: Thus it follows that there is a greater stringency for taking out than for tearing down.

phrases.he: נִמְצָא חֹמֶר בַּחֲלִיצָה מִבַּנְּתִיצָה.
רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר, בַּיִת הַבָּנוּי רֹאשׁ וּפִתִּין, נִרְאָה בָרֹאשׁ, נוֹטֵל אֶת כֻּלּוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar says: if a house is built of rows of head stones and small stones, and a nega appears on a head stone, all of it must be taken out; but if it appeared on the small stones, he takes out his stones and leaves the others.

phrases.he: נִרְאָה בַפִּתִּין, נוֹטֵל אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ וּמַנִּיחַ אֶת שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ
בַּיִת שֶׁנִּרְאָה בוֹ נֶגַע, הָיְתָה עֲלִיָּה עַל גַּבָּיו, נוֹתֵן אֶת הַקּוֹרוֹת לָעֲלִיָּה.
phrases.en: A house in which a nega appeared if it had an upper chamber above it, the beams are considered part of the upper chamber.

phrases.he: נִרְאָה בָעֲלִיָּה, נוֹתֵן אֶת הַקּוֹרוֹת לַבָּיִת.
phrases.en: If the nega appeared in the upper chamber the beams are considered part of the lower room.

phrases.he: לֹא הָיְתָה עֲלִיָּה עַל גַּבָּיו, אֲבָנָיו וְעֵצָיו וַעֲפָרוֹ נִתָּצִין עִמּוֹ.
phrases.en: If there was no upper chamber above it, its stones and wood and earth must be torn down with it.

phrases.he: וּמַצִּיל עַל הַמַּלְבְּנִים, וְעַל שְׂרִיגֵי הַחַלּוֹנוֹת.
phrases.en: He may save the frames and the window lattices.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מַלְבֵּן הַבָּנוּי עַל גַּבָּיו, נִתָּץ עִמּוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: a frame that is built over the house must be torn down with it.

phrases.he: אֲבָנָיו וְעֵצָיו וַעֲפָרוֹ מְטַמְּאִין בְּכַזַּיִת, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר חִסְמָא אוֹמֵר, בְּמַה שֶּׁהֵן
phrases.en: Its stones and wood and earth convey uncleanness if they are of the minimum size of an olive. Rabbi Eliezer Hisma says: whatever their size.

phrases.he: בַּיִת הַמֻּסְגָּר, מְטַמֵּא מִתּוֹכוֹ. וְהַמֻּחְלָט, מִתּוֹכוֹ וּמֵאֲחוֹרָיו.
phrases.en: A house that has been isolated conveys uncleanness from its inside; And one that has been certified unclean, both from its inside and from its outside.

phrases.he: זֶה וָזֶה מְטַמְּאִין בְּבִיאָה
phrases.en: Both convey uncleanness if one enters in.

phrases.he: הַבּוֹנֶה מִן הַמֻּסְגָּר בְּטָהוֹר, וְחָזַר נֶגַע לַבַּיִת, חוֹלֵץ אֶת הָאֲבָנִים.
phrases.en: If one who builds in cleanliness with stones from a house that was isolated and the nega returned to the [former] house, the stones must be taken out.

phrases.he: חָזַר עַל הָאֲבָנִים, הַבַּיִת הָרִאשׁוֹן יִנָּתֵץ, וְהָאֲבָנִים יְשַׁמְּשׁוּ אֶת הַבַּיִת הַשֵּׁנִי בְּסִימָנִין
phrases.en: If it returned to the stones, the first house must be torn down, and the stones serve the second house while the signs are under observation.

phrases.he: בַּיִת שֶׁהוּא מֵסֵךְ עַל גַּבֵּי בַיִת הַמְנֻגָּע, וְכֵן אִילָן שֶׁהוּא מֵסֵךְ עַל גַּבֵּי בַיִת הַמְנֻגָּע, הַנִּכְנָס לַחִיצוֹן, טָהוֹר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.en: If a house overshadowed a house with a nega and so also if a tree overshadowed a house with a nega, anyone who enters the outer [of the two] remains clean, the words of Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, מָה אִם אֶבֶן אַחַת מִמֶּנּוּ מְטַמָּא בְּבִיאָה, הוּא עַצְמוֹ לֹא יְטַמֵּא בְּבִיאָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar said: if one stone of it causes uncleanness by entering, should not the house itself cause uncleanness by entering?

phrases.he: הַטָּמֵא עוֹמֵד תַּחַת הָאִילָן וְהַטָּהוֹר עוֹבֵר, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If an unclean person stood under a tree and a clean person passed by, the latter becomes unclean.

phrases.he: הַטָּהוֹר עוֹמֵד תַּחַת הָאִילָן וְהַטָּמֵא עוֹבֵר, טָהוֹר. אִם עָמַד, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If a clean person stood under a tree and an unclean one passed by, the former remains clean. If the latter stood still, the former becomes unclean.

phrases.he: וְכֵן בְּאֶבֶן הַמְנֻגַּעַת, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Similarly in the case of a leprous stone he remains clean.

phrases.he: וְאִם הִנִּיחָהּ, הֲרֵי זֶה טָמֵא
phrases.en: But if it was set down he becomes unclean.

phrases.he: טָהוֹר שֶׁהִכְנִיס רֹאשׁוֹ וְרֻבּוֹ לְבַיִת טָמֵא, נִטְמָא.
phrases.en: If a person who was clean put his head and the greater part of his body inside an unclean house, he becomes unclean.

phrases.he: וְטָמֵא שֶׁהִכְנִיס רֹאשׁוֹ וְרֻבּוֹ לְבַיִת טָהוֹר, טִמְּאָהוּ.
phrases.en: And if an unclean man put his head and the greater part of his body inside a clean house he causes it to be unclean.

phrases.he: טַלִּית טְהוֹרָה שֶׁהִכְנִיס מִמֶּנָּה שָׁלשׁ עַל שָׁלשׁ לְבַיִת טָמֵא, נִטְמְאָה.
phrases.en: If he put three fingerbreadths square of a clean cloak into an unclean house, the cloak becomes unclean; And if he put even the size of an olive of an unclean [cloak] into a clean house, the house becomes unclean.

phrases.he: וּטְמֵאָה שֶׁהִכְנִיס מִמֶּנָּה אֲפִלּוּ כַזַּיִת לְבַיִת טָהוֹר, טִמְּאַתּוּ
מִי שֶׁנִּכְנַס לְבַיִת הַמְנֻגָּע וְכֵלָיו עַל כְּתֵפוֹ וְסַנְדָּלָיו וְטַבְּעוֹתָיו בְּיָדָיו, הוּא וָהֵן טְמֵאִין מִיָּד.
phrases.en: If a person entered a house afflicted with a nega, carrying his clothes upon his shoulders, and his sandals and rings in his hands, both he and they become unclean immediately.

phrases.he: הָיָה לָבוּשׁ בְּכֵלָיו וְסַנְדָּלָיו בְּרַגְלָיו וְטַבְּעוֹתָיו בְּיָדָיו, הוּא טָמֵא מִיָּד, וְהֵן טְהוֹרִין עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁהֶה כְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס.
phrases.en: If, however, he was wearing his clothes and had his sandals on his feet and his rings on his hands, he becomes unclean immediately, but they remain clean, unless he stayed as much time as is required for the eating of half a loaf of wheat bread and not of barley bread, while in a reclining posture and eating with some condiment.

phrases.he: פַּת חִטִּין וְלֹא פַת שְׂעֹרִים, מֵסֵב וְאוֹכְלָן בְּלִפְתָּן
הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּפְנִים וּפָשַׁט יָדוֹ לַחוּץ וְטַבְּעוֹתָיו בְּיָדָיו, אִם שָׁהָה כְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס, טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: If he was standing inside, and he stretched his hands outside, with his rings on his hands, if he stayed [inside] as much time as is required for the eating of half a loaf, they become unclean.

phrases.he: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בַּחוּץ וּפָשַׁט יָדוֹ לִפְנִים וְטַבְּעוֹתָיו בְּיָדָיו, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַמֵּא מִיָּד.
וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁהֶה כְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס.
phrases.en: If he was standing outside, stretching his hands inside, with his rings on his hands: Rabbi Judah says that they are unclean immediately, But the sages say: only after he leaves them there as much time as is required for the eating of half a loaf.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, מָה אִם בִּזְמַן שֶׁכָּל גּוּפוֹ טָמֵא, לֹא טִמֵּא אֶת מַה שֶּׁעָלָיו עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁהֶה כְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס, בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין כָּל גּוּפוֹ טָמֵא, אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁלֹּא יְטַמֵּא אֶת מַה שֶּׁעָלָיו עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁהֶה כְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס:
phrases.en: They said to Rabbi Judah: if when all his body is unclean he does not render that which is on him unclean unless he stayed there long enough to eat half a loaf, when all of his body is not unclean, is it not logical that he should not render that which is on him unclean unless he stayed there long enough to eat half a loaf?

phrases.he: מְצֹרָע שֶׁנִּכְנַס לְבַיִת, כָּל הַכֵּלִים שֶׁיֶּשׁ שָׁם טְמֵאִין, אֲפִלּוּ עַד הַקּוֹרוֹת.
phrases.en: If a metzora entered a house all the vessels in it, even up to the roof beams, become unclean. Rabbi Shimon says: only up to a height of four cubits.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, עַד אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת. כֵּלִים, מִיָּד טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: Vessels become unclean immediately.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם שָׁהָה כְדֵי הַדְלָקַת הַנֵּר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: only if the metzora stayed there as much time as is required for the lighting of a lamp.

phrases.he: נִכְנַס לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת, עוֹשִׂים לוֹ מְחִצָּה גְבוֹהָה עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים עַל רֹחַב אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.en: If he enters a synagogue, a partition ten handbreadths high and four cubits wide must be made for him. He should enter first and come out last.

phrases.he: נִכְנָס רִאשׁוֹן, וְיוֹצֵא אַחֲרוֹן.
phrases.en: Any vessel that affords protection by having a tightly fitting cover in the tent of a corpse affords protection by a tightly fitting cover in the house of one afflicted by a nega, And whatsoever affords protection when covered in the tent of a corpse affords protection when covered in the house of one afflicted with a nega, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: כֹּל הַמַּצִּיל צָמִיד פָּתִיל בְּאֹהֶל הַמֵּת, מַצִּיל צָמִיד פָּתִיל בְּבַיִת הַמְנֻגָּע.
וְכֹל הַמַּצִּיל מְכֻסֶּה בְאֹהֶל הַמֵּת, מַצִּיל מְכֻסֶּה בְּבַיִת הַמְנֻגָּע, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, כֹּל הַמַּצִּיל צָמִיד פָּתִיל בְּאֹהֶל הַמֵּת, מַצִּיל מְכֻסֶּה בְּבַיִת הַמְנֻגָּע.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: any vessel that affords protection by having a tightly fitting cover in the tent of a corpse affords protection when covered in the house of one afflicted with a nega; and whatsoever affords protection when covered in the tent of a corpse remains clean even when uncovered in a leprous house.

phrases.he: כֹּל הַמַּצִּיל מְכֻסֶּה בְאֹהֶל הַמֵּת, אֲפִלּוּ מְגֻלֶּה בְּבַיִת הַמְנֻגָּע, טָהוֹר
כֵּיצַד מְטַהֲרִין אֶת הַמְּצֹרָע.
phrases.en: How would they purify a metzora?A new earthenware flask and a quarter of a log of living water was put in it.

phrases.he: הָיָה מֵבִיא פְיָלִי שֶׁל חֶרֶשׂ חֲדָשָׁה וְנוֹתֵן לְתוֹכָהּ רְבִיעִית מַיִם חַיִּים, וּמֵבִיא שְׁתֵּי צִפֳּרִים דְּרוֹר.
phrases.en: Two undomesticated birds are also brought. One of these was slaughtered over the earthenware vessel and over the living water.

phrases.he: שָׁחַט אֶת אַחַת מֵהֶן עַל כְּלִי חֶרֶשׂ וְעַל מַיִם חַיִּים. חָפַר וְקוֹבְרָהּ בְּפָנָיו.
phrases.en: A hole was dug and it was buried in his presence.

phrases.he: נָטַל עֵץ אֶרֶז וְאֵזוֹב וּשְׁנִי תוֹלַעַת וּכְרָכָן בִּשְׁיָרֵי הַלָּשׁוֹן, וְהִקִּיף לָהֶם רָאשֵׁי אֲגַפַּיִם וְרֹאשׁ הַזָּנָב שֶׁל שְׁנִיָּה.
phrases.en: Cedarwood, hyssop and scarlet wool were taken and bound together with the remaining ends of the strip of wool. Near to these were brought the tips of the wings and the tip of the tail of the second bird.

phrases.he: טָבַל וְהִזָּה שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים לְאַחַר יָדוֹ שֶׁל מְצֹרָע, וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים, עַל מִצְחוֹ.
phrases.en: All were dipped together, and sprinkled upon the back of the metzora's hand seven times. Some say that the sprinkling was done upon his forehead.

phrases.he: וְכָךְ הָיָה מַזֶּה עַל הַשְּׁקוֹף שֶׁבַּבַּיִת מִבַּחוּץ
phrases.en: In the same manner one would sprinkle on the lintel of a house from the outside.

phrases.he: בָּא לוֹ לְשַׁלֵּחַ אֶת הַצִּפּוֹר הַחַיָּה, אֵינוֹ הוֹפֵךְ פָּנָיו לֹא לַיָּם וְלֹא לָעִיר וְלֹא לַמִּדְבָּר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ויקרא יד), וְשִׁלַּח אֶת הַצִּפֹּר הַחַיָּה אֶל מִחוּץ לָעִיר אֶל פְּנֵי הַשָּׂדֶה.
phrases.en: He now comes to set free the living bird. He does not turn his face towards the sea or towards the city or towards the wilderness, for it is said, "But he shall let the living bird go out of the city into the open field" (Leviticus 14:53). He now comes to shave off the hair of the metzora.

phrases.he: בָּא לְגַלֵּחַ אֶת הַמְּצֹרָע, הֶעֱבִיר תַּעַר עַל כָּל בְּשָׂרוֹ, וְכִבֵּס בְּגָדָיו, וְטָבַל, טָהוֹר מִלְּטַמֵּא בְּבִיאָה, וַהֲרֵי הוּא מְטַמֵּא כַשֶּׁרֶץ.
phrases.en: He passes a razor over the whole of his skin, and he [the metzora] washes his clothes and immerses himself. He is then clean so far as to not convey uncleanness by entrance, but he still conveys uncleanness as does a sheretz.

phrases.he: נִכְנַס לִפְנִים מִן הַחוֹמָה, מְנֻדֶּה מִבֵּיתוֹ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים, וְאָסוּר בְּתַשְׁמִישׁ הַמִּטָּה
phrases.en: He may enter within the walls [of Jerusalem], but must keep away from his house for seven days, and he is forbidden to have intercourse.

phrases.he: בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי מְגַלֵּחַ תִּגְלַחַת שְׁנִיָּה כַּתִּגְלַחַת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, כִּבֶּס בְּגָדָיו וְטָבַל, טָהוֹר מִלְּטַמֵּא כַשֶּׁרֶץ, וַהֲרֵי הוּא טְבוּל יוֹם, אוֹכֵל בַּמַּעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.en: On the seventh day he shaves off his hair a second time in the manner of the first shaving, he washes his garments and immerses himself. He is clean in so far as not to convey uncleanness as a sheretz, but he was still like a tevul yom. He may eat second tithe. After sunset he may eat terumah.

phrases.he: הֶעֱרִיב שִׁמְשׁוֹ, אוֹכֵל בַּתְּרוּמָה.
phrases.en: After he had brought his offering of atonement, he may also eat sacred things.

phrases.he: הֵבִיא כַפָּרָתוֹ, אוֹכֵל בַּקָּדָשִׁים.
phrases.en: Thus there are three grades in the purification of a metzora and three grades in the purification of a woman after child birth.

phrases.he: נִמְצְאוּ שָׁלשׁ טְהָרוֹת בַּמְּצֹרָע וְשָׁלשׁ טְהָרוֹת בַּיּוֹלֶדֶת
שְׁלשָׁה מְגַלְּחִין וְתִגְלַחְתָּן מִצְוָה, הַנָּזִיר וְהַמְּצֹרָע וְהַלְוִיִּם.
phrases.en: There are three who must shave their hair, and their shaving of it is a commandment: the nazirite, the metzora, and the Levites.

phrases.he: וְכֻלָּן שֶׁגִּלְּחוּ שֶׁלֹּא בְתַעַר אוֹ שֶׁשִּׁיְּרוּ שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת, לֹא עָשׂוּ כְלוּם
phrases.en: If any of these cut their hair but not with a razor, or if they left even two remaining hairs, their act is of no validity.

phrases.he: שְׁתֵּי צִפֳּרִים מִצְוָתָן שֶׁיְּהוּ שָׁווֹת בַּמַּרְאֶה וּבַקּוֹמָה וּבַדָּמִים, וּלְקִיחָתָן כְּאֶחָת.
phrases.en: With regard to the two birds: the commandment is that they be alike in appearance, in size and in price; and they must be purchased at the same time.

phrases.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָם שָׁווֹת, כְּשֵׁרוֹת.
phrases.en: But even if they are not alike they are valid; And if one was purchased on one day and the other the next they are also valid.

phrases.he: לָקַח אַחַת הַיּוֹם וְאַחַת לְמָחָר, כְּשֵׁרוֹת.
phrases.en: If after one of the birds had been slaughtered it was found that it was not wild, a partner must be purchased for the second, and the first may be eaten.

phrases.he: שָׁחַט אַחַת מֵהֶן וְנִמְצֵאת שֶׁלֹּא דְרוֹר, יִקַּח זוּג לַשְּׁנִיָּה. הָרִאשׁוֹנָה מֻתֶּרֶת בַּאֲכִילָה.
phrases.en: If after it had been slaughtered it was found to terefah, a partner must be purchased for the second and the first may be made use of.

phrases.he: שְׁחָטָהּ וְנִמְצֵאת טְרֵפָה, יִקַּח זוּג לַשְּׁנִיָּה. הָרִאשׁוֹנָה מֻתֶּרֶת בַּהֲנָאָה.
phrases.en: If the blood had been spilled out, the bird that was to be let go must be left to die.

phrases.he: נִשְׁפַּךְ הַדָּם, תָּמוּת הַמִּשְׁתַּלַּחַת.
phrases.en: If the one that was to be let go died, the blood must be spilled out.

phrases.he: מֵתָה הַמִּשְׁתַּלַּחַת, יִשָּׁפֵךְ הַדָּם
מִצְוַת עֵץ אֶרֶז, אָרְכּוֹ אַמָּה וְעָבְיוֹ כִרְבִיעַ כֶּרַע הַמִּטָּה.
phrases.en: The mitzvah of the cedarwood is for it to be one cubit in length, and in thickness a quarter of that of the leg of a bed, when one leg is divided into two halves and these two into four.

phrases.he: אֶחָד לִשְׁנַיִם, וּשְׁנַיִם לְאַרְבָּעָה.
phrases.en: The mitzvah of the hyssop is that it should be neither ezovyon (lavendula) nor blue hyssop nor Roman hyssop nor wild hyssop nor any kind of hyssop that has an accompanying name.

phrases.he: מִצְוַת אֵזוֹב, לֹא אֵזוֹב יָוָן, לֹא אֵזוֹב כּוֹחֲלִי, לֹא אֵזוֹב רוֹמִי, לֹא אֵזוֹב מִדְבָּרִית, וְלֹא כָל אֵזוֹב שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ שֵׁם לְוָי
בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי מֵבִיא שָׁלשׁ בְּהֵמוֹת, חַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם וְעוֹלָה.
phrases.en: On the eighth day he would bring three beasts: a sin-offering, a guilt-offering and a whole burnt-offering.

phrases.he: וְהַדַּל הָיָה מֵבִיא חַטַּאת הָעוֹף וְעוֹלַת הָעוֹף
phrases.en: And a poor man would bring a sin-offering of a bird and a burnt-offering of a bird.

phrases.he: בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל הָאָשָׁם, וְסָמַךְ שְׁתֵּי יָדָיו עָלָיו, וּשְׁחָטוֹ, וְקִבְּלוּ שְׁנֵי כֹהֲנִים אֶת דָּמוֹ, אֶחָד בִּכְלִי, וְאֶחָד בַּיָּד.
phrases.en: He comes to the guilt-offering and he puts his two hands on it. He then slaughters it. Two priests receive its blood, one in a vessel and the other in his hand.

phrases.he: זֶה שֶׁקִּבֵּל בַּכְּלִי, בָּא וּזְרָקוֹ עַל קִיר הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
phrases.en: He who received it in the vessel proceeded to sprinkle it on the wall of the altar.

phrases.he: וְזֶה שֶׁקִּבֵּל בַּיָּד, בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל הַמְּצֹרָע.
phrases.en: The one who received it in his hand would approach the metzora.

phrases.he: וְהַמְּצֹרָע טָבַל בְּלִשְׁכַּת הַמְּצֹרָעִים.
phrases.en: The metzora had in the meantime immersed himself in the chamber of the metzoraim.

phrases.he: בָּא וְעָמַד בְּשַׁעַר נִקָּנוֹר.
phrases.en: He would come and stand at the Nikanor gate.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ טְבִילָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: he did not require immersion.

phrases.he: הִכְנִיס רֹאשׁוֹ, וְנָתַן עַל תְּנוּךְ אָזְנוֹ.
phrases.en: [The metzora] put in his head inside and [the priest] applied [the blood] to the tip of his ear; [He put in] his hand and [the priest] applied [the blood] to the thumb of his hand.

phrases.he: יָדוֹ, וְנָתַן עַל בֹּהֶן יָדוֹ.
רַגְלוֹ, וְנָתַן עַל בֹּהֶן רַגְלוֹ.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, שְׁלָשְׁתָּם הָיָה מַכְנִיס כְּאֶחָד.
phrases.en: [He put in] his foot and [the priest] applied [the blood] to the big toe of his foot.

phrases.he: אֵין לוֹ בֹּהֶן יָד, בֹּהֶן רֶגֶל, אֹזֶן יְמָנִית, אֵין לוֹ טָהֳרָה עוֹלָמִית.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: he put in all three at the same time. If he had no thumb on his hand or no big toe on his foot or no right ear he could never become clean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, נוֹתֵן הוּא עַל מְקוֹמָן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: [the blood] is applied to the place where they were.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אִם נָתַן עַל שֶׁל שְׂמֹאל, יָצָא:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: if he applied it to the left side, the obligation has been fulfilled.

phrases.he: נָטַל מִלֹּג הַשֶּׁמֶן וְיָצַק לְתוֹךְ כַּפּוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ.
phrases.en: [The priest] then took some [of the contents] of the log of oil and poured it into his colleague's hand; And if he poured it into his own hand, the obligation is fulfilled.

phrases.he: וְאִם יָצַק לְתוֹךְ כַּף עַצְמוֹ, יָצָא.
phrases.en: He then dipped [his right forefinger] in the oil and sprinkled it seven times towards the Holy of Holies, dipping it for every sprinkling.

phrases.he: טָבַל וְהִזָּה שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים, עַל כָּל הַזָּיָה טְבִילָה.
phrases.en: He then approached the metzora, to the same places that he applied the blood he now applied the oil, as it is said, "Over the same places as the blood of the guilt offering; 29 and what is left of the oil in his palm the priest shall put on the head of the one being cleansed, to make expiation for him before the Lord.

phrases.he: בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל הַמְּצֹרָע, מְקוֹם שֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן אֶת הַדָּם, שָׁם הוּא נוֹתֵן אֶת הַשֶּׁמֶן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ויקרא יד), עַל מְקוֹם דַּם הָאָשָׁם.
phrases.en: (Leviticus 14:28-29).

phrases.he: וְהַנּוֹתָר מִן הַשֶּׁמֶן אֲשֶׁר עַל כַּף הַכֹּהֵן יִתֵּן עַל רֹאשׁ הַמִּטַּהֵר לְכַפֵּר. אִם נָתַן, כִּפֵּר.
phrases.en: If he "put upon," he has made atonement, but if he did not "put upon," he did not make atonement, the words of Rabbi Akiba.

phrases.he: וְאִם לֹא נָתַן, לֹא כִפֵּר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri says: these are but the remainders of the mitzvah.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר, שְׁיָרֵי מִצְוָה הֵן, בֵּין שֶׁנָּתַן בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן, כִּפֵּר, וּמַעֲלִין עָלָיו כְּאִלּוּ לֹא כִפֵּר.
phrases.en: Whether he "put upon" or did not "put upon," atonement is made, only it is accounted to him as if he did not make atonement.

phrases.he: חָסַר הַלֹּג עַד שֶׁלֹּא יָצַק, יְמַלְאֶנּוּ.
phrases.en: If any oil was missing from the log before it was poured out it may be filled up again; if after it was poured out, other oil must be brought anew, the words of Rabbi Akiva.

phrases.he: מִשֶּׁיָּצַק, יָבִיא אַחֵר בַּתְּחִלָּה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, חָסַר הַלֹּג עַד שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן, יְמַלְאֶנּוּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: if any oil was missing from the log before it was applied, it may be filled up; but if after it had been applied, other oil must be brought anew.

phrases.he: מִשֶּׁנָּתַן, יָבִיא אַחֵר בַּתְּחִלָּה
מְצֹרָע שֶׁהֵבִיא קָרְבָּנוֹ עָנִי וְהֶעֱשִׁיר, אוֹ עָשִׁיר וְהֶעֱנִי, הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר חַטָּאת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.en: If a metzora brought his sacrifice as a poor man and he became rich, or as a rich man and he became poor, all depends on the sin-offering, the words of Rabbi Shimon.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַחַר הָאָשָׁם:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: all depends on the guilt-offering.

phrases.he: מְצֹרָע עָנִי שֶׁהֵבִיא קָרְבַּן עָשִׁיר, יָצָא.
phrases.en: A poor metzora who brought the sacrifice of a rich man has fulfilled his duty; But a rich metzora that brought the sacrifice of a poor man has not fulfilled his duty.

phrases.he: וְעָשִׁיר שֶׁהֵבִיא קָרְבַּן עָנִי, לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.en: A man may bring a poor man's sacrifice for his son, his daughter, his slave or his female, and thereby enable them to eat of the offerings.

phrases.he: מֵבִיא אָדָם עַל יְדֵי בְנוֹ, עַל יְדֵי בִתּוֹ, עַל יְדֵי עַבְדּוֹ וְשִׁפְחָתוֹ קָרְבַּן עָנִי, וּמַאֲכִילָן בַּזְּבָחִים.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף עַל יְדֵי אִשְׁתּוֹ מֵבִיא קָרְבַּן עָשִׁיר, וְכֵן כָּל קָרְבָּן שֶׁהִיא חַיָּבֶת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: for his wife also he must bring the sacrifice of a rich man; and the same applies to any other sacrifice to which she is liable.

phrases.he: שְׁנֵי מְצֹרָעִים שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ קָרְבְּנוֹתֵיהֶם, קָרַב קָרְבָּנוֹ שֶׁל אַחַד מֵהֶם, וּמֵת אַחַד מֵהֶם, זוֹ שֶׁשָּׁאֲלוּ אַנְשֵׁי אֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִיָּא אֶת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
phrases.en: If the sacrifices of two metzoraim were mixed up and after the sacrifice of one of them had been offered one of the metzoraim died: this is what the men of Alexandria asked of Rabbi Joshua.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, יִכְתֹּב נְכָסָיו לְאַחֵר וְיָבִיא קָרְבַּן עָנִי:
phrases.en: He answered them: let him assign his possessions to another person, and bring the poor man's sacrifice.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, עֶגְלָה, בַּת שְׁנָתָהּ. וּפָרָה, בַּת שְׁתַּיִם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: the heifer is no more than one year old and the cow no more than two years old.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, עֶגְלָה, בַּת שְׁתַּיִם.
phrases.en: But the sages ruled: the heifer may be even two years old and the red cow even three or four years old.

phrases.he: וּפָרָה, בַּת שָׁלשׁ אוֹ בַת אַרְבַּע.
רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, אַף בַּת חָמֵשׁ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: even five years old, though she is old.

phrases.he: כְּשֵׁרָה הַזְּקֵנָה, אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין מַמְתִּינִין לָהּ, שֶׁמָּא תַשְׁחִיר, שֶׁלֹּא תִפָּסֵל.
phrases.en: But they did not wait with it so long since it might in the meantime grow some black hairs and [thus] become invalid.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי אֶלָּא שְׁלָשִׁית.
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua said: I only heard of [a cow] that was three years old [shelashit].

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, מַה הַלָּשׁוֹן שְׁלָשִׁית.
phrases.en: They said to him: What does "shelashit" mean? He replied: thus have I heard it without any explanation.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, כָּךְ שָׁמַעְתִּי סְתָם.
phrases.en: Ben Azzai said: I will explain: if you say "shelishit" the meaning is ‘the third’ in number to others, but when you say "shelashit" the meaning is one that is three years old.

phrases.he: אָמַר בֶּן עַזַּאי, אֲנִי אֲפָרֵשׁ.
phrases.en: Similarly they said a vineyard that is "revai.

phrases.he: אִם אוֹמֵר אַתָּה, שְׁלִישִׁית, לַאֲחֵרוֹת בְּמִנְיָן.
וּכְשֶׁאַתָּה אוֹמֵר, שְׁלָשִׁית, בַּת שָׁלשׁ שָׁנִים.
כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ אָמְרוּ, כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי.
אָמְרוּ לוֹ, מַה הַלָּשׁוֹן רְבָעִי.
phrases.en: They said to him: what does "revai" mean? He replied: thus have I heard it without any explanation.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, כָּךְ שָׁמַעְתִּי סְתָם.
phrases.en: Ben Azzai said: I will explain: if you say "revii" the meaning is the fourth in number to others, but when you say "revai" the meaning is one that is four years old.

phrases.he: אָמַר בֶּן עַזַּאי, אֲנִי אֲפָרֵשׁ.
phrases.en: Similarly it was ruled: if a man ate in an afflicted house half a loaf, three of which can be made from a kav, he becomes unclean.

phrases.he: אִם אוֹמֵר אַתָּה, רְבִיעִי, לַאֲחֵרִים בְּמִנְיָן.
וּכְשֶׁאַתָּה אוֹמֵר, רְבָעִי, בֶּן אַרְבַּע שָׁנִים.
כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ אָמְרוּ, הָאוֹכֵל בְּבַיִת הַמְנֻגָּע פְּרָס, מִשָּׁלשׁ לְקָב.
אָמְרוּ לוֹ, אֱמֹר מִשְּׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה לִסְאָה.
phrases.en: They said to him: say rather "eighteen of which are made of a se'ah.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, כָּךְ שָׁמַעְתִּי סְתָם.
phrases.en: He replied: thus have I heard it without any explanation.

phrases.he: אָמַר בֶּן עַזַּאי, אֲנִי אֲפָרֵשׁ.
phrases.en: Ben Azzai said: I will explain: when you say, three of which are made of a kav it would not contain hallah, but if you say, eighteen of which are made of a se'ah, it has been reduced by its hallah.

phrases.he: אִם אוֹמֵר אַתָּה מִשָּׁלשׁ לְקָב, אֵין בּוֹ חַלָּה.
וּכְשֶׁאַתָּה אוֹמֵר, מִשְּׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה לִסְאָה, מִעֲטַתּוּ חַלָּתוֹ
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר, פָּרִים, בְּנֵי שְׁתַּיִם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (במדבר ח), וּפַר שֵׁנִי בֶן בָּקָר תִּקַּח לְחַטָּאת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose the Galilean said: bulls must be no more than two years old, for it is said, "And the second bull you shall take for a sin-offering" (Numbers 8:8).

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אַף בְּנֵי שָׁלשׁ.
phrases.en: But the sages say: they may be even three years old.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, אַף בְּנֵי אַרְבַּע וּבְנֵי חָמֵשׁ כְּשֵׁרִים, אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין מְבִיאִים זְקֵנִים, מִפְּנֵי הַכָּבוֹד:
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: even those that are four or five years old are valid, but old animals are not brought out of respect.

phrases.he: כְּבָשִׂים, בְּנֵי שָׁנָה. וְאֵילִים, בְּנֵי שְׁתַּיִם. וְכֻלָּם מִיּוֹם לְיוֹם.
phrases.en: Lambs no more than one year old, And rams no more than two years old.

phrases.he: בֶּן שְׁלשָׁה עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ אֵינוֹ כָשֵׁר לֹא לְאַיִל וְלֹא לְכֶבֶשׂ.
phrases.en: And all these years are reckoned from day to day. One that is thirteen months old is not valid, neither as a ram nor as a lamb.

phrases.he: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן קוֹרֵהוּ פַּלְגָּס.
phrases.en: Rabbi Tarfon called it palges.

phrases.he: בֶּן עַזַּאי קוֹרֵהוּ נוֹקֵד.
phrases.en: Ben Azzai called it noked.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל קוֹרֵהוּ פַּרְכָדִיגְמָא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Ishmael called it parakhrigma.

phrases.he: הִקְרִיבוֹ, מֵבִיא עָלָיו נִסְכֵּי אַיִל, וְלֹא עָלָה לוֹ מִזִּבְחוֹ.
phrases.en: If a man offered it he must bring for it the libation of a ram, but it is not counted as his offering.

phrases.he: בֶּן שְׁלשָׁה עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ וְיוֹם אֶחָד, הֲרֵי זֶה אָיִל
phrases.en: One that is thirteen months old behold it is a ram.

phrases.he: חַטֹּאת הַצִּבּוּר וְעוֹלוֹתֵיהֶן, חַטַּאת הַיָּחִיד וַאֲשַׁם נָזִיר וַאֲשַׁם מְצֹרָע, כְּשֵׁרִין מִיּוֹם שְׁלשִׁים וָהָלְאָה, וְאַף בְּיוֹם שְׁלשִׁים.
phrases.en: The sin-offerings of the congregation and their burnt-offerings, the sin-offering of an individual, the guilt-offering of a nazirite and the guilt-offering of a metzora are valid from the thirtieth day onwards, and also on the thirtieth day.

phrases.he: וְאִם הִקְרִיבוּם בְּיוֹם שְׁמִינִי, כְּשֵׁרִים.
phrases.en: If they were offered on the eighth day they are valid.

phrases.he: נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת, הַבְּכוֹר וְהַמַּעֲשֵׂר וְהַפֶּסַח, כְּשֵׁרִים מִיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי וָהָלְאָה, וְאַף בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי
phrases.en: Vow-offerings and freewill-offerings, firstlings and the tithe of cattle and the pesach are valid from the eighth day onwards, and also on the eighth day.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, פָּרַת חַטָּאת הַמְעֻבֶּרֶת, כְּשֵׁרָה. וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹסְלִין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: a [red] cow for the hatat that is pregnant is valid, But the sages say: it is invalid.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אֵינָהּ נִלְקַחַת מִן הַנָּכְרִים. וַחֲכָמִים מַכְשִׁירִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: it may not be bought from non-Jews, But the sages say: it is valid.

phrases.he: וְלֹא זוֹ בִלְבַד, אֶלָּא כָל קָרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּבּוּר וְהַיָּחִיד בָּאִין מֵהָאָרֶץ וּמִחוּץ לָאָרֶץ, מִן הֶחָדָשׁ וּמִן הַיָּשָׁן, חוּץ מִן הָעֹמֶר וּשְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם שֶׁאֵינָן בָּאִין אֶלָּא מִן הֶחָדָשׁ וּמִן הָאָרֶץ:
phrases.en: And not only this, but all sacrifices of the congregation or the individual may be brought from the land of Israel and from outside the land, from new produce and from the old; Except the omer and the two loaves, which may be brought only from new produce and from within the land.

phrases.he: פָּרָה שֶׁקַּרְנֶיהָ וּטְלָפֶיהָ שְׁחוֹרִים, יָגֹד.
phrases.en: If the horns or the hoofs of the [red] cow are black they are chopped off.

phrases.he: גַּלְגַּל הָעַיִן וְהַשִּׁנַּיִם וְהַלָּשׁוֹן אֵינָם פּוֹסְלִים בַּפָּרָה. וְהַנַּנֶּסֶת, כְּשֵׁרָה.
phrases.en: The eye ball, the teeth and the tongue cause do not invalidate the [red] cow. One that is dwarf-like is valid.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה בָהּ יַבֶּלֶת וַחֲתָכָהּ, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה פוֹסֵל.
phrases.en: If there was on it an extra digit and it was cut off: Rabbi Judah says that it is invalid.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, כָּל מְקוֹם שֶׁנִּטַּל וְלֹא הֶעֱלָה מְקוֹמוֹ שֵׂעָר אָדֹם, פְּסוּלָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: wherever, if removed, no red hair grows in its place is it invalid.

phrases.he: יוֹצֵא דֹפֶן וְאֶתְנָן וּמְחִיר, פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.en: One that is born from the side, the hire of a harlot or the price of a dog is invalid.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מַכְשִׁיר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים כג), לֹא תָבִיא אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה וּמְחִיר כֶּלֶב בֵּית ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ, וְאֵין זוֹ בָאָה לַבָּיִת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says that it is valid, as it says, "You shall not bring the hire of a harlot or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord your God," (Deuteronomy 23:19) and this was not brought into the house.

phrases.he: כָּל הַמּוּמִים הַפּוֹסְלִים בַּמֻּקְדָּשִׁים, פּוֹסְלִים בַּפָּרָה.
phrases.en: All blemishes that cause consecrated animals to be invalid cause also the [red] cow to be invalid.

phrases.he: רָכַב עָלֶיהָ, נִשְׁעַן עָלֶיהָ, נִתְלָה בִזְנָבָהּ, עָבַר בָּהּ אֶת הַנָּהָר, קִפֵּל עָלֶיהָ אֶת הַמּוֹסֵרָה, נָתַן טַלִּיתוֹ עָלֶיהָ, פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.en: If one had ridden on it, leaned on it, hung on its tail, crossed a river by its help, doubled up its leading rope, or put one's cloak on it, it is invalid.

phrases.he: אֲבָל קְשָׁרָהּ בַּמּוֹסֵרָה, עָשָׂה לָהּ סַנְדָּל בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא תַחֲלִיק, פָּרַס טַלִּיתוֹ עָלֶיהָ מִפְּנֵי הַזְּבוּבִים, כְּשֵׁרָה.
phrases.en: But if one had only tied it up by its leading rope or made for it a sandal to prevent it from slipping or spread one's cloak on it because of flies, it is valid.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כֹּל שֶׁהוּא לְצָרְכָּהּ, כְּשֵׁרָה. לְצֹרֶךְ אַחֵר, פְּסוּלָה
phrases.en: This is the general rule: wherever anything is done for its own sake, it remains valid; but if for the sake of another, it becomes invalid.

phrases.he: שָׁכַן עָלֶיהָ עוֹף, כְּשֵׁרָה.
phrases.en: If a bird rested on it, it remains valid.

phrases.he: עָלָה עָלֶיהָ זָכָר, פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.en: If a male beast mounted it, it becomes invalid.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם הֶעֱלָהוּ, פְּסוּלָה. וְאִם מֵעַצְמוֹ, כְּשֵׁרָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: if the male was made to mount, it becomes invalid; but if it did so of itself, it remains valid.

phrases.he: הָיוּ בָהּ שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת שְׁחוֹרוֹת אוֹ לְבָנוֹת בְּתוֹךְ גֻּמָּא אַחַת, פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.en: If it had two black or white hairs growing within one follicle, it is invalid.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ בְתוֹךְ כּוֹס אֶחָד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah said: within one kos; if they grew within two kosot that were adjacent to one another, it is invalid.

phrases.he: הָיוּ בְתוֹךְ שְׁנֵי כוֹסוֹת וְהֵן מוֹכִיחוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ, פְּסוּלָה.
רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ אַרְבַּע, אֲפִלּוּ חָמֵשׁ, וְהֵן מְפֻזָּרוֹת, יִתְלֹשׁ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: even if there were four or five but they were dispersed, they may be plucked out.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ חֲמִשִּׁים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: even as many as fifty.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ אַחַת בְּרֹאשָׁהּ וְאַחַת בִּזְנָבָהּ, פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua ben Batera says: even if it had but one on its head and one on its tail, it is invalid.

phrases.he: הָיוּ בָהּ שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת, עִקָּרָן מַשְׁחִיר וְרֹאשָׁן מַאְדִּים, עִקָּרָן מַאְדִּים וְרֹאשָׁן מַשְׁחִיר, הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַנִּרְאֶה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: If it had two hairs with their roots black and their tips red or with their roots red and their tips black, everything goes according to what is visible, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אַחַר הָעִקָּר:
phrases.en: But the sages say: by the root.

phrases.he: שִׁבְעַת יָמִים קֹדֶם לִשְׂרֵפַת הַפָּרָה מַפְרִישִׁין כֹּהֵן הַשּׂוֹרֵף אֶת הַפָּרָה מִבֵּיתוֹ לַלִּשְׁכָּה שֶׁעַל פְּנֵי הַבִּירָה, צָפוֹנָה מִזְרָחָה, וּבֵית אֶבֶן הָיְתָה נִקְרֵאת, וּמַזִּין עָלָיו כָּל שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים מִכָּל חַטָּאוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ שָׁם.
phrases.en: Seven days before the burning of the [red] cow they would separate the priest who was to burn the cow from his house to a chamber that was facing the north-eastern corner of the birah, and which was called the Stone Chamber. They would sprinkle upon him throughout the seven days with [a mixture of] all the sin-offerings that were there.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, לֹא הָיוּ מַזִּין עָלָיו אֶלָּא בַשְּׁלִישִׁי וּבַשְּׁבִיעִי בִּלְבָד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose said: they sprinkled upon him only on the third and the seventh days.

phrases.he: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגָן הַכֹּהֲנִים אוֹמֵר, עַל הַכֹּהֵן הַשּׂוֹרֵף אֶת הַפָּרָה, מַזִּין כָּל שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Hanina the vice-chief of the priests said: on the priest that was to burn the cow they sprinkled all the seven days, but on the one that was to perform the service on Yom Kippur they sprinkled on the third and the seventh days only.

phrases.he: וְעַל שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, לֹא הָיוּ מַזִּין עָלָיו אֶלָּא בַשְּׁלִישִׁי וּבַשְּׁבִיעִי בִּלְבָד
חֲצֵרוֹת הָיוּ בִירוּשָׁלַיִם בְּנוּיוֹת עַל גַּבֵּי סֶלַע וְתַחְתֵּיהֶם חָלוּל, מִפְּנֵי קֶבֶר הַתְּהוֹם.
phrases.en: Courtyards were built in Jerusalem over rock, and beneath them there was a hollow which served as a protection against a grave in the depths.

phrases.he: וּמְבִיאִים נָשִׁים עֻבָּרוֹת וְיוֹלְדוֹת שָׁם וּמְגַדְּלוֹת שָׁם אֶת בְּנֵיהֶן.
phrases.en: And they used to bring there pregnant women, and there they gave birth to their children and there they raised them.

phrases.he: וּמְבִיאִים שְׁוָרִים וְעַל גַּבֵּיהֶן דְּלָתוֹת, וְתִינוֹקוֹת יוֹשְׁבִין עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן וְכוֹסוֹת שֶׁל אֶבֶן בְּיָדָם.
phrases.en: And they brought oxen, upon whose backs were placed doors, and the children sat upon them with stone cups in their hands.

phrases.he: הִגִּיעוּ לַשִּׁלּוֹחַ, יָרְדוּ וּמִלְאוּם, וְעָלוּ וְיָשְׁבוּ עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן.
phrases.en: When they reached the Shiloah spring they got down and filled the cups with water and then they ascended and sat again on the doors.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, מִמְּקוֹמוֹ הָיָה מְשַׁלְשֵׁל וּמְמַלֵּא:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose said: each child used to let down his cup and fill it from his place.

phrases.he: בָּאוּ לְהַר הַבַּיִת וְיָרְדוּ.
phrases.en: They arrived at the Temple Mount and got down.

phrases.he: הַר הַבַּיִת וְהָעֲזָרוֹת, תַּחְתֵּיהֶם חָלוּל, מִפְּנֵי קֶבֶר הַתְּהוֹם.
phrases.en: Beneath the Temple Mount and the courts was a hollow which served as a protection against a grave in the depths.

phrases.he: וּבְפֶתַח הָעֲזָרָה הָיָה מְתֻקָּן קָלָל שֶׁל חַטָּאת, וּמְבִיאִין זָכָר שֶׁל רְחֵלִים וְקוֹשְׁרִים חֶבֶל בֵּין קַרְנָיו, וְקוֹשְׁרִים מַקֵּל וּמְסַבֵּךְ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל חֶבֶל, וְזוֹרְקוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַקָּלָל, וּמַכֶּה אֶת הַזָּכָר וְנִרְתָּע לַאֲחוֹרָיו, וְנוֹטֵל וּמְקַדֵּשׁ, כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּרָאֶה עַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם.
phrases.en: And at the entrance of the courtyard there was the jar of the ashes of the sin-offerings. They would bring a male from among the sheep and tie a rope between its horns, and a stick or a bushy twig was tied at the other end of the rope, and this was thrown into the jar. They then struck the male [sheep] was so that it started backwards. And [a child] took the ashes and put it [enough] so that it could be seen upon the water.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַל תִּתְּנוּ מָקוֹם לַצְּדוֹקִים לִרְדּוֹת, אֶלָּא הוּא נוֹטֵל וּמְקַדֵּשׁ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose said: do not give the Sadducees an opportunity to rule! Rather, [a child] himself took it and mixed it.

phrases.he: לֹא הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין, לֹא חַטָּאת עַל גַּבֵּי חַטָּאת, וְלֹא תִינוֹק עַל גַּבֵּי חֲבֵרוֹ.
phrases.en: One may not bring a sin-offering by virtue of [the purifications made for] another sin-offering, nor one child by virtue of [the preparations made for] another.

phrases.he: וּצְרִיכִין הָיוּ הַתִּינוֹקוֹת לְהַזּוֹת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי.
phrases.en: The children had to be sprinkle on each other, the words of Rabbi Yose the Galilean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, לֹא הָיוּ צְרִיכִין לְהַזּוֹת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: they did not need to sprinkle.

phrases.he: לֹא מָצְאוּ מִשֶּׁבַע, עוֹשִׂין מִשֵּׁשׁ, מֵחָמֵשׁ, מֵאַרְבַּע, מִשָּׁלשׁ, מִשְּׁתַּיִם וּמֵאֶחָת. וּמִי עֲשָׂאָם.
phrases.en: If they did not find the residue of the ashes of the seven [red cows] they performed the sprinkling with those of six, of five, of four, of three, of two or of one.

phrases.he: הָרִאשׁוֹנָה עָשָׂה משֶׁה, וְהַשְּׁנִיָּה עָשָׂה עֶזְרָא, וְחָמֵשׁ, מֵעֶזְרָא וָאֵילָךְ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: And who prepared these? Moses prepared the first, Ezra prepared the second, and five were prepared from the time of Ezra, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, שֶׁבַע מֵעֶזְרָא וָאֵילָךְ. וּמִי עֲשָׂאָן.
phrases.en: But the sages say: seven from the time of Ezra.

phrases.he: שִׁמְעוֹן הַצַּדִּיק וְיוֹחָנָן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל עָשׂוּ שְׁתַּיִם שְׁתַּיִם, אֶלְיְהוֹעֵינַי בֶּן הַקּוֹף וַחֲנַמְאֵל הַמִּצְרִי וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן פִּיאָבִי עָשׂוּ אַחַת אֶחָת
phrases.en: And who prepared them? Shimon the Just and Yohanan the high priest prepared two each; Elihoenai the son of Ha-Kof and Hanamel the Egyptian and Ishmael the son of Piabi prepared one each.

phrases.he: וְכֶבֶשׁ הָיוּ עוֹשִׂים מֵהַר הַבַּיִת לְהַר הַמִּשְׁחָה, כִּפִּין עַל גַּבֵּי כִפִּין, וְכִפָּה כְנֶגֶד הָאֹטֶם, מִפְּנֵי קֶבֶר הַתְּהוֹם, שֶׁבּוֹ כֹהֵן הַשּׂוֹרֵף אֶת הַפָּרָה, וּפָרָה וְכָל מְסַעֲדֶיהָ, יוֹצְאִין לְהַר הַמִּשְׁחָה:
phrases.en: They made a ramp from the Temple Mount to the Mount of Olives, being constructed of arches above arches, each arch placed directly above each foundation [of the arch below] as a protection against a grave in the depths, whereby the priest who was to burn the cow, the cow itself and all who aided in its preparation went forth to the Mount of olives.

phrases.he: לֹא הָיְתָה פָרָה רוֹצָה לָצֵאת, אֵין מוֹצִיאִין עִמָּהּ שְׁחוֹרָה, שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמְרוּ, שְׁחוֹרָה שָׁחֲטוּ.
phrases.en: If the cow refused to go out, they may not take out with it a black one lest people say, "They slaughtered a black cow" nor another red [cow] lest people say, "They slaughtered two.

phrases.he: וְלֹא אֲדֻמָּה, שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמְרוּ, שְׁתַּיִם שָׁחֲטוּ.
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, לֹא מִשּׁוּם זֶה, אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (במדבר יט), וְהוֹצִיא אֹתָהּ, לְבַדָּהּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: it was not for this reason but because it is said "And he shall bring her out" by herself.

phrases.he: וְזִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיוּ מַקְדִּימִים בְּרַגְלֵיהֶם לְהַר הַמִּשְׁחָה, וּבֵית טְבִילָה הָיָה שָׁם.
phrases.en: The elders of Israel used to go first by foot to the Mount of Olives, where there was a place of immersion.

phrases.he: וּמְטַמְּאִים הָיוּ אֶת הַכֹּהֵן הַשּׂוֹרֵף אֶת הַפָּרָה, מִפְּנֵי הַצְּדוֹקִים, שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ אוֹמְרִים, בִּמְעֹרְבֵי שֶׁמֶשׁ הָיְתָה נַעֲשֵׂית
phrases.en: The priest that was to burn the cow was (deliberately) made unclean on account of the Sadducees so that they should not be able to say, "It can be done only by those on whom the sun has set."

phrases.he: סָמְכוּ יְדֵיהֶם עָלָיו וְאָמְרוּ לוֹ, אִישִׁי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, טְבֹל אֶחָת.
phrases.en: They laid their hands upon him and said, "My Lord the high priest, perform immersion once.

phrases.he: יָרַד וְטָבַל וְעָלָה וְנִסְתַּפֵּג.
phrases.en: He went down and immersed himself and came up and dried himself.

phrases.he: וְעֵצִים הָיוּ מְסֻדָּרִים שָׁם, עֲצֵי אֲרָזִים וָאֳרָנִים וּבְרוֹשִׁים וַעֲצֵי תְאֵנָה חֲלָקָה.
phrases.en: Different kinds of wood were set in order there: cedar wood, pine, spruce and the wood of smooth fig trees.

phrases.he: וְעוֹשִׂין אוֹתָהּ כְּמִין מִגְדָּל, וּמְפַתְּחִין בָּהּ חַלּוֹנוֹת, וַחֲזִיתָהּ מַעֲרָבָה
phrases.en: They made it in the shape of a tower and opened air holes in it; and its foreside was turned towards the west.

phrases.he: כְּפָתוּהָ בְחֶבֶל שֶׁל מֶגֶג וּנְתָנוּהָ עַל גַּב הַמַּעֲרָכָה, רֹאשָׁהּ בַּדָּרוֹם וּפָנֶיהָ לַמַּעֲרָב.
phrases.en: They bound it with a rope of reed and placed it on the pile with its head towards the south and its face towards the west.

phrases.he: הַכֹּהֵן עוֹמֵד בַּמִּזְרָח וּפָנָיו לַמַּעֲרָב.
phrases.en: The priest stood in the east with his face towards the west.

phrases.he: שָׁחַט בִּימִינוֹ וְקִבֵּל בִּשְׂמֹאלוֹ.
phrases.en: He slaughtered with his right hand and received the blood with his left.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בִּימִינוֹ הָיָה מְקַבֵּל וְנוֹתֵן לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ, וּמַזֶּה בִימִינוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah said: he received the blood with his right hand and put it in his left hand. He sprinkled with his right.

phrases.he: טָבַל וְהִזָּה שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים.
phrases.en: Seven times he dipped his finger in the blood and sprinkled it towards the Holy of Holies, dipping once again for each sprinkling.

phrases.he: עַל כָּל הַזָּיָה, טְבִילָה.
phrases.en: When he finished the sprinkling he wiped his hand on the body of the cow, came down and kindled the fire with wood chips.

phrases.he: גָּמַר מִלְּהַזּוֹת, קִנַּח אֶת יָדוֹ בְּגוּפָהּ שֶׁל פָּרָה.
יָרַד וְהִצִּית אֶת הָאֵשׁ בַּאֲלִיתוֹת.
רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, בַּחֲרִיּוֹת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva said: with dry branches of palm-trees.

phrases.he: נִבְקְעָה, וְעָמַד חוּץ מִגִּתָּהּ.
phrases.en: It burst and he stood outside its pit and he took the cedar wood, hyssop and scarlet wool.

phrases.he: נָטַל עֵץ אֶרֶז וְאֵזוֹב וּשְׁנִי תוֹלַעַת.
אָמַר לָהֶן, עֵץ אֶרֶז זֶה, עֵץ אֶרֶז זֶה.
phrases.en: He said to them, "Is this cedarwood? Is this cedarwood?" "Is this hyssop? Is this hyssop?" "Is this scarlet wool? Is this scarlet wool?" Three times he repeated each question and they answered him "Yes, yes" three times to each question.

phrases.he: אֵזוֹב זֶה, אֵזוֹב זֶה.
שְׁנִי תוֹלַעַת זֶה, שְׁנִי תוֹלַעַת זֶה.
שָׁלשׁ פְּעָמִים עַל כָּל דָּבָר וְדָבָר.
וְהֵם אוֹמְרִים לוֹ, הֵין וְהֵין, שָׁלשׁ פְּעָמִים עַל כָּל דָּבָר וְדָבָר
כְּרָכָן בִּשְׁיָרֵי הַלָּשׁוֹן וְהִשְׁלִיךְ לְתוֹךְ שְׂרֵפָתָהּ.
phrases.en: He then wrapped them together with the remains of the strip of wool and cast them into the fire.

phrases.he: נִשְׂרְפָה, חוֹבְטִין אוֹתָהּ בְּמַקְלוֹת, וְכוֹבְרִין אוֹתָהּ בִּכְבָרוֹת.
phrases.en: When it was burnt up they would beat it with sticks and then sift it with sieves.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, בְּמַקָּבוֹת שֶׁל אֶבֶן וּבִכְבָרוֹת שֶׁל אֶבֶן הָיְתָה נַעֲשֵׂית.
phrases.en: Rabbi Ishmael says: this was done with stone hammers and stone sieves.

phrases.he: שָׁחוֹר שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ אֵפֶר, כּוֹתְשִׁין אוֹתוֹ.
phrases.en: If there was a black coal on which there were some ashes they would crush it but if there were no [ashes] they would leave it.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁאֵין בּוֹ, מַנִּיחִין אוֹתוֹ.
phrases.en: A bone was crushed in either case.

phrases.he: הָעֶצֶם, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ הָיָה נִכְתָּשׁ.
phrases.en: It was then divided into three parts: one part was deposited on the hel, one on the Mount of Olives, and one was divided among the priestly watches.

phrases.he: וְחוֹלְקִים אוֹתוֹ לִשְׁלשָׁה חֲלָקִים, אֶחָד נִתָּן בַּחֵיל, וְאֶחָד נִתָּן בְּהַר הַמִּשְׁחָה, וְאֶחָד הָיָה מִתְחַלֵּק לְכָל הַמִּשְׁמָרוֹת
פָּרַת חַטָּאת שֶׁשְּׁחָטָהּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ, קִבֵּל וְהִזָּה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ, אוֹ לִשְׁמָהּ וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ, אוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ וְלִשְׁמָהּ, פְּסוּלָה. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מַכְשִׁיר.
phrases.en: If a hatat cow was slaughtered not for its own name, or if its blood was received or sprinkled not for its own name, or if this was done for its own name and for some other name, or for some other name and for its name, it is invalid. Rabbi Eliezer rules it valid.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁלֹּא רְחוּץ יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם, פְּסוּלָה. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מַכְשִׁיר.
phrases.en: If [the service] was performed by one whose hands or feet were unwashed, it is invalid. Rabbi Eliezer rules that it is valid. If it was performed by one who was not the high priest, it is invalid.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁלֹּא בְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, פְּסוּלָה. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַכְשִׁיר. וּמְחֻסַּר בְּגָדִים, פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah rules that it is valid. If it was performed by one who was not wearing all the prescribed garments, it is invalid.

phrases.he: וּבִכְלֵי לָבָן הָיְתָה נַעֲשֵׂית
phrases.en: And in white garments it was to be prepared.

phrases.he: שְׂרָפָהּ חוּץ מִגִּתָּהּ, אוֹ בִשְׁתֵּי גִתּוֹת, אוֹ שֶׁשָּׂרַף שְׁתַּיִם בְּגַת אַחַת, פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.en: If it was burnt outside its pit, or in two pits, or if two cows were burnt in the same pit, it is invalid.

phrases.he: הִזָּה וְלֹא כִוֵּן כְּנֶגֶד הַפֶּתַח, פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.en: If [the blood] was sprinkled but not in the direction of the entrance of the Holy of Holies, it is invalid.

phrases.he: הִזָּה מִשִּׁשִּׁית שְׁבִיעִית, חָזַר וְהִזָּה שְׁבִיעִית, פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.en: If he made the seventh sprinkling out of the sixth and then sprinkled again a seventh time, it is invalid.

phrases.he: מִשְּׁבִיעִית שְׁמִינִית וְחָזַר וְהִזָּה שְׁמִינִית, כְּשֵׁרָה
phrases.en: If he sprinkled an eighth time out of the seventh and then sprinkled again an eighth time, it is valid.

phrases.he: שְׂרָפָהּ שֶׁלֹּא בְעֵצִים, אוֹ בְכָל עֵצִים, אֲפִלּוּ בְקַשׁ אוֹ בִגְבָבָה, כְּשֵׁרָה. הִפְשִׁיטָהּ וְנִתְּחָהּ, כְּשֵׁרָה.
phrases.en: If he burned it without wood, or with any kind of wood, and even if only with straw or stubble, it is valid. If he flayed it and cut up, it is valid.

phrases.he: שְׁחָטָהּ עַל מְנָת לֶאֱכֹל מִבְּשָׂרָהּ וְלִשְׁתּוֹת מִדָּמָהּ, כְּשֵׁרָה.
phrases.en: If he slaughtered it with the intention of eating its flesh or drinking its blood, it is valid.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אֵין מַחֲשָׁבָה פוֹסֶלֶת בַּפָּרָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer rules: no intention can invalidate the red cow.

phrases.he: כָּל הָעֲסוּקִין בַּפָּרָה מִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף, מְטַמְּאִין בְּגָדִים, וּפוֹסְלִים אוֹתָהּ בִּמְלָאכָה.
phrases.en: All who are occupied with the preparation of the [red] cow from the beginning until the end, defile their clothing, and they also render it invalid by [doing other] work.

phrases.he: אֵרַע בָּהּ פְּסוּל בִּשְׁחִיטָתָהּ, אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה בְגָדִים.
phrases.en: If some invalidity occurred while it was being slaughtered, it does not defile clothing.

phrases.he: אֵרַע בָּהּ בְּהַזָּיָתָהּ, כֹּל הָעוֹסֵק בָּהּ לִפְנֵי פְסוּלָהּ, מְטַמְּאָה בְגָדִים.
phrases.en: If it occurred while the blood was being sprinkled, for all who were occupied with it before the invalidity occurred, it defiles their clothing, but for those who were occupied with it after it had become invalid it does not defile their clothing unclean.

phrases.he: לְאַחַר פְּסוּלָהּ, אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה בְגָדִים. נִמְצְאָה חֻמְרָהּ, קֻלָּהּ.
phrases.en: Thus it follows that the stringency turns into a leniency.

phrases.he: לְעוֹלָם מוֹעֲלִים בָּהּ, וּמַרְבִּין לָהּ עֵצִים, וּמַעֲשֶׂיהָ בַיּוֹם, וּבְכֹהֵן, הַמְּלָאכָה פוֹסֶלֶת בָּהּ, עַד שֶׁתֵּעָשֶׂה אֵפֶר, וְהַמְּלָאכָה פוֹסֶלֶת בַּמַּיִם, עַד שֶׁיַּטִּילוּ אֶת הָאֵפֶר
