phrases.en: It is always subject to the rules of trespassing. Wood may be added to the fire. The service must be performed by day and by a priest. Work renders it invalid. [All of this is only] until it becomes ashes And work causes the water to be invalid until the ashes are put into it.

phrases.he: הַמֵּבִיא כְּלִי חֶרֶס לְחַטָּאת, טוֹבֵל וְלָן עַל הַכִּבְשָׁן.
phrases.en: He who brings the earthen vessel for the hatat must immerse, and spend the night by the furnace.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף מִן הַבַּיִת הוּא מֵבִיא וְכָשֵׁר, שֶׁהַכֹּל נֶאֱמָנִים עַל הַחַטָּאת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: he may also bring it from the house and it is valid, for all are deemed trustworthy in regard to the hatat.

phrases.he: וּבַתְּרוּמָה, פּוֹתֵחַ אֶת הַכִּבְשָׁן וְנוֹטֵל.
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, מִן הַסֵּדֶר הַשֵּׁנִי.
phrases.en: In the case of terumah one may open the furnace and take out [the vessel].

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, מִן הַסֵּדֶר הַשְּׁלִישִׁי:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: from the second row. Rabbi Yose says: from the third row.

phrases.he: הַמַּטְבִּיל כְּלִי לְחַטָּאת בְּמַיִם שֶׁאֵינָם רְאוּיִים לְקַדֵּשׁ, צָרִיךְ לְנַגֵּב.
phrases.en: If one immersed a vessel for the hatat in water that is not fit for the mixing he must dry it; If in water that is fit for the mixing he need not dry it.

phrases.he: בְּמַיִם שֶׁהֵם רְאוּיִים לְקַדֵּשׁ, אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְנַגֵּב.
phrases.en: But if [he intended] to collect in it water that was already mixed with the ashes, he must dry it in either case.

phrases.he: אִם לְהוֹסִיף לְתוֹכוֹ מַיִם מְקֻדָּשִׁין, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ צָרִיךְ לְנַגֵּב
קֵרוּיָה שֶׁהִטְבִּילוּהָ בְמַיִם שֶׁאֵין רְאוּיִין לְקַדֵּשׁ, מְקַדְּשִׁין בָּהּ עַד שֶׁתִּטְמָא.
phrases.en: If a pumpkin shell was immersed in water that was not fit for the mixing, it is permissible to mix in it the ashes with the water, as long as it had not been defiled.

phrases.he: נִטְמְאָה, אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין בָּהּ.
phrases.en: If it has been defiled, one cannot mix in it the ashes with the water.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, אִם מְקַדֵּשׁ הוּא בָהּ בַּתְּחִלָּה, אַף בַּסּוֹף יְקַדֵּשׁ בָּהּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua says: if one is allowed to mix in it the ashes and water at the beginning, one should also be allowed to do so at the end; and if one is not allowed to do this at the end one should not be allowed to do it at the beginning.

phrases.he: אִם אֵינוֹ מְקַדֵּשׁ בָּהּ בַּסּוֹף, אַף לֹא בַתְּחִלָּה.
phrases.en: In either case it is not permissible to collect in it water that has already had ashes mixed in.

phrases.he: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ, לֹא יוֹסִיף לְתוֹכָהּ מַיִם מְקֻדָּשִׁים
שְׁפוֹפֶרֶת שֶׁחֲתָכָהּ לְחַטָּאת,
phrases.en: A reed pipe that was cut [for use as a container] for the hatat: Rabbi Eliezer says: it must be immersed immediately.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, יַטְבִּיל מִיָּד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua ruled: he defiles it and then immerses it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, יְטַמֵּא וְיַטְבִּיל.
phrases.en: All are eligible to prepare the mixture, except a deaf mute, an imbecile and a minor.

phrases.he: הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִים לְקַדֵּשׁ, חוּץ מֵחֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says a minor is eligible, but disqualifies a woman and a hermaphrodite.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַכְשִׁיר בְּקָטָן, וּפוֹסֵל בְּאִשָּׁה וּבְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס
בְּכָל הַכֵּלִים מְקַדְּשִׁים, אֲפִלּוּ בִכְלֵי גְלָלִים, בִּכְלֵי אֲבָנִים, וּבִכְלֵי אֲדָמָה. וּבִסְפִינָה, מְקַדְּשִׁין בָּהּ.
phrases.en: They can make the mixture in all kinds of vessels, even in vessels made of cattle dung, of stone or of earth. The mixture may also be prepared in a boat.

phrases.he: אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין לֹא בְדָפְנוֹת הַכֵּלִים, וְלֹא בְשׁוּלֵי הַמַּחַץ, וְלֹא בִמְגוּפַת הֶחָבִית, וְלֹא בְחָפְנָיו, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין מְמַלְּאִין וְאֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין וְאֵין מַזִּין מֵי חַטָּאת אֶלָּא בְכֶלִי.
phrases.en: It may not be prepared in the walls of vessels, or in the sides of a large jug, or in the stopper of a jar, or in one's cupped hands, for one does not fill up, or mix in, or sprinkle the hatat with anything but a vessel.

phrases.he: אֵין מַצִּילִין בְּצָמִיד פָּתִיל אֶלָּא כֵלִים, שֶׁאֵין מַצִּילִים מִיַּד כְּלֵי חֶרֶס אֶלָּא כֵלִים
phrases.en: Only on a vessel does tightly fitting cover afford protection, for only in vessels is protection afforded against uncleanness within an earthen vessel.

phrases.he: בֵּיצַת הַיּוֹצְרִים, כְּשֵׁרָה. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי פוֹסֵל.
phrases.en: A potters’ egg is fit [as a vessel]. Rabbi Yose rules that it is unfit.

phrases.he: בֵּיצַת הַתַּרְנְגֹלֶת, רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַכְשִׁירִין, וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹסְלִין
phrases.en: A hen's egg: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Judah rule it is fit [as a vessel]; But the sages rule that it is unfit.

phrases.he: הַשֹּׁקֶת שֶׁבַּסֶּלַע, אֵין מְמַלְּאִין בָּהּ וְאֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין בָּהּ וְאֵין מַזִּין מִמֶּנָּה, וְאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה צָמִיד פָּתִיל, וְאֵינָהּ פּוֹסֶלֶת אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה.
phrases.en: It is not permissible to collect the water in a trough set in the stone, nor is it permissible to prepare the mixture in it, nor may the sprinkling be done from it, nor does it require a tightly fitting cover, nor does it render a ritual bath invalid.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה כְלִי וְחִבְּרָהּ בְּסִיד, מְמַלְּאִין בָּהּ וּמְקַדְּשִׁין בָּהּ וּמַזִּין מִמֶּנָּה, וּצְרִיכָה צָמִיד פָּתִיל, וּפוֹסֶלֶת אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה.
phrases.en: If it was first a movable vessel and then was subsequently joined to the ground with lime, it is permissible to collect the water in it, to prepare the mixture in it and to sprinkle from it.

phrases.he: נִקְּבָה מִלְּמַטָּן, וּפְקָקָהּ בִּסְמַרְטוּט, הַמַּיִם שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ פְּסוּלִין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵינָן עֲגֻלִּים כֶּלִי.
phrases.en: And it needs a tightly fitting cover and renders a ritual bath invalid. If there was a hole in it below, and he stopped it up with a rag, the water in it is invalid since it is not wholly enclosed by the vessel.

phrases.he: מִן הַצַּד וּפְקָקָהּ בִּסְמַרְטוּט, הַמַּיִם שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ כְּשֵׁרִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵם עֲגֻלִּים כֶּלִי.
phrases.en: If the hole was in the side and it was stopped up with a rag, the water in it is valid since it is wholly enclosed by the vessel.

phrases.he: עָשׂוּ לָהּ עֲטָרָה שֶׁל טִיט, וְהָלְכוּ הַמַּיִם לְשָׁם, פְּסוּלִין.
phrases.en: If he made a rim of clay for the vessel and the water had risen to that spot, it is invalid; But if it was solid enough for the vessel to be moved with it, the water is valid.

phrases.he: אִם הָיָה בָרִיא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּנָּטֵל עִמָּהּ, כְּשֵׁרִים
שְׁתֵּי שְׁקָתוֹת שֶׁבְּאֶבֶן אַחַת, קִדֵּשׁ אַחַת מֵהֶם, הַמַּיִם שֶׁבַּשְּׁנִיָּה אֵינָן מְקֻדָּשִׁין.
phrases.en: If there were two troughs in one stone and the mixture was prepared in one of them, the water in the other is not prepared.

phrases.he: הָיוּ נְקוּבוֹת זוֹ לָזוֹ כִּשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הַנּוֹד, אוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ הַמַּיִם צָפִין עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן אֲפִלּוּ כִקְלִפַּת הַשּׁוּם, וְקִדֵּשׁ אֶת אַחַת מֵהֶן, הַמַּיִם שֶׁבַּשְּׁנִיָּה מְקֻדָּשִׁין
phrases.en: If a hole of the size of the spout of a water skin passed from one to the other, or if the water overflowed both, even if only [to a depth of] the thickness of garlic peel, and the mixture was prepared in one of them, the water in the other is also prepared.

phrases.he: שְׁתֵּי אֲבָנִים שֶׁהִקִּיפָן זוֹ לָזוֹ וַעֲשָׂאָן שֹׁקֶת, וְכֵן שְׁתֵּי עֲרֵבוֹת, וְכֵן הַשֹּׁקֶת שֶׁנֶּחְלְקָה, הַמַּיִם שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶם אֵינָן מְקֻדָּשִׁין.
phrases.en: If one placed two stones close to one another and made them into a trough, and so also in the case of two kneading troughs, and so also in the case of a trough that was split, the water between them is not deemed to be prepared.

phrases.he: עֲשָׂאָן בְּסִיד אוֹ בְגִפְסִים וְהֵן יְכוֹלוֹת לְהִנָּטֵל כְּאַחַת, הַמַּיִם שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶם מְקֻדָּשִׁין
phrases.en: If they were joined together with lime or gypsum and they can be moved together, the water between them is deemed to have been prepared.

phrases.he: הַמְקַדֵּשׁ וְנָפַל הַקִּדּוּשׁ עַל יָדוֹ אוֹ עַל הַצַּד וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָפַל עַל הַשֹּׁקֶת, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: If one was about to mix the ashes with the water and the ashes fell upon his hand or upon the side of the trough and then fell into the trough, the mixture is invalid.

phrases.he: נָפַל מִן הַשְּׁפוֹפֶרֶת לַשֹּׁקֶת, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: If they fell from the tube into the trough, the mixture is invalid.

phrases.he: נָטַל מִשְּׁפוֹפֶרֶת וְכִסָּה, אוֹ שֶׁהֵגִיף אֶת הַדֶּלֶת, הַקִּדּוּשׁ כָּשֵׁר, וְהַמַּיִם פְּסוּלִים. זְקָפָהּ בָּאָרֶץ, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: If he took the ashes from the tube and then covered it, or shut a door, the ashes remain valid but the water becomes invalid. If he put it up erect on the ground, the water becomes invalid.

phrases.he: לְתוֹךְ יָדוֹ, כָּשֵׁר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר
phrases.en: If in his hand, the water is valid, since it is impossible [otherwise]

phrases.he: הָיָה קִדּוּשׁ צָף עַל פְּנֵי הַמַּיִם, רַבִּי מֵאִיר
phrases.en: If the ashes floated on the water: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Shimon rule: one may take some of them and use them in another preparation; But the sages say: with any ashes that have touched water no other mixture may be prepared from them.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים, נוֹטֵל וּמְקַדֵּשׁ.
phrases.en: If he emptied out the water and some ashes were found at the bottom: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Shimon rule: one may dry them and then use them for another preparation; But the sages rule: with any ashes that have touched water no other mixture may be prepared.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, כֹּל שֶׁנָּגַע בַּמַּיִם, אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין בּוֹ.
זָלַף אֶת הַמַּיִם וְנִמְצָא קִדּוּשׁ מִלְּמַטָּן, רַבִּי מֵאִיר
וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים, מְנַגֵּב וּמְקַדֵּשׁ.
וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, כֹּל שֶׁנָּגַע בַּמַּיִם, אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין בּוֹ:
הַמְקַדֵּשׁ בַּשֹּׁקֶת וְהַטְּפִי בְתוֹכָהּ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁפִּיו צַר כָּל שֶׁהוּא, הַמַּיִם שֶׁבְּתוֹכוֹ מְקֻדָּשִׁין.
phrases.en: One who mixes the water in a trough while a bucket was in it, even though its neck was narrow as can be, the waters in it are prepared.

phrases.he: אִם הָיָה סְפוֹג, הַמַּיִם שֶׁבְּתוֹכוֹ פְסוּלִים.
phrases.en: If there was a sponge in the trough, the water in it is invalid.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד יַעֲשֶׂה, יְזַלֵּף עַד שֶׁהוּא מַגִּיעַ לַסְּפוֹג.
phrases.en: What should he do? He should empty out the water until he gets to the sponge.

phrases.he: נָגַע בַּסְּפוֹג, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַמַּיִם צָפִין עַל גַּבָּיו כָּל שֶׁהֵן, פְּסוּלִין
phrases.en: If one touched the sponge, however much the water that washes over it, the water becomes invalid.

phrases.he: נָתַן יָדוֹ אוֹ רַגְלוֹ אוֹ עֲלֵי יְרָקוֹת כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּעַבְרוּ הַמַּיִם לֶחָבִית, פְּסוּלִים.
phrases.en: If he placed his hand or his foot or leaves of vegetables in such a manner as to enable the water to run into a jar, the water is invalid.

phrases.he: עֲלֵי קָנִים וַעֲלֵי אֱגוֹז, כְּשֵׁרִים.
phrases.en: If he used leaves of reeds or leaves of nuts the water is valid.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: This is the general rule: [water passing over] that which is susceptible to uncleanness is invalid, but [water passing over] that which is not susceptible to uncleanness is valid.

phrases.he: וְדָבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה, כָּשֵׁר
הַמְפַנֶּה אֶת הַמַּעְיָן לְתוֹךְ הַגַּת, אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַגֵּבִים, פְּסוּלִים לַזָּבִים וְלַמְצֹרָעִים וּלְקַדֵּשׁ בָּהֶן מֵי חַטָּאת, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְמַלְּאוּ בְכֶלִי:
phrases.en: One who diverts a spring into a wine vat or into pools, the water is invalid for zavim and metzoraim. And also for the preparation of the hatat water. Because it was not drawn into a vessel.

phrases.he: חֲמִשָּׁה שֶׁמִּלְאוּ חֲמִשָּׁה חָבִיּוֹת לְקַדְּשָׁן חֲמִשָּׁה קִדּוּשִׁין, וְנִמְלְכוּ לְקַדְּשָׁן קִדּוּשׁ אֶחָד, אוֹ לְקַדְּשָׁן קִדּוּשׁ אֶחָד וְנִמְלְכוּ לְקַדְּשָׁן חֲמִשָּׁה קִדּוּשִׁין, הֲרֵי כֻלָּן כְּשֵׁרִים.
phrases.en: If five men filled five jars to prepare with them five mixtures, and then they changed their minds to prepare one mixture from all of them, or if they filled the jars to prepare with them one mixture and then they changed their minds to prepare with them five mixtures, all the water remains valid.

phrases.he: יָחִיד שֶׁמִּלֵּא חָמֵשׁ חָבִיּוֹת לְקַדְּשָׁן חֲמִשָּׁה קִדּוּשִׁין, וְנִמְלַךְ לְקַדְּשָׁן קִדּוּשׁ אֶחָד, אֵין כָּשֵׁר אֶלָּא אַחֲרוֹן.
phrases.en: If one man filled five jars intending to prepare five [separate] mixtures, [even though] he changed his mind to prepare one mixture from all of them, only the last is valid.

phrases.he: לְקַדְּשָׁן קִדּוּשׁ אֶחָד וְנִמְלַךְ לְקַדְּשָׁן חֲמִשָּׁה קִדּוּשִׁין, אֵין כָּשֵׁר אֶלָּא זֶה שֶׁקִּדֵּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.en: If he intended to prepare one mixture from all of them and then he changed his mind to prepare five separate mixtures, only the water in the one that was mixed first is valid.

phrases.he: אָמַר לְאֶחָד, קַדֵּשׁ לְךָ אֶת אֵלּוּ, אֵין כָּשֵׁר אֶלָּא רִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.en: If he said to another man, "Prepare mixtures from these for yourself," only the first is valid; But if he said, "Prepare a mixture from these for me," all are valid.

phrases.he: קַדֵּשׁ לִי אֶת אֵלּוּ, הֲרֵי כֻלָּם כְּשֵׁרִים

הַמְמַלֵּא בְאַחַת יָדוֹ וְעוֹשֶׂה מְלָאכָה בְאַחַת יָדוֹ, הַמְמַלֵּא לוֹ וּלְאַחֵר, אוֹ שֶׁמִּלֵּא לִשְׁנַיִם כְּאַחַת, שְׁנֵיהֶן פְּסוּלִין, שֶׁהַמְּלָאכָה פוֹסֶלֶת בַּמִּלּוּי, בֵּין לוֹ בֵּין לְאַחֵר:
phrases.en: One who filled the water with one hand and did some other work with the other hand, or filled the water for himself and for another man, or filled two jars at the same time, the water of both is invalid, for work causes invalidity whether one acts for oneself or for another person.

phrases.he: הַמְקַדֵּשׁ בְּאַחַת יָדוֹ וְעוֹשֶׂה מְלָאכָה בְאַחַת יָדוֹ, אִם לוֹ, פָּסוּל. וְאִם לְאַחֵר, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: One who prepared the mixture with one hand and did some other work with the other hand, the mixture is invalid if he prepared it for himself, but if he prepared it for another man, it is valid.

phrases.he: הַמְקַדֵּשׁ לוֹ וּלְאַחֵר, שֶׁלּוֹ פָּסוּל, וְשֶׁל אַחֵר כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: If he prepared a mixture both for himself and for another man, his is invalid and that of the other man is valid.

phrases.he: הַמְקַדֵּשׁ לִשְׁנַיִם כְּאֶחָד, שְׁנֵיהֶן כְּשֵׁרִין
phrases.en: If he prepares mixtures for two men simultaneously, both are valid.

phrases.he: קַדֵּשׁ לִי וַאֲקַדֵּשׁ לָךְ, הָרִאשׁוֹן כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: [If one said to another] "Prepare the mixture for me and I will prepare the one for you," the first is valid.

phrases.he: מַלֵּא לִי וַאֲמַלֵּא לָךְ, הָאַחֲרוֹן כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: [If he said,] "Fill the water for me and I will fill the water for you," that of the latter is valid.

phrases.he: קַדֵּשׁ לִי וַאֲמַלֵּא לָךְ, שְׁנֵיהֶם כְּשֵׁרִים.
phrases.en: [If he said,] "Prepare the mixture for me and I will draw the water for you," both mixtures are valid.

phrases.he: מַלֵּא לִי וַאֲקַדֵּשׁ לָךְ, שְׁנֵיהֶם פְּסוּלִים
phrases.en: [If he said,] "Fill the water for me and I will prepare the mixture for you’, both mixtures are invalid.

phrases.he: הַמְמַלֵּא לוֹ וּלְחַטָּאת, מְמַלֵּא אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ תְּחִלָּה וְקוֹשְׁרוֹ בָאֵסֶל וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְמַלֵּא אֶת שֶׁל חַטָּאת.
phrases.en: One who is drawing water for his own use and for the mixture of the hatat, he must draw for himself first and fasten [the bucket] to the carrying pole and then he can draw the water for the hatat.

phrases.he: וְאִם מִלֵּא שֶׁל חַטָּאת תְּחִלָּה וְאַחַר כָּךְ מִלֵּא אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: If he drew first the water for the hatat and then he drew the water for himself, it is invalid.

phrases.he: נוֹתֵן אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ לַאֲחוֹרָיו וְאֶת שֶׁל חַטָּאת לְפָנָיו.
phrases.en: He must put his own behind him and that for the hatat before him, and if he put that for the hatat behind him it is invalid.

phrases.he: וְאִם נָתַן אֶת שֶׁל חַטָּאת לַאֲחוֹרָיו, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: If both were for the hatat, he may put one before him and one behind him and both are valid, since it is impossible to do otherwise.

phrases.he: הָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶן שֶׁל חַטָּאת, נוֹתֵן אֶחָד לְפָנָיו וְאֶחָד לַאֲחוֹרָיו, וְכָשֵׁר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר
הַמּוֹלִיךְ אֶת הַחֶבֶל בְּיָדוֹ לְדַרְכּוֹ, כָּשֵׁר. וְשֶׁלֹּא לְדַרְכּוֹ, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: One who carries the rope in his hand, If in his usual manner, the mixture is valid; But if not in his usual manner, it is invalid.

phrases.he: זֶה הָלַךְ לְיַבְנֶה שְׁלשָׁה מוֹעֲדוֹת, וּבְמוֹעֵד שְׁלִישִׁי הִכְשִׁירוּ לוֹ הוֹרָאַת שָׁעָה
phrases.en: The question was sent on to Yavneh on three festivals and on the third festival, it was ruled that the mixture was valid, as a temporary measure.

phrases.he: הַמְכַנֵּן אֶת הַחֶבֶל עַל יָד עַל יָד, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: If a man coils the rope around his hand little by little, [the mixture] is valid; But if he coiled it afterwards, it is invalid.

phrases.he: וְאִם כִּנְּנוֹ בָאַחֲרוֹנָה, פָּסוּל.
אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, לָזֶה הִכְשִׁירוּ הוֹרָאַת שָׁעָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose said: this also had been ruled to be valid as a temporary measure.

phrases.he: הַמַּצְנִיעַ אֶת הֶחָבִית שֶׁלֹּא תִשָּׁבֵר, אוֹ שֶׁכְּפָאָהּ עַל פִּיהָ עַל מְנָת לְנַגְּבָהּ לְמַלֹּאת בָּהּ, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: One who puts the jar away in order that it shall not be broken, or if he inverted it in order to dry it, [If he did one of these things] so that he might draw more water with it, [the water he had already drawn] is valid; But if he intended to carry in it the ashes, it is invalid.

phrases.he: לְהוֹלִיךְ בָּהּ אֶת הַקִּדּוּשׁ, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: One who cleared potsherds from a trough: If in order that it may hold more water, the water is valid; But if he intended that they should not hinder him when he pours out the water, it is invalid.

phrases.he: הַמְפַנֶּה חֲרָסִין מִתּוֹךְ הַשֹּׁקֶת בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁתַּחֲזִיק מַיִם הַרְבֵּה, כְּשֵׁרִין.
וְאִם בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ מְעַכְּבִין אוֹתוֹ בְשָׁעָה שֶׁהוּא זוֹלֵף אֶת הַמַּיִם, פָּסוּל
מִי שֶׁהָיוּ מֵימָיו עַל כְּתֵפוֹ וְהוֹרָה הוֹרָאָה, וְהֶרְאָה לַאֲחֵרִים אֶת הַדֶּרֶךְ, וְהָרַג נָחָשׁ וְעַקְרָב, וְנָטַל אֳכָלִים לְהַצְנִיעָם, פָּסוּל. אֳכָלִין לְאָכְלָן, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: One was carrying his water on his shoulder and he ruled in a matter of law, or showed others the way, or killed a snake or a scorpion, or picked up food in order to store it, it [the water] is invalid; But [if he picked up] food to eat, it is valid.

phrases.he: הַנָּחָשׁ וְהָעַקְרָב שֶׁהָיוּ מְעַכְּבִים אוֹתוֹ, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: [And if he killed] a snake or a scorpion that hindered him, it remains valid.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא מִשּׁוּם מְלָאכָה, בֵּין עָמַד בֵּין לֹא עָמַד, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah said: this is the general rule: If the act was is in the nature of work, the mixture is invalid whether the man stopped or not, If it was not in the nature of work: If he stopped, it is invalid; But if he did not stop it remains valid.

phrases.he: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִשּׁוּם מְלָאכָה, עָמַד, פָּסוּל.
וְאִם לֹא עָמַד, כָּשֵׁר
הַמּוֹסֵר מֵימָיו לְטָמֵא, פְּסוּלִין. וּלְטָהוֹר, כְּשֵׁרִין.
phrases.en: If one gave over his water to someone who was unclean, it is invalid. But if to a clean one it is valid.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַף לְטָמֵא כְּשֵׁרִין, אִם לֹא עָשׂוּ הַבְּעָלִים מְלָאכָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: even if it was entrusted to an unclean man it is valid, provided the owner did no other work in the meantime.

phrases.he: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁהָיוּ מְמַלְּאִין לְחַטָּאת, וְהִגְבִּיהוּ זֶה עַל זֶה וְנָטַל זֶה לָזֶה קוֹצוֹ, בְּקִדּוּשׁ אֶחָד, כָּשֵׁר. בִּשְׁנֵי קִדּוּשִׁין, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: Two men who were drawing water for the hatat and one assisted the other to raise it or one pulled out a thorn for the other: For one mixture, it is valid; For two mixtures, it is invalid.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַף בִּשְׁנֵי קִדּוּשִׁין כָּשֵׁר, אִם הִתְנוּ בֵינֵיהֶן:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: even if there are to be two mixtures it is valid if they had made a mutual agreement between them.

phrases.he: הַפּוֹרֵץ עַל מְנָת לִגְדֹּר, כָּשֵׁר. וְאִם גָּדַר, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: One who broke down a fence [even] with the intention of putting it up again, the water remains valid; But if he put a fence up, the water becomes invalid.

phrases.he: הָאוֹכֵל עַל מְנָת לִקְצוֹת, כָּשֵׁר. וְאִם קָצָה, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: If he ate figs intending to store some of them, the water is valid; But if he stored figs it is invalid.

phrases.he: הָיָה אוֹכֵל וְהוֹתִיר וְזָרַק מַה שֶּׁבְּיָדוֹ לְתַחַת הַתְּאֵנָה אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַמֻּקְצֶה בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא יֹאבַד, פָּסוּל
phrases.en: If he was eating figs and, leaving some over, threw what was in his hand under the fig tree or among drying figs in order that it shall not be wasted, the water is invalid.

phrases.he: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁהָיוּ שׁוֹמְרִים אֶת הַשֹּׁקֶת, נִטְמָא אַחַד מֵהֶם, כְּשֵׁרִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ שֶׁל שֵׁנִי.
phrases.en: Two men were guarding a trough: If one of them became unclean, the water remains valid, since it is in the domain of the other.

phrases.he: טָהַר, וְנִטְמָא שֵׁנִי, כְּשֵׁרִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ שֶׁל רִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.en: If the first became clean and the other became unclean the water is still valid since it is in the domain of the first.

phrases.he: נִטְמְאוּ שְׁנֵיהֶן כְּאַחַת, פְּסוּלִין.
phrases.en: If both became unclean simultaneously the water becomes invalid.

phrases.he: עָשָׂה אַחַד מֵהֶן מְלָאכָה, כְּשֵׁרִין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ שֶׁל שֵׁנִי.
phrases.en: If one of them did some work, the water remains valid since it is in the domain of the second.

phrases.he: עָמַד, וְעָשָׂה הַשֵּׁנִי מְלָאכָה, כְּשֵׁרִין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ שֶׁל רִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.en: If the first stopped doing work and the other did some work, the water still remains valid since it is in the domain of the first.

phrases.he: עָשׂוּ שְׁנֵיהֶן כְּאֶחָד, פְּסוּלִין
phrases.en: If both did some work at the same time the water becomes invalid.

phrases.he: הַמְקַדֵּשׁ מֵי חַטָּאת, לֹא יִנְעוֹל אֶת הַסַּנְדָּל.
phrases.en: One who prepares the mixture of the hatat should not wear his sandals, for were some of the liquid to fall on his sandal it would become unclean and [the sandal] would defile him.

phrases.he: שֶׁאִם נָפְלוּ מַשְׁקִין עַל הַסַּנְדָּל, נִטְמָא וְטִמְּאָהוּ.
phrases.en: Behold he would say [to the sandal], "That which defiled you did not defile me, but you did defile me.

phrases.he: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר, מְטַמְּאֶיךָ לֹא טִמְּאוּנִי וְאַתָּה טִמֵּאתָנִי.
phrases.en: If some of the liquid fell on his skin he remains clean.

phrases.he: נָפְלוּ מַשְׁקִין עַל בְּשָׂרוֹ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If it fell on his garment it becomes unclean and defiles him.

phrases.he: נָפְלוּ עַל כְּסוּתוֹ, נִטְמֵאת וְטִמְּאַתּוּ.
phrases.en: Behold he would say [to the garment], "That which defiled you did not defile me, but you did defile me.

phrases.he: הֲרֵי זֶה אוֹמֵר, מְטַמְּאֶיךָ לֹא טִמְּאוּנִי וְאַתָּה טִמֵּאתָנִי
הַשּׂוֹרֵף פָּרָה, וּפָרִים, וְהַמְשַׁלֵּחַ אֶת הַשָּׂעִיר, מְטַמֵּא בְגָדִים.
phrases.en: The one who burns the red cow or bulls and he that leads away the scapegoat, defile garments.

phrases.he: פָּרָה וּפָרִים וְשָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ עַצְמָן אֵין מְטַמְּאִין בְּגָדִים.
phrases.en: The red cow and the bulls and the scapegoat do not themselves defile garments.

phrases.he: הֲרֵי זֶה אוֹמֵר, מְטַמְּאֶיךָ לֹא טִמְּאוּנִי וְאַתָּה טִמֵּאתָנִי
phrases.en: Behold [the garment] would say [to the person], "That which defiled you did not defile me, but you did defile me.

phrases.he: הָאוֹכֵל מִנִּבְלַת הָעוֹף הַטָּהוֹר וְהִיא בְּבֵית הַבְּלִיעָה, מְטַמֵּא בְגָדִים.
phrases.en: One that eats of the carrion of a clean bird, while it is yet in his throat, causes garments to be unclean; But the carrion itself does not cause garments to be unclean.

phrases.he: הַנְּבֵלָה עַצְמָהּ אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה בְגָדִים.
phrases.en: Behold [the garment] would say [to the person], "That which defiled you did not defile me, but you did defile me.

phrases.he: הֲרֵי זֶה אוֹמֵר, מְטַמְּאֶיךָ לֹא טִמְּאוּנִי, וְאַתָּה טִמֵּאתָנִי
כָּל וְלַד הַטֻּמְאוֹת אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא כֵלִים, אֶלָּא מַשְׁקֶה. נִטְמָא מַשְׁקֶה, טִמְּאָן.
phrases.en: Any derived uncleanness does not defile vessels, but [it does defile] a liquid. If a liquid became unclean it defiles them.

phrases.he: הֲרֵי זֶה אוֹמֵר, מְטַמְּאֶיךָ לֹא טִמְּאוּנִי וְאַתָּה טִמֵּאתָנִי
phrases.en: Behold [the vessel] would say [to the liquid], "That which defiled you did not defile me, but you did defile me.

phrases.he: אֵין כְּלִי חֶרֶשׂ מְטַמֵּא חֲבֵרוֹ, אֶלָּא מַשְׁקֶה. נִטְמָא מַשְׁקֶה, טִמְּאַתּוּ.
phrases.en: An earthenware vessel does not defile another such vessel, but [it does defile] a liquid. And when the liquid becomes unclean it defile the vessel.

phrases.he: הֲרֵי זֶה אוֹמֵר, מְטַמְּאֶיךָ לֹא טִמְּאוּנִי וְאַתָּה טִמֵּאתָנִי
phrases.en: Behold [the vessel] would say [to the liquid], "That which defiled you did not defile me, but you did defile me."

phrases.he: כָּל הַפּוֹסֵל אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה, מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַמַּשְׁקִין לִהְיוֹת תְּחִלָּה לְטַמֵּא אֶחָד וְלִפְסֹל אֶחָד, חוּץ מִטְּבוּל יוֹם.
phrases.en: Whatever causes terumah to be invalid causes liquid to become unclean in the first grade so that it can convey uncleanness at one remove, and render unfit at one other remove, except for a tevul yom.

phrases.he: הֲרֵי זֶה אוֹמֵר, מְטַמְּאֶיךָ לֹא טִמְּאוּנִי וְאַתָּה טִמֵּאתָנִי
phrases.en: Behold [the food] would say [to the liquid], "That which defiled you did not defile me, but you did defile me."

phrases.he: כָּל הַיַּמִּים כְּמִקְוֶה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (בראשית א), וּלְמִקְוֵה הַמַּיִם קָרָא יַמִּים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: All seas are equivalent to a ritual bath (mikveh), for it is said, "And the gathering (ulemikveh) of the waters He called the seas" (Genesis 1:10), the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל כְּמִקְוֶה, לֹא נֶאֱמַר יַמִּים, אֶלָּא שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ מִינֵי יַמִּים הַרְבֵּה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: only the Great Sea is equivalent to a ritual bath, for it says "seas" only because there are in it many kinds of seas.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, כָּל הַיַּמִּים מְטַהֲרִין בְּזוֹחֲלִין, וּפְסוּלִין לַזָּבִים וְלַמְצֹרָעִים וּלְקַדֵּשׁ מֵהֶן מֵי חַטָּאת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: all seas afford cleanness when running, and yet they are unfit for zavim and metzoraim and for the preparation of the hatat waters.

phrases.he: הַמַּיִם הַמֻּכִּים, פְּסוּלִים. אֵלּוּ הֵן הַמֻּכִּים, הַמְּלוּחִים וְהַפּוֹשְׁרִים. הַמַּיִם הַמְכַזְּבִים, פְּסוּלִין.
phrases.en: Spoiled waters are unfit. The following are spoiled waters: those that are salty or lukewarm. Waters that disappoint are unfit.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ הֵם הַמַּיִם הַמְכַזְּבִים, הַמְכַזְּבִים אֶחָד בַּשָּׁבוּעַ.
phrases.en: The following are waters that disappoint: those that disappoint even once in a seven year cycle.

phrases.he: הַמְכַזְּבִים בְּפֻלְמְסָיוֹת וּבִשְׁנֵי בִצָּרוֹן, כְּשֵׁרִים. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה פוֹסֵל
phrases.en: Those that disappoint only in times of war or in years of drought are fit. Rabbi Judah says: they are unfit.

phrases.he: מֵי קַרְמְיוֹן וּמֵי פוּגָה, פְּסוּלִין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵם מֵי בִצִּים.
phrases.en: The waters of the Karmiyon and the waters of Pugah are unfit, because they are marsh waters.

phrases.he: מֵי הַיַּרְדֵּן וּמֵי יַרְמוּךְ, פְּסוּלִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵם מֵי תַעֲרֹבוֹת.
phrases.en: The waters of the Jordan and the waters of the Yarmuk are unfit, because they are mixed waters.

phrases.he: וְאֵלוּ הֵן מֵי תַעֲרֹבוֹת, אֶחָד כָּשֵׁר וְאֶחָד פָּסוּל, שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ.
phrases.en: And the following are mixed waters: a fit kind and an unfit kind that were mixed together.

phrases.he: שְׁנֵיהֶן כְּשֵׁרִין וְנִתְעָרְבוּ, כְּשֵׁרִין. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה פוֹסֵל
phrases.en: If two kinds that are fit were mixed together both remain fit: Rabbi Judah says that they are unfit.

phrases.he: בְּאֵר אַחְאָב וּמְעָרַת פַּמְיָס, כְּשֵׁרָה.
phrases.en: Ahab's well and the pool in Banias cave are fit.

phrases.he: הַמַּיִם שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּנּוּ וְשִׁנּוּיָן מֵחֲמַת עַצְמָן, כְּשֵׁרִין.
phrases.en: Water that has changed its color and the change arose from itself, remains fit.

phrases.he: אַמַּת הַמַּיִם הַבָּאָה מֵרָחוֹק, כְּשֵׁרָה, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיִּשְׁמְרֶנָּה שֶׁלֹּא יַפְסִיקֶנָּה אָדָם.
phrases.en: A water channel that comes from a distance is fit, as long as it is watched so that no one cuts it off.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הֲרֵי הִיא בְחֶזְקַת מֻתֶּרֶת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: the presumption is that it is permitted.

phrases.he: בְּאֵר שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹכָהּ חַרְסִית אוֹ אֲדָמָה, יַמְתִּין לָהּ עַד שֶׁתִּצַּל, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל.
phrases.en: If some clay or earth fell into a well, one must wait until it becomes clear, the words of Rabbi Ishmael.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְהַמְתִּין:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiba says: he need not wait.

phrases.he: צְלוֹחִית שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹכָהּ מַיִם כָּל שֶׁהֵן,
phrases.en: If the smallest amount of water fell into a flask: Rabbi Eliezer says: the sprinkling must be done twice; But the sages say that the mixture is invalid.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, יַזֶּה שְׁתֵּי הַזָּיוֹת. וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹסְלִין. יָרַד לְתוֹכָהּ טַל,
phrases.en: If dew dropped into it: Rabbi Eliezer says: let it be put out in the sun and the dew will rise.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, יַנִּיחֶנָּה בַחַמָּה וְהַטַּל עוֹלֶה. וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹסְלִין.
phrases.en: But the sages say that the mixture is invalid. If a liquid or fruit juice fell into it, all the contents must be poured away and it is also necessary to dry the flask.

phrases.he: נָפַל לְתוֹכָהּ מַשְׁקִין וּמֵי פֵרוֹת, יְעָרֶה וְצָרִיךְ לְנַגֵּב.
phrases.en: If ink, gum or sulphate of copper, or anything that leaves a mark, fell into it, the contents must be poured away but it is not necessary to dry the flask.

phrases.he: דְּיוֹ, קוֹמוֹס, וְקַנְקַנְתּוֹם, וְכָל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא רוֹשֵׁם, יְעָרֶה וְאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְנַגֵּב
נָפַל לְתוֹכָהּ שְׁקָצִים וּרְמָשִׂים וְנִתְבַּקְּעוּ, אוֹ שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּנּוּ מַרְאֵיהֶם, פְּסוּלִין.
phrases.en: If insects or creeping things fell into it, and they burst apart or the color [of the water] changed, the contents become invalid.

phrases.he: חִפּוּשִׁית, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ פּוֹסֶלֶת, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא כִשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת.
phrases.en: A beetle causes invalidity in any case, because it is like a tube.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמְרִים, הַדִּירָה וְהַכִּנָּה שֶׁבַּתְּבוּאָה כְּשֵׁרִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם לֵחָה
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Eliezer ben Jacob ruled: a maggot or a weevil of the grain causes no invalidity, because they contain no moisture.

phrases.he: שָׁתָת מֵהֶן בְּהֵמָה אוֹ חַיָּה, פְּסוּלִין.
phrases.en: If a domesticated beast or a wild animal drank from it, it becomes invalid.

phrases.he: כָּל הָעוֹפוֹת פּוֹסְלִין, חוּץ מִן הַיּוֹנָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא מוֹצֶצֶת.
phrases.en: All birds cause invalidity, except the dove since it only sucks up the water.

phrases.he: כָּל הַשְּׁרָצִים אֵינָם פּוֹסְלִין, חוּץ מִן הַחֻלְדָּה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא מַלֶּקֶת.
phrases.en: All creeping things do not cause invalidity, except the weasel since it laps up the water.

phrases.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, אַף הַנָּחָשׁ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא מְקִיאָה.
phrases.en: Rabban Gamaliel ruled: the snake also because it vomits.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַף הָעַכְבָּר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer ruled: the mouse also.

phrases.he: הַחוֹשֵׁב עַל מֵי חַטָּאת לִשְׁתּוֹת,
phrases.en: If one intended to drink the hatat water: Rabbi Eliezer says: it becomes invalid.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua says: only when one tips the flask.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, כְּשֶׁיַּטֶּה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose said: To what does this apply? To water that had not yet been prepared, But in the case of water that had been prepared: Rabbi Eliezer says: it becomes invalid [only] when one tips the flask; And Rabbi Joshua says: [only] when one drinks.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בְּמַיִם שֶׁאֵינָם מְקֻדָּשִׁים. אֲבָל בְּמַיִם הַמְקֻדָּשִׁין,
phrases.en: And if it was poured directly into one's throat, it remains valid.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, כְּשֶׁיַּטֶּה.
רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, כְּשֶׁיִּשְׁתֶּה. וְאִם גִּרְגֵּר, כָּשֵׁר:
מֵי חַטָּאת שֶׁנִּפְסְלוּ, לֹא יְגַבְּלֵם בְּטִיט, שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲשֵׂם תַּקָּלָה לַאֲחֵרִים.
phrases.en: Hatat water that became invalid, it may not be mixed into the mud since it might become a snare for others.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בָּטְלוּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: it becomes neutralized.

phrases.he: פָּרָה שֶׁשָּׁתָת מֵי חַטָּאת, בְּשָׂרָהּ טָמֵא מֵעֵת לְעֵת.
phrases.en: A cow that drank of the hatat water, its flesh becomes unclean for twenty-four hours.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בָּטְלוּ בְמֵעֶיהָ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: it becomes neutralized in its bowels.

phrases.he: מֵי חַטָּאת וְאֵפֶר חַטָּאת, לֹא יַעֲבִירֵם בְּנָהָר וּבִסְפִינָה, וְלֹא יְשִׁיטֵם עַל פְּנֵי הַמַּיִם, וְלֹא יַעֲמוֹד בְּצַד זֶה וְיִזְרְקֵם לְצַד זֶה.
phrases.en: Hatat waters and hatat ashes one may not carry them across a river on a ship, nor may one float them upon the water, nor may one stand on the bank on one side and throw them across to the other side.

phrases.he: אֲבָל עוֹבֵר הוּא בַמַּיִם עַד צַוָּארוֹ.
phrases.en: One may, however, cross over with the water up to his neck.

phrases.he: עוֹבֵר הוּא הַטָּהוֹר לְחַטָּאת וּבְיָדָיו כְּלִי רֵיקָם הַטָּהוֹר לְחַטָּאת, וּבְמַיִם שֶׁאֵינָם מְקֻדָּשִׁין
phrases.en: He that is clean for the hatat may [sail] across [a river] carrying in his hands an empty vessel that is clean for the hatat or water that has not yet been prepared.

phrases.he: אֵפֶר כָּשֵׁר שֶׁנִּתְעָרֵב בְּאֵפֶר מִקְלֶה, הוֹלְכִין אַחַר הָרֹב לְטַמֵּא, וְאֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין בּוֹ.
phrases.en: If valid ashes were mixed up with wood ashes, we follow the majority with regard to uncleanness, but [the mixture] may not be prepared with it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, מְקַדְּשִׁין בְּכֻלָּן:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: the mixture may be prepared with all of them.

phrases.he: מֵי חַטָּאת שֶׁנִּפְסְלוּ, מְטַמְּאִין אֶת הַטָּהוֹר לִתְרוּמָה, בְיָדָיו וּבְגוּפוֹ.
phrases.en: Hatat waters that have been invalidated [still] defile one who is clean for terumah [by contact] with his hands or with his body.

phrases.he: וְאֶת הַטָּהוֹר לְחַטָּאת, לֹא בְיָדָיו וְלֹא בְגוּפוֹ.
phrases.en: And one who is clean for the hatat they defile neither [by contact] with his hands nor [by contact] with his body.

phrases.he: נִטְמְאוּ, מְטַמְּאִים אֶת הַטָּהוֹר לִתְרוּמָה בְיָדָיו וּבְגוּפוֹ.
phrases.en: If they become unclean, they defile one who is clean for terumah [by contact either] with his hands or with his body, And one who is clean for the hatat they defile [by contact] with his hands but not [by contact] with his body.

phrases.he: וְאֶת הַטָּהוֹר לְחַטָּאת, בְּיָדָיו, אֲבָל לֹא בְגוּפוֹ
אֵפֶר כָּשֵׁר שֶׁנְּתָנוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי הַמַּיִם שֶׁאֵינָן רְאוּיִין לְקַדֵּשׁ, מְטַמְּאִין אֶת הַטָּהוֹר לִתְרוּמָה, בְּיָדָיו וּבְגוּפוֹ.
phrases.en: If valid ashes were put on water that was unfit for the preparation, [the latter] defiles one that is clean for terumah [by contact] with his hands or with his body, But to one who is clean for the hatat it conveys uncleanness neither [by contact] with his hands nor with his body.

phrases.he: אֶת הַטָּהוֹר לְחַטָּאת, לֹא בְיָדָיו וְלֹא בְגוּפוֹ
כֹּל הָרָאוּי לִטַּמֵּא מִדְרָס, מַדָּף לְחַטָּאת, בֵּין טָמֵא בֵּין טָהוֹר. וְאָדָם, כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ.
phrases.en: Any object that is susceptible to midras uncleanness is for the purpose of the hatat waters deemed to have madaf uncleanness, whether it was otherwise unclean or clean.

phrases.he: כֹּל הָרָאוּי לִטַּמֵּא טְמֵא מֵת, בֵּין טָמֵא בֵּין טָהוֹר,
phrases.en: A person too is subject to the same rule.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אֵינוֹ מַדָּף.
phrases.en: Any object that is susceptible to corpse uncleanness, whether it is otherwise unclean or clean: Rabbi Eliezer says: it does not have madaf uncleanness.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, מַדָּף.
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua says: it has madaf uncleanness; And the sages say: that which was unclean has madaf uncleanness, and that which was clean does not have madaf uncleanness.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, הַטָּמֵא, מַדָּף. וְהַטָּהוֹר, אֵינוֹ מַדָּף:
הַטָּהוֹר לְחַטָּאת שֶׁנָּגַע בְּמַדָּף, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: One who was clean for the hatat waters who touched something that has madaf uncleannes, he becomes unclean.

phrases.he: לָגִין שֶׁל חַטָּאת שֶׁנָּגַע בְּמַדָּף, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: A flask that was designated for the hatat waters that touched something that has madaf uncleanness, it becomes unclean.

phrases.he: הַטָּהוֹר לְחַטָּאת שֶׁנָּגַע בְּאֳכָלִים וּמַשְׁקִים, בְּיָדוֹ, טָמֵא. וּבְרַגְלוֹ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: One who was clean for the hatat waters who touched food or liquids with his hand, he becomes unclean, but if he did it with his foot he remains clean.

phrases.he: הֱסִיטָן בְּיָדוֹ, רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מְטַמֵּא, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִים
phrases.en: If he moved them with his hand: Rabbi Joshua says that he becomes unclean, And the sages say that he remains clean.

phrases.he: קָלָל שֶׁל חַטָּאת שֶׁנָּגַע בְּשֶׁרֶץ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A jar of hatat waters that touched a [dead] sheretz, remains clean.

phrases.he: נְתָנוֹ עַל גַּבָּיו, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְטַהֵר, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַמְּאִים.
phrases.en: If the jar was put on it: Rabbi Eliezer rules that it remains clean, And the sages rule that it becomes unclean.

phrases.he: נָגַע בְּאֳכָלִים וּמַשְׁקִין וּבְכִתְבֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If the jar touched foods or liquids or the Holy Scriptures, it remains clean.

phrases.he: נְתָנוֹ עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְטַהֵר, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַמְּאִים
phrases.en: If it was put on them: Rabbi Yose rules that it remains clean; And the sages say that it becomes unclean.

phrases.he: הַטָּהוֹר לְחַטָּאת שֶׁנָּגַע בְּתַנּוּר, בְּיָדוֹ, טָמֵא. וּבְרַגְלוֹ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: One who was clean for the hatat waters and then touched an oven: With his hand becomes unclean, With his foot he remains clean.

phrases.he: הָיָה עוֹמֵד עַל גַּבֵּי תַנּוּר וּפָשַׁט יָדוֹ חוּץ לַתַּנּוּר, וְהַלָּגִין בְּתוֹכוֹ, וְכֵן הָאֵסֶל שֶׁהוּא נָתוּן עַל גַּבֵּי הַתַּנּוּר וּבוֹ שְׁנֵי קְלָלוֹת, אֶחָד מִכָּאן וְאֶחָד מִכָּאן, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַהֵר, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַמְּאִין
phrases.en: If he stood on an oven and put out his hand beyond the oven with the flask in his hand, And so also in the case of a carrying-yoke which was placed over the oven and from which two jars were suspended one at either end: Rabbi Akiva says that they remain clean; But the sages say that they are unclean.

phrases.he: הָיָה עוֹמֵד חוּץ לַתַּנּוּר וּפָשַׁט יָדָיו לַחַלּוֹן וְנָטַל אֶת הַלָּגִין וְהֶעֱבִירוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי הַתַּנּוּר, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַמֵּא, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין.
phrases.en: If he was standing outside an oven and he stretched out his hand to a window and he took a flask and passed it over the oven: Rabbi Akiva says that it is unclean, And the sages say that it is clean.

phrases.he: אֲבָל עוֹמֵד הוּא הַטָּהוֹר לְחַטָּאת עַל גַּבֵּי תַנּוּר וּבְיָדוֹ כְּלִי רֵיקָן הַטָּהוֹר לְחַטָּאת, וּבְמַיִם שֶׁאֵין מְקֻדָּשִׁין
phrases.en: But he who was clean for the hatat waters may stand over an oven while holding in his hand an empty vessel that is clean for the hatat waters or one filled with water that has not yet been mixed [with the ashes of the red cow].

phrases.he: לָגִין שֶׁל חַטָּאת שֶׁנָּגַע בְּשֶׁל קֹדֶשׁ וְשֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, שֶׁל חַטָּאת, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: A flask containing hatat waters that touched [a vessel] containing consecrated food or terumah: that containing the hatat waters becomes unclean, but the one containing the consecrated food or the terumah remains clean.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל קֹדֶשׁ וְשֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: If he held the two vessels one in each of his two hands, both become unclean.

phrases.he: שְׁנֵיהֶן בִּשְׁתֵּי יָדָיו, שְׁנֵיהֶן טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: If they were both wrapped in separate papers, they remain clean.

phrases.he: שְׁנֵיהֶם בִּשְׁנֵי נְיָרוֹת, שְׁנֵיהֶם טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: If the vessel of the hatat waters was wrapped in a paper while that of the terumah was held in his hand, both become unclean.

phrases.he: שֶׁל חַטָּאת בִּנְיָר וְשֶׁל תְּרוּמָה בְּיָדוֹ, שְׁנֵיהֶן טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: If the one containing the terumah was wrapped up in paper while that containing the hatat waters was held in his hand, both remain clean.

phrases.he: שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה בִּנְיָר וְשֶׁל חַטָּאת בְּיָדוֹ, שְׁנֵיהֶן טְהוֹרִין.
רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, שֶׁל חַטָּאת, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua says: that containing the hatat waters becomes unclean.

phrases.he: הָיוּ נְתוּנִין עַל גַּבֵּי הָאָרֶץ וְנָגַע בָּהֶם, שֶׁל חַטָּאת, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If both were placed on the ground and he touched them, that of the hatat waters becomes unclean but that of the consecrated food or terumah remains clean.

phrases.he: שֶׁל קֹדֶשׁ וְשֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: If he shifted it [without touching it]: Rabbi Joshua says that it is unclean, And the sages rule that it is clean.

phrases.he: הֱסִיטָן, רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מְטַמֵּא, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין
צְלוֹחִית שֶׁהִנִּיחָהּ מְגֻלָּה, וּבָא וּמְצָאָהּ מְכֻסָּה, פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.en: A flask that one has left uncovered and on returning found it to be covered, is invalid.

phrases.he: הִנִּיחָהּ מְכֻסָּה וּבָא וּמְצָאָהּ מְגֻלָּה, אִם יְכוֹלָה הַחֻלְדָּה לִשְׁתּוֹת הֵימֶנָּה, אוֹ נָחָשׁ לְדִבְרֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, אוֹ שֶׁיָּרַד בָּהּ טַל בַּלַּיְלָה, פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.en: If one left it covered and on returning found it to be uncovered, it is invalid if a weasel could have drunk from it or, according to the words of Rabban Gamaliel, a snake, or if it was possible for dew to fall into it in the night.

phrases.he: הַחַטָּאת אֵינָהּ נִצּוֹלָה בְּצָמִיד פָּתִיל.
phrases.en: The hatat waters are not protected by a tightly fitting cover; But water that had not yet been mixed with the ashes is protected by a tightly fitting cover.

phrases.he: וּמַיִם שֶׁאֵינָן מְקֻדָּשִׁין נִצּוֹלִין בְּצָמִיד פָּתִיל
כָּל הַסְּפֵק טָהוֹר לִתְרוּמָה, טָהוֹר לְחַטָּאת.
phrases.en: Anything that is doubtfully pure in the case of terumah is regarded as clean in the case of the hatat waters.

phrases.he: כָּל הַתָּלוּי לִתְרוּמָה, נִשְׁפָּךְ לְחַטָּאת.
phrases.en: Anything that is "suspended" where terumah is concerned, the hatat waters are poured out.

phrases.he: אִם עָשׂוּ עַל גַּבָּיו טָהֳרוֹת, תְּלוּיוֹת.
phrases.en: If clean things were handled on account of it, they must be "suspended.

phrases.he: הָרְפָפוֹת, טְהוֹרוֹת לְקֹדֶשׁ וְלִתְרוּמָה וּלְחַטָּאת.
phrases.en: Wooden lattice work is clean in respect of holy food, terumah, and the hatat waters.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, הָרְעָדוֹת, טְמֵאוֹת לְחַטָּאת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: Loosely connected wood is unclean in respect of hatat waters.

phrases.he: דְּבֵלָה שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְתוֹךְ מֵי חַטָּאת וּנְטָלָהּ וַאֲכָלָהּ, אִם יֶשׁ בָּהּ כַּבֵּיצָה, בֵּין טְמֵאָה בֵּין טְהוֹרָה, הַמַּיִם טְמֵאִין, וְהָאוֹכְלָהּ חַיָּב מִיתָה.
phrases.en: Pressed figs of terumah which fell into hatat waters and were taken out and eaten: If the amount is the size of an egg, whether [the figs] were clean or unclean the water becomes unclean, and he who eats the figs is liable for death; If their size is less than the size of an egg, the water remains clean but he who eats them is liable for death.

phrases.he: אֵין בָּהּ כַּבֵּיצָה, הַמַּיִם טְהוֹרִין, וְהָאוֹכְלָהּ חַיָּב מִיתָה.
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, בִּטְהוֹרָה, הַמַּיִם טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: if they were clean the water remains clean.

phrases.he: הַטָּהוֹר לְחַטָּאת שֶׁהִכְנִיס רֹאשׁוֹ וְרֻבּוֹ לְתוֹךְ מֵי חַטָּאת, נִטְמָא
phrases.en: If one who was clean for the hatat waters puts his head and the greater part of his body into the hatat waters, he becomes unclean.

phrases.he: כֹּל הַטָּעוּן בִּיאַת מַיִם מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ וְאֶת הַתְּרוּמָה וְאֶת הַחֻלִּין וְאֶת הַמַּעֲשֵׂר, וְאָסוּר עַל בִּיאַת הַמִּקְדָּשׁ.
phrases.en: All that require immersion in water according to the rulings of the Torah defile consecrated things, terumah, unconsecrated food, and [second] tithe; And he is forbidden to enter the sanctuary.

phrases.he: לְאַחַר בִּיאָתוֹ, מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ, וּפוֹסֵל אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: After immersion [but before the sun sets] he defiles holy things and invalidates terumah, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, פּוֹסֵל בַּקֹּדֶשׁ וּבַתְּרוּמָה, וּמֻתָּר בַּחֻלִּין וּבַמַּעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.en: But the sages ruled: he invalidates consecrated things and terumah. But he is permitted to unconsecrated food and [second] tithe.

phrases.he: וְאִם בָּא אֶל הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, בֵּין לִפְנֵי בִיאָתוֹ בֵּין לְאַחַר בִּיאָתוֹ, חַיָּב
phrases.en: And if he entered the sanctuary, whether before or after his immersion, he incurs guilt.

phrases.he: כֹּל הַטָּעוּן בִּיאַת מַיִם מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים, מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ, וּפוֹסֵל אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה, וּמֻתָּר בַּחֻלִּין וּבַמַּעֲשֵׂר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִים בַּמַּעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.en: All that require immersion in water according to the words of the scribes defile consecrated things and invalidate terumah to be unfit, but they are permitted to unconsecrated food and second tithe, the words of Rabbi Meir. But the sages forbid second tithe.

phrases.he: לְאַחַר בִּיאָתוֹ, מֻתָּר בְּכֻלָּן.
phrases.en: After immersion [but before the sun sets] he is permitted to all these.

phrases.he: וְאִם בָּא אֶל הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, בֵּין לִפְנֵי בִיאָתוֹ וּבֵין לְאַחַר בִּיאָתוֹ, פָּטוּר
phrases.en: And if he entered the sanctuary, whether before or after his immersion, he incurs no guilt.

phrases.he: כֹּל הַטָּעוּן בִּיאַת מַיִם, בֵּין מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בֵּין מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים, מְטַמֵּא אֶת מֵי חַטָּאת וְאֶת אֵפֶר חַטָּאת וְאֶת הַמַּזֶּה מֵי חַטָּאת, בְּמַגָּע וּבְמַשָּׂא.
phrases.en: All that require immersion in water, whether according to the words of the Torah or according to the words of the scribes, defile hatat waters, hatat ashes, and the one who sprinkled the hatat waters, either through contact or through carrying.

phrases.he: הָאֵזוֹב הַמֻּכְשָׁר, וְהַמַּיִם שֶׁאֵינָן מְקֻדָּשִׁים, וּכְלִי רֵיקָם הַטָּהוֹר לְחַטָּאת, בְּמַגָּע וּבְמַשָּׂא, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: And [they defile] hyssop that has been rendered susceptible to uncleanness, and water that had not yet been prepared, and an empty vessel that is clean for the hatat through contact and carrying, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בְּמַגָּע אֲבָל לֹא בְמַשָּׂא:
phrases.en: But the sages say: only by contact but not by carrying.

phrases.he: כָּל אֵזוֹב שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ שֵׁם לְוַי, פָּסוּל. אֵזוֹב זֶה, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: Any hyssop that has an accompanying name is invalid. "This" hyssop is valid.

phrases.he: אֵזוֹב יָוָן, אֵזוֹב כּוֹחֲלִית, אֵזוֹב רוֹמִי, אֵזוֹב מִדְבָּרִי, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: Ezovyon (lavendula) hyssop, blue hyssop, Roman hyssop or wild hyssop is invalid. That of unclean terumah is invalid.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל תְּרוּמָה טְמֵאָה, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: That of clean terumah should not be used for sprinkling, but if one had used it for sprinkling it is valid.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל טְהוֹרָה, לֹא יַזֶּה. וְאִם הִזָּה, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: The sprinkling must not be done either with the young shoots or with the berries.

phrases.he: אֵין מַזִּין לֹא בְיוֹנְקוֹת, וְלֹא בִתְמָרוֹת.
phrases.en: He is not liable [after the sprinkling had been done] with young shoots for entering the sanctuary.

phrases.he: אֵין חַיָּבִין עַל הַיּוֹנְקוֹת עַל בִּיאַת הַמִּקְדָּשׁ.
רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַף לֹא עַל הַתְּמָרוֹת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: also not if it was done with the berries.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ הֵן הַיּוֹנְקוֹת, גִּבְעוֹלִין שֶׁלֹּא גָמָלוּ
phrases.en: The following are regarded as young shoots: the stalks before the buds have ripened.

phrases.he: אֵזוֹב שֶׁהִזָּה בוֹ, כָּשֵׁר לְטַהֵר בּוֹ אֶת הַמְּצֹרָע.
phrases.en: The hyssop that was used for sprinkling [the hatat waters] is also fit for cleansing the metzora.

phrases.he: לִקְּטוֹ לְעֵצִים וְנָפְלוּ עָלָיו מַשְׁקִין, מְנַגְּבוֹ וְהוּא כָשֵׁר.
phrases.en: If it was gathered for firewood, and liquid fell upon it, it may be dried and it becomes fit.

phrases.he: לִקְּטוֹ לְאֳכָלִין וְנָפְלוּ עָלָיו מַשְׁקִין, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּגְּבוֹ, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: If it was gathered for food, and liquid fell upon it, even though it was dried, it is invalid.

phrases.he: לִקְּטוֹ לְחַטָּאת, כִּמְלֻקָּט לְאֳכָלִין, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: If it was gathered for [the sprinkling of the waters of] the hatat, it is subject to the same law as if it were gathered for food, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים, כִּמְלֻקָּט לְעֵצִים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah, Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Shimon ruled: as if it were gathered for firewood.

phrases.he: מִצְוַת אֵזוֹב, שְׁלשָׁה קְלָחִים וּבָהֶם שְׁלשָׁה גִבְעוֹלִין.
phrases.en: The mitzvah of the hyssop: it should have three stalks bearing three buds.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, שֶׁל שְׁלשָׁה שְׁלשָׁה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: each stalk should have three buds.

phrases.he: אֵזוֹב שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ שְׁלשָׁה קְלָחִים, מְפַסְּגוֹ וְאוֹגְדוֹ.
phrases.en: Hyssop that consists of a growth of three stalks should be cut apart and then bound together.

phrases.he: פִּסְּגוֹ וְלֹא אֲגָדוֹ, אֲגָדוֹ וְלֹא פִסְּגוֹ, לֹא פִסְּגוֹ וְלֹא אֲגָדוֹ, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: If the stalks were cut apart but were not bound together, or if they were bound together but were not cut apart, or if they were neither cut apart nor bound together, they are nevertheless valid.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, מִצְוַת אֵזוֹב, שְׁלשָׁה קְלָחִים, וּבָהֶם שְׁלשָׁה גִבְעוֹלִים, וּשְׁיָרָיו שְׁנַיִם, וְגַרְדֻּמָּיו כָּל שֶׁהוּא:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: the mitzvah of the hyssop is that it should have three stalks, and on them three buds, but its remnants need only have two, while its stumps may be of the smallest size.

phrases.he: הָאֵזוֹב הַקָּצָר, מְסַפְּקוֹ בְחוּט וּבְכוּשׁ, וְטוֹבֵל וּמַעֲלֶה, וְאוֹחֵז בָּאֵזוֹב וּמַזֶּה. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.en: Hyssop that is too short may be lengthened with a thread and a spindle-reed. He then dips it and brings it up again. He grasps the hyssop itself and sprinkles with it.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַזָּיָה בָאֵזוֹב, כָּךְ טְבִילָה בָאֵזוֹב:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah and Rabbi Shimon say: just as the sprinkling must be done with the hyssop itself so to must the dipping be done with the hyssop itself.

phrases.he: הִזָּה, סָפֵק מִן הַחוּט, סָפֵק מִן הַכּוּשׁ, סָפֵק מִן הַגִּבְעוֹל, הַזָּיָתוֹ פְסוּלָה.
phrases.en: If a person sprinkled and it is doubtful whether the water came from the thread or the spindle-reed or the buds, the sprinkling is invalid.

phrases.he: הִזָּה עַל שְׁנֵי כֵלִים, סָפֵק עַל שְׁנֵיהֶם הִזָּה, סָפֵק מֵחֲבֵרוֹ מִצָּה עָלָיו, הַזָּיָתוֹ פְסוּלָה.
phrases.en: If he sprinkled upon two vessels and it is doubtful whether he sprinkled on both or whether some water from the one dripped on to the other, it is invalid.

phrases.he: מַחַט שֶׁהִיא נְתוּנָה עַל הַחֶרֶס, וְהִזָּה עָלֶיהָ, סָפֵק עַל הַמַּחַט הִזָּה, סָפֵק מִן הַחֶרֶס מִצָּה עָלֶיהָ, הַזָּיָתוֹ פְסוּלָה.
phrases.en: If a needle was on a piece of earthenware and one sprinkled upon it, and it is doubtful whether he sprinkled on the needle or whether some water dripped on it from the earthenware, his sprinkling is invalid.

phrases.he: צְלוֹחִית שֶׁפִּיהָ צַר, טוֹבֵל וּמַעֲלֶה כְדַרְכּוֹ.
phrases.en: A flask with a narrow mouth, one may dip in and draw out in the usual way.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הַזָּיָה רִאשׁוֹנָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: this may be done only for the first sprinkling.

phrases.he: מֵי חַטָּאת שֶׁנִּתְמַעֲטוּ, טוֹבֵל אֲפִלּוּ רָאשֵׁי גִבְעוֹלִין וּמַזֶּה, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְסַפֵּג.
phrases.en: Hatat waters which were diminished, one may dip only the tips of the buds and sprinkle, provided the hyssop does not absorb [any of the moisture on the sides of the flask].

phrases.he: נִתְכַּוֵּן לְהַזּוֹת לְפָנָיו וְהִזָּה לְאַחֲרָיו, לְאַחֲרָיו וְהִזָּה לְפָנָיו, הַזָּיָתוֹ פְסוּלָה.
phrases.en: If one intended to sprinkle in front of him and he sprinkled behind him, or behind him and he sprinkled in front of him, his sprinkling is invalid.

phrases.he: לְפָנָיו, וְהִזָּה עַל הַצְּדָדִין שֶׁלְּפָנָיו, הַזָּיָתוֹ כְשֵׁרָה.
phrases.en: If he intended to sprinkle in front of him and he sprinkled to the sides in front of him, his sprinkling is valid.

phrases.he: מַזִּין עַל הָאָדָם מִדַּעְתּוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ.
phrases.en: It is permitted to sprinkle upon a person with his knowledge or without his knowledge.

phrases.he: מַזִּין עַל הָאָדָם וְעַל הַכֵּלִים, וַאֲפִלּוּ הֵן מֵאָה
phrases.en: It is permitted to sprinkle upon a person and vessels even though there are a hundred of them.

phrases.he: נִתְכַּוֵּן לְהַזּוֹת עַל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה וְהִזָּה עַל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה, אִם יֵשׁ בָּאֵזוֹב, לֹא יִשְׁנֶה.
phrases.en: If he intended to sprinkle upon a thing that is susceptible to uncleanness and he sprinkled upon something that is not susceptible to uncleanness, if any of the water still remained on the hyssop he should not sprinkle with it again.

phrases.he: עַל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה, וְהִזָּה עַל דָּבָר שֶׁמְּקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה, אִם יֵשׁ בָּאֵזוֹב, יִשְׁנֶה.
phrases.en: [If he intended to sprinkle] upon a thing that is not susceptible to uncleanness and he sprinkled on that which is susceptible to uncleanness, even though there was still some water on the hyssop, he can sprinkle with it again.

phrases.he: עַל הָאָדָם, וְהִזָּה עַל הַבְּהֵמָה, אִם יֵשׁ בָּאֵזוֹב, לֹא יִשְׁנֶה.
phrases.en: [If he intended to sprinkle] upon a man and he sprinkled upon a beast, if any of the water remained on the hyssop he should not sprinkle with it again; But [if he intended to sprinkle] upon a beast and he sprinkled upon a man, even though there was still some water on the hyssop, he can sprinkle with it again.

phrases.he: עַל הַבְּהֵמָה, וְהִזָּה עַל הָאָדָם, אִם יֵשׁ בָּאֵזוֹב, יִשְׁנֶה. הַמַּיִם הַמְנַטְּפִים, כְּשֵׁרִים.
phrases.en: The water that drips off is valid, and therefore it conveys uncleanness as the usual hatat waters.

phrases.he: לְפִיכָךְ הֵם מְטַמְּאִין לְשֵׁם מֵי חַטָּאת
הַמַּזֶּה מֵחַלּוֹן שֶׁל רַבִּים וְנִכְנַס לַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְנִמְצְאוּ הַמַּיִם פְּסוּלִים, פָּטוּר.
phrases.en: If one was sprinkling from a window in a public domain and [a man who was thus sprinkled upon] entered the sanctuary, and the water was found to be invalid, he is exempt; But if the sprinkling was done from a private window and [a man who was thus sprinkled upon] entered the sanctuary, and the water was found to be invalid, he is liable.

phrases.he: מֵחַלּוֹן שֶׁל יָחִיד וְנִכְנַס לַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְנִמְצְאוּ הַמַּיִם פְּסוּלִין, חַיָּב.
phrases.en: A high priest, however, is exempt, whether the sprinkling upon him was done from a private window or from one in a public domain, for a high priest is never liable for entering the sanctuary.

phrases.he: אֲבָל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, בֵּין מֵחַלּוֹן שֶׁל יָחִיד בֵּין מֵחַלּוֹן שֶׁל רַבִּים, פָּטוּר, שֶׁאֵין כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל חַיָּב עַל בִּיאַת הַמִּקְדָּשׁ.
phrases.en: [The people] used to slip before a certain window in a public domain, and [nevertheless] they trod [on that spot] and did not refrain [from entering the sanctuary], because they said that hatat waters whose mitzvah had been performed do not defile.

phrases.he: מַחֲלִיקִין הָיוּ לִפְנֵי חַלּוֹן שֶׁל רַבִּים וְדוֹרְסִין וְלֹא נִמְנָעִין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָמְרוּ, מֵי חַטָּאת שֶׁעָשׂוּ מִצְוָתָן, אֵינָן מְטַמְּאִין
אוֹחֵז הוּא הַטָּהוֹר בַּקַּרְדֹּם הַטָּמֵא בִּכְנָפוֹ, וּמַזֶּה עָלָיו.
phrases.en: A clean person may hold in the corner of his garment an unclean axe and sprinkle upon it; And even though there is on it enough water for a sprinkling he remains clean.

phrases.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו כְּדֵי הַזָּיָה, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: How much water is necessary for sprinkling? Sufficient for the tops of the buds to be dipped and for the sprinkling to be performed.

phrases.he: כַּמָּה יְהֵא בַמַּיִם וְיִהְיֶה בָהֶם כְּדֵי הַזָּיָה.
כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּטְבִּיל רָאשֵׁי גִבְעוֹלִין וְיַזֶּה.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, רוֹאִים אוֹתָם כְּאִלּוּ הֵן עַל אֵזוֹב שֶׁל נְחשֶׁת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah ruled: they are regarded as though they were on a hyssop of brass.

phrases.he: הַמַּזֶּה בְאֵזוֹב טָמֵא, אִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ כַבֵּיצָה, הַמַּיִם פְּסוּלִים, וְהַזָּיָתוֹ פְסוּלָה.
phrases.en: One who sprinkles with unclean hyssop: if [the hyssop] was the amount of an egg the water becomes invalid, and the sprinkling is invalid.

phrases.he: אֵין בּוֹ כַבֵּיצָה, הַמַּיִם כְּשֵׁרִים, וְהַזָּיָתוֹ פְסוּלָה.
phrases.en: If it was less than the amount of an egg, the water remains valid but the sprinkling is invalid.

phrases.he: וּמְטַמֵּא אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ, וַחֲבֵרוֹ אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ, אֲפִלּוּ הֵן מֵאָה
phrases.en: It also defiles other hyssop, and that other hyssop to other, even if they be a hundred.

phrases.he: הַטָּהוֹר לְחַטָּאת שֶׁנִּטְמְאוּ יָדָיו, נִטְמָא גוּפוֹ, וּמְטַמֵּא אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ, וַחֲבֵרוֹ אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ, אֲפִלּוּ הֵן מֵאָה:
phrases.en: If the hands of a man who was clean for the hatat waters became unclean, his body also becomes unclean, and he conveys uncleanness to his fellow, and his fellow to his fellow, even if they be a hundred.

phrases.he: לָגִין שֶׁל חַטָּאת שֶׁנִּטְמְאוּ אֲחוֹרָיו, נִטְמָא תוֹכוֹ, וּמְטַמֵּא אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ, וַחֲבֵרוֹ אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ, אֲפִלּוּ הֵן מֵאָה. הַזּוֹג וְהָעִנְבָּל, חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: A flask for hatat waters whose outer part has become unclean, its inner part also becomes unclean, and it conveys uncleanness to another flask, and the other to another, even if they are a hundred. A bell and a clapper are regarded as connected.

phrases.he: כּוּשׁ שֶׁל רוֹבָן, לֹא יַזֶּה לֹא עַל הַכּוּשׁ וְלֹא עַל הַפִּיקָה. וְאִם הִזָּה, מֻזֶּה. שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן, חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: In the case of a spindle stick used for coarse material, one should not sprinkle on its stick or ring, but if he sprinkled on one, both are regarded as having been sprinkled upon.

phrases.he: עוֹר שֶׁל עֲרִיסָה שֶׁהוּא מְחֻבָּר לַפִּיקוֹת, חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: A spindle stick used for flax they are regarded as connected. If a leather cover of a crib is fastened to its knobs, both are regarded as connected.

phrases.he: הַמַּלְבֵּן, אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר לֹא לְטֻמְאָה וְלֹא לְטָהֳרָה.
phrases.en: The base is not regarded as connected either in respect of uncleanness or cleanness.

phrases.he: כָּל יְדוֹת הַכֵּלִים הַקְּדוּחוֹת, חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: All drilled handles of utensils are regarded as connected.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר, אַף הַחֲרוּקוֹת
phrases.en: Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri says: also those that are wedged into holes in the utensils.

phrases.he: הַסַּלִּים שֶׁבַּקַּנְתָּל, וְהַמִּטָּה שֶׁל טַרְבָּל, וְקֶרֶן שֶׁל כְּלִיבָה, וּקְרָנִין שֶׁל יוֹצְאֵי דְרָכִים, וְשַׁלְשֶׁלֶת הַמַּפְתְּחוֹת, וּשְׁלַל הַכּוֹבְסִים, וְהַבֶּגֶד שֶׁהוּא תָפוּר בְּכִלְאַיִם, חִבּוּר לַטֻּמְאָה וְאֵינוֹ חִבּוּר לַהַזָּיָה:
phrases.en: The baskets of a pack-saddle, the bed of a barrow, the iron corner of a bier, the [drinking] horns of travelers, a key chain, the loose stitches of washermen, and a garment stitched together with kilayim are regarded as connected in respect of uncleanness but not in that of sprinkling.

phrases.he: כִּסּוּי מֵחַם שֶׁהוּא מְחֻבָּר לְשַׁלְשֶׁלֶת,
phrases.en: The lid of a kettle which is joined to a chain: Bet Shammai say: these are regarded as connected in respect of uncleanness but not in respect of sprinkling.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, חִבּוּר לַטֻּמְאָה וְאֵינוֹ חִבּוּר לַהַזָּיָה.
phrases.en: Bet Hillel say: if he sprinkled on the kettle, it is the same as if the lid also was sprinkled upon; but if he sprinkled on the lid only it is not the same as if the kettle also was sprinkled upon.

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, הִזָּה עַל הַמֵּחַם, הֻזָּה הַכִּסּוּי.
phrases.en: All are eligible to sprinkle, except a tumtum, a hermaphrodite, a woman, and a child that is without understanding.

phrases.he: הִזָּה עַל הַכִּסּוּי, לֹא הֻזָּה הַמֵּחָם.
phrases.en: A woman may assist [a man] while he sprinkles, and hold the water for him while he dips and sprinkles.

phrases.he: הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִים לְהַזּוֹת, חוּץ מִטֻּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס וְהָאִשָּׁה.
phrases.en: If she held his hand, even if only at the time of sprinkling, it is invalid.

phrases.he: וְתִינוֹק שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דַעַת, הָאִשָּׁה מְסַעַדְתּוֹ וּמַזֶּה, וְאוֹחֶזֶת לוֹ בַמַּיִם וְהוּא טוֹבֵל וּמַזֶּה.
אִם אָחֲזָה בְיָדוֹ, אֲפִלּוּ בִשְׁעַת הַזָּיָה, פָּסוּל
טָבַל אֶת הָאֵזוֹב בַּיּוֹם וְהִזָּה בַיּוֹם, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: If he dipped the hyssop during the day and he sprinkled during the day, it is valid.

phrases.he: בַּיּוֹם וְהִזָּה בַלַּיְלָה, בַּלַּיְלָה וְהִזָּה בַיּוֹם, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: If he dipped it during the day and sprinkled at night, or dipped at night and sprinkled on the following day, it is invalid.

phrases.he: אֲבָל הוּא עַצְמוֹ טוֹבֵל בַּלַּיְלָה וּמַזֶּה בַיּוֹם, שֶׁאֵין מַזִּין עַד שֶׁתָּנֵץ הַחַמָּה.
phrases.en: But he himself may immerse at night and then sprinkle on the following day, for sprinkling is not allowed until the sun is risen.

phrases.he: וְכֻלָּן שֶׁעָשׂוּ מִשֶּׁעָלָה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר, כָּשֵׁר
phrases.en: And if any of these was done as early as the rise of dawn it is valid.

phrases.he: שֵׁשׁ מַעֲלוֹת בַּמִּקְוָאוֹת, זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ, וְזוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ.
phrases.en: There are six degrees of mikvaot, each superior to the other.

phrases.he: מֵי גְבָאִים, שָׁתָה טָמֵא וְשָׁתָה טָהוֹר, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: The water of pools [smaller than 40 seah] if an unclean person drank of it and then a clean person drank of it, he becomes unclean; If an unclean person drank of it and then drew water from it in a clean vessel, [the vessel] becomes unclean; If an unclean person drank of it and then a loaf of terumah fell in: If he washed [his hands] in it, it becomes unclean; But if he did not wash [his hands] in it, it continues clean.

phrases.he: שָׁתָה טָמֵא וּמִלֵּא בִכְלִי טָהוֹר, טָמֵא.
שָׁתָה טָמֵא וְנָפַל כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, אִם הֵדִיחַ, טָמֵא.
וְאִם לֹא הֵדִיחַ, טָהוֹר
מִלֵּא בִכְלִי טָמֵא וְשָׁתָה טָהוֹר, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If one drew water from it in an unclean vessel and then a clean person drank [out of the pit], he becomes unclean.

phrases.he: מִלֵּא בִכְלִי טָמֵא וּמִלֵּא בִכְלִי טָהוֹר, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If one drew water [from it] in an unclean vessel and then drew water from it in a clean vessel, it becomes unclean.

phrases.he: מִלֵּא בִכְלִי טָמֵא וְנָפַל כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, אִם הֵדִיחַ, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If one drew water [from it] in an unclean vessel and a loaf of terumah fell in: If he washed [his hands] in it, it becomes unclean; But if he did not wash [his hands] in it, it is clean.

phrases.he: וְאִם לֹא הֵדִיחַ, טָהוֹר
נָפְלוּ מַיִם טְמֵאִים וְשָׁתָה טָהוֹר, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If unclean water fell into it and a clean person drank of it, he becomes unclean.

phrases.he: נָפְלוּ מַיִם טְמֵאִים וּמִלֵּא בִכְלִי טָהוֹר, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If unclean water fell into it and then water was drawn from it in a clean vessel, it becomes unclean.

phrases.he: נָפְלוּ מַיִם טְמֵאִים וְנָפַל כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, אִם הֵדִיחַ, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If unclean water fell into it and a loaf of terumah fell in: If he washed [his hands] in it, it becomes unclean; But if he did not wash [his hands] in it, it is clean.

phrases.he: וְאִם לֹא הֵדִיחַ, טָהוֹר.
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, בֵּין שֶׁהֵדִיחַ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא הֵדִיחַ, טָמֵא:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: it becomes unclean whether he washed in it or whether he did not wash in it.

phrases.he: נָפַל לְתוֹכָן מֵת, אוֹ שֶׁהָלַךְ בָּהֶן הַטָּמֵא, וְשָׁתָה טָהוֹר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If a corpse fell into it or an unclean person walked in it, and a clean person drank of it, he is clean.

phrases.he: אֶחָד מֵי גְבָאִים, מֵי בוֹרוֹת, מֵי שִׁיחִים, מֵי מְעָרוֹת, מֵי תַמְצִיּוֹת שֶׁפָּסְקוּ, וּמִקְוָאוֹת שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, בִּשְׁעַת הַגְּשָׁמִים הַכֹּל טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: The same rule applies to the water of pools, the water of cisterns, the water of ditches, the water of caverns, the water of rain flows which have stopped, and mikvehs of less than forty seahs.

phrases.he: פָּסְקוּ הַגְּשָׁמִים, הַקְּרוֹבִים לָעִיר וְלַדֶּרֶךְ, טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: They are all clean during the time of rain; When the rain has stopped those near to a city or to a road are unclean, and those distant remain clean until the majority of people pass [that way].

phrases.he: וְהָרְחוֹקִים, טְהוֹרִין, עַד שֶׁיְּהַלְּכוּ רֹב בְּנֵי אָדָם
מֵאֵימָתַי טָהֳרָתָן.
phrases.en: When do they become clean?Bet Shammai say: when their contents have been increased [by more than the original quantity] and they overflow.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מִשֶּׁיִּרְבּוּ וְיִשְׁטֹפוּ.
phrases.en: Bet Hillel say: when their contents have been increased [by more than their original quantity] even if they do not overflow.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, רַבּוּ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁטְפוּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: when they overflow although their contents have not been so increased.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, שָׁטְפוּ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא רַבּוּ.
phrases.en: [These] are valid [for preparing dough] for hallah and for the washing of the hands.

phrases.he: כְּשֵׁרִין לַחַלָּה וְלִטֹּל מֵהֶן לַיָּדָיִם
לְמַעְלָה מֵהֶן, מֵי תַמְצִיּוֹת שֶׁלֹּא פָסְקוּ.
phrases.en: Superior to such [water] is the water of rain flows which have not stopped.

phrases.he: שָׁתָה טָמֵא וְשָׁתָה טָהוֹר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If an unclean person drank of it and then a clean person drank of it, he is clean.

phrases.he: שָׁתָה טָמֵא וּמִלֵּא בִכְלִי טָהוֹר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If an unclean person drank of it and water was then drawn from it in a clean vessel, it is clean.

phrases.he: שָׁתָה טָמֵא וְנָפַל כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵדִיחַ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If an unclean person drank of it and a loaf of terumah fell in, even if he washed his hand in it, it is clean.

phrases.he: מִלֵּא בִכְלִי טָמֵא וְשָׁתָה טָהוֹר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If one drew water from it in an unclean vessel and then a clean person drank [out of the pool], he is clean.

phrases.he: מִלֵּא בִכְלִי טָמֵא וּמִלֵּא בִכְלִי טָהוֹר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If one drew water from it in an unclean vessel and a loaf of terumah fell [into the pool], even if he washed his hands in it, it is clean.

phrases.he: מִלֵּא בִכְלִי טָמֵא וְנָפַל כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵדִיחַ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If unclean water fell into it and a clean person drank of it, he is clean.

phrases.he: נָפְלוּ מַיִם טְמֵאִים וְשָׁתָה טָהוֹר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If unclean water fell into it and one drew water from it in a clean vessel, it is clean.

phrases.he: נָפְלוּ מַיִם טְמֵאִים וּמִלֵּא בִכְלִי טָהוֹר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If unclean water fell into it and a loaf of terumah fell in, even if he washed his hands in it, it is clean.

phrases.he: נָפְלוּ מַיִם טְמֵאִים וְנָפַל כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵדִיחַ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: [All such water] is valid for terumah and for the washing of the hands.

phrases.he: כְּשֵׁרִים לַתְּרוּמָה וְלִטֹּל מֵהֶם לַיָּדָיִם
לְמַעְלָה מֵהֶן, מִקְוֶה שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, שֶׁבּוֹ טוֹבְלִין וּמַטְבִּילִין.
phrases.en: Superior to such [water] is [the water of] the mikveh containing forty seahs, for in it people may immerse themselves and immerse other [things].

phrases.he: לְמַעְלָה מֵהֶן, מַעְיָן שֶׁמֵּימָיו מֻעָטִין וְרַבּוּ עָלָיו מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין, שָׁוֶה לַמִּקְוֶה לְטַהֵר בְּאַשְׁבֹּרֶן, וְלַמַּעְיָן לְהַטְבִּיל בּוֹ בְּכָל שֶׁהוּא
phrases.en: Superior to such [water] is [the water of] a spring whose own water is little but has been increased by a greater quantity of drawn water. It is equivalent to the mikveh in as much as it may render clean by standing water, and to an [ordinary] spring in as much as one may immerse in it whatever the quantity of its contents.

phrases.he: לְמַעְלָה מֵהֶן, מַיִם מֻכִּין, שֶׁהֵן מְטַהֲרִין בְּזוֹחֲלִין.
phrases.en: Superior to them are "smitten waters" which can purify even when flowing [on the ground].

phrases.he: לְמַעְלָה מֵהֶן, מַיִם חַיִּים, שֶׁבָּהֶן טְבִילָה לַזָּבִים, וְהַזָּיָה לַמְצֹרָעִים, וּכְשֵׁרִים לְקַדֵּשׁ מֵהֶן מֵי חַטָּאת
phrases.en: Superior to them are "living waters" for in them there is immersion for zavim and sprinkling for metzoraim, and they are valid for the preparation of the hatat waters.

phrases.he: הַטָּמֵא שֶׁיָּרַד לִטְבֹּל, סָפֵק טָבַל סָפֵק לֹא טָבַל, אֲפִלּוּ טָבַל, סָפֵק יֶשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה סָפֵק אֵין בּוֹ.
phrases.en: An unclean man who went down to immerse himself: If it is doubtful whether he did immerse himself or not; And even if he did immerse himself, it is doubtful whether the mikveh contained forty seahs or not; And if there were two mikvehs, one containing forty seahs but the other not containing forty seahs, and he immersed himself in one of them but he does not know in which of them he immersed himself, In such a doubt he is unclean.

phrases.he: שְׁנֵי מִקְוָאוֹת, אֶחָד יֶשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה וְאֶחָד שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ, טָבַל בְּאַחַד מֵהֶם וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ בְּאֵיזֶה מֵהֶן טָבַל, סְפֵקוֹ טָמֵא
מִקְוֶה שֶׁנִּמְדַּד וְנִמְצָא חָסֵר, כָּל טָהֳרוֹת שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל גַּבָּיו לְמַפְרֵעַ, בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: If a mikveh was measured and was found lacking [in its prescribed quantity], all things which had been purified in it, whether in private domain or in a public domain, are accounted unclean retroactively.

phrases.he: בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בְּטֻמְאָה חֲמוּרָה.
phrases.en: To what does this rule apply? To a serious uncleanness.

phrases.he: אֲבָל בְּטֻמְאָה קַלָּה, כְּגוֹן אָכַל אֳכָלִים טְמֵאִים, וְשָׁתָה מַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִים, בָּא רֹאשׁוֹ וְרֻבּוֹ בְּמַיִם שְׁאוּבִים, אוֹ שֶׁנָּפְלוּ עַל רֹאשׁוֹ וְעַל רֻבּוֹ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין, וְיָרַד לִטְבֹּל, סָפֵק טָבַל סָפֵק לֹא טָבַל, אֲפִלּוּ טָבַל, סָפֵק יֶשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה סָפֵק אֵין בּוֹ.
phrases.en: But in the case of a lesser uncleanness, for instance if he ate unclean foods or drank unclean liquids, or if his head and the greater part of his body entered into drawn water, or if three logs of drawn water fell on his head and the greater part of his body, and he then went down to immerse himself and he is in doubt whether he immersed himself or not, or even if he did immerse himself there is [still] a doubt whether the mikveh contained forty seahs or not, or if there were two mikvehs, one containing forty seahs and not the other, and he immersed himself in one of them but does not know in which of them he immersed himself, in such a doubt he is accounted clean.

phrases.he: שְׁנֵי מִקְוָאוֹת, אֶחָד יֶשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, וְאֶחָד שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ, טָבַל בְּאַחַד מֵהֶן וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ בְּאֵיזֶה מֵהֶן טָבַל, סְפֵקוֹ טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose considers him unclean, for Rabbi Yose says: anything which is presumed to be unclean always remains in a condition of unfitness until it is known that it has become clean; but if there is a doubt whether a person became unclean or caused uncleanness, it is to be accounted clean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְטַמֵּא, שֶׁרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא בְחֶזְקַת טֻמְאָה, לְעוֹלָם הוּא בִפְסוּלוֹ, עַד שֶׁיִּוָּדַע שֶׁטָּהַר.
אֲבָל סְפֵקוֹ לִטָּמֵא וּלְטַמֵּא, טָהוֹר

סְפֵק מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין שֶׁטִּהֲרוּ חֲכָמִים, סָפֵק נָפְלוּ, סָפֵק לֹא נָפְלוּ, אֲפִלּוּ נָפְלוּ, סָפֵק יֶשׁ בָּהֶם אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה סָפֵק אֵין בָּהֶם, שְׁנֵי מִקְוָאוֹת, אֶחָד יֶשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה וְאֶחָד אֵין בּוֹ, נָפַל לְאַחַד מֵהֶן וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ לְאֵיזֶה מֵהֶן נָפַל, סְפֵקוֹ טָהוֹר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ בַמֶּה יִתְלֶה.
phrases.en: The case of a doubt about drawn water which the sages have declared clean;If there is a doubt whether [three logs of drawn water] fell into the mikveh or not, Or even if they did fall in, there is a doubt whether [the mikveh] contained forty seahs or not, Or if there were two mikvehs one of which contained forty seahs and the other did not, and drawn water fell into one of them and it is not known into which of them it fell, In such a doubt it is accounted clean, because there exists [a possibility] on which we may depend [in declaring it clean].

phrases.he: הָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם פְּחוּתִים מֵאַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, וְנָפַל לְאַחַד מֵהֶם וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ לְאֵיזֶה מֵהֶן נָפַל, סְפֵקוֹ טָמֵא, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בַמֶּה יִתְלֶה
phrases.en: If they both contained less than forty seahs, and [drawn water] fell into one of them and it is not known into which of them it fell, in such a doubt it is accounted unclean, because there exists no [possibility] on which we may depend [in declaring it clean].

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, רְבִיעִית מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין בַּתְּחִלָּה, פּוֹסְלִין אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה, וּשְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין עַל פְּנֵי הַמַּיִם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: a quarter-log of drawn water in the beginning makes the mikveh invalid, and three logs on the surface of the water.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בֵּין בַּתְּחִלָּה בֵּין בַּסּוֹף, שִׁעוּרוֹ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין:
phrases.en: But the sages say: both in the beginning and at the end, the measure [which makes the mikveh invalid] is three logs.

phrases.he: מִקְוֶה שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ שָׁלשׁ גֻּמּוֹת שֶׁל מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין שֶׁל לֹג לֹג, אִם יָדוּעַ שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹכוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאִין מַיִם כְּשֵׁרִין עַד שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעוּ לַגֻּמָּא הַשְּׁלִישִׁית, כָּשֵׁר. וְאִם לָאו, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: If there were three cavities in a mikveh each holding a log of drawn water, if it is known that forty seahs of valid water fell in before reaching the third cavity, [such a mikveh is] valid; otherwise it is invalid.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַכְשִׁיר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא כְמִקְוֶה סָמוּךְ לְמִקְוֶה
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon declares it valid, since it resembles a mikveh adjoining another mikveh.

phrases.he: הַמְסַנֵּק אֶת הַטִּיט לַצְּדָדִין וּמָשְׁכוּ מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: If one scraped mud to the sides and then three logs [of water] were drawn out from it [from the mud], [the mikveh is still] valid.

phrases.he: הָיָה תוֹלֵשׁ וּמָשְׁכוּ מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: But if removed the mud away and three logs were drawn from it [into the mikveh] it becomes invalid.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַכְשִׁיר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְכַּוֵּן לִשְׁאֹב
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon pronounces it valid, since there was no intention to draw [the water].

phrases.he: הַמַּנִּיחַ קַנְקַנִּים בְּרֹאשׁ הַגַּג לְנַגְּבָן וְנִתְמַלְּאוּ מַיִם,
phrases.en: If one had left wine-jars on the roof to dry and they became filled with water: Rabbi Eliezer says: if it was the season of rain and there was [in the cistern] a little water, one may break the jars; otherwise one may not break them.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אִם עוֹנַת גְּשָׁמִים הִיא, אִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ כִמְעַט מַיִם בַּבּוֹר, יְשַׁבֵּר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua says: in either case one may break them or tilt them over, but one may not empty [them into the cistern].

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, לֹא יְשַׁבֵּר.
רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ יְשַׁבֵּר, אוֹ יִכְפֶּה, אֲבָל לֹא יְעָרֶה:
הַסַּיָּד שֶׁשָּׁכַח עָצִיץ בַּבּוֹר וְנִתְמַלֵּא מַיִם, אִם הָיוּ הַמַּיִם צָפִים עַל גַּבָּיו כָּל שֶׁהוּא, יְשַׁבֵּר.
phrases.en: A plasterer forgot his lime-tub in a cistern and it became filled with water: if water flowed above it a little, it may be broken; and if not, it may not be broken, the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, לֹא יְשַׁבֵּר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ יְשַׁבֵּר:
phrases.en: But Rabbi Joshua says: in either case it may be broken.

phrases.he: הַמְסַדֵּר קַנְקַנִּים בְּתוֹךְ הַבּוֹר וְנִתְמַלְּאוּ מַיִם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבָּלַע הַבּוֹר אֶת מֵימָיו, הֲרֵי זֶה יְשַׁבֵּר:
phrases.en: If one had arranged wine-jars in a cistern and they became filled with water, even though the water of the cistern was all soaked up, they may be broken.

phrases.he: מִקְוֶה שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה מַיִם וָטִיט,
phrases.en: A mikveh which contains forty seahs of water and mud [combined]: Rabbi Eliezer says: one may immerse objects in the water but one may not immerse them in the mud.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, מַטְבִּילִין בַּמַּיִם וְאֵין מַטְבִּילִין בַּטִּיט.
phrases.en: But Rabbi Joshua says: in the water and also in the mud.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, בַּמַּיִם וּבַטִּיט. בְּאֵיזֶה טִיט מַטְבִּילִין.
phrases.en: In what kind of mud may objects be immersed? Mud over which water floats.

phrases.he: בְּטִיט שֶׁהַמַּיִם צָפִים עַל גַּבָּיו.
phrases.en: If the water was on one side only, Rabbi Joshua agrees that objects may be immersed in the water but may not be immersed in the mud.

phrases.he: הָיוּ הַמַּיִם מִצַּד אֶחָד, מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ שֶׁמַּטְבִּילִין בַּמַּיִם וְאֵין מַטְבִּילִין בַּטִּיט. בְּאֵיזֶה טִיט אָמְרוּ.
phrases.en: Of what kind of mud have they spoken? Mud into which a reed will sink of itself, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: בְּטִיט שֶׁהַקָּנֶה יוֹרֵד מֵאֵלָיו, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין קְנֵה הַמִּדָּה עוֹמֵד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: [mud] in which a measuring-rod will not stand upright.

phrases.he: אַבָּא אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן דּוֹלְעַאי אוֹמֵר, מְקוֹם שֶׁהַמִּשְׁקֹלֶת יוֹרֶדֶת.
phrases.en: Abba Elazar ben Dulai says: [mud] into which a plummet will sink.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, הַיּוֹרֵד בְּפִי חָבִית.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: such as will go down into the mouth of a jar.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, הַנִּכְנָס בִּשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הַנּוֹד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: such as will enter into the tube of a water- skin.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר, הַנִּמְדָּד בַּלֹּג
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar bar Zadok says: such as can be measured in a log measure.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, שְׁנֵי מִקְוָאוֹת שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, וְנָפְלוּ לָזֶה לֹג וּמֶחֱצָה וְלָזֶה לֹג וּמֶחֱצָה וְנִתְעָרְבוּ, כְּשֵׁרִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא נִקְרָא עֲלֵיהֶן שֵׁם פְּסוּל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: two mikvehs neither of which contains forty seahs and a log and a half [of drawn water] fell into this one and a log and a half into this one, and then they are mixed together, they remain valid, since they had never been called as invalid.

phrases.he: אֲבָל מִקְוֶה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה וְנָפְלוּ בוֹ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין וְנֶחֱלַק לִשְׁנַיִם, פָּסוּל, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּקְרָא עָלָיו שֵׁם פְּסוּל.
phrases.en: But if there is a mikveh holding less than forty seahs, and three logs [of drawn water] fell into it, and it was then divided into two, it is invalid, since it had already been called invalid.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מַכְשִׁיר, שֶׁהָיָה
רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, כָּל מִקְוֶה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה וְנָפְלוּ לוֹ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין וְחָסַר אֲפִלּוּ קֹרְטוֹב, כָּשֵׁר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁחָסְרוּ לוֹ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua declares it valid, for Rabbi Joshua used to say: any mikveh containing less than forty seahs into which three logs [of drawn water] fell and from which a kortov was withdrawn becomes valid, since the three logs have also been diminished.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, לְעוֹלָם הוּא בִפְסוּלוֹ, עַד שֶׁיֵּצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ מְלוֹאוֹ וָעוֹד:
