phrases.en: Rabbi Nehemiah and Rabbi Shimon declare them clean in these cases.

phrases.he: זָב שֶׁהָיָה מֻטָּל עַל חֲמִשָּׁה סַפְסָלִים אוֹ עַל חָמֵשׁ פֻּנְדִּיּוֹת, לְאָרְכָּן, טְמֵאִין. לְרָחְבָּן, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: A zav who lays across five benches, or five money-belts: If lengthwise, he [makes them] unclean; But breadthwise, they are clean.

phrases.he: יָשֵׁן, סָפֵק שֶׁנִּתְהַפֵּךְ עֲלֵיהֶן, טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: If he slept [on them], and it was doubful that he had turned over onto them, they are unclean.

phrases.he: הָיָה מֻטָּל עַל שִׁשָּׁה כִסְיוֹת, שְׁתֵּי יָדָיו עַל שְׁנַיִם, שְׁתֵּי רַגְלָיו עַל שְׁנַיִם, רֹאשׁוֹ עַל אֶחָד, גּוּפוֹ עַל אֶחָד, אֵין טָמֵא אֶלָּא זֶה שֶׁתַּחַת הַגּוּף.
phrases.en: If he was lying on six seats, with two hands on two [seats], two feet on another two, his head on one, with his body on another one, only that one on which his body lay is rendered unclean.

phrases.he: עוֹמֵד עַל שְׁנֵי כִסְאוֹת,
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אִם רְחוֹקִין זֶה מִזֶּה, טְהוֹרִין:
phrases.en: If [a zav] stood on two seats: Rabbi Shimon says: if these were distant one from the other, they remain clean.

phrases.he: עֶשֶׂר טַלִּיּוֹת זוֹ עַל גַּב זוֹ, יָשֵׁן עַל גַּבֵּי הָעֶלְיוֹנָה, כֻּלָּן טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: Ten cloaks one on top of the other, if he sat on the uppermost one, all are unclean.

phrases.he: הַזָּב בְּכַף מֹאזְנַיִם וּמִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב כְּנֶגְדּוֹ, כָּרַע הַזָּב, טְהוֹרִין. כָּרְעוּ הֵן, טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: A zav who was on one scale of a balance and in the other scale opposite there were objects fit to sit or lie upon: If the zav pushed them up, they are clean. But if they pushed him up, they are unclean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, בִּיחִידִי, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: if there was one object it becomes unclean, but if there were many they remain clean, since none of them had borne the greater part [of the zav's weight].

phrases.he: וּבִמְרֻבִּין, טָהוֹר, שֶׁאֵין אֶחָד נוֹשֵׂא אֶת רֻבּוֹ
הַזָּב בְּכַף מֹאזְנַיִם וְאֳכָלִין וּמַשְׁקִין בְּכַף שְׁנִיָּה, טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: If a zav [sat] in one scale of the balance, while food and liquids were in the other scale, [the latter become] unclean.

phrases.he: וּבַמֵּת, הַכֹּל טָהוֹר, חוּץ מִן הָאָדָם.
phrases.en: In the case of a corpse, everything remains clean except for a man.

phrases.he: זֶה חֹמֶר בַּזָּב מִבַּמֵּת.
phrases.en: This is [an example of] the greater stringency applying to a zav than to a corpse; and there is a greater stringency in the case of a corpse than a zav.

phrases.he: חֹמֶר בַּמֵּת מִבַּזָּב, שֶׁהַזָּב עוֹשֶׂה מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב מִתַּחְתָּיו לְטַמֵּא אָדָם וּלְטַמֵּא בְגָדִים, וְעַל גַּבָּיו מַדָּף לְטַמֵּא אֳכָלִין וּמַשְׁקִין, מַה שֶּׁאֵין הַמֵּת מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.en: For whereas the zav defiles all objects on which he sits or lies upon, so that these likewise convey uncleanness to people and garments, and he conveys to what is above him madaf uncleanness, so that these in turn defile food and liquids. Whereas in the case of a corpse no such uncleanness is conveyed.

phrases.he: חֹמֶר בַּמֵּת, שֶׁהַמֵּת מְטַמֵּא בְאֹהֶל וּמְטַמֵּא טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה, מַה שֶּׁאֵין הַזָּב מְטַמֵּא
phrases.en: Greater stringency is also found in the case of a corpse, since it can convey uncleanness by overshadowing, and it defiles seven days’ defilement, whereas in the case of a zav no such uncleanness is conveyed.

phrases.he: הָיָה יוֹשֵׁב עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּטָּה וְאַרְבַּע טַלִּיּוֹת תַּחַת אַרְבַּע רַגְלֵי הַמִּטָּה, טְמֵאוֹת, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לַעֲמֹד עַל שָׁלשׁ. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַהֵר.
phrases.en: If he sat on a bed and there were four cloaks under the four legs of the bed, all become unclean, since the bed cannot stand on three legs; But Rabbi Shimon declares them clean.

phrases.he: הָיָה רוֹכֵב עַל גַּבֵּי בְהֵמָה וְאַרְבַּע טַלִּיּוֹת תַּחַת אַרְבַּע רַגְלֵי בְהֵמָה, טְהוֹרוֹת, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא יְכוֹלָה לַעֲמֹד עַל שְׁלשָׁה.
phrases.en: If he rode on a beast and there were four cloaks under the legs of the beast, they are clean, since the beast can stand upon three legs.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה טַלִּית אַחַת תַּחַת שְׁנֵי יָדַיִם, תַּחַת שְׁנֵי רַגְלַיִם, תַּחַת יָד וָרֶגֶל, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: If there was one cloak under its two forelegs or its two hindlegs, or under a foreleg and a hindleg, it becomes unclean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, הַסּוּס מְטַמֵּא בְרַגְלָיו וְהַחֲמוֹר בְּיָדָיו, שֶׁמִּשְׁעֶנֶת הַסּוּס עַל רַגְלָיו וּמִשְׁעֶנֶת הַחֲמוֹר עַל יָדָיו.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: a horse conveys uncleanness through its hindlegs and a donkey through its forelegs, since a horse leans upon its hindlegs and a donkey upon its forelegs.

phrases.he: יָשַׁב עַל קוֹרַת בֵּית הַבַּד, כֵּלִים שֶׁבָּעֵקֶל טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: If he sat on a beam of an olive-press, the vessels in the olive-press receptacle are unclean.

phrases.he: עַל הַמַּכְבֵּשׁ שֶׁל כּוֹבֵס, כֵּלִים שֶׁתַּחְתָּיו, טְהוֹרִין. רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה מְטַמֵּא
phrases.en: [If he sat] on a clothing press, the garments beneath it are clean. Rabbi Nehemiah declares them unclean.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹגֵעַ בַּזָּב אוֹ שֶׁהַזָּב נוֹגֵע בּוֹ, הַמַּסִּיט אֶת הַזָּב אוֹ שֶׁהַזָּב מַסִּיטוֹ, מְטַמֵּא אֳכָלִים וּמַשְׁקִים וּכְלֵי שֶׁטֶף בְּמַגָּע, אֲבָל לֹא בְמַשָּׂא. כְּלָל
phrases.en: One who touches a zav, or whom a zav touches, who moves a zav or whom a zav moves, defiles by contact food and liquids and vessels that are rinsed, but not by carrying.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, כָּל הַמְטַמֵּא בְגָדִים בִּשְׁעַת מַגָּעוֹ, מְטַמֵּא אֳכָלִים וּמַשְׁקִין לִהְיוֹת תְּחִלָּה, וְהַיָּדַיִם לִהְיוֹת שְׁנִיּוֹת, וְאֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא לֹא אָדָם וְלֹא כְלֵי חֶרֶס.
phrases.en: A general principle was stated by Rabbi Joshua: anyone that defile garments while still in contact [with their source of uncleanness] also defiles foods and liquids so as to become [unclean] in the first grade, and the hands so that they become [unclean] in the second grade; but they do not defile people or earthenware vessels.

phrases.he: לְאַחַר פְּרִישָׁתוֹ מִמְּטַמְּאָיו, מְטַמֵּא מַשְׁקִין לִהְיוֹת תְּחִלָּה, וְהָאֳכָלִין וְהַיָּדַיִם לִהְיוֹת שְׁנִיּוֹת, וְאֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא בְגָדִים
phrases.en: After they separated from their source of uncleanness they defile liquids so as to become [unclean] in the first grade, and food and the hands so that they become [unclean] in the second grade, but they do not defile garments.

phrases.he: וְעוֹד כְּלָל אַחֵר אָמְרוּ.
phrases.en: They said yet another general principle: All that is carried above a zav becomes defiled, but all those things above which he is carried are clean except objects on which he can sit or lie upon, and a person.

phrases.he: כֹּל הַנִּשָּׂא עַל גַּבֵּי הַזָּב, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: How so? If a zav had his finger beneath a layer of stones and one that was clean was above, he conveys uncleanness at two [degrees of remove] and disqualifies [terumah] at one [further remove].

phrases.he: וְכֹל שֶׁהַזָּב נִשָּׂא עָלָיו, טָהוֹר, חוּץ מִן הָרָאוּי לְמִשְׁכָּב וּלְמוֹשָׁב וְהָאָדָם. כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: If he separated [from the source of uncleanness] he still defiles at one remove and disqualifies [terumah] at yet one [further remove].

phrases.he: אֶצְבָּעוֹ שֶׁל זָב תַּחַת הַנִּדְבָּךְ, הַטָּהוֹר מִלְמַעְלָן, מְטַמֵּא שְׁנַיִם וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד.
phrases.en: If the unclean one was above, and the clean person below, he defiles at two [removes], and disqualifies [terumah] at yet one [further remove].

phrases.he: פֵּרַשׁ, מְטַמֵּא אֶחָד וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד.
phrases.en: If he separated [from the source of uncleanness], he defiles at one [remove] and disqualifies [terumah] at yet one [more remove].

phrases.he: הַטָּמֵא מִלְמַעְלָן וְהַטָּהוֹר מִלְּמַטָּן, מְטַמֵּא שְׁנַיִם וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד.
phrases.en: If foods or liquids, or objects on which he could sit or lie upon or other articles were above, they defile at one remove, and disqualify [terumah] at one [further remove].

phrases.he: פֵּרַשׁ, מְטַמֵא אֶחָד וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד.
phrases.en: If they had become separated [from the source of uncleanness], they defile at one [remove] and disqualify [terumah] at one [more remove].

phrases.he: הָאֳכָלִין וְהַמַּשְׁקִין, הַמִּשְׁכָּב, וְהַמּוֹשָׁב וְהַמַּדָּף מִלְמַעְלָן, מְטַמְּאִין שְׁנַיִם וּפוֹסְלִין אֶחָד.
phrases.en: All objects fit to sit or lie upon that were below defile at two [removes], and disqualify [terumah] at one [more remove].

phrases.he: פֵּרְשׁוּ, מְטַמְּאִין אֶחָד וּפוֹסְלִין אֶחָד.
phrases.en: If they had become separate [from the source of uncleanness], they defile at two [removes] and disqualify [terumah] at one [more remove] Foods and liquids and other articles that are below, remain clean.

phrases.he: וְהַמִּשְׁכָּב וְהַמּוֹשָׁב מִלְּמַטָּן, מְטַמְּאִין שְׁנַיִם וּפוֹסְלִין אֶחָד.
פֵּרְשׁוּ, מְטַמְּאִין שְׁנַיִם וּפוֹסְלִין אֶחָד.
הָאֳכָלִין וְהַמַּשְׁקִין וְהַמַּדָּף מִלְּמַטָּן, טְהוֹרִין
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָמְרוּ, כֹּל הַנּוֹשֵׂא וְנִשָּׂא עַל גַּבֵּי מִשְׁכָּב, טָהוֹר, חוּץ מִן הָאָדָם.
phrases.en: Whatever carries or is carried by objects on which one sits or lies upon remain clean, except for a person.

phrases.he: כֹּל הַנּוֹשֵׂא וְנִשָּׂא עַל גַּבֵּי הַנְּבֵלָה, טָהוֹר, חוּץ מִן הַמַּסִּיט.
phrases.en: Whatever carries or is carried by carrion is clean, except for one that shifts it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַף הַנּוֹשֵׂא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: also one that carries it.

phrases.he: כֹּל הַנּוֹשֵׂא וְנִשָּׂא עַל גַּבֵּי הַמֵּת, טָהוֹר, חוּץ מִן הַמַּאֲהִיל, וְאָדָם בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא מַסִּיט
phrases.en: Whatever carries or is carried upon a corpse remains clean, except for one that overshadows, or a person when he shifts it.

phrases.he: מִקְצָת טָמֵא עַל הַטָּהוֹר וּמִקְצָת טָהוֹר עַל הַטָּמֵא, חִבּוּרֵי טָמֵא עַל הַטָּהוֹר וְחִבּוּרֵי טָהוֹר עַל הַטָּמֵא, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If part of an unclean person rests upon a clean person, or part of a clean person upon an unclean person, or if things connected to an unclean person [rest] upon a clean person, or if things connected to a clean person upon one unclean, he becomes unclean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, מִקְצָת טָמֵא עַל הַטָּהוֹר, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: if part of an unclean person is upon a clean person, he is unclean; but if part of a clean person is upon one that is unclean, he is clean.

phrases.he: וּמִקְצָת טָהוֹר עַל הַטָּמֵא, טָהוֹר
הַטָּמֵא עַל מִקְצָת הַמִּשְׁכָּב וְהַטָּהוֹר עַל מִקְצָת הַמִּשְׁכָּב, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If an unclean person rests upon part of an object fit to lie upon, or a clean person rests upon part of an object fit to lie upon, it becomes unclean.

phrases.he: מִקְצָת טָמֵא עַל הַמִּשְׁכָּב וּמִקְצָת טָהוֹר עַל הַמִּשְׁכָּב, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If part of an unclean person rests on an object fit to lie upon, or part of a clean person rests upon an object fit to lie upon, it remains clean.

phrases.he: נִמְצֵאת טֻמְאָה נִכְנֶסֶת לוֹ וְיוֹצֵאת מִמֶּנּוּ בְּמִעוּטוֹ.
phrases.en: Thus we find that impurity enters it and goes out of it by its lesser part.

phrases.he: וְכֵן כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה שֶׁהוּא נָתוּן עַל גַּבֵּי מִשְׁכָּב וְהַנְּיָר בֵּינְתַיִם, בֵּין מִלְמַעְלָן בֵּין מִלְּמַטָּן, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Similarly, if a loaf of terumah was placed upon an object fit to lie upon [that was unclean] and there paper in between, whether it was above or below, it remains clean.

phrases.he: וְכֵן בְּאֶבֶן הַמְנֻגַּעַת, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Similarly, in the case of a stone with scale disease it remains clean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַמֵּא בָזוֹ
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon pronounced such a case unclean.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּזָב, וּבְזָבָה, וּבְנִדָּה, וּבְיוֹלֶדֶת, וּבִמְצֹרָע, בְּמִשְׁכָּב, וּמוֹשָׁב, מְטַמֵּא שְׁנַיִם וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד.
phrases.en: He who touches a zav, or a zavah, a menstruant, or a woman after childbirth, or a metzora, or any object on which these had been sitting or lying, conveys uncleanness at two [removes] and disqualifies [terumah] at one [further remove].

phrases.he: פֵּרַשׁ, מְטַמֵּא אֶחָד וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד, אֶחָד הַנּוֹגֵעַ וְאֶחָד הַמַּסִּיט וְאֶחָד הַנּוֹשֵׂא וְאֶחָד הַנִּשָּׂא
phrases.en: If he separated, he still conveys uncleanness at one [remove], and disqualifies [terumah] at one [further remove]. This is true whether he had touched, or had shifted, or had carried, or was carried.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּזוֹבוֹ שֶׁל זָב, וּבְרֻקּוֹ, בְּשִׁכְבַת זַרְעוֹ, בְּמֵימֵי רַגְלָיו, וּבְדַם הַנִּדָּה, מְטַמֵּא שְׁנַיִם וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד.
phrases.en: If one touches the discharge of a zav, his spittle, semen or urine, or the blood of a menstruant, he conveys uncleanness at two [removes], and disqualifies [terumah] at one [more remove]; If he separated, he defiles at one [remove] and disqualifies [terumah] at one [more remove].

phrases.he: פֵּרַשׁ, מְטַמֵּא אֶחָד וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד, אֶחָד הַנּוֹגֵעַ וְאֶחָד הַמַּסִּיט.
phrases.en: This is the case whether he had touched or moved it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַף הַנּוֹשֵׂא:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer said: also if he had carried it.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹשֵׂא אֶת הַמֶּרְכָּב וְהַנִּשָּׂא עָלָיו וְהַמַּסִּיטוֹ, מְטַמֵּא שְׁנַיִם וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד.
phrases.en: If he carried something which was ridden upon, or if he was carried on it, or he had shifted it, he defiles at two [removes], and disqualifies [terumah] at one [more remove]; But if he became separated [from the uncleanness], he defiles at one [remove] and disqualifies [terumah] at one [more remove].

phrases.he: פֵּרַשׁ, מְטַמֵּא אֶחָד וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד.
phrases.en: If he carried nevelah (carrion), or the hatat waters sufficient for a sprinkling, he defiles at two [removes], and disqualifies [terumah] at one [more remove]; But if he became separated, ,he defiles at one [remove] and disqualifies [terumah] at one [more remove].

phrases.he: הַנּוֹשֵׂא אֶת הַנְּבֵלָה, וְאֶת מֵי חַטָּאת שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהֶם כְּדֵי הַזָּיָה, מְטַמֵּא שְׁנַיִם וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד.
פֵּרַשׁ, מְטַמֵּא אֶחָד וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד
הָאוֹכֵל מִנִּבְלַת עוֹף טָהוֹר וְהִיא בְּבֵית הַבְּלִיעָה, מְטַמֵּא שְׁנַיִם וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד.
phrases.en: He who ate nevelah of a clean bird, and it still is in his gullet, defiles at two [removes], and disqualifies [terumah] at one [more remove].

phrases.he: הִכְנִיס רֹאשׁוֹ לַאֲוִיר הַתַּנּוּר, טָהוֹר, וְטָהוֹר הַתַּנּוּר.
phrases.en: If he put his head within the air-space of an oven, the oven remains clean.

phrases.he: הֱקִיאָהּ אוֹ בְלָעָהּ, מְטַמֵּא אֶחָד וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד.
phrases.en: But if he vomited or swallowed it, he defiles at one [remove] and disqualifies [terumah] unfit at one [more remove].

phrases.he: וּכְשֶׁהִיא בְתוֹךְ פִּיו, עַד שֶׁיִּבְלָעֶנָּה, טָהוֹר
phrases.en: But as long as it is still in his mouth, until he swallows it, he remains clean.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּשֶׁרֶץ וּבְשִׁכְבַת זֶרַע, וּבִטְמֵא מֵת, וּבִמְצֹרָע בִּימֵי סָפְרוֹ, וּבְמֵי חַטָּאת שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם כְּדֵי הַזָּיָה, וּבִנְבֵלָה, וּבְמֶרְכָּב, מְטַמֵּא אֶחָד וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד.
phrases.en: He who touches a dead sheretz, or semen, or he that has suffered corpse uncleanness, or a metzora during his days of counting, or hatat waters of insufficient quantity with which to perform the sprinkling, or carrion, or an object ridden upon [by a zav], defiles at one [remove] and disqualifies [terumah] at one [more remove].

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כֹּל הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּאַחַד מִכָּל אֲבוֹת הַטֻּמְאוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה, מְטַמֵּא אֶחָד וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד, חוּץ מִן הָאָדָם.
phrases.en: This is the general principle: anyone who touches anything that according to the Torah is a "father of uncleanness" defiles at one [remove] and disqualifies [terumah] at one [more remove], except [for the corpse] of a human.

phrases.he: פֵּרַשׁ, מְטַמֵּא אֶחָד וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד
phrases.en: If he had become separated, he defiles at one [remove] and renders [terumah] unfit at one [more remove].

phrases.he: בַּעַל קֶרִי, כְּמַגַּע שֶׁרֶץ.
phrases.en: He who has had a seminal emission is like one who has touched a dead sheretz.

phrases.he: וּבוֹעֵל נִדָּה, כִּטְמֵא מֵת, אֶלָּא שֶׁחָמוּר מִמֶּנּוּ בּוֹעֵל נִדָּה, שֶׁהוּא מְטַמֵּא מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב טֻמְאָה קַלָּה לְטַמֵּא אֳכָלִין וּמַשְׁקִין
phrases.en: And one who has had sex with a menstruant is like one who has suffered corpse uncleanness. But one who has had sex with a menstruant is more stringent in that he conveys minor grades of uncleanness to what he lies or sits upon, so as to make foods and liquids unclean.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ פוֹסְלִים אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה.
phrases.en: The following disqualify terumah:One who eats foods with first degree uncleanness; Or one who eats food with second degree uncleanness; And who drinks unclean liquids.

phrases.he: הָאוֹכֵל אֹכֶל רִאשׁוֹן, וְהָאוֹכֵל אֹכֶל שֵׁנִי, וְהַשּׁוֹתֶה מַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִין, וְהַבָּא רֹאשׁוֹ וְרֻבּוֹ בְּמַיִם שְׁאוּבִין, וְטָהוֹר שֶׁנָּפְלוּ עַל רֹאשׁוֹ וְעַל רֻבּוֹ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין, וְהַסֵּפֶר, וְהַיָּדַיִם, וּטְבוּל יוֹם, וְהָאֳכָלִים וְהַכֵּלִים שֶׁנִּטְמְאוּ בְמַשְׁקִים
phrases.en: And the one who has immersed his head and the greater part of him in drawn water; And a clean person upon whose head and greater part of him there fell three logs of drawn water; And a scroll [of Holy Scriptures], And [unwashed] hands; And one that has had immersion that same day; And foods and vessels which have become defiled by liquids.

phrases.he: הַמְכַנֵּס חַלּוֹת עַל מְנָת לְהַפְרִישׁ, וְנָשְׁכוּ,
phrases.en: If one had collected hallah [portions] with the intention of keeping them separate, but in the meantime they had become stuck together: Bet Shammai say: they are connected in the case of a tevul yom.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, חִבּוּר בִּטְבוּל יוֹם.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel say: they are not connected.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: Pieces of dough [of terumah] that had become stuck together, Or loaves that had become joined, or one who bakes a batter-cake on top of another batter-cake before it could form a crust in the oven, or the froth on the water that was bubbling, or the first scum that rises when boiling groats of beans, or the scum of new wine (r.

phrases.he: מִקְרָצוֹת נוֹשְׁכוֹת זוֹ בָזוֹ, וְכִכָּרוֹת נוֹשְׁכוֹת זוֹ בָזוֹ, הָאוֹפֶה חֲמִיטָה עַל גַּבֵּי חֲמִיטָה עַד שֶׁלֹּא קָרְמוּ בַתַּנּוּר, וְקוֹלִית שֶׁל מַיִם הַמְחֻלְחֶלֶת, וּרְתִיחַת גְּרִיסִין שֶׁל פּוֹל רִאשׁוֹנָה, וּרְתִיחַת יַיִן חָדָשׁ,
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף שֶׁל אֹרֶז,
phrases.en: Judah says: also that of rice): Bet Shammai say: they are connected in the case of a tevul yom.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, חִבּוּר בִּטְבוּל יוֹם.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel say: they are not connected.

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: They agree [that they serve as connectives] if they come into contact with other kinds of uncleanness, whether they be of minor or major grades.

phrases.he: וּמוֹדִים בִּשְׁאָר כָּל הַטֻּמְאוֹת, בֵּין קַלּוֹת בֵּין חֲמוּרוֹת

הַמְכַנֵּס חַלּוֹת עַל מְנָת שֶׁלֹּא לְהַפְרִישׁ, הָאוֹפֶה חֲמִיטָה עַל גַּבֵּי חֲמִיטָה מִשֶּׁקָּרְמוּ בַתַּנּוּר, וְקוֹלִית שֶׁל מַיִם שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְחֻלְחֶלֶת, וּרְתִיחַת גְּרִיסִין שֶׁל פּוֹל שְׁנִיָּה, וּרְתִיחַת יַיִן יָשָׁן, וְשֶׁל שֶׁמֶן לְעוֹלָם, וְשֶׁל עֲדָשִׁים,
phrases.en: If one had collected pieces of hallah without the intention of separating them afterwards, or a batter-cake that had been baked on another after a crust had formed in the oven, or froth had appeared in the water prior to its bubbling up, or the second scum that appeared in the boiling of groats of beans, or the scum of old wine, or that of oil of all kinds, or of lentils, Rabbi Judah says: also that of beans; All these are defiled when touched by a tevul yom.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף שֶׁל טֹפַח, טְמֵאִים בִּטְבוּל יוֹם, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר בְּכָל הַטֻּמְאוֹת:
phrases.en: And there is no need to say, [this is the case if touched] by other sources of uncleanness.

phrases.he: מַסְמֵר שֶׁאַחַר הַכִּכָּר, וְגַרְגֵּר מֶלַח קָטָן, וְחַרְחוּר פָּחוּת מִכָּאֶצְבַּע,
phrases.en: The nail shaped knob on the back of the loaf, or the small globule of salt, or the burnt crust less than a finger's breadth: Rabbi Yose says: whatever is eaten with the loaf becomes unclean [when touched by the tevul yom].

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, כָּל שֶׁהוּא נֶאֱכָל עָלָיו, טְמֵאִים בִּטְבוּל יוֹם, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר בְּכָל הַטֻּמְאוֹת:
phrases.en: And one doesn't need to say, this is so [when touched] by other unclean things.

phrases.he: הַצְּרוֹר שֶׁבַּכִּכָּר, וְגַרְגֵּר מֶלַח גָּדוֹל, וְהַתֻּרְמוֹס, וְהַחַרְחוּר יָתֵר מִכָּאֶצְבַּע,
phrases.en: A pebble in a loaf or a large globule of salt, or a lupine, or a burnt crust larger than a finger's breadth Rabbi Yose says: whatever is not eaten with the loaf remains clean even when touched by a father of impurity; And it isn't even necessary to say [is this so when touched] by a tevul yom.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ נֶאֱכָל עִמּוֹ, טְהוֹרִים בְּאַב הַטֻּמְאָה, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר בִּטְבוּל יוֹם:
הַשְּׂעֹרָה וְהַכֻּסֶּמֶת בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵינָן קְלוּפִים, הַתִּיאָה וְהַחִלְתִּית וְהָאֲלוּם,
phrases.en: Unshelled barley or spelt, root of crowfoot, asafoetida, silphium--Rabbi Judah says: even black beans remain clean even [when coming into contact] with a ‘father of uncleanness’, and there is no need to say [if touched] by a tevul yom, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף אֲפוּנִים שְׁחוֹרִים, טְהוֹרִים בְּאַב הַטֻּמְאָה, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר בִּטְבוּל יוֹם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: But the sages say: they are clean if touched by a tevul yom, but unclean [when touched] by other sources of impurity.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, טְהוֹרִים בִּטְבוּל יוֹם, וּטְמֵאִים בְּכָל הַטֻּמְאוֹת.
phrases.en: Shelled barley or spelt, or wheat whether shelled or unshelled, or black cumin, or sesame or pepper Rabbi Judah says: also white beans become unclean even when touched by a tevul yom, and there is no need to say [when they have come into contact] with other sources of impurity.

phrases.he: הַשְּׂעֹרָה וְהַכֻּסֶּמֶת בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן קְלוּפִים, וְהַחִטָּה בֵּין שֶׁהִיא קְלוּפָה בֵּין שֶׁאֵינָהּ קְלוּפָה, הַקֶּצַח, וְהַשֻּׁמְשׁוֹם, וְהַפִּלְפֵּל,
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף אֲפוּנִים לְבָנִים, טְמֵאִים בִּטְבוּל יוֹם, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר בְּכָל הַטֻּמְאוֹת:
מַשְׁקֵה טְבוּל יוֹם, כְּמַשְׁקִין שֶׁהוּא נוֹגֵעַ בָּהֶן.
phrases.en: Liquids that come out of a tevul yom are like those which he has touched: neither of them causes defilement.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ, אֵינָן מְטַמְּאִין.
phrases.en: With regard to all others that are unclean, be they of minor or major [degree], the liquids that come out of them are like those they touch; both have first degree impurity.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַטְּמֵאִין, בֵּין קַלִּין בֵּין חֲמוּרִין, הַמַּשְׁקִין הַיּוֹצְאִים מֵהֶן, כַּמַּשְׁקִין שֶׁהוּא נוֹגֵעַ בָּהֶן.
phrases.en: Except for liquid that is a "father of impurity.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ תְּחִלָּה, חוּץ מִן הַמַּשְׁקֶה שֶׁהוּא אַב הַטֻּמְאָה
קְדֵרָה שֶׁהִיא מְלֵאָה מַשְׁקִים וְנָגַע בָּהּ טְבוּל יוֹם, אִם הָיָה מַשְׁקֵה תְרוּמָה, הַמַּשְׁקִין פְּסוּלִין וְהַקְּדֵרָה טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A pot which was full of liquid and a tevul yom touched it: If it is terumah, the liquid is disqualified, but the pot is clean. But if the liquid is non-sacred [hullin] then all remains clean.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיָה מַשְׁקֵה חֻלִּין, הַכֹּל טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If his hands were defiled [and he touched the liquids in the pot], all becomes unclean.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיוּ יָדָיו מְסֹאָבוֹת, הַכֹּל טָמֵא.
phrases.en: This is a case defiled hands are treated more stringently than a tevul yom.

phrases.he: זֶה חֹמֶר בַּיָּדַיִם מִבִּטְבוּל יוֹם.
phrases.en: But a greater stringency is applied to a tevul yom than to defiled hands, since a doubtful tevul yom disqualifies terumah, but doubts with regard to defiled hands are clean.

phrases.he: וְחֹמֶר בִּטְבוּל יוֹם מִבַּיָּדַיִם, שֶׁסְּפֵק טְבוּל יוֹם פּוֹסֵל אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה, וְהַיָּדַיִם סְפֵקָן טָהוֹר
הַמִּקְפָּה שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה וְהַשּׁוּם וְהַשֶּׁמֶן שֶׁל חֻלִּין, שֶׁנָּגַע טְבוּל יוֹם בְּמִקְצָתָן, פָּסַל אֶת כֻּלָּם.
phrases.en: If the porridge was of terumah and the garlic or oil [it contained] was of hullin, and a tevul yom touched part of them, he has disqualified the whole thing; But if the porridge was of hullin and the garlic or oil it contained was of terumah, and a tevul yom touched part of them, he disqualifies only the part he has touched.

phrases.he: הַמִּקְפָּה שֶׁל חֻלִּין וְהַשּׁוּם וְהַשֶּׁמֶן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, שֶׁנָּגַע טְבוּל יוֹם בְּמִקְצָתָן, לֹא פָסַל אֶלָּא מְקוֹם מַגָּעוֹ.
phrases.en: If the greater part was garlic then they go after the majority.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיָה הַשּׁוּם מְרֻבֶּה, הוֹלְכִין אַחַר הָרֹב.
אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן גּוּשׁ בַּקְּעָרָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah said: When is this so? When it formed one cohesive mass in the pot, but if it was scattered small in the mortar, then it is clean, since he wishes that it should be scattered.

phrases.he: אֲבָל אִם הָיָה מְפֻזָּר בַּמְּדוֹכָה, טָהוֹר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא רוֹצֶה בְּפִזּוּרוֹ.
phrases.en: [Similarly] with all other mashed foods which were mashed with liquids.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַנִּדּוֹכִין שֶׁדָּכָן בְּמַשְׁקִין.
phrases.en: But those which are usually mashed with liquids and yet were mashed without liquids, though they formed one cohesive mass in the pot, are regarded as a cake of preserved figs.

phrases.he: אֲבָל אֶת שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לָדוּךְ בְּמַשְׁקִים וְדָכָן שֶׁלֹּא בְמַשְׁקִין וְהֵן גּוּשׁ בַּקְּעָרָה, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ כְעִגּוּל שֶׁל דְּבֵלָה
הַמִּקְפָּה וְהַחֲמִיטָה שֶׁל חֻלִּין וְהַשֶּׁמֶן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה צָף עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן, וְנָגַע טְבוּל יוֹם בַּשֶּׁמֶן, לֹא פָסַל אֶלָּא הַשֶּׁמֶן.
phrases.en: If the porridge and batter-cake were of hullin and oil of terumah was floating above them, and a tevul yom touched the oil, he disqualifies only the oil.

phrases.he: וְאִם חִבֵּץ, כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהוֹלֵךְ הַשֶּׁמֶן, פָּסָל
phrases.en: If he stirred it altogether, all the places where the oil goes are disqualified.

phrases.he: בְּשַׂר הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁקָּרַם עָלָיו הַקִּפָּה, נָגַע טְבוּל יוֹם בַּקִּפָּה, חֲתִיכוֹת מֻתָּרוֹת.
phrases.en: Sanctified meat over which the porridge crusted, and a tevul yom touched the crust, the slices [of meat] are permitted.

phrases.he: נָגַע בַּחֲתִיכָה, חֲתִיכָה וְכָל הָעוֹלִים עִמָּהּ, חִבּוּר זֶה לָזֶה.
phrases.en: But if he touched one of the slices, that slice and all [the crust] that comes up with it form a connective with the other.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר, שְׁנֵיהֶם חִבּוּר זֶה לָזֶה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri says: the two of them serve as connectives to each other.

phrases.he: וְכֵן בְּקִטְנִיּוֹת שֶׁקָּרְמוּ עַל גַּבֵּי פְרוּסוֹת.
phrases.en: Similarly, with [cooked] beans that have formed a layer over pieces of bread.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֵׂה קְדֵרָה בַקִּטְנִיּוֹת, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן פְּרוּדִים, אֵינָן חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: Beans or other foods cooked in a pot: when they are still separate, do not serve as connectives; but when they become a solid pulp, they do act as connectives.

phrases.he: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן גּוּשׁ, חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: If they formed several solid masses, they are to be counted.

phrases.he: אִם הָיוּ גוּשִׁין הַרְבֵּה, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ יִמָּנוּ.
phrases.en: If oil floats on wine and a tevul yom touched the oil, only the oil is disqualified.

phrases.he: שֶׁמֶן שֶׁהוּא צָף עַל גַּבֵּי הַיַּיִן וְנָגַע טְבוּל יוֹם בַּשֶּׁמֶן, לֹא פָסַל אֶלָּא הַשֶּׁמֶן.
phrases.en: But Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri says: each serves as a connective with the other.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר, שְׁנֵיהֶם חִבּוּר זֶה לָזֶה
חָבִית שֶׁשָּׁקְעָה לְתוֹךְ בּוֹר שֶׁל יַיִן וְנָגַע בּוֹ טְבוּל יוֹם, מִשָּׂפָה וְלִפְנִים, חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: A jug which sunk into a cistern containing wine, and a tevul yom touched it: If [he touched it] from the rim and inwards, it serves as a connective; If from the rim and outwards, it does not serve as a connective.

phrases.he: מִן הַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ, אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri says: even though [the level of wine in the cistern] is the height of a man [above the sunken jar], and he touched [the wine] directly above the mouth of the jar, it serves as a connective.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ עַל גַּבָּהּ רוּם קוֹמָה וְנָגַע כְּנֶגֶד פִּיהָ, חִבּוּר
חָבִית שֶׁנִּקְּבָה בֵּין מִפִּיהָ בֵּין מִשּׁוּלֶיהָ בֵּין מִצִּדֶּיהָ וְנָגַע בּוֹ טְבוּל יוֹם, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: If a jug had a hole either at its neck, bottom or sides, and a tevul yom touched it [at the hole], it becomes unclean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מִפִּיהָ וּמִשּׁוּלֶיהָ, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: if the hole is at its neck or bottom it becomes unclean; but if on its sides, on this side or on that, it remains clean.

phrases.he: מִן הַצְּדָדִין, מִכָּאן וּמִכָּאן, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If one poured [liquid] from one vessel into another, and a tevul yom touched the stream, and there was something within the vessel, then [whatsoever he touches] is neutralized in a hundred and one.

phrases.he: הַמְעָרֶה מִכְּלִי לִכְלִי וְנָגַע טְבוּל יוֹם בַּקִּלּוּחַ, אִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ, יַעֲלֶה בְאַחַת וּמֵאָה
בִּעְבּוּעַ שֶׁבֶּחָבִית שֶׁנִּקַּב בֵּין מִבִּפְנִים בֵּין מִבַּחוּץ וּבֵין מִלְמַעְלָן בֵּין מִלְּמַטָּן, זֶה כְנֶגֶד זֶה, טָמֵא בְאַב הַטֻּמְאָה וְטָמֵא בְאֹהֶל הַמֵּת.
phrases.en: A bubble on a jug which was pierced with holes on its inner side and on its outer side, whether above or below: If [the holes are] opposite one another, it becomes unclean [if touched] by a "father of uncleanness" and it becomes unclean if it is in a tent in which there is a corpse.

phrases.he: הַפְּנִימִי מִלְּמַטָּה וְהַחִיצוֹן מִלְמַעְלָן, טָמֵא בְאַב הַטֻּמְאָה וְטָמֵא בְאֹהֶל הַמֵּת.
phrases.en: If the inner hole is below and the outer above, it becomes unclean [if touched] by a "father of uncleanness," and it becomes unclean in a tent in which there is a corpse.

phrases.he: הַפְּנִימִי מִלְמַעְלָן וְהַחִיצוֹן מִלְּמַטָּן, טָהוֹר בְּאַב הַטֻּמְאָה וְטָמֵא בְאֹהֶל הַמֵּת
phrases.en: If the inner hole is above and the outer below, it remains clean if touched by a "father of uncleanness," but it becomes unclean in a tent in which there is a corpse.

phrases.he: כָּל יְדוֹת הָאֳכָלִים שֶׁהֵם חִבּוּר בְּאַב הַטֻּמְאָה, חִבּוּר בִּטְבוּל יוֹם.
phrases.en: Handles to food, which count as connectives when touched by a "father of uncleanness," also count as connectives when touched by a tevul yom.

phrases.he: אֹכֶל שֶׁנִּפְרָס וּמְעֹרֶה מִקְצָת,
רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, אִם אוֹחֵז בַּגָּדוֹל וְהַקָּטָן עוֹלֶה עִמּוֹ, הֲרֵי הוּא כָמוֹהוּ.
phrases.en: If a food was divided into two yet a small part was still attached: Rabbi Meir says: if one takes hold of the larger part and the smaller part is pulled away with it, behold it is like it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם אוֹחֵז בַּקָּטָן וְהַגָּדוֹל עוֹלֶה עִמּוֹ, הֲרֵי הוּא כָמוֹהוּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: if one takes hold of the smaller part and the greater is also pulled away with it, then behold it is like it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר, בַּטָּהוֹר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Nehemiah says: [this refers] to the case of the clean portion.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בַּטָּמֵא. וּשְׁאָר כָּל הָאֳכָלִים, אֶת שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לֵאָחֵז בֶּעָלֶה, אוֹחֵז אוֹתוֹ בֶּעָלֶה.
phrases.en: But the sages say: [it refers] to the unclean portion. In the case of all other foods, those usually held by the leaf should be taken by the leaf, and those usually held by the stalk should be taken by the stalk.

phrases.he: וּבַקֶּלַח, אוֹחֲזִין אוֹתוֹ בַּקָּלַח
יָרָק שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה וּבֵיצָה טְרוּפָה נְתוּנָה עַל גַּבָּיו, וְנָגַע טְבוּל יוֹם בַּבֵּיצָה, לֹא פָסַל אֶלָּא הַקֶּלַח שֶׁכְּנֶגְדּוֹ.
phrases.en: If a beaten egg was on top of vegetables of terumah, and a tevul yom touches the egg, then he disqualifies only that stalk [of the vegetables] that is opposite the part [of the egg] he touched.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, כָּל הַסֵּדֶר הָעֶלְיוֹן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: the entire upper layer.

phrases.he: אִם הָיָה כְמִין כּוֹבַע, אֵינָהּ חִבּוּר
phrases.en: But if it was arranged like a cap it does not serve as a connective.

phrases.he: חוּט שֶׁל בֵּיצָה שֶׁקָּרַם עַל דְּפָנוֹת שֶׁל לְפָס, וְנָגַע בּוֹ טְבוּל יוֹם, מִן הַשָּׂפָה וְלִפְנִים, חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: The streak of an egg that had become congealed on the side of a pan and a tevul yom touched it: If within the rim [of the pan] it serves as a connective; But if outside the rim, it does not serve as a connective.

phrases.he: מִן הַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ, אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר.
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, חוּט וְכָל שֶׁנִּקְלָף עִמּוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says that the streak and the part that can be peeled away with it [serves as a connective].

phrases.he: וְכֵן בְּקִטְנִיּוֹת שֶׁקָּרְמוּ עַל שְׂפָתָהּ שֶׁל קְדֵרָה
phrases.en: The same applies to beans that had congealed on the rim of the pot.

phrases.he: עִסָּה שֶׁנִּדְמְעָה אוֹ שֶׁנִּתְחַמְּצָה בִשְׂאֹר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, אֵינָהּ נִפְסֶלֶת בִּטְבוּל יוֹם.
phrases.en: Dough that had been mixed [with dough of terumah] or that had been leavened with yeast of terumah, is not disqualified by tevul yom.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן פּוֹסְלִין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Shimon declare it unfit.

phrases.he: עִסָּה שֶׁהֻכְשְׁרָה בְמַשְׁקֶה וְנִלּוֹשָׁה בְּמֵי פֵרוֹת וְנָגַע בָּהֶן טְבוּל יוֹם, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן יְהוּדָה אִישׁ בַּרְתּוֹתָא אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, פָּסַל אֶת כֻּלָּהּ.
phrases.en: Dough that had become susceptible [to uncleanness] by a liquid, and it was kneaded with produce juice, and later touched by a tevul yom: Rabbi Elazar ben Judah of Bartota says in the name of Rabbi Joshua: he disqualifies all of it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר מִשְּׁמוֹ, לֹא פָסַל אֶלָּא מְקוֹם מַגָּעוֹ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says in his name: he disqualifies only the part that he touched.

phrases.he: יָרָק שֶׁל חֻלִּין שֶׁבִּשְּׁלוֹ בְשֶׁמֶן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, וְנָגַע בּוֹ טְבוּל יוֹם, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן יְהוּדָה אִישׁ בַּרְתּוֹתָא אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, פָּסַל כֻּלָּהּ.
phrases.en: Vegetables of hullin were cooked with oil of terumah and a tevul yom touched it: Rabbi Elazar ben Judah of Bartota says in the name of Rabbi Joshua: he has disqualified the whole thing.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר מִשְּׁמוֹ, לֹא פָסַל אֶלָּא מְקוֹם מַגָּעוֹ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says in his name: he disqualifies only the part that he touched.

phrases.he: טָהוֹר שֶׁנָּגַס מִן הָאֹכֶל וְנָפַל עַל בְּגָדָיו וְעַל כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A clean person who chewed food and it fell on his garments and on a loaf of terumah, it [the loaf] is not susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: הָיָה אוֹכֵל זֵיתִים פְּצוּעִים וּתְמָרִים רְטֻבּוֹת, כֹּל שֶׁהוּא רוֹצֶה לָמֹץ אֶת גַּרְעִינָתוֹ וְנָפַל עַל בְּגָדָיו וְעַל כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If he ate crushed olives or moist dates, [or] if his intention was to suck out the pit, and it fell on his garments and on a loaf of terumah, it is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: הָיָה אוֹכֵל זֵיתִים נְגוּבִין וּתְמָרִים יְבֵשׁוֹת, כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה לָמֹץ אֶת גַּרְעִינָתוֹ וְנָפַל עַל בְּגָדָיו וְעַל כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If he ate dried olives, or dried figs or it was not his intention to suck out the pit, and they fell on his garments and on a loaf of terumah, it is not susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: אֶחָד טָהוֹר וְאֶחָד טְבוּל יוֹם, כָּאֵלּוּ.
phrases.en: This is the case irrespective of whether it was a clean person or a tevul yom [who was eating].

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ טְמֵאִין בִּטְבוּל יוֹם, שֶׁמַּשְׁקִין שֶׁל טָמֵא מַכְשִׁירִין לִרְצוֹנוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא לִרְצוֹנוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: in either case it becomes susceptible to uncleanness in the case of a tevul yom, since liquids issuing from unclean persons render anything susceptible whether it was to his liking or not.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵין טְבוּל יוֹם טָמֵא:
phrases.en: But the sages say: a tevul yom is not regarded as an unclean person.

phrases.he: אֹכֶל מַעֲשֵׂר שֶׁהֻכְשַׁר בְּמַשְׁקֶה, וְנָגַע בּוֹ טְבוּל יוֹם אוֹ יָדַיִם מְסֹאָבוֹת, מַפְרִישִׁין מִמֶּנּוּ תְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר בְּטָהֳרָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא שְׁלִישִׁי, וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁי טָהוֹר לְחֻלִּין:
phrases.en: If food that was tithe had been rendered susceptible to impurity by a liquid, and a tevul yom or one with unwashed hands touched it, terumah of tithe may still be removed from it in purity, since it only has third degree uncleanness, and third degree uncleanness counts as clean in hullin.

phrases.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהִיא טְבוּלַת יוֹם, לָשָׁה אֶת הָעִסָּה, וְקוֹצָה לָהּ חַלָּה וּמַפְרַשְׁתָּהּ, וּמַנַּחְתָּהּ בִּכְפִישָׁה מִצְרִית אוֹ בִנְחוּתָא, וּמַקֶּפֶת וְקוֹרָא לָהּ שֵׁם, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא שְׁלִישִׁי, וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁי טָהוֹר לְחֻלִּין:
phrases.en: A woman who is a tevulat yom may knead dough, cut off the hallah, and set it apart, and she should arrange it on an Egyptian basket, or on a tray, and then bring it near and call it by its name. For it [the dough] has third degree uncleanness and third degree uncleanness is clean in hullin.

phrases.he: עֲרֵבָה שֶׁהִיא טְבוּלַת יוֹם, לָשִׁין בָּהּ אֶת הָעִסָּה וְקוֹצִין מִמֶּנָּה חַלָּה, וּמַקֶּפֶת וְקוֹרִין לָהּ שֵׁם, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא שְׁלִישִׁי, וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁי טָהוֹר לְחֻלִּין:
phrases.en: A trough which is a tevulat yom, one may knead dough in it and cut off the portion for hallah and bring it near and call it by name [as hallah]; for it [the trough] has third degree uncleanness and third degree uncleanness is clean in hullin.

phrases.he: לָגִין שֶׁהוּא טְבוּל יוֹם, וּמִלְאָהוּ מִן הֶחָבִית מַעֲשֵׂר טֶבֶל, אִם אָמַר, הֲרֵי זוֹ תְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר מִשֶּׁתֶּחְשָׁךְ, הֲרֵי זוֹ תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.en: A flagon was a tevul yom and they filled it from a cask containing tithes from which terumah had not yet been taken: If one said, let this be terumah of tithe after nightfall, it becomes terumah of tithe. But if he said: let this be the food for the eruv, he has said nothing.

phrases.he: אִם אָמַר, הֲרֵי זֶה עֵרוּב, לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם.
phrases.en: If the cask was broken, the contents of the flagon still remain tithe from which terumah had not yet been taken.

phrases.he: נִשְׁבְּרָה הֶחָבִית, הַלָּגִין בְּטִבְלוֹ.
phrases.en: If the flagon was broken, then what is in the cask still remains tithe from which terumah had not yet been taken.

phrases.he: נִשְׁבַּר הַלָּגִין, הֶחָבִית בְּטִבְלָהּ
בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ אוֹמְרִים, מְחַלְּלִין עַל פֵּרוֹת עַם הָאָרֶץ.
phrases.en: Originally they said: one may redeem [second tithe] for the produce of an am ha-arez.

phrases.he: חָזְרוּ לוֹמַר, אַף עַל מְעוֹתָיו.
phrases.en: Later they reconsidered and said: also for money of his.

phrases.he: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ אוֹמְרִים, הַיּוֹצֵא בַקּוֹלָר וְאָמַר, כִּתְבוּ גֵט לְאִשְׁתִּי, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ יִכְתְּבוּ וְיִתְּנוּ.
phrases.en: riginally they said that if a man was being led out to execution and said, “Write a get for my wife”, they may write a get and give [it to her].

phrases.he: חָזְרוּ לוֹמַר, אַף הַמְפָרֵשׁ וְהַיּוֹצֵא בִשְׁיָרָא.
phrases.en: Later they reconsidered and said, even if he were leaving on a sea voyage or on a caravan journey.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שְׁזוּרִי אוֹמֵר, אַף הַמְסֻכָּן
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says: even if he were dangerously ill.

phrases.he: הַכַּדּוּמִין הָאַשְׁקְלוֹנִים שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרוּ וְאֻנְקְלִי שֶׁלָּהֶם קַיֶּמֶת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: If Ashkelon grappling-irons were broken but their hooks remained, they remain susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: הַמַּעְבֵּר וְהַמַּזְרֶה וְהַמַּגּוֹב וְכֵן מַסְרֵק שֶׁל רֹאשׁ שֶׁנִּטְּלָה אַחַת מִשִּׁנֵּיהֶן וַעֲשָׂאָן שֶׁל מַתָּכוֹת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְמֵאִין. וְעַל כֻּלָּן
phrases.en: If a pitch-fork, winnowing-fan, or rake, and the same applies to a hair-comb, lost one of its teeth and it was replaced by one of metal, it is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, דָּבָר חָדָשׁ חִדְּשׁוּ הַסּוֹפְרִים וְאֵין לִי מַה לְּהָשִׁיב:
phrases.en: And concerning all these Rabbi Joshua said: the scribes have here introduced a new principle of law, and I have no explanation to offer.

phrases.he: הַתּוֹרֵם אֶת הַבּוֹר וְאָמַר, הֲרֵי זוֹ תְרוּמָה עַל מְנָת שֶׁתַּעֲלֶה שָׁלוֹם, שָׁלוֹם מִן הַשֶּׁבֶר וּמִן הַשְּׁפִיכָה, אֲבָל לֹא מִן הַטֻּמְאָה.
phrases.en: If one was taking terumah from a cistern and said: "Let this be terumah provided it comes up safely," [it is implied that he meant] safely from being broken or spilled, but not from becoming impure; But Rabbi Shimon says: also from impurity.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אַף מִן הַטֻּמְאָה. נִשְׁבְּרָה, אֵינָהּ מְדַמַּעַת.
phrases.en: If it were broken, it does not render [the contents of the cistern] subject to the restrictions of terumah.

phrases.he: עַד הֵיכָן תִּשָּׁבֵר וְלֹא תְדַמֵּעַ.
phrases.en: How far away can it be broken and still not make [the contents of the cistern] subject to terumah restrictions? Only so far that if it rolls back, it can reach the cistern.

phrases.he: כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּתְגַּלְגֵּל וְתַגִּיעַ לַבּוֹר.
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַף מִי שֶׁהָיָה בוֹ דַעַת לְהַתְנוֹת וְלֹא הִתְנָה, נִשְׁבְּרָה, אֵינָהּ מְדַמַּעַת, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא תְנַאי בֵּית דִּין:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: even if one had the intention of making such a stipulation, but did not do so, and it broke, it does not make the [contents of the cistern] subject to terumah restrictions, for this is a stipulation laid down by the court.

phrases.he: מֵי רְבִיעִית נוֹתְנִין לַיָּדַיִם, לְאֶחָד, אַף לִשְׁנַיִם.
phrases.en: [A minimum of] a quarter [of a log] of water must be poured over the hands for one [person] and even for two.

phrases.he: מַחֲצִית לֹג, לִשְׁלשָׁה אוֹ לְאַרְבָּעָה.
phrases.en: A minimum of half a log must be poured over the hands for three or four persons.

phrases.he: מִלֹּג, לַחֲמִשָּׁה וְלַעֲשָׂרָה וּלְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: A minimum of one log [is sufficient] for five, ten, or one hundred persons.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יִפְחֹת לָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁבָּהֶם מֵרְבִיעִית.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: as long as there is not less than a quarter of a log left for the last person among them.

phrases.he: מוֹסִיפִין עַל הַשְּׁנִיִּים וְאֵין מוֹסִיפִין עַל הָרִאשׁוֹנִים
phrases.en: More [water] may be added to the second water, but more may not be added to the first water.

phrases.he: בְּכָל הַכֵּלִים נוֹתְנִין לַיָּדַיִם, אֲפִלּוּ בִכְלֵי גְלָלִים, בִּכְלֵי אֲבָנִים, בִּכְלֵי אֲדָמָה.
phrases.en: Water may be poured over the hands out of any kind of vessel, even out of vessels made of animal dung, out of vessels made of stone or out of vessels made of clay.

phrases.he: אֵין נוֹתְנִין לַיָּדַיִם, לֹא בְדָפְנוֹת הַכֵּלִים, וְלֹא בְשׁוּלֵי הַמַּחַץ, וְלֹא בִמְגוּפַת הֶחָבִית.
phrases.en: Water may not be poured from the sides of [broken] vessels or from the bottom of a ladle or from the stopper of a jar.

phrases.he: וְלֹא יִתֵּן לַחֲבֵרוֹ בְחָפְנָיו, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין מְמַלְּאִין וְאֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין וְאֵין מַזִּין מֵי חַטָּאת וְאֵין נוֹתְנִים לַיָּדַיִם אֶלָּא בִכְלִי.
phrases.en: Nor may one pour [water] over the hands of his fellow out of his cupped hands. Because one may not draw, nor sanctify, nor sprinkle the water of purification, nor pour water over the hands except in a vessel.

phrases.he: וְאֵין מַצִּילִין בְּצָמִיד פָּתִיל אֶלָּא כֵלִים, שֶׁאֵין מַצִּילִין מִיַּד כְּלִי חֶרֶשׂ אֶלָּא כֵלִים
phrases.en: And only vessels closely covered with a lid protect [their contents from uncleanness]. And only vessels protect [their contents from uncleanness] inside earthenware vessels.

phrases.he: הַמַּיִם שֶׁנִּפְסְלוּ מִשְּׁתִיַּת הַבְּהֵמָה, בְּכֵלִים, פְּסוּלִים. וּבְקַרְקָעוֹת, כְּשֵׁרִים.
phrases.en: Water which had become so unfit that it could not be drunk by a beast: If it was in a vessel it is invalid, But if it was in the ground it is valid.

phrases.he: נָפַל לְתוֹכָן דְּיוֹ, קוֹמוֹס, וְקַנְקַנְתּוֹם וְנִשְׁתַּנּוּ מַרְאֵיהֶן, פְּסוּלִין.
phrases.en: If there fell into [the water], dye, or gum or sulphate of copper and its color changed, it is invalid.

phrases.he: עָשָׂה בָהֶם מְלָאכָה אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁרָה בָהֶן פִּתּוֹ, פְּסוּלִין.
phrases.en: If a person did any work with it or soaked his bread in it, it is invalid.

phrases.he: שִׁמְעוֹן הַתִּמְנִי אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ נִתְכַּוֵּן לִשְׁרוֹת בָּזֶה וְנָפַל לַשֵּׁנִי, כְּשֵׁרִים
phrases.en: Shimon of Teman says: even if he intended to soak his bread in one water and it fell into another water the water is valid.

phrases.he: הֵדִיחַ בָּהֶם אֶת הַכֵּלִים אוֹ שֶׁמִּחָה בָהֶם אֶת הַמִּדּוֹת, פְּסוּלִים.
phrases.en: If he cleansed vessels with the water or scrubbed measures with it, [the water] is invalid.

phrases.he: הֵדִיחַ בָּהֶם כֵּלִים מוּדָחִים אוֹ חֲדָשִׁים, כְּשֵׁרִים.
phrases.en: If he rinsed with it vessels which had already been rinsed or new vessels, it is valid.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי פוֹסֵל בַּחֲדָשִׁים
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose declares [the water] invalid if they were new vessels.

phrases.he: הַמַּיִם שֶׁהַנַּחְתּוֹם מַטְבִּיל בָּהֶם אֶת הַגְּלֻסְקִין, פְּסוּלִים.
phrases.en: Water in which the baker dips his loaves is invalid; but if he moistened his hands in the water it is valid.

phrases.he: וּכְשֶׁהוּא מֵדִיחַ אֶת יָדָיו בָּהֶן, כְּשֵׁרִים.
phrases.en: All are fit to pour water over the hands, even a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor.

phrases.he: הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִים לִתֵּן לַיָּדַיִם, אֲפִלּוּ חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן.
phrases.en: A person may place the jug between his knees and pour out the water, or he may turn the jug on its side and pour it out.

phrases.he: מַנִּיחַ חָבִית בֵּין בִּרְכָּיו וְנוֹטֵל.
phrases.en: A monkey may pour water over the hands.

phrases.he: מַטֶּה חָבִית עַל צִדָּהּ וְנוֹטֵל. וְהַקּוֹף נוֹטֵל לַיָּדַיִם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose declares these [latter] two cases invalid.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי פוֹסֵל בִּשְׁנֵי אֵלּוּ
נָטַל לְיָדוֹ אַחַת מִשְּׁטִיפָה אַחַת, יָדוֹ טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If he poured water over one of his hands with a single rinsing his hand becomes clean.

phrases.he: לִשְׁתֵּי יָדָיו מִשְּׁטִיפָה אַחַת, רַבִּי מֵאִיר מְטַמֵּא, עַד שֶׁיִּטֹּל מֵרְבִיעִית.
phrases.en: If over both his hands with a single rinsing: Rabbi Meir declares them to be unclean until he pours a minimum of a quarter of a log of water over them.

phrases.he: נָפַל כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, טָהוֹר. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְטַמֵּא
phrases.en: If a loaf of terumah fell on the water the loaf is clean. Rabbi Yose declares it to be unclean.

phrases.he: נָטַל אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים לְמָקוֹם אֶחָד, וְאֶת הַשְּׁנִיִּים לְמָקוֹם אַחֵר, וְנָפַל כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה עַל הָרִאשׁוֹנִים, טָמֵא, וְעַל הַשְּׁנִיִּים, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If he poured the first water over his hands [while standing] in one place, and the second water over his hands [while standing] in another place, and a loaf of terumah fell on the first water, the loaf becomes unclean.

phrases.he: נָטַל אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים וְאֶת הַשְּׁנִיִּים לְמָקוֹם אֶחָד, וְנָפַל כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: But if it fell on the second water it remains clean. If he poured the first and the second water [while standing] in one place, and a loaf of terumah fell onto the water, the loaf becomes unclean.

phrases.he: נָטַל אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים וְנִמְצָא עַל יָדָיו קֵיסָם אוֹ צְרוֹר, יָדָיו טְמֵאוֹת, שֶׁאֵין הַמַּיִם הָאַחֲרוֹנִים מְטַהֲרִים אֶלָּא הַמַּיִם שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי הַיָּד.
phrases.en: If he poured the first water over his hands and a splinter or a piece of gravel is found on his hands, [his hands] remain unclean, because the latter water only makes the first water on the hands clean.

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, כֹּל שֶׁהוּא מִבְּרִיַּת הַמַּיִם, טָהוֹר
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel says: if any creature from the water [was on the hands while they are being cleaned] they are clean.

phrases.he: הַיָּדַיִם מִטַּמְּאוֹת וּמִטַּהֲרוֹת עַד הַפֶּרֶק. כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: Hands become unclean and are made clean as far as the joint.

phrases.he: נָטַל אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים עַד הַפֶּרֶק, וְאֶת הַשְּׁנִיִּים חוּץ לַפֶּרֶק, וְחָזְרוּ לַיָּד, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: How so? If he poured the first water over the hands as far as the joint and poured the second water over the hands beyond the joint and the latter flowed back to the hands, the hands are clean.

phrases.he: נָטַל אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים וְאֶת הַשְּׁנִיִּים חוּץ לַפֶּרֶק וְחָזְרוּ לַיָּד, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: If he poured the first and the second water over the hands beyond the joint and they flowed back to the hands, the hands remain unclean.

phrases.he: נָטַל אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים לְיָדוֹ אַחַת וְנִמְלַךְ וְנָטַל אֶת הַשְּׁנִיִּים לִשְׁתֵּי יָדָיו, טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: If he poured the first water over one of his hands and then changed his mind and poured the second water over both his hands, they are unclean.

phrases.he: נָטַל אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים לִשְׁתֵּי יָדָיו וְנִמְלַךְ וְנָטַל אֶת הַשְּׁנִיִּים לְיָדוֹ אַחַת, יָדוֹ טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If he poured the first water over both his hands and then changed his mind and poured the second water over one of his hands, his one hand becomes clean.

phrases.he: נָטַל לְיָדוֹ אַחַת וְשִׁפְשְׁפָהּ בַּחֲבֶרְתָּהּ, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: If he poured water over one of his hands and rubbed it on the other hand it remains unclean.

phrases.he: בְּרֹאשׁוֹ אוֹ בַכֹּתֶל, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If he rubbed it on his head or on the wall it is clean.

phrases.he: נוֹטְלִין אַרְבָּעָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה זֶה בְצַד זֶה אוֹ זֶה עַל גַּבֵּי זֶה, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיְּרַפּוּ שֶׁיָּבֹאוּ בָהֶם הַמָּיִם
phrases.en: Water may be poured over the hands of four or five persons, each hand being by the side of the other, or being one above the other, provided that the hands are held loosely so that the water flows between them.

phrases.he: סָפֵק נַעֲשָׂה בָהֶם מְלָאכָה סָפֵק לֹא נַעֲשָׂה בָהֶם מְלָאכָה, סָפֵק יֵשׁ בָּהֶם כַּשִּׁעוּר סָפֵק שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם כַּשִּׁעוּר, סָפֵק טְמֵאִים סָפֵק טְהוֹרִין, סְפֵקָן טָהוֹר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָמְרוּ, סְפֵק הַיָּדַיִם לִטָּמֵא וּלְטַמֵּא וְלִטָּהֵר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If there was a doubt whether any work has been done with the water or not, a doubt whether the water contains the requisite quantity or not, a doubt whether it is unclean or clean, in these cases the doubt is considered to be clean because they have said in a case of doubt concerning hands as to whether they have become unclean or have conveyed uncleanness or have become clean, they are considered to be clean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, לִטָּהֵר, טָמֵא. כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: in a case [of doubt as to] whether they have become clean they are considered to be unclean.

phrases.he: הָיוּ יָדָיו טְהוֹרוֹת וּלְפָנָיו שְׁנֵי כִכָּרִים טְמֵאִים, סָפֵק נָגַע סָפֵק לֹא נָגַע, הָיוּ יָדָיו טְמֵאוֹת וּלְפָנָיו שְׁנֵי כִכָּרִים טְהוֹרִים, סָפֵק נָגַע סָפֵק לֹא נָגַע.
phrases.en: How so? If his hands were clean and there were two unclean loaves before him and there was a doubt whether he touched them or not; Or if his hands were unclean and there were two clean loaves before him and there was a doubt whether he touched them or not; Or if one of his hands was unclean and the other clean and there were two clean loaves before him and he touched one of them and there was a doubt whether he touched it with the unclean hand or with the clean hand; Or if his hands were clean and there were two loaves before him one of which was unclean and the other clean and he touched one of them and there was a doubt whether he touched the unclean one or the clean one; Or if one of his hands was unclean and the other clean and there were two loaves before him one of which was unclean and the other clean, and he touched both of them, and there is a doubt whether the unclean hand touched the unclean loaf or whether the clean hand touched the clean loaf or whether the clean hand touched the unclean loaf or whether the unclean hand touched the clean loaf The hands remain in the same state as they were before and the loaves remain in the same state as they were before.

phrases.he: הָיוּ יָדָיו אַחַת טְמֵאָה וְאַחַת טְהוֹרָה וּלְפָנָיו שְׁנֵי כִכָּרִים טְהוֹרִים, נָגַע בְּאַחַד מֵהֶם, סָפֵק בַּטְּמֵאָה נָגַע סָפֵק בַּטְּהוֹרָה נָגַע.
הָיוּ יָדָיו טְהוֹרוֹת וּלְפָנָיו שְׁנֵי כִכָּרִים, אֶחָד טָמֵא וְאֶחָד טָהוֹר, נָגַע בְּאַחַד מֵהֶן, סָפֵק בַּטָּמֵא נָגַע סָפֵק בַּטָּהוֹר נָגַע.

הָיוּ יָדָיו אַחַת טְמֵאָה וְאַחַת טְהוֹרָה וּלְפָנָיו שְׁנֵי כִכָּרִים אֶחָד טָמֵא וְאֶחָד טָהוֹר, נָגַע בִּשְׁתֵּיהֶן, סָפֵק טְמֵאָה בַטָּמֵא וּטְהוֹרָה בַטָּהוֹר, אוֹ טְהוֹרָה בַטָּמֵא וּטְמֵאָה בַטָּהוֹר, הַיָּדַיִם כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ וְהַכִּכָּרִים כְּמוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ
הַמַּכְנִיס יָדָיו לְבַיִת הַמְנֻגָּע, יָדָיו תְּחִלּוֹת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.en: If a person puts his hands inside a house with scale disease, his hands have first degree uncleanness, the words of Rabbi Akiba.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, יָדָיו שְׁנִיּוֹת.
phrases.en: But the sages say: his hands have second degree uncleanness.

phrases.he: כֹּל הַמְטַמֵּא בְגָדִים בִּשְׁעַת מַגָּעוֹ, מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם לִהְיוֹת תְּחִלּוֹת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.en: Whoever defiles garments: at the time when he touches [the uncleanness], he defiles hands so that they have first degree uncleanness, the words of Rabbi Akiba.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, לִהְיוֹת שְׁנִיּוֹת.
phrases.en: But the sages say: such that they have second degree of uncleanness.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, הֵיכָן מָצִינוּ שֶׁהַיָּדַיִם תְּחִלָּה בְכָל מָקוֹם.
phrases.en: They said to Rabbi Akiba: where do we find anywhere that hands have first degree uncleanness? He said to them: but how is it possible for them to become unclean with first degree uncleanness without his whole body becoming unclean? Only in these cases [can they have first degree uncleanness].

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, וְכִי הֵיאַךְ אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶן לִהְיוֹת תְּחִלָּה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִטְמָא גוּפוֹ, חוּץ מִזֶּה.
phrases.en: Foods and vessels which have been defiled by liquids convey second degree of uncleanness to the hands, the words of Rabbi Joshua.

phrases.he: הָאֳכָלִין וְהַכֵּלִים שֶׁנִּטְמְאוּ בְמַשְׁקִין, מְטַמְּאִין אֶת הַיָּדַיִם לִהְיוֹת שְׁנִיּוֹת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֶת שֶׁנִּטְמָא בְאַב הַטֻּמְאָה, מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם.
phrases.en: But the sages say: that which has been defiled by a father of uncleanness conveys uncleanness to the hands, but that which has been defiled by an offspring of uncleanness does not defiled the hands.

phrases.he: בִּוְלַד הַטֻּמְאָה, אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם.
אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
מַעֲשֶׂה בְאִשָּׁה אַחַת שֶׁבָּאָת לִפְנֵי אַבָּא, אָמְרָה לוֹ, נִכְנְסוּ יָדַי לַאֲוִיר כְּלִי חֶרֶשׂ.
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel said: it happened that a certain woman came before my father and said to him, "My hands went into the air-space inside an earthenware vessel.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהּ, בִּתִּי, וּבַמֶּה הָיְתָה טֻמְאָתָהּ, וְלֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי מָה אָמְרָה לוֹ.
phrases.en: He said to her: "My daughter, what was the cause of its uncleanness?" But I did not hear what she said to him.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים, מְבֹאָר הַדָּבָר.
phrases.en: The sages said: the matter is clear that which has been defiled by a father of uncleanness conveys uncleanness to the hands, but that which has been rendered unclean by an offspring of uncleanness does not defiled the hands.

phrases.he: אֶת שֶׁנִּטְמָא בְאַב הַטֻּמְאָה, מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם.
בִּוְלַד הַטֻּמְאָה, אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדָיִם
כֹּל הַפּוֹסֵל אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה, מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם לִהְיוֹת שְׁנִיּוֹת.
phrases.en: Anything which disqualifies terumah defiles hands with a second degree of uncleanness.

phrases.he: הַיָּד מְטַמְּאָה אֶת חֲבֶרְתָּהּ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
phrases.en: One [unwashed] hand defiles the other hand, the words of Rabbi Joshua.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵין שֵׁנִי עוֹשֶׂה שֵׁנִי.
phrases.en: But the sages say: that which has second degree of uncleanness cannot convey second degree of uncleanness.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, וַהֲלֹא כִתְבֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ שְׁנִיִּים מְטַמְּאִין אֶת הַיָּדַיִם.
phrases.en: He said to them: But do not the Holy Scriptures which have second degree of uncleanness defile the hands? They said to him: the laws of the Torah may not be argued from the laws of the scribes, nor may the laws of the scribes be argued from the laws of the Torah, nor may the laws of the scribes be argued from [other] laws of the scribes.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, אֵין דָּנִין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים, וְלֹא דִבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְלֹא דִבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים:
רְצוּעוֹת תְּפִלִּין עִם הַתְּפִלִּין, מְטַמְּאוֹת אֶת הַיָּדַיִם.
phrases.en: The straps of the tefillin [when connected] with the tefillin [boxes] defile the hands.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, רְצוּעוֹת תְּפִלִּין אֵינָן מְטַמְּאוֹת אֶת הַיָּדַיִם:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: the straps of the tefillin do not defile the hands.

phrases.he: גִּלָּיוֹן שֶׁבַּסֵּפֶר, שֶׁמִּלְּמַעְלָן וְשֶׁמִּלְּמַטָּן שֶׁבַּתְּחִלָּה וְשֶׁבַּסּוֹף, מְטַמְּאִין אֶת הַיָּדַיִם.
phrases.en: The margin on a scroll which is above or below or at the beginning or at the end defiles the hands.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, שֶׁבַּסּוֹף אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא, עַד שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה לוֹ עַמּוּד:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: the margin at the end does not render unclean [the hands] until a handle is fastened to it.

phrases.he: סֵפֶר שֶׁנִּמְחַק וְנִשְׁתַּיֵּר בּוֹ שְׁמוֹנִים וְחָמֵשׁ אוֹתִיּוֹת, כְּפָרָשַׁת וַיְהִי בִּנְסֹעַ הָאָרֹן, מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם.
phrases.en: A scroll on which the writing has become erased and eighty-five letters remain, as many as are in the section beginning, "And it came to pass when the ark set forward" (Numbers 10:35-36) defiles the hands.

phrases.he: מְגִלָּה שֶׁכָּתוּב בָּהּ שְׁמוֹנִים וְחָמֵשׁ אוֹתִיּוֹת כְּפָרָשַׁת וַיְהִי בִּנְסֹעַ הָאָרֹן, מְטַמָּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם.
phrases.en: A single sheet on which there are written eighty-five letters, as many as are in the section beginning, "And it came to pass when the ark set forward", defiles the hands.

phrases.he: כָּל כִּתְבֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ מְטַמְּאִין אֶת הַיָּדַיִם.
phrases.en: All the Holy Scriptures defile the hands.

phrases.he: שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים וְקֹהֶלֶת מְטַמְּאִין אֶת הַיָּדַיִם.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם, וְקֹהֶלֶת מַחֲלֹקֶת.
phrases.en: The Song of Songs and Kohelet (Ecclesiastes) defile the hands. Rabbi Judah says: the Song of Songs defiles the hands, but there is a dispute about Kohelet.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, קֹהֶלֶת אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם וְשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים מַחֲלֹקֶת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: Kohelet does not defile the hands, but there is a dispute about the Song of Songs.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, קֹהֶלֶת מִקֻּלֵּי בֵית שַׁמַּאי וּמֵחֻמְרֵי בֵית הִלֵּל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: [the ruling about] Kohelet is one of the leniencies of Bet Shammai and one of the stringencies of Bet Hillel.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן עַזַּאי, מְקֻבָּל אֲנִי מִפִּי שִׁבְעִים וּשְׁנַיִם זָקֵן, בַּיּוֹם שֶׁהוֹשִׁיבוּ אֶת רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה בַּיְשִׁיבָה, שֶׁשִּׁיר הַשִּׁירִים וְקֹהֶלֶת מְטַמְּאִים אֶת הַיָּדַיִם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai said: I have received a tradition from the seventy-two elders on the day when they appointed Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah head of the academy that the Song of Songs and Kohelet defile the hands.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, לֹא נֶחֱלַק אָדָם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל עַל שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים שֶׁלֹּא תְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם, שֶׁאֵין כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ כְדַאי כַּיּוֹם שֶׁנִּתַּן בּוֹ שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁכָּל הַכְּתוּבִים קֹדֶשׁ, וְשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiba said: Far be it! No man in Israel disputed that the Song of Songs [saying] that it does not defile the hands. For the whole world is not as worthy as the day on which the Song of Songs was given to Israel; for all the writings are holy but the Song of Songs is the holy of holies.

phrases.he: וְאִם נֶחְלְקוּ, לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא עַל קֹהֶלֶת.
phrases.en: If they had a dispute, they had a dispute only about Kohelet.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חָמִיו שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, כְּדִבְרֵי בֶן עַזַּאי, כָּךְ נֶחְלְקוּ וְכָךְ גָּמְרוּ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yohanan ben Joshua the son of the father-in-law of Rabbi Akiva said in accordance with the words of Ben Azzai: so they disputed and so they reached a decision.

phrases.he: בּוֹ בַיּוֹם נִמְנוּ וְגָמְרוּ עַל עֲרֵבַת הָרַגְלַיִם, שֶׁהִיא מִשְּׁנֵי לֻגִּין וְעַד תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין שֶׁנִּסְדְּקָה, שֶׁהִיא טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: On that day the votes were counted and they decided that a footbath holding from two logs to nine kavs which was cracked could contract midras uncleanness.

phrases.he: שֶׁרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, עֲרֵבַת הָרַגְלַיִם כִּשְׁמָהּ
phrases.en: Because Rabbi Akiva said a footbath [must be considered] according to its designation.

phrases.he: בּוֹ בַיּוֹם אָמְרוּ, כָּל הַזְּבָחִים שֶׁנִּזְבְּחוּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן, כְּשֵׁרִים, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא עָלוּ לַבְּעָלִים לְשׁוּם חוֹבָה, חוּץ מִן הַפֶּסַח וּמִן הַחַטָּאת.
phrases.en: On that day they said: all animal sacrifices which have been sacrificed under the name of some other offering are [nevertheless] valid, but they are not accounted to their owners as a fulfillment of their obligations, with the exception of the pesah and the sin-offering.

phrases.he: הַפֶּסַח בִּזְמַנּוֹ, וְהַחַטָּאת בְּכָל זְמַן.
phrases.en: [This is true of] the pesah in its correct time and the sin-offering at any time.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַף הָאָשָׁם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: [with the exception] also of the guilt-offering; [so that this refers to] the pesah in its correct time and to the sin- and guilt-offerings at any time.

phrases.he: הַפֶּסַח בִּזְמַנּוֹ, וְהַחַטָּאת וְהָאָשָׁם בְּכָל זְמַן.

אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן עַזַּאי, מְקֻבְּלַנִי מִפִּי שִׁבְעִים וּשְׁנַיִם זָקֵן, בַּיּוֹם שֶׁהוֹשִׁיבוּ אֶת רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה בַּיְשִׁיבָה, שֶׁכָּל הַזְּבָחִים הַנֶּאֱכָלִין שֶׁנִּזְבְּחוּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן, כְּשֵׁרִים, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא עָלוּ לַבְּעָלִים לְשֵׁם חוֹבָה, חוּץ מִן הַפֶּסַח וּמִן הַחַטָּאת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai said: I received a tradition from the seventy-two elders on the day when they appointed Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah head of the college that all animal sacrifices which are eaten and which have not been sacrificed under their own name are nevertheless valid, but they are not accounted to their owners as a fulfillment of their obligations, with the exception of the pesah and the sin-offering.

phrases.he: לֹא הוֹסִיף בֶּן עַזַּאי אֶלָּא הָעוֹלָה, וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים
phrases.en: Ben Azzai only added [to these exceptions] the wholly burnt-offering, but the sages did not agree with him.

phrases.he: בּוֹ בַיּוֹם אָמְרוּ, עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב, מַה הֵן בַּשְּׁבִיעִית.
phrases.en: On that day they said: what is the law applying to Ammon and Moab in the seventh year? Rabbi Tarfon decreed tithe for the poor.

phrases.he: גָּזַר רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן, מַעְשַׂר עָנִי.
phrases.en: And Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah decreed second tithe.

phrases.he: וְגָזַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה, מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי.
אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה, עָלֶיךָ רְאָיָה לְלַמֵּד, שֶׁאַתָּה מַחְמִיר, שֶׁכָּל הַמַּחְמִיר, עָלָיו רְאָיָה לְלַמֵּד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Ishmael said: Elazar ben Azariah, you must produce your proof because you are expressing the stricter view and whoever expresses a stricter view has the burden to produce the proof.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה, יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָחִי, אֲנִי לֹא שִׁנִּיתִי מִסֵּדֶר הַשָּׁנִים, טַרְפוֹן אָחִי שִׁנָּה, וְעָלָיו רְאָיָה לְלַמֵּד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah said to him: Ishmael, my brother, I have not deviated from the sequence of years, Tarfon, my brother, has deviated from it and the burden is upon him to produce the proof.

phrases.he: הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן, מִצְרַיִם חוּץ לָאָרֶץ, עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב חוּץ לָאָרֶץ, מַה מִּצְרַיִם מַעְשַׂר עָנִי בַשְּׁבִיעִית, אַף עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב מַעְשַׂר עָנִי בַשְּׁבִיעִית.
phrases.en: Rabbi Tarfon answered: Egypt is outside the land of Israel, Ammon and Moab are outside the land of Israel: just as Egypt must give tithe for the poor in the seventh year, so must Ammon and Moab give tithe for the poor in the seventh year.

phrases.he: הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה, בָּבֶל חוּץ לָאָרֶץ, עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב חוּץ לָאָרֶץ, מַה בָּבֶל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בַשְּׁבִיעִית, אַף עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בַשְּׁבִיעִית.
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah answered: Babylon is outside the land of Israel, Ammon and Moab are outside the land of Israel: just as Babylon must give second tithe in the seventh year, so must Ammon and Moab give second tithe in the seventh year.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן, מִצְרַיִם שֶׁהִיא קְרוֹבָה, עֲשָׂאוּהָ מַעְשַׂר עָנִי, שֶׁיִּהְיוּ עֲנִיֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל נִסְמָכִים עָלֶיהָ בַּשְּׁבִיעִית, אַף עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב, שֶׁהֵם קְרוֹבִים, נַעֲשִׂים מַעְשַׂר עָנִי, שֶׁיִּהְיוּ עֲנִיֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל נִסְמָכִים עֲלֵיהֶם בַּשְּׁבִיעִית.
phrases.en: Rabbi Tarfon said: on Egypt which is near, they imposed tithe for the poor so that the poor of Israel might be supported by it during the seventh year; so on Ammon and Moab which are near, we should impose tithe for the poor so that the poor of Israel may be supported by it during the seventh year.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה, הֲרֵי אַתָּה כִמְהַנָּן מָמוֹן, וְאֵין אַתָּה אֶלָּא כְמַפְסִיד נְפָשׁוֹת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah said to him: Behold, you are like one who would benefit them with gain, yet you are really as one who causes them to perish.

phrases.he: קוֹבֵעַ אַתָּה אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם מִלְּהוֹרִיד טַל וּמָטָר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (מלאכי ג), הֲיִקְבַּע אָדָם אֱלֹהִים כִּי אַתֶּם קֹבְעִים אֹתִי וַאֲמַרְתֶּם בַּמֶּה קְבַעֲנוּךָ הַמַּעֲשֵׂר וְהַתְּרוּמָה.
phrases.en: Would you rob the heavens so that dew or rain should not descend? As it is said, "Will a man rob God? Yet you rob me. But you: How have we robbed You? In tithes and heave-offerings" (Malakhi 3:8). Rabbi Joshua said: Behold, I shall be as one who replies on behalf of Tarfon, my brother, but not in accordance with the substance of his arguments.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, הֲרֵינִי כְמֵשִׁיב עַל טַרְפוֹן אָחִי, אֲבָל לֹא לְעִנְיַן דְּבָרָיו. מִצְרַיִם
phrases.en: The law regarding Egypt is a new act and the law regarding Babylon is an old act, and the law which is being argued before us is a new act.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה חָדָשׁ, וּבָבֶל
phrases.en: A new act should be argued from [another] new act, but a new act should not be argued from an old act.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה יָשָׁן, וְהַנִּדּוֹן שֶׁלְּפָנֵינוּ
phrases.en: The law regarding Egypt is the act of the elders and the law regarding Babylon is the act of the prophets, and the law which is being argued before us is the act of the elders.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה חָדָשׁ. יִדּוֹן
phrases.en: Let one act of the elders be argued from [another] act of the elders, but let not an act of the elders be argued from an act of the prophets.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה חָדָשׁ מִמַּעֲשֶׂה חָדָשׁ, וְאַל יִדּוֹן
phrases.en: The votes were counted and they decided that Ammon and Moab should give tithe for the poor in the seventh year.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה חָדָשׁ מִמַּעֲשֶׂה יָשָׁן. מִצְרַיִם
phrases.en: And when Rabbi Yose ben Durmaskit visited Rabbi Eliezer in Lod he said to him: what new thing did you have in the house of study today? He said to him: their votes were counted and they decided that Ammon and Moab must give tithe for the poor in the seventh year.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֵׂה זְקֵנִים, וּבָבֶל
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer wept and said: "The counsel of the Lord is with them that fear him: and his covenant, to make them know it" (Psalms 25:14).

phrases.he: מַעֲשֵׂה נְבִיאִים, וְהַנִּדּוֹן שֶׁלְּפָנֵינוּ
phrases.en: Go and tell them: Don't worry about your voting.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֵׂה זְקֵנִים. יִדּוֹן
phrases.en: I received a tradition from Rabbi Yohanan ben Zakkai who heard it from his teacher, and his teacher from his teacher, and so back to a halachah given to Moses from Sinai, that Ammon and Moab must give tithe for the poor in the seventh year.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֵׂה זְקֵנִים מִמַּעֲשֵׂה זְקֵנִים, וְאַל יִדּוֹן
מַעֲשֵׂה זְקֵנִים מִמַּעֲשֵׂה נְבִיאִים.
נִמְנוּ וְגָמְרוּ, עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב מְעַשְּׂרִין מַעְשַׂר עָנִי בַּשְּׁבִיעִית.
וּכְשֶׁבָּא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן דֻּרְמַסְקִית אֵצֶל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּלוֹד, אָמַר לוֹ, מַה חִדּוּשׁ הָיָה לָכֶם בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ הַיּוֹם.
אָמַר לוֹ, נִמְנוּ וְגָמְרוּ, עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב מְעַשְּׂרִים מַעְשַׂר עָנִי בַּשְּׁבִיעִית.
בָּכָה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְאָמַר, סוֹד ה' לִירֵאָיו וּבְרִיתוֹ לְהוֹדִיעָם (תהלים כה).
צֵא וֶאֱמֹר לָהֶם, אַל תָּחֹשּׁוּ לְמִנְיַנְכֶם.
מְקֻבָּל אֲנִי מֵרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי, שֶׁשָּׁמַע מֵרַבּוֹ, וְרַבּוֹ מֵרַבּוֹ עַד הֲלָכָה לְמשֶׁה מִסִּינַי, שֶׁעַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב מְעַשְּׂרִין מַעְשַׂר עָנִי בַּשְּׁבִיעִית
בּוֹ בַיּוֹם בָּא יְהוּדָה, גֵּר עַמּוֹנִי, וְעָמַד לִפְנֵיהֶן בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ.
phrases.en: On that day Judah, an Ammonite convert, came and stood before them in the house of study.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, מָה אֲנִי לָבֹא בַקָּהָל.
phrases.en: He said to them: Do I have the right to enter into the assembly? Rabban Gamaliel said to him: you are forbidden.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, אָסוּר אָתָּה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua said to him: you are permitted.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, מֻתָּר אָתָּה.
phrases.en: Rabban Gamaliel said to him: the verse says, "An Ammonite or a Moabite shall not enter into the assembly of the Lord: even to the tenth generation" (Deuteronomy 23:4).

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר (דברים כג), לֹא יָבֹא עַמּוֹנִי וּמוֹאָבִי בִּקְהַל ה' גַּם דּוֹר עֲשִׂירִי וְגוֹ'.
phrases.en: R.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, וְכִי עַמּוֹנִים וּמוֹאָבִים בִּמְקוֹמָן הֵן.
phrases.en: Joshua said to him: But are the Ammonites and Moabites still in their own territory? Sanheriv, the king of Assyria, has long since come up and mingled all the nations, as it is said: "In that I have removed the bounds of the peoples, and have robbed their treasures, and have brought down as one mighty the inhabitants" (Isaiah 10:1.

phrases.he: כְּבָר עָלָה סַנְחֵרִיב מֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר וּבִלְבֵּל אֶת כָּל הָאֻמּוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ישעיה י), וְאָסִיר גְּבוּלֹת עַמִּים וַעֲתוּדוֹתֵיהֶם שׁוֹשֵׂתִי וְאוֹרִיד כַּאבִּיר יוֹשְׁבִים.
אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר (ירמיה מט), וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן אָשִׁיב אֶת שְׁבוּת בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן, וּכְבָר חָזְרוּ.
phrases.en: Rabban Gamaliel said to him: the verse says, "But afterward I will bring back the captivity of the children of Ammon," (Jeremiah 49:6) they have already returned.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר (ירמיה ל ג), וְשַׁבְתִּי אֶת שְׁבוּת עַמִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל וִיהוּדָה, וַעֲדַיִן לֹא שָׁבוּ. הִתִּירוּהוּ לָבֹא בַקָּהָל:
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua said to him: [another] verse says, "I will return the captivity of my people Israel and Judah" (Jeremiah 30:3). Yet they have not yet returned. So they permitted him to enter the assembly.

phrases.he: תַּרְגּוּם שֶׁבְּעֶזְרָא וְשֶׁבְּדָנִיֵּאל, מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם.
phrases.en: The Aramaic sections in Ezra and Daniel defile the hands.

phrases.he: תַּרְגּוּם שֶׁכְּתָבוֹ עִבְרִית וְעִבְרִית שֶׁכְּתָבוֹ תַּרְגּוּם, וּכְתָב עִבְרִי, אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם.
phrases.en: If an Aramaic section was written in Hebrew, or a Hebrew section was written in Aramaic, or [Hebrew which was written with] Hebrew script, it does not defile the hands.

phrases.he: לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא, עַד שֶׁיִּכְתְּבֶנּוּ אַשּׁוּרִית, עַל הָעוֹר, וּבִדְיוֹ
phrases.en: It never defiles the hands until it is written in the Assyrian script, on parchment, and in ink.

phrases.he: אוֹמְרִים צְדוֹקִים, קוֹבְלִין אָנוּ עֲלֵיכֶם, פְּרוּשִׁים, שֶׁאַתֶּם אוֹמְרִים, כִּתְבֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ מְטַמְּאִין אֶת הַיָּדַיִם, וְסִפְרֵי הוֹמֵרִיס אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם.
phrases.en: The Sadducees say: we complain against you, Pharisees, because you say that the Holy Scriptures defile the hands, but the books of Homer do not defile the hands.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי, וְכִי אֵין לָנוּ עַל הַפְּרוּשִׁים אֶלָּא זוֹ בִלְבָד.
phrases.en: Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai said: Have we nothing against the Pharisees but this? Behold they say that the bones of a donkey are clean, yet the bones of Yohanan the high priest are unclean.

phrases.he: הֲרֵי הֵם אוֹמְרִים, עַצְמוֹת חֲמוֹר טְהוֹרִים וְעַצְמוֹת יוֹחָנָן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל טְמֵאִים.
אָמְרוּ לוֹ, לְפִי חִבָּתָן הִיא טֻמְאָתָן, שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם עַצְמוֹת אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ תַּרְוָדוֹת.
phrases.en: They said to him: according to the affection for them, so is their impurity, so that nobody should make spoons out of the bones of his father or mother.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, אַף כִּתְבֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ לְפִי חִבָּתָן הִיא טֻמְאָתָן, וְסִפְרֵי הוֹמֵרִיס, שֶׁאֵינָן חֲבִיבִין, אֵינָן מְטַמְּאִין אֶת הַיָּדָיִם:
phrases.en: He said to them: so also are the Holy Scriptures according to the affection for them, so is their uncleanness. The books of Homer which are not precious do not defile the hands.

phrases.he: אוֹמְרִים צְדוֹקִין, קוֹבְלִין אָנוּ עֲלֵיכֶם, פְּרוּשִׁים, שֶׁאַתֶּם מְטַהֲרִים אֶת הַנִּצּוֹק.
phrases.en: The Sadducees say: we complain against you, Pharisees, that you declare an uninterrupted flow of a liquid to be clean.

phrases.he: אוֹמְרִים הַפְּרוּשִׁים, קוֹבְלִין אָנוּ עֲלֵיכֶם, צְדוֹקִים, שֶׁאַתֶּם מְטַהֲרִים אֶת אַמַּת הַמַּיִם הַבָּאָה מִבֵּית הַקְּבָרוֹת.
phrases.en: The Pharisees say: we complain against you, Sadducees, that you declare a stream of water which flows from a burial-ground to be clean? The Sadducees say: we complain against you, Pharisees, that you say, my ox or donkey which has done injury is liable, yet my male or female slave who has done injury is not liable.

phrases.he: אוֹמְרִים צְדוֹקִין, קוֹבְלִין אָנוּ עֲלֵיכֶם, פְּרוּשִׁים, שֶׁאַתֶּם אוֹמְרִים, שׁוֹרִי וַחֲמוֹרִי שֶׁהִזִּיקוּ, חַיָּבִין.
וְעַבְדִּי וַאֲמָתִי שֶׁהִזִּיקוּ, פְּטוּרִין.
מָה אִם שׁוֹרִי וַחֲמוֹרִי, שֶׁאֵינִי חַיָּב בָּהֶם מִצְוֹת, הֲרֵי אֲנִי חַיָּב בְּנִזְקָן.
עַבְדִּי וַאֲמָתִי, שֶׁאֲנִי חַיָּב בָּהֶן מִצְוֹת, אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁאֱהֵא חַיָּב בְּנִזְקָן.
אָמְרוּ לָהֶם, לֹא. אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם בְּשׁוֹרִי וַחֲמוֹרִי, שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם דַּעַת, תֹּאמְרוּ בְּעַבְדִּי וּבַאֲמָתִי, שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם דָּעַת.
phrases.en: Now if in the case of my ox or my donkey for which I am not responsible if they do not fulfill religious duties, yet I am responsible for their damages, in the case of my male or female slave for whom I am responsible to see that they fulfill mitzvot, how much more so that I should be responsible for their damages? They said to them: No, if you argue about my ox or my donkey which have no understanding,

phrases.he: שֶׁאִם אַקְנִיטֵם, יֵלֵךְ וְיַדְלִיק גְּדִישׁוֹ שֶׁל אַחֵר וֶאֱהֵא חַיָּב לְשַׁלֵּם
phrases.en: can you deduce from there anything concerning a male or female slave who do have understanding? So that if I were to anger either of them and they would go and burn another person's stack, should I be liable to make restitution?

phrases.he: אָמַר צְדוֹקִי גְלִילִי, קוֹבֵל אֲנִי עֲלֵיכֶם, פְּרוּשִׁים, שֶׁאַתֶּם כּוֹתְבִין אֶת הַמּוֹשֵׁל עִם משֶׁה בַּגֵּט.
phrases.en: A Galilean min said: I complain against you Pharisees, that you write the name of the ruler and the name of Moses together on a divorce document.

phrases.he: אוֹמְרִים פְּרוּשִׁים, קוֹבְלִין אָנוּ עָלֶיךָ, צְדוֹקִי גְלִילִי, שֶׁאַתֶּם כּוֹתְבִים אֶת הַמּוֹשֵׁל עִם הַשֵּׁם בַּדַּף, וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁאַתֶּם כּוֹתְבִין אֶת הַמּוֹשֵׁל מִלְמַעְלָן וְאֶת הַשֵּׁם מִלְּמַטָּן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמות ה) וַיֹּאמֶר פַּרְעֹה מִי ה' אֲשֶׁר אֶשְׁמַע בְּקֹלוֹ לְשַׁלַּח אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.en: The Pharisees said: we complain against you, Galilean min, that you write the name of the ruler together with the divine name on a single page [of Torah]? And furthermore that you write the name of the ruler above and the divine name below? As it is said, "And Pharoah said, Who is the Lord that I should hearken to his voice to let Israel go?" (Exodus 5:2) But when he was smitten what did he say? "The Lord is righteous" (Exodus 9:27).

phrases.he: וּכְשֶׁלָּקָה מַהוּ אוֹמֵר (שם ט), ה' הַצַּדִּיק
כֹּל שֶׁהוּא יָד וְלֹא שׁוֹמֵר, מִטַּמֵּא וּמְטַמֵּא וְלֹא מִצְטָרֵף.
phrases.en: That which serves as a handle but does not protect, both contracts uncleanness and conveys uncleanness; but it is not included.

phrases.he: שׁוֹמֵר, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָד, מִטַּמֵּא וּמְטַמֵּא וּמִצְטָרֵף.
phrases.en: If it protects but is not a handle, it contracts and conveys uncleanness and is included.

phrases.he: לֹא שׁוֹמֵר וְלֹא יָד, לֹא מִטַּמֵּא וְלֹא מְטַמֵּא
phrases.en: If it neither protects nor serves as a handle, it neither contracts nor conveys uncleanness.

phrases.he: שָׁרְשֵׁי הַשּׁוּם וְהַבְּצָלִים וְהַקַּפְלוֹטוֹת בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן לַחִין, וְהַפִּטְמָא שֶׁלָּהֶן בֵּין לַחָה בֵּין יְבֵשָׁה, וְהָעַמּוּד שֶׁהוּא מְכֻוָּן כְּנֶגֶד הָאֹכֶל, שָׁרְשֵׁי הַחֲזָרִים וְהַצְּנוֹן וְהַנָּפוּס, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: Roots of garlic, onions or leeks that are still moist, or their top-parts, whether they are moist or dry, also the central stalk that is within the edible part, the roots of lettuce, the radish and the turnip, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, שֹׁרֶשׁ צְנוֹן גָּדוֹל מִצְטָרֵף, וְהַסִּיב שֶׁלּוֹ, אֵינוֹ מִצְטָרֵף.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: only the large roots of the radish are included, but its fibrous roots are not included.

phrases.he: שָׁרְשֵׁי הַמִּתְנָא וְהַפֵּיגָם וְיַרְקוֹת שָׂדֶה וְיַרְקוֹת גִּנָּה שֶׁעֲקָרָן לְשָׁתְלָן, וְהַשִּׁדְרָה שֶׁל שִׁבֹּלֶת וְהַלְּבוּשׁ שֶׁלָּהּ,
phrases.en: The roots of the mint, rue, wild herbs and garden herbs that have been uprooted in order to be planted elsewhere, and the spine of an ear of grain, and its husk.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר, אַף הַסִּיג שֶׁל רְצָפוֹת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מִטַּמְּאִין וּמְטַמְּאִים וּמִצְטָרְפִין:
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar says: also the earth covering of roots; All these things contract and convey impurity and are included.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ מִטַּמְּאִין וּמְטַמְּאִין וְלֹא מִצְטָרְפִין.
phrases.en: The following are both defiled and defile, but do not join together [together with the rest]: Roots of garlic, onions or leeks when they are dry, the stalk that is not within the edible part, the twig of a vine a handbreadth long on either side, the stem of the cluster whatsoever be its length, the tail of the cluster bereft of grapes, the stem of the ‘broom’ of the palm-tree to a length of four handbreadths, the stalk of the ear [of grain] to a length of three handbreadths, and the stalk of all things that are cut, to the length of three handbreadths.

phrases.he: שָׁרְשֵׁי הַשּׁוּם וְהַבְּצָלִים וְהַקַּפְלוֹטוֹת בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵם יְבֵשִׁים, וְהָעַמּוּד שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְכֻוָּן כְּנֶגֶד הָאֹכֶל, וְיַד הַפַּרְכִּיל טֶפַח מִכָּאן וְטֶפַח מִכָּאן, יַד הָאֶשְׁכּוֹל כָּל שֶׁהוּא, וְזָנָב שֶׁל אֶשְׁכּוֹל שֶׁרִקְּנוֹ, וְיַד הַמַּכְבֵּד שֶׁל תְּמָרָה אַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים, וְקָנֶה שֶׁל שִׁבֹּלֶת שְׁלשָׁה טְפָחִים, וְיַד כָּל הַנִּקְצָרִים שְׁלשָׁה, וְשֶׁאֵין דַּרְכָּן לִקָּצֵר יְדֵיהֶם וְשָׁרְשֵׁיהֶם כָּל שֶׁהֵן, וּמַלְעִין שֶׁל שִׁבֳּלִין, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מִטַּמְּאִים וּמְטַמְּאִין וְלֹא מִצְטָרְפִין
phrases.en: In the case of those things not usually cut, their stalks and roots of any size whatsoever. As for the outer husks of grains, they defile and are defiled, but do not join together.
