phrases.he: אֵלּוּ לֹא מִטַּמְּאִין וְלֹא מְטַמְּאִין וְלֹא מִצְטָרְפִין.
phrases.en: The following neither defile nor can they be defiled and they do not join together: The roots of cabbage-stalks, Young shoots of beet growing out of the root, and [similar] such turnip-heads, [And produce whose roots] that are ordinarily cut off but in this case were pulled up [with their roots].

phrases.he: שָׁרְשֵׁי קוֹלְסֵי הַכְּרוּב, וְחֻלְפוֹת תְּרָדִים, וְהַלֶּפֶת, אֵת שֶׁדַּרְכָּם לִגָּזֵז וְנֶעֱקְרוּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose declares them all susceptible to contract uncleanness, but he declares insusceptible cabbage-stalks and turnip-heads.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְטַמֵּא בְכֻלָּן וּמְטַהֵר בְּשָׁרְשֵׁי קוֹלְסֵי הַכְּרוּב וְהַלָּפֶת
כָּל יְדוֹת הָאֳכָלִין שֶׁבְּסָסָן בַּגֹּרֶן, טְהוֹרִים. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.en: Stalks of all foods that have been threshed on the threshing-floor are clean. Rabbi Yose declares them unclean.

phrases.he: פְּסִיגָה שֶׁל אֶשְׁכּוֹל שֶׁרִקְּנָהּ, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A sprig of a vine when stripped of its grapes is clean, but if one grape alone is left on it, it is unclean.

phrases.he: שִׁיֵּר בָּהּ גַּרְגִּיר אֶחָד, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: A twig of a date-tree stripped of its dates is clean, but if one date remains on it, it is unclean.

phrases.he: שַׁרְבִיט שֶׁל תְּמָרָה שֶׁרִקְּנוֹ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Similarly, with beans, if the pods were stripped from the stem it is clean, but if even one pod alone remains, it is unclean.

phrases.he: שִׁיֵּר בּוֹ תְּמָרָה אַחַת, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah declares [the stalk] of the broad bean clean, but declares unclean the stalk of other beans, since it is of use when [the pulse] is handled.

phrases.he: וְכֵן בַּקִּטְנִיּוֹת, שַׁרְבִיט שֶׁרִקְּנוֹ, טָהוֹר.
שִׁיֵּר בּוֹ גַּרְגִּיר אֶחָד, טָמֵא.
רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה מְטַהֵר בְּשֶׁל פּוֹל וּמְטַמֵּא בְּשֶׁל קִטְנִיּוֹת, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא רוֹצֶה בְּמִשְׁמוּשָׁן
עֳקָצֵי תְאֵנִים וּגְרוֹגָרוֹת וְהַכְּלוּסִים וְהֶחָרוּבִים, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מִטַּמְּאִין וּמְטַמְּאִין וּמִצְטָרְפִין.
phrases.en: Stems of figs and dried figs, kelusim, and carobs are both defiled and defile, and they join together.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַף עֹקֶץ דְּלָעַת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: also the stalks of the gourd.

phrases.he: עֳקָצֵי הָאַגָּסִין וְהַקְּרֻסְטְמֵלִין וְהַפְּרִישִׁין וְהָעֻזְרָדִין, עֹקֶץ דְּלַעַת טֶפַח, עֹקֶץ קוּנְרָס טֶפַח, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר, טְפָחַיִם, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מִטַּמְּאִין וּמְטַמְּאִין וְלֹא מִצְטָרְפִים.
phrases.en: The stems of pears and krutumelin pears, quinces, and crab-apples, the stalks of the gourd and the artichoke [to the length of] one handbreadth. Rabbi Elazar bar Zadok says: two handbreadths; [All] these are defiled and defile; but do not join together.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הָעֳקָצִים, לֹא מִטַּמְּאִין וְלֹא מְטַמְּאִין
phrases.en: As for other stems, they are neither defiled nor do they defile.

phrases.he: זֵיתִים שֶׁכְּבָשָׁן בְּטַרְפֵיהֶן, טְהוֹרִים, לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא כְבָשָׁן אֶלָּא לְמַרְאֶה.
phrases.en: Leaves of olives pickled together with the olives remain clean, for their pickling was only for the sake of appearances.

phrases.he: כְּשׁוּת שֶׁל קִשּׁוּת וְהַנֵּץ שֶׁלָּהּ, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: The fibrous substance on a zucchini and the flower-like substance on it are clean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהִיא לִפְנֵי הַתַּגָּר, טְמֵאָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: that as long as it is still before the merchant, it is unclean.

phrases.he: כָּל הַגַּלְעִינִין מִטַּמְּאוֹת וּמְטַמְּאוֹת וְלֹא מִצְטָרְפוֹת.
phrases.en: All kinds of pits can be defiled and defile but do not join together.

phrases.he: גַּלְעִינָה שֶׁל רֹטֶב, אַף עַל פִּי יוֹצְאָה, מִצְטָרֶפֶת.
phrases.en: The pits of fresh dates, even when detached [from the edible part], do join together; but those of dried dates do not join together.

phrases.he: שֶׁל יְבֵשָׁה, אֵינָהּ מִצְטָרֶפֶת.
phrases.en: Accordingly, the stems of dried dates do join together, but that of fresh dates do not join together.

phrases.he: לְפִיכָךְ, חוֹתָל שֶׁל יְבֵשָׁה, מִצְטָרֵף.
phrases.en: If only part of a pit is detached, then only that part near the edible portion joins together.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל רֹטֶב, אֵינוֹ מִצְטָרֵף.
phrases.en: [Similarly] with a bone on which there is flesh, only that part that is close to the edible part joins together.

phrases.he: גַּלְעִינָה שֶׁמִּקְצָתָהּ יוֹצְאָה, שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד הָאֹכֶל, מִצְטָרֵף.
עֶצֶם שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו בָּשָׂר, שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד הָאֹכֶל, מִצְטָרֵף.
הָיָה עָלָיו מִצַּד אֶחָד,
רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, רוֹאִין אוֹתוֹ כְּאִלּוּ הוּא מַקִּיפוֹ בְטַבַּעַת.
phrases.en: [If a bone] has flesh only upon one of its sides: Rabbi Ishmael says: we take it as though [the flesh] encompasses it like a ring; But the sages say: [only] that part close to the edible part is included [as is the case] for example with savory, hyssop and thyme.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד הָאֹכֶל, מִצְטָרֵף, כְּגוֹן הַסִּיאָה וְהָאֵזוֹב וְהַקּוֹרָנִית:
הָרִמּוֹן וְהָאֲבַטִּיחַ שֶׁנִּמּוֹק מִקְצָתוֹ, אֵינוֹ מִצְטָרֵף.
phrases.en: If a pomegranate or melon has rotted in part, [what is rotten] does not join together.

phrases.he: שָׁלֵם מִכָּאן וּמִכָּאן וְנִמּוֹק מִן הָאֶמְצַע, אֵינוֹ מִצְטָרֵף.
phrases.en: And if [the fruit] is sound at either end but has rotted in the middle, [what is rotten] does not join together.

phrases.he: הַפִּטְמָא שֶׁל רִמּוֹן, מִצְטָרֶפֶת.
phrases.en: The stem of a pomegranate does join together, but the fibrous substance in it does not join together.

phrases.he: וְהַנֵּץ שֶׁלּוֹ אֵינוֹ מִצְטָרֵף.
רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַף הַמַּסְרֵק טָהוֹר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: also the comb is not susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: כָּל הַקְּלִפִּין מִטַּמְּאוֹת וּמְטַמְּאוֹת וּמִצְטָרְפוֹת.
phrases.en: All kinds of peels defile and are defiled, and join together.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, שְׁלשָׁה קְלִפִּין בַּבָּצָל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: an onion has three skins: the innermost one whether it is in its entire state or whether it be pierced with holes joins together; the middle one when it is in a whole state joins together, but when it is pierced with holes does not join together; the outermost skin is in either case insusceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: הַפְּנִימִית, בֵּין שְׁלֵמָה בֵּין קְדוּרָה, מִצְטָרֶפֶת.
הָאֶמְצָעִית, שְׁלֵמָה מִצְטָרֶפֶת, וּקְדוּרָה אֵינָהּ מִצְטָרֶפֶת.
וְהַחִיצוֹנָה, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ, טְהוֹרָה
הַמְחַתֵּךְ לְבַשֵּׁל, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא מֵרַק, אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: If one chops up [fruit] for cooking, even if [the chopping had] not been completely finished, it is not regarded as connected.

phrases.he: לִכְבֹּשׁ וְלִשְׁלֹק וּלְהַנִּיחַ עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן, חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: If his intention had been to pickle or to boil it, or to set it on the table, then it is regarded as connected.

phrases.he: הִתְחִיל לְפָרֵק, אֹכֶל שֶׁהִתְחִיל בּוֹ, אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: If he began to take [the pieces] apart, [only] that part of the food which he began to take apart is not considered connected.

phrases.he: הָאֱגוֹזִים שֶׁאֲמָנָן, וְהַבְּצָלִים שֶׁחֲמָרָן, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: Nuts that had been strung together, or onions that had been piled together, count as connected.

phrases.he: הִתְחִיל לְפָרֵק בָּאֱגוֹזִים וּלְפַקֵּל בַּבְּצָלִים, אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר.
phrases.en: If he began to take the nuts apart, or to strip the onions, they are not connected.

phrases.he: הָאֱגוֹזִים וְהַשְּׁקֵדִים, חִבּוּר, עַד שֶׁיְּרַסֵּס
phrases.en: [Shells of] nuts and almonds are considered connected [with the edible part] until they are crushed.

phrases.he: בֵּיצָה מְגֻלְגֶּלֶת, עַד שֶׁיָּגוֹס. וּשְׁלוּקָה, עַד שֶׁיְּרַסֵּס.
phrases.en: [The shell of] a roasted egg [is considered connected] until it is cracked.

phrases.he: עֶצֶם שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ מֹחַ, חִבּוּר, עַד שֶׁיְּרַסֵּס.
phrases.en: That of a hard-boiled egg [is considered connected] until it is entirely broken up. A marrow-bone serves as connected until it is wholly crushed.

phrases.he: הָרִמּוֹן שֶׁפְּרָדוֹ, חִבּוּר עַד שֶׁיַּקִּישׁ עָלָיו בְּקָנֶה.
phrases.en: A pomegranate that has been divided into sections is connected until it has been knocked with a stick.

phrases.he: כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ, שְׁלַל הַכּוֹבְסִין וְהַבֶּגֶד שֶׁהוּא תָפוּר בְּכִלְאַיִם, חִבּוּר, עַד שֶׁיַּתְחִיל לְהַתִּיר
phrases.en: Similarly, loose stitches of laundrymen or a garment that had been stitched together with threads of kilayim, are connected until one begins to loosen them.

phrases.he: עֲלֵי יְרָקוֹת יְרֻקִּים, מִצְטָרְפִין. וּלְבָנִים, אֵינָן מִצְטָרְפִין.
phrases.en: The [outer] leaves of vegetables: if they are green they join together, but if they have whitened they not join together.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר, הַלְּבָנִים מִצְטָרְפִים בַּכְּרוּב, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן אֹכֶל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar bar Zadok says: the white leaves of cabbage join together because they are edible.

phrases.he: וּבַחֲזָרִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מְשַׁמְּרִין אֶת הָאֹכֶל
phrases.en: So also those of lettuces, because they preserve the edible part.

phrases.he: עֲלֵי בְצָלִים וּבְנֵי בְצָלִים, אִם יֵשׁ בָּהֶן רִיר, מִשְׁתַּעֲרִין בִּכְמוֹת שֶׁהֵן.
phrases.en: Onion leaves or the offshoots of onions, if there is moisture in them they are to be measured as they are; if there is empty space within them, it must be squeezed tightly together.

phrases.he: אִם יֵשׁ בָּהֶן חָלָל, מְמַעֵךְ אֶת חֲלָלָן.
phrases.en: Spongy bread is measured as it is, but if there is empty space within it, it must be pressed firmly.

phrases.he: פַּת סְפוֹגָנִית, מִשְׁתַּעֶרֶת בִּכְמוֹת שֶׁהִיא.
phrases.en: The flesh of a calf which had swollen, or the flesh of an old [beast] that has shrunken in size, are measured in the condition they are in.

phrases.he: אִם יֶשׁ בָּהּ חָלָל, מְמַעֵךְ אֶת חֲלָלָהּ.
בְּשַׂר הָעֵגֶל שֶׁנִּתְפַּח וּבְשַׂר זְקֵנָה שֶׁנִּתְמַעֵט, מִשְׁתַּעֲרִין בִּכְמוֹת שֶׁהֵן
קִשּׁוּת שֶׁנְּטָעָהּ בְּעָצִיץ וְהִגְדִּילָה וְיָצְאָה חוּץ לֶעָצִיץ, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A cucumber planted in a pot which grew until it was out of the pot is pure.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, מַה טִּיבָהּ לִטָּהֵר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon said: what is its nature to make it clean? Rather, that which has already become unclean remains unclean, and only that which is pure can be eaten.

phrases.he: אֶלָּא הַטָּמֵא בְּטֻמְאָתוֹ, וְהַטָּהוֹר יֵאָכֵל
כְּלֵי גְלָלִים וּכְלֵי אֲדָמָה, שֶׁהַשָּׁרָשִׁים יְכוֹלִין לָצֵאת בָּהֶן, אֵינָם מַכְשִׁירִים אֶת הַזְּרָעִים.
phrases.en: Vessels made of cattle dung or of earth through which the roots can penetrate, do not render the seeds susceptible.

phrases.he: עָצִיץ נָקוּב אֵינוֹ מַכְשִׁיר אֶת הַזְּרָעִים.
phrases.en: A perforated plant-pot does not render seeds susceptible; but if it has no hole, the seeds do become susceptible.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ נָקוּב, מַכְשִׁיר אֶת הַזְּרָעִים.
phrases.en: What should be the hole's dimension? Such that a small root can push its way through.

phrases.he: כַּמָּה הוּא שִׁעוּרוֹ שֶׁל נֶקֶב, כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּצֵא בוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ קָטָן.
phrases.en: If it was filled with earth to its brim, it is deemed as a frame without an edge.

phrases.he: מִלְאָהוּ עָפָר עַד שְׂפָתוֹ, הֲרֵי הוּא כְטַבְלָא שֶׁאֵין לָהּ לִזְבֵּז
יֵשׁ צְרִיכִין הֶכְשֵׁר וְאֵינָן צְרִיכִים מַחֲשָׁבָה, מַחֲשָׁבָה וְהֶכְשֵׁר, מַחֲשָׁבָה וְלֹא הֶכְשֵׁר, לֹא הֶכְשֵׁר וְלֹא מַחֲשָׁבָה.
phrases.en: Some things need to be rendered susceptible [to uncleanness] but they do not need intention, [Other things need] intention and to be rendered susceptible. [Other things] need intention, but do not need to be rendered susceptible, [And other things] need neither to be rendered susceptible nor intention.

phrases.he: כָּל הָאֳכָלִים הַמְיֻחָדִים לָאָדָם צְרִיכִין הֶכְשֵׁר וְאֵינָן צְרִיכִים מַחֲשָׁבָה
phrases.en: Any food that is meant for people need to be rendered susceptible, but does not need intention.

phrases.he: הַחוֹתֵךְ מִן הָאָדָם, וּמִן הַבְּהֵמָה, וּמִן הַחַיָּה, וּמִן הָעוֹפוֹת, מִנִּבְלַת הָעוֹף הַטָּמֵא, וְהַחֵלֶב בַּכְּפָרִים, וּשְׁאָר כָּל יַרְקוֹת שָׂדֶה חוּץ מִשְּׁמַרְקָעִים וּפִטְרִיּוֹת.
phrases.en: That which has been severed from a human, beast, wild animal, bird, or from the carrion of an unclean bird, and the fat in villages. And all kinds of wild vegetables, except for truffles and mushrooms; Rabbi Judah says, except for field-leeks, purslane and ornithagolum.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, חוּץ מִכְּרֵשֵׁי שָׂדֶה וְהָרְגִילָה וְנֵץ הֶחָלָב.
phrases.en: And Rabbi Shimon says: except for cynara sycaria.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, חוּץ מִן הָעַכָּבִיּוֹת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: except for muscari comusum.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, חוּץ מִן הַכְּלוּסִין, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ צְרִיכִין מַחֲשָׁבָה וְהֶכְשֵׁר:
phrases.en: Behold all these need both intention and to be rendered susceptible [to uncleanness].

phrases.he: נִבְלַת בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה בְּכָל מָקוֹם וְנִבְלַת הָעוֹף הַטָּהוֹר בַּכְּפָרִים, צְרִיכִין מַחֲשָׁבָה וְאֵינָן צְרִיכִין הֶכְשֵׁר.
phrases.en: The carrion of an unclean beast at all places, and of a clean bird in villages, need intention but do not need to be rendered susceptible.

phrases.he: נִבְלַת בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה בְּכָל מָקוֹם, וְנִבְלַת הָעוֹף הַטָּהוֹר וְהַחֵלֶב בַּשְּׁוָקִים, אֵינָן צְרִיכִין מַחֲשָׁבָה וְלֹא הֶכְשֵׁר.
phrases.en: The carrion of a clean beast in all places, and that of a clean bird and also fat in the market places, require neither intention nor to be rendered susceptible.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אַף הַגָּמָל וְהָאַרְנֶבֶת וְהַשָּׁפָן וְהַחֲזִיר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: also [the carrion of] the camel, rabbit, hare or pig.

phrases.he: הַשֶּׁבֶת, מִשֶּׁנָּתַן טַעְמוֹ בַּקְּדֵרָה, אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם תְּרוּמָה, וְאֵינוֹ מִטַּמֵּא טֻמְאַת אֳכָלִים.
phrases.en: The aneth stalk after having given its taste to a dish is no longer subject to the laws of terumah, and also no longer imparts food uncleanness.

phrases.he: לוּלְבֵי זְרָדִים וְשֶׁל עֲדָל וַעֲלֵי הַלּוּף הַשּׁוֹטֶה, אֵינָן מִטַּמְּאִין טֻמְאַת אֳכָלִים עַד שֶׁיִּמְתֹּקוּ.
phrases.en: The young sprouts of hawthorn, of lapidum, or leaves of the wild arum, do not impart food uncleanness until they are sweetened.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אַף שֶׁל פַּקּוּעוֹת כַּיּוֹצֵא בָהֶם:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: also [the leaves of] the colocynth are like them.

phrases.he: הַקֹּשְׁטְ, וְהַחֶמֶס, וְרָאשֵׁי בְשָׂמִים, הַתִּיאָה, וְהַחִלְתִּית, וְהַפִּלְפְּלִין, וְחַלּוֹת חָרִיעַ, נִלְקָחִים בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר וְאֵינָן מִטַּמְּאִין טֻמְאַת אֳכָלִין, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.en: Costus, amomum, principal spices, [roots of] crowfoot, asafoetida, pepper and lozenges made of saffron may be bought with tithe money, but they do not convey food uncleanness, the words of Rabbi Akiva.

phrases.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי, אִם נִלְקָחִים בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר, מִפְּנֵי מָה אֵינָן מִטַּמְּאִין טֻמְאַת אֳכָלִין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri to him: if they may be bought with [second] tithe money, then why should they not impart food uncleanness? And if they

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינָן מִטַּמְּאִין טֻמְאַת אֳכָלִים, אַף הֵם לֹא יִלָּקְחוּ בְכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר
phrases.en: do not impart food uncleanness, then they should also not be bought with [second] tithe money?

phrases.he: הַפַּגִּין וְהַבֹּסֶר, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַמֵּא טֻמְאַת אֳכָלִין.
phrases.en: Unripe figs or grapes: Rabbi Akiva says: they convey food uncleanness; Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri says: [this is only] when they have reached the season when they are liable to tithes.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁיָּבֹאוּ לְעוֹנַת הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת.
phrases.en: Olives and grapes that have hardened: Bet Shammai says: they are susceptible to uncleanness, Bet Hillel says: they are insusceptible.

phrases.he: פְּרִיצֵי זֵיתִים וַעֲנָבִים, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מְטַמְּאִין וּבֵית הִלֵּל מְטַהֲרִין.
phrases.en: Black cumin: Bet Shammai says: is not susceptible, Bet Hillel says: it is susceptible.

phrases.he: הַקֶּצַח, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מְטַהֲרִין, וּבֵית הִלֵּל מְטַמְּאִין. וְכֵן לַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת
phrases.en: Similarly [they dispute with regard to their liability to] tithes.

phrases.he: הַקּוֹר, הֲרֵי הוּא כְעֵץ לְכָל דָּבָר, אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא נִלְקָח בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.en: The heart of a palm is like wood in every respect, except that it may be bought for [second] tithe money.

phrases.he: כַּפְנִיּוֹת, אֳכָלִין, וּפְטוּרוֹת מִן הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת
phrases.en: Unripened dates are considered food, but are exempt from tithes.

phrases.he: דָּגִים מֵאֵימָתַי מְקַבְּלִין טֻמְאָה,
phrases.en: When do fish become susceptible to uncleanness? Bet Shammai say: after they have been caught.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מִשֶּׁיִּצֹּדוּ.
phrases.en: Bet Hillel say: only after they are dead.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מִשֶּׁיָּמוּתוּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: if they can still live.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אִם יְכוֹלִין לִחְיוֹת.
phrases.en: If a branch of a fig tree was broken off, but it was still attached by its bark: Rabbi Judah says: [the fruit] is still not susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: יִחוּר שֶׁל תְּאֵנָה שֶׁנִּפְשַׁח וּמְעֹרֶה בַקְּלִפָּה, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַהֵר.
phrases.en: But the sages say: [it all depends] whether they could still live.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אִם יָכוֹל לִחְיוֹת.
phrases.en: Grain that had been uprooted, but is still attached to the soil even by the smallest of roots, is not susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: תְּבוּאָה שֶׁנֶּעֶקְרָה וּמְעֹרָה אֲפִלּוּ בְשֹׁרֶשׁ קָטָן, טְהוֹרָה
חֵלֶב בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה, אֵינוֹ מִטַּמֵּא טֻמְאַת נְבֵלוֹת, לְפִיכָךְ הוּא צָרִיךְ הֶכְשֵׁר.
phrases.en: The fat [of the carcass] of a clean beast is not regarded as unclean with carrion uncleanness; for this reason it must first be made susceptible.

phrases.he: חֵלֶב בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה, מִטַּמֵּא טֻמְאַת נְבֵלוֹת, לְפִיכָךְ אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ הֶכְשֵׁר.
phrases.en: The fat of an unclean beast, however, is regarded as unclean with carrion uncleanness; for this reason it need not be made at first susceptible.

phrases.he: דָּגִים טְמֵאִים וַחֲגָבִים טְמֵאִים, צְרִיכִין מַחֲשָׁבָה בַּכְּפָרִים
phrases.en: As for unclean fish and unclean locusts, intention is required in villages.

phrases.he: כַּוֶּרֶת דְּבוֹרִים,
phrases.en: A bee-hive: Rabbi Eliezer says: it is treated as if it were land; and one can write a prozbul on it security, it is also not susceptible to uncleanness as long as it remains in its own place, and the one who scrapes honey from it on Shabbat is liable to a sin-offering.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, הֲרֵי הִיא כְקַרְקַע, וְכוֹתְבִין עָלֶיהָ פְּרוֹזְבּוּל, וְאֵינָהּ מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה בִמְקוֹמָהּ, וְהָרוֹדֶה מִמֶּנָּה בְּשַׁבָּת חַיָּב חַטָּאת.
phrases.en: But the sages say: it is not to be treated as if it were land, and one many not write a prozbul on its security; it is susceptible even if it remains in its own place; and the one who scrapes honey from it on Shabbat is exempt [from a sin-offering].

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵינָהּ כְּקַרְקַע, וְאֵין כּוֹתְבִים עָלֶיהָ פְּרוֹזְבּוּל, וּמְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה בִמְקוֹמָהּ, וְהָרוֹדֶה מִמֶּנָּה בְּשַׁבָּת פָּטוּר:
חַלּוֹת דְּבַשׁ, מֵאֵימָתַי מִטַּמְּאוֹת מִשּׁוּם מַשְׁקֶה.
phrases.en: When do honeycombs become susceptible to uncleanness on account of their being regarded as liquids? Bet Shammai says: from the moment he begins to smoke the bees out.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מִשֶּׁיְּחַרְחֵר.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel says: once he breaks up the honeycomb.

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מִשֶּׁיְּרַסֵּק:

אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַנְחִיל לְכָל צַדִּיק וְצַדִּיק שְׁלשׁ מֵאוֹת וַעֲשָׂרָה עוֹלָמוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (משלי ח), לְהַנְחִיל אֹהֲבַי יֵשׁ וְאֹצְרֹתֵיהֶם אֲמַלֵּא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: In the world to come the Holy One, Blessed be He, will make each righteous person inherit three hundred and ten worlds, for it is written: "That I may cause those that love me to inherit yesh (numerical value of; and that I may fill their treasuries" (Proverbs 8:21.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן חֲלַפְתָּא, לֹא מָצָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא כְּלִי מַחֲזִיק בְּרָכָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֶלָּא הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (תהלים כט), ה' עֹז לְעַמּוֹ יִתֵּן ה' יְבָרֵךְ אֶת עַמּוֹ בַשָּׁלוֹם:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Halafta said: the Holy One, Blessed be He, found no vessel that could contain blessing for Israel save that of peace, as it is written: "The Lord will give strength unto his people; the Lord will bless his people with peace" (Psalms 29:11).
